reviews.title: Best looking console/HTPC style case that can fit some larger GPU's
reviews.comment: This review is for the Fractal Ridge ITX case in black color. I purchased this case specifically for its looks and horizontal configuration ability. I think it looks great and matches my other black components on my TV console table. The white components inside the case really isn't noticeable at all outside of the case. Component installation is very easy and straight forward. Just follow the directions for the power supply (SFX form factor only) and GPU installation. For GPU size, I recommend no more than a 2.5 slot thick GPU to keep the stock preinstalled case fans. The two case fans are 140mm and standard thickness. To use a 3 slot GPU you would be limited to a slim fan or no case fans and cooling performance would be affected. The GPU in my pictures is the Asrock 9070 XT Steel Legend and is 2.5 half slots thick. The case fans are right on top and touch the GPU shroud, but it keeps the GPU cool. I do strongly recommend removing the top of the case, then remove the preinstalled fans, install the GPU, then carefully slide the fans down into position and screw them in and make sure they are intaking air (blowing air onto the GPU). Note the included 140mm case fans have a lip and are specially designed to fit this case as intake so that the fan blades do not rub against the frame. If you replace the fans, you may have to use spacers to prevent the fan blades from touching the frame. Do note that the CPU heatsink is limited to 70mm in height. This severely limits CPU choices. For me I found that my Ryzen 7 7800X3D would overheat and cause a system shutdown. My Ryzen 5 8400F gets really hot, at 95 Celsius but does not shutdown. My advice is to stick with Ryzen 5 or Core i5 series for this case. There is room at the top of the frame where the CPU is that can hold an 80mm fan but the screw holes are smaller than typical fan screws, so I'll have to see if I can find some screws that will fit. The side panels work on either side. I chose to have the CPU facing down and the GPU facing up to give better cooling for the GPU. Having the CPU facing up did not make a difference to the CPU temps. I think it really needs 80mm fan in CPU chamber. If this case was slightly thicker/wider to accommodate taller CPU coolers and 3 slot GPUs with the standard thickness side case fans, then it would have been the perfect small form factor build with no compromises. Due the compact layout, the thermal performance limits your component options. For me this works out because I'm using this PC with a 4k TV and gaming performance isn't bound by the CPU at 4k resolution and my 8400F is perfectly reasonable. I also recommend getting a motherboard with overclocking features not for overclocking but for the voltage controls to lower or limit the CPU voltage. I do recommend this case overall if you're looking for a home theater or console style case that looks great and fits in with other components. There just aren't too many options that have the looks, price, and compact size. Do note that there are some component choice compromises due the compact size.

reviews.title: Beautiful case, works well with a few tweaks
reviews.comment:
First Impressions:
First off, the case is beautiful and is built with quality.
- An all white build is a nice change and it doesn't show dust as bad as darker colors.
- This case does NOT have the iCUE option, or the fans that can be linked by iCUE.
- You have to use your RGB controller from your motherboard or other RGB controller.
- If you get a Corsair CPU water cooler with one, you can replace the case fans with iCUE fans later and link them together as there is a spot in the back of the motherboard mounting plate for an iCUE hub or 2.5" SATA Drives
Extra features:
The case has a lot of room* for a large motherboard build and some cool features
- Sliding mount for water coolers or large fans at the top
- Rotating PCIE slot mounting plate
- GPU Support bracket
- Thumbscrew PSU connection
- Lots of airflow and places to mount more fans
- Support for rear connection motherboards
- White magnetic strip to cover the gap from the motherboard to the case
Build:
- I built with a Gigabyte Aorus X870E Pro X3D ICE
- *I had to remove and flip the GPU support bracket over as the bracket was blocking a USB 3 header on the motherboard. This also prevented me from using the white magnetic strip to cover the gap between the motherboard and case.
- I changed the orientation of the water cooler radiator to allow the addition of a rear fan in case I wanted to add one later as there is not a lot of room in the top/rear of the case.
Functionality:
- Front USB ports and button work well
- With a water cooled, overclocked 9800X3D and a GeForce 3090, everything stays very cool in the case
- The stock fans are very quiet
- Plenty of room for PSU cable management with white 1000W Corsair PSU
- It is wider than other cases

NZXT H6 was a close second because I have built inside at least 6 NZXT H210 cases and they are quality cases.  The C5 included a fan controller and 7 ARGB fans and that swayed me in that direction.
Overall impression is good.  If it just had another 25-35mm of space past the edge of the bottom of the motherboard for cable management that would have been perfect.  The bottom edge of the ATX motherboard sits next to the fans.  I had to take out a fan to get the GPU cables in this area.  You can see the limited room in one of the attached pictures.  Still have lots of spaghetti in the back.  Overall a very sweet case.

Build quality feels solid for the price, and the tempered glass side panel really shows off the components nicely. The white finish looks sleek, though it does attract fingerprints more than I expected—so be ready to clean it now and then.

reviews.title: An engineering marvel!
reviews.comment: I had a full size tower to the side of my computer desk. I wanted to downsize to a mid-tower so that the case would fit under the desk. This case had the right size, and looked great in pictures. I'd have to give up my Blu-Ray burner, since this case has no drive bay cutouts. I haven't used that drive in a year, meaning it wasn't an issue. I ordered the color they call 'Matcha Green', with the optional LCD. Once I unboxed this case, I began to see how vast an improvement it was over what I had previously. Nearly every panel attaches with magnets or push clips. No screws.  Only two small 4" panels don't come off. Space is tight, despite the larger size. Removing all panels makes installing components (almost) trivial. More on that below. There are channels for routing cables, lots of cutouts for going from front to rear, and enough fan options to make a hovercraft. Only two fans on the top are included.  There are a few fan mounts that have the two sets of holes for four screws, but primarily the fans install on rails. Put them wherever on the rail you want! The case supports the new 'hidden connector' motherboards. Mine is an old-style ATX, but it worked fine. Very clever engineering went into the drive mounts. There are no bays as such. The drives mount to thumbscrew panels on the underside of the motherboard tray. The resulting case, with lights on full display, impressed even my wife (who wishes the computer gear was in some closet). My liquid cooling system is fairly simple and left plenty of height. The LCD is still on order. The case comes with two base panels for this. One has the cutout for the LCD, the other does not. And, did I mention that there are multiple mesh screens that slide out for cleaning? What's there to say on the negative side? * I had to remove the power supply mounting bracket in order to install the power supply, then put the bracket back. There was physically no way to squeeze a standard size power supply in otherwise. * This again is ingenious engineering, but is a pain as well: the motherboard mounts such that the back panel connectors are at the top of the case, totally invisible from the outside. You route cables out through a hole in the back of the top cover. After I had the installation complete and got ready to attach cables, I looked at that internal connector and wondered if I'd need medical instruments to access connections. Then I noticed the 2nd half of the cleverness here: unscrew a single thumbscrew, and the entire top fan assembly lifts out. Awesome! * Getting access to the GPU connectors was more problematic, as they're further 'in'. With my dexterity-missing fingers, I did have to use a pair of thin needle-nose pliers. Some smart people really did their homework on this case. You just have to disassemble it to REALLY appreciate it.
reviews.author: W. Lee

reviews.title: Truly A Showpiece
reviews.comment: I love this case. Everything about it is a showpiece, so it's meant to be on full display on a desk or other sturdy surface. Don't hide this beauty under your desk or off in a corner! If you have a lot of RGB elements, they will really shine in this case. Pros: - Great visibility, you can see everything from the top mounted fans to the PSU cover on the bottom - Very sturdy glass panels that are press-to-release (like your grandma's old curio cabinet doors) - Compatibility with different sizes and configurations of case fans and radiators - Airflow! There's so much room for airflow and the sides are all protected by mesh covers - Sideways motherboard mounting gives a refreshing new look to an existing build - Hidden compartment on the back of the top panel for wires to run to the back of the motherboard, makes for a very clean looking build - Should fit almost any chonky or long GPU as long as you take one of the removeable metal coverings on the bottom off - Has the option to buy add-ons such as a screen for the bottom front panel and a stand to display the case on its side Cons: - Standoffs are low quality and the holes for them may not be machined right, I had to replace many standoffs with extras I had and even then, some had to be forced into the holes because they hadn't been machined properly - Back wiring can be an issue, especially if you have any kind of limited mobility in your hands. Lots of tight spaces, especially if you need to use the hard drive bay - If you don't buy the add-on screen for the bottom front panel, you may see wires through the mesh depending on how you wired your system - Very difficult to wire the PSU unless you have one with side-facing or angled connectors - You can't have Wi-Fi antennas installed on the back of the motherboard with this case, they will not fit. If you have an antenna that sits away from the motherboard it will be fine, but antennas that come directly off the back of the motherboard will not fit. I suggest using Ethernet for this case - Cannot put a radiator at the top of the case, only on the sides - Will need a splitter for the USB ports on the front of the case for most motherboard models unless it has two inputs for case USBs All in all, I'm really glad I bought this case even though the price made me feel a bit sick. I would not suggest it for beginners since the motherboard is rotated 90 degrees and can cause some issues with running wires, and the fans up top are a bit awkward. I can't attest to the fans that came with the case because I didn't use them, I already had case fans on hand that I used instead. Quality control on the hardware (screws, standoffs, etc) could be better but as long as you have extras on hand, it shouldn't be a big deal.

reviews.title: Make no mistake, its big
reviews.comment:
Just make sure you are going into this case understanding its size well.

The new Frame cases from Corsair are slightly bigger in every way compared to the previous versions.

Now, to be honest I was not going to really write this review until I Corsair came through with their promises of the modular add-ons to customize the case to your liking.

They recently released a bunch of new front grills, side panel, motherboard tray and PSU cover options, I can say that this is now a fully fleshed out product.  

As the product stands on its own, its good.  Its high airflow, its quite simple yet attractive at the same time.  Yes, it does seem like its a plain case, but there are so many options to be had in the 5000.  You have three 360 radiator options, up to 12 120mm fans, any CPU air cooler should fit in this beast.

The only points I can really take away from the case is that the stock panels do feel a little "cheap" and I mean for the price of the FRAME cases, I don't think I can be too harsh.  In a time when everything is expensive, being able to get your hands on a case with a much versatility as the FRAME cases, is actually great.

I think overall this is a 5 star product, especially now with all the new panels that are being offered.  If you are not interested in any of those, then this is a solid 4 star case with only points off for the lower quality side panels that come with it.  Pure performance wise, this case will not let you down.

reviews.title: Built like a tank and might be the last case I ever buy for all my builds
reviews.comment: This case is an investment well worth the money. I see myself never having to upgrade my case for my future builds, so I can easily seeing this case lasting me well over two decades or more. I have had other cases that weren't as well made and built with quality material like this Corsair Air 5400 and those have lasted well over a decade, so this one being built like a tank will definitely last longer as long as you handle the doors with care. It's a hefty case and wide as it's a triple chamber case, so keep it in one spot and it will last you a long time. The triple chamber innovation is definitely on point as it deviates the hot air from your CPU AIO directly out of the open chamber. It looks super clean, well made, allows you to manage and hide cables from view, and is easy to work with when installing your components. I really love this case and plan on using this over and over. I just built my new rig so this is going to be protecting some expensive components as well as showcasing those components in an organized and clean way. I really like that the metal has no sharp corners so there's no chance of accidentally cutting a finger or jabbing yourself while putting your rig together. The finish is top notch and honestly, I could see this selling for more than it is. So, there's still a lot of value even at the current market rate.

Build: X670E Tomahawk, 9800x3d, 64G Corsair CL30 6K, Phantom Spirit 120, Nitro+ 7900xtx, A1000GL, 4-140mm, 5-120mm + 2-120mm CPU fans, Blu-ray RW, and 5.25 USB-C 3.2 expansion. reviews.title: Easy and Clean PC Building!
reviews.comment: This case is easy to build with since all the panels are removable. The Icue link products are pricey, but they are well worth it. It cuts down on cables and centralizes all of your products under one controller by daisy chaining them together. All of the fans and ARGBs use a single cable type with the Icue Link. The new Corsair fans and Icue 360 Titan are nearly silent. I'm not a fan of the rubber edge covers for the wire management cutouts. It looks much cleaner without them. The cutouts are rounded off nicely so your cables and wires won't get chaffed or cut. This is the best case that I have ever used.
reviews.author: Rh3mY

reviews.title: Great Case for airflow AND aesthetics!
reviews.comment: Absolutely love my 3500X with the Icue link system! It's a beautiful case and I love the different options for fan sizes, I have a 140mm set for intake at the bottom front and every other slot filled with 120mm Icue link fans. The airflow in this case is top tier, I'm running a 5700X3D and a 9060XT with the Corsair Icue link titan 360 aio in this case, and even under full load on a 100 degree summer day I have never seen temps over 62 degrees C on cpu or GPU, I attribute that mostly to the airflow design of the case and the efficiency of the Icue link titan cooler. My only knock against this case is the big glass panel has gotten loose up at the top from the amount of times I have opened and closed it over the last year to clean or upgrade components. Other than that I have zero complaints, it's a beautiful case that's intuitive to build in, with cable management tie down points all over the place, several spots to put storage such a 2.5 inch and 3.5 inch Sata SSD or HDD. It's got plenty of room for even massive graphics cards and options for mounting the aio in the front or the top. It's worth noting that if you intend on doing a push pull configuration for the aio (fans mounted on both sides on the radiator) you'll want to side mount it rather than top mount because your ram will most likely gg in the way. I would absolutely recommend this case to anyone interested in building in a "fishbowl" case that's also looking for top tier airflow and cooling potential. There's plenty of room for even a custom water cooling loop, which will be my next adventure with this case

reviews.title: Clean Build, Great Cooling, and Efficient Setup
reviews.comment: We built two gaming rigs using this case—one for me and one for my son—with slightly different hardware but the same result: clean, efficient builds with excellent cooling, thanks to the Corsair iCUE Link system. The simple cable setup for the fans and the iCUE Link Titan 360 RX RGB Liquid CPU Cooler made cable management much easier compared to traditional setups. Each rig is running 10 fans, and the cooling has been quiet, efficient, and reliable, even during long gaming sessions. The iCUE software does take some time to learn—it’s not the most intuitive—but once you get used to it, it works well. I appreciate that it can control all Corsair iCUE Link fans and the cooler in one interface, with prebuilt or custom fan curve options. Overall, if you’re looking to build a clean, great-looking PC with efficient cooling, the Corsair 3500X iCUE Link case is a fantastic choice.

reviews.title: Well designed and easy to build in case!
reviews.comment: TLDR: This is a great case from Lian Li that's priced well and easy to build in with excellent cable management and component space! I build computers and I've had the opportunity to build in dozens of cases.  Lian Li is a brand that consistently delivers in terms of quality and ease of use.  I've build in a few versions of the LANCOOL 217 and personally, I prefer the black with walnut version.  The INF version has a beautiful mirror exterior that's definitely a love it or hate it thing, but the large speaker looking front fans provide a unique look and provide great air flow.  The build I did had a 9800X3D and RTX 5080 and even under load the system remained relatively quite. The matching Lian Li 360mm AIO was only $99 too and complimented the build well. The only con I can see is not touching the mirror finish or you will get finger prints.  Not touching the front of the case was a new challenge for me, but it turned out well.

reviews.title: A Great Case For Airflow At Reasonable Price!
reviews.comment: A case that's glorious for nice airflow at a good price.  The quality of the case is outstanding and compatible with any motherboard you use.  The assembly is quite easy with the ability to remove the top to easily install an AIO. It also allows for a side PSU orientation that makes getting to the sockets easier.  The only downside to this orientation is not having access to the PSU switch that's available if you use the traditional orientation with the case. The case has various features allowing for various ways to configure your build. Noise level is great and the overall size of the case is perfect for your PC building needs!  One reviewer gave the case a 1 star because of the fan noise due to the pre-installed fans running at max by default.  While this is an annoying issue it is easily resolved by simply switching the fans from "DC" to "PWM" in your bios!  Don't let that review deter you from this purchase unless you take issue with needing to deal with your BIOS just to change a default fan setting compared to other cases.

reviews.title: Surprisingly great case
reviews.comment:
I was not sure how this case would compare to the 6500x or 2500x in terms of cabling space and routing or overall esthetics. Even once the case was in and I was planning everything out, I was skeptical.
Boy did it turn out better than I expect.  The cable management was a lot easier to route and take care of, build quality is in par with Corsair, everything fit the way you would want from a standard mid-size case. Of course, have the iCue Link fans makes cabling a lot easier as there is just 2 cables at most for fans to route into the back.
I have a mix of LX and RX fans, all 120mm, and the airflow is pretty steady. With a Titan 360mm AIO, I am seeing CPU and main board temps staying steady in the 30-40*C range, which is awesome. GPU still runs hot at around 70*C but I think that is more about the age (Sapphire 5700XT Nitro+) than with the case.
Absolutely love the included GPU anti-sag bracket, the function of the modular design, and how easy it is to access compared to previous cases (CM 690II Advanced and Corsair Graphite 780T).
Bottom line, for a budget case and build, huge improvement and esthetics all around.

Between the busted cheap fans and the support bracket not fitting i of course emailed thermaltake support about warranty and have not heard back days later. Best buy support in the app assured me I could go to my local store and have them at least replace the fans with the same model (the store did NOT). Regardless of the physical aspects, it's a great case. Every panel is easy to remove, and there's plenty of space. The brown is a little lighter in person than it looks online, but it's still nice.

It's a little unclear from the images, but the top panel pops off to expose the mobo's I/O shield, and cables can route through a couple of holes in the back. I have a wifi antenna and HDMI cable running out of mine and there's enough room between the plugs and the top panel so that the cables aren't squished down or anything. Like I said, plenty of room.

This was delivered from the manufacturer in the original box that includes product images on the sides, and could easily be mistaken for a computer by any porch pirates, so keep that in mind. The packaging inside was fine and my unit had no damage issues.

reviews.title: Admirable performance for the cost, but it is tall
reviews.comment: TLDR: you can get better cooling from an AIO, but the price and performance of this tower perfect for your average user on a budget. Make sure it fits in your case. The mounting system is secure and makes good contact with the CPU die. The included thermal compound is good enough to not require another purchase as well. My issue with the mounting bracket was that it required more force than I anticipated to align the screws and I had to remount the cooler to ensure even pressure because I had missed that one screw was not threaded into the bracket. - perhaps it could have used slightly taller standoffs. Otherwise installation was easy and the fan mount looks nicer than clips would for this styling. RGB is bright and the selection of colors and modes are fun. I appreciate that I can pick a plain white light or just leave it off. In terms of performance, I see ~20C difference above ambient from my stock cooler (wraith stealth) and the noise is potentially blower under load depending on your fan curve. Under heavy load with a slight OC my temps are stable below 75C and idle around 35C. The main downside to look out for is it's height from the GPU. My case is wide and accommodates the cooler, but if you have a narrow case I would look for another solution.

reviews.title: Sturdy and Effective Cooling with Appealing Aesthetics
reviews.comment: This fan was selected for use in my new desktop computer, and my experience with it thus far has been positive. It looks good, with attractive color accents that enhance the overall appearance of my new desktop. Beyond aesthetics, the fan exhibits a robust and sturdy construction, instilling confidence in its long-term durability. Most importantly, it performs well, and moves a lot of air, which is crucial for maintaining optimal system performance. The fan's sturdy build is a notable advantage, suggesting resilience and longevity. Additionally, the appealing color scheme adds a welcome visual element to the computer's internal components. Its capacity to move a substantial amount of air is a critical pro, ensuring efficient cooling and contributing to the overall stability and performance of the system. At this time, no drawbacks have been identified. In conclusion, this fan proves to be a solid choice for a computer build, offering a combination of effective cooling performance, durable construction, and pleasing visual design. Its ability to move a significant volume of air, coupled with its sturdiness and attractive colors, makes it an excellent choice.
reviews.author: Tommy Amos

reviews.title: This product is amazing.
reviews.comment: So prior to this purchase I bought a msi mag 240mm(garbage). Troubleshot this AIO for 2 months before finally rma'ing it at the time of posting this. Playing games was 80+, prime95 tests/cinebench 80-90c and specifically destiny two sometimes I'd see 93c, apex 75-85c. I installed the 212 black argb last night. The temps are absolutely amazing. Once I played for about an hour to get an accurate reading I didn't even hit 70c most of the time i was under 60c even at 100% cpu loadwith this thing on my 5600x at stock with a -25 curve. Bang for buck this product is amazing especially when it is on sale, it is a huge value and works amazing for a 65w chip. Only thing that sucked was the mount on the back of the motherboard. I had to take 8 or 9 screw out of my motherboard to get enough clearance for the bottom left screw on the backplate. It wasn't hard just an extra step. The fan is not addressable rgb(which I am just going to replace it). I just used the little switch it comes with for the time being. If you add another fan for a push/pull I'd imagine temps would drop a little lower even. If you're like me and research until your crazy on pc parts. Just buy this thing. Just make sure you're not on a like 12900k it won't cool super high wattage cpus but for mids like the 5600x. Absolutely amazing. 1 weird thing I want to add just in case anyone else has this issue. First boot up even with the stock fan plugged into the cpu fan pwm. I got "cpu fan error!" The workaround for this is just to turn off the monitor on the cpu fan in bios. Super weird, I didn't care much since I am replacing that fan anyways, but just so you know! Even if you disable the monitoring of the fan, works fine

reviews.title: The Best-Looking AIO Money Can Buy (But Your Walle
reviews.comment:
The Kraken Elite 360mm is basically the cool kid of CPU coolers—literally and figuratively. The new 2.72-inch IPS screen is gorgeous, way brighter and bigger than before, and throwing a custom GIF on there never gets old . Cooling performance is legit too—NZXT ditched Asetek for their own "Turbine" pump, and it keeps high-end chips like the 7800X3D or 14900K surprisingly chilly even under load . Installation is straightforward with pre-applied paste and a single breakout cable, so you won't be cursing at your motherboard for an hour .

That said, it's not all smooth sailing. The CAM software is the usual love-it-or-hate-it situation—cool when it works, annoying when it bugs out or feels bloated . The price stings too; you're paying a premium for that screen more than raw cooling performance . Also, some users have reported pump noise or software glitches over time, so reliability isn't a sure thing . If you want the best-looking AIO on the block and don't mind the cost, go for it. If you just care about thermals, a cheaper Arctic Liquid Freezer III will get you 90% of the way there for half the cash.

reviews.title: This AIO Cooler Is a Monster
reviews.comment: After a lot of research and comparing different options, I finally decided to invest in the ROG Ryujin III 360 ARGB Extreme, and honestly, it’s one of the best hardware upgrades I’ve made to my PC. If you’re looking for a top-tier, powerful AIO cooler with insane aesthetics, this is it. Right out of the box, you can tell this is a premium product. The build quality is exceptional — everything feels solid, high-end, and well thought out. The 3.5-inch LCD screen is next-level. Not only is it super customizable, but also extremely useful for monitoring system temps, loads, and even displaying custom images or GIFs. It adds a futuristic, high-tech vibe to your setup. Performance-wise, the Ryujin III 360 is a beast. I’m running a high-end CPU, and this cooler keeps it running cool even under heavy workloads. The integrated pump fan and the Noctua radiator fans do an amazing job — whisper-quiet and super efficient, which is something I really appreciate during long gaming or work sessions. The integration with Armoury Crate is smooth too. From there, I customized both the screen and the ARGB lighting to match the rest of my ROG setup. It synced perfectly and gave me full control over the visual side of things. I 100% recommend this AIO to anyone who wants the best cooling performance with standout aesthetics. Yes, it’s a premium product and it’s not cheap — but you get what you pay for: stability, silence, power, and style. Perfect for gamers, streamers, and content creators who want nothing but the best. In short: • Insane thermal performance • Sleek, futuristic design • Quiet and powerful • Highly customizable • A must-have for enthusiasts and power users The ROG Ryujin III 360 ARGB Extreme is an absolute powerhouse and a centerpiece in any serious build.

If you’re looking for a top-tier, powerful AIO cooler with insane aesthetics, this is it. Right out of the box, you can tell this is a premium product. The build quality is exceptional, everything feels solid, high-end, and well-thought-out. The large LCD screen is loaded with options and is awesome for those who want to know what their CPU and GPU stats are, you can also load custom images or GIFs and videos. As far as performance is concerned, the ASUS ROG Ryujin III 360 is on a level all its own. I’m running an AMD 9950X3D CPU on a ASUS ROG Strix X870E-E Gaming MB and this cooler not only keeps my CPU at very manageable temps, it's busy cooling my VRMs as well, which is a huge plus considering I have 96GB of RAM and a 7900XTX GPU also creating heat, my temps at idle are sitting around 42 C, and while gaming I have not gone over 70C, I can't ask for more than this. The integration with Armoury Crate so far has been smooth, too. Everything synced perfectly, giving me full control over the visual software side of things. I definitely recommend this AIO to anyone looking for the best cooling solution with excellent aesthetics. It’s a premium product, it’s not cheap — but we all know you get what you pay for: quality, stability, style, power, and options. reviews.title: Good AIO, exceptional display
reviews.comment: This worked well and looks great.  I ended up switching to a 420 liquid freezer for my system though because it was working a little too hard in my Ryzen 9 system since my office does not have central air.  You do need to commit to running the software (windows only) and it will revert to the default logo images when windows is not actively running the program.  This looks good while you are using your computer, but expect it to show just the default images if your computer is hibernating or you the software is not running in the background.  Overall, I had no issues with the software though.  I enjoyed the "capture" feature which allows you to basically create any 30 sec video you want for looping.  I had a lightning dragon in flight and my son is currently showing a black hole image on his that looks amazing.  For me the temps were a little off from what my MB said, but that just may be different sensor readings.  Is it overpriced, probably. reviews.title: Great buy and great product
reviews.comment: Building my first PC, I wanted a cooler that offered both performance and style, and the TRYX Panorama 360 did not disappoint. The packaging was impressive, and the cooler itself has a premium look that instantly adds a polished touch to my setup. I was worried about the installation process since I’m new to building, but it turned out to be much easier than I expected. The instructions were straightforward, and I got it installed without any issues. It fits well in my case, and the quality feels top-notch. Performance-wise, this cooler keeps my Ryzen 5800X3D running comfortably cool, with idle temps staying in the low 30s. Even during intense gaming sessions, it barely reaches the mid-60s. I also appreciate how quiet it runs—I hardly notice the fans. The standout feature is definitely the OLED screen. The display quality is sharp, and the L-shaped design gives my build a unique and modern look. I included a video to show just how detailed the panoramic screen is with the default software graphics—it’s very clean and adds a whole new level of customization to the setup. Pros: - Sleek design with a stunning OLED display - Great cooling performance for gaming and everyday use - Runs quietly, even under load - Installation-friendly for beginners - High-quality construction Cons: - It's a bit expensive, but the features and quality justify the cost - After using this, I don’t think I could go back to a basic cooler For my first build, this AIO was definitely the right choice, and I'd recommend it to anyone looking to step up their cooling game.

reviews.title: GOAT AIO!
reviews.comment: I've built many PCs over the years, and I doubt another AIO will top this one anytime soon. TRYX nailed the details, from the packaging and cooler design to the ease of installation. The AIO looks premium, and the build quality is outstanding. This CPU cooler is perfect for gamers and professionals who need top-notch reliability, performance, and cooling. I'm running a Ryzen 5900x, and the CPU stays in the low 30s on idle, and rarely exceeds the high 60s under gaming load. It runs cool and quiet so you can focus on work or play without distraction. What sets this AIO apart is its crystal-clear Panorama OLED display. It's the best-looking AIO on the market, featuring a large L-shaped OLED screen that plays custom videos in high resolution and frame rates. The TRYX Kanali software makes managing the display/fans simple and intuitive. Pros: • Best looking AIO and Display technology • Excellent cooling performance, especially under load. • Quiet operation, even with multiple fans running. • Premium build quality and reliable pump performance. • Easy to install, even for first-time builders. • Compatible with a variety of CPU platforms. Cons: • High end product with matching price point, but it’s worth the money. • Will be difficult to go back to another CPU cooler after using this one.

I ordered it last night and it was delivered this morning. It took about an hour (maybe a little more) to install start to finish and worked perfectly as advertised. Once I got it installed, I downloaded and installed the software, made some config changes and jumped into a game (COD7). Watching my temps - they never got over 72C which is great as I am usually in the 90s and sometimes hitting the 100C threshold that you want to stay away from. I really expected some issues as far as connectivity and things like that, but I had 0 issues. Very happy with this AIO and I would recommend to anyone that is looking for a liquid cooler. My only advice is to do some research on what you currently have so you make sure you have things like the SATA power plug available and know where to plug in the internal USB connection and the AIO connector on the MB.

If I wasn't an electronics technician by trade this AIO would likely have been returned due to the paucity of the instructions. As it was, it took far more thinking and fiddling than one should reasonably expect from a (relatively) non-technical component.

reviews.title: Screen DOA
reviews.comment:
I have pretty mixed feelings about this cooler because the actual cooling performance has been excellent, but the experience getting everything fully working was much more frustrating than it should have been.

The biggest issue is that the LCD screen was completely dead right out of the box. Unfortunately, the screen was one of the main reasons I specifically purchased this version instead of a standard AIO cooler, so opening everything up, installing it, and realizing the display wouldn’t turn on at all was incredibly disappointing. The pump itself worked, the fans spun normally, and cooling performance was fine, but the LCD module was totally DOA.

To CORSAIR’s credit, their customer service was ultimately good to work with, but the process felt far more drawn out and complicated than necessary. Initially, they wanted me to remove the entire cooler from my system and mail the whole thing back. That would have meant removing the radiator, fans, thermal paste, and basically tearing apart a freshly completed build over what was clearly just a failed LCD module.

After some back and forth, I explained that the screen itself is removable and that CORSAIR literally sells the LCD module separately as its own standalone product. Once they understood that, they finally agreed to just send me a replacement screen instead of requiring me to return the entire unit. That was definitely the correct solution, but it took longer than I expected to get there.

There was also a bit of frustration regarding shipping costs. At first they wanted me to pay for postage, which honestly didn’t sit well considering the part arrived defective from day one. Thankfully, after additional communication, they eventually provided a prepaid shipping label and handled it properly. Again, they made it right in the end, but the overall process could have been much smoother.

Now for the actual cooler itself, because outside of the LCD issue, it has honestly been fantastic.

Cooling performance has been excellent on my system. Temperatures stay low even under heavy gaming and productivity workloads, and the pump and fans are impressively quiet. I was expecting a 360mm cooler to perform well, but I’ve still been pleasantly surprised with how efficiently this thing handles heat while remaining relatively silent.

Installation itself was also pretty straightforward. The mounting hardware felt solid, the pre-applied thermal paste made setup easier, and the daisy-chained fan connections helped reduce cable clutter significantly. Once installed, it gives the system a really clean look overall.

After receiving the replacement screen, the LCD functionality has worked perfectly. The display is vibrant, sharp, and very customizable through iCUE software. I really enjoy being able to display CPU temperatures, GIFs, and custom images directly on the pump head. It adds a lot of personality to the build and honestly looks great once everything is functioning properly.

The software customization is fairly easy as well. I had no trouble setting up screen layouts, animations, and monitoring information. The display quality itself exceeded my expectations once I finally got a working module.

Overall, this cooler performs extremely well and looks fantastic when fully functional. The only reason this experience was frustrating was because the LCD screen arrived dead and the RMA process took longer than necessary. Still, CORSAIR did eventually make things right, and since getting the replacement screen installed, the cooler has been reliable and issue-free.

The airflow is strong and consistent, keeping my system cool even during intense gaming or rendering sessions.
What really sets these fans apart is the iCUE LINK ecosystem. The single-cable connection per fan makes cable management a breeze, and the magnetic dome bearings keep noise levels impressively low. The RGB lighting is vibrant, smooth, and fully customizable through iCUE, with layered lighting effects that look absolutely premium.
If you're building a high-end rig and want fans that deliver both form and function, this kit is a no-brainer. Corsair continues to raise the bar for smart cooling solutions.

I tried regular RGB fans (plenty of those in 140mm) which looked great but they were made for airflow and just didn't do the trick against my radiator, temps were still higher than I wanted. High static fans in that size in RGB are far more limited in selection and the "best" were about $45 each, these I got for half of that and they work awesome.  Temps are down, quiet noise and they look awesome. The only complaint I have is that the fans have very low LED count, (only 8 per fan, most have at least 16+) and they cant be controlled individually, both fans are seen as one.  Outside of that I couldn't be happier and I highly recommend them if you want something made to go against a radiator

Just the right amount of RGB for a beautiful build while keeping the heat monster at bay. One cable to attach 8 fans daisy chained while still being able to address each fan individually is just incredible. I absolutely love this set up. I tried these and the qx icue link fans and could not stand the qx series. These hands down blow those qx series fans out of the water. Corsair nailed it with this design. My rig specs: 3500x case Auros 879e pro board, 9950x3d chip 64 gig Vengeance 3cl times at 6200mhz 7900xtx GPU Titan 360 aio 3 reverse 120s for intake 3 standard 120s for radiator 1 140 reversed for intake 1000 EVGA PSU Love it!

reviews.title: A Smooth Setup and Great Performance
reviews.comment: I recently upgraded my PC with the CORSAIR iCUE Link LX120-R RGB 120mm 3-Fan Pack, and I’m genuinely impressed. The fans are sleek and stylish, with a reverse rotor design that keeps the RGB lighting visible even when mounted as intake fans . The dual light loops create smooth, synchronized lighting effects that really enhance the look of my build. Installation was a breeze. The iCUE Link system uses a single cable to connect all components, reducing cable clutter and simplifying the setup process. The included iCUE Link System Hub allows for easy management of up to seven devices per port, and the reversible cables make connecting components straightforward . Performance-wise, the fans are quiet and efficient. They operate at a noise level ranging from 10 to 38 dBA and can reach speeds up to 2400 RPM, providing a good balance between airflow and noise . The magnetic dome bearing ensures low friction and contributes to the fans' quiet operation. One thing to note is that the iCUE Link system is not backward compatible with older Corsair controllers, so you’ll need to use the included hub and cables . The CORSAIR iCUE Link LX120-R RGB 120mm 3-Fan Pack is a solid choice for anyone looking to enhance their PC's aesthetics and cooling performance. The easy installation, clean design, and reliable performance make it a worthwhile investment.

reviews.title: Stunning Color, Easy Installation, and Plenty of Compliments!
reviews.comment: I couldn't be happier with the Thermaltake SWAFAN EX 14 ARGB fans. From the moment I installed them, they have been an absolute standout addition to my build — and everyone who has seen my setup has had nothing but compliments about how good they look. The white colorway is crisp and clean, and the ARGB lighting takes it to another level entirely. Inside my case, the colors pop beautifully and really tie the whole build together. Whether cycling through colors or locked onto a specific theme, these fans look fantastic and add that premium aesthetic that really makes a build stand out. What really surprised me though was how straightforward the wiring process was. I was a little nervous going in, expecting the usual cable management headache that comes with RGB fans, but the SWAFAN EX 14 made it so much easier than I anticipated. Everything was well organized and the connectors were intuitive, which made the whole installation process smooth and stress-free. On top of the looks, the fans run quietly and perform well across the 500~2000 RPM range, giving me solid cooling without any distracting noise. If you're looking for PC fans that deliver on aesthetics, ease of installation, and reliable performance, the Thermaltake SWAFAN EX 14 ARGB in white is an excellent choice. Highly recommended — my build has never looked better!

This Z-Edge 27” curved gaming monitor completely exceeded my expectations! The 300Hz refresh rate and 1ms response time make gameplay incredibly smooth and responsive—perfect for fast-paced FPS and racing games. No screen tearing or lag, especially with FreeSync enabled.
The curved screen adds a nice immersive feel, especially in darker gaming environments. The full HD 1080p resolution is crisp and clear, and while it’s not 4K, it’s more than enough for gaming at high frame rates. The colors are vibrant, and the frameless design makes it look sleek on my desk.
Setup was simple with plenty of ports—2 DisplayPorts and 2 HDMI—so I can easily switch between my PC and consoles. The built-in eye care features are a nice touch too, reducing strain during long sessions.
Overall, this is an incredible value for a high-performance gaming monitor at this price point. Highly recommend if you want a fast, stylish, and reliable display!

It's strengths are the price, the colors/contrast, and of course the resolution, and it's amazing for workflow and content viewing.
Is HDR any good? I'm not sure. Enabling it requires changing all of my settings and I didn't see enough of a difference to bother. It is not VESA HDR certified, which means if you really want good HDR you'll have to find it somewhere else.
Refresh rate and response time: this monitor has slower response time than you'd want if you want to do a lot of gaming, you'd see ghosting most likely.
Color and contrast: the contrast is good, on the order of a high end TN panel from a few years ago. The color seems to be on the same order or better, but I have no good way to test this objectively.
Overall, if you just want a 4k monitor and aren't too picky about anything but resolution, this will exceed your expectations.

reviews.title: UHD 4K@60Hz refresh rate via HDMI!
reviews.comment:
I'm not sure why all of these comments are saying that 4K@60Hz is only possible via Display Port. Because that is a whole bunch of shenanigans. As you can see in the photo attached, this monitor is fully capable of achieving 4K@60Hz refresh rate through an HMDI cable!
There are 2 HDMI ports on the back of this monitor. The only effort you need to put into this is to make sure you plug the HDMI cable into the HDMI port that supports 4K@60Hz refresh rate, not the 30Hz refresh rate--Easy Peezy. Another thing you might want to confirm is that the processing core on your laptop/desktop is able to support that high of a resolution@60Hz refresh rate. That info is a little harder to find, as you’d need to go to the manufacturer’s site that makes your exact processing cpu and find the specifications of your exact chip model.

Received the monitor the next unboxed it and immediately the stryfoam goes all over the place. Set up the monitor and immediately found the screw to connect the stand to the base was missing. Annoying, but I emailed support. They wanted a photo, which I couldn't provide through the Best Buy portal, so I explained the situation in writing and they said they'd send it. It's the only screw that's supposed to come in the box. 

I needed a monitor, so I drove to a hardware store to improvise while the correct screw shipped. Spent an hour finding the right one.

Got home, used the improvised screw, set up the stand, plugged everything in, and the monitor wouldn't detect my computer. Never had this issue before despite similar exact same setup with different monitor at two homes! Two hours of troubleshooting later, I finally got it working. Image quality was immediately disappointing. Adjusted every setting available and couldn't fix it. You get what you pay for, I suppose.

While waiting for the replacement screw, I ordered a monitor arm. The VESA housing didn't fit. Assumed I had the wrong arm, ordered another. Replacement screws arrived -- also wrong. 

Bought a new monitor arm, but due to timing had to ship it to my other house and bring it back to this location. Set it up, and the VESA housing still didn't fit. On closer inspection, there's a physical imperfection in the housing itself.... the last straw. 

I returned it but Deca Brands owes me three hours of my life back.

I am not a purchaser of this product through Best Buy, however, I was a backer through the original Kickstarter campaign and received my monitors in February 2023. 

A few months ago, the top monitor to my base Geminos developed a streak of shadow vertically through the monitor and a constant high-pitched noise that was not too loud but always present and loud enough while working to be a clear distraction. I reached out to Mobile Pixels and asked if they could fix it and they said even though I was a backer to this project that the monitor was out of warranty and they could only fix it through a fee. Fine, the problems didn't make the monitors inoperable and I could work through the noise with basically any cheap headphones. Just yesterday, the top monitor got extremely worse. Constantly turned off, then when it was on there was either glaring blue pixel problems plaguing the screen, then constant green flashes and glitches across the entire monitor, making it entirely broken. The bottom monitor working perfectly as expected just made this entire process even worse because I could see the potential of both monitors being a perfect work-from-home companion that doesn't take a lot of desk space. Incredibly disappointed with this project, would not recommend Geminos to anyone if this is what happens less than two years of owning the monitors, and the lack of care from Mobile Pixels to help repair their own products from confirmed backers that helped get these off ground in the first place.

reviews.title: Wish it worked out for me
reviews.comment:
This might be a 5-star monitor for some, but unfortunately, it didn't work out for me. I loved the clean, chinless design with no branding on the front. I loved the amount of connectivity--that pop-down hub on the left is so useful, and the Ethernet is a great extra feature. I loved having 120hz. The panel had no backlight bleed and felt very uniform. The KVM worked quickly to swap between my PC and my Macbook.

But for whatever reason, the monitor gave me awful eye strain. I tried everything--adjusting height, distance, brightness, contrast, scaling, and nothing seemed to help. Most of the strain seemed to come while using my Mac, and I learned that 4K does not scale properly within MacOS, leading to slightly blurry edges. Because my primary use-case for this monitor is text and writing (I stare at words for many hours a day), this was not acceptable. I've since changed to an Asus 5K monitor, and the improvement in clarity is obvious. 

Text is crisp and scaled properly within Windows, so if you are a PC user, this monitor will probably be fine for you. But some Mac users, particularly those who need perfect clarity, may have issues.  I also experienced the dreaded "coil whine" issue after about a week of use, and it's not nearly as bad as some people make it out to be if you don't share a bedroom with your computer. However, for something of this price, I would expect better quality control.

I do recommend the monitor, because I'm sure it will work great for most people.

Overall – This is a great little monitor.  It quietly does almost everything right. Dell took a lot of key items - IPS color, 144Hz refresh, FreeSync, adjustable stand – and packed them into an everyday use monitor that works in office and home environments.  If you have limited desk space or just need something extra with a laptop, it’s great. That said, it is a bit small for everyday use. 
Packaging – Dell seems to have this figured out. It’s well-protected with everything neatly organized. Nothing fancy, but everything secure, clearly labeled, and ready to go. 

Assembly – Assembly is a strong point here. Tool-less setup, the stand clicks together easily, and the monitor snaps right in place. Take it out of the box, screw the base on, and snap it into place – took me more time to get the HDMI plugged in than to put it together. 

Touch and Feel – Dell kept the design clean and professional. Thin bezels make it look modern, and the stand is actually better than what you normally get in this class—height, tilt, and swivel adjustments instead of the usual tilt-only budget stand. It doesn’t feel like a $500 monitor, but it does not feel cheap by any means. 

Setup & Functionality – The IPS panel gives good color accuracy and wide viewing angles, text is crisp, and the 144Hz refresh makes everything—from spreadsheets to gaming—feel noticeably smoother. FreeSync worked OK, there was no noticeable shutter.  I used it for about 4 hours straight and did not notice any eye fatigue that I experienced from the smaller footprint.  Awitch between inputs was easy and straightforward, as were all of the other monitor settings – exactly what I would expect from Dell.

It’s nice to see them expand to 2 HDMI ports; however, a display or usbc would have been nice and maybe added some extra flexibility.  The only other drawback is that I may be spoiled with my standard setup of OLED monitors, but the IPS panel doesn’t get the black right – it’s more of a dark gray.  I did notice a bit of motion smoothing, but not significant. 
I
f you have limited desk space or just a little extra for a laptop, I would highly recommend this – not sure there’s much better at this point.  However, for me and usual set up of 34in coupled with a 27in or dual 32ins the 24in did feel a bit small.

reviews.title: A Solid Everyday Monitor With a Few Gotchas
reviews.comment:
Refresh Rate Reality Check: The 144Hz That… Isn’t

On paper, this 27" Dell monitor promises a 144Hz refresh rate, which sounds great - until you look at the ports. Since it only includes HDMI 1.4, you can’t reliably hit that full 144Hz. Modern DisplayPort handles high refresh rates effortlessly, but HDMI 1.4 tends to tap out closer to 120Hz unless you’re using the newest HDMI 2.2 hardware and cables.

Because Dell skipped DisplayPort entirely on this model, the advertised 144Hz ends up being more of a “nice idea” than something most users will actually experience. If you’re buying this specifically for high-refresh gaming, that’s a meaningful limitation to know upfront.

Resolution & Panel Quality: Great for Work, Not Built for Pros or Competitive Gamers

The SE2726HS runs at 1080p, which is perfectly fine for everyday use - browsing, spreadsheets, schoolwork, general productivity. For that crowd, it looks clean and sharp enough.

But if you’re a competitive gamer chasing every pixel of clarity or a content creator who needs precise detail, 1080p on a 27" screen isn’t going to cut it. You’ll probably want something sharper or more color-accurate.

The IPS panel itself is solid. Colors stay consistent from different angles, which is great for office setups or shared workspaces. It’s not a color-grading monitor and it’s not trying to be - so while it won’t wow professional creatives, it handles day-to-day tasks beautifully.

One nice bonus: AMD FreeSync. It does a great job reducing screen tearing in games that support it, which helps smooth out the overall experience even if the panel isn’t built for high-end gaming.

Final Verdict: Who This Monitor Is Actually For

The Dell SE2726HS is a straightforward, dependable monitor that does exactly what most people need it to do. The picture is clean, the colors are decent, and it’s comfortable to use for long work sessions. For the price, it’s genuinely a strong value - especially for students, professionals, or anyone who just wants a reliable display without spending a fortune.

If you’re expecting OLED-level visuals or a cutting-edge gaming experience, this isn’t the monitor for you. But if you want something practical, affordable, and easy to live with, the SE2726HS fits the bill nicely. It’s not my favorite monitor ever, but it’s definitely not a bad one either. For everyday tasks, it gets the job done without fuss.

I've been upgrading my rig and wanted a clean, efficient, and durable solution for powering my new NVIDIA GPU. The CORSAIR 12-Pin GPU Power Cable (Sleeved - Black) exceeded expectations on every front.

Aesthetics & Fit:
This is where Corsair shines. The sleeving gives the cable a premium, custom look that really elevates the build. If you're using a Corsair PSU and want to avoid bulky adapters, this cable is a clean and elegant solution. Compatibility:
It’s a perfect match for Corsair modular PSUs and plugs directly into the PSU side without any need for converters. Be sure to check compatibility (it works with Type 4 PSUs), but if you're in the Corsair ecosystem, it's essentially plug-and-play.

Bottom Line:
This cable is a must-have if you're running a modern GPU and want a clean look without sacrificing performance or reliability. It's a small investment that makes a big difference in both aesthetics and system stability. Highly recommended for anyone doing a custom build or a GPU upgrade.

reviews.title: Compact SFX PSU that actually delivers full-size performance
reviews.comment:
I picked up the NZXT C850 SFX Gold for a small form factor build, and it’s been exactly what I was hoping for. Finding a power supply that can handle modern GPUs without compromising on size or stability isn’t easy, but this one checks the important boxes. The SFX footprint makes it much easier to work inside tighter cases, and the shorter cable runs help keep things manageable when space is limited.
Performance-wise, it’s been solid. Voltage delivery has been stable under load, and I haven’t noticed any odd behavior during startup or heavy GPU usage. The inclusion of the 12V-2x6 connector is a big plus for newer cards, and it’s reassuring to have a unit that’s built around current standards rather than feeling like an afterthought adaptation. The zero RPM fan mode works well too. Under lighter workloads, the system stays quiet, and even when the fan does spin up, it’s not intrusive.
Cable quality is better than average for this category. The fully modular setup helps a lot in small builds, and the included combs make routing cleaner than expected. That said, as others have pointed out, SFX builds are still inherently tight, so you’ll want to plan your cable routing ahead of time. It’s not difficult, just something to be aware of if you’re new to compact builds.
At $199.99, it’s definitely not a budget option, but that’s pretty typical for high-quality SFX units with this level of output and efficiency. You’re paying for reliability, modern GPU support, and a compact design that doesn’t cut corners where it matters. For a high-performance SFF build, it feels like money well spent.

reviews.title: Rock Solid Power, Clean Rails & Quiet Cooling, Handles Dual GPUs Like a Champ: Excellent Stability

I got this from Amazon warehouse.  It looked brand new, and even though they said the packaging was opened everything was there.  It's a good budget motherboard.  It works fine for me with a Ryzen 5 3600, GTX 1660 Super, and PNY Anarchy-X 16gb (2x8 gb) DDR4-3200 ram.  The ram runs at 3200 mhz with xmp turned on without a problem.  With precision boost overdrive, I think that's what it's called, the cpu runs up to the rated boost clock regularly when gaming.
My only complaint so far is the lack of fan headers.  I know it's a budget board, but an extra 4-pin fan header or two would be nice.  This board only has two 4-pin fan headers, one for the cpu fan and one chassis fan.  There is another 3-pin fan header, but my fans only ran at full speed when attached to that.  I could not change the fan speed with either the bios or Asrock's fan control program when using the 3-pin header.  Thankfully, my fans were low enough draw that I could daisy chain five pwm fans off the one 4-pin case fan header.  That was my only issue, as the fans were way too loud when running wide open.

reviews.title: AMD Ryzen 9 7950X3D: Unmatched Gaming Performance with Cutting-Edge Technology
reviews.comment: ### Introduction As a tech enthusiast, I was eagerly awaiting the release of the AMD Ryzen 9 7950X3D, and it did not disappoint. This 16-core, 32-thread processor is a powerhouse designed for those who demand the best in gaming and multitasking performance. ### Performance The AMD Ryzen 9 7950X3D excels in gaming, thanks to its innovative 3D V-Cache technology, which significantly boosts L3 cache capacity to a whopping 128MB. This translates to smoother, faster performance in gaming scenarios where cache size makes a noticeable difference. In my experience, games that are CPU-bound saw substantial improvements, with frame rates soaring and load times reducing dramatically. ### Technical Specifications - **Cores/Threads**: 16/32 - **Base/Boost Clock**: 4.2 GHz / 5.7 GHz - **L3 Cache**: 128MB (3D V-Cache) - **TDP**: 120W - **Recommended Cooler**: 280mm water cooler or better The processor maintains a boost clock of 5.7 GHz, matching the standard 7950X, but operates at a lower base clock of 4.2 GHz to fit within its efficient power envelope. Despite this, the performance in gaming and other CPU-intensive tasks is remarkable. ### Power Efficiency One of the standout features of the 7950X3D is its power efficiency. With a TDP of 120W, it runs cooler and quieter compared to its Intel counterparts. This not only makes for a more pleasant gaming experience but also reduces the overall power consumption of your build. ### Compatibility and Build Considerations However, it’s important to note that the 7950X3D requires the AM5 platform and DDR5 memory, which can be more expensive than older platforms. Additionally, the lack of a bundled cooler means you will need to invest in a high-quality cooling solution to ensure optimal performance. ### Conclusion In conclusion, the AMD Ryzen 9 7950X3D is an exceptional processor that redefines what’s possible in gaming performance. While the initial investment is higher due to the need for DDR5 memory and an AM5 motherboard, the performance gains in gaming and multitasking make it a worthwhile upgrade for any serious gamer or content creator. For those who prioritize top-tier gaming performance and efficiency, the Ryzen 9 7950X3D is the processor to beat. **Pros:** - Unmatched gaming performance - High efficiency and lower power consumption - Future-proof with DDR5 and AM5 compatibility **Cons:** - Higher cost due to new platform requirements - No bundled cooler I highly recommend the AMD Ryzen 9 7950X3D for anyone looking to build a high-end gaming PC or workstation.
reviews.author: Trevor K Smith

reviews.title: This CPU destroys any workload thrown at it! A++ 100% recommended.
reviews.comment: AMD has restored my faith in their brand. Way back in early 2000s I had an AMD processor and it was terrible. 15-20 years later after deciding I didn't want to risk Intel's notoriously bad latest generation of CPUs in my new gaming PC build, I decided to give AMD another try. I did a lot of research about this little powerhouse and while some have had issues I've found it's more than likely a configuration issue on the users end rather than an issue with the CPU itself. The Ryzen 9 7950X3D completely obliterates anything I throw at it. I've run multiple resource intensive games simultaneously with this and it stayed at or below 70C. The base 4.20Ghz clock speed is zippy for everyday users, and the max 5.7Ghz clock is hard to even approach with how insanely well this thing performs. Mind you this is all my personal experience running notorious resource hogs like Diablo 4, World of Warcraft or even Ark. With this CPU and my RTX 4070 Super GPU, I'm running every game on the absolute max settings and it doesn't slow down. I've also used this same CPU as a work processor, I work in IT and it handles a heavy workload like it's a light breeze. Processing code, compiling data mapping, or having 70+ chrome tabs open. You can't slow this thing down. Keep in mind you'll need a AIO Liquid Cooler instead of typical air cooled units and a highly breathable PC Case to keep up with this CPU but the bang for the buck is worth it. Recommended MB is the Gigabyte Aorus X670 AX Elite. Dedicated CPU/SSD bus delivers lightning processing speed. Be sure to pair this with a low latency RAM kit and you'll be amazed. Can't recommend this CPU enough.
reviews.author: James Ferris

reviews.title: Beast of a CPU, sayonara Intel
reviews.comment: Bought this for gaming and multitasking after being thoroughly let down by recent Intel CPU offerings. Got sick of issues with e-cores being total garbage that killed my fps, and turning off most of the cores on my cpu didn't seem like a good solution so I went back to AMD after 12 years of Intel chips. Installation was a breeze, was able to get Expo to work on DDR5 6000MT ram that was on my motherboard QVL no problem. 16 cores is nuts. Mine is stable at 5.4 GHz on a full custom water loop, temps are never higher than 55C. Uses less power than my old i5-13600k and temps are better, too! It is so weird playing a cpu heavy game and seeing 10% cpu usage. Installed with a thermalright AM5 socket mount on a MSI X670E Tomahawk mono. The socket mount is great, it makes it impossible to get thermal paste all over the caps on the cpu and keeps it on the cpu heat-spreader. Extremely happy with the performance, this cpu is a monster. Intel's design ideas of strapping on 10 year old garbage atom cores to their new high performance cores is a really annoying decision because if you are like me still on windows 10, any core can get assigned any task. Had a game get assigned e-cores to render threads and the fps was bouncing between 60 and 7, it was a nightmare. After installing AMD chipset drivers and switching power plan back to balanced, I haven't had any issues at all with this chip. Was even able to use the same windows install I used for my Intel setup without issues.

reviews.title: The best all-around CPU before 9950X3D is released
reviews.comment: This is the best all-around CPU before 9950X3D is released. Its productivity performance is very strong, and the gaming scheduling issue has been resolved. All you need to do is use the "Balanced" power plan, install the latest chipset driver and press Win + G to open the game bar -> settings -> remember this is a game. Most games are auto-recognized, so this step isn't even necessary at all. In most cases, it performs similarly to a 7800X3D, and due to higher max frequency, the 7950X3D can even perform better in some cases. However, I do want to note that AMD has stopped the production of these units, and it'll be a pain to RMA when you encounter an issue. Most likely AMD will upgrade you to a later chip which is great if it doesn't take a long time. Also, there are some memory-related things people need to know before buying: 1. DDR5-8000 is the maximum the CPU will support. Anything higher is only supported by the Ryzen 9000 series, and DDR5-8000 is not necessarily a guarantee despite AMD / Mobo manufacturers advertising its support. 2. The CPU is incredibly unstable if you enable Memory Context Restore and *disable* Power Down Mode. If you want super fast (< 10s) boot times by enabling Memory Context Restore, you need to sacrifice the performance a little bit by enabling both Power Down Mode.

reviews.title: Wowsers
reviews.comment:
If you are not familiar with Amazon Vine, it is basically Amazon trading free* products for honest reviews. You see a lot of Vine reviews that are cookie cutter and based on templates. I aim to make my reviews honest and non-cookie cutter (other than this intro and disclaimer).
* These items are not actually free as Vine members pay income tax on the items they receive. Therefore, I will never order something from Vine unless I actually intend to use it. I think this is important for readers to understand because it means I will never order an item just to provide a fake five star review to a company. If I review something as good, it means I actually enjoyed using it or it fills its intended purpose correctly. Items that don't meet my expectations will be reviewed accordingly.
Why I ordered this item: My AMD 5700x was having a hard time keeping up with my audio production needs. This CPU went on sale so I jumped on it.
Likes:
* This processor offers pretty extreme performance. Twelve full-featured cores is absolutely bonkers on a CPU that was on sale for $370.
* This thing absolutely churns through Ableton. I can have 30 tracks with multiple plugins and effects on each one, and this CPU does not break 10% usage. I don't know how that is possible considering how hard the same song was on my old 5700x. It's the most powerful CPU I have ever used.
* I have had no operational issues with this CPU at all. Everything on my new PC runs smoothly. Games are glassy and productivity apps are rock solid.
No likes:
* This CPU can get hot. I knew that going in and bought an adequate cooler. Still, it's something to consider.
Would I pay full price for this product: I would pay the $370 I paid again because this processor is awesome.
Final thoughts: I'm very happy with my choice on this processor. I had a lot of options and almost went with an X3D model, but I don't game much any more and I knew this would be better for audio production. One word of advice - if you are considering this CPU vs an Intel option, know that AMD processors have full-fledged cores while Intel uses Performance and Efficiency cores. Efficiency cores are not as powerful as the full featured cores AMD offers, so in multithreaded applications in general, AMD offers a more powerful experience when comparing similar core counts to Intel.

reviews.title: The best CPU I'd spend my own money on
reviews.comment:
Once I got past the problem of Amazon sending me an AMD CPU box that had the actual CPU stolen out of it, I finally got ahold of this monster and replaced an elderly Skylake build. Let me tell you, Zen 4 CPUs are... incredible. It's just jaw-dropping how much these pure 16-core/32-thread beasts can do, especially with a proper PBO configuration. Unlike the current-gen Intel consumer parts, which seem to be focusing on packing in weird "efficiency" cores and uneven performance curves, a 7950X delivers consistent, constant, gargantuan throughput across all 32 threads.
I've done everything from gaming under Proton/WINE, language model merging/inference/quantization, and software development on this system in the 3 months I've had it. The 7950X has never stopped impressing me with how *incredibly* potent it is. There are workloads I used to rent AWS compute instances (at almost $2/hr!) to run, and I can take care of them in minutes on my home machine now. And gaming? Pfft! ZERO problems. Turn everything up to Ultra. I'm not going to have to think about CPU power for another 5 or 6 years, easy.
I was an AMD fanboy going back to the AMD 386-20, and I've owned more AMD CPUs than Intel over the decades.  But the last time I owned an AMD CPU was in the mid-2000s, an Athlon FX-57 (the last, fastest, single-core Athlon 64). Ever since then, I've been waiting for AMD to ship a "good" architecture. That finally came with Zen 3, but by the time I was ready to buy... Zen 4 was here. And BOY AM I GLAD IT IS.
Long story short: if you're even *thinking* about buying the best of the consumer Zen 4 CPUs, you found it.
BTW, this is the better of them, between this one and the "3D" one, for applications that are going to stress all the cores simultaneously. The way the 3D thing works looks a little bit faster on benchmarks, but when you are really putting the thing to the test, you'll be glad you went with the real thing.

Boot is twice as fast, and all my applications load fast and windows 11 is actually snappy and a breeze to work with. Not only that, but the advertised 4.6 ghz rating on the chip is misleading because if you are doing any kind of multithreaded application, the chip stays at around 5.2ghz.  The main issue with this chip is the supposed heat range being high compared to other chips, but I've been gaming for a while and haven't hit the "optimal" temperature for the chip yet at 95 degrees centigrade.  Having said that, I threw a darkrock 4 cooler on it, and it seems to be working just fine.  I go with air coolers if I can, and having a GOOD cpu cooler is pretty much mandatory.  Here. reviews.title: The 9700x is THE CPU to get for SFF builds if you're concerned about power and thermals
reviews.comment:
I've always wanted to do an SFF build that was just as capable for gaming as well as some creative work, video editing, etc,  as my larger rigs.
I currently have 2 main systems in the house: Asus Astral 5090 + 9950x3d and 4090FE + 9800x3d, both on larger Lian Li 011D Evo cases with 360 AIO and plenty of fans.  Without those extra fans and larger cases, these systems would run hot, especially with the GPUs they were paired with, so I knew I wanted a CPU that would not only run cooler but also more power-efficient.  Enter the 9700X.
This is my current build and it's a supremely capable and thermally sustainable beast of an SFF build even under heavy 4K gaming loads.  9700X + 5080FE, MSI Mortar mATX mobo, 32gb CL30 Trident Z5 DDR5 6000 expo, Corsair H100i Elite 240mm AIO, and 3 Noctua 120mm low profile Chromax fans (1 intake from rear, 2 intake from bottom) all shoehorned in a tiny Jonsbo(Jonsplus) Z20 case.  Passes all thee stress tests, and even at full 4K gaming loads, thermals are amazing for a SFF build with a 5080!  At these loads, both the 9700x and the 5080FE temps are in the low to mid 60s, and rarely spikes over 70.  These thermals are comparable to my larger builds with only a small sacrifice in performance mainly because the 9700x just can't compete with those X3D chips but can certainly hold its own at a much lower TDP.  Gaming performance is amazing as paired with the 5080FE.
That said, for me at least, an SFF is the only situation where I think the 9700x makes sense.  Price was great and I bought this from amazon for $265.  I was originally going to do this SFF build with another 9800X3D but those have not come down from their $480 price yet and I already knew they ran warmer and drew more power, so I'm extremely happy with the 9700x and wouldn't hesitate to use it again on another SFF build.  Highly recommend.

reviews.title: Excellent CPU if X3D Is Not Necessary, Or Not Available
reviews.comment:
Wanted to buy a 9800X3D, but they went out of stock right as I went to buy, so I opted for the 9700X. Managed to pick this up for $285 via an Amazon deal, and it has more than paid itself off. It's not an X3D CPU, so its gaming performance isn't going to win any awards, but what is there is still fantastic. I have only managed to max out this CPU in Blender and synthetic tests, not games: sandbox games, open worlds (e.g. Abiotic Factor), and VR—including Into the Radius 2, which runs in UE5—just can't push this CPU to its limit.
If your primary focus is gaming and cores/thread counts don't need to reach the stars, buy the Ryzen 5 9600X, the older 7600X3D, or even wait for the upcoming 9600X3D. The 9600X and 9700X are nearly identical in gaming. I bought the 9700X only because I need multithread performance and the 9800X3D was not available for two months.
Perhaps the 9700X's one true advantage over the 9800X3D is its TDP; this is a 65W CPU, whereas the 9800X3D is 120W. Besides consuming less power, the thermal load is more easily managed. I had a weird issue for a while where this CPU would spike to its TJMax and throttle when I opened File Explorer, but that was caused by my motherboard having an outdated BIOS, and has since been fixed. This CPU does not include a stock cooler, but this is a plus in my book; I quite enjoyed the Wraith Prism, but other Wraith coolers leave a lot to be desired. I happen to have an AiO on my CPU (Cooler Master PL240 FLUX), but for those on a budget, the Thermalright Peerless Assassin is $30-$40 and will do just as good.
This CPU does average high temps; normal idle temps can reach 50°C. This feels really weird, but after the BIOS update, high-load temps take a while to reach 80°.
I cannot give overclocking feedback, but it can overclock. PBO can give a little extra performance if necessary, but I have not enabled it yet, and don't intend to for the foreseeable future.
