This E-ATX Silent Modular Full Tower Computer Case is an absolute powerhouse of design, functionality, and versatility. Internal Layout: 5/5 One of the standout features of this case is its expansive internal layout. The label placement on the motherboard mounting points is a thoughtful touch, making it easy to identify where each mounting hole is located. This attention to detail ensures that I can properly configure my build without any confusion. Noise Cancellation: 5/5 The Define 7 XL truly delivers on its promise of silence. The sound dampening is superb, and the included case fans (which, by the way, are excellent quality like all Fractal products) work in perfect harmony to keep noise levels at bay. Whether I'm running demanding tasks or just browsing the web, this case ensures a peaceful environment. Cable Management: 5/5 The rubber cable channels on the rear of the case are an absolute delight. They're well-designed, easy to install, and provide more than enough room for my cables to breathe. This feature is often overlooked in other cases, but it's a game-changer for keeping your build looking tidy and organized. Build Quality: 5/5 The metal used in the case itself is top-notch quality. It feels solid, sturdy, and built to last. The brushed aluminum finish adds a touch of sophistication to the design, making this case a beautiful addition to any room. Versatility: 4.5/5 While the instructions could be improved, the included videos online are more than helpful in reorganizing the internal components. This case truly offers excellent versatility and functionality, making it an ideal choice for builders who want a high level of customization. Conclusion: The Fractal Design Define 7 XL is a masterclass in design and engineering. Its attention to detail, quiet operation, and versatility makes it an exceptional choice for any build. I would wholeheartedly recommend this case to anyone looking for a top-notch E-ATX Silent Modular Full Tower Computer Case.
reviews.author: Jonathan Wilson

reviews.title: Almost perfect
reviews.comment: Very high quality and tons of room for HDD (I installed 16 successfully), with purchase of optional trays, makes this a no brainer. Huge flaw is the weight of it when it's done, and no way to lock down the sides so it wants to explode when you move it into place after building. Add some friggin' handles to the thing, please.
reviews.author: Father of Twelve

reviews.title: Money well spent
reviews.comment: This is easily the best case I have ever owned. There are so many thoughtful details like cable runs, built-in velcro ties and molecularity that allows different types of configuration. I use mine as a NAS/Home server and I have 8 drives (not counting the NVME). I also appreciate that it comes with a vented top (my rig runs HOT) and (get this) it has fine mesh screens at all the ingress/egress points to keep the dust down. This is money well spent. Beware, it is HEAVY though.
reviews.author: M. Tucker Bradford

reviews.title: Amazing PC Case for the price.
reviews.comment: This has been one of my favorite cases to build in so far. It looks very nice to begin with, comes with 3 140 mm "DRGB" fans, and has excellent airflow. Included I/O is two USB 3.0 ports and a USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type C port. The case has tempered glass side panel which opens with small hinge in the back of the case, and both side panels close with magnets. The side panels are thin and yet surprisingly well built. They can be easily taken off the hinges if needed, but they're generally thin enough not to get in the way. There's a fan hub+RGB controller in the top of the case which all of the fans connect to, then all you have do is plug in a SATA power cable, fan header, and ARGB header. The SATA power cable is required for the lighting and fan hub in the case. As for the other headers, you will have a USB Type C header, USB 3.0 header, and HD Audio header. There's integrated cable covers, which some may love and others may hate. For me, I found the cable covers along with the integrated cable ties to make cable management far easier. Like it or not, those covers help you hide the mess of the cables in in the back. Lastly the front panel header is one cable, which shows that Phanteks truly cares about the person building the PC. I have almost no complaints with this case, as it's one of the best cases I've ever owned. There's so many quality of life features that set it apart from most others. The cable covers, included cable ties, magnetic side panels, and even single cable front panel header make building your PC far easier. If you're willing to pay the $159 for this case, it's absolutely worth buying. For the record, if you're not a fan of the RGB, there are basic airflow version of the G500A with no lighting, but still great airflow.
reviews.author: Jared Armbruster

reviews.title: Amazing case! Excellent airflow!
reviews.comment: Take your time understanding the wiring as there are lots of wires put in place! They are pretty clearly labeled to understand what goes where though. TONS of room to assemble in this case. Very easy to setup. Adding the 360mm AIO to the top was a breeze. Lots of hidden slots for wiring to keep the open side clean. Love the magnetic doors on both sides for quick and easy access. Magnets are certainly strong enough to not worry about the doors opening by mistake. Love the cable covers to keep it extra clean and tons of cable management Velcro preattached on the backside for ease of use. The RGB was a little bit confusing but figured it out. Do not plug into the motherboard if you intend to use the case preinstalled controller. With the 360mm AIO during heavy gaming, kept my CPU AT ABOUT 42-48C and the GPU at under 60C, LOVE IT! It also looks super clean, worthy showcase case! Another note, this thing is silent! While gaming, I do not hear any fan noise whatsoever. The Al ask is right next to me on the desk as well. Would highly recommend!
reviews.author: Cory

reviews.title: Nice quality PC Case with good design
reviews.comment: This is the second Phanteks case I have owned.  They both are excellently designed allowing you to easily install and add components.  The wires are placed in such a way that they can easily be stored nicely out of the way and in an organized manner. The case is ventilated well and comes with 3 intake fans at the front.  The sides are easily opened with hinges and one side has a glass side which allows you to look inside and see your components and with the lighting provided with many components makes for a cool looking desktop tower. The size of the mid tower case provides more than enough room for most user's needs and expansion plans. The cases are priced attractively given the quality and versatility of the build.
reviews.author: John C

reviews.title: Holy airflow Batman!
reviews.comment: Well first off with a little background, this is my first pc build in 4 years and it was very fun! specs: r5 2600, x470 tuf, 32gb vengeance pro, 500gb wd black nvme, 1tb crucial nvme sapphire nitro+ 6700xt,  a 650w seasonic, and a corsair h115i 280mm. Most of these parts are from my older build in a corsair 275r case. This case is pretty beefy for a mid tower, at about a inch or so wider, 2 inches or so taller, and longer. This case has plenty of space for my gpu with about maybe 2 and a quarter inches from the front fans, and thats with a gpu length of about a foot and some change. AIO fitment is great aswell, even after installing my aio I had plenty of space to cable manage up top still aswell and space to route the 8 pin up top. As for this being the airflow version it came with 4 fans, the front 3 daisy chained together from factory, which makes cable managing so much easier, front panel has 2 usb ports, a type c, and a single combined audio jack like for some apple earbuds. The packaging is incredible, the case sleeve, the packing materials, they really made sure the case wasnt going to arrive in bad shape. In the box comes the case, and a little box, of which when opened reveals HDD cages and within those cages are more parts, the screws for the case, and the parts for the vertical mount gpu (exlcuding the riser cable). The case is really easy to build in with lots of rear cable management options, But my favorite part about this case is all the swinging panels, the glass swings out and is removable, the metal side panel swings out and is removable, the interior panel that covers most of the wiring from the front panel is removable, and the bottom swing panel also swings down for easy access to the power supply. The pcie slots are thumbscrews which made it real easy to remove, aswell as the bracker for the psu is thumbscrews, which made installing the psu very easy. The singular gripe I have about this case is the power supply shroud Personally I dont like showing off the power supply, and wish they would have included a sliding mechanism that allows you to show it off or not, or a cover. Id hope they manufacture one as a extra or start giving it in the box to new costumers, but it makes sense to have it exposed as some psu have bright LEDs and such on them, Personally not a fan but since my psu is all black except for the name on the side, ill let this slide. The airflow this case provides is really great aswell and the included fans move lots of air. TLDR very good cable management, airflow, build quality, packaging and attention to detail.
reviews.author: Joe

reviews.title: Best case that I ever owned!
reviews.comment: This has been a fantastic case! I've had it for almost 2 years now and I just love it. The big selling point for me are the side panels are on hinges, which makes accessing the inside a super breeze. It's also very cable management friendly, for those that want that clean look ;) It has a 7 fan capacity, which is plenty for what I need. Temps are still really low even when under load. Over all, just a really good case and I'm happy with my investment :)
reviews.author: jeremy

reviews.title: 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟 Stunning Case with Smart Design & Great Airflow!
reviews.comment:
I recently built my new PC using the Corsair iCUE LINK 6500X RGB Mid-Tower Case, and it’s easily one of the best cases I’ve ever worked with. If you’re looking for a beautiful, well-designed, and airflow-friendly case, this one is a winner.
🔥 Aesthetics & Build Quality (10/10)
This case is a showpiece! The dual-chamber design with panoramic tempered glass makes everything look super clean, and the reverse-connection motherboard compatibility keeps cable management hidden for a sleek build. The white finish with RGB lighting makes it perfect for an all-white setup—it looks high-end and modern.
💨 Airflow & Cooling (9.5/10)
I’m using a Corsair iCUE Link Titan 360 RX AIO cooler on top, plus four RX140 fans on the bottom and rear exhaust, and the airflow is phenomenal. Temps stay low even under heavy workloads, and the included RX120 fans are quiet and effective. The case supports plenty of cooling options—it’s perfect for high-end builds.
• Supports up to a 360mm AIO (top or side)
• Bottom-mounted fans for additional airflow
• Dual-chamber keeps cables and PSU heat away from main components
⚡ Features & Ease of Build (9/10)
• iCUE LINK system makes RGB and fan management a breeze 🎛️
• Tool-free access for panels – easy to swap components
• Spacious layout – even with a large GPU, there’s plenty of room
• Reverse motherboard design is amazing for cable management
💡 Only minor note: If you’re used to traditional cases, the reverse layout might take a moment to get used to, but once you do, it’s so much cleaner.
🏆 Final Verdict: One of the Best Mid-Towers for a Clean, High-End Build
This case is perfect for showcasing a premium build, especially if you love clean aesthetics, great airflow, and easy cable management. If you’re considering it—just get it. The iCUE LINK system + sleek dual-chamber design makes this one of the best cases in its class.
💯 Final Rating: 5/5 – Absolutely Recommended! 🚀🔥
reviews.author: Wakenbank

reviews.title: Worth the premium
reviews.comment:
This case is a joy to work with. It is incredibly spacious, robust, and an obvious effort has been made to facilitate cable management and make the presentation of your work stand out and look professional. This turned my PC into the showpiece of my room. It is incredibly simple to assemble/disassemble, yet there are no squeaky loose panels and everything fits right. Included was more spare hardware, cable ties and screws than I would have ever needed, thank you Corsair for the nice thought. The extra mile has been taken to make sure the little details are coherent. For instance, the extra fan screws the case came with are also white. The tempered glass is of obvious quality and the dust screens on the side and bottom are simple to access and clean. You definitely won't have issues with air flow. I feel I paid a premium for this case but received a product that was on par with the price. The included iCUE fans do help offset the cost, as ordering a set of three by themselves would easily run you around $100.
The two-chamber format, while in my opinion looking better than more traditional PC cases, uses more room. This case is wide and heavy, so if desk space is tight, you should take measurements before ordering (I measure the case at almost 13 inches wide).
There was only one spot I could find where the fit and finish was less than superb, but it didn't bother me enough to knock a star off, only a mention. I would probably buy this case again if I had to do it all over.
reviews.author: Jason Elwood

reviews.title: good compact case
reviews.comment:
this is a really nice case and everything the 3500x SHOULD have been (because they're not cutting corners).  the included hardware, especially the fan screws, is really nice.  the metal is strong and this tears down and builds up similar to a lian li case.
I love the pop off windows!
it's a little heavy (which isn't necessarily a bad thing) and room to work with is limited (because it's an itx) but cable management is nice.
the Icue system is really nice, but a little confusing.  they only include 1 hub with the case and the hubs can only attach 2 sets of devices, and that's a little annoying BUT the fans that come with are nicer than the general Corsair fans.  so if you commit to iCue, this is a good place to start and it will avoid you some clutter.
airflow is good, color is nice and I love that they include rubber covers on the wire insert holes
reviews.author: Milarsaurus

reviews.title: High Quality, Heavy, Sturdy, Looks Great
reviews.comment:
Rebuilt my desktop in this case, moving from an NZXT H9 Flow.
Comes with icue link hub and 2 RGB fans. Super high quality case, built like a tank.
Moved away from the H9 Flow because it was enormous, and I had no reason for a case that big. Turned it into a treehouse instead.
Make sure you have a micro-ATX (mATX, generally ends with “m, ex: B850M), or a mini-ITX mobo - it’s required.
Gigabyte B850M Eagle ICE micro ATX mobo
9800x3D
PCCooler DS360 AIO
KLEVV - 32GB 6000mhz DDR5 Expo ram
Gigabyte 5080 Gaming OC
It appears to be about 1/2 the size of an H9 Flow. It’s built like a stump. I like it.
reviews.author: Max

reviews.title: VERY BIG case
reviews.comment: Incredible case that has everything you'd want, but it's much wider than you'd expect. I'm happy with my purchase but in hindsight I would have gotten a smaller one so that it's not taking up so much space.
reviews.author: Matt

reviews.title: Is this WiFi 7 wireless router any good?
reviews.comment:
PROS:
- Really fast WiFi 7
- Pretty easy setup even without following the videos.
- Relatively inexpensive compared to other WiFi 7 routers that are double the price
- Monolithic stature design
- Has 2 additional LAN ports at the back
CONS:
- Plasticky and cheap to touch (but who really touches a router often anyways?)
- By real-world use, when I situated this inside our bedroom connected to a LAN outlet, the WiFi 7 speed begins to drop significantly at about 40-50  feet away
VERDICT
My 1Gb ATT connection is almost always at full duplex (~940Mb up and down), thanks to this relatively inexpensive WiFi 7 router. Now i have this reliable wireless connection at the opposite end of our house extending to the backyard.
reviews.author: The Reviewer™

reviews.title: Great Coverage and Fast
reviews.comment: First time I've owned a mesh system and this WiFi system works well. Good range coverage and fast. I love the strong connection throughout the house.
reviews.author: Ron  S

reviews.title: Great / Easy Mesh system
reviews.comment: Great mesh system. Super easy setup. Took away a star because even tough I set up the same SSID and password, I had to log in all my devices again. Although I have heard that could be a wifi 7 thing.
reviews.author: D

reviews.title: Works Flawlessly!!! Love it!
reviews.comment: Excellent product! Very easy to set up. So far it works flawlessly. My home WiFi has never been so fast. I’m finally able to take advantage of the faster WiFi speed I’m paying for.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Avoid at all costs
reviews.comment: for three weeks the units ran ok. Then my Wi-Fi suddenly just stopped working. I rebooted all nodes and all was fine two weeks later the same thing ..... another reboot! One week later same problem! this went on for another few weeks rebooting  every five or six days. Also noticed the nodes would have to be unplugged and replugged for them to communicate. So i was glad to see an update available. After the update the units became so unreliable  that i would reboot at least once a day. This product is really a waste of time! I would steer clear and purchase another brand
reviews.author: great white north

reviews.title: Great case Lots of customization
reviews.comment: Great case. It seems well built and good quality.  Love the customization and cable management. Very easy to disassemble and work on. Love the fact the front panel connector is one plug and not five separate. It’s nice having the rgb header pre installed. There’s also plenty of room to add more rgb headers and ssd drives if needed. The front panel I/O can be relocated if needed, from the top to the side. The top will accommodate many different cooling options. Plus the front fans can be replaced with smaller ones. I’ve had no problems with temperatures with this case, and airflow is excellent. You are getting a lot for the price in my opinion.. Can’t recommend this case enough.
reviews.author: Pantherfan315

reviews.title: Solid Case with Great Features and Cooling
reviews.comment:
I went with this case for my latest build, and it’s been a really solid choice. It has a sleek look, but more importantly, it’s functional and easy to work with. It feels durable and well-made, which is what I was looking for.
There’s plenty of room inside, and it easily accommodates larger components without feeling cramped. Cable management was surprisingly smooth, and the built-in routing channels kept everything organized with minimal effort. Airflow has been great too, thanks to the included fans.
What I appreciated most was how user-friendly it is. The case design makes installation straightforward, and everything fit together nicely. The removable panels and tool-free features were a big help during setup.
Overall, if you’re after a roomy, well-designed case with good cooling and easy assembly, this is a great option. It checked all the boxes for me.
reviews.author: Juzgub

reviews.title: Bought it for the cooling - quite pleased
reviews.comment:
The air throughput is absolutely superb.
And that's coming from a guy running 3090 FE and a 13900KF (if you know, you know).
Basically a well functioning space heater rofl.
The removable glass panel is great for accessing internals quickly, and cable management absolutely sublime. Perfect negative pressure system I've ever used, though certainly could do positive. Those front fans are crazy good.
Caveats:
- I wish it was about an inch taller (from the base of power area) though so I could fit an extra gfx card on the bottom for more monitors.
- The SSD access isn't bad considering the airflow design, but wish it was a bit easier - as a guy who constantly works and switches drives.
- power management panel on bottom is a bit funky, but you get used to it and it grows on you.
- bit tight for the LGA1700+ chipset mobo's (gaming type boards have large heat sinks everywhere).
Pros:
- best cable management I've ever seen in a sub $300 case.
- best airflow period. feeding off previous: direct air pathways across board and heat sinks. HIGH volume. Unless you are building your own water cooling system (mobo, gfx, and cpu), and assuming you aren't using Peltier with liquid nitrogen, this is the best you're gonna get in my opinion.
- Tons of room considering it's not a "full tower".
Shoutout to GamersNexus for doing thorough reviews on all the latest and greatest computer cases, and I mean THOROUGH, which led me to this product. :)
reviews.author: Barry

reviews.title: Sleek Design with Excellent Airflow
reviews.comment:
I recently purchased the Lian Li 216 PC case, and it has exceeded my expectations. The sleek and minimalist design not only looks fantastic but also provides a functional and practical build experience. The tempered glass side panel beautifully showcases the internals, making it a great choice for those who want to display their components.
One standout feature is the outstanding airflow. The case comes with well-placed ventilation and fan options, keeping temperatures in check even during intense gaming sessions. Cable management is a breeze with ample space behind the motherboard tray, contributing to a clean and organized build.
The toolless drive installation is a nice touch, making the overall assembly process smooth and efficient. The case supports various cooling configurations, allowing for customization based on individual preferences and component choices.
While the case is compact, it offers plenty of room for high-end components, and the PSU shroud adds a neat and tidy look. The build quality is top-notch, reflecting Lian Li's commitment to craftsmanship.
In conclusion, the Lian Li 216 PC case is a fantastic choice for both aesthetics and performance. Whether you're a seasoned builder or a first-time PC enthusiast, this case delivers on style, functionality, and quality. Definitely of the best PC case in 2023. Highly recommended.
reviews.author: Sergei Kardailskii

reviews.title: Amazing PC case
reviews.comment: I select this case for my next build, after watching few reviews videos at youtube.  My idea was to install a AIO cooling system at the top, and this case is ideal for that task because the top of the case can be removed and you can install the radiator outside the case and then replace this top part and done very easy.  The case have a lot of other flexibilities very convenient for components installations and cable management. Be aware that if you want to use the area below the MB, in which are two removable grills to installing 2.5" SSD you will need sata extensions in straight angle, PS sata cables came in  90 degrees.  Also this case have an option to install the MB in two positions lower (default) and upper, if you leave the standup in their default location you will not be allow to use the fan at the back of the case.  Otherwise I think is a great case and at the moment with the fans included and the AIO, the case has a good air flow and temp at the cpu are under 60 degrees Celsius under normal use.
reviews.author: David F. Deal

reviews.title: 5 stars - rated within it's price point. Great for a simple build with direct front to back airflow.
reviews.comment:
Expectation management is important.  If you're familiar with higher-end computer cases, you know you usually get what you pay for, such as:  Thicker metal, no sharp edges, glass windows, robust accessory package, etc.  Though this case has several water cooling radiator mounting options, I wouldn't build a higher end build in this case.
This case is decidedly lower-end, befitting its' price point. But it is not "a cheap/junky case" and has several really good attributes.
I'm using this case for a dedicated PC to connect a 3D scanner to.  The case had to hold a mATX motherboard, a full size, 2-slot GPU and a full size ATX power supply and most importantly, stay cool while doing it.
Pros:
- Great airflow, front to back. f you tape over the vents on the top panel, you get excellent front to back airflow. I replaced the POS stock 120mm exhaust fan with a Noctua.
- Case is only a midtower but it is fairly deep, especially considering the side panels which have bump-outs that give you about another 1/2" of CPU cooler height. I'm using a Noctua NH-D15 with 140mm fans and it barely fits. But it fits. Between the CPU HSF and the Noctua rear fan, my 5900x running at stock speeds stays under 40C under load, even in my hot garage.  You can't hear the PC from more than a few feet away.
- Three 5.25" bays!  How many high end cases today have even one 5.25" bay?
- Has basic cable management cutouts in the motherboard tray
- Front bezel is toolless  and has no wires attached to it, it just pops off. The USB ports and power buttons are part of the case body. The front bezel is it's own piece. This means you can clean the front dust filter while the computer is running.
- Plenty of room for a larger ATX power supply
- Plenty of standard locations for 3.5" and 2.5" drives.  More than usual for a midtower
- The PSU has a slide out dust filter that slides out from the back
- QUIET.  If you put a decent CPU HSF on your CPU and a quiet rear 120mm fan, the case is basically silent.
- Metal edges and openings are rounded over. Not perfectly, but I didn't find any finger-chopping edges.
Cons:
-  Case frame is steel, but it's really thin. This makes the case light but kind of flimsy, especially with the side panels off
- No USB 3.2 on the front panel. Just old style USB3.0.
- No front fans. Though you can physically fit two, 120mm fans behind the front bezel there is no way to mount them. There are no mounting holes.  You'd have to drill your own.  I think this is a design oversight. The depth for the fans is there. The bezel is plenty ventilated, but no way to mount front fans without modding the case.
- Does not come with a way to seal off the vents/fan mount locations on the top panel.  The inclusion of a cheap plastic panel that screws or snaps in would've been nice. I used black duct tape. The PC lives in my garage and I don't care that it has duct tape on it.  You don't notice the black duct tape until you're right on top of the case anyway.
- The front panel dust filter is under the front bezel and the filter is not removeable, it's part of the case structure, under the front bezel. To clean it, you need to pop off the front bezel (easy and fast) and vacuum the dust off the filter (pain in the butt)
For my use case, I'm very happy with this case.  If you're looking for an inexpensive case that will fit a mATX or ATX motherboard and you're not looking to water cool and don't care about RGB lights and such, and maybe need at least one 5.25" bay (but you get 3!), this is a really good option. I'd buy it again for a similar use case. It was a pleasant surprise.
reviews.author: Cosmo

reviews.title: I really like the forward and backward compatibility in an affordable tower.
reviews.comment: So far bought two of these, and will be buying another one soon. Comes with a rear fan, and has multiple ports front and top for cooling fans. The drive bays have mounting room for 3 full size SATA hard drives, 3 2.5" SSD SATA drives, and 3 CD rom bays (for things like hot swap-able drives and system monitors). Perfect for my system as I already had my favorite ball bearing case fans and didn't need a glass side cover.
reviews.author: S Cobb

reviews.title: Great case for the money, lots of nice options
reviews.comment:
I was pretty happy with this case overall.  It was a bit of a tight fit stepping down from a full tower Lian Li case that I was previously using but managed to get all the components to fit after a bit of trial and error.  A couple of things to note.  The drive bays are a little strange but actually kind of cool once you get used to them.
The drives will "snap" into the carriers, thing is you actually put them in so the sata connectors are towards the back of the case.  If you put them in toward the front the cables won't fit properly under the side cover as there is very little space there once that cover is on.  However it is easy enough to just feed them through the case to the back and you've got a lot more room to work with.  Makes for good cable management I guess but it was a bit unexpected so I was scratching my head for a minute or two.
This will mount 2 120mm fans up front, on in the rear and two up top of standard size which is a lot of airflow.  My setup is a bit different, my CPU uses a water cooling rig with a single 120mm radiator so I mounted that out the back, relocated the 120 mm fan that was there to the top (only room for one in this case, you can't really mount the second fan as the radiator is just a touch too big to allow the fan to go in up top, then I mounted two 120mm fans up front.  Works very well, keeps the system quite cool and I'm very happy with thermal management.
Hard drive bays are nice, you've got room for 3 x 5.25 and the covers for those slots can be removed and then replaced if you decide to change your setup which is very nice, they just snap in.  Internally you have 3 2.5 bays which work great for SSD drives and 3 3.5 inch bays that I used for some 8tb sata drives for a good amount of storage.
I did add a fan controller, having all those fans running full blast was a bit noisy and I liked being able to turn them down a bit to quiet the system a tad.  But all in all it's a good little case, I liked it because it is just low key and doesn't have all that silly acrylic side panel look at all the LED lights like a lot of other mid tower cases have.  I know people love those for gaming rigs but I'm building a computer, not a landing strip for aircraft.. lol.
I would purchase this again, for the money it's pretty hard to beat for mid tower cases.  I did give it 4 out of 5 stars due to the lack of well written documentation, getting this together was more trial and error than anything else, and the location of the 120mm fan exhaust port on the rear, if they had just moved that down a centimeter or two I would have had room for another fan.  I don't need it for cooling you understand up top but it's an OCD thing, I've got one slot with a fan and one without which just looks a little off.  But other than that, great case.
reviews.author: Todd Robbins

reviews.title: Excellent case with great airflow and lighting
reviews.comment: This MUSETEX ATX PC case exceeded my expectations with its spacious design, strong airflow, and impressive pre-installed ARGB fans, making it a great choice for anyone who wants a case that looks fantastic, stays cool, and offers plenty of room for a clean and powerful build.
reviews.author: Alexander Kazanski

reviews.title: very good quality for price
reviews.comment: everything about this was great it came pre installed with fans very easy to cable manage and looked phenomenal and never overheated very cheap for what it was and handles very nice all case buttons worked exactly how they should’ve and it was simple, the case is quite large so make sure you have enough desk room
reviews.author: etahadna d.

reviews.title: Nice case but plan your wiring - Read Below
reviews.comment: Overall the case is very nice and arrived in perfect condition. All six of the stock case fans work fine. If you're not going with liquid cooling and plan to add more fans like I did, I would suggest moving the two side intake and the rear exhaust down to the bottom. Leave the other three on the top. The reason for this is that the stock fans are 6pin and connect to an adapter cable that has your 3pin argb and 4pin pwm. There are two adapters cables, each of which connect 3 fans, but each branch that connects to a fan is pretty short, and spreading the fans apart will make it near impossible to connect all of them. As others have mentioned, a full atx board goes right to the bottom of the case. You'll only be able to fit flat cables under the board, and even that is a bit challenging. PLAN YOUR WIRING OUT AHEAD OF TIME AND GET YOUR CABLES IN PLACE BEFORE INSTALLING YOUR MOBO. You'll never fit anything under there once the mobo is in place. The rear chamber was spacious enough for all of the excess cable, granted I didn't install any drives back there. I'm no expert at cable management, but I was able to get everything tucked and tied without having to force the back on lol.  I ended up using the HDD compartment in the top right for a fan hub. This is a very nice looking case and has a spacious interior for airflow. If you plan everything out ahead of time you shouldn't have too much trouble.
reviews.author: Kathy

reviews.title: Good case, but best for a micro ATX motherboard
reviews.comment: The pros: good looking, solidly built, quiet fans, air flow, dust filters, easy to assemble, price. The cons: build space, cable cutouts, cable management. This is a good case overall, but it’s definitely best for a *MICRO ATX* motherboard. You can use a standard ATX, but space is limited. I think cases need silicon cable cutout liners (to hide where the cords are stored and eliminate sharp edges; aesthetically more pleasing). Also, there are no cutouts and absolutely no space at the bottom, if you’re using an ATX MB (standard/full size MB), to route cables which, if you’re a stickler for cable management/going for the neatest look you can get, you’re better off spending a little extra for a case that has those features. This is my first build, and it wasn’t so bad that I couldn’t finish, but I will likely upgrade cases somewhere down the line for a more user friendly and cleaner looking case. Overall, great case for the price and I believe this might be one of the best (price to performance) if you’re doing a micro ATX build.
reviews.author: Brandon

reviews.title: Outstanding !!!!!
reviews.comment: I have built lots of PC's and have never had a case which was better for an easy install. Having the power supply behind the motherboard is much better than having it on the bottom. Sure the case is wider but that means plenty of room for cables instead of the customary squeeze job with a standard ATX case. I used an ATX motherboard and I don't see why some had problems with it. Asus Aura Sync worked perfeclty for the RGB fans and they are very quiet . I would not hesitate to but this case again. It's an amzing value
reviews.author: winet

reviews.title: Anthony
reviews.comment: I bought this case as for a home NAS and Plex server. Honestly this is a pretty great case! Cons: The metal is a little thin and sharp in areas. But over all nothing that I haven't seen before in lower price point cases. Pros: I mean where to start, for the price this case is really a great case! Perfect for a sever or NAS. "Officially" it holds 12 3.5 drives, and 2 2.5 drives. Unofficially (with the help of a 3D printer) you can easily fit a LOT more 2.5 drives in and up to 4 more 3.5 drives. It has lots of room for a large power supply, full size ATX motherboard, as well as a full size graphics card. The fans it comes with are nice and quiet and move plenty of air. It looks really good for a case you're probably going to hind in a closet or under a desk. It has a great front panel. It's SUPER easy to build in, and has lots of area for cable management. It comes with more than enough hardware and screws. This is the PERFECT case for a budget server build that looks like you spent a lot more on it then you did. Honestly Darkrock keep up that great work!
reviews.author: Kacie Pettit

reviews.title: Huge, well constructed easy to build at a great price.
reviews.comment: This case has all the bells and whistles at an unbelievable price.  I'm building some mass storage file servers to divorce myself from expensive cloud storage.  For the price of a single years online storage I have 2 servers using older drives I had laying around.  This enables having two copies in case one server or drive fails by using simply robocopy commands or even the free backup software that comes with Windows.  Either way is free and allow piece of mind that I won't loose my files and save some money as well.  The case will fit as many hard drives as I can imagine anyone could ever want as well as other powerful gaming components with little drought that anything you want to add to your system will fit.
reviews.author: Ray Sulich Jr.

reviews.title: Great storage case, minor flaws
reviews.comment: This thing is huge! It's pretty good, I was not able to find very many options for storage focused PC cases outside of a prebuilt NAS or actual server. Very easy to build into, lots of space, good cable management, pre installed fans with a triple splitter, room for a 360 radiator. PSU area has plenty of space for when you realize you *did* actually need that second PCIe mod cable but everything else is already installed... Couple issues worth noting, it is designed for 3.5" drives only, you cannot install 2.5" in those 10x bays. There are holes drilled in the top of each bay that will hold 5x drives, but they are too far from the edge for cables to fit. There are 2.5" carriages behind and under the motherboard if you only need a few. Also the vertical PCI slot blanks don't fit over the top horizontal slot screw and I had to remove it.
reviews.author: Drake

reviews.title: A highly versitile case great for using as a storage server.
reviews.comment: The Darkrock Classico is an amazing case.  I was not expecting much from a lessor known brand but I was pleasantly surprised by it's build quality.  No sharp edges anywhere and the side panels come off with ease.  I went with the Max version due to it being 1 inch larger in depth as I was concerened my Epyc CPU cooloer would have been to large for the regular version.  I think I could have gotten away getting the smaller one but getting the Max gave me more peace of mind.  The amount of storage this case holds is insane.  I currently have six spinning rust HDD,  two on the bottom, not seen from the front and four on top.  I still have space for four more HDD and even two more SSD on the back.  I'm using this case for my Proxmox server with a Supermicro H12SSL-i  ATX motherboard.  The case itself is not heavy which is great as adding all my components increase the overall weight a bit.  Airflow and temps are reasonable with 3 120mm fans in the front and top of the case and a single 140mm in the back.  Overal all I am quite happy with the case, it's size and it's overall functionality.
reviews.author: LC (GDG)

reviews.title: Great Chassis - Great Price
reviews.comment: This case provides everything I was looking for, especially at this price point. I'm coming from a smaller NAS enclosure that became very crowded and restricted airflow. This chassis offers plenty of space for cable management and can hold up to 10 (possibly even 11) hard drives if you place one on top of the bottom drive. I currently have 6 HDDs and 1 SSD installed, and there's still plenty of room to grow. With seven fans running, the temperatures for each drive and the processor stay around 30°C, which is impressive. This is my first time building inside a tower-style case, and the experience was much easier than working with smaller cube-style NAS enclosures. The build quality feels durable, and while I don't have much to compare it to, I'm genuinely happy with it. If you're looking for a chassis that can hold several drives and still maintain great airflow, this is a solid choice. I'm fairly new to building PCs and servers, but after a year of learning, I can confidently say I wish I had started with this unit from the beginning.
reviews.author: Jacob

reviews.title: Awesome case!!!  Built like a tank with plenty of room to have a build that doesn't look cramped!!
reviews.comment:
Very Happy with this case.  I looked at hundreds before choosing this one and can't really remember why exactly I chose it over the others but I am really happy with how it turned out.  I never thought I would like a white case but after looking at others builds I just found I liked the white aesthetic better.  This case comes with 6 rgb fans as well so toss in a 360 aio or something similar and it looks great.
I have seen other case reviews where people talk about flimsy easily bent cases.. well let me tell you the Foifkin F600 I got isn't one of them.  Its well built and larger than I was expecting as I didn't really look at the dimensions all that well but that is the best part about it.  Your build doesn't feel cramped and crammed in there.  There is ample room for working and cable management is easy.
The fans that were included all match my Thermalright frozen warframe aio perfectly.  They worked great.  I had a small issue with one and contacted the seller who was super helpful and sent replacement immediately.
I love that this case is built well, I was worried about getting a thin little flimsy something that wouldn't last or would be a pain to build in.  With this case everything went as smooth as one could hope for.  The metal is solid and has some weight to it especially with the parts installed.  It doesn't feel cheap like a lot of cases I have seen and had.  I have an old hp desktop and the metal is thicker than that I am pretty sure. Its not one of those you look at it wrong it gets a bend or dent in it.  I did need to sit it good and level for the door to shut perfectly which its the same with any of these cases.  When I had it sitting on a couple different things I was having to lift it slightly into place but when I got the shelf built for it, it started opening and shutting perfect.  It just needed a flat hard surface.
The front glass panel is on hinges and the side glass has the little plastic connectors that make it super easy to pop in and out if you need access.  The top mesh comes off to clean and install aios or fans.  Not sure if the bottom does but it may as well (I checked it is removable but not magnetic).  The top one is magnetic.
The only issue I had was when I upgraded the gpu to a sappire pulse 9060xt 16gb I had trouble getting the screws in that hold the gpu to the back of the case.  The case is so solid that I couldn't push the back in and get it to go in as good as I would have liked but I still got it in.  Will have to look again though now that I got a proper screwdriver to user there.  I was improvising at the time.  To install these you need to remove a piece from the back and then open a little door which lets you put it in place.  This could be a issue with the gpu or mobo itself though as I had a rx6600 in there before and it fit just fine and the screws went in easily so I can't blame the case on that.
Also it fits the psu really well and I like the large area in the back to hide the psu instead of sticking it out in the front or beneath the case.  It just looks nice to me.  I mean everyone has their own tastes but I really like it.  I have thought of getting some of those rgb cables to go in as well.
Oh the fans in this case are already connected together so I just plugged them into the mobo and they were ready to go.  They also had the wiring for the fans done nicely it wasn't all messy looking like I have seen in some other cases.
reviews.author: kat

reviews.title: Great Case!
reviews.comment:
The case looks great and the deal there is absolutely worth your cash. 7 fans for $80, can’t beat that.
Only bother is the ssd/hdd plate holder (whatever the specific name is) is very hard to work with, my ssd would bend, there’s no clearance between the plate and ssd you just screw it straight into the case. It makes it very hard to plug cables in due to there being no clearance. If that doesn’t make sense you’ll end up running into it. I have the ssd hanging off the plate and secured it with 2 screws. It’ll do for now, but I recommend buying a aftermarket stand off that matches the dimensions of the cases.
I was surprised by the quality of the case in general and that includes the fans. The noise is minimal and they are very effective. I can feel the air flowing throughout the case when it’s open. You can definitely depend on them.
Last thing I wanted to mention is that the case is pretty big so I recommend looking at the size/dimensions of the case and make sure it aligns with the kind of desk you are running.
Great product!
reviews.author: isaias

reviews.title: Awesome quality case at an amazing value. Quality and style almost exactly matches big name cases.
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/C1X0jrj0diL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/71xv3intTeL._SY256.jpg I was skeptical since this case is such a low price point compared to a lot of the other big name brand "fish tank style" cases I was looking at, but I have to say I was pleasantly surprised once it came in! I was going to go with a name brand one at a big box store, but I decided to roll the dice on this case for my build.
The fans came preinstalled and it came with all the hardware I needed for my build. It has plenty of slots to mount your GPU and a great mounting process for the power supply. Everything in my build fit seamlessly in this case, and it felt like everything was sturdy, attached well. I'm not a fan noise snob, so take this for what you will, but I find the included fans to be pretty quiet, not making any insane noises or making me feel like I'm sitting next to an AC unit. Keep in mind the image may show seven fans, but you will only get the 6 fans as stated in the description (which wasn't a problem because I read through the whole item description). I ended up liking their included fans so much, that I bought my seventh exhuast fan from them once the case came in. When it comes to cooling, this case stays very cool and the exhaust fan definitely helps the fan flow.
When it came to installing all the components of my PC build, I found it easier to just remove the bottom fans since they're quite seamless to reinstall. All the RGB synced up perfectly and the top power button rapidly alternates between a cotton candy blue and pink led whenever the build is on. All the I/O ports that I hooked up to the MB work perfectly and the placements are convenient.
This case has been working flawlessly for over two months now and I have zero complaints (if that changes I will update the review). The glass door is easy to remove from the hinges (just lift up vertically) during cleanings or whenever you're doing the initial PC build. Based on the way my GPU mounts to the case and the MB, I did have to get a GPU sag brace, but it was super cheap and easy to install between the GPU and bottom fans.
Highly recommend this case due to its quality for the low price point. I will be getting another one for my wife when I start her next build.
reviews.author: RJ

reviews.title: Great Case, Bad Instructions
reviews.comment:
Overall, I was very pleased with my purchase of the MUSETEX ATX PC case. The build quality is solid, and the value you get with 7 pre-installed PWM ARGB fans is excellent. Right out of the box, the fans were properly aligned for optimal heat dissipation, making airflow setup stress-free and effective. Cooling performance has been great, and the system stays cool even under load.
The case looks fantastic, with a clean and modern design highlighted by the tempered glass panel. Once assembled, everything feels sturdy and well thought out from a performance and layout standpoint.
The built-in dust filters are another strong point. The bottom filters are solid pieces held securely in rivet-like channels, while the top dust cover is magnetic, easy to remove, and holds firmly in place. The USB 3.0 ports are controlled by a single plug and perform at expected speeds without issue.
The pre-installed power, reset, and HDD LED connectors were a nice touch and saved time during setup. I also appreciated the pre-installed Velcro-style cable ties, combined with multiple rear access points, which made cable management much easier and cleaner.
The only real downside is the documentation. The instruction pamphlet was printed on very thin paper that tore easily, with small text that was difficult to read. Accessing the documentation while working inside the case was inconvenient, and the tempered glass panel removal was confusing at first. Since the glass appears to be magnetically held, clearer instructions—such as external diagrams or simple directional stickers—would greatly improve the user experience.
Pros:
Excellent cooling with 7 pre-installed PWM ARGB fans
Fans correctly oriented for efficient heat dissipation
Secure dust filters and thoughtful design features
Clean aesthetics and solid build quality
Great overall value
Cons:
Poor instruction quality (thin paper, small text)
Documentation difficult to reference during installation
Glass panel removal needs clearer guidance
Despite the documentation issues, this is still a great case with strong performance, cooling, and aesthetics. If MUSETEX improves the instructions and paper quality, this would easily be a near-perfect product.
Note: The included video I submitted does not show the side tempered glass installed or final cable management.
reviews.author: Wendell Keoughan

reviews.title: Cheap but NOT!
reviews.comment: This is a very nice case! i love building computers and the ease of moving my old pc over to this new case was amazing! there is so much space and i love all the glass and the amount of fans you could have in here! its very light compared to most full towers and the style of it is very modern! i am very happy with this case!
reviews.author: Shuujuu

reviews.title: Perfect case! Buy if you need good quality!
reviews.comment: I dont usually write reviews, but this case deserves one. 10-10  I recently upgraded my old stgaubron pc, all i was using was the case. That became an issue with the wires being everywhere, and i needed a bigger case. this one was PERFECT. Came with the fans complete and put together nicely, Installation was really easy, It doesn't overheat anymore as well. My old case was too small for my big ahh heat sink and this one gives it a bit more room for air to circulate around it. overall, strong build, easy to navigate and install stuff in, and really nice in general. def. recommend to anyone buying or upgrading their case.
reviews.author: Trace

reviews.title: Awesome Beginner Case For A Great Price $$$
reviews.comment:
Although I’m ashamed to admit it took me quite long to assemble everything, I will say that this case and the six included RGB fans are amazing and work great. They run quiet and everything inside the PC is nice and cool. The tempered glass is very durable and looks so good once you peel the satisfying plastic layer off (don’t leave fingerprints!!!).
The included screws and manual help with installing and wiring the fans, and the wiring is mostly neat and already tucked away for you, all you have to do is hook it up to your motherboard! I could be biased because I got this case for $38 after using a coupon and a gift card but still for its base price I would hands down buy this again for my next build if I were to switch cases.. but I will probably stick with this one for quite some time because it looks so good.
P.S. For those who are new like me and are concerned about compatibility, this case and a few of the other cases from MUSETEX are available to select on pcpartpicker.com and will make the build process so much easier!
reviews.author: Dax Helmert

reviews.title: Good case but buy new fans the RGB lights go out on them pretty quick
reviews.comment: I bought this case for my First ever pc Build, I bought it because the Case i wanted would not fit the power supply i wanted at the time. so i returned it and bought this one, I like it i do not love it, 2 weeks ago the RGB lights on the fans burned out, so now I'm Staring into a black void i only see the RGB on my ram still working, so i would advise getting better fans from the start and trashing these, it is easy to remove the panels to get to the back where the Power supply and the cables are, The cooling is nice 6 fans but i have to replace them because my RGB lights went out. to quote Todd Howard here It just works, if you want a functional case then this is a good one Decent price, But it makes me want to change it
reviews.author: Caleb

reviews.title: It's a really good case.
reviews.comment: This case is what I was looking for. It's not too different from the SSUPD cause but, IMO the build quality is better. I appreciate I do not need right angle adapters for the GPU (or to buy taller feet), PCIE Gen 5 riser and lastly, the split glass looks dope without compromising on temps. Downsides would includ only being able to use sfx/sfxl PSU, only itx boards but for me, it's a non issue as space is a premium.
reviews.author: CDubbsW0rld

reviews.title: Awesome Case!
reviews.comment: Great case, easy to build in!
reviews.author: James Jones

reviews.title: Good-looking itx case 8/10
reviews.comment: **Quick notes / TLDR** - SFX psu required, good looking case, great accessibility. Arctic 240/280mm radiators will fit with fans mounted on the inside and rad mounted outside of removable bracket. Your average dp cable and hdmi cables work fine, don’t need angled. Price vs performance is good but debatable. 8/10. First off I want to say I am a fan of nzxt cases. I ordered this case with a bias that it would be of good all around quality as I’ve owned and appreciated almost every variant of their flow series. That being said here is my pros and cons. Cons: - too much space in all the wrong places. I moved my itx build over from a TT TR100, and while I appreciate the smaller footprint, the open spaces of this case near the psu(bottom of the case) and near the top of the case(between the motherboard and case fan housing) seem counterintuitive. There is little to no cables or cable management that need to be done in these areas and leads to unnecessary cable run lengths and wasted space when looking at it from a sff case perspective. - Cpu thermals are subpar* When comparing this to cheaper mitx cases such as the TT TR100 and Tower 250 I’ve actually seen a RISE in temperatures on the cpu side of cooling. About 5~7c degrees idle and 10~15c under load or gaming, while using the same kraken plus 280 AIO cooler with reapplied thermal grizzly kryonaut across all 3 builds. - Small but notable con; the pcie riser has a bit too much slack and is going to be pressed against the gpu somewhat firmly. Pros: - It looks good, the glass panel is a nice-to-have and is well implemented. The glass meets the mesh panel right above where you would begin to see your psu cabling so the build will look clean with minimal ocd level cable management. - Accessibility, as with most NZXT cases, building in this case was very easy. Every panel is removable and you have access to every cable, plug, and header you need to reach. Nothing on the case needed to be modified, shimmed, or shaved, it just fit. - Gpu temps are on average better vs. cases with no immediate exhaust fans. *AIO in pictures is kraken 240 not 280 as I wanted to ensure the cooler was not failing after checking temps.
reviews.author: Layne Phariss

reviews.title: They’ve mastered format!
reviews.comment: They made an amazing case. The format is perfect. I don’t really change my displays often but I do change my keyboard, mouse, headset, whatever way more. I do wish they sold a replacement for the glass panel that was just another mesh panel for air coolers. Very good experience overall.
reviews.author: Cort Oliver

reviews.title: Nzxt h2 flow review
reviews.comment: Love it, look clean, bit big for an itx.
reviews.author: Riccardo

reviews.title: UPDATED: One of the 140mm fans doesn’t work
reviews.comment: I haven’t been able to build a pc in over 10 years, so I was pretty excited to put one together. I ordered the Montech X3 Mesh & I was initially pretty happy with it… until after I spent several days putting everything together & discovered that the front middle fan isn’t spinning, although the LEDs work. As far as everything else, I think it’s a great case for the sale price of $50. UPDATE: After contacting the seller Skytech, they offered me a partial refund because of the non-working fan. They also gave me an email address for the manufacturer Montech. After communicating with them via email, they sent me a replacement fan which arrived today. I haven’t tried replacing the defective fan yet, but I’m trusting that the new one will work. Overall, an excellent customer service  experience in dealing with both companies. Changing my rating to add another star 👍 UPDATE #2: Montech did send me another fan, but it’s not the same one. It’s a 2-wire instead of 3-wire (which means it can’t be monitored/controlled by the mobo or software) & the LED lights are different enough that it’s noticeable. Not the end of the world & I do appreciate the fact that they sent one. Negatives: •Took 1 week to receive, which is a bit much •1 fan doesn’t spin (replaced)* •Fans are LED & not addressable RGB as the pictures might lead some to believe (although this is pretty clearly stated). •Fans have older style Molex connections that are all daisy chained together. •Cabling is fairly inelegant & comes held together with metal twist ties. •No PC speaker. •Materials aren’t the greatest. The gauge of the metal is pretty thin & a bit flimsy. •No rubber grommets in the cabling passthroughs •It’s perhaps a bit small for some ATX builds Positives: •Although the geometric aesthetic seems heavily “inspired” by Fractal brand cases, it’s a nice looking case regardless. •Pretty quiet at idle considering the 6 original case fans, the 2 additional fans I added & a 3 fan GPU •Good, simple design of the side panel, which is easily removable by just lifting it off, although the nylon ribbon loop used as a handle might turn some people off. •Side panel is tempered glass instead of plexiglass/plastic. •Small-ish mid tower case, but ATX motherboard, top mounted radiator in a push/pull configuration, 3 140mm, 5 120mm fans, a Corsair RM750 PSU & a 303mm Radeon 6650xt 3 fan GPU all fit in a nice looking package (although connecting the wiring & cable management is a bit of a chore). •Good airflow •It has a decent magnetic dust filter on the top, although that’s actually not great for airflow & will actually trap dust & restrict the hot air that you want to exhaust from your case. •I’ve seen some reviews that complain about the rear expansion card slots being the cheap kind that you have to bend or cut to remove, but the ones I removed when installing a GPU were secured with a slot & screw (much better). •Although the specs say it officially supports GPU’s up to 303mm I managed to squeeze in an MSI Gaming X Trio GeForce RTX 3080 which is 323mm with maybe even a couple of mm’s to spare. Conclusion: *After living with this case for about a month & the experiences that I had with both the seller & manufacturer, I’m adding the 5th star to my rating. It’s more of a budget case so you can’t expect perfection, but for $50 it’s an extremely good case & continues to perform very well.
reviews.author: D. C. Ellis

reviews.title: Sleek looking case awesome airflow design
reviews.comment: The Montech X3 Mesh is an absolute beast when it comes to PC gaming cases. With its six fixed RGB lighting fans (3x 140mm and 3x 120mm), this case is designed to deliver both aesthetics and performance. First off, the airflow in this case is phenomenal. The mesh front panel and the pre-installed fans ensure that your components stay cool even during intense gaming sessions. The high airflow design is a key feature that sets this case apart from many others in its price range. The tempered glass side panel is another highlight. It opens like a door, which is super convenient for accessing your components. Plus, it adds a sleek, modern look to your setup, allowing you to showcase all your internal hardware and those vibrant RGB fans. In terms of build quality, the Montech X3 Mesh feels solid and well-constructed. The black finish gives it a professional look, and the interior is spacious enough to accommodate a variety of setups, including larger GPUs and multiple storage drives. The inclusion of USB 3.0 ports on the front panel is a nice touch, ensuring fast data transfer speeds for your peripherals. Overall, the Montech X3 Mesh is an excellent choice for gamers and PC enthusiasts looking for a high-performance case with great airflow, stunning RGB lighting, and a user-friendly design. It's a fantastic blend of functionality and style, making it a standout option in the mid-tower category. **Scratch Resistance:** The Montech X3 Mesh features a tempered glass side panel, which is generally more resistant to scratches compared to acrylic panels. However, it's always a good idea to handle it with care to avoid any potential damage over time. **Value for Money:** In terms of value, the Montech X3 Mesh offers a lot for its price point. With six pre-installed RGB fans, a high airflow design, and a sleek tempered glass side panel, you're getting a lot of premium features without breaking the bank. It's definitely a solid investment for gamers looking to build a high-performance rig. **Screws:** The case comes with all the necessary screws and standoffs for mounting your motherboard, drives, and other components. The screws are of good quality, ensuring a secure fit for all your hardware. **Cable Management:** Cable management in the Montech X3 Mesh is quite decent. There are several cutouts and tie-down points to help you route and organize your cables neatly. The spacious interior also provides ample room to tuck away cables, which helps in maintaining a clean and efficient build. Overall, the Montech X3 Mesh excels in providing a balance of aesthetics, performance, and practicality, making it a great choice for any PC builder.
reviews.author: Hunter K.

reviews.title: Great budget case
reviews.comment: It’s not the highest quality material but it still remains sturdy enough to bang around without worrying about it. The bonus there, it’s VERY light weight. You won’t throw your back out picking this up. The fans included are a huge plus, they are fixed so the speeds cannot be adjusted, but they keep my pc cool and they’re quiet enough to not get annoying. I thought the cable management was going to be a nightmare but it actually turned out to be very manageable. And I gotta say I really like the look of the case itself, very appealing. The ability to shut off the rgb with the simple press of a button on top of the case is a huge W. The rgb is fixed as well, so the colors cannot be changed, but it looks really nice when it’s lit up. I’m very satisfied with my purchase. The case looks great, and my cpu stays cool. I would definitely recommend this case to someone looking to upgrade. 10/10 ***UPDATE*** I also ordered the XR fish tank case for my primary pc. It is absolutely stunning. The fans included were decent quality (5v 3 pin) but I swapped them out to match my aio. There is plenty of room for up to 9 120mm fans. The rear exhaust can fit 1 140mm fan, and the top supports 120mm or140mm fans. Airflow is excellent throughout the case. Cable management was a breeze. Beyond satisfied with my second Montech case.
reviews.author: Isaac

reviews.title: Good case for value but some flaws
reviews.comment: Good case with pretty nice airflow. Lot of space and is good for the value. Only downside is it came with 1 fan not working and the RGB doesn’t work. Don’t care much for rgb anyway but kind of annoying.
reviews.author: Jaime

reviews.title: Roomy case with 6 fans for a good price
reviews.comment: Nice roomy case. Handles my 300mm long GPU no sweat. 6 fans comes with it. They all light up RGB and are the same. They cannot be synch or programmed, just static RGB, no breathing/cycling. But you get 6 working large fans that are quiet in the price and they're preinstalled and prewired and it's done well. Lots of room and places for cable management. Looks modern without looking like cheese. Comes with mesh filters on all areas. Overall can't say anything bad about it, its a good case, easy to build in, no fussy weird stuff. Lots of room on the back side for cables so you're not trying to stuff it all and hide it.
reviews.author: Marty

reviews.title: Another beautiful Lian Li case
reviews.comment: Fantastic case. Having built in the two previous versions of the O11 Dynamic Line, I had high expectations. The Evo was already a marked improvement over the original O11, but the Vision changed the game with the addition of a new glass panel on the top. Slightly less airflow, and you can't top mount a radiator if you use the glass panel, but you have both options available. Build quality was impressive as usual from Lian Li, and even with less airflow with the top pane, there was still more than enough to keep everything running cool. Plenty of room inside the main chamber for all of my parts, and plenty of cable management space in the back chamber. Just make sure all of the bottom cables on the mobo are properly arranged if you are using fans on the bottom of the case. It is definitely a larger case for fitting into a workspace but definitely worth making the room for it.
reviews.author: Ignacio Tomas

reviews.title: Sleek, Spacious, and Built for Performance!
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/D1vAeqK5M0L.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/51n8GiTvhJL._SY256.jpg The Lian Li O11 Vision Compact Black ATX Mid Tower Case is an absolute winner for anyone looking to build a clean, modern, and well-ventilated PC. From its premium materials to its smart layout, this case makes building both effortless and visually stunning.
Build Quality & Design:
✅ High-Quality Construction – The steel frame feels solid and durable, while the tempered glass panels add a premium touch.
✅ Compact Yet Spacious – Despite being a compact mid-tower, it provides plenty of room for high-end components, including large GPUs and multiple cooling options.
✅ Panoramic View – The three-sided tempered glass design makes this case perfect for showcasing your build, especially with RGB lighting.
Cooling & Airflow:
✅ Great Ventilation – The airflow is surprisingly good, thanks to well-placed vents and the option for multiple fan and radiator configurations.
✅ Customizable Cooling Options – Supports liquid cooling and high-performance air cooling with ease.
Ease of Building & Features:
✅ Easy Cable Management – The back-connect motherboard support makes routing cables much cleaner, resulting in a clutter-free build.
✅ Tool-Free Installation – Installing components is quick and hassle-free with the tool-less design.
A Few Things to Consider:
⚠️ Cable Routing Needs Planning – The compact design means that cable management requires some extra effort to keep everything neat.
⚠️ Limited Front I/O – The front ports are minimal, so if you need a lot of front-facing connectivity, you might need a hub.
Final Verdict:
If you're looking for a stylish, well-built, and feature-packed case that makes your PC look incredible while keeping it cool, this is the one to get. The tempered glass panels make it a showpiece, and the smart layout ensures excellent performance and easy upgrades. Highly recommended for anyone wanting a clean and high-end build experience.
reviews.author: Wolf Girls Tavern

reviews.title: A pleasure to build in.
reviews.comment:
Wow this case was a joy to build with. I don’t think it says in the description but this case was a collaboration with Lian Li and the PCmasterrace subreddit and it shows that people with a lot of PC building experience had a hand in this. There are just so many quality of life things engineered into the case, I was amazed at how easy it was to install every component without fighting the case in any way. The cable management in the back is a dream as well with all the built in tie downs available it was easy to get everything nice and tidy. The airflow is great with how I have my fans set up, and there are a ton of options for fan location to account for many different preferences and needs. Build quality of the case is exceptional, and it comes with screws and hardware to mount anything you could possibly want to in the case.
The only tiny gripe I have is that the SDD mount on the swinging door inside the back of the case didn’t have enough clearance for the SATA cable to plug into the drive on the mount, but was easy enough to attach it to one of the HDD cages nearby. Very happy with the purchase and I’ll be hard pressed to buy a case from another brand going forward.
reviews.author: Jake Justice

reviews.title: Lian LI 4 The Win!!
reviews.comment: What More Can You Expect From Lian Li Cases!!! There Out Right Awesome!! I Run The 6 Intake Fans and 2 Exhaust Fans and The Glass Top Option!! Cooling is Not an issue!! Max Temps seen on gpu (72 degrees C and CPU (60 Degrees C) Playing Cyberpunk 4k High Settings 60fps Cable Management is Great!! Installation is Easy(If You Done This Before)!! One of the best looking cases on market that gives easy setup options using the thumb screws to remove panels etc The Value this brings for the money can’t be match! Size this great!! It’s Little Wide but not so tall. I was to fit on my desk from ikea which is about 58in with my 27in monitor and has plenty of room for another bigger monitor!!
reviews.author: DonovanRamos

reviews.title: Great for what it is
reviews.comment: This is a great case as long as you know what you are in for. Can you build a gaming pc in it, yes. Should you, no. Mainly due to cooling potential. This is, however, an ideal case for a workstation. I will be using it to build a new pc for my senior-citizen relatives. Pros: low cost, lightweight, has a 5.25inch bay for optical drive, surprisingly small for an ATX mid-tower case (fits a full size ATX motherboard easily). Meh: metal is thin (contributes to both light-weightedness and top-heaviness). No venting on the top or bottom (good or bad is use-case dependent). Finally a very minor issue, IF you are using this case for ATX build, be aware only 6 of the 9 necessary motherboard standoffs are pre-installed, the remainders/extra are included with the other hardware but must be installed yourself. Cons: Biggest issue for me is the mount for the power supply is at the top and makes it very top heavy, definitely would have preferred psu mounting on the bottom for such a lightweight case. Might not be ideal for beginners as the case is very tight with ATX build and can be difficult to work in, let alone cable manage. No USB-C on the front I/O panel. All the screws come together in one bag with no separation, 3 types of screws, 4 if you include mb standoffs, all in one non-ziplock bag... irritating. Personal: Zalman is a trusted brand. In the last 22 years I've had 3 pc cases and 2 were Zalman, which lasted about 18-19 of those years. Overall, this case is great. But again, it depends on your what you'll use it for. I am using integrated graphics from cpu and a low profile cooler which means there is a lot of empty space in the case, which likely contributes to the top-heavy nature I previously mentioned. That being the case, I wish there was a version where it is half the width and the spot for the optical drive was rotated 90 degrees to remain included, a bottom mounted psu, and perhaps more venting on top to compensate for the smaller size and fan size.
reviews.author: ~OoO~

reviews.title: Inexpensive and Lightweight and just perfect for my build.
reviews.comment: The case is inexpensive but sturdy, especially once you start mounting stuff in it. Removing the metal punch-outs for Optical drive and Video Card requires in addition to pushing the with your fingers bending the metal with a pair of pliers and then using a small file (and a paper or tissue underneath to catch the filings) to remove the resulting sharp metal jagged edges. There are about a dozen motherboard stand-offs included, which require a 3/16" or 5mm socket to screw into the case. I used a flat tip medium size screwdriver to start to pry the front panel, after which it came off easily. I removed two adjacent rear punch outs and also the thin section between them (which bent easily) to mount the double width video graphics card. And of course using a small file (and a paper or tissue underneath to catch the filings) to remove the resulting sharp metal jagged edges. I mounted a single 120mm fan blowing air in the front. You have to mount the front panel and then insert the optical drive from the front, and then screw in the drive mounting screws. Tight fit with the power supply and optical drive up top, and tucking in and using cable ties to secure the cables somewhat so they don't fall down or wind up hitting the CPU fan blades. I took some pictures and captioned some of them to hopefully help other people see what could be involved in using this case. I like that this inexpensive case has an option for mounting an optical drive. Some of use still use CDs and DVDs for software and video and music. It took some time to get everything in and doesn't look the neatest, but the result is a small compact unit.
reviews.author: Wendy Stringer

reviews.title: Very Good Case at my Price Point
reviews.comment: I needed an inexpensive mid-sized case for an ATX MoBO build which I was transferring from a much larger case. I needed this case to fit under a particular piece of furniture.  Bottom line, this fit the bill nicely.  Couple points: Metal sheet is pretty thin, which makes for a light case, but it's not real heavy duty.  I used (and recommend) at least one aftermarket fan in the front to pull air in to the case (I used two).  These need to be installed before anything else (another buyer noted that same point) particularly if putting in a full ATX MoBo.  You will not have the room after the board is in to get the fan screws in place.  The front plastic panel is most easily pulled off from the bottom.  Just be gentle and firm and it will pop right off.  Goes back on easy as well. Recommend removing the enclosed exhaust fan prior to mounting the MoBo.  You'll need some maneuver space. I had 2 SSD's for this build, a 500 GB and 250 GB.  These are mounted outside the main part of the case, which takes a little consideration for cabling.  Easily done though. ATX MoBo is s tight fight, but it fits.  Don't forget your standoff nuts, these are not all in place for the ATX board.  I also used aftermarket cooling.  The tower is too high to allow for a side mount fan in this case. Back panel is a little loosey-goosey.  This is where the thin metal sheet is most evident.  To allow for the GPU to seat one must pop out the panels.  They will be destroyed doing this so make sure you line up your cards correctly.  It looked wonky initially, but once the GPU was in place everything locked down tight, no issues. Power supply mounts on top, which I was initially a little concerned about but it worked out nicely.  This particular power supply is not modular, so it's a bit of beast in terms of excess cables, but there was more than sufficient space to store them away.  Since this isn't a display build I did not concern myself with fancy cable management, a few enclosed zip ties to keep things tidy was about it. So again, good case for the money.  Not sure I would use it for my first build though. I'd recommend laying out a little more to get a more modular and flexible case, something with a bit more room and more heavy duty.  However if you've got a build or two under your belt, and you aren't concerned with being the Michelangelo of PC building, this will work fine.
reviews.author: Cat

reviews.title: old school budget case
reviews.comment: for the price this is a great old school stile case with a CD drive bay (I wanted)and some how i squeezed a Hell Hound 9070 in it and its tight but it fit with a full ATX MB and a r5 5600x3d and yes a dvd burner ..I did add a fan in the front to push fresh air under the video card for better cooling and it is decent and the temps are good even under full gaming load  ..this is a budget build with a 750w Apevia PSU and I am running Linux Mint and its a gaming beats at 1080p on my 280hz 27" monitor .....
reviews.author: redneck270

reviews.title: Very basic case for low profile (stealthy) gaming builds.
reviews.comment: Update: I’m posting a picture of exactly why I bought this case and of the fifth fan installed where the 5.25” bay is. I bought this handle in a four pack for about $15, it’s for play sets. Original: I like this case more than I thought I would. First thing you should know is that you can fit a fifth fan behind where the 5.25 slot is, on the inside of the case. I highly recommend doing that to keep airflow optimized. I will say that this is a very flimsy and lightweight case. Both would normally be cons, but for my purposes they really aren't. I bought this case to build a gaming PC that I can easily transport. It has a solid top that I can attach a handle to. It's light weight helps keep it light weight, I know, shocking. Compared to my other gaming PC I recently built, this feels a bit lighter. I haven't weighted either but perhaps I will in the future. Honestly, I like this case. I like the solid black panels, the OEM look it tends to have, and the mounting for a fan in the side cover. Although it is cheap feeling, with how thing the steel is, it's really easy to build in and pretty well thought out. The only cable management issue is the power supply cables have to be directly fed through a hole to the "back" side panel. Other than that it seems fine to me. Although I do like this case, if you spend just $20-30 more you can get a better case. You should only buy this if you're on an extremely tight budget and need a case right now or if you want a low profile OEM looking build.
reviews.author: The Guy

reviews.title: Real talk!
reviews.comment: Heyhey my name is Toji am a big gamer/programmer about this pc now->.  Stunning "Aquarium" Aesthetics on a Budget! I am absolutely obsessed with this case! If you want that high-end, wrap-around glass look without spending a fortune, this is the one. It looks like a premium showpiece once it’s all lit up. The Build & Cable Management Setting everything up was surprisingly easy. The cable management was a breeze for the most part, but I do have one major tip for future builders: • The USB 3.0 Challenge: The USB 3.0 cable is quite thick and can get in the way of the bottom fans. • The Fix: I actually removed all the fans to properly route the thicker cables through the back of the case instead. • The Result: It makes the internal chamber look much cleaner (check the pic!). It was well worth the extra few minutes of effort to get that "floating" look for the components. Pros: • Insane Value: Comes with almost all the fans you need (just one short of a full set!). • Easy to Build In: Plenty of room to work and great accessibility. • Top-Tier Aesthetics: The way the fans reflect off the glass panels is beautiful.
