Final Verdict: If you want a cool-looking PC for a great price, buy this case. Just be prepared to do a little extra routing for the thicker cables to keep it looking perfect!
reviews.author: Reda.b

reviews.title: Built My Son a Gaming PC… Accidentally Built a Disco
reviews.comment: Bought the ANSAITE ATX PC Case with 7 PWM ARGB Fans for my son’s gaming PC build and I’m honestly impressed. The case has plenty of room to work in and the infinity fans look awesome. Once we powered everything on, the RGB lighting was so bright his room looked like a small nightclub. We added a separate RGB controller to customize everything and now the lighting effects are even better. Airflow seems great, the case feels solid, and everything installed easily. My son loves it, which means the build was a success and I’m still the household IT hero for now. Great case and definitely recommend it if you like RGB builds.
reviews.author: Josh Frensley

reviews.title: A great case at a superior price!
reviews.comment: I managed to snag a 5070TI before the prices explode and it wouldn't fit in my old case.  So, after some shopping around I found this one and really liked the look.  The case design is awesome and while some folks were saying the build quality felt cheap, it feels good to me.  I've had way flimsier cases before.  I loved that the fans were pre-installed, so all I had to do was wedge in my components and off she went!  I didn't do a great job on the cable management but I was in a hurry.  I'll go back and clean it up later.  Even slightly messy, it still looks fantastic!
reviews.author: Shea B.

reviews.title: Case is good- arrived with some damage.
reviews.comment: I'm an experienced PC builder who's built multiple PCs for myself and others. The case looks great and I expect some amazing airflow from it, but I was quite disappointed to find a noticeable dent on the back-top of the case, as well as a smaller "inverted" dent at the mid-top of the case. I will be reaching out to customer service in hopes of resolving it. The case is pretty solid and of decent quality. Unlike how some reviewers had mentioned, the PCIe slot covers in the back do have a threaded screw hole to replace them once snapped off, and the case also included an extra PCIe cover. Everything that really needs "removed" is removed easily and without any problems, though as with most cases, you'll need a screwdriver to initially take off the "hand-tightened" screws. There is plenty of space for most of what you'll ever need to fit, so I'm not too worried about what I'll end up installing. The review will be updated come the install of those parts and the completion of the build. Logistically, there were some things that came off odd or confusing. The manual includes install instructions for fans throughout the case, but fails to include instructions for fans being installed at the bottom of the case. Turns out, you use the hardware included with the case and screw the fans in from the inside of the case, not the outside like you usually would. I purchased extra fans from the seller to match everything, and installed these on the bottom- as seen in the photos. Furthermore, I'd highly recommend NOT powering even the 7 included fans via motherboard and daisy chain, get a SATA fan hub. Pulling that much power from the motherboard is not the best idea, and its probably a good idea for the seller to mention a "fan hub sold separately" for the newer folks who are not aware of this. I'm excited to see the completed build, and hopefully the seller takes these comments into consideration.
reviews.author: Mariella Morelli

reviews.title: Great Case
reviews.comment: Well worth the money since everything works perfectly. It’s nice that it did come with 9 fans, but it was also nice and easy to switch it around a bit. Aesthetically it looks great, and works fine for a i7 12700kf CPU and a 5070 ti GPU. I’d say if you don’t plan on putting in super high end components, these case fans will do the job to keep it cool. Very quiet, and when the fans ramp up it’s not super loud. Overall I’ve had much worse cases, and this one is a keeper in my book.
reviews.author: Jordan

reviews.title: Great case at a great price
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/E1AfF0IGyBL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/51bpUwYvdpL._SY256.jpg I'm writing this review because this is a great PC case and you're probably reading this review because it's under $100 and you want one. Great news for you because this case has what you need without the premium price. The big draw is the 6 RGB fans that come preinstalled. The fans are quiet and they cool nicely and if RGB is your thing, that look nice too. The case has a button next to the power button that lets you cycle through different colors and thankfully you can also turn them off if you don't care for the light show. The case has a hub on the back that has all the fans connected to it, so all you have to do is tame the ball of wires that come from all directions. Good luck to you!
Another draw to this case is that it's a fish tank that's so trendy these days. There's a metal hard drive bay next to the PSU slot to put a HDD which can be moved further into the case if your PSU is too long like mine is and there's two slots for SATA SSDs about mid-right of the back of the case. The top of the case is roomy and there's plenty of space for 360mm AIO and there's no worry slotting in those giant GPUs; there's plenty of room for them in this case.
Of course, to keep the price under $100 it had to cut some corners. The only real problem for me is that the filter for the PSU is absurdly inadequate. It's less a filter and more of a square cut from a window screen and the inserts on the case to put it in place are simple clips that are hard to put on even while looking at them. I was having trouble putting the filter back on while the case was empty and I had the thing upside down looking at it straight on; now imagine trying to remove the filter, clean it, and put it back on while the case is sitting on the desk. This is the only major screw up as far as I'm concerned. The filter at the top of the case is more or less the same however it has a magnetic border all around it, so there's some weight to it and stays in place nicely. Another drawback is that the holes don't have grommets for cable management; your cables are simply going to stay at the bottom of the holes. Not a deal breaker but you should know what you're getting into. This last one may or may not affect you. Instead of the power button being at the top of the case it's at the bottom near the front. If your case is sitting on your desk this is great; it's at desk level, just reach a little to the right and your PC is on! But if your case is under your desk you're going to have to reach further down to turn it on every time.
I upgraded from a case that only had five fans and poor ventilation for high-end parts and when I changed to this case I saw my temps lower by 20 degrees Celsius. That's an amazing improvement! The case is so roomy that I won't have to worry about future upgrades not fitting for the foreseeable future so I'm staying with this case for a long time through multiple builds.
reviews.author: Francis C.

reviews.title: Overall an amazing case with minor flaws.
reviews.comment:
Pros:
Case looks great, plenty of internal room, more than enough fans pre installed, great airflow, removable hdd cage, and fans have a decent color as well.
Cons:
Fans are a bit loud and the back of case doesn't have the most room for cable management
If you plan on setting it up with an air cooler like me I suggest moving the bottom fans to the top to exhaust heat and flip the fans towards the front of the case around so they intake cooler air giving you positive air pressure.
Overall great value for the overall performance especially coming with 6 fans argb fans preinstalled.
reviews.author: Breanna Morrissey

reviews.title: One of best case you can buy right now for less than $100.
reviews.comment:
First off, the build quality of this case is awesome, and you get 6 rgb fans included, which can be customized to however you want using any rgb control software.
Also, you get a RGB hub on the back panel that will take 6 rgb fans. So you’re good to go with the included fans. This case can actually 9 fans total (two in the front, three in the bottom, one in the back, and three on the top).
You get tempered glass front and side panel, which is awesome. Also super easy to pop them off and on. Literally takes 10 seconds to do both.
Also, every pc components fit perfect. The motherboard lines up with the mounting holes/standoffs perfect. My ASUS TUF 4060ti GPU fits in the case with plenty of room, and I’ve also verified that a 7800xt will also fit, but sadly I had to RMA the 7800xt because it was defective and it didn’t allow my pc to post or boot at all.
You also get a couple black zip ties, which definitely comes in handy.
The case feels solid, it’s got some weight to it, which is nice.
One downside is the fans can get pretty loud, and sound deadening isn’t too good, there’s plenty of ventilation which is good, but that means more noise will escape the case.  You will want to get some sort of fan controller software to control the fan speeds to your liking, it will have to use you M/B BIOS. I recommend “Fan Control” software. It’s free, and easy to use.
Great buy!
reviews.author: SRTRANDY

reviews.title: Perfect case for budget build
reviews.comment: The case looks amazing and the Rgb modes are very nice, would buy again for another build compatibility with matx/micro/atx builds is good, the build is Good for a budget case. Love the small screen that displays the GPU temps and CPU temps and functions as expected after software download. The airflow is good as far as I know cpu temps are on point. Instructions are abit off but not hatd if u know what ur doing.
reviews.author: Jose

reviews.title: Nice case
reviews.comment: Cool case very versatile and solidly built. Good airflow as well for a smaller case.
reviews.author: ShoeBox

reviews.title: Great case, good price point, decent build quality and top notch styling.
reviews.comment: I honestly love the look and feel of this case, the glass looks amazing and the build feels strong enough to keep up with moving this around if you ever have to. it's very easy to do cable management with lots of grooves and areas for you to tie cables too. There are 2 slots for 2.5 ssd's and one for a full-size hard drive that a little harder to locate unless you download the manual off their website. The motherboard standoffs are a little annoying to remove but other than that everything seemed ready to go out the box. Air flow is great, temps are great but there are only filters at the top and bottom not the side or rear so if you set those to intake it will be sucking in dust. Overall extremely functional just be aware the front temp screen will require a motherboard USB connection to run. My main gripe is the rear GPU slots that are usually removable are snap off style and one remove can not be reinstalled.

reviews.title: Awesome
reviews.comment: I'm sold on this case.  The price and reviews make you assume it's decent for the price.  It's truly better than that.  It's good enough for me to waste my time to give the mfg props for perfect fit and finish.  I'm buying 2 more
reviews.author: Pjl3

reviews.title: perfect mid size!
reviews.comment: the perfect size great quality for sure! Great CPU compartment and cable management space.
reviews.author: Grant klann

reviews.title: S-tier build quality!
reviews.comment:
After doing tons of research and watching a hundred different videos reviewing cases i decided to go with the Montech King 95 Pro. This would be my 1st official build by myself. First off, i have to say, this case is HEAVY. It will take up a quarter of your desk space, which i ended up using a 2nd desk to set it on, as to keep all of my desk real estate intact.
This case is beautiful, and even though it was my 1st build , the case was incredibly easy to build in. All the sides come off, and everything opens up. It gives you quite a few ways to set things up depending on what youre wanting to do. The openings found throughout the inside provide easy access for cable management
All of the accessories Montech includes are awesome and helpful during the build process. The included fan controller works great, LED's look amazing, and my CPU and GPU temps are great as well.
All in all, i would definitely recommend this case. Its built exceptionally well, its solid as a rock and does not feel cheap whatsoever.
reviews.author: Richie Caldwell

reviews.title: Designed for builders
reviews.comment:
This is the 3rd PC I’ve built, prior to this build I used Thermaltake Cases, and I was able almost immediately notice when building this PC how much better this case is manufactured. One important thing that needs to be addressed is that the case states that it can accommodate a 360mm radiator in the top section. Well that’s true, but close to not being so. Depends ultimately on which radiator you select. I installed a PrimoChill 360SL Eximo for the radiator, and it barely fits. (10mm of free play +/-) I had to install low profile plug fittings from Barrow to accommodate the lack of space on the two terminals not being used for this build.
With that out of the way,
The case fits new Megatron-sized GPUs.
Comes with 6 Argb case fans.
Generous cable management room.
Beautiful showcase glass.
Modular staging bracket for the Two 140mm fans.
Mounting adapters & Modules + various locations hardest on the case for HDDs (2.5 & 3.5).
Excellent Price/value.
And just so many things I see that really shows the design team really put their heads together when it came to making this case. I would highly recommend this case for newcomers building PCs and seasoned builders alike.
1 other con besides the radiator accommodation on top is the belly screen on the bottom is kinda cheap/ flimsy. Would swap it for a magnet style like I’ve seen on some other cases if possible.
With all that said I still give it 5/5. It’s been a blast building this PC. Time to see how many instances of Windows Solitaire I can open at once before crashing it.
reviews.author: Alexander

reviews.title: Very good value for a dual chamber PC case
reviews.comment:
I got the King 95 pro, with the preinstalled fans. The ability to remove the top, front, and both sides easily made it a dream to build in. So easy to get to everything. All the extra space made cable management very easy, and you could say not even really needed. The included ARGB fan hub works well also. It did take a me a few days, however, to figure out how to use it. I had to RTM that one. There is a button on the front, which you can press to change the built in ARGB effects, or you can hold it for 3 seconds to switch it over to being controlled by the onboard mobo ARGB headers. The air flow is good, and so are the temps, without being loud. The 3 bottom fans blowing on the GPU help a bunch with keeping the temps pretty low, even when it's over clocked.
All in all, this case is by far the easiest to build in that I've ever had, and I have built well over a hundred PCs. The dual chamber design is the biggest reason. imho
reviews.author: Jtv

reviews.title: Loved the look
reviews.comment: Nice case! looks really good, and has a nice durability, also the glass panel lets you look through and it has a nice fit an fan capacity even for a 5080
reviews.author: Christian

reviews.title: Great large case
reviews.comment: This is a bit bigger than it looks so check measurements. The airflow is great. The assembly was easy. It's super easy to clean. The glass looks fantastic. The build is solid. Overall, a great choice for the price.
reviews.author: Jonsey Jones

reviews.title: Great value, modern looking, the RGB fans are an awesome bonus!
reviews.comment: This case is a great value. I was in a pinch, and needed something next day, so honestly that was one of my primary criteria. I was hoping to get something white, with lots of glass so I could show off the RGB lights of all of the internal components, so having a case preloaded with all of the cooling fans with RGB built in was an unexpected and awesome bonus. The case is roomy without being bulky, modern in that it doesn't have 5-1/4" drive bays, has a front (actually top) multimedia panel including USB 2.0, 3.0 as well as usb-c, power and reset buttons, and even an RGB on/off button (if you can make that work with your setup, I had a few extra steps I had to go through it make it work, but worth it!). Again, lots of room without being too big, no fitment issues with anything. Cons.. I guess the pci card slot blanks could be better quality - these are break away style, so once you snap one out, you'll have that hole in the back of the case if you remove, or move, the card. Simple enough, buy a couple of blanks for a few bucks, but would have been a nice touch if they included that from the start. Edges are a bit sharp on the case internals - I cut my hand pretty good while installing the power supply cables, not knowing the sheetmetal inside where the power supply lives was never rounded or machined, it's just the sharp edge that happens after stamping the metal. The external edges are all machines and nice, so once set up a total non issue, but just be aware while assembling, use caution. The RGB fans comes prewired and jumped together. The final hookup cable however was very short, and on the opposite side of the motherboard from where my connections had to be made. I was able to do disconnect all of the fans and daisy chain them together in opposite arrangement, and have a tight stretched cable diagonally across the top of the mother board to get it to plug in, but it was ugly. Ultimately, I wound up buying a few extension cables for the RGB and actual fan power cables, and then everything dressed in nice. Again, would just be nice if they included those same jumper cables so it was in the package ready to use. I'd happily pay an extra $10 or whatever to include the cables and PCI blanks and have them in the kit, rather than having to find out 90% of the way through the build they are needed and not in the box The power supply mounts in a welded in cage that's part of the case. This makes for a nice, clean looking install when its all done. However, it also makes it a bit of a challenge to work on getting all of the cables routed through and if you need to add an extra cable later, be prepared to potentially have to unplug everything , remove the power supply and cables, add the new cable and then reinstall everything, as there really is no direct access to the back of the power supply because of that cage. Minor issue, and does look nice when it's done, but would have been awesome if there was a removable panel that could make servicing or changes easier. Overall, the 'cons' I list are very critical and minor issues, and I would still purchase it again in a heartbeat, and fully recommend to anyone looking for a decent small desktop tower form factor case in white, with lots of glass and very modern look and feel, at an incredible price point. I would not hesitate to pay $100 for this, especially if those issues I mentioned were addressed, but I paid significantly less, even having purchased the blanks and cable extenders. Great value, very happy with the final result.
reviews.author: J. R.

reviews.title: Modern and spacious
reviews.comment: Absolutely beautiful case. Well built and straight forward. Even with an the wiring, there is plenty of room to still do a clean build. Also has nice thermals and fans can move some wind if needed
reviews.author: Caesar

reviews.title: Stylish, Spacious, and Easy to Build In – Great Value Case!
reviews.comment: I recently used the darkFlash ATX Mid-Tower Case for a new build, and it exceeded my expectations. The tempered glass side panel gives it a premium look, and the RGB fans included are vibrant and surprisingly quiet. The airflow is excellent right out of the box, which keeps my system cool even under load. The interior is very builder-friendly—plenty of room for cable management, space for full-sized GPUs, and mounts for multiple SSDs and HDDs. I also appreciated the PSU shroud, which keeps the bottom area clean and organized. Overall, this case looks great, performs well, and offers features usually found in more expensive cases. Highly recommend for gamers or anyone looking to build a clean, modern PC on a budget.
reviews.author: JRussett

reviews.title: Great at this price point
reviews.comment: Great Buildability 4/5 (plenty of room for building but had 1 screw hole strip with light torque) Cable management 3/5 (Would rate higher if there was gromets or covers for the holes) Build Quality 3/5 (noticed some flexing in a few spot while building) Appearance 5/5 (Really nice shade of white especially at this price) Serviceability 5/5 (Opening the case is completely toolless and the side panel is just one screw while still very secure)
reviews.author: Ryan N.

reviews.title: Well built, lot of space!
reviews.comment: Great case, lot of space for discrete wiring, ultra silence and glass extremely clear once I removed the protective film looks like there where no glass at all!
reviews.author: Manuel A. Soto Avila

reviews.title: Awesome case!!!  Built like a tank with plenty of room to have a build that doesn't look cramped!!
reviews.comment: Very Happy with this case.  I looked at hundreds before choosing this one and can't really remember why exactly I chose it over the others but I am really happy with how it turned out.  I never thought I would like a white case but after looking at others builds I just found I liked the white aesthetic better.  This case comes with 6 rgb fans as well so toss in a 360 aio or something similar and it looks great. I have seen other case reviews where people talk about flimsy easily bent cases.. well let me tell you the Foifkin F600 I got isn't one of them.  Its well built and larger than I was expecting as I didn't really look at the dimensions all that well but that is the best part about it.  Your build doesn't feel cramped and crammed in there.  There is ample room for working and cable management is easy. The fans that were included all match my Thermalright frozen warframe aio perfectly.  They worked great.  I had a small issue with one and contacted the seller who was super helpful and sent replacement immediately. I love that this case is built well, I was worried about getting a thin little flimsy something that wouldn't last or would be a pain to build in.  With this case everything went as smooth as one could hope for.  The metal is solid and has some weight to it especially with the parts installed.  It doesn't feel cheap like a lot of cases I have seen and had.  I have an old hp desktop and the metal is thicker than that I am pretty sure. Its not one of those you look at it wrong it gets a bend or dent in it.  I did need to sit it good and level for the door to shut perfectly which its the same with any of these cases.  When I had it sitting on a couple different things I was having to lift it slightly into place but when I got the shelf built for it, it started opening and shutting perfect.  It just needed a flat hard surface. The front glass panel is on hinges and the side glass has the little plastic connectors that make it super easy to pop in and out if you need access.  The top mesh comes off to clean and install aios or fans.  Not sure if the bottom does but it may as well (I checked it is removable but not magnetic).  The top one is magnetic. The only issue I had was when I upgraded the gpu to a sappire pulse 9060xt 16gb I had trouble getting the screws in that hold the gpu to the back of the case.  The case is so solid that I couldn't push the back in and get it to go in as good as I would have liked but I still got it in.  Will have to look again though now that I got a proper screwdriver to user there.  I was improvising at the time.  To install these you need to remove a piece from the back and then open a little door which lets you put it in place.  This could be a issue with the gpu or mobo itself though as I had a rx6600 in there before and it fit just fine and the screws went in easily so I can't blame the case on that. Also it fits the psu really well and I like the large area in the back to hide the psu instead of sticking it out in the front or beneath the case.  It just looks nice to me.  I mean everyone has their own tastes but I really like it.  I have thought of getting some of those rgb cables to go in as well. Oh the fans in this case are already connected together so I just plugged them into the mobo and they were ready to go.  They also had the wiring for the fans done nicely it wasn't all messy looking like I have seen in some other cases.
reviews.author: kat

reviews.title: Great Case!
reviews.comment: The case looks great and the deal there is absolutely worth your cash. 7 fans for $80, can’t beat that. Only bother is the ssd/hdd plate holder (whatever the specific name is) is very hard to work with, my ssd would bend, there’s no clearance between the plate and ssd you just screw it straight into the case. It makes it very hard to plug cables in due to there being no clearance. If that doesn’t make sense you’ll end up running into it. I have the ssd hanging off the plate and secured it with 2 screws. It’ll do for now, but I recommend buying a aftermarket stand off that matches the dimensions of the cases. I was surprised by the quality of the case in general and that includes the fans. The noise is minimal and they are very effective. I can feel the air flowing throughout the case when it’s open. You can definitely depend on them. Last thing I wanted to mention is that the case is pretty big so I recommend looking at the size/dimensions of the case and make sure it aligns with the kind of desk you are running. Great product!
reviews.author: isaias

reviews.title: Awesome quality case at an amazing value. Quality and style almost exactly matches big name cases.
reviews.comment: I was skeptical since this case is such a low price point compared to a lot of the other big name brand "fish tank style" cases I was looking at, but I have to say I was pleasantly surprised once it came in! I was going to go with a name brand one at a big box store, but I decided to roll the dice on this case for my build. The fans came preinstalled and it came with all the hardware I needed for my build. It has plenty of slots to mount your GPU and a great mounting process for the power supply. Everything in my build fit seamlessly in this case, and it felt like everything was sturdy, attached well. I'm not a fan noise snob, so take this for what you will, but I find the included fans to be pretty quiet, not making any insane noises or making me feel like I'm sitting next to an AC unit. Keep in mind the image may show seven fans, but you will only get the 6 fans as stated in the description (which wasn't a problem because I read through the whole item description). I ended up liking their included fans so much, that I bought my seventh exhuast fan from them once the case came in. When it comes to cooling, this case stays very cool and the exhaust fan definitely helps the fan flow. When it came to installing all the components of my PC build, I found it easier to just remove the bottom fans since they're quite seamless to reinstall. All the RGB synced up perfectly and the top power button rapidly alternates between a cotton candy blue and pink led whenever the build is on. All the I/O ports that I hooked up to the MB work perfectly and the placements are convenient. This case has been working flawlessly for over two months now and I have zero complaints (if that changes I will update the review). The glass door is easy to remove from the hinges (just lift up vertically) during cleanings or whenever you're doing the initial PC build. Based on the way my GPU mounts to the case and the MB, I did have to get a GPU sag brace, but it was super cheap and easy to install between the GPU and bottom fans. Highly recommend this case due to its quality for the low price point. I will be getting another one for my wife when I start her next build.
reviews.author: RJ

reviews.title: FOIFKIN F600
reviews.comment: Great Looking Case with Solid Build, But Front Panel Has Limitations The FOIFKIN F600 PC case looks amazing right out of the box. The panoramic 270° tempered glass gives it a premium and modern feel, and the materials seem sturdy and well-made. The 7 pre-installed ARGB PWM fans are a nice touch and keep the airflow smooth and quiet. The inclusion of a USB Type-C port is also appreciated for a case at this price point. However, one important limitation is the front panel space. Unfortunately, it does not support a 360mm liquid cooler like the CORSAIR Nautilus 360 RS ARGB. I had hoped to mount it there, but there simply isn’t enough room to fit the radiator and fans comfortably. This could be a dealbreaker for those planning to install a large AIO cooler in the front. Overall, it’s a great mid-tower case for the price, especially if you’re not planning to use a front-mounted 360mm AIO. Just make sure to check your cooler dimensions before buying.
reviews.author: Lazaro

reviews.title: Will Use with Multiple builds in the future. Great PC Case.
reviews.comment: The F600 case is a great case for any build.  Cost effective, easy to build in and beautiful when finished. comes with 7 Pre-installed ARGB Fans and room for a 360 AIO at the top.  I will definitely use with future builds.
reviews.author: JRM71

reviews.title: Best value for money
reviews.comment: Amazing case both aesthetic wise and practicality, has much room for bulky GPUS, airflow is great too, comes with complete cable management accessories. A little tricky for PSU fitment and  cables, larger PSU will be hard to fit and can press against IO cables.
reviews.author: Abdullah Asif

reviews.title: Excellent GAMING CASE W RGB FANS
reviews.comment: I have been building computers for over 40 years now and I have had a lot of different cases with a gaming theme.  This one is one of my favorites and it is very easy to build in and make changes afterwards which always seems to be the case after I complete a build. It looks great and the fans are top notch and the airflow is good also keeping my 13600K at a very low temperature. 32c in case anyone wants to know and this is using a COOLMASTER 212 APEX CPU AIR COOLER.
reviews.author: “ SCOTT”

reviews.title: Stylish and Practical, Requires Planning
reviews.comment: Excellent case if you're looking for a more straight edge design that is flashy without being gaudy over over-presenting. It has a nice mix of aesthetics, enough room in the back to build in, but you have to make sure you pre-plan because it's a nightmare if you don't. One of the smallest ATX cases that fits a 420 AIO and an EATX motherboard, though I would definitely recommend a regular ATX motherboard. And you CAN build this with a lian li-edge PSU you just have to unscrew the left most usb-a (which I would have done anyways to give data to the edge's included fan hub.) It was easy to take apart, easy to build in, and easy to cable manage after building in. Everything is toolless and the most you will need tools for is to "break" the factory tightened hand-screws, after that you can practically build and rebuild it with no problems whatsoever. Their customer service is quick to respond and very kind as well, answering all of my questions within 24 hours. I would purchase this case as well as other cases they make in the future.
reviews.author: ronda h.

reviews.title: Highly Recommended - Use a Small Power Supply
reviews.comment: There are plenty of reviews you can find online for this case (Kitguru, Robeytech, PCMag etc.) and you ought to look at them before you buy. I’ll agree with some and disagree with others. First, this case is NOT difficult to build in if you buy a SMALL power supply – I bought a SFF. People complain about not having enough wiring space – I had no trouble – maybe it’s because I planned everything before I started (thanks MaximumPC). I’ve never had such a clean looking build before (look at the pictures) and I’ve been building PC’s for a long time. Yes, you will have to take out one of the lower fans to access the fan/RGB headers depending on your motherboard (and if you buy the case with the fans included…obviously) but that’s pretty standard. Yes, you may need to run your wiring a different way than you have before (assuming you have done previous builds) but if your power supply comes with short cables you don’t have to buy extensions or specialized cables from MODDIY. I ran the GPU wiring over the GPU rather than under because the Gen 5 12VHPWR PSU cable that came with the power supply was really short (sorry Corsair) – but the power supply is right there, so it’s not an issue.  Yes, the shipping packaging is not great – the first one I ordered came with the plastic bottom broken, and the second with the RGB on the back fan not functioning. Amazon replaced the first and Geometric Future replace the fan (I received 3 fans a couple of days after I posted the problem to the seller’s comments – I’d say that’s pretty superior customer support). I may have just been unlucky, but I thought you should know of my experience. Yes, there are some minor misalignments (e.g. the thumb screw on the power supply bracket does not line up very well... as noted by Kitguru) but overall, the build quality is very good, the case is sturdy, and the finish is stylish. I've had no issues with cooling and consistent with online reviews, air flow is excellent. The bottom line, you might have to use your brain a little bit, but once you’re finished, you will have a great looking machine inside and out. Highly recommended.
reviews.author: Dave P.

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.comment: I love this case! This is the kind of layout I have been looking for over a decade. Pros: Layout. The case fits a ton of cooling in a standard mid tower size. 420mm rad support on top. Value Will fit even the insane-sized gpus. Build quality is good for the price features. I'd say about NZXT level (2021 h5 flow) build quality. Better than Thermaltake (tower 200). Worse than Phanteks (enthoo pro and enthoo evolv) and lian li (v3000+). Basically, sturdy and well-built, but not luxurious. Easy to build inside of (assuming you don't have tons of HDD/SSD to mount/wire - there are better options for data/server/nas cases). Chimney style cooling. Great airflow. Light weight for how sturdy it is. Fits in a server rack when laid on its side Cons: The PSU cage limits your options, especially if looking at a power-hungry equipment like the 5090. I had been looking at this case for a while but wanted 1200W for future gpu. The Montech century II 1200W recently released and reviewed very well at hardware busters, is very good value, and fits the size limitations. If you want to switch off the power button on the PSU, you have to remove the top panel (but removal would be easy in most circumstances). Depending on your situation, you may want to purchase a filter kit. The bottom intake is the only part that is filtered, and it is a pretty open case. Due to the high air flow, it can get loud depending on your fans and fan curves. Hard to find 160mm fans for the front fan (optional) Honestly, the unknowns of this brand and seemingly buried coverage might scare you off. But this is a great case. Some of the YouTube reviews are perplexing. I think these product schills just did not get paid for their review and decided to bash things that were not even relevant or correct.
reviews.author: KAS

reviews.title: Great case! Outstanding Support
reviews.comment: It's a great case at a good price. The design is what you expect from a dual chamber layout, but they take care of the details. All the panel feel strong and easy to remove and put back in place.  Plenty of room for everything! My big CPU cooler fits wells. The cable management is easy, even you can do it without removing the air duct partition. The accessories kit included is good, you won't need anything else. The cooling is good just using 3 120mm fans on the side and one 140mm fan in the rear. The only thing they could improve is the power button on the front. It looks great Update: After 6 months, Had a few broken clips on my ANTEC C8 Wood case and emailed support late Sunday night. To my surprise, they replied within minutes and shipped the replacement part the next day. Incredible response time and top-notch customer service—Antec really impressed me!
reviews.author: Alex Lozada

reviews.title: Makes Big Builds Feel More Manageable...and Looks Awesome!
reviews.comment: I picked up the Antec C8 Wood because I needed more room for a dual-GPU setup to split my AI workloads. Everything came packed really well, and the glass panels look great once they’re on. The walnut front actually matches my desk, which I didn’t expect. I’m running an i7-13700K, a Noctua cooler, an RTX 5080 and 4070 Ti, plus about ten case fans total. For now I’ve only tested with one GPU since I’m waiting on a new PSU, but even with half the setup running, it already feels like the right case for the job. I attached my thermals for CPU Idle, CPU Max and GPU Maxed if interested. Its a significant improvement from my old case, as stress testing gave a ton of headroom for the extra GPU. What I Like: Airflow is honestly great. With all the ARGB fans going, the whole system looks like it’s about to jump through time—but in a classy, wood-accent kind of way. Bottom intake is clever and definitely helps, though it does make my feet a little cold. Building in this thing was easier than I expected for such a big case. I didn’t have any issues with knobs falling off or anything like that. And the front-panel connection being a single plug is a lifesaver. Cable management was almost relaxing with how open the chambers are. What I Don’t Like: There’s a small gap where the two glass panels meet. It’s not terrible, but it does make me wish I’d gone for the curved version. This case is also huge—like “measure your space twice” huge. Luckily I really like it, so thankfully I don't need to return it hah. Would I Recommend It: Yes, especially if you’re running a lot of hardware or just want a clean, roomy layout without fighting cables or airflow.
reviews.author: heyviet

reviews.title: Excellent case for your PC Build
reviews.comment: The case is spacious and well thought out. There are plenty of diffrent ways to route cables with an adaquate amount of tie down points.  It is easy to remove all the panels, as there arn't any major screws holding down the side pannels or the front panel. I was able to easily remove the front panel without too much issue, as I have had with some fish tank style cases that have 8+ screews for the front glass. I have a custom water cooling loop inside and I do not have any issues with space with 2 360mm radiators. This isn't the most popular water-cooling case, but I don't think it was a necessary difficult case to build a custom loop in. I did find that my combo of radiator and reservoir had a tight curve for soft tubing. I am not sure on the best way I could have mitigated that issue, but It is fine none the less with plenty of fiddling. It is a solid looking case with a nice wood accent that feels like real wood. I didn't have any defects in my wood.
reviews.author: Layne Myers

reviews.title: buy it
reviews.comment: This case is fantastic. its solid as hell even without the glass in place. easy to build in. plenty of airflow and is large enough for even the biggest of video cards. the only thing i dont love about it is the hdd slots. you get two ssd slots but they are at the very top of the chamber and only once hdd slot at the very bottom. bneyond that though i couldnt be more impressed with the money. oh and it looks gorgeous in person. the wood is actual wood.
reviews.author: John Tyler Wittig

reviews.title: Great case and very beginner friendly to build in due to its tool-less design.
reviews.comment: I really enjoyed building in this case and yes its huge but if you have room for it then I highly recommend it. Its also easy to maintain and clean the filters. I have had it for a year and it still looks as good as new. The tool less design for removing the glass panels is great and the build quality is very high. Also the wood version looks cool and goes well with my desk aesthetics.
reviews.author: Jason Chaser

reviews.title: Budget Build Dream Case
reviews.comment:
In short, you won’t find better looking and better quality for this price.
For the overall compact size of the case it has great features. Comes with 3 pre installed argb fans which are quite nice. Plenty of front panel IO. The ease to build in for me was very easy. I would highly recommend this for an ITX or mATX build. For my build I installed two reverse airflow fans in the bottom and a 120mm AIO (for the nostalgia) and kept the two others in the top of the case. Running an I7 and 5700XT temps on GPU stay under 55 and CPU has never reached 68. (Don't judge my one stick of ram it was a placeholder while my kit arrived) As a side note DarkFlash has a great after sales and customer service team.
reviews.author: Lazaro Gonzalez

reviews.title: Amazing case
reviews.comment:
It surprises me to see the negative reviews this case has.  I've built over 90 computers as a side project flipping for fun.  This is one of the best cases I've ever used.
Airflow:  Yes, the top fans are mounted to blow air up.  They're easy to flip to draw air in.  Then you get as much air flow as any normal front mounted.
Quality:  The metal on this case is relatively thick and doesn't flex, especially compared to other budget or even high-end cases.  The glass panels fit together nicely.  Yes, the metal side panel is a little tricky to get on, but it's not bad.  The rounded edges on top look nice and make this case stand out some in a good way.  The cover on the case back for covering the PCEI ports is on hinges, which is convenient and looks nice.  The holes on the floor of the case between the main chamber and PSU provide for additional airflow.  The power button feels solid and is nice to press.
Cable routing:  There is plenty of space to route cables in the back and under the case, even with non-modular PSUs.  This was easy.  The holes for cable routing are nicely placed and make sense.
Fans:  They are amazing--quiet and beautiful.  They have a different, round profile on the side that makes them look premium.
Yes, the cabling is black.  So are the cables on most PSUs.  If you really want, you can get cable extensions and hide the cabling behind them.  Black doesn't stand out, so it's not like it's highlighted.  I personally usually don't like white cables, even for all white builds, because the RGB highlights it, almost makes it glow, and I don't want the attention to be drawn to cables.
I've had great results with Dark Flash products, I like their CPU coolers also.
reviews.author: Minty

reviews.title: Great Bang for your Buck!
reviews.comment: This is a great case and is very compact! Only issue i have with it is the air flow options: it only has 5 120mm fan mounting options: 2top, 1rear, 2bottom. Which isnt great for optimal airflow as I have to have the top and rear as exhaust and the bottom 2 (bought separately) as the only intakes. Other than that one gripe its a great case for the price point for sure!
reviews.author: Jacob

reviews.title: Quality case, rolled metal edge, good fans, super nice finish.
reviews.comment:
This has to be one of the best cases I've used.
I've been building computers for over 20 years, gaming systems for 10+.
Every metal edge is rolled, not a single sharp edge. The metal is thick and makes for a nice ridgid case. the glass is perfectly flat with no worbly effect. Fans are quiet, blow we'll, and are very crisp and bright.
Good choice of wire run ports,
The finish is excellent. Not just a spray over the outside, the whole chair is finished, not a single spot showing the metal underneath.
This build did not use an AIO, however there is plenty enough room, even in this mATX case to easily fit  one.
I went back to their store to see what other cases they have. Sadly my other two computers are we'll established and I can't justify just upgrading a case. But oh, how I want to
reviews.author: Carol L. Mccawley

reviews.title: Terrible airflow. Hugely disappointed
reviews.comment:
Terrible airflow.
Looks nice, but cannot house any modern CPUs.
9600X
5070
Idle temps are fine, around 40C, but during gaming the cpu jumps to a steady 75C with peaks at 82.
Has “flow holes” on the bottom, but nowhere for cool air to actually intake (power supply directly underneath one and a sealed cavity otherwise).
reviews.author: Chris

reviews.title: Absolutely Incredible — Nobody’s Ever Seen Cases Like This Before!
reviews.comment: The HAVN HS420 is unbelievable. A case so good, it’s obnoxious how perfect it is. Strong, solid, powerful — just like America used to be. This case has fantastic airflow, the best airflow, people tell me. Your components stay cool, very cool. They stay happy — no overheating, no problems. The build quality is tremendous. Thick panels, not that cheap thin stuff you see on other cases. You tap it — sounds like success. The cable management is cleaner than some of the elections, believe me. Beautiful case. And the design — modern, elegant — everyone says, “Sir, that’s the best-looking PC case we’ve ever seen.” Look, you would think this case is too good to be true. But every single detail is so carefully thought after. It’s incredible. They have a rubber piece in every single screw hole, making it impossible to hear it running. Absolutely the best PC case in the world, by far. Nobody’s even close. HAVN did an amazing job. They really did. If you want your build to look and feel like a win — this is the one. Totally five stars. Maybe more. I can’t imagine anybody rate it below 5 stars. We are gonna have to see what’s happening. Thanks for your attention to this matter.
reviews.author: Whatupyall

reviews.title: Amazing case BUT
reviews.comment: First complaints then the positive at the bottom. there are a few manufacturing details I struggled with and still am in a way. the top panel doesnt fall into place as easily as all those doing the YT reviews. usually takes several attempts to get it just so so to fall into the power button. heir front panel connections are great BUT, they are soooo long, I have no clue how they think you need all of the cables to reach the lower far corner of the mobo. this caused me to use the channel ment to run fan wiring along the top to holding these. design wise the back panel could have most of it covered as you arent really using the back 4/5 of the case for fans. makes it more suceptable to possible splashes (ask me how I found this out)... also means cable routing is even more important as its all on show through the back. the fanhub towards teh rear is in a bad spot, its where someone is likely to put their hand when grabbing to turn the case. outside of these things however (you are probably wondering why the 5 star review), this is the easiest case I have worked with. easy to route most of the cabling, no cussing trying to get wires or cables to fit through a tiny gap (CPU power 8pin x2) lower board headers easy to reach, lots of fan/AIO options. mounting options for storage and/orfans and/or LCD screen. even without the panels on it is a very sturdy design (albiet HEAVY). no flippy floppy is it gonna break worries. if you have the room to put this monster of a case, I would recomend it above all other cases Ive dealt with. whether you are a first or second time builder or you just have hand issues (like myself) this case makes it so easy to build in. and for those that remember... this thing is almost Tonka tough. for their first case design... they hit the mark. if they continue they will be undisputed in case designs.
reviews.author: Brett L.

reviews.title: Top notch fit, finish and design.
reviews.comment: Never thought I’d write a review about a computer case. Initially was considering a bunch of cases in the $150 to $180 range such as flux master pro and fractal design north. After researching for about a week, it was clear to me that while they are good for cooling the build quality is subpar. On top of that the wood accents look cheap and kind of like an afterthought in a afterschool home project. You could tell the way they designed the Havn case that they paid attention to every single detail: beautiful single piece glass display panel, rounded corners everywhere including the glass, bottom air vents and the fit and finish is top notch. The case is quite substantial in terms of weight. The best analogy I could give is that it is like my first experience driving a BMW or other luxury car after only having driven low to mid tier cars. While the Havn cooling is not top of the range unless you add 3 more fans in the back, it’s not far from it.  Unless you are looking to be an overclocking champ it is pretty irrelevant. You can actually display this case in your living room as part of a centerpiece. It’s that nice. I cant help but look at how nice it is. It just exudes quality. Personally I suggest the white case with black components. The white elements frame the black components beautifully. Absolutely worth retail price. If they made another case about 2/3 the size I would buy it as a secondary PC.
reviews.author: J P

reviews.title: Stellar case. Never been so happy to not be a cheapskate.
reviews.comment: I have in nearly all cases cheaped out on a case. I resolved with the 9800X3D build I was doing to not do this on anything, to get good, not best, but solid quality everything. Initially I wanted to go with the hyte y70, but that would not work with my capture card+gpu. so after exhaustively reading a LOT of motherboard manuals and case manuals, I landed on the HAVN case and man, building in this was an absolute dream. From the little wheels that help make removing the single glass panel a breeze to every single panel having slots and thoughtful insertion mechanics to make it easier to use and test fit, it was delightful. The HUGE cable area behind the motherboard was amazing and wildly simplified my build. Every single passthrough was thoughtful and useful to have. The ability to REMOVE RADIATORS AND REFIT THEM AFTER INSTALL was game changing - each fan/radiator mount is a shock mounted cage you can sit-fit before screwing in, so when you realize 'oh yeah, I need power to my cpu, woops' you can just lift the cage! I have never had a build be less frustrating than in this case. I had a ton of fun doing it pretty much everything came together without issue. My only problem was that the lowest possible PCIE slot on a supported motherboard size - in this case, full ATX, was unavailable on the case. I wish this was detailed explicitly in the manual and would strongly recommend to HAVN to detail this, or have a knock-out there, as I had to use a riser to get my capture card mounted in a kind of janky way. It works, and sure I could have spent even more time finding a motherboard with pcie4x that didn't drop the 16x speed down in a supported slot, but I think it should be a safe assumption if you say it supports full ATX that you support all PCIE slots a board can have, or you asterisk this information. But that said, that's my only complaint with this case. If you are someone who normally spends 60 bucks on a case, you will be deeply pleased building in this. Do I think you should cut into CPU or GPU budget to get a nicer case? No. Do I think you should try to save a little longer to get a nicer case? Oh, absolutely. And I can't recommend this one enough.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Big case, big quality
reviews.comment: A real pleasure to build in this case.  Fit a 240mm radiator on top while waiting for my 420mm to arrive.  Both work fine.  Thicker radiators could be an issue with some large motherboard heat sinks, but my 420 rad is only 30mm and it wasn’t an issue. The airflow can work very well even without filling all the fan slots, however most people will want to run at least 6 (3 reverse blade fans on bottom, 3 standard blade fans on top) for appearances.  8 will be normal for most people I think.  It can take 11 but that will be overkill for most, and fancy rgb fans aren’t cheap. I used Squama fans on top and bottom, and light wings in the rear.  Well, I’m still waiting for 1 fan to arrive, but it all looks good already as it is. With the huge xfx Mercury 9070xt, probably the largest version of the 9070xt, there’s tons of room to spare.  Even 90 tier cards will have more than enough space. If you build with the horizontal GPU version like I did you will want a large GPU or the case is going to look empty. I think the horizontal version is tragically under-appreciated; it’s an amazing case even though it lacks the novelty of a vertical GPU. Build quality is amazing.  I’ve never owned a case this nice.  The glass is surprisingly thick. Lots of room for cable routing, although a few cables do have to go through a tight space above the PSU to get to the bottom of the mobo.  It also doesn’t have quite as much space around the PSU as a true dual chamber case would, but it’s still more than any case I’ve previously owned. All of the panels have magnetic latching, although I wish the magnets were just a little stronger especially on the large back side panel behind the mobo.  If your cable management isn’t tight bulging cables will push the panel right off.  An extra magnet on that side would be a good update for HAVN to make.  The panels can be screwed down and you will likely want to do so, although it’s not required.
reviews.author: Sean C

reviews.title: Affordable, Cheap
reviews.comment:
Fantastic case for the price. Perfect for a cheap build. The case is lightweight, thin, and cheap, but just sturdy enough to work.  Discrete styling, easy to access case buttons and USB 3 and audio jacks.  Rare to find three external 5.25 drive bays in this price range.
A lot of sharp edges, so be careful.  The plastic 3.5 bay cover was exceptionally difficult to pop out.
The case is small and cramped.  Everything will fit, barely.  It is clearly smaller in comparison to the Antec Sonata II below it in the photos (although the Sonata II cost twice as much).  No fancy drive rails for easy installation, but none to misplace either.
Cable management can be challenging due to the tight space.
Very tight fit getting the motherboard installed. There is less than a quarter inch between the motherboard and the 5.25 drive mounts, and even less once the power cable is plugged into the motherboard.
Keep the included screws in a safe place, because they are all smaller than typical case screws. such as the motherboard standoffs and screws, and the pci card screws.
Airflow is good due to the large perforated area above the motherboard and cpu, however dust might be an issue.
Overall, affordable and cheap but works.  I'd buy it again.
reviews.author: Sid

reviews.title: Quality case-no frills, very practical and roomy.
reviews.comment: Excellent case!  No frills so no high price.  Very modern--the cables for the front panel reflect the latest motherboard connectivity standards and supports USB 3.0.  Bright blue LED indicates power, and the power switch has an unmistakable click sound/feel to it.  I'm still working on troubleshooting the RESET switch.  I may have connected it incorrectly but thus far, it does nothing.  Bays for drives are accessible on both sides as both sides of the case are removable.  Does NOT come with power supply of course.  The feet are hard plastic, which is fine for most installations but I've got the case in a location where soft rubber feet are ideal, so I glued third party feet in place of the original.  The one fan is 6" in diameter, powers nicely from mobo connectors and is whisper silent.  Provisions for a second fan of the same dimensions are present at the front of the case.  The front face comes right off without tools, but is tethered by electrical cables of course for the buttons and lights.  Room for 4 exposed 5.25 devices, and plenty of room for more 3.5" devices inside.  Does not come with a PC speaker.
reviews.author: Snoo

reviews.title: Decent case overall, with some caveats
reviews.comment:
I'll start with the positive aspects of the case. It has a clean and simple style that I think is aesthetically pleasing. The hard drive cage is (almost) entirely metal. I find metal cages to be preferable to plastic, because the metal allows for better heat conduction and thus cooler hard drive temperatures.
On the downside, the build quality is mediocre. The sheet metal is a bit thin and flimsy. There are some sharp edges, so the user needs to be careful when handling components inside the case to avoid getting cut. My biggest criticism of the case is the shortage of motherboard standoffs and screws. There were only 6 motherboard standoffs in my package, so this results in a lot of flex in the motherboard as you attempt to assemble the components (like other reviewers have mentioned). I ran out of screws when installing disk drives in my computer. This is a really sad cost-cutting measure, since it would probably cost Antec only a couple of cents to include a few more screws and motherboard standoffs in the package.
I think 3.5 stars is probably a more realistic rating for this case as it is, which is unfortunate, because it would probably cost Antec only a few more dollars to address some of the issues mentioned in this review and other reviews to make a much better case that earns a solid 4.5 stars.
reviews.author: DC

reviews.title: Exactly What I Needed
reviews.comment: All the criticisms of this case are true. There's a few funky hole locations, no cable management space, and flimsy sheet metal. But it is one of the few cases with enough 5 1/4 front panel bays, which is exactly what I was looking for. I'm building a utility box to save files, test distros, and record from an old Sony DV camera. This box fit the bill. Every old desktop box I had, I was constantly crawling under the desk and switching hard drives and stuff. With that in mind, I put a 6 bay icy dock, drive switch, USB 3.0 panel. and a multi port card reader on the front panels. Its a budget build, so I didn't want to break the bank on the case. I did a couple of light mods including mounting a couple fans on the side panel for intake. This case was an excellent solution to my problems.
reviews.author: bntcashen

reviews.title: Bad experience
reviews.comment:
I bought this case as it supports an atx motherboard and it had exactly the right number of front drive bays I was looking for.
However as I picked up the box I could hear rattling coming from inside, while the case itself was ok and honestly I liked the style of it the front bezel wasn't attached and EVERY clip that would allow it fasten to the case was broken so the front bezel is useless, I know Amazon shipping can be rough but I also have to chalk it up to poor quality, I'll use the metal part of the case for another project but I won't be able to use it for it's intended purpose, I would of bought a couple more if my first experience was ideal but now I will avoid this brand like the plague as I was left with a bad first impression
reviews.author: anthony

reviews.title: Great home server case!
reviews.comment: I need a relatively mid server to as a data backup repository and to power my media server, some tech in my home, plus a few services that I use professionally. Was running off a self-contained NAS for a few years and honestly it just isn't scaling well and we needed more drive bays. Using this case, I built a new server with a high end ITX mobo and a real processor. SO much better! This has some amazing features. The backplane that connects the HDDs works great with the bays. My ONLY complaint is the dang 4-pin molex power connectors on that backplane. Those are old and unnecessary. I had to get adapters so I didn't have to add yet another power cable from my PSU (especially with such tight space inside). Anyway, the trays work great. The rubber screw gromit system is simple and firm. I like it a lot. Only could have been better if it was toolless maybe, though I don't think the 4 screws per drive are bad. There is plenty of space for everything I needed. Love the amount of tiedown points. Cable management was really satisfying. My only other complaint is the top section being secured by 4 hex screws. I feel like now that the system is done and running it won't have to be accessed all that often I guess? Either way I had some anxiety trying to figure out when I finally wanted to close it up. Overall I think this unit is solidly built. Cooling has been totally adequate under load so far as long as you tune the fans well. No complaints about noise either. The included fans are totally fine. Footprint is compact enough to keep tucked away, though cool looking enough to show off to your tech friends.
reviews.author: Gyakusetsu

reviews.title: Great case with an unusual design, but works well
reviews.comment: This case has been great so far. Probably the most challenging aspect is finding a Mini ITX board that is suitable for NAS, and finding a suitable power supply. I’ll touch briefly on these, but this review is about the case. The build is solid - nothing feels cheap, although I am not a huge fan of the drive mounts (basically rubber grommets attached to the drives with screws and a pull handle to assist in removing the drive from the bay). It works though, and I hopefully will not be swapping drives often, so not a huge deal to me. Inside the case, with a SFX power supply and mini ITX motherboard, there is plenty of room, and nothing feels cramped. The power cable is a bit odd, as the PSU mounts in the top of the case at the front, with an extension leading to the back of the case for the external power cable. It prevents you from using the power switch on the PSU, but again, not a deal breaker for me. Cable management is pretty easy, and there are options for different motherboard configurations and presumably PSUs. Heat management has been fine so far, but there are mount points for additional fans if needed. Noise is a bit high (I can’t measure it), but it is on par with my 2022 era tower case. I can hear both of them, but it’s bot terrible. I would not recommend it in a recording studio though. The weird bits… First, mini ITX - finding a board with 10GBe and at least 6 SATA ports is challenging. I could find maybe 4 total, but I am sure other options exist. Most ITX boards lack both of those features, and only one or the other can be added via the PCIe slot. I did find one though, and while it mostly works, the network chip on the mobo is not really designed for server use. I seek kernel warnings from TrueNAS regularly, and gave to wonder if it is responsible for the occasional network performance issues I see.  I may try another board at some point, but my recommendation is to do your homework - there are not really a lot of options. If you don’t need 10GBe, then you have more of a selection. Overall though, I am quite happy with the case. In fact, I am already thinking about future upgrades, and the N5 case is at the top of my list.
reviews.author: Jay

reviews.title: Fantastic case. Horrible fans!
reviews.comment: Bought this to build a NAS running Unraid since an 8 bay NAS from Synology was far more expensive than just building my own. It is a small for factor case so if you're not used to building in ITX cases it can be a bit cramped, but more than doable. The manual isn't very helpful when installing the PSU so pay attention to how and when you route the power cable. The only downside of this case I have found are the stock fans. They are super loud so if you have this case on your desk, or in an area in your house you'll hear the fans all the time. The stock fans are 100mm according to Jonsbo. I was able to replace them with a pair of Noctua 92mm fans. They mount just fine and the included fan grills work as well. Using the low noise adapters that come with the Noctua fans they are barely audible. Chances are your HDDs are louder. Max temps I see on the drives are never past 28c, which is ideal! Love this case and as of now if really seems to be best and smallest form factor case that also supports 8 HDDs AND a spot for an SSD cache. Loving the setup and my wallet is happy I went this route instead of the Synology setup I was looking at.
reviews.author: Ryan Tarbutton

reviews.title: Great SFF NAS Case
reviews.comment: Finding a SFF case for a DIY NAS isn’t as easy as I thought it’d be when I decided to build my own instead of buying something like a Synology. There are really only a few options and this one was by far the most aesthetic, in my opinion. That said, it took way more planning than any build I’ve attempted in the past. ITX is not ideal for large storage options due to limited SATA ports as well as a single PCI-E slot on the vast majority of ITX motherboards. Because of this, you really need to plan your build around your priorities and be willing to make some sacrifices. For example, I had to really hunt for a motherboard that had onboard 10GBE as well as enough SATA ports for 8 drives to run at full capacity without sacrificing the NVME or PCI-E slots. I found exactly 1 lol. Regardless,  once you do nail down your plans, this is a great case that allows you to slam a decently sized GPU and CPU cooler in it without too much hassle (RTX 3050 and Noctua NH-U9S is what I’m running with room to spare). That said, I’m knocking a star off for 2 reasons: 1) I *hate* the rubber handles on the HDD drives. They’re sloppy and loose and make it an absolute chore to get your drives out 2) The PSU you can use is very restrictive. I went with a Corsair SF750 only after realizing the SF850 (which is cheaper and more readily available) was a few mm too long. This is because it’s mounted very oddly in the case that forces you to run an extension cable out the back rather than plugging in directly to the PSU. Consequently, this means you can’t access the power switch directly when the case is buttoned up. It’s pretty annoying when first building and testing but not as bad once you’re ready to set it and forget it. All and all I do recommend this to anyone looking for a good looking SFF NAS. Just be ready for its quirks.
reviews.author: Will & Marianne

reviews.title: surprisingly well built for what is at least for me a thus far unknown brand
reviews.comment: I'm slightly obsessed with this odd case... I was in the market for many years for a storage dense atx or matx or itx case, I was actually very much trying to find a well build older atx case like an antec that had the old school front hdd mount stack that was commen befor we all went and becase obsessed with putting radiators everywhere and started building graphics cards that are longer than some of our more commen mid tower are long lol, but I apparently have zero luck when it comes to realizing what I need befor there is already a wide demand and I could find an nice antec or equivalent used atx case on the market even as a antiquated full or partial build or I could find any that were appropriately showing the inside of the case, and I'd been eye balling this jonsbo for a while, basicly since it became avalible on Amazon, and yes I had held off for a while because the price, I just assumed it was ur typical pressed sheet metal cheap build that couldn't be water cooled and couldn't bairly be air cooled but has 8x 3.5in bays so we haf to charge and arm an a leg for it... and to be fair to the target market here yes that is what this is so expensive, just go look around at the options and youl see what I'm saying... BUT no this is not just cheap stamped metal it is thick aluminum, I'm sure it's still mostly press formed but wow is it well built, these guys have put together a very compelling product here and knowing what I know now I actually realy love the price for what you get here... just to maybe prove how not full of it I am, I just picked up another one of these just cuz lol, the first one was built out as a very odd build becase I'm insane lol, I put in a am4 asrock pro b550 with a ryzen 7 5700x3d(had a 3600 in it as a temp waiting for this cheaper 5800x3d that was announced last year) and 32gb of ddr4 at 3800mhz and a 4tb m.2 pcie 4.0 nvme ssd for file caching and a simple 500gb sata ssd for the linux install and I put in a dual m.2 pcie 4.0 risser that also passes threw 8x pcie 4.0 lanes to a physical 16x slot and turns a full hight pcie slot into a half height slot(the mounting screws point need to be modified to make this work tho as I found out here, I had no idea after 20years of experience on custem consumer and commercial systems building and servicing that the screw point for the low profile bracket is actualy located on the opposite side as it is on the taller bracket, lol, I can see how I missed that, as why tf would anyone "need" to put a low profile bracket into a full hight slot...) and in that now half hight pcie 4.0 8lane slot I have a low profile rtx 4060 8gb card from gigabyte and on the 2 m.2 slots I have one populated with a m.2 marvel AQC107 10GBps ethernet adapter that works amazingly and in the other slot I haf a m.2 to 6x sata ports adapter to supplement the 4 ports I have on this motherboard, what I did is take 4 of these ports to 4 of my 16tb segate exos helium filled enterprise HDDs and 4 of the ports on this m.2 adapter to the other 4 same drives becase I wanted to build out a array and give myself the best chance of "load balancing" across controler, yes it works fantasticly and the other 2 sata ports on the m.2 are occupied by a esata to sata i/o adapter so I can easly plug in esata devices as needed and the other is used for my target operating system drive, I needed to be able to use pcie bifurcation 8x4x4 and with this board and core I can easly do that, and when  that setting isn't set I don't get a booting system so it's kind of self incriminating when it dosnt eventually present itself to the network after remote power up, no kvm necessary lol, I also put in a 850watt true sfx(you can't use sfxl in this case, like I belive you can with the 5bay version, trust me u tried) that systems works so well, I also absolutely do not want my hdd bay fans running at 12v full speed all the time so I paired them with an adapter and ran the non pwm fans to a motherboard fan header so I can controle those via linux depending on the reported temperature of the hdds, and I also added in 2 80mm high quality pwm fans for exhaust and also tucked in another small pwm fan over the m.2 10GB nic to keep it cool,  this system works so well I'm absolutely gitty lol, it's not even that powerfull compared to any of my large water cooled gaming rigs BUT I can remote into this "server" from a cheap quad core celeron based few watt mini pc that I also put 10gb nit into and BOOM I'm looking at an aggressively competive linux gaming system without any of noise or heat anywhere near me lol, I build a nice "poor man's swith" into a cheap hp usf system with a quad port 10GBps ethernet adapter also from the marvel product line, I belive its a new in box dell nic I got of ebay for way to cheap and works good enough that I went a purchased another from the seller becase they work much better than all the x540-t2 or t4 or even tbe newer x550 nic iv been testing over the last couple months, and then I was thinking... "I like this case so much, I also have another 8x 8tb HDDs from seagate(I think the are terrascale drives that run fantasticlyrics fast compared to other budget white label drives from them) I also now have a spare cheap sfx non modular psu on hand and I have this spare b450 asrock fatality board that I just pulled from another itx 4bay server that was also equipped with 32gb of ddr4 and has a ryzen 7 4750GE 35watt chip and low profile cooler, and I can get another of those m.2 rissers(why thay are so cheap is beyond me, I only paid $17 each for these for 2 of them now) and the 6ports sata m.2 adapter was only about $30 seriously... so ya I'm going to build another system in this case that is a bit less crazy that will focus on low power consumption and always on functions and will replace or supplement my cheap poor man's 10Gig switch and will also have a substantial amount of local storage but just the basic Vega graphics of that core which is fine becase I will probably run alpine on this "swich/archival target" with only local ssh access and no remote desktop and I will be tuning down everything except the nics to be low power with he help of underclocking and spinning down drives and tunning down fsns... ya I think iv made my point... lol... it's a solid case option, perfect for the homelab or nas, iv also had a flood of my enterprise clients requesting I build them a storage solution in this case so I will likely be aqureing a substantial percentage of the supply of these and who knows how long this maybe limited product will be on the market so if you catch it on sale for the $200 or less regular price point shaped just get it, you wount like how challenging it is to build a complex system in but you will feel away once your done and admiring your wierd acsentric pc lol
reviews.author: theking8713

reviews.title: Nice compact case.
reviews.comment: Nice case with adaquate space for a basic PC build. WHile I didnt install a graphics card on this build it does appear that there is room for one.
reviews.author: R. Mcaleer

reviews.title: Adorable Little Case
reviews.comment: This adorable little case ate up my entire mATX system into less than 20 liters. That is less than half the size of my last case! For the price (both of the case and the cheaper mATX standard), it cannot be beat. It can be a little bit complicated to work in, but you only have to do it once and then you're good. My main concern when purchasing this case was temperatures. I did not want a loud computer, and I did not want an overheating computer. I am pleased to say that the case can handle my Ryzen 5700x and RX 580 just fine; the loudest part of the computer is my graphics card fans, and they are not disruptively loud. I found that the best configuration was to have the fan on the bottom and front of the case blow air into the case, while the top fan would blow air out. A couple of things to keep in mind to make your life easier: - I used and recommend using slim 120mm fans on all three sides. It made everything so much easier. I personally used Arctik P12 Slims and have been very satisfied. - I also used fan grills on each of the fans, though they ended up being mostly useless. You may or may not find them helpful. They're cheap enough that I would recommend them either way. - The side panels are all held on with plastic pins. I thought that these pins would not hold the panels on all that well, but it seems to be holding up fine. - I would not use an ATX power supply where the cables cannot be removed. There's just enough room for the motherboard, CPU, and GPU cables, nothing more. - Similarly, I would not recommend this case if you want to use a sata drive. I would only recommend m.2 drives. - My build with the mATX board and two fan graphics card did not allow enough space for the front connectors, so I have no USB in the front, only the power button. I was half expecting this, and the case is so small that it's easy to reach around back and use the rear connectors, but it is something to keep in mind. A one-fan graphics card should have no issue fitting the connectors. - An ATX power supply will only fit into the case with the fan pointing outwards (you cannot point the fan towards the CPU.)
reviews.author: Nathan P.

reviews.title: Nearly Perfect - Cheap Fix
reviews.comment: Almost perfect. I’ve not bought a new case to build with for over 10yrs. I built my 7yo son a budget gaming PC with it. The fact the panels all come off with no tools is great. It’s a good balance of space inside vs total case size, moveable mounting brackets are great, it’s mesh so you can put your fans wherever you’d like, and it feels solid in spite of the panels having no screws holding them on. It also fits a full size PSU, which is cool and the source of my single complaint. In a normal size case and the ITX cases I’ve used before the PSU doubles as a default exhaust fan for the system. This is a very efficient setup. So KISS good that it annoyed me when PSUs started to be put on the bottom of lots of cases. This PSU setup manages to be even worse than that. It’s directly “above” the CPU. In an effort to let the CPU fan still do its job of pulling air down they flipped the intake for the PSU to outside the case. This completely removes the PSU from the case’s airflow. It’s wasteful design which I fixed by flipping the PSU the correct way and using a piece of cardboard to separate the CPU fan’s flow from the PSU fan’s. Overall I’m happy, but it’s a little weird that they created a problem that didn’t need to exist with really no upside.
reviews.author: Joshua

reviews.title: Great fun build, wish it had better cable management.
reviews.comment: The Build Experience: This case is a straightforward, high-quality option that does exactly what it’s supposed to do. It feels very sturdy—the frame isn't wobbly or weak at all. I know some reviews mentioned the plastic snap pieces for the mesh panels failing, but I’ve popped mine on and off 30–40 times while wrestling with cables and haven't had a single issue. Layout & Customization: While it’s a compact mATX/ITX space, it offers decent customization. However, cable management is the one area where it falls a bit short. There aren't many channels or tie-off anchors (or I missed them), so be prepared to get creative. Airflow & Cooling: The mesh panels are great for constant airflow, though they can disrupt "channeled" air paths. To compensate, I managed to snugly fit 5 fans for a "bottom-to-top" and "front-to-back" flow: Bottom/Top: Two 140mm fans (Intake/Exhaust). 3rd picture is from top down. Front: Two 120mm fans (one for the GPU, one feeding the CPU cooler). CPU: One 90mm fan. Pro-Tips for New Builders: PSU Choice: Use an SFX/SFF PSU if possible, ideally fully modular. Since the PSU sits directly over the CPU, a smaller unit is a lifesaver for airflow. PSU Orientation: Face the PSU fan outward, away from the CPU. If your PSU has a mesh frame, it can actually act as an additional exhaust. The build: Mobo: ASRock B365M Phantom Gaming 4 CPU: i7 9700 GPU: 9060XT 32GB DDR4 Cooler: Thermalright AXP-90 X53 Black Low Profile CPU Air Cooler Swapped the stock fan with a Noctua NF-B9 redux-1600 PWM CPU temps around 68C during cyberpunk 2077 1440p ultra GPU sits around 72C Verdict: Excellent value for the money. If you already have your components ready, this makes for a fantastic "stealth" build or a dedicated Steam machine. I'm very happy with this purchase!
reviews.author: Major Bizzell III

reviews.title: Minimalist Case
