reviews.comment: I got this case to cut down my gaming time and clutter. My bequiet500 I believe was just to big and bulky for my room and moving my pc got to much of a hassle to lug around. I opted for the C6 mesh case after catching the SFF Case bug watching SFF builds. Realizing I have a Asus tough Matx board I bought this. It works well with a full size Psu which I am currently running the RM750 by Corsair. Its a bit tight on the fans so Opt for Slim Fans it will make your life a lot easier that way. I plan on making that change in the future. Also go for custom short cables will save you in the long run. It can get a bit messy with cable management.  Overall satisfied with the just the appealing of it being so small. However Jonsbo if your listening. You should of made the bottom detachable like the rest of the case. So you could access the fan on the bottom easier then taking screws out and the mesh feels a little cheap. Thats my only complaint.
reviews.author: L

reviews.title: Perfect Small factor NAS
reviews.comment: This is the best small factor NAS case there is. I tried a few and this is leagues above the others. Build quality is great, almost all brushed metal construction. Style is timeless. Easy access to hot-swap drive bays. Good separation of mobo and drives. Good airflow. Easy to build. And takes a tiny amount of space. The only things that would make it even better are: 1 - A better built-in fan for the drives, I swapped it for a silent arctic cooling one. 2 - Slightly better layout that may allow for more space between the drives and fan, and perhaps the PSU. But this might come at the expense of the small size.
reviews.author: Zergbit

reviews.title: Sick mITX NAS Case!
reviews.comment: Great little case! Just put it together and it was really simple. Has instructions on cable management and fit everything I needed in it. Time will tell if the hotplate holds up but so far so good. The fan it comes with is pretty loud since the plate runs it at full speed, but I’m going to replace it with a 15mm Noctua with the quiet cable. If you’re going to have this on your desk, I’ll plug the fan it comes with into the motherboard instead for PWM control. Tip: Enable Hot Plug in PCH Storage Configuration, BIOS!
reviews.author: Cody

reviews.title: Nice case, good cable routing, noisy fan
reviews.comment: Overall I like this case except for the noisy, slightly non-standard fan. Pros: - For a small case it has very good support for neat cable routing. - Most of the case is assembled with small screws so you can easily partially disassemble it to help route cables in best positions. - The power supply can be mounted with the fan facing either the louvers on the case side or inward toward the case interior. This is handy at least in my case where the power supply fan was the noisiest fan (after replacing the case fan) and orienting so it faced the interior of the case made it much quieter. Cons: - The case fan is very noisy for a case that is obviously designed to be attractive and used in an occupied room or office. And while it is a 120mm fan, it is only 15mm thick instead of the normal 25mm of standard PC case fans. This limits the options for quieter replacements. I did replace it with a Noctua fan the same size but it runs at a higher speed than their really quiet case fans and is therefor somewhat noisier. It would have been nice if they had made the case a minor 10mm deeper so it fit a standard fan. As it is, there is not enough clearance with the cables to allow a 25mm fan to fit. - A minor annoyance is that the front panel board has both USB-A and USB-C 3.0 connectors, but it seems that most low power motherboards that would likely be used in a NAS system do not have a compatible USB-C motherboard connector (some don't even have a USB-A 3.0 connector) and the heavy cables from these are difficult to route, especially hiding an unused one. Fortunately, the connectors for these are easily removed from the front panel board with two small screws each if they are not needed. As I said, a pretty nice case overall. The hot plug drives seem to fit and seat quite nicely.
reviews.author: Chris S.

reviews.title: Can't get much better for a compact, stealth NAS.
reviews.comment: I don't have a lot of space in my apartment, so this NAS sits less than 2 feet from my head as I work at my desk. ITX form factor with the compute on top and the drive storage below means that it fits in your average ikea shelving unit made to fit those cloth storage bins. Cooling seems sufficient, I can easily feel the air from the back fan flow out the front of the case. I did replace the stock fan with a Noctua one, using a 3D printed bracket to mount the thicker Noctua to the back of the case. Nose level was pretty good with the stock fan, and with a Noctua case fan and CPU cooler this thing is near silent. Build quality is very great, nice finish to the metal, hardware is tucked away so it's there when I need to get into the case, and access is quick with the two screws on either side of the lid. Getting cables under the motherboard once it's screwed down is near impossible, so you want to do all your SATA power cable routing before lowering the motherboard into place, but I'm pretty sure they mention this in the instructions. As an added bonus, there's just enough space around the ventilation at the front of the case to do a bit of sticker-bombing.
reviews.author: Alex

reviews.title: Great little case for home NAS
reviews.comment: Used this for a TrueNAS home install.  Great case, easy to setup.  If I ever need to go to the basement where the server equipment is, it looks great (lol).
reviews.author: nicka

reviews.title: Great for a TV PC setup!
reviews.comment: I’ve been curious about this case for a while and decided to order it. It is such a neat little case! It is very small, smaller than I expected. I like small cases though so I’m happy with it. This would be perfect for someone who wants a small PC for a TV or need the spare room a standard micro atx case would take. It seems to be decently built. I didn’t realize it came with an 80mm fan for the rear exhaust - nice touch. You can actually mount a 92mm fan for the exhaust if you’d like. It’s drilled out and everything already, as well a 120mm fan in the front for intake. You could probably fit two up front somehow with some thought. I haven’t built in it yet, but the cable management is going to be a mess - it’s expected with a case like this. Nowhere to really hide the cables away like a standard tower. Even so, it could end up being a very clean build. Overall, this is a great case for the price. Small, compact, decent quality materials, great price. Would definitely recommend.
reviews.author: Isaac

reviews.title: Compact, quality, good value
reviews.comment: A very compact mATX case, cable management can be a bit of a struggle, but the overall look and size is nice once completed.  Build quality seems good for the price, all metal panels.  I was able to install an additional 80mm and 120mm fan in the front, mounted with zip ties.  I am running a Ryzen 1700x with the Wraith Prism cooler, and an RX570 (MSI Armor OC).  Temps are acceptable, even with fan curves that keep everything fairly quiet. The temps aren't quite as good as the same system when in a full ATX tower, but nothing is close to thermal limit throttling.  When running a Cinebench R23 and FurMark at the same time, I am getting ~71C on the CPU and ~65C on the GPU while installed in the Cubix case. It can only hold GPUs on the smaller side of things, a single fan or small double fan card are the limit.  For the CPU cooler, a downdraft style fits fine, but I am considering the ThermalRight Assassin mini as that is just within the case's limitation of 137mm for the cooler. 5 stars for value. The challenge of building in smaller cases is not unique to this one, so no deduction.  Included cable ties are a good thought and well executed at this price point.
reviews.author: Chupacabra1

reviews.title: Works well
reviews.comment: Not really for beginners, although it appears that way. Cable management will require some planning if you care about that kinda thing, but overall its a good case. QC could use a bit of attention, one panel was warped causing it to pop in/out when I pick it up.
reviews.author: Peter

reviews.title: Effective, cheap and easy to build. Good option for a simple machine.
reviews.comment: Cheap and functional, basic and nice looking. It is very affordable but easy to build in and has great airflow for a mid-tier system. This is a great compromise on space, price, cooling, and looks if you want a very simple machine.
reviews.author: VisibleMonkeyShakes

reviews.title: Small footprint.  Can be placed on its side for horizontal use
reviews.comment: Decent small micro atx case.  I have a AM4 motherboard with apu, with a  PCIe Gen3 NVMe 1TB SSD with no video card or other peripherals except a monitor. So only 2 cables from regular sized modular power supply needed. Cable management not great but works.  I wouldn’t recommend this with a video card , but with a simple setup like mine it works great.
reviews.author: Robert Halstead

reviews.title: Excellent quality case - good for a starter build
reviews.comment:
I was extremely lucky to stumble upon this case while looking for a Mini-ITX. It's made of durable, good quality metal that's heavy (but not too heavy), small with a lot of room, and extremely versatile (just about every panel of this thing comes off without any tools - just need a screwdriver for the top and bottom panels). It's pretty much perfect for both experts and first-time builders who want a smaller compact PC.
This was my very first time building my own PC, and despite it being inside such a small case, the NR200 made it extremely easy to install. There are tons of places for cable management ties with unlimited potentional for different layouts. The case also has so much airflow that it cools the case extremely well. You also can't beat the price either - it's comparable to a Ncase M1 (but slightly bigger) while being less than half the cost.
There are only a couple issues that I ran into:
- The backside of the case does not have a lot of room to run cables. Not a deal breaker (it was still very doable) but you'll need to strap down the cables on the backside as well in order to get the panel to shut. If it had just another half inch it would be perfect.
- There are many mixed answers on this, but the version without the riser does NOT come with a glass side panel (or at least mine didn't). If you want a see-through side panel, you'll have to opt for the PCI riser version.
Overall I'm extremely happy with this case, it made my first build in a Mini-ITX case very easy. My PC runs very cool and there's lots of room for expansion once the 20 & 30 series cards drop in price again.
My build:
- AMD Ryzen 5 3600
- GeForce GTX 1050 Ti 4GB
- Team T-Force Vulcan TUF 16GB 3200MHz
- 512GB M.2 NVMe Boot Drive w/ 2 500GB 2.5 SSDs
- Gigabyte B550I Aorus Pro AX MOBO
- Corsair SF 450 Watt PSU
- 3 x 120mm PWM Fans
reviews.author: Ty Eslick

reviews.title: Not the tiniest sff case but maybe the easiest to build in.
reviews.comment:
The TLDR is that this case is great.  I bought another to build a new work computer, and both cases are keeping cool. I did replace the fans with Scythe 140mm fans on the radiator and 120mm slim fans for the bottom on both my home and work builds since both are similar enough.
It's been a while since I built a computer and kind of set it and forgot about it.  I've dusted out the home machine once since I got that one.  Otherwise my only gripe was the paint on the original case but again, that literally buffed out.  The second case didn't even have much in the way of spots on the paint or anything.
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Original review below:
I had an original nr200 that I moved an old itx build into about a year ago and loved it.  I honestly wish I had kept it instead of selling and keeping my atx build.  But I probably wouldn't have gone with this then. So, it's a win. After waiting 7+ months for this case, between seeing it in reviews and not knowing where to get it until it hit Amazon/Newegg, I'd say it was worth the wait.
This comes with two minor caveats, for me at least, that I can't imagine many people have run into.
I got my *first* delivery and was missing the riser cable and one of the pcie power cables.  The box looked unopened so I'll say it was a packing issue from the factory.  I did try to just go through the order page to exchange it but was only given the option to return.  I'd imagine this is due to the cost of the item as a whole.  A call with an Amazon rep got this turned into an exchange.
The second little gripe I have is with the paint.  On the first and second item, the paint looked a little weird.  Not really scuffs but I had to take a little polish to the panels to clean them up.  Not a big deal, but if someone is paying close to or over 450 for this great package, and technically for a specific color, I would think the qc on the paint would be a better.
I popped an x570i Strix board with my 5900x and Strix 3080.  Everything fit like a glove.  The cooler does have a little whine in the pump but I keep the machine of to the side and have a fan on most of the time so it's not audible.  I did change the top fans out though for the Silverstone Penatrator ARGB fans to get a little more flair but the stock fans were more than capable of get the hot air through the radiator.  I matched these up with their 120mm Slimmer fans.
If you don't already have a computer built or want to downsize from an ATX build like my situation, this is the way to go.  Be weary that the psu comes with 2x PCIE power cables that have 2 plugs daisy chained each.  I don't really see this as a problem but I know there are disadvantages to this according to the internet pc building gods.  I had a custom cable made anyway to add a third and there are plenty of people on etsy that can provide such a product or a full set of cables if needed. I paired this with a set of those 90 degree adapters too so it looks extra clean.
I think if Coolermaster sold this version of the case, without the psu, cooler, riser, etc, for the same price as the normal nr200, I think they'd still sell a ton.  Great case overall, probably never going mid/full size build again because of it.
reviews.author: j

reviews.title: Beautiful Case With a Classic Wood Design and Great Functionality
reviews.comment: I used this case for my custom PC build and I absolutely love it. What originally drew me to it was the design. The wood front immediately reminded me of my dad’s old stereo cabinet, and that warm brown wood detail gives the case a very clean and classic look that stands out from typical gaming cases. Beyond the looks, the build experience was excellent. I was able to fit an AIO cooler and a full sized graphics card with no issues at all. There was plenty of room to work in, and everything felt well thought out during installation. The case also has a lot of great features that make building and maintaining a system easier. Airflow is solid, cable management is straightforward, and the overall construction feels sturdy and high quality. It manages to look stylish without sacrificing performance or practicality. If you want a case that combines modern PC functionality with a timeless design, this one is an excellent choice. It looks great in a room and performs just as well as it looks.
reviews.author: Jakari Jones

reviews.title: ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ This Case Made My First PC Build Feel Like a Premium Showcase
reviews.comment: I honestly couldn’t have picked a better case for my first PC build. The Fractal North is technically a mid-tower, but once you start building in it, it feels incredibly spacious. There’s plenty of room for a full-size GPU, large air cooler, and clean airflow paths without ever feeling cramped or awkward. Everything fits exactly how you want it to. The design is what initially sold me—and it looks even better in person. The modern, minimalist aesthetic paired with the real wood slat front panel is stunning. It’s understated, mature, and premium without screaming “gaming PC.” This is a case you’re proud to display, not hide under a desk. Cable management is excellent. The layout, tie-down points, and space behind the motherboard tray make it easy to get a clean, professional look—even for a first-time builder. You can see from my build how well everything routes and disappears. On top of that, it’s incredibly easy to maintain: dust filters are accessible, panels come off smoothly, and cleaning doesn’t feel like a chore. Airflow has been fantastic. I’m running a full-size GPU and a large dual-fan air cooler, and temps stay consistently solid. I liked the case so much that I even designed and 3D-printed a custom bottom piece to improve GPU airflow while hiding cables—and the case handled that customization beautifully. It invites creativity. I’ve owned this case since August 2025, and it’s been rock solid long-term. No rattles, no flex, no regrets. This was my first PC build, but it absolutely won’t be my last—and I can confidently say it won’t be the last time I choose Fractal for a case. If you care about design, airflow, build quality, and actually enjoying the build process, this case is an easy recommendation. Fractal nailed it. 🔥
reviews.author: Luke McKinnon

reviews.title: A premium quality case with great features and lots of room.
reviews.comment: I needed a good size case with lots of room for a work machine running a I-9 Core 285k with a Nvidia 5070ti. This case is very roomy and is very easy to use without cutting your hands up. The airflow is excellent with my temps well within expected ranges. It isn't cheap but you get what you pay for. Everything feels solidly built and very premium. While it wasn't a big consideration for me, if you like a mid century modern design, this case has a beautiful look that appears like a piece of fine furniture.
reviews.author: sonik

reviews.title: Beauty meets brains, with just enough brawn
reviews.comment: I have built in many cases and the North still feels special. The genuine walnut slats on the front, the dark tinted tempered glass, and the brushed accents give it a furniture grade vibe that actually looks at home in a living room or studio. Airflow is strong for a design first chassis, cable management is painless, and the build quality is exactly what you expect from Fractal. It is solid, thoughtful, and quiet. I did squeeze an ASUS ROG Astral RTX 5090 in here. It fits but it is right at the envelope. If you are running a 360 mm front radiator or an especially long or thick 5090, expect careful measuring and some compromises. The fact that it can be done in a compact mid tower with real wood aesthetics is impressive. What I loved - Stunning design that does not scream gamer. Real walnut front, dark tinted glass, clean lines - Excellent airflow for the size. Open front plus fine mesh, two 140 mm Aspect PWM fans included - Easy build experience. Removable panels, smart cable routing, captive screws where it matters - Modern I O. Front USB C Gen 2x2 alongside dual USB A and audio - Versatile cooling. Up to 360 mm front radiator, 240 mm top with RAM clearance to check, 120 mm rear - Respectable GPU support for a mid tower. Up to 355 mm with front fans with careful planning for big 4000 and 5000 series cards - Quiet out of the box. Sensible fan tuning and airflow path keep noise restrained What could be better - Tight for ultra flagship GPUs. 5090 class cards fit but it is a squeeze. Front AIOs reduce clearance further - Limited PSU and HDD space combo. Long PSUs with dual HDD trays can get cramped - Top radiator RAM clearance. Tall RAM and thick top radiators can clash. Measure before you commit - No fan hub in the TG version. The Mesh variant typically fares better here. Plan motherboard headers accordingly - Glass version has fewer total fan mounts than the Mesh. If maximum airflow is your priority then consider the Mesh side panel Build notes and tips if you are pushing big GPUs - Measure twice and mount once. The case supports GPUs up to around 355 mm with front fans installed. If you add a 360 mm front radiator the effective GPU length drops noticeably. Look up your specific GPU length and cooler thickness before buying - Consider air cooling or a top mounted 240 mm AIO if you are using a very long GPU. This preserves front clearance - Keep PSU length modest if you need both HDD trays installed. Shorter PSUs make cabling and airflow easier - Use low profile or standard height RAM if you plan a top radiator to avoid clearance headaches Verdict The North Charcoal Black TG Dark blends premium and timeless design with competent thermals and a smooth build experience. If you want a PC that looks as good as it runs and you are willing to plan your component sizes it is fantastic. For maximal airflow or the absolute largest GPUs without compromises the Mesh version or the larger North XL are worth a look. As a tasteful and compact mid tower that can still handle a powerful build the North is a winner.
reviews.author: showmestuff

reviews.title: A great looking case that also cools well.
reviews.comment: I've been a Fractal Design fan for many years.  This one caught my eye when it was released.  I like the wood slats on the front.  They make it look more luxurious.  It has typical Fractal build quality.  That is to say it is excellent.  Building the system is easy.  Components fit exactly as they should.  Fractal's approach for air filters works well.  They are easy to clean.  I generally just run water over them in the sink and then dry them off.  The whole system is reasonably quiet.  Cable routing works well.  I've never been great at making the cables look professional but with this, it still looks good.  There are convenient Velcro strips to help. I do have three suggestions: - There should be a DIN plug for connecting all the front panel connections. - I miss having an LED to indicate drive activity. - They should make more of this model with a solid side panel.  I would prefer that over the glass side panel.  I don't really need to see inside the machine but would prefer the increased sound isolation an insulated, solid panel could provide.
reviews.author: Darrin J. Fangman

reviews.title: Superb design and quality
reviews.comment: This is a beautiful case in all white.  The is more than enough room for just about anything you want to put in there.  Even with a vertically mounted 5070 ti, there is a lot of extra space left over, giving the final result a nice open feel.  That said, it's a large case - make sure you have room for it at close to 13" deep.  There a several things that made this the easiest build I have done.  Aside from the interior size, the dual chambered design makes cabling easy and keeps the front side clean-looking.  Additionally, every bracket, screw hole and snap connection matched up perfectly with overall fit and finish being near-perfect.  I have six intake fans and four exhaust fans, including the AIO cooler for plenty of airflow, though on the down side, the slatted exterior covers probably restrict the airflow to some extent.  One other concern is that it will be a tight fit to get even one low-profile pci card in along with the gpu and pci riser.  Not an issue right now, but possibly in the future.  The case does not come with any fans, though given the range of fan choices and options, included fans probably be not what the user wants anyway.  The case is not inexpensive, but I think worth the cost.  It is heavy also, but built very sturdily.
reviews.author: EricAZ

reviews.title: Love this case!
reviews.comment:
I adore this case! Yes, it's definitely a luxury case as it's pricier than others, but this version does have the 2k screen included. The glass is tempered and I didn't have any issues with it cracking or scratching during the pc build. The bottom compartment does fit three fans, just know you need to fit one inside the case before attaching it to the bracket to make them all fit.
As far as the screen goes, it's a beautiful screen, do note, you need to connect it directly to the motherboard for the picture to work and download the software so you can set your picture/widgets. The cables to hook it up are already ran to the back of the case when it arrives, so you'll just need to hook them up to your motherboard and power supply.
The top of the case does have a compartment that lowers if you want to mount fans or your AIO closer to your motherboard.
Do note, this case includes a PCIe riser 4.0 to connect your GPU to your MOB so the GPU sits upright in the case. IF you need a 5.0 connection like I did, you'll need to purchase the 5.0 riser off Hyte's website, at the time I purchased, they were $99 and you can choose which color you'd like.
The case has plenty of places to route your cables for easy cable management as well as preinstalled Velcro in the bottom to hold some of the cables.
The only downside I saw was needing to buy an updated PCIe riser, I wish they would have had that as an upgrade option at purchase, as well as there being two open spots on the back of the side where you mount the GPU etc. I'm assuming its for easier access, but I do worry about the amount of dust etc that allows into the pc, though I'm sure it's great for airflow.
reviews.author: Amazon_Customer

reviews.title: Premium Case with a Built-In Touchscreen – Still One of the Best After 2 Years
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/E15OAZcxEjL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/61kkYUGl7UL._SY256.jpg ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ – One of the Best Cases I’ve Ever Built In
I’ve had the HYTE Y70 Touch Infinite Dual Chamber ATX Case for about two years now, and honestly, it’s one of the best PC cases I’ve ever built in.
First off, the build experience is incredibly smooth. The dual-chamber design gives you tons of room to work with, making cable management clean and stress-free. Everything feels thoughtfully laid out, so even more complex builds come together easily without feeling cramped.
Compatibility and size are a huge plus. This case easily supports larger GPUs, multiple radiators, and high-end components without any issues. Whether you’re running a high-performance gaming setup or a workstation build, there’s more than enough space to work with.
One of the standout features is the built-in touchscreen, which is honestly amazing. It adds a completely different level of customization and functionality—you can display system stats, animations, or anything you want. It’s not just a gimmick, it actually enhances the overall experience and makes the build feel premium.
Installation overall is very straightforward. Panels come off easily, parts line up well, and the modular design helps speed things up. It’s clear this case was designed with builders in mind.
Price-wise, it’s definitely on the higher end, but after using it for two years, I can say it’s absolutely worth it. The quality, features, and overall experience justify the investment.
Pros:
• Extremely easy and enjoyable to build in
• Spacious with excellent compatibility for high-end parts
• Dual-chamber design keeps everything clean and organized
• Built-in touchscreen is a standout feature and works great
• Premium look and feel
Cons:
• Higher price point, but you get what you pay for
Overall, if you’re looking for a high-end case that combines performance, aesthetics, and innovation, this is a top-tier choice.
reviews.author: Aaron medina

reviews.title: Amazing case
reviews.comment:
So apparently I've become a Fractal Designs fanboy. Whatever, sue me.
I built my last machine on a Fractal Meshify Compact, and then decided I should upgrade to a Threadripper Pro. The Asus Sage motherboard that I'd settled on is EATX, and the Meshify can't handle that, and this one ostensibly can, so here I am. Alas, I should've read the manual and checked actual numbers... EATX isn't really a standard per se, just something bigger than ATX with the same holes, and that Sage board is bloody huge and about 2mm too wide to fit this case. Drat. So I'm putting the Sage into a full size Torrent and upgrading a friend's computer into the compact one, and passing the Meshify down to someone else. In other words I like this case so much that even though I can't use it myself I won't return it.
So far all of Fractal's cases I've worked with have been really thoughtfully designed and beautifully manufactured. They're an absolute joy to build a system in and I would absolutely recommend them to everyone. Honestly I don't think I'll use another brand again.
Just make sure that if you're using a board larger than regular ATX you double check with the manual to make sure it'll actually fit before you order one. They don't make case stretchers and taking a cutoff wheel to your motherboard probably won't result in a lot of joy.
reviews.author: Some random trucker dude

reviews.title: Really nice case
reviews.comment:
Very nice, high quality case. Switched from a mini-ITX case (NZXT H210) to this for better airflow, and my 3080 is running 7-8 degrees cooler, overall my entire build is significantly quieter. The materials feel of quality, the case frame is metal with plastic outer covers. It shipped fast and arrived with no issues.
My favorite parts about the case are the giant 180mm fans up front that can move air very quietly and the airflow of the case as a whole. All of the intake areas are covered by removable mesh panels to filter the air, and there are plenty of holes in the rear for air to escape. A couple downsides I noticed are the limited room for cable management depending on your PSU cables and the documentation doesn't show how to hook up the ARGB cables, just the PWM cables and the fan power hub. One other thing I wish I knew about the case before buying is that the RGB fans come with Y splitters built into the ARGB cables so you can daisy chain them off of one motherboard ARGB header (no need to buy a separate ARGB splitter cable if your motherboard only has one ARGB header like mine).
reviews.author: JuliaP.

reviews.title: Quality is great
reviews.comment: Absolutely love the look, great quality
reviews.author: Erik Gallo

reviews.title: Great Case
reviews.comment: I love this case outside of the cable management issues. Low noise and strong materials. Fans have great airflow and very clean and professional look. My only complaint is if you are building with rgb in mind or anything with more cables the back tends to push out with the limited space and I'd go with the full size. I'd prefer a solid back of plastic or metal but this still looks great.
reviews.author: Taylor

reviews.title: Fantastic case for rack mounting!
reviews.comment: I got this case to mount horizontally in my server rack. I removed the bottom feet/panel, slid it onto a universal rail set and it fits perfectly! The big front fans provide more than enough airflow and keeps my system quiet. I have it loaded up with a 7800X3D as well as an RX 7900 XTX Nitro+ and everything fits wonderfully.
reviews.author: Mike

reviews.title: Stop thinking about it and buy it
reviews.comment: Lots of space and room for expansion. The quality of the case and ease of getting everything installed were top notch. The air flow is excellent. No complaints.
reviews.author: Jeremy Alford

reviews.title: A great and stylish case
reviews.comment: The case is sleek and very easy to work with. Built in cable management supplies, optional disk drive holders, and tons of space allow this case to be worth the money on functionality alone.
reviews.author: Truman Douglas

reviews.title: This case is GREAT!!!
reviews.comment: Personally, I am all about practicality.  I think things have gone a bit too far with all the extra RGB lights that people put in their cases but to each their own.  I am not bad-mouthing anyone who has that going on for their system, I am just saying some of it is too much for ME. There is only 1 con that bothers me thus far.  The case comes with a stock vertical mount, however, I don't feel comfortable using it as it positions the GPU too close to the glass for my liking.  Other than that I don't have any other real complaints.  Now that we've got that out of the way, let's move on to what I DO like about the case. The practicality of this case is excellent, the functionality is what I have been looking for for quite some time now.  I am upgrading from an NZXT H510 which was a good case too but my major complaint with it was airflow.  In this case, airflow is not an issue as the front panel is open which allows my Corsair H100i Elite LCD to breathe appropriately. The number 1 feature of the Meshify 2 is modularity.  When you take the case apart you have so much room to work with.  The top cover comes off completely which keeps you from having to contort yourself or move the case a bunch of times in order to get the right angle to plug something in that is hard to reach.  It has so many different configurations you can use for your setup.  There are so many different options from the size of the motherboard you choose to use to drive mount locations/configurations and cable management is a breeze.  The 2 USB 3.0 and Type-C connections on the front panel are an added bonus as well. Shout out to Fractal for a job well done, this case is exactly what I was looking for and suits my needs perfectly.
reviews.author: Snap

reviews.title: Good heavy well ventilated
reviews.comment: Great case, lots of room to breathe, but is very large and quiet heavy. Cable management is good.
reviews.author: ALLEN Family

reviews.title: Clean, spacious case with excellent airflow
reviews.comment: This case arrived in perfect condition and was well packaged. All components and accessories were included, and nothing was damaged or missing. The build quality is solid, and the design is clean and minimal. The airflow is excellent thanks to the mesh front, which is exactly what I was looking for. There’s plenty of space inside for an ATX build, and it looks like cable management will be straightforward. Overall, very satisfied with the purchase. Great value for the price and shipped quickly. Would definitely recommend.
reviews.author: Wayne Martin

reviews.title: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Great SSD for External Enclosures — Works Perfectly With My Mac mini M4
reviews.comment: I’m using the Silicon Power UD90 2TB inside a VANGREE 80Gbps NVMe enclosure connected to my Mac mini M4, and it has been rock‑solid. Even though this drive is rated for up to 5,000/4,800 MB/s on PCIe Gen4, real‑world speeds over Thunderbolt4 land right around 3,000 MB/s, which is exactly what you should expect from an external setup. No throttling, no disconnects, and no heat issues so far. Installation was simple, and the drive was immediately recognized by macOS. I formatted it as APFS and have been using it for apps, large files, and video exports without any slowdown. The UD90 runs cooler than many Gen4 drives I’ve tested, which makes it a great match for compact enclosures. For the price, performance, and reliability, this SSD is an excellent choice if you’re planning to use it externally with a Mac mini M4, MacBook, or any Thunderbolt/USB4 device. reviews.title: False Advertising: Not TLC but QLC NAND – Incredibly Slow Performance
reviews.comment: Absolutely, here’s the review rewritten from your perspective, making it clear that you also experienced the slow speeds and recommend staying away from this drive: --- **Avoid This Drive – Slow and Disappointing!** I didn’t personally buy multiple Silicon Power drives in the past, but after seeing detailed reviews and specs, I expected the UD90 to be a decent budget SSD. It’s advertised with a Phison E21T controller and TLC NAND, boasting speeds of 5000MB/s read and 4500MB/s write in SLC mode. On paper, it looked like a solid choice with a 3000TBW rating. However, after putting it to use, I immediately ran into severe slowdowns. Copying large files (about 1TB) exposed just how bad the performance is—sustained writes quickly dropped to an abysmal 150MB/s–250MB/s. Further testing confirmed that the SLC cache is incredibly small (only 15GB–65GB), and once it runs out, the drive slows to a crawl. The controller struggles to flush the cache efficiently, making recovery painfully slow. Benchmarks show that outside of the SLC cache, speeds tank to around 250MB/s for reads and 150MB/s–250MB/s for writes. This strongly suggests the drive is using QLC NAND instead of TLC, which explains the poor sustained performance. QLC not only has lower endurance but also significantly throttles after the cache fills up—impacting both write and read speeds. And for what? To save $10–$20 over a proper TLC drive? Absolutely not worth it. Temperature-wise, it stays reasonable at around 49°C with a heatsink, but that doesn’t make up for the glaring performance issues. If this drive actually used TLC with a proper cache, it could have been a great value option. Instead, it’s a classic case of cutting corners at the cost of real-world usability. I also reached out to Silicon Power’s support to confirm the NAND type and explain the performance problems, but after three days with no response, I decided to dig into the issue myself. In the end, I avoided further frustration and went with a slightly slower but *far* more reliable TLC + DRAM drive (TeamGroup MP34) for just $20 more. If you’re considering this drive—don’t. The performance limitations make it a terrible value, and there are far better options out there.

reviews.title: Realllly fast! Amazing!
reviews.comment:
First off, for someone reading this review that may not be fully aware, do NOT buy this hard drive if you have an older or more cost-efficient motherboard that only has up to PCIe Gen4 capability, as it will not allow you to achieve the manufacturer's target speeds.  This is a PCIE Gen 5 NVMe SSD, which means it is made to pump with the latest PCIe Gen5 technology to maximize throughput.
My Gaming Rig Build: I have an MSI MEG X670E ACE motherboard in a full MSI build prioritized for gaming, with an AMD Ryzen 9 7950X 16-core CPU with all performance cores. I went this route becuase WD Black NVMe SSD's were/are arguably more optomized for performance gaming over the Samsung Pro's, but you cannot go wrong with a Samsung Pro SSD either.
I originally ran (2) WD Black SN850X PCIe Gen4 SSD's in the build, as PCIe Gen5 SSD's were still new at that time, so I wanted to wait until they were more mainstream, tested, and the kinks were worked out. I finally decided to clone my primary boot drive (Using Acronis True Image for Sandisk) and upgrade to this one, and it is literally double the speed.
Using Blackmagic's Disk Speed Test for Comparison w/ 5GB loading:
- WD Black SN850X PCIe Gen4 - 5,200 MB/s Write and 5,250 MB/s Read (Avg. rounded up)
- WD Black SN8100 PCIe Gen 5 - 10,500 MB/s Write and 10,200 MB/s Read (Avg. rounded up)
The results speak for themselves. I would assume that even newer PCIe Gen5 motherboards with the latest CPU's can get more performance out of this drive, but it is literally double the speed of it's fastest predecessor the SN850X. So far, it is stable and zero issues. Thermals also running around 82-degrees Farenheit right now on the SN8100, as my Gen5 SSD slot has a dedicated heat sink and the drive is fully exposed to the open case.

After switching to this Gen5 SSD, load times dropped across the board and games feel much smoother. Microstutters I used to get during intense moments are now completely gone.
If you're gaming on modern hardware and still using Gen3 drives, you're probably not getting the performance you think you are. This SSD is fast, stable, and absolutely worth the upgrade. I posted my benchmark screenshot so others can see the numbers for themselves. Very happy with the purchase.

reviews.title: Good, practical desktop drive
reviews.comment: I gave this drive to someone as a gift, and they've been using it for backups for 10 months without issue. My review is based on another unit of this drive which I bought for myself some months later.  I've been using it as my primary desktop OS/programs drive since 5/29/2014, so it's about 5 months now.  There have been no problems thus far.  It's really quite a bargain for desktop use if 1TB is all you need. The actual capacity of this drive is 931.5GB. That's an old marketing trick which can be blamed for the pointless redefinition of all our real, long established data measurements with those silly "i" characters. I won't dwell on it any further, but 931GB is the true capacity when measured in base 2, as all data is correctly measured. This 1TB Blue drive uses a single 1TB platter spinning at 7200rpm.  There are 2 heads (each side is 500GB). A single platter design is usually better for reliability than having multiple smaller platters, because there are fewer points of failure, the assembly is lighter, the motor doesn't have to work as hard, and less heat is generated. Single platter drives will also tend to be quieter, but due to my configuration I can't judge the noise level. There has been much discussion and testing among users in online forums, including WD's forum, which repeatedly show that the 1TB Blue and 1TB Black perform the same. It appears the only benefit of the 1TB Black is a longer warranty. Some Blacks are faster than this drive, but the 1TB model is not. Compared to a Green, the Blue is faster owing to it's faster rotation speed.  The Green drives also have an "intellipark" feature which causes them to keep parking the heads after a few seconds of inactivity.  This can cause laggy response and extra wear.  I dislike that design - I believe power management functions should be left under the control of the operating system, which can account for user preferences and what is happening in the rest of the system.  Hardcoding this behavior into the drive is ridiculous, in my opinion.  The Blue behaves the way I prefer - it does not use "intellipark", it stays ready to roll until directed otherwise through power management commands from the OS. I wish they were making the Blue series in larger sizes - it seems this 1TB is the end of the line.  I don't care for the Greens and the Blacks are more expensive. Partition/Sector Alignment -------------------------------- Please be aware that like most modern drives, this drive uses 4KB sectors (also known as "advanced format").  If you are using Windows 2003, Windows XP or older, as I am, don't let Windows handle the partitioning of this drive.  This is even an issue on unpatched versions of Vista and Windows 7.  These older versions of Windows will believe that the physical sectors are 512 bytes, when in reality they are 4KB.  As a result, the partition(s) will not be aligned with the physical sectors.  It will still work, but performance will be reduced. Windows Server 2003 and Windows XP and older do not have any update to fix this, but it's not a problem as long as you do the partitioning with a suitable 3rd party utility.  I think Western Digital offers a tool for this, but I've never tried it.  Once the partitions are set, it's fine to let Windows format them. For my Windows XP install, I used a recent version of GParted to partition the drive.  GParted can be downloaded and burned to a bootable CD, or installed to a USB flash drive.  Just use the option to align your partition(s) on 1MB boundaries.  This is the easy way to ensure they are aligned correctly for the best performance.  Then boot your WinXP install disc and let it format the partition that you already created.  It sounds harder than it is, it's a minor hassle but it's simple. If you ever change the partitions, once again use GParted or a similar utility that handles alignment for modern hard disks.  Don't use the built-in XP partitioning.  But again, once the partitions are created, it's fine to let Windows format them. The built-in partitioning is fixed in Windows 8. According to Microsoft, it is fixed in Windows 7 after installing Service Pack 1 - you would need to have that service pack before partitioning the drive, not after. Again according to Microsoft, it is also fixed in Windows Vista *after* installing update MS KB 2553708 - I assume this is automatically installed for people who use automatic updates, but I don't know that for a fact.  This won't do you any good if you're doing a fresh install and your install disc predates the required update. The partition alignment detail I've described above is an issue you will encounter with any recent hard drive, it's not unique to this model.  If you ignore it, performance will be affected but it will still work.  You may see Seagate drives implying that they are immune from this, but in reality, they are not.  All modern "advanced format" drives, of any brand, will perform better if sectors are properly aligned.  But it's not a big deal - just use a modern partitioning utility and then you're set. ---------------------- I just tested this drive using "Roadkil's Disk Speed" on Windows XP 32-bit.  I'll cut out all the variables and just give the linear transfer results with large block sizes.  My drive has a few partitions and there are lots of files on it, so this might affect results. First partition (first 20GB):  170-178MB/sec linear read 3rd partition (physical location range is from 28-628GB):  153-177MB/sec linear read Last 300GB is unpartitioned so I can't test that range. I don't think the random access test is useful, because my partitioning greatly influences the result. There's a test mode for the whole physical disk, but it's results are too inconsistent. This drive is a great bargain if you just need a simple, inexpensive, well performing 7200rpm hard disk.  I was tempted to try a Seagate SSHD, but I couldn't justify the cost compared to this.  If I was shopping today, I'd look carefully at the HGST and Toshiba offerings as well, but from the WD side this is my pick for a general purpose 1TB desktop drive. Update: It is now 11/2015.  This drive is in my desktop PC, used daily, and still works fine. Some months ago I ran a benchmark on this drive using the linux utility "gnome-disks".  The random access performance measured out to a 15.7ms average. This is mediocre, but expected from a quiet drive. Screenshot is attached. It also shows the transfer rate across the disk (read test only, I didn't test writes).

reviews.author: Dmitry

reviews.title: Careful: You Can No Longer Return 1TB Capacity Drives
reviews.comment: I have utilized Western Digital HDDs exclusively for decades. I have only owned another brand (Seagate) when that drive came with my PC; it failed within a year. While it appears the brand is no longer as reliable as it once was (i.e., more reviews with issues than I have ever seen), it is the company I still go with. When I saw a 1TB WD internal drive for the lowest price ever, I did not hesitate to hit the order button. After purchase, I noticed reviews claiming that Amazon does not allow returns on problem drives that arrived with issues and were not the buyer's fault. I confirmed that Amazon does not allow returns on the 1TB WD internal drives (this does not apply to larger capacities yet). It is my first time encountering this, and it is troublesome/worrisome. Why would a company (Amazon) and a brand (Western Digital) suddenly remove the ability to return NEW HDDs shipped and sold by Amazon? It is highly concerning. I am glad the price was so low that if anything goes wrong, I will not have to learn an expensive lesson (I am also happy I did not buy more than one). It is a reminder to check return eligibility before clicking to purchase. Additionally, the drive came in a box unlike any other. It had no bracket devices on each end (which suspends the drive to avoid impact). Although the drive was in a reasonably hard clamshell case and sealed anti-static sleeve, the coverage was a single layer of bubble wrap. I always film the opening of my hard drives, and you can hear the drive sliding around while I pick it up and open the box. It blows my mind that whoever packed it believes having a hard drive with moving parts sliding around is acceptable. Although having HDDs shipped to your front door is convenient (and honestly, there are not many brick-and-mortar stores that sell HDDs left), I am going to have to start buying my HDDs (both internal and external) from another online retailer with better packing methods or from a physical retailer. Data storage devices are too necessary (and costly) to risk buying with no return ability (primarily if it is delivered DOA or with problems that render it unusable) and problematic/little protection shipping boxes. The last external Western Digital drive I received was so banged up that I did not even open it; I immediately initiated a return and replacement (the box was crushed, and you could hear floating pieces inside). And those are still shipped in retail packaging. I will not make the same mistake. I hope Amazon changes its return policy and protects drives better. The convenience and price of delicate products are not enough for me to risk it (especially when the product comes from the official store). I will go elsewhere and spend more if things remain the same. While I ran scans, and the drive works (and there are no sounds of clicks or loudness), I can say I was merely fortunate in that regard. So, I am only deducting one star for the packing method. It is far too risky, and I believe removing one star (for that alone) is fair and more than necessary. I got lucky (so far). After two and a half decades of WD-only drives, it is time to research and take a shot with another, more caring (and, I suppose, reliable) brand. Packing and return policies matter regarding computer components, especially HDDs.

reviews.title: SO MUCH BETTER THAN STOCK!
reviews.comment:
This is a great read speed for a PS5! 6
Here's why your 6527MB/s reading is excellent:
* PS5 Requirements: Sony recommends a minimum sequential read speed of 5,500 MB/s for an M.2 SSD to be compatible and perform well in the PS5. Your drive is well above that requirement.
* Faster than the Internal SSD: The stock internal SSD in the PS5 has a read speed of around 5,500 MB/s. So, your new drive is actually faster than the one that came with the console, which is fantastic.
* Normal for High-End SSDs: Many high-performance M.2 SSDs rated for speeds of 7,000 MB/s or more will often show a slightly lower speed when tested inside the PS5. Your reading of 6527 MB/s is right in the range of what many users see with top-tier drives.
In short, your EDILOCA EN870 is a very good choice and that speed will ensure you have quick loading times and a smooth gaming experience.
Installed quick and easy First disconnect power then just pop the cover off, unscrew the small panel for access, take out circuit board screw and spacer, move spacer to 80 hole under not on top of EN870 board. Slide board in, fasten screw, put ps5 back together, start ps5 and format and make sure to go to storage in settings and set storage place as M.2 SSD STORAGE. Youre ready to go. I've noticed faster speeds and no lag especially on server games like MOD, ESO

Then boot your WinXP install disc and let it format the partition that you already created.  It sounds harder than it is, it's a minor hassle but it's simple. If you ever change the partitions, once again use GParted or a similar utility that handles alignment for modern hard disks.  Don't use the built-in XP partitioning.  But again, once the partitions are created, it's fine to let Windows format them. The built-in partitioning is fixed in Windows 8. According to Microsoft, it is fixed in Windows 7 after installing Service Pack 1 - you would need to have that service pack before partitioning the drive, not after. Again according to Microsoft, it is also fixed in Windows Vista *after* installing update MS KB 2553708 - I assume this is automatically installed for people who use automatic updates, but I don't know that for a fact.  This won't do you any good if you're doing a fresh install and your install disc predates the required update. The partition alignment detail I've described above is an issue you will encounter with any recent hard drive, it's not unique to this model.  If you ignore it, performance will be affected but it will still work.  You may see Seagate drives implying that they are immune from this, but in reality, they are not.  All modern "advanced format" drives, of any brand, will perform better if sectors are properly aligned.  But it's not a big deal - just use a modern partitioning utility and then you're set. ---------------------- I just tested this drive using "Roadkil's Disk Speed" on Windows XP 32-bit.  I'll cut out all the variables and just give the linear transfer results with large block sizes.  My drive has a few partitions and there are lots of files on it, so this might affect results. First partition (first 20GB):  170-178MB/sec linear read 3rd partition (physical location range is from 28-628GB):  153-177MB/sec linear read Last 300GB is unpartitioned so I can't test that range. I don't think the random access test is useful, because my partitioning greatly influences the result. There's a test mode for the whole physical disk, but it's results are too inconsistent. This drive is a great bargain if you just need a simple, inexpensive, well performing 7200rpm hard disk.  I was tempted to try a Seagate SSHD, but I couldn't justify the cost compared to this.  If I was shopping today, I'd look carefully at the HGST and Toshiba offerings as well, but from the WD side this is my pick for a general purpose 1TB desktop drive. Update: It is now 11/2015.  This drive is in my desktop PC, used daily, and still works fine. Some months ago I ran a benchmark on this drive using the linux utility "gnome-disks".  The random access performance measured out to a 15.7ms average. This is mediocre, but expected from a quiet drive. Screenshot is attached. It also shows the transfer rate across the disk (read test only, I didn't test writes).

reviews.title: Careful: You Can No Longer Return 1TB Capacity Drives
reviews.comment: I have utilized Western Digital HDDs exclusively for decades. I have only owned another brand (Seagate) when that drive came with my PC; it failed within a year. While it appears the brand is no longer as reliable as it once was (i.e., more reviews with issues than I have ever seen), it is the company I still go with. When I saw a 1TB WD internal drive for the lowest price ever, I did not hesitate to hit the order button. After purchase, I noticed reviews claiming that Amazon does not allow returns on problem drives that arrived with issues and were not the buyer's fault. I confirmed that Amazon does not allow returns on the 1TB WD internal drives (this does not apply to larger capacities yet). It is my first time encountering this, and it is troublesome/worrisome. Why would a company (Amazon) and a brand (Western Digital) suddenly remove the ability to return NEW HDDs shipped and sold by Amazon? It is highly concerning. I am glad the price was so low that if anything goes wrong, I will not have to learn an expensive lesson (I am also happy I did not buy more than one). It is a reminder to check return eligibility before clicking to purchase. Additionally, the drive came in a box unlike any other. It had no bracket devices on each end (which suspends the drive to avoid impact). Although the drive was in a reasonably hard clamshell case and sealed anti-static sleeve, the coverage was a single layer of bubble wrap. I always film the opening of my hard drives, and you can hear the drive sliding around while I pick it up and open the box. It blows my mind that whoever packed it believes having a hard drive with moving parts sliding around is acceptable. Although having HDDs shipped to your front door is convenient (and honestly, there are not many brick-and-mortar stores that sell HDDs left), I am going to have to start buying my HDDs (both internal and external) from another online retailer with better packing methods or from a physical retailer. Data storage devices are too necessary (and costly) to risk buying with no return ability (primarily if it is delivered DOA or with problems that render it unusable) and problematic/little protection shipping boxes. The last external Western Digital drive I received was so banged up that I did not even open it; I immediately initiated a return and replacement (the box was crushed, and you could hear floating pieces inside). And those are still shipped in retail packaging. I will not make the same mistake. I hope Amazon changes its return policy and protects drives better. The convenience and price of delicate products are not enough for me to risk it (especially when the product comes from the official store). I will go elsewhere and spend more if things remain the same. While I ran scans, and the drive works (and there are no sounds of clicks or loudness), I can say I was merely fortunate in that regard. So, I am only deducting one star for the packing method. It is far too risky, and I believe removing one star (for that alone) is fair and more than necessary. I got lucky (so far). After two and a half decades of WD-only drives, it is time to research and take a shot with another, more caring (and, I suppose, reliable) brand. Packing and return policies matter regarding computer components, especially HDDs.

reviews.title: Firmware update bricked my OTHER SSD?!? Read/write error on entire drive in less than 5 hours use.
reviews.comment: I absolutely DO NOT recommend you buy anything from TeamGroup - definitely not this. I have built literally hundreds of systems. I generally have good luck with everything. I thought this time I would give a chance to a different SSD than Samsung, who I've really had by far the best luck with. I don't think I've seen more than 1 failure ever with Samsung in those systems I've built. So, I got this one. I bought a little SSD heatsink with fan for this one too, since others said it ran hot. I got my PC built, handed off my old one to my partner, installed the OS on a new Samsung 870 EVO I still had in box and just recently found, and used this 2TB drive as a storage drive. I got my drivers installed, Steam installed, and installed literally two games on it. While running one game, it crashed after around an hour and I experienced a very odd "read/write" error to the entire drive. I restarted the PC - that resolved it. I decided I would update the firmware. Holy smokes, my mistake! How dare I do something such as UPDATE THE FIRMWARE?! My reward: It literally bricked my Samsung SSD! The brand new one! Immediately after restart, I noticed it took around 5 minutes to start - and it went to BIOS. I ran a BIOS check on the SSD - all looked good, it passed the test - but then I noticed my BIOS didn't see my Samsung SSD plugged into a SATA port. I restarted - same issue. I restarted again after a hard power clear (unplug power, wait 15 seconds, hold power button for a bit, plug back in) - same issue. I tried a different SATA port - same issue. I tried a different SATA cable - same issue. I tried moving it to my "old" PC - having it plugged in also made it take about 5 minutes to boot! I saw the drive in Disk Management on old PC - showing 0 bytes total - Initializing failed, "This device does not exist." That's a very bad message, I'd rather have had an I/O error there. I tried to boot to the Samsung 870 EVO firmware installation image, but it just can't get to it - the bad drive causes it to fail when loading the Linux kernel. It legitimately bricked my freaking OTHER SSD - I mean, what do I even say? How can you trust a company who makes such bullcrap software?! I have NEVER seen that happen before! I know what I'm doing, and my poor brand new but old SSD got bricked. Unbelievable. Just after I'd gotten everything set up the way I wanted. I am highly disappointed, and furious that this could even happen. I also had the actual read/write error on the drive in less than 5 hours of use - something I've never seen before. Surely a bad sign. I'm returning it, and I suggest you stay far away. If price is an issue - just get a PCIe 4 SSD, instead. It really is fast enough. I'm very sad I wasted time on this drive. Just make sure you’re using a Gen5 M.2 slot, or you’ll be limited to Gen4 speeds. ✅ Final Verdict: A Beast of an SSD If you’re looking for one of the fastest NVMe SSDs on the market, the T-Force GC PRO delivers. reviews.title: Buyer Beware!!!
reviews.comment: I bought what I thought was a retail 14tb IronWolf Pro, seller was GO VIRTUAL IT STORE.  The drive arrived in an Amazon box, inside was the drive in an anti-static bag, no traditional hard drive box, just the drive wrapped in bubble wrap.  I was skeptical right out of the gate but installed the HD in my QNAP NAS. Immediately I noticed it is MUCH louder than my other Seagate drives.  I immediately checked the warranty on the Seagate website and found the drive had no warranty.  I contacted the seller, and they informed me that was correct, there is no manufacturers 5 year warranty, but they offered a 1 year warranty.  I paid near retail price for what I thought was a retail drive.  I am just done buying hard drives on Amazon.  The details need to be clearer on what type of drive you are actually buying, is it retail, OEM, bulk, and more importantly what warranty you are getting.  If I go back to that same listing 2 days after receiving it, the same drive is listed by another seller and the listing details states there is a "3-Year-Manufacturer" warranty which is shenanigans, because the manufacturer offers a 5 year warranty on the IronWolf Pro drives.  Big waste of time and money.

reviews.title: Do not buy this cheaply made hunk of junk!!!
reviews.comment: I am an IT Director for a hospital in Texas. Purchasing PC equipment and knowing whether it's good or not is what a lot of my occupation requires. That being said, I would stay as far away from this drive as I could. I took a chance on it because Dato ram is decent. You can't really get any accurate info on this ssd on the net, so I knew the chanbce I was taking but I knew I could return it also if I didn't like it. The ssd is sharp looking I must say and it's fast, but that means absolutely nothing if it is cheaply made. manufacturers of ten change the components of their products to cheap ones to cut costs and man this is the cheapest, sorriest ssd I think I've ever seen. The pcb is as thin as paper and light as a feather. The only thing that gives it any strength is the heatsink. I pulled the heatsink back to check the controller and nand and it has an older Innogrit controller. Now I'm a big Innogrit 5236 fan. After they fixed it's original issues with firmware updates it has turned out to be a very good gen 4 controller. On par with the Phison E18 controller. But this controller one of the first innogrits that are dramless to come out if I'm not mistaken and I couldn't figure out who made the nand. You would think Micron since Dato is a Micron brand. However these nand flash chips are very thin and must be older nand and I wouldn't doubt they aren't QLC. Not that QLC is all that bad but for the price of this drive, I was shocked. Needless to say, it went back pretty quickly for a full refund. I would stay away from this one!

reviews.title: Solid Modular PSU Handles a Full Build Without Issue
reviews.comment:
The Corsair RM750e has been powering my full system build without any complaints. The setup includes an Intel i7-14700K, ASUS TUF Gaming Z790-Plus WiFi DDR5 motherboard, 32GB of DDR5, an MSI 5060 Ti, an SSD, and two hard drives. The 750W capacity has been more than enough for everything I have thrown at it.
The fully modular design made the build process much cleaner. Only plugging in the cables I actually needed kept the case tidy and improved airflow. The included 12V-2x6 cable is a nice touch for current generation GPUs and saves the hassle of dealing with adapters.
Power delivery has been rock solid. No coil whine, no shutdowns under load, and no weird behavior during boot or sleep cycles. The Cybenetics Gold efficiency rating shows up in practice with the unit running cool and the fan staying quiet during normal use. I rarely notice it running at all.
Build quality feels appropriate for a modern PSU. The casing is sturdy, the cables are flexible enough to route easily, and the connectors seat firmly. The 105°C rated capacitors are a good sign for long term reliability, which matters for a component you want to forget about once installed.
For anyone building a mid to high end system, this is a sensible choice that does not cut corners. Corsair delivered a clean, capable power supply at a reasonable price point.

This is the updated ATX 3.1 / PCIe 5.1 version, so it’s fully ready for the latest hardware without needing messy adapters. The fully modular design allowed me to use only the cables I needed, keeping the build very clean. It’s a reliable, high-efficiency power supply that gives my client peace of mind for their professional work. Great value for a high-quality Corsair unit.

reviews.title: This is the best rated, best in class power-supply on the market
reviews.comment:
This is the best rated, best in class power-supply on the market.  These are basically rebranded Superflower PSU's, pretty much the best made.  It puts out perfect, clean voltage with no noise or out of spec voltages.  Also I run my PC 24/7 so I'm already seeing a savings on my power bill from the platinum rating.
The reason you want a nice power supply is stable, clean power produces a stable, crash-free system.  At worst a cheap power supply will burn your house down, at best a crappy one will cause random and unexpected crashes.  And I won't even get started on the atrocious efficiency ratings of junk PSUs.  In as little as 1 years time you will end up giving the "savings" of a cheap PSU and this to your local power company, I promise you.  And its not a big investment.  My previous PSU lasted me 3 system builds before I upgraded, mostly to go from bronze+80% efficiency to Platinum 98% efficiency.  For the laymen that means this power supply will convert 98% of the energy it consumes into usable DC power for your computer.  That means less heat in your room, and lower power bills.
The fact its 100% modular is even better.

This PSU looks high quality with a non-standard finish (for a PSU) applied to it. I like it myself but I assume it won't fit everyone's tastes or style of build. Comparing to an older low quality (like 1/4 the price) PSU I had around the house, weight was maybe almost half and looking at the parts you could tell the difference in quality.The cables that came with the PSU are much higher quality than I've had with any previous PSU. They are easy to bend and will stay mostly in position on doing so which means doing proper cable management is easy enough. They also are longer than what I have been accustomed to which was a huge plus being I was upgrading my case also (Phanteks Enthoo Evolv ATX Tempered Glass) and it requires some longer than normal routes from PSU.
Fan stays off at low usage, my video card does not turn on fans at low usage, and my CPU cooler does not turn on fans at low usage. This means my computer makes zero noise when I am just browsing the web or watching youtube and netflix. This was a factor in my purchase.

reviews.author: MacBits LLC

reviews.title: Seasonic takes care of you!
reviews.comment:
Excellent! Well worth the investment if you can afford it. The most important component of a pc. Everything else in your system relies on it, so why not protect them the best you can. The warranty is VERY long, so it could be used on multiple pc builds before you need to upgrade (as long they don't keep changing the GPU power cables. Figure it out NVIDIA!).
Seasonic really takes care of you with this PSU. The TX-1300 comes with all the current cables that you will need (including a 12v 2x6). And it comes with a nice PSU tester! I HIGHLY suggest using the tester first, before you get into hooking up any cables to the motherboard. You can even test the PSU without a motherboard. It could save yourself alot time trouble shooting. One GREAT bonus feature of the tester is that it is also a 90 degree adapter for the 24 pin cable. You can leave the tester on and use it permanently (I emailed Seasonic support to confirm). Helps with esthetics and better air flow.
Another feature is that it has auto fan mode if you want it quiet. I have not heard it once yet while gaming, so I leave it in standard mode.
-VERY SMALL cons:
It comes with clear wire combs that I found to difficult to get on to the individual wires. They were very tight, so the wires are difficult to put in. I had to had to stretch them with my teeth (I am not proud about this or recommend). I am still deciding if I like the clear plastic of the combs also. I think I prefer black or white better.
The TX-1300 is long. Make sure you have room in the case. I have the FLUX PRO, which has an option of installing a PSU sideways for better cable access. I was not able to use this feature of the case, due to the PSU length. No big deal.
All and all, this is a excellent PSU. If you want high quality 1300 watts, this is the one to get! No doubt!

reviews.title: Amazing Power Supply for the Price!
reviews.comment:
EVGA is known for making quality products, and the EVGA SuperNova 1300 G+ is no exception!  It's an exceptional performing power supply, especially for the price.  I purchased this from Amazon when it was on sale for $199.99 and now currently own three of these (I bought two directly from EVGA).  For what you're getting at that price, I couldn't be more pleased.
Pros:
- Price
- Fully Modular
- Sleeved Cables
- 10 Year Warranty
- Minimal Coil Whine
- 100% Japanese Capacitors
- Quiet 135mm Fan w/ ECO Mode
- Excellent Performance & Voltage Regulation
- Plenty of Cables for a Variety of Builds & Applications
Cons:
- 4 of the 6 PCIe Cables are Single 8-Pin (6+2)
- As Stated Above, Only Includes Two Dual 8-Pin (6+2) PCIe Cables
- None.  My EVGA 1300w G+ PSU's Have Been Running Flawlessly Under Constant Load
I highly recommend this PSU.  You simply can't go wrong with EVGA.
Note: I read through some of the One-Star Reviews.  My experience with this power supply doesn't at all reflect their claims (PSU exploding, catching fire, destroying PC, etc.).  I can't say that any of those events didn't happen, but I'm usually a bit skeptical when a review ends with "Don't EVER buy EVGA!  Go with X brand(s) instead!"  I've personally owned close to a dozen EVGA power supplies throughout my lifetime.  I've only had to RMA one after it kept powering off after 6-7 years of continuous use, which was an 850w G2 that EVGA discovered was faulty.  They quickly replaced it with an 850w G3.  This was about 2-3 years ago, and there have been no issues since the RMA.
EVGA's Customer Service and RMA process is among the very best in the business.

reviews.title: Decent but overpriced in my opinion as most Form factor parts are.
reviews.comment: The Cooler Master V850 SFX Gold packs a serious punch in a miniature package, but is it the perfect PSU for your mini-ITX build? Let's dive in: Powerhouse in a Pint-Sized Package: 850W of juice makes it suitable for even the most power-hungry builds, from high-end CPUs to RTX 3080s. 80+ Gold efficiency keeps energy waste and your electricity bill in check. Compact SFX form factor fits snugly in mini-ITX cases, leaving room for your other components to shine. Whisper-Quiet Cooling:  (mostly) FDB fan spins silently under normal loads, keeping your rig a tranquil oasis. Even under heavy pressure, noise levels stay surprisingly low, although some users report a noticeable hum. Modular Magic: ✨ Fully modular cables let you ditch the clutter and keep your case looking sleek and tidy. High-quality braided cables are durable and flexible, making installation a breeze. A Few Snags to Consider: Price tag reflects the premium performance and compact size, making it pricier than some non-SFX options. The included SFX-to-ATX bracket might be unnecessary for some mini-ITX cases and adds extra bulk. A couple of user reports mention coil whine under specific workloads, though not a widespread issue. Verdict: The Cooler Master V850 SFX Gold is a top contender for mini-ITX builders seeking top-tier power and quiet operation. Its compact size, high efficiency, and modular cables make it a dream for building clean and cool rigs. However, the premium price tag and potential for minor noise quirks might give budget-conscious or noise-sensitive users pause. In short: Get it if: You want the best power delivery and efficiency for your mini-ITX build, prioritize low noise, and appreciate quality craftsmanship. Skip it if: You're on a tight budget, can tolerate a bit more noise, or don't need the absolute power-house performance for your setup.

So great power supply. Quite. Due to it being modular it's easy to manage cables as you only need the ones you plan to use. Functions as intended, not much to say about that. reviews.title: Great Modular system with room to grow!
reviews.comment: I recently decided to make the leap into the world of AM5 CPUs. Because of this, I needed to upgrade a lot of parts in my PC and one of these things was my PSU. I wanted something that was going to withstand the test of time, have a good warranty, and was efficient with its power usage. After searching far and wide, I decided on this Thermaltake. The Experience: Installing this PSU was very easy. All of the cables come in a convenient reusable bag which makes storage of extra cables a nice compliment to the overall experience. Everything feels premium, and the modular design ensures that unnecessary cable clutter is cut down as much as possible. All cables are labeled, making this an easier experience for newer PC builders. This Unit comes with the 600W 12VHPWR connector, which supports NVIDA's newest card models, and what i believe will be the standard going forward. First off, some Stats: Noise Levels: Cybernetics Standard (40-45 dB[A]) Modular: Fully Operating Temperature (Continuous Full Load): 0 - 47°C Cooling: 135mm Fluid Dynamic Bearing Fan Form Factor: ATX12V v3.0, EPS 2.92 Pros: - 10 year warranty - Great Build Quality - Fully Modular - Over and Under Voltage protection - Short circuit protection - Over Temp protection - Surge protection - Inrush Current Protection - ATX v3.0 compatible - PCIE 5.0 compatible - All cables are 16AWG gauges, great for lower voltage drops at high loads. - Japanese Capacitors - Great Efficiency - Full power operates at 47 degrees C Cons: - Higher fan noise at full load - If you need lots of Legacy PCI connectors, the amount on this system is low. - Large inrush current at 230V Overall: This PSU seems to have most of the bells and whistles that more expensive models have at a lower price.  The build quality of this unit is great and should out live the warranty that they are offering. While there are some downsides to this unit, I feel that the positives far outweigh any negatives that are present. I wanted a unit that I feel safe will protect my investment in my PC, and I feel that this PSU does that and more. I look forward to using this PSU in more builds to come, and I feel confident that it will most likely meet your needs as well.

reviews.title: Compact Beast: Premium SFX Power with Outstanding Reliability and Low Noise
reviews.comment: The Corsair SF1000 (2024) SFX Power Supply shipped incredibly fast and showed up the next day with Prime, which is always a great start. Right out of the box, Corsair’s attention to detail is obvious - excellent packaging and a premium feel throughout. Installation was straightforward, especially with the included SFX-to-ATX bracket, and it fit my L300 case perfectly. Compatibility was spot-on for a compact build, though it’s still smart to double-check cable lengths depending on your setup. Speaking of cables, there are plenty included, they’re nicely sleeved, and they make cable management clean and efficient. Performance-wise, this PSU delivers serious power with rock-solid stability. The 80 Plus Platinum efficiency and 105°C-rated Japanese capacitors translate into excellent reliability, even under heavy loads. The low noise level is another big win - the 92mm PWM fan stays quiet while keeping everything cool. Cybernetics rating this as one of the best SFX PSUs of all time definitely shows here. That said, I’d recommend waiting for deals around the $180 mark with coupons - t’s an absolute no-brainer at that price. Overall, this is a top-tier SFX unit that nails power delivery, reliability, cable management, and ease of installation in a compact form factor.

reviews.title: Received a used unit
reviews.comment: I bought this item brand new, shipped and sold directly from Amazon, so I expected a factory-sealed product. Unfortunately, that wasn’t the case. The PSU I received was clearly used — it had the well-known LPN label on the box, which is usually a dead giveaway. On top of that, the box wasn’t shrink-wrapped, and the cables weren’t sealed in their original packaging. Everything was just loose inside, which isn’t what you expect when buying a “new” product. After looking through other reviews, it seems like this isn’t an isolated issue either, which is pretty disappointing for something advertised as brand new. That said, the PSU itself seems solid. It’s clearly a high-end unit — efficient, well-built, and easy to install, with great connectors. No complaints there. I just wish I actually received a new one like I paid for. At this point, I’m going to keep it because I don’t have the time or energy to deal with a return and wait for a replacement, but it’s definitely frustrating. I’d recommend buying from somewhere else if you want to be sure you’re getting a truly new unit.
