reviews.title: Premium Case with LOTS of RGB and breathing room
reviews.comment: This is a well made case. Plenty of airflow to keep your PC components cool, and plenty of mounting space for 120mm fans and 360mm radiators in the front and up top. Front IO comes with 4 USB 3.0, which means this case has 2 usb 3.0 wires. As most motherboards only have one usb 3.0 header, this means you might need to buy a splitter, or an internal hub to get full utilization out of the front IO. Also, LOTS of RGB. This is also a MASSIVE case, much bigger than the typical mid-tower. Size-wise, it’s about the size of a full-tower, but internally it’s slightly more spacious than a mid-tower. My only gripe is that the case is a bit complicated to get around. Trying to take off the side fan mount, the cable cover and the PSU shroud was not easy. There are screws that aren’t the most accessible, and I would most certainly recommend looking up the user manual (on Corsair’s website).
reviews.author: cvictor

reviews.title: Nice industrial looking case.
reviews.comment: Nothing fancy, just a nice well designed case with everything needed for a complete build. Heavy, mostly metal construction with a glass side (not acrylic). Fans look good and are fairly quiet unless you are really pushing your system. Easy to hide most of the cables on the backside and the included Velcro cable management straps work well. I also like the included iCUE RGB controller that handles up to 6 RGB fans and has 2 included thermal sensors that can be placed in different areas of the case. The iCUE device also controls the 6 RGB strips with the additional included driver.
reviews.author: jdc

reviews.title: It's a nice case
reviews.comment: It's a fantastic case, don't let the price steer you in the wrong direction, this case comes with an included and installed, pre wire managed control module, everything with the module and the RGB strips, fans, are all very nearly pre installed and wire managed. Came with extra ties and wire management straps, screws, and temperature sensors, it says it's a mid case, but this is quite literally the size of a full tower case, it's HUGE!!!! It's more of a mid plus case, it's the size of a full, but the space to work with is the size of a mid plus. Overall, great case!!
reviews.author: Mikey

reviews.title: Super product with great cable management
reviews.comment: The box is really nice.  It was super easy to build my computer with this thanks to the excellent set up for vable management, etc.  The led lights are cool.  If you use an SSD hard drive versus an older disc hard drive, corsair has provide a way to open the unused space for additional cable storage.  This was perfect for me.  The box is heavy.  Let me repeat, the box is heavy!  So be sure it is either on the floor or a sturdy table.  I have loved mine so far.
reviews.author: Matthew H

reviews.title: I like it
reviews.comment: I like it
reviews.author: James Moore

reviews.comment: Does the job. All in one power supply and the cables look a mess and not very good to look at through the case. Would recommend a different power supply but works for the price.
reviews.author: Austin

reviews.title: Excellent power supply unit
reviews.comment:
Excellent PSU. It is modular, well built and so far works great
Thank you for a great product
reviews.author: DDS

reviews.title: All the power I need
reviews.comment:
This power supply has a complete set of connections for anything I could want to do. It has everything you would expect: motherboard, motherboard 12V, two PCIe power (6+2), lots of SATA and Molex power. The lengths of the wires are fine, the connectors on each wire are just flexible enough, which is good. No one wants a brittle power connector.
It's very quiet, even when I'm using the CPU and GPU at full power. That makes sense, since my whole machine only pulls at most about 500 watts, only half of what this PSU can produce. I definitely can't hear the PSU over the GPU noise.
Installation was easy, the most time consuming part is cable management, as usual. I prefer the non-modular style of this power supply, because it means that I don't have a big wad of cables I need to keep forever in a drawer.
reviews.author: David Heigl

reviews.title: Best case I've built in.
reviews.comment: Fantastic case, I enjoyed building in it. Looks good and can fit all my components with room for more if I decide to add to my pc. Cable management is simple and you can really spend some time with it and make it nice. Room for fans keeps this case pretty cool, really helped my build that easily overheats normally, and has good dust filters and everything to keep it nice inside. Not a lot of thought went into the look of my build but it still looks quite nice in this case. Worth it for the price for sure.
reviews.author: Andie

reviews.title: Easy to build in, great case for beginner builders and experienced builders alike.
reviews.comment: No dust filter on top, dust filter in front and bottom. The infinirail is neat, and does save time and effort. Just not a lot. Hands down, this is the easiest case I have ever built in. Both of my sons have a PC using this case, and I would strongly recommend it as a top tier budget case. This case has what is, in my opinion, the greatest functionality improvement in years. The consolidated front panel connector. The mesh filter in front is easy to remove and clean, allowing for plenty of airflow. The case itself is sturdy.
reviews.author: Brandon Wirtz

reviews.title: Exceptional Case — Airflow, Style, and Ease of Build All in One
reviews.comment: ✅ Review: 5 out of 5 stars The CORSAIR 4000D RS ARGB Frame is one of the best cases I’ve ever built in. It perfectly balances a clean, minimal aesthetic with thoughtful functionality, making it ideal for both first-time builders and experienced enthusiasts. 🧩 Modular & Spacious The modular design is a huge plus—panels, PSU shroud, and drive trays are all easy to remove and reposition. It fits full ATX motherboards, supports reverse-connector boards (like ASUS BTF), and has plenty of clearance for modern GPUs and cooling setups. Installation was smooth with excellent cable management features like Velcro straps, channels, and a clean PSU shroud. 🌬️ Airflow and Cooling Out of the box, it comes with three RS120 ARGB fans that are quiet and look great. The front mesh panel allows for incredible airflow, and you can install up to ten 120 mm fans or a 360 mm radiator without issues. Temps in my build dropped noticeably compared to my older case. ✨ Design & Aesthetics It has a sleek look that doesn’t scream “gamer,” but still feels modern and premium. The pre-installed ARGB fans add just the right amount of lighting without being overbearing—and no separate RGB controller is needed. The tempered glass side panel showcases your build beautifully. 🛠️ Practical Touches USB-C on the front I/O is a welcome addition, and the GPU support arm is a great touch to avoid sag. I also appreciated the tool-free panel design—it makes upgrades and maintenance fast and painless. ⚠️ Minor Downsides The side panel feels a bit thin and needs to be handled gently, especially when removing it. Also, if you plan to mount a 360 mm AIO on the top, be aware that RAM or VRM clearance might be tight depending on your motherboard. 🔍 Final Thoughts This case is a top-tier pick for airflow-focused builders who want clean aesthetics, solid thermal performance, and ease of use. Whether you’re doing a standard ATX build or going for something more high-end with reverse cable routing, the 4000D RS ARGB handles it all gracefully. Highly recommend!
reviews.author: Austin P.

reviews.title: Best Case Scenario
reviews.comment: Awesome case. I was told the front looks like a cheese grater, but other than that it is very spacious and easy to build in. The modernized features make accessing all components easy. Wish it came with a dust cover for the top like a couple of the other cases I've used. It seems very open and susceptible to dust, but time will tell if that becomes an issue.
reviews.author: mikaela

reviews.title: Great mid-sized case.
reviews.comment: Nice, cozy look, as you can see in the photo (build isn't done yet so not pictured is the power supply shroud that can mount two more fans pointed at the graphics card.) Excellent fan placements, although I think they could have at least included the rear exhaust fan. Still gets a little cramped for your hands while working on it as any.mod-sized case does. Being mid-sized means the fan mounts on the power supply shroud will be fairly close to the graphics card and should cool it down by a good couple degrees, though. The built-in structural support for the graphics card is a nice touch, but the panel it's attached to is too wide for some videocards; I had to remove it to fit my RX9070 into the case and use a more typical brace to prevent sagging. With the side panel off you can clearly see the empty space where it went. Fortunately, all the different parts are easy to remove or replace. The one actual thing that makes this four stars instead of five, however, is that the bottom side panel and the top panel do not have dust filters pre-installed. Technically you don't need either, but if you're going to use the power supply shroud fan mounts, you're going to need to put a filter in the bottom side panel because that's where those fans are going to get their intake from. Baffling that there isn't a dust filter already there.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Nice stealthy, non rgb build
reviews.comment: This case is really cool. Lots of different ways to configure the storage and space within. One complaint is not being able to fit as many fans as i thought. But it would be overkill anyway. 3 removable mesh filter trays, this version has the non see thru sides. I'm impressed by the manufacturing. Only other negative was some parts that are removable are really tough to get out. But the doors and filters come out with ease and snap in perfectly!
reviews.author: josh

reviews.title: Nearly perfect
reviews.comment: PROS: Extremely easy to build in well thought out case. Excellent airflow for water cooling in top and front. Fits 2x360mm radiators. Dust filters everywhere but the back. Available with a solid side panel, unlike most other high end cases. Sturdy, including the mesh parts. Came with 3 good 140mm 3-pin fans. CONS: Expensive.  Version without glass side or RGB should be under $150. Only 2 USB-A ports on the top.  There's space enough to add 2 more but Fractal chose not to. No front 5 1/4" or 3.5" bays to allow adding more front I/O. The rotated vertical GPU slots won't fit 3-slot GPUs. Other Thoughts: As close to perfect as I could hope for. This is ideal for water cooling.  If you're using air cooling, probably get the Fractal Torrent instead.
reviews.author: Noah

reviews.title: Best Airflow Case out There
reviews.comment: The best looking airflow catered case out there. Great quality and presentation of the product. Love all of the HDD bay and built in cable management. The fact that I had the flexibility to but a solid side panel and pay less was a huge reason I went with this case.
reviews.author: Pierson Allston

reviews.title: Best case for building a PC
reviews.comment: So much of the case is removable to allow easier access, excellent cable management tools right out of the box. It is minimalist and elegant, no cursed tempered glass. So happy with it!
reviews.author: Pj

reviews.title: Good air flow
reviews.comment: Great looking case, good airflow. Responsive customer service at Fractal when I needed to replace the headers.
reviews.author: SleepyGoodSpirit

reviews.title: Great Case!
reviews.comment:
Pros: Super easy to build in. HDD Cage comes out with just thumb screws giving you the whole basement for power cable management. Tons of clearance in the front and top for any radiator with 120mm or 140mm fans. My Xfx Speedster Swft 319 rx6800 graphics card fits with tons of room to spare. Four 140mm fans are included (3aRGB, 1 black) as is a control hub. Magnetic dust screens are awesome and air flow is exceptional. Both the glass and metal sides attach with captured thumb screws so you can't lose them. All of the expansion slots in the back have thumb screws as well. Build quality and finishes are above average for the price range.
Cons: Included fans are on the louder side, but tolerable if you set up a custom fan curve. Only average room for cable management in the back. Power and front I/O are on the side that you would normally face  away from you. Definitely not deal breakers though.
Bottom Line: Definitely the budget king! It has everything most people need, tons of space, easy to build in, excellent airflow, 4 included fans, and it looks good. You can't do better without spending twice as much.
reviews.author: Teddy West Side

reviews.title: Great case but terrible coil whine from the exhaust
reviews.comment:
The case itself is great to build in, with plenty of space and openings to route cables; I had no issues getting anything to reach its intended destination. Excellent airflow/thermal performance - the pre-installed fans move a lot of air, and the ARGB is nice. The included fan hub worked perfectly with my B850 Tomahawk motherboard.
Chief Downside: The exhaust fan has very noticeable coil whine, and can't be set above 20% speed without driving me crazy; it's like having a dentist's drill whirring right next to me. I detached this fan from the hub to run it at a constant low speed, thus allowing the intake fans (which do not have any coil whine) to run an actual curve.
I will replace the exhaust fan at some point; you should budget the cost of a new fan into the cost of this case, imo.
reviews.author: brian olson

reviews.title: Excellent case, a bit loud but has great features.
reviews.comment:
I love how this looks and how easy cable management was. Having a PSU shroud was amazing for hiding excess cable.
The front fans are powerful, but a little loud when they ramp up. The RGB is nice and functions well. It fits my large GPU just fine, and had plenty of space for AIO coolers.
This is one of the easiest cases I have built in and I would gladly buy this again for future builds
reviews.author: CC

reviews.title: Sleek Design and Excellent Airflow Make This Case a Winner
reviews.comment:
This computer case really caught my eye with its modern styling, and I was even more impressed when I finally built my new desktop using it. One of the standout features is definitely how much air this case can move. Keeping the components cool is crucial for performance and longevity, and this case seems to do an excellent job of promoting airflow throughout the system.
The inclusion of RGB lighted fans is also a fantastic touch. They add a vibrant and customizable aesthetic to the build, allowing for a personalized look that's visually appealing. Furthermore, the case comes equipped with all the essential cables needed for setup, which is a thoughtful detail that simplifies the building process.
For anyone who appreciates a clean and organized interior, this case shines in its cable management design. The strategically placed pathways make it easy to route and conceal cables, resulting in a tidy build that not only looks better but can also contribute to better airflow. The user-friendly design facilitates easy access to the internal components by making opening the case straightforward.
Pros:
The product has the ability to move a lot of air.
Looks great.
Low noise.
The cable management is excellent.
I am extremely satisfied with my purchase.
Cons:
None I found.
Overall, this computer case offers a winning combination of attractive design and practical functionality. The excellent airflow, coupled with the stylish RGB fans and thoughtful cable management, makes it a fantastic choice for any PC builder. I am thrilled with this purchase and would highly recommend it to others looking for a high-quality case.
reviews.author: Tommy Amos

reviews.title: Decent for the price
reviews.comment: Pretty good case, I like the cable management and the airflow is good. The fans are very pretty with the aRGB lights. The thumb screws are pretty wonky though, they don’t screw in very easily. The panels for the graphics card in the back feel pretty cheap as well. Overall a good case for the money with a few minor annoyances.
reviews.author: Ansley Worrell

reviews.title: Terrific case with huge expansion potential (but it's heavy)
reviews.comment:
I knew Lian Li was popular, but now I know why. I got this case for around $155 and couldn't be happier. The quality is excellent, and the cable management is outstanding! I love the glass panel that shows off the innards of my PC (AMD Phantom Nova motherboard and Ryzen 9070XT graphics card) too.
Now, let me tell you, this is a big case. Do NOT expect it to fit easily in a corner under your desk unless you have a good amount of room (or are going to make space for it). In my case, I redid the furniture to accommodate the case (which tells you how much I loved it). Also, at around 30 pounds empty, this is a heavy case. Install it near the final location you'll have it if you can, it sucks to lug around.
After all that though, I don't think I'll ever get another case again - the expansion potential is huge! And it comes with a graphics card support bracket so you don't need to get a separate one of those (like I did). Love my Lian Li III!
reviews.author: Aj100

reviews.title: Beautiful and elegant
reviews.comment:
The lines on this case are amazing. It looks incredible from every angle. The back panel makes cable management a breeze. There are many places to attach zip ties and an abundance of apertures from the front in which to tuck your cables. You can be as clean as you want front and back. The HDD/SSD brackets are screwed in, making it east to remove them if you won't be utilizing them. The glass side panels and all of the mesh panels slide off thick pins which is super convenient for getting everything out of the way so that you can open the case up. The RGB works great, airflow is amazing, I'd recommend this case to anyone.
The only thing that I dislike about the case is that I had to flip the PSU cover backwards in order to line the holes up with my PSU, so that looks a little funny. I wish they'd send 2 panels to cover either option.
reviews.author: Thomas Pederson

reviews.title: Lian Li Lancool III best case
reviews.comment: Amazing PC case with plenty of room and looks fantastic. With the case you can be very creative with the look you want.
reviews.author: pzrtek

reviews.title: price, quality of life features.
reviews.comment: great case, well constructed, nice to have features, plenty of space, plenty of airflow,  huge fans. downsides the rear van isnt RGB kinda lame.
reviews.author: sacramsento

reviews.title: Great case
reviews.comment: The case assembly was a little difficult but I was able to fit my 420mm AIO on top with barely any room to spare and cable management is very easy with this case. I also really like the built in GPU anti-sag bracket. Overall amazing quality case for the price. The case is also fairly heavy, my entire system ended up weighing about 60lbs
reviews.author: Thaddeus Richardson

reviews.title: Superb design and quality
reviews.comment: This is a beautiful case in all white.  The is more than enough room for just about anything you want to put in there.  Even with a vertically mounted 5070 ti, there is a lot of extra space left over, giving the final result a nice open feel.  That said, it's a large case - make sure you have room for it at close to 13" deep.  There a several things that made this the easiest build I have done.  Aside from the interior size, the dual chambered design makes cabling easy and keeps the front side clean-looking.  Additionally, every bracket, screw hole and snap connection matched up perfectly with overall fit and finish being near-perfect.  I have six intake fans and four exhaust fans, including the AIO cooler for plenty of airflow, though on the down side, the slatted exterior covers probably restrict the airflow to some extent.  One other concern is that it will be a tight fit to get even one low-profile pci card in along with the gpu and pci riser.  Not an issue right now, but possibly in the future.  The case does not come with any fans, though given the range of fan choices and options, included fans probably be not what the user wants anyway.  The case is not inexpensive, but I think worth the cost.  It is heavy also, but built very sturdily.
reviews.author: EricAZ

reviews.title: Love this case!
reviews.comment:
I adore this case! Yes, it's definitely a luxury case as it's pricier than others, but this version does have the 2k screen included. The glass is tempered and I didn't have any issues with it cracking or scratching during the pc build. The bottom compartment does fit three fans, just know you need to fit one inside the case before attaching it to the bracket to make them all fit.
As far as the screen goes, it's a beautiful screen, do note, you need to connect it directly to the motherboard for the picture to work and download the software so you can set your picture/widgets. The cables to hook it up are already ran to the back of the case when it arrives, so you'll just need to hook them up to your motherboard and power supply.
The top of the case does have a compartment that lowers if you want to mount fans or your AIO closer to your motherboard.
Do note, this case includes a PCIe riser 4.0 to connect your GPU to your MOB so the GPU sits upright in the case. IF you need a 5.0 connection like I did, you'll need to purchase the 5.0 riser off Hyte's website, at the time I purchased, they were $99 and you can choose which color you'd like.
The case has plenty of places to route your cables for easy cable management as well as preinstalled Velcro in the bottom to hold some of the cables.
The only downside I saw was needing to buy an updated PCIe riser, I wish they would have had that as an upgrade option at purchase, as well as there being two open spots on the back of the side where you mount the GPU etc. I'm assuming its for easier access, but I do worry about the amount of dust etc that allows into the pc, though I'm sure it's great for airflow.
reviews.author: Amazon_Customer

reviews.title: Premium Case with a Built-In Touchscreen – Still One of the Best After 2 Years
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/E15OAZcxEjL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/61kkYUGl7UL._SY256.jpg ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ – One of the Best Cases I’ve Ever Built In
I’ve had the HYTE Y70 Touch Infinite Dual Chamber ATX Case for about two years now, and honestly, it’s one of the best PC cases I’ve ever built in.
First off, the build experience is incredibly smooth. The dual-chamber design gives you tons of room to work with, making cable management clean and stress-free. Everything feels thoughtfully laid out, so even more complex builds come together easily without feeling cramped.
Compatibility and size are a huge plus. This case easily supports larger GPUs, multiple radiators, and high-end components without any issues. Whether you’re running a high-performance gaming setup or a workstation build, there’s more than enough space to work with.
One of the standout features is the built-in touchscreen, which is honestly amazing. It adds a completely different level of customization and functionality—you can display system stats, animations, or anything you want. It’s not just a gimmick, it actually enhances the overall experience and makes the build feel premium.
Installation overall is very straightforward. Panels come off easily, parts line up well, and the modular design helps speed things up. It’s clear this case was designed with builders in mind.
Price-wise, it’s definitely on the higher end, but after using it for two years, I can say it’s absolutely worth it. The quality, features, and overall experience justify the investment.
Pros:
• Extremely easy and enjoyable to build in
• Spacious with excellent compatibility for high-end parts
• Dual-chamber design keeps everything clean and organized
• Built-in touchscreen is a standout feature and works great
• Premium look and feel
Cons:
• Higher price point, but you get what you pay for
Overall, if you’re looking for a high-end case that combines performance, aesthetics, and innovation, this is a top-tier choice.
reviews.author: Aaron medina

reviews.title: Best Case Around
reviews.comment: I've built into this case at least half a dozen times, and I've made builds for other people in it as well. If you want a minimalist case that can fit large components without compromise, this case is nearly perfect. It's not flashy, but it's far smaller and more durable than most big, ugly cases with glass on them, which waste tons of space.
reviews.author: Nicholas

reviews.title: Versatile ITX Case
reviews.comment:
This case is EXACTLY what you want in a mini ITX case. Breathable, flexible mesh panels (which can bend easily if you aren't careful. If you have OCD, I suggest you take your time with taking the side panels off and on). This case comes with a multitude of configurations, from a ATX, matx, ITX motherboard fit to a SF, SF-L and ATX PSU configurations.
The shipping does come with an instruction manual with all these possible configuration ideas if not more.
Pro: This case is multifunctional. Meaning, it has a huge customizable option depending on what exactly you want.
If you do your research before buying, this case can be a replacement for those huge bulky chassis that most people think you need. YOUTUBE is also a major help when it comes to needing videos outside of pictures as to what the case can and cannot do.
CON: the only con I have about the case is, ALL THE SCREWS ARE TINY. I mean EXTREMELY small. So having magnetized tools can make building easy. Also, if you have big hands, cable management might be an issue but not impossible, as most small ITX cases because of the lack of space.
Overall its a really good case especially for a first time builder like myself who wanted a small but not too compact gaming PC for streaming. It definitely fit everything I wanted but again, thats because I did my research and googled everything I wanted in it BEFORE I purchased it.
reviews.author: Kindle Customer

reviews.title: Best case ever
reviews.comment:
Love everything about this case.  My first sff build and it just flowed together.
I ended up buying the glass panel and i figured out feet.
reviews.author: Brian Epstein

reviews.title: Fits huge video card!
reviews.comment: My ASUS 5080 Tuf fits like a glove. 👌 I replaced my meshalicious with this new version so I could fit the card.
reviews.author: Reid W.

reviews.title: Great case bad parts
reviews.comment: Came with a faulty pcie riser cable had to buy my own
reviews.author: Aaren Lovelady

reviews.title: Great case, designed for people who enjoy putting together computers.
reviews.comment: Case was fantastic for cable management and thoughtfully put together, especially if you have the older 3.5/2.5 style hard drives. Lights are beautiful. The one thing that is tricky is the tin panel that goes between the super IO board on the motherboard and the case itself. We had to remove the chassis fan on the back to get that piece to slide into place. Everything else was easy.
reviews.author: Kristina F.

reviews.title: A lot of Case for the money!
reviews.comment: I gotta admit. I am a fan of Phanteks cases. This case has so much going for it. For starters, it's big and easy to work in. I can get my big hands in everywhere I need to. Their are no sharp edges. The fans look great and airflow is good with the stock fans. Massive room for large cpu coolers (I'm using double tower). The usual phanteks attention to detail is there ( a single front connector is awesome!) and accessories include ample screws, ties ect.... The case is not perfect though. Construction is a lot lighter than in the more expensive phanteks cases. The side screws are not captive or hinged. I do wish there was a little more connectivity up front, too. Overall, I can easily recommend this case at this price point.
reviews.author: james karl  krantz

reviews.title: Good product and will get more when need to get another gamer tower
reviews.comment: I got two of these gaming towers for me and family member and we love them.
reviews.author: Helena

reviews.title: Solid Case w/ Fans for a Small Price
reviews.comment: A solid case especially at this price point.  If I had to complain about something, maybe the included fans are a little noisy.  But, for the most part, it's an easy case to work with.  I was able to stuff 6 SATA SSD's in it.  And it seems to have pretty decent airflow.
reviews.author: William Z.

reviews.title: Beautiful case with amazing airflow.
reviews.comment:
Amazing case well worth the money. Airflow for days keeping my temps well below TDP.
Pro: a breeze to build with this case offers so many options for cable management.
Fit my chunky 4070 and full atx mother board with room to spare.
Removable Hard drive case made it super easy.
Cons: issues getting glass door in just right.
reviews.author: Jacob

reviews.title: Great airflow case with easy cable management and plenty of space
reviews.comment: This is a great case for building your own PC. I picked it up for my 11 year old son to build his first gaming PC and it worked out really well. There is plenty of space inside for components, and the layout is very well designed. It makes cable routing easy and helps keep everything clean and organized. Even for a first time builder, it was straightforward to work in. Airflow is excellent. The case is designed to move air efficiently and includes two 120mm fans to get you started. There is also support for larger radiators if you want to upgrade cooling later. We installed an RTX 5070 with no fitment issues, so there is good clearance for larger GPUs. The tempered glass side panel looks great and lets you show off RGB lighting, cooling setups, and internal components. The black finish also gives it a clean, modern look. For the price, this case offers a lot of value. It is well built, easy to work with, and performs well. Great option for both new and experienced builders.
reviews.author: JD_reviews

reviews.title: Sweet Rig
reviews.comment: This has to be the best case I have ever build in. Love that it included fans, and was perfect size for my XFX 6900x. With room to spare! Keeps my rig super cool, though I do have 8 fans in it, and was a breeze to set up. Looks amazing, and has barely any dust build up thanks to the filters. Great price too when you get it on sale! Highly recommend.
reviews.author: Leon

reviews.title: Brilliantly good design in a case with great value
reviews.comment: At this price point I wasn't expecting something as good as this case. After having built in it I would certainly not be mad if priced at nearer MSRP. The build quality is there, no sharp edges, well considered wire routing and anchor points for cable management. The design comes about as close to an open-air rig as I have used which is actually enclosed. The only aspect I see as a very minor detraction is the fact that with the mesh panel placements it is impossible to hide your basement cable management. This seems to have been dealt with by way of making the rear side panel spacing a bit larger. It has been a consideration to pursue using some manner of cable sleeve, tape, or even a shrink-wrap type solution to neaten up that "shadow" footprint. Temps and noise levels are quite acceptable, build process was easy with many options, and overall, one of the best cases I have ever purchased at this price point. Would recommend.
reviews.author: M Jordan

reviews.title: a decent case from an established brand
reviews.comment: So, when this is on sale (about 60 USD) I think it is great value. This case looks very clean, nothing particularly flashy. It isn't difficult to build in unless you really care to try to cable manage, but that is true for almost all cases. Here are some pros and cons after building in it for the first time. Pros: Size - this case is a mid tower case, it houses an ATX motherboard without feeling excessively large or too small to build in. Pre-installed fans - there are two fans installed, one for the front intake and one for the back exhaust. While buying more fans is better, having some airflow regardless is nice. Cable management - one of my favorite components of this case are the options for cable management. There are many well disguised holes to slide and hide cables through. I can completely hide cables for fans. There are trays on the back with straps to tie around cables, which makes it easy to keep cables where they need to be. There is also a lot of space at the bottom for cables from the power supply, especially convenient with cable extensions. Functionality - there is lots of space and it is easy to build in. Cons: No holes for intake under the power supply - I think this is my biggest gripe with the case. I always like to place the power supply so the fan is taking in cool air from outside the case. It shouldn't matter too much, but I think the fan on the power supply might be louder as a result. Quality is not exceptional - some paint on the case chipped pretty easily. Also, the screws that hold the metal backplate of the GPU on the case don't line up perfectly and there is a small gap between the metal backplate and the PCIe slot cover. Overall, would recommend this case especially when it is on sale.

reviews.title: NZXT H9 Flow RGB+ – Stylish, Spacious, and Perfectly Cooled
reviews.comment: The NZXT H9 Flow RGB+ is an exceptional case that combines style, functionality, and airflow efficiency. Its sleek design, tempered glass panels, and customizable RGB lighting make it a centerpiece in any build. The airflow is excellent, keeping high-end components cool even under heavy load. Cable management is straightforward, and installation is user-friendly. With ample space for large GPUs, multiple storage drives, and advanced cooling solutions, this case is perfect for both gamers and content creators seeking performance and aesthetics.

reviews.title: My Favorite PC Case Yet – And I’ve Built Over 35 Systems
reviews.comment:
The NZXT H9 Flow RGB+ (2025) is hands-down the best case I’ve ever worked with.
Build Quality & Design:
The dual-chamber layout is a builder’s dream—tons of room for cable management, airflow, and clean component placement. The black finish with tempered glass panels gives it a premium, showcase-ready look.
Cooling & Airflow:
With 7 included RGB fans (6 × 140mm and 1 × 120mm) plus support for up to a 420mm radiator, cooling performance is outstanding. Even under heavy loads, temps stay well under control, and the fans run smoothly without excess noise.
Ease of Build:
Everything about the design feels intentional—ample space for large GPUs, great radiator mounting options, and full back-connect readiness for the cleanest builds possible. Cable routing is effortless, and the included control hub makes RGB and fan management simple.
Bottom Line:
After building over 35 PCs, this is by far my favorite case to date. NZXT nailed the combination of looks, functionality, and cooling performance. An absolute joy to build in.

reviews.title: Great case. Easy and fun to build in
reviews.comment: Absolutely beautiful case. Lots of space to build in and fit any GPU you could want. The back chamber makes it super easy to manage wires (or avoid managing wires) and gives plenty of space for the PSU to breathe. The fans are a little noisy but very clean and effective. The paneling locks in very firmly even without the thumb screws. Fitting a 420mm radiator inside was no problem. Will be building in it again

Combine this with a quality AIO or heatsink fan, and you won't have to worry about your components overheating.  The price you have to pay is space to place this thing, and the WEIGHT.  This feels like 25 lbs empty.

Fan controller included - but only good for controlling the NZXT fans.

Quality, heavy duty construction
Outstanding interior air flow dynamics
CONS

reviews.title: Do Not Buy Unless Using Small GPUs

I wish I could go back in time and have actually read the manual online instead of watching a video on the case from the manufacturer which I thought would be more informative. Bought this pc case for my friends budget pc with a ryzen 5 5500 and an rx 7600 and it looks beautiful. Some thing though.

Overall a very good budget case and fits well in desk, I’d recommend a semi modular or modular psu so cables are everywhere. Also it’s micro atx, and the front supports dual 140mm fans. Overall very nice case.
reviews.author: Jennifer Naponelli

reviews.title: Pretty, but do NOT buy this for your first build
reviews.comment:
I love this case. I hate this case. Such wonderful and hateful things to say about the same case. Lets review.
The good: This case is pretty. I love the aesthetics of this case. It's also very compact. It looks like a midget compared to my old Coolermaster HAF 900 series case. That's nice, since I get a lot more room on my desk, and I can position this tower in places I couldn't fit my old one. It's allowed me to do some really cool things with my desk setup that I couldn't do before. The dust covers are pretty, and they make it much easier to clean the case more frequently. (You'll still need deep cleaning every once and a while.)
The bad: Boy oh boy does it suck to install things in this case. Like, cable routing is a FREAKING NIGHTMARE. If you don't care about that stuff, then it's still going to suck working in this case. "Cheap crap" is a nice description of everything about this case. The window? Cheap plexiglass that scratches easily. The PCI-E holes at the back of the case require you to pull them off using excessive force, potentially risking bending the thin metal between the slots. I ended up bending the back PCI-E screw pannel by overtightening the screws. Airflow? Gamer's Nexus tested the Q500L version of the case, and it was literally the worst case they ever tested for air flow. It caused components to thermal throttle (read: slow your computer down) at even low workloads. The Q300L is better, but it's still not winning any competitions. NEVER buy the Q500L.
That seems like a long list of negatives, and it is. But I haven't gotten to the worst sin this case commits: Cable routing. I'm sure this is better than some other cases out there, but it's still pretty bad. Let's enumerate the problems you'll likely run into when routing cables: The movable button panel doesn't stretch long enough to route in convenient locations. The only place to run cables to the top of the case is a small hole that doesn't fit a standard power connector without causing you crazy amounts of grief and bending the plastic connectors while tearing chunks of flesh off your finger as you pull it through. There's not enough room on the back of the case to run your standard SATA cables for SSDs, and installing front fans means you lose out on a lot of potential cabling options. (You HAVE to move the button panel to the bottom/top if you use front fans)
Why did I get this? I couldn't find a reasonably priced small sized case to put a Threadripper build in. I could have sprung for one of the smaller cases designed for compact builds, but each one of them had a deal-breaking problem. (Out of stock, couldn't fit micro-atx mobo, costs like 400$, etc.) I knew what I'd suffer through to get all the hardware to fit inside this case, while running custom cables for aesthetics. I consider it a worthwhile purchase. I spent several extra hours building this when compared with a case that was well designed. I ran into like 20 different configurations where things barely didn't fit by a millimeter or less, and the current configuration fits because I spent like 3 extra hours cabling this monster. But it was cheap, pretty, and small, so I'd probably do it again. Probably not the right case for you.
Overall:  This is a cheap case. It's an affordable place to put your computer. Don't expect much more than that. You can spend like 20$ more to get something truly worth holding your components.
reviews.author: Alex

reviews.title: Amazing Case For an Amazing Price! (Model: Q300L)
reviews.comment:
So first I'd like to state that this review is specifically for the Q300L model. Amazon does this annoying thing where they mix all the reviews of all the models together and I can't stand it so I'm just stating the model flat out.
I just built my 10 year old nephew’s PC using this case and I have to say that I was very surprised at how much I loved building in this case. Originally I bought the Compucase HEC HX300 case for 30$ from Newegg and I was just frustrated at the lack of air flow from that case. It only had room for one fan which was the back exhaust and that's it. It didn't even have holes for the power supply's intake fan! It was my fault for not researching enough and buying something so cheap. Then I did a little research and came across this case. It is only 50$ but has everything I want. I've seen PC builders on youtube build with this case and they all had great things to say.
So the first thing I like about this case is obviously how much airflow it allows. It's an interesting design because there are holes all over the top, all over the bottom, and all over the front and you can install 4 fans if you wanted to (2 up top, 2 in front, 2 in bottom) in addition to the included exhaust fan at the back making it support up to 5 fans! Now with all those holes you might be thinking this is going to be an ugly case but as you'll see in the pictures this is not the case (pun intended) and it has very sleek looking dust filters to cover the top, front, and it’s not obvious from the picture but it has a filter on the bottom as well. I was pleasantly surprised to see that the filter is magnetic which made removing them to install my fans a breeze (pun intended). I also imagine cleaning them when they get dirty will also be very simple. You can simple remove them and just rinse with water. One tip when installing fans is that since there’s air holes all over, they actually made a very small indentation around the holes that you should screw in your fans. These “guides” are hard to notice but if you look closely you’ll see them. They have space for 140mm and 120mm fans depending on whatever you want. Air is able to easily flow through the filter so my air flow issues were resolved!
The case also looks very nice in my opinion. I have the black model just because that’s what my nephew wanted but in review videos I’ve seen, the white one looks very nice as well. Cable management at the back is pretty good too and the case comes with a lot of zip ties. The filters I mention above are also very aesthetically pleasing. The power button,  2 USB ports, headphone jack, and speaker jack are on the side which I don’t mind. The interesting thing is that this IO panel can be unscrewed and moved to the other side which is nice. The clear side panel is acrylic but it’s a 50$ case so it’s fine. It doesn’t look bad at all. There’s also room in the cable management area for a 3.5” hard drive and 2 SSD’s inside the main area which is very good.
Overall the case was pretty simple to build in. It’s designed very well to maximize airflow while looking great. I think this  is an excellent case especially for the price. If you’re in the market for a cheap but good PC case, then you my friends have stumbled on a cheap but GREAT PC case. I would highly recommend this case and am willing to do even more expensive builds with this case in the future.
One final note I’ll add, I built my nephew’s pc with a Ryzen 5 1600  processor and RX 480 gpu reference model targeting 1080p gaming and the heat in my old case with that one exhaust fan was reaching around 87 degrees C. After I added two intake fans in the front and one exhaust fan in the top along with the back exhaust fan that comes with this case my temperatures went down into the mid 70’s while gaming which is great. If you want looks as well as functionality for a great price, go with this case.
reviews.author: Fa

reviews.title: Another beautiful Lian Li case
reviews.comment: Fantastic case. Having built in the two previous versions of the O11 Dynamic Line, I had high expectations. The Evo was already a marked improvement over the original O11, but the Vision changed the game with the addition of a new glass panel on the top. Slightly less airflow, and you can't top mount a radiator if you use the glass panel, but you have both options available. Build quality was impressive as usual from Lian Li, and even with less airflow with the top pane, there was still more than enough to keep everything running cool. Plenty of room inside the main chamber for all of my parts, and plenty of cable management space in the back chamber. Just make sure all of the bottom cables on the mobo are properly arranged if you are using fans on the bottom of the case. It is definitely a larger case for fitting into a workspace but definitely worth making the room for it.
reviews.author: Ignacio Tomas

reviews.title: Sleek, Spacious, and Built for Performance!
reviews.comment: The Lian Li O11 Vision Compact Black ATX Mid Tower Case is an absolute winner for anyone looking to build a clean, modern, and well-ventilated PC. From its premium materials to its smart layout, this case makes building both effortless and visually stunning. Build Quality & Design: ✅ High-Quality Construction – The steel frame feels solid and durable, while the tempered glass panels add a premium touch. ✅ Compact Yet Spacious – Despite being a compact mid-tower, it provides plenty of room for high-end components, including large GPUs and multiple cooling options. ✅ Panoramic View – The three-sided tempered glass design makes this case perfect for showcasing your build, especially with RGB lighting. Cooling & Airflow: ✅ Great Ventilation – The airflow is surprisingly good, thanks to well-placed vents and the option for multiple fan and radiator configurations. ✅ Customizable Cooling Options – Supports liquid cooling and high-performance air cooling with ease. Ease of Building & Features: ✅ Easy Cable Management – The back-connect motherboard support makes routing cables much cleaner, resulting in a clutter-free build. ✅ Tool-Free Installation – Installing components is quick and hassle-free with the tool-less design. A Few Things to Consider: ⚠️ Cable Routing Needs Planning – The compact design means that cable management requires some extra effort to keep everything neat. ⚠️ Limited Front I/O – The front ports are minimal, so if you need a lot of front-facing connectivity, you might need a hub. Final Verdict: If you're looking for a stylish, well-built, and feature-packed case that makes your PC look incredible while keeping it cool, this is the one to get. The tempered glass panels make it a showpiece, and the smart layout ensures excellent performance and easy upgrades. Highly recommended for anyone wanting a clean and high-end build experience.
reviews.author: Wolf Girls Tavern

reviews.title: A pleasure to build in.
reviews.comment: Wow this case was a joy to build with. I don’t think it says in the description but this case was a collaboration with Lian Li and the PCmasterrace subreddit and it shows that people with a lot of PC building experience had a hand in this. There are just so many quality of life things engineered into the case, I was amazed at how easy it was to install every component without fighting the case in any way. The cable management in the back is a dream as well with all the built in tie downs available it was easy to get everything nice and tidy. The airflow is great with how I have my fans set up, and there are a ton of options for fan location to account for many different preferences and needs. Build quality of the case is exceptional, and it comes with screws and hardware to mount anything you could possibly want to in the case. The only tiny gripe I have is that the SDD mount on the swinging door inside the back of the case didn’t have enough clearance for the SATA cable to plug into the drive on the mount, but was easy enough to attach it to one of the HDD cages nearby. Very happy with the purchase and I’ll be hard pressed to buy a case from another brand going forward.

reviews.comment: What More Can You Expect From Lian Li Cases!!! There Out Right Awesome!! I Run The 6 Intake Fans and 2 Exhaust Fans and The Glass Top Option!! Cooling is Not an issue!! Max Temps seen on gpu (72 degrees C and CPU (60 Degrees C) Playing Cyberpunk 4k High Settings 60fps Cable Management is Great!! Installation is Easy(If You Done This Before)!! One of the best looking cases on market that gives easy setup options using the thumb screws to remove panels etc The Value this brings for the money can’t be match! Size this great!! reviews.author: DonovanRamos

reviews.title: The devil is in the details, and Lian Li thought of the details
reviews.comment: Best case I've ever built with. Airflow is good. 7800x3D idles at 40 degrees. I appreciate the little things that this case provides and I never even knew I needed. Pros: - You can strip just about every panel off the case which gives you all the room you need to maneuver and route wires - Bottom and side radiator/fan brackets come out so you can mount your fans to the bracket and install all at once. Especially convenient on the bottom if you need to wire something on your mobo after the fans have been installed. No need to remove each fan individually to get back there. - Tons of room in the case, both in the front compartment and rear. - Hard drive cages allow you to secure the drives outside the case and then install with a single thumbscrew. - PSU mount is in the vertical center instead of the bottom so you don't have to run all cables the exact same way and cause a traffic jam. - Swinging gate on the back holds your wires in place and allows you to mount HDDs and hubs on the outer wall. - Grommets keep things looking clean - Everything fits tightly, provides good airflow, and assembles with the minimum amount of screws necessary while still feeling sturdy and secure - Glass is so clear it's easy to think it's not there. Cons: - GPU anti-sag bracket is a good idea but if you have a triple fan GPU, the bracket will interfere with your third fan. If you're not using it, it's just in the way. I will be removing the bracket.
reviews.author: troyal

reviews.title: A good product deserves a good review.
reviews.comment:
HIGHLY IMPRESSED BY THIS CHASSIS.
I usually purchase the more premium chassis from the more known and premium manufacturers. However, wanting to give my old 9900k system a fresh look and a few upgrades (new AIO, RAM and GPU), being it's five years old, I didn't want to purchases an expensive case from the more known manufacturers. So in my search, I came across this Musetex NN8 of a hidden gem. $80 for a chassis with included 5 ARGB fans? Let's do it!
Though not as hefty as the "premium" brands, the build quality is solid. It has a premium look and premium feel without the premium price. The included ARGB fans look nice, move a lot of air and are quiet even at max speed. There's plenty of room for cable management and a lot of tie down points for zip ties or velcro straps.
Someone mentioned in the reviews they had issues fitting their full size ATX motherboard. I did not share that experience as mine fit like a glove and went in nicely and comfortably. The chassis supports up to five 2.5" SATA SSDs OR three 2.5" SATA SSDs with one 3.5" HDD. Usually with inexpensive chassis such as this one, it's a pain to build a PC as there are usually a lot of charp edges you could cut yourself with. Well not with this chassis. They definitely paid attention to detail, polished off the edges while doing it in a cost effective mannor.
Definitely a good chassis especially for budget builders or people wanting to freshen up their older/aging PCs.
Intel Core i9 9900k CPU
MSI Z390 Gaming Plus motherboard
32gb Kingston Renegade 3600mhz CL16 RAM
AMD Radeon RX6750XT (reference) GPU
Seasonic 620 watt PSU
Thermalright 240mm AIO

reviews.title: Best Bang For Your Buck Case With 6 RBG Fans
reviews.comment: One of the best cases I've owned and for 80 bucks!? Its a steal! Very good case, light weight (easy to move around and maneuver as required), love the glass side, all 6 RGB fans work and keep the internal components cool. Went from having a water cooled CPU to air cooled and this case and its fan are delivering excellent cooling capabilities. Love all the cable management areas and SSD/HDD mounting points, you should have no issue with space for storage devices; note, if your PSU is not modular and you have a clump of left over power cables, you may have to remove the bottom SSD/HDD cage, very easy to do so but just something to note. I did buy two more fans for the bottom of the case (right above where the PSU sits) and could not figure out how to screw them in. Ended up using zip ties to mount the fans but not a huge issue at all and probably something I missed. I have never heard of MUSETEX before this case but their first impression has been stellar! Would strongly recommend this case if you want preinstalled fans, a lightweight case that can hold an ATX board, and is easy on the wallet.

reviews.title: Love this case!!
reviews.comment: I’ve been using the MUSETEX ATX PC Case Y6 for a bit now, and I’m really impressed with both its performance and overall design. Right out of the box, it looks sleek and modern, and the 270° tempered glass panels give it a clean, high-end showcase feel. If you care about aesthetics, this case definitely delivers—it makes your build look like a centerpiece. One of the standout features for me is the airflow. With three 120mm fans pre-installed, it already provides solid cooling without needing immediate upgrades. The support for a 360mm radiator is also a big plus, giving you flexibility if you want to go with a more advanced cooling setup later. My components have been running cool and stable, even during longer gaming sessions. Building in this case was also a smooth experience. There’s enough room to work comfortably, and cable management is pretty straightforward with the available space and layout. The inclusion of a USB Type-C port on the front panel is a nice modern touch that makes it feel more future-proof and convenient for everyday use. Overall, I think the MUSETEX Y6 is a great value for the price. It combines strong airflow, solid build quality, and a visually striking design that really stands out. If you’re looking for a case that performs well and looks great on your desk, this one is definitely worth considering.
reviews.author: Barbara Torres

reviews.title: A stellar purchase, highly recommend
reviews.comment: Best case I have purchased in 20+ years of building computers. I bought this case because my previously purchased case (from Coolermaster) was oriented to have the PSU fan feed into the GPU fans and vice versa. This case has great orientation, cable management, and fan space. Three standard (I think 120mm fans pre-installed) and mounting/venting for additional side fans and chimmeney fans. The sides are screwless, which is simply convenient. The manufacturer includes multiple Velcro ties, plastic cable ties, and three varieties of screws. It's a robust case, and it's large too, all intentional and purpose built for a tremendous case. Great value, at least moderate cooling without adding fans, and it even has little feet.
reviews.author: Tyler Bjerke

reviews.title: Good
reviews.comment: Amazing case. Beautiful glass. Amazing airflow. Good dust filter top and bottom. If you want to use the front sides fans as intake you can buy a pc mesh magnetic filter and cut it too fit the opening for the side intake and the power supply intake. Plenty of room for my cpu cooler and graphics card. and lots of room inside to work with. the back chamber for the psu and cables was really nice and also very spacious. The quality is very good and the removable brackets for the gpu or graphics card have screws and don't need to be broken off. Excellent quality and the price was very nice allowing me to spend more on my pc's performance. and internal quality parts. Very good case
reviews.author: sami

reviews.title: Nice But Not Without Issues
reviews.comment: Not a novice - Been building computers since the XT, AT, 386, 486, Pentium, all iNtel’s, and AMD’s, including Threadrippers, and, you get the idea. Lost count after 3,000 builds. Having said that, I never thought it necessary to write a review before. First Impressions: The case looks nice, as expected. Challenge 1 - Getting it open for the first time.  There are no screws to release the covers.  The instructions are inside the covered case.  All you have to try to figure out how to get the covers off, is a yellow warning label, advising you to be careful not to break the glass trying to get the cover off. Challenge 2 - Backplate.  This should have been a simple, “Remove the parts from the old case, and put them in this one.” But, the I/O backplate (ASUS), which easily fit in annother other case, would not snap into place in this one.  No biggie.  It’s not unusual to have a glitch or two with a new case. Challenge 3 - Standoffs - Putting the motherboard into this case was, without a doubt, the most challenging out of any computer build I’ve ever done.  First, the suppled screws had difficulty screwing the motherboard down.  They stopped, not because they bottomed out, but as though the screw threads didn’t exactly match the threads in the standoffs. Eventually, they all (gently) screwed all the way in.  That is, until the last one snapped off with almost no force. Time to remove the motherboard, replace the standoff, and start over. Challenge 4 - Standoff Spinning. When trying to remove the motherboard, another standoff (not the broken one) spun loose, preventing me from removing the motherboard. Out of thousands of computer builds, I’ve seen this maybe twice.  Oh well, removal was difficult, but, I was able to get a tiny pair of channel locks down there to hold the stan doff while unscrewing the screw. If this had been one of the stand off’s in a tighter spot, I would have had to resort to drilling it out - Which would have been very very difficult to clean up after. Challenge 5 - At this point, I thought it necessary to pre-install every screw into the standoffs, then back them out, to ensure a smooth motherboard installation.  This proved challenging.  The last thing you want to do, is struggle to get a motherboard screwed in, then, if you ever have to remove it, have the stand off’s spin.  So, prudence dictated just go ahead and change all 9 standoff’s, which I did. Challenge 6 - Alignment. One of the 9 standoff screw holes is enough out of alignment, that it is not possible to get a screw into it.  Not worth fussing over.  This install will have to do, with only 8 screws in the motherboard. Well, I’m tired and disappointed.  What should have taken 15 - 20 minutes, has taken half the day. going to hit it again tomorrow.  I’ll update this review when I’m done. The next day, things went more as expected. The rest of the build was easy. The only other critique, is that this case lacks rubber grommets where cables pass through. It also lacks a HDD LED, and could use more Hard Drive mount locations. Hated the build. Love the results. Here’s how I rate this case, 10 being best: Quality - 6 Ease of build - 3 Precision - 6 Functionality - 9 Air Flow - 10 3 Fans - 10 Quiet - 9 Looks - 10
reviews.author: Barry Jenkins

reviews.title: Great quality
reviews.comment: Functioned great as a cheaper but quality starter case for me when i first got into pc building. Fans can be connected together to help with a limited number of fan headers. No issues with space or cable management that i ran into. Can easily fit a massive gpu, cpu tower cooler, or even a 360mm aio. Fans coming pre installed was amazing for me as i did not yet know how to figure out which way a fan is blowing. Overall highly recommend for anyone looking for a good quality case for not a lot of money.
reviews.author: Keilani

reviews.title: Perfect budget Mid-tower
reviews.comment: You won't find something less expensive at this quality I'd wager. This is an incredible value for a mid tower. Got it for 55 bucks. It's much more compact than the average mid tower (240mm top not 360) but that was a huge positive I didn't even check for. The smaller size, assuming you don't have a 5090 is literally perfect for asthetics and setting up a nice clean build. Removable GPU panels instead of breakaways, extremely near easily removable opening glass door. I like this case better than my main build, and that is a 120 dollar case! Don't get me wrong, it's very nice, but it's heavy and too much glass. This is the perfect size and feature list for PC without going micro ATX. 1 Free case fan in the back, and no fan hub, just fair warning. I didn't need those for this because I'm just repurposing parts for a build for my friend, but it should be noted that's where some price cuts went. But they didn't go to quality! Fantastic case.
reviews.author: Joe

reviews.title: SOLID budget case
reviews.comment:
You literally won't find a better case at this price point. Absolutely terrific value.
It's not much bigger than the case I replaced, which was about the same price when I bought it 10 months ago, but everything is just structured better, and the metal doesn't feel super cheap. There's more room for a bigger graphics card (340mm as opposed to my last case's max of 280mm), so there's plenty of space for upgrades. Cable management was a breeze with the abundance of holes and openings for cables to go to all the right places on my motherboard. Also, there's plenty of space on the rear side of the case for cable management, with more than enough cable tie points. The PSU shroud is nice and roomy as well, with an included hard drive bay tucked inside, which I appreciate, as my last case did not include one. The shroud also allows for even better cable management, especially if you're using a non-modular PSU with extra cables that you don't need. I just bundled them up and zip tied them together and tucked them away, allowing my case to stay fairly clean and open for maximum airflow, while also not making me worry if I would be able to get my side panel back on without a fight. The swiveling tempered-glass side panel that is fully removeable is a nice touch.
With the mesh front panel, bottom and top vents (with dust filters; the top filter being magnetic), and rear exhaust, the case feels practically open for lots of air flow. As far as noise level, as with any mostly-open, high-volume airflow case, it strongly depends on your setup. With room for up to eight (8) 120mm case fans, or six (6) 120mm fans and two (2) 140mm fans (top vent), there's lots of room for efficient cooling. But if you're like me, you don't care too much about the noise, as you tend to tune it out when you're immersed in an intense gaming session. So, I have my GPU switched to performance mode, and my case fans are set to keep things nice and chilly, so it can get a bit noisy at times, but again, nothing that really bothers me too much. If you have a dual-BIOS GPU set to quiet mode, and have your fans fine-tuned to perform at maximum efficiency with minimal noise, the openness of the case, while creating the possibility for more noise exposure, also allows for plenty of airflow for efficient cooling, allowing your fans to keep things moving at a nice, low dB.
Overall, it's a solid case. As stated at the beginning, you won't find a better value case for the price.
reviews.author: Seth Shaffer

reviews.title: Great budget case
reviews.comment: For the price I paid this was great. There is room for improvement but honestly that comes down to preference. I could and probably should have gone for a two fan GPU for a case like this since tbh the airflow is so good I would have gotten the same or very similar thermal performance. The airflow on this case is so good and I’m rocking three DARKROCK intake fans than run super smooth and quiet. The LED power light is overly bright, like I got a laser pointed at my ceiling bright, so that’s a thing. The cable management side feels a bit cramped and I feel like it could be better but this is my first build so your mileage may vary. The glass panel is nice but for my aesthetic it feels almost wasted. The build came out super clean despite me being an amateur and I’m confident someone more experienced could probably make it even better, not blaming my PSU but some extensions may help with this. Not a huge fan that the top fans can only go up to 280mm and wish it was a bit longer to 360mm but that’s me nitpicking.
reviews.author: Jose

reviews.title: Good budget mid tower
reviews.comment: Package arrived without issue (all the way to Fiji). Normal styrofoam was used with single boxing but no damages. The case is a decent budget case (with 1 each usb2,3 and c front ports) and comes with a rear exhaust fan which is nice (i replaced it for aesthetic). Side glass is sturdy and hinged which is also nice. Fits 06 fans (used corsair rgb 120s) 3 front intakes, 2 for upper exhaust and replaced the rear case fan with another corsair for exhaust. There is nothing wrong with no rgb/argb but this was a gift for a friend so spruced the build up with rgb (but really hate the icue software). Am not into rgb (no rgb is the norm) but gotta admit it does add personality (mentally) to an otherwise all black case (used white static lighting at its dimmest which makes it look kinda like the b/w superman logo aesthetic). Can fit a 3 slot gpu comfortably but do consider a 90 degree adaptor for clearance from the glass panel. Airflow is very nice and airy, no inner dust guards (top one is a magnetic mat only so its nice) and temps are good (idling in 30s celcius and 60-70C under loads...in Fiji's hot December room temps) (specs: msi mpg edge wifi ddr5, 64gb vengeance, 13700k, dc-ak620 aircooler, wdblack sn770 1tb and another crucial 2tb ssd with a stock 10gb 3080). All front ports work and cable management takes some time but no bulging of the side panel with decent cabling/zipties etc. Would buy again as Fiji retailers don't have any (all over Fiji) tower cases at all with front usb c ports (the msi mobo would've been a bit of waste without front usbc). So far no issues from my friend and I hope this build lasts him a decent number of years (the refurb optiplex we got gave up after about an year). Overall, a decent product and vinaka to retailer.

reviews.title: Worth the money, it is gorgeous

reviews.title: Great value case
reviews.comment: It's a great tower, especially for the price.  If you're looking for a case that won't break the bank, but will look amazing showing off the inside of your computer, this is one to look at.  The built in RGB fans look great if you're into that and they provide plenty of airflow to keep temperatures stable.  There's room at the top to add a radiator for a watercooler, and also plenty of space for an air cool tower if you prefer.  Cable management is easy, with rubber gaskets surrounding the holes and a good bit of space hidden behind the panel.  It is a bit of a tight squeeze and I had to apply a little pressure to get that side back on the case, but I am very happy with the final results.
reviews.author: Donald Benhardt Jr

reviews.title: Best Mid ATX Case for the price, I love MONTECH!
reviews.comment:
This PC case is amazing! I bought this case to replace my be quiet case that looked ugly, and I switched from an aio to an air cooler.
Pros:
-Size: Mid tower but has a lot of room
-Fans: The 3 preinstalled fans are pre daisy chained which made installing easy.
-High quality: The case is super high quality, lots of cable management room, the process for installing the components were easy and straight forward compared to my be quiet case.
-Easy to add extra case fans: I bought thermalright c12c-s fans in a 5 pack and installed 3 intake on the bottom and 2 exhaust fans on the top middle. They all connected so all my components have the same rgb showing at the same time

reviews.author: Bryce

reviews.title: Best case I have ever bought
reviews.comment:
I recently upgraded my setup with the montech xr Gaming Computer Case, and I couldn't be happier! From the moment I unboxed it, the build quality stood out. The sleek design and tempered glass panels give it a premium look that fits perfectly in my gaming corner.
Installation was a breeze thanks to the well-thought-out cable management features and ample space for all my components. I appreciate the tool-less drive bays, which made adding my SSD and HDD hassle-free. The airflow is exceptional—my system runs cool even during long gaming sessions.
One of my favorite features is the customizable RGB lighting. It adds a vibrant touch to my rig and syncs seamlessly with my other peripherals. Plus, the noise levels are impressively low, allowing me to immerse myself fully in my games.
Overall, the montech xr Gaming Computer Case offers fantastic value for money. Whether you’re a casual gamer or a hardcore enthusiast, this case has everything you need to showcase your build beautifully. Highly recommend!
reviews.author: Eli

reviews.title: Hands down best value for the price it’s at
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/B1DdFn10gPL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/51zNa3fHbqL._SY256.jpg For the price this is the best bang for your buck when it comes to cases. The actual case is metal and it’s high quality. It doesn’t bend or it’s not malleable, it’s a material you would see in a 100+ dollar case. In addition the glass and back panels are very easy to take off and on.
The fans are neatly managed in the back and are very quiet and have exceptional lighting. In addition in the actual case are cutouts for easy cable management and have a dedicated spot for a hard drive, sata drive, and a spot to stuff PSU cables in.
The temps are normal when using it, no problem with that. In addition it comes with three dust filters; one on the PSU, side, and top. My PSU dust filter actually came in damaged but the customer service was so fast and shipped one to me right away .
This case is such a W and the best in the market for an aquarium style case. It has amazing cable management and looks so good including the fans. Would 100 percent recommend.
reviews.author: Sameer

reviews.title: A most excellent case.
reviews.comment: Lots of room, airy, easy to work with, easy to hide wires. I LOVE the power button on the lower front of the case, I'm so tired of power buttons on top, it's not friendly for cat owners because those lovable furballs WILL get on top when you aren't looking and switch the pc off. I also dropped the big front panel on the floor, edge first and while giving me a stroke and fear of it shattering, IT DID NOT. Super sturdy. Heavy. Good design.
reviews.author: JollyNova

reviews.title: Exceeding expectations
reviews.comment:
I have been a longtime fan of Phantek cases, but I had a relative who didn't want the typical looking case. They wanted something more professional looking and with an understated aesthetic. So, based on positive reviews by, well, everybody, I thought I'd give this a try. I can honestly save that this is one of if not the best case at this price point I have ever had the pleasure of purchasing.
There are many features at work here. First, the black case with dark wood is absolutely classy. The case is well built with sturdy parts all around.
The case comes with 5 built in fans, including 2 170mm fans up front. The 120's on the bottom have 11 blades and excellent pressure, pulling air through the bottom surprisingly well. The fans can be moved to different locations completely toolless. It is really stupid easy to move those fans. I chose the front 'gpu' arrangement. The cooling is solid, even with the dust filter (provided) added to the front. (I'm using a Noctua D15S on 12 cores). The fans are all connected with a provided fan hub. Be sure to enter bios and set the fan connecter to PWM or things will get loud.
Connections are easy to reach with 2 power switches. Further, the front panel connections come in a single connector. Why doesn't everybody do this now? Don't they know my eyes are getting too old?
The power supply has the option of side mounting your PSU. I didn't use this feature. I just put my PSU in the normal position, no problems.
Cable management if fine. There is plenty of room, hard points and Velcro to route your cables. There are well placed grommets that can also be adjusted for different sized motherboards. There is also an adjustable GPU support. The case comes with an excellent selection of screws and other parts in a nifty plastic case.
In conclusion, this is one heck of a case for the money and I can easily recommend.
reviews.author: james karl  krantz

reviews.title: Just get it ALREADY
reviews.comment: The Lian Li LANCOOL 217 Genuine Walnut Wood Computer Case is an absolute standout for both looks and performance. Its elegant black body paired with real walnut wood accents gives it a premium, modern feel that fits beautifully in any setup. Cooling is where this case truly shines — with massive front mesh panels and large pre-installed fans, it delivers exceptional airflow that keeps components running cool even under heavy load. The spacious interior supports high-end builds with ease, offering plenty of room for cables, large GPUs, and extra cooling options. With its stunning design, incredible cooling power, and thoughtful layout, the LANCOOL 217 is an awesome choice for builders who want both style and performance in one perfect package.
reviews.author: Steve Gingell

reviews.title: Amazing Bang for Buck Case
reviews.comment:
-Incredible build quality
-Looks sleek
-Comes with 5 fans / great cooling out of the box
-Easy to build in. Having the PSU sit sideways makes routing cables super easy. Plus, it's a pretty unique case design.
-Quiet considering it's pretty open and with lots of fans going on.
-Great price point for what you get compared to similar products
-Toolless fans are great
0 cons. This was my first Lian Li case as I was always a Cooler Master HAF guy. You're basically spending $30-50 less than similar tier cases while getting way more fans included. Just incredibly impressed with this case.
reviews.author: Teja

reviews.title: Great case: both Performance and Value
reviews.comment:
Sufficiently large ATX case with plenty of room for a large GPU, includes a GPU standoff and relief support.
Comes equipped with 5 case fans, one exhaust in the rear, two intake on the bottom, and two very large intakes on the front. The front fans work best in the "CPU mode", but can be slid up or down to bias the air intake towards the cpu or the GPU. There is room for an additional 360mm fan array along the top as well. To support the case fans, there is a fan hub which requires sata power cable directly from your psu.
The case supports an ATX power supply in two configurations which can help cable management as well.
Speaking of cable management, the case makes cable management straight forward and the design, while station-wagon-esque, is elegant and attempts a timeless minimal feel.
The case has some satisfying heft to it and while the panels mostly all snap on or off of the main chassis, the case connects flush with the side panels and has a sturdy construction.
I'm very satisfied with the case and I think lian Li make it very hard to beat it's performance for this price point. While the lancool 207 will accomplish nearly the same performance, the 217 has some slight differences and a price bump for the aesthetic.
reviews.author: Matthew

reviews.title: The Perfect Case!
reviews.comment: The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/D1fAXiB2-yL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/710aYDqhEcL._SY256.jpg As you can see by the title, this is the perfect case. Airflow couldn’t be better, the two 170mm case fans on the front are phenomenal. If you create your own fan curves they push so much air through while being inaudible. The best part about the case how easy the cable management was. I’ve never had such a clean look because you can mount the PSU to face the outside. This way the cables face directly towards you. Another great feature is how easy it is to pull off the glass front and the back. No screws needed and they snaps back into place with a satisfying click and without feeling loose at all. I did replace the bottom intake fans and the rear exhaust fan just for the rgb look, but the fans it came with were good.
reviews.author: Geeky Lion

reviews.title: Great Case, Bad Instructions
reviews.comment: Overall, I was very pleased with my purchase of the MUSETEX ATX PC case. The build quality is solid, and the value you get with 7 pre-installed PWM ARGB fans is excellent. Right out of the box, the fans were properly aligned for optimal heat dissipation, making airflow setup stress-free and effective. Cooling performance has been great, and the system stays cool even under load. The case looks fantastic, with a clean and modern design highlighted by the tempered glass panel. Once assembled, everything feels sturdy and well thought out from a performance and layout standpoint. The built-in dust filters are another strong point. The bottom filters are solid pieces held securely in rivet-like channels, while the top dust cover is magnetic, easy to remove, and holds firmly in place. The USB 3.0 ports are controlled by a single plug and perform at expected speeds without issue. The pre-installed power, reset, and HDD LED connectors were a nice touch and saved time during setup. I also appreciated the pre-installed Velcro-style cable ties, combined with multiple rear access points, which made cable management much easier and cleaner. The only real downside is the documentation. The instruction pamphlet was printed on very thin paper that tore easily, with small text that was difficult to read. Accessing the documentation while working inside the case was inconvenient, and the tempered glass panel removal was confusing at first. Since the glass appears to be magnetically held, clearer instructions—such as external diagrams or simple directional stickers—would greatly improve the user experience. Pros: Excellent cooling with 7 pre-installed PWM ARGB fans Fans correctly oriented for efficient heat dissipation Secure dust filters and thoughtful design features Clean aesthetics and solid build quality Great overall value Cons: Poor instruction quality (thin paper, small text) Documentation difficult to reference during installation Glass panel removal needs clearer guidance Despite the documentation issues, this is still a great case with strong performance, cooling, and aesthetics. If MUSETEX improves the instructions and paper quality, this would easily be a near-perfect product. Note: The included video I submitted does not show the side tempered glass installed or final cable management.
