reviews.title: ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ This Case Made My First PC Build Feel Like a Premium Showcase
reviews.comment:
I honestly couldn’t have picked a better case for my first PC build.
The Fractal North is technically a mid-tower, but once you start building in it, it feels incredibly spacious. There’s plenty of room for a full-size GPU, large air cooler, and clean airflow paths without ever feeling cramped or awkward. Everything fits exactly how you want it to.
The design is what initially sold me—and it looks even better in person. The modern, minimalist aesthetic paired with the real wood slat front panel is stunning. It’s understated, mature, and premium without screaming “gaming PC.” This is a case you’re proud to display, not hide under a desk.
Cable management is excellent. The layout, tie-down points, and space behind the motherboard tray make it easy to get a clean, professional look—even for a first-time builder. You can see from my build how well everything routes and disappears. On top of that, it’s incredibly easy to maintain: dust filters are accessible, panels come off smoothly, and cleaning doesn’t feel like a chore.
Airflow has been fantastic. I’m running a full-size GPU and a large dual-fan air cooler, and temps stay consistently solid. I liked the case so much that I even designed and 3D-printed a custom bottom piece to improve GPU airflow while hiding cables—and the case handled that customization beautifully. It invites creativity.
I’ve owned this case since August 2025, and it’s been rock solid long-term. No rattles, no flex, no regrets. This was my first PC build, but it absolutely won’t be my last—and I can confidently say it won’t be the last time I choose Fractal for a case.
If you care about design, airflow, build quality, and actually enjoying the build process, this case is an easy recommendation.
Fractal nailed it. 🔥

reviews.author: sonik

reviews.title: Beauty meets brains, with just enough brawn
reviews.comment:
I have built in many cases and the North still feels special. The genuine walnut slats on the front, the dark tinted tempered glass, and the brushed accents give it a furniture grade vibe that actually looks at home in a living room or studio. Airflow is strong for a design first chassis, cable management is painless, and the build quality is exactly what you expect from Fractal. It is solid, thoughtful, and quiet.
I did squeeze an ASUS ROG Astral RTX 5090 in here. It fits but it is right at the envelope. If you are running a 360 mm front radiator or an especially long or thick 5090, expect careful measuring and some compromises. The fact that it can be done in a compact mid tower with real wood aesthetics is impressive.
What I loved
- Stunning design that does not scream gamer. Real walnut front, dark tinted glass, clean lines
- Excellent airflow for the size. Open front plus fine mesh, two 140 mm Aspect PWM fans included
- Easy build experience. Removable panels, smart cable routing, captive screws where it matters
- Modern I O. Front USB C Gen 2x2 alongside dual USB A and audio
- Versatile cooling. Up to 360 mm front radiator, 240 mm top with RAM clearance to check, 120 mm rear
- Respectable GPU support for a mid tower. Up to 355 mm with front fans with careful planning for big 4000 and 5000 series cards
- Quiet out of the box. Sensible fan tuning and airflow path keep noise restrained
What could be better
- Tight for ultra flagship GPUs. 5090 class cards fit but it is a squeeze. Front AIOs reduce clearance further
- Limited PSU and HDD space combo. Long PSUs with dual HDD trays can get cramped
- Top radiator RAM clearance. Tall RAM and thick top radiators can clash. Measure before you commit
- No fan hub in the TG version. The Mesh variant typically fares better here. Plan motherboard headers accordingly
- Glass version has fewer total fan mounts than the Mesh. If maximum airflow is your priority then consider the Mesh side panel
Build notes and tips if you are pushing big GPUs
- Measure twice and mount once. The case supports GPUs up to around 355 mm with front fans installed. If you add a 360 mm front radiator the effective GPU length drops noticeably. Look up your specific GPU length and cooler thickness before buying
- Consider air cooling or a top mounted 240 mm AIO if you are using a very long GPU. This preserves front clearance
- Keep PSU length modest if you need both HDD trays installed. Shorter PSUs make cabling and airflow easier
- Use low profile or standard height RAM if you plan a top radiator to avoid clearance headaches
Verdict
The North Charcoal Black TG Dark blends premium and timeless design with competent thermals and a smooth build experience. If you want a PC that looks as good as it runs and you are willing to plan your component sizes it is fantastic. For maximal airflow or the absolute largest GPUs without compromises the Mesh version or the larger North XL are worth a look. As a tasteful and compact mid tower that can still handle a powerful build the North is a winner.

reviews.title: Stocky, Sleek, and Practical at a Good Price
reviews.comment:
This is a fantastic "fishtank" style mid-size PC case. It has great cooling/airflow capabilities with tons of tiny holes in the case for intake and exhaust air in the side, rear, and top panels. It also is prepped for mounting two additional intake fans in the main cabin of the case above the PSU housing area for additional cooling.
It fits a Micro-ATX size motherboard perfectly. Has lots of openings in the mounting panel around the motherboard mount for cables. I believe it can also fit a mini-ITX motherboard as well. Also has plenty of conveniently located anchor points to help with cable management using a combo of zip-ties, velcro straps, etc. It comes with a few velcro straps and several zip ties for further convenience.
This case is even prepared for Back Connect motherboards.
For most AM4 chipsets motherboards, they will not be able to enjoy the USB 3.0 bandwidth cable that powers the front panel USB ports, so an adapter for a USB 2.0 header will be required. Not a knock on the case, just an awareness note for PC builders.
I love that this case has a buying option for additional fans at a very reasonable price.
Because it is a mini version of the V100 Lian Li case, some space is lost in the PSU housing area for stowing away cables and especially putting in more hard drive storage below decks. But with some thoughtful cable management, it is still spacious enough for most PC builds.
Speaking of storage: there is a nice spot on the other side of the MB mounting panel for mounting a SATA-connector SSD (2.5 in.). I don't currently take advantage of this feature.
My build with this case:
MB: Gigabyte B450M DS3H V2
CPU: AMD Ryzen 5 2600
CPU Cooler: Wraith Stealth
RAM: 2x16gb RipJaws 2933MT/s CL18
GPU: MSI GelTX 1660 Gaming X 6G
PSU: Seasonic S12II 500W 80+ Bronze (non-modular)
Added 3 exhaust fans under the top panel and had room for 2 intake fans above the PSU housing (mentioned earlier).

reviews.title: Seems to be a decent budget case
reviews.comment: This is an interesting offering for an ATX case. It is pretty straightforward to build in but lacks a bit for access from the rear to the front. Most notably you have to run the CPU power cable behind/between the motherboard and case to come out in a hidden run sort of way. Otherwise, it would just be running across the motherboard. If the power supply is a model with thick wires/sleeve that routing may not even be possible, so one hole there would be nice. The front and bottom as related to the motherboard are workable. The lighted fans are just molex, no speed control, but the description was clear that this was the case. They all spin up without making an insane amount of noise and the color is soft and welcome. Ventilation seems to be adequate with the fans as is. The motherboard tray comes with the standoffs set for an M-ATX motherboard. For the particular ATX motherboard I am using the parts pack was short one standoff. I was able to find something suitable in my parts bowl, but others may not have anything on hand. There are a few sharp edges inside but found that overall, the look and feel of the case is good particularly when together. I do find it a bit odd that this case is apparently the same as another model using a metal door on the glass side. The same sort of slide to fasten 'holes' are visible through the glass. IMO this is a workable ATX solution for a budget build.

reviews.title: Nightmare Case With Zero Thought Put Into Design
reviews.comment: Cool looking case at first glance, but that’s where the positives end. The fans are cheap and there’s no way to control the RGB colors. Competitors in the same price range offer full control, so this feels like a big downgrade. Cable management is the worst I’ve ever dealt with. The motherboard sits almost flush with the top of the case, which makes clean routing basically impossible. Forget about neat cables or installing top exhaust fans, but there’s simply no space. This is marketed as a mid-tower, but it’s noticeably smaller. I own two other mid-towers and they’re easily 20% bigger. Everything feels cramped. Building in this case was a nightmare. Tight clearances everywhere, constant re-routing, and nothing lines up comfortably. Cooling is at best below average. Because of the limited space, adding extra fans for proper airflow isn’t really an option. Overall, I regret buying this case. I’m already ordering a different one while writing this review.

reviews.author: Theron

reviews.title: Excellent case: high quality, spacious, and silent
reviews.comment: The Flux Pro is hands down the best case I have ever personally come across in years of building PCs for myself, friends and family. - Nicely shipped, comes in a box with molded foam padding holding the case securely in place. - Includes plenty of screws etc. for various arrangements, multiple SSDs, as well as a nice transparent plastic screw case/organizer with movable separators. - Spacious and easy to build in. Plenty of space for large CPU coolers and GPUs. Comfortably fits Noctua NH-D15 with room to spare. - Great options for cable management inside the case with preinstalled loop straps for cable bundling.  Existing cables inside the case (e.g. for front panel) are very well managed also. - Included fans are very efficient and high quality, getting 6 of them included makes this case not only great quality but also a great value. They come pre-installed and hooked up to a small daughter board near the front/top panel with nicely routed cabling. - Excellent and quiet air cooling performance. Using AMD 9800X3D and NH-D15 cooler, Sapphire AMD 7900XT GPU with default curves on the case fans, baseline 40% on the NH-D15 up to about 60C and an aggressive curve ramping quickly to 100% by 80C. The resulting system is totally silent for basic use and nearly all gaming loads; fans only become audible under very CPU heavy loads like code or shader compilation. Most of the time the GPU fan (and some GPU coil whine...) are the loudest thing in the system. I rarely ever see the CPU above about 65C, and even maxing out all cores I simply can't get it much above 76C with instant peak of 81-82C before fans catch up. Of course the 9800 and Noctua also get credit for this, but it's truly impressive how quiet it is. - The HDD rack in the lower bay is easy to completely remove if you aren't using it, for slightly better airflow from the two lower fans pulling up through the bottom of the case. - Power supply is easy to install with plenty of room for dealing with cables thanks to the large mostly empty lower bay. - The mesh front panel and small holes on the bottom panel do a good job of minimizing dust in the case. Not perfect, but very good given the outstanding airflow of the case. The spacious interior also makes it easy to clean. - The USB ports and power button on the top/front panel are solid and firmly mounted. - The CPU/GPU temperature display works well (with required software installed) and is kind of cool. - I didn't really care about the wood accent when I purchased, but it looks quite good and is a nice "premium" touch. - No quality issues with my unit of any kind. A small nit, but depending on the arrangement of your motherboard, the cables from the front panel may be very slightly on the short side. Not really a problem, but for one of the cables from the front panel I had to basically force a shortest path diagonally across the back of the motherboard (ignoring most cable management) to be able to reach the far left side of the bottom edge of the mobo.

reviews.title: Great case, wonderful aesthetic, and even better airflow.
reviews.comment: Absolutely wonderful. It's genuinely a beautiful case where functionality and artistic sense come together. The aesthetic is perfect with the wood frame on the front giving it a nice classy feel without being over the top. The case fits my ATX motherboard + RTX 4090, and a 360mm AIO with ease. It does wonders to help with temps, the larger size and design (upgrading from a Corsair 5000D which I liked, but struggled with high temps) guarantees good airflow and the fans it come with work great from the get-go, no extra fan purchases are really needed unless you absolutely need the quietest of the quietest fans. Noise level is pretty standard, but definitely not silent. However it may be possible to make it very quiet with some tweaks in the BIOS. There's a little rubber piece that was missing where the PSU sits I think (it has been a while since I purchased) but in the end it's not that big of a deal, my satisfaction with how it performed and the ease of working with it far outweighed that little minus. Overall, this is it for me, my forever case. I have no need nor want to ever use another case. I'm so satisfied with this one. I don't think it's possible for this case to not be a good purchase, unless it simply didn't fit your needs.

reviews.author: Gregx0ry

reviews.title: Blown away by the engineering and quality!
reviews.comment: This is without question the best case I've ever built a system in, after 25 years of building computers. Everything was thought out extremely well and everything has a purpose. The ventilation into the shroud area is present front, back and bottom, with reverse flow fans to draw some of that air up to the GPU. The top comes completely off for full access to placing fans, radiators, or even hooking things up through the top while installing components. The top and rear have a sliding track that you can move your fans along to be in the location you want, and the whole 3 fan assembly up front has 5 different positions to move, up or down. The altered direction PSU is a game changer for installing and removing cables and for cable management.  All the cable routing can easily be done in pre-made paths that are all velcro'd. I didn't have to use one zip tie and ended up with the best cable management I've ever had in probably 30 builds thanks to the multitude of perfectly located cutouts and the velcro cable tracks. Included is a quality screw box with strong, good quality metal screws of all the types you will need to build your system. All are in labeled packets. I had no problem fitting any of my components in. Every piece has room and air around it and my system stays much cooler than it ever did with a 4070 Ti Super and a12900k. The case is rather heavy, so be aware of that before you lift your completed system. It is solid steel for the most part and I found very little if any flex, even with both sides and the top off. I highly recommend this beautiful, well-designed case. It is on the more expensive side, but you'll likely keep it for many years.

I love Lian Li and the cases they design but I've been wanting something smaller and with this being the smallest case out there that can still fit a Full size ATX Mobo and PSU it's just one of the best cases to come out in the past decade in my opinion.

reviews.title: Easy to build in; amazing airflow and surprisingly durable
reviews.comment: This case made building my PC honestly enjoyable. Ease of installation is top-tier; plenty of room to work with, even for a large E-ATX board. Cable management channels and tie points are super well thought out, so everything stays clean. It supports a ton of fans — I’m running 9 total (Fan capacity is excellent) and still have space for a thick radiator. With all that airflow, cooling has been outstanding. My temps dropped compared to my last case even under full load. The tempered glass panels make the setup look gorgeous, and despite my doubts, they’re surprisingly scratch-resistant. I’ve moved it around a couple times already and no marks so far. Ease of cleaning is also a win. The dust filters come off easily and the internal layout doesn’t trap debris in weird corners. For power supply, there’s lots of space in the bottom chamber and even with a large 850W PSU, everything fits without stress. Highly recommend this if you're into clean builds and airflow-focused setups; it’s just a really well-engineered case all around.
reviews.author: Jonas

reviews.title: amazing case great space, cable management, and airflow
reviews.comment: I recently purchased the Lian Li O11D EVO RGB (ASIN B0CRKVN35N), and overall, it’s an impressive case with a lot to offer — spacious, clean, well-designed, and excellent for airflow. However, there is one major fitment issue that buyers should know about, especially if you plan on installing a 2.5″ SSD behind the motherboard tray. The Good Let’s start with the positives, because there are many. The space inside the case is outstanding. The dual-chamber layout gives you plenty of room to work comfortably, mount radiators, and route cables without feeling cramped. I installed a large GPU and a 360 mm AIO with zero problems, and there’s still room for future upgrades. Cable management is one of the strongest aspects of this case. Lian Li clearly put a lot of thought into the backside compartment. There are channels, Velcro straps, tie-down points, and wide routing gaps that make it extremely easy to build cleanly. Even with a fully modular PSU and multiple accessories, I ended up with a surprisingly tidy backside. Airflow, as expected from the O11 line, is excellent. With support for large radiators and plenty of fan mounting locations, I had no trouble achieving a cool and quiet setup. The tempered-glass front and side panels look premium without suffocating airflow, thanks to the well-designed ventilation paths. Everything about the design feels modern and intentional. The Issue: Back Panel Does Not Sit Right With SSD Installed Now for the problem — and unfortunately, it’s a pretty frustrating one. When mounting a 2.5″ SSD behind the motherboard tray, the case includes rubber stoppers that must be attached directly to the SSD using screws. These stoppers are meant to act as cushions so the back panel can rest against them without stressing the drive. However, once these rubber stoppers are installed, the back panel’s top nubs — the latch points that are supposed to hook into the frame — cannot fully engage. The SSD plus the rubber stoppers push the panel outward just enough that the top corners refuse to seat properly. You can press the panel in, but the nubs won’t catch, leaving the panel slightly proud and preventing it from locking flush like it should. This isn’t a minor cosmetic issue — if the panel can’t latch, it can’t fully secure. I spent a good amount of time repositioning cables and rechecking the SSD mounting, but the clearance issue seems unavoidable. Without the SSD, the panel fits perfectly. With the SSD and rubber stoppers installed (as designed), it simply doesn’t. Final Thoughts This is an amazing case overall: fantastic space, great airflow, premium materials, and some of the best cable management you’ll find at this price point. But the back panel does not sit right when the SSD is installed with the screw-mounted rubber stoppers, and the top panel nubs cannot latch into the frame, which is disappointing for an otherwise premium chassis.
reviews.author: Thai A.

reviews.title: Stunning, versatile chassis for serious builders
reviews.comment: I recently upgraded to the Lian Li O11D EVO RGB in white, and it’s been an absolute dream to build in and live with. 💡 Aesthetics & Build Quality The EVO’s sleek tempered glass front and side panels—complete with addressable RGB lighting—make it look phenomenal, especially when paired with daisy-chained RGB fans. It really lets your components shine without feeling overdone. 🔧 Build Flexibility & Features This case is incredibly modular. I used the reconfigurable bracket system to build dual workstations in one case (gaming + home office), and it was a snap. The included 90-degree GPU riser, vertical PSU mount, and removable SSD trays make layout options endless. Cable routing is clean and effortless; even in E-ATX mode, it looks neat on day one. 🔥 Cooling & Airflow Between the front-facing mesh, top and bottom ventilation, and room for up to 10 fans or multiple rads, airflow is outstanding. I’ve been running a 360 mm top and 360 mm side radiator setup with zero thermal issues—even with a high-core-count CPU and overclocked GPU. 🔇 Noise The included fan controller helps keep everything running quietly, and the solid build minimizes vibration. I’m getting optimal airflow and great noise control simultaneously. 👎 Minor Quibbles • It’s on the larger side—make sure you have the desk space for it. • Pricier than some mid-towers, but absolutely worth it if you value build quality and expandability. ⸻ Final Verdict: The Lian Li O11D EVO RGB E‑ATX is a top-tier, future-proof case that delivers gorgeous looks, extreme flexibility, excellent cooling, and solid value for premium builders. If you want a case that performs beautifully while looking like a showpiece, this one’s a winner.
reviews.author: Luxvibe PC

reviews.title: Just get the O11 that speaks to you! You'll love it as I do!
reviews.comment: This case is, by far, one of the best cases I've ever had the pleasure of building a system with. Its dual chamber design makes an easy job of cable management and creating a supremely clean build. It has ample airflow options, ample mounting options for virtually everything and it is STUNNING to see in person filled with RGB fans and gizmos! One thing that surprised me is the fan noise. It's basically silent. Just to test, I set every fan and the pump to 100% and it's... silent.  It does a great job at silencing the fans. I currently have all 120mm fans, but I will be swapping out the bottom intake fans to the 140mm size at some point for the additional airflow they can provide at slower RPMs, but even if you use all 120mm fans like I did, you just won't hear them. The built-in RGB light strips on the top and bottom of the O11D-Evo look exceptional if you're going for that Flashy, Ritzy build, too! My only question is... Why couldn't we have had this case 25 years ago? THIS is the future of PC cases. Whether you're someone that wants to build a clean, modern, blacked out look with no lights or you're someone that wants all the flash you can possibly cram into a PC case... This is what you're looking for. Do be aware, however, that there are *ZERO* external bays. You won't be putting an internal CD/DVD/Blu-Ray drive or anything else that requires an external 3.5" or 5.25" bay. This case just doesn't have it... But let's all be honest here, who uses those these days? I've been building PCs since the late 1980's and in the past 10 years, I haven't had the need of an external drive bay for ANYTHING. Get this case. Or ANY of the Lian Li O11 cases. You won't be dissatisfied. You will, however, be absolutely amazed by the time you build your system! The options for mounting fans and radiators for water cooling is ample and the wide open view of your internals, especially loaded with RGB "things" is just jaw dropping! These are beautiful cases and an absolute JOY to build with!
reviews.author: Frozen Acorns

reviews.title: Good Case
reviews.comment: Everyone knows it's a good case. Actually, most people know this as one of the best cases available especially for the price range. I can confirm this is an impressive case and would only suggest a few improvements or things to be aware of before buying. The mesh system in the panels will hinder airflow a significant amount. You will need high static pressure fans for the metal mesh areas, such as the side and top. I currently have thermalright argb infinity mirror fans installed and the airflow of the fans themselves is great, but the metal mesh greatly reduces the airflow. Get high static pressure fans. Some Pros: Extreme amounts of configurations. Beautiful argb light strips unique to this model. Comes with awesome accessories case for screws and such, can store all your pc screws, rubber mounts, etc neatly. Comes with graphics card sag support, unfortunately my card is too short for it, sigh. Some Cons: Metal mesh highly reduces airflow, high static pressure fans required for those areas or just deal with it like I did because I want the fans I have and that's that. Cable management is ok, though is reduced because of the side fan intakes. Doesn't come with any fans, which isn't a big deal as people obviously like buying different fans, though it will make the case eventually cost upwards of $250 and a lot higher depending. Summary: I recommend this case. Actually, I give this case an extremely high recommendation. I've never paid so much for a case and I have 0 regrets, kthx. Because of this case, I now have rgb vomit everywhere and it looks pretty cool, I wasn't even planning on so much rgb vomit, but here we are.
reviews.author: Gary Woodsmith

reviews.title: Excellent case with great airflow and lighting
reviews.comment: This MUSETEX ATX PC case exceeded my expectations with its spacious design, strong airflow, and impressive pre-installed ARGB fans, making it a great choice for anyone who wants a case that looks fantastic, stays cool, and offers plenty of room for a clean and powerful build.
reviews.author: Alexander Kazanski

reviews.title: very good quality for price
reviews.comment: everything about this was great it came pre installed with fans very easy to cable manage and looked phenomenal and never overheated very cheap for what it was and handles very nice all case buttons worked exactly how they should’ve and it was simple, the case is quite large so make sure you have enough desk room
reviews.author: etahadna d.

reviews.title: Nice case but plan your wiring - Read Below
reviews.comment: Overall the case is very nice and arrived in perfect condition. All six of the stock case fans work fine. If you're not going with liquid cooling and plan to add more fans like I did, I would suggest moving the two side intake and the rear exhaust down to the bottom. Leave the other three on the top. The reason for this is that the stock fans are 6pin and connect to an adapter cable that has your 3pin argb and 4pin pwm. There are two adapters cables, each of which connect 3 fans, but each branch that connects to a fan is pretty short, and spreading the fans apart will make it near impossible to connect all of them. As others have mentioned, a full atx board goes right to the bottom of the case. You'll only be able to fit flat cables under the board, and even that is a bit challenging. PLAN YOUR WIRING OUT AHEAD OF TIME AND GET YOUR CABLES IN PLACE BEFORE INSTALLING YOUR MOBO. You'll never fit anything under there once the mobo is in place. The rear chamber was spacious enough for all of the excess cable, granted I didn't install any drives back there. I'm no expert at cable management, but I was able to get everything tucked and tied without having to force the back on lol.  I ended up using the HDD compartment in the top right for a fan hub. This is a very nice looking case and has a spacious interior for airflow. If you plan everything out ahead of time you shouldn't have too much trouble.
reviews.author: Kathy

reviews.title: Good case, but best for a micro ATX motherboard
reviews.comment: The pros: good looking, solidly built, quiet fans, air flow, dust filters, easy to assemble, price. The cons: build space, cable cutouts, cable management. This is a good case overall, but it’s definitely best for a *MICRO ATX* motherboard. You can use a standard ATX, but space is limited. I think cases need silicon cable cutout liners (to hide where the cords are stored and eliminate sharp edges; aesthetically more pleasing). Also, there are no cutouts and absolutely no space at the bottom, if you’re using an ATX MB (standard/full size MB), to route cables which, if you’re a stickler for cable management/going for the neatest look you can get, you’re better off spending a little extra for a case that has those features. This is my first build, and it wasn’t so bad that I couldn’t finish, but I will likely upgrade cases somewhere down the line for a more user friendly and cleaner looking case. Overall, great case for the price and I believe this might be one of the best (price to performance) if you’re doing a micro ATX build.
reviews.author: Brandon

reviews.title: Outstanding !!!!!
reviews.comment: I have built lots of PC's and have never had a case which was better for an easy install. Having the power supply behind the motherboard is much better than having it on the bottom. Sure the case is wider but that means plenty of room for cables instead of the customary squeeze job with a standard ATX case. I used an ATX motherboard and I don't see why some had problems with it. Asus Aura Sync worked perfeclty for the RGB fans and they are very quiet . I would not hesitate to but this case again. It's an amzing value
reviews.author: winet

reviews.title: Outstanding Airflow, Smart Design, and Premium Feel for the Price
reviews.comment:
. If you’re on the fence, this is one of those cases that’s easy to recommend and easy to upvote.
Build quality:
As expected from Lian Li, the materials feel solid and well-finished. No sharp edges, no flimsy panels, and the steel frame feels sturdy without being overly heavy. The side panel fits perfectly and doesn’t flex or rattle.
Airflow & thermals:
This case absolutely nails airflow. The mesh front is wide open without looking cheap, and airflow-focused layouts clearly drove the design. My CPU and GPU temps dropped noticeably compared to my previous case, even under load. You can tell this was designed by people who actually care about cooling.
Layout & ease of building:
Cable management is straightforward and forgiving, even if you’re not a perfectionist. There’s plenty of room behind the motherboard tray, sensible routing holes, and good clearance for modern GPUs and air coolers. Everything just makes sense when you’re building in it.
Looks:
Clean, modern, and not overdone. It looks great on a desk without screaming “RGB gamer box,” but still gives you plenty of room to show off components if that’s your thing.
Value:
For the price, this case punches way above its weight. You’re getting Lian Li quality, excellent airflow, and a builder-friendly layout without paying a premium.
Final thoughts:
If you want a case that’s easy to build in, keeps components cool, and looks great. One thing to add is I wouldn’t recommend if you are moving your PC around a lot as it’s all snap in panels.
reviews.author: Jesse

reviews.title: Great case
reviews.comment:
I got this case to transfer my build from a less desirable one. Building in this case is very easy! The cable management can take a bit of finagling, but it can be done and look well. It's a solid and while compact, does still provide plenty of room to work with. I like the simple, clean looks of the case.
The only thing I'm not a fan of is the included front fans (not enough to remove a star). They can be a bit noisy/resonant on the case. I've read that tuning fan curves helps. Ultimately, I installed rubber/silicone gaskets between the case and front fans and the fans are quiet again.
reviews.author: medivh86

reviews.title: Budget Case that feels premium!
reviews.comment:
A sleek and modern case with excellent airflow. Feels premium too!
Important Details:
- Cable management is a little tight but not impossible!
- Stock fans aren't silent, but they aren't loud by any means. Either way, 4 free fans is a steal, and you can always upgrade them later on!
- I would say OpenRGB is the best software to mess around with the RGB fans on the front.
reviews.author: Mob

reviews.title: Great Case, Minor Flaws
reviews.comment:
Saw this a few times on Gamer's Nexus and got it based on their reviews
Pros:
+ Looks great
+ Cheap price
+ Cools well
+ Lots of room despite small size
+ Easy to install everything
+ Easy to remove and clean filters/mesh
- Fans have annoying humming noticeable when room is quiet
- GPU makes contact with case near front of case
- Not a lot of room on the side for cable management. Recommend flat cables
- No reset button ,only power button
- No filter for bottom back intake
~ LED fans cannot be manged in Linux
reviews.author: Brandon Nass

reviews.title: The perfect pc case (w/ room for improvements)
reviews.comment:
This is an amazing case.
1. Airflow is just perfect, at most you'll need 3 additional fans for exhaust, no need for to buy extra intake fans.
2. RGB looks good and can be disabled if wanted for stealth look.
3. It has built in GPU Support bracket to avoid sag.
4. Opening/Closing is really well design, building a pc is a delight as well as changing components.
5. Front USB-C is a nice detail.
6. Enough space for large gpu and cpu cooling
7. The best case on it's price range.
Cons:
1. Due to the placement of the PSU, you might need a modular power supply.
2. Manually switching the PSU requires screwing (fortunately it's a easy screw by hand).
3. Cable management could be difficult on complex builds (RGA controllers, etc). For simple builds this is not a real issue imo.
4. Power supply air intake could have a bit more room.
5. Graphics card intake doesn't have a filter, could led to pet hair / more dust getting into the system. (easily fixable by using a DIY PC Case Dust Mesh Filter).
reviews.author: Robert

reviews.title: Great Case for Budget Builds!
reviews.comment: Wonderful tower case for the price. Plenty of room for a Micro-ATX build, and I’d imagine a full size ATX would be more than feasible. Fans are PWM capable, but the power cable from the fan hub is a 3 pin, so through the hub you won’t get PWM control. Still worth it though, the noise is noticeable in a quiet room but hardly notice it while doing anything. I’d rather have slightly noisy fans that actually cool the pc adequately, which these do. Cable management is very easy, though the ARGB and PWM headers from the fans going into the hub are mildly tangled, it’s pretty easy to manage them still. Though there’s room for more fans to be mounted, I think depending on your build the four that come pre installed may be more than enough. The overall look of the case is very clean and the tempered glass allows for a nice look into the case to admire your build. Case comes with plenty of screws and standoffs for mounting as needed, and though it doesn’t come with a physical manual, you can easily find one online by searching the case model name + user manual. Overall I’m very happy with this case and would recommend if you need a M-ATX or ATX case and care about airflow, aesthetics, and affordability this is a solid case to get.
reviews.author: Sk8rboi_87

reviews.title: Very good Case
reviews.comment: You hear from time to time "what's in a case?" Regarding this case? Quite a bit. It fits an ATX motherboard just fine. The (4) Fans do an amazing job at keeping  the inside very cool. The case also has a built in fan hub that all the fans connect to and also an ARGB output if your motherboard supports it (mine does). If your motherboard doesn't have an ARGB input there is a button on the top of the case that marked "LED" and you can press that numerous times changing the colors or how the fan lights display. The case also supports a USBC hook up if your mother board supports the connection (mine does) which comes in pretty handy. The case also supports USB3 and HD Audio connections to your mother board. The case is nice and light but very sturdy and the side glass is "real glass" and adds a nice touch. Price point was nice for what you get. So if you're looking for a mid-tower with a fair amount of room I would highly recommend this case.
reviews.author: Jer

reviews.title: Good PC case but has ONE flaw
reviews.comment: I really liked the car, the build quality is pretty good, it cools my Ryzen 5 3600 and GTX 1660 just fine with my 2 intake 120mm fans and one 120mm in the rear, I used the black one when I brought the non-mesh model but the white one looks pretty good, If I were Gamdias, I would remove the tinted tempered glass side panel, there’s a bunch of cases on that price that does not have tinted glass panels, I just think that it just cost more to manufacture it than leaving the side panel clear, like why would I not like to see the work I did on the case after I just built the pc in it? It has RGB which I liked, it’s using proprietary connectors for the fan to power and light functionality but you can always buy a rgb hub to connect the case fan and other ARGB products to it but I have a feeling that the light button on the case would not let you unplug from the stock case fan rgb to the aftermarket ARGB controller.. for a $60 case, I think it should have removable but reusable PCIE brackets so if you plan on selling the case in a few years after they discontinue this case, then you can pop them on no problem. But besides all the rant, it’s easy to build on. 4-5 stars.
reviews.author: Jonathan H

reviews.title: Great value, sturdy and looks good as well
reviews.comment: This review is for the Gamidas Argus M1 ATX gaming case. They offer a different case with three front fans but this one has a LED lighting slash across the front. I read reviews of the case where some complained about there not being spaces for a 3.5” HDD but mine did have two spaces in a rack accessible from the back side. My primary HDD is a solid state M.2 but I also use a 2TB 3.5” HDD for additional storage. This case seemed very sturdy and well constructed and has a tempered glass side panel. I used Ryzen 7 CPU that came with a heat sink. The heat sink and fan fit perfectly with room to spare. The LED slash across the front is kind of cool but and not distracting. My case came with two installed silent fans (not LED) but I preferred it that way. The only hesitation one might have is the lack of an optical drive bay so if needed, you would have to set up a external drive. I have no need for an optical drive so this was of no consequence to me. Once completed, the computer is a bit heavier than most (probably from the glass side panel) but that is not a problem for me. All in all I consider this case a steal at the sale price I got it for. It’s solid, looks great, comes with 2 silent case fans and magnetic dust screens. I have paid twice as much for much poorer quality in the past. I would buy it again in a heartbeat.
reviews.author: tip909

reviews.title: Worked for us
reviews.comment: Good quality, good price, looks decent, very easy to set up. No complaints!
reviews.author: Seth Williams

reviews.title: A great solid case for the money and looks!!!
reviews.comment: Case is amazing. It looks solid. And for how solid it looks it’s not heavy at all. There is tons of space for cable management. It looks clean and lots of fans. It looks tool less and screw less for the most part and it will be easy for my son to build his first time PC. It was very affordable and the case is solid and good quality material. A right mixture of plastic, glass in order to see the work and metal. I love that the PSU will be hidden once it’s built.
reviews.author: Kami Pereira

reviews.title: Excellent case and overall value for the price!
reviews.comment: Fantastic case at a very reasonable price. Plenty of room for wiring and my system's components. The fans are pretty quiet while still providing great airflow. The case fits in my leg mount adapter on my Secretlab Magnus Pro and complements the overall aesthetic of the desk with its sleek and classy look. The ventilation is excellent, and I removed the feet to optimize the look since its mounted. I had to use some tape to cover the open holes left by the mounting dowels for the feet, but no big deal. I especially enjoy how functional the glass side panel is for supporting easy removal and replacement for quick access to my system's components. The unit came pretty much fully assembled, so set up really boiled down to transferring my system components from the old case to the new one. All ports and wiring worked as they should OOTB. I am extremely pleased with this purchase overall!
reviews.author: Bill

reviews.title: Really good for the price
reviews.comment: Plenty of space, good looking fans with good airflow and cooling. Very quiet, can sometimes make a faint, almost angelic hum which I find quite pleasent. Thin metal, but is smoothed down so you don’t cut yourself. Plenty of space in the drive bay, and the SSD mounts are a nice touch. Cable management system is nothing special but gets the job done, and I appreciated that it came with zip ties for this. It can be hard to plug stuff into the bottom motherboard headers (if you are using ATX) so I recommend removing or pushing out of the way. the bottom fans before building. One thing is that the fans are daisy chained with a non-standard connector, but unless you plan to replace them while keeping some of the original, this shouldn’t be too much of an issue. Overall excellent case for the price, would recommend.
reviews.author: Isaiah Nabatian

reviews.title: Great deal on a good 6 fan case 2 thumbs up
reviews.comment: It is a light weight case but fully functional. Great budget build in a stylish 6 included fan case. It has Newer ARGB 5V light harness so you need a converter from 12V to 5V on older RGB motherboards. Other than that everything went well. I even moved the 3 bottom fans to top where they actually mover more air. The wiring is short on the fans so had to spin the 2 side fans to daisy chain all 6 together. Large bottom area if longer power supply. The Drive tray is removable and has 2 SSD drive holders on the back motherboard mounting plate area. Two Thumbs Up for $70.
reviews.author: GZ

reviews.title: Extra Wide - Great for Large CPU Coolers!
reviews.comment:
This is a good quality case and I am glad I went with this as it was wide enough for my CPU cooler. I wish it came with extra fan screws, as I purchased extra fans but couldn't install as neither came with hardware haha. Otherwise is quiet, no vibrations.
Overall arrangement is good, lots of options for cable management. The two glass walls make for a gorgeous view of the interior. No assembly required on the case. The removable glass panel is a bit hard to pry away, but it goes back together with ease.
reviews.author: Ben

reviews.title: High quality and enough space (and some)
reviews.comment:
I had a slim form factor computer with M-ATX components that were beginning to show age. I effectively gave it to my 10-year old son for his minecraft and occasional writing. I had an Intel Core i3 from 2011 with integrated graphics HD-200. It was good enough for Minecraft although it got "laggy" occasionally according to my son. So I thought it was probably due to the integrated graphics performance. These days, CPU performance improvements seem to have hit a ceiling and I don't really see significant performance improvement from generations to generations, except maybe when you run heavy-duty applications like video editing and large data set processing. For browsing, youtube, minecraft, I suspect new SSD drives and graphic cards would address the bottlenecks better.
Since the slim factor case was too small for any graphic cards, I had to buy a new case. I didn't want to buy a regular ATX case, because he's only 10. I don't expect him to need 3 hard drives, 2 graphic cards, water cooling systems, 1000W PSU in the next 3 years. Micro-ATX seems to be the sweet spot for sufficient expansion flexibility and efficient space. I also wanted a good quality case. My last one was partially made of plastics (it had two plastic stands to stand up the main case that recently broke). I want to build a cost effective, high quality minecraft PC that has more than enough power to make him happy for Xmas.
For this purpose, this computer case is really PERFECT. What I like about it:
1. Quality build: The whole case except for the front cover is made of metal (not sure what type), and painted evenly with black paint. This is much nicer than a "high-end" Dell XPS I saw in Costco. The screws that come with the case also seem to have high quality. The two pre-installed fans are made by Cooler Master, not a no-name maker. That's reassuring to me. The fans are very quiet, too.
2. Surprisingly large space: This is a case for Micro-ATX motherboard, or the smaller mini-ITX. But the space left after you install the motherboard is surprisingly large to me. Usually small cases have trouble installing large graphics cards. For that reason, I was going to compromise for a single-fan Gigabyte GTX 960. The heat dissipation probably isn't very good, but I wanted to build a small computer. Then I found this case that can easily support Gigabyte GTX 960 Windforce (the 2-fan model). The case layout is very smart. It positions the 5.0 and 3.5 internal bays on top, the PSU and additional hard-drive bays at the bottom. So the middle part is wide open. You effectively have the entire front to back case depth to install your graphic card. It handles my Gigabyte with so much easy. I suspect I could've installed a 3-fan model if I had wanted to. And then on storage bays, I have a DVD drive, a hard drive only, which I put all on the top internal bay. There is another internal rack that can host 3 3.5 HDs. I doubt I'd ever need that many drives. In total, with 1 DVD rom, 1 HD, 1 mATX motherboard, 1 2-fan graphic card, 1 WIFI PCI card, 1 mTAX 450X PSU, the stock CPU fan, the case inside doesn't seem crowded at all. It's not empty, just well utilized. Very smart design for a mATX case.
3. Reasonable cost: 49.99. If you buy from newegg, I saw a $20 rebate. I just skipped the hassle and bought here. This is a pretty decent price.
What I don't like about it:
1. It supports ATX PSU. This would be a plus to most people because of the ATX PSU flexibility and power. I already have a mATX PSU. Thus I needed a converter plate. Fortunately I saved the mATX to ATX converter plate that came with my PSU (which I bought a year ago). It didn't turn out to be an issue for me, but if I had bought my PSU many years ago, or it came from another pre-assembled PC, I would've been out of luck. My point is, this is a mATX case. It's great that it can support ATX PSU, but it should include a converter for mATX PSU.
2. The HD audio head for the front audio panel got broken when I tried to install / uninstall / reinstall it over the 2 days as I received several upgrade components (e.g. the WIFI PCI card). Because of the limited space, I needed to unplug the head from the motherboard a couple of times to make room. It was really hard to reach the head itself, so I pulled the wire attached to the head. After a few times, the speaker wire came off. I was able to fix it myself in 30 minutes. But it worried me a little at first that I had to buy another case. Net net, this might not be the vendor's fault, but I wished the wire fixture were stronger. Next time I will be very careful.
In summary, this case is great for me: a minimalist and (somewhat) perfectionist. It has just enough space (and a little extra) for a high quality mTAX build with high-end graphic cards, quality and quiet fans and case build quality and materials, and at a good price. If you want a monster case to play with constant upgrades, this might not be for you. I just wanted a good case for a good 10-year old boy's game PC and then be done with it. This worked really well for me. My son is super happy. :-)
reviews.author: XL

reviews.title: Great case, somewhat retro look
reviews.comment: Very good case. I bought it because it reminded of some older cases I owned a decade or two ago. Metal is a decent thickness so it won't fall apart anytime soon. Comes with thumb tightened screws so it's easy to take apart, which makes it very easy to clean. Airflow is pretty good due to the two fans input in front, an exhaust fan in back and another exhaust on top. There's also a fan port on the side panel, but I don't need that one. I just wish it had more room for hard drives.
reviews.author: Dyhhan

reviews.title: Great case for the price, only 1 issue to consider
reviews.comment:
This is a great computer case for a budget build. It is a well constructed steel chassis that is great for a mATX motherboard build. I liked the front ports and the ability to add a DVD/Bluray drive. I had no issues adding my components to the case either.
There is one issue to consider though, and the reason why I dropped this down to 4 stars. The fan on the front has a bit more RPM than most fans I've worked with and for some reason it sounds very noisy and annoying with how it lays against the front grill. When taking it out, the noise was almost a non-issue, but when it was inside against the case, it was an issue. My theory is that the airflow going through the grill created the sound problem.
I had a solution to fixing this issue. I took two steps: the first was to replace the fan with a better fan that didn't spin as fast. This fan still created the sound, but it was less noticeable. The second and more important change was that I went to a hardware store and bought a few small rubber washers that I added as padding between the fan and the case, which allowed the fan to sit back maybe a quarter inch or so which helped prevent the airflow from creating the noise against the fan. Now it's a 5 star case!
reviews.author: Kyle N.

reviews.title: Still an excellent mATX case
reviews.comment:
I have built a number of computers utilizing this case and it is one of my all-time favorites.
The Good
Supports more 3.5” hard drives than anyone should ever need in the modern era of SSDs and M-2s. If you don’t need it the hard drive cage at the bottom of the case can be removed.
Supports multiple SSDs, but the one at the top of the case is usually the only one I need. The ease of removing and installing that one is appreciated.
The case comes with a bottom mounted power supply with a removable dust filter.
The location of the hard drive cage and the other drive mounts leaves lots of room in the middle of the case to install large video cards.
Never have had any issues using air cooling with this case, but it will also support 240mm liquid cooling solutions if you are a gamer.
For those who want a neat build there is some room for cable management between the side panel and the internals.
I never feel cramped for space when building with this case.
Other Stuff
I would rather have two USB 3 connections on the front panel. But for me, not a deal breaker, since I can always add a couple of USB 3 connections with a 3.5” adapter on the front panel and a USB 3 card on the motherboard.
I like this case best without an optical drive since it looks better without breaking the flow of the front panel. That is becoming less of a problem these days since CD’s & DVD’s have gone the way of the cassette in this era of streaming everything.
If you move your case around a lot you may end up scratching the front panel plastic. If you don’t move it around it shouldn’t be a problem.
Although the current price seems a little high, I still highly recommend this case for anyone building an mATX based computer that will include multiple drives and a high-end graphics card.
reviews.author: Jeff

reviews.title: Really good case for the price and feature
reviews.comment: I was very pleasantly surprised with the quality and look of this case in relation to its price. It is well laid out, easy to build in and looks really nice all together. The big 200mm fans in the front are ARGB and have a button the case as well as an ARGB header that can be used to control the colors. They are fixed speed but move enough air for that not to be an issue and are very quiet. I had some concern that temps would be an issue with the glass front. The sides are open and there is plenty enough room for those fans to pull in cool air. The fan at the rear is a no-nonsense standard type fan that can be speed controlled by the motherboard header. I would recommend this case not only from a price perspective....and I am not sure how they do it but it comes off seeming of a higher quality than the price point. The edges and whatnot on the inside are well finished, not sharp. No issues with my hands during the build. The only detractor was that it was missing one of the standoffs for the motherboard. I had more on hand but it would be an issue if you didn't have more available. All in all one of the better case purchases I have made.
reviews.author: M Jordan

reviews.title: This case is perfect. Period.
reviews.comment: I don't know how you could design a better case. The screws are perfect for hand twisting, The glass is super cool, The air flow is awesome, The lights are neat, The amount of space is perfect, The orientation of the PSU and CPU is perfect, It has magnetic dust covers that can be removed and washed, It has USB and headphones on the top (perfect!) and not on the side like some cases, It has a cute and not obnoxious power led, You can see inside the case perfectly, Lots of ties and such to manage your cables, It's super lightweight, Removing the metal plate covers for the GPU didn't feel like I had to bend the whole frame like some cases Both sides of the case are removable in case one part is more accessible from the other side to make things easy. The fans are super quiet. It's perfect.
reviews.author: TonyD

reviews.title: Keeps great temps!
reviews.comment: Overall happy with this case. I've had it now for about 6 months and so far it's great. I bought it with the thermalright Assassin X cpu cooler and this pc stays very cool. It's always at around 25c and when I'm gaming it sits at around 40c. Real easy to put together. This case is almost operates and is about the same size like the corsair 3000 and 4000 series of cases. Front pops off to get to the fans in the front and everything feels pretty solid. If you can get this at a good price it's definitely worth it
reviews.author: IronBuddha

reviews.title: Overall nice case.
reviews.comment: Decent case. A bit small to fit hands in but looks great and fit everything in I put into this computer build. Cable management seems to work.
reviews.author: Steve

reviews.title: Good, cheap PC case with good thermals, but has cheap build quality.
reviews.comment: The case is good and sturdy, but there are some things to note. Without computer components installed, it is REALLY light. The front cover over the triple fans is also made cheap plastic. It's no surprise that the fans are also plastic, but one of my fans' plastic frame broke, but it still works when it's screwed in. Note however, the top front fan is inverted by default and exhausts air, so you have to open the plastic front panel to switch it around if you want. And do this FIRST before installing computer components. Cable management is only okay. The back side panel feels very thin and flexible, even if it's made of metal, and it shows a small buldge if you shove all of your cables into the back. There is however ample room to stuff cables under the metal box next to the power supply. The screws are also not exactly ATX standard, since I confused myself and used the wrong screws from a different ATX case. Just make sure to read the instructions and use the correct screws that come with the case. On a more positive end, the RGB does look nice, and the fans have an option to be plugged into your motherboard or just left on their own. You can also change the RGB lighting with the extra button next to the power button. There is also LOTS of airflow so I don't worry about anything getting over 75°C. It does come with a magnetic mesh for the top and a removable mesh for the PSU at the bottom, but it won't be incredibly effective at keeping out dust. Overall good budget case. It feels cheap and has some plastic parts, but if all you want is a cheap case with good thermals, this is a decent choice.
reviews.author: Luke

reviews.title: Solid Build, Clean Design, but Limited Cable Management
reviews.comment: I recently built my PC using the Lian Li A3, and I’m overall pleased with the case. It delivers excellent build quality, a clean aesthetic, and decent cooling, but there are a few things to consider before making your purchase. Pros: Build Quality: The Lian Li A3 has a premium feel with its aluminum construction. It’s solid and lightweight, making it easy to handle and position on your desk. Design: The minimalist design is sleek and clean. The front panel is simple, with a nice look that fits well in any setup. The side panel is a mix of mesh and aluminum, providing a nice balance of airflow and durability. Cooling: While it doesn't have a dedicated front mesh panel, the case still has adequate airflow, especially when combined with good quality fans. The mesh-aluminum side panel does a decent job of letting air flow in while maintaining the case’s clean design. Compact Size: The A3 is a compact case, perfect for users who are working with limited space but still want to fit in full-size components like a standard GPU. Cons: Limited Cable Management: The cable management space behind the motherboard tray is quite tight, which made organizing cables a bit tricky. It’s doable, but not as easy as some other cases that offer more space and options for cable routing. Overall: The Lian Li A3 is a solid choice for anyone looking for a high-quality, minimalist case. While the limited cable management space and the lack of a tempered glass side panel might be drawbacks for some, it’s still a great option for users who prioritize design and compactness over flashy features. If you're okay with a bit of effort in cable management, this case is a great value.
reviews.author: Victor

reviews.title: Seriously impressive case for the size!
reviews.comment: I’m really loving this Lian Li A3 case. For a micro-ATX setup, the flexibility is insane—being able to move the PSU around made cable management way easier than I expected. It feels super solid and well-built, which you’d expect from a DAN Cases collaboration. Even though it’s compact, it fits everything perfectly without feeling cramped. The modular design is a lifesaver, and it just looks sleek on my desk. If you're looking for a small form factor build that doesn't make you compromise on parts, this is definitely the one. 5 stars all day!
reviews.author: ANH NGUYEN

reviews.title: Great case, tricky planning and build
reviews.comment: The main gimmick of this case is the ability to mount psu at different heights depending on your needs, if you want watercooling you'll need to place it lower for more room at top, want a long gpu place it higher to increase clearance upto over 400mm, want both you'll need a sfx psu which is easier to cable manage anyway, want a thick gpu, upto 4 slots but anything thicker than 2 you won't be able to have bottom fans or drives Pros. Compatible with fullsize components Looks nice(imo) Easy front panel connector Relatively compact Outstanding build quality Affordable Cons. Horrible cable management options Screws come mixed in bag Limited compatibility(may not match the maximum listed dimensions) Parts used in my build GPU: 7900gre hellhound PSU: Toughpower gf3 1000w CPU: ryzen 7 7800x3d Motherboard: mag b650m mortar wifi Cpu cooler: deepcool assasin IV(may be unavailable due to recent ban, I bought it a while before I learned of the Russia issue) Fans: artic 120mm 5 pack, I could only fit 3 with my gpu blocking the bottom 2 Would definetly reccomend to experienced builders or anyone willing to do the research on each components compatibility(or want to take the gamble) Edit: it's also important to mention that come cpu coolers like mine will prevent you from installing the side fan bar, whcih means even tho there is room between my cpu cooler and psu for a fan I can't put one there since the part the fan attaches to is blocked, because of that I could only fit 3 fans, 2 on the top and 1 in back, all exhaust unfortunately whcih means it's a negative pressure system, air can get in through the sides but this will lead to some dust build up
reviews.author: austin

reviews.title: Very cool case
reviews.comment: Awesome case, I was able to fit a full water cooler, fans, and a 3 fan 3060 into it. Very easy to assemble and compatible with many different options. Some of it is plastic, some is metal so do with that what you will. Very hard to cable manage it but I got it to fit onto my desk better anyway so it doesn’t bother me.
reviews.author: Logan Webb

reviews.title: Nice case, but it's much bigger than I expected.
reviews.comment: This is a nice case. It's well-made and very spacious. VERY SPACIOUS. I thought this would be a nice SFF case, but wow, it's big. I ended up returning it because I was trying to transplant an HP OMEN motherboard and build into this case, but after looking to order my third adapter cable, I ended up returning the case. If you're new to SFF builds, yes, this is nice and should make for an easy build. You don't have to really manage any cables, and any aftermarket (read: not OEM) motherboard should have the connections in the right place. Screws and all included components fit fine. You have tons of functionality and can add AIOs for the CPU and GPU. Overall, it's a good value for the money, but I don't think it's a SFF case, so I dock -1* for the huge volume. I ended up selling the HP Omen and building in another Lian Li case, the Dan A4-H20, and love the far smaller build. It's 11L instead of 26L and truly feels like a SFF case.
reviews.author: Adam

reviews.title: Great build quality and utility for under $60
reviews.comment:
I absolutely love this case. It looks fantastic, from the real wood trim and mesh design to the sleek fans and front I/O. It is also about as compact as an mATX case gets, which is perfect for simple, budget builds with shorter graphics cards and air tower CPU coolers. Never had any issues mounting graphics cards in, and it has a functional amount of cable management space on the back. I have built 5 PCs in it for resale, and I've decided to build my new personal rig in it. And yes, I am going to cram a 3-fan graphics card and liquid cooler in here. Because I'd rather build a smaller computer than buy a slightly bigger desk. Someone please help me I'm not right in the head.
ALSO, this just happened today which is why I'm writing this review, I accidentally sat down, full weight, on the tempered glass panel for this case because I laid on my desk chair and then forgot I laid it on my desk chair. Now I'm a fat slob, and I can't believe that I didn't shatter the glass immediately. And I didn't even notice it until I stood up again several minutes later. It is, in fact, completely unscathed, and I would bet that any other glass panel from any case at the same price point that I have used would NOT have been able to boast the same. So not only is it durable, but it's also pretty comfy.
(Please note that the above anecdote, while completely true, is not meant to advise any individual to take it as license to play stupid games and then blame me when they win stupid prizes. Do not sit on glass, stoves, asbestos, airplane wings, counter tops composed of uranium-235, or other potentially hazardous surfaces.)
reviews.author: Maestro2442

reviews.title: Nicely built, cool, and looks good doing it.
reviews.comment: I really liked this case, it's built very well for the price, compact, and looks quite nice in my opinion. The included fans, while not fancy, work well and are silent. Additionally, the components I put in here (i712700K and RTX 3070) barely got warm under load, unlike the previous full size ATX case they were in. Overall, easy to buld in, good airflow, and looks nice.
reviews.author: Logan Mitchell

reviews.title: It looks small but is very well designed and easy to work in
reviews.comment: This case was amazing to build in beautiful to match any build I went black in black but in today's market a nice case makes the build and this is a wonderfully nice case with lots of room and a very well designed layout with plenty of zip clip points and cable layout positions
reviews.author: Montgomory pritchett

reviews.title: Beautiful case, one small inconvenience
reviews.comment:
The case itself is absolutely gorgeous, easy to build in, and quite spacious while also remaining compact. The wood on the case feels great as well, and appears to be real wood
Interior inconvenience is that one of the included fans was not operational, and I had to swap in a backup from my pile
I did like that they included a fan spreader, and four fans, and quality wood panels all for around $60 after taxes. Great value for the money, and an easy recommendation for a wood mATX case
reviews.author: Spencer

reviews.title: Clever $55ish Mid / Micro Tower Case
reviews.comment:
Cleverly designed mid / micro tower for ITX and mATX builds. Good build ergonomics for the $55ish price point, including fan cable routing and 4 (!?) lowish speed 3-pin preinstalled fans so that they're not awfully loud stock (your mobo may have voltage fan speed mode in addition to PWM mode, control may be possible). I wouldn't put the most expensive mATX hardware in it because the metal is thin but high end ITX builds seem feasible.
Primary wins:
High airflow, high end features ex. Lian Li like the side panel PSU compartment upflow intake, neat grille patterns, good side i/o, good cable management options for the price, high quality wood with some sort of certified forestry card (!?), lots of fans and mounting locations, I showed my friend and he bought one.
Ergonomic Wins:
Large motherboard cutout is pleasant and provides extra ITX cable routing options. I tested the power supply length support claims with a 180mm HX850 Platinum PSU, and with aggressive cable management it /just/ fits with the HDD cage installed. Having the option to show off a lot of fans or accommodate a longer GPU is nice.
Sketchy:
The rear expansion slots probably need to be retapped in a bigger screw size if you swap GPUs a couple times. They are terribly easy to strip. GPU support strongly recommended, or at minimum one of the mobos with a reinforced PCIE x16 slot for a graphics card.
Conclusion:
This is the most well executed "cheap" case on the market; the design is only let down by its panel thickness. A nicer version with grommets in cable management cutouts and thicker panels (otherwise zero design changes) would be worth paying more for, so long as it didn't get bigger by more than a few millimeters.
reviews.author: Kindle Customer

reviews.title: Room for days!
reviews.comment: My husband’s build with the Fractal Design Meshify 2 XL has been nothing short of impressive. This case is a powerhouse when it comes to space and airflow, especially when paired with his 4090 GPU. The full tower design offers an insane amount of room, making cable management and future upgrades super easy. He’s already eyeing the next-gen CPU pairing with a motherboard update with DDR5, and with all the expansion space available, it’s comforting to know there’s no need to change cases when the time comes. The tempered glass side panel looks sleek without being overly flashy, giving just the right amount of visibility to showcase the internals. The airflow is also top-notch no surprise with the Meshify name. Even with the 4090 running (and limited fans), the system stays cool under heavy load, and the case design does a great job of minimizing dust buildup. For anyone building with large GPUs or planning major future upgrades, the Meshify 2 XL is a no-brainer. It’s flexible, spacious, and perfectly engineered to handle high-performance setups like this one. Highly recommend for anyone who needs room to grow without compromising on cooling or aesthetics. Warning, if you are running an older cpu and board setup, with a 4090, and limited fans... the case will amplify the noise levels. When max tracing is on in a very stress inducing game, the limited build will get loud. So put lots of fans and male sure not to bottle neck to much.
reviews.author: Raven

reviews.title: Modular High Airflow Full Tower | Matte Black
reviews.comment: The Fractal Design Meshify 2 XL was an incredibly spacious full tower case that gives the user more than enough space to work with cable management. I would like to note the provided GP-14 are subpar in performance and are 3 pins non-PWM fans (up to 1000 RPM), so I replaced the fans with PWM fans. Make sure to note the airflow directions for your setups. I love the modularity of the case and the simple instructions provided with the manual where everything is labeled and visual for hands-on learners. Please note you will have to remove one of the drive cages to cleanly manage your PSU wires. You can mount bottom fans to the case, but it will be moot from all the metal/wire obstructions. The case is extremely sturdy, and it has a clean matte black finish. The top of the case can support up to a 480 mm radiator, the front can support up to 480 mm, and the rear of the case can support a 140mm fan (check for clearance if your top AIO is big). I appreciate how Meshify has many air filters that trap dust particles (can be removed if you want more airflow). I had also fitted an EATX motherboard and just removed the rubber grommets to the right for my wires. If you're lacking length in the case, I suggest you use a fan extension cable for a clean look. This is the case people are looking for high-end builds and mass storage configurations.
reviews.author: Paul Luu

reviews.title: Great full tower case.
reviews.comment: This is my second Fractal case. I have a mid tower as well. Very pleased with both cases. If you need a full tower this is a great case. There is a lot of flexibility built in as to where you can mount things as well as various uses for the case. For me this was for a gaming PC and I needed more space for my GPU. There is a lot of built in cable management as well as several different options for routhing cables through the case. Easy to take the top, front and side panels off and I like the built in filters on the top bottom and front.
reviews.author: FloTownTiger

reviews.title: It's so big and black 😳
reviews.comment: The 2 XL is the cream of the crop, the king of all ATX cases, one that leaves so much room that you won't know what to do with it until you find a nerdy comic book statue to fill the space in the void in your heart. There is plenty of room in the back for proper wire management, so you have no excuses to create a spaghetti mess. Seriously, with the 140mm fan placement in the case, you’re going to create the best possible airflow, not to mention with this amount of space, there isn’t an issue with the hot air not being displaced correctly. Way down the line, when you’re done with this case, you can repurpose it as a server or even a NAS, given how many hard drives you can install on the chassis.
reviews.author: William

reviews.title: Excellent case
reviews.comment: This thing is huge with enough space to do what I want to do (although I'm not using an odd-shaped EE whatever it's called or an E-ATX). I wish it was a little taller so you could have a 420 radiator upfront a 140mm fan up top towards the front and dvd/cd read/write drive in the front I do agree with the door not opening enough to get the finer filter out. I don't know what people are complaining about it being flimsy but the glass does make me nervous and just like any computer, the plastic clips for the front cover are nerve racking but these are common. The only complaint I have (for me anyway) is the two trays for 2.5" drives that you can put in top of the PSU, for $50 a pair?! Really?! This case is like a Transformer, you can do all sorts of wacky things with this thing as far as relocating things but damn if it's not hurting my bank account for the layout I need out of necessity (not for fun).
reviews.author: Terrible T.

reviews.title: A surprisingly good little case!
reviews.comment:
I wasn't expecting much from this case, but this little guy is surprisingly sturdy and easy to build in.  I just wanted something that looked decent for a living room gaming PC.  That meant it had to be small and without a lot of distracting RGB.  I was going to go for a fully mesh case until I saw this. It fit perfectly into the space I had, and was more than big enough for the components I planned to use.
Those components are an MSI B550 MATX motherboard with a Ryzen 5600, Powercolor Radeon 7700XT and Maingear 850w PSU.  There are zero issues with space, although I DID try using an XFX 6800XT and the case was just a few MM too small for that.
Building was easy, since just about every panel is easily removed.  The only exception is the front glass panel, which requires a few screws to be removed first. Instructions would have come in handy there, but documentation is one area where this case is sorely lacking.  They may as well not exist. If you've ever built a PC before you won't really need them, but it would have saved some time with that front panel.  Fortunately, it doesn't really NEED to come off anyway--it just makes things a little easier.
There's plenty of space for cable management although a modular power supply is ideal. That's par for the course with smaller cases.  There's room on the top for a 240mm radiator, but I went with air--the Thermalright Phantom Spirit.  The 3 included fans are perfectly sufficient for airflow, and they aren't especially noisy unless they have to ramp up quite a bit--something that shouldn't be necessary unless you have a pretty aggressive fan curve set.  I didn't see any need to add fans to the top.  If you want RGB, obviously you will need to replace them.
If you're looking for a small fishtank-style case on a budget, you could certainly do worse than this--just make sure it fits your GPU.  If you don't mind a more traditionally-sized tower-- and you  can spend $10-$15 extra dollars--there are better cases on Amazon that won't break the bank (I also like the Montech XR) but if small + tempered glass is what you're looking for, this is worth considering!
reviews.author: Tmach

reviews.title: Overall a decent product with a few minor caveats.
reviews.comment:
When I picked up this case on sale (39.99$), I wasn't exactly anticipating it to be particularly great to build in. Initially, I anticipated the fans to be excessively loud and for measurements to be off somewhere. I was very wrong.
Don't get me wrong, this product is by no means perfect, but for the 40-50$ you can often find this little guy at, it's a pretty good bargain. This is one of the very few super budget cases I can find myself recommending new builders to consider.
The case overall is a pretty good size. It's compact enough to avoid eating up all of your desk space, while remaining just large enough to maintain good airflow to components and easy to build in. The magnetic dust filter was cut to a very good fit for the top vents. Cooling isn't a concern either, with components remaining well within acceptable margins. I also really like how the GPU can pull fresh air directly through the bottom of the front chamber. Additionally, the hard drive cage is really nicely put together, although I do suggest removing it when cable managing, especially if you don't have a modular power supply.
My only relatively minor issue with this case comes from the cable management channels for the headers at the bottom of the motherboard. The distance between the back of the power supply unit, in my case a Corsair CX650M is a little bit lackluster. If you have a motherboard with less-than-ideal header placement at the bottom, especially the USB 3.1 header, you may find that you have to use the larger cutouts to the right of the board, so do keep that in mind. Additionally, although the product listing photos show the front chamber to be a metallic silver, it's actually painted black.
Overall, while this is no Lian Li O11 Evo, this case has a lot of value to offer and is priced very fairly when keeping its minor flaws in mind.
reviews.author: J.L.

reviews.title: Great Bang for the Buck!  Just order it already.
reviews.comment: Great little case!  Not the thickest metal, nor the strongest feeling glass...but its $50.  I didnt use the fans that came with it so i cannot comment on those.  i swapped in 3 intake and 3 exhaust fans.  My GPU sits at 61C while AAA gaming for an hour so it has great airflow if you set it up right.  While cable management is tight and i could do with some small changes I cannot give it less than 5 stars given the value here.
reviews.author: HaveTaco_WillTravel

reviews.title: Great case for the Price!!
reviews.comment:
Very happy with my build!
Pro: good airflow and temperatures for a 5080 and 130w CPU.
Pro: attractive design
Pro: easy to figure out
Con: small amount of cable management space IF you keep the drive tray attached inside (I did not, see pics)
Con: the rear panels that you remove for the GPU are NOT able to be put back in if you take them out. Beware!
Con: Has a slightly cheap feel to it compared to premium cases, but totally worth it considering the price
reviews.author: Lucas

reviews.title: Not the best designed case
reviews.comment: I really don't like how the powersupply is mounted trying to mound my 750 Watt EVGA supply in here was a nightmare the holes don't line up with the connectors so you have to force it through very little wiring room for fans cables etc, honestly the intake is meh I put a 120mm water cooler and an exhaust fan and it cools my i9 13th gen cpu just fine the quality is fine you get tempered glass and steel and it a sold case I just don't think it's good for the MicroATX form factor if you were doing a mini ITX build this case might be a good option I just hated the minimal build room and It was a struggle to get my 5070ti it will fit a 350mm GPU but it's a tight squeeze and it's a pain to get the cable look good in the case only reason I gave it a 3 star is because the price was good I think I spent 50 to 75 bucks at the time I bought the case if you're looking for a starter case to put an air cooler in and some fans then yes get the case I think it would be easier to cable manage at that point
reviews.author: Jonathan N.

reviews.title: Great value, Sturdy Sleek and Stylish!
reviews.comment: I just wanted to give a shout-out to this brand and their product before I build (orange version). Though I had never heard of them before, they seem to know what they doing and have an intuitive grasp for how to effectively blend Form and Function. I've uploaded some photos from the unboxing, one which includes a view behind the removed side-panel and an example of their cable management accommodations (though there are more within the case body).
