This 'use-case' is for a small video production studio and I needed it to fit on a short-scale skinny table that I'm using as the desk, which would also snugly house my micro-ATX motherboard. Needed room for the camera and the lights, afterall! Honestly, it's a lot nicer than I was even expecting - particularly for this price.  If you were on the fence about grabbing one before they run out, I'd highly recommend it! (Will upload more photos and commentary once the build is complete) ==== UPDATE: Well, my view on the manufacturers and designers of this product have not changed, but have actually improved somewhat - or let's say, I was pleasantly surprised. I have seen some reviews stating that the instructions are not clear. I emphatically disagree. They ARE minimalist, but you can tell a lot of thought went into the point of view of the person reading the instructions, and how they were laid out, such that an average builder could mostly understand and not have to guess. They label ALL of the screws and components with their own alphabetic letters (pictured), separate each piece-group into a bag with the letter actually printed on it and, they provide spare parts of which I actually did need one - and even give you multiple arrangements for how to hang your power supply. I was able to follow the instructions from beginning to end and I actually haven't done an in-case build for a long time. My last build was a TEST BENCH and you can see some photos for that if you look at my other reviews. SOME THINGS TO CONSIDER: The quarters ARE tight in the case of a Micro-ATX, particularly at the bottom of the case (pictured), in that there isn't much clearance between the mobo and the case itself.  This was only an issue when I attempted to connect the front panel wires included in the case. Speaking of which, you want to make sure your motherboard has the USB-C front-panel pins on it (wire is pictured), because mind didn't, and now the wire is just kind of hanging-out! (not their fault)  But even these wires are labelled as well and the directions are very clear on which is which, as they're all differently-sized as well. That being said, you may want to connect such components as may be required to interact with any of the pins on the bottom edge of your mobo BEFORE you screw it into the case, it just might be a little bit more difficult to get to afterward. But not impossible. I stand by my assessment that for this price range, and even significantly above it, this is a very well-designed and sleek product, as well as being thoughtfully put together and presented to the customer.  I will upload some additional photos of the bags and the instructions for now, and when my lighted fan finally comes in, the finished build. For now, I'm just raw-dogging it with the Heatsink block, but no fans (except the PSU)!  And yes - it still works.  My temps stayed in the 40-50 range at most, and often far below.  Pretty amazing, actually. (note on PSU: I am NOT using a modular power supply unit on this build, repeat am NOT, and yet I still had room for all the cables in that little management cubby on the back which is pictured.  So even if you have a power supply for which you cannot remove/obviate unnecessary cables from the brick, they still managed to all fit here.  And I will add that to my pictures when the fans arrive as well.  Thought that might be something worth mentioning.)
reviews.author: SMITH

reviews.title: Excellent SFF Micro ATX case!
reviews.comment: What an amazing little case! Small yet extremely sturdy. The all metal design is perfectly sleek and feels heavy in a nice way. I would almost say it's underpriced for the material quality you receive. A few recommendations for those eyeing the case. Plan plan plan and then plan again. It is truly SFF. I don't have the biggest hands and even I had issues maneuvering inside it. Things get tight real fast. Make sure to read the instal guide before you start. Everything MUST be done in a specific order. Also get your cable management on point. Has excellent 5 fan capcity but if you are like me and have a thicker GPU 2.5 or 3 slot (Asus dual Radeon 7600) you'll need to pick up some ultra thin fans for the bottom of the case (15mm)
reviews.author: Mark

reviews.title: Sleek and Tight Case, but plan out your build what to put in there.
reviews.comment: This is a well built and sturdy case, its cable management is near perfect for what it is.  USBs are a little lacking so make sure you have a good amount on back of Motherboard, but there is what you see in the picture.  The Power button is unique and neat but it almost like a unfocused laser.  Pay attention to all of the parts in the case as it has some nice extras that most wouldnt notice like GPU Riser.  I would highly suggest a modular small form power supply for the extra space and fitment but the full size will work.  Overall im very happy with the quality, the value, the airflow and the functionality and it's a very nice looking case.  good job Jonsbo
reviews.author: Joel C Allen

reviews.title: Very clever cable management, strong!!!!!
reviews.comment: A pleasure to work in, though I had to re-install fans couple times to get cable right.  Extremely good air flow with 2 BeQuiet 140s on bottom and top!  (I disposed the dust filters except for bottom.)  Theralright Peerless Assassin works nicely.  Handle works nicely to keep people from putting things on top blocking air flow.  Excellent sturdy build quality, at this price. My 1st micro-atx after 30+ builds, and I'm a fan!!  Mobo runs much cooler than ITX with more features and lower cost.  This case is very compact!!!
reviews.author: Don H

reviews.title: Sleek Metal Frame Case
reviews.comment: It's a great sleek metal frame compact case for a MATX build. Packaging was excellent and well protected. Got this on sale, so price was great. This was the first time I built in case this small, so it was a learning experience. The side panels came off easily. Some of the screws inside the case were screwed in too tight, so I ended up stripping some of the screw heads. Getting the motherboard in was a little difficult getting the screw holes to match up. I think I spent an hour trying to get all the screws in, but the case had one less motherboard screw hole to what my board had. This case has some sharp edges inside so that's something to watch out for, because I did cut my finger. This is a great compact affordable case. Build quality is solid. Easy cable access and well-designed cable management section on the side. There is an additional dust filter for the back of the case, if you do want to pull air in from the back. For my build I use the back for exhaust. I don't need the handle, but it's nice to have it as an option. This is my build so others can see what fits inside -ASRock B860M X Wifi 6E DDR5 Motherboard -Crucial Pro DDR5 32GB -Arctic P14 Pro Reverse A-RGB 140 mm fans (2 installed on the bottom) -Arctic Freezer 36 A-RGB CPU Cooler -Termaltake Toughpower GT 750W ATX 3.1 Standard Power Supply -Asus Dual Geforce RTX 5060 8GB
reviews.author: David Lam

reviews.title: Absolutely Gorgeous Case and absolutely huge : )
reviews.comment: Update:  10-2-25  This is still the best case I have ever built in.  Still going strong after almost 2 years and I still would pick this case over any other I have seen since.  I have done some more fishy upgrades to make it my own : ) Update: 11-26-23 My build is complete, I figured that if my case looks like a fish tank, why not add some fish : ) This is simply the best case I have ever had, and will be my show case for some time.  I'm so glad that Lian Li did not tint the glass on this case.  Being that the glass is clear, lets the lights colors glow off the glass giving it even more class.  If your even thinking of building in this case "and you have the desk space" then don't even hesitate.  It is fully worth the money. This was such a "huge" upgrade to my Corsair 680X.  In fact, it made that case look kinda small in comparison.  I have built my own custom desk and it's sole design is to show off my build.  But the Corsair simply did not have the space to show anything.  It was a fairly large case but was very small in the actual build area.  The Lian Li O11 Dynamic EVO XL is simply in a league of it's own.  It was a dream to build in and met all the requirements that I needed to replicate my old build, but in something that would actually show it off (compare to my old build pic).  There was plenty of room for wire management and even gave me space for my hard drive switch.  The build quality is top notch.  If I had any complaint at all, it would be that the blanks that they use in the card slots do not stay tight when other cards are in the same locking tab.  The blanks are thinner, and feel cheap compared to other brands I have built in, and thus require some sticky tape to keep them from vibrating around.  It's a small gripe, but if you have a sub woofer close to your tower, they will vibrate and make noise, and since they are specifically designed for this case, you can't use other blanks to replace them. All in all, this will be the last case I build in for some time.  It is my third, and every time I built in one of the older cases, it just didn't feel right.  This case is a work of art and will fill the bill for some time. Oh, one other small incidental issue is that due to the design of where the ssd's mount and how they mount, you cannot use a 90 degree sata on your hard drive.  The ssd's mount the wrong direction and you cannot hook the sata cable up to them.  I ended up just double sticking my drive backwards to the same area since it's the only black sata cable I had.  Not a huge issue, just something to note.
reviews.author: Handy

reviews.title: The XL is HUGE and amazing, front ports are USB 3.0/3.1
reviews.comment: I lost count of how many times I smiled when realizing all the cool things this case could do like hinged panels and so on. It was a breeze to remove the motherboard panel to get everything installed, and the wiring setups are really great. I bought the XL and it's HUUUGE. The size will be great for airflow and I bought this case specifically because it can be "reversed" (flipped so the PC can be on the left of your monitor and you still get to see everything), though the instructions for disassembling the case could be slightly better. I snapped a few plastic guides off of two panels because the instruction's images made it look like "lift" when you needed to slide a panel slightly and THEN lift. When reversing the case, the instructions for removing the bottom say, "make sure you remove the IO block" (with the USB plugs) without telling you how ... those instructions were on the next page. Also, the USB on the front panel is USB 3.1 for the USB-C port, and USB 3.0 for the USB-A ports; I wish the product page would have been more clear about that. Also, the USB-A ports are not colored blue. Overall, great case, I'm very happy with my purchase. Packaging was great, arrived completely intact, but the XL case is VERY large... maybe too large for what I'm going to need, but it'll sure look great on my desk. :)
reviews.author: Ian Douglas

reviews.title: Evo XL classic
reviews.comment: There's a reason this case has won so many awards back in it's prime. It's a great case with a ton of options. Love it! Will do several builds in this case before I ever consider switching it. It may be overkill if you don't watercool but for watercooling, it's one of the best cases out there. Absolutely gorgeous and spacious.
reviews.author: Seltic

reviews.title: Nice case🔥
reviews.comment: Amazing case, it can fit 2 AIO’s, airflow is amazing. It’s fully aluminum besides the glass, and it’s stylish. I’ve got a 9950x3d and a 5090 LC
reviews.author: Wesley Pavnick

reviews.title: See it all
reviews.comment: The Lian Li case was perfect for my new build. The X870e motherboard and 5090 would need a big case. This case still has room to spare with those parts in it. Building in the case was pretty easy and straightforward. The front pillar being removable to give an appearance of wrap-around glass really pulls it together. Still plenty of room for fans and cooling; in this case, 10 total fans were installed. I have a 360 AIO on the top, and with the option to change where the MB is located, it made fitting everything very easy. My recommendation to build in this case would be to make sure you have enough room to show it off.
reviews.author: Ryan

reviews.title: Great for all-black builds, very much recommend
reviews.comment: This case is very good. The glasspanels come off very easily. The weight is very nice, its light which helps a lot with portability. I decided to build my current PC based off this case. I dont like the fans that come with the PC as its not controllable. I decided to just get other fans that were controllable. The aesthetics are nice, great for all-black builds. It was surprisingly easy to build around the case as the panels were removable, and again- its weight. My only issue is that the front panel power button is finnicky, sometimes the first press you do doesnt register, having to press pretty deep for it to register.  The value for money is very nice, I would recommend this to other people.
reviews.author: Russell C.

reviews.title: Perfect looking case :)
reviews.comment: This is a perfect pc case, airflow is perfect with almost zero noise. The size is small, which I was looking for, and the cable management is also perfect. The only issue I encountered was with the annoying fan vibration. The issue was caused by resonance, as the fans were running at identical speeds due to being connected through the provided splitter cable instead of directly to the motherboard fan headers. I resolved the problem by plugging each fan into separate motherboard ports and adjusting the fan curves so the top two fans operate at slightly different speeds. I only figured this out after ordering a second Okinos Aqua 3 case from Amazon, and it had the same problem. Now I have to return the extra case.
reviews.author: Shan Aziz

reviews.title: Beautiful case
reviews.comment: Great case, looks fantastic at a good price when purchased. Received in perfect condition with everything expected. The removable screen is nice and airflow is great.
reviews.author: Kodaaa

reviews.title: Clean little budget MATX case with nice perks.
reviews.comment: Clean little Micro-ATX case with fans, fan/RGB controller and USB/Aux ports. Definitely recommend upgrading fans and controller as both are cheaply built. Easy to use and budget friendly. Black and dark gray. Compatible with MATX and ITX motherboards. Fits most 2 or 3 slot graphics cards. Fan noise pretty normal.
reviews.author: paquettemr

reviews.title: Overall, I love this case, it looks beautiful, has style, and works very much as intended
reviews.comment: Bought as a gift for my son, so this is his review: Taking a chance with this brand of case with both style and affordability, I was quite pleased at how well the case is constructed and feels.  Yes, the metal is thin and has a little flex, it’s not that big of a deal and is well built.  Contrary to some complaints other reviewers had with the PCI-E cover on the back, I had zero issues with this and feel it might be user error as you’re only supposed to unscrew it a little and slide it back and forth.  The only time the thumb screw for the back plate needs to be removed, is to access the screw for the 3rd slots screw, but because the plate itself has holes for a screwdriver to go through it’s clear this plate is simply not designed to be removed; thus, I encountered no issues, and it worked as advertised. The RGB fans and fan controller work quite well actually.  The fans each house 6 LEDs, and the fan controller can be plugged into the motherboard.  If you press the LED switch on the front of the case, your motherboard is overridden and the fans follow your preference (there is no way to allow the motherboard to regain control of the controller if you do this, you have to power the computer down and turn it back on to allow the motherboard to regain control over the LED controller).  If you wish to allow the motherboard full control over the LED controller and not have a button, you can absolutely repurpose the LED button as a “reset” button instead if you desire as well. The glass is extremely clear, and I mean extremely clear.  I love how well the glass looks, and the edge-to-edge corner is quite straight.  In fact, the glass door is so nice and easy to slide, compared to my ThinkCentre I had before this (which was designed to be easily maintained in the field) had a door that took more effort to slide, and this Okino’s case does.  In fact, you can open the panel with one pinky finger it’s that smooth to open. Also, while it’s not entirely obvious, the fans at the top come shipped as exhaust fans.  One reviewer complained this is backwards and would heat up your computer, however this is not correct.  Per convection cooling, hot air rises, thus you want to pull that air out.  The “skirt” on the bottom of the computer is also an intake vent, and with very fine mesh holes it acts as a natural filter that simply needs a wipe down over time, but you do absolutely want the 3 fans it ships with set as exhaust, or you might trap heat in.  You can however if you purchase slim 120mm fans, mount them to the bottom inside of the case, as the case comes with long screws just for this purpose, that way if you use slim 120mm fans at the bottom inside of the case they can be configured as intake and pull cold air into the system.  There are spots for 2 slim fans, however with a 1080 Ti and Ryzen 5 8600G (both are not overclocked and the 8600G is using the Wraith Stealth cooler it comes with), neither are actually thermal throttling though do get close to Tjmax (both are 10c short, so if you do add intake fans to the bottom, you can greatly improve this). Overall, I love this case, it looks beautiful, has style, and works very much as intended.  I will say this, when you construct the computer and are routing the power cables, due to limited space in the bottom, take your time and have a lot of patience.  If you have a modular PSU like I do, while it is a pain to get cables attached unless you have small hands, it will help with airflow however by not having lose cables in the bottom skirt just for the sake of having them there.  Remove un-used cables for best airflow from your modular PSU and the convection cooling will work far more efficiently.
reviews.author: Michael MacEachern

reviews.title: Best MATX Case For The Money!
reviews.comment: The ASUS Prime AP201 is a stellar compact micro-ATX case that offers a fantastic combination of ease of building and excellent value. As someone who has had the pleasure of working with it, I can confidently say it's a gem in the realm of PC cases. Firstly, let's talk about its design. The ASUS Prime AP201 boasts a sleek and modern exterior that will complement any setup. Its compact size makes it perfect for those looking to save space without compromising on performance. Whether you're a seasoned builder or a newcomer to PC building, you'll appreciate the thoughtful layout of this case. It's incredibly easy to work with, thanks to its tool-less design and ample cable management options. The interior is spacious enough to accommodate most micro-ATX motherboards and high-end graphics cards, ensuring that you can build a powerful system without feeling cramped. One of the standout features of the ASUS Prime AP201 is its excellent airflow design. Despite its small size, this case provides ample airflow to keep your components cool under load. The strategically placed vents and fan mounts ensure efficient cooling without excessive noise. Additionally, the dust filters help keep your system clean and running smoothly for longer periods. In terms of value, the ASUS Prime AP201 punches well above its weight. Considering its build quality, features, and performance, it offers incredible value for money compared to other cases in its class. Whether you're on a tight budget or simply looking for a great deal, this case delivers in spades. Overall, the ASUS Prime AP201 is a standout choice for anyone in need of a compact micro-ATX case that's easy to build in and offers excellent value. Its sleek design, thoughtful features, and impressive performance make it a top contender in its price range. Whether you're a casual user or a hardcore gamer, this case has everything you need to build a powerful and stylish PC setup. Highly recommended!
reviews.author: Alex

reviews.title: Great size, well made case
reviews.comment: Great case, feels very well built and it has no glass! I had some old parts from a previous computer kicking around and wanted to repurpose them in a smaller case for a living room PC. I heavily considered the classic N200 case (which I’ve built in before) but the AP201 brings more modern features which will be more future proof if I decide to upgrade later. I especially like how wide the case is. It lists 170mm max CPU cooler height, and my old cooler is 161mm. Plenty of breathing room. Even with a semi-modular full size 750W PSU, I had no issue with cable management. The side panels that pop off are an excellent feature which makes access inside incredible. The fan mounting rails on top and in the rear are nice to make small adjustments, but the bottom fan mounts are fixed and there is no front fan mount (other than the PSU’s fan). For those of us holding onto 3.5” drives, there’s room for them too alongside the 2.5” mounts. All in all, a very nice home for my old i5 2500K and GTX 970 which I dug out of the closet.
reviews.author: Dan

reviews.title: Perfect for Building a PC in a Tight Space
reviews.comment: I used this for my Micro ATX build and it may be the best product I've purchased all year. First of all, all the panels are removable - they all come off for easy access when building. They stay put when you need them to, but are fairly easy to take off by sliding and pulling. Second, I have to mention the cable management. This case provides incredible cable management options. There are holes, channels, and attachment points everywhere. It's really impressive how much they managed to fit in here, both in terms of structure and in terms of negative space. The air flow - wow. This entire case is like a giant mesh, but it's also extremely sturdy. It's a work of engineering genius. It puts every other case to shame. As my title mentions, the size is perfect if you're like me and had to build for a shelf with limited height. I actually struggled for days to find a case that would meet my height and width requirements, but this one was perfect. It does make up for it with a lot of depth, so if you have a shelf that doesn't have a ton of depth, you may have to turn the case sideways or choose something else. As compact as this case is though, there is plenty of room inside for whatever you need. It's a bit like that bag from Harry Potter, or the suitcase from Halloweentown. The power button is easy to find and press without looking. The audio jacks and front USB ports are also conveniently located on the front in a time when many cases are putting them on top (again, this was imperative for me with limited shelf height). Overall, this case was absolutely perfect in every way for me. I really can't believe how fortunate I was to find it.
reviews.author: Kathy S.

reviews.title: Really nice case for the money but larger than expected
reviews.comment: High quality case.  The front, sides, and top pop off with some effort - no tools required and they securely stay attached.  Case is heavy metal not cheap and flimsy.  Has two front USB 3.0 ports (which is hard to find) plus a USB C port. There is plenty of space behind the motherboard tray for routing cables, which makes for a clean look.  I didn't want a window or care about RGB since the case is on its side on a shelf. Only two cons are the fan that comes with the case is only a 3 pin not a 4 pin.  The other con is the case is very deep from the front to the back.  It is meant to hold a 360 MM radiator. The power supply is mounted in the front of the case, and there are 3 different heights it can be mounted at.  Audio and USB cables are more than long enough for any application.  There are 3 velcro loops for cable management.
reviews.author: Matt

reviews.title: Good case overall.  But it does have issues.
reviews.comment: This is a solid case overall with great airflow and build quality. It’s clearly designed for modern builds using M.2 and 2.5" SSDs. However, the 3.5" hard drive support is not truly universal. The mounting points appear to be designed for very specific drive placements and don’t line up properly in many configurations. The included mounting options work best for 2.5" drives, which fit without issue. If you plan to use a standard 3.5" hard drive, you will likely need to purchase a separate mounting adapter or bracket to install it properly. This should be made clearer, because out of the box it can be confusing and frustrating.
reviews.author: Traye Chesser

reviews.title: Quality of computer cases
reviews.comment: Phenomenal Case – Looks Great, Runs Cool! 🔥🔥🔥 The RUIX OV303 ATX Mid-Tower PC Case is absolutely a gem for PC builders who care about both performance and aesthetics. From the moment I opened the box, I was impressed by the stunning white finish and clean, modern design. It comes pre-installed with 4 x 120mm Prism ARGB PWM fans, which not only look fantastic but also provide excellent airflow. My system stays cool and quiet even under heavy gaming loads. The ARGB lighting is vibrant and easily customizable — it really brings the build to life. I also love the fact that this case includes both USB 3.0 and Type-C ports on the front panel — it’s super convenient for connecting modern devices. The internal layout is spacious and well-structured, making cable management effortless. Plus, the tempered glass side panel showcases your components beautifully. Tool-less side panels and support for 360mm radiators on the top, side, and front make this case very flexible for future upgrades or custom cooling setups. It even comes with a built-in GPU support bracket — a thoughtful touch that shows real attention to detail. In short: great airflow, premium design, excellent compatibility, and unbeatable value for the price. This case exceeded all my expectations. Highly recommended! 10/10! 🌟
reviews.author: Jia Sun

reviews.title: Perfect for the Price
reviews.comment: Case was easy to build in, and the quality is fair enough for the price. Aesthetically, I could not be more pleased with it. I had some slight issues with cable management, but nothing that can’t be fixed fairly easily. My only gripe is that the PCIE slot covers are breakaway, but that’s fine for the price. The case is quite heavy, and as such, seems very sturdy and durable. Overall, for the price, you won’t be disappointed — that’s for sure!
reviews.author: Braxton Kinlaw

reviews.title: Not so good build quality but great in concept
reviews.comment: Its absolutely awesome in design and everything but the window is not good and had a unevenly cut glass piece for the front. They offered to replace it but it was too late because i already set it up, id recommend inspecting it before installing your parts.
reviews.author: zackary alzoghool

reviews.title: A ballin style case on a non-baller budget!!
reviews.comment: It's an extremely wonderful case the hard drive cage worked perfectly with both of my Seagate and my team Vulcan all the fans are working fantastically the build for my buddy to do the labor for my PC was surprisingly easy to wire in compared to a very small mid-tower case that I had before all the panels were good slid on easily slid off easily a little hard at first but not too bad this is a picture perfect case at not high prices if you want your PC to have that baller look but not spend the baller prices on a high-end case this is pretty much your best bet to have a nice show worthy case for a computer build I'll just let the work in progress picture speak for themselves since now I have a firing system and we need to put in a few more components later on down the line but it definitely shows for a nice build it flows extremely nicely having a dual chamber design and my PC temperatures are a lot cooler and I'm not even running the full fan set up this thing can fit maxed out and I'm already running about four or five degrees cooler with my x299 motherboard which is notorious for being a big heat draw again look no further than this for your next case if you want that baller feel on a cheap budget price
reviews.author: Jarred M White

reviews.title: Good quality
reviews.comment: It's for sure worth the money looks good, good size everything I will most definitely buy it again or recommend one of my friends or family members to buy.  PC has to look good because I do social media so it's a good fit for me.
reviews.author: larry

reviews.title: Real talk!
reviews.comment: Heyhey my name is Toji am a big gamer/programmer about this pc now->.  Stunning "Aquarium" Aesthetics on a Budget! I am absolutely obsessed with this case! If you want that high-end, wrap-around glass look without spending a fortune, this is the one. It looks like a premium showpiece once it’s all lit up. The Build & Cable Management Setting everything up was surprisingly easy. The cable management was a breeze for the most part, but I do have one major tip for future builders: • The USB 3.0 Challenge: The USB 3.0 cable is quite thick and can get in the way of the bottom fans. • The Fix: I actually removed all the fans to properly route the thicker cables through the back of the case instead. • The Result: It makes the internal chamber look much cleaner (check the pic!). It was well worth the extra few minutes of effort to get that "floating" look for the components. Pros: • Insane Value: Comes with almost all the fans you need (just one short of a full set!). • Easy to Build In: Plenty of room to work and great accessibility. • Top-Tier Aesthetics: The way the fans reflect off the glass panels is beautiful. Final Verdict: If you want a cool-looking PC for a great price, buy this case. Just be prepared to do a little extra routing for the thicker cables to keep it looking perfect!
reviews.author: Reda.b

reviews.title: Built My Son a Gaming PC… Accidentally Built a Disco
reviews.comment: Bought the ANSAITE ATX PC Case with 7 PWM ARGB Fans for my son’s gaming PC build and I’m honestly impressed. The case has plenty of room to work in and the infinity fans look awesome. Once we powered everything on, the RGB lighting was so bright his room looked like a small nightclub. We added a separate RGB controller to customize everything and now the lighting effects are even better. Airflow seems great, the case feels solid, and everything installed easily. My son loves it, which means the build was a success and I’m still the household IT hero for now. Great case and definitely recommend it if you like RGB builds.
reviews.author: Josh Frensley

reviews.title: A great case at a superior price!
reviews.comment: I managed to snag a 5070TI before the prices explode and it wouldn't fit in my old case.  So, after some shopping around I found this one and really liked the look.  The case design is awesome and while some folks were saying the build quality felt cheap, it feels good to me.  I've had way flimsier cases before.  I loved that the fans were pre-installed, so all I had to do was wedge in my components and off she went!  I didn't do a great job on the cable management but I was in a hurry.  I'll go back and clean it up later.  Even slightly messy, it still looks fantastic!
reviews.author: Shea B.

reviews.title: Case is good- arrived with some damage.
reviews.comment: I'm an experienced PC builder who's built multiple PCs for myself and others. The case looks great and I expect some amazing airflow from it, but I was quite disappointed to find a noticeable dent on the back-top of the case, as well as a smaller "inverted" dent at the mid-top of the case. I will be reaching out to customer service in hopes of resolving it. The case is pretty solid and of decent quality. Unlike how some reviewers had mentioned, the PCIe slot covers in the back do have a threaded screw hole to replace them once snapped off, and the case also included an extra PCIe cover. Everything that really needs "removed" is removed easily and without any problems, though as with most cases, you'll need a screwdriver to initially take off the "hand-tightened" screws. There is plenty of space for most of what you'll ever need to fit, so I'm not too worried about what I'll end up installing. The review will be updated come the install of those parts and the completion of the build. Logistically, there were some things that came off odd or confusing. The manual includes install instructions for fans throughout the case, but fails to include instructions for fans being installed at the bottom of the case. Turns out, you use the hardware included with the case and screw the fans in from the inside of the case, not the outside like you usually would. I purchased extra fans from the seller to match everything, and installed these on the bottom- as seen in the photos. Furthermore, I'd highly recommend NOT powering even the 7 included fans via motherboard and daisy chain, get a SATA fan hub. Pulling that much power from the motherboard is not the best idea, and its probably a good idea for the seller to mention a "fan hub sold separately" for the newer folks who are not aware of this. I'm excited to see the completed build, and hopefully the seller takes these comments into consideration.
reviews.author: Mariella Morelli

reviews.title: Great Case
reviews.comment: Well worth the money since everything works perfectly. It’s nice that it did come with 9 fans, but it was also nice and easy to switch it around a bit. Aesthetically it looks great, and works fine for a i7 12700kf CPU and a 5070 ti GPU. I’d say if you don’t plan on putting in super high end components, these case fans will do the job to keep it cool. Very quiet, and when the fans ramp up it’s not super loud. Overall I’ve had much worse cases, and this one is a keeper in my book.
reviews.author: Jordan

reviews.title: An excellent budget friendly case solution
reviews.comment:
Tried out this budget friendly option for my fourth pc build. I liked the aesthetic of the fans and wraparound glass, so I took a chance on it. I’m so glad I did! It’s a very clean looking case with decent room to build in. The fans are surprisingly high quality and run quite even at full speed. Seems to keep everything cool and under high temp. Cable management is decent. No instructions but the case itself is pretty straightforward.
My only complaint is the orientation of the I/O ports on top of the case. If they were rotated 45 degrees, I would be completely satisfied, but overall I am still pleased!
reviews.author: Michael

reviews.title: Best case I’ve gotten
reviews.comment: It works really well! It looks great on my desk, all the rgb works, and it has great cooling. Its value is good, perfect size, and it’s easy to remove the glass panels. Only thing is that it looks like it has cut corners.
reviews.author: Jon Higgins

reviews.title: Good value for money but not for high end builds
reviews.comment: This is a great MATX case. Wood accents look nice build quality good for the price of the case.  Overall definite value proposition for budget / mid level builds
reviews.author: Andrew M

reviews.title: Amazing Gaming PC case, Absolutely Love it
reviews.comment: Everything about this case is absolutely amazing. The Design, Detail and Room for upgrades. Used this case for a build with a customer. Was absolutely flawless when building in. Every fan connection is daisy Chained, This it only uses one connection per 3 fans, Also the RGB connection was also daisy Chained making for an easy and fast install. Also has a ton of room for cable management. Including little pockets to house your Power supply cables. All and all, was a great and very easy pc case to build in. While including 7 Rgb fans. Would totally recommend this case to anybody wanting to build a Gaming Pc. Look great KEDIERS keep up the great Products
reviews.author: PearlofGr8Value

reviews.title: Great budget friendly case
reviews.comment: So I wanted to write a review for beginners. If youre considering this case, please read this review. The case is great if you can afford slightly better go that route. This was my first time building a pc. Self trained vigorously (Thanks youtube). The metal on this case is a bit flimsy but do-able. Also from what I have learned your only supposed to daisy chain 3 fans max. This case daisy chained four which makes to top middle fan flicker once the pc start to pick up power. This case also comes with an extra 2 pin led connector to control the fans by case button. If your motherboard is not clear on where to place don't place it anywhere. You can control the color via rbg sync software your motherboard has. Case is roomy you can definitely decorate to your hearts content. Assembly is super easy. Also the line up where gpu goes is a bit wonky. Once again for beginners, If you can get slight better do so. But if on a budget, best bang for your buck!
reviews.author: Brian Allen

reviews.title: Outstanding case for the price range
reviews.comment: This was my first dual-chamber case, and I will not go back to the older style.  The 380 TG was very easy to build in.  There was plenty of room to run cables.  Mounting 3 additional fans and a 360mm liquid cooler was a breeze, with plenty of room to run everything inside the case's main chamber.  I also appreciated the motherboard being slightly raised, with grommets running along the 24-pin side.  This allows for the versatility of where to run the cables and wires, exactly where you need them, while maintaining a clean look.  The glass panels look great, and I appreciate that they took the time to put protective film on the inside of the case as well.  The case seems well-built, but only time will tell if that holds true. My only issue with the case is that the brackets covering the GPU ports are not screwed in, so they have to be broken off to slot your GPU into the motherboard.  It may be nitpicky for a $70 case, but I don't like the idea of being forced to permanently remove something from it.
reviews.author: Dack Man

reviews.title: A Nice PC Case
reviews.comment: If you want a mid-size PC case has a lot of room for cable management and to display RGB lighting this is a good case.  It has plenty of room for your components, a lot of room behind the MOBO for cable routing and room for two SSD drives and more.  With 3 fans it is whisper quiet while providing plenty of airflow.  I only added one extra fan in the top of the case.  All panels are very easy to remove requiring from 0 to 2 screws at most.  I only have two (Minor) complaints, one is no bays for a CDROM/DVR drive, but I solved that by buying an external USB drive.  The other is the slot covers you remove to access the add-in cards (GPU) are not screwed in, once removed always removed unless glued or taped back in place.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Plenty of room, looks great.
reviews.comment: This is a sweet little aquarium, with enough lights that you don't need or probably want any more inside. It is setup to hide the PSU and all the wiring and it is still smaller then the last case i replaced with this one. I also holds the 360 radiator on top with the fans installed and is still above the mobo enough to move the fan plugins if you need to. I think they could have made more hard drive mounting spots as there is plenty of room but I just stacked my six in the bottom in the back with room to spare. It come fully assembled and the fans are quiet enough to run at full speed without any noise and with an AIO cooler my I9 idles in the low 20's.Honestly it is so uncluttered it looks like it should have a lizard lying around in there, yeah for it's price it is really nice.
reviews.author: shadowdr

reviews.title: Great PC Case to Build, Many Features
reviews.comment: I usually never write reviews, but I was blown away by the design and overall finished product that I felt inclined to share my experience. This is a very versatile PC case IMHO, great for both those stepping into the world of PC Building and Seasoned PC Builders alike.  Initially the look alone is what lead me to give this TT View 380 a try as I was wanting to upgrade my case for a cleaner overall look, but I received much more.  This case is well worth the price ($99.00 at time of this review), no doubt about it.  It features support for the forthcoming BTF Hidden connector design for those who want to be ready for the direction that Motherboard manufacturers are headed in, as well as Hideaway PSU mounting support behind motherboard, interior rubber grommet access for feeding 24v MOBO connector, SATA and other MOBO cables. I went with a top mounted radiator configuration.  The SSD/HDD tray allows for support of 1 HDD and 2 SSD easy mounting with enough room for cable storage behind.  The 4 pre-installed fans is great, add those with the 2 fans for my radiator and I am starting with 6 fans all synced beautifully together with support for 3 more on the bottom due to the decision to move mounting of the PSU behind the motherboard. If I had to find a con, it would be the pop out PCI-E port brackets. I personally would prefer these to be removable and able to be removed/replaced based on ones need.  Also, I do have a rattling noise from my radiator fans that I am still trying to figure out if it is my AIO or an issue with the mount support, as I did not have this issue in the case I just moved from.  Still testing and will update once I figure out what is really going on. Overall: Awesome Case, Beautiful Case for a Great Price Based on all the features.  This has definitely opened eyes and I even have friends ordering this exact case. Great Job Thermaltake!!!!
reviews.author: Chill Will

reviews.title: Awesome case. 10/10 would recommend
reviews.comment: It’s a perfect fit with my ASUS B650E-E WiFi motherboard, gigabyte nvidia 5070 gpu, thermalright liquid cooler and my 850w century 2 psu. Everything fit perfectly. I never had to move any screws around. I currently have 7 fans in the case and have room for 3 more if I want for maximum cooling; there are even slots at the top of the motherboard area so wires to go through it made everything clean with easy cable management and a super easy build.
reviews.author: Alex Burch

reviews.title: Crazy good value
reviews.comment: This case is top notch. I transferred everything from a musetex case and difference is night and day. Way more of a premium feel for a similar price point. Plenty of room in the back and beneath the case to build. Loving it so far. It looks amazing with my components. Cable management was also super easy.
reviews.author: Jared Henderson

reviews.title: I'm impressed!
reviews.comment: Quite the epic case. It is very large but looks stunning. RGB accent lighting. Gpu anti sag brace included. Extra hardware with an organizer. I have always enjoyed this brand. While others cheap out in quality, this company continues to release high quality products. This case is a steal at it's price. The panels measure around 0.85mm in thickness. It's heavy. None of that cheap flimsy crap you seem in most cases that use 0.45mm steel, so low risk to damage. Great for reusing through several builds. I'm impressed. My only complaint is I wish they had a slightly smaller version of this same design.
reviews.author: John B

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.comment: Everything arrived good and well. No damage from shipping so it was well packaged specially traveling so far away and  a place knowed for damaging packagages. Im very happy with the quality of product it have smooth metal edge the case feels strong, the case glass feels soo good to pull out giving amazing large space to work with. the wires for the front panel is one singular connection which is perfect no need hasle and what amazed me also is that the cable came white if you order it white which comes perefectly with the theame of the build. Overall im happy with my purchase

reviews.title: Beautiful case
reviews.comment: Very nice case, easy to build in. Plenty of holes for cable management. Airflow seems good for a budget case. Front and side glass panels give this case a very modern look.
reviews.author: Justin

reviews.title: Great case, great price.
reviews.comment: Very nice case for the price, I was impressed.
reviews.author: Diana Garcia

reviews.title: Excellent case, very well made, very easy to work with.
reviews.comment: I've owned a lot of PC cases through the years, and this one is definitely one of the nicest.  The fit and finish is excellent, and it's very sturdy.  There is a lot of flexibility in how to set up the internals, and I was able to easily fit a dual Xeon ATX board in with plenty of room to route cables and install a full load of PCI-E cards and multiple SSDs and an HDD drive.  Ventilation is excellent - I built a workstation, not a gaming rig, so I am not taking advantage of the top and bottom fan mounts, but it's nice to know I can if needed.

A little Issue i had was not so clear mounting instructions for at the ATX psu (bottom mounted) and another issue i have is the fan mounting plate is warped and causes both 140 or 120mm double fans and to have vibration/humming sound.  I have 2 different fans.  Wonder if cooler master could send me another one of the fan mounts thats not so warped.

reviews.title: Yes!
reviews.comment: Awesome case, looks awesome and very spacious.

reviews.title: Pain,and painful to assemble.
reviews.comment: Is okay, but case is a nightmare for cable management. For oversize GPU is a tight fit. The psu mounting kit only designed for old school layout psu, if you have a Corsair RM 850xshift, you have to plug in the cables and squeeze it in. The mounting bracket screws is too small, especially for the front I.O panel and 360mm aio mounting bracket.  2.5 SSD mounting is okay but buy M.2 instead to save you the trouble for wire management.

reviews.title: No for first timers, Yes for vets
reviews.comment: The build quality here for a budget case is unmatched in material selection and ease of transport. However cable management and path selection for wire aesthetics is unbelievably meticulous, and RIP any beginner who wants a sleek looking case display. 5 of 5 for expert value. 3 of 5 for a beginner or casual builder.
reviews.author: Jakefromboston

reviews.title: Great quality
reviews.comment: Excellent PC case for a great price.  Nice build quality.  Just what I was looking for to replace an older full size tower I had been using.  Comes with 3 fans and they are nice and quiet!
reviews.author: Brian4x4

reviews.title: Its a really nice, budget case that does the job. I got a corsair rmx 850 watt power supply into it.
reviews.comment:
Its a nice case and despite being fairly small there is a good amount of space in here. The case is fairly thin metal which makes it feel cheap but does it matter when its just sitting somewhere? In fact it may even be a good thing, less metal = less weight. And the plastic panel is light as a feather too. The parts inside will weight it down nicely. The case has a few usb ports at the top, and 3 fans included which is real nice. The fan at the back uses this tiny 3 pin cable that connects to the motherboard, the two front fans use this big molex pin connecter, my power supply had a cable for those thankfully. So the only one controlled by the motherboard is the back fan. They are pretty quiet fans tho, so running at full speed isn't really an issue imo. There is a hard drive area and it comes with a few plastic caddy guides you use to install them in the case, real nice for big storage.
Now lets talk about the issue ppl have with this case: The power supply area.
People are on here complaining about the power supply space and I'll admit it IS cramped but you can get a pretty big one in there with some patience. Really the problem is the cables being chunky, this corsair rmx 850 w  has some of the chunkiest cables I've ever seen. They are massive, thick, woven cables and EVEN then with some problem solving I got them all in, no cutting the case or anything required. The trick is, connect up all the cables first to the power supply if you are using modular and get the power supply in first. The huge motherboard one you may wanna thread in first but other than that do it after, because getting the power supply in will be impossible otherwise, the cables get in the way and you kind of have to angle it in. Then once its in you can carefully thread all the rest of the cables in. I know you may be thinking I cheated, using modular because I only used the ones I needed. WRONG. I installed several extras for less hassle in the future, even two extra pcie power cables direct from the supply for an RTX 30-series upgrade soon. I used up almost all the cables included, trust me you can get it all in.
This is a good case, and I love the aesthetic. That ps2 ribbed look is a look I love and my laptop is a G5 with that look too. And in the case of this case there is a mesh behind the ribs so you get really good airflow. There is a magnetic filter at the top of the case and a slide one underneath the case for the power supply. Unfortunately not all the vents are covered by removable meshes. But this is a budget case so I'm okay with that. Overall I really recommend this one!
reviews.author: Gadgetman

reviews.title: -1 terrible side window, -1 3.5 bay location, -1 "quiet" fans, +1 cheap, +1 good airflow
reviews.comment:
Well I just finished an ultra budget build for a friend using this case so here's my post build hot take...
Pros:
1. Cheap, literally the cheapest option with good airflow potential. This is it's shining star.
2. Quite a bit of ventilation. I love it.
2. Comes with 3 120mm fans labeled "quiet."
3. Will accommodate a fairly long GPU.
4. Fits a hyper 212 with a tiny bit of headroom.
Cons:
1. The three included fans are not quiet and allow no PWM control. There is 1 setting: droning noise. In a room with 3 other PC's it's easily the loudest of the 4 at idle and is comparably loud to the noisiest under full load with a Vega Frontier Edition. You may want to replace these fans if you want a respectably quiet computer at idle. I'm a bit of a stickler when it comes to PC noise so if you're not as sensitive to fan noise this might not be a problem for you.
2. Side window feels awful and doesn't line up or seat particularly well or securely. We're debating just leaving it off.
3. 3.5" drive bays pretty heavily obstruct access to even a modest PSU and make cable management less than ideal down there. I'd probably avoid a modular PSU for this case, as in the event you ever need to run another power cable later on you might find yourself needing to pull the PSU from the case to have reasonable access to see and feel what you're doing. On the flip side a non modular PSU has to deal with a ton of cables stuffed in between the 3.5" bay and the PSU or in the 3.5" bay itself. I'm not really sure what the best situation is here. Maybe tin snips and cut the bay out if you don't need it :)
Misc:
1. There is a bit of room for cable management under the motherboard. Not a ton but enough to route a few wires down there. With only the CPU and motherboard power connected presently in this build (PCI powered GPU) the back side was already starting to show signs of flexing despite a few attempts to try to shifting and flatten the wires prior to reinstalling it.
Final thoughts:
If you're on a shoe string budget and need an inexpensive case to round out your build this might be the best option. After having built with it though I'd recommend just spending the extra 15 or 20 and getting something like a MasterBox NR600 which I've used for 3 different builds and absolutely adore.
Complaints aside the system ran cool. After an hour of running prime95 the i3's highest recorded CPU temp in HWMonitor was 52 C and generally when we were looking in on it the temps were in the neighborhood of mid to high 40s.
I think an update to this design with the 3.5" bay removed or relocated and a sturdier side panel would be great. I personally would have taken a non-window flat black option if it felt solid
Honestly the three included fans are a welcome perk but YMMV if they are quiet enough for you.
reviews.author: Jared

reviews.title: Beautiful, durable, and great airflow
reviews.comment: Beautiful case that has great airflow and opportunity for lots of fans! This case looks clean with and without RGB, it’s made of durable metal and excellent quality. The noise level is minimal with arctic fans, and has plenty of room for large GPU’s
reviews.author: Austin

reviews.comment:
A wonderful and easy to use modular case.
Stylish and easy to clean and plenty of room to tweak and make changes as you upgrade your build.
Want to go from 120 to 140mm fans you can even up to 160mm fans.
You can even swap in the included side panel for 3 additional side fans for more airflow.
Truly a pc gamers dream for making their own build. <3
Super quiet and sleak just a perfect case thank you Corsair 😊

reviews.title: Great product, great price, great looks

Great quality and easy to work with. Looks amazing. Very happy with this (Frame 4000D - white) case.
Only downside so far is my new GPU (Sapphire 9070XT) isn't in the right spot for the adjustable support peg. It misses in the normal slot, and hits the fan when using the extra part that it comes with to put said peg closer to the mobo.

reviews.title: Solid First-Timer Case
reviews.comment: Roomy and easy to build in. The front, sides and top panels can all be removed, and the front panel includes a magnetic mesh panel that can be quickly detached and cleaned. My only complaint is that the InfiniRail system was confusing as a first time PC builder. It's a handy feature for enthusiasts with fans/radiators of different sizes, but for a first build it largely over-complicates fan/radiator installation. Other than that, the case offers a largely pleasant building experience.
reviews.author: Steph

reviews.title: Great case!
reviews.comment: I am very happy with this case. Very airy, love the dust screens, and the glass side is really nice. Plenty of room to work around inside and do cable management as well.
reviews.author: tommy

reviews.title: Beautiful Case With a Classic Wood Design and Great Functionality
reviews.comment:
I used this case for my custom PC build and I absolutely love it. What originally drew me to it was the design. The wood front immediately reminded me of my dad’s old stereo cabinet, and that warm brown wood detail gives the case a very clean and classic look that stands out from typical gaming cases.
Beyond the looks, the build experience was excellent. I was able to fit an AIO cooler and a full sized graphics card with no issues at all. There was plenty of room to work in, and everything felt well thought out during installation.
The case also has a lot of great features that make building and maintaining a system easier. Airflow is solid, cable management is straightforward, and the overall construction feels sturdy and high quality. It manages to look stylish without sacrificing performance or practicality.
If you want a case that combines modern PC functionality with a timeless design, this one is an excellent choice. It looks great in a room and performs just as well as it looks.
reviews.author: Jakari Jones

reviews.title: ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ This Case Made My First PC Build Feel Like a Premium Showcase
reviews.comment:
I honestly couldn’t have picked a better case for my first PC build.
The Fractal North is technically a mid-tower, but once you start building in it, it feels incredibly spacious. There’s plenty of room for a full-size GPU, large air cooler, and clean airflow paths without ever feeling cramped or awkward. Everything fits exactly how you want it to.
The design is what initially sold me—and it looks even better in person. The modern, minimalist aesthetic paired with the real wood slat front panel is stunning. It’s understated, mature, and premium without screaming “gaming PC.” This is a case you’re proud to display, not hide under a desk.
Cable management is excellent. The layout, tie-down points, and space behind the motherboard tray make it easy to get a clean, professional look—even for a first-time builder. You can see from my build how well everything routes and disappears. On top of that, it’s incredibly easy to maintain: dust filters are accessible, panels come off smoothly, and cleaning doesn’t feel like a chore.
Airflow has been fantastic. I’m running a full-size GPU and a large dual-fan air cooler, and temps stay consistently solid. I liked the case so much that I even designed and 3D-printed a custom bottom piece to improve GPU airflow while hiding cables—and the case handled that customization beautifully. It invites creativity.
I’ve owned this case since August 2025, and it’s been rock solid long-term. No rattles, no flex, no regrets. This was my first PC build, but it absolutely won’t be my last—and I can confidently say it won’t be the last time I choose Fractal for a case.
If you care about design, airflow, build quality, and actually enjoying the build process, this case is an easy recommendation.
Fractal nailed it. 🔥
reviews.author: Luke McKinnon

reviews.title: A premium quality case with great features and lots of room.
reviews.comment: I needed a good size case with lots of room for a work machine running a I-9 Core 285k with a Nvidia 5070ti. This case is very roomy and is very easy to use without cutting your hands up. The airflow is excellent with my temps well within expected ranges. It isn't cheap but you get what you pay for. Everything feels solidly built and very premium. While it wasn't a big consideration for me, if you like a mid century modern design, this case has a beautiful look that appears like a piece of fine furniture.
reviews.author: sonik

reviews.title: Beauty meets brains, with just enough brawn
reviews.comment:
I have built in many cases and the North still feels special. The genuine walnut slats on the front, the dark tinted tempered glass, and the brushed accents give it a furniture grade vibe that actually looks at home in a living room or studio. Airflow is strong for a design first chassis, cable management is painless, and the build quality is exactly what you expect from Fractal. It is solid, thoughtful, and quiet.
I did squeeze an ASUS ROG Astral RTX 5090 in here. It fits but it is right at the envelope. If you are running a 360 mm front radiator or an especially long or thick 5090, expect careful measuring and some compromises. The fact that it can be done in a compact mid tower with real wood aesthetics is impressive.
What I loved
- Stunning design that does not scream gamer. Real walnut front, dark tinted glass, clean lines
- Excellent airflow for the size. Open front plus fine mesh, two 140 mm Aspect PWM fans included
- Easy build experience. Removable panels, smart cable routing, captive screws where it matters
- Modern I O. Front USB C Gen 2x2 alongside dual USB A and audio
- Versatile cooling. Up to 360 mm front radiator, 240 mm top with RAM clearance to check, 120 mm rear
- Respectable GPU support for a mid tower. Up to 355 mm with front fans with careful planning for big 4000 and 5000 series cards
- Quiet out of the box. Sensible fan tuning and airflow path keep noise restrained
What could be better
- Tight for ultra flagship GPUs. 5090 class cards fit but it is a squeeze. Front AIOs reduce clearance further
- Limited PSU and HDD space combo. Long PSUs with dual HDD trays can get cramped
- Top radiator RAM clearance. Tall RAM and thick top radiators can clash. Measure before you commit
- No fan hub in the TG version. The Mesh variant typically fares better here. Plan motherboard headers accordingly
- Glass version has fewer total fan mounts than the Mesh. If maximum airflow is your priority then consider the Mesh side panel
Build notes and tips if you are pushing big GPUs
- Measure twice and mount once. The case supports GPUs up to around 355 mm with front fans installed. If you add a 360 mm front radiator the effective GPU length drops noticeably. Look up your specific GPU length and cooler thickness before buying
- Consider air cooling or a top mounted 240 mm AIO if you are using a very long GPU. This preserves front clearance
- Keep PSU length modest if you need both HDD trays installed. Shorter PSUs make cabling and airflow easier
- Use low profile or standard height RAM if you plan a top radiator to avoid clearance headaches
Verdict
The North Charcoal Black TG Dark blends premium and timeless design with competent thermals and a smooth build experience. If you want a PC that looks as good as it runs and you are willing to plan your component sizes it is fantastic. For maximal airflow or the absolute largest GPUs without compromises the Mesh version or the larger North XL are worth a look. As a tasteful and compact mid tower that can still handle a powerful build the North is a winner.
reviews.author: showmestuff

reviews.title: 4.5 stars but I'll round up. This is a great case, no question
reviews.comment:
I really like this case with the solid side panel. I know tempered glass looks great and generally pretty durable, but I prefer the idea of metal since this won't really be a showpiece.
The fans are pretty quiet unless running at high speeds, and building inside this case was really easy. Lots of room and the cable ties make it easy to keep things fairly organized. A 4090 easily clears inside this case without bending the 4X PCIe -> 12VHPWR adapter severely.
The biggest negative I've discovered is the lack of handles on this case or easy way to pick it up. The top panel is plastic and not designed for picking up from, so you pretty much have to carry it from the bottom any time you want to move it. In other words, not the case to go for if you want to haul your rig around to LAN parties.
Something that's not necessarily a negative or positive but just to be aware of is that the front panel audio connectors don't seem to have a TRRS connector, so you'll need to split out separate headphone/mic jacks. Would have been nice to see a Y adapter come with the case so that you can connect your typical 3.5mm gaming headset.
This is my favorite case to date though. No, it's not the quietest, but for an air cooled build it offers unrivaled performance. If you're thinking of adding water, maybe look at saving a few bucks with a Meshify 2 or 2XL.
reviews.author: Matt

reviews.title: Looks awesome, great airflow, tons of space
reviews.comment:
Every time I upgrade from an older Fractal case to a new one, I don't think it can be better than the last, but somehow they've always managed it. For the most part, I would say computer cases are almost entirely solved and at this point you're going for looks and build quality. The Torrent (I think) looks great and is built well, with easy to remove, well, everything. This case is so easy to build in I almost couldn't believe I was finished without having any hiccups at all. There's tons of room to work with and it of course has a massive amount of airflow with five included fans - that alone is nearing $100 these days.
My only complaint is the support bracket for the GPU. I felt it was over complicated and would add even more steps to changing a GPU for a different sized one later. It's still easier to just use a smaller support that sits between the bottom of the case and the GPU. If you're really worried about that interfering with the fans, then I'd use the bracket I guess, but it's like a logic puzzle to put together the first time.
I hope this case lasts me over 5 years like my Define R6 did.
reviews.author: Mario

reviews.title: Very Sexy and Very Cool
reviews.comment: I have to admit I bought this case based purely on looks I had seen it on several YouTube review channels and I loved the clean look of the large fans and the repositioning of the power supply to the top. This unique idea allowed for smoother airflow and a better overall build. I was slightly concerned since I had a Corsair AIO and didn't want to lose cooling, but it was time for me to switch cases, so I took the leap. I figured that I could always buy a new AIO down the road if things didn't work out. I have to say this is by far the best case I have ever built in, and it has exceeded my expectations for both form and function it is gorgeous, and as the Torrent name suggests it stays very cool without much effort. I would recommend this to anyone who has a gaming system and doesn't want to spend all the time with water cooling rigid pipe or any of that other stuff. I mean it's not like you couldn't do it in this case if you didn't want to. I am pleased to know that this will last for a good long time and I have flexibility going forward when I am ready to build in it again.
reviews.author: Alster

reviews.title: NEW Parts ARE HARD TO GET.
reviews.comment: Not easy to find or get replacement parts for this case. I tried reaching out to the manufacturer. They couldn't sell me the dust fliters..but they ((would)) warrant them.. AGAIN,(( not sell them)). In order to warrant them, they asked for information I couldn't provide due to not wanting to give other people's personal information. I was super disappointed.. However,  It's the best PC case for gaming and simple workstation builds, in my opinion.
reviews.author: Supper C.

reviews.title: Not as premium feeling as it looks
reviews.comment:
The case loos premium and high quality online, but in person it looks plasticy and cheap.
The positives:
The case features a very open build style, with plenty of room for creator motherboards and multiple GPU builds. The PSU is shrouded at the stop of the case, with just enough room to route the cables to the motherboard.
The negatives:
It really does look cheap. Sadly, aside from the glass panels (which are on both sides?? Why?? Nobody wants to see my cable un-management) everything else is plastic and tacky. It's not a smooth polished plastic either, it's smoother than being 3D printed but gives the same vibe. The PSU cabling can be a little difficult. Really the most rateable thing is build quality, and for the price it just feels lacking.
reviews.author: gb

reviews.title: Beautiful Case With a Classic Wood Design and Great Functionality
reviews.comment:
I used this case for my custom PC build and I absolutely love it. What originally drew me to it was the design. The wood front immediately reminded me of my dad’s old stereo cabinet, and that warm brown wood detail gives the case a very clean and classic look that stands out from typical gaming cases.
Beyond the looks, the build experience was excellent. I was able to fit an AIO cooler and a full sized graphics card with no issues at all. There was plenty of room to work in, and everything felt well thought out during installation.
The case also has a lot of great features that make building and maintaining a system easier. Airflow is solid, cable management is straightforward, and the overall construction feels sturdy and high quality. It manages to look stylish without sacrificing performance or practicality.
If you want a case that combines modern PC functionality with a timeless design, this one is an excellent choice. It looks great in a room and performs just as well as it looks.
reviews.author: Jakari Jones

reviews.title: ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ This Case Made My First PC Build Feel Like a Premium Showcase
reviews.comment:
I honestly couldn’t have picked a better case for my first PC build.
The Fractal North is technically a mid-tower, but once you start building in it, it feels incredibly spacious. There’s plenty of room for a full-size GPU, large air cooler, and clean airflow paths without ever feeling cramped or awkward. Everything fits exactly how you want it to.
The design is what initially sold me—and it looks even better in person. The modern, minimalist aesthetic paired with the real wood slat front panel is stunning. It’s understated, mature, and premium without screaming “gaming PC.” This is a case you’re proud to display, not hide under a desk.
Cable management is excellent. The layout, tie-down points, and space behind the motherboard tray make it easy to get a clean, professional look—even for a first-time builder. You can see from my build how well everything routes and disappears. On top of that, it’s incredibly easy to maintain: dust filters are accessible, panels come off smoothly, and cleaning doesn’t feel like a chore.
Airflow has been fantastic. I’m running a full-size GPU and a large dual-fan air cooler, and temps stay consistently solid. I liked the case so much that I even designed and 3D-printed a custom bottom piece to improve GPU airflow while hiding cables—and the case handled that customization beautifully. It invites creativity.
I’ve owned this case since August 2025, and it’s been rock solid long-term. No rattles, no flex, no regrets. This was my first PC build, but it absolutely won’t be my last—and I can confidently say it won’t be the last time I choose Fractal for a case.
If you care about design, airflow, build quality, and actually enjoying the build process, this case is an easy recommendation.
Fractal nailed it. 🔥
reviews.author: Luke McKinnon

reviews.title: A premium quality case with great features and lots of room.
reviews.comment: I needed a good size case with lots of room for a work machine running a I-9 Core 285k with a Nvidia 5070ti. This case is very roomy and is very easy to use without cutting your hands up. The airflow is excellent with my temps well within expected ranges. It isn't cheap but you get what you pay for. Everything feels solidly built and very premium. While it wasn't a big consideration for me, if you like a mid century modern design, this case has a beautiful look that appears like a piece of fine furniture.
reviews.author: sonik

reviews.title: Beauty meets brains, with just enough brawn
reviews.comment:
I have built in many cases and the North still feels special. The genuine walnut slats on the front, the dark tinted tempered glass, and the brushed accents give it a furniture grade vibe that actually looks at home in a living room or studio. Airflow is strong for a design first chassis, cable management is painless, and the build quality is exactly what you expect from Fractal. It is solid, thoughtful, and quiet.
I did squeeze an ASUS ROG Astral RTX 5090 in here. It fits but it is right at the envelope. If you are running a 360 mm front radiator or an especially long or thick 5090, expect careful measuring and some compromises. The fact that it can be done in a compact mid tower with real wood aesthetics is impressive.
What I loved
- Stunning design that does not scream gamer. Real walnut front, dark tinted glass, clean lines
- Excellent airflow for the size. Open front plus fine mesh, two 140 mm Aspect PWM fans included
- Easy build experience. Removable panels, smart cable routing, captive screws where it matters
- Modern I O. Front USB C Gen 2x2 alongside dual USB A and audio
- Versatile cooling. Up to 360 mm front radiator, 240 mm top with RAM clearance to check, 120 mm rear
- Respectable GPU support for a mid tower. Up to 355 mm with front fans with careful planning for big 4000 and 5000 series cards
- Quiet out of the box. Sensible fan tuning and airflow path keep noise restrained
What could be better
- Tight for ultra flagship GPUs. 5090 class cards fit but it is a squeeze. Front AIOs reduce clearance further
- Limited PSU and HDD space combo. Long PSUs with dual HDD trays can get cramped
- Top radiator RAM clearance. Tall RAM and thick top radiators can clash. Measure before you commit
- No fan hub in the TG version. The Mesh variant typically fares better here. Plan motherboard headers accordingly
- Glass version has fewer total fan mounts than the Mesh. If maximum airflow is your priority then consider the Mesh side panel
Build notes and tips if you are pushing big GPUs
- Measure twice and mount once. The case supports GPUs up to around 355 mm with front fans installed. If you add a 360 mm front radiator the effective GPU length drops noticeably. Look up your specific GPU length and cooler thickness before buying
- Consider air cooling or a top mounted 240 mm AIO if you are using a very long GPU. This preserves front clearance
- Keep PSU length modest if you need both HDD trays installed. Shorter PSUs make cabling and airflow easier
- Use low profile or standard height RAM if you plan a top radiator to avoid clearance headaches
Verdict
The North Charcoal Black TG Dark blends premium and timeless design with competent thermals and a smooth build experience. If you want a PC that looks as good as it runs and you are willing to plan your component sizes it is fantastic. For maximal airflow or the absolute largest GPUs without compromises the Mesh version or the larger North XL are worth a look. As a tasteful and compact mid tower that can still handle a powerful build the North is a winner.
