reviews.title: A great looking case that also cools well.
reviews.comment: I've been a Fractal Design fan for many years.  This one caught my eye when it was released.  I like the wood slats on the front.  They make it look more luxurious.  It has typical Fractal build quality.  That is to say it is excellent.  Building the system is easy.  Components fit exactly as they should.  Fractal's approach for air filters works well.  They are easy to clean.  I generally just run water over them in the sink and then dry them off.  The whole system is reasonably quiet.  Cable routing works well.  I've never been great at making the cables look professional but with this, it still looks good.  There are convenient Velcro strips to help. I do have three suggestions: - There should be a DIN plug for connecting all the front panel connections. - I miss having an LED to indicate drive activity. - They should make more of this model with a solid side panel.  I would prefer that over the glass side panel.  I don't really need to see inside the machine but would prefer the increased sound isolation an insulated, solid panel could provide.
reviews.author: Darrin J. Fangman

reviews.title: Great Case at Great Price
reviews.comment: This case is pretty awesome. It looks very sharp. Plenty of room for cable management and even has a hidden hard drive bay. It feels pretty sturdy considering the price point. I even dropped the glass panel and it didnt shatter. The airflow is fantastic. The included fans are surprising great. The colors match perfectly to my Corsair and Thermaltake fans. The size is also a huge pro. Its smaller than my old case, but roomy where it matters. I have plenty of clearance with my AIO which was a massive problem with my old, larger case. I am pretty surprised at how good this is for its price point. Ive had it a month and I can honestly say I have no cons yet.
reviews.author: Ria

reviews.title: Excellent Buy
reviews.comment: I find the case a great value.  No it is not the thickest of metal, but I would not say it is not flimsy by any means.  Especially once assembled it is quite solid.  Fans work great and quiet.  Plenty of room for my RTX 5070.  Tons of ways to tie down cables and route them in a neat way. Short: Pros: Great cable management with many tie off places built in. Plenty of pass through holes Ample room for full sized graphics cards Ability to easily add top fans Comes with fans Nice looking Neutral: Material thickness.  Do not over tighten screws, snug then quarter turn. I found this neither a plus or negative, but could be problematic for the over zealous. Fits most if not all mobo sizes, if you have a case this big it is ideal for full ATX. Cons: Only one cable to control all fans Would like to control back fan separately Unable to find another breakout cable. On my mobo it was tight to get cpu power plugs plugged in as it was close to top cavity. Photos do not have power supply installed yet.  Note the pass throughs and tie offs.  Also a good +1 inch gap for gpu.
reviews.author: jblues

reviews.title: Pretty good, especially for the price.
reviews.comment: It's fine. It looks nice, but it did miss a lot of marks. The ports are on the bottom which I guess if you have a desktop PC then that's a good thing. It would have been so easy to make the front plate reversible like so many other cases are, but this one specifically has line up holes that prevent that. The USB 3 port was extremely tight and I was worried I was going to break something. The LED lights don't have a controller so they're not individually addressable, they are all just in series in the fans. Fans work pretty good and keeps decent airflow and the case feels fine especially for the price. I was going to consider returning it, but I think it will stay for now.
reviews.author: Austin H

reviews.title: JUST BUY IT (if you have a hdd get a ssd it’ll be fine)
reviews.comment: I’ll be honest—I almost canceled my order because I saw a review claiming this case was plastic. That couldn’t be further from the truth. It’s mostly metal, with some high-quality plastic that feels just as solid as metal. Whoever wrote that review nearly cost me this gem of a case. This case is AMAZING. The airflow is fantastic, and while it’s not a full tower, the interior space is surprisingly roomy for a mid-size. The only tight spots are around the PSU and HDD bay (you’ll run into clearance issues if you try to keep both), but thankfully the HDD bay is removable, which solves that problem. Cable management space behind the side panel is slimmer than I expected—they really could’ve given it an extra inch—but the number and placement of cutouts for routing cables is excellent. Even the tricky CPU power cable at the top has a perfect pass-through. The walnut finish is flush and looks great with the rest of the case. Honestly, for $90 this case blows me away—it’s hands down the best I’ve owned so far. The front I/O panel is also perfectly placed (especially for anyone with cats) and the USB ports are just right: not too tight, not too loose. Everything works as it should. If you’re hesitating on this case, don’t. It’s an easy build, great airflow, and looks incredible. In three words? JUST BUY IT.
reviews.author: Nathan G

reviews.title: Good quality Fractal alternative
reviews.comment: It’s a cheap but reliable alternative to a Fractal case. For the cost I expected it to be a lower quality case but it’s actually pretty sturdy, I was pleasantly surprised. Only thing some might consider a downside is the fact it can only fit up to a 305mm gpu. I personally was in the market for a more compact ATX case like this one, but if you plan on going with anything bigger than a 4080 or 5070, depending on the specific card, you might want a different case. I’m currently running a PNY 8gb 3060ti with 2 fans, and it fits just fine. I plan on upgrading to the Asrock 16gb steel legend dark 9070xt, which crams 3 fans in a 298mm package.  Another thing to consider is that the fans are on the louder side, so if your pc is on your desk like mine is, you will definitely hear it. Airflow has been really good, but my setup isn’t powerful enough to throw out any major heat, so results may vary. After a couple months of regular usage, I give it 5/5 for checking all my boxes and looking fly doing so🫡
reviews.author: RJ from Over the Hedge, the hit Hollywood masterpiece

reviews.title: H1 HYXN ATX PC Case (White)
reviews.comment: I’m extremely impressed with this H1 HYXN ATX PC case. The build quality is solid, and the dual-chamber design makes cable management surprisingly easy and clean. The case comes pre-installed with 7 PWM ARGB fans, which provide excellent airflow right out of the box while also looking absolutely stunning. The white finish is clean and modern, and the tempered glass panels really showcase the components inside. I especially like that it supports up to three 360mm radiators simultaneously — plenty of room for high-end builds and custom cooling setups. The front I/O with USB-C is a great bonus and feels very premium. Overall, this case offers fantastic value for the price. Great airflow, beautiful RGB, and smart internal layout. Highly recommended for anyone building a clean white gaming or workstation PC.
reviews.author: SIARHEI LUNIOU

reviews.title: Great case
reviews.comment: This case is so worth it. Not complicated, no issues, great space. My only caveat is that the ports are on the bottom which is weird to me. Not a convenient spot for them but that’s the only issue. Airflow is great, noise level is amazing. Cable management is also great!
reviews.author: Nathan S.

reviews.title: Great case and great price
reviews.comment: Build quality is good. Great for this price point for sure. I was definitely impressed how clean it looks! Instructions were pretty straight forward and didn’t run into any crazy issues when installing. Overall I have no regret!

reviews.title: Beautiful aesthetics and good temps
reviews.comment: Wonderful case that’s easy to work in and looks beautiful when finished. Temperatures are really good with my Thermalright peerless 120 duel tower and duel fans with 5” screen air cooler when gaming at 4k. I’m extremely pleased and recommend this pc case
reviews.author: James T

reviews.title: Pink Value for a small price!
reviews.comment: This is a great value for the price. The fit and finish is really nice - the tempered glass appears to be a quality glass. No blemishes, no jagged edges, and the case is straight with clean lines. The included ARGB fans are quiet with vibrant colors. My daughter picked this for her new Intel Ultra build. She is very happy with the result.
reviews.author: Soldots

reviews.title: Best micro ATX case
reviews.comment: This case is phenomenal inside and out. It was very well protected in the box it came in and was easy to build in. The design is well laid out and compact, not obnoxiously bulky or spread out like typical towers. Despite its smaller size, it fit everything beautifully and the airflow is excellent throughout. The GPU I used is 270mm and it fit perfectly in the standard version. If you get anything longer, I’d recommend the pro edition even though the standard looks like it might fit longer cards. The quality you get for the money is worth it alone, it looks and feels solid in every aspect. If you’re looking for the perfect case for a micro ATX build, look no further than this.

reviews.title: Spacious and affordable
reviews.comment: This case is tiny, but has lots of space to put everything inside. It is a very recommended and elegant case yo buy. I just would like there would be a combo with artic fans or be quiet! with it.

reviews.title: Great case for anybody looking for a simple design
reviews.comment: I thought I bought a cheap Amazon case for my budget build, but it ended up being very high quality and wonderful to use. There’s a million places for cables and zip ties making it very easy to manage and it easily accommodates medium-large GPUs and CPU coolers. It fits the design I was going for perfectly and I would totally recommend it to anybody looking for a stylish case even if they’re not on a budget

reviews.title: Great looking and easy to build in case.
reviews.comment: This is a great case for the M-ATX form factor. I am very happy I chose this case and it was a pleasure to build with. The build quality is very nice and sturdy. There were no issues with any of the hardware. It was the perfect size to connect everything and cable manage. I loved the front IO and cables, very high quality. My only grips is, I do wish they would have used thumbs screws to secure all sides instead of just the glass panel.
reviews.author: Fridayone8

reviews.title: Nice Case for Simple Builds
reviews.comment:
Overview - The case is solid for what it is. It's open enough to fit most of what you might want and straight forward enough that instructions aren't that important. I believe that it did come with instructions but it was obvious enough in how it worked that it wasn't necessary.
Space - I have a rather large gpu in the case (roughly 340mm), a 240mm AIO, 6 fans, and an SFX power supply. Not sure if a standard ATX power supply would have allowed the longer length GPU, so that should be considered. The only issue that I found regarding space is that in the side of the case for cable management. It literally had no extra space between my fan controller and the side panel. Actually, as the mobo tray is so cut out for cables, there isn't anywhere that's really good for putting a fan controller. It's kinda just hanging onto a couple of points instead of full contact. On top of that, my mobo didn't have a usb-c connection so I used a 3.1 splitter to connect it there. That splitter barely fit. Regarding bottom fans, you may need to go with fans narrower than normal. My gpu is a 2.5 slot card, so 25mm fans contact the gpu itself and do not work with it. I had to use 15mm fans to fit it all in. As I see them in the case as well as the marketing shots, I'm pretty sure that's what they had installed for their bottom fans. Comes up just above the lip of the case where the glass panel butts up against it.
Ease of Use - As stated, it's pretty straight forward. There's no puzzle element to the case unlike some others that require multiple parts to be removed just to install the AOI/radiator. The case allows for fans to be adjusted to wherever suits them best, always nice though mostly standard these days. The only knock here is that the PSU is installed at the front end of the case and connected to the back via an extension cable. This means that once the top is placed back onto the case, you cannot flip the switch on the psu itself. Not a huge deal but another thing to be considered.
Value - I'd say that it is a very good case for what it costs. It doesn't have the toolless features of more expensive cases, but it does things simply and without being convoluted. It has a bottom dust filter only, so it appears that that's how they expect air flow to be routed. There isn't a whole lot that can be changed there, but the temps my system has maintained have been really good. Not to mention fan speeds have been able to stay really low so sound pollution is at a minimum.
As it has limited room for cable management and no flat panel or space to put a fan controller, I feel that the loss of a star is fair. If the case had those two things, I wouldn't have any real gripes to speak of.
reviews.author: KG

reviews.title: Fantastic case
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/B1GTM-YAQoL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/618xVww89vL._SY256.jpg This is my first time using a product from this company. I researched for months for my build which is the top of the line everything. I didn’t want to skimp on the case, I wanted a case where I could hide the psu and cables easily. I wanted a case with a unique fan appearance if possible, I actually didn’t think it was possible. After much consideration I chose this case, the fact the reviews all mention high quality materials, glass, arrangement and fans was a big factor in my decision.
The good
-This case is large, perfect for a build that includes the 9950x3d cpu and a 5090 gpu. Plenty of space for everything without being cramped.
-this case comes with one or four fans. I would like to have had the option of 7 fans but getting 4 is still a bonus compared to most other cases.
-this case comes in white or black, and the fans match. I was going to do a white build but lack of available parts in white and the fact I really liked this cases looks black, caused me to lean towards the black version.
-the layout is perfect. It has a place to mount the psu sideways so you can easily access your psu plugs and cables. It has routing ties and plenty of access holes to route anything, anywhere. It has room for a single 120 fan on the back, 3 on bottom, side and top which is a total of 10 fans. This allows for easy fan and/or radiator installation as well as utilizing directional fans so you have bottom and side pulling in cold air and the back and top putting out hot air.
- additional facts on the psu mount. The fact the psu is mounted in a separate section not only allows it to pull in cold air from the side but also prevents hot air from going into the case. This is a legit problem with cases where the psu is in the primary section on the bottom of the case. The cables excess wiring is able to be kept in this section, out of sight and also not hindering air flow for the components. This is a huge plus for rigs that produce heat like mine does.
-motherboard mount is simple, and allows cables from all components to run behind the motherboard in the separate section so again, no wire clutter to look at or reduce heat dissipation. You only use a few inches to plug into the motherboard. There are access holes all the way around so you route the cables in the separate section and only bring in enough of the wire to effectively plug it in. This is the cleanest install I ever experienced and I have built a lot of rigs in the past 24 years.
-the fans are unique not only in their look but they also utilize a proprietary connection method. This may make some people nervous but for complex high end builds, this is yet another bonus feature that shows how much engineering went into this case. The fans connect to one another using a plate to plate method, the final fan has the wires to plug into the motherboard or controller. The rgb lights on these fans are also unique in their design, utilizing clean lines but also the mirrored sides. When you see these fans you can’t help but exclaim “wow” because with the organization that you get from this case, the fans can be seen in all their glory. No wires blocking the view what so ever. The rgb control is easy to use and easily combined with all other lighting on the pc.
-another bonus feature many might miss seeing is the fact they include a gpu support, that is adjustable and is built into the case. This is huge for cards like the 5090. Simple, effective, absolutely fantastic. Just another way you can see the engineering that went into this creation of this case.
-filters, this is something becoming common so it’s not unexpected but they do have them for all incoming air locations which many cases still lack. The bonus feature is how easily they can be removed and cleaned without dismantling anything.
-access to the panels is excellent, they have thumb screws on every panel but also the glass is plug mounted on the front edge. So it pops off easily. You have easy access to every section via panels for front, top and back side. The thumb screws can unscrew entirely if you can leave them in the panel when they release from the case. This prevents losing if the said screws, another nice bonus feature that seems small.
Many of the features I mentioned may seem small but they are not insignificant by any stretch. When you put them all together then you have much less of a headache being possibly caused by something small going wrong. I know I’m repeating myself here but with this case you can tell how much thought went into engineering every detail even the small ones that alone seem insignificant. They really focused on the little things here and I can appreciate that as a builder. I will absolutely purchase from this company again in the future.
Note: I did need to contact the company to find the reverse fans for this case. The responded quickly and advised me how to obtain the fans I needed. They were eager to learn why thoughts I might have had about the case and fans, I imagine this is because when they design the next case, much like this case, they want to focus on the details that matter. So gaining my input helps them be more effective on the next design. I respect that from a company.
As always if I encounter anything good or bad from this point on, I will come update my review accordingly. :-). No builder can go wrong with this case and dare I say, this company. I can’t wait to build my next rig, maybe I can do the white build soon.

reviews.title: Dual Liquid AIO Coolers - Fit!
reviews.comment:
First, the only downside: it doesn’t come with a vertical GPU mount kit, and I couldn’t find an official one online. Also, the case is a bit cheaper now than when I bought it. That said - everything else about this case is awesome. I chose the DY470 not only for the 310° view, excellent cable management, “angles on angles” design, and the crazy leg-mounted USB ports, but also for its superb airflow, generous working space, and vert-mount capability. The real surprise? It can fit two liquid AIO radiators. I searched forever for a case with BTF support (even though I opted for a reg ATX mobo), vertical mounting options, and room for two triple-fan AIOs - and this one delivered (see pics).
I grabbed a simple vertical-mount faceplate, a GPU sag support, and the floating look is sic. The CPU cooler hoses are almost completely hidden behind the GPU while still running to the bottom of the radiator for the ideal 2nd mounting position. I also added DIY mesh screens to the back panel (see pic) and they work flawlessly. All in all, I’m extremely happy with the Darkflash DY470. This case absolutely rocks!

reviews.author: BrainBuster865

reviews.title: Dream Case!
reviews.comment: This is absolutely the best case I've ever used. Frankly, I haven't been as impressed by a case since my CoolerMaster Stacker 830 EVO... and that's going back some! HAVN really pulled out all the stops on this one. The HS420 is beautiful, inside and out... functionally and aesthetically! The ease of access is excellent. The dangerous, sharp edges to bust your knuckles are minimal, and there is plenty of space to work on and install goodies in! The panels are all sturdy and snap in place extremely well with the rollers that let the somewhat heavy side/front glass panel settle into place securely, even without the screws. In fact, all of the panels can be left "screwless" is you don't plan to move it around, and there's no worry about anything falling off... but having the screws on the top edge, under the drop in top panel, is a convenient way to lock it all down if that's your play. I got the Vertical GPU version, and I run the angled lower fan bracket and the glass airflow guide, and cooling is never a problem for me. I built the PC a while back now, but it's been stable and cool for the entire experience. The rig I built has a Hybrid cooled 3080 and an AIO for the CPU, and the only issue I had, was trying to decide which rad to put up top, and which to but on the right side. There was plenty of room at both locations for either 120mm width rads up to 360 in length, for sure. I think a 140 x 420 would be tricker on the top side, with clearance being very tight near the top rear corner of the MB 8pin power, but would be the only potential issue. As I was routing cables, I was endlessly surprised by all the well-thought out, built in velcro securing straps, the tie down slots/loops, and the abundance of Fan Headers. Good stuff! The only thing that will require a bit of exploration, care, and planning when putting everything together, is making sure you have the angled lower fan bracket installed early... including the glass airflow guide, since you'll need to bolt that onto the bracket before you secure it. If you run the vertical GPU, like me, check your installation space there as well, since you kind of have to remove the whole bracket to do any work down below, like installing SSDs or other PCIE cards. You could have issues with the vertical GPU mount and air coolers on the CPU, depending on how big the cooler and card is. Last thought on the Vertical GPU: Since these kinds of mounts require a ribbon cable to turn the GPU vertical, keep that in mind. When I first put the rig together, I popped the EVGA 3080 Gaming 12GB in as is, no problems. Over the last year or so, I had begun to have some odd black screen GPU crashes... and upon researching, it appears that gen4 and (especially) Gen5 PCIEX Link Speed can make these crashes a lot more likely when running slot extenders/ribbon cables. Moral of the story is, if you aren't running bleeding edge hardware that can use the gen 5 speed, set it to gen3 for the long haul. And if you are running something that can use the gen5 (or even gen4) link speed, you might want to use the non-vertical mount case to avoid this potential complication.

reviews.title: Very Unique Design Allows for CPU and GPU AIOs (Measure Carefully!)
reviews.comment:
This case first came to my attention over the summer, but I didn't think much of it until I had to put a new system together in November. The triple chamber design allows you to put your CPUs AIO into the third chamber which is sealed off from the rest of the system so that exhaust air never enters the other two chambers. The front mesh panel and top panel are sturdy and tool-less. The glass panels open easily, but the main side glass panel must be opened first before the front glass panel since it doesn't have it's own detente at the bottom. The metal panel on the right that gives you PSU access is also easy to pen.
The case was very easy to work in and I enjoyed my build. This is compatible with BTF boards which I did use. The cable management features were excellent and let me keep things tidy.
I wanted to use two AIO's in this, one for the CPU and one for the GPU. I put the GPU radiator into the third, dedicated chamber, while the CPU radiator is in the top of the main chamber. My temps have been great. My 5090 has not gone over 65C while gaming for hours, my CPU (AMD 9950x3D) sits around 60 and below. My idle temps are incredible as well.
Overall, I'm very happy with this case.
reviews.author: Kerwin

reviews.title: 99% Amazing! Missing on technicality.
reviews.comment:
I had a Lian Li O11D with 9 140mm Corsair QX-140 fans, Corsair h170i huge AOI, Rog Strix OC 4080 super.  I had the fans and the AIO set up for max cooling.  With a 9800X3d running 100% use CPU temps would throttle out at 85C.  GPU running at 100% would hit 90C with all fans maxed out and end up throttling.
Swapped to this case.  Now have a 360mm cooler which is a huge size smaller, have 3 intake, 3 exhaust on top, and 1 exhaust in the back.  New AOI is the MSI P13, new fans are the MSI EZ120.  CPU max temp so far at 100% is 58C, and GPU at 100% is 55C.  This case has amazingly cooled down my components.  Every fan is 20mm smaller and every aspect of temperature is lower.
The feet keep the case nice and high so the intake fans at the bottom can pull air easily, all that while keeping a snazzy look.  There are many places to route cables out of the way and keep things hidden.  At first I didn't like the look of the furry brush type cable entries but that is growing on me.  It was easy to get the cables through.  I really like the modularity and easy the case can come apart to place things.  I am not a fan of the included velcro straps they provide, the little finger grab thing just doesn't hold which had me use alternative cable restraints, but that is ok.
I love the wrap around glass and how it joins together that is really super smooth!  It has a front panel opening which is easy to access for AOI monitoring, and the power supply side panel makes for super easy access.
Things to know before hand.
The back exhaust fan looks pretty janky.  Only half the fan is usable and the other half hangs over the glass.  Every thermal review I read says it helps gpu temp by 3C minimum so I still use it, but it looks bad.  I am not sure how strong the glass would be but I would have rather had a square cut out of the glass and the vent go all the way through.
AOIs when mounted vertically should have the hoses at the bottom of the AOI.  This allows air bubbles to float to the top of the radiator and not have to be pumped through the pump.  When the hoses are at the top any air in the radiator floats to the top and gets sucked into the cooling stream and into the pump.  This reduces pump life, reduces cooling capacity, and makes noise when the pump cavitates.  Corsair even has a document stating the tubes need to be at the bottom.  Even when the cooler is higher than the pump hoses on top is a problem as it puts the suction where all the air will be.  Why I share this is with the heat shield and without cutting it there is no off the shelf AOI that will install with hoses down.  The heat shield blocks it and the hoses needed would be longer than options on the market.  This case REQUIRES the hoses to be mounted at the top of the AOI.
One more note on the AOI, many AOIs come only with 400mm tubes between the pump and the radiator.  This can be extremely tight on this case.  I found that having the tubes at the bottom of the pump makes the 400mm really a stretch on the P13 AOI.  It looks really bad covering my memory like that.  If you have one with 400mm save yourself a cryosheet or some thermal paste and mount the pump with the hoses on the right side.  Or, you can go with the Corsair Titan cooler that has 450mm hoses.  Not saying any one AOI is better than the other just saying the Titan 360 has 50mm longer hoses that may help with routing if you want the hoses on the bottom of the pump.
Interestingly enough, the PSU takes a suction close to where the AOI is dumping its warm air.  This has not caused any issues and the PSU runs at a cool temp.  The fluid dynamics of the AOI seem to port the air away from the suction though it looks close, in my experience it has not been.
Last note, I use NVME drives that mount on motherboard.  But if you don't or need to use other drives the place they want you to mount the drives requires you to remove the fan controller in the upgraded model, or if you add a fan controller you will have to think again.

Case is large, takes a lot of desk space, however very premium build, super high quality parts.  Integrated GPU stand. easy to get to back of power supply.

reviews.title: Not a gimmick - It truly works!
reviews.comment: Needed a case and this one is very clever.  No longer is hot intake recirculated inside the case.  A vertical mounted 360 AIO is in an isolated chamber.  It gets its own fresh air and exhaust directly out of the case away from the other intakes and, if seated on a desk, away from the user too.  I thought it was a gimmick but I was happily surprised!  I use two 360 radiators, one for CPU (7800x3d) and the other for GPU (5080).  Both rads fit fine.  Only issue is that the removable duct on the top cannot be mounted.  No biggie it is toolless removeable.  With all fans on silent curve I cannot hear any fan sound.  Even with GPU at 100% (Temps high 30C to high 60C) and CPU (Temps low 50C to mid 60C) at 80% I hear no noise.  I am using a BeQuiet silent loop 3 and MSI 5080 suprim liquid with stock fans.  If you need a case give this one serious thought!!

reviews.title: Awesome Looking Case With Great Airflow and Tons of Fans Included
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/C1eIcT9HfuL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/71dzXqp4LpL._SY256.jpg This MUSETEX Y6 case is a really strong value, especially if you want a clean showcase-style gaming PC without having to buy a bunch of extra fans separately.
The biggest thing customers should know is that the case looks way better in person than a basic mid tower. The 270° tempered glass gives the build a full-view display look, and the included infinity mirror ARGB fans make it feel premium right out of the box. Having 7 pre-installed PWM ARGB fans is a huge plus because it saves money, saves setup time, and gives the case solid airflow from the start.
Building in it is pretty straightforward. There is enough room for an ATX build, cable management is manageable, and the Type-C front panel port is a nice modern feature. Once everything is powered on, the RGB looks sharp without needing much extra work.
A couple things to keep in mind: because this is a glass-heavy case, you’ll want to spend a little time on cable management so the build looks clean. Also, double-check your GPU length, cooler height, and motherboard connections before building, just like with any case.
Overall, this is a great pick for someone who wants a flashy, modern gaming PC case with good airflow, lots of fans included, and a premium display-style look without spending crazy money. 🔥

reviews.title: A good choice for a good PC
reviews.comment: Great case. Excellent cable management options. It accommodates large graphics cards and 360mm liquid cooling systems. The rear panel is designed to allow cables to be routed without tension. The fans with adjustable lighting are quiet, and there are enough of them to keep the beer inside the case cool in the summer. I was very pleased with the price of the case. Great visibility through the glass panel and an excellent overall look; in fact, the case isn’t bulky at all. I recommend it. A good choice for a good PC.

reviews.comment: Needed a new case for my all white build. Purchased a used one and it arrived pretty quickly. Had no issues installing components. No issues with thermals either. Did wish it came with a dust filter. My only issues was that the case did arrive missing a connector for the front panels LED's. Amazon support gave me a slight refund because of this. Also reached out to Fractal an about this and have yet to hear back. Otherwise been a pretty good case.

reviews.title: A near perfect case.
reviews.comment: Rarely write Amazon reviews, but I love this case. The lighting is GORGEOUS (not unicorn vomit, adds ambiance to a stealth build). The XL version provides tons of space for sure, but I still felt a little cramped in some parts of the build. For one - the cable cover is a bit derpy with an EATX motherboard - and I guarantee you WILL scrape the finish of it against your GPU backplate. It’s a bit questionable that they didn’t make the flaps a little more flexible. If you’re adding more momentum fans, BE PREPARED FOR A BIT OF HEADACHE. You NEED to buy a 3 pack in order to get the extensions - this means if you get a single one for the back, you will be forced to use a jank combination of the legacy splitter back to the USBC converter. The momentums are a great fan, but I’m not entirely convinced that USBC is the move, it actually led to a bit of headache getting those cable ends to fit in some crevices and I just had to settle for it not being the prettiest in some spots. Aside from that, I love this case. I say this every time I do a new build, but this is a new favorite (and maybe it’s because they keep getting better!) Airflow is phenomenal, I’ve never had a PC this quiet.

reviews.title: One of the largest mATX case that fits an extremely large GPU
reviews.comment: TLDR: THIS CASE FITS ONE OF THE LARGEST AND LONGEST GPUS AROUND THE MARKET (XFX 7900XT BLACK EDITION WITH Z SUPPORT BRACKET). IT ALSO IS ONE OF THE MOST HIGHLY VENTILATED CASES I'VE SEEN. I rarely write reviews, but this deserve one of those moments. I really like this case. It's not expensive for what you're getting and the 360 AIO Liquid Cooler front and top mount is really rare in a mATX case specifically. This also fits GPUs around 380mms of length. My GPU, XFX 7900XT, fits in this case with a bit of length to go, although, I had to top mount my AIO, Arctic Liquid Freezer 3 360, which is still impressive as I had ease installing my parts in this case. Additionally, this case has 5 PCI cover slots that are REUSABLE. Many cases in this price point are only removable but not reusable; this is such a nice inclusion to this case. Also, it came with all the screws and even zip ties to complete my re-casing of my PC. Build quality is better than anything I have seen at this price point. No sharp edges, a lot of spaces to hide and route cables. PSU and Motherboard power cable shroud is present. Front panel is easily removable for cleaning and actually building a computer. This case also comes with two EXTREMELY LARGE FILTERS: it spans almost the whole top and bottom of the case which are also highly perforated for cooling. DOWNSIDE: It DOES NOT COME WITH ANY FANS. This is a budget price point. Many people who are looking to use this case are in a tight budget. It would have been nice to at least include one or two fans with this case. Overalll, this is one of the biggest compatibility mATX case there is. It has class leading GPU support and ventilation. 360 AIO Liquid Cooler support in front AND top is hard to find in ANY mATX case specifically.

reviews.title: Great bang for the buck!!
reviews.comment: Was skeptical of the low price but the ASUS name was the key plus the board and few other components installed are ASUS that went into this case. Quality for the price is great! Ryzen 3 3100 + rtx 2060 + 16gb ddr4 rams to a ryzen 7 5700x + rx 9060xt 16gb + 32gb ddr4 rams. So much better and cleaner. This will last him for a while. Happy with the case and build. The price is cheap and has 6 built in fans. Recommend the case to others for a M-ATX build.
reviews.author: Okami

reviews.title: Buy it, you can't go wrong with it
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/H1aaQ3ZzY-L.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/81CHuD58TaL._SY256.jpg This is the first time I've built a compact Micro ATX PC and let me you, this case made it way easier than it had any right to. Do keep in mind that you are getting what you pay for.
The quality is definitely not poor, but it's does not look or feel cheap in the places it matters.
This thing offers so much space to cram whatever PSU cables or sata cables you need to. Everything you do in the back panel is nearly invisible to what you'll see on the other side.
Don't bother replacing the fans if you're on a budget! These things run shockingly quiet and if you're looking for RGB then you've already got a good set! I've got no complaints with these.
Overall this thing is great. Are there better ones in the same price? Absolutely. This is all preference based. I chose this case due to it already having 6 fans and a really sleek design! I'm was really happy to see Antec still making really good cases! Also this thing has built in GPU support, that was such a nice surprise cause I had no idea it did.
reviews.author: Robert S.

reviews.title: Good quality, excellent hardware support, easy to work inside and fairly priced.
reviews.comment:
The Antec Flux M is a nice micro-ATX motherboard with a nice air flow design, a clean interior and front-mounted PSU compartment. Besides the power and reset buttons, there is a USB-A port, a USB-C ports and audio jack on the front.
I was looking for the Phanteks XT M3 for this PC build, which is a very similar unit. It was not available, so I went with this unit and it was a pleasure to build on it. There was plenty of openings around the motherboard to route cables and also space on the rear to hide them.
There are six 120mm fans included, three of them black and three are ARGB fans.
The case has a toolless glass side panel and there are magnetic dust filters on top and bottom of the case. I removed the top air filter, since it exhausts air from the radiator and it works better without it.
This case supports up to 175mm air coolers, so it should handle large coolers, such as Noctua NH-D15. It supports 360mm radiators and when using low-profile RAM it can support some thick units.
I like the 2.5" SATA support and the nice cover to hide PSU wires on the back. I still use 2.5" SATA SSD to backup data.
The PSU compartment has a mesh air intake, an air exhaust and is it isolated from the other components.
The Antec Flux M supports long and thick graphic cards and there is a GPU support bracket built-in into the case.
Depending on the motherboard PCIe place or thickness of the GPU, you might have to remove the included 120mm fans located at the bottom of the case.
There are a few things Antec should revise. The cutout to insert the GPU should be a tad taller. I had to wiggle the GPU rear bracket and it was too close to motherboard capacitors. You definitely do not want to knock out motherboard capacitors when installing a GPU.
I think Antec should have supported back-connect motherboards, just in case I decide to upgrade to one of those motherboards in the future.
I would have like if all six fans were all one color for better aesthetics. Either pick all black or all ARGB fans. Even just three matching fans would have been better.
All six fans' wires came daisy-chained together. I do think is a good idea to runs six fan from a single fan header.
reviews.author: J. Salce

reviews.title: Perfection
reviews.comment:
This case was incredibly easy to build in. It’s very spacious, so you don’t have to worry about parts fitting, and cable management is simple thanks to the rear panel and plenty of tie-down points to keep everything clean.
It comes with 6 preinstalled fans (3 RGB), which saved a lot of setup time. I built a mid-range gaming PC with used parts and even a massive PowerColor 6700 XT Red Devil fit without any issues. The built-in GPU support bracket was also a nice bonus for such a heavy card.
I had just built a PC in a cheap $40 micro-ATX case before this, and it was a nightmare in comparison. Spend the extra money — it’s worth it.
reviews.author: W. Wall

reviews.title: FOIFKIN F100 mATX case
reviews.comment: This was my first time buying a brand-new PC case. I originally built my PC in an old Gateway case, but airflow and cooling became an issue, so I decided to upgrade. There isn’t much real-world information on the F100 outside of the Amazon listing, so most of my expectations came from reviews of other Foifkin cases. I expected thin metal, a slightly flimsy top corner above the glass panels, and break-away PCIe covers. The metal is thin and the top corner has some flex on its own, but once the front glass panel is installed it stiffens the case up nicely. I was pleasantly surprised that the PCIe slots use replaceable covers, not break-away ones. Cable management is a bit tight, but that’s expected for a smaller mATX case—especially if you’re using cable extensions and using the HDD mount like I was. I also ran into a minor issue where the 3 different SATA SSD mounts all somewhat conflicted with my PSU’s SATA power cable, but I was able to make it work. If you’re only running an NVMe drive (or NVMe + one SATA drive), cable management should be much easier. The biggest improvement was cooling. Coming from a case with poor-airflow and the stock AMD cooler, pairing this case with a Thermalright 240mm AIO dropped my CPU temperatures by about 10-20°C, which was a huge improvement. Overall, for the price, I’m very happy with this case. It looks good, has solid airflow, and most of the downsides are situational. If you’re on a budget and want a clean-looking mATX case, this is a solid option.

reviews.title: A near perfect case.
reviews.comment:
Rarely write Amazon reviews, but I love this case. The lighting is GORGEOUS (not unicorn vomit, adds ambiance to a stealth build).
The XL version provides tons of space for sure, but I still felt a little cramped in some parts of the build. For one - the cable cover is a bit derpy with an EATX motherboard - and I guarantee you WILL scrape the finish of it against your GPU backplate. It’s a bit questionable that they didn’t make the flaps a little more flexible.
If you’re adding more momentum fans, BE PREPARED FOR A BIT OF HEADACHE. You NEED to buy a 3 pack in order to get the extensions - this means if you get a single one for the back, you will be forced to use a jank combination of the legacy splitter back to the USBC converter. The momentums are a great fan, but I’m not entirely convinced that USBC is the move, it actually led to a bit of headache getting those cable ends to fit in some crevices and I just had to settle for it not being the prettiest in some spots.
Aside from that, I love this case. I say this every time I do a new build, but this is a new favorite (and maybe it’s because they keep getting better!)
Airflow is phenomenal, I’ve never had a PC this quiet.

reviews.title: Great looking case for the price.
reviews.comment:
Pros
+Good ventilation
+Pleasing design and profile whilst supporting large GPUs
+Has USB C and a free ventilation fan for less than 60 dollars
Cons
-The dust filter in the front intake often gets in the way of the lid preventing it from snapping shut fully
-The same dust filter likes to stick to the front lid creating a bypass for dust in the space between the lid and intake. You need to poke it with a stick after closing the lid to get it back into place
-Cramped design and no removable top panel makes modifying your PC while the mobo is installed fairly difficult especially if you have a large CPU cooler
-The side where the cables are stored is cramped and doesn't allow room for thicker cables. The metal panel bends if there are wires sticking outwards making it difficult to properly close.
-The audio header cable is not shielded. You will probably need to apply your own shielding to avoid static interference.
While there are more cons than pros in this review the cons, aside from the issue with the filter mesh in front, are mostly nickpicks that can be avoided. If they don't bother you then this case is a steal for the price.

reviews.title: Phenomenal Case, Good Vallue, Amzing Performance, Extremely Quiet and Cool!
reviews.comment: I have always been a fan of Fractal cases for their quality and used them exclusively for my own builds. I am a very sound conscious person so my last case that this Be Quiet has now replaced was the Define 7 Mini. I think it's a great case, but it was a hot box for sure and caused me concern for my components life span. So I bought this Be Quiet 501 Airflow which had a lot of great Youtube reviews. One in particular is Matt Lee, he does the airflow smoke tests after a build, and this was impressive. Yesterday I finally swapped out my Fractal case for this Be Quiet and OMG, the difference in sound and temps alone were huge. Even though the Fractal case was a silent case, the fans kept ramping up because of the heat. No exaggeration I dropped 8 to 10c and my fans barely ramp up under gaming load, including my GPU which will shut the fans off when not needed. I am shocked at how performant this case is for what I have in it. My system is a Ryzen 7 5800x, RX 6700XT 12GB, 750W PSU, 2-Nvme's, 2 - 2.5" SSD's, a Mugen 5 Cooler with 2-Fans (push/pull), and wifi card. The case insluded 2-140mm fans, I added a second front fan. Sadly, I do hear a faint tick out of the original front included fan and will be replacing it. My only other very minor two issues are the rear space could have been just slightly more for cable management. Even so, it was very easy to do, and I love, love, love the single front IO header connector and the single USB 3 connector to run all the ports. And I would have liked to see a second front fan included in the same cost as it was only $12 retail. Those aside, I would with out hesitation highly recommend this case and even invest in another I ever found need for one. I love Be Quiet. The case is good value for what you receive.

reviews.title: Very Quiet… but Massive Airflow = Dust Monster
reviews.comment: It certainly is quiet. The filters are fairly accessible and the glass removes nicely. I have a high end PC build, so I can feel the hot air escaping. I’ve optimized my fan set-up, so this case is great at taking in lots of cool air. However, it would be nice to have another exhaust. I use the back and one of the slots on the top for exhaust. Three fans in front and one on top. This maximizes efficiency, air flow, and exhausting, but I feel like a secondary back port would be great. With that said, this thing is a dust eater. There’s plenty of space in the front to add a slot for a HEPA filter (if only). The top “filter” is paper thin, which is where the vast majority of the dust gets in. The top filter is virtually ineffective.

reviews.title: Premium case at an affordable price.
reviews.comment: Since my old case had very restrictive airflow (NZXT H500), I wanted to upgrade to one with a similar form factor to the Lian Li Lancool 207. The looks of this Okinos case, especially the wood detail, really caught my attention because of how elegant it looks. I’d also heard good things about Okinos, so I decided to give it a shot. I was pleasantly surprised by the build quality and the cleverness of the design. It’s basically a premium case at an affordable price. The materials feel high quality, almost all the panels can be removed without the need for thumbscrews, the airflow is insane (temps dropped by around 10 - 12 degrees), and my build looks hella clean in it. Since I never use the front panel connectors, I really liked the fact that it also includes rubber plugs to prevent dust buildup. One thing to keep in mind is that if you use stiff cable extensions like I do, cable management can get a bit tricky, but that has more to do with this type of form factor than with this case in particular. From what I saw in a Gamers Nexus review of the Lancool 207, that one seems much less forgiving. Very happy with my purchase and I’d definitely recommend it.

reviews.title: Superb design and quality
reviews.comment: This is a beautiful case in all white.  The is more than enough room for just about anything you want to put in there.  Even with a vertically mounted 5070 ti, there is a lot of extra space left over, giving the final result a nice open feel.  That said, it's a large case - make sure you have room for it at close to 13" deep.  There a several things that made this the easiest build I have done.  Aside from the interior size, the dual chambered design makes cabling easy and keeps the front side clean-looking.  Additionally, every bracket, screw hole and snap connection matched up perfectly with overall fit and finish being near-perfect.  I have six intake fans and four exhaust fans, including the AIO cooler for plenty of airflow, though on the down side, the slatted exterior covers probably restrict the airflow to some extent.  One other concern is that it will be a tight fit to get even one low-profile pci card in along with the gpu and pci riser.  Not an issue right now, but possibly in the future.  The case does not come with any fans, though given the range of fan choices and options, included fans probably be not what the user wants anyway.  The case is not inexpensive, but I think worth the cost.  It is heavy also, but built very sturdily.

reviews.title: Love this case!
reviews.comment:
I adore this case! Yes, it's definitely a luxury case as it's pricier than others, but this version does have the 2k screen included. The glass is tempered and I didn't have any issues with it cracking or scratching during the pc build. The bottom compartment does fit three fans, just know you need to fit one inside the case before attaching it to the bracket to make them all fit.
As far as the screen goes, it's a beautiful screen, do note, you need to connect it directly to the motherboard for the picture to work and download the software so you can set your picture/widgets. The cables to hook it up are already ran to the back of the case when it arrives, so you'll just need to hook them up to your motherboard and power supply.
The top of the case does have a compartment that lowers if you want to mount fans or your AIO closer to your motherboard.
Do note, this case includes a PCIe riser 4.0 to connect your GPU to your MOB so the GPU sits upright in the case. IF you need a 5.0 connection like I did, you'll need to purchase the 5.0 riser off Hyte's website, at the time I purchased, they were $99 and you can choose which color you'd like.
The case has plenty of places to route your cables for easy cable management as well as preinstalled Velcro in the bottom to hold some of the cables.
The only downside I saw was needing to buy an updated PCIe riser, I wish they would have had that as an upgrade option at purchase, as well as there being two open spots on the back of the side where you mount the GPU etc. I'm assuming its for easier access, but I do worry about the amount of dust etc that allows into the pc, though I'm sure it's great for airflow.

reviews.title: Premium Case with a Built-In Touchscreen – Still One of the Best After 2 Years
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/E15OAZcxEjL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/61kkYUGl7UL._SY256.jpg ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ – One of the Best Cases I’ve Ever Built In
I’ve had the HYTE Y70 Touch Infinite Dual Chamber ATX Case for about two years now, and honestly, it’s one of the best PC cases I’ve ever built in.
First off, the build experience is incredibly smooth. The dual-chamber design gives you tons of room to work with, making cable management clean and stress-free. Everything feels thoughtfully laid out, so even more complex builds come together easily without feeling cramped.
Compatibility and size are a huge plus. This case easily supports larger GPUs, multiple radiators, and high-end components without any issues. Whether you’re running a high-performance gaming setup or a workstation build, there’s more than enough space to work with.
One of the standout features is the built-in touchscreen, which is honestly amazing. It adds a completely different level of customization and functionality—you can display system stats, animations, or anything you want. It’s not just a gimmick, it actually enhances the overall experience and makes the build feel premium.
Installation overall is very straightforward. Panels come off easily, parts line up well, and the modular design helps speed things up. It’s clear this case was designed with builders in mind.
Price-wise, it’s definitely on the higher end, but after using it for two years, I can say it’s absolutely worth it. The quality, features, and overall experience justify the investment.
Pros:
• Extremely easy and enjoyable to build in
• Spacious with excellent compatibility for high-end parts
• Dual-chamber design keeps everything clean and organized
• Built-in touchscreen is a standout feature and works great
• Premium look and feel
Cons:
• Higher price point, but you get what you pay for
Overall, if you’re looking for a high-end case that combines performance, aesthetics, and innovation, this is a top-tier choice.

reviews.title: Decent case but case doesn't support as much as product page says
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/D1FY0j4L8oL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/61kCD8rCkZL._SY256.jpg I do like the the idea of a limited run case, makes it feel exclusive in a way. The case itself is ok quality, for 140$ I did expect the metal to be thicker than the 60$ case I ordered but it wasn't. This case is fairly modular no doubt however the fan and radiator support is not correct with the documentation. First it lists 140mm support in a lot of areas, however the only way these are supported is if you only use a 120-240mm radiator anywhere or only use air cooling.
I'm using a 360 AIO and I am not able to put 140mm fan in the back front or side because it will hit the aio or fans or tubes if using larger radiator, it is also impossible to use push pull on radiator anywhere and still maintain full fan support and sad part is, it's only by a very small amount so they could have made the case like 1 inch bigger and it would have fit everything with no issues.
I didn't feel comfortable forcing things to fit because of the crazy expense to replace anything if it broke. Overall this case is good but it's lacking in a lot of areas, and honestly if you're buying it specifically because of exclusivity more power to you, however if it were a normal case it would definitely be better to go with a different case if you use 140mm fans, want full aio support, or just want full use of the space properly.
reviews.author: Jordan

reviews.title: Pictures don’t do it justice
reviews.comment:
First of all, hats off to those whose packages arrived broken due to poor handling and packaging. That is not fair and Corsair should most have definitely packaged the items better.
I was extremely scared for my own package to arrive shattered as well but thankfully it made it.
Pictures just do not do this justice. Very fun to build in. It was a little hard to close the case with the extension cables I got but that’s because they are pretty chunky and hard to bend. The whole process was mostly a breeze. I put two 200mm fans in the front, 3x120mm reverse fans on the side of the case, and 3x120mm more reverse on the bottom. One 140mm in the back. And my 360mm aio. Since my initial review, I have slowly been switching around my fan configuration and decided to start swapping out my fans for the icue link system for less cable clutter. Anti Sag bracket works great. My little Lian li screen fit perfectly on the left side. One little cool feature about this case is that the power button can be synced with the color of your fans or if you put it on a different argb header just pick something else that’s custom. Airflow is good. Glass panel is a little tricky to get on because you need to make sure the right side latches on to its correct slots and then you push in the left side and secure it. But yeah overall it’s simple and showcases my components nicely without putting the whole focus on a fish tank.
reviews.author: Lizzy B.

reviews.title: YEAH BUDDY!
reviews.comment: I’ve had this case for about a week now and I am very happy with it! I try to future proof my PC about once a year if I can, but this year I decided to take it a bit future and rebuild the majority of it. (Still have more on the way). My buddy loved this case for his new build and it just gives off a nice customizable and clean look that I was looking for. The space in the back for the power supply is a god send. I just wired in PSU Cable Extension Sleeves and I still have plenty of room back there for more drives that I plan to throw in. I’ve seen some comments and opinions about the case, saying that for the price, it doesn’t make a good fit for a moderate build, etc. However, I argue that it all depends on what you want. I’m able to throw pops and theme it much easier and add more fans in, if I want to. And easily upgrade to an AIO if that’s what I want to do later on... So, if you want a well built case, with tough glass, with tons of space for upgrades, cable management, and or just a case to gives off a clean look and to give it a personal feel, then I recommend going with this one. Worth the money, for sure! (Just make sure you have the desk space haha)
reviews.author: Noah

reviews.title: Best case I've bought
reviews.comment: Great build quality, super roomy, and looks amazing. More than enough space to handle just about any hardware you can think of (that's a 3080 so not much larger you can go for a GPU) The secondary chamber that you put your PSU (and basically everything else) into is amazing for helping make cable management super easy. All in all, great case that makes it very easy to set up a fantastic looking system (and the airflow is top notch). Only stinker is that iCue is wonky as h*ck but it's currently working smoothly for me now so there's that.
reviews.author: Reid Slingerland

reviews.title: Great case, temps are great even with an i9!
reviews.comment: I watched reviews on this case and on the Lian-li, but ultimately went with this case.  I was going for a full Corsair build, this came with three less fans (LL120) that I would need to purchase.  I ended up purchasing a few more LL140's to replace the one in the rear, which unfortunately was not an RGB fan, purchased a power commander, some LED's and a Corsair H115-0 Platinum for the CPU cooler.  Everything fit perfectly, case has great build quality, and Corsair's website provides clear layouts for fan sizes and radiator sizes the case would fit. The rear side of the case has plenty of space for cable management, 2 RGB pro, Power Commander, and LED controllers.  Motherboard was a Z390-A and fit perfectly. The only thing I did not do was front mount the GPU because it would be resting against the front screen and that would only give it about half an inch of breathing space with the front glass panel.  All temps are nice and cool and everything looks great for fans of RGB.  I would definitely recommend this case.
reviews.author: Marin

reviews.title: The best looking case made!
reviews.comment: I purchased this case because of the styling and the big glass windows to show off the components. One of the coolest features is that the big glass door on the side opens on a hinge and stays closed using a magnet. I love that I was able to hide the cables and the power supply in the second compartment. Plenty of room as you can see from the pics of my water cooled system. The power button and the usb's are on the top of the case and make it easy to get to. The front and top fans mount on a removable bracket that makes install a breeze. I am very impressed with the overall quality of the case and as you can see from the pics it looks amazing. If you want a high quality case with great ventilation to showcase your pc build then this is the winner.
reviews.author: LoneStar4Life

reviews.title: Beautiful big case
reviews.comment: This is a big case, but honestly needs to be a couple inches wider. If you use a 360mm front radiator like me, you have 12ins of GPU clearance, meaning no high end GPU with fit as they're all over 12in, unless you get a water cooled one like my Asus ROG strix LC 3080ti. (Edit: amd 7900xtx are only 11.3in so high end AMD cards will fit too) Then you'll run into your next problem. Fitting a radiator on top with a front radiator there. Can't have the front radiator tubes on top bc the top radiator, and with the GPU traditionally mounted, you'll see how tight of a fit it was for my CPU cooler tubes to fit behind the GPU. My CPU was also running hotter than usual with it installed like this. Not too hot, but a little hotter. You can't install the top radiator with all 8 screws either, the front radiator is in the way, so I shifted it over on the top mounting plate and was able to get 6 screws in the top radiator, not worried with that many. I got an Asiahorse brand pcie 4.0 extension cable and vertical mounted this GPU and my CPU temps went back to normal. This GPU is beautiful and deserves to be vertical mounted though haha. I was just worried about performance loss, but this cable handles my 3080ti at 2100mhz no problem. I game on a 4k 144hz gigabyte m32uc monitor. I'm sure there's a little performance loss using an extension, but nothing I'm going to notice. Now the back of the case. It's huge but I have it packed with cables bc I use fancy PSU extensions with combs. I read about stuff getting hot back there if you had a lot of drives. I removed the HDD cage and installed the SSD cage lower in its place where some screw holes and mesh lined up, plus a zip tie on the top of it for a little extra support. I installed a 120mm intake fan that came in the case on the back panel, 2 screws fit in the metal mesh, and then 2 zip ties where it didn't line up. The fine mesh fliter that goes over the white metal mesh over this makes it unnoticeable. I then installed a steel mesh screen on the other side on this intake fan so no wires could poke in there when I close the panel (this isn't pictured). I then installed a 90mm be quiet fan above the SSD cage for some exhaust in the back chamber. I can remove my back panel and place it on the shelf below my PC without having to disconnect the back panel intake fan, so it is of no inconvenience. I also put my case on 4 steel foot risers to give better bottom air intake for my 2 140mm fans down there. Beautiful case. Overall I'd recommend, but just be aware of your dimensions and what you want to do in this case.
reviews.author: Steven Gormely

reviews.title: Great!
reviews.comment:
This is the first pc case I've ever bought and had to transfer into. I'm kind of new to pc gaming. Only been at it for the past couple years, and never did anything like this before. Thankfully, this case made it super easy.
The size, options and components make transferring into this case super easy. The cable management looks incredibly clean by the time you're finished. The holes for the cables have these nice rubber padded openenings, and the openings are all over the place to maximize which cables come out where.
All the panels (the top, sides, cable channel covers marked 1 and 2) are simple to remove. They utilized these metal notches that slot in, so you only need one thumb screw to secure them, which is pretty neat. Even without the thumb screws, there are these ball joint things the panels snap into, so the thumb screws are just an added redundancy.
I had 2 3.5" HDDs. In my original review, I said there was only space for one but it turns out I'm bad at reading directions. There is space for 2. There's room for 3 separate 2.5" drives on the cable management side, so plenty of options for expanded storage.
The ventilation is all over the place on this thing, so it shouldn't have any problems staying cool, and keeping air going.
Speaking of air, the fans it comes with are big 140s in the front, and from what I can tell, they pull a lot in through that magnetic front vent panel.
I had a situation with my motherboard in my old case, and my wishes were granted with my top mounted AIO here. The old case had a problem with space for said AIO at the top because I have the extra thick Arctic 360 radiator + fans, which had to be installed kinda of slanted to get out of the way of the CPUs power cable (the connector for which was at the very top of the motherboard). With this new case, there's enough space for everything to fit as it's supposed to.
I haven't done any customizing of fan curves or anything, but I played some Cyberpunk 2077 at 4k with Path Tracing and all bells and whistles on, although not for very long yet, and my cpu and gpu stayed cool as a cucumber. My 3080 used to get up to the 80s. The 4090 doesn't go over 70. I don't know if it's the case, or the cooling system on the GPU, or both, but regardless, it's running nice and cool.
I saw a video on YouTube about this particular case being a little more noisy than the more pricey ones like the Meshify 2, but if what it produced was more noise, I couldn't hear it. It's much quieter than my last case, that for certain.
I'm not sure what else to add that is worth while. If you get a 4090 for this case, you may have to slip the top pci slot cover in over the back of the 4090, because the plate on the top of the card sticks out a hair on the back side. You sort of have to wedge it in (angled 45, tuck in the bottom edge over that plate, then put it upright, then push it in toward the motherboard, then you can screw it in, or even just leave the screw, because it can be a hassle, and it being slightly wedged in will keep it in place).
One of the neat things about it is the screens are very easy to remove. The bottom one can be slid out from the front, like a lint trap on a dryer. The front most panel just.. Pops off with a light tug because it's magnetic.
I'll be up front here, as I said, I am fairly new to pc gaming, cases, etc., but I am thorough, and from what I have found and seen for myself, it's a great case, while also being very affordable.
The biggest selling point other than the ease of use, is definitely the cable management. It is CLEAN when you do it right. It looks awesome if you don't care for the RPG puke, and enjoy a nice dark and sleek appearance.
Also, for being a "full" tower, it really doesn't look much bigger than the mid tower I had previously. Maybe if you jump from a small tower to this one it'll be more noticeable to you, but it fit great in the same spot.
All in all, I definitely can recommend this case. Especially for those on a more beginner/intermediate level who want a lot of open space to work with.
reviews.author: Zero

reviews.title: beautiful case
reviews.comment:
The Antec Performance 1 FT is a mid-tower computer case that offers a balanced combination of features and performance. In this unbiased review, we'll delve into its various aspects to provide you with a comprehensive overview.
**Design and Build Quality (4/5):** The Performance 1 FT features a minimalistic design with a brushed aluminum front panel that gives it a premium appearance. The case is well-constructed and feels sturdy, which is a positive aspect in terms of build quality. However, some users may prefer a more flashy design, and the overall aesthetic may not appeal to everyone.
**Airflow and Cooling (4.5/5):** This case is equipped with multiple cooling options, including support for up to six 120mm or four 140mm fans. It also offers compatibility with liquid cooling solutions, making it a good choice for those who want to keep their system cool, even during heavy workloads. The airflow design is efficient, and cable management options are decent, allowing for clean airflow paths.
**Compatibility (4/5):** The Performance 1 FT supports ATX, micro-ATX, and mini-ITX motherboards, offering versatility in terms of motherboard compatibility. It can accommodate graphics cards up to 370mm in length and CPU coolers up to 165mm in height, which should cover the majority of user requirements. However, some larger graphics cards or CPU coolers may not fit.
**Storage Options (4/5):** This case provides a good number of storage options with support for up to four 2.5" SSDs and two 3.5" HDDs. This should be sufficient for most users, but it's worth noting that the drive bays aren't tool-free, which might be a minor inconvenience for some.
**Ease of Installation (4/5):** The Performance 1 FT offers a relatively straightforward installation process with well-labeled cable routing channels and plenty of cable management options. However, it lacks some premium features like a removable motherboard tray, which could make the installation process even more user-friendly.
**Price and Value (4/5):** The price point of the Antec Performance 1 FT is reasonable, given its build quality, cooling options, and compatibility. While it may not be the cheapest case on the market, it strikes a good balance between quality and affordability.
**Conclusion:**
The Antec Performance 1 FT is a well-constructed mid-tower case with a minimalist design that might not appeal to users looking for more flashy aesthetics. It excels in terms of airflow and cooling options, making it a suitable choice for users who prioritize thermal performance. The case offers good compatibility for most standard components, but it may not accommodate larger components. The price is reasonable, considering the features and build quality it offers.
Ultimately, the Antec Performance 1 FT is a solid choice for users looking for a reliable, mid-range computer case, provided that the design and size constraints align with their preferences and requirements.
reviews.author: ILoveWritingReviews

reviews.title: Great for a first build.
reviews.comment:
Chose this for my first build. I found it easy to work with and the cable management is nice. The side panel is easy to remove for cleaning internals, and the included fans work great. The size inside is plenty, honestly I think I could have gone with something smaller but this future proof's for larger cards.
One thing to note is the LED panel will not work if you don't install the Antec software, which can be a deal breaker on Linux as it's Windows only. There are some community workarounds on GitHub and I was able to code a workaround in an evening.
reviews.author: PV

reviews.title: Amazing retro pc gaming case
reviews.comment:
big fan of be quiet! fans and now i have a sweet looking pc case, Pure Base 600.
*Airflow is great because fans are powered from the top front Switch (positions are Low-Med-High)
*this pc case met all my needs:

reviews.author: smallproject_guy

reviews.title: Quiet.  High quality.  For experienced builders.
reviews.comment: You can't hear it when it's on, but you can feel a vast amount of air being pushed.  The top vent can actually fit a 3 fan cooler(barely) despite manufacturer stating otherwise.  The instructions aren't clear, so this is not a beginners build. This is a high quality case.  The top vent cover seems kinda cheap.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Super quiet!  Really great design.
reviews.comment:
I have the non-window variant.  My build just uses pretty standard-size equipment.  I've got a micro ATX motherboard and a Radeon RX 580, and that all fits without issue.
I use the stock CPU cooler on my Ryzen 5 2600, and the case fans do a great job of keeping everything cool even when gaming at 4K in GTA V.  And the whole time it's /really/ quiet.  In a room with some background noise you can't even hear it running, and in a silent room it's utterly inoffensive.  It's not even in a particularly well-ventillated space, either.  It's been about six months since I put it together and it's still just as quiet despite being on thick carpet and not being cleaned yet.
There are a lot of clever holes for cable management, and it's really easy to get it tidy on the inside.  I really like the built-in fan controller; I think it's awesome to have that capability and I use it often.  I also really love that you can selectively remove the parts of the rear where PCI devices like graphics cards and wireless adapters might go, while leaving the other slots covered.  It forms this metal grille in the back that allows for airflow but won't let you accidentally drop anything inside.
I got the all-black one and it has an understated yet really gorgeous look to it.
The only detriment I can think of is that the manual is lacking in instruction.  I think someone else who reviewed this encountered the same mistake I made with the SSD mounts -- I put them on backwards.  Don't try to squeeze your SSD into the underside of the mount next to the motherboard; the SSD goes on top of the mount away from the motherboard, and the screws to mount the SSD go in through the side of the mount that faces the motherboard, and then screw into your SSD.  Once you have it on the mount, you just reattach the mount to the case with the thumbscrew and you should be looking at the full unobstructed face of your SSD.  I don't know why they designed it this way, but I like the flexibility of its placement once it's attached to the mount, as there are two places in which to attach the mount to the case.
Overall, great design -- it works stupendously for my purposes.  Couldn't be happier.
reviews.author: Homegrown Handyman

reviews.title: Acceptable, but would be nice to know about the flaws ahead of time
reviews.comment:
Overall I'm pleased. It fits the gigabyte aolus ultra motherboard with a noctua NH-U14S. It is quiet even with a total of eight fans running (three front, one back, two CPU, one chipset, one power supply), and the damping material on the case sides seems to be at least somewhat effective. I like the just plain black case with no place for multi-color LEDs. The power button is centrally located on the top front bezel and is easy to get to, and the reset button is small and unlikely to press accidentally. The tall feet on the bottom are a good idea especially if you mount the power supply to use the bottom vent. (I know other reviews complain about a motherboard standoff without the thread hole, and mine had that too, but I think it's intentional and not considered a mistake.)
Unfortunately, there were a few downsides.
The thumbscrews are cheap, and on my unit screw arrived slightly bending the thin steel it was screwed into. At this price point I expected quality screws throughout, engaged with standoffs or bushings. All the screw are cheap, inside and out. They thread into tapped holes in thin metal. I expect these to cross-thread and strip out easily, even handled with care.
Cleaning the filter in the front panel is going to be inconvenient, because I can't pop the front panel off to get at the captive air filters without taking off the side panels to release the front panel tabs. I prefer cases where the front panel can be popped off without taking the case apart.
It comes with three drive trays, and five slots to hold those trays, and no one has the extra be quiet HDD cage in stock.
The 2.5" cages on the back of the motherboard tray are jokes. I'm not sure what drives they would actually fit. Maybe the 5mm ultra thin drives? The 7mm drive I tried certainly wouldn't fit at all. In any case, there is no effective air flow in that location behind the motherboard tray anyway, so I would consider those cages to be there only for show.
The USB 3 slots in the front are not color-coded blue, and I wish they were.
There is no USB-C connector on the front, nor any convenient way to add one. It would be nice to have a USB-C 3.1 connector with a type-e connector on the other end to work with modern motherboards. If you want that installed nicely in the front, you'll probably want to use a 5.25" drive bay adapter, in which case you can't have a fan mounted in front of the 5.25 drive bay.
It looks as if you could fit 3 of the be quiet Pure Wings 2 140mm fans in the front, there are references to being able to add fans, and I thought somewhere I had seen a reference to placing three of them in front, but you can't actually fit three. It comes with one in the middle, which you could move to the top or bottom of the front, or you can have one fan at the top and one fan at the bottom, but you can't have three covering the front. I bought two extra Pure Wings 2 140mm fans, and then discovered that only one of the two extra would fit. I solved this by putting the third fan in the middle, but inside the case closer to the hard drive cages, and used four M4x60 bolts through the middle-most mounting holes in the upper and lower fans, through the mounting holes in the case, and then through the mounting holes in the inner, middle fan. Also, the fan switch on the front can control three fans. It comes connected to the 120mm fan in the back and the 140mm fan in the front, and there is one extra header for a second fan in the front. I have connected all three 140mm fans to the motherboard instead, and have the fan control switch connected only to the fan in the back.
reviews.author: Michael K Johnson

reviews.title: Worth the consideration!
reviews.comment: I like the case quality. Rigid structurally and flexible as to how cabling and the amount of drive space. Fans of good quality and quiet. The top cover could be a better design as far as ease of adjustment, like the ability to lift and secure at different ventilation levels for the fans.
reviews.author: patsfan

reviews.title: Excellent quality case - good for a starter build
reviews.comment:
I was extremely lucky to stumble upon this case while looking for a Mini-ITX. It's made of durable, good quality metal that's heavy (but not too heavy), small with a lot of room, and extremely versatile (just about every panel of this thing comes off without any tools - just need a screwdriver for the top and bottom panels). It's pretty much perfect for both experts and first-time builders who want a smaller compact PC.
This was my very first time building my own PC, and despite it being inside such a small case, the NR200 made it extremely easy to install. There are tons of places for cable management ties with unlimited potentional for different layouts. The case also has so much airflow that it cools the case extremely well. You also can't beat the price either - it's comparable to a Ncase M1 (but slightly bigger) while being less than half the cost.
There are only a couple issues that I ran into:
- The backside of the case does not have a lot of room to run cables. Not a deal breaker (it was still very doable) but you'll need to strap down the cables on the backside as well in order to get the panel to shut. If it had just another half inch it would be perfect.
- There are many mixed answers on this, but the version without the riser does NOT come with a glass side panel (or at least mine didn't). If you want a see-through side panel, you'll have to opt for the PCI riser version.
Overall I'm extremely happy with this case, it made my first build in a Mini-ITX case very easy. My PC runs very cool and there's lots of room for expansion once the 20 & 30 series cards drop in price again.
My build:
- AMD Ryzen 5 3600
