- GeForce GTX 1050 Ti 4GB
- Team T-Force Vulcan TUF 16GB 3200MHz
- 512GB M.2 NVMe Boot Drive w/ 2 500GB 2.5 SSDs
- Gigabyte B550I Aorus Pro AX MOBO
- Corsair SF 450 Watt PSU
- 3 x 120mm PWM Fans
reviews.author: Ty Eslick

reviews.title: Not the tiniest sff case but maybe the easiest to build in.
reviews.comment:
The TLDR is that this case is great.  I bought another to build a new work computer, and both cases are keeping cool. I did replace the fans with Scythe 140mm fans on the radiator and 120mm slim fans for the bottom on both my home and work builds since both are similar enough.
It's been a while since I built a computer and kind of set it and forgot about it.  I've dusted out the home machine once since I got that one.  Otherwise my only gripe was the paint on the original case but again, that literally buffed out.  The second case didn't even have much in the way of spots on the paint or anything.
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Original review below:
I had an original nr200 that I moved an old itx build into about a year ago and loved it.  I honestly wish I had kept it instead of selling and keeping my atx build.  But I probably wouldn't have gone with this then. So, it's a win. After waiting 7+ months for this case, between seeing it in reviews and not knowing where to get it until it hit Amazon/Newegg, I'd say it was worth the wait.
This comes with two minor caveats, for me at least, that I can't imagine many people have run into.
I got my *first* delivery and was missing the riser cable and one of the pcie power cables.  The box looked unopened so I'll say it was a packing issue from the factory.  I did try to just go through the order page to exchange it but was only given the option to return.  I'd imagine this is due to the cost of the item as a whole.  A call with an Amazon rep got this turned into an exchange.
The second little gripe I have is with the paint.  On the first and second item, the paint looked a little weird.  Not really scuffs but I had to take a little polish to the panels to clean them up.  Not a big deal, but if someone is paying close to or over 450 for this great package, and technically for a specific color, I would think the qc on the paint would be a better.
I popped an x570i Strix board with my 5900x and Strix 3080.  Everything fit like a glove.  The cooler does have a little whine in the pump but I keep the machine of to the side and have a fan on most of the time so it's not audible.  I did change the top fans out though for the Silverstone Penatrator ARGB fans to get a little more flair but the stock fans were more than capable of get the hot air through the radiator.  I matched these up with their 120mm Slimmer fans.
If you don't already have a computer built or want to downsize from an ATX build like my situation, this is the way to go.  Be weary that the psu comes with 2x PCIE power cables that have 2 plugs daisy chained each.  I don't really see this as a problem but I know there are disadvantages to this according to the internet pc building gods.  I had a custom cable made anyway to add a third and there are plenty of people on etsy that can provide such a product or a full set of cables if needed. I paired this with a set of those 90 degree adapters too so it looks extra clean.
I think if Coolermaster sold this version of the case, without the psu, cooler, riser, etc, for the same price as the normal nr200, I think they'd still sell a ton.  Great case overall, probably never going mid/full size build again because of it.
reviews.author: j

reviews.title: very great gaming case
reviews.comment: Airflow is on point - 7 ARGB fans move air perfectly. · Really well built with great materials. · Looks modern and sleek. · Huge compatibility - fits almost everything. Overall: A fantastic case that does it all
reviews.author: FeITaI

reviews.title: 2026 best gaming case under 100
reviews.comment: Amazing case! The airflow is perfectly balanced with 7 ARGB fans keeping everything cool (and looking awesome). Build quality is top-notch, looks super stylish, and it fits pretty much any hardware you throw at it.
reviews.author: kenson

reviews.title: Top quality case. Great
reviews.comment: My Dark flash t20 came undamaged, on time, and as it was advertised. Specs of the system I installed in this case: Cpu: Ryzen 3600x (no OC) Gpu: Rx 5700(Oc-1850, men-930) Ram:16g Ram 3200( OC-3666 COOLING EFFICIENCY: I couldn’t be more pleased with the cooling efficiency.  I did install five additional fans to take advantage of extra fan slots but I did not install an aftermarket cpu cooler. Now, what makes that impressive is I ran a full load stress test through AIDA64 today for 90secs and the CPU stayed never went over 83C. QUALITY: Case was well made with nice materials. Components were installed correctly and securely. Everything was machined nice and removed of burrs. Came with ample screws and standoffs as well as stand-off drivers which was a nice touch. RGB function properly and really add a unique look you don’t see out of most pc builds. Now as for what I would change? Nothing really, I did swap out the included fan but just so it would match the rest of mine. It would awesome if they had a removable slot for an intake fan on the bottom if something was not using the HDD and is fan crazy like myself but to be honest at this price point, you will not find a higher quality case
reviews.author: William J.

reviews.title: Solid case with pre installed fans. Easy to build
reviews.comment: Nice fish tank case to build with. Basically you don’t need to buy more case fans to finish your build. Solid case with strong materials.
reviews.author: lee

reviews.title: Good case terrible fans
reviews.comment: Case is fine but the every fan they sent with the case was bad and did not work at all
reviews.author: zack jones

reviews.title: One case to rule them all...
reviews.comment: I, like many others, am on the search for a case that is both functional and has the right amount of RGB. I have gone through all the phases with my PC - mini itx cases (Coolermaster NR200P, Jonsbo D31 mesh, Lian Li Q58), Mid Towers (Corsair 4000D, NXZT H510), Open Air Cases (Thermaltake P1 & P3). Recently, I have decided to go down the route of a full tower PC case that can house all of my fans, hubs, and RGB accessories with ease. This case caught my eye as its sister case 700 EVO is out of my price range. This case was designed for one thing, airflow. There is no shortage of fan configurations in this case. I currently have 2 (200mm front fans), 3 (140mm Noctua bottom fans), 3 (140 Noctua side fans), 2 (120mm back fan), 1 (200mm top fan) & 3 (120mm LL's top). Needless to say, my PC stays cool under any load placed upon it. My CPU ( Ryzen 9 5900x) @ idle stays around 35C-40C. Under load, it stays below 60C, which is impressive for that specific CPU as it runs hot. My GPU (EVGA 3090 FTW) @ idle stays around 35C. Under load, it doesn't go past 72C. I do not have any overclocking/underclocking enabled. All stock. The case is massive, compared to what I am used to. However, this is by design. The building was seamless. For the most part, this is a toolless case. I liked the locking mechanism that Coolermaster has designed to be used for most of the pieces. Specifically, the back panel is used to "hide" or rather, keep all the cables/hubs in one place without having them protrude and prevent the back cover from being snapped on. This stood out as I have 4 hubs (2x corsair Commander XT, 1 Commander core & 1 Node lighting). The front mesh panel of the case allows for adequate airflow. If fans are set at an appropriate fan curve, the case is silent. Coolermaster included two fan hubs. One that allows for the RGB/fan speed and another to accommodate additional fans for the case. All of these will be controlled via the motherboard, but a nice "must-have". The RGB is standard if that's your thing. The Coolermaster software is bland compared to icue (corsairs version). For my case, I have cables that convert basically any manufacturer 3-pin RGB to be compatible with icue (thank you PirateDog.com). Overall, I am satisfied with this case and if the full tower setup is what you're looking for, include this case as one of your options. Keep in mind that it's LARGE. So, if you are limited in space, this may not be the right choice. Happy building!
reviews.author: B

reviews.title: Sheer size, Great looks, Extreme versatility, durability, and quality.
reviews.comment: I have been a fan of Cooler Master cases for many years. Having built several personal PCs over the last couple of decades. So when I decided that it was time to build one last one (wife laughing in background) I chose the EVO 700. I was not disappointed. I has a huge capacity for any MB/cooler/graphics combo you wish to build and that's just the main compartment! A second compartment allows for your power Supply and storage drives. It supports a mix of 3.5, 2.5 HDDs or SSDs with a well designed tool less system that is sufficient for almost any use case from Gamer PC, Workstation or even as a server. My only personal con has to do with the mounting of the Power Supply. I chose an ASUS ROG Thor 1200W Power Supply which has an ARGB display area. Since the case is designed with a divider and the Power Supply fits in the lower rear right area of the case the display is not visible. There may be a mod to remedy this but I did see an easy solution for now and since I can monitor the Power Supply voltages and temps onscreen it is only a minor concern compared to all the advantages this case offers.
reviews.author: Daniel W.

reviews.title: Panels and compartments make easy access. Plenty of ventilation and room for liquid cooler.
reviews.comment: This is a great case with plenty of options and space for every size motherboard. If you are short on space then this case  may not be for you. It is well constructed and compartment have removable panels as well as easy access for the filters. I purchased a Cooler Master case 11 years ago and replaced it with this one. There have been a lot of improvements and updates.  I really like the way it is constructed and would recommend it to anyone looking for a full tower case. I would like a little better manual with this case, but it does work. Cables are easy to hide and connect, and it is compatible with just about any board.
reviews.author: Ken

reviews.title: My favorite case so far.
reviews.comment: I have always liked HAF cases and this one is by far my favorite amongst them. Tons of cooling options and an awesome front panel with some of the best RGB lights I have seen, the small round screen is great for showing all kind of PC related info and optionally gifs or still pictures, it does lag with gifs though, a 10 second animation might take twice the time to show. The case is roomy inside although it might still be unable to accommodate very thick GPU cards from previous generations. The HDD compartment behind the motherboard is nice but gets a bit hotter than the rest of the case, it could use some dedicated cooling.
reviews.author: C. U.

reviews.title: Coolermaster haf 700
reviews.comment: I think it's the best case out there. Im not a fan of lights on any case. When you load it up with PC hardware it's going to be extremely heavy and takes some space. Great cooling and cable management.
reviews.author: Aaron Reas

reviews.title: Perfect Left Side PC Case
reviews.comment: Absolutely goated PC case. I picked this specifically because I wanted my PC on the left side of my desk, and this PC looks great! The fan hubs are also great even though I’m using daisy chained fans. Plenty of room in the back for cable management, and I was able to fit a high end custom water cooled build in it.
reviews.author: Austin

reviews.title: Amazing PC Case
reviews.comment: Purchased the case without fans since I had plans to have all matching fans for this build.  The case arrived in great shape ... Bequiet did great with providing plenty of protection for the case 👍. I had one small hiccup with one of the RGB headers that came with the case ... someone in production didn't give enough slack for one of the wires running from the RGB header and it pulled the connection off the header a little ... didn't break or compromise the performance of the lighting for the case. I even contacted Bequiet and explained the situation ... they didn't skip a beat with responding by sending me 4 extra RGB headers ( my kind of customer service!). The build quality of the case is SOLID. They also did a great job with the white paint for the case ... no missed spots and no imperfections 👍 This case has plenty of room for cable management, its super easy to take part to get easy access for installation. I purchased AsianHorse PC Fans for this build... Half the price of Lian Li's pc fans and they provide great lighting and airflow! ***The photos attached are from testing the RGB lighting for the case ... as well as making sure all the fan performed properly and there were no issues. **
reviews.author: Brendan Campo

reviews.title: This case
reviews.comment: Love this case!
reviews.author: Devin

reviews.title: Pretty good overall
reviews.comment: One of the best cases for an inverted build. Cable manegment options could be better so - 1 star.
reviews.author: Customer42

reviews.title: Lot of space + nice RGB
reviews.comment: A lot of space. I've easily migrated from my old PC case. Nice RGB lights.
reviews.author: Yulian

reviews.title: IT IS A BIG AND WONDERFUL CASE
reviews.comment: This is a great full ATX case.  Plenty of room for the installation of my RTX 4080 Super on a ASUS TUF Games Z890 Mother board.  The power supply unit installs at the bottom in separate air flow than the main box.  Cable management is made easy as you can run everything behind the mother board.  The glass is tempered and looks great.  It comes with 4 RGB fans that interface though an included RGB hub.  The directions that come with this case are not good and provides no guidance on how the RGB hub should be hooked into the mother board.  If you get this case use a SATA power cable from your PSU to power the RGB fan hub and connect the ARGB cable from the hub to one of the three prong ARGB connectors on the mother board.  You can manually change the colors using the LED button on the front control panel or if you push and hold that LED button for 7 or 8 seconds the mother board can control the case fans colors.  Also know, there is no fan speed control for the fans that come with the case, the hub does not have that interface. The fans do keep air flowing very effectively.  I installed a TRYX Panorama SE 360 ARGB 360mm AIO and running a full bench test my CPU and GPU temps have never exceeded 65C.  Normal temps average around 37 to 50 C while gaming.  The fans that come installed in the case are very quiet.
reviews.author: Shel J.

reviews.title: In love with this case!
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/B1kCfI4ScVL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/41gBEpepxLL._SY256.jpg I decided to go with this case for my ultimate build, and I don't regret it a bit.
The case looks even better in person, it is big though, and a bit heavy, perfect for me as I like my computers big and imposing.
The fans are nice, syncs well with the rgb in my cooler and rams, the light modes are varied and cool, there's multiple choices to make your pc lighting look great.
A small problem would be the cable management at the back of the case, the cables come a bit tangled up and you must rearrange everything to make it snug and clean. Besides that I didn't have any other problem and the installation was swift.
Totally recommended for its price as the quality is incredible.
reviews.author: Nicolas Corral

reviews.title: Lots of space, great show case and exactly what I wanted in a set up!
reviews.comment:
BIG NOTE!!! For this case when purchased in black! The glass is tinted, the images almost make you think they are clear but it's definitely tinted you can see in the photos. Luckily for me with how easy it is to remove the panels I run it with no glass when I play it. Second note the 3 fans not on the rear of the tower are reverse finned to allow air flow in with the aesthetic of not looking that the fan supports for the motor. Last note when tucking the wires on the black side and you have a larger wad of wires, if sticking out just too far it will push against the panel and it'll not hold on.. learned the hard way.
Overall its what I wanted from a case, I wanted to put my 360mm radiator on the side like I have it in this one. Love the glass and how easy it is. The removable corner piece perfect. I like the sneak a fan or hard drive under the bottom little drop shelf there and the hide away everything for your wires. It's also set up for the graphics card to be side mounted I'm definitely considering. The adjustment possibilities for all the fans are great because the holes are slotted it's amazing. Now you can set them to where it feels right rather than it being set although those slots end up making it feel flimsy that's just the other end of the coin when it comes to that. Great for supporting your radiators because most of the time when you have a corner of the case and your hoses coming off the radiator end up hitting the fan and makes you end up needing to try something different. So definitely satisfied, if I get another definitely white but I do love my grey and black theme!
reviews.author: Elizabeth Willor

reviews.title: I was initially disappointed, but this ended up being one of my smoothest builds...
reviews.comment:
I've built roughly 20 PCs in the past two months.  I personally run a Corsair 5000D, so I've done more Corsair cases than any other brand, but have been trying a few others out, as Corsair and NZXT want an arm and a leg for their AIO and Fans.  The other atrocity with Corsair is them shipping their white cases with basic black fans unless you pay more for the RGB option and then it is their basic RGB fans...
I've bought a grip of SAMA PSUs recently, as they have been very reasonably priced for their rated powers and 80+ Gold and Platinum offerings.  I saw this case and found that SAMA's AIO was reasonably priced and you could order reverse blades fans at a reasonable price.  The case comes with 3 reverse blade fans on the rear to the right of the MOBO and a regular rear exhaust fan.  The disappointment came when I opened the back panel to find a 4 fan and ARGB hub that was full before extra fans and AIO.  Then I recognized that the ARGB cables all had the ability to daisy chain more, though the pre-installed fans did not, this was a relief.  The front panel controls are actually on the base of the tempered glass panel and tucked into the bottom of the case, which was really easy to work with.  I thought I would be able to add 3 fans to the bottom, but it looks like I was mistaken.  There are only two holes to mount a fan, either 120 or 140 on the lower level at the front, whereas the space elevated below the motherboard has a few screw holes, but I don't think one could mount fans with 1 screw and expect them to be stable.  Either way they only had one reverse fan blade fans in white in stock last week, but I had already ordered 2 more today before I started this build.  The top cover is mounted with pressure mounts, but they provide two silver thumb screws to secure it, which is nice.  They also provide two replacement female pressure mounts in the event one fails over time.  Reasonable cable management options and clean finish.  This build was SAMA case, PSU, AIO and additional fans.  One of the easiest builds, very little tight/cramped spaces and I can't wait til I plug it in and setup the OS and see how it looks lit up.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Bunger

reviews.title: Best case i have bought!!!
reviews.comment: Best case i have ever bought, and i have gone through many.  If you want the bet showcase for your gear, this is it.  The modularity of it allows for your own personal touch.  And having all the drives, and powersupply in the back chamber, the classic clutter of cables is fixed!  I got the white one for my windows, and now i want the black one for my linux build.  All the side panels and glass are screwless, a simple button to release them.  The option to mount the GPU vertically if you desire works great too!  I have 5 fans in the front chamber, and two in the rear chamber.  It runs so much cooler then my past few cases, and looks so nice.  Now, remember it is much wider than a normal case, about 1/2 inch + a PSU wider, since you mount the PSU on the back side, hidden from view.  Cable routing is easy, and with all the extra room in the back, you don't feel like you are bending the panel around the cables, like most cases that don't have any room behind the mobo.  10 stars!  What did you expect thoug, it's ASUS.
reviews.author: Mac MacAnanny

reviews.title: A Personal Take on the ASUS TUF Gaming GT502 White ATX Mid-Tower Computer Case
reviews.comment: From the moment I first set my eyes on the ASUS TUF Gaming GT502 White Case, I knew it was something special. Its stylish white finish, combined with a refined yet tactical look, immediately caught my attention. It’s not often that a gaming case makes you pause and appreciate its aesthetics, but this one certainly did. Friends who build PCs as regularly as I do have been wowed by this case. The white version, in particular, is something they hadn’t seen before, and it has received nothing but compliments. But let’s not stop at appearances. This case isn’t just a pretty face; it’s a powerful performer too. The build quality is outstanding - it feels robust and well-put-together, a clear sign of the meticulous workmanship that has gone into its creation. What impressed me further was how this case handles heat. Armed with a Raptor Lake flagship processor and a 360mm AIO, my rig stays cool under pressure, with temperatures hovering around a comfortable 32°C. The case’s excellent thermal performance ensures my gaming sessions are smooth, even when the action ramps up. The GT502 also boasts a host of handy features. The front panel RGB button and ARGB hub let you add a splash of color to your setup. The inclusion of USB 3.2 Type-C and dual USB 3.0 ports adds to the case’s convenience. Plus, the fabric handle on top is a nice touch for portability. In a nutshell, the ASUS TUF Gaming GT502 White ATX Mid-Tower Computer Case is more than just a good-looking case. It combines striking aesthetics with high-level performance, offering a fantastic package for PC builders and gaming enthusiasts. I couldn’t be happier with my choice, and I’m sure you will be too.
reviews.author: Dr. Derp

reviews.title: Awesome Case to build in.
reviews.comment: Such an easy case to build in, It’s very sturdy looks amazing in white and there’s plenty of space for your components in one chamber and cable management in the back chamber. Still an awesome case, even though it’s not a newer model.
reviews.author: Richard Cash

reviews.title: Love this case!
reviews.comment: I've been building pc's for years now, and saw this some time back and knew I wanted one.  I recently jumped up to 14700k, and knew I wanted to put it in this case.  The case has plenty of room, everything has a very high quality feel to it, no easy bending or flexing the metal.  It just feels like it will last a long time.  It looks great, I just wish I was able to get a white mother board and white gpu, but I was using a 4090 from my old system, not going to buy another one of those if I don't have to, $$$$!  All in all very happy with it, was easy to build in, and get everything setup the way I liked it.  The only other thing I wish I had did was go with some Lian Li fans, less cable management then your standard RGB fans, saved a few dollars since  I had some corsair LL 120 rgbs fans already.  I might get the black version for another build later.
reviews.author: Rich and Jen

reviews.title: Great Case
reviews.comment: My favorite case ever. Plenty of room.
reviews.author: Customer

reviews.title: Easily the Most Premium and Well-Designed Case I’ve Ever Owned
reviews.comment: I’ve built a lot of PCs, and the ASUS ROG Hyperion GR701 is on a completely different level from any other case I’ve used. The moment you take it out of the box, you can feel how solid and overbuilt it is. The semi-open structure gives it a really aggressive, high-end look, and the airflow is excellent without needing a ton of extra adjustments. The tool-free side panels are one of my favorite things about this case — being able to open it instantly makes cable routing and upgrades way easier than on traditional cases. Inside, it has more space than you think. I was able to route cables cleanly, mount large radiators, and install everything without feeling cramped. Supporting dual 420mm radiators is a huge plus, especially for anyone running high-end CPUs and GPUs. The built-in GPU holder is also extremely helpful because modern graphics cards are heavy, and this keeps everything perfectly level with zero sag. The dual front Type-C ports are another small detail that make everyday use way more convenient. Overall, the Hyperion feels like it's designed by people who actually build PCs themselves. It’s sturdy, spacious, easy to work in, and looks amazing once everything is installed. If you’re building a high-end system and want a case that actually matches that level of quality and performance, this one is absolutely worth it.
reviews.author: Alex

reviews.title: LOVE THIS CASE! (IT'S HUGE THOUGH)
reviews.comment: This case is AMAZING for me, however it is HUGE and HEAVY, so it definitely will not be for everyone. PROS: - High quality sturdy premium construction (I bought mine used/open box so it was less than MSRP, but if you need a big spacious high quality case it's worth the price) - HUGE inside that will fit everything you need and very easy DIY setup, it was my first build and everything worked the first time I powered it on - PLENTY of large 140mm fans for adequate cooling, 1 minor issue with the rear fan though you must pull it out in order to install your MOBO, and it will cover the top left side of it a little so it there's an LED screen it will be covered which is an odd design considering I installed an ASUS ROG Crosshair X870E Hero MOBO and the word CROSSHAIR was completely covered by the rear fan - Like I previously mentioned everything functioned properly right out of the box, you can choose to control your ARGB with the case itself or connect everything to your MOBO and control the ARGB with ASUS Armory Crate - Heavy duty aluminum construction feels very solid and scratch resistant, although the previous owner seemed to not know what they were doing and there were a few scratches on the inside and the glass led wall was all loose inside with some scratches as well (not visible with everything installed for me though) - I installed an ASUS Thor 1600W power supply in mine and even that big boy fit in no problem and even had connections to control it's ARGB with either the case or MOBO Overall very impressed and love this case! I hope they continue in this direction and the next case like this is even bigger and unique looking. It's for sure a head turner and friend's that see if always want to take a closer look, especially when it's on! 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟 FIVE STARS HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!
reviews.author: MVRK

reviews.title: ASUS 4 LIFE
reviews.comment: The ROG Hyperion GR701 BTF Edition is more than just a PC chassis—it’s a statement piece for serious builders who demand style, space, and cutting-edge airflow. With its Back-to-the-Future (BTF) layout, this case redefines build aesthetics by hiding cables and connectors behind the motherboard, delivering a sleek and ultra-clean presentation. Built with premium materials, the GR701 offers exceptional modularity and cooling performance. It supports E-ATX motherboards and massive GPU clearance, while its dual-chamber design keeps temperatures in check even with the most powerful components. Its generous internal space allows for ambitious custom loops or multiple fans and radiators, making it a dream for enthusiasts and overclockers. Every detail is thoughtfully crafted—from the integrated ARGB lighting and tool-less panels to the versatile front I/O placement. Whether you're showcasing the latest ROG components or creating a minimalist powerhouse, the GR701 BTF Edition turns your build into an art piece.
reviews.author: john alexander

reviews.title: Awesome Looking Case
reviews.comment: Case as well thought out. From installing graphics card and removing side plates(which need to remove the door for) to already preset cable management compartments that work well so that nobody notices. Plenty of area space all future proof upgrades. Thanks to the double doors on unit and glass even with noisy fans It seems quiet. Expensive keys, but you do get the cool factor would recommend for more experienced and intermediate PC builders.
reviews.author: Dylan

reviews.title: Great and Massive Case
reviews.comment: Legendary case Quality built Very big! Make sure you have the space for it Glad I was able to get it
reviews.author: Diamant_Noir

reviews.title: Great Case at Great Price
reviews.comment: This case is pretty awesome. It looks very sharp. Plenty of room for cable management and even has a hidden hard drive bay. It feels pretty sturdy considering the price point. I even dropped the glass panel and it didnt shatter. The airflow is fantastic. The included fans are surprising great. The colors match perfectly to my Corsair and Thermaltake fans. The size is also a huge pro. Its smaller than my old case, but roomy where it matters. I have plenty of clearance with my AIO which was a massive problem with my old, larger case. I am pretty surprised at how good this is for its price point. Ive had it a month and I can honestly say I have no cons yet.
reviews.author: Ria

reviews.title: Excellent Buy
reviews.comment:
I find the case a great value.  No it is not the thickest of metal, but I would not say it is not flimsy by any means.  Especially once assembled it is quite solid.  Fans work great and quiet.  Plenty of room for my RTX 5070.  Tons of ways to tie down cables and route them in a neat way.
Short:
Pros:
Great cable management with many tie off places built in.
Plenty of pass through holes
Ample room for full sized graphics cards
Ability to easily add top fans
Comes with fans
Nice looking
Neutral:
Material thickness.  Do not over tighten screws, snug then quarter turn.
I found this neither a plus or negative, but could be problematic for the over zealous.
Fits most if not all mobo sizes, if you have a case this big it is ideal for full ATX.
Cons:
Only one cable to control all fans
Would like to control back fan separately
Unable to find another breakout cable.
On my mobo it was tight to get cpu power plugs plugged in as it was close to top cavity.
Photos do not have power supply installed yet.  Note the pass throughs and tie offs.  Also a good +1 inch gap for gpu.
reviews.author: jblues

reviews.title: Pretty good, especially for the price.
reviews.comment:
It's fine. It looks nice, but it did miss a lot of marks. The ports are on the bottom which I guess if you have a desktop PC then that's a good thing. It would have been so easy to make the front plate reversible like so many other cases are, but this one specifically has line up holes that prevent that.
The USB 3 port was extremely tight and I was worried I was going to break something.
The LED lights don't have a controller so they're not individually addressable, they are all just in series in the fans. Fans work pretty good and keeps decent airflow and the case feels fine especially for the price. I was going to consider returning it, but I think it will stay for now.
reviews.author: Austin H

reviews.title: JUST BUY IT (if you have a hdd get a ssd it’ll be fine)
reviews.comment:
I’ll be honest—I almost canceled my order because I saw a review claiming this case was plastic. That couldn’t be further from the truth. It’s mostly metal, with some high-quality plastic that feels just as solid as metal. Whoever wrote that review nearly cost me this gem of a case.
This case is AMAZING. The airflow is fantastic, and while it’s not a full tower, the interior space is surprisingly roomy for a mid-size. The only tight spots are around the PSU and HDD bay (you’ll run into clearance issues if you try to keep both), but thankfully the HDD bay is removable, which solves that problem. Cable management space behind the side panel is slimmer than I expected—they really could’ve given it an extra inch—but the number and placement of cutouts for routing cables is excellent. Even the tricky CPU power cable at the top has a perfect pass-through.
The walnut finish is flush and looks great with the rest of the case. Honestly, for $90 this case blows me away—it’s hands down the best I’ve owned so far. The front I/O panel is also perfectly placed (especially for anyone with cats) and the USB ports are just right: not too tight, not too loose. Everything works as it should.
If you’re hesitating on this case, don’t. It’s an easy build, great airflow, and looks incredible.
In three words?
JUST BUY IT.
reviews.author: Nathan G

reviews.title: Good quality Fractal alternative
reviews.comment:
It’s a cheap but reliable alternative to a Fractal case. For the cost I expected it to be a lower quality case but it’s actually pretty sturdy, I was pleasantly surprised. Only thing some might consider a downside is the fact it can only fit up to a 305mm gpu. I personally was in the market for a more compact ATX case like this one, but if you plan on going with anything bigger than a 4080 or 5070, depending on the specific card, you might want a different case. I’m currently running a PNY 8gb 3060ti with 2 fans, and it fits just fine. I plan on upgrading to the Asrock 16gb steel legend dark 9070xt, which crams 3 fans in a 298mm package.  Another thing to consider is that the fans are on the louder side, so if your pc is on your desk like mine is, you will definitely hear it. Airflow has been really good, but my setup isn’t powerful enough to throw out any major heat, so results may vary.
After a couple months of regular usage, I give it 5/5 for checking all my boxes and looking fly doing so🫡
reviews.author: RJ from Over the Hedge, the hit Hollywood masterpiece

reviews.title: Bulding a high end computer? Check out this case.
reviews.comment: This case exceeded my expectations. It is big enough to accommodate a very large cpu air cooler and EATX motherboard. They both fit easily with room to spare. The 2 huge front fans and large rear fan provide great airflow through the king sized interior. And if you're not water cooling, the top (where the radiator would go) can easily mount 3 more fans if desired. Quality of the case was impressive with clean, not flashy cosmetics. Cable management is the best I've seen. There are a host of thoughtful design items that made my build enjoyable rather than a task. Casters can be installed, which I did, to easily roll the finished computer around the floor as needed. A very useful feature incorporates "handles" as part of the case but they don't look like obvious handles. That helps a lot when you need to move or lift. For a great video review that details many features, search: proart pa602 chassis kleo yan. Watching it helped me determine this was the case I've been looking for.
reviews.author: Bruno Bitin

reviews.title: Sleek Design, Great Cooling & Creative Cloud Bonus
reviews.comment: I’ve been really impressed with the PA602 ProArt Case. The cable management is excellent, making it easy to keep the build clean and organized. The design and aesthetics are sleek and professional, perfect for a creative workstation. The included fans are powerful and efficient, providing great airflow to keep everything cool even under heavy workloads. On top of the hardware, the added Adobe Creative Cloud account makes this purchase even more valuable for creators. It’s a thoughtful bonus that complements the case’s focus on creative professionals. Overall, the PA602 delivers on both form and function, making it a fantastic choice for anyone building a high-end workstation or creative rig.
reviews.author: Behnam B

reviews.title: Excellent, high-quality case
reviews.comment: awesome case, runs cool, silent; made it easy to build my workstation. This is a high quality case, panels attach and detach smoothly, the pre-installed large fans (front and back) are quite good (silent at normal medium speeds) and save some time. Running cool with a 24-core AMD Threadripper and Blackwell 6000 GPU - and at some point with 2 of those of GPUs (yes, there's enough space of that). One piece of warning: if you are using CPU cooling with the radiator on the top of the case (like I did), install the radiator fans before installing the CPU, for otherwise you likely won't have enough space to screw in the screws to hold the fans in place.
reviews.author: Mauro

reviews.title: It's huge, beautiful and quiet!
reviews.comment: This is the first high end case I bought, and my 10th or so tower build over 35 years. This was the easiest case I've ever worked with and it has great cable management. The quality is impressive, the 200 mm front fans and rear fan are very quiet (of course under high load you can hear them). The air filters are very well designed. I'm running an Asus Z790 MB with an i7-14700K, RTX3080, a 280 mm CPU water cooler from Corsair, and an Asus 1000W power supply. I was very surprised how much cooler this machine stays even with barely audible fans vs. my past few machines. Even with MS Flight Sim running maxed out its still pretty quiet. Also, no issues with regard to my 2 TB M.2 PCIe 5.0 x4 SSD heating wise using the stock heat sink on the MB. Everything fits well, just have one complaint. The 2.5" bays on the backside are set up such that a normal 90 degree SATA cable is backwards, so I think Asus should have included reverse 90 degree sata cables. But if you have a flexible set you can make it work, or just use one of the the 3.5 in bays with an adapter.
reviews.author: D. Smith

reviews.title: A Well-Built and Designed, Full Featured Case that Creatives Will Love
reviews.comment: Let me say this from the jump, this case is for those whose computer usage requires high-end processors or multiple GPUs like the RTX 5090, i.e. editors, 3D artists, data miners, etc. Unless future expandability is a consideration, its size may be overkill for most gamers and those that don't need the extra space. I purchased this case as part of a new build due to overheating issues I encountered with my previous build, which was housed in a regular ATX case with 2 RTX 3070s. I work as a video editor and 3D artist who does a large amount of rendering and other processor-intensive tasks. With reports circulating at the time on heating issues with the higher-end Nvidia GPUs (I have two RTX 5080s) and Intels Arrow Lake CPUs (I have a Core Ultra 9), I worked on prioritize airflow when it came to case selection. 14 months later and I can say I couldn't be happier. The case itself is solid and very well-built from the dust filters to the glass panel, with parts that feel premium across the board. It comes with two large fans that run extremely quiet at high speeds, with plenty of space for additional fans or AIOs.. Its massive size not only helps with airflow, but it makes assembly that much easier even with multiple GPUs. It's also comes with wheels pre-built into the case itself, which makes it easy to move without having to physically lift it. Overall, I could see using this case for years so long as everything that can't be replaced holds up. If I can get two builds out of this case (or a decade of use) before having to replace it, I absolutely would consider it money well spent. An easy recommendation for professionals across the board.
reviews.author: Delise LePool

reviews.title: Really, really nice!
reviews.comment: This is an awesome case! My last case was a Corsair Carbide Series Air 540 White, so I wanted to give the vertical liquid cooled design a try and I’m impressed! Running a Ryzen 7800X3D and 5080 - Cyberpunk 2077 maxed out 1440p barely makes the the cpu and gpu reach 55C. They barely hit 70C @ 4k. The space for a full 360 AIO cooler, two 160mm lower case fans, three 120mm front/side fans, and one 140mm fans in so many different configs is awesome. You’ll be able to find your sweet spot regardless of your setup. The preinstalled cable management into the case gives you an idea of how the flow of wires should or could go. Very helpful for new builders and vets alike. The case comes with extra Velcro straps and zip ties. It also includes a tool kit for your screws. For being essentially only tempered glass and shell mesh, it’s quite sturdy and rigid. I never feel like I have to be gentle with it. Dust could be a problem as there is only one dust filter on the bottom. Overall this is a great case with a lot of space and well thought out engineering for gamers.
reviews.author: Major Bizzell III

reviews.title: Nice Case. Very Happy
reviews.comment: I like this case. Was fine to build my computer in and I like the large fans on the bottom. Seems like plenty of airflow. It looks nice with the the glass in it. Very happy with this purchase.
reviews.author: Chris

reviews.title: Great case, maybe skip the fans
reviews.comment: This case is very well designed, looks great and has really high build quality. Building in this is very easy. All of the panels come off as you would expect, all of them feel very sturdy. There is a lot of room to work in and build in. I bought the ARGB version, which comes with the fans. I would not due so if I were to buy it again. The fans work great and move a ton of air. I really like the 160mm reverse blade bottom fans. However, both of the bottom fans made a high pitched humming sound when above 40% fan speed and the 140mm exhaust fan made a rattling noise. Antec customer service was super responsive and sent me out replacement fans 2 day air from Taiwan. Unfortunately the new bottom fans also made the same noise. In the end I bought 3 140mm reverse blade fans to replace them. Maybe yours won't make the noise, or you won't be sensitive to it, but I would just buy the version without fans and choose your own. For anyone wondering, the bottom and top will fit 3 120 or 140mm fans or 2 160mm fans. It will fit a 360mm radiator, but not most 420s. The side will fit 3 120mm fans or 3 140mm fans if you either don't screw in the top two screws on the top 140 or drill holes in the case for those screws. I have 140mm Uni Fans that connect together mounted there, so I didn't feel the need to put in the top two screws. The bottom air filter is a fine screen and blocks dust well, but is very delicate and has no bracing, so be gentle with it. It takes up the entire bottom, so you can't really have anything standing there if it's not already covered by fans. The side intake is just small holes in the panel. I know those are in style now, but they are still a lot larger than the screen filter and let in a lot more dust, so I wish there was a screen filter there as well. All in all I love the case and if I had bought the one without the fans I would give it 5 stars.
reviews.author: Jaethos

reviews.title: quality case, roomy, cable management, drive capacity
reviews.comment: awesome case, glad to see Antec back in the game. My last Antec case is 12 years old and still no rust, in an island environment. plenty of room for drives in the back (4ssd and 2hdd), good cable management, great thick glass panels. the 160mm fans on bottom keep my 3080ti at 50c during gaming, lol!
reviews.author: awGuru

reviews.title: A case offering an easy build while looking good to boot.
reviews.comment: This case has been an excellent case. It’s easy to build in and fairly priced $150 w/fans. Though I would buy without fan next time as I switched to 3x 140mm bottom and rear, 120mm every where else. LIAN Li fans. Low resistance for airflow. Keeps the 9950x3d and 5090 cool while offering a clean look.
reviews.author: Andrew Jasper

reviews.title: Excellent alternative to the Y70
reviews.comment: Decided to go from a Hyte Y70 to this case.  Unfort, I had issues with Hyte's proprietary pcie riser card and couldn't get it warrantied.  So decided to just switch cases to something I could either horizontal mount my gpu or not rely on Hyte only parts.  (just fyi, the vertical mount width is 12.5-12.8cm.  Tried a LinkUP riser but base was too small.) PROS: Real metal parts, not plastic (except for the bottom cover) Can mount a 420 aio Switch from horizontal or vertical gpu mounts Both front glass panels swing open and can be taken off Can be built upright or laid down flat (which looks like a toaster oven lol) The red color pops! CONS: Not an EATX case as stated The bottom and top covers use plastic connectors that may break Corner of the front glass has a cutout where the pull tag is.  Saw a review where that section came apart. The bottom fans under the case are set too far in.  There's a large empty channel near the front of the case where they could have centered the floor fans instead. Even with those odd choices, I still love this case.  There is so much room inside.  I was able to use all 140 fans and 420 aio.  Wish they would have release the Pro model in red!
reviews.author: Jonny Quest

reviews.title: If you have the space, this is a great case!
reviews.comment: Fantastic case. Well made. Easy to access all areas. easy cables from front panel (integrated header instead of the usual individual single pin cable terminals, except power button but that's no biggie). And lots and lots of room. Which was needed in this build because I wanted to run this PC with 2 graphics cards for better rendering time (RTX 3090 ti and RTX 5070 ti). The ability to orient in landscape mode was a big factor in choosing this case given how close the GPUs are to each other (can't be helped on consumer mobos). And the size and configuration of the fans for air flow was also key. I know, the front fans blowing directly at the glass front isn't the greatest, but in this case that glass panel is angled such that the air hitting it will be deflected back at the GPUs/across the mobo, so I was inclined to give this a go for the looks as much as the size/space. I was rewarded with GPU and CPU temps barely 10 degrees over room temp at typical gaming load (so far maxing out at about 20C over, i.e., 50ish during ~80% CPU/GPU load), which is crazy. We'll see how well that is maintained during an extended blender render, but so far very confident in this build. Note, the fans were purchased separately (and they are quite good and I'll review them too). Overall this was a great purchase and value. For reference, this build included 4x140 fans, 3x120 fans, a 360 AIO, Ryzen 7 9800x3D, crucial pro 36gb ddr5 6000 ram, the mentioned gpus, and asus B650E max gaming wifi W mobo all running on a be quiet straight power 1500w psu. All stock, no OC, nice and stable thus far. And although not entirely planned, I think the red, white/ice, and black all work well visually. If you have the space, this is a great case! The only downside is pay attention to the warnings from others about potential to break screws/spacers/connectors. I can see where that could happen, but honestly, take your time and carefully start threads and align connectors. Don't be tempted to tighten (just snug up nicely), force, or assume things are aligned and you just need to apply more torque/force. and you should be good to go.
reviews.author: Chris B

reviews.title: Great spacious case for display and easy building
reviews.comment: Fantastic case to build my new PC in. It has maximum space for my super-large hands to install any component. I went with the vertical GPU, and this case comes with everything necessary to make that happen. I haven't tried the lay down flat position yet, but I am considering it for the summer. It has the meshes over all the intake fan positions, and my inner case stays as dust-free as possible. I even have room to put my Funko Pops! It allows for 3 120mm bottom case fans, not 3 140mm. It allows for 3 140mm case fans on the side for intake. It allows for a 140/120mm rear case fan for exhaust.
reviews.author: David Eaton

reviews.title: Budget Looks Premium Feel
reviews.comment: Cable management is surprisingly easy with 25mm of space behind the motherboard tray and plenty of velcro tie points. Fits my ATX board plus 360mm AIO up top with no clearance issues. The tool-less panels and magnetic dust filters saved me a ton of time. Room for up to 10 fans means airflow isn't a problem
reviews.author: Albert

reviews.title: The best case that ever had.
reviews.comment: The case is excellent. It's easily manageable, has a lot of useful features. The case can be placed in two positions. There is even a shelf for ARGB hub inside of the case. hAVE NOT SEEN A BETTER CASE.
reviews.author: EG

reviews.title: Awesome case
reviews.comment: Better than expected. Solid case, great design, easy to remove panels, and quality build, no sharp edges. Highly recommend. Project zero motherboard fits  great.
reviews.author: Simon C Robinson

reviews.title: Good!!
reviews.comment: very unique, works well and is easy to take off
reviews.author: pc building

reviews.title: really nice case!
reviews.comment: fan hub in the back is a little unorganized but it all works really well.
reviews.author: m

reviews.title: Super clean case but with one ironic flaw
reviews.comment: So the case is exceptionally well designed and easy to build in, the quality is a lot better compared to MSI cases in the past and the aesthetics are just beautiful. The one flaw is that MSI decided to use 3 pin fans for the 4 provided fans so you won't get pwm controls, if you plan on using different fans then it shouldn't pose as an issue. For me personally it isn't a huge deal breaker as I normally run my applications/games, monitor my temps, adjust my fan speeds to a fixed speed and leave it at that. The fans running at 100% isn't loud surprisingly with great airflow, I have the stock fans running into a splitter with fan reduction set to 60% operation so they're silent and still moving adequate air for my components. Main reason I wanted to use stock fans was to save cost plus the 3 intake fans are reverse blade design so no backside fan support bracket exposed. There are a couple of fans on the market with reverse blade designs that I've used that I prefer not to use again because I'm not a huge fan of the design or software issues.. "cough" thermaltake tt rgb plus. I wanted simple so the stock fans did just fine but better with a splitter that has a resistor in it for reduction in operation. If MSI could in the future go with 4pin PWM fans so speeds can be controlled either bios or software it would definitely be an easy 5 stars but given the fact it's also 2024 to even use 3 pin fans is comical and sad especially when you're trying to market this case with project zero as an innovative leap..
reviews.author: Vincente

reviews.title: very straightforward case for MSI project zero
reviews.comment: The case is very well built and highly compatible with Project zero and Lian li products.  Case is whisper quiet even under load when playing games at 1440p,  very clean with little to no cables showing upfront.  Just be careful when closing the back panel as whatever clearance you have for cables may push it open.  If MSI were to improve on this design I highly recommend they go for magnetic seals as opposed to plastic clips and prongs, as this was an issue I had with Thermaltake's Tower 300 case.  Also be aware of the ARGB hub on the back, as mine came with one of the screws stripped already from whomever shipped it or checked for distribution.
reviews.author: Taylor

reviews.title: A decent small case
reviews.comment:
I was able to put in a single slot card to hold 4x PCI-e NVMe card from Sabrent. This ended up being a great little UnRaid NAS that's 5TB of NVMe storage. It's quiet, and plenty of power to host some dockers.
The case is not as thick of metal you'd expect but it is sturdy once assembled. The finish is fine and the edges aren't sharp. I was able to fit the power supply in just enough, but this case is definitely cramped due to its size. You can't really do anything about that because it's designed to be that small.
reviews.author: Donald Kiiskila

reviews.title: Smallest mini itx case that supports a single fan GPU! Heat management and airflow were tough.
reviews.comment:
Excellent mini ITX case! Once all the panels are on, it becomes very solid and is the smallest case I've ever worked with. For size comparison, the size of the monitor to the left is 15.6" portable display.
Pros:
~Smallest possible case that reasonably supports a single fan GPU
~Solid structure
~Easy to assemble/disassemble
Cons:
~Paint scratches easily, especially around the screw holes
~Poor heat management and airflow
~Limited to a handful of CPU coolers and GPUs due to the small size
Overall, it was an interesting build. I was able to run a Ryzen 7 5700X and a GTX 1050 Ti just fine under small loads. However, heat built up quickly when gaming, and since there are no fans mounted to the case for airflow, thermal throttling was inevitable. No space to install fans. I have seen some crazy DIY modifications to these cases to support larger components which is pretty neat but I preferred keeping my case stock.
reviews.author: NolanQ7

reviews.title: Perfect tiny case.  Z690m-itx. Modded
reviews.comment:
I bought two of these cases as a mini desktops and then started modding.  Systems are both Asrock Z690m-itx, 14900k and a 12700K, 64gb Crucial ddr4-3200 with heatsink, 2x Crucial 2tb gen4, RX 6650xt and other 3070FE, both have a Intel RH1 cooler and 600 watt PS.  (won't clear a stock Intel cooler without cutting out a hole in the side panel)
Modded the case with a Dremel.  Measured and cut the access for the cpu fan and GPU.  Total time to mod each case with trial and error= 45 minutes.
Temps go over 100 and throttled during benchmarks on the 14900k, but the 12700k was at 92 and got a better 3dmark score.  Temps were 40-75 on  Win11 with no case fans.  For everyday and gaming, it is the smallest case I could find that would fit stuff.
PCIe riser cable is gen3 and is replaceable with a Gen4 one if needed.  Yes, I like the Intel RH1 cooler, the RGB's on it are cool, but not my thing.
TLDR- Great case.  Easy to mod for full size cards.  Dremel's are great. 12700k runs cooler.
reviews.author: Stan

reviews.title: Limited airflow and riser cable was a bit short on installation.
reviews.comment:
Riser that came with it a bit short and airflow is limited with the mesh design. Heats up fast but the aluminum case did cool down fast when AC was on but if you’re in a place with no ac it’s going to heat up.
Cable management was good and fits everything as advertised. The material is pretty good too and I liked that the front panel came off.
Just components heats up because the airflow is limited due to the mesh design. If the front panel had some perforations and if the mesh design allowed for more airflow I think that it will be a really good ITX case.
reviews.author: radyumi

reviews.title: Best sff/itx I've ever built — my favorite!
reviews.comment:
Despite the panels bowing, this case is sturdy and clean. I honestly love the simplicity and efficient use of space for the components. This is a great looking little case.
Heat management could be better improved by removing the panels altogether, but playing at reasonable settings (medium/mid-high) didn't melt my parts. I plan to mod the panels to get some better airflow.
Overall, a great and inexpensive alternative sff case!
reviews.author: VictorySpin

reviews.title: Good price good quality build. Exactly as described on page.
reviews.comment:
Great case, priced at exactly how it should be and works like a charm. I just wish that the standoffs were unscrew able so I can take them off and put custom ones but that’s preference and not what the product is.
I was able to fit in 5 fans inside which made airflow great and the temps went down from my last MATX case. 4 120mm and 1 90mm fan could fit on the rear.
reviews.author: radyumi

reviews.title: ALL GOOD but beware of Video card power location
reviews.comment: having built a number of computers there is a MAJOR chance you will need to modify something. you get a L shape power supply cable if the power supply fan faces the front of the case it cant suck in air to cool it so you have to have it face the mother board so you have to squash the given L shape cable to get the power supply in. Next the case is so thin I bet the handle will bend the top so I didn't use it. Next you have to screw ALL fans/hard drives to the honeycomb mesh top/bottom/rear and they don't all line up square for the different sizes so they sit at small angles. The inside width is 2 ssd side by side IF ONLY THE MESH HOLES LINED UP to do it but NO...rrrrrr... RECOMEND slim fans for the bottom, regular fans work for back & top. MAJOR problem is if your vid card power cables are on the top (going down from the glass like my rx 580 red devil or 580 fatmax) vs the back of the card they hit the glass so it wont close I had to drill the hole bigger and use mother board mounting offsets to lift the glass higher and they cables still touch so hope you want a smaller card or the power is located somewhere else. ITS REAL GLASS so beware. The bars across the top of the power supply bend with ease a baby using it to stand up might bend them YA its that easy. The dust mesh screens are useless. they attach with junk magnets on 2 sides only  NOT all 4 so any screws used for fans/HD better be small or they over power the magnets, if on the bottom the dust screen just falls off.  For a small case it rocks there is nothing better at this size only 2 problems are mounting the power supply and size / location of power of your vid card if these 2 check out I would get it.
reviews.author: BT

reviews.title: Okay, not great MATX case with front-mount PSU layout
reviews.comment:
This case is a copy of some other cheap front-mount PSU MATX cases that have come out in the last few years. It can be found under other names like SGPC K133 or K88.  At the end of the day it is a very low budget alternative to a premium case like the NCase M2.  But, there are a lot of compromises on build quality when you’re spending 1/5th the amount of money.
This case comes with no instructions, very limited accessories, low quality screws (especially the countersunk ones - they strip very easily), and the case itself is easily bent out of shape. Because the entire side panel is a sheet of tempered glass with holes drilled into it for mounting, the case is essentially a 5 sided metal box with no cross-supports meaning that it can flex at each corner quite easily.  Adding the glass panel on does not really help either because the mounting holes are oversized.  For this reason I’d strongly recommend against using the included carrying handle and leaving this case on your desk. Just for fun I tried picking up my case after finishing my build and my graphics card visibly moved almost 2 cm up and down as the case flexed. Yikes!
For most people, I’d recommend spending $20 more and getting a Jonsbo D32 STD which is a bit wider but has a back panel behind the motherboard tray for hiding wires, has a frame around the glass side panel for durability, and has much higher build quality with bent/rolled sheetmetal for rigidity. This V500 case is literally just a few straight cut panels that are riveted together.  Unfortunately my desk is very narrow and this case was one of the only choices. If I had 2” more width to work with, I would not have bought this case.
On the flip side, this case can fit a full ATX PSU, a full width MATX motherboard, a 135mm tower cooler, large modern GPU’s, and has room for four 120mm fans (2 top, 2 bottom) without making any modifications.  If you’re going to build your PC and never move it around, this might be an okay choice.
reviews.author: TempleJD

reviews.title: Poorly made very bad product.
reviews.comment: The case is practically bare bone. It's lies there's nothing about this case that was pre-installed. It does not look like the picture. It does not come with the RGB fans or any fans in general like seen in the pictures . It doesn't have a lot of room and it has to be modified just to get anything to work. Nothing about this case with ease of removal besides the front glass. It doesn't seem to function like I thought it would because it's something that they put together and with cheap parts looks more like something that was 3D printed. You can practically see the side panel where it looks like it's screws were protruding through. I won't return it I'll just buy another case from somewhere else. This is a waste of time and money.
reviews.author: Cecil Smith

reviews.title: Huge interior and massive airflow for easy building
reviews.comment: I wasn't sure what to expect from a non-name brand, but the build quality on this case actually feels solid. The metal isn't flimsy, and the tempered glass panels give it a clean, open look that makes the internal components the star of the show. Moving my Asus ITX motherboard into this was a breeze because the interior is so spacious. I had plenty of room to maneuver my hands without scraping my knuckles against the top or sides. The cable management holes are well-placed, which kept the finished build looking tidy rather than like a bowl of spaghetti. I do wish the motherboard mounting plate was removable to make the initial install even faster, but it wasn't a dealbreaker. The airflow is massive with nine fans running. You can feel the air moving through the case immediately, which is great for keeping temps down during long sessions. The ARGB lighting looks vibrant through the glass, though the documentation is pretty thin. I had to go hunting online to figure out the specifics of the lighting controller, so be prepared to do a little digging if you want to customize the effects. This is a great choice for anyone looking for a roomy, high-airflow case that comes with all the fans you’ll likely ever need.
reviews.author: 4898inc

reviews.title: Great for a pc build.
reviews.comment: Works great, plenty of room and easy to install. Highly recommend for builds using larger GPUs like the 5080 or 90. Fans were all set up great and it looks amazing. Great value and lots of fans. Only down side was that the cable management isn’t the best.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Best case I have so far
reviews.comment: In complete honesty this case is everything you want from a premium case at an affordable price. It's awesome. I can't wait till I am done with the entire build and I will post pictures. Already comes assembled and cable management is super easy. I highly recommend it.
reviews.author: Ariel

reviews.title: Fast and Easy to work with.......
reviews.comment: I take pride in knowing what is good based of experience and this case is simple. I didn't need the one with all the LED Fans because I have a whole set from another PC. I am glad I decided to go with the fans included in the case. They are far superior to the old LED fans I have. The LEDs of the fans frame also light up. Also, super quiet. If you closed your eyes, you wouldn't know the computer was on.  I have seen Corsair brand PC cases that look like this one, but I don't need a name to be on it as it works like a charm.  The system booted up and has been working like a charm. Simple but looks like more than I was expecting! You will find lots of room for the cable management in the back along with one slot for a 3.5" Hard Drive or smaller, where it is out of sight, leaving the front looking very neat and tidy through the class. That's important to me. I loaded a couple of photos & a short video for your reference.  I hope this helps.
reviews.author: 2CLOS2C

reviews.title: The Case is Great. But Not That Great.
reviews.comment: The case is roomy for the most part. Plenty of ventilation built in, even without the provided fans. The fans will cover the bottom pcie lane of your mobo. Assembly was relatively easy and painless. My only two big complaints would be, the birds nest the fan wires create going to the controller in the back, and the actual front of the case is rather cheesy. But neither is a dealbreaker for me, and it looks just fine under my desk.
reviews.author: JoeDirt

reviews.title: A wonderful case for building a mega-powerful PC!
reviews.comment: The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/E1RN9UpptFL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/61NG2QNKUqL._SY256.jpg A wonderful case for assembling a mega powerful PC. Very pleased with the case. The quality of the material is excellent. The latches are reliable, the glass is thick. There is a lot of space inside for everything you want. I assembled a PC for the first time in my life and spent a long time choosing a case for myself. I wanted to take a case with two glasses. But I still decided to take one, because I was assembling a really powerful computer with all the latest components that get very hot under load, so I took this model because it is very well ventilated. The only downside is that the kit only comes with 5 fans and you will have to buy 5 additional 120 fans. You put three in the front (it looks more effective with three) and put two behind the motherboard on top, in the upper part of the case you put a 420 mm radiator and it already comes with 3 fans, so you do not need to buy separately. From the back, where you have all the cables, you can very neatly place two HDDs, which is what I did, for archiving and storing data. Many people write that they have problems with cable management, but I did not have such problems, everything turned out neat and roomy, although I, again, assembled a PC for the first time in my life. There is a pull-out filter at the bottom that can be cleaned from time to time. There are no filters anywhere else. Although it would not hurt to have one in the front either. I definitely recommend this case for purchase to those who are looking for a beautiful design and practicality for little money. And I recommend that developers add 5 120mm fans to this model.
reviews.author: dim-deep

reviews.title: BEST AIRFLOW CASE OUT THERE!
reviews.comment:
1. Love the case so far! I’m a beginner at building PCs and it was easy to put together. The only thing I advise is to check your PSU dimensions. It is very important to have a semi or fully modular PSU, and specs must be 160mm max.
2. Airflow is amazing and it cools off my i9 13900k very well.
3.  Built in fans move a good amount of air, but tend to get noisy at higher rpm’s. I don’t mind because it cools my pc anyways :)
4. There’s plenty of room for the new GPUs and air towers. 5 fingers of space for my build from the tower to the upper area.
5. It looks amazing and has great airflow! Build quality is good.
reviews.author: Hellwalker

reviews.title: Good case for the price
reviews.comment: This is a large, well ventilated case.  The steel frame is a little flimsy in some areas, but overall well made.  I added two more 140mm fans on the front.  ATX mobo, i9-14900 with 360mm AIO and rtx5090 all fit well and are staying cool.  As others have stated, cable management in the PSU compartment are will get tight.
reviews.author: cfs3user

reviews.title: Great Case
reviews.comment:
I've got to say I am really liking this case. This case was very easy to build in, it's been several years since I have last built a PC and this case was trouble free. Cable management was not as big of an issue as I had worried, took a little more finesse but not worse than any other mid tower cases on the market. I purchased this case mainly for the fan capacity as I'm running a 3090ti Suprim and wanted to make sure of good airflow around my older card.
PSU I would make certain of one thing before buying this case for a build or upgrading on your older case is making sure your PSU will fit. I've got a Corsair RM1000x modular PSU in this case with no issues for room, cabling will be a little tight but not at all an issue if you take your time.
Fans for me do not seem to be noisy for the size or price. I do mainly use my pc for gaming and play with headphones, but even during benchmarking and testing fans at full speed were not obnoxiously loud.
I've got a Micro-ATX Motherboard with a full-size GPU and it clears the PSU housing and shelf well.
reviews.author: Jacob

reviews.title: Poor power supply bay design.
reviews.comment: Very well built but has some quarks. As others have said the power supply bay is a nightmare. There is very little room for the extra cable length and not a place to put them on the side or anywhere else. I just had to cram it all in and hoped nothing came loose. Whatever the benefit is from having it in the front is outweighed by the room issue. Plus now most the standard cables are barley long enough to reach the gpu. With such a big case they should have made some room for cables! But there is no room . Plus now you have to remove the top cover to switch the ps on or off? Just doesn't seem worth it to me. But I did get it built and it is beautiful, you just have to decided if the headache is worth it, and its not like the case is low cost. I expected more for the money, thanks.
reviews.author: Cbaracuta

reviews.title: Great APU option
reviews.comment: Needed a more travel friendly case for my 5600G PC, and after some research settled here. I found the case quite easy to work in, everything fit without difficulty. Quality seems good throughout, and it's a nice looking case. I did need to be a little thoughtful when routing cables, as there is very little room for cable management.. but everything did fit. The front panel cables are a bit long, I suppose that's better than the alternative! I did notice it's a little noisy when under heavy loads, but such a small case can't be expected to contain the noise of a CPU fan running at high RPM. I can't hear the power supply fan at all in my copy, something others had complained about. Just three things to watch out for. First, as I mentioned cable routing is important to consider. Take your time making those connections, and be prepared to reroute as necessary. I found it best to run the 12V CPU power first, lay the 24 pin connector in place, then route the drive cable through the cutout, THEN seat the 24 pin connector. SSD data cable next, I switched to one of the thin cables to make routing a bit easier. Then FP audio, FP power cable, then the USB 3.0. My board doesn't have a USB C header, so I just tucked that in last. Manage each cable as you connect them rather than waiting to the end and trying to deal with it that way. Second, the motherboard tray covers quite a bit of the back of the motherboard. If you have a rear mounted nvme you will not have space for a heat sync unless it fits the small cutout you can see in the photo. Third, rear mounted SSDs are retained by a flexible clip that can interfere with the cooler mount in some instances. I made it work, but removing it would be tight. My only regret is waiting so long to switch to this case. If you aren't planning to use a GPU, and don't use a high TDP CPU, I can't think of a better option. Longevity of the power supply is a concern, mostly because it's proprietary, but there are options if it fails.
reviews.author: M. Kane

reviews.title: Great Product if you don't need a Video Card
reviews.comment: You only need a video card if you're a gamer. This case will allow you to build a decent PC without needing a video card, most mothercards will have you covered. It's a great case, and you will be satisfied.
reviews.author: Larry

reviews.title: Great case for PC
reviews.comment: The perfect case for Mini ITX with minimal need for upgrades. I took the whole case apart the moment it was delivered and burned off the INWIN decal. Solid Aluminum case exterior. Great airflow. Good quality. Can't give five stars because if you take the bulky expensive aluminum shell off, there is a beautiful barebones chassis that can be tucked away so simply. This case could be $40 without the Aluminum shell and no front panel ports. Noctua fan duct kit brought temps down 8c, dissipates well with Noctua LP cooler.

reviews.title: Feels Like an Aquarium, Builds Made Easy
reviews.comment: The best thing I can say about this case is that I didn’t have any problems with my build.  When it comes to PC cases, that’s high praise - something that isn’t always guaranteed with budget cases. I like the airflow design, with 3 intake fan positions providing positive pressure with plenty of exhaust venting and good passive airflow.  Not only essential for good cooling but also helps with dust management.  The magnetic dust filters on both the top and bottom are easy to remove and clean. The glass design really gives this case a unique look.  It feels like an aquarium, which I love.  I’m even thinking about setting up a small diorama inside to really lean into that effect.  It’s the kind of case that isn’t just functional but also has a great aesthetic, making it feel like a display piece rather than just another PC case. The top panel layout is generous. There are three USB ports (USB 2.0, USB 3.0 and Type-C) plus a microphone and headphone jack.  Plenty of room to plug in flash drives or a headset without reaching around to the back.  There’s also a dedicated LED switch, which is a nice feature for people with motherboards or controllers that support it. Cable management was solid, making it easy to keep cables neatly tucked away.  Most of the board standoffs were already installed, so I only had to install a couple for my motherboard size.  Overall, everything was good to go out of the box with almost no prep.  The small conveniences really add up when you’re building. The only real complaint I have is with the tool-less thumb screws for the side panels - it was done in the cheapest way possible.  The threading wasn’t great and one screw feels like it’s going to strip or break.  And that screw doesn’t line up quite right, making it worse.  The low quality approach here was a little disappointing considering how well everything else in the case is designed. Overall, it’s a great case.  Easy for installs, excellent airflow, great cable management, and a clean aesthetic that makes it feel like a display piece.  Aside from the cheap thumb screws, everything was well-designed and made for a hassle-free build.

reviews.title: Great case for my first PC build! 🎀💗

reviews.title: The best PC case there is.
reviews.comment: I have been building PC's since the XT was new. This is the best case I have ever built a PC in. I have two minor complaints. 1. Weight, this is heavy at 33 pounds empty. More aluminum please! 2. 4 Top of case USB 3.1 ports has two mother board header connectors. Every mother board in the world only has 1 USB header plug which means you have too get a splitter for all 4 top of case USB 3.1 ports to work. This splitter should have been included. If you get the splitter available on Amazon, be advised it is too short, so get the extension cable too. Corsair did an excellent job wiring the iCUE fans, controller with the ARGB strips. Just daisy chain plug in your additional iCUE fans and devices using the iCUE USB cables. I have all 10 fans in mine. Keeps all components very cool. A minor issue with iCUE is it auto dims profiles because they want a maximum of 7 fans. Some profiles look drastically different than they would in a case with fewer fans because of this auto dimming. I hope they fix this issue. An iCUE Link Titan 360 RX LCD Liquid CPU Cooler keeps my Ryzen 7 9800X3d around 34c idle. I have never seen my CPU above 40c. I left the LX fans in the case front. I used Corsair QX fans on the cooler and side, rear fans so I have even more LED lights! Just beautiful.
