reviews.author: G

reviews.title: The perfect case the make the smallest possible m atx full size psu build!
reviews.comment:
To preface this review here are my specs for the build
CPU: I5 13700T
GPU: RTX 4070 (Gigabyte)
RAM: 64gb of Trident z Neo
PSU: 850W EVGA Semi Modular
When it comes to building in this case you absolutely need to plan accordingly for its size and your build order definitely matters.
I have used the thermalright Peerless assassin 90 se cpu cooler which is a super nifty 92mm dual tower cooler that’s good up to 120w of tdp peak and fits neatly in this case
The listed gpu length is about 260mm and my gpu is pretty much exactly that but it really is a physical limit and isn’t something you would want to run normally UNLESS you plan for it like I did and order some ultra thin 120mm fans (Thermalright TL-C12015W-S) to get it to fit and you WILL have to remove the front fans to fit gpus close to that 260mm length limit
The mobo I used is the gigabyte b760m gaming plus WiFi ddr4 a decent ddr4 based lga 1700 board that is in a m atx form factor of which I will say that you are best served going with a m atx board for the best look with the case being filled in nicely, honestly a itx case would be easier to build
With but it would look a little small in here.
The panels are actually really easy to remove and once all of the panels are off it gives you a ton of room to work with considering the size of the case.
The quality of this case is actually pretty great! I know it’s not the cheapest case on the market but it’s no slouch jonsbo has definitely earned my business in the future and the curved glass is very neat and gives you a great view of your components!
From a performance standpoint the airflow is not bad at all even with the ultra thin fans and only a single 92mm exhaust (you can also run 2 80mm in the rear but chose otherwise) and as long as you aren’t trying to stuff super large and power hungry components in here it still stays super quiet even under full load and that’s from my own personal experience on my fairly high end components considering the size of the chassis
Building in this case definitely requires some setup, first I would remove all the panels (duh) and remove the front fans, then I would install your PSU (yes before your mobo) and ideally run your power cables and other connectors now before you install your motherboard.
Now this case does include a hard drive tray and a additional 2.5” ssd mount at the bottom of the case but I most definitely WOULD NOT recommend you get this case if you are planning on using any spinning storage, I have a nvme ssd and a singular 2.5” ssd and the cable routing wasn’t bad and cable management was doable with no drive cage installed as I immediately removed it before starting to build.
If you plan out your parts and build in the right order this case can look absolutely stunning and I’m in love with it especially for under $150 bucks well worth the money I spent on it!
reviews.author: Angela

reviews.title: Overall a very nice case, with a few "would be nice to haves"
reviews.comment:
A very nice case, and surprisingly easy to build in (granted, I had a very simple build with no graphics card and only M.2 drives).
A little bigger than I was hoping for this particular build, but I was limited by already-purchased parts, and this is one of the smallest Micro ATX cases that supports an ATX PSU that is available and not too cheap-looking or too expensive.
Cable management was certainly good enough, though one of the fans' connectors broke somehow.  Thankfully it was the daisy-chain extension and so didn't interfere with the build, but it seemed a little cheap.  Fans are ARGB though, which is definitely nice.
I also had to remove the drive bay because the PSU was just barely too long, which I was warned about by my PC build site.  Not a problem because I wasn't going to use it anyway, but it would be nice if it could shift a little.
The wood is definitely a nice touch; I love that case manufacturers are adding things like that, it brings the computer from a box sitting under the desk to a real piece of furniture.
Speaking of boxes, I also appreciate the design deviating from the traditional design language of "black steel rectangular prism with angles edgier than a mid-2000s high-school yearbook".
reviews.author: Falro the Great

reviews.title: Great little case. PSU cable routing can be difficult if you don't have at least a semi-modular PSU.
reviews.comment:
This a nice little case with a wood panel front.  It was very easy to build my PC in.
Pros:
o The screws and other hardware were all in their own separate and labeled mini ziplock bags.  Not quite as nice as the parts box you get with some other high-end cases, but better than other cases where everything is in a single bag you have to tear open and try to figure out which screw is which.
o panels were easy to remove and replace.
o I didn't find any sharp edges to cut myself on.
o the USB, FPANEL and AUDIO header cables are all plenty long enough to reach anywhere on your motherboard.
o it is very easy to connect cables once the motherboard is installed.
Would have been nice:
o It does not come with a rear fan.  Even without, the airflow was quite good.  I could feel the flow of air coming out the rear above the IO panel.
o It does not have an RGB fan hub.  It isn't necessary if you have ARGB headers on your motherboard as the fans do daisychain.
CONs:
o cable routing is difficult if you don't have a full or semi modular PSU, and it is darn near impossible if you leave the hard drive cage in place.  There is not a lot of room for all the cables.
o you can mount a 2.5" HDD or SSD to the 3.5" drive cage, but see directly above.  Or you can mount the 2.5" drive to the bottom of the case next to the PSU.  However, since it mounts flush to the bottom, it makes plugging and unplugging the power and SATA cables more of a chore.  They could have raised the screw holes a mm or two and that would have made it much easier.
Overall, a really nice case.  It is basically a cube, but it looks nice and has a small footprint.  I really want to give it a 4.5.

reviews.title: Fantastic case with small imperfections
reviews.comment:
It's a great case with a few small points that could be better, but aren't bad.
It's well constructed and feels solid.  Definitelyan EATX case, which is hard to always pin down when liking fit cases, but you'll still want to make sure you route your CPU power cables BEFORE you mount the motherboard and AIO if you're using one because they'll both make plugging cpu power in next to impossible if you don't.
The preinstalled fans looks nice and run quietly; they're good quality ARGB fans, though you should know that the bottom fans are not RGB and are one single triple fan plate.
If your looking for rgb fans in the bottom to blow up into the gpu, you'll need to remove the 3 fan plate and install 3 of your own for that.
Airflow is perfect with a top mounted AIO radiator.  If you aren't using an AIO, you'll want to install your own top fans for more exhaust or intake as you see fit.
There's plenty of space in the bottom as well as the rear side panel for excellent cable management, hiding any fan/rgb hubs you might want and so on.
All in all, this case feels nicely premium to build in and strikes a great balance between efficient use of space and comfortable working area for your build.
For a full tower case, it's not wildly huge and isn't going to take up a bigger footprint than most midtown cases do.
Main Complaints -
The tempered glass panel is affixed by a hand screw rather than just snapped in as on more premium brands, but it does mean it has more stability in thy end.  It does snap as well and I suspect you could leave the hand screw out but I'm not sure if it's solidly clipped in enough for that by the clips alone.
The tempered glass side panel is also difficult to remove without also removing the top panel, which is affixed by two hand screws.  You can do it but it's very snug and won't seem at first lile you even can.
reviews.author: Frank Atkisson

reviews.title: Great Box
reviews.comment: Awesome looking box that does the job in keeping my CPU and GPU comfortably cool. Especially in heavy gaming and it looks good.
reviews.author: Karla Greenwalt

reviews.title: Seller confirmed, no Vertical GPU mount, unlike description states. Not good Quality to price
reviews.comment:
-1 Star for misinformation and -1 Star for price to quality. However, the design is goodin general.
Negatives : If you plan to vertically mount your GPU, This case (Black) has NO vertical Mount included in the box, even though it clearly states otherwise.  Ask, seller about the White one before buying.  For the price of the case it is disappointing that it is not included (to and confirmed with seller, especially how its build feels cheap. For example bottom dust mesh is plastic, so before handling the case during your hardware install, remove it. The front panel grid also feels plastic with a non-removable metal dust mesh attached to the panel.  The back area around PSU is also a grid without a dust mesh that will allow some dusty airflow, but other places are well protected from dust. I scotch taped my back-side grid around the PSU, which is not visible.  Last negative, if you plan on using both 3.5" and 2.5" drive bays, one power SATA cable potentially won't be enough to reach for both locations.
Positives: Airflow is definitely good. It dropped my GPU temps by 10C during furmark compared to my old case that also had case fans.
The snap-on type cover panels (top, front and sides) are a great design.  It will definitely be easy to clean, though I don't know how many removal/snapping back in place cycles can the front panel handle.  Also, cable management is quite well thought out., outside of the distance between 3.5" and 2.5" bays.
This one is debatable:  the bottom "three" fans are actually a panel with 3 fans and no RGB. It has only 1 power cable feeding all three fans, which was a benefit to me. I don't care about it missing RGB as I don't see it anyway when sitting. The other 4 fans are proper 120mm fans with RGB.
Note, the front panel should be able to support 3 140mm fans based on tape measurement though I didn't try. It might be tight placing all three in, so a word of caution. Also, my MB has aRGB and case fan sockets at the bottom, I had to rearrange the plug connections between the front panel fans to allow them to reach those locations. The back side fan did not have long enough cable to reach the bottom sockets on the MB, so I sent this one to the top.
Afterthought, with the quality, I would doubt that if the vertical mount for GPU was included it would be any good.
reviews.author: Encrypted

reviews.title: top quality, easy to work with
reviews.comment: For a mini-itx case I don't think you can go any smaller than this. And it's just beautiful ! The quality is top notch, everything feels robust and rigid, nothing's loose or wobbly. It's easy to remove the panels and to work with, and I even fit 2 SSDs in it. Which means I can only use 1 case fan, but since I don't use a dedicated gpu for me one case fan is more than enough, at normal usage (web browsing, text editing..etc) the cpu (65w, ryzen 3200g) temperature is 33C. And no, I don't have water cooling either. At full load it stays under 60C, which is remarkable. One thing to keep in mind: don't even try to fit an atx power supply, go with sfx form factor. In theory you could use atx, but it would take a miracle to manage the cables, plus that it won't leave any room for the cpu cooler. With that in mind, it's the perfect mini-itx case !
reviews.author: Adrian

reviews.title: Sophisticated design, allows for standard PC parts
reviews.comment: This was the SFF case I was hoping for! Sophisticated design and fabrication. The creativity and trial-and-error that went into making this case is evident. Hats off to the Silverstone product team. It's a pretty case. What I like: Volume: 13 liters I think is about the smallest one can get without resorting to pico-sized PSUs and PCI riser cables. Also, is small enough to fit on top of the desk. Aesthetics: White, my preferred color for electronics. The dynamic design of the perforation (hole) pattern are so nice, setting this case apart from other cases. I think it's one of the most attractive cases out there. The durable steel material also allows me to attach my favorite magnets. Compatibility: I was able to use standard parts, such as a SFX power supply, stock AMD cooler and, 120mm case fans. No silly proprietary parts required--thank heavens. It comes with it's own internal PSU extension cable. The Sugo-16 can also take a short double-slot GPU, although I didn't install one yet. Airflow: 4 of the 6 sides have ventilation. Comes with a black dust filter on top. I arranged the air intake from the rear and exhaust out the front.  A surprise--the case comes with no fans. I installed two 120mm Noctua Redux case fans. I used the Stock AMD cooler too--with the pre-applied thermal paste!--there's room to upgrade to something larger later. Convenience: The ball-and-socket joints are a nice choice to easily remove the front and side panels. I was able to build in here fairly easily. However, there are no closets to hide the internal cables--I'm fine with that. Value: At about a hundred bucks, I feel this is a good value. At first I didn't realize it lacked any case fans, but I can live with that--I'm particular about using my own quiet fans anyway. My build: CPU: AMD 5600G APU (with stock AMD cooler) GPU: See APU PSU: EVGA SuperNOVA 450 GM MB: Gigabyte B550I Aorus Pro Max RAM: G.Skill Trident Z 16GB (2x8) SSD: Crucial 1TB NVMe PCIe Case: Silverstone Sugo-16! (white) Case fans: Two Noctua NF-P12 Redux 120mm

The case is also built very strong 💪 No flimsy case here. It Also Easily fit my cooler master 120 water cooler. But I would definitely recommend a SFX power supply or your going to have a lot harder time Building in it. My only gripe is the bottom panel does not come off or it would be allot easier to build in. You definitely don’t want to get a case smaller than this if you want to fit decent sized  graphics cards. This is probably the best ITX case you can get for the size. It’s not to difficult to build in easier then some other ITX cases I have built in.

reviews.title: Title: Looks slick, but acoustics and layout are a dealbreaker
reviews.comment: Visually, the L280M nails the aesthetic—curved glass, ARGB fans, and a built-in display that should elevate the build. But once you get past the glamor, the flaws stack up fast. Rear mesh design amplifies tonal flutter and fan resonance, especially with a rear-mounted AIO. Even at idle, pump hum is audible and persistent. Fan layout is restrictive—bottom intake only, no front mesh, and rear panel overloaded with 3 exhaust fans. Airflow suffers, and acoustics take a hit. RAM clearance is tight for tower coolers. My 44mm modules forced a fan lift, which nearly maxed out the case’s 157mm cooler clearance. LCD display software is dead—links on darkFlash’s site are broken, and no support available. PCI slot guards are tear-out style, not reusable, which feels dated and cheap. If you’re chasing silence, thermal headroom, or clean cable routing, this case will fight you every step of the way. I ended up swapping it out entirely to restore acoustic integrity and simplify my layout. Bottom line: Great showroom piece, but not built for serious builders or resale polish.

reviews.comment:
Very happy with this case. I love the console-like size, and the fact that the face of the pc is solid (no holes). Not so great for air flow, but perfect for stickering! The product info was missing a lot so here's what I found:
- The front panel connectors are a usb 3.0 header, a usb 2.0 header, HD audio header, and power with LED.
- The usb c port is hooked up to the usb 2.0 header. I've included images of the usb c and 3.0 ports speed tests.
- SFX power supplies fit very nicely inside the case. The instructions do say that a full size psu should fit, but I feel like cables would interfere with the GPU.
- I tried using a notcua 92mm fan I had lying around, but the hole in the case do not align. Noctua 120mm and 80mm fans fit perfectly tho.
- I'm surprised with how sturdy the case feels for the price.
During my testing, without any case fans the cpu stuck around 80 degrees C and with two 120mm fans at the bottom and one 80mm outtake in the back, cpu went down to low 70s.
The only negative thing I have to say for this case is that Im unhappy with the usb C port being hooked up the usb 2.0 speeds.

reviews.title: No-RGB Stealth Builder's Dream

Pros: 1) all side panels including the top are entirely toolless and can be popped off with ease (dw, they're fully secure) 2) you have two mounting options for the PSU in case you want to use a BTF motherboard 3) the overall build-quality is top notch 4) i can't hear a thing from this case, even under full-load, so it lives up to the name Cons (not really) 1) While the bottom intake and 3 side-intakes are filtered, the PSU area is not, but this is easily rectifiable by simply buying a small magnetic dust filter and slapping it onto the inside of the right panel above the PSU. I used the Brand: YIMATEECO here on Amazon and and it costed 8 bucks for a 2 pack of their nylon dust filters. Issue solved. 2) I highly recommend you buy an extra 3 reverse-blade Pure Wings 120mm fans to fill the bottom of the case and give it that "complete" look.

reviews.title: Amazing Compact ATX Case With Great Aesthetics, But Has A Very Tricky Build Process.
reviews.comment: There are numerous dual chamber/fish tank cases available. I opted for the Light Base 500 due to its compact size and a few design choices made by Be Quiet. I chose the non-LX version because I wanted to use my own fans to match the Arctic Liquid Freezer III Pro. (The 6 intake fans are reverse Arctic Pro fans.) Pros: -The intake fans are recessed into the case, making them flush with the surface. I have a sound card (yes, I still have one of those) that needs to be placed in the bottom PCIe slot. In many dual chamber designs, mounting the fans would obstruct the bottom PCIe slot. Additionally, I appreciate the visual appeal of having the bottom fans flush with the case’s bottom. -Another design decision by Be Quiet is that the vertical intake fans mounting points lack any mounting rails that interfere with the aesthetics of the RGB fans. Surprisingly, many dual chamber cases have this feature. -I like the design of the angled, vertical intake fans, which are quite similar to those found in NZXT cases. -Be Quiet has installed fine mesh filters over the intake fans. While fine mesh filters restrict air intake, they also significantly reduce dust buildup inside the case. This is a much better option compared to the larger 1 mm metal mesh that many case manufacturers are currently using. Cons: -Due to its smaller size, this case can be a challenging build, which can be frustrating at times. It’s crucial to be very mindful of the order in which you place components. I often had to remove one component I installed to make room for another because I got ahead of myself. This would be an extremely difficult case for a first-time builder unless they were using much smaller components. As you can see from the pictures, I put a lot of larger components into the case. I knew this beforehand due to my research, so I can’t complain too much about it. -The only legitimate complaint is that Be Quiet didn’t include any smaller cable tie off points on the back of the motherboard mount area. I had to get quite creative and use zip ties as tie-down points, which then allowed me to tie down a cable to those points. This seems like a significant design oversight on Be Quiet’s part. Despite the challenges during the build process, the end result was worth it and looks fantastic on my desk. I highly recommend this case provided you’re prepared to tackle the challenge of fitting full-size components into a compact space.

I currently have it set up on 50/50 intake exhaust, but I may swap the rear fan for intake to keep positive case pressure. I do worry this will effect cooling performance as the only way (from what I can tell) of having positive case pressure, is by having the rear intake and top exhaust fans right next to each other.
Otherwise great case design and the ability to house a full size ATX power supply is a huge plus. Would definitely buy again

reviews.title: Good case overall
reviews.comment:
A nice case overall. Hybrid Fish tank and standard narrow case design which is great. Get the benefits of both styles with some sacrifices. Being narrow and not deep, means bottom mounted power supply. Which is fine, but does mean that the furthest to the rear bottom mounted fan is sitting VERY close to the PSU....Which can generate some additional noise based on the very low clearance space. I would say it was only a few MM of a gap between the psu and the fan. Overall didn't affect temperatures really, so I'm not going to dock it a star for that...Overall a compromise that was worth it.
Temps are good, looks nice....Cable management can be a bit tedious, as there isn't a lot of clearance in the back at all, and most of the cables need to be hidden underneath in the bottom compartment. If you don't have fans on the bottom, you may be able to see them through the airflow mesh holes. But with fans there it's not visible whatsoever.
I was considering docking it a star for that, but redeemed as the case has white front panel cabling. I HATE it when white cases have black cabling, defeats the purpose of a white case....But Jonsbo had an all white setup which gets my seal of approval. Great case overall, just a bit tight to work with in the back.
Works with a Hydroshift AIO, although will NOT work with Lian-li's veritcal gpu bracket if you have bottom fans. I had to settle with the cooler master vertical kit instead. No worries though, still a good case.

reviews.title: Great looking case that is easy to install in!
reviews.comment:
This seems to be a really nice case and is worth the asking price in my opinion. Here is the breakdown.
Pros:
- This thing seems well build and well thought out. Access to the different mounting points is easy and the material edges are not sharp or difficult to work around.
- Mainboard mounting is easy with the panels off.
- PSU installation is easy as well, with plenty of room to maneuver.
- Lots of room and options for cable routing.
- Lots of space for fans. Side accepts a 360 fan / radiator if needed.
- The internal structure of the case is very perforated with holes. This makes airflow easy and makes installation easy as well, as there are very few spaces with the panels off where your vision is blocked until you have installed the mainboard. Great airflow in general.
- Case is pretty lightweight. The top is mostly plastic, and the internal frame is rigid but lightweight with all the perforation. Gets heavy with internals, but makes for a really easy to work with starting point.
- The wraparound glass looks pretty great and fits well - no weird large gap or anything.
- Supports vertical GPU mounting (cable not supplied), if that sorta thing is your bag.
Cons:
- Not a lot of thumbscrews, so tools are needed to do anything past removal of the top and panels.
- 3.5" HDD space is limited, and depending on your PSU you may or may not have to move your PSU to access the lower drive mounting space.
- Doesn't come with fans or really any hardware other than standoffs / screws for the mainboard.
Regarding the Cons, none of them a real problems for my build. I don't expect to need to remove components with any regularity, so while I love thumbscrews I don't expect to need more than the 2 required (and provided) to take the top and side panels off. The 3.5" HDD space is not needed, I'll be running all M.2. And I generally like my fans to match whatever I have on the radiator, so not having the case come with fans means a bigger cost but one I was probably going to pay anyway. YMMV.
Unfortunately, with RAM prices being what they are, I haven't acquired all the parts for the build. But for what I have gotten in I am extremely impressed with this case, the ease of working with it, and the overall look - much happier than I expected with a case from a brand I was not familiar with. Kudos! Only thing I haven't really been able to really test so far is noise level with fans and all since that will require at least most of the build. I'll update when complete.

reviews.title: Elegant and well made
reviews.comment: The pictures don't do it justice, it's very attractive and well finished. It feels sturdy. This is a premium case with no plastic bits and a very understated power LED recessed above the power button, no HDD led, reset button, or front audio jacks and one USB-C port on the front. There are extra screws provided in case you lose one. The instructions are clear and the order of assembly in them should be followed for ease of setup in this tiny case. It fits an Asus 2.5 slot SFF ready 5070 card in the middle adjustable position, this leaves enough room for an ITX board with a reasonably sized CPU cooler. With a full length card like this you cannot mount a full size 3.5" mechanical hard disk. There is a spot for a 2.5" SSD or laptop hard disk under the power supply but it gets crowded by the cables fom the power supply. Since the sides and top are all vents cooling is dependent only on your setup. For the 120mm top system vent fan I placed mine so the air exhausts outward/upward, this pulls air through my Cooler Master V750 SFX Gold ITX SFF power supply when it is in zero fan speed mode. The open vents do mean that fan noise will come right through so choose your fans wisely. The only caveat is that the model came with a PCIe 4.0 riser cable, forcing me to set the PCIe bus speed for the video card to the slower 4.0 speed. The Jonsbo web site shows the model coming with a 5.0 cable but I could not find this model for sale with that cable.

There is supposed to be room for a 2.5" ssd, also couldn't put one in due to the mounting position of the psu being so low the cables hit where the drive would sit.  The case comes with a gen 4 riser cable, so if you want to get use gen 5 you'll need a 22cm double reverse and the mounting holes are too far apart to attach both ends so good luck with that. All in all it's a nice case, but so many little things that stop it being truly great.

Another fan could be squeezed in there, but I don't think I'll need it.  I installed an ASRock B550m-HDV motherboard and GeForce GTX 1660 Super.  The 1660 is 225.6mm and fit with a couple mm to spare. No cable management, so be prepared with zip ties to keep the cables off the fans.  Fitting everything is tight, and has no instructions, not an easy build for novices. I'm reviewing this as a budget case, comparing it to other budget cases, as such it exceeded all expectations.

reviews.title: Perfect Small Budget PC Case *(with one minor issue)*
reviews.comment: Due to the limited size of my room, a small PC is all I wanted. I searched through the expensive, more popular brands (such as Fractal Terra) and figured anything above 100 was eating into my budget. Then I saw this PC case. At the time it had no reviews on Amazon but it looked perfect in terms of design and size, so I took a chance. A chance that came good, perfect infact. For 50 bucks, the PC case was easy to build in and easy to cable manage surprisingly. People mention the material being easily bendable but it's sturdy and solid. The description mentioned the case being mini-ITX and micro-ATX compatible but I went for a micro-ATX motherboard which ended up taking the entirety of the inside in a snug and comfortable way. *(Now for one minor gripe that I can't overlook. The two top fans and the side fans fit perfectly, aka the three pre-installed fans, but adding the bottom two fan was annoying. I had to manually widen the screwholes to get the fans screwed down.)* Moving away from that issue, I had to go with a smaller dual-fan 5060 TI gpu since the space is limited, but for what I play, it's absolutely perfect. So please don't get this if you plan on having any gpu size above 280mm. Air Flow is nice, I have three intake and two exhaust fans which keeps the whole things nice and cool. This will be my case for a good while, what an affordable and absolutely amazing option for budget builders.

reviews.title: Buy It & Thank Me Later
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/H13S4eX+gUL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/41I0IiqdlZL._SY256.jpg First thing you need to know is that I do not write reviews lightly or even at all really, but I was really blown away by the performance of this CPU cooler and I felt like I needed to let people know to just pull the trigger on it and don't think twice. I also am not paid or associated in any way with Noctua.
It improved my thermals by over 40° C. I had a 3 year old Lian Li 360 AIO that was showing it's age. I have a great Fractal case and it moves a ton of air. I also am running a i9-12900k which is power hungry at all moments and tends to run hot. I did not know there was a problem with temps until my computer shut down while I had a game open and I wasn't home. My computer shut down on it's own, warning that the CPU temps are way to high and that it shut down. I was unable to restart my computer for about 15 minutes and my AIO felt pretty warm near the CPU. I started seeing artificing after a OCCT stress test.
So I started first with trying the two main things which were replace thermal paste and try and reorient my tubes so they face down. Well I could not do the tubes down due to no flexibility in the tubes, so I knew there was a reason why I put them near the top of the AIO. I replaced thermal paste, and it did not do anything. So I replaced with this cooler and man, it has far exceeded my expectations.
It is so quiet even under load, I cannot tell it's running. Install was overall pretty easy, but just be careful and follow directions closely. There is a lot of value for the money. It is overall more expensive than a competitive AIO, but I digress. I know Noctua's quality, so I expected nothing less. I thought I would need the G2 since I have that power hungry i9-12900k, but I needed to ensure clearance of the RAM. The size is great to clear ram, it still has a little space. So I'm glad I compensated for that and did my research beforehand. The quality is top notch, and it looks great inside of my case.
Worse case scenario, I spent a little more money, but air cooling just makes sense for my particular build since it's literally built to move a ton of air. I may have to replace the fans in like 7 years, but that'll still be cheaper than buying another pump that will eventually fail in 3 years. I would do this over again 100x.

I have always preferred air cooling because they dont require disassembly for maintenance like AIOs. I have always herd that Noctua is the best around when it comes to air coolers and I now see why. reviews.title: Noctua quality ain’t cheap, but it’s Noctua quality.
reviews.comment:
Having run this cooler for the past five months, I believe that although it is very expensive, the cooler is will-worth the money. Here’s some notes I would like to make:
- Excellently well-built fans: The fans here is unlike other PC fans. The fins on the fans are reassuringly stiff, the fins spin up and runs with minimal noise, and the noise that does appear does not bother me. It can be described as a wind blowing noise, without much whirring.
- Heatsink: It is very easy to install per Noctua instructions. It’s still recommended to follow the instructions carefully to avoid any problems, but if you do, installation is a breeze with this cooler in contrast to other coolers I have installed. Coupled with the included fans, the coolers runs very well. The system I used had a liquid cooling system in the past, which kept the CPU at around 65 degrees. This cooler does run slightly hotter at around 70, but as an air cooler, this performance is excellent regardless, especially considering the longer reliability for air coolers in comparison to liquid coolers.
- Accessories: There is abundant accessories included. From adapters to mounting hardware for all sorts of platforms. For Noctua coolers, they even have a program for users to ask for mounting brackets for future sockets, making this cooler a good investment. (If noctua keeps their support, which historically speaking, they have.)
This cooler is definitely expensive compared to others. But I believe that it is a sound investment that is very performant.
reviews.author: The Wandering Tech Guy

reviews.title: Incredible ROI
reviews.comment:
I have had cooling problems on my 11th gen Intel i7 for three years. Every AIO system I’ve purchased has failed, the pump goes out or it just isn’t effective enough. So I decided this time to try a fan cooler.
This thing is perfect. It holds my computer temperature to idek levels (30-50 degrees Celsius,) even with heavy loads like gaming or the video editing I do every week for work. It is big enough to have the power necessary, but not so big it won’t fit in my case. It’s not loud at all, and with how cool my system is now, my case fans aren’t running on high all the time. It isn’t just as quiet as the all in one system, it’s made the computer noise go down all together.
With two more fans, I was a little worried about the power draw, because that’s where I’d had problems before where the pump would give me issues. I have a 750w supply, and it has not even come close to the danger zone.
All in all, I won’t buy another liquid cooling system again. This cooling rig is absolutely worth the money, it’s the best cooler I’ve ever had in my PC, and it is also the least expensive. It’s got the bang for your buck that you’re trying to achieve when building a PC that can perform under heavy loads so you can take what you were going to invest in a cooling system and put it toward more RAM or a better GPU.

reviews.title: Massive Cooler — Keeps My Core Ultra 7 265K Extremely Cool
reviews.comment: This cooler is definitely a beast. It keeps my Intel Core Ultra 7 265K running cool, and I’ve never ever heard the fans ramp up to full speed—even when stressing the processor. It’s probably overkill for my setup, but the performance and quiet operation are excellent.

reviews.title: The King of Air Coolers retains its Crown.
reviews.comment:
This has to be hands down the greatest air cooler ever made.
I am using this on a Core Ultra 9 285k, and under load my CPU rarely passes 50c. I was using the previous Noctua Tower Cooler(Noctua NH-D15). Setup and instructions are extremely easy to follow and simple to install. They made some changes to the screws, but the overall setup remains the same.
Like the previous model, this cooler is quite huge - it's around 15% bigger than their previous generation, and it has a ton more heat pipes. This is almost equal to an AIO in cooling performance. In fact, I think it's even better.
The real major downside to this cooler, is cost. There are AIOs that are cheaper than the NH-D15 Gen2, but what you get is unbeatable. Not recommended for low power CPUs (i3/i5. Non overclockable CPUs, etc.).

reviews.title: Sufficient to keep Intel Core Ultra 9 285 at stable 80-81 C at full CPU load
reviews.comment:
I installed this Noctua air cooler in my new PC build, which includes MSI Z890 Tomahawk motherboard and Intel Core Ultra 9 285K processor. I initially thought I would need a water cooler to meet the 250W which my CPU can easily generate, and was hesitant because I had some doubts about longevity and long term reliability of water cooling. Of course, gamers who upgrade their PCs regularly probably upgrade their watercoolers too, but in my case I wanted a PC which I can use for at least 8 years with minimal maintenance. I was very happy to find out that this Noctua cooler can handle that amount of heat. There was a concern about enough clearance for DRAM; I got one of the slimmest DRAM modules on the market, Crucial Pro DDR5 RAM 64GB Kit (2x32GB) 6400MHz CL40, but even that DRAM was  a little taller (34-35 mm) than the default clearance of 32 mm over DRAM shown in drawings of Noctua. Luckily, it is extremely easy (and approved and recommended by Noctua, if needed) to move the fan which hangs over DRAM slightly upwards on the radiator (it is held in place by wire clips, so one can take it off and install again anywhere on the radiator without tools) to create a few mm of additional clearance. In my case, this fan sticks out a little more than the fan in the middle, but there is still more than enough clearance of the cooler in Fractal Design R7 case. Since fan is bigger than the radiator, there is no reduction in cooling from its repositioning. Manual of Noctua is excellent, written in good English, good pictures, even a screwdriver is included! Very easy to install. Thermal paste included.
I am very pleased with the result. The cooler is quite. Noctua has a reputation of a long lasting brand (6 years warranty).  Cooling is even better than I expected: in AIDA64 Extreme stress test at full CPU load (without overclocking), the CPU temperature is kept steadily at 80-81 C. A little more money than AIO, but no risk of pump failure or water damage. The worst that can happen is one of the fans fails, but there are two of them and massive radiator would work as a passive cooler even without fans.
Talking about water leak risk, I found FAQ on Corsair web site, they say that they see water leak failure rate of 0.016% with their sealed AIO water coolers, i.e., one out of 6250 AIO coolers will leak water-based coolant in the PC. If/when when it happens, I would imagine, liquid may kill the motherboard and/or GPU or PSU. I found no data for frequency of pump failures in AIOs, but people say that pump failures are more frequent as many saw pump failures but not water leaks. Anyhow, air cooler would not leak and fans are very reliable these days, so there is basically nothing to fail :)
Noctua has a database on their web site with compatibility of different models of their coolers with processors and motherboards, a good resource to check before buying.

reviews.title: Wonderful CPU Cooler
reviews.comment: The Dark Rock Pro 5 was used for two builds based on the Gigabyte B850 AORUS ELITE WIFI7 motherboard. One build went in a new Corsair Frame 4000D ATX Mid Tower case, the other in a Cooler Master Cosmos 1000 case from 2007. The CPU in both builds is the AMD Ryzen 9 9900X, a 120W part for which this 270W cooler has plenty of capacity. A middle fan sits between two radiators, covered by a plate bearing the be quiet! logo that is held in place with magnets. Underneath the cover plate is a Q/P switch that allows the cooler to run in Quiet or Performance mode. The fan wiring allows the two fans to be daisy chained and connected to a single CPU_FAN header that is typically located just above the CPU socket on the motherboard. Hardware is included with the cooler that supports Intel 1851, 1700, 1200, 1150, 1151 and 1155 sockets, and AMD AM4 and AM5 sockets. The directions were clear and installation was very easy. The cooler seems to have enough capacity relative to a 120W CPU that the fans tends to stay at low RPM and are inaudible, and it really looks great on a black motherboard in a black case. The Dark Rock Pro 5 is a high quality, well designed and manufactured CPU cooler that should run for a long time.

reviews.title: Great AIO cooler for a very fair price
reviews.comment: Why did you pick this product vs others?: I picked the Be Quiet pure loop 280mm because I needed a two fan AIO cooler for my open air build and this one seemed to be a very fair price from a manufacturer that has gotten decent reviews lately Ease of installation: Overall this was not a difficult installation. I probably would recommend using a pressure plate from thermal grizzly or someone else to prevent board flex, as it did seem possible to over-tighten this design... but if you know what you are doing and use some common sense it isnt really needed. I do not have a pressure plate installed and have even reinstalled after a CPU upgrade and it is working perfectly. The way the pump is positioned on the lines is a little awkward, and I dont necessarily love the look of it as much as bare lines, but it was not an issue for me. Temperature control: I originally installed this on a 9800x3d and it did great. The room this PC is in stays around 70-72F (~21-22c) and the 9800x3d idled at 38c. I have since swapped my CPU to a 9950x3d and it idles very similarly, sometimes a degree or two more. under heavy load like a CPU-z all core stress test I can get the CPU temps to climb into the 80s but never come close to thermal throttling even on a 30minute continuous run. Added Notes: I did not use the included thermal paste, I used thermal grizzly kryonaut extreme. there isnt an issue I know of with the included paste, I just keep the kryonaut extreme on hand and it is a brand I trust. I currently have not PBO enabled on my motherboard, so this likely lowered my thermal needs a small amount while under load, but still the 9950x3d is hitting its all-core boost of 5.1-5.2ghz and max boost of 5.6 to 5.7 without issue while hitting the above thermals. I will be purchasing another of these coolers for a 14700k which eats more power and generates more heat and will update the review at that time, but at the moment I am very impressed with its performance on the 9950x3d.

reviews.title: Excellent performance, but would partially recommend depending on the usage
reviews.comment: Having tried this on 12700k, 285k, 9900x, and 9950x3d, here's my honest review. This cooler performance rocks on intel CPUs. The temps go really low and the cooler is not too loud. It does get noisy at full load, but not too loud. However, I'd not recommend this for 285k because you'll be removing the Reduced Load ILM feature of the socket when you mount it with a contact frame (removing basically doesn't guarantee the factory state if you reassemble). However, for 14th gen and below (which will need a contact frame anyways), this cooler is the best cooler I'd get all the time. For AMDs though, they still cool the CPU really well, but gets really loud. This may be the case for only the 9900x and 9950x3d I've tested, so take this with a grain of salt if you're using lower gen or different AMD CPUs. At full load, this cooler is by far the noisiest cooler I've used, making a noise like a jet engine. I won't really care too much if it was just occasionally loud at higher load, but this cooler also occasionally gets extremely loud at idle state. I suspect it's from temp spikes, and AMDs of course have a smaller surface area and denser hotspot compared to intel. I noticed that I'm not the only person experiencing this, there's a famous youtube video comparing AIO performance, and this issue is exactly replicated. The video even used three Artic LF III to mitigate defective unit possibility, but all performed exactly the same for the 9800x3d, having very high noise levels. I suspect it's something to do with the mounting frame not so secure for AMD motherboards, but this needs investigation. Aside from Intel vs AMD comparison, this cooler does offer a very straightforward cabling, you can either choose to simply plug one cable to your CPU_FAN header, and it's done. Also, the fans are pre-assembled and cleanly cable-managed which is excellent. So my final verdict would be: hands down the best cooler for intel CPUs equal or below 14th gen, cant fully recommend for AMDs. This is because the cooler performance doesn't drastically differ from others (1~2C at max), and you won't really notice the difference given the environmental factors that'll affect the most. So personally, I'd rather choose the most quiet cooler, and this LC is a bit of a mix.
reviews.author: JP

reviews.title: Excellent water cooler, if you have the case for it
reviews.comment: So for those that do not want to read the review, I'll just say it is an excellent CPU water cooler, and a must if you have a higher end CPU that likes to run hot. Now for those that want to read more, here's my review: Before I start with the details, I definitely need to stress that is imperative that you measure your case before purchasing this CPU cooler, since the manufacturer isn't lying, it requires a lot of space.  That being said, if you have a case that can handle it, it works great and keeps the CPU nice and cool. Okay so on to the review.  The reason I purchased the Artic Liquid Freezer 3 Pro is after building a new system with an Intel Core I9 processor, I found that the CPU cooler I purchased for it (Cooler Master 120L) wasn't really rated for such a powerful CPU, and under load the CPU temp was hitting 85c.  Now 85c isn't a killer if it's just a quick spike, but when doing video encoding it was hitting and staying at that temp, which just isn't good for the CPU.  So doing a little more research, I saw that  Artic Liquid Freezer 3 Pro got great reviews, and was recommended for high end processors like the I9. Installing the Artic 3 Pro is extremely easy, unfortunately I built the system in a smaller full size tower case, and the new CPU cooler wouldn't fit the chassis.  Luckily my secondary machine was in an even bigger chassis, and it turns out it had mounting holes and rubber grommets already there to mount the Artic 3 Pro. So after stripping the 2 systems bare and swapping all of the components, booted up the new system with the Artic 3 Pro and checked the temps, and my basic idle temp is 26-28c, a good 10 degrees lower than the idle with the old water cooler.  I haven't had a chance to stress it out with some video encoding yet, but I've already noticed that the heat spikes I was seeing previously seem to be gone. So in summary, I love the new CPU water cooler!  I did run across one issue that had me worried when I first booted it up, and that was that there was a constant low humming noise that seemed to be coming from the unit.  I'd read a couple of other people comments saying there was a low hum, but I figured it was a one off for them.  Of course I like my rigs to be as quiet as possible, and since the PC sits right under my desk I knew this was going to drive me nuts. Luckily I was able to figure out the problem, which was the tubes from the CPU to the radiator are long and stiff enough that they were touching the side panel, and the humming sound was the noise from the liquid moving and being amplified by the metal door.  Fixed this issue with a few zip ties to move the tubes slightly inward so they didn't contact the door, and now the system is as quiet as can be. I hope this review has been helpful, cheers.

reviews.title: Biggest waste of money in my current build
reviews.comment:
I generally don't write reviews, but this thing has been such a thorn in my side.
First of all, when you first turn your computer on you'll notice that the pump is extremely loud at default settings. Like hearing it down the hallway loud. I waited a week to see if the bubbles would settle and make it quiet like people say it is, tilted my PC to work them out, and no change. So I figured maybe I had a dud and returned it to swap them out. Same story. I asked their support about it, gave videos, showed the audio spectrum near the PC at different pump speeds, and was told this is normal. I had to lower the pump speed from the what is already mid-range 2300rpm default to specifically 1690rpm as both 1700rpm and 1680rpm have higher noise.
Then there's the software. It's terrible. For months it didn't even work properly and you had to regularly reinstall it to reset and have it working again for another couple of weeks until it tried to do an update and crashed itself. And the service running in the background is constantly polling the hardware for information like power usage, temperatures, etc. Which makes sense for something like this, but it was causing issues for me in SteamVR and some games with stuttering until I killed the process. And it's a dice roll every time there's an update whether it will start using up 10% of your CPU constantly; increasing the temperatures and eating up resources. This is on a 14900k, mind you.
But the LCD has its own issues: the one of the big things that made me want to pay $275 for this on launch. It works great for about 6 months, but then you'll notice once in a while the image flickers. Then it happens more and more frequently. You try to change images or background colors to see if it fixes it and notice the previous images are "sticking" like there is screen burn in or something, but it very slowly resolves itself over time if you're lucky. Then it really looks like there is screen burn in when you have nothing but a white background on that LCD and the whole thing looks like someone held a candle to it. This has happened to me with the original LCD that came with it AND the replacement they sent me 8 months ago. Which, by the way, they won't just replace the cooler. They'll send you a new LCD and have you rip apart your cooler to put the LCD on. So, if you're not prepared to do that, be ready to ask someone for help.
Pros:
- Cools a 14900k decently well considering how much heat that puts out.
- Infinity fans look nice and are pretty quiet when not cranked up really high.
- LCD looks nice when it works and there is a simple editor to put videos and gifs in it.
Cons:
- LCD has a life span of 6-8 months and has needed replacement twice.
- Loud unless you lower the pump speed a lot and find the magic number to make it silent.
- Troublesome RMA process that some people won't be comfortable with.
- The supporting software is terrible and either causes issues or eats up too much system resources for what it does.
Not worth it. I gave it 1 star since it did a decent job of cooling, especially for running at only 1690rpm and being attached to a 14900k. Maybe just get the non-LCD version if noise doesn't bother you and use third party software or motherboard controls, because I'm not sure they have a QA process or proper testing procedures.
reviews.author: Zoey

reviews.title: Excellent cooler!
reviews.comment: Easy to mount Ease of setup Not too loud Excellent performance, keeps the beast that is a Ryzen 9850X3d running cool, and isn't that the whole reason to buy a cooler. Great price to performance

reviews.title: Great
reviews.comment: Best 420mm AIO on the market. Dead silent even when the pump is on max (I run it at 70% but tested it higher). I think the RGB looks very classy. Excellent value for what you get, and this thing is built like an absolute unit. The tubing is very stiff, but it's hardly a reason to knock a star off.
reviews.author: Zachary Barber

reviews.title: Worth the upgraded!
reviews.comment: Been 1 year since I upgraded from my be quiet! Dark Rock 4 CPU cooler, for my Ryzen 9 7900x. This was easy to install and had many how to videos on the manufacturer website. Noticeable difference in temps since the upgraded. Used to be in the 80s° to high 90s° and my pc used to always ran hot. Now my cpu temps are in the range of 65° to 74°. For me the fans are not loud even if its running on full speed. If your looking to upgrade to an AIO cooler and without spending a lot of money this is worth it. Great price and product.
reviews.author: Nicole Velez

reviews.title: Amazing product
reviews.comment: I wish I could rate this cooler higher than 5 stars. I upgraded from the (still excellent) Arctic Freezer 4U air cooler because my use case changed to  require a liquid cooled solution. After searching through frankly overpriced options ($600+), I found this model. Even at full retail, this product is an absolute steal. I am using the AIO with an AMD EPYC 7F52 (240W TDP), utilizing the seamless fit of the Threadripper (sTRX4) bracket on the SP3 socket. The performance is phenomenal: At idle, the temperature sits between 16C – 19 C (though, room  ambient was around that, so you can expect near ambient room temperatures on the cpu under normal usage ). Curious, I ran Prime95 to pull the full 240W. The CPU would not exceed 48C. To call this product overkill is an understatement. It cools so effectively that the air pushed out by the fans is cold enough to turn your fingers stiff, thankfully computers are far  more cold tolerant than my hand. On top of the raw performance, the build quality is like a tank, and the installation took barely 10 minutes thanks to the clear instructions. I highly recommend this product to anyone. Whether you're cooling an ordinary gaming CPU or a high-wattage server/workstation chip, this cooler can handle it, with included mounting brackets for both use cases. Buy this, put it on your CPU, and it will likely never feel what anything higher than 50C feels like again.
reviews.author: Carl P. Morgan

reviews.title: Outstanding performance, but mounting system needs refinement
reviews.comment:
The Arctic Liquid Freezer III Pro 360 is keeping my Ryzen 9 9900X exceptionally cool. Under controlled 24‑thread stress testing—including sustained AVX/matrix workloads—the CPU holds around 62 °C, which is excellent for a processor of this class. In real‑world workloads like photo & video upscaling, batch video encodes and large software builds, I typically see temperatures in the mid to high 60s and occasional spikes into the 70s, which is completely normal for the 9900X and still well within comfortable thermal limits. I've also observed idle temperatures as low as 35c, but they usually sit between 36-39c.
The pump is very quiet, the radiator fans move a lot of air without excessive noise, and overall thermal stability has been outstanding.
Installation was mostly smooth, but the CPU block mounting system needs refinement. Once the mounting brackets were secured to the motherboard, they ended up just a little too close together, which meant the two screws on the CPU block didn’t line up with their holes. I had to loosen the bracket screws, mount the block, then retighten everything. It worked, but it shouldn’t require that workaround. I also wish the block used four mounting screws instead of two for more even pressure.
Despite that hiccup, the cooling performance is exceptional, and once installed, the unit has been rock‑solid. For high‑core‑count CPUs like the Ryzen 9 9900X, this AIO has more than enough thermal headroom for both synthetic stress tests and demanding real‑world workloads.
reviews.author: Nimbleo

reviews.title: Very good cooler
reviews.comment: Works great and keeps temps super cool + looks pretty. Rgb is really nice and fans are quieter than i thought theyd be! I do recommend it is good for a budget 360 cooler! i was gonna get the kraken elite but some financial stuff came up so i opted cheaper, not disappointed.
reviews.author: May

reviews.title: Great Cooler But Buy Thermal Paste
reviews.comment:
This is the second ARCTIC cooler I have purchased with the first being the Freezer II. I think it is a fantastic product. The price is great and it cools wonderfully. However, the thermal paste with both coolers was dried out. I went from idle temps being 40 even 50 C and fans annoyingly loud to 29C and fans quiet. Gaming was a big difference going from upper 80C to 60C. I am unsure why I had bad luck with the paste, but I would recommend this product regardless.
Installation has even gotten easier and the RGB is pretty if that is your sort of thing. It fit my case, but it is a snug fit at the top of a Montech AIR 903 MAX. It seemed easier to mount this one than my other cooler and the screws was fairly easy to screw in unlike the last cooler I had.
It is a hefty cooler and I think it will hold up nicely. The magnetic CPU fan is interest and simple to install. The RGB part does not spin so don't worry about that as the fan itself is underneath that.
reviews.author: Kay M.

reviews.title: Excellent AIO cooler for Ryzen 5800x3D!
reviews.comment: Purchased for 5800x3d and I couldn't be happier. My previous AIO pump is assumed stopped working. And during games would sit at 91c. Assuming due to the CPU throttling. So I was not getting full power. Decided to replace it eith this one based on online recommendations and reciews. I could nor my CPU could not be happier. Now my CPU never goes over 70c. It runs at full clock speeds, including boost. I did personally undervolt the CPU with curve to keep my clock speeds. But it runs flawlessly! Couldn't recommend a better AIO cooler. And it works with Intel, and both AMD sockets (AM4 and AM5). The size is huge, make sure you do research to make sure it fits in your case/motherboard. For me, I use Lian Li Dynamic 011 Razer Edition with Gigabyte z570s Aurora ELITE AX. And I have room to push pull setup. Installation was not difficult with the videos from Arctic YouTube channel. Does not come with instructions. I did upgrade the Termal paste as well as suggested. I went with Corsair xtm70 instead.
reviews.author: Tony

reviews.title: Excellent cooler for AM4, but buy your own thermal paste!!
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/D1jcvOUaIEL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/712G0Y4zw9L._SY256.jpg *Update*: RGB works flawlessly
GREAT product for AM4 CPU's.
I have been looking to replace my aging Corsair H100i Pro AIO, which I bought in 2019, for some time now. After I read all the glowing reviews, I was really excited to get this cooler. I did not see many reviews from folks with AM4 processors, though, so I was a little bit wary, especially when the instructions said not to worry about some of the chip being visible after install! D:
I need not have worried. This cooler dropped temps about ~14 degrees C across the board. Went from 80 degrees under load to 66! Idle went from 50 to 36. For reference, I have an AMD R9 5900x, one of the hotter-running AM4 chips. Also I do have PBO enabled! (check screenshot for temp/load details).
As others have stated, the radiator on this unit is quite large/thick, so make sure to measure your case to make sure there is room to accommodate it. My mid-tower case is old, but quite roomy, so I luckily had no trouble fitting it in my case. It is also significantly louder than my old two-fan cooler, but its not even as loud as my GPU, so I am not particularly bothered. Others may be, though, so you may want to modify your fan speed curve.
Installation was not particularly difficult, and did not take much time. I found instructions using the QR code on the box (click on the 'Manuals' tab), and they were more than adequate. They included some graphics, gifs, and videos. I have a few decades of exp building PC's, so take this with a grain of salt, but I think beginners will not have too much trouble with this install. The trickiest part was removing the standard AM4 mount brackets and installing the ones included with the cooler. I had to hold the backplate (on the back of mobo) with one hand, while I installed the brackets one screw at a time. Bit of a pain, but the results were worth it.
The only (and biggest) con, is that the MX-6 thermal paste included with the cooler had the consistency of silly putty. It was basically a solid. Seeing as the 8G MX-6 tube I bought, to replace the minuscule amount that arrived with the cooler, had a more viscous consistency, I assume it was a bad batch. This delayed my build by a period of two days (while waiting for thermal paste to arrive), and is the only reason why I am giving this product 4 stars instead of 5.
I have not tested ARGB functionality, since I do not have a header on my old X570 motherboard, but I have ordered a header for it, and will update this review once it arrives.
In short: buy this cooler for sure. Great value for money, and incredible performance. But!! Make sure to order your own thermal paste, because they may include Playdough in the box instead of actual thermal paste D:
reviews.author: Tanvir S

reviews.title: Saved My Build — Finally Working Perfectly!
reviews.comment: I was seriously starting to regret my entire build. I have an i9-12900KS and couldn't even get into the BIOS — just black screens and endless frustration. Tried reseating the CPU, swapping RAM, checking cables, you name it. Eventually realized the issue might be thermal-related, so I picked up the Hyper 212 Black after seeing solid reviews. Installation was smooth, especially for an air cooler this size. The mounting brackets for LGA 1700 worked without any fuss. Once it was on, temps dropped dramatically — like, instantly noticeable. And best of all? My system booted right up. BIOS, Windows, everything. The SickleFlow fan is surprisingly quiet, and the all-black design with the aluminum top gives it a premium look that blends nicely into my case. Honestly can’t believe this solved the issue, but I’m glad it did. If you're building with a high-end CPU like the 12900KS and running into weird stability or boot issues, don’t overlook cooling. This thing just works.
reviews.author: S.b

reviews.title: Much quieter than a stock AMD cooler but it took some work to install it.
reviews.comment: I like this product.  Here's my day 1 experience... First you need to be ok with potentially removing the mother board, clearing thermal paste and reapplying thermal paste. If that is too much for you then find another solution! My stock AMD fan was driving me CRAZY!  It was so loud that I didn't want to use the system for more time than necessary. I was not sure which fan was making all the noise but with a tooth pick narrowed it to the CPU fan. At that point I looked for a solution and here's my experience: Good: + Price to me was fair and Amazon arrived the same day! + Very Quiet (compared to my stock fan) + Keeping my cpu between 38 - 60C + Comes with thermal paste! + fits Intel/AMD  (mine is AMD) + able to add a second fan but not included + directions with basic steps Not as good: - Installation took me about 90 minutes (I don't do this daily... so I am a bit slow) - If you're reapplying thermal paste you need 99% alcohol to clean the old paste (not included) - Installation required removing my system board- not a huge deal but takes time (case didn't allow access to under the system board) So this could be because I have an older case. Be ready. - If you have a small case it may not fit... check the case size, it's tall.  Mine is full size Lian-Li and fit nicely. - second fan not included but can be added. - second fan may be tight against the memory on your system board. - split cable to power the first fan and add a second fan made my cpu fan speed unreadable. I added it so that the cable would be there for a future second fan. All in all, I like this solution. It's very quiet, inexpensive and working nicely. Happy Computing!

reviews.author: Spike

reviews.title: There's a reason for the ridiculous rating.
reviews.comment: As of writing this review (12.24.25) It has a 4.7/5 star rating with well over 18,000 votes. That should tell you something. This baby is inexpensive, and it just works. If you're not running a super hot processor, this thing will absolutely do it's job and then some. I'm running just the single provided 120mm fan pushing air through it and exhausting out the back. It's a Ryzen 5 5500 inside a Thermaltake Versa H18 case. 3x120s up front sucking freshness in, with a matching 120 on the back farting the hot stuff out. I could sit here and ramble on, "blah blah this temp under load" "yada yada whatever on idle" but every system is completely different. As long as you're not trying to ice down a 14900K or R9 9950X3D, you'll be fine. Mine came with a syringe of generic thermal paste, but I had a stick of Arctic MX5 on hand, so I used it. I got the B550 motherboard, processor and Hyper 212 all at the same time, and when I got it all fired up and Windows 11 installed, I ran Prime95 for a couple hours to "break in" everything. No overheating, no thermal throttle. I forget the actual temp numbers, but they're irrelevant anyway. If you're reading so deep into the reviews that you find this one, you're already convinced to spend thirty bucks and snag this puppy. Just do it, dude.
reviews.author: Doug Dennis

reviews.title: Decent CPU Cooler for the Price (for Folding at Home)
reviews.comment: Before I got this Cooler I used the stock cooler that came with my Ryzen 3600. I didn't apply any overclock so in games it worked well. When the COVID-19 Pandemic began, I learned I could donate my computer's power to the Folding@home project, who would use computing resources for COVID-19 research. Unfortunately, the stock AMD cooler was not up to the task of cooling my CPU when this program was running. Even when I set the folding program to only use "light" resources, my CPU was between 90 - 100 Celcius, even with all the fans set to maximum. Unfortunately, my case does not support water cooling and I don't think the Noctua D15 could have fit. I decided to go with the Cooler Master Hyper 212 Black Edition since it had four heat pipes and cost less than $40 US dollars. Overall the installation isn't too bad until you get to mounting fans to the heatsink. It's very easy to drop those fan brackets into your case because the holes on the fans are way bigger than the mounting bracket diameter. Getting the fan brackets to line up with the groves on the heatsink was also a struggle, especially when you are working in a cramped computer case. Once the fans were on the heatsink, everything fit. There is plenty to clearance for the ram on my motherboard and case but this may turn out differently for you. I also appreciated that the included fan cable included a fan header splitter for an optional second fan, which I took advantage of since I had a 2nd 120mm fan laying around. By the way, you don't have to use cooler master fans if you don't want to. I used an Arctic fan for the 2nd fan because that's what I had laying around and it works fine. Once I had the cooler installed I fired up Folding@home and was pleased by the temperatures I was getting now. Even when telling the program to use full power, this CoolerMaster cooler was able to keep the CPU between 70-80 C. I had the program running for over 30 mins and the highest temperature I'm getting is 77 C. I did not enable overclocking in the BIOS but the CPU is turboing to 3.9 GHz. I also have the CPU and Case fans set to maximum, but this CPU cooler is still very quiet. To summarize, this is a great value CPU cooler for its price and size, but don't expect installation to be easy.
reviews.author: Ricky

reviews.title: So good I bought another one! Best bang for the buck cooler out there.
reviews.comment:
2nd one I've purchased, and for this price, if you have the room for it in your case, I don't know why you would buy an air cooler. It's quiet, easy to install, great looking ARGB, everything needed comes in the box (even a small tube of thermal paste which is enough for 1 application, although I used paste I already had).
Purchased my first one in July 2024 to cool a Ryzen 7 5800X3D, and it kept that cpu around 70°c under my most intensive usage scenario, even in the hottest room in my house during summer( 80°f + ambient temp) using Corsair TM70 paste.  Several months ago, I upgraded to a Ryzen 7 7800X3D, and the cooler is performing great on this cpu with temps in the 75° range under full load on extended Cinebench R23 stress tests, and closer to 60° on even the most CPU intesive games I have in my steam library. 19 months with no issues, and great temps!
Recently purchased another for my step son's new PC after trying to use the stock AMD cooler on a Ryzen 5 5600X and watching temps hit 90° in cinebench. We decided to spring for the Aqua Elite 240, and since then, temps are staying in the 60° - 65° range during stress tests, and in the 50's during gaming using Arctic MX-4 paste (which I think I may use to re-paste my 7800X3D in the future, since it performs better than the TM70).
I recommend this to anyone looking for really good cooling at an affordable price. The only reason I'd get a different AIO would be to have something flashy like a mini lcd on the cpu block that shows the temperature or cpu usage or whatever, which is totally unnecessary, but I can't resist shiny objects lol. It's quiet enough that I don't feel the 360mm version is necessary unless you are trying to make a super stealthy build while doing CPU intesive rendering or the like.

reviews.title: Quality at affordable price
reviews.comment:
I’ve used a variety of different AIO’s for PC builds (Corsair, MSI, NZXT) and was impressed by the quality of this AIO, considering the affordable price.
Recently installed the AIO and so far no issues, cpu temps remain stable and within normal operating ranges. I like that the RGB is subtle, not overwhelming. The installation was straightforward and included all the necessary mounting hardware. My favorite part is the water block doesn’t stick out too far, allowing me to attach the metal panel to the side of my micro itx case (Lian Li A4 H2O). Fans are relatively quiet and seem to provide plenty of airflow.

reviews.title: Fits perfectly in Lian Li A4 & cools ~247w with i7-14700K
reviews.comment: This works great in a Lian Li A4 case to cool an Intel i7-14700K and mounted without issue. I tested the cooling capacity with Handbrake and encoding some old home videos, and I could cool about 247 watts and keep the CPU at 90* C.  Moving up to the 250-255w range would bring the temp up to 95* C and cause the frames processed to drop. I do have a Thermal Right cooling frame installed on the CPU, but overall, I'm pleased with this AIO - and very impressed for its price point. I have another Thermal Right AIO in a PC with a 9800x3d, and it keeps the CPU cool with a +200 Mhz overclock. The RGB colors are nice & bright, and they are easily controlled with Open RGB. I've been using the other TR AIO for about a year and a half at this point, and I have no lifespan concerns. Overall, I highly recommend this AIO for anyone seeking great performance in a small case.
