reviews.author: Gabriel Swenson

reviews.title: A budget‑friendly 240 mm AIO that keeps temps in check—but expect a few budget quirks
reviews.comment:
I picked up the Thermalright Aqua Elite 240 V3 (ASIN B0CCNS5NZ9) after seeing it priced under fifty bucks. On paper, it ticks most of the boxes for a mid‑tower gaming build: 240 mm radiator, twin 120 mm PWM fans, and addressable RGB. After three weeks of use on a Ryzen 7 5800X, here’s how it really stacks up.
What impressed me
Solid value: routinely sells around $45–$50, which is crazy cheap for a 240 mm AIO.
Amazon
Respectable cooling: keeps my 5800X in the low‑70 °C range under Cinebench with fans set to 1,500 RPM and pump at stock 3,300 RPM.
Fans aren’t screamers: spec’d at 25.6 dBA max and subjectively quieter than the case fans that shipped with my tower.
Thermalright
Full socket kit: AM4/AM5 and Intel LGA 1700/1200/115x brackets are in the box, so no aftermarket hardware hunt.
Amazon
Decent build quality: radiator fins arrived straight, pump top has a nice satin finish, and the sleeved 400 mm tubes reach the top of an ATX case without strain.
Newegg.com
Where it cuts corners
Tubes are a bit stiff; routing in cramped cases is doable but not elegant.
ARGB daisy‑chain is old‑school: a single 3‑pin 5 V lead for each fan and pump means extra cables if your board is light on headers.
Newegg.com
Pump whine above 60 % duty: at ~3,000 RPM it’s fine, but full tilt introduces a faint buzz you’ll hear if the case sits on your desk.
Thermal paste packet is “just enough.” Grab a better tube if you plan on remounting later.
Manual is pictogram‑style and tiny—YouTube installers are your friend here.
Bottom line
If you want liquid cooling temps on an air‑cooler budget, the Aqua Elite 240 V3 delivers. It won’t dethrone premium AIOs in acoustics or polish, but for everyday gaming and moderate overclocks, it’s hard to beat the price‑to‑performance ratio—provided you can live with a few rough edges.
reviews.author: Dustin Garner

reviews.title: Replaced My Old Cooler Master Hyper 212 RGB With Thermalright PS120SE ARGB
reviews.comment: I recently upgraded my system's cooling with the Thermalright PS120SE ARGB, moving from a single-fan Cooler Master air cooler hyper 212 RGB, and the difference is night and day. This dual-tower, dual-fan behemoth has completely transformed my PC's performance and acoustics. Previously, with my single-fan Cooler Master cooler Hyper 212 RGB, I was constantly battling high temperatures, especially under load. My CPU would frequently hit uncomfortably high temperatures during gaming sessions and productivity tasks, which was a constant source of worry. The single fan, trying to keep up, was also incredibly noisy, sounding like a jet engine lol when the heat started to build up. The jump to a dual-tower design with two 120mm fans immediately paid off. My temperatures have dropped dramatically across the board. Under the same heavy workloads that used to push my old cooler to its limits, my CPU now runs significantly cooler, often staying in a temperature range I never thought possible with an air cooler. But what truly surprised me was the NOISE LEVEL. The Thermalright PS120SE is whisper-quiet, even when the fans ramp up. The two fans work in tandem to provide airflow without the high-pitched whine that plagued my old Air Cooler Master hyper 212 RGB. The combination of quiet operation and stellar cooling performance is a fantastic one-two punch that makes my gaming experience so much more enjoyable. The ARGB lighting is a nice bonus, adding a touch of style to my build. But at the end of the day, it's the raw cooling power and near-silent operation that make this cooler a truly worthwhile investment. The Thermalright PS120SE ARGB has proven that you don't need a liquid cooler to achieve top-tier performance and quiet operation. For anyone looking to dramatically improve their CPU's cooling and reduce system noise, I can't recommend this cooler enough! seriously buy it! youll thank this review later!. Despite its imposing size, the installation process for the Thermalright PS120SE ARGB is quite straightforward. It comes with clear, step-by-step instructions and mounting hardware. The brackets and screws are well-made and fit securely. While aligning the screws can be a little tricky at first, following the instructions and tightening them a little at a time in a criss-cross pattern makes the process much easier. The fans are also simple to clip on once the heatsink is in place If you also have 4 ram sticks you will have to slide your fan up juuuust a little tad bit but it won't be above the heatsink.
reviews.author: RedragonReviews

reviews.title: Fast to Assemble, Great Performance
reviews.comment: Note that the cooler's size means one fan will likely interfere with non low profile RAM (Vengeance LPX). The fan that interferes (if it does) can be moved slightly upwards, which will not harm performance in any meaningful way but will look a bit worse. Reasonably quick to assemble, but do pay attention to the side the thermaltake logo and heap pipes are facing. Comes with thermal paste, keep in mind the paste is very thick so you may want an old card on hand to help with application (does not need to be spread if it's a large pea size dot near the center of the cpu, the cooler spread it out once applied). The card (or any other small edged tool - plastic to avoid scratching the cpu) will help with getting the paste to stop sticking to the applicator and moving the blob to the center of the cpu! Keeps even the Ryzen 9 9950x3d at good temps up to a 78 celcius max after sustained workloads, with minimal thermal throttling (cinebench scores remain high). The cooler is overall quiet (no AIO pump whir helps), well built (lifted the relatively heavy X870E Nova with it). And the fans are PWM adjustable with RGB support using the standard ARGB header.
reviews.author: CC

reviews.title: fantastic CPU cooler at a fantastic price.
reviews.comment: This is awesome I wish I'd installed it sooner. I had a Corsair AIO water cooler and it never seemed to act right. I know it was installed correctly (i've built quite a few PC's over the decades), but for example sometimes the CPU block light would come on, sometimes it wouldn't. My CPU would run hot (5800x3d) and I felt that the AIO just wasn't working well enough. It WAS working, just not as well as I thought it should. Saw this cooler on Amazon for less than $40. and on impulse picked it up, and it sat under my desk for probably more than half a year. I just never seemed to have the time to take apart my desktop and remove the AIO and install this. Well last week I got tired of feeling like I had a space heater under my desk and finally swapped them out and the difference is like night and day. For one thing it blows the hot air 'back' instead of 'up' at me, and somehow it's about 5-8 degrees cooler. Which doesn't sound like a lot but it does make a difference. Maybe I should've used a 3 fan AIO instead of a 2 fan AIO, but I was worried the larger 3 fan wouldn't fit. The desktop is running fine, temps are low, this CPU cooler looks 'cool' and everything is running fine. I wish the fan aRGB wires were just a tiny bit longer, even just an inch or two would've been better. I had to run them down behind the MB and up through the bottom to get to the right header on my ASUS mb, and the cords just barely reached. But other than that there were no issues. the RGB for them is controlled by the Armoury Crate software and I've had no issues with it. All in all it's a great cooler and I'd recommend it pretty highly.
reviews.author: William

reviews.title: Strong CPU Cooler with Nice ARGB Look
reviews.comment: This Thermalright PS120SE ARGB CPU cooler feels well-built and performs nicely. The dual 120mm fans and 7 heat pipes help keep temperatures under control, and the ARGB lighting gives the build a clean look. It’s a good option if you want solid air-cooling performance without spending too much.
reviews.author: FK

reviews.title: Works great, looks mostly good, instructions lacking
reviews.comment: Most importantly, keeps my CPU cool. I have a Ryzen 5 7600X which already burns hot and this keeps temps in place. The included thermal paste was good, wish I had realized it was in there before I bought some. Installs easily, although since one side has more heat pipes than the other, I spent way too long trying to figure out which way it was supposed to go (never actually did so I just installed it). The RGB on the fan is cool if you are into RGB. I didn't care but my case came with RGB fans and luckily the RGB pattern matches well with the case fans. The instructions are very lacking and there are surprisingly not as many YouTube videos on it. Unfortunately, the logo sticker on the fan is not centered and I notice it quite often and it really drives my wife crazy when she sees is. But I never think about taking it off when I'm not actively working on something. IT WILL  ABSOLUTELY INTERFERE WITH YOUR RAM. Just know, your RAM and the fan compete for space. You can change the fan layout so the fan is pulling air instead of pushing air onto the heat pipes but who wants to do that. You can raise the fan over the RAM sticks but depending on the height of the RAM and your case size, it may not fit. My first RAM were RGB but one stick was bad. I got lucky though and found a set that was better priced and better specs that were also low profile and not RGB so my fan is only a little higher than the heat pips and doesn't bother me. I'd definitely buy it again if I built another PC.
reviews.author: Cycling Addict

reviews.title: Unbeatable value: performance air cooling at a budget price
reviews.comment:
I recently installed the Peerless Assassin 120 SE ARGB in my build and I’m extremely pleased with the results. A few highlight points:
With 6 heat-pipes and a dual-tower heatsink, this cooler handles high thermal loads surprisingly well for the price.
It supports both Intel (LGA 115x/1200/1700) and AMD (AM4/AM5) sockets out of the box — easy to integrate into different systems.
It is impressively quiet. According to the official spec the noise level tops out at ~25.6 dBA, which means minimal fan noise in daily use.
The ARGB lighting is a nice bonus for anyone who cares about aesthetics, and it does not seem to compromise performance.
My experience in use:
Installation was straightforward (with the back-plate and mounting brackets included). After setup I noticed lower idle and load temperatures vs the stock cooler, and the system remained quiet even under sustained load. It also had good clearance around my RAM slots and GPU (always good to check fit in your case). In terms of value vs performance, this cooler really stands out.
Minor note:
You’ll want to check your case’s CPU cooler clearance, the heatsink is ~155mm tall.
Also, if you’re doing extreme overclocking or very high-end CPUs at 300 W+ loads, this may not quite match the very top-tier 280/360mm liquid-coolers, but for most builds it gives excellent bang for the buck.
Bottom line:
If you’re looking for a high-performance air cooler that doesn’t break the bank, the Peerless Assassin 120 SE ARGB is hard to beat. Highly recommended.
reviews.author: pbourdon

reviews.title: Quiet, Cool, and Looks Great
reviews.comment: Installed this cooler in my PC, and it’s honestly one of the best air coolers I’ve used. Temps dropped significantly compared to my old one, and it’s super quiet even under load. Installation was straightforward, and the ARGB lighting looks clean inside the case. Build quality feels premium, and the fans are smooth and silent. For its price, it’s an amazing value for keeping your CPU cool. It works perfectly as it is compatible with my R9 5900 XT. It has lasted around 2 years since I bought it and looks nice!
reviews.author: Felipe Velandia

reviews.title: Great quality, great price.
reviews.comment: I have purchased 2 of these so far for different builds. They work and look great. Great build quality and good thermals. Granted, I hardly ever max out one of my CPUs, but it keeps my 12900k cool without issue. My other CPU is less powerful but it gets ran at 100% regularly and also doesn't have cooling problems. As long as this fits in your case, I'd recommend it to anyone looking for a solid, but still budget friendly, air cooler.
reviews.author: JK

reviews.title: SAVED MY LIFE
reviews.comment: First off let me start by saying I have built computers before, but am by no means a computer expert. I spent 2 years trying to figure out why my PC experienced so much stuttering and low performance in some games. I bought new GPU's, new CPU's, more RAM, and still the same performance issues. One day I decided to check my temps and noticed they seemed to REALLY high in some games, and almost seem to correlate with drops in performance. That's when I did some research and learned that CPU's tend to throttle themselves when temps are too hot. I bought this hoping it would drop my temps and holy mother of god - it's like I'm gaming on an entirely different set up. The air flow is insane. It dropped my temps by about 10-15 degrees at least. Every game I played was running so much more smoothly and could be ran at higher graphic presets without stuttering or major frame lag. The fan itself is pretty large so make sure you're not putting it in a tiny case, but man its SO worth the price. Installation was pretty simple if you know your way around the inside of a computer. As for noise, I can't hear it at all, its very quiet. I could not recommend a product more if you're experiencing issues with CPU high temps. save yourself the money and hassle of expensive cooling set ups and try this first.
reviews.author: Ricky Tellez

reviews.title: Does a great job keeping it cool, a bit large though.
reviews.comment: Keeps my i7 very cool. 25 to 27° C idling & plenty of headroom under load. Cheap but very effective cooler. Installation was tricky due to it being awkward to get paste on because of it's size & shoe. Also screws have to be turned a lot before contact so you have to screw fast to keep the paste from getting tacky. Was certainly doable though. Fans are very quiet, especially at idle. Downside is it's big, very big. You need small memory or you'd have to put a fan on the back side to use bigger memory sticks. Maybe not for a novice but worth a shot.
reviews.author: FloJay

reviews.title: One of the best air coolers available
reviews.comment: This is a review of the Thermalright Phantom Spirit 120SE. I read many performance reviews online before purchasing this. According to those reviewers, this offers top-tier cooling vs noise at a fraction of the price. It even competes with some AIOs. I recently replaced an AIO with this, the first air cooler I've used in a while. I did it because this computer is getting long in the tooth, and I'm more concerned about long-term reliability than a couple of degrees Celsius. If you are building a new computer, this is much easier to install and more reliable than an AIO water cooler. Compared to my old NZXT Kraken X63, this gets very similar cooling performance. The temperatures fluctuate more than they did with the AIO, but the minimum idle temperature is now slightly lower than it was with the AIO, and the max temps are only a couple of degrees hotter than they were with the 280mm AIO. This is all despite the fact that I used about half of the normal amount of thermal paste due to a screwup on my part. As long as you're not using a processor with a very high TDP, this is the ideal cooler. Note: you should prefer this over the 120 EVO. Yes, the EVO has RGB and can get you a couple of degrees cooler on higher TDP processors, but at the cost of much higher noise. If you're using anything less than 170watt CPU, this is probably the better choice. Addendum: now using this on two computers. Zero regrets. Addendum: this cooler does make it more difficult to replace the M.2 drive without removing the cooler. Not impossible, just obnoxious. Addendum (November 2024): started getting obnoxious fan noises about a half year later. Thankfully, there are a variety of fans you can replace these with that will produce reasonably similar performance, including the Arctic P12 or the Noctua NF-A12x25 (the latter being about as expensive per fan as this entire cooler with included fans).
reviews.author: Paul

reviews.title: Excellent Cooler for 7800X3D - Outstanding Performance and Value
reviews.comment: I've been using the Thermalright Phantom Spirit 120SE with my AMD Ryzen 7800X3D, and I couldn't be more satisfied with its performance. This cooler has exceeded my expectations in every way. Performance: The Thermalright Phantom Spirit 120SE keeps my 7800X3D at idle temperatures in the 40s, and during gaming sessions, it stays impressively cool between 50s and 60s. This is a testament to its excellent thermal management and efficiency. Price/Performance Ratio: Considering its price, the performance of this cooler is outstanding. It's hard to find another cooler that offers such a great balance of cost and cooling capability. Installation: The installation process was straightforward, and the included instructions were clear. The cooler fits perfectly in my mid-tower case without any clearance issues. Build Quality: The build quality of the Phantom Spirit 120SE is solid. The fins and heat pipes are well-constructed, and the overall design is sleek and functional. Noise Levels: One of the pleasant surprises was how quiet this cooler is. Even under load, the noise levels are minimal, making for a much more enjoyable gaming experience. Conclusion: If you're looking for a high-performance cooler for your 7800X3D that won't break the bank, the Thermalright Phantom Spirit 120SE is an excellent choice. It delivers exceptional cooling, is easy to install, and offers fantastic value for money. Highly recommended!
reviews.author: iamplayer40

reviews.title: Keeps my 9950X3D nice and cool!
reviews.comment: Recently upgraded to a 9950X3D (a very hot chip - 170W) and after a hours of research of Air vs Water cooling decided to pull the trigger on this guy. And let me tell you, saying I was/am pleasantly surprised would be an understatement! Note: I did pair it with a couple of Noctua NF-P12 redux-1700 fans instead of the stock fans which made a major difference (more on that below). This little guy, well, not little at all - ITS HUGE! handles the 9950X3D perfectly, all my concerns about needing water cooling went out the window as soon as I saw Prime95 causing the CPU to draw 260W and the temp hit 94c. Lets get into it: Location: NY, average room temp around 70-75f (20-23c). Use cases: work, gaming, AI. Work: office apps, web, light photo editing. Gaming: Diablo 4, Borderland 4, Assassins Creed Shadows... AI: mostly code generation. CPU: undervolted (-15), +200MHZ PBO. No power draw cap. Temps (with Noctua fans): Idle: as low as 28c (max draw 36W). Work: 35-40c (max draw 90W). Gaming: 67c highest I hit during a BL4 fight (max draw 162W). AI: 60c highest on large requests (max draw 140W). Prime95: hit 94c while drawing 260W. Cinebench: 72c max while drawing 220W. (see attached HWMonitor screenshot - system has been on for about 2 weeks at this point). Fans: The main problem (and reason) for the changing the stock fan is noise and performance at higher speeds. Noise: Stock fans are fine in low speeds, barely audible. In high speeds though.. they are hard to ignore, not the worse, but hard to ignore. Temps: Prime95 hit 96c and capped the power draw at 210W. Idle was around 34c. BL4 hit 78c. Sum up: - Can't beat for the price (even with buying 2 extra fans). - Huge - make sure your case has room. - Replace stock fans for quieter / better performance. - Can easily handle 9950X3D. - Installation was super easy and straight to the point on AM5. Took longer to fully unpack it than it did to install. Why not water cooling ? In my specific case, the noise. Even the quieter pumps hit 40-45db on load and some even 35db on idle. I like my system quiet. Large slow fans = quiet (see fan speeds in HWMonitor)
reviews.author: Tomer P

reviews.title: An absolutely stellar CPU cooler for the price.
reviews.comment: I owned a 5700x3d, and I wanted to replace the default stock cooler that I previously owned because my temperatures were climbing into the 90s. I had heard good things about this CPU cooler but this absolutely beat my expectations and then some. Out of the box, this thing felt solid and looked premium, much more premium than I expected at the price. It came with a packet of thermal past as well, which I did not use so I cannot speak on that. Installing it was as simple as it could be, although I ended up needing to use the bracket that came with my motherboard. Thankfully, I still had that but it was a bit of a pain, to say the least. Once I got it installed with some fresh thermal paste, I ran some stress tests. It absolutely killed it. My temperatures went from low 90s to, at most, 75c or so. That was at a worst case scenario too. In game, I was getting closer to 70c or so. I was shocked at how much value I got out of this cooler. Without a doubt, I would buy this again if iw as building another computer. This is a fantastic cooler that's deserving of all the praise that it gets.
reviews.author: Corey Rutter

reviews.title: No issues with cooling
reviews.comment: The installation was decent the clips are easy to use and it provides pretty cool temperatures for Ryzen 9000 cpus. The noises is pretty quiet the quality is good for the price and performance is decent for budget cooler.
reviews.author: Candace

reviews.title: 6-Year Review: The Silent King of Air Coolers
reviews.comment: I purchased the Noctua NH-D15 chromax.black six years ago for a high-end workstation/gaming build. After over half a decade of near-constant operation, I can confidently say this is the best, most reliable, and quietest component in my PC. 1. Performance: Still Chilling After 6 Years When I first installed the D15, I was blown away by the temperatures. Even when overclocking my CPU, it kept temps well below dangerous thresholds. Fast-forward 6 years: I have never had a single thermal issue. The dual-tower, 6-heatpipe design is just as effective today as it was in 2020. The build quality is legendary; the heatsink has not oxidized, and the copper base remains perfectly flat. It regularly keeps my CPU in the 30s-40s°C at idle and keeps things remarkably cool even under heavy rendering loads. The cooling performance rivals many 240mm+ AIO water coolers without the fear of pump failure or leaks. 2. Sound: The Definition of "Silent" My biggest requirement was silence, and Noctua delivered. The two NF-A15 140mm fans are inaudible. I often find myself checking the case window just to make sure the fans are actually spinning because I can't hear them at all, even during intense cpu usage tasks. They use SSO2 bearings, which are incredibly durable and do not grind or hum over time like cheaper alternatives. Even when the fan curve ramps up slightly, it’s a low-frequency hum rather than a high-pitched whine. If you want a silent PC, this is the gold standard. 3. Aesthetics: The "Chromax" Touch The original NH-D15 is infamous for its beige/brown color scheme. The chromax.black version solves this completely. The matte black coating on the fins, the black fans, and the black anti-vibration pads look incredibly sleek and premium. Six years later, the black coating hasn't chipped or faded, adding a stealthy, high-end look to the build. 4. The Long-Term Experience (Maintenance) The mounting system (SecuFirm2) is, in my opinion, the best in the industry. It made installation straightforward 6 years ago. Since then, I simply remove it to clean off the dust out once a year. Installation & Maintenance tip: One fan I had to offset by a few millimeters due to RAM height. Still works great and just a heads up that it does not impede functionality or performance at all. Keep the fins clean with compressed air or even wife off with lightly damp cloth. I foresee this lasting another 6 years easily. 5. Reasons to Buy (Why it holds up) Absolute Silence: The fans are virtually inaudible in daily use. Excellent Thermal Performance: Keeps high-TDP CPUs very cool, competing with liquid coolers. 6-Year Warranty (and Longevity): Noctua provides a 6-year manufacturer's warranty, which speaks to their confidence in the product's lifespan. Long-term Support: Noctua often provides free mounting kits for new CPU sockets, meaning this cooler can be used for decades. Minor and relative "Cons": Size: This thing is massive and helps it look . Ensure your case has enough clearance (165mm+ height), but like I said earlier, your RAM height may require you to offset the front fan upward just a few millimeters...you can't really see the difference between fans. Cost (worth every penny: It is a premium product, but at 6 years+ of use, the price-per-year is incredibly low. Final Thoughts Six years ago, I wanted a quiet, powerful cooler that looked good in a black-themed build. The Noctua NH-D15 chromax.black exceeded all expectations. It has never failed, never made a sound, and never let my CPU get too hot. It is quite simply the best air cooler on the market.
reviews.author: A.S.

reviews.title: Worth it - Excellent Air Cooler
reviews.comment: Excellent air cooler and a very good deal for the price. I didn’t use the thermal paste it came with. I bought some NT-H2 separately, but NT-H1 is still good. These are very quiet fans. Almost inaudible. Higher speeds will generate noise, but still quiet. It was easy to install but it is somewhat heavy so you will need to be careful not to drop it on your motherboard. The copper transfers the heat from the cpu very quickly. Highest CPU temp I’ve seen is 49C with an I7-12700kf. Definitely the best functioning cpu cooler I’ve bought. I can’t recommend it enough. My one complaint, is that the connecting wires are supposed to be held along the frame of the fan and then extend to be plugged into the motherboard. Those wires come out of the frame really easily and will be hit by the fan. So if you hear any noise besides a light breeze that’s what it is. Pushing the wires back into the frame does fix it, at least for a while.
reviews.author: Brandon

reviews.title: Excellent Cooling Performance, Very Quiet (But Large)
reviews.comment: The Noctua NH-D15 chromax.Black does an outstanding job keeping my AMD Ryzen 9 7950X3D cool. Even under load, temperatures stay under control, and the cooler remains very quiet. Build quality is excellent, as expected from Noctua, and installation was straightforward. Once installed, it performs exactly as advertised. The only downside is the size. This cooler is very bulky, which makes working around it inside the case more difficult. In my setup, I need to remove one of the fans in order to access or work on the RAM. That said, I understand that the large size is a big reason why it performs so well. If you have enough case clearance and don’t mind the size, this is an excellent air cooler and easily one of the best available.
reviews.author: Eric Espinoza

reviews.title: Still the King
reviews.comment: Installed with little issues.  Please note due to the size of this thing (it is massive), you may need to uninstall your gpu for ease of installation (I had to do this).  however once I had access it was a breeze to install (and this was my first cpu cooler install by myself).  Please note if you have taller than normal ram sticks you may need to consider just leaving off the front fan, or you may need to slide it up (but sliding it up means the overall height will be taller so make sure your case can handle the adjusted tolerances).  For reference my Corsair 4000d has no issues.  I had to slide the front fan up a couple mm but doesn't hit the glass display. Some of the things I like immediately about this cpu cooler: 1. It's huge.  Makes my Coolermaster 212 Spectrum V3 look like a midget. 2. Super quiet.  I opted for the low noise adapters which limit the fan speed to 1200 rpm (as opposed to 1500).  You cannot hear it run unless you really put your ear to the case. 3. Idle temps hover between 35 cel to 41 cel.  Gameplay maxes at 71-72 cel. 4. 6 year warranty (holy cow). 5. Chromax Black edition (not a big fan of the creme/brown color) 6. Quality Quality Quality - as a reference my Thermalright Peerless Assassin 120 SE fan clips were such a pain in the butt to install on the heatsink.  The Noctua NH-D15 was an absolute breeze. Some things I dislike about this cooler: 1. Price, obviously very expensive vs some other good budget options with similar performance. 2. Having to remove the gpu to complete the install (not a dealbreaker but more annoyance than anything). 3. Not the best looking cooler on the market (BeQuiet! Dark Rock Pro 5 or Elite looks so much better) I had no issue spending the extra money for this as I was looking for both performance but also longevity.  6 years warranty really showed me that Noctua is serious about their products and backs it up. If you can front up the money for this I would say it's a well-worthy investment.  My goal was to build a PC setup that could sustain for 5-10 years and I can say with the help of this Noctua DH-15 I will definitely get to that benchmark.
reviews.author: Byron King

reviews.title: Its HUGE.. and its POWERFUL... AND its Quiet..
reviews.comment: I built my machine about 3 months ago.. but noticed while the NH-9DL did a good job with the i7-9700K. If I wanted to overclock, it got a bit toasty and unstable. So I looked at a AIO, and after seeing LinusTechTips review of the D15 decided to go with it. A few things I wondered and soon found out: #1 - I have 64GB of ram and noticed the D15 was a bit large, but figured give it a try. As you can see it clears the Ram, BUT didn't clear the other heat spreader on the MB.. ( NOCTUA did say that the second fan may not fit.. ) #2 - Although the other fan did not fit exactly where it needed it DID fit in the case about an 1" away from the fins.. and was a big improvement over the original case fan and was close to the intended location. #3 - If curious, YES the original motherboard mount for the NH-9D does work on the new fan so saved me that time and made install even easier. #4 - BONUS the 9D fan with the 15D springs FIT where the 15D Could Not !! So it was like having 3 fans on the cooler ;) #5 - ANOTHER BONUS - They give a number of extension cables for the Fans.. So I was able to mount the fans and get them all power. After doing all that.. I went and got to overclocking.. and stress testing.. I ran Cinebench R20, and custom set it to have 256 render threads to really stress the chip. I then ran them back to back to back until the chip wouldnt get any hotter.. ( an average of 6 times ). As you can see, the results speak for themselves. I went from : 89 degrees C when stress testing it in Default settings... to 64 degrees MAX when stress testing it WHILE IT WAS OVERCLOCKED !! I was MORE stable overclocked.. ! WOW and WOW and WOW.. Noctua hit it out of the park.. As for how loud it is.. it is a LITTLE louder than just the 9D.. but I can't tell you exactly how much as its not a lot. UPDATE: I downloaded OCCT and ran its burnin test, and got to 75C after minutes of maxing everything. The amazing thing is anytime it got off the overclocking settings the CPU dropped back to 35C in a matter of seconds.  So unless your both overclocked to 5.1MGZ AND using a LOT of hardcore video or 3D Graphic editing for hours, I think the D15 will keep your system supercool. I personally overclock for gaming, and I DO BIM and 3D Scanning, so I have to process GB size 3D Point clouds, and convert them to Mesh.. THAT does force my CPU to run 100% for a hour to process. BUT even then I never saw higher than 70 and was rock stable the whole time. So I guess what I am saying is custom water cooling MAY do a tad better, but HIGHLY doubt a AIO could do any better at all, and especially not at this cost point and if your upgrading from a Noctua 9 or 12 you can reuse the fans with all the extras that come in the kit here.
reviews.author: CharlesG

reviews.title: Good Quality
reviews.comment: This fan runs great and is very quiet and definitely keep my cpu in good temps
reviews.author: Awesome game it showed on time was in great condition

reviews.title: Excellent CPU Cooler
reviews.comment: I've been using this cooler for my Home Server and they are quiet enough that my relatives do not hear the PC in the family room. They were not difficult to install using the fan clips. The fan appears to be high quality and sounds the same too. They are black, and go well with a dark build, like mine was.
reviews.author: William

reviews.title: Quiet and cool
reviews.comment: The fan is quiet and amazing. The SE Black model looks amazing behind the glass. I was worried about it fitting in the case but it was no problem. My only complaint is that the thermal paste it came with was dried up and the tube barely had any in it to begin with. Good thing I had a backup thermal paste. For the price and quality of air cooler though I'm not complaining.
reviews.author: SR

reviews.title: Good Value and Performance
reviews.comment: Happy with aesthetics, sound-level, price/performance, packaging and intuitive installation. Please note difficulty may be encountered due to cable clearances and flush fan mounting could be impeded by tall RAM modules, luckily minor for my use case of an NZXT Manta. Provided thermal paste is quite thick, so take care with application.
reviews.author: Cameron

reviews.title: Great cooler
reviews.comment: Great product, nothing bad to say. Quiet and keeps CPU cool
reviews.author: Trey S.

reviews.title: Affordable Performance
reviews.comment:
This is a terrific heatsink/fan combination that is well made and highly affordable.  A y-splitter cable is provided to combine the 2x 4 pin PWM connectors into a single 4pin PWN mobo header.
The fan even comes with a large tube of Thermalright TF7 paste which is quality paste.
This product was purchased for a stock 12700kf, no undervolt or overclock, just stock with intel pref settings (none of that MCE stuff) inside of a H9 Flow case (2025) and there's no issue with noise or sound; keeps the CPU in the low to mid 60's with small bursts to 71c at 70% power in Cyberpunk 2077 with all Raytracing settings maxxed.
One thing worth mentioning, if you have large RAM heatsinks, you will need to get creative. If you have low profile ram, you should be fine.
Overall, this is a great product with easy installation and quality performance that would rival AIO's.
reviews.author: Daniel Krause

reviews.title: Works suprisingly well and is super affordable!
reviews.comment:
I bought this to replace a 240 mm water cooler that was giving me issues. This is very much a budget cooler with good performance. After applying the correct amount of thermal paste, repositioning the fans in my case to blow air out the top and front, I am idling between 37-40 c. It does great at idle and during light loads, loading up some 4k high on Battlefield 6, and it hits as high as 73c on an AMD 9700X. I don't think you can ask more of a sub $40 cooler.
UPDATE: I just swapped out the stock fans with three, that's right three, Noctua Redux 120mm fans and idle temps have dropped by 2-3 degrees (35c at idle)! The Noctua fans spin 200 rpm faster at peak and push about 10 more CFM and are quieter. I think performance and value with this setup is a better cooler for your dollar than Noctua's own flagships. If you have some cheap, fast and reasonable pushy fans lying around you can easily improve this HSF already good performance for great performance.
reviews.author: Garrett G. Graham

reviews.title: Excellent cooling, very high quality radiator and fans. Well earned reputation.
reviews.comment:
I constantly saw this cooler recommended as the best basic air cooler around. I have to say, it's very well earned as this is an excellent cooler. The package includes a nice set of brackets and standoffs for both AMD and Intel CPUs. A good thermal paste TF7 is also included which I used.
Setup was pretty easy, it was a little finicky to seat the two main screws that hold the plate to the CPU. I had to watch a short video to figure out how to attach the metal wires to the fans and then stretch them over the radiator.
One thing to note is that the front fan might not fit if your RAM is on the taller side. I had to move the front fan up a few notches which was pretty easy.
Performance seems amazing, even under load the fans are quiet and my Ryzen CPU doesn't even break a sweat. It seems AIOs are popular now but I wanted something as simple as possible with good performance and I'm really pleased with this.
reviews.author: zo

reviews.title: Keeps my CPU cool!!!
reviews.comment: This fan works great and it was straight forward to install. My original CPU fan would start to spin at a very high RPM when playing video games and had poor cooling performance. This new CPU cooler is extremely quit even when playing videos games and keeps the CPU's temperature cool and stable. The only issue I had with it was that I could not fit both fans on the towers because my ram was sitting to tall. So I installed one fan in the middle of the coolers towers which work perfectly.
reviews.author: Glyn

reviews.title: Everything you need
reviews.comment:
This thing is awesome. I was previously using a Noctua NH-U12S, but I upgraded my CPU and these newer Ryzen chips are known to run pretty hot so I needed to reconsider my cooling. The Noctua was nice and silent, but it was only a single tower cooler. I installed this bad boy and saw a significant drop in temps under load, and it's still relatively quiet. I will say that if you're not using low profile RAM, like really low profile, the front fan on this will stick out a bit further than the back one. That doesn't bother me too much though and I doubt it has an effect on cooling performance. It's worth noting that the box includes everything you'll need like mounting brackets, standoffs, thermal paste, daisy chain cable, etc.
Certainly worth picking this up if you're in the market for a solid CPU cooler with incredible value. Thermalright knocked it out of the park!
reviews.author: Justin

reviews.title: Excellent Budget AIO With Great Cooling, Quiet Fans, and a Surprisingly Premium Screen
reviews.comment: The Jungle Leopard PF 360 CPU Water AIO turned out to be a much better cooler than I expected for the price. The build quality out of the box feels solid, and installation on my Intel i7‑14700K was straightforward. The kit includes brackets for Intel 115X, 1200, and 1700 sockets, along with AMD mounting hardware. Setting the bracket size for LGA 1700 was simple, and attaching the backplate through the motherboard was just as easy. The pump head bracket twists and locks into place cleanly, and choosing the correct LGA 1700 spacers made securing the pump to the CPU quick and hassle‑free. The included 360mm fans were a pleasant surprise. They’re very quiet, even under load, and the RGB implementation looks fantastic. The 360 fans has four infinity‑mirror accents on the front plus full-length infinity mirrors along both sides, giving the radiator a premium look. I usually replace stock AIO fans, but in this case I don’t feel the need to—the performance and aesthetics are already excellent. Cooling performance is strong as well. At idle, my 14700K sits between 36–46°C across the cores. Under a full 100% burn‑in load, temperatures rise to 60–70°C, and none of the cores hit thermal throttling. For a CPU known to run hot, that’s impressive for an AIO in this price range. The pump‑head screen is another highlight. It’s removable and can be mounted in three different orientations. I chose the vertical position with the tubes entering from the bottom, which limits the screen’s rotation options, but it still ended up exactly how I wanted it. If you want the screen oriented vertically downward, you’ll need the tubes coming in from the side due to the pin alignment—but the flexibility is still better than many AIOs. The software worked with some issues on my system. The interface isn’t immediately intuitive, so I watched a couple of YouTube videos to get familiar with it. Once I understood the layout, I was able to upload video clips or screen captures, add system stats like CPU temperature, and customize the screen with various widgets. reviews.title: Amazing Air-Cooling Performance
reviews.comment: ==================================== ===Review for 2025 (AMD AM5)=== I'll still recommend this cooler for most CPUs, and for newer gen chips you can even get the NM-AM5/4-MP83 mounting kit for free from Noctua. However, I've moved to the NH-D15 G2 LBC for AM5 and have submitted a review for that model on its product's page. ==================================== ===Review for 2022 (AMD AM4)=== Bought another one of these recently for a new AM4 build, and once more the performance is outstanding. There were minor changes to this model's packaging where they added parts for the AM4 socket. From what I understand you can also request these parts from Noctua directly with proof of purchase on an older model NH-D15. I have a higher core count on this CPU with higher clocks compared to my previous build below, and it's holding the temps between 37-53C from idle to max load. It's also nearly silent with only some very minor wind noise under load. The RAM I'm using on this build is a bit taller than I'd like, but the case does allow the secondary fan to fit just fine with the slightly added height from the fan adjustment above the RAM. I can absolutely recommend pairing this with the Fractal Torrent given its size and the overall purpose of these being air-cooling. Keywords to help searches for fitment: -MSI MAG X570S Tomahawk -Fractal Torrent (full size) -G.SKILL Trident Z Neo ======================================== ===Review for 2017 (Intel LGA1151)=== This air cooler defeated my old Corsair H100i v2 in cooling efficiency, noise, quality, and likely overall space consumption (no tubes or radiators blocking sides of the case). I'm getting at least 8-10C cooler with this thing over water and it's not even running at full speed. Not to say the water cooler was bad, but just weigh your options depending on how you set up your case cooling. Even with the slight offset of the optional fan, using Corsair Vengeance LPX sticks, I had plenty of headroom in the Air 540 even though it stated a 170mm clearance. Keywords to help searches for fitment: -Gigabyte GA-Z170X-Gaming 7 -Corsair Air 540 -Corsair Vengeance LPX ======================== ===Notes for both G1 models=== It's awesome that this thing fits so many different socket types, should I choose to switch to AMD then I don't have to buy a different kit I just change out the mounts. The build quality of the hardware is outstanding, none of the parts feel cheap or of poor manufacturing. Assembly and installation is easy to follow even though it looks way too large to sit on the socket. Some may be concerned about strain on the CPU/socket but I'd say it's comparable to some AIOs in this category, the tubes on some AIOs can absolutely put tension on the socket. If you're not concerned with the interior looks of your case then you should seriously buy this thing. If you *are* concerned with the interior looks of your case then search for the Chromax product line to compliment this hardware. If you're unsure about the optional secondary fan fitting, take a 140mm case fan and set it on top of your RAM (vertically as if it were on the cooler sitting above the RAM). If it still clears the side of your case with a few millimeters to spare then you're likely OK. Both 140mm fans are almost fully adjustable, they move/notch up and down on wire clips using the heat-sink fins as mounting points. The fans are 140mm with 120mm mounts, probably for compatibility to fit a 120mm fan as the optional for those with taller RAM. These do come with thermal paste as well.
reviews.author: Captin

reviews.title: The most powerful, yet quiet, air cooler available today.
reviews.comment: I've got two D15s and a D15S for point of reference. I'll compare it here with alternatives like the Silver Arrow IB-E Extreme, NH-U14S, D15S, Cryorig R1 Ultimate and the Dark Rock Pro 3. The D15 deserves its reputation. It is, without any doubt, the most powerful cooler for the real world. It's true that the Reeven Okeanos can keep up with it, and the Silver Arrow IB-E Extreme can even surpass it, but in the real world, owners won't put up with coolers that loud. Those two are leveraging high RPM fans to compensate for inferior efficiency, and as a result, most owners are going to clamp down on fan speed and end up with lower performance coolers. The D15 is so quite, even under full load, that inside a case it might as well be silent. Its full performance range is, thus, accessible in the real world. If you're alright with loud heat sinks, I have to imagine that using two Noctua NF-A14 iPPC 3000s would still defeat all comers. I'm not sure how well those fans would fit given the NF-A15's (stock fan) strange frame. In my view, the Okeanos and Silver Arrow don't offer serious competition for this because of the way they achieve their performance. Far more interesting, for a comparison, are its direct competition from Be Quiet! and Cryorig, namely the Dark Rock Pro 3 and the R1 Ultimate. The R1 Universal, in my opinion, is the direct competitor to the D15S, so I won't get into it much here. The Dark Rock Pro 3, while it is measurably quieter, is simply not in the same league of performance as the D15. On top of this, it's harder to install, and in practical terms, both are virtually silent anyway. The DRP3 has more in common with the outgoing D14 anyway, with its dissimilar front and middle fans for memory clearance. The R1 Ultimate poses a much bigger challenge for the D15. It is ever so slightly behind the D15, and a little louder, but in some ways it's more, and in some ways it's less, compatible. The R1 is significantly taller than the D15, so people with certain case limitations will be left out. However, it's also narrower than the D15, meaning not only is it more friendly to the neighboring PCI-E slot, it's also easier to reach down and unlock the GPU from the motherboard. Furthermore, it overhangs the memory less, although due to the way the fans are mounted, it may still have less clearance than the D15. Perhaps the R1 Ultimate's biggest weakness, relative to the D15, is the fans. The XF140s do look great and are actually quite good fans, but they're still using modified sleeve bearings that will negatively impact noise and longevity, as well as severely limit orientation (not a problem for most builds). Although the D15 is probably the most powerful air cooler ever made, at least in terms of noise levels that normal people would find tolerable, it does have several weaknesses. The first is its extreme width, which I've already discussed. On some of my more poorly spaced motherboards, like my new Crosshair VI Hero, I actually have to remove the middle fan to reach the GPU lock. The other is, I'm sad to say, quality control. I've had many Noctuas before and never found an appreciable scratch. But I've had two D15s and a D15S and all three have had minor blemishes. The first D15 had a small, but deep, scratch on the top plate/fin. The second had other, smaller scratches, although these are not really noticeable. The D15S was the worst, which had a small, but easily recognizable, corrosion spot on it, and it's being returned now. I can only guess that the increased surface area, probably about twice that of the next largest current-generation Noctua cooler, the U14S, makes it that much more likely for a scratch to occur. Still, I've come to expect better from Noctua. That said, you simply cannot find an air cooler that puts out this performance at this volume. There is almost no reason to use anything else in general. That's why it gets 5 stars. Although it's arguably the most powerful, is it the best? Probably not. I'd say that, depending on your needs, the D15S or the U14S is better. The D15S comes with only a single fan, but it moves the heat sink away from the GPU, making it easier to work on the computer and clearing the GPU on smaller motherboards. The U14S has infinite RAM compatibility on both sides, making it easier to work on your computer and allowing you to use any RAM you like. Thus, depending on which compatibility issue concerns you more, I'd go with either a D15S or a U14S. Each gives up between 1 and 2 degrees Celsius in overclocked loads, due almost exclusively to being single fan heat sinks. If you want D15 performance, simply add a second fan to the D15S, and a dual fan U14S will get very, very close to the D15. In many tests, I've ever seen dual fan D15Ses beat D15s, although it's unclear why that would be. Perhaps they're better aligned with the intake and exhaust fans in the case. Perhaps they are less affected by the heat coming off of the GPU. I'm not really sure, but suffice it to say, you can achieve D15 performance without some of the hassles of the D15. I've added photos of the D15 (non-S) with and without the front fan to give you an idea of memory overhang. For compatibility reasons, some people may decide just to go without the front fan altogether, with also works fine.

reviews.title: !!! Stock CPU backplate require for AM3 sockets. !!!
reviews.comment: This is a great cooler that has a lot of little things that make it superb to all other fan coolers I've seen.  It also works so well you could argue unless you are OC for super extreme numbers, its way safer than a water cooled system.  So here are some general pros and cons... Cons 1.  The stock CPU back-plate is require for AM3 sockets but, that isn't specified anywhere here, just in the AMD AM3 manual it comes with.  I used some low profile nuts I had plus my cooler-master back-plate to hold this in place as I replaced mine long ago.  You could probably find these at any hardware store so its not worth dropping stars for. 2.  It is really big and probably won't fit in some mini-to-mid-ATX case. I have a pretty big 6yr old cooler-master HFX tower and it is fine. 3.  The tolerance between the top of the cooler and the edge of my case is so tight that I had to use a strange "cheese knife" that has a set of hooked blades as its tip to grab the wire locks that secure the fans to the heat-sink. Pro's 1.  Dropped my 3.78ghz OC FX-8300 8 core Vishera CPU from 57°c to max 39-42°c while running OCCT 4.4.1 and on Primer95.  Before I couldn't run longer than 2-3 minutes before my bios set alarm of 60°c would hit while Core temp read 57°c.  FYI I was using an old, cheap, vertical blowing cooler master heat-sink, w/a 2200rpm fan. 2.  Very quiet, even when I tested overclocking at 4.4ghz, max temp was 50°c, the case fans and NB fan are still louder. 3.  Moves a lot of air in 1 of 2 directions of your choice.  The fan wire clips can be on either side of the heat sink and fan. 4.  No vibration - the dark brown triangles on the fans are actually soft bushings that keep the fan housing off the heat sink by 1-2mm's 5.  Much safer and less expensive than top water cooling which I personally think this competes with based on the OC I was able to do. 6.  Great packaging ensures it arrives undamaged and manuals in multiple languages. 7.  Comes with full back plate, nuts, and screws for 2 different Intel CPU sockets. 8.  Great - 6yr warranty, responsive customer service, and many different models to choose from. My system= hope it helps MB- 6yr old Gigabyte GA-890-fxa-ud5 rev 2.1 w/ f7e Bios to run 8core AM3+ CPU's (Win10 Pro 64bit) CPU - AMD AM3+ FX-8300 OC @ 4.1ghz 1.3v RAM- GSkill Aries 2x8gb 21300 running @ 1866mhz w/ timing 8-9-9-21 1.60v GPU- XFX-HD-5830 stock numbers, never OC- replacing soon CASE- 6yr old Cooler-Master HFX full tower, 5x HD bays, 5x 5.25" bays, w/ fans= 3x 200mm, 1x140mm, 2x120mm PSU - Antec 750w

reviews.title: One of the best AIOs, especially considering the price
reviews.comment:
I have been using and testing this AIO since I received it shortly after Black Friday. Please note that my computer sits on a separate platform next to my computer, so it's about 2.5 feet away from my ears, and it's contained in a Corsair 5000x RGB. Intel 12700k CPU, Asus TG H670 Pro Wifi D4 mobo.
I ran this in all 3 positions (top, side, front), with tubes up and down (front & side).
Even during Cinebench, LinPack Extreme, Time Spy and Prime 95, the temperatures ranged no higher than 89C with ambient (room) temperature around 23C. It was always quiet although, after the few 3 months, I noticed an occasional harmonic resonance tone, which I assume was from the fans, and I little bit of noise from the pump. The best position for both the CPU and GPU in my case was on the side, exhausting the air, with the tubes going from the side of the block to the top of the radiator. Indeed, it was also one of the best positions overall, as it also did a good job keeping both the VRM heatsinks and motherboard cooler than 6 of the 10 positions I have tested so far.
This is the first AIO I have tested, and you can watch my initial video about it on YT on my channel, The PC Expert Amateur. There will be at least one follow-up video with technical results once I complete the other 10 tests I need to do.
Please note that WelshyTech (YouTube) deemed this and the Frozen Magic Scenic V2 to be loud, but he has his computer on his desk less than a foot from his head. He also noted that the MS V2 is slightly more powerful than the Notte.
The mounting system is a bit awkward. At one point, I had to reorient the block and was unable to see (that's the bad thing about putting it on the floor) that I had missed putting two of the mounting screws through the bottom holes for the block, which resulted in bending them and slightly damaging the blue plastic stand-offs. Also, the knurled nuts are easy to turn by hand, and also have a large Philips cross for a screwdriver, but it is very easy to have them drop down to the bottom of the case. Aside from that, it's not bad, especially considering that you can mount the block in any orientation (I suggest top or right side). If you have a LONG graphics card and want to mount it on the front or side, you will likely have to vertically mount the GC (and if the case design is poor, as the 5000x's is, you will struggle to find a mount that won't choke the fans because it's too close to the left side panel) in order to do so. If you want to do a front mount with the tubes going to the bottom of the radiator (i.e. the radiator is positioned so that the tube apertures are at the bottom, not the top), it will probably be a tight fit, especially if you have a very long case, you may not be able to do it without modifying the tubes, so make sure that the block is mounted with the tubes on the side. Before finalizing the mounting of the block and rad, make sure to verify it will fit without putting too much pressure on the fittings on the block and rad. The block does have swiveling fittings for the tubes, so that does help, but it can still be a bit difficult.

reviews.title: Noctua's trademark quality strikes again.
reviews.comment:
I'll start off by saying I paired this with an Intel Core i5-12600KF 3.7 GHz 10-Core Processor and TLDR: temps are great
So I was building a PC for a friend that had never had a PC before and really wanted one.
I cobbled up a build for her using a spare motherboard I had laying around as a starting point which led me to picking a CPU that didn't have a cooler, but not to worry, Noctua exists and man they just really do make awesome coolers.
Installation is actually quite simple, (don't do what I did and unlatch the fan from the heatsink, not a problem or anything, just unnecessary on my part because I had a different cooler from them that did require moving the fans off, but that's besides the point), the instructions are laid out in such a way where it's difficult to really go astray. the visual diagrams are concise and easy to comprehend, and even gives some thermal paste tips for beginners who may not know how much or where to put the paste which is helpful because something like this can be very stressful for a newbie.
As for performance, The most intensive game we had on hand was deep rock galactic which can be a very demanding game in some circumstances because of the way it renders, we cranked the settings to max and the game didn't stutter once, more a testament to the CPU but how was the cooling with this performance? stayed pretty consistent at a frosty 60-63C for the hour we ran the game at max settings.
The room temp ambience was on the hotter end too with that level of cooling performance, it's winter so we have some heaters running in other rooms and the house contains the heat quite well, was maybe around 75 F (23* C), and like I said, it stuck around 60-63C. well under the 65C minimum average temp CPUs hang around at.
Very impressed with this cooler and as always, I'll continue buying noctua products when I need cooling solutions.

The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/F1vQvTpM9bL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/61jII5r3bVL._SY256.jpg I bought this on Black Friday and replaced my DeepCool LT720 because I have had my eye on the original Panorama ever since it was shown off at CES 2025.
I wasn't really sure what to expect with temps or noise levels, since there were not any in-depth reviews from large YouTubers when I bought this, but I was willing to take a gamble since I got a little over $100 off the $249 sale price (cash back on my Amazon card). I have a Ryzen 7 9800X3D, and my DeepCool AIO consistently idled about 42-43C with the pump at full speed. With the pump on this Tryx set to "normal" in the BIOS, I am idling around 41-42C. Full speed will push it a little lower, but the noise of the pump running at full speed was unbearable, it's very loud at full speed.
The DeepCool AIO was around $130 when I bought it, and unless you are after a clean looking sensor panel or just having a cool screen inside your tower, you'd be much better off just buying something else instead of this boutique AIO. For pure cooling performance, I don't feel the MSRP price of this Tryx AIO is worth it, you'd just be wasting money. You are paying the extra money for the OLED screen.
The hoses on this Tryx AIO are longer than they were on the DeepCool, allowing me more slack in my hoses inside my case (Lian Li O11 Vision). The old AIO hoses just barely reached, so I really liked the extra hose length provided.
The radiator is vertically mounted to the motherboard side of my case, exhausting out the side of the case.
I replaced the Tryx fans with three Phanteks PH-F120D30 fans because that's what I'm using in the rest of my case. I did not use the fans Tryx included, so I cannot speak to how loud they might be. I did have to use the Phanteks fan screws, as the Tryx screws were too short for the new fans. The fans on my old DeepCool AIO had a horrible resonance, so I had replaced those with these same fans - I just moved the fans from the old AIO to the new one. It was pretty painless, it only took about 10 minutes.
The screen connects to your PC via a USB 2.0 header. My power supply (Lian Li Edge 1300) has a powered USB hub built in, so that's what I connected my screen to.
Pros
You can upload your own videos and images to the AIO screen. I scoured the internet for animated pixel art and I am using that on mine, but you can do videos, jpegs, etc. There is a decent selection of animations provided in the Kanali software too, but I'd like to see more options.
The screen looks great, the 1440p resolution is more than perfect for this screen size.
The screen is basically a stripped down Android tablet, and handles images/videos on its own without bogging the PC down. Once they are loaded up onto the screen, the minimized Kanali software mostly has no CPU usage. Enabling system information to be displayed will of course negate that, because the software will need to be pinging the screen constantly with updates.
When I powered it on the first time, I saw some Android UI elements, so a resourceful modder could probably do some very cool stuff with this display. I'd love to see apps like SignalRBG updated to support sensor panels like these.
Acceptable temperatures for an AIO. Some Noctua fans designed for AIOs would probably shave a couple more degrees from my idles.
The AIO keeps up with CPU usage spikes, with temps leaping up, but quickly being brought back down by the AIO's pump speeding up.
The software allows you to shut off the screen with a simple toggle.
Customer support chat is built into the Kanali software, and they are fairly fast at responding.
Cons
Loud pump! It buzzes like a fish tank air pump, and I found it unbearable at full speed. Setting to Normal in BIOS made it much quieter. I was honestly shocked by how loud it was.
The software is limited - "Shuffle" just plays my GIFs once then cycles to the next GIF, which is annoying for short looped GIFs. I messaged Tryx and suggested adding a feature to loop them X times fore displaying the next GIF, or even offer a shuffled slideshow mode instead.
The software advises against displaying the same image for more than a couple of hours to avoid burn-in, but has no options to have a slide show with the video/image changing ever X minutes like Windows does for wallpaper. This would be a solid addition to the software.
The Kanali software doesn't allow you to control fans or pump speed. For some people, this is a deal breaker, but for me, I honestly don't care, I am happy to let the computer's BIOS control these automatically.
The magnets on the base of the screen/block could be stronger, the weak magnets leave the screen feeling flimsy when installing, but the screen isn't falling from its water block either, so it's sufficient.
Notes
Auto-launching Kanali is a must, otherwise the screen will not power up when Windows is loaded. You will need to *enable* Start with Windows within the Kanali software - BUT - you will also need to *disable* Kanali in as a start up item in Windows Task Manager, otherwise Kanali will not auto start itself minimized to the system tray like other apps typically do, it will instead just open its own window. I messaged Tryx to express my annoyance with the Kanali software opening itself in a window when I log in, and this is what they advised me to do and it does work just fine now. They said that it's something that will be addressed in an update.
The screen shots I've included with my review are from Kanali 1.2.1 - all my complaints and praise about the Kanali software are for this version.
The firmware update tool is a separate download from the Kanali software, though the software does claim it can check for updates. When I tried, the update window just sat on a spinning wheel for several minutes. When you install this AIO, download both and update your firmware.
The GamersNexus YouTube channel has recently stated that they plan to do an in-depth review of the Panorama, so keep an eye on YouTube for that if you are still unsure about buying one of these AIOs, but do keep in mind that the price might go up because the Android powered screen does have RAM and storage built in.
If you are looking at the Panorama SE vs. the older model - the older AIO has a fan on the water block, intended to blow air at the motherboard VRM to assist with cooling. The SE does not have this fan, but it does have a better screen. I picked the better screen, because I have a decent motherboard. If you have good air circulation in your PC case and a decent midrange/high-end motherboard with a good VRM cooler setup, you don't need to really worry about additional cooling for the VRM.

reviews.title: A no-frills, GREAT, budget 280mm AIO Liquid CPU Cooler
reviews.comment: ===TL;DR=== For the price point and the performance this cooler offers, I am beyond satisfied with my purchase and definitely recommend this cooler for anyone looking to get a no-frills, high performance, 280mm AIO without having to break the bank. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ===PROS=== ▶ Price ▷ Paid $49.99 (pre-tax) ▶ Performance ▷ 280mm Radiator vs a 240mm radiator = More surface area and larger fans that can run at lower RPMs to achieve the same level of cooling performance ▷ Works well being setup as a front intake push configuration ▷ It keeps my i7-11700K temperatures in check even under extreme synthetic load (230-250w sustained at 4.5GHz all core) with temps staying between 90-93c. ▷ Under a more reasonable load (125-150w), temps hover around the mid 50's! ▷ Under idle, temps hover around 30C or below. ▶ Fans ▷ The included 140mm fans come with a highly compact and convenient daisy chaining connector to reduce the amount of wires to route ▷ Fans move A LOT of air. Especially at higher RPMs ▷ The fans do their job without being obnoxiously loud as well. The loudest noise they make is from pushing air through the radiator when at higher RPMs. ▶ No Frills ▷ Installation was quick and easy ▷ Only 2 connectors / cables for the whole unit (one for the pump, and one for the daisy chained fans) ▷ Neutral design on the pump for both the lighting and logo (white LED ring with backlit pentagonal logo) ▷ No additional software needed to operate the unit ===CONS=== ▶ Pump ▷ Pump does have a noticeable hum to it at 100% speed, but reducing the speed to 75-80% makes it virtually inaudible over the rest of the system fans ▷ Wish the tubing connecting the pump and radiator was a little bit longer for easier routing ▶ Fans ▷ Wish the fan motors were quieter. Don't get me wrong, they are quiet, but they do make a noticeable sound. Overall, the sound isn't that disrupting to me because I am able to keep the fans spinning at a constant PWM of 35% (~750RPM) while maintaining great temperatures on my i7-11700K during most usage scenarios. ▶ Lighting / LEDs ▷ Very minor, but you can't turn off the LEDs on the pump even if you wanted to because their activation and brightness is directly controlled by the voltage being supplied to the pump. ===OTHER THOUGHTS=== I recently upgraded the CPU in my PC that I built back in 2021 from an i5-11600K to an i7-11700K. As part of the upgrade, I wanted to replace the CPU cooler I was using (be quiet! Dark Rock 4) because I had planned to transition the i5 and the previous CPU cooler into a Media Center PC build. Paying $49.99 (pre-tax) for a 280mm AIO feels like a steal because even the cheapest 120mm AIOs are sold at around $35 in price. So to only pay $14.99 more (pre-tax) to get OVER DOUBLE the amount of surface area is more than worth it! I have this cooler mounted as a front intake using a push configuration on my be quiet! Pure Base 500DX case. I ensured to mount the radiator inlet / outlet tubes oriented at the bottom to aid in preventing air bubbles from frequently entering the pump. I had originally wanted to mount it at the top of my case as an exhaust using a push config but I was unable to due to some clearance issues with the dual 8-pin CPU power cables going into my motherboard. Due to the physical size of the GPU I am using and the relatively compact nature of the case I am using, I had to route the tubes over the top of my GPU because the tubes are relatively short and it was the only way I could ensure the inlet and outlet remained at the lowest point of the loop. But, aside from a minor aesthetic difference, it was no big deal because I was able to get everything (tightly) squeezed in without any clearance issues. Overall, installation was easy although the installation guide was pretty minimal on instructions provided. I did not use the included thermal paste as I have another paste I prefer to use (Zalman ZM-STG2) so I cannot comment on that. I really like that they have a "daisy chaining" connection for the included fans so only having to connect and route 2 total wires was very nice. As mentioned in my Pros, I am running this on an i7-11700K. I have the pump set to run at 75% until the CPU temp reaches a sustained 90C where it then increases to 90% and then up to 100% if temps were to reach a sustained 95C. I have the fans configured to run at 35% PWM until CPU temperatures reach a sustained 90C where they increase to 70% PWM and then up to 100% PWM if temps were to reach a sustained 100C. Under normal gaming and usage loads, the pump never increases its speed past the 75% mark and the fans never increase their speed past the 35% mark which means that everything remains cool and quiet! This is one of the benefits of running a larger radiator with larger fans is that you are able to run everything at lower speeds to reduce noise levels while still maintaining low temperatures (see the Pros for more details on the CPU temps). To conclude, for the price point and the performance this cooler offers, I am beyond satisfied with my purchase and definitely recommend this cooler for anyone looking to get a no-frills, high performance, 280mm AIO without having to break the bank or pay for things like RGB, USB connection or other non-essential features.
