reviews.title: Solid High Quality and Well Engineered Full Tower Case 901 Pro - White
reviews.comment:
I just received the  new be Quiet! 901 Pro Computer case in all white from Amazon. The Corrugated box arrived in perfect condition, as did the Computer case inside. Unboxing was just like the on-line videos, and everything that was supposed to come with the case was delivered. My initial impressions of the case are that there was a lot of thought and real quality put into the design and manufacturing. The fit and the finish of this case is outstanding. Very well built and robust, and no rough edges, no bad paint, and a ton of options to configure this full tower case the way you want it. Yes, I like having the Optical Drive bay, and I will use it. The case is heavy, but that is due to having a very solid build with thick steel, and thick tempered glass side panel. Even all the wiring from the front panel is white in color. The case is easy to dis-assemble, and none of the thumb screws or phillips screws were jammed in tight, where you strip the heads of the screws to loosen the screw. I think this is one of the few modern cases with a removable motherboard tray. That is a very nice feature when you are assembling your build. Yes, some may think the cost of this case is a bit steep, but for all that you are getting, I really think this case represents real value, and something one can work with and or change for a good many years. This one is a winner. Very glad I purchased this.
Addendum: I will add that this case was a pleasure to build my new rig in. There is plenty of space for EATX Motherboards, large Video cards, and ample places for additional drives if you need them. Cable management is fairly easy with a large area in the back of the case. I went with the new DT Phanteks fans, and a 360 water cooling radiator in the front. I am using BIOS for the fan control, but nice to have the option of the case fan speed too. Very happy with this build and the new case to contain it all. Cheers!
reviews.author: Antony Steele

reviews.title: Expensive but really nice
reviews.comment: Tons of flexibility and huge. Pricey but understandable given all the ways it can be configure.
reviews.author: Katherine A. De Vos

reviews.title: Best case I’ve owned
reviews.comment: Love this case! Great price, well made, great air flow. Fits my 5070ti comfortably. Looks awesome as well. Highly recommend.
reviews.author: Tom F

reviews.title: Look's Great!
reviews.comment: Great case, easy to build in. Lacking in the 3.5" drive department, but the two included SSD slots behind the motherboard should prove adequate if you need to expand storage. The quality is as to be expected from Corsair, and the case itself is priced really reasonably for what you get.
reviews.author: Zaden

reviews.title: Love this case and recommend it
reviews.comment:
This case is by far my favorite PC case of all time, it has ample space inside for up to 9 case fans, a large CPU cooler, full sized GPU, among all the other things you may want to place inside. It can support up to an e-atx motherboard and has great cooling. It is a very sturdy case with no structural problems, and has a comfortable thickness that makes the case overall weighty but manageable. Additionally, the dust filters are nice and work well
I have seen no component compatibility issues an to close, the case is highly functional with no issues housing a high end computer build.
Absolutely love and recommend this case
reviews.author: Sirenz

reviews.title: Case to easily build in but with some qorks.
reviews.comment: Great case easily to build in. It does have limited space for SSDs. Can only mount two in the slot and cannot mount HHDs in the case even though it is labeled that you can.  Glass panels are held very well and buildings close to Lian Li cases if you’ve ever used those cases.  Corsair Shift PSU fit very well with plenty of room for cable management.  There are several tie points throughout the case but no secure straps. Would have been nice if it would have came with Velcro straps.  Case is of good weight and strength. Fan placement is ok.  Fan sizes are very strange.  120mm it is fine for but if mounting 140mm fans leaves a look that might be less desired.  Case would be a lot better if it came with rubber grommets for the cable routing holes.  Side panel only holds three 120mm or two 140mm which looks odd with 140mm. The ability to use 3 140mm fans would be a better look.  Size of case is perfect and hold quite a bit of items.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Beast of a Case
reviews.comment:
In love with this case. I probably spent more time selecting a case for my build than any other part, but man am I glad I picked this one. The wraparound glass panels are just sooo sleek, and the build itself is very high quality, though I am a sucker for corsair cases.
I got my aio 360 up top as exhaust, and the 3 intakes on the front side just look great. I even fit another fan on the bottom, right in front of the psu slot, and the cooling on this thing is amazing. It's heavy, but that's what you get from a beast of a case like this. Hiding all the fan cables was a bit of a puzzle, but manageable.
Overall, I'm stoked with this purchase. My pc looks friggin awesome.
reviews.author: jberna

reviews.title: Quite possibly the easiest Case I have ever built in.
reviews.comment: This case is quite possibly the most builder friendly case I have ever worked with. Almost every single panel is removable; no need to fumble around the case attempting to attach fans, the chassis has completely detachable front, top and side panels. The Frame is quite sturdy, I don't feel a wobble or like its going to bend easily. It's also one of the few cases that are compatible with a 420 AIO and has the clearance for a gigantic tower cooler at the same time. If you want, you can also order a tempered glass side if you ever feel like you want to show off your components, but be aware that this will affect noise level and air flow if you do. It will also shave off a little bit of tower cooler compatibility. All in all, this is a case I would recommend in a heartbeat. It's incredibly easy to add extra fans, and it's cable management is great. Recommended for anyone using a high end GPU and CPU!
reviews.author: Carlos Canales

reviews.title: Great pc case!
reviews.comment: This is probably the best case I’ve ever built in. All black, no fluff, fantastic design for space, access, airflow, cable management paired with the Corsair 850x psu is awesome. I was looking for an all black no lights, power & usb’s on top & this fit the bill perfect! Price was good as well!
reviews.author: David Mayger

reviews.title: New pc use
reviews.comment: Ease of use is insane and the value has felt fantastic for its price. Highly recommend and it feels extremely solid with no chance of falling apart. No tempered glass in my purchase but looks very sleek!
reviews.author: Logan

reviews.title: Not new
reviews.comment: Not new.
reviews.author: P. William Bane

reviews.title: I really like the H5 Flow and recommend it
reviews.comment: I’ve been using the H5 Flow RGB case for a while now, and it’s definitely a solid choice for anyone looking to build a PC with great airflow and some sleek RGB flair. Here’s what stood out to me: Design & Aesthetics The case looks awesome with its minimalistic design and integrated RGB fans. The RGB lighting is bright but not too over-the-top, and it’s easy to customize using the included software. The tempered glass side panel shows off the internal components really well, making it a nice centerpiece for my setup. Airflow & Cooling Airflow is the standout feature of this case. The mesh front panel and spacious interior allow for great air circulation, which keeps my components cool, even during long gaming sessions. It comes with two pre-installed fans, but there’s room to add more if needed. My RTX 3070 and i5 11400F stay at solid temps without any heat issues, which is exactly what I was hoping for. Before this case my GPU was at 65 idle and 81 gaming now it’s 35 idle and  65-70 gaming Build Quality & Ease of Use The build quality is impressive. The case feels sturdy without being overly heavy. It’s
reviews.author: Dave S.

reviews.title: Insane cooling, looks good, good quality.
reviews.comment: I've had this case for about 9 months, got it for an entirely fresh build. I have multiple great things to say, and one complaint. Here's the synopsis: - cooling so good you wouldn't believe it until you have it. - spacious. - no annoying software. - looks great. - tough assemble. Ignore the finger prints in the photo, I refuse to peel off plastic protectors until they're falling off. Cooling. I mostly got this case for looks and price. However, I found out recently that apparently my CPU basically requires liquid cooling. Not with this case, it doesn't. My temps are always cool, everywhere. On that note, I also have an unreasonably large CPU cooler that fits very nicely in there. Looks. It's held up very nicely, no scratches or issues, even after a move. Lights do their own thing, not annoyingly bright, I'm not super invested in that aspect personally. Easily to clean and keep looking nice. All the matierals feel very sturdy, and are very sturdy. Complaint. When I put this thing together I wanted to pull my hair out. It was really frustrating. There are not indicators on the fan directions. They really, really, really need some videos and extra material to help along the process. Very very small thing, the bottom fan needs one of those magnetic wire covers. I lost two screws during the build to that area.
reviews.author: Alex

reviews.title: Inexpensive, easy to build, and cool temps!
reviews.comment: Swapped cases from a smaller Corsair to this H5 Flow and I couldn't be happier. The case looks beautiful and not at all inexpensive. Twin 140mm fans in the front also look great when lit up with ARGB. The side panel definitely is tinted so your computer innards aren't TOO visible, but ARGB definitely shines through. It was a pleasure to build in with the nice removable tray for the front fans and has plenty of room on the back side to hide all of the shameful wires. It looks great and the angled GPU fan light shines through the bottom of the case which gives a nice "underglow" look in the evening. I utilize Fan Control and have custom curves for all of my fans. When web browsing I am able to keep all fans at their minimum speed of ~6XX rpm to keep things quiet and the CPU stays around 30-35C. I never see 100% fan speed on my curves and the temps stay around 70C even with 100% CPU load over an extended time.
reviews.author: Alex

reviews.title: Perfect for budget builds!
reviews.comment: Best case I've gotten, everything fits easily and it has so many fans + usb ports so it won't overheat and is great with accessories. Easy to install, pc has been quiet, works great.
reviews.author: Jayden Germana

reviews.title: Beautiful case. Hassle for an old computer.
reviews.comment: I had some trouble with this case, getting it to work with my old Dell computer. But it's so nice I have to give it four stars. I re-cased my ancient Dell PC's motherboard along with adding a new faster hard drive and more RAM. I was very surprised by the very nice, heavy duty construction and nice styling of the case. The motherboard screwed right in, and my large Nvidia graphics card went in nicely. But the cables that came with it weren't entirely compatible. It seems to be better suited to a newer gaming motherboard. I couldn't get the LED lights to function. I found some YouTube videos and articles showing what I needed. I had to buy two adapter kits and now it works great, except that I can't use the power switch or jacks on the front of the case. I had to mount my old switch on the back of the case. But my kid isn't complaining, he loves it, and now we have a super fast powerful and beautiful gaming PC for a minimal cost.
reviews.author: Rod

reviews.title: Really good case for the price and feature
reviews.comment: I was very pleasantly surprised with the quality and look of this case in relation to its price. It is well laid out, easy to build in and looks really nice all together. The big 200mm fans in the front are ARGB and have a button the case as well as an ARGB header that can be used to control the colors. They are fixed speed but move enough air for that not to be an issue and are very quiet. I had some concern that temps would be an issue with the glass front. The sides are open and there is plenty enough room for those fans to pull in cool air. The fan at the rear is a no-nonsense standard type fan that can be speed controlled by the motherboard header. I would recommend this case not only from a price perspective....and I am not sure how they do it but it comes off seeming of a higher quality than the price point. The edges and whatnot on the inside are well finished, not sharp. No issues with my hands during the build. The only detractor was that it was missing one of the standoffs for the motherboard. I had more on hand but it would be an issue if you didn't have more available. All in all one of the better case purchases I have made.
reviews.author: M Jordan

reviews.title: This case is perfect. Period.
reviews.comment: I don't know how you could design a better case. The screws are perfect for hand twisting, The glass is super cool, The air flow is awesome, The lights are neat, The amount of space is perfect, The orientation of the PSU and CPU is perfect, It has magnetic dust covers that can be removed and washed, It has USB and headphones on the top (perfect!) and not on the side like some cases, It has a cute and not obnoxious power led, You can see inside the case perfectly, Lots of ties and such to manage your cables, It's super lightweight, Removing the metal plate covers for the GPU didn't feel like I had to bend the whole frame like some cases Both sides of the case are removable in case one part is more accessible from the other side to make things easy. The fans are super quiet. It's perfect.
reviews.author: TonyD

reviews.title: Keeps great temps!
reviews.comment: Overall happy with this case. I've had it now for about 6 months and so far it's great. I bought it with the thermalright Assassin X cpu cooler and this pc stays very cool. It's always at around 25c and when I'm gaming it sits at around 40c. Real easy to put together. This case is almost operates and is about the same size like the corsair 3000 and 4000 series of cases. Front pops off to get to the fans in the front and everything feels pretty solid. If you can get this at a good price it's definitely worth it
reviews.author: IronBuddha

reviews.title: Overall nice case.
reviews.comment: Decent case. A bit small to fit hands in but looks great and fit everything in I put into this computer build. Cable management seems to work.
reviews.author: Steve

reviews.title: Good, cheap PC case with good thermals, but has cheap build quality.
reviews.comment: The case is good and sturdy, but there are some things to note. Without computer components installed, it is REALLY light. The front cover over the triple fans is also made cheap plastic. It's no surprise that the fans are also plastic, but one of my fans' plastic frame broke, but it still works when it's screwed in. Note however, the top front fan is inverted by default and exhausts air, so you have to open the plastic front panel to switch it around if you want. And do this FIRST before installing computer components. Cable management is only okay. The back side panel feels very thin and flexible, even if it's made of metal, and it shows a small buldge if you shove all of your cables into the back. There is however ample room to stuff cables under the metal box next to the power supply. The screws are also not exactly ATX standard, since I confused myself and used the wrong screws from a different ATX case. Just make sure to read the instructions and use the correct screws that come with the case. On a more positive end, the RGB does look nice, and the fans have an option to be plugged into your motherboard or just left on their own. You can also change the RGB lighting with the extra button next to the power button. There is also LOTS of airflow so I don't worry about anything getting over 75°C. It does come with a magnetic mesh for the top and a removable mesh for the PSU at the bottom, but it won't be incredibly effective at keeping out dust. Overall good budget case. It feels cheap and has some plastic parts, but if all you want is a cheap case with good thermals, this is a decent choice.
reviews.author: Luke

reviews.title: Best mini itx case
reviews.comment: I bought this to replace a fractal node 202. I liked the original node, but hated having to take the entire chassis apart for maintenence. The Ridge improves upon the original design in several ways. Instead of a monolithic frame it can be taken apart on each side. Top and bottom of the case have 4 screws, and the sides have a captive screw and pop into place. Super easy to access the inside of the case if you make a mustake or need to access the mobo. I HATE the new middle gpu bracket! I had to remove it 3 times before getting my gpu to seat properly. Im not sure if its supposed to but my case did not include an external power cable. Luckily i had a spare. The form factor can be intimidating, but i really like the new design, and it was a very easy build overall. For comparison, i also own a Cooler Master NR200, and found this easier to assemble.
reviews.author: Rodger

reviews.title: Rigid, high quality, easy to build, lots of cooling options.
reviews.comment: Incredible case. It was first time for me to build a PC and it was such a pleasant experience. Case feels rigid and let's you build comfortably. If your hand grow from the right place -- you can finish your build in a hour easily, maybe faster. good stuff. recommended. Temperatures are ok as well if you're not putting 5090 in there and you are using 100W TDP processor. In my case, i was using Minisforum BD790i X3D board. It comes with the pre-installed processor and cooler. Also, the airflow of this cooler goes out of the pc case, which is amazing. Noise levels are great and CPU temps in my case are below 85 C. My RTX 5060 stays at 65 C.
reviews.author: TOMMY

reviews.title: Best looking console/HTPC style case that can fit some larger GPU's
reviews.comment: This review is for the Fractal Ridge ITX case in black color. I purchased this case specifically for its looks and horizontal configuration ability. I think it looks great and matches my other black components on my TV console table. The white components inside the case really isn't noticeable at all outside of the case. Component installation is very easy and straight forward. Just follow the directions for the power supply (SFX form factor only) and GPU installation. For GPU size, I recommend no more than a 2.5 slot thick GPU to keep the stock preinstalled case fans. The two case fans are 140mm and standard thickness. To use a 3 slot GPU you would be limited to a slim fan or no case fans and cooling performance would be affected. The GPU in my pictures is the Asrock 9070 XT Steel Legend and is 2.5 half slots thick. The case fans are right on top and touch the GPU shroud, but it keeps the GPU cool. I do strongly recommend removing the top of the case, then remove the preinstalled fans, install the GPU, then carefully slide the fans down into position and screw them in and make sure they are intaking air (blowing air onto the GPU). Note the included 140mm case fans have a lip and are specially designed to fit this case as intake so that the fan blades do not rub against the frame. If you replace the fans, you may have to use spacers to prevent the fan blades from touching the frame. Do note that the CPU heatsink is limited to 70mm in height. This severely limits CPU choices. For me I found that my Ryzen 7 7800X3D would overheat and cause a system shutdown. My Ryzen 5 8400F gets really hot, at 95 Celsius but does not shutdown. My advice is to stick with Ryzen 5 or Core i5 series for this case. There is room at the top of the frame where the CPU is that can hold an 80mm fan but the screw holes are smaller than typical fan screws, so I'll have to see if I can find some screws that will fit. The side panels work on either side. I chose to have the CPU facing down and the GPU facing up to give better cooling for the GPU. Having the CPU facing up did not make a difference to the CPU temps. I think it really needs 80mm fan in CPU chamber. If this case was slightly thicker/wider to accommodate taller CPU coolers and 3 slot GPUs with the standard thickness side case fans, then it would have been the perfect small form factor build with no compromises. Due the compact layout, the thermal performance limits your component options. For me this works out because I'm using this PC with a 4k TV and gaming performance isn't bound by the CPU at 4k resolution and my 8400F is perfectly reasonable. I also recommend getting a motherboard with overclocking features not for overclocking but for the voltage controls to lower or limit the CPU voltage. I do recommend this case overall if you're looking for a home theater or console style case that looks great and fits in with other components. There just aren't too many options that have the looks, price, and compact size. Do note that there are some component choice compromises due the compact size.
reviews.author: Wesley

reviews.title: Fractal created a winner
reviews.comment: Been in IT for over 20 years and this has been one of the most thoughtfully designed cases I've worked inside of. They didn't just rivet everything into place, it's actually screwed together and can be torn down pretty much completely. Cable management is thought out and serves it's purpose well. The PSU mounting solution keeps everything very tidy and gives the exterior a pretty nice minimal feel all around. I liked working with it so much that I ended up getting a Torrent (also by Fractal Design) for my personal build. Again, another very nice case to work in. Fractal seems to consistently offer very well designed and manufactured cases. I'd recommend this to anyone looking for an ultra-compact performance build in a heartbeat.
reviews.author: Mike

reviews.title: Great little case looks really good
reviews.comment: It's a great form factor and it is really well put together!
reviews.author: Travis Nelson

reviews.title: Unique PC case for modern builds
reviews.comment: Great case, fun to build in. Love the old school aesthetic. Plenty of air flow too.
reviews.author: Joel

reviews.title: Amazing Case
reviews.comment: Absolutely beautiful vintage looking case, temps are looking great. Recently built my pc but was in the market for one of these for a while. It’s a little small on the inside based on what you might expect, but was extremely easy to switch my build over. It’s extremely sturdy but also on the lighter side which is a huge plus, and although it might be expensive, it is hands down the best looking case vintage-style case on the market!
reviews.author: Matthew

reviews.title: A sleeper hit!
reviews.comment: While yes it's an expensive case I think it's worth every penny, it's very well built. If you grew up tinkering with PC's in the 90's you'll truly appreciate the rounded edges inside, no more randomly getting cut. It has plenty of room for modern hardware with some configuration. Great airflow with Arctic P12 Pro fans using the integrated fan hub controller. Weight is what you'd expect from an all metal case and it's easy to build in. Thank you SilverStone for bringing this to the masses!
reviews.author: Christian J. Hattery

reviews.title: Great Modern Case with a Retro Look.
reviews.comment: I absolutely love this case. It arrived in great condition and was packed very well. The modern necessities are implemented great with the retro look. There is plenty of space to work in and moves a lot of air with the preinstalled case fans,
reviews.author: DarthVaderVan

reviews.title: Great sleeper build.
reviews.comment: Best thing since sliced bread.
reviews.author: Pkay Technology

reviews.title: Awesome Case!
reviews.comment: Got white and Black ones, about 13 for a client. Love these cases. Not one part missing, nothing broken, everything worked great. Had zero complaints while building in them. They have great air flow and price point is GREAT with the fans included and fan controller. Fans are nice and tie into mobo software or lighting software. Would recommend and will be building computers in the future with Montech cases. Fans were silent when tuned. Nice small-esk mid-tower that look nice in the office with lights turned off or on a nice white. Easy to build in. Let's go Montech! Thanks for doing it right.
reviews.author: RestartFirst

reviews.title: Great-looking case with awesome airflow and lights out of the box
reviews.comment: I recently built a new gaming PC and went with the Montech Sky Two case — and I’m really happy with it. It was my first time buying a Montech product, but after seeing the build quality and features, I’ll definitely consider them again. First off, this thing looks sharp. The dual tempered glass panels on both sides make it easy to show off all your parts — and trust me, it looks really good with RGB lighting inside. The front has a clean, modern look with good ventilation. What sold me was that it comes with 4 ARGB PWM fans already installed. That saved me a bunch of money and time because usually you have to buy fans separately and wire them up yourself. These are bright, colorful, and sync up well with my motherboard via the included controller. Lights look great without being too over the top. Airflow is solid too. With the front and side panels open for intake and the rear exhaust, temps on my GPU and CPU are staying nice and low. I did install an extra fan just for extra cooling, but even before that, things were running smoothly. The Type-C port on the front panel is super convenient. My old case had USB-A only, and now I can plug in my phone or flash drive super fast without having to dig around back. Build quality feels strong — thick metal, sturdy glass panels, and the cable management channels in the back are wide enough to run wires through easily. Took some time to set everything up, but the layout makes it manageable even if you're not a pro builder. Overall, if you want a sleek, high-airflow case with RGB already built in, this is a great pick. Feels like a premium case for a mid-range price.
reviews.author: Shailesh Kalloe

reviews.title: Yeah, this case rocks.
reviews.comment: I decided to go with the Montech Sky Two for my first ever PC build and I am glad I did! The case is large and beautiful. It's able to fit my 3070 Ti and has plenty of room for an even larger card. The front and side glass panels give you an excellent view of the components inside. The pre-installed fans are just the best. They have great lighting effects and airflow. I even bought an extra one to place at the top for extra exhaust. My case and the air flowing out are always pretty cool to the touch when even playing more demanding games like Stalker 2 and Helldivers 2. Not noticeably loud for me either. My home is naturally very dusty, but I think the filters do a good job at keeping most of it out. The cable management was done well and it comes with tons of extra screws and zip ties for all your needs. Sleek design, spacious interior, easy cable management, pre-installed fans... This case checked all the boxes for me and I think you can't go wrong with it.
reviews.author: Linda Samudio

reviews.title: My go to for budget builds without sacrificing aesthetics
reviews.comment: stylish and budget-friendly mid-tower case that offers excellent airflow and build quality. It comes with four pre-installed ARGB fans, supports large GPUs up to 400mm, and features dual tempered glass panels for a sleek look. Cable management is straightforward, making it a great choice for both new and experienced builders. Overall, it’s a solid case that delivers great value for its price.
reviews.author: Gabe

reviews.title: Affordable, but well built!
reviews.comment: Great case and fanatics looking. However the rear fan does not support 240mm aio cooler, but with some engineering I mad it work. Cheap case but well built. The cable management was easy with all the holes and slots to run the cables. It was perfect size to fit under my desk. The fans are honestly a lot quieter then my old Be Quiet! Fans.
reviews.author: Sean

reviews.title: Better then i expected
reviews.comment:
I must say , i am pleasantly surprised with this case . I just bought it because i had to rebuild my spare pc to have as a back up but end up using it as main pc because after i did it i liked it so much that i swapped the parts and now it`s mine pc #1 lol .
Pros:
Lots of room , pretty , love the front mash it gives you good airflow , cable management is really awesome and easy to do . Also , bottom shroud front panel easy removal so you can connect the cables to psu without hassle . It was the best cable management i ever did because it was easy to rout the cables .  I love that i can install 3x140mm fans on top front back AND bottom , which gives more air like i already mentioned it previously . Lots of usb ports which gives me possibility to connect my mouse and headphones at front for better signal . You can change front and top mash for solid panels if you want more quiet which i dont care about but its there if you need . Latch button for taking the side panel's off is great addition too .
Cons:
Very tight on the bottom between motherboard and shroud so you have to connect the motherboard and front panel connector and other wires before you install the motherboard because it is tough to do it after .
Vertical gpu opening on the back is useless if you have big air cooler which in my case is BeQuiet Dark Rock Pro 4 . There is no room for gpu to stand vertical because the air cooler is too big . Not sure if installing other vertical bracket will work either because motherboard sits too low , so you are stuck with horizontal gpu position only . That is actually big deal because all the hot air from gpu goes into the cpu cooler and temps are higher on cpu because of it . Fan hub could be made for pwm 4 pin fans instead of 3 pin but you can add one i guess for a few dollars .
All in all its a awesome case with those few things to improve but for $180 its not bad .
reviews.author: Hector

reviews.title: Favorite case so far
reviews.comment:
One of the best ATX cases I’ve ever built in.
Super solid case with zero flex in the structure. Very roomy which makes it a breeze to build in. Tons of customization options such as an inverted layout, removable power supply shroud, cable management channels, pull out radiator mounts, swappable front panel, and swappable top panels. The tempered glass is slightly tinted which makes the case look cohesive with all the black. The side panels are easily removed with the press of a button and come completely off, rather than other cases which open as a swinging door. Also makes closing the panels easy even if your cables poke out slightly. Dust filter for the front panel and under chassis. Optional dust filter for the top panel, but I use the noise reducing panels instead. I also use the top as an exhaust, so there’s no need for the dust filter anyway. Tons of channels for cable management and grommets to cover any holes not used. Space for an optional reservoir/pump if you decide to run a custom loop. Plenty of room in the front to run a push/pull configuration and still have a reservoir behind it all. Amazing sleek design. After getting a bequiet case, I’m not sure I can get anything else.
reviews.author: Steven Dang

reviews.title: Great
reviews.comment: I guess this case is a bit old now?  Anyway, I purchased it and really like it.  It's a 5 star case in all ways.  I didn't do my homework and that's on me.  This is a big case.  I thought I accidentally purchased a full tower.  It doesn't fit in my little desk computer area.  That area now houses my modem and router.  That noted, I very much appreciate the space and ease of being able to work in it for a mid-tower, easy cable routing, SSD controller, good instruction manual and online help, and aesthetics.  It's quiet enough that I honestly don't hear my CPU or vid card fans at all.  Doors are very easy to click on and off with the one button push (no screws!!!!).  I only hear my 850w PSU when it kicks on and that's rarely.  It was nice to have the 3 fans included.  I didn't get, but I will eventually get, a water cooler for my CPU.  It's clear that it would be easy to setup a 2 or 3 fan system.  Taking it apart to route wires and do an install was great.  It's a tad heavy but that's ok for me anyway.  Can't go wrong with this case unless you need very light or a smaller case.
reviews.author: msan_msw

reviews.title: Very good overall, but not as quiet as I expected.
reviews.comment:
There may be a contradiction between my 4-star rating and overall assessment of the case.
It went into a high-end gaming PC. It is an awesome modular case, with plenty of space, great cable management. The guts stay cool, as expected. So why 4 stars then? I have a nearly identical setup inside a Thermaltake F30 and it is significantly quieter with the front closed, with pretty much the same temperatures - so it is lacking a bit, and for the price I was expecting more. In fact this beQuiet is quite audible when running, while I wouldn't be able to tell if the Thermaltake is running without paying attention to it - again, when the front is closed and the system is idle. Both systems are using the same CPU, same type of fans and liquid cooling, so it is truly apples to apples, but fans at low speed can still be heard.
reviews.author: DJC

reviews.title: Great case for a good price
reviews.comment: Excellent case. Glass side panel and Acrylic front panel. Lots of extra room to work in with plenty of options to route your cables through. Fans have adequate performance for a decent budget build. They are not completely silent but not loud at all. They run at approximately 1500rpm and it's enough that you do feel the air moving from the case. The aesthetics are great and easy to control. All the fans come connected to a single controller which can control the RGB with the default LED button or if you hold the button down for 5 seconds it will work with your other RGB settings in your lighting software like Aura or Mystic Light. If I had one complaint, it would be that the cables from the fans to controller do not come combed out, they are tangled and shoved inside, but for that being the only issue and easily manageable I don't think it is a problem. If you're working on the bottom of an ATX motherboard, you will have to remove the lower back 2 fans but it is simple to do. The magnetic dust filters are a nice addition as well, easily removed for cleaning and don't disrupt airflow too much. It came with all the necessary hardware but I did have to install the forward 3 stand offs for the ATX board. Case buttons and USB ports are good quality with decent cables that aren't too stiff or hard to work with. Overall, I am very happy with the purchase and the way my build turned out.
reviews.author: DD85

reviews.title: Amazing value for the case and fans
reviews.comment: Couple of things: 1) The 7 fan LEDs are controlled by a button on the case that changes color. I dont know if you can put it into a mode where the controller can be fed by a 3 pin ARGB header or not, I just simply picked a color and matched it to the SAMA L60 360mm AIO. UPDATE, hold the led button down for 5 seconds, that will tell the controller to use the ARGB port if you have it plugged into the MB. 2) After you install the MB, just the MB. Flip the case over and unscrew the 3 x 120mm fans on the bottom, let them hang. Continue to wire any items like your case system header, with the fans in place it will be near impossible with large hands. If you fiddle without taking out the fans it will probably take 20 minutes to plug things in. Spend the 2 minutes, remove the fans. do your work on the bottom of the MB and then put the fans back in. Outside of that everything is easy and there is a TON of room behind the MB to stuff cabling. I had 1 SAMA product before, a black widow 1000w PSU which I used a in test system and it was fine, worked, so I took a chance and bought this case, the 1000w PSU in white and a L60 360mm AIO all from SAMA. Everything works, no issues. I came from be quiet! products which are exceptional quality, and pretty pricey. But those cases dont speak to the 13 year old nerd in me. This case does. Only the side panel is glass, the front panel appears to be acrylic, other people have noted that its glass but I can see the waves in the plastic from the molding if I look at it down the barrel. Still looks great. Temps are super good, obvious this is a very positive pressure case, the bottom and side/vertical fans are intake, the rear and the aio are exhaust. I set the fans to 50% pwm and they are pretty silent.
reviews.author: Phillip

reviews.title: Great budget case, but expect to spend hours on cable management.
reviews.comment: pros: honestly, it was a great budget case, especially coming with all of the fans. I absolutely love the look. It’s very beautiful and very spacious to put figures. The airflow is really great too. cons: absolutely atrocious fan cable management and poor RGB hub. I honestly wish all the fans came uninstalled, Because in order to work in the case, you have to take them all off and I probably spent over an hour and a half redoing all of the fan cables. Also, I’d recommend getting your own RGB hub. The one that comes with the case is really cheap. overall, I definitely recommend it, even though it’s a headache, it’s very much worth it because it is a pretty high-quality case and comes with all the fans so you are saving a lot of money
reviews.author: Kitty Lover Needs

reviews.title: Great Product! Great Support!
reviews.comment: -After many years of using an ugly case that had sub-par airflow, I decided to get one that looks good and has good circulation. -I got the SAMA V60 in white and it looks incredible. It has very good airflow and awesome lighting and fans that come preinstalled and wired through a hub. -The interior is very spacious, and there is plenty of room to store excess cables in the back where they are not in the way or seen. -It was easy to set up and had all of the hardware/screws that I needed. -I had some minor difficulties with getting my RGB and fan speed controls to work through my MSI software at first, so I contacted customer support. The seller was super helpful and gave me detailed instructions on how to solve the issues on my end. Now, everything is working great! -In case anybody has the same issues I had: -make sure that you enable the PWM fan setting (Not DC) in your bios so that you can control fan speeds through your MoBo software. -If you can't control your ARGB fans through your software, press and hold the "LED" button on the front panel of the case. This will enable the ARGB controlling. -If you want a sleek-looking PC case with great product support at a good price, I highly recommend buying from SAMA. And no, I am not sponsored by them!
reviews.author: gabe

reviews.title: A good case
reviews.comment: Built my first PC recently and opted for the V60 by SAMA. The chassis itself is great; a lot of room to work with and the quality is there. It looks wonderful. My main complaint would be that ATX boards do work but are very close to the base. I, unfortunately, installed my motherboard prior to feeding cables under it and being lazy, I had to feed a couple of cables through the side as opposed to the cleaner option. Not deducting any point for that because, as stated, the ATX board *does* fit. The included fans work well, though the hub is affixed to the base in the back. The cables also looked like spaghetti and required being detangled then reconnected prior to working on everything else.
reviews.author: S.

reviews.title: Good case
reviews.comment: Spacious for internals. Great look. Came with four fans, holds 10. Sturdy as hell and comes apart easy too.
reviews.author: Okami

reviews.title: Best case I’ve used so far
reviews.comment: I love this case it’s so cool and has a bunch of interesting features. It’s a little bulky I won’t lie but if you get the RGB version it looks really good. Pretty easy to build in it has plenty of room.
reviews.author: Richard John Ruiz

reviews.title: Amazing case!
reviews.comment: I got this to replace my Be Quiet Pure Base 500 FX so that I could accommodate a new 360mm AIO (Also Be Quiet) and a larger GPU. This is one of the easiest cases I have ever built in. Moving everything over went smoothly. The built in fan/ RBG hubs made wiring those a breeze. My PC is beautiful now. Can't wait for my new GPU to get here on Friday. Temps have been fantastic so far.
reviews.author: Todd

reviews.title: Great Case, with some Quirks
reviews.comment: Picked this up during Amazon Prime Days. This case seems like is a premium, quiet mid-tower with a clean design, good airflow, and solid materials.  setup experience might not be so  smooth, especially for first-time or occasional builders. The case itself is great: very sturdy construction, thick steel panels, quality Silent fans pre-installed, and plenty of room inside for a full-size GPU and 360mm AIO. I had issues with sliding the back vented panel off: it was very stuck to the point where I thought I’d need a pry bar (or return it for replacement) but eventually came off. I had no issues fitting an RTX 4080 and a front-mounted 360mm AIO cooler. Cable management is great with lots of room behind the motherboard tray, zip ties, and rubber grommets. Where it falls short is the documentation. The included manual is your typical Chinese pictograms; very basic. Not all cables are labeled, and there’s no clear diagram showing where everything is inside the case. If you’re a beginner, this could definitely slow you down or leave you guessing what goes where. A simple labeled diagram or cable map would have made a huge difference. SSDs are to be installed along the “door” of the back of the case. However, the provided screws will not work with the smaller holes of SSDs. With the rubber standoff grommets provided, no screws will work. The RGB lighting is minimal but tasteful — just a front strip with motherboard sync support or using the dedicated button on the front case controls. If you’re into subtle lighting, this fits the aesthetic perfectly. Airflow is solid out of the box, and with one extra fan for exhaust, temps stayed excellent while still whisper-quiet. Pros: • Very quiet, even under load • Nice build quality with a clean, minimal look • Spacious interior with great cable routing • DX ARGB fans included • Good airflow and support for large GPUs/AIOs Cons: • Poor documentation and unlabeled cables • Not very beginner-friendly • Need to unstick the sliding back panel • Screws for SSD installation or improved mounting. Bottom Line: If you’re an experienced builder or willing to take your time, the 600 LX is a great case. It runs cool and quiet and looks premium without going over the top. But if you’re new to PC building, be prepared to do some trial-and-error or look up extra help online, because the instructions definitely leave something to be desired.
reviews.author: Erik

reviews.title: Great case
reviews.comment: Beautiful case. Very spacious. Love the different positions you can have it in. I have mine laying flat. Couldn't be happier
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Super Cheap - But still looks nice.
reviews.comment: looks great, added 120MM fans and still has room for 2xSata SSDs and and small video card. Zero built in cable management, going to require old school zip tieing and only one side paneled comes off What saved it, and why I gave it five stars is depending on sales, seller, and branding this case can be had between $30-$39 in multiple colors.  The only valid competition at that price is open air benches, and noting at this price point in white.  Nothing as clean looking in this price range. I have a full build video up.
reviews.author: Jordos TechShack

reviews.title: Very Smart and Simple Build
reviews.comment: I can't wait to build this one.  It's so simple and wastes no metal anywhere.  I've built PCs dating back to the early 90s when they would use enough steel that you could melt it down and probably build a truck!  This case is so simple and to the point.  I like building gaming PCs once in a while but I also like to build a fast but still efficient machine too.  This is going to be just that.  I've been seeing reviews giving it less stars because it's not as tough as a safe.  It's not supposed to be.  I've gone through countless PCs in my life and I've never once relied on the strength of the steel case to hold my car up while I changed a tire or anything like that.  I came close once but that's a story for another time.  If you need a simple case that will hold your PC together, this is going to be it.  I can do cable management but to be honest, not one person has ever come to my house and commented on what the inside of my computer looks like.  I've waited but gave up.  The only review I read that helped mentioned that if your motherboard's SATA ports point outward instead of straight up, you'll need to get some 90-degree connected SATA cables.  Very smart.  Thanks to whoever wrote that.
reviews.author: Escobar Fam

reviews.title: Nice but not for itx at all
reviews.comment: This is a micro atx case, itx will not fit,despite their information, nice case but very bacis,no screws,no paperwork, but still nice if you can fit into it...
reviews.author: blkfngrs

reviews.title: Good case for the money
reviews.comment: This is a decent case for the price.  You need to be aware that you are not getting a high end case with solid structure and options for wire management and storage.  This is a perfect case if you are looking for a smaller case.  This is my 10th computer build.  I used a micro ATX board and like others shared, it barely fits.  While I made it work, this would be better with a mini ATX.  You can only get one 120mm fan on the front since the motherboard power plug interferes with the second spot (mATX board).  The case is thin, but it works.  There are no case fans, but those are cheap and easy to install.  It was better to put everything in and then fit the fans around it.  I installed one 120mm fan on front and one 80mm on the back.  The three design issues with this are 1) The power supply mounts on the top and there is no vent for the PSU fan.  For that reason, I had to mount with the fan pointing into the case (not ideal).  2) The opposite side cover is not removable which makes it more challenging to mount the CPU cooling unit  3) The mounting points for the motherboard do not extend to the mATX.  Therefore the edge closest to the front does not have mounting points.  This is not a huge issue but made it harder to securely plug in the motherboard power connector.  Overall, very happy with the size and design.  For the price, this is a good value.
reviews.author: Grall Gang

reviews.title: Great little compact case.
reviews.comment: Great basic little compact case that keeps the atx power supply.  Has just enough clearance to accommodate this 6pipe cooler for my Xeon.  Space is constrained, so plan your build accordingly.

reviews.title: Great compact MSI case
reviews.comment: The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/D1RIUSImvlL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/61yaXv2OOwL._SY256.jpg Excellent case, more compact than I thought but still plenty of space, it also has the premium feel from other ones more expensive and for the price you can’t ask for more.

reviews.comment: Luvvvvv it excellent product for the money

reviews.title: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Compact Powerhouse - The Revolt 3 Delivers!
reviews.comment: This case is a fantastic choice for anyone looking for a small footprint build without sacrificing performance.  The Revolt 3's clever design eliminates the need for a PCIe riser, which is a huge plus.  It also comes with a surprisingly decent PSU, saving you money and hassle.  While the compact size does present some challenges, the result is well worth it. My only real gripe was the limited space for top fans.  While it's designed for one, I managed to squeeze in two slim fans with some creative maneuvering.  It was a bit tricky, so be prepared to get your hands dirty!  Similarly, component selection requires careful planning.  I ended up going with the ASUS ROG Strix B760-I motherboard (despite my personal dislike of Asus!) which proved to be a perfect fit.  Cooling was another consideration, but I successfully installed the be quiet! Dark Rock TF 2, albeit with a slight modification.  I swapped the stock fan for two be quiet! Silent Wings Pro 4 140mm fans, one of which I cleverly mounted as a top-mounted CPU fan.  This setup keeps my system running cool and quiet.  I also had to make a small modification to my GPU cooling by adding some foam to ensure proper separation between intake and exhaust airflow, preventing them from mixing and impacting cooling efficiency. Overall, the Revolt 3 is an excellent case.  The small form factor, included PSU, and clever design make it a winner. Just be prepared to put in a little extra effort during the build process, especially when it comes to cooling, fan placement, and potentially some minor GPU adjustments.  The end result is a powerful and compact machine that's sure to impress.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Absolutely GREAT case, with GREAT value
reviews.comment: Good: -No riser cable needed -Comes with a 700W gold rated power supply with three PCIE 8-pin power connectors -Very sturdy handle, headphone holders on the sides -Side panels come off very easily, -Plenty of space for installing a decent air cooler (if you don't install a side fan) -Support for two 2.5 in drives AND one 3.5 inch drive -3 slot expansion card bracket with room to fit coolers that extend beyond that. HOWEVER, be mindful of your graphics cards height. For demonstration, I included a picture of my graphics card that's in my main PC. Physically, it can fit, but would not be able to close the side panel because the power connectors going to the graphics card interfere. Bad: -The power button is part of an integrated circuit board that also has a drive activity LED built in. The LED light shows through the power button. I didn't know this, nor is it stated anywhere. So I thought the power button was defective. -CPU power connector may not reach the port on your motherboard depending on the motherboard and what CPU cooler you have installed (I did not have this problem, but other have that I've read). -Not really a bad thing for me, but the I/O is all on the bottom of the case. I've had to get a few right angle adapters to take some strain off of cables. -The front USB-C port does NOT plug into the motherboard, but is an EXTENSION cable. Meaning you have to plug this into the motherboards I/O. I had to buy an adapter to use the motherboard port rather than the one on the I/O. -VERY hard to install the motherboard if you are using SATA storage devices, if you have a motherboard with SATA ports that are angled. I have the Asrock Phantom Gaming B550 ITX/AX. The ports must be plugged in PRIOR to installing the motherboard, otherwise you can fit them in the connector for lack of space from the Power supply container. MAJOR oversight from Hyte. Overall, VERY good Mini-ITX case with broad GPU compatibility, and and surprisingly good CPU air cooler compatibility. HIGHLY recommend!
reviews.author: James Nakashian

reviews.title: 9.10 case!
reviews.comment: Great case. Hyte paid attention to the top side and it's greatly appreciated! Very easy to build. Need to pay attention if you want to upgrade to newer cards. 4070 from ASUS doesn't fit!
reviews.author: C L C

reviews.title: Does almost everything right but brings nothing new to the table.
reviews.comment: This case is very good but its brought down by one thing, competition. Its a competitor to the smaller and more affordable SSUPD which does everything this case does but better in terms of radiator support, size and pricing, with build quality being very similar. If you want a small form factor case the SSUPD and the NR200 outperform this case while being priced better. This case is still great, with great cooling and airflow, gpu support and good overall quality of the materials and I will give it a solid recomendation as a good competitor in the SFF market, that said, only get this case if you like its style, if this case looks the best to you buy it, you wont regret it, but be aware there are better more functional options for less in this market. Quality 4/5 Stars Solid case, the top panel is easily bent and its pretty bad quality, everything else is exelent using a ghost s1 as a standard. The carriying handle feels like it could break under load but only time will tell. Cooling 3/5 It can fit a 280 radiator and it has good airflow,but cant do much outside of that. The 80mm fan has made no difference in thermal testing. Its competitors can fit more fans and radiators. Ease of use 5/5 Easiest itx case to work with compared to the ghost S1, Ncase, SSUPD, Silverstone RVZ03 and NR200, its very beginer friendly and well designed, good overall cable management as well and great space for 2.5inch ssds in the back and a full size hard drive, though more on that later. Things to improve upon and thoughts: The hard drive cage chokes one of the radiator fans if placed from the inside, having the option to remove it would help with cable management, airflow and even give you space to fit a pushpull configuration on a radiator using a mix of slim and regular sized fans, it would also give you more space to potentially mount a pump for a custom loop, overall I think the forced hard drive cage hurts the case more than it helps. The case is more expensive than its competitors and it does nothing to stand out from them, its fairly priced but theres no reason to pick it up over the SSUPD(unless you like this one more). Overall a solid case that offers healthy competition in the SFFPC market. Edit: Ive used the handle atleast once a week to transport the computer since November 2021. Despite being carried moderate distances with only one hand its held up, I will edit this post if the handle fails in the future. Edit:2026 still holding
reviews.author: Felix

reviews.title: Excellent ITX case.  The power supply is also excellent.
reviews.comment: First of all the power supply that comes with this case is made by High Power a top manufacturer of power supplies in China, right up there with Super Flower in terms of company size and quality of their product.  This is NOT some "tier C" PSU regardless what any other  reviewers might claim.  That is bull.  Look at their other power supplies, High Power is top shelf. It's based on some unvetted list floating around the internet,  that was a complete guess and conjecture.  It even says on that list  '( speculative position )', meaning someone made a wild guess without facts or even testing it.  The power supply that comes with this case is warranted for 10 YEARS.  I challenge anyone to find a  SFX-L PSU as good as this one  for even $80 standalone, yet you are getting it essentially for free when the combo deal comes along. The fan on it is completely silent. After you build the first one of these the second one is much easier. I have bought two of these when the combo deal comes along.  It's an unbeatable deal no other maker can touch at this price.  The voltages are rock solid.  Extremely stable with Ryzen 5 5700X CPU and AMD RX 6750 TX GPU with power to spare. I am running a Radeon RX 6750 TX video card and it's rock solid.  My only nit is the 8 pin CPU cable needs to be about two inches longer because crosses over the top of the motherboard which is a ASROCK B550-ITX/ac. It fits but is not perfect cable managment, another two inches and it could have been tucked along the side of the board.
reviews.author: William N

reviews.title: 4000D killer, but QC needs to be improved.
reviews.comment: It’s a great package for the price and I would highly recommend it. I got the black 903 MAX version for 70$ on sale, and at that price it simply cannot be beat. The construction of the case feels solid and does not feel cheap, perhaps a slight notch below the 4000D’s overall sturdiness, but still very good. You get nice front I/O including an RGB button, reset SW, premium power button with metal, and USB type C (which I think is the biggest selling point. The cable management in the case is overall very good. I have worked with the 4000D and it is just as good as that. You have included velcro cable ties and a decent amount of tie off points. The included fan hub in the back is an absolute lifesaver for cable management and all of the fans and what not are already connected to it. The only thing you really need to connect from it is the SATA power 6 pin from your PSU to power all your fans. It’s helpful be cause it completely mitigates the amount of fans you have to awkwardly try to plug into your motherboard, it also just really cleans up the rear cable management and makes it much easier to understand which cables go where. The only real cables you have to manage are: your USB headers (type C and A), your very small front panel pinouts (Reset SW, Power SW, HDD LED, etc.), two other small cables (HD audio and and ARGB header), then just your main power cables (24 Pin PSU, 8 pin CPU, 8 Pin GPU/VGA). I did have two minor gripes with the case, though,  that I want other customers to be aware of and perhaps Montech themselves. I was using a Micro ATX motherboard in this case and when I went to put the motherboard in the case and had started to screw it down, I finally noticed that the bottom 2 stand-offs were never installed. So I had to take back out the motherboard and install the 2 (3 provided) to fix the issue. So beware that you very well may have to install the standoffs before you put in your motherboard. Second gripe is quality control. I know that I have heard multiple people complain online about how they received cases from Montech that were slightly damaged/defective. On JaysTwoCents review of this case, he also received on with a pretty noticeable dent. Similar to Jay, I also received a small contour in the metal toward the back left of the case. If you looked at if from the right angle, you could tell that the contour/angle was not intended. So I am not sure if these cases are being damaged in shipping or if it is just Montech’s factory QC that is leading to these f defects. But overall, I am happy with the case and am not returning it because the damage  was still very minor. I would provide pictures of my build, but I don’t want to give Amazon access to all my photos 🙃
reviews.author: emdiff

reviews.title: Solid budget case with a ton of features
reviews.comment: I've bought some budget $80 cases that were not this nice. The build quality, the cable routing and features are all outstanding. I upgraded my son's case from a coolermaster MB320L that was way too small so it was cutting off airflow to, well everything, his cpu, gpu and hard drives were all putting out a ton of heat because the airflow was just bad. Get this, The MB320L is now MORE expensive than this one. Once I switched, all of the temps dropped. He has more fans, his pc is quieter, gets better fps in his games (seriously, temps dropped that much) and fully addressable RGB fans. Ok enough comparing, this case was extremely easy to work with. The side panels come with captive screws that make it near impossible to lose or drop. The tempered glass is a full panel with an internal ps basement to hide all of those cables. The full mesh panels on the front have an air filter (It IS a filter despite what reviewer BigChonk says) that's easy to clean and the top vent has a removeable filter that is magnetic. There is tons of space to fit up to a 360 radiator on the front or top, or both for water cooling. The rubber grommets for cables are a nice addition and the moulded cable management chanels are extremely roomy. The only issue I had with this case is I can't use the usbc port because the motherboard he has doesnt have the right port to connect it to so keep that in mind if you have an older board. I definatly would have bought this case three years ago for my own build if it had been out. I mean honestly it's the little touches like the screws and the fan hub and the magnetic filters and led button (OH HOLD FOR 3 SECONDS to put it in software controled mode) that make this case the frontrunner for the best budget case of 2023.
reviews.author: Chris Deluna

reviews.title: Montech AIR 903 MAX
reviews.comment: What is Great: This Montech AIR 903 MAX case is built well and looks good. It offers excellent value and is favorably priced. Overall, I do like it and recommend it. Air flow is good. The 140mm fans (four included) are pushing more air than I imagined they would and run very quiet. The PWM fan/RGB hub is a nice feature that works well. I like the included lighting control button. It sucks to have to install trashy OEM bloatware for lighting control and with this case you do not find yourself needing to do so. Leaving the ARGB unplugged from the motherboard headers allows you to use the button on the case. This case is a great option for those using a basic AIO for the CPU or air cooling. What Can Be Improved: The rear I/O panel 140mm fan is not RGB like the rest. That is silly and unfortunate. The space above the motherboard and behind the motherboard tray needs to be greater. Making the case 1.5 to 2.0 inches taller and about an 1.0 inch or so wider would remarkably improve the usefulness to a broader audience. Above the motherboard it only has enough room for thin radiators and push fans. No way you can install fat radiators and push/pull. That sucks, but I understand "normal" is their target market and gamerboy AIOs is what 99% of their customers are going to be installing. So, since I am using a gamerboy AIO for this application it's OK. It would NOT be OK with a custom loop. There is not enough space for a custom loop to be accommodated comfortably. Behind the motherboard tray it would be nice to have an extra 25-30mm of space. I got the cable management done in a way that is aesthetically acceptable without a bulge in the side panel, but man it sure was tight. My PSU is an RM1200x SHIFT and there is barely enough space for the modular cables.
reviews.author: Mr. Fox

reviews.title: Very premium case for the price, easy for a newcomer to build with
reviews.comment: This is my first ever gaming PC build and I'm impressed by the quality of this case for the price. As a beginner, I was able to assemble a gaming PC on my own without any help. Just online research and patience. The tower is bigger than I thought it would be, but I'm getting used to its size. I really love the dust filters on the top and bottom, really helps with dust management. I also love how all the fans come preinstalled and already plugged into a fan controller. Which made building as a newcomer so much easier. The fans on the front can be heard when the room is quiet, but if you have a box fan in your room like I do, it overrides the noise from the PC. The fans aren't loud, but don't expect complete silence. The air flow in this case is amazing. Combined with the air cooler for the CPU, I'm getting 24 C idle temps. The airflow is so strong that you can see pieces of dust being sucked up against the front panel, which I wipe off with my hand every now and then. It filters out the thicker pieces of dust from getting sucked into the system. The only complaint I have is I couldn't figure out how to mount the hard drive, even while looking at the manual. I can't fit the bent shaped SATA cable into the hard drive so I had to use the other end of the cable. My other complaint is that some of the front panel cables that need to be inserted to the motherboard are lost in the bundled up wires but I eventually worked them out and got them through the grommet. My last complaint is that the manual doesn't explain at all that the fan controller is included or what it is. As a newcomer builder, I had no idea what it was or what was connected to it. I only learned what it was through videos of people building their PC. But once I learned that it's a fan controller, I appreciated it being there and already setup.
reviews.author: Matthew

reviews.title: Looks great, works greater
reviews.comment: I really love this case. It is large enough to store all the basic components you'd need for a computer including my rather large graphics card and extra HDD. It comes with all the screws needed along with mini zip ties to help with wire management and even had spots to attach those zip ties to so the wires wont go anywhere. The case looks very nice and sleek. The included rgb fans look great and work well. I've never had any issues with overheating and i have it up against a wall in the back. The integrated rgb controller let me attach my cpu  air cooler with rgb function so all fan lights are in sync with each other and can be switched with just one button on the top of the case. The quick off removeable mesh screen on the top and dust screen on the front come off fast and easy to make cleaning it simple. Overal this has been a great case an id recommend it.
reviews.author: Pat

reviews.title: Fortnite Creator Samzirra Approves!!! TOP NOTCH
reviews.comment:
ASUS TUF Gaming GT502 Case – Real Fortnite Creator, Samzirra, APPROVED
I’ve had a lot of PC cases over the years, but this one blows them all away. It’s not just big and functional—it actually feels classy. Here’s why I’m seriously impressed:
