⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (Easily 5 stars. If I could give it more, I would.)
reviews.author: Samzirra

reviews.title: Built like a tank
reviews.comment: This thing is built like a tank. It offers an excellent view, tons of space for working inside the case, great airflow, good cable management and allows up to 10 case fans to be installed. This does not include the GPU or AIO, in which case it would bring the total up to 16. It's an excellent case all in all. I had zero issues building in this case. For my next build, I will purchase the white GT502 Horizon.
reviews.author: Sherwin D.

reviews.title: Great case. Highly recommend.
reviews.comment: Had this case for I think 2 years now. No issues at all. Looks great, fit everything I needed and then some.
reviews.author: Ruben m.

reviews.title: Best case in it's class
reviews.comment:
I really like this design. Although similar to a Lian Li 011 (and others) in layout, this is a far superior product. Every aspect was thought of and well planned. From the release of the side panels, the top cover's magnetic retention, to the way the radiator rack on the top pivots out, EVERYTHING was designed and made by someone who, like me, build PC's on a regular basis. I've Been building PC's since 1990 and have seen a lot of good and bad over the decades. This is by far the best case I have ever used.  I had to track a wire with a bad connection and within seconds I was able to remove a few panels and move a radiator to find the offending connection. All that without cutting up my hands or popping a zip-tie. The GPU vertical mount kit works better than any other I've used and the included anti-sag was a really nice, effective bonus.
I initially thought the straps on top were cheap gimmick until I started using them. Today, most high-end components are full of heatsinks, heat pipes, radiators and chunks of metal just to look cool. A  motherboard and radiator can be 20 pounds, before you add in the heft of a video card. Instead of putting that weight into the meat of your hands while grabbing onto metal and glass corners, lifting by the straps is so much easier and less likely to do damage (to you or the case). This has changed how I do a lot of things, and all for the better. My hat's off to Asus on this one I don't know how they will top it, but for now this will be the only tower I recommend.
reviews.author: Paul K

reviews.title: Solid case.
reviews.comment: Great case with amazing airflow. The only downside is the glass face is a bit on the thinner edge but that’s my own preference.
reviews.author: J Dinwiddie

reviews.title: Great Value & Quality
reviews.comment: Excellent airflow and the cable management space is a lifesaver. The 3 included ARGB fans look premium and the Type-C port is a nice modern touch for a build at this price.
reviews.author: Pretty good over all good quality chain is good length for 5,11 height packaging is nice good product nothing wrong with it

reviews.title: Great budget case for under $60. Would definitely recommend
reviews.comment: I just got this case and it looks great! The fan hub that comes pre installed makes the building process faster and easier. The fans that come with it are pretty quiet and look good. Cable management is easy. It doesn’t take up too much room on my desk, and it doesn’t seem flimsy or cheap (for the price). Airflow doesn’t seem to be a problem so overall just a nice case. The best I could find for the price. The only complaint I have so far is that the side panel isn’t the easiest to take off. I have to use a little bit more force than I’d like to but it still functions.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Yet another amazing case from Okinos!
reviews.comment: Why did you pick this product vs others?: I’ve had experience with another Okinos case in the past, and you can’t beat the quality at this price point. It also has room for an AIO on the top. This case checks all the boxes for my application and at an amazing price. Airflow: I used some Thermalright TL-C12RB-S V2 fans in place of all the Okinos fans because I wanted them to be PWM fans. I believe they may cool a bit better than the ones that come with the case as well. I also made all 3 fans reverse blade so it’s also pulling from the back of case as well. I wanted a bit of positive pressure in the case to keep fresh air in, but I was also worried the bottom fans would have quite a bit of resistance pulling through the small air gap. I may change this later, but it seems to keep pretty good air flow and temps as it is right now. It seems as though it gets great airflow with the current set up now even with its small size and fish tank style. Cable management: There is a ton of space in the back of the case for cable management, so (in my opinion) it was a breeze getting everything organized. Lots of room with a regular full modular 850w ATX power supply and I even have an HDD installed back there. Noise level: Noise level is very low but I don’t have an air cooled CPU. I’m using an AIO, so it helps with keeping temps cooler and fan speeds lower. Side note: The case is no where near as loud in person as it sounds in the video. I think my phone just tries to enhance low level sounds automatically. lol Functionality: There is a ton of functionality in this case. I even had room to mount a huge sensor panel where the ssd spot is. I love that it has plenty of front panel ports as well as a USB-C port. I do wish it had the ports on the bottom toward the side of the case like the Aqua 9 has but it’s understandable when the case is this small. Summary: Overall, I highly recommend this case for those looking to make a high end small form factor Micro ATX build. It worked great for me and I’m very satisfied with this case at the price point.
reviews.author: NachoSlacker

reviews.title: Awesome case. Great price
reviews.comment: Awesome case. Great for a matx motherboard. I added a 240mm radiator on top and it fit without a hitch. The only thing that stumped me was the argb control panel on the back. I wasnt sure what I needed but i eventually got every thing set straight. The metal is high quality and so is the glass. The fans that come with it are quiet and haven't had a problem with them. It has one usb c connector and 2 usb a connector. I also love the magnetic filters on the top and bottom of the case. Its easy to clean. So far I haven't found a single bad thing on this case. Also it brings enough screws in the case to add all your components.
reviews.author: Itsmoy

reviews.title: Dual Chamber, Compact, Impressive Designed Case.
reviews.comment: The Mirage 4 is one of my new favorite cases. When I got it in person the size surprised me. The weight and packaging surprised me it was very well packed and came with nice foam for protection during shipping. The GPU support is surprisingly large and the fish-tank design is great. The Dual Chamber design makes this system easy to use and manage cables and have a full size power supply as well with no compromises. The quality of the case and lightweight design of the case surprised me.
reviews.author: heath_va

reviews.title: A great budget case with solid quality of life that knows what to prioritize
reviews.comment: This case is not the greatest case in the world. The magnetic filter on the top slides around too much. The side panels don't have the greatest fit tolerances I've ever seen on a case. The hard-drive bay in the bottom is virtually useless, because you can't run any significant number of power cables past them from the PSU to the rest of the computer. The cables running to the daughter board are delicate to the point where I was concerned about accidentally damaging them. There are a lot of individual screws, many of which I really wish were captive so you didn't have to worry about loosing/misplacing them. The metal outside panels are flimsy and a bit thin. There are no good dust-filters built into the system. But despite all these shortcomings, I'm very happy with this case. The fans are great, relatively quiet and with fancy lights that plug onto the RGB header on your motherboard. You've got a great selection of front IO ports, though most budget oriented motherboards out there that I've seen don't have a USB C header, making the inclusion of a USB C port for front IO a bit of a waste. I would have rather seen a 3rd non-USB C port, but the 2 that are there are certainly welcome. The air flow is great, keeping my GPU and CPU cool with only an additional CPU cooler needing to be installed (Ryzen 5700x and Radeon 6700xt). The case was shipped with good packing materials, making me optimistic that the glass panel would not be damaged in transit. The instructions aren't the best I've ever seen, but I was able to follow them without any great degree of trouble. You've got good Sata SSD mounts hidden between the motherboard panel and the outside non-glass panel. Cable management options are (hard-drive bay aside) excellent, with lots of intelligently placed gaps and clear routing lanes. It's well optimized, so the case doesn't have any huge dead zones of empty space, and as a result is more compact than you might expect from a desktop case. It supports a variety of configurations, and in a PC where you  don't have a GPU that requires dedicated PCIE power cables, you might have the space for the hard drive bay in the bottom. For a budget case, you get a clear priority of functionality > aesthetics > build quality here, while not sacrificing too much to the point where it becomes a liability. If you're trying to save a bit of money on your case, I can certainly recommend this one.
reviews.author: Doodledibob

reviews.title: Excellent value, versatile, and well-designed
reviews.comment: The Lian Li Higher Flow ATX case is an excellent budget-friendly option for gaming, workstations, or everyday PCs. It offers fantastic airflow with plenty of fan space, clean and simple cable management, and a sturdy, well-designed build. For the price, it’s hard to beat, easy to build in, looks great, and delivers everything you need for a reliable, versatile PC case.
reviews.author: Kevin Glover

reviews.title: Very good airflow leads to very good temps
reviews.comment: Whenever the parts shortage was going on, I had purchased a PC through a PC Builder (Cyberpower, don't recommend). The case I chose was a really terrible case, the cheapest they had because I had every intention of replacing it. As expected, it had basically no air flow, and caused my PC to overheat to the point of shutdown, no bluescreens. This case arrived and I could already tell it was a very nice quality. And for the price, I was pleasantly surprised. The front fans that come with the case are huge, and the back one seems like a great quality one even if it is the normal size. The front mesh panel lets plenty of air through, and I've been more than happy with its performance. Since switching to this case, my temps have remained lower, and I have yet to see the computer crash or otherwise throttle due to temperature, with the only change being the case itself. I'm more than happy with this purchase, and even put my brother-in-law's computer in the same one. Until I decide that Lian Li has made an even better case that I need, I think I'll continue to purchase and recommend this specific case to anyone who needs one.
reviews.author: John Swanger

reviews.title: Nice, good case for the money
reviews.comment: I used this case for a recent gaming build for a friend. It looks really great with the glass side panel and installation was without issues. I will say that my older Lian Li cases are much nicer being that they used to make them from 100% Au. Now they have stamped steel in there but it's a sign of the times I suppose. Still, I would buy this again.
reviews.author: David Erickson

reviews.title: A good one
reviews.comment: My last case was awful for air flow and this fixed all of those issues. Good build quality, easy to install parts with a straight-forward layout. The front ports work, which is nice for a change. Aesthetically I like the look and the included fan leds aren't visually obnoxious or loud,  can always turn off the leds or adjust the speeds. Magnetized screens are easily removed for cleaning, though the top mounted fans were making a bit of noise/vibration so I had to wrap the screen "pegs" with rubber string to dampen it. Didn't have trouble fitting any components, feels like enough internal room but isn't an enormous case either. Doors can be a little finicky to line up but I've definitely encountered worse on different cases. Depending on price or deals available this is a case I'd recommend and may reuse for future builds.
reviews.author: M

reviews.title: Incredible Airflow and Build Quality A Dream Case for PC Enthusiasts!
reviews.comment: I’ve built several PCs over the years, and the HAVN BF 360 Flow has quickly become one of my favorite cases to work with. It perfectly combines high-end design, cooling performance, and build-friendly features. Airflow & Cooling: The airflow on this case is phenomenal. The two massive 180mm fans at the front move a ton of air quietly, and the included 140mm rear fan complements them perfectly. My temps dropped significantly compared to my old mid-tower case, even under heavy loads. The 360mm radiator support is a huge plus for custom or AIO liquid cooling setups. Design & Build Quality: The semi-open design gives it a unique, industrial look that really stands out. The SGCC steel frame feels incredibly sturdy and premium no cheap, flimsy panels here. The magnetic panels are a brilliant touch, making it easy to access components without fiddling with screws every time. Cable Management: The SimpliCable system makes routing cables a breeze. It’s clean, intuitive, and saves a ton of time. Even with a fully loaded setup (GPU, multiple drives, RGB fans), I managed to get a super tidy build without much effort. Ease of Build: Everything about this case feels builder-friendly. There’s plenty of space for large GPUs, solid clearance for radiators, and smart layout choices for airflow optimization. Aesthetics: The black finish looks sleek and professional. The semi-open design gives it a modern, showcase-style appearance that highlights internal components beautifully, especially with RGB lighting. Overall, this case is a fantastic choice for gamers, enthusiasts, or anyone who values performance and smart design. HAVN really delivered something special here high airflow, premium materials, and an awesome building experience. Highly recommend it if you want a case that looks great, stays cool, and makes building fun again!
reviews.author: Joshua Senibaldi

reviews.title: Fantastic case if it fits your needs.
reviews.comment: A premium case with a premium price tag. This is a very well engineered product, solidly constructed with high quality materials. It's very easy to build in, with ample room for components and cable runs, and plenty of thoughtful touches. If you have a build that'd benefit from the airflow, and has room in the budget, this deserves a place on your short list. Couple caveats: -Only worth considering if you want/need high airflow. It's a big case that doesn't fit a ton of drives/etc. It's nothing against this product as it's typical for the category. -As many Youtubers/etc pointed out, at least at time of writing, the fans-included version does not come with the adapter plate needed to use something other than 180mm fans in the front.
reviews.author: Chris M.

reviews.title: Works great for standard ATX cases or bigger.
reviews.comment: I'll start this review by saying that this mount is well made. The metal feels durable and the design doesn't feel flimsy at all. Overall it is very robust and the articulation in the mount feels smooth and sturdy. Again nothing flimsy here at all. The mount itself is fairly easy to install. The kit comes with a couple of different GPU sag bracket options to choose from. Both connect to your motherboard but in different configurations. You'll have to decide which works for you. Overall the mount is great and does its job well. Now to the one downside which is a very specific thing. If you are using a Lian Li O11 Dynamic mini case then this mount will fit by just barely. You'll only have the option to sit your gpu at the highest configuration and you will not be able to use the 45 degree tilt feature unless you want to remove your bottom fans. The tight space doesnt allow the mount to articulate forward or backward nor up and down. So yes this vertical mount does work well for the O11D mini but only for the one configuration type so buyer beware. I considered returning it when I realized this but figured the mount still works better than my previous riser cable and I'm not losing anything but I'm just not gaining anything either except the RBG strip which is nice. The color is vibrant and it connects to argb so it talks to SignalRGB instead of L Connect 3 which I'm not a fan of for RGB. All in all its a great mount and if your case is a standard ATX or bigger then you shouldn't have many issues.

reviews.title: Absolutely great purchase
reviews.comment: Absolutely beautiful mount, love the rgb strip it’s nice and bright. The riser cable is pretty flexible and I was able to cram it in despite the tight space in between the mount and my motherboard. It feels nice and sturdy, the included anti sag bracket makes it even more rigid. Hardware and bolts are all included. Fits very well in my case.

reviews.title: Awesome mount!

The instructions are clear enough came with extra parts and multiple sections the manual in case you have a setup other than ATX. Looks great even in my yet to be upgraded case! LED’s are BRIGHT lol

reviews.title: Great vertical mount, as long as it fits
reviews.comment: Works great, I can now display my 7900 XT properly. Did have to modify my case though, but that's not the fault of this mount. So a warning, if you have a Corsair 4000D airflow, or any other case with thin horizontal "supports" between the rear slot covers, you may have to cut said supports to access the rear of your gpu and plug in your cables. But that's on me, not this mount. Another warning, if you have a mid-tower case and a large cpu air cooler, you likely won't be able to use the two angled display options, and if your gpu is big enough, it might not work at all. For me it fits, but just barely, and I definitely can't use the two angled positions, which sucks. But aside from that, it looks great, the RGB lighting is tasteful and is a nice replacement for the RGB support stand I had before. The build quality is very good, and I also like the included hook to support the end of the mount so it doesnt sag. It doesn't impact cooling performance at all, my gpu still runs just the same temps as before.
reviews.author: Jacob Fossum

reviews.title: Solid construction, the best mount on the market
reviews.comment: I have tried a bunch of the vertical GPU mounts and this has been the sturdiest and best fitting in my PC. It looks absolutely gorgeous, but I ended up returning it because Lian-li case that I ordered already had a vertical mount that came with the case, and I didn’t realize it until after I installed this. Super pleased with the fit and finish and it’s much better than the other others.
reviews.author: Rainyday

reviews.title: Come on Steve...
reviews.comment: This case got a bad rap from Gamer's Nexus and some other popular YouTube personalities (which almost caused me not to buy it). I just really liked how it looks so I took a chance on it. These YouTube channels really need to stop judging every case like it's for the enthusiast crowd. This case was not designed to compete with a gaming chassis. However, the front fabric absolutely DOES breathe!  I'm not saying it breathes as well as mesh would, but it's not nearly as bad as these YouTube personalities are claiming. For my Steam console gaming HTPC build, I used a thin Noctua NF-A12x15 fan in the front bottom of the fan bracket, and a Noctua NF-F12 in the top. I did some testing and got the best cooling results when I had the bottom front fan (above the CPU) blow in, and the top front fan blow out (as exhaust). If you have the top front fan blow in, it can impede the hot air exhaust from the CPU chamber. This hot air needs to get pulled out of the case by the big fan at the very top. By having the front top fan push air in, it creates air pressure like a wall of air which can keep this hot air from escaping effectively. The CPU cooler I'm using is a Thermalright SI-100 down-blower style air cooler. In the above configuration, my CPU temps are well within an acceptable range. My GPU temps are great as the GPU chamber is well designed and allows for good airflow (just remember no three slot cards!). In conclusion, you absolutely can build a living-room PC in this case that can play AAA games better than any console (I did exactly that!). It looks great and has become something of a conversation piece. Building in this case is pretty straight forward if you know what you're doing. You may run into some issues getting everything to fit just right but that's part of the fun. Just make smart decisions with this case in mind when picking out all your hardware and have plenty of wire ties available.
reviews.author: JJ

reviews.title: Looks great
reviews.comment: A great case for a simple and visually pleasing home server or pc. You do have to be careful not to get the mesh fabric dirty though. Over all it was easy enough to build in and looks great.
reviews.author: josh

reviews.title: A Lovely-looking Case with some Quirks and Heat.
reviews.comment:
The case's interior design provides flexible options - an option to install 2.5 SSD or 3.5 HDD, install SFX or SFX-L PSU, more flexibility of low profile CPU heatsink choice (or AIO, but you might give up option to install 3.5 HDD if that's an issue), and have (almost) any GPU install with ease. And the exterior shell makes it so the PC doesn't stick out like a sore thumb if you don't want your setup to look like the average gaming case. It's overall genral size, once together, feels like a bigger Xbox Series X - I recommend looking at the dimensions if you are tight on desk space to mke sure it will be good for you.
Currently, my setup as of August 2025 is:
Ryzen 7 9800X3D
Thermalright Silversoul 110 Black
Corsair 64GB DDR5 6000MHz CL30
ASUS RTX 4070
Seagate 4TB HDD
(2x) 1TB NVME SSD PCI Gen4.
Corsair SFX-L 850W
Temperatures for the case are as follows:
CPU:
---51-55C idle and web browsing/videos.
---80-91C gaming
GPU:
---32-40C idle and web browsing/videos.
---60-78C gaming.
NVME:
---55-65C idle and general tasks
---68-75C gaming and/or data transfer
As you can see, both your CPU and NVME will sit at higher tempatures. The fabric of the case, while it gives minimalistic aesethetic, does not allow the case to breathe very well. It *does breathe*, but it is restrictive. You will find that undervolting your CPU is a must in order to get idle temperatures if you do not want it constantly at 90C+. And the NVME is just stuck between both your CPU and GPU, which is normal for ITX builds, but gets further hotboxed with the restrictive airflow of the case - a NVME heatsink may be something you'll want to look into. However, the GPU temperature are amazing - it has its own mesh panel to enable better airflow, and the top case fan being set to exhaust air out takes all the out air out from the GPU side with no problem.
Now, if you are someone like me who still uses a 3.5 HDD, I must warn you now - if you are going to perform maintenance on your PC and have to remove the HDD cage, PLEASE REMOVE YOUR CONNECTORS FIRST. You will break your HDD's SATA connectors if you do not catch yourself on this - ask me, the person building their own PC for 18+ years and knows better, how I know :'(
Overall, IMO this is a nice case. The case's exterior design is what sold it for me, including the ability to still have a HDD and free up more desk space by having a tower design instead. CPU Temps, however, left me feeling it could be way better w/o need of undervolting. If you know the CPU you have will not get as hot or power hungry, you will be fine otherwise.
reviews.author: Ezekiel

reviews.title: Beautiful SFF Case — Tight Build, Amazing Final Result
reviews.comment: This is my case, and I absolutely love it. Building in it takes patience because the space is tight, but once everything is in, the end result is amazing. The finish feels solid and premium, and the fabric design makes it blend perfectly with my desk setup. It honestly looks more like a piece of furniture than a PC case. If you’re willing to take your time, the payoff is well worth it.
reviews.author: JahNile

reviews.title: One Of My Top Picks
reviews.comment:
The Fractal Mood is getting a bad rep around here in the comments and certain outlets. This is a casual mITX beast, if that makes sense. No over clocking.....no stress testing.....or heavy workloads. Just productivity and casual AAA Ultra settings while gaming....that's it. A Super Console of sorts.
Temps aren't a problem when the Top fan is set to Turbo/High to grab all that heat before it ramps up. Set it to that and keep it at that......no mods...that defeats the purpose of the Mood case.
If Fractal does a Mood 2... I'll be there.
Black color is an off-black color. Not deep black....but that is for the better. A premium 'smart speaker' colorif you will.
Case is easy to build in as usual with Fractal case. Their UX on these products is top notch.
reviews.author: T. Anthony

reviews.title: Plenty of room
reviews.comment: A great case!  The 6 fans do a great job cooling.  There is more room than I have ever had inside a case, making it extremely easy for cable management.  Very sturdy and well made.  Easily the best case I've had and for a great price.  Everything assembled and fans ready to hook up to power.  Glass panels make it look awesome.
reviews.author: Elizabeth Stewart

reviews.title: A Stunning and Functional Gaming PC Case!
reviews.comment:
I recently had the pleasure of building my new gaming rig using the LINEDEPOT ATX PC Case, and I must say, it has exceeded my expectations in every way. This case not only boasts a sleek and modern design but also offers excellent functionality, making it a fantastic choice for any gamer or PC enthusiast.
One of the standout features of this case is its full-view dual tempered glass panels. They provide a crystal-clear view of my components, allowing me to showcase my RGB lighting beautifully. The black finish of the case adds an elegant touch, making it suitable for any setup, whether in a gaming den or an office environment.
The case comes pre-installed with six PWM ARGB fans, which is an incredible value. These fans not only provide ample airflow, keeping my components cool during intense gaming sessions, but they also add a vibrant splash of color to my build. The ARGB lighting is easily customizable, and I love being able to sync the fans with my other RGB components for a cohesive look.
Installation was a breeze, thanks to the well-thought-out design of the case. There is plenty of space for cable management, which helped me keep my build neat and tidy. The tool-less drive bays made it easy to install my SSDs and HDDs without any hassle. Additionally, the Type-C port on the front panel is a fantastic feature, allowing for speedy data transfer and making it convenient for connecting modern devices.
Airflow is critical in any gaming setup, and the LINEDEPOT case delivers with its excellent ventilation options. The strategically placed mesh panels ensure that my components receive sufficient airflow, and I’ve noticed a significant decrease in temperatures compared to my previous case.
Another aspect worth mentioning is the overall build quality. The materials used feel sturdy and durable, which gives me confidence in the longevity of the case. It has a solid feel, and I appreciate the attention to detail in the design.
In conclusion, the LINEDEPOT ATX PC Case is a remarkable choice for anyone looking to build a gaming PC that combines aesthetics with functionality. With its stunning full-view tempered glass design, six pre-installed PWM ARGB fans, and thoughtful features like the Type-C port and excellent cable management, it truly stands out in the market. I highly recommend this case to anyone looking to elevate their gaming experience—it's a perfect blend of style and performance that you won’t regret!
reviews.author: Fred

reviews.title: It works but install was a nightmare
reviews.comment:
The case isn't too bad but it was a nightmare to work with. I spent 3 hours transfering wverything from my old case to the new one and installing a new cpu cooler/radiator.
So first issue is i have an ATX form factor motherboard which this case does support however i had to take off all the bottom fans and the back fan to get it in to place (bare mind you) my back place couldnt slide under the back fan cause of the small medel outline, i had to remove bottom ones because all my ports were at the bottom for usb and such, i had to completely remove the middle one because it was right over the usb 3.0/3.2 socket and that cable is too thick to move out the way and the fan cant fit above it.
As for the fans whoever wired mine mist have been an electrician iykyk cables were criss crossed everywhere light a tangle christmas light noghtmare, took me awhile to find a plug that i could put to the motherboard.
The case states that there are 2 HDD mounts which is one of the main reasons i got the case because i have 2hdd and 2ssd, the first mount is a lil metal bracket where its monted dead center of the bottom right behind the power supply(see one of the photos i linked) and that is the only spot that had holes for mounting which it cant go right behind power supply because thats where all the cables go in... the second hdd mount? Non existent the image in the store shows them next to each other? Or somehow stacked? But theres only one mounting bracket so i couldntnt mount them, i literally have them sitting in there towards the front of pc non mounted.
When u mount a radiator on top be sure to put it in last because it will get in the way of the motherboard install and cable install for cpu and such at the top of the board, and the mesh on top sits wird because they didnt rase the edges so that if u put screws in for radiator the mesh could lay flat, so the mesh looks like a bumpy road lol
Idk if im forgetting anything but all in all took me about 3 hrs because i had to keep taking stuff back out and reputting stuff back in and trieing to figure out the electricians maze of cables since i had to take out one of the fans permanently so had to rewire, its a nice case and functions fine but the design is a lil flawed for installation, maybe give an option to have fans in the box but not installed that woulda saved me alotta time lol oh and haveing the bottom part only accessible from the metal side of the case and the rear of the case, when you are installing everything on the glass side and only access to the power supply from the other side, you have to constanly keep flippping the case over to feed cables and stuff and thats kinda risky with a glass case, and also for some reason the glass plate wants to pop off if u slighty bump the pc at all which if i didnt have a bar on the side it woulda fell and shattered, i think that is everything sorry for the rant, it works great just a nightmare to work with if u are using a full sized motherboard.
reviews.author: George

reviews.title: Great Case, looks good and good airflow
reviews.comment: The case is amazing to look at. 2 clear sides of tempered glass, not plastic. The power supply is at the bottom, and there is venting all over, allowing great airflow. The included 6 fans allow it to stay cool and my new build is very happy.
reviews.author: Turner Blanchard

reviews.title: Great case for a beginner’s first pc build
reviews.comment:
Great cable management, all rgb already hooked up. Building my first pc - pic is midway through build. Still running cords etc, but the entire process has been very easy and intuitive because the case came with all hardware etc.
Note: fans aren’t the best, lower end case
Also not a lot of room if you have a 3rd pcie slot.
reviews.author: Mark

reviews.title: Surprisingly nice
reviews.comment: I bought this for a build for my daughters. My main qualification was it needed to be cheap, but look nice. I was very surprised with his this case turned out. This was a great case to build in. There are some good channels for wire management and it fit a 315mm graphics card. I also appreciate the captive screws to open the case up. If you are putting a large card in this I might recommend checking out an SFX power supply. I managed to get mine to fit, but it took some creative placement of the cables since there is like 3/4 inch clearance
reviews.author: Mat Jones

reviews.title: Super cute, minor flaws
reviews.comment: Great small case for a budget pc. Pros: it’s cute my gf loves it. It’s also made very well, I love how strong it feels. Cons: it’s tight, cable management is almost impossible. Also it shows 6 fans ur lucky to get 4 realistically. Also u need a tiny PSU I ordered my go to corsair but even installed at the tallest bracket it would not work. Had to fight Amazon for a return and ended up buying the matching one from the same brand. Over all I give it a 4.5 for Minecraft gaming PCs.
reviews.author: Timothy J Steen

reviews.title: Extremely compact !
reviews.comment: Great case for the size. Fit was better than expected, I was able to install an RTX 3070 with no issues. For a compact case, the airflow is solid, though temps run slightly on the warmer side, which is expected. The build quality feels good and sturdy, and the appearance is clean and modern. It looks great on the desk without taking up much space. In terms of versatility, it handles larger components better than you’d think for a Micro-ATX/Mini-ITX case. Value for money is excellent considering what you can fit into it. Overall, a great compact case that balances size, performance, and looks. Definitely recommend.
reviews.author: Nick C

reviews.title: Great little case!
reviews.comment: I bought this to build a light gaming and steaming rig for my wife. It was tight as expected but not too bad. I think it turned out better than expected and I am very happy with the quality of the case.
reviews.author: jereme morton

reviews.title: Good value case with some problems.
reviews.comment: The quality of the case reflects its price. It's good value, but you get what you pay for. I wish there were included dust filters in the bottom of the case, but again, hard to ask for a ton at this price. The size of the case is decent. Fits mATX boards well. Some of the cables in the front panel were short and didn't reach very well. The included fan was fine. Didn't notice and excessive noise from running it. The case is kinda thin, so it's easy to bend when working on it. When it's put together it's sturdy enough. I did have some issues with the finish of the paint in some spots, but not a huge deal. Overall, if you're making a budget mATX build, this case will function admirably, but if you can spend a little more you'll probably enjoy the quality of life that can come with a better case.
reviews.author: Nicholas S.

reviews.title: A great customizable PC case.
reviews.comment:
The components in this kit were of pretty good quality, I wish the plastic components were made of metal as well but for the price I'm definitely satisfied with the quality of this kit.
If you're purchasing something like this chances are you already have tools for PC assembly but this kit also came with a set of pliers and a nice little screwdriver set, so if you happen to have zero tools at your disposal this kit will give you something to start with.
If you're building PCs for a hobby you can definitely handle the DIY aspect of this kit. If you're in the market for an open air case for your build this is a great budget option. The kit also comes with black plastic pieces if you aren't a fan of the red accents.
reviews.author: Sean J.

reviews.title: Awesome test bench
reviews.comment: Love this test bench case. My server is in a closet where I don't have to worry about it getting hit. The openness make it easy to clean. Could use better drive and gpu mounts but with the extruded aluminum you can make whatever you want.
reviews.author: nwneisen

reviews.title: Good
reviews.comment:
Pros:
1. Material quality is good.
2. Assembly instructions/pictures very good.
3. Comes w/small hand tools.
4. Comes with custom "ruler" for assembly, great idea.
Cons:
1. Need to go online for assembly instructions/pictures.
2. A lot assembly required.
3. Small hand tools, low quality.
4. GPU bracket not so great, but work.
Anyone building PCs has hand tools, remove small hand kit and lower price.
Amazon picture shows "horizontal" GPU mounting, kit does not come with PCI adapter.
reviews.author: Todd

reviews.title: LOVED this frame
reviews.comment:
I can't call it a case really, but this was great.
I recently rebuilt my media center PC with a newer motherboard, CPU, RAM, Nvidia 5060, and a water cooler for the CPU.  And thanks to the wonderful Amazon search feature, and my lack of paying close attention, I ended up purchasing a full sized ATX case despite the search for mini atx...  Needless to say it wouldn't fit my old case.
Since I had everything apart, I wanted something that could arrive overnight.  This was one of the few things that could, and so I tried it.
LOVED the simplicity.  Setup was ridiculously easy.  I still have three 20 TB spinning drives to supplement my Synology in the basement for media, and local is where I keep all the 4k stuff.  I was concerned that the noise level may be higher without the case helping keep some of those small internal noises muffled, but it's dead silent sitting on the floor behind my entertainment center and TV.
The ease of placing things was such a unique experience.  Put it where you want it, not in the bays that it has to go in.
The handle up top was the cherry on top for me.  When I'd need to pull this out for something it was a bit of a pain getting it picked up in the limited space I have behind the TV.  The handle now makes that a gamechanger.
Absolutely worth every penny.
reviews.author: LegoDude

reviews.title: Surprisingly Easy to Assemble and Very Well Made
reviews.comment: I was genuinely surprised by how well this was packaged and how much came with it. Assembly was straightforward—follow the YouTube video instructions; they make everything straightforward. Once put together, it feels solid and sturdy, which honestly isn’t always the case with products like this
reviews.author: Eric M. Milam

reviews.title: Great value, Easy-Build Case
reviews.comment:
A great little case. The layout is very well thought out to make it easy to build in for an ITX case and if you go for a 3-fan cooling arrangement does surprisingly good with thermals while staying quiet. The build quality is better than expected for the price. I also find it looks even better in person than in pictures. I did a spare parts AM4 build in it with an older 6600XT to give to my kid.
Potential negatives depending on your build:
1- It only fits a 250mm graphics card and I'd recommend keeping it to 230 or less for cable management.
2 - It's on the large side for an ITX case. This does help with easy of building and air flow, but something to consider.
reviews.author: Marsi K.

reviews.title: Small and portable, big enough for good equipment.
reviews.comment: Great case, solid build, clean installation.  Built a case to carry to work, and it’s small enough and strong enough to be moved constantly.  Fits everything I would want in it without issue.
reviews.author: Bobby

reviews.title: Great Mobile PC Case for Price
reviews.comment:
I needed something that could be taken with me on plane in the Carry on, and something of this size was great for all of my needs. I put a 3090 3 fan from Dell (deshrouded), and a Noctua NH-D15 G2.
PROS:
- Amazing build quality, everything is easy to take apart for great build space. Full metal and IO is also better than most along with a solid power button
- Easy to manage the internals and build it if you get a smaller GPU and Air Cooler.
- INSANE VALUE at only $60, I found that the case was perfect for me at a price about half of my other options.
- Great looks. Sleek matte black/grey case allows for a more professional looking build
- Best additional screws/washers that I've seen come with a PC case.
CONS:
- Bags aren't properly labeled for screws, so I was guessing which screws go where. I was totally fine with it because of quality of items, but did mean I had to plan my route of building more.
- Like many ITX cases, it requires a lot of planning to build in this case. Especially with almost no cable managing areas for it, it really tried to make me fight to put the GPU in at the end (the Power Supply plugs are attached where the GPU will be, might be better with modded cables).
- Airflow is limited in the case unless you have extra fans. The CPU cooler tower doesn't have a lot of room due to ATX PSU.
Overall, very satisfied with the PC case, will probably not build in it often due to sanity reasons (or just get smaller components). But nonetheless, it's the best bang for buck PC case that is ITX with ATX PSU for the price.
reviews.author: Kimngoc M.

reviews.title: VERY satisfied. 10/10.
reviews.comment:
Durable, rugged, the handle isn't flimsy and the panels don't pop off on their own. It's pretty much 100% metal, so there's no cheap bits. The feet have rubber on them, and all the panels are painted.
I genuinely have nothing bad to say about this other than the fact that it doesn't have a reset button, and the power button sticks out a bit so you might accidentally press it.
10/10 Product.
reviews.author: Christopher Kouzios

reviews.title: Good small case, make sure you plan ahead for the size limitations.
reviews.comment:
Honestly, by planning and making sure everything is as small as you can building in this case wasnt all thaty cramped at all. I was able to fit a 120m AIO coller and I was BARELY able to fit an Arc b580. Defintely the biggest things you will need to think about are GPU size and CPU Cooler size. They show these very clearly on the product page though as far as maximum sized the case will fit. It's definitiely on the "smaller" side of sff cases but by no means is it too small. As is always with SFF builds, there is less room for cable management so you will need to think ahead and see where the cables will run before you assemble everything into the case. I was able to get everything neatly organized with velcro straps and zipties but however much that matters to you personally I cannot speak to. All of the panels can be removed without tools, and they align with very small, consistent gaps.
Smaller dual fan GPUs will make your life a lot easier for all of that. I think you would be able to fit a dual fan 5070 easily for example, but the three fan models will almost certainly not fit.
reviews.author: daniel devine

reviews.title: Great case on a budget itx/sfx
reviews.comment:
Awesome case for itx motherboard and sfx power supply. If you run m-atx it’s going to be an air cooled build as it would cover intake fans. It does not fit rad and fans on top so 240aio has to be side mounted or a 120aio exhaust. You can fit an atx power supply but then not much room for the cables.
That being said itx/sfx build/side mount aio was a breeze, used the ssd tray to store the fan hub.
Highly recommend.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Easy build...clean and cool
reviews.comment: Amazing case.  Nice layout for easy clean look.  Perfect man cave upgrade.  Price was great, shipping was a day early!!
reviews.author: Derick E

reviews.title: Thinnest gauges steel I've ever seen
reviews.comment:
This is the best looking case for ITX with two fans bottom and top!  All the big name brands try to check too many boxes on paper such as 120/140mm fan support, radiator/fan mounting brackets, and they just end up looking a mess.  This case:
1. Doesn't have a huge gap to the right of an ITX motherboard
2. Only has mounting holes for 120mm fans resulting in a clean look
3. Has room for a 240mm radiator on the side, with push and pull fans!
4. No support in the corner blocking your view
5. Tempered glass is nicely tinted for black version
6. Fits full size ATX power supply
7. Doesn't waste space trying to fit a 360mm radiator
This is kinda cheap though, so there are some downsides:
1. You can bend this steel with your hands
2. The ventilation has way too much material-to-hole ratio, blocking airflow.  This goes for both the steel and magnetic screen/filter.
3. The height should have been raised 30mm above the motherboard to allow a radiator to be mounted on the top.  There is only room for fans, and adding a 30mm radiator would cause a collision with your RAM and CPU cooler.
4. The black strips on the glass edge should be as thin as possible to allow you to see the sides of your fans.  Unless you have ugly fans?
I ended up cutting out the steel where fans are placed, and 3D printing fan filters with a 0.2mm nozzle instead.  Much better airflow.
reviews.author: Amazing customer

reviews.title: Bit of a disappointment
reviews.comment:
The case is a bit flimsy and on the cheaper side. Too small for a proper fit of a m-atx board and too large for an itx board. Cable management took a long time because the routing is strange. Nowhere convenient to anchor cables to the case. Ended up replacing the cheap fans that were included. Mine only came with a top dust screen despite there being the exact same size and shape cutout on the bottom. I contacted customer service and they claimed that its only supposed to have one dust screen, so you get to choose if you want dust to get sucked in through the bottom or you can have an unfinished look on the top. Your choice. They would not sell me a spare dust screen.
I do like the shape of it and the location of the psu mounted along the side panel in the back is pretty cool, but they should've raised it a tiny bit for better access to cable management. Alternatively you can mount a sff psu and have more space.
I'm sure you can make this case work, but I've gotten great cases for the same price and this is not it.
reviews.author: Thunderdog

reviews.title: Nice quality
reviews.comment: The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/C155V8FuaPL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/61B2rIDyMQL._SY256.jpg Easy to work in nice case
reviews.author: jesse

reviews.title: Quality built case, some restrictions being SFF but it looks great and easy to build
reviews.comment: Love this case with the fish tank look. Build quality is really nice, I was kind of worried with company named JONSBO sometimes you're taking your chances. Lots of spots for fans, especially if you want to get creative. 4 120mm, 2 top 2 bottom. Then you can get 2 92mm in the bottom of the second compartment cooling psu and behind the motherboard. Another 2 92mm fans attached to back air intake area, I'm using those small square velcro pads and have no noise issues or anything coming loose. Finally 2 80mm fans in front air intake area blowing at cpu and back of gpu. All this and my pc is literally at ambient at idle. 50-60 during heavy gaming. I am using the P9 and P8 max fans which are pretty heavy duty but they're pretty quiet at middle of rpm range. So it stays super cool with 12600K and 1080ti. Great case, I left out the bottom 120mm fans cuz i didnt want them blowing straight into my 1080ti and knocking a gpu fan off balance. Obviously glass is dust and fingerprint magnet. Plus its kinda a pain to take on and off if you want to fiddle. Other than that easy peasy build with a SFF psu but its not a necessity.
reviews.author: Dan

reviews.title: Beautiful case with great features
reviews.comment: EXCELLENT and beautiful case design with very good build quality.  Compact in size, perfect for an M-ATX motherboard.  It was a big pleasant surprise to see that the all the normally individual cables for Power SW, Reset, LED, HHD LED were all combined into a solid Plug-in connector (matching the Asus MB. This should be a STANDARD procedure with all PC cases.  It's so frustrating when you have to plug each of those 9 individual cables into the correct PIN one at a time in the proper order! The Power button lights up white (not bright) with Power ON, and Blinks when computer is in a dormant state to let you know.  Smart, Awesome feature. More expensive than most cases, but as usual, you get what you pay for.
reviews.author: M. Alberto

reviews.title: very nice case
reviews.comment: Its stunning in person, love the curved glass and its very strong. I would def recommend this case to anyone looking
reviews.author: Dallas nabor

reviews.title: Glass does not go back on easy.  Other than that, I love it.
reviews.comment: Love the look and function of the case.  Easy to pull of the back and sides and put all the parts in.  Running the wires was a breeze, before you put the fans in.  The only thing that is not cool about this is the glass front does not go back on easily because the holes for the screws on the left and right DO NOT perfectly match up.  On mine the glass hangs very slightly lower on the left, maybe off by 2mm or something.  It's noticable if you're looking for it from the front visually.  VERY noticable when you're trying to secure the glass back on after making changes.
reviews.author: Edster

reviews.title: Sturdy
reviews.comment: This actually feels like a quality case heavy and sturdy only issue I can find is I think it should come with plastic peel on the glass
reviews.author: Trevor P

reviews.title: Best Value RGB Case at This Price Point
reviews.comment: For the price, the Raidmax I802 is honestly a steal—especially since it comes with five RGB infinity fans included. The case looks great its really sturdy once built and is easy to cable manage, even for beginners. The side panel comes off easily, but just a heads up: the front panel does take a bit more force to remove. My only gripe is that all the fans are powered by molex and have fixed RGB—there’s no way to control the lighting or fan speed. If Raidmax had made the RGB controllable, this case would be unbeatable for value. Even with this downside, I’d still recommend it for anyone wanting an affordable, stylish “fishtank” case with lots of included fans.
reviews.author: JoelTech

reviews.title: Pretty good case
reviews.comment: There are a few nice things in this case, for example, the lower-mounted fan (to cool a graphics card) and the fact that both glass panels open without screws (which makes working on it pretty awesome). Plenty of space, glass is so clear that it seems it's not there at all, good airflow. Not so great: - The metal is soft (mine arrived a little bumped in the lower part due to transport, and there is no way I can fix that; however, this case is for my kid, and he didn't care at all about that little imperfection. - The fan screws in the bottom screw directly into the metal (which is soft), so there is a risk of stripping it. Not worth removing starts for those, just be careful when using it.
reviews.author: Ottaviani Luigi

reviews.title: Unbeatable cost
reviews.comment: Built my girlfriend’s first pc for Christmas. For the cost it’s easily recommended. Very easy to build in and the included fans are already daisy chained. Knocked 1 star off due to also ordering a White cpu cooler that they sell but they sent a black one instead. Not a huge biggie and I still used it. P.s if anyone is confused where the 4 pin connector is to power the fans, it uses SATA cable so make sure you plug a sata cable into Your power supply before installing power supply.
reviews.author: Juwan

reviews.title: First PC case
reviews.comment: Great case not problems I bought this case because there are barely any purple pc case out there. I ended up using a different brand of fans but the case is good and serves it's purpose. Keep making purple cases RaidMAX!
reviews.author: Janice

reviews.title: Quality & Price Thanks & It Fits The Description!
reviews.comment: The Best Yet For The Price Lovin It!
reviews.author: Clifford Blount

reviews.title: Highly recommended
reviews.comment: Awesome case & hardware, I even bought a 2nd case.
reviews.author: Sonny G TX

reviews.title: Good but......
reviews.comment: Super Quite Fans!!! RGB works nicely with my AMD mother board. My only complaint is, as a few others have noted.....Some of the standoffs are stripped so you may not be able to use all the screws to hold down your motherboard. I built two computers with this tower and both had the same issue. I was tempted to return it but decided to over look this flaw because I really like the case. I had specific needs and this one fit my needs just fine. I would buy again even with the know issue. The issue might be significant to others which is why this got a 3 star instead of a five star review.
reviews.author: K. Thibault

reviews.title: 80% Work But Light Controller Failed
reviews.comment: Most of the parts are functional except the light controller. The cable for controlling or the part responsible for controlling just does not work. And this controller is the main reason I bought this case otherwise I can get cheaper cases so will just give 2 stars. Luckily the motherboard I bought gives a splitter which allows me to control the lights via software so didn’t return it.
reviews.author: ShelbyZ

reviews.title: Happy first time builder!
reviews.comment: The Montech XR Wood offers a simple but classy design with the wood accents. Access throughout the entire case is easy and makes building a PC a clean experience. The open panel design allowed a novice/first time builder such as me to smoothly add my PC components. I like the magnetic vent covers although they can fall off easily with minimal manipulation or a brush against them so be aware when handling the case. Also, the fan cords can be a bit tight in binding so don't pull too tight.  Overall, the case has plenty of options for adding extra storage such as HDDs, SSDs and M.2. and has good airflow throughout.
reviews.author: Hamp

reviews.title: Great case for the money
reviews.comment: Great case and I have nothing wrong about it. It came assembled and it was easy to pop off the front panel and back panel. The cooling is good and the fans are able to keep my PC cool. I run a 5070TI and a 7800x3d.
reviews.author: Matthew

reviews.title: Great built in fans
reviews.comment: Great build quality, cable management is a bit difficult with the already built in cooling fan cables.
reviews.author: Ron Perrymore

reviews.title: stylish
reviews.comment: My husband built his PC in it, and it’s both stylish and spacious with excellent airflow. Very happy with this case!
reviews.author: Vasiliy

reviews.title: A beautiful case that only requires a little finesse
reviews.comment: I purchased the Jonsbo TK-0.  This ITX case is beautiful and quite functional without taking up too much room on your desk.  The secondary compartment for power supply, extra drives, and wiring is perfect for organizing your cabling and easily connecting all your parts.  The build quality of the case is excellent, with my only gripe being the tiny and mediocre quality screws provided to screw in the glass and the PSU side panel.  I would recommend being very gentle with them to avoid stripping.  The top panel is a simple in design but fantastic in form and function, and even has silicone protectors to keep everything tight and vibration-free when it’s put together.  There are some things to consider with this case.  Unfortunately, you cannot fit even a 120mm AIO in the top of the case, due to the top fan sticking out about 1-2mm into the PSU compartment through a cutout, constraining the depth of fan—25mm thickness (the standard) is the maximum that would fit.  Watch out because some TUF and other fans are actually 28mm thick, and will not fit.  The rear fans are a dual 90-92mm pair, which align perfectly to the other parts in the case.  A 120mm fan will not work there.  I personally used a very nice pair of Silverstone 92mm ARGB fans that worked great.  The graphics card slot (which, I’m still waiting to receive my card from Amazon, so I will update once I get that) accommodates a 2.5 slot thick card, which should work with most smaller dual fan graphics cards.  Very importantly, keep in mind that the best cool air intake location is at the bottom of the case, and unfortunately, if my measurements are correct, only a 15mm thick specialty fan will fit.  Once I get my graphics card I will update this.  The case does come with mesh dust screens—one is built into the PSU side panel, while one is magnetic on the bottom of the case.  Keep in mind that you CAN change the location of the feet and the case orientation, which changes the air flow pattern. Overall, this case is amazing so far, easy to work inside, and is definitely worth the price.  If you want a beautiful case that you can display on your desk without taking up a ton of room, I cannot recommend this one enough!
reviews.author: David S.

reviews.title: Fantastic tiny case
reviews.comment: This is a remarkably well-built little case. The metal is much thicker than I expected, as is the glass; I'd compare the subjective evaluation of its build quality favorably to my Fractal and Hyte cases. It's kind of a pain to work in, but no more so than any other case as densely packed as this. The fiddly aspect of it is just the nature of tiny systems. The only real gripe I have is that if you use a 140mm fan in the bottom, depending on how you need to orient the power wires to the fan (e.g. if you have an infinity mirror fan or something that can only go in in one of two orientations), you may find that you need to really pinch the power wires to the fan against the motherboard tray to get it installed. Another 3mm is all they would have needed. Otherwise, it's a great-looking case of much higher quality than I was expecting.
reviews.author: Siorus

reviews.title: Great kit, looks nice
reviews.comment: Looks very nice on my desktop.  Easy to build in.  Looks like a piece of furniture or show case.
reviews.author: Peter Peel

reviews.title: Tk-0 mini power house
reviews.comment: Looks awesome and unique. I was able to fit Msi shadow x2 Rtx 5070. Good size with decent airflow. The build quality is impressive.
reviews.author: Miguel Alvarado

reviews.title: TK-0 Great case to show off!
reviews.comment: Thought I'd make a review since there isn't a lot of TK-0 reviews. This case is pretty dope. Instructions were pretty clear and easy to take a part and put together with a screw driver. Ended up buying a new GPU because my 3060 12gb couldn't fit in there. Took out the memory holder in the back because I do have a lot of cables due to having aftermarket extensions but doesn't matter since I don't use them anyways. Running artic 92mm and 120mm fans fits perfectly with a few MM to spare. Also a lot of room if you want to run a bigger CPU cooler as well. I will say if I would go back I'd buy some better quality fans. The screws on these kept threading incorrectly. Definitely don't recommend 140mm for the bottom fan.
reviews.author: Kevin rath

reviews.title: Amazing case needs a couple tweaks.
reviews.comment: I love this case! It is a great size and the 90 degree rotation of the motherboard is awesome. I bought this case because of my belief that hot air from my GPU shouldn't rise up to my CPU. I'm not a professional PC builder and do minimal overclocking, so I work with what I can afford. I also live in a warmer region so the least amount of warm air in my case I can get, that's what I'm going to do. It fits my Tomahawk B550 MAG perfectly! Plenty of cutouts for cables to come through reducing the jumbled mess blocking airflow. I love how the I/O panel is on the top as well for looking down. The case comes with quite a few velcro straps for cables also. The only real problem I have with the case is that the CPU power cable has to do one of two things: either run down the back and out a cutout then back up to the plug, or use a vent hole for the PSU to slide the connector through. I chose the second option to reduce cord from running further length. Works and still looks pretty clean! Great case for a new look. Highly recommend!
reviews.author: Mr. K

reviews.title: Unique case, smaller than some full ATX cases, yet fits everything.
reviews.comment: I bought this case almost a year ago.  I was at first skeptical by the lack of reviews but the case definitely is a premium case. I did want a case where the GPU doesn’t sag, and I wasn’t sure if my 360mm radiator would fit. If you see in the 2nd picture I was able to mount my Arctic Liquid 360mm radiator without modifications through the top and back behind the GPU. Since the motherboard has a 90degree turn with the rear I/O facing upwards, it’s very easy to connect all your accessories. The only mod I added was buying rubber furniture raisers so that the four bottom fan pulls enough air into the case. No drilling necessary the bottom is flat, 3M double sticky tape did the job. The negative I could see is that the glass is pretty dark (also can be a positive since you see much of the cable management inside the case). The case is definitely heavy, but I was aware of that since this was a fully new build PC. PC Parts used: CPU - Intel i7-13700k (no issues) AiO - Arctic Liquid Freeze 360mm RGB MSI MPG Z690 Edge DDR5 M-Board G.Skill Trident Z5 RGB 48GB-DDR5-6800 RAM Zotac Trinity OC RTX4080 GPU (big card) Samsung 980pro 1TB OS Win10pro drive NVMe Samsung 980pro 2TB game drive NVMe Samsung 970evo 500GB file backup NVMe MSI 482 pro 2TB Picture/ video drive NVMe Samsung 850evo 500GB OS Ubuntu SSD 5x Noctua 120mm fans Samsung G8 34in OLED 175hz primary Alienware 34in IPS 120hz secondary
reviews.author: JTrend

reviews.title: Great Case.
reviews.comment: Thermal performance is a bit meh but case despite is configuration was easy to build in and looks absolutely incredible. I’m not one to give the germans too much credit but they did good here.
reviews.author: Christopher Oakley

reviews.title: slightly unconventional case. looks sharp.
reviews.comment: wanted a slightly less conventional PC case that was mostly for an aesthetic i liked. the airflow with the availability of fan configuration looks a little unconventional upon quick observation. the back (glass) panel & compartment for wires is somewhat tight for how big the case is. it's fine, you will need to ziptie or velcro things together to get the glass panel on comfortably with a little more attention to wire management. the front compartment holds the power supply, typically where 3 or 4 fans would go in an open face, instead. the power supply compartment is probably oversized but that is okay because it leaves room for stuffing the extra wire length for the motherboard and gpu. i ended up placing a 3 fan CPU cooler + radiator on the back side, 1x 140mm fan on the top and 3x 140mm fans on the bottom. i'm running an AM4 with a 9070xt, which run a little warmer than nvidia cards and a Ryzen 7 5800XT, also a tad warm. configured the fans in bios to run a little more aggressively because of those factors. with the nominal suggested or average temperatures; both CPU and GPU run on the very coolest side. one thing i did do out of caution was 3d print feet to raise the entire case off the ground since the 3x 140mm fans on the bottom are doing most of the 'PUSH' for the airflow since it only has 1 top fan doing the 'PULL'. the 3x fans on the back run through the water cooled radiator and the GPU blows onto it, as well. they're doing a bit of heavy lifting. all-in-all, looks cool and doesn't seem to have any issues with the available airflow options.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Just different
reviews.comment: Pretty nice case. Alittle odd design but once ots all together it fnctions well. Would he nicernif the feet were taller
reviews.author: Chris B.

reviews.title: This is the "NZXT at home" of Fishtank cases
reviews.comment: Incredible airflow considering the way the case is designed.  PCCooler is basically like the "generic OEM" for a lot of parts in China.  If you have an NZXT H5/H6/H7, it's obvious a lot of corners were cut to make this case hit the below $50 price point, but there's nothing wrong with that.  If you come in expecting a budget case, you will get great value for your money. The packaging is very utilitarian - it comes in a box and has two styrofoam supports - and that's it.  Nothing else.  The case comes plain with no other extra packaging except a plastic bag covering it. You will find a 5 page manual inside the case and a bunch of "spare" parts/accessories.  Screws for hard drives, additional hexagonal standoffs for your mobo, etc. You can tell a lot of corners were cut to make it work, but for a beginner budget PC builder this case is more than enough - installation for everything was a breeze as the dual chamber "fishtank" design makes cable management easy and painless. Just beware that the PCI-E covers are PUNCH OUTS and not true covers - once you remove them there is no way to put them back on easily.  Hint: if you have a modern GPU, only punch out the second and third from the top of the case. Doesn't come with fans and has no RGB, not a big problem.  If you've worked with other modern builds this should be very familiar to you. The case does not give you threaded screws for fans, but most fans come with them as part of the purchase, so start digging your pockets or help from computer guys for them. The metal is much thinner, but this might be a good thing because it makes the case VERY light.  Only room for 1 3.25 HDD and one 2.5 SSD.  This case would be ideal for a MicroATX build.  The motherboard back side panel of the case (to your right if you were looking at the front of the case) also screws on via traditional thumb screws, whereas the front side can be easily pulled off using clips. No preinstalled straps for cable management - they just give you a few very thin twist ties. No removable magnetic mesh on the bottom intake/exhaust, only on the top. I could go on, but that's what you pay for a budget build - if you're a beginner use a lot of these won't be a big deal for you.
reviews.author: M. Park

reviews.title: great buy on sale....dont pay full price for it.
reviews.comment: Pretty nice case overall, missing some minor things like gromet covers, wider gaps and holes under motherboard better GPU power running, it looks dumb coming from the giant side gromet. PCI slot cover is janky as can be, I hate it and it sucks lol case metal is a tad thin but it work fine, seems sturdy when built out. Sure looks cool and seems to have decent airflow. Can fit a 360 rad on the side or top....my previous case could only do a 240. had no issue with Motherboard IO and PSU mounting, and plenty of space in back for cables to get tied up side glass panel works but the clips are pretty bad, feel like im going to break something taking it off most the time.
reviews.author: kellyrx8

reviews.title: Great case overall. Bad PCI covers
reviews.comment: This case is an excellent fish tank PC build with ample space for fans, and case management. Purchased during a sale and I think it was well worth the price as it comfortably fits my computer parts with space for cable management and room for future upgrades/growth. I didnt realize it came with an opening for a vertical GPU mount so it can work with many types if builds and have great airflow while doing so. The only issue I had was finding out the pci tabs are punch outs and not reusable but that isnt much of an issue.
reviews.author: Bruh.mp4

reviews.title: Spacious!
reviews.comment: This case is amazing. Everything fit perfectly with plenty of room to work in. I originally started my build in a smaller case and quickly realized I needed more space, so I ended up switching to this one. I just wish I had chosen it from the start. It’s super spacious, easy to build in, and had no problem fitting my oversized RTX 3080. Definitely a great choice if you want a hassle-free build with plenty of clearance. Highly recommend.
reviews.author: Richard Sanchez

reviews.title: Great Budget Case
reviews.comment: I got the case over others I preferred because I was low on funds after buying everything else. I went into the build sort of like ehhhhh this might work out. The case is a little thin and will flex somewhat until everything is in and screwed down. I loaded it up with 10 120mm fans. Running 6 as intake and 4 as exhaust. Three fan AIO is mounted at the top and will not fit on the side as they say. 140mm fans will not fit at the bottom as the edge of the fan comes into contact with the motherboard. However, even with the negatives I love the case. Has great air flow and stable temps. I run a Ryzen 9 7900x with a 9060 XT OC Edition and a 34 inch OLED and my temps are flat out awesome. GPU under load in COD never goes above 55c, case temp hovers around 28c max. I feel the wire management is great. I didn't have any issues with that at all. It's a cheap low budget case that will hang with others way above it's price range.
reviews.author: Warren L.

reviews.title: Top notch product and Even better customer service!
reviews.comment:
This case is awesome.  I can fit a bunch of optical and hard drives that are accessible from the front!  Lots of room and even fits a 5090 after moving some drive bays around.
The real gem here is the customer service.  It's outstanding.
I have an older MoBo that has a 20-pin split loose control panel connectors (power, reset, HD light, etc) this case comes with a new style combined 8-pin solid connector.  It would not fit... Devastating.
You know that disappointment when you get something new and it doesn't work out of the box?  I had this sad feeling.  I figured I was going to have to source some random adapter that may or may not be the right one.  It was a dark time for me and this magnificent tall steel tower.
From the darkness came the light that is Rosewill customer service.  They looked at my sadness and said "Hold my beer kid, we're going to send you out the correct adapter, today, for free".  I lifted my head and a tear slowly formed and ran down my cheek.  I handed them back their well earned beer and, smiled, and said in a whisper,  thank you.
Sure enough the cable arrived shortly after and I could power on and reset my system.
Much respect and will be a loyal customer.
reviews.author: J

reviews.title: Choice for NAS Home server with more room in Storage cage Motherboard e-ATX
reviews.comment:
Pro:- Drive Interface SAS & SATA fits. Verify if Hot-Swap support works with SAS drive. Information for SDD-HDD attach in bay: Download manual of ‘Rosewill RSV-SATA-Cage-34 Internal SATA/SAS Hot-Swap Cage’. Strong Metal body. Front USB-C port cable doesn’t find port in my e-ATX motherboard of Gigabyte MU92-TU1 so I may buy PCIe expansion card that has a USB Type E and 19 pin interface.
Con:- Cage does not support SAS 12Gb/s. Very less space behind cage to attach cable of SATA and 4 pin Molex power cable if one uses motherboard form factor of e-ATX. Removed fan to make room behind cage since I used e-ATX.

reviews.title: Uses IDE/Molex 4-pin power.  Buy adapters.
reviews.comment:
Great case, fit my full-size ATX (ASUS Z890-P) board like a glove.
Not worth taking off a star but for whatever reason Rosewill designed power for their hot-swap bays with the old-style IDE(4-pin molex) connectors.  Unless your power supply is old school, you'll want male-sata -> female molex power adapters.
reviews.author: Scott S Sinno

reviews.title: Decent large case with SAS/SATA 6G drive cages, some adjustment required
reviews.comment:
This case is OK for the purpose, but can't reach a 5-star review given its issues:
- alignment and tolerances of slots for openings for things like the case sides are off by enough to cause issue when replacing the screws,
- alignment of one side of the drive bay area with respect to the other are off enough to cause problems in 3rd party equipment,
- the top of the case and the top of the motherboard section are too close to properly install and place a 240 or 360 water cooling radiator, since the motherboard will collide with the attached fans--meaning I had to install the fans outside of the case at the top (there are no other suitable locations), obtain extension cords for the PWM fans, and widen an unused slot for attaching a fan/cooler to feed the cable extension into the case to attach back to the water cooler controls.  Given the case layout, moving the motherboard down 3-4 cm would solve the problem.
Next there is the issue that in a current day NAS case, SAS drive cages should be 12G speed, not limited to 6G speed, which meant I had to replace the Thor NAS Pro native SAS/SATA drive cages with ones that were 12G SAS capable.
If I had known the drive cages were this level, I would have not bought the Thor NAS Pro, but just the Thor NAS and used the difference in cost to buy the needed 12G SAS drive cages.
The main reason I bought this case was the available capability to have external facing drive bays, something many current trend cases no longer provide, neither for optical drives nor for drive cages and hot-swap hardware.
I would not buy this specific model of case again, but the Thor NAS version and supply my own drive cages.
Other issues in alignment and openings are rectifiable with tools and some sweat equity.
reviews.author: Eric James Beasley

reviews.title: Poor machining, lots of plastic, but works well enough
reviews.comment:
There are very few cases like this one and it does the job well enough. Lots of space to get a server board put in (I used an ASRock Rack board). Putting everything together was easy enough. The fans are silent enough that I didn't even bother replacing them. Heat has never been an issue even during burn-in testing. This isn't in a dusty area (it's in the basement where nobody is most of the time) so I don't know how well the dust filters will work over time.
Some stuff I didn't like: every screw goes in like it's cross threaded. All the drive trays are plastic, but to be fair, they are pretty solid. I've pulled drives in and out while building and testing this thing and they go in and out very smoothly. Just felt like a lot of plastic for such an expensive case. I would have preferred a metal chassis like I have in an old external drive array. The 3.5" drives just slide and latch in, no tray needed.
Also, to power the drives adequately, esp. with enterprise drives, you'll likely need at least two separate power cables from the PSU. I had to get SATA to Molex adapters in order to connect all four ports.
It's hard as heck to get the SATA cables connected to the backplane. I had to take the fans off to get everything connected. The SATA connectors felt flimsy too. They aren't mounted very sturdily.
Overall, despite these issues, I'm happy enough w/ this case and would recommend it to anyone looking to do a custom 8-bay NAS / home server like I did.
reviews.author: Phil

reviews.title: Perfectly sized mATX case! Best one I’ve ever seen
reviews.comment:
I love this case! It is perfect and it was just what I needed for my build. As someone who values desk space and was coming from have a sff pc that was in a fractal terra jade case, this case fit my requirements perfectly.
It is a little on the girthy and wider side, but that helps as you have more room to work and also for ventilation. I was able to fit 9 fans in here, the 3 that come with the case, and I had a 360 mm AIO on that that fit with enough space and 3 intake fans at the bottom as well.
The fan/connection hub in the back is great and lets you add more fans than what your motherboard will allow, but forewarning, doesn’t have any fan sensors built in, so dont be shocked if you can’t manually control the speed of each fan.
The quality of the temper glass is strong and durable, as well as the metal parts of the case.
I will say the most annoying part is that there is no physical manual that comes with it, but there is a QR code that you can scan that’ll take you online to see how to build it.
Also, it is a bit uncomfortable to connect the front usb 3.2 case connectors to your motherboard as while it seems like it’s a straight angle, since the case cable is a bit short and the angle is tight, you have to finagle with it a lot while connecting it to the port on the motherboard, so maybe investing in a 90 degree adapter would be a good idea.
For size and context, the gpu that is installed is a 9070 Hellhound, and as you can see, I still have space to spare and the case comes with a built in support bracket for the gpu. I don’t really use it however as it would sit directly on top of one of the gpu fans.
All in all, I am very satisfied with the case and would highly recommend this to anyone who wants to have the appeal of seeing your parts like a big fish tank pc case, without taking up all the space in your desk.

I swapped the stocks fans with 6 bequiet silent wings 4 fans to increase airflow while still keeping noise low. reviews.comment: Case has been great, looks good, great airflow.

reviews.title: Quality is first-rate and at a nice price-point, but ...
reviews.comment: Pros: Quality is very good.  Covers on both sides, front and top easily remove without tools leaving an open framework.  Ample space for a graphics card at the front of the case. Cons: Space is very tight, especially if your MB is ATX and has traditional top-mounted connections.  Instructions are limited as with a lot of other cases.  Power and reset buttons are mounted at the bottom front and could be tripped with a foot.  USB ports are likewise at the bottom on the side and requires a stretch to bend over if the case is sitting on the floor.  Control of the case RGB lighting is less than straightforward.  Cooling with fans only will require purchasing an additional fan and mounting it in a "cage" that attaches to the rear of the case. Summary: Best for bottom connection motherboards, especially smaller sizes, with water cooling and separate graphics card.  I could not get the case RGB lights to operates according to the instructions (and after looking online) and finally just disconnected the power.

reviews.title: Compact yet heavy
reviews.comment: The layout in the case is uncommon but works out better than it seems. Space in the rear behind the motherboard is limited but there's enough clearance for cables and airflow from the sides. Lighting looks great with the integrated light strip and the front panel cables have good length plus match the case's color. The included fans are simple with no lighting but are high quality with good airflow. Performance wise, there's enough airflow and most of it will exhaust from the right side (mesh panel). I have had no issues with video card temperatures and my AMD Ryzen 9 7950X does not throttle with a 360 AIO.

reviews.title: Great case
reviews.comment: I bought this case to build a PC using spare parts I had lying around for casual couch gaming. The case looks great, features an interesting layout, and was very easy to build in. I would recommend using a low-profile CPU cooler, as the AMD Wraith Prism is too tall to fit properly.
