reviews.comment: Every part of me wants to give it 4 but the riser cable is defective doesn’t put out video unfortunately. My daughters destroyed the box so I can’t return excellent looking case but my components don’t like the riser cable I guess

reviews.comment: Great case! Solid made. The video card being flipped can be confusing, but it's an intelligent design

reviews.title: Zalmon Tempered Glass PC Case
reviews.comment: Awesome case. It's not large but can fit a full size atx motherboard.  It has all the fans you need and that in led lighting.  It's super easy to setup as you don't even need tools of any kind.  It doesn't take up hardly any surface space as it's well suited for the floor or table. I have a water cooler in my setup and it's super quiet. It is very durable and thought out nicely for cable management.  I highly recommend it for anyone who is in looking for a nice PC build.
reviews.author: Samuel Medina

reviews.title: Good looking and deceptively easy to build in.
reviews.comment: It's really tight for a standard ATX motherboard but that's why I purchased it. Despite its size it's really easy to build in due to how light weight it is without the side panels and just how much room you get after removing them. My only dislike is the limited power supply space but they don't really tell you what length of power supply it will accommodate. This should probably be listed with the rest of the specs. Aside from that, there's plenty of room behind the motherboard tray and cable management provisions are fairly decent. The case fans are kind of bleh but the thermals are about the same as a standard ATX case with the same number of fans. In all it's small and it looks really good for the price.
reviews.author: Kenneth

reviews.title: Great case, with only one minor issues.
reviews.comment: I gave this 5 stars because I like the case.  The power plug is on the correct side, and where I placed the tower, it works out perfectly.  It is much quieter than my last case, and keeps the computer running nice and cool.  It looks great, just like the photo, and the build quality is nice as well. Now for the minor issue(s). 1. It was difficult to remove the glass.  Take your time and look at the manual online. (the paper manual is inside the case) 2. There should be support for the video card. I found that my video card was drooping, and I did not want to have an issue, so I designed and 3D-printed a small jack to hold it up.  One of the photos shows an item that holds up the card, but it was not included in the box. Overall, I still give it 5 stars because it's still a nice case.
reviews.author: Bill's Workbench on YouTube

reviews.title: Unique, Yet Cheaply Flawed
reviews.comment: I jumped at this case, as I was building a new PC and I liked the idea of an mATX-sized case that can fit an ATX motherboard. Its footprint is small; I believe I read it’s a little over 30L in space. The size, footprint, and aquarium-glass design are where the fun stops, though. This has been the hardest computer case I’ve worked in throughout the 25 years I’ve been building computers. The space is exceptionally cramped and requires a lot of forethought into building inside of it. I’ve gone back and spent hours making several revisions to rearranging cabling to get the cleanest overall look possible. The front USB ports are 3.0 (5Gbps) only, including the USB-C port. For the price, I’d have expected proper USB 3.0 and 20GBps or faster connectivity. In addition, changing the fans requires removing the USB front panel, which is difficult to get to and difficult to put back on. The fans that come with the case are nothing to write home about. Thermals will suffer in this case, unless the fans are replaced. In my pictures, you’ll see I replaced 3 of the fans with Thermalright TK-12 fans (2 intake and 1 exhaust), leaving the poorer packaged fans to simply feed my GPU. My temps fared much much better with fans that can push more air and are better adept to static pressure. The whole case feels cheap. Coming from an NZXT H7-Flow, the flimsy steel of this case was immediately apparent. The glass is very light and very thin. In addition, the extra feet that can be placed on the side of the case, so as to change the orientation, come with cheap 3M adhesive film that came off nearly immediately. I wound up using velcro as a remedy, which works well, but this again points to the cheap quality of the case. If this case were $50-$60, it would be a better purchase. However, at $100, its novelty quickly wears off. Nonetheless, the case’s aesthetics are nice, as you can see with it full of computer components. In addition, my PC lives in my living room, so the smaller space is even more welcome.  However, know what you’re getting into, should you purchase this case. Or wait until a much less cheaply made offering from another manufacturer comes out. —EDIT— I’ve now included an image of the backside of the motherboard. I’m using a normal size power-supply, which results in a very tight fit. The HDD tray was especially troublesome to get screwed in, on account of cable management. Once complete, though, everything looks great in the case. It’s the working inside of it where things get tricky. One piece of advice I can give is run the fan cabling before installing the motherboard. This made life easier for me, at least.
reviews.author: 46w500

reviews.title: Compact atx cause
reviews.comment: Love this case very much, good quality, would definitely recommend. Assembly is easy with all of the removable glass panels. If you enjoy cable management and want a compact atx cause this will be the perfect choice
reviews.author: Brock Smith

reviews.title: Killer Case for 11 fans! All white minimalist look!
reviews.comment: GPU will sit lower to the bottom intake fans. Make sure you have 90 degree gpu power connector to route above your GPU. Side mounting my 420mm would not fit. Definitely top mount the 420mm if you can. Overall case is great! Watch out when you handle the top corner of the case after removing all the front and side glass. The metal is weaker without the glass support. It will bend if you lift from there. Also don't use the stock fans it comes with unless you love 39 decibels as loud as a dishwasher in your ear hole.
reviews.author: Daniel

reviews.title: Build came to life.
reviews.comment: The case has its flaws because its not everything your going to get well be flawless i bought the one without rbg fans considering i was planning on making my own style lighting. This case will allow me to look at a creation i mapped in my head and brought to life. I love it, thanks Hyxn.
reviews.author: Nyles Hudson

reviews.title: Nice case
reviews.comment: Case looks amazing
reviews.author: Jonah childress

reviews.title: Disappointed. Poor quality and design, overpriced, misleading specs
reviews.comment: Watched this item for awhile wanting to do a 420mm radiator build in a budget friendly 140mm fan case. Fans included at this size aren't common so went it went on sale from $189 to $159 figured I'd give it a try. First order arrived with fans in pieces right out of the box and the dust filters missing. Amazon support was great and sent a replacement immediately. The case itself its mediocre at best and quite frankly less so. As others have pointed out it's very cheaply made and not worth the price, even on sale. $100 +/- is the most I'd recommend after hands on with it. Cheaply built sheet metal, poorly laid out cable management, very odd placement of SSDs, the wiring in the included fans was hanging out of the daisy chain on a few connectors, the LEDs were flickering, and the includes motherboard screws were just raw in the case rattling around, to name a few issues. The glass panels don't fit toegther as nicely as they look online; personal opinion. Top issue for me is this case does not support 420mm radiators (at least not all brands) as listed. My Arctic 420mm does not fit properly on any side. Period. Its too long for the bottom and side by almost an inch. The top it almost fits but requires removing the exhaust fans; the picture shows removing one fan to do a push-pull setup, but I had to remove it for the radiator to fit at all and the holes didn't line up right to attach it to the roof. I'm not buying a new radiator to fit this case. I couldn't complete the build so there may be additional oversight in the design. Overall, it's going back. Should have bought a HAVN case to start and saved myself the time and multiple trips to UPS. Cheers to Amazon customer support once again.

reviews.title: Espectacular
reviews.comment: Espacio suficiente para hacer lo que gustes

reviews.title: Exceeded all expectations
reviews.comment:
Take a look at the 1 negative remark I have at the end of this review if this happens to be the one that convinces you to buy.
Exceeded all expectations, plenty of room for any graphics card on the market, looks sharp, solidly built, plenty of cable management options, all panels can be removed for full access extremely easily. I originally was trying to get a different case however due to either amazon or usps logistical issues and not getting that case twice, I opted for this one. I do not regret it in the slightest.
The 1 negative remark is when removing the tempered glass side panel you have to make sure that you have a hand in place to catch the glass. I was not prepared for this the 1st time. I didnt break it but it did come as quite a shock that it was not in a channel guide, hooked in place or something of that nature.

reviews.title: Beautiful and Great-Value White Case!
reviews.comment:
The darkFlash DY460 White case looks absolutely stunning! The design is clean and minimalistic — that pure white finish gives it such a premium and elegant vibe. It comes with four built-in RGB fans, which look super cool and vibrant once powered on.
The airflow is excellent, keeping the system cool and running smoothly. Building inside this case was a breeze — plenty of space for cable management, and everything fits perfectly. The packaging was also solid and secure, with no damage during shipping.
Overall, this is a great-looking, high-performance, and budget-friendly case. Highly recommend it to anyone who loves a clean white build setup!

reviews.title: Great value
reviews.comment: Nice quality! Plenty of room!

reviews.title: Not bad for a first build
reviews.comment: Definitely a great case for my first ever PC build. I've no complaints so far,  and delivery was smooth without any hitches.

reviews.title: Premium Build Quality with Flawless Back-Connect Support
reviews.comment: We build a lot of showcase PCs, and the JONSBO X400 in Gray has quickly become one of our top recommendations for a premium ATX chassis. If you are looking for a case that supports the new wave of back-connect motherboards (like BTF or Project Zero), this case executes it flawlessly, allowing for an incredibly clean, zero-cable aesthetic. The Technical Specs & Clearances: Motherboard Support: ATX, Micro-ATX, and Mini-ITX (Fully back-connect compatible). GPU Clearance: A massive 427mm. It will fit any RTX 4090 or 5090 on the market with plenty of room to breathe. Cooling Potential: Unbelievable airflow. It supports up to 13 x 120mm fans and can comfortably house 360mm AIO radiators on the top, bottom, or side. CPU Cooler & PSU: Fits CPU air coolers up to 176mm tall and ATX power supplies up to 180mm. Aside from the specs, we highly recommend this case for its build quality. Weighing in at over 22 lbs empty, the SPCC steel chassis feels incredibly rigid and durable, and the tempered glass panels mate together beautifully without any massive gaps. It’s a heavy-duty, premium canvas for high-end components. 5/5 stars!

reviews.title: Good, but does not come with any case fans.
reviews.comment:
"【ADVANCED MESH COOLING SYSTEM】: Dual 120x15mm ultra-slim fans..."
That statement, along with their pictures, is misleading, and implies that this L300 case comes with 2 120x15mm fans when it does not include fans.
Both case fans are basically needed. Unlike regular ATX builds that are usually over 30 liters, these much smaller cases need to exhaust heat. The CPU, and video card will intake air, and both case fans should be set to exhaust for best results. Arctic, Thermalright, Noctua, Silverstone, etc all have 120x15mm fans, but that's another $15-$50.
My build:
Shiny Snake L300 case
Thermalright AXP90x47 Full Copper
SFX PSU
Intel 13600k
2 120x15mm case fans
Triple fan video card
Initial impressions:
This L300 case is well made, and thought out. It looks like it does in the pictures. It's a clean mesh design. It's not high end, but it doesn't feel, or look cheap. Ports are where they should be for a desktop. The lighting on the power button isn't diffused evenly, and I don't think you can turn it off since it's a full header that covers motherboards front panel connectors.
The video cards ports are on the bottom of the case, and besides the included display port cable, you will need 90 degree cable or adapter for each additional monitor you plan to use. The included cable will most likely block at least one slot.
The case is all mesh, it's metal, and pretty solid.
It's not too difficult to build in. Like any SFF build using the right parts, and some planning is needed.
It saves some desk space. If you have the space consider the L400. It's slightly taller, and longer, but mostly wider by almost 1.5'. It has more space for better cooling.
Cooling is decent with the right parts. It's as loud as your fans are. It's not silent, but with ambient noise, it is not very noticeable unless gaming because that ramps up all of fans.
The included PCIE riser, and angled display port cable work fine so far, and the little handle is a nice touch.
No issues installing the motherboard, or PSU. You may want to route some cables before screwing parts down. Cable management was ok. I could keep most of the fan areas free from obstruction.
My Intel CPU has been gaming in the 60's. For Intels, 65w CPU's are probably ideal as they are usually well under 100w while gaming. With their higher wattage CPU's, you will want to undervolt if heat, and noise is a concern. The efficient AMD/x3d CPU's should also work well due to their low power while gaming.
If you plan to do intensive work with your CPU, maybe look at the L400, etc instead. The L400 can fit 73mm coolers, and something like the Thermalright AXP120-67 CPU cooler is a better option for that.
L300 with 60mm space, does allow for several decent low profile CPU coolers. Thermalright AXP90x47, or x53 full copper are 2 of the best options with the ID Cooling is-55 coming in just a bit warmer than the coppers generally. Even the regular Thermalright AXP90-x53 can work well with 65w CPU's, but will be a bit hotter, and louder. You will want to mount whatever cooler with the fins orientated vertically, to make it easier for the top fan to exhaust the hot air from the CPU, etc.
No issues installing the PCIE riser, and video card. You might want to leave the riser a bit loose, and tighten it safely after the card is locked down. My triple fan card has plenty of space. Again, being a mesh case, you shouldn't have too many issues with temps as long as exhaust fans are installed, and not too obstructed. I would not recommend "blower" style cards in this case as it would have to exhaust out of the bottom the case. Try to keep your video cards heatsink fins unobstructed so that heat can escape easier.
Both fans were easy to install. You might want to do this step last so you have room to work. Be sure to try to keep both fans unobstructed so they can help remove hot air as that could make the difference with heat, and noise. The front fan mainly helps with video cards, and the top handles the CPU, and any other heat that rises. Minor complaint, there's 2 positions for the top fan, front, or back. It would have been nice if it had a center position so it sits right above the CPU cooler.
Not great for RGB obviously. No windows, and it will probably require some cable management to show RGB through the mesh.
1 star has come off for the false advertising of fans. Besides that, this case is probably 4-4.5 stars. Price was ok, no issues building it, performance is as expected, and quality is decent. An angled cable that doesn't block ports, and option to turn off the light on the power switch would be nice, along with both fans. There is PCIe 3, 4, and even PCIe 5 riser options. Not sure why they still produce PCIe3, and charge such a premium on PCIe4+, but it reflects market pricing.

reviews.title: Cools well and that ends well.
reviews.comment: Noctua has always been reliable (at least for me) and this huge cpu cooler (using it on a 9950x3d) is a decent alternative from liquid cooling. 8 heat pipres and robust noctua quality fans keep my ryzen 9 from throttling (stressed using aida64 and cinebench). Idle temps (ambient room temps in humid/tropical Fiji right now get up to 30degCelcius) so 50degCel is fine at idle (no I don't use aircon, we are fan people and am not rich enough to comfortably/consistently afford AC cooling). Under stress temps shoot up to 84 and sometimes has spiked to 88degC but still manageable and actually really cool (no pun) vis-a-vis ambient tropic humid temps. I have tried testing in AC controlled environment at my friends house (low as 18degC) and obviously the cooler performs way better with idling the 9950x3d at 40degC (under volted only with negative curves at 31/25 per ccd, i don't OC) and load temps never exceeding 78degC. Please don't take this the wrong way, this cooler is just as decent as an overpriced AIO or a reasonably priced AIO and lesser failure points. This is my backup if my current 420aio (no need to name names) ever craps out. Noctua gives me peace of mind and this cooler is a piece of cake to setup and use. Noise is negligible for me (using a havn hs 420 non vgpu; maxed 140 fans as recommended). I don't have any form of anechoic chambers (thanks Steve) to test for noise but to my naked ears, a noticeable "whoooom" sound (somewhat subdued) under load is fine while normal use noise is non-existent (subjective since I boldly assume my hearing is average/normal). I would buy again but given the quality, there will be no need (unless I can ever afford to build another PC). Overall, vinaka (thanks) Noctua and Amazon. Vinaka vakalevu from hot hot hot Fiji.

reviews.title: A Massive Leap in Clearance and Thermal Efficiency
reviews.comment: After years with the G1, the upgrade to the G2 has been incredible. The revised design solves the clearance issues that previously forced me to run only a single fan due to motherboard and RAM interference. The Thermal Difference The "heat soak" I experienced with the G1 is gone. Using FanControl to sync with my exhaust, the "wicking" is night and day: Arc Raiders (High/Epic Settings): Dropped from 80°C–85°C (G1) down to 58°C–65°C (G2). Idle/Lobby: Dropped from 45°C–60°C down to 35°C–48°C. Build Quality & Installation The G2 feels much denser; the fins are sturdy and don't "ping" or flex during installation like the G1. The shift in the bracketry—moving the stack about 1/8" inward and 1/2" toward the bottom—drastically improved clearance, finally allowing a dual-fan setup. A few standout details: They included a custom Wera Torx driver. If you know tools, you know that's a premium touch they didn't even have to include. Aesthetics: The all-black finish perfectly matches my color-coordinated build and will for others. Quiet Efficiency: Paired with "be quiet!" Pure Wings-3 140mm fans at 60–80% duty cycle (1000–1200 RPM), the rig is whisper-quiet. I’ve stuck with air cooling over AIOs for the reliability and ease of installation. In a climate-controlled room with positive airflow, this unit is a beast. If you’re debating the upgrade for the clearance improvements alone, it’s worth every penny.

reviews.title: The Last Case You'll Ever Need — A True Builder's Masterpiece
reviews.comment: I've built in a lot of cases over the years, but the Cooler Master Cosmos Alpha is on a completely different level. From the moment it arrived, it was clear this wasn't just a case — it's a platform built for people who are serious about their builds. The sliding motherboard tray is a game-changer. Reconfiguring between air and liquid cooling layouts used to mean hours of frustration. Now it's genuinely painless, and being able to fine-tune the GPU distance from the side panel is a thoughtful touch I didn't know I needed until I had it. Same goes for the adjustable fan bracket — sliding it closer to your hottest components to dial in airflow feels like something every case should have offered years ago. The thermal headroom here is absurd in the best way. The two pre-installed 200x38mm fans move serious air out of the box, and knowing I can scale all the way up to 15 fans and a 420mm radiator means I'll never outgrow this case no matter how extreme my next upgrade gets. Compatibility is another huge win. E-ATX/EEB motherboard support, room for GPUs up to 400mm, a 240mm PSU bay, and seven tool-free drive bays — this thing swallows a full enthusiast build without breaking a sweat. If you're an overclocker, a modder, or just someone who refuses to compromise, the Cosmos Alpha is the answer. It's the apex of what FreeForm 2.0 is all about, and it absolutely earns that title. Highly recommended.
reviews.author: Daniel

reviews.title: Best Case Ever Designed Beyond Any Doubt
reviews.comment: Absolutely stunning case. I've had 2 earlier models the C700P and the C700M I missed anniversary edition because it sold out so fast, I wasn't going to miss this one at all. This case is even MORE advanced than thte c700P. It allows you to hold up the video card with a dynamic shelf, the mother board can also slide, I used the slide above the case for the liquid cooling radiator that also slides!! There was even an extra fan to extract the heat behind the case for the cables.. the filters are all magnetic, the segregated powersupply area was more advanced than before and the dedicated metal covers for the cable management are top tier, this is a total upgrade! On the c700p the glass would also fall off, NOT this design, they have claps that are actually holding the glass door! WELL DONE!
reviews.author: Brandon Heinrich

reviews.title: Beautifuly painful
reviews.comment: I'll keep this review short. This case is gorgeous, but boy, is it quite a pain to work with. The good- The case itself is gorgeous. Sure, the grilles are the only spots where there is plastic (which I don't mind), but overall,  the build quality is very solid. This thing is also incredibly customizable, with the whole free from 2.0 gimmick, you have a lot of options on how you want the layout to be. The doors also have a very simple lift mechanism, making putting on and taking off the side doors really easy, especially during building and maintenance. The case is also super spacious, so be prepared to have big things inside, otherwise it will look very empty. The bad- This thing by itself is heavy, and depending on what parts you get, this build, fully loaded, can weigh up to 70+ pounds. Making it a workout to just move. I already knew it would be one, but it's something to keep in mind. Free Form 2.0, while a really nice gimmick, has its issues. On the sliding motherboard tray, even when tightened still had movement, so when plugging in cables or trying to put my GPU in the mobo tray, it would slide back instead of staying in place. Also, the tray never really slid the best, either, which made the struggle a little worse. I'll probably add on to this review as I continue to upgrade my build, but as first impressions go. It's a stunningly huge case, even better in person. But be prepared to put on some elbow grease, you'll be fighting this case a lot more than actually building.
reviews.author: Tyler

reviews.title: Product looks great but amazon dropped the ball
reviews.comment: Paid for next day shipping.  Still hasn't been shipped. Said delivery Jan 29th. Now it say March 5th and on the item page it says get by Feb 7th.
reviews.author: Derek Dechy

reviews.title: The Cosmo Alpha Case is Future Proof.
reviews.comment: The Cosmo Alpha is the best case I have ever own. It looks great and the case quality is amazing! Money well spent!
reviews.author: Wes-T3

reviews.title: Great Cooling Power and Exemplary Quality!
reviews.comment:
This cooler is made by Noctua. This is my first purchase from them, and they live up the their reputation for excellent quality and performance!
I was using the stock AMD cooler (Wraith?) that came with my Ryzen 3600. While the stock cooler was adequate for simple tasks such as word processing or the Internet, it fell short for intensive tasks such as video encoding. Starting an encode would immediately shoot temperatures up to 95°C and stay there, severely throttling the CPU.
After installing this cooler (it comes with a tube of Noctua's own quality NT-H1 thermal paste) and a fan curve adjustment to accommodate the greater cooling performance, the CPU temperatures are much lower and the computer is much quieter! Idle temperatures are about 32°–36°C. Testing the performance with some video encoding, temperatures where at 70°–75° after an hour and the CPU never throttled once—Full boost throughout the entire process!
Mounting the cooler was simple and straightforward with excellent instructions and diagrams. All necessary parts are included in the box. The AMD and Intel components are separate to avoid mixing them up. Extra mounting pads and brackets where provided in case you wanted to install a second fan in a push/pull configuration.
The black color looks great, as black goes with everything! (No, I am not just saying that because the rest of my build is black as well.) I also used the included paste to reapply the thermal compound on my PS4 Pro, with more left over for future applications as well!
Overall, Noctua has earned a costumer in me and a spot on my recommendation list.
reviews.author: Raymond

reviews.title: A beast of a cooler. Both functional and gorgeous.
reviews.comment:
I bought this to replace the stock cooler for the i7 9700f that came in my prebuilt. The product was packaged beautifully, with a small box for mounting hardware, thermal paste and a few other accessories in the top. There was a large box containing the cooler itself in the bottom. (edited) 
The installation took about 2 hours (mind you, I am new at upgrading computers)  and would have taken a lot less time if I had realized initially that the back panel of my PC case was removable and had a cutout allowing me to access the rear of my motherboard.
Noctua provides very well written and clear instructions for how to mount this cooler. In the box, you will find instructions for both Intel and AMD platforms. If you're building a system and you know what you're doing, it'll probably take no more than 10-15 minutes for you to put this cooler in. If you're swapping a cooler like me and have no clue what to do, you'll get by with the instructions in 1-2 hours, maybe faster. (edited) 
As for noise, when my system is idling, I don't hear this cooler at all. At full load, it ramps up to about 1200RPM, but the noise level remains minimal and it is certainly a huge improvement over my original cooler. Sound tests show it peaking at around 30 decibels, whereas my old cooler would top out around 55.
The performance of this cooler is beyond anything I could have expected. My CPU used to idle at around 55C and would heat up to 88+ with my old stock cooler. Thanks to the NHU 12 S I am now seeing idle temps at 33C and peak temps no higher than 55. Overall , my system feels much more stable thanks to this upgrade.
Lastly, this cooler is absolutely gorgeous. I've made a few upgrades since purchasing my prebuilt and I think it really pulls them all together. I did make the mistake of not measuring the inside of my case, however, and I failed to account for the raised position of the body of the cooler over the CPU. The heatsink has a couple of protrusions on the top of it which have prevented me from being able to place the glass panel back onto my case once I finished swapping coolers. My case is 19.61" x 7.28" x 16.57", so if your case has a similar width 7.28", you might want to consider buying the smaller NHU 9S cooler.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: The little cooler that could
reviews.comment:
I purchased this cooler to cool an AMD Ryzen R5 3600 in a Fractal Design Meshify C case. The stock cooler for the 3600 is anemic (and loud) and the goal for this build was quiet operation. After reading a bunch of reviews, I opted for this cooler (even though it was more expensive than some of the Scythe options I was looking at and I love Scythe products) as the black color would look nice in the case and the emphasis in reviews on how silent it operated.
The install was extremely easy. The only complaint I have is that you have to remove the fan from the cooling tower to install it; in contrast I can pull and install my Scythe Fuma 2 without having to do so (though I often remove the middle fan for ease when blowing apart my build for various reasons). I found the spring clips on the Noctua for securing fan to be a bit more temperamental than Scythe's, but no so much that it warrants giving this cooler anything less than 5 stars.
The cooler comes with Noctua's NT-H1 thermal paste, which is my go-to paste for my builds, so that's a nice feature if you don't already have a syringe of this lying around (and would set you back about $13 US to buy separately).
The real proof of what a gem this cooler is appears when you first power on your system. The fan spins to life without so much as a whisper. Even under load you can barely notice it running. I repeatedly had to look at the cooler to make sure the fan was spinning (the case fans are also very quiet as is the EVGA 2060 SC Ultra GPU in the case). I was very impressed at the noise level. What's even more astonishing is how effective this thin tower, single fan cooler is at cooling the CPU at such a low noise level. Noctua really knows what they are doing with their cooler and fan designs. The recipient absolutely loves the performance and noise level of the build as well as the aesthetics of the components (cooler included), so thanks for making me look good, Noctua!
reviews.author: isaki

reviews.title: Best Budget Air Cooler I’ve Used – Insane Performance for the Price
reviews.comment: The Thermalright Peerless Assassin 120 SE has honestly been one of the best upgrades I’ve put in my PC. I’ve been using it for a while now in my setup, and the performance has been amazing for an air cooler in this price range. It keeps temps low and stable even under load, and it just quietly does its job without any drama. The dual 120mm PWM fans move a lot of air while still staying fairly quiet, and the 6 heat pipe design really seems to make a difference in heat dissipation. Installation was straightforward, and it’s been fully reliable across long gaming and everyday use sessions. It also fits a wide range of sockets, which made it perfect for my setup. Overall, it’s easily one of the best or the best value cooler out there.
reviews.author: Tanner Pomeroy

reviews.title: For the price, its a really great cooler.
reviews.comment: My Ibuypower water cooler failed on my system. (I discovered this is very common). I was debating on either getting a water cooler or going to Air cooling.  I checked a lot of videos online and this air cooler kept coming up in the top 5 replacement recommendations over and over again.  (search water coolers vs Air coolers) Since I don't do any overclocking and the fact that they are much more reliable, I bought this unit. It works really great.  It cost so much less than a water cooler and (in my opinion) is easier to install that a water cooler unit with hoses and radiator and cpu block. Positives: Very Affordable Cools very well Very well made Package comes with everything you need. (different cpu socket mounts and thermal paste) Extremely reliable.  (no worries about coolant leaks or pump failure or in my case, clogged lines) The fans that come with it seemed pretty quiet. (more than my cheap water cooler fans) Negatives: Can be a little difficult to install. The most difficult part was installing the fans. The instructions could be better. (they're not horrible). I do recommend watching online videos. Its big, you definitely need to make sure you have enough room in your case. Additional Recommendations: The thermal paste that comes with the package is ok, but I would highly recommend buying a high quality NON CONDUCTIVE thermal past. (Thermal Grizzly Kryonaut, Artic-mx4, Cooler Master MasterGel Pro v2 etc) This is important! Make sure its NONCONDUCTIVE.  Some thermal paste uses metallic ingredients to aid in thermal conductivity. The problem with this is that if you apply too much, it can go into the cpu electronic components and damage your system.  With noncoductive thermal paste, this isn't a issue so you don't really need to be too exact. (If its a little too much, it doesn't hurt anything.) This Air cooler also comes in single or double tower configurations, if your case can support it, I would definitely get the double tower. Make sure you get the fans installed/oriented correctly. I would also recommend installing cpu temperature monitoring software as well to make sure that everything is working correctly. I would definitely recommend this to anyone who wants a very reliable and very affordable air cooling option.
reviews.author: Jeff M

reviews.title: Cool Runnings
reviews.comment: Works great so far. 10900k at idle was sitting at around 30°c when the ambient temp in the room was 85°f. This does come with its own tube of thermal paste but I had some leftover Thermal Grizzly Kryonaut so I used that instead. Not sure how good or had the Thermalright paste is but its a pretty big tube of it, its enough for 5-6 PCs. Can't comment on how loud it is, I couldn't hear it but my room has a lot of background noise. All in all installation was fairly simple (its pretty much like any other after market air cooler) and it did include a 4pin splitter so if you only have one cpu fan header you can still run both fans that come with this cooler. And for the price its a no trainer. This cooler is essentially the modern era version of the Hyper 212 Evo.
reviews.author: Steven Carousos

reviews.title: Great CPU Cooling for a Good Price
reviews.comment: When I built my PC five years ago I installed a Dark Rock Pro 4 for my CPU cooler. It worked very well, but over the years the fans grew louder, the cooling became less efficient, and dust began to accumulate in hard to clean places. I decided to look for an affordable replacement and settled on the Thermalright Peerless Assassin. Overall, I believe this was a very good choice. Compared to my Dark Rock Pro 4, the Thermalright Peerless Assassin was a breeze to install. The LGA 155x bracket fit my motherboard and was easy to install. The thermal paste seemed thicker than other pastes I've used, but it went on neatly and is clearly working. The spring screws seem to have secured the cooler to the brackets very well. My biggest complaint with my old cooler was installing the fans. Happily, I can report that the Peerless Assassin's fan are easy to install, and remove if needed, and are secure. In terms of performance, I'm completely satisfied. The fans are not as quiet as my Dark Rock Pro 4 when I first installed it. However, they are an acceptable low volume. My PC has an Intel Core i7-8700k CPU and the cooler has no problem keeping it between 20C to 30C while idle or under a light load. I am no longer an avid gamer, and do not play modern video games, however I did test the thermals while playing Minecraft. It kept my CPU around 40C most of the time and would briefly shoot up to 50C when loading parts of the map. At less than 40 USD this cooler is a fantastic option for CPU cooling. Its significantly less expensive than comparable coolers, is easy to install, and delivers good performance.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Great Cooling, Slight Fitment Quirks
reviews.comment: This cooler does an excellent job keeping temps under control. Even during heavier workloads, it handles heat really well and keeps everything running stable. For the price, the performance is honestly impressive and competes with much more expensive options. That said, installation took a bit more patience than expected. The mounting process isn’t difficult, but it can feel a little awkward, especially in tighter cases. Also, make sure you have enough clearance for RAM and your case, since it’s a fairly large cooler. Once it’s in, though, it’s solid—quiet, efficient, and reliable. If you don’t mind spending a few extra minutes on setup and double-checking fitment, it’s definitely worth it.
reviews.author: jimmy

reviews.title: Very big and effective
reviews.comment: This cooler is a member of group of large coolers for power hungry processors. Mine has up to 270 Watts of power requirement (I have not seen it so far, even in benchmark tests), so this cooler should be able to handle it. It does it with flair, but (there is always a “but”) it comes with the price of a big size. On my MSI motherboard it sits over memory slots and makes one M2 slot difficult to access. Not a deal breaker (install the memory first), just something to keep in mind. Works well and definitely worth it, especially considering the low cost.
reviews.author: Mirek

reviews.title: Buena compra por el precio que ofrece
reviews.comment: Excelente compra, mantiene fresco mi ryzen 5 9600x, es fácil de instalarlo que si necesitas un buen gabinete ya que es muy grande. Nota: no compres una pasta térmica ya que este enfriador de torre tiene uno en la caja, olvidé revisar a fondo ese detalle
reviews.author: Erick Chavez

reviews.title: Nice
reviews.comment: Works pretty good
reviews.author: Daniel Acosta

reviews.title: A CPU cooler worth its weight in copper!!! Have you seen how much copper cost these days!
reviews.comment: Cooling performance seems to be what stands out the most for this CPU cooler! The seven 6 mm heat pipes takes care of the heat extremely well! And doing so without very much noise in the process. I came up with 27 DB when pushing the fans, which I feel was outstanding! The way this cooler produces air flow is also unique. The way the fins are mounted keeps the air flowing in an up and down vertical wave that keeps your CPU in a very happy place! Never went above high 60's Celsius when gaming. Overall for its price you get a very decent and game excelling CPU. And not to mention, a very easy install As you are given all the parts to make it go without issues all the way through. So if you're looking for an inexpensive air cooling PC cooler, for the price, this should definitely be on your list!
reviews.author: Skeeter

reviews.title: Ridiculously good for the price
reviews.comment: Fantastic cooler, especially for this price. Mounts easily, looks good, and keeps my 9800x3d ice cold Fits into the tiny Lian Li a3 if you’re wondering as well.
reviews.author: S Holmes

reviews.title: It's new to me 10-10
reviews.comment: It is a used/refurbished unit! When I got it it looked brand new, had all the cables you need. It came in a generic brown box but was packed pretty good. I put it in my dell 3630 and it went in no problem and works super well! It dropped my temps by 5-10°c! I was skeptical at first since I have had good luck with used/refurbished but I would highly recommend this to anyone!
reviews.author: Dustin

reviews.title: review
reviews.comment: muy bueno la temperatura bajo mucho lo malo venia sin manual
reviews.author: Darwin Silva

reviews.title: Item was not in original packaging, just shoved in a cardboard box.
reviews.comment: This did not come in the original box and was missing screws and no instruction manual for installation.  I had the appropriate stuff from other corsair coolers I have installed on other pc's, just letting you know there is no expectation of stuff you order to be new in original box with all the parts/instructions.  The cooler was stuffed in a cardboard box with paper wadding to protect the cooler during shipping but there is probably no way to return it if I have problems with it since it was not in the original packaging.
reviews.author: Jennifer Ross

reviews.title: Good Product
reviews.comment: Very easy to install and works literally with two connections. Heads up: RGB requires seperate connections. Recommend buying an RGB splitter with SATA power if you don’t have a motherboard with a RGB out. Comes with adapters for the RGB and fan and cooler power. All these comments saying “lack of instructions” or “it was just thrown in a box” don’t do the product justice. Came in a box that had good protection of the component, and it’s as simple as screwing it to your motherboard, and then the radiator and fan together to the case. Really not that hard.
reviews.author: carey

reviews.title: Fits Alienware R12 - a must have upgrade for the higher end CPUs which are thermal bound
reviews.comment: Can confirm it fits in an Alienware R12 case, with a push/pull fan setup with the original fan. Tip: Plug the included splitter into the CPU_FAN jumper, bottom left of the LGA1200 socket, and plug the original top fan and new radiator fan into this, this prevent the BIOs error. Gave me a huge boost in my Passmark scores. The refurbed unit looked like new, hoses were perfect, and the thermal paste was brand new.
reviews.author: Digigator

reviews.title: be quiet! Pure Rock 3 does the job silently while looking good
reviews.comment: This is the first be quiet! Pure Rock 3 heatsinks I worked with. It's easy to install and keeps my Intel Core Ultra 5 250K Plus nice and cool. No problem with noise levels, very quiet. It does come with pre-applied thermal paste. The all-black appearance is a welcomed look in this age of bright lights and rainbow colors.
reviews.author: Patrick F. Sullivan

reviews.title: Awesome Air Cooler
reviews.comment:
Easy to setup and super quite. It kept my i7 CPU nice and cool through every bench test I tried.
I would recommend this if your looking to cut down on noise and space without sacrificing cooling.
reviews.author: Solidchris

reviews.title: I'm surprised
reviews.comment:
I just paired this with a Ryzen 9 5900X, I had some doubts that it may not be enough since people in the reviews for the 5900X went on about needing either a monstrosity of an air cooler that takes up a ton of room or a massive water cooler to keep it cooled properly (how far are you guys overclocking this thing??), even after reading into these coolers and their website rating it for Ryzen 9 at 195W TDP. Well, my doubts were put to rest, it idles in the low to mid 40C range and running a stress test and watching it while I was working in ASUS Armory Crate today after installing, the highest I had seen was mid 70C range and I had ran through some more of the demanding stuff to see what it would do, no throttling, no warnings, no blue screens, no problem. I am also not overclocking it and have no intention to do so. It was also pretty easy to install as long as you follow the directions, everything was metal aside from the spacers that fit onto the screws for the AMD mounting bracket.
This cooler isn't small either, I have a wider Zalman case and it is just tall enough to where it fits without impeding the glass side cover, but any further I wouldn't be able to get the side cover on, so make sure it will fit your case (my last case on an older machine I had to cut a hole in the cover to fit a larger cooler, bummer). The good thing is that it doesn't block the RAM sockets or anything else on my B550 Plus. I did not want to get a water cooler, and I'm glad this worked out and I'll probably buy more of their products in the future. You may also want to consider buying thermal paste with it, when I got mine it said it was already applied but it was not and thankfully I had some in my desk drawer (I had a tube of Corsair TM30), and I did see some reviews of apparent mishandling of the packaging that caused it to shift and smear paste all over inside the box.
reviews.author: Matt

reviews.title: Very quiet
reviews.comment: Very quiet and efficient at cooling. Just apply some thermal paste and even in my small case the installation was easy and fit perfectly. Looks great with all the lighting I have in my case.
reviews.author: Vladimort Poopin

reviews.title: Thermal paste comes on the pipes already!
reviews.comment: So far so good, Ryzen 5 9600x holding strong: max 68C under load. It jumps a bit when idle around 40c ish, I remember that happening with my last CPU for awhile until the tech settled in. Or my memory is off but it’s the strongest cpu I ever owned. Not a sound coming from the PC at all. I regret not going bigger for the CPU cause of how well this is doing temp wise. I don’t like dealing with water cooling.
reviews.author: Koshernet

reviews.title: Quality cou cooler
reviews.comment: Paired with the hub and a Nzxt H6 flow case. Awesome design and really simple to install. Absolutely quite and the color settings are nice. Moves a lot of heat. The cam software works great and has some nice customization options. Keeps my Ryzen 9 CPU chilly. Added the rgb fan unit and it's a perfect.
reviews.author: Toby

reviews.title: Good pick
reviews.comment: Works great! Easy install keeps the cup nice and cool.
reviews.author: D’zyre

reviews.title: Great buy
reviews.comment: Does a great job cooling my CPU. Ibpower game and have no issues.
reviews.author: Christopher S.

reviews.title: Good product
reviews.comment: Works as intend. No performance issues. Pumps can be a little loud at times as expected with any water cooling
reviews.author: Sawyer

reviews.title: Good when it works
reviews.comment: Cooling a 9800x3d it idles in the high 30s. Stays very cool. You definitely need to have the Nzxt Cam software though or you’ll have no control over pump speed unless you play around in bios. Pump is kind of noisy when running at full speed, sounds like an old school HDD writing files. Update : after a couple a weeks I was downloading a file and the fans went crazy. CPU spiked to 90 degrees. The NzxtCam software couldn’t connect to the AIO. Pump just stopped running. I’m an IT technician by trade so it didn’t bother me initially but after updating Bios (the new 550 boards had an issue with usb enumeration) , that didn’t fix the issue, uninstalling the device in device manager, uninstalling nzxtcam, that didn’t work. Finally the fix was to use RevoUninstaller and remove that crap, delete all registry entries, unplug the pc from the wall, drain the power supply, turn on pc and reinstall everything. Completely unacceptable.
reviews.author: vwsunangel

reviews.title: Amazing cooler!
reviews.comment: Great AIO cooler! This cooler was significantly better than my tower cooler, my tower cooler (dark rock slim) averaging around 50 to 60 Celsius, and with this cooler, it went down to 40 to 50 Celsius, granted I have a 7600x CPU, but I bought it for aesthetics, and it looks amazing of course! Installing this though, took me about 3.5 hours to try setting this up, took way too long, but the mounting wasn't so bad, it was easy, not too difficult. connectivity works just fine, needing iCUE to work properly, it had plenty of cables verifying in size but make sure you use the right one, I personally used a youtube video so I knew i didn't do anything wrong and installed it right. The only negative I'd say is that, theres so many cables, about 6 of them? compared to just 1 cable for my previous cooler but for the RGB and aesthetics? so worth it!
reviews.author: Ian Sanchez

reviews.title: Highly recommend for the gamers
reviews.comment: Built my first new PC in 10 years and chose the parts carefully as I know I won’t be able to afford another for a while.  And I wanted to go with an all White build as I like the look, especially when all the lights are set to white too.  Went with the Corsair AIO because every PC I have built for me or others I have always used Corsair and never had an issue That combined with the looks and lcs info screen made this the obvious choice.  The quality is there for everyone to see and it just feels well made When it came to installation it was very straight forward and before putting it in place I was a little concerned about the pre applied paste.  It just didn’t look like enough but I trusted Corsairs judgement on this.  Everything is included for installation on Intel and Amd bird as which I am going with an AMD 9800X3D Got it installed and finished the rest of the build and hit the switch.  Was greeted with a beautifully clear lcd screen showing the Corsair splash screen and once windows fired up I installed the Icue software to provide the temp info for the lcd. Also have to mention the ability to show images and custom graphics on the display is awesome. Everything was very easy to follow and I have to say I am very impressed with the temps.  On idle the PC sits around 30c and when in a heavy load the max I have seen it reach was 80c but on average when gaming it stays around the 50c mark Overall extremely happy with the outcome and my choice of AIO
reviews.author: Steve

reviews.title: Great AIO, Corsair makes good stuff!
reviews.comment: You know, what sold me on this was the temp display. I have a Ryzen 7 and I considered the 3 fan, but it would have been overkill. As far as cooling, this does a fantastic job. As far as system link connections, this is a game changer. I honestly don't think I'll put any other fan type in my cases in the future. 1 cable linking all my fans? What a time to be alive. I bought another fan and chained it off of one side of the radiator. If my 4000x case didn't already have AF-120s mounted to the front into a lighting core I would have replaced those as well. The system is quiet. I walk in the room and I honestly can't tell if it's on or not. Everything stays cool. The system link and lighting core sync up and the plug-ins for my gigabyte board and msi GPU work well. iCUE gets better every day. I really like that I can set device memory mode and turn off icue if necessary or in my case turn off the lighting when I lock my system and walk away. I highly recommend this AIO, but if you want even more color, the "groove" modular piece puts off even more light and you can swap it out for the LCD. The modular pieces are easy to swap.
reviews.author: Michael

reviews.title: Corsair Titan RX 360 - a standout in the AIO crowd
reviews.comment: Corsair gets a bad wrap sometimes and with a market so flooded with different AIOs, it’s rare a product stands out as much as the Titan Rx 360. The first thing that really struck was the packaging and build quality. This Titan Rx feels like a premium product, well made and packaged. Clear instructions for install. And it looks great. Beautiful, crisp screen that can show anything from GIFs to temperature or power draw. Great color from the LEDs. All of which is controlled through the Corsair iCue software which is MILES ahead of anything else I have ever used for RGB or fans. The software is clean, easy to use, with tons of options to dial in LED color, patterns, fan speed. The fans are quiet and responsive, kicking in quickly when they need to keep my 9800x3d. Have to say I am more than happy with my purchase. I feel that for the money, I got a premium quality product that does exactly what I need from it and would recommend it to others.
reviews.author: Mike

reviews.title: Excellent Cooler
reviews.comment: This is by far best aio I have tried so far! I bought this because my Deep cool 360mm aio pump failed and caused constant crashes, it was a decent cooler, but this one though is a whole different beast! Stock, before tuning my chip it would keep my Intel i7 13700k around 41c idle and 62c heavy CPU games! But after tuning in bios, I am now sitting cool around 31c idle and 38c heavy gaming full settings all ray tracing enabled! I do have push pull setup with 6 fans on the rad. The rad has some thought put into it when it comes to the fins/airflow they are perfectly spaced not smudged together allowing great airflow! Allowing it to run quite even under heavy loads, with the balanced tune on ICUE not the extreme, with these temps I have no need in the extreme setting. I am very impressed with this cooler, if you are looking for a good looking and good working cooler, this is it!
reviews.author: Jerrry

reviews.title: Impressively engineered and high performing product.
reviews.comment:
Packaging: 10/10
Instructions: 10/10
Build quality: 10/10
Cooling Performance: 10/10
Noise: 8.8/10
Price 10/10
The packaging is premium quality and I was very impressed. They obviously dedicated a lot of time and detail into designing it, and the unboxing experience was something that they clearly had a focus on.
The included manual is very detailed with complete step by step instructions with diagrams for each step, for both Intel and AMD CPUs in several languages.
I replaced a Noctua NH-D15 with this EK 360mm AIO and have incredibly low temps under load and am now able to aggressively undervolt my 5900x even more with PBO and am getting much better single and multi-threaded performance. With this aggressive OC I am still only hitting a high temp of 71C under extended full loads on Cinebench 2026.
There is no observable pump noise whatsoever. The fans are quite high quality but got a bit whiny for me around the 1300-1350 rpm range.
The unit comes with preapplied thermal paste on the copper cold plate and also with a tube of their own thermal paste for future repastes. The hose connections at the pump are adjustable and can be rotated to help best orient and route the hoses through your case. The cover in the center of the pump can also be rotated.
I paid $119.95 for the unit. This beats everything on the market for 360mm AIOs in price/performance ratio in my opinion except for probably the ARCTIC Liquid Freezer III which is $30 cheaper and has nearly as good performance with it's massive radiator.
If you are pushing overclocks and want the best performance that you can get, and don't care about RBG nonsense, buy this.
reviews.author: J

reviews.title: Good cooler
reviews.comment: Swapped from deepcool 240 to this 360 and saw my 5800x go from avg 80-90c to avg 50-60c. Great 👍
reviews.author: BR1ZZO

reviews.title: Works.......can get loud when it ramps up
reviews.comment: I moved my rig into a antecs performance 1ft case. Figured I would go head and change out the cpu and cooling all at once. I had a 3800x and upgraded to a 5800x3d. They have the same tdp.......hot. While gaming it runs around 51 to 53 c. My case has 3 140's in the front and one 120 in the rear. Very good air flow. This was mounted on the top. When you boot up or a game is loading it will ramp up and its loud. After game gets going fan speeds will lower. My rig sits 1.5 feet away level with me. I can hear the fans at all times. I notice this because the case I had before ran with four 200mm fans........silent.
reviews.author: Nick C

reviews.title: The Most Powerful AIO Cooler for Intel i9-13900K CPU
reviews.comment:
For those who seek a maximum sustained performance of the Intel i9-13900K CPU or its equivalent, the EK Nucleus CR360 AIO Liquid CPU Cooler is one of the best liquid cooling options as of 2023. With this AIO, I was able to push Cinebench R23 score above 40,000 (40,100 in my benchmark test), where the Intel i9-13900K CPU was overclocked and all the power limits were removed in the BIOS. The new score represents a 6% improvement over the 37,800 score obtained from the built-in AIO CPU cooler (ThermalTake Water 3.0 240mm ARGB Sync CPU Waterblock Cooling System) on the same i9-13900K based PC.
During the benchmark’s 10-minute run, the new AIO was able to keep the average CPU Package Power at 315~320W, while the built-in one was only able to keep the power at 245W. The extra power draw contributed to the performance gains that would improve CPU-intensive tasks, e.g. the rendering of intermediate- and long-duration videos where both CPU & GPU are heavily utilized, complex video editing where some of the edits are performed by CPU instead of GPU, RAW photo editing and RAW-to-JPEG conversion where the work is done by CPU.
On the other hand, the EK Nucleus CR360 AIO cooler is unnecessary for those who only occasionally need a peak performance of the Intel i9-13900K CPU for a short burst of a few seconds. In this situation, there’re cheaper alternatives like 240mm AIO CPU coolers.

The included System Hub makes cable management and control through iCUE much easier. Everything feels high-quality and well-designed. Installation was straightforward, but keep in mind this is a large 420mm AIO, so you need a compatible full tower or spacious case. ✅ Excellent thermal performance ✅ Very quiet operation ✅ Beautiful, customizable RGB ⚠️ Requires a large case Highly recommended for high-performance CPUs and premium builds.

reviews.title: Whisper-Quiet and Excellent Temps – Setup Was Smooth
reviews.comment: I picked up the Corsair iCUE Link Titan 360 RX to cool my new build, and I’ve been really impressed so far. This is Corsair’s latest 360mm AIO with their new iCUE Link ecosystem, and I wasn’t sure what to expect—but everything just worked. Usage: I installed it with no issues on an Intel [insert your CPU model] inside a mid-tower case. The iCUE Link system made cable management much cleaner than my last setup, and it booted right up without any firmware hassles or fan curve weirdness. Pros: Extremely quiet – even under load, the system stays silent Cool and stable – CPU temps have been consistently healthy so far Clean build – the iCUE Link cables cut down on clutter Looks great – RGB is tasteful and well diffused No setup issues – everything worked out of the box for me Cons: You’ll need an available USB 2.0 header for the hub iCUE software still isn’t perfect, but it’s stable enough for me Tips: Update iCUE before installation if you haven’t used it in a while Try mounting the pump head upright—the Corsair logo looks better aligned that way Don’t forget to enable custom fan curves in iCUE if you want to fine-tune your setup later Verdict: If you’re looking for a premium AIO that’s quiet, cools well, and makes your build look clean and modern, this cooler nails it. Setup was smoother than expected, and performance has been solid. Highly recommended if you’re building in the Corsair ecosystem or just want less cable clutter.

reviews.title: top notch AIO
reviews.comment: came exactly as expected. it was super easy to put together and install. probably one of the smoothest AIO installs i’ve ever had to do. it also looks super nice in my pc. the temp control is also top notch. it’s super quiet unless you amp up the speed of the fans but that’s to be expected. also the price is great for this - on corsair it’s at least $200+. the cables can be a little short but that’s also just case dependent. overall 10/10 i would purchase again.
reviews.author: Dani Vogler

reviews.title: Fantastic Cooler, but Expensive. Extremely Quiet
reviews.comment: Can't say enough good things about this cooler, with the one draw back being that it is very pricey. However, it does come with 2 of Noctua's new NF-12Ax25 fans which by themselves are $30 each.  So the actual heatsink is only 1/3 the total price and is a consideration when looking at the cost/value proposition. Heatsink: The heatsink itself is very good. Has 7 heatpipes which is the most I've seen in a 120mm tower cooler. It also doesn't cover/block any of my ram slots (even on my mini-ITX board) with the fans mounted. My Coolermaster Hyper 212 EVO with the fan mounted would still cover the first ram slot, so I'm not sure how Noctua managed to pull this off as according to the specs the Noctua bare heatsink is 7-8mm wider than the Coolermaster.  Mounting system is typical Noctua SecureFirm and fantastic. Fans: The 2 included fans are Noctua's new fans that took them 3 years to develop. There's never been so much hype on a fan than these, and you should read up on why it took so long to develop, it's an interesting article. What I can say after using them is that they are much quieter at a given RPM than my other high performance fans. I have to put my ear with in an inch or two to hear them under normal operation (about 50%-60% speed is where they normally running at) and they are barely audible at 100% when they spin up to full speed when I first turn on my PC.  Note that the fans have pretty short power cables, and the heatsink does not include extension cables like you get if you purchase the fans separately. Performance:  I am using one fan on the heatsink in a push configuration and the other fan as a case exhaust fan about one inch away from the heatsink. So it's similar to the intended push/pull configuration, but with a small gap between. Under 100% synthetic load my delidded i7 7700k runs in the high 50s low 60s degrees Celsius at ~1.3v vCore and ambient temp of 24C (75F). Under real word gaming load, the CPU was running at an average 48C with occasional short spikes into the 50s. All this in a very small, but well ventilated ~13L mini-itx case. This is fantastic performance and rivals bigger coolers like the Noctua D15 but is so much easier to fit in a small mini-itx case. Overall: I think the performance of this cooler is the best you can get at this size point. Compared to my Hyper 212 EVO, it performs better, is quieter under load, doesn't cover my RAM, and has a MUCH better mounting system. All this comes at a price, it's considerably more expensive than a Hyper 212 EVO. But in my opinion it's worth it if you aren't on an extremely tight budget. Noctua products are premium products, the best of the best, and the quality shows both in performance and ease of installation.
reviews.author: Jason A Wiese

reviews.title: The Noctua legend lives on!
reviews.comment: Best temperature control of any air CPU cooler I’ve ever purchased!💯 This replaced a prior Noctua cooler, the NH-D15S, which in its right was great too. But this one ships with faster & slimmer 120mm fans & able to clear many tall RAM kits (the NH-D15S was good for the latter too), and is quieter, even on Performance Mode with some MB’s. The fans runs in full mode to 2,000 rpm, but typically slows in Performance Mode (best option). This mode allows for great control depending upon load. BTW, these are better fans than the earlier, thicker model which it replaced, the airflow is superior in both speed & lower. The cooler itself, while single tower versus dual, does an excellent job, keeping a Ryzen 7 9700X in the middle 30’s to mid 50C range during normal usage. Gaming and other high intensive usage may mean higher temperatures, but not overwhelmingly so. Just be sure to check compatibility on the Noctua site. This model is standing with their top line coolers when it comes to getting the job done. One warning, make sure your case is deep enough. Mine was a mid tower model (NZXT H5, I believe), those with mini towers need to look at a different model. I’m happy, despite the price increase. Not much we can control about this. We either pay or go for lower quality, period. I’d rather pay for peace of mind.
reviews.author: cat1092

reviews.title: Incredible cooling, but not really silent
reviews.comment: (PLEASE SEE MY EDIT AT THE BOTTOM OF THE REVIEW) Like most, I decided on this particular Noctua model because it offers excellent cooling in a relatively small form factor. This is my first "proper" air cooler. Pros: - It *does* work, and amazingly well. My system consists of a Ryzen 5 3600, an MSI X570 Motherboard, 32GB of RAM, and some M.2 drives. With the stock AMD cooler, idle temperatures (just Chrome open) were 55 to 62 degrees, which was simply insane and unacceptable. With the Noctua, my system now idles at 35 degrees. Impressive! Heavy loads never exceeded 75 (this was running Cinebench... I never actually saw those temperatures again). Con: - This is a biog deal to me. The Noctua was supposed to be "silent", as per all the reviews I read everywhere. Not so. In fact, it is considerably louder than the stock AMD cooler, and the noise is very, very noticeable in a quiet room and inside my Corsair Carbide 600Q case, which is optimized for silence and includes lots of noise-dampening materials. I suffer from hyper-accusis and a silent system is a MUST, and I'm disappointed at this aspect. I may return the cooler if I am not able to live with the noise. And this is with the noise reduction adapter that Noctua includes in the box, which does really help, although by no means makes the cooler silent. Torn... Cooling-wise, it performs admirably and I think the price is justified when you consider all the accessories included. But if you are sensitive to noise like I am, and work in a quiet room, this is *not* a silent cooler. EDIT: I take the above "con" back. I did not realize this, but it seems the fans were essentially spinning at their full speed. This is why I felt they were not really as silent as I had hoped. It turns out there is a setting in the BIOS of my motherboard (and MSI X570 Godlike) that allows you to enable "Smart Fan" mode. I selected this option and the RPM's immediately dropped from about 1800 to about 500, and the noise was gone. Just like that, the Noctua was now almost literally inaudible from a distance of about 3 feet. I strongly recommend enabling this mode and/or using a similar setting if your hardware offers it. Even *after* this change, the Noctua still keeps everything nice and cool. Fan speeds alternate between 20% and 45% and using the Windows "Balanced Plan" the CPU stays at 40 / 42 degrees. Impressive!

reviews.author: relichunter

reviews.title: Cools a non-delidded Intel I9 PERFECTLY!
reviews.comment: My computer CPU was reaching 100 degree C temps and subsequently ruined a 400 dollar motherboard and that was with water cooling. I am not sure if my water cooler was defective or what. I decide I did not want the complexity of another water cooler breakdown. So, I went with this device. I was confused about the types of thermal paste to use, some are goopy and thin and melt away and some are thick and still melt away with hot temps. So, I went with an, "Innovation Cooling Graphite Thermal Pad" (on Amazon). I was thinking it was a fail-safe approach. With those installed, my idle temps on a 12 core non delidded  I9 are 'under' 40 degrees C and the temps rarely ever hits 60 degrees under load and that is only for moments and it goes back down usually. That is with rendering huge 3D scenes with tons of geometry. You cannot go wrong with this combo Noctua NH-U12A and the thermal pads. Just check the fins for dust every few months. This cooler solved a huge heat problem for me and I am glad I am not relying on a pump working right and/or possible air bubbles in a factory sealed system... I can just look in through the side of my case and see if the fans are still running. Runs quiet too! I recommend this cooler for a non-dellidded I9 cpu and whatever else it fits.  It completely cleared my RAM and I have a large case with fans blowing in and sucking out. I thought it might be heavy on my motherboard but running as cool as it does it is not too heavy and the mounting system seems completely stable and solid. I do not plan to overclock my CPU... It is not worth possibly damaging a $1000.00 processor even if it does stay below critical temps.. Lots of RAM and dual (non overclocked) 1080ti graphics cards will provide me with the headroom I need while keeping things cool and stable on the processor end. The performance of this product far surpasses my expectations! Some complain about the look of this cooler but I prefer function over fashion. Buy it, (and the thermal pads) they are worth very single penny.
reviews.author: RexRed

reviews.title: Excellent value
reviews.comment: TBD on longevity, but this AIO took my CPU temp down from 97 degrees celsius during Battlefield 6 to about 75. I originally built my PC with a Thermalright Assassin Spirit 120 EVO DARK 70.4 CFM cooler, but as you can see it just couldn't hold up during Battlefield. Furthermore, while idle, this AIO took my CPU from 54ish degrees to around 40. Very pleased with the performance thus far. It does have a bit of a high pitched ring while running. A lot of people probably will never hear it, but I can. A bit annoying, but not a huge deal.
reviews.author: Wyatt

reviews.title: Good AIO
reviews.comment: I've only about 6 days into this PC building put together, so take my words with a grain of salt, I can't really speak to the endurance of the AIO. With that said, my cooling is great, the bracket was very easy to install, my CPU is performing very well and the radiator while top mounted on my system works as a great exhaust system. If you have three fans of the same size bringing air into your case, I find that this plus one auxiliary exhaust fan (there is some resistance from the radiator) keeps my case in relatively negative pressure with great thermal performance. The water block looks good, it's not super gaudy or anything and you can control it with whatever ARGB software you want. I'm using the gigabyte control center And it works fine. I'll edit this if anything goes wrong, but I anticipate getting roughly 5 to 7 years out of this water cooler. In my photo you might notice that one of the fans doesn't have ARGB, that's my own doing as I just did not daisy chain the last one because I had already done my cable management and forgot it lol. Noise level is super low, if I have any issues I'll come and edit this review.

reviews.comment: bought this to stop the jet-engine noise and it delivered. Under load it stays surprisingly quiet and keeps temps under control. Install was smooth and the tubing length worked perfectly in my case. Now my GPU is the loud one… and I’m coming for it next.

reviews.title: Amazing value beginner AIO
reviews.comment: I've never had water cooling or an AIO before. I got this one based on the Tom's hardware review and the great price point. The braided hoses are a little stiff and makes placing the cooling block a little tricky, but otherwise the installation is pretty straightforward and easy on AM4. I'm sure I could lower temps under load, but the fans would have to run harder and louder and I've found a good balance of performance to noise. The included fans are great. Nice and quiet and the ARGB looks great. We'll see how the quality and longevity is, but pretty impressed so far.

I'm very sensitive to noise, as my hearing is very sensitive and I hear many things that other people don't, and this cooler has been an excellent purchase because it only makes noise with the fans and only does so when it really needs to.

reviews.title: Great cooler
reviews.comment: 10m after opening the box, the installation was done. The unit's cooling is quite good, significantly better under a heavy load than the unit it replaced.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Perfect Match for AMD 9 9950X – Cool and Quiet - 420m
reviews.comment: The cooler’s performance has been excellent. With AMD 9 9950X, completely stock (out of the box, no overclocking or voltage tuning), inside an ASUS ROG Hyperion GR701 case. During a 6-minute stress test, the CPU maintained boost frequencies around 5.2 GHz, with package temperatures staying around 68°C. Power consumption reached approximately 200W under full load. VRM temperatures remained well controlled, and the fans never reached their 2400 RPM maximum. Even under heavy stress, the noise level was extremely low. During 2K gaming, CPU temperatures stayed in the mid-60s, with boost frequencies ranging between 5.5–5.7 GHz. Power consumption while gaming fluctuated between 120W and 160W. Fan speeds remained around 1400 RPM, with very low and unobtrusive noise levels. Overall, excellent thermal efficiency and impressively quiet operation. Installation was very easy — the fans come pre-mounted on the heatsink, and the mounting process is straightforward, requiring no prior experience. Additionally, the radiator is 38mm thick, noticeably thicker than the typical 27mm radiators found in most standard AIO coolers, contributing to its strong cooling performance.
reviews.author: Muhanand Samara

reviews.title: Completely solved temperature issues but has a few downsides to consider.
reviews.comment: I'm writing this as of 2 days of use after installation on an I9-14900k, one of the hottest-running and most troubled processors on the market. It is installed on the front panel of a Fractal North XL case, with fans in front in an intake configuration. This seems ideal to intake cold air instead of using the already hot air within the case to cool the radiator, and to avoid the convection heat from being at the top of the case. These conditions seem minimal but should increase thermal performance. The Bad: *Amazon lied about the shipping. Under the product listing, it claimed next day shipping, and then when it was in my cart it would only offer 2-day shipping. *Installation was a little weird as there was no rear bracket and I used the one I had from another aftermarket brace, which fit. Not a big deal for me, but some people may be confused or be missing a back bracket for LGA1700 chips. *Tightening the 2 screws on the pump header was a bit nerve-wracking since they had such heavy resistance and there's no physical instruction book. *The front panel of the Fractal North XL doesn't seem to click in fully with these big fans in the front, but I'll figure that out later. *The noise at full load is significant, but not really a problem for me since my headset has good ANC. *The "pseudo-fan with small fan inside" just magnetically clips onto the pump header. I'd feel better if it clipped on or screwed on. *The fan power cords that go through the water tubes are not long enough for the config I chose. I had to pinch the power cords a bit to get them in the front of the radiator. The Good: *That said, this cooler completely solved my temperature issues. I previously had an NXZT Kraken 360mm, and it was absolute garbage. One of the fan bearings went bad and made a ton of noise after just one year. The LED screen on the pump header never worked. It was either defective or just entirely inadequate for my processor, which is INSANE for how much I paid for that AIO (320$ at the time). I have been through hell trying to get this processor in a functional state between the BIOS updates and custom BIOS settings to limit voltage, and I was regularly pegging 100c on Battlefield 6 and other demanding games. I have it thermal throttled to 100c, but was is not ideal. *With the Liquid Freezer III Pro 420, I have not seen temps over 70c peak. Battlefield 6 causes that peak but runs at around 60-65c. Cities Skylines 2 is running at 55c currently. *The price point for this beast of a cooler cannot be beaten, especially if you don't need the LED version. All the bad points honestly negated by how relieved I am that I have my temps under control with this ridiculous processor plagued by issues. Whoever wrote the default intel settings and/or bios code must have lazily used AI and didn't troubleshoot or test it at all.
reviews.author: Troy

reviews.title: Liquid cooling doesn't get much better than this
reviews.comment: The good: -Keeps a 9800X3D system cool as can be (around 40c idle/45c typical load) with fan speeds as low as 50%, so there's plenty of thermal headroom. -Quiet as a mouse.  I'm fairly certain my chassis fans are louder than this thing. -Unlike the last two CLC's I've built with, the fans are already pre-mounted (as exhaust) so there's a step saved. -With the sole exception of the mounting screws, assembly and installation was a breeze. -The non-RGB model, at least, is crazy good value for the overall performance. The not-so-good -The included MX-6 paste was extremely thick, almost to the point of being a bit lumpy, and preferred to stick to the tube's nozzle rather than the CPU IHS, making it's application much more difficult than I'm used to.  Based on thermals, I was still able to get it done correctly and it's working as intended. -No printed manual is included, just some QR codes the bring up a YouTube video.  While the video is certainly adequate, a small set of printed diagrams would be much easier to reference than trying to awkward seek to a specific point on a video with my phone. -The mounting screws on the pump block were a bit difficult to line up with the brackets, and it took me a few tries to finally get them both started.
reviews.author: Casey Chilbeck

reviews.title: This Cooler works well, it's a beast, and it fits in the NZXT H7 Flow 2024.
reviews.comment: I waited to write this because I wanted to give this monster a useful review. After I installed it in my NZXT H7 Flow 2024 and fired it up there were a few issues I wanted to look at. The fans were incredibly loud. I'm no stranger to loud fans but these are mechanically loud, not the noise of air getting the crap beat out of it. I ran the fans up and down their rpm ranges, the only place I could run them with acceptable noise was 25-30%. Then I hooked up the fans one at a time hoping I had one bad one and couple of good ones. One was a little quieter but not by much, these "pro" fans are louder than my bathroom fan and I'm not joking. I took them out and replaced them with other high performance fans I have. These are supposed to be good fans, with a name like "ARCTIC P14 PRO fan" I expected better. You shouldn't have to shop for better fans after you install a new AIO with supposedly premium fans. At the price point this is a fantastic cooler, it cools my 14900k build like no other. I'd buy another in a heart beat. I will not be returning it! Just know you are going to be replacing the fans, even if you wear noise canceling headphones. You'll see in the pictures that it squeezed into my NZXT H7 Flow 2024 case, there wasn't much wiggle room. It's a preexisting build, so I had to move stuff out of the way to get it in the case. Pro's It's a beast, I can see it cooling any CPU you attach it to. The pump is powerful and quiet, very little noise at full speed. The VRM fan is a nice addition, the fan is quiet as a mouse at full rpm. Con's - The stock fans are horrible. C'mon Arctic you can do better. Besides people returning this cooler because they didn't thoroughly check the case size the fans are probably another reason. - It's beyond me why the cooler head is designed for the PWM control cable to go under the head before it's installed on the CPU.  If you change your mind about which control cable (there's 2) you want to use, you'll have to pull the head off the CPU change the cable, re-paste the CPU and reinstall. I chose not to follow this step of the install "Connect the PWM control cable before mounting the cooler on the mainboard", I recommend you don't do it either. I'll notch the VRM head where the wire comes through at a later date. For now the cable is squeezed underneath.
