reviews.title: Awesome!
reviews.comment: This works awesome.  I can overclock to the CPU's capability and don't have to worry about overheating.  The highest I've been able to get the CPU to is 72c and that is cranking 4800MHz.  Wasn't perfect stability at that speed though so I'm back down to 4700MHz and it is rocking along.  I love this cooler.  It is simple to install, stupid proof and incredibly quiet.  The fans don't seem to move much air so I replaced them with the bgears 1800rpm versions.  Now they make noise and move lots of air but I don't think it really did  much for the temps so I might just go back to the stock ones that are pretty darn impossible to hear.  I literally have to stick my head really close to the computer to even know it is on it is so quiet with the stock fans.  So yes if you want to be able to run at the fastest possible stable speeds of your CPU then this cooler will do the trick.
reviews.author: SUPERDELL

reviews.title: Arctic cold and quiet
reviews.comment: This baby cools.  I installed this in my new Fractal Mid Tower case.  You can see the review under my other posts.  This cooler was the finishing touches to complete my build.  I was running 50-60 celsius on my cpu under medium load.  I have an ASUS motherboard with an AMD 8 core 4.0 ghz processor.  The stock fan sounded like a blow dryer trying to keep it cool.  The temp was in the 40 celsius range under idle.  After installing the H110, I am at idle with as low as 7 celsius and usually no more than low 20's under medium load.  The fans are large so they are very quiet.  I have a very large case and barely fit this thing in.  You will want to measure before purchasing. The reason for choosing the H110 over the H100.  I have two sons who built awesome machines.  One has the H100 the other has the H110.  The H100, which is further from the door, can be heard as you enter the room.  You have to get close to the computer with the H110 in order to hear it.  I wanted quiet.  They both work excellent for cooling.  The larger fans on the H110 just make it better.  Worth the extra few bucks.  Just make sure you measure.
reviews.author: Robert N.

reviews.title: Icy cold, but crummy fans.
reviews.comment: First thing you need to do is buy a Y-Splitter cable for either 3 or 4-pin so you can connect your fans to the CPU OPT, otherwise you'll need to use the regular fan headers - which is not idea or wise. I gave this a 4/5 for the sole reason that one of the two fans rattled out of the box, and I can't live with that. Rather than RMA them I ditched them for better ones. Outside of that I love this thing, it keeps my OC'd 3770k very cold, I never exceed 45C after the heaviest applications and it typically never goes above 37C for most games. I have since replaced the somewhat weak fans with two Noctua NF-A14 PWM (HINT: They come with a free Y-Splitter 4-pin and move a ton more air, or CFM) and really unlocked the potential of this badboy. I suggest the pull configuration rather than push (fans between the radiator and case) so you can easily clean the radiator as dust accumulates. Also for those with the Corsair 650D (like myself) you need to put it in pull configuration, because the radiator is to long to mount in push.
reviews.author: Redacted

reviews.title: Works Like a Charm and Definately Worth The Price
reviews.comment: Had the H90 installed in my other gaming build and this thing is larger than my oil cooler on my old Kawasaki GPz 750 motorcycle I had! With the two 120mm high flow fans from Corsair acting to push the cooler room air through the cooler vents from the front, for me it's the perfect setup. Running 16GB of DDR4 and the 780 ti for graphics the air being vented from the top is just as cool as the air in the room, which stays pretty cool. So once the replacement MOBO comes back in and I can monitor CPU specs like they should be I'll be back with an update but so far very impressed. Be advised I don't know about other board setups, (running the ASUS Rampage V) but with the Corsair Graphite case and having the H110 cooling  setup in the front, the hoses to the CPU reach fine. BUT if you add memory cooling to those already heavy heat sinker DD4 sticks, the hoses will just barely clear the memory fan tops with their sharp metal corners. Memory in the left banks of course are uneffected. So in the end I elected to return the memory coolers since one, I think in their inherent design they will stay cool enough as is and two, I don't want to have to worry over time of having a sudden cooling leak inside a $2,500 machine. Sometimes less is better.
reviews.author: mrmertz

reviews.title: WOW! It's HUGE!
reviews.comment: First of all, this thing is huge. I wanted a liquid CPU cooler for my rig for a few reasons: 1) It's quieter than air cooled, 2) It keeps the CPU much cooler than air cooled systems, 3) It looks a lot cooler (pun intended) than air cooled CPU coolers. I use it on an Intel i5-4690K 3.5Ghz OC @ 4.5GHz and during heavy loads it runs at around 50-60°C, if that high. At regular everyday use, it's at 25-40°C. It varies depending on what I'm doing (usually running multiple things at one time). I don't mind those temps at all. This rad/fan combo works amazingly. I have the 140mm fans in between the case and the radiator pulling the air through the radiator (I tried both ways and it seems better and quieter in this configuration than having the fans pushing air through the radiator). Also, I picked this one over the H100i mainly because this radiator was bigger and could dissipate more heat than the H100i. There were also less plugs with the H110 (just one for the pump and two for the fans) whereas the H100i, I believe, has one more plug for monitoring fan speed. If you have the room like I do in the Corsair 750D, this is definitely the best one you could get without going into actual water-cooling systems.
reviews.author: Rick

reviews.title: Ultimate performance. 0 noice. Already using for 6 years. Q U A L I T Y ! ! !
reviews.comment:
This cooler is:
- Super silent. Literally 0 db.
- Excelent performance. ~35C idle. Cools cpu beyond it`s official TDP.
- Very accurate. No spiky edges, everything very detailed and smooth.
- Package is also very cool, all the connectors, even that cute screwdriver that has perfect size to do mounting job.
-  Q U A L I T Y ! ! ! Beyond any expectations.
- You can just buy mounting kit whenever you decide to upgrade mobo+cpu, so you can use it on another socket.
Also, mount upgrade option is free now - when you upgrade your CPU Noctua can send you a free mounting kit, so now I will continue using this magnificient cooler for the next 6 years too.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Worth every penny!
reviews.comment:
Short review
I've used both water cooling and air cooling and this is hands down one of the best coolers I have ever used. The cooler is a bit bigger then expected but that's alright and fits just right with my NZXT elite case. The packaging was great and came with everything needed, especially the AM4 bracket that most coolers do not include right out of the box but require a form to be filled out and a few days for the bracket to be shipped to you. This beast was able to shave off 20c and my cpu rarely goes beyond 50c even when gaming or rendering at 3.7 ghz with a Ryzen 1600x. I was so impressed with Noctuas products I bought additional fans to run a dual fan configuration and it brought normal temps down an additional 6-8c. Highly recommended and I dont miss water cooling one bit.
Long review
I lived in a very hot environment and my Ryzen spire cooler just wasn't cutting it anymore. I was using a Ryzen 1600x (1600x doesn't include the spire cooler but it's a long story) and my temperatures were pretty hot. Gaming could bring it up to 70c and rendering a video in Premiere would run it all the way to 95c before shutting down. I tried premium thermal paste and reinstalling the cooler but nothing changed so I began researching for the best replacement. I spent a couple weeks looking into many options in both water cooling and air cooling such as the Corsair AIOs and many air cooling options. Although I've used water cooling in the past I just couldn't pull the trigger because I did not want to risk any leaking because although the warranty may cover any damages I can't be without my PC for long. Originally I really wanted to purchase the DH-15 to get the biggest and baddest cooler possible I was not able as my ram was not compatible so I settled on the U12S or at least I thought I was settling. This was my first Noctua product and although they have some of the best reviews around the main reason I went with them was this cooler came with the AM4 bracket right out of the box as oppose to buying the cooler and filling out a form to have the company ship one to you. Firstly I was very impressed with the packaging, everything nicely separated making it easy to unbox. Next thing I noticed is just how big this cooler was. Although it uses 120mm fans this thing was solid and I couldn't imagine how big the DH-15 would have been. No issues from the size though and it fit nicely in my NZXT Elite case. Installation was among the easiest of all the coolers I've installed. The most impressive of all and the most important is the performance. This thing is an absolute cooling monster and cut my temperatures while gaming by 20c. I was so impressed with the performance I bought two additional Noctua fans with higher RPMs to run a dual fan configuration and brought temps even lower by about 6-8c. It feels great to game and render video on my Ryzen 1600x at 3.7 at 45c for hours. Money well spent and I'm a fully satisfied customer.
reviews.author: Justice Bringer

reviews.title: Super cool and will not get in way of memory slots or gpu
reviews.comment:
I've been building computers for 20 years and outside of an SSD this is one of the best purchases I've made. The only downside is the color is not very pretty, but I have a way to fix that as well.
I read about some complaining the installation is hard, but it's not. I did it by myself, very simple. I'm using MSI Tomahawk B450 with Ryzen 5 2600 and a case with the back open to get to the motherboard while installed. I put the case on a table facing up. Moved it off the edge so one hand could hold the backplate up, put 2 spacers over the backplate and then slowly tightened a screw to just make it catch a little. Once one of them catch it's even easier, you don't have to hold it up anymore.
I have 3 intake fans on the front 2 top and 1 rear. I put the cooler vertical to the ground with the fans faced the same way as the intake fans. The stock fan is pushing air coming from the front thru the heatsink and I put a 120mm rhermaltake riing on the other side pulling the air and pushing it a few inches to my 140mm exhaust fan which pulls it out. I wanted to try this first to get a baseline before swapping the fans to make it look better.
Going to swap the 2 fans position so the led fan is seen more from the cases glass side and the ugly brown fan is on the back out of sight. I think this might actually work even better since my other fan is a very high static pressure fan great for pushing air thru. You could also swap the stock fan and put it somewhere in the case it won't be seen.
As good as they are suppose to be in not paying 25$ for another fan from noctua, it's just too high. You can get 3 riings with a rgb and speed controller for 30$ on sale from 60$. Credit to noctua for giving us another clip and having this to work with any other fans. It was very easy to put my other fan on.
Now to the temps which are very impressive. I played Madden 19 no frame cap, max settings @ 1080p for 10 minutes and the wraith stealth was between the upper 50s to mid 60s and highest temp was 70. During benchmarks, it would hit as high as 72, but I didn't stress it that much. CPU idles in the upper 30s and during very light usage like browsing or Netflix it is in the mid 40s with spikes to low 50s.
Now I can idle as low as 27 with ambient temps of 24, but typically idle right at 30. I out the cpu under full load stress test 100% across all cores for 6 minutes. It went from 30 to 50 really really fast, within a couple seconds and then over 6 minutes climbed to only 53. Stock cooler can hit 70c in a 2 min benchmark and this can't even clear 60 over 6 minutes. Highest temp I hit so far after overclocking +450mhz is 56.
The fan is insanely quiet, I can see why they charge 25$. My case is naturally quiet though with the fully sealed sides and a filter over front and top, it keeps the sound in. Even during every fan at 100% I can only really notice it if I am not doing anything. Any sort of light sound going on will cover it.
If you want your cpu to run crazy cool, but don't want a huge heatsink that will block your RAM then buy this. I have so much ram clearance that I'm actually considering returning the memory I have to get something with big heat spreader and rgb lights.
reviews.author: To.Ze

reviews.title: Excellent Cooling, Quiet, and High Quality
reviews.comment: The ARCTIC Liquid Freezer III 240 A-RGB delivers outstanding cooling performance with very low noise. The PWM-controlled pump and fans keep temperatures under control even under heavy loads, while staying quiet during normal use. Installation is straightforward, and the included LGA1851/LGA1700 contact frame is a great bonus for improved CPU contact. The white A-RGB design looks clean and modern, making it a perfect match for themed builds. Reliable, efficient, and great value for a 240mm AIO.
reviews.author: Jason Acosta

reviews.title: Fantastic performance - Easy to install on AM5
reviews.comment: Lowered my idle temps from from 38c to 36c. However, the biggest change is at load, benchmarking my CPU @ 100% load for 15 mins my previous AIO(Coolermaster ML240) I went from 72.4c down to 68.2c. I will say at max fan speed it is rather loud in my normally very quiet system. Modifying fan curves to not ramp up to 100% so quickly resolved most of this. Also, I am running a 7800x3D, which I believe this cooler is more designed(meaning AMD in general) for, and the ease of installation and performance vs Intel is proof of that.  Also, CHECK YOUR CASE AND COMPONENTS FOR CLEARANCE! This radiator and fan combo is around 12mm thicker than most AIOs on the market. It fit perfectly in my Corsair 4000D case with my Asus ROG Strix B650e-e motherboard. I could probably have gone for the 360mm version of this but some reviews show that one sometimes gets worse performance than the 240mm version, so just a word of caution there. Final verdict: This is a must buy for the AM5 platform. Great build quality, performance and at an incomparable price!
reviews.author: Brooks P Barberio

reviews.title: Great product for the price!
reviews.comment: Great product, runs quiet, easy install besides header clearances on MB (not the product's fault,  my case needed an extra 1/2" clearance to make it a kid-friendly install). LEDs are bright. I wish the hoses had integrated cable management, but not going to detract stars since it was not a selling point. Performance is great, dropped CPU temp by 30* C over stock air cooler during stress test comparison. Stock air cooler experienced thermal throttling, this AIO never exceeded 65* C on Ryzen 9 3900 chip. I setup BIOS to have pump to run flat 100% all time, and fans on a curve based on CPU temp. Besides the stress test, fans rarely spool up, and even more rarely reach 80% speed. 100% would recommend to anyone looking to purchase a cheap AIO.
reviews.author: Christal

reviews.title: Very Nice Cooler, Install Has some issues.
reviews.comment: Very nice RGB, noise, fans with good performance with my AMD 5800x3D. Install was not bad until applying the cooler to the processor itself. It was a nightmare to get the plate down and took quite a bit of force compared to other AIOs.
reviews.author: Brandon

reviews.title: Great but very loud
reviews.comment: He’ll yeah works great little hard to install very cold good for its price and the one 4 pin connector makes it very compatible hooks up easy it is very loud full tilt
reviews.author: caden edwards

reviews.title: Best AIO in the game!
reviews.comment:
Arctic AIO's have been my favorite for a while now. They are the best, the numbers and tests don't lie. Even the Arctic 240mm AIO beats out some of the most popular 360mm AIO's. It's because the radiator is much thicker and the fans have much better static pressure than most because you need more pressure to push air through a thicker radiator effectively.
People don't realize how good the Arctic 280mm AIO is. The Arctic 280mm AIO is better than 360mm AIO's. It's been proven time and time again, and I'm not sure why, but the Arctic 280mm AIO beats even the Arctic 360mm AIO, and for the relatively low price you're paying for this 280mm AIO, you are getting absolutely insane performance.
I have 2 Arctic 280mm AIO's. One RGB and one Non-RGB. I also have a 240mm Arctic AIO, and I used to have an Arctic 360mm until I realized the 280mm is better than the 360mm. I've used the 280mm on the Ryzen 9 7900x and the Ryzen 9 7950x and the temps are awesome, even during benchtests. As long as Arctic keeps making AIO's, they will always be my first choice for a cooling solution. Also because of their Arctic MX-4 thermal paste. MX-4 is amazing, and well known as one of the best. They have Arctic MX-6 now and It's even better.
I love this AIO, and the only consumer CPU on the marker that it can't handle is a 13900KS, You would need the Arctic 420mm for that, but this 280mm can and will handle a 13900K just fine, even better than an Arctic 360mm will. This 280mm is an absolute beast and a god send for anyone wanting to cool their CPU the best they can without setting up a custom loop with multiple radiators.
It's also worth mentioning that their warranty program is awesome. I had a fan start rattling after 2 months once and when I got in touch with their warranty department, (it was easy and pretty fast) they just asked for my receipt and a video of it rattling. After I sent the email, I got a replacement fan in the mail 2 days later.
I have been building PC's for quite some time now and Arctic is top dog. 2nd to none... and this isn't just my opinion. This is fact.
reviews.author: Austin

reviews.title: Reduced Noise & Temps from NH-D15
reviews.comment:
I upgraded from a Noctua NH-D15 Chroma.black to this AF II 280 ARGB.  So far so good.  I watched the GN reviews about the ~6c temp difference compared to the Noctua.  My results were similar, possibly slightly more.  This was my first AIO.  I watched a YouTube video where someone mounted it on a LGA1700 platform.  Not rocket science, but I preferred the video versus the manufacturer's instructions.  For those wondering, both MX-5 paste and the LGA1700 mounting hardware were included.  My order was in early March 2022.  For the fan/pump (one wire), I used the "silent" setting curve as outlined on Arctic's website -- e.g., 0-60c at 20%, 75c at 50% and 85c at 100%.  The pump/fan is quieter than the curves I had my Noctua set at.
Regarding thermals, I'm using an i9-12900K.  With the Noctua, I had it overclocked to 50p/39e all cores, with 1.26v on Override Mode LLC6 (MSI Z690 Edge WiFi DDR4) which resulted around 1.18v to 1.186v load while running P95 Small FFT Non-AVX and CB23 multi loops.  Wattage was upwards of 230w-260w depending the test program.  The Noctua was good to cool around 230w or so.  There was overclocking headroom left, but I needed better cooling.  After installing the 280, I'm still tinkering, but easily cleared 51p/40e at 1.28v LLC6 which is around 1.206v load.  I do have other cores set higher, but "all" 8 P and E cores are set as described.  Max peak single core temp was 91c; the others stayed in the low-to-mid 80's.  I looped CB23/P95 Small FFT In-Place (no AVX) test for an hour each.
My case is an older Phanteks Enthoo Pro M Tempered Glass.  Yes, I still use an optical drive.  The case does allow for this thicker radiator to work (yes, even tubes down) after removing the preinstalled hard drive cage and the front radiator insert cover.  In the slim chance someone else is wondering about this case/AIO configuration, it can still accommodate one mechanic HDD.  You have to buy the $9 Phanteks (ph-hddkt_01) accessory that allows for a single drive to be mounted.  Very easy installation.  The 2x140mm fans on the top for exhaust is a tight fit with the ODD, but it works.  In my use case, with my computer being in a cubby space, I front mounted the AIO since I have minimal clearance along the top of case in this cubby space.
Very happy with the purchase.  Recommended.
reviews.author: ezfl

reviews.title: Great for ITX build using i5-12000k
reviews.comment:
CASE, MOBO, CPU, RAM, GPU:
Black Lian Li Q58, ASRock Z690M-ITX/ax, i5-12000k, Corsair LPX RAM (16GBx2)- low profile RAM, MSI 3060 TI
PC USAGE:
I do some light gaming, and run multiple VM's but not at the same time. Occasionally some beginner level video editing.
REVIEW:
If you want to air cool this case with this CPU/GPU combo or similar team RED, this is the best cooling option for you IMO. The build quality is excellent, the fan is dead quiet. I am using low profile RAM, so your mileage may vary. The case clearance is 67mm and this has a height of 66mm, and while tight, I can assure you it does not touch the case and I have no issues with turbulence. I believe there is about 1.5mm-2mm of gap between the rad and the case.
The fan sits a bit lower than the top of the radiator and vents 100% to the mesh panel of the case, so pretty much ideal. The radiator is perhaps 15% obstructed when the case is closed.
Mounting: attach base plate prior to installing MOBO in case (the threads on the plate are mounted up) There is provided Noctua thermal paste with at least two applications. The radiator screws down into the base plate (using a provided screwdriver) through two holes in the radiator.- Mine came with AMD4 mounting hardware as well as LGA 1700.
This will likely be the last step to complete the build. Make sure you plug into all the correct headers prior to mounting because the cooler/radiator will cover some of the headers and RAM. You will not be able to see the cooler fan in the case, as it is behind the rad.
PS- the green glow is a MOBO light I never notice it while working and it does not bother me at night, I think the radiator diminishes/ shadows it.
reviews.author: JB

reviews.title: Ideal for SFF. Be prepared to underclock high end CPUs.
reviews.comment:
CPU: 9950x3d
MB: Gigabyte x870i AORUS
Case: Falcon NW Tiki
Upgraded the internals of my SFF PC. Previous MB/CPU combo allowed for Corsair H50 but the upgraded MB did not allow space.
PC used for gaming and work. Temperatures reached 98*C when gaming. Proceeded to underclock to 1.15V with no major detriments to performance. Did not use PBO, simply voltage underclock. Temperatures never break 70*C now.
Highly recommend this but be prepared to underclock and run benchmarks to find the specs that fit your needs!
reviews.author: Nick

reviews.title: Fit in my NZXT H1 v1
reviews.comment: Man...NZXT should be ashamed. The 140mm rad they included in the H1 was absolutely destroyed by this thing. Dropped idle temps by 10°C easily, and I'm hovering at 75°C on a full Blender run. Legitimately the best air cooler I've ever encountered. Just be careful, the thing is...BEYOND pointy ;)
reviews.author: Trevor H.

reviews.title: Good cooler, quality control issues.
reviews.comment: It's a good cooler. It's easy to install, performs well, and the fan is quiet for its size. However, the heatsink was slightly bent sideways and not perfectly parallel with the motherboard. This could not have happened during shipping since it is packed very well and safely inside the box. It must be a manufacturing defect. Which is why I am taking away one star. It is mostly a cosmetic defect and does not affect its performance.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Fits inside NXZT H1 V1
reviews.comment:
This is a great low profile CPU cooler. The AIO on my H1 V1 was end of life so I replaced it with this NH-L12 S1, and it's amazing. My 11700k idles around 34 and underload hits about 60, which is muchhh better than the stock AIO. The Noctua is also very quiet, although I can hear it spin under heavy load.
Overall I'm very happy with the purchase especially since its compatible with my current setup. The height allows you to use the included 90mm fan on the underside of the heatsink, and the top side lays flush with the 140mm case fan, for a push/pull configuration.
Great stuff, would recommend
reviews.author: JK

reviews.title: Amazing Product. Tricky install
reviews.comment: This AIO is the best performer out there, period. Whisper silent and does a splendid job cooling my 13900k. Take your time with the installation for this. The mounting system is straightforward? However short cutting will lead to an awful time.
reviews.author: Alexander Darby

reviews.title: Best cooler I've had in years well worth the money. Just make sure it fits in your tower
reviews.comment: Why did you pick this product vs others?: This is the best cooler I've ever had. I did have two minor issues getting it in to my tower in order to be able to get it in my tower because it'll massively bigger motherboard that I had. I had to take the fans off. Put the radiator on the top of my towel and then secure the fans to the inside of the tower and into my radiator. That was the only way it would fit the whole thing inside the tower cuz my Tower is like 9 years old. That was the only way it fits but it works like a dream. I like the RGB setup and cuz I have a gigabyte motherboard and with a gigabyte RGB system and everything it works really well. I've never had any trouble with coolers over there. They've worked fine but this one seems to work better than the other one. Later I mean the temps on my CPU or in the '40s and '50s that was after adjusting some overclock things that were set by default on the CPU in the BIOS. Otherwise turning those overclock things off. I forget what they're called. I'm like why is my thing hitting 70 80 I said my thing never hit 70 80° not in 20 years. So the artificial intelligent thing that I was talking to said you need to adjust this setting in this setting and turn these two off and soon as I did the temps went back down to 40 to 50. I never overclocked so I was like what's going on here. But this thing works like a dream and it's the best one that I've ever had. And I have a core i7 ultra CPU and it works great
reviews.author: wildwitch

reviews.title: High Quality AIO, Open-Source-Feel
reviews.comment: The quality of this radiator and block is exceptional in my opinion.  I was replacing a Corsair AIO that was a few years old and had failing RGB and a broken bracket.  I was not expecting the product that showed up which was as heavy as a brick and built like a tank. The install was mildly annoying for an AMD chip as I'm sure you'll read about if doing research.  The radiator is also extra thick which can cause some interference issues if you have a tight case.  Double check your case specs for this.  I was impressed enough by the build quality that I exchanged for a larger case to accommodate this AIO.  I'm disappointed that the arctic logo on the block can not be rotated to match odd install orientations. There is zero software or drivers required for this AIO which is a huge plus for me since I don't want to be locked into some ecosystem.  It does require some hardware/motherboard/sofware of choice with ARGB capability to use the rgb and utilizes the standard PWM (cpu_fan) header for controlling the system (there are many combos possible- look into it specifically if interested). My processor stays cool under heavy load and it's relatively quiet. I would definitely recommend this product if it fits with your build.
reviews.author: Daniel M

reviews.title: Great Design & Cooling
reviews.comment: I don't understand why there's bad reviews. Looks like there were a few people that received used/returned items. That aside, this cooler is fantastic. GamersNexus has this rated pretty high and it Looks great and keeps my 7800x3D cold. The fans do ramp up a little prematurely in my opinion, but never to a major level if the cooler and thermal paste are properly installed. It's a thick boy at 38mm for just the radiator, so make sure it's going to fit, but if you do your due diligence for planning your PC build, you should be fine. I suspeect this would fit most modern cases with front radiator support. Top is preferable in my opinion for exhausting hot air, but may be a little less compatible unless the radiator is offset plenty from the motherboard VRM heatsinks. Install wasn't hard if you follow the instructions. The only gotchas for me was that the brackets are left and right AND I accidentally installed them upside down the first time, so I didn't think that was intuitive, at least for me.  Also the pump block isn't centered on the die, so it goes right to the edge of the CPU heatspread on the top and that preplexed me greatly, but it's by design. I think they designed it so the waterblock fan blows on that edge I guess. It's cold so it works. Only other thing that was weird with mine was the waterblock fan was ticking for the first hour or so. Not sure what that was about, tried adjusting things, eventually it went away. Not sure if there was a flap of tape or something? FYI, a 280mm is only about 10% less surface area than a 360 AIO, yet 36% more cooling than a 240, not to mention the thickness and waterblock design.  So a pretty good alternative when you can't fit a 360mm. I think this think just looks so slick and I'm going to buy another one for my old PC.
reviews.author: skylander

reviews.title: Performance-Per-Dollar
reviews.comment: Positives: My 14900k dropped an average of 3-5 degrees C from my Noctua NH-d15 and it’s half the price. Negatives: Based on reviews on major hardware sites I expected cooler temperatures overall. My processor is referenced in many reviews as being tamed by this cooler, but during rendering in After Effects and Premier Pro Temperatures were spiking over 100C and throttling occurred often enough to completely stall the render. The 14900k runs notoriously hot, but having to underclock the CPU to maintain stability is disappointing. Average temperatures during idling are around 40C which is still too hot. Its  loud. Not the worst thing for most people, but when recording audio this has to be mitigated through other means. I never heard a peep from the NH-D15. Overall: I can deal with the sound, and it’s way better performance per dollar than the Noctua. If the dBs aren’t an issue go for it. It can hang with the big dogs, but don’t expect miracles if you’re running a bleeding edge CPU. You want the biggest radiator your case can handle, but make sure to measure before you order. Installation was no more difficult than other comparable coolers at least on the ASUS ProArt z700 Creator mobo.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Quiet, Efficient, and Reliable After Two Years
reviews.comment: I've been using the Cooler Master Hyper 620S for almost two years now, and it continues to deliver excellent performance. This dual-tower air cooler features six direct-contact copper heat pipes and two PWM fans that keep my CPU temperatures low, even under heavy loads. It's impressively quiet even during gaming or stress tests, the noise level stays minimal. The power consumption is also very efficient, with each fan drawing only about 3 watts, making it a great choice for energy conscious users. The 154.9 mm height fits well in most mid-tower cases, though it's worth noting that high profile RAM might have clearance issues. Installation was straightforward, and the ARGB lighting syncs nicely with my motherboard, adding a clean, modern look to my build. Overall, it's a reliable, quiet, energy efficient cooler that I highly recommend.
reviews.author: Danny TR

reviews.title: Is not that difficult to install
reviews.comment: This cooler.master is a beast looks good cools good and I like  that it came with installation instructions. The temperature is much cooler, and so far so good I highly recommended.
reviews.author: Carlos

reviews.title: Great cooler
reviews.comment: One of, if not the best cooler I've ever owned. I'm not a fan of liquid cooling products and I think Cooler Master makes some of the best products.
reviews.author: Dtoolman

reviews.title: This unit works great for cooling but not so much with the ARGB Lighting
reviews.comment: I purchased this unit for an older I7-8700K machine I found for cheap and made it into a project after the mounting on the Noctua fans I got on that machine broke. It was cheaper to replace the fan rather than look up the mounting kit, which for that Noctua setup seemed impossible to find. I then opted for this unit as the reviews claim that it was keeping their systems cool Two days later I got it and went to install it. The mounting kits are all included. This comes with a PWM header splitter for both fans in case your MB does not have two headers for fans. It also comes with aa 4 pin  RGB header connector for 5V. Fans are mounted properly and silent. However the RGB would not sync up with my MB and other components. The RGB would not align with the other components. I asked amazon for a replacement and got it fast. I then setup the lights on and no fans on and tested. This worked. So I went ahead and set it up again. To my surprise the RGB colors are no longer matching again. I decide ok I will take off the RGB headers. Well guess what, the RGB lights still come on. That is when I realized that the fan spinning made it to where the RGB lights did not sync. I then unplugged the fans to the MB header and realized that they no longer sync. Long story short, I used the Noctua fans from the one I had got on my system and attached them to this. IDK if I was unlucky and got 2 sets of bad RGB lights and fans but it makes no sense as to what I encountered. If you buy these and are using a mother board that has rgb memory, rgb motherboard lights, rgb exhaust fan and rgb front fans and think that this will sync, it may not. Note that my RGB exhaust fan also spins and syncs with all other components. Just my experience with this fan.
reviews.author: Karina N.

reviews.title: Graeat for keeping a 12700k cool
reviews.comment: This cooler works very well to keep my cpu running cool. When I am running cinebench the cpu reaches a maximum of 75c, and in games the cpu barley reaches 70c. Along with how well this cpu performs it also looks really nice. The only downside that I have with this cooler is that one of the fans hangs over my ram sticks, so I cant see one of the sticks. However that is a mionor issue as the performance of the coooler is worth no seeing one of the ram sticks.
reviews.author: Colton Rehberg

reviews.title: Great cooler for the price.
reviews.comment: I ordered this for my son's 13700k, and the cooling performance has been fantastic. I preferred this cooler to the fancier ones that have displays linked to software because there is a lot of negative reviews about the ASUS software and support. My reasoning was that this is just a stripped-down hardware solution with a nice logo, zero software required - and it works exactly as expected. In fact, it's about the same price as a nice Noctua air cooler, and it looks super slick inside the case. I don't really get the idea of the in-case displays anyhow, usually a computer is sitting in a location that would make that useless, and you can just look at a software display on-screen anyhow. Bottom line - definitely recommeded.
reviews.author: The Invisible Man

reviews.title: Best AIO bought
reviews.comment: very nice AIO beautiful color and performance and created a great experience with hot CPUs. Works good with AM5 platforms and it fits the case perfectly. Also very quiet.
reviews.author: Wei Wang

reviews.title: Cools well and looks good
reviews.comment: I ordered a pc and picked all the parts for it but I guess I forgot to pick a cpu cooler so they installed a generic one. Well when I got it I didn't like it and immediately started looking for an upgrade. Found this cooler and since I'm familiar with the brand and and price was good I went with it. It arrived packaged very well, one of those boxes that's to nice to throw away types. It came with everything needed to install it even thermal paste pre installed. The lights look good and synced up with the rest. This keeps my cpu nice and cool even while gaming the temp barely goes up.
reviews.author: Tommy L Evans JR

reviews.title: I mean, wow! Great AIO for my Ryzen 9 5900
reviews.comment: Great build quality and now I can overclock my Ryzen 9 5900X to 4600 @ 1,3 volts at 48C --- really amazing; tried a Corsair but it sucked.  The mounting system is really great and super easy to install! Great cooler for the $ The only issue is warranty registration the Serial Number and Code were a mismatch in the ASUS system - saying it had already been registered.  And it gave the wrong part description as well. The Customer Support is great and they are trying to sort this issue out, Hardware is solid and a great max for my ROG STRIX B500-F Mobo
reviews.author: momentSkier

reviews.title: Good, but fans are questionable
reviews.comment: I opted to make a new build for XMas and used this AIO. I've always gone air-cooled in the past and since I was going small form factor this time around I figured that I'd go AIO - mostly for space considerations but a bit for quiet as well. Cools an AMD 78003D like a champ. Nice and quiet - can hardly even hear the pump (my hearing aids are in for repair, so I admit that I'll need to reassess this in a couple weeks.) Installed without too much trouble - enough length of tubing to accommodate any positioning I could think of for this case, but would work well with other case sizes, too. If I wasn't building SFF I'd probably go with the 360mm version, all considered. Pre-applied paste seems to have been up to the task - it was a thin silkscreen layer that looked dry on-sight and to a light touch, but was sufficient (and not dry at all - just a bit stiff). Had to re-position the pump and block and noticed good smooshy coverage of the CPU. Box had everything a boy could need in there - a variety of different standoffs for AMD4-5/INTEL setup, a mess of screws and a pretty good installation guide.  Anyhow, the real bugbear was the fans - one of the fans, to be precise. It had bad bearings and sounded like a rattletrap the moment I did my check for post. It was soooo obvious and even a finger-spin would set it off. I swapped out both fans for a pair of 3-wire scrap coolermasters I had laying around from an old machine. Problem solved, done-and-dusted. Not sure how important the 4-wire (they're in a ribbon) stock fans are, but 3-wire seemed to throttle up and back as needed. Whatever magic conversation the pump is having with the CPU over the USB header, the fans seem to be getting the right message. Conclusion: Don't trust the stock fans on these things. Buy nice fans... you don't have to go Noctua, but get something decent and quiet. ASUS makes a lot of really good stuff, but whoever they get fans from is wicked bad at running the most basic tests. I sorta wish that I'd looked around for a version that didn't have fans so that I'd just have to buy a pair of my choice and it would not have been an issue. Also, when screwing the radiator snug up to the case, I noticed that the threaded ends of some of the mounting screws did dent the radiator vanes a bit - no punctures (thank goodness) but if you're sensitive to that kind of thing just get some thin rubber grommets to achieve enough space to avoid interference. Good coooler, happy with the result.
reviews.author: DudeFromDenver

reviews.title: Nice colors and great performance!
reviews.comment: Bought this to replace a different pump that went bad. The RGB colors are great, looks very sharp and ties into my computer well. I didn’t need to use the software as my RGB motherboard controller did the job, but their software is an option if you need it. This pump actually ran cooler than the original pump I bought ever did! I was running about 90c which is way too hot and my CPU was throttling. Once this was installed it was down to 65c!! That’s a huge difference! Setup was easy, good directions, and it had all the adapters for an AMD or Intel CPU. It was also cheaper than a lot of others I looked at, so a great value!
reviews.author: Edward Traylor

reviews.title: This makes me wish I'd ditched the air coolers years ago now...
reviews.comment: Simply Amazing. I've never been one afraid to spend on my PC, but also valued reliability and above all, noise.  As such, I've firmly been in the Noctua (with the occasional deviation) air-coolers, culminating most recently in the NH-D15 G2... an absolute beast of a cooler that overwhelmed everything in my case, made it hard to work on anything, and was way noisier than I expected. So after a TON of research, this replaced it....and man, is it quiet.  Definitely nothing flashy about it if you're looking for RGB (there is zero), but I have RGB in the other elements of my case - I don't need it everywhere.  What this DOES give me is the ability to keep both fans and pumps turned down to inaudible (on a 9800X3D), which I love.  I can hear the pump if I put my ear next to it, but with the case on?  Nada.  All this, while dropping the ambient temps of my CPU by around 5C at idle, and way more at load (while being quieter at every level). Highly recommend if you value silence.
reviews.author: Kevin Whitley

reviews.title: Don't wait make the swap AIO is the way to be and this is the one!
reviews.comment: I bought a Costco Prebuilt PC (Aegis R2) with a I9 14000f  and a 4070 Super the CPU Cooler was a radiator/FAN. I mostly play WoW on almost ultra settings and my CPU Temp was idle about 74c and under load could range from 80c-94c! so not optimal for long term gaming, with a little dust it was riding the higher end of the temps more often. I decided to finally break down and buy an AIO Cooler and its been absolutely impressive, Idle at desktop is 25c-30c, idle in game With my setting cranked to ultra I am 45c-54 and under complete load in game I am around 54c-61c max. I have also run the Cinebench CPU Benchmark and max Temp throughout the test was 74c. Another note any Temp below 70c My PC is almost Completely silent after the install and even above that its quieter than it ever was. I purchased the 360 Atmos because I could fit it and it was like $20 more than the other unit. It was a snug to fit into my case opening however once it was in it fit very nicely. It is definitely a high quality item that was packaged very well and everything included was well labeled. Also I did not see it mentioned anywhere but there is thermal paste included. I ended up ordering some Artic thermal paste for the install I did end up using the one I ordered. The only "CON" if you can call it that is that the installation instructions are pictures only and if you aren't 100% sure what you are looking at it can be a touch confusing as they give you extra cords for different ways to set up the LEDS. it hung me up for a bit however there was a fantastic YT tutorial that gave in detail instructions for this exact unit and he even talks about all of the extra parts as well. I am intermediate in PC building knowledge and it took about an hour to replace the radiator setup. I did accidentally follow the wrong wire and unplug a wrong wire and had to do some tracing to find out what it was and where it plugged into that was my bad lol... All in all I would absolutely recommend this unit to anyone looking to cool their CPU down price is 100% reasonable for what you get.
reviews.author: Kmikelg

reviews.title: Quiet cooler !
reviews.comment: I'm using this to cool my 7950x3d. Granted, it doesn't need a 360mm AIO, but I care more about the noise the fans make. The Atmos Stealth is quiet as a mouse, I can barely hear it during day to day productivity tasks. It keeps temps. low in the 50s. The only time the fans become audible is during gaming sessions. Note, at full blast, these fans will be loud and sound like an industrial blower.
reviews.author: Monil

reviews.title: Is Good.
reviews.comment: Ice cold. Quiet. Easy to install. Hadn't used liquid cooling before, but upgrading from an intel gen 7 to a Ryzen 9800 required new mounts. This works, keeps the new processor cooler than the old Cooler Master fan+radiator setup on the old processor and is quieter. Plus it's cheap.
reviews.author: Talon Townley

reviews.title: 1st ever aio and I am impressed
reviews.comment: Been building and using PC`s longer than most of the readers out there have alive. I have always used air coolers and again my latest build was with an air cooler. It did a great job at keeping a 9950x3d cool, but with some loading doing workstation task, the cpu temp started creeping up. My retired threadripper had air cooling, but it never suffered from heat creep during work. So, I did some research on AIO`s and particular the 240mm size because that's all I could fit in case. Saw the reviews for the Arctic coolers and I liked the design and the fact that the only difference with each model was the radiator and fan size or count. The price was also a plus. So here goes. Installation for the ASUS Crosshair X870E Hero had a problem right off the bat which were identified in the compatibility chart on Arctic`s website. Solution 1 was a new NVMe M.2 heatsink which they would provide for free with motherboard proof of purchase or 2, turn pump assembly 180 degrees. For now, I installed it 180 degrees like they recommended. Next install the AMD brackets, thermal paste which was MX-7 from the kit, and the PIA procedure of trying to bend leaf spring retainer enough the get the unit secured to the motherboard. So now it's done and I used the 3-plug cable assembly and hooked everything up per the recommendation from Arctic tech support. Make sure you install cable assembly to pump head before stating pump install. Went into Armory Crate and then tuned the fans. After running the system for a 1/2 hour at moderate load to seat the contact plate thermal paste to cpu surface, I performed another fan tuning. For a small 240mm cooler I am impressed with the little bugger. In reviews for this cpu reviewers say 280mm for smallest, 360mm cooler optimum for the 9950x3d for best cooling. From what I am seeing 75c under load is a pretty good result. My air cooler was good at 80c but was showing some temp creep. I also like that at high loads; this thing was actually not too noisy. This instructions and videos on Arctic`s website were excellent and helped a lot during install and setup. Customer tech support replied overnight which was impressive. So only issue I had was the install position of the pump head. Make sure before you buy this is to go to Arctic website and review the installation information and verify the pump head will mount without any conflicts with your motherboard. My ASUS M.2 heatsink is big and tall. This caused the issue. Arctic had the solution in their great install information so go there first. So, for now I am sold on this cooler. Time will tell how I feel. The other thing to make sure of now is to keep an eye on the complete system temps in case you need to add or remove or even change the fan size for your case cooling. Systems temps will change when you go from air cooling to aio cooling. So, I provided a pic so you can see how little room I have for cooler and my installation in my case. The reason for a 240mm rad system is my PC has 5.25" drives and front usb headers. If I didn't have those, I would have installed the 360mm version. My case is a Silverstone SETA D1. So, about a week later and now the MX-7 thermal paste has set and broke in, my temps are lower yet. Been running Cinebench r23 with the multitask test and this cooler keeps the 9950x3d sitting right at 65c. I am not into overclocking mainly because of why. I just spent a butt load on a new pc and really don`t feel like frying the cpu. Only setting different from default are I set memory to EXPO2 and PBO is still in auto. Tried ASUS AI overclocking and the whole pc heated up like heating pad. Turned that off and back to nice and cool and stable. That ASUS AI Overclocking needs a little work imo.
reviews.author: Ordinary Joe Blow

reviews.title: Little complicated to setup but works amazingly well
reviews.comment: I've installed quite a few cooling systems in my years but this one did give me a little bit of trouble due to the packaging not coming with instructions. The video guide skips a few steps as well but once i figured it out, it went on like a glove. I got this for a 12th gen i7 cpu LGA 1700 and while trying to install the cooling plate onto the cpu, I was trying to turn it to optimize the hoses not hitting any other components which caused the plate to be upside down. Trying to install the plate upside down when the bracket is right side up makes it impossible to screw into (good design but wish there were some instructions that stated not to attempt it). Once i got it mounted and tightened up though, i fired up the computer and it was super quiet sitting at idle. I dont even notice the fan noise unless im stressing out the system and even then, they are quiet compared to my previous cooling system. I've overlocked my cpu to its max and tracked it using AI Suite 3. It's keeps my cpu at sub 90 F at idle and under 110 F at 100% load (video compression, gaming & streaming simultaneously) which is quite impressive for the price. I was a little skeptical about the quality of this because the box arrived heavily damaged and semi opened but its really sturdy and a great size for a mid size ATX tower.
reviews.author: Sergio Torres

reviews.title: Great with a few caveats
reviews.comment: This is a highly reviewed and rated aio cooler.  Most people get it because of that.  But having ran air coolers for decades, this is my first AIO, and I have several thoughts below. First of all - you don't need a water cooler unless your CPU draws lots of power, or you run extended CPU intensive things for extended durations.  A good air cooler is more than sufficient.  Spend more on water only adds to money and potential failure points.  I ran an air cooler for almost 16 years and the fan still held strong. So why did I go AIO?  For the novelty mostly, and because I applied thermal paste poorly in my last build and had higher temperature than I expected.  By comparison, the AIO kept my CPU 10C cooler than my air cooler - due a combination of better thermal paste application, and it being a brand new, undirtied cooler. Some tips on getting the most mileage out of this unit. First, fan speed above 50% is loud.  I set my fan curve in my bios to keep 50% until I hit 70C, which is very unlikely with my 5700X3D.  Second, this device is noticeably louder than my air cooling setup.  The reason being that the air cooler has top panels to deaden the noise, while this exposes the whole case to sound. For an easier install on AMD, do not tighten down the side brackets first.  You'll need to secure the cooler to them first, and the extra little leeway will make your life much easier.  And there's a backplate to your motherboard that you will screw into -- do not unscrew everything at once.  The backplate will fall out, requiring you to reattach it.  Instead, remove just one side and attach a bracket from this kit.  It'll save you a lot of time. Finally - this does cool very well. At 50% fan speed, the noise is pretty acceptable. Overall - only buy if you need the extra cooling.  These things wear out, so 6 years is probably time to get another one, vs 16 years on my air cooler.  But if you do want to try this out, it's a pretty good product.
reviews.author: AnotherUser

reviews.title: Gets loud, but effective
reviews.comment: People saying it's quiet are either lying or doing very light tasks. When the fans kick on it gets LOUD. However, it does a good job of cooling. So far has kept my 7800X3D around 60°C while gaming. Does not include instructions so you have to look up a guide (includes a QR code to a video that wasn't very good). Regardless, it was a PAIN to install.
reviews.author: Rue

reviews.title: Great quality and real results.
reviews.comment: I bought this for my Intel i7 11700k that was using a traditional ThermalTake cooler. It was running so hot that the computer would shut off to protect itself. Running HWMonitor it showed that the CPU cores would frequently hit 100 degrees (C). I tried cleaning the processor and re-applying thermal compound, which made it slightly better. Once the new cooler was installed the CPU runs at about 25-30 degrees when idle and has so far peaked at 63 degrees under load. Had I not seen the before and after with my own eyes I would have a hard time believing that a cooler could have such a huge impact. Dropping 35-40 degrees is significany, so say the least. It was easy to fit inside my case and the quality of the build is excellent. One thing I will say is that the cooler has two options for power, one uses a single fan header and the other uses three for individual fan controls. Make sure you have enough fan headers for the application you prefer. Very quiet operations so far, even under load.
reviews.author: Anders

reviews.title: Awesome cooler from new brand Sudokoo
reviews.comment:
Awesome cooler from new brand Sudokoo. I saw from creators on YouTube that the SK700V made its debut at Computex 25 and it caught my interest. The only place I was able to find reviews for this cooler (that weren’t just a regurgitation of specs) was Amazon, so I’m thankful for the reviews before me and hope mine is helpful as well.
I have nothing but good things to say about this cooler. It certainly does its job and does it well. My 9600X idles right at 35°C and never went above 60°C under heavy load on multiple benchmark apps.
This cooler is extremely easy to install and I was grateful for all the included kit. It comes with a torx Allen key so you can take off the stock CPU retention mechanism and comes with a long screwdriver to install the tower. I was impressed that the included screw driver was magnetized and it came in handy when I used it during the rest of the PC building process. The design of how the fan mounts by sliding on rails is fantastic. It’s very easy to take on and off and is much better than those metal clips that come on most coolers. The fan is pretty quiet: I didn’t note any louder than average noise during my testing.
The included AM5 contact frame fits the CPU like a glove and holds it securely with 8 screws. I like the tight fit as it keeps a potential thermal paste spillage from getting in the CPU socket.
I couldn’t find an answer for this before I bought it, so for those who are wondering, the cooler DOES come with thermal paste. I couldn’t see that advertised in the listing, so ordered a gram of some Thermal Grizzly paste instead. The included paste comes with a spatula and is more than a gram, but it is completely unmarked. Sudokoo also includes a grease-cleaning wipe in case you’re replacing your existing cooler. My project was a new build, so I didn’t need it.
I also really appreciated that the sticker that covers the cold plate isn’t clear. It is a bright pink and yellow that catches the eye and reminds you to take it off before installation.
The LCD screen is bright enough to see even with my Fractal Torrent’s tinted glass panels. I appreciate being able to see my CPU’s temp and freq. with a quick glance.
Overall, I’m extremely pleased with this cooler and would not hesitate to buy it again if I’m building another AMD machine.
reviews.author: Dominique & Daniel

reviews.title: Excellent build quality and excelent performance
reviews.comment:
I found out about this cooler thanks to GamerNexus, as I was looking for a replacement for my old Arctic Freezer 34, and I really loved the design. It doesn't cover the RAM (my RAM is RGB) and offers very good cooling, keeping my Ryzen 7 5800x at 50°C. I think if it had better airflow, it could lower the temperatures a little more.
The only drawback I see is that support for AM4 and other Intel processors has to be purchased separately.
reviews.author: Steffano

reviews.title: Nice quiet cooler, screen software needs work.
reviews.comment: Install was pretty straight forward. Had to replace the motherboard backing plate with the one supplied but it was OK overall. Noise is low, cooling is efficient, did not overheat when running stress test. Screen is nice when it works, this is where the 4 instead of 5 stars come in. You need to have their software running in order to have the screen display anything. Not a big deal, just set it to run when windows starts. The other big issue with the screen is that Windows doesn't always seem to recognize the USB device. Sometimes it does, works great, next re-start and no dice. Other than that it works great.
reviews.author: Jose R

reviews.title: Fantastic cooler!
reviews.comment:
Man does this thing get the job done. I'm using this to cool an AMD 9800X3D and it does as good of a job as the 240mm AIO I had on it, sometimes beating it. So initial response is great! During Cinebench, temps didn't get above 70 degrees. Gaming was dependant. Mid to upper 50's in STALKER 2, 60-65 in Black Ops 7.
I do have a -20 offset to the voltage so that's helping with temps and also using MX-7 thermal paste instead of the supplied paste.
It might be a little pricy but not Noctua pricy and this thing does a wonderful job keeping my CPU cool and the full RAM clearance helps a lot and it was really easy to install as well. Just had to take out the mobo, but if you're building and not replacing, it should be alot more straight forward.
Great job by Sudokoo!
reviews.author: JD.BuildsPC's

reviews.title: Impressive Air Cooler For It's Size
reviews.comment:
It's able to cool my 5800x3d no problem, around 70C is where it's tops up at. For the price, it is expensive, but damn does it look nice! I don't really hear it when it's working so it must be quiet. Small enough to not block my ram slots.
It's not cheap, but it's fancy, reliable, is literally a huge chunk of metal! Get it if you want SOME aesthetics with your cooling.
reviews.author: Andrew S.

reviews.title: Great cooler with smart RGB and quiet performance
reviews.comment:
I’ve been using the Thermalright Aqua Elite 240 V3 on my Ryzen build, and it’s performing far better than I expected for the price. The RGB lighting isn’t just for show — I set mine so that it turns blue when the CPU is cool and red when it heats up, which makes it easy to keep an eye on temps while gaming or editing. Most of the time it stays blue, meaning the cooling is doing its job perfectly.
Installation was straightforward, and the fans are very quiet — barely noticeable even under load. The pump design looks premium, and the overall build feels solid.
Only downside is that the instructions could be a bit clearer for first-timers, especially around mounting orientation. But once set up, it runs smooth, quiet, and keeps temps low.
For anyone building a clean RGB setup, this is a fantastic budget AIO that performs like a high-end cooler.
reviews.author: Jackjones

reviews.title: Be Cool, buy this cooler!
reviews.comment: Amazing Cooler at a price you cant beat! I was a huge Thermalright fan back in they early 2000s and I thought they were dead and gone, but oh baby they are back with a sweet cooler at a sweeter price. Great quality rad and pumphead. doesnt feel cheap at all. good hardware, fairly easy to install. not loud and cools well. rgb connected up and looks awesome as well.
reviews.author: Eric Johnson

reviews.title: This one is one of the best ngl
reviews.comment:
This is a really nice AIO ngl. I bought this a long time ago and have since had 3 different ones so far including a $130 lian li water cooler. But surprisingly this was the easiest one to install and the fans are actually quiet. So yur diss is pretty good!
Btw can u pls send over some products, I would love to do reviews for ur business. thank you💪😃👍
reviews.author: Rockit Sanders

reviews.title: Amazing budget AIO.
reviews.comment: Excellent cooler for X3D chips, I use it with my 5700X3D and it keeps it nice and cool around the 50-60c range in games. Fairly quiet, mounting is simple, and it just works well overall.
reviews.author: Memekiller

reviews.title: Outstanding performance.
reviews.comment: I ran my I51200F for 1 hour on 100% and the temp did not exceed 63C.  Outstanding cooler.
reviews.author: Dogbreath077

reviews.title: Best 100mm Low Profile Cooler
reviews.comment: I bought this cooler for a motherboard that had poor quality VRMs that needed downdraft cooling. The SI-100 just so happened to fit every single tick that I needed, and I'm not disappointed. The cooler was easy to install, however you will need a thin diameter screw driver to install it since accessing them requires you go through a narrow hole in the fin stack. Otherwise installation was effortless. Item was well packaged, fit and finish was good, and it cooled a Ryzen 7 CPU easily without a hiccup. I saw an average of 78°C while running a Blender CPU rendering benchmark without any TDP limitations on the processor, and VRMs were surprisingly about as cool. Noise is about average. The included fan can spin up to 2000 RPM, but I never see it go that fast. Performance overall is great.
reviews.author: M Sainz

reviews.title: Worked perfectly in Multiple Builds
reviews.comment: This is the second one ive bought, except this time i bought the white one. Both installations went incredibly well, and they cool well too. The first one i mounted in a prebuilt of mine, and it tucks in the case very nicely
reviews.author: Some guy

reviews.title: Good Quality Low Profile Cooler
reviews.comment: Good quality low profile cooler. Cools down my Ryzen 5 5500 just fine. Packaged well, arrived with thermal paste in box. I don't think I would want to use this cooler on a 5950x or even a 5900x but it does a pretty good job keeping my Ryzen 5 5500 low temps. It occasionally peaks to 71 or 72 Celsius and I have the fan curve set to 80% blow at 60 C then Maximum Blow at 70 C, on average though this cooler keeps the temps more around 50 C. Idle is even lower but I don't keep my rig at low idle very often. Thermalright has been around for a while. I wanted a low profile cooler that did the job for my new Ryzen 5 5500 build and this fits the bill. No RAM clearance issues on my MSI B550 Gaming Plus despite using high profile g skill ram. I like the cooler, if I do upgrade my CPU though I will probably buy a beefier cooler than this SI-100. And I did not use the included fan FYI, I used a Noctua 3000 industrial fan, has extreme performance to the decibel and the Noctua fans run forever. I did read that the included fan doesn't last long so I didn't even try it. I believe I bought my Noctua 3000 industrial fans for 30 USD each after tax, maybe even cheaper. This cooler was 30 including the fan so I wouldn't expect to get great mileage on this cheap included fan. Installation was fairly straight forward and easy. You need a 6 inch length Phillips, a drill bit holder extension is too wide so you need to use a standard handheld Phillips screwdriver with probably at least a 4 inch length shaft. Torquing it down was easy, you can hear and feel when it's all the way torqued down, and the way the socket bracket is mounted there is probably no risk with over torquing. I like this cooler though. Despite it being summer and my rooms ambient temps being quite high this cooler is doing a great job. My ambient temps are around 85 F here, and my CPU is peaking at about 72 C under maximum load.
reviews.author: Ben W.

reviews.title: Excellent Cooling
reviews.comment: Needed a new cooler as I upgraded the processor to the best one my motherboard could support.  I have limited space, restricted to 5 inches in height.  Reviewed 2 quality tower coolers.  Both had disappointing results.  In fact, I went back to the stock cooler.  The stock cooler worked until I get to a more CPU/graphics intensive programs.  Although, not a gamer, I would like to try some.  I then tried Heaven for a benchmark.  As mentioned, the two new tower coolers didn't do the job, and the stock did ok until stressed. I decided to try a downdraft cooler.  I initially tried the JIUWU 92 mm, but due to tight space, and cooler design, I could not install.  I did keep it and installed on my other computer.  What a surprisingly great job this does! Back to this cooler, installation was great!  Easiest installation for any multiple adaptable CPU coolers I've tested.  I'll give a shout out to the quality thermal paste provided too! This is a quality build cooler!  The price of a cooler was not my primary concern, I needed something to do the job!  Tried the expensive ones and I must say this does the best job and at a great price at that!  Yes, the best downdraft cooler I've tested.  !n reviews that I've noted, I have found this to be one of the leaders in its class.  I've noted at least a 15 degree difference! I'd buy this one again!  This is surely one, if not the best coolers I can get for my computer setup!
reviews.author: Carolyn Cobbs

reviews.title: Helps me chill
reviews.comment: Fits an LG1700 socket, among others.  Keeps an i9/Nvidia 5060 Micro ATX rig in the low 80c's under full 100% load at turbo for ten minutes.  It will never see close to that in full tilt gaming operation, so it will work quite well.  In my case, I had to remove the motherboard to mount the bracket that holds it as the LG1700 adapter installs from underneath.  Plugging all the wiring back in to the board with the radiator mounted and the board back in the case was an adventure, so I suggest plugging connectors back in before securing the radiator to the mounting bracket.  The fan then clips on easily.  Any way you do it, if you are installing in a small case you'll have some tight spots to fuss with.  In the end, the instalation effort was well worth it.
reviews.author: McDo-it

reviews.title: Works Great! No Issues So Far.
reviews.comment:
I ordered this because I had a defective Arctic Liquid Freezer III 240mm AIO. I don't return broken products. I let the company keep the money so they can maybe one day fix their stupidity.... on that note I wont continue to complain about the Arctic Cooler!
This unit was extremely simple to install. One thing I noticed in terms of design was that you rotate the cooler 90 degrees for AMD where the tubes are either left/right of the CPU socket where as Intel will have the tubes top/bottom. Wont knock a star for aesthetics, I bought something that needs to cool my PC and its doing it swimmingly (ha, water joke).
I skipped out on using the MSI paste. I never trust paste that comes with manufacturer parts. Not knocking MSI, the paste is probably decent. But I want the highest quality paste possible. KINGPIN KPx is known to be insane especially for overclocking, which means it will remain cool. I usually buy Arctic Silver 5 (different "arctic" company than the AIO company) but lately on Amazon they are sold by 3rd party and shipped by Amazon. For all I know those pastes have been sitting for so long they "separated" by now. Not gonna risk it. The KPx I got was sold and shipped my Amazon. Hashtag winning (haha). So far my temps have been great and there is no weird noises. Double winning. I have my fans in push pull as per image. With rear fan as exhaust and PSU as exhaust. I know weird right? Most people would want their PSU to get fresh air.... WELL, this improves airflow so that air moves bottom to top of case. It works.
Many will notice the slim fans at the bottom. This is a jonsbo d32pro case. And you can also notice the motherboard is a back connect b650m project zero board. All connectors are on the back! making it super sleek and once again improving airflow. So if you are curious if you can fit the 7900xtx Red Devil from PowerColor utilizing this motherboard (top slot is x16 as apposed to many m-atx boards where its second slot) then you CAN fit two slim fans down there. I think I could have wedged in some full size fans, but I like having the air gap to help with any turbulence that might occur between the two. So far my temps are insanely low. But that's to be expected since all sides of the case are perforated except for the glass side cover that is frosted black (not installed in picture).
Obviously I didn't use the MSI fans... I dont care for RGB. And sure enough the only light from my pc comes from the GPU which is always red because "designed that way." I could plug in some color matching cables into the gpu but im lazy and that's also extra cables on the front section which I dont want. I like it clean.... So I cant comment on fan brightness/quality, or even the AIO pump section lighting. Its all disabled.
Value for money? I mean its a 240mm AIO and its not the cheapest but also not the most expensive. Its working. I dont have hard testing data to say if its good or not, maybe one of the youtuber reviewers will get to this unit eventually.... for now, its working, and that's all that matters.
The tubes are VERY easy to move around, which I like. The Arctic tubes are so hard to bend that manhandling them makes you cringe. These, they have a bit of flop but retain some stiffness. IMO the perfect "in-between."
SADLY, I ruined my silver/black aesthetic I was originally going for. I already own like 12 noctua NF-A12x25 fans so reusing them after having to rebuild my system after a failed Arctic AIO, I said EFF it. Performance is more important. No, I am not spending $100's of dollars to buy all the fans I have in black flavor.... waste of money when I have perfectly functional fans I can use. And this is only 5 of them. I have more in storage.... This build was a consolidation of size. I wanted something smaller and sleeker. I had a huge case that was super large prior which had all the fans installed including push/pull on a 360mm aio. But 360mm aio on a 7800x3d is overkill, so far my temps look the same as my 360mm setup previously. So winning.

reviews.title: Excellent product and a sweet price and comes with thermal paste
reviews.comment: I put this on the PC that I use specifically for my AtGames Legends Pinball to play in OTG.  My PC is an older 1150 Z97 motherboard with an Intel chip. This came with all sorts of mounting plate options so I figure everything is covered with the kit. This needed the backplate behind the motherboard, 4 standoff, 2 rails, and the 4 screws to mount, then the cooler bolds on top with 2 spring loaded screws for tension. The radiator mounted with 8 screws tho 4 seemed to be fine for a top mount. The 2 fans were already bolted into place. Honestly it's super quiet, I can't hear a thing, no pump noise at all and doesnt seem to be any louder or quieter than the Cooler Master Hyper 212 I had on it. The screen is pretty sweet, once you get the software and know how to work it it's a breeze to pick the settings and colors of the display. It will show pics if you want or gifs. I learned how to make a video of 7 gifs patched together into 1 long gif and put ir on there. Everything was crisp and top notch, excellent price as well since this wasn't something I actually NEEDED at all, my Hyper 212 was just fine,  this was more eye candy and without breaking the bank. The one thing people need to post about so you dont have to worry or buy any, is that this DOES come with the Thermal Paste. That was something I worried about as didn't want to have to run to the store to grab any and there are other similar kits on here that don't say whether they do or not. I kept trying to search the term thermal paste to see if people had it and just never found it. So this kit comes with thermal paste but it may be my only gripe is the quality. I put a full on 9 dot pattern on my cpu and the paste quality seems pretty dry and thick glue type, not a more liquid glue texture if that makes sense. So it may not be the best thermal paste and may dry out faster I'm not sure. I ended up pulling the cooler off a few days later and added an extra beed to the middle as it seemed like it didn't spread well.

Not only can you upload any pic or gif that you want, there are a ton of selections that you can chose from and they look stellar. I'm not aware of anything at this price point that can compete. It isn't even close. Installation is easy, in fact it is the first water cooler that I have installed myself. It does come with everything that you'll need, including thermal paste (although I bought a different brand not knowing it came with some). If you're on the fence then just buy it. In fact you can go online, look at reviews, and you'll see this cooler tests extremely well among all of the higher priced competitors. I ended up buying an aRGB hub because my MB only has one aRGB connection, and now they're all in sync with my Steam games via ASUS aura creator. The cooler fans are connected with the box of 5 aRGB case fans from Thermalright as well and they all perform flawlessly.  The only thing that folks may count as a detractor is the fact that you must load the TRCC image/gif each time you log on to your computer ...but there are so many options, try a new one each time!

reviews.title: Fairly simple install

The radiator may or may not be the standard thickness but the fans are like all my other 120 mm fans. Also, note the images in the product descriptions of this product are correct.  Only 2 fans and not 3 as stated in the product description. Another note. If after you install the software and the display does not work a reboot does seem to remedy the issue. The LCD customization works at first but goes back to default after a while. The custom image goes away and the localization converts back to non US datetime. I have contacted Thermalright to see if there is a resolution. I will update this review based on the support I get. I am hopeful. Update on update: I emailed customer support about my problem. reviews.title: AM4 Compatible, despite negative reviews saying otherwise
reviews.comment:
IF YOU HAVE AN AM4, READ THIS BEFORE PURCHASING!
I saw a few people complaining in the reviews about how this cooler doesn’t fit am4 motherboards. They’re both right and wrong. I have an AM4, and was unable to mount the cooler on my old AM4 mounting bracket. AM4 cooler mounting brackets have changed over the years, and only the current model works/fits with the cooler.
You can easily find an AM4 CPU bracket for less than $10 on Amazon. They’re super easy to install, and once I installed a newer bracket, the CPU cooler fit just fine.
Aside from the initial instillation hiccup (due to my older model of CPU cooler mounting bracket), this CPU cooler works great. My only complaint is that the mounting bracket doesn’t come with the cooler. Most CPU coolers come with that bracket. Not a huge deal, but definitely something to keep in mind.

reviews.author: ian

reviews.title: (UPDATED) Incredible performance, one annoying issue
reviews.comment:
This is by far the best CPU cooler I have ever owned when it comes to raw thermal performance. I've been fortunate enough to have tried the older D15, NH-U12A, Thermalright PS120 Evo, and the Be Quiet Dark Rock Elite. The NH-D15 G2 totally blows everything else away when it comes to how well it can keep my 12900K cool.
I tested out all those coolers whilst playing Forza Horizon 5 and Apex Legends for roughly 45 minutes to an hour. I generally found the likes of the older D15, NH-U12A, PS120 Evo, and Dark Rock Elite to hit a maximum temperature of roughly 70-75°C on the CPU package. The D15 G2, on the other hand, consistently keeps its peak temperatures below 65°C. Its performance is hands down the best I have ever seen for an air cooler trying to keep a power-hungry CPU like the 12900K cool.
However, not all is well. A wide variety of NH-D15 G2s are coming with a distinctive rattle-like noise when the fans speed up. Noctua says this is caused by a shipping-related incident that causes the top few fins to become loose, thus making a rattling noise. It’s really only heard with fan speeds over 75%, but it’s still there and can be quite audible depending on your hearing. It’s a shame, because the cooler performs exceptionally, and for a company that prides itself on quality and having the absolute quietest systems and fans, it's just unacceptable to have an issue this widespread for the insanely high price of this cooler. I have personally tried out 3 different G2 units and all of them have experienced the rattling issue. Not good.
Overall, the cooler lives up to its next-gen status by providing very meaningful temperature reductions. However, the rattling noise causes an annoyance that just should not exist for a product of this caliber. Because of that, I cannot recommend this cooler right now for those looking for the absolute quietest cooling option. Should Noctua correct this rattling issue, I will update my review accordingly.
UPDATE (Sep 9, 2024): Noctua has now implemented a fix for this cooler. They'll be shipping affected customers metal adhesive plates for the sides of the cooler to prevent the rattling from happening. Just reach out to their customer support and they'll hook you up, free of charge of course. They also still offer a full refund and a replacement towards the end of October when they begin shipping out revised units of the G2 with the rattling permanently fixed from the factory. This is fantastic customer support and shows Noctua genuinely cares about customer satisfaction. Thanks for being awesome, Noctua!
UPDATE (Sep 17, 2024): Just received the adhesive metal covers, and all I can say is wow. They actually eliminated any and all forms of rattle the cooler had! Plus, they look pretty cool as well. Because of this fix, the fact that both the covers and shipping from Austria were free of charge, and Noctua's prompt replies and eagerness to please customers AND on top of the cooler already being phenomenal in terms of performance, I will update the review to 5 stars. Thank you Noctua for being so awesome!
