reviews.title: Superb CPU Air Cooler on the market!
reviews.comment:
I was impressed that noise level and CPU temperature was outstanding! It's very quiet and my CPU temp was roughly around 60-70 degrees Celsius on average while I'm gaming with Intel Core i9-14900K (running at 5.7Ghz). In addition, it comes with 8 Heatpipes, high fin density to disperse more heat in order to keep your CPU run cool, dual 140mm G2 fans with excellent airflow and quiet noise level performance, Torx Hex Screw Driver, Thermal Compound, Brackets, etc.  It fits no problem inside Cooler Master H500M Medium size chasis and has enough clearance for RAM as well.
As for 1mm shimm washer, it's optional but I don't recommend installing 1mm shimm washer since it's a lot more difficult to install it with Intel's default ILM (Independent Loading Mechanism) which I highly recommend to get contact frame which fits no problem with LGA 1700 socket. By the way, this is HBC (High Base Convexity) which is ideal for Intel's LGA 1700 socket in order to prevent CPU deformation after long-term use.
As for price point, it is now very expensive which you'll be paying about $149.99 USD MSRP, compared to previous generation. But nonetheless, you pay what you get.
Other than that, I'm happy with product and Noctua has never let me down. And besides, this is by far the best CPU air cooler I've purchased.
P.S. I believe 140mm G2 (Square Frame) fans should be coming out in September 2024. If you want to improve CPU temperature for Intel's LGA 1700 socket, you must install contact frame before you install your actual cooler. Also, keep your backplate installed on the back of your motherboard too. Be sure to keep your CPU installed to prevent damaging your CPU socket pins.

reviews.title: Great Heat pipe cooler.
reviews.comment: This heat pipe cooler has 8 heat pipes rising onto each side of the cooler. And it comes with two 140mm fans to blow thru the fin stacks to cool the fluid down inside the heat pipes allowing it to be wicked back down to the cooling plate where it gets reheated again and expands quickly up the pipe to be cooled again and again over and over. This CPU cooler is very tall. I mean very tall! As in it barely fits into my Lian Li V1000 Aluminum case. The CPU Cooler requires enough space to allow the heat stack to fit below your side cover and the height required is 168mm or 6.62 inches. As well as the CPU cooler having the most heat pipes, the tallest in its class it has the largest price tag for a CPU cooler. It comes in three varieties, the one I am reviewing is for intel socket LGA1700 and LGA1851 CPUs. You can tell the version of cooler you are purchasing by the abbreviation after G2 in the name. HBC stands for High Base Convexity. As the Intel CPUs are prone to be concave in nature this cooler is predisposed to that shape thus providing an optimal adherence to the CPU when tightened down to the motherboard.

reviews.title: It's the best you can get for the price!
reviews.comment:
I had several doubts when buying because it looked very good for the price, and usually when a product offers a lot for a low cost, it tends to be a disappointment. This is not the case here.
ADVANTAGES:
- To begin with, the price is half or less than what a similar product from one of the top brands costs.
- Aesthetically, it's just as good as other brands. It comes with LED fans and an LED on the processor cooler, giving the PC a more stylish look.
- It keeps the CPU cool, has good heat dissipation. I live in a very hot city, and at idle, my processor doesn't go above 40°C; under full load, it reaches up to 60°C. I currently have a Ryzen 5700X.
CONS:
Installing the CPU cooler can be a bit frustrating. It only has two screws that attach to the CPU, but you have to give it a tiny turn to get it to fit on one side, and then do the same on the other. If you overtighten, it will pop off the other side. It's quite annoying, and it's the only downside I've found so far compared to installing other AIO coolers. However, it just takes a little patience.
P.S. I modified the fan coolers to perfectly match the case, but the stock ones are very good and look nice; they don't make much noise.
In conclusion, I highly recommend this product. For the price, it offers excellent performance and LEDs that will make your PC look even better.

reviews.title: Bright RGB and good performance
reviews.comment: The AIO replaced my small, $30 air cooler on my Ryzen 9 7900X. I tried to do some benchmark comparisons but realize my bio settings so I reset in between so I can't make a one-to-one comparison and I'm too lazy to go back and re-run test on my old cooler. Running the 7900X for 10 minutes straight on Cinebench R23, the cooler was able to keep CPU temps at around 86 or 87°C. In my books, keeping the CPU under 90C on sustained full load is good performance for this CPU. I thermal throttles at 95C. At full load, the fans and pump were audible, but that's something I expect a full load when I put my bio settings back to settings I'm used to which is running at 65 W TDP Eco mode, the fans and the pump were not audible at all, which is definitely an improvement from my previous cooler. In terms of build quality, everything from packaging to the actual hardware it feels well made. The contact plate came with a plastic cover to protect the pre-applied thermal paste the waterlines between the pump and radiator come with clips to keep the waterlines tidy. The kid comes with all the brackets screws standoffs and whatever else you'll need to front mount or top mount the radiator, and for Intel or AMD cpus. The insulation instructions were clear and concise, and I had no problems at any point during the installation. the rgb lighting on the CPU block is super bright and worked fine in the default mode of rotating rainbow colors along with the other RGB lights in my case. One thing that I didn't get to test is the software which I assume is used to control the RGB and fan curves. I'm guessing that the drivers for this didn't come out at the time of this review since it's pretty new currently the software simply just displays the computer stats like CPU utilization RAM utilization CPU clock speed, etc. etc.. there's a device page which did not detect the this AIO. The link and the instructions actually don't point to the software download page either I had to search for it on their website. I think the driver software is needed for the lighting to sync up with razor chroma or any of the other RGB software because razor chroma did not recognize that there was a device I could control when I tried. All in all, this AIO performed well under full load on my non-overclocked Ryzen 9 7900 X. The rgb is bright and pretty. I can safely recommend that you'll be get tying a quality product if you buy this.

reviews.title: Big change in temps, exceeded my expectations right out of the box.
reviews.comment:
Moved my last build into a new case,  replaced my huge air cooler with the MAG CORELIQUID A15 240.
This is my first experience using liquid cooling. I had the biggest baddest air cooler and wasn't real happy with it's performance in my 14900k build. Figured I'd give this cooler a shot, I was moving into a new case anyway.
The install was easy, not any more difficult than installing any other cooler. I was pleasantly surprised when I first fired up the rebuild, my temps were down considerably compared to my air cooler with the 240 cooler installed in the top panel. Then I moved it to the front panel to see what happens since I had plenty of room in the new case.  The result was better, I was able to push my tune and bench marks a little bit higher.
The fans that come with the cooler aren't bad, they're quiet, push a decent amount of air and don't require a fan header that pulls over 1amp.
If you're going to do a push pull configuration you'll need to get extra fan screws separately. The kit does not include extra fans screws, only the screws on the pre installed fans. There are plenty of case screws.
The 360 A15 will be my next liquid cooler for a new build. I can only imagine how the 360 A15 will perform when the 240's performance was so impressive right out of the box.

reviews.title: Well built, functional, great looking AIO pump setup
reviews.comment: My first use of an AIO water cooler met with reasonable success in this big fella.  Installed on my new Ryzen 7 5700X3D, it runs very cool even under extreme gaming stress.  I checked the BIOS temp readings alongside HW Monitor app and they show the same thing, it hasn't topped 52 C under stress.  Along with switching to this cooler from my old Noctua monster heatsink, I replaced my older Ryzen 5 2600 with a new Ryzen 7 5700X3D, all that said, this review is after running everything as is, I have not overclocked anything yet but will explore that with this new setup down the road, I doubt I will experience any issues with overclocking alongside this AIO providing sufficient cooling.  The overall construction is great, it comes well packaged with everything you'll need to install on any AMD or Intel CPU.  The instructions didn't mention using the included plastic stand off washers on the screws used to attach the radiator unit to the case frame but it's pretty easy to figure out.  Nice how it comes with pre-applied thermal paste too.  I have yet to read about any coolant leaks on other reviews, I suppose there's only so much that could be done about that given the entire concept of liquid cooling.  My AM4 mainboard is an older Asus B-450M-A which doesn't have a dedicated 4-pin AIO header, so I connected to pump to the CPU fan header, temps and fan speed register in the BIOS and on various hardware monitoring apps, so I'm guessing that's the speed of the pump???  The three fans on the radiator are wired together with a separate 4-pin plug which I plugged into one of the two chassis fan PWM connectors.  That being said, make sure PWM mode is enabled because at first the radiator fans would surge and throttle sounding like a V-22 on take off, but once PWM was enabled on the CPU fan header via the BIOS it calmed down.  Now even under load its no louder than the other five 140mm case fans I have running.  My only issue is my mainboard has one older 4-pin RGB header (already in use with strip lighting synched to Asus Aura), this has the newer 3 pin (and different voltage / non-compatible with 4 pin) ARGB plugs, so the lighting on the radiator fans and pump do not work, but it's hardly a big deal.  I'm trying to squeeze every year out of this already eight year old mainboard that I can, so if this is my only issue switching to AIO cooling, I cannot complain.  I have been a fan of ASUS for decades and this cooler holds true to form.

reviews.title: AIO works, but premium features (lcd) bricked on Lian Li initiated update, so not great. UPDATE
reviews.comment: Update: Lian Li's customer support stopped communicating with me after their troubleshooting steps failed to resolve the LCD screen issue. I've sent multiple communications to my rep to get my RMA processed, but I've been ghosted. So, the LCD screen is DOA, and their support is DOA. Pro: The AIO was easy to install and reasonably straightforward, although the system wiring was more challenging than needed. Cooling has been good after installation. I'm getting 38-45 degrees Celsius on idle or minimal load. A couple of passes through Cinebench multi-core tests produced a high of 88 degrees Celsius under full load, better than the 92 degrees I experienced with a Deepcool LS720 I used before. Con: Let's talk about the LCD screen. On the first boot, I got it to display without issue. However, it wasn't natively discovered by the Lian Li 3 Connect version I used. So, I updated the L-Connect software and got it to report. When I went to update the firmware on the device, I got an "Update failed. Reboot system and try again..." (or something along those lines. I haven't gotten the LCD screen to light up since then. In my experience, the firmware update failure bricked the unit, so now I have a really expensive (but quality AIO) without the premium feature I purchased. Other than the cooling, I wanted to use the LCD screen for this since I was moving to a new case and removing the LCD screen I used to monitor my old Jonsbo D41 case. Also, I utilize SL120 and 140 V2 Uni fans from Lian Li, so this is a good way to integrate everything into one controller. I can't integrate the cooler wiring into my Lian Li controller, which is fine, but the inability to even manage the cooler via L-3 Connect creates a problem. Final Thought: Get the version without the LCD screen if you are on the fence, or wait for the Deepcool Mystique AIO to come back in stock if you need the LCD screen. Also, NZXT Kraken is inexpensive for 360mm AIOs with an LCD screen, which I ultimately purchased to replace my bricked Galahad II LCD screen. I want my RMA to go through with Lian Li; otherwise, I will just pay the cost of the device for poor manufacturing quality on their part.
reviews.author: Michael

reviews.title: Great cooler, software is progressing well.
reviews.comment: Overall, I am very happy with this AIO.  It is installed on an Intel 14900K, with idle temps around 28-30C (ambient between 22-25C).  I used a different thermal paste (Arctic MX-6) than what was pre-installed on the AIO, and am happy with the results.  The Asetek 8th Gen pump provides peace of mind, and the radiator and fans provide ample cooling ability.  Cinebench R23 does see near 100C temps during multiple runs, but only 3 of the cores actually reached that temp, and the throttling was minimal (40000 multicore).  I have not attempted any undervolting at the time of this review, so temps might be more under control afterwards. As for the software, there are (were) minor bugs that I have experienced, but I have also seen said bugs get patched with frequent software/firmware updates.  With L-Connect 3 v2.0.4 and LCD firmware 0.9, I have a stable solution, with no more issues.  Lian Li seems keen to work hard at fixing these issues, and quickly, providing frequent updates as they solve more issues with a brand new product.  Hats off to them for the excellent customer service in that regard. System fans are all Lian Li, plugged into a hub, and MSI Mystic Light used to set G.Skill RAM and MSI 4090 Suprim Liquid X 24G RGB.  I have had no conflicts with any of the RGB in my system. For those with software or RGB conflicts/issues, my only advice is to be patient.  As I stated above, Lian Li seem like they are focused on providing a great product with great software to support it, but these things take time to work out all the kinks with the massive variety of products that could be combined in a user-built PC.

reviews.title: Good quality for the price, extremely thick. Check fit/clearance with motherboard and case
reviews.comment:
So far so good,
Temps:
Keeping my i9 14900KF at decent temps. Did not benchmark it but on gaming load and when going CFD projects the CPU didn’t go past 80c. The CPU I have is pretty fast so full load times were not observed in long periods but so far on idle it’s not bad averaging at 38c.
Aesthetics:
Lian Li is known for their aesthetics and this AIO is one of the nicest ones I’ve used. I like the LCD screen. It’s nice but I wish it was better. I primarily use a monitor that’s 240hz and the difference really bugs me. Also the resolution is pretty low which I wish was better because I don’t like the newer curved AIO screens and prefer the simple ones. I was able to test an NZXT AIO and their screens were at a better resolution. Likely because the pixel density was better.
I do wish the software was better, I’d like to be able to customize my AIO screen more and I like Thermalrights customizable software vice this Lian Li software.
The fans and RGB lights are good, not too obnoxiously bright.
Value:
You get what you pay for and this is more of a premium AIO and it functions well for temps but the screen is a bit lackluster in clarity. Everything else performs as advertised. Like the cooling function works better than I thought it would on an Intel i9 14900KF.
INSTALLATION:
Easy. Follow the instructions and it’s just like all the other AIOs. Though it’s a dense and big AIO so make sure you look at the clearance before you buy it. I tried using it in three cases and the only case it fit in were the ones where 360 AIOs fit. Though I do have to blame this on the ROG motherboard because the VRM heatsink and ROG logo is thick. That was the main reason it didn’t fit and if you have, let’s say, a tomahawk or a more budget motherboard then you should be able to fit it in most 280 compatible cases. It’s just super thick (fans and tubing) so some cases where the PSU is front mounted it won’t fit. The tubes or fans will get in the way.
Overall satisfied with the purchase and let’s see how long it lasts.

reviews.title: A bit loud, installation not for beginners, but does work well
reviews.comment: This Liquid CPU Cooler is designed to give you a more advanced cooling system for your computers processor than the standard fan system. While it does its job well once in place, there are a few problems that need addressed. First, and something that will probably affect people the most long-term: this thing is pretty loud. It's not "jet engine" levels but it's very noticeable and for a lot of environments its probably just too much. Second, installation instructions on this are not the best. While you can follow them if you know what you're doing, they aren't for a beginner. Could be pretty easy to miss something that someone experienced would assume you already know, so I wouldn't recommend doing this yourself if you're new to PC building or water cooler systems. Lastly, there's quite a bit of excess cable, which is great if you have a larger case, but if not then it's a little tough to keep things clean. Keep the size of your setup in mind before purchasing something like this. That said, this does its job really well. Does a great job keeping things cool, and the RGB looks really nice. It's compatible with any brand processor, and price-wise this is in a good spot. As long as the pros outweigh the cons for you, this does seem to work really well. Just be sure you know what you're doing going in, and be ok with a lot of noise.

reviews.title: Unbeatable Value & Performance: The Budget ARGB Fan King!
reviews.comment:
After installing the Thermalright TL-C12C-S 5-pack in three custom builds (gaming rigs, workstations, and a media server), I’m stunned by how these $20–$25 fans outperform competitors costing 3× more.
Core Strengths
Elite Cooling for Pennies:
Each fan delivers 66.17 CFM airflow and 1.53 mm H₂O static pressure at max speed—enough to handle dense heatsinks and case ventilation. In testing, they dropped CPU temps by 8°C vs. stock fans in a Ryzen 5 7600X build. Even at 50% PWM, airflow rivals premium brands like Noctua and be quiet!
Whisper-Quiet Operation:
The S-FDB bearings minimize vibration, keeping noise ≤25.6 dBA at full tilt (1550 RPM). At 800–1000 RPM (typical gaming loads), they’re near-silent. Far quieter than cheaper jet-engine alternatives
Stunning ARGB Lighting:
High-brightness LEDs with 17 customizable effects (rainbow, pulse, static, etc.). The translucent blades diffuse light evenly, creating a "halo" effect. Daisy-chaining support simplifies wiring—connect 5 fans to one ARGB header!
Minor Nitpicks
Wire Management: Daisy-chaining 5 fans creates cable clutter—use zip ties!.
Documentation: Chinese-only manuals may confuse beginners (YouTube solves this).
ARGB fans need a 3-pin (5V) header on Motherboard.
Pick up SATA to 5V 3PIN Fan Controller incase motherboard doesn't have a specify ARGB  3-pin (5V) header.
Full-Speed Noise: Audible at 1550 RPM—set a PWM curve below 1300 RPM for silence
For under $30, this 5-pack is a no-brainer for builders, upgraders, and RGB enthusiasts. It trounces budget rivals (like Arctic P12) in aesthetics and matches premium fans in cooling. Whether you’re decking out an O11 Dynamic or reviving an old rig, Thermalright proves you don’t need to splurge for brilliance.

reviews.title: Great fan for open intake/exhaust
reviews.comment:
To start, I ordered this fan to replace the stock ibuypower rgb exhaust fan. From testing and data collected from other manufacturers this fan is one of the best in terms of non restrictive air transfer while being slightly underwhelming in terms of static pressure. This means it is perfect for an exhaust fan without any mesh or radiator to push through.
Operation is nearly silent at full rpm and I have this fan’s curve set much more aggressively being the only exhaust fan & I never notice it changing rpm. Sound is more of a whoosh than a hum like other fans similar in the way noctua fans are. This is most likely from the fins on the blades and the difference between this fan and my previous ibuypower branded fan is night and day.
Bonus points for having a black and white logo on the intake side of the fan Be quiet!! Previous fan offerings have all been orange and subjectively unsightly in an all black setup like the one I have.
Overall I ended up just getting one of these for the exhaust, and arctic p12s for intake as I use a push pull on my radiator making the static pressure a must have.

They’re just about dead silent at idle and audible but tolerable at higher RPMs, no annoying whine or whistle with these just a rush of air.  Wanted RGB for the kids and the colors and diffusion look fine to my eye.  These are pricey however they don’t have rubber pads at the mount holes and they have comically short power and RGB cables which caused an additional purchase of 4 pin extension cables.  A nice long RGB cable on my 120mm thermalright cpu fan had a daisy chain part to it and is the only reason I could finish the build without RGB extension cables.  So these aren’t perfect but they’re fair quality with decent overall performance.  Hope they last!

reviews.author: Keith Jones

reviews.title: Better airflow. Better noise performance. Better quality.
reviews.comment:
Setup (Idle):
1) NF-A12 as an intake fan (1400 RPM)
2) ARCTIC P12 as exhaust. (1300 RPM)
3) CPU Heatsink: Noctua NH-U12S chromax.Black paired with NF-F12 120mm (500 RPM)
Under load:
GPU temps never rise above 68*C. The key difference between the NF-A12 and the ARCTIC P12 is that the NF-A12 never lets the hot air stay in the case long enough to get hot. It truly moves air extremely well. And that's with just one NF-A12 intake fan.
Next experiment:
I will be adding an other NF-A12 as an exhaust fan to see if it improves temperatures even more.
I do not know if older iterations had complete sets of 4 bumpers for each color, but the current version has four bumpers for all of the colors available, including black. There is also a sound dampener, I think? Please see photo.
Important note: Reviews stating that there are only gray bumpers must be older versions. If you purchase it as of February 25, 2024, rest assured you will receive four black bumpers. It also comes with hardware - four screws. Be aware that the threading is very tight. If the fan is in a position that is hard to tighten the screws, please have patience. I dropped the screws at least four times. This is good, though. That means the material is not low quality.
My only caveat is that the length of the cable that comes with the fan is a little too short. I was barely able to reach the SysFan header at the bottom of the motherboard. Please see photo. The cable has a sleeve so it makes for a bad bend when you insert the 4-pin connector to the SysFan pins. Be careful not to force it or else you could damage the pins and the motherboard. Most motherboards were not designed to accommodate enough space for 4-pin cable and sleeves like this. Usually, case fans or fans in general come with 4-pin wires that have no sleeves so it is much easier to cable manage and maneuver around small openings.
I would have preferred a longer cable as most cases these days have good cable management. You can loop it to the back of the case and get rid of cables hanging over your motherboard. Noctua made it too short and not long enough. The cable does not know whether to be short or long. It is a bad length. I have a slightly larger than usual, mid-tower case - NZXT H7 Flow. It is larger than the NZXT H500. For smaller mid-towers, you should be okay. And if you have the NZXT H7 Flow, it should be okay as well, as I had about 1-2 inches of cable to pull on.
At 1300-1400, it becomes quite audible. But the idea with this fan is to keep it at around 500-900 RPM because that's where it's most quiet and moves a lot of air. Even at 1400 RPM, I cannot hear it from where I am sitting, although there is a slight hum. I have my PC case underneath my desk, so please keep that in mind. With NZXT case fans, I can clearly hear them. And with ARCTIC P12s, I can barely hear them, if at all.
Compared to the ARCTIC P12, they both have different sound or noise signatures. The NF-A12 has a much more rounded sound. Not nearly as grating as the ARCTIC P12. If I had to choose, I would go with the A12x25. I am very sensitive to noise and I have excellent hearing. If you are sensitive to sound and you have high sensory, then please keep this in mind.
I think for those reasons, some people are buying The Noctua NF-A12x25 as case fans. I am using it as case fans. I wanted a quiet fan that outperforms other case fans in terms of air flow and getting rid of hot air from inside the case while remaining quiet/silent.
Even then, I think I hear a slight hum from the NF-A12x25, where as the ARCTIC P12 does not have a hum at all. Arguably, the P12 is quieter and more silent than the A12x25. It is only when you put your ear directly next to the P12, you can hear its sound or noise signature.
Ultimately, the NF-A12 is not significantly better than the ARCTIC P12. It is more like a sideways upgrade. It depends on what you prefer. As far as temperatures, The NF-A12 slightly edges out the P12 by a couple of degrees (Celsius). Nothing to write home about.
If you already have the P12 and you are not bothered by its sound and noise levels, then stick with them. The value of the P12 is difficult to beat. A 5-pack of ARCTIC P12 is about $24, but one NF-A12 is about $35. The extra accessories such as the bumpers stay in the box because I purchased it to match the black and white theme for my case.
Again, there are four black bumpers despite what other reviews have stated. But not eight bumpers to cover all corners. I think that is what other reviewers were alluding to, but it isn't the biggest deal. I would have preferred eight black bumpers and no other colors, and an extra cable that is longer. If you are planning to use the NF-A12 as an exhaust fan, I do not think it will reach one of the top 4-pins on the motherboard. If it does, it will probably droop over the motherboard.
When it comes to NF-A12 as an intake fan, I cannot confirm with absolute certainty that it has improved my GPU hot spot temps, but it has dropped from 42*C (with ARCTIC P12) to 38*C (with NF-A12), so far. For the first time, my GPU temp and Hot Spot temps, according to HWMonitor, is within 8*C of one another while idle. This is considered excellent.
Ultimately, the NF-A12 is difficult to recommend over excellent value propositions such as the ARCTIC P12. The NF-A12 moves significantly more air, but idle temps are only slightly better by 2-3*C. The more rounded noise or sound signature is preference, as the ARCTIC P12 is nearly inaudible unless you put your ear next to it. The NF-A12 has a humming sound that I can hear even though my PC is underneath my desk. That is about 3 feet away from my ears. Where as with the ARCTIC P12, I was unable to hear any humming noise.
With that said, if you have the ARCTIC P12, you may want to consider hanging onto them and save your money. The value proposition just isn't there for me. I do not plan to return it, though. I like experimenting with different case fans to get the lowest probable temps while idle or under load. The humming noise kind of bothers me even with headphones on, listening to music. The NF-A12 @ 1300-1400 RPM isn't as quiet as some reviewers make it out to be and it can be misleading due to biases and echochambers.
Update:
While my previous assessment noted that the NF-A12 is more of a side upgrade, I have changed my conclusion to it being a superior case fan than the ARCTIC P12. The main reason being because it has effcient airflow. It moves hot air out of the case far better than the P12.
Temperatures in every category have improved and it doesn't let the ambient temperature climb. It gets rid of the heat and doesn't let temperatures become too hot. This is the key factor and difference the A12 does far better than the P12 and other generic case fans.
reviews.author: Elann

reviews.title: Fantastic airflow with VERY minimal noise
reviews.comment: Absolutely amazing. I did a LOT of research into my fan upgrades as I was swapping out all the fans in my case with these. When I say it's dead quiet, it's DEAD quiet. I normally have fans in my room going and I can barely hear them with them on OR off. The airflow is fantastic, with my Ryzen 7 9700X been having some problems controlling temps as my case fans came with the case and weren't controllable. At 50-60% speed idle and 60-75% under load it is barely noticeable. I will say, they are VERY expensive. At $37-$45 ish that I saw when I was looking online, they are by far the most expensive fan I've ever bought. Worth EVERY penny. Performance is top notch. The cables were the perfect length to run along the edge of the chassis and to the back for cable management, barely noticeable and not blocking the fans. PWM connects like any normal fan, nothing special, just a 4 pin connector. The step up and down is fantastic and barely noticeable on the ramp up during initial load temps. I do very much enjoy the little color corners for the fans. I don't have any RGBs in my case so I quite like the very small red accent the corners give my build. The rubber anti vibration gasket it comes with does it's job well. I hear my GPU fans more than I do the Noctuas. Overall 9/10. Would be a 10/10 if they were cheaper.
reviews.author: Gabriel Sturek

reviews.title: Perfection. I have 11 of them in my PC
reviews.comment:
I got tired of fans failing, starting to make annoying noises over time, etc. I have tried fans from Corsair, Cooler Master, Scythe, Arctic, etc etc. Have had issues with them all.
I've had these 11 fans in my PC for a year now and haven't had a single issue. They are whisper quiet, powerful. I love them.
reviews.author: ZoteTheMitey

reviews.comment:
Expensive, but you get what you pay for.
Noctua is the absolute best in the business when it comes to cooling. These fans push a butt load of air, all while being nearly silent.
That, combined with the sleek design, minimal branding, and all black color, make these fans a great addition to a clean setup. 10/10 would buy again
reviews.author: CaT

reviews.title: Expensive but worth every penny.  Exceptional engineering and build quality.
reviews.comment: Most people would balk at the idea of spending $35 for a 120mm fan, when there are literally hundreds of other options in the $5 to $10 range.  However, if you are looking for the pinnacle of quality, reliability and as close to completely silent operation as possible, then this fan is worth the entry price.  Another key point about the NF-A12 is that it provides enough static pressure to work with any heatsink or radiator out there.  The cheaper fans can move air just fine when used as a case fan, but put an impedance in front of them and they will quickly lose up to 100% of their efficiency.  For my build, I put this fan on a Thermalright SI-100 heatsink  over a Ryzen 5 7600X.  With de-volting, I am happily sitting at 60c under load and a computer you cannot hear at all.  This fan is fantastic and I am glad I bought it.
reviews.author: Mark Twain

reviews.title: So for builds that 25mm fans are slightly too thick, this is a perfect solution. Otherwise, stick with whatever brand fan u like
reviews.comment:
Haven't tested the radiator fan-temp, but on full speed, it is a bit noisy than 1350rpm Arctic F12, which I give 5 stars without hesitation.
The air flow is concentrated comparing with Arctic F12, which feels like a ring air flow. I did feel the air pressure is a tad stronger at full speed.
To be honest, if Arctic makes 15mm fans, I will not buy this one, because Arctic fan gave me good experience, and also provides 6 years warranty.
Only reason to buy this was because I need to put 360 radiator into Define C TG, but there is not much space for regular 25mm fans.
All things putting aside, this fan is excellent, only con would be the high price. However,
You will get some spitter/extender cables, so considering those prices, it is fine. It is more like a fan combined with some accessaries sold for a relatively high price.
Very quiet, very quality build, soft pads are big pluses.
One more thing I noticed was when it is running at full speed, fan blades are invisible, which is interesting. I like it. Maybe that's the reason it used such color.
I didn't plan on this review, so it is completely write as I think.
Finally, I decided to change 4 stars to 5 stars.
It is expensive, but everything else related to a fan is satisfying.
I only have one fan, so I cannot test the radiator performance, so I will skip that.
Final thoughts:
For my current build, a relatively large case, I tend to use Arctic fans for 800-900rpm which return a really good temp result with almost no noise at all.
If I need to build a tight small form case, I will definitely go with this one.
Quietness is the only important thing for me. Otherwise, there are tons of cheap fans provide similar performance with jet engine noise.

reviews.author: Cody

reviews.title: Best Option For A DIY Receiver Cooler
reviews.comment: My Onkyo TX-NR7100 was constantly hitting triple digits (Fahrenheit), so a cooling solution was definitely needed.  I’m equally not fond of the aesthetics of just placing fans over the receiver’s exhaust vents (I needed front exhaust anyway) or the prices of the much more visually appealing Infinity AIRCOM products, so it was DIY time.  There are plenty of less expensive fans that I could have used, but I feel like Noctua brings a little more to the table than the others and I was still able to make this for half the cost of a front exhaust AIRCOM S10.  Any other fan would have required a PWM control or adjustable voltage power adapter to reduce RPMs for quieter operation, but Noctua had me covered with the included LNA (low noise adapter) cables that drop the noise level down to a whisper quiet 34 dBA (combined) while providing solid airflow at 83 CFM (combined).  I can faintly hear the fans from my main listening position that is 12’ from the receiver if the room is perfectly quiet, but that noise completely disappears at even the lowest volumes I listen to.  The cooling is excellent with the highest temp I’ve seen with my laser thermometer being about 89F with the receiver’s volume up to 65 (which is the loudest I ever go), but most often the temp stays around 83F-84F, which is pretty much ideal.  Exceptional materials and build quality, excellent airflow to noise ratio, a 6-year warranty, and the insane 150,000 hours MTBF made these fans an easy choice for my project.
reviews.author: Richard3107

reviews.title: Great thin fans for tight spaces
reviews.comment:
So I was building a new PC finally after over 5 years on the old one without upgrading a single thing. I decided I wanted to go with an AIO water cooler on this new build and I picked up a case that was setup with that in mind. Unfortunately I didn't think to consider the clearance on the motherboard and heatsinks of the memory and when the time came to install I found the motherboards memory slots were way up at the top of the board and the giant "wings" that made up the memories heatsinks made that problem even worse. When I installed the AIO with the fans that came with it they actually slightly covered the memory slots to the point even a stick without a heatsink wouldn't fit in there (just barely).
I knew I'd seen thin form-factor fans before and I know Noctua has a great reputation (aside from their ugly color scheme). I picked these up and they fit on the AIO with ease and provided just enough space for the memory sticks to fit in the slots successfully. Best part is these are rated even better than the fans that came with the AIO in the first place and they are very quiet. It seems price is the only drawback to these fans as they match or exceed your average 120mm in all other respects. Of course, there's also the ugly colors but luckily on the roof of my case they aren't really seen anyway.

I'm seeing a 15% temperature difference in my entire system GPU included love the appearance color is amazing. installation was easy. they seem to be pretty reliable for the short time I've had them they fit perfect I love the little rubber isolators that they have in the backs of the fan

reviews.comment: super quiet. very powerful. low power consumption allowing you to daisy chain many fans. vibrant color. piece of cake to install, mounting screws were included. they keep my system cooler than the stock fans at a lower noise level. They have separate very long cables for the pwm fans and the argb lights making your options limitless. solid construction and function perfectly.

reviews.author: Ethan Kouts

reviews.title: The most amazing FAN you could ever want in your case.
reviews.comment:
Let me state this first.  I absolutely hate noisy fans and then I hate underperforming ones.  If your case FANs are underperforming or doing excessive noise, then this is your chance to make it right.
Noctua has been a long time friend in my life now. They keep saving me from having to suffer the horrendous high-pitch noise that can be heard on other FANs.  Trust me when I say this,  I'm completely bend on silent PCs.  The problem is that I also like performing PCs and having to cool down an Ryzen 9 3950X with 128GB of RAM and an RTX2080 Ti is no easy fit.
I've purchased a couple of P14 (3 in fact) to replace the current ones in my shiny new NZXT H710i case.  The default FANs were silent enough but they were definitely underperforming, also, when turned to max power they are noisy too.
I've replaced the 3 intake front fans with 2 of these P14 beauties and also the rear FAN.  Put in tandem onto the same controller the front and the read are incredible powerful.  When on idle I've set them to 600 RPM.  Trust me when I say this,  it is impossible to hear them work,  it's like you do not have a PC connected at all.
I'm using a Silent Corsair power supply so the only noise I hear from my PC now is the actual pump from the watercooler.  As soon as I throw a heavy game into the mix those fans will speed up to a max of 1570 RPM. Yes, they can be heard at this point but the whole idea is that they throw power when needed and be silent when they are not.
At max power though they are less noisy than the ones installed on the case and since I'm now have 3 FANs in total compared to 4, it's much more quiet too.  The peformance has also increased.  My GPU is now at 78  full load compared to 81 with default FANs and the CPU is also cooler by 3 degrees.
For me the whole point about using this FANs is to reduce noise and still have competent FANs in the system.  It was no surprise that I've ended up with a better performing system that is now dead silent when on idle.
Noctua never dissapointed me.  I could get the premium version of this FAN but this one was better looking for my case so I went with the REDDUX which is a cheaper version in grey.  The technology is about the same and the results are similar, it's just these FANs do not have the premium parts such as the low power adaptor and noise dumpeners, fortunately I had a couple of dampeners from my other Noctua FANs so paying more for the premium versions was not required in this case.
If you have any doubts that these fans could do good to your system, doubt no more, they are also beautiful  !
If I ever change the case again, swapping default FANs for these is a must. Nobody can do FANs the way Noctua does, they are so passionate about it and it shows.  Their products are TOP quality, you will not be dissapointed.
reviews.author: Alex Vojacek

reviews.title: Quiet and High Flow
reviews.comment:
I bought 2 of these fans to replace the exhaust 200mm I had for my case. The 200mm had started to slow and become an issue.
Replacement was extremely easy and straight forward, at least for me, since they are plugged directly into the power-supply so the fan controller is bypassed and also on full speed.
The moment I plugged them in these things started to put out some major air, and also made my PC cooler. I have ordered another 140mm and 2 of the 120mm (same brand) just to replace all of my fans.
honestly great price for great fan, specially since the ones that came with my case are hitting 10 years old
definately get them to replace stock fans
reviews.author: Joseph

reviews.title: Good
reviews.comment: Nice fan. Silent, long cable, as expected from Noctua.
reviews.author: Ohead

reviews.title: Great fan!
reviews.comment: Excellent silent fan.  Noctua fans never disappoint.  I'm using it to cool a tube headphone amplifier, and it works great.  You can't go wrong with Noctua fans, highly recommended.
reviews.author: MossManPNW

reviews.title: Good fans for circulating air around houseplants.
reviews.comment:
This review is for the "Noctua NF-P14s redux-1500 PWM" 140mm fans.
I bought these because I wanted some very quiet fans that could provide good air movement to the plants I have indoors. I tried a few non-computer fans first, but found them to be a bit too noisy. After doing some brainstorming, I found a way that I could mount some PC fans to my wire shelving unit, so that left trying to find some PC fans that could move lots of air.
There are some other 140mm fans that can move more air, specifically ones that are 38mm thick. However, most, if not all of those use ball bearings and tend to be noticeably more noisy. I feel like these Noctua NF-P14 Redux fans are a very good middle ground.
Definitely recommend these for plants if you can mount them within a couple feet of the plants. They are quiet and effective. They're not the most inexpensive option, but I feel that the low noise level and high air movement are worth the bit of extra cost.
reviews.author: S.H.

reviews.title: GOOD FANS AND EXTREME PERFORMANCE
reviews.comment: I bought these to replace the fans that came with my DeepCool LT720 liquid cooler, and I'm really happy with the change. Visually, there's no comparison: these Arctic P12 PRO RGB fans look much nicer, the RGB is more vibrant, and the case looks much better. As for performance, they move a lot of air. I didn't feel any performance loss compared to the original fans of the liquid cooler; on the contrary, the temperatures remained good. Regarding noise, with a well-adjusted speed curve, they don't bother me during normal use. However, when I set them between 70% and 100%, the noise becomes more noticeable and can be a bit annoying, but I think that's normal given the amount of air they move. Overall, I'm happy with the change. If anyone is thinking about replacing their liquid cooler fans with something that offers better aesthetics and good performance, these Arctic fans are a great fit; you just need to configure them properly.
reviews.author: David Sarmiento

reviews.title: Skeptical but happily proved wrong
reviews.comment:
I cannot speak to longevity quite yet. What I can say is that the lofty claims of nearly 7mm H20 static pressure are probably true. Which to be completely honest, I was expecting it to be more marketing fluff then reality. I've been building custom waterloops in PCs for about 20 years. Finding extremely high static pressure fans that aren't poop brown and don't sound like a 747 used to be darn near impossible. This will be my 3rd time purchase Arctic brand fans and my first time with this model. I like their slim 15mm thick fans for builds with very little space to work. Never a single mechanical issue and they've performed exceptionally well for me. So buying this model was an easy decision. Firstly the fans have a really nice weight and feel to them. When you pick them up they do not feel chintzy or low quality. I have two of these going in to a very small Lian Li ITX case so they are my only source of air movement. On top of that, they have to push through a very dense EK radiator. And boy do they! At 100% they are quite audible but not annoyingly so. They push so much air, I don't think you'd ever need 100%. They feel of great quality, they look fantastic if you're in to ARGB and they've very affordable. Compared to top name brands like ASUS, Corsair, Thermaltake, they're like half the cost which is just crazy. I've owned fans from all of those brands and had mechanical issues. Not with Arctic.
Bottom line is they do as advertised and are a reasonable price. I plan to buy extras just incase they discontinue the model.
reviews.author: MB

reviews.title: These fans are perfection, at least for me
reviews.comment:
Big pressure push. Very quiet until they need to be less quiet to provide better airflow. At or near idle, silent.
Excellent value from one of the only companies left that doesn't force you onto their own software just to adjust the fans or use the ARGB. They're all happily controlled by the FanControl app and SignalRGB via an Airgoo ARGB controller. There are no proprietary gymnastics in the wiring whatsoever. Full functionality with whatever you want to use to control them.
They don't have a hint of fragility to them, unlike the Corsair fans I've dealt with recently. Color accuracy seems good, but I only have these and the 140mm version as case fans.
They are exactly what I was looking for in ARGB fans. Big CFM, big pressure, totally open controls.
reviews.author: Ferret

reviews.title: Quality
reviews.comment: Fans are good. RGB are vibrant. Quality LED.  Yes they are loud but very low noise compared to other 3000 rpm fans. And you can adjust fan speed in bios or download a fancurve program to lower speeds a bit for less noise. Only complaint is cables are short and had to buy a extender to work with my rig. Other than that happy with purchase.
reviews.author: Geovanni haro

reviews.title: Great ARGB high performance fans.
reviews.comment: First things first, they are loud IF you have them at full rip. Keep them under 60-70% and I promise they are not loud and they still move plenty of air. These things spin up all the way to 3000rpm which is about 1000rpm more than what most people are used to and they are far quieter at 3000rpm than most other fans that spin up to that speed. They are pretty high quality especially when you take into account their price and they’re far more powerful than the regular P12s that everyone has loved for years. I’d say they’re a wonderful value and you’ll love them as long as you setup your fan curves right. Download Fan Control on your pc to make things way easier on yourself.
reviews.author: Cody Hargo

reviews.title: Best fans on the market
reviews.comment: Amazing quality, and you cant beat the price. Looks great and performs well. Low noise. No vibration. Plenty fast and moves a lot of air. I would recommend for anyone.
