reviews.title: Bargain price for a quality fan
reviews.comment: They work great and are quiet
reviews.author: gary

reviews.title: Always Arctic for the Win!
reviews.comment: Fantastic Fans - These are 3k RPM fans designed to move large volumes of air. Undoubtedly, Arctic makes top-tier fans. They are easy to install, and the ARGB is fantastic. Like others have stated, run each fan to a controller; in my case, an Airgoo controller. The colors are vibrant, and the cooling is off the charts. The static pressure these create is outstanding. I've tuned my fan curves so there really is no noise issue.
reviews.author: David

reviews.title: Look good, feel good, work good.
reviews.comment:
These are great. I replaced my Corsair 4000D's intakes and bought another for the exhaust. It started with how satisfied I was with the Arctic Freezer Pro III. These fans ramp up to 3000 easily. You'll most likely not need those RPMs, and you'll start to hear the fans spinning at those rates. Once I tuned them down, they are very quiet. I can receive positive air pressure in my rig, and I'm running my 9 9950x under 60C playing BG3 in 4k Ultra.
I'd give them 5 stars if they had a little less profile depth and were a little quieter at 3k RPM, if possible.
reviews.author: Joe

reviews.title: Excellent
reviews.comment:
Excellent reverse fan, put at the bottom of the case and tuned with pwm  bios profile at slight lower speed than the forward fans (they naturally make a bit more noise but it is typical of reverse fan). Since they here to ease fresh air into the case, I have no pb with lower speed to keep the overall system very silent.
I own noctua fans, and they are a premium alternative when price comes into play
reviews.author: Julien

reviews.title: Reliable, Quiet Performance—Not the Prettiest, But the Best for PC Builds
reviews.comment: I’ve been building PCs for a while, gaming, content creation, and sometimes even working on tight low-profile builds. Noctua fans are always a go-to for me, and the NF-A9x14 PWM is no exception. First off, the looks: let’s be real, the classic beige-and-brown Noctua color scheme is not exactly pretty, and honestly, it never matches my cases. But honestly, you buy these for the performance, not the aesthetics. The airflow is excellent for such a slim (92x14mm) fan, and the noise levels are super low. I used this one for one of my early Ryzen builds and it held up for years, still ran like new when I finally upgraded my setup. One of the reasons I stick with Noctua is the reliability. Their quality control is top tier. This fan worked perfectly out of the box, no issues with installation, and always maintained good thermals in my system. I’ve never had a Noctua fan die on me, and their thermal paste kits are just as good, always my go-to for builds. Yes, Noctua fans cost a bit more than the cheap brands, but it’s worth it for the peace of mind. You get what you pay for: quiet operation, long lifespan, and consistently good airflow. The included 4-pin PWM connector means it’s compatible with basically any modern motherboard, and you get precise fan control in BIOS or with your favorite software. For anyone who builds their own PCs, whether you’re a gamer, a content creator, or just want a reliable and quiet fan, Noctua is a name you can trust. I’m a bit of a tech junkie, and I always find myself coming back to Noctua for any important cooling job. Overall: not the prettiest fan, but easily one of the best on the market for performance and reliability. Highly recommended for any DIY build.
reviews.author: Paulryanp

reviews.title: Super quiet and efficient
reviews.comment: This is a very good quality fan that has a great cooling capacity due to the rpm 1700-2200 depending on your needs. It comes with cables for different setups, and a low noise adapter. It also has a low profile design making it a perfect fit to rreplace the fan in the amateur radio G90 cooling fan base. It is very quiet and worth the price. Simple to install and runs very efficiently. Would buy again and would recommend for other uses.
reviews.author: Ben E

reviews.title: I'm a Big Noctua Fan....um....Fan.
reviews.comment: Reviewing the Noctua NF-A9x14 PWM: I bought two of these Noctua fans for my dual-zone solid state (non-refrigerant) wine chiller.  The original fans that removed heat from the hot side of the Peltier modules (the solid state coolers) were very noisy. After measuring them, I realized that they were a standard size and that Noctura made fans that size. The only modification needed was drilling out the Noctura fan mounting holes to work in my wine chiller. I had always used Noctura fans when building computers and have felt they were the best and quietest computer fans out there.  So, when I needed quieter fans for a wine chiller, I knew Noctura would come through for me. Their appearance is great for certain computer cases but not so important when they're hidden inside a wine chiller. They provide at least as much cooling for the Peltier modules as the original fans. In solid state wine chillers the fans tend to run almost continuously due to the relatively weak chilling ability of the Peltier modules.  Keeping the air inside at 55 F when the room is 75 F can be taxing. So, having well-functioning and quiet fans for years is a must. Noctua fans are a top-shelf solution and are definitely not cheap compared to the bottom-tier choices. But in the long run, not having to tear into a computer or wine chiller sooner than expected due to a fan failure is enough of a reason for me to want to pay more. I'm a big "fan" of Noctua fans.
reviews.author: marktrimarc

reviews.title: Quiet, Effective & Reliable
reviews.comment: I use 2 Noctua fans in my Media PC. It's a mini ITX case, with an ATX Power Supply Unit. That leaves very little room inside for clunky coolers! The Noctua low-profile CPU cooler, uses this exact model 90mm fan. I built this PC almost 7 years ago, and have never replaced the Notua fan on the CPU cooler! I do clean my system every 6 months or so, and remove dust, but have never oiled the fan since it's install. To my amazement, it has not failed! I've turned and spun the fan by hand a few times, and it still freely flows. I also have a BeQuiet PSU, which has it's original fan. I noticed that when the room is cold, there is a very slight vibration noise from one of the fans (probably the PSU fan) which goes away after a minute or so of running. After almost 7 years, I am amazed that this slight noise is only just starting to creep in. So, I installed a Noctua 140mm fan in the PSU (since it's out of warranty now anyway) and replaced the CPU cooler fan with this Noctua 90mm fan (a like for like replacement). In my previous setup, I was not using the low-noise connector that you get in the Noctua box. However, this time I installed the low-noise connector on both the CPU fan and the PSU fan, and connected both fans directly to the Motherboard for optimum fan performance and monitoring. Without the low-noise connectors, the system was extremely quiet and never intruded on my movies or TV shows. And now with the low-noise connectors installed, the system is so quiet you cannot hear it at all! I also have a passively cooled nVidia GT1030 graphics card in the case, creating additional heat and have not noticed any problems or noise increase. Quiet - With the low-noise connector, I have to shine a flashlight into the case to see if the fans are spinning! >.< Effective - My tiny mini-ITX case remains cool and operational even after hours of use. Reliable - After almost 7 years of daily use, it's still going strong! Why did I replace it then? Simply for peace of mind. I highly recommend Noctua fans. They're definately worth the money. Additionally in the case, you get a low-noise adapter, Y-splitter cable and extention cable. There are also some low noise rubber mounts.
reviews.author: Tom Hegener

reviews.title: Quality Product and Excellent Customer Service
reviews.comment: I bought this fan 5 years ago. It failed finally last week, but there is no doubt that this is a truly excellent product that has lived up to its name. I had turned it on 24/7 for nearly 5 years without stopping it for a single day on my PC and it has served me very faithfully and quietly, keeping the system cool at all times. When it finally failed this week, I thought I would simply buy a new one to replace it, but was surprised to see on the original box (Yes, I kept it.) stating that the warranty is 6 years. I am based in Singapore and bought this from Amazon USA, and the company is headquartered in Austria. I thought even if I had raised an RMA request, it might be too cumbersome and costly to ship the defective fan back to Noctua in Austria. Still, I tried my luck to write in. Surprisingly, within a day, I was told by a Mr. Anthony Maleschitz from the Noctua Support Team that all I need to do is to break a few blades from the defective fan to render it unusable, and send a picture of the broken fan to him as proof, and that would save me the trouble and cost of shipping back the defective fan. I did as instructed and by the next day, I was informed by Mr. Maleschitz that a replacement fan would be shipped out to me soon (In fact, it was shipped out the next day and I would expect to receive it within 4 days). It's completely hassle free and I am truly touched and impressed by his excellent customer service. I have no doubt at all to recommend this product to anyone who looks forward to buy a genuinely quiet and quality product, and above all, to patronize a company that truly values and takes great care even of a small and faraway customer like me.
reviews.author: YK

reviews.title: Maximum cooling, cool look, make sure you understand how these work before you buy
reviews.comment:
Why I ordered this item: I have a new PC build that required a lot of cooling. I decided to go with RBG fans because I thought they would look cool, and I picked this model because of the performance and reviews.
Likes:
* These move a lot of air. I put six of them in my PC and they really work well.
* The RGB function looks awesome and is very bright! Make sure your motherboard has ARGB headers.
* Mounting was easy and installation was very straight forward.
* The materials used on these feel very high quality.
* Noise levels are low which is what I wanted. It never gets above a very quiet whirring sound.
No likes:
* The way these work is neat, but it could also be considered a bad thing for some people. There is one cable that goes to a fan header on your motherboard, and then these fans slot together using contact pins and pads. There is only one cable that goes to the motherboard, which means that these fans have to be installed in a row of three and cannot be moved apart from each other. This worked for me, but it might be an issue for other users that expect three individually controllable fans.
Would I pay full price for this product: Yes these are a bargain.
Final thoughts: Super happy with the function on these. The cost is low and they are functional and quiet.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Highly recommend!
reviews.comment: I haven't used anything from Thermalright in years. I recently felt board with my pc and wanted to downsize things. I bought these fans because I liked the RGB and are reasonably inexpensive. After installing the fans I have to admit, Thermalright has come along way since the last time I used them because these fans are very pretty with their RGB and are surprisingly very quiet for budget fans! Let's just say that the pump on my TR 360 AIO is quiet and its louder than the fans itself while spinning at 1000rpm. After using Arctic p12 max fans for a longest, the amount of quietness from these fans have been a breath of fresh air. I love how the fans snap together and only use one rgb cable and fan cable. They aren't the best I've ever had at moving air but the performance is pretty impressive. The RGB is plenty bright and its gives you plenty of cable length as long at you don't have massive full tower case. Overall I give these fans 5 stars because they look great, move plenty of air and are budget friendly.
reviews.author: Preston sudduth

reviews.title: Stunning fans at a great price.
reviews.comment:
Thermalright, known for its exceptional cooling technology, has once again delivered some of my favorite fans at an excellent price. These fans not only look great but also maintain a low noise level. Their robust locking mechanism ensures that they stay securely connected. Currently, I have two sets of three fans daisy-chained together to synchronize their RGB lighting and fan speed. This setup eliminated the need for a separate controller.
These fans are a great choice, and they even come in white if you prefer that color.
reviews.author: Jordan

reviews.title: Best fans out there!
reviews.comment:
These fans are great, especially for the price. The TL-M12Q X3 set offers good airflow and good static pressure while staying surprisingly quiet, even at higher RPMs. Build quality feels solid, and the daisy-chain design makes cable management simple and clean.
I paired these with my Thermalright Frozen Infinity 360 cooler, and they work perfectly together the matching design and ARGB lighting make it look seamless.
For "budget fans", they perform way above expectations. Great cooling, low noise, and excellent compatibility with Thermalright’s coolers — an easy recommendation, will be buying more.
reviews.author: Ronnie Tobin

reviews.title: Pretty colorful and cool fans! Great value for price!
reviews.comment: These fans are fantastic! They’re pretty fast, suck in a lot of air, so much so that my gpu hardly has to use its own fans. Playing Fortnite, my cpu and gpu temps average 50-60c in an mATX case, which is pretty nice. And the light show and mirrors make it look sleek and fantastic. Only reason why I didn’t give it five stars is that the instructions for how to install the cables all correctly were a bit confusing, especially for a beginner like me. But other than that, it was pretty simple to install and great value for the price compared to name brand ones. Would highly recommend this, especially for budget or mid tier builds
reviews.author: Benniccette Perez Pena

reviews.title: Style & performance!
reviews.comment:
I have been running a case full of SL120 Infinity fans for around 5 months now. Recently moved my build into a new O11D Dynamic Evo, so I was in need of an extra rear exhaust fan. These guys had one in stock when everyone else seemed to be sold out at the time - and for regular price. Best fans I have owned! Incredibly easy to install, especially if you have a L Connect Controller already. The ability to click them together in groups and use only one cable per group, makes cable management and the installation process a breeze. For reference, before I switched to these Infinity fans, I ran a whole case of Corsair fans. I went from 18 individual cables going to a controller, down to 3. Adding this extra fan only added one more cable, for a total of 4. That is amazing! As for noise, at low speeds you don't even hear them. Medium speeds they are audible, but quiet. Of course at the highest speeds they can get loud because of their very high rpm capability. But they rarely, if ever need to be that high. In terms of price to performance, they are up there with some of the best. Sure, you can get some BeQuiet or Noctua fans without RGB that can move more air, but the fact you get this kind of performance out of one of the most beautiful fans out there, is well worth the price. Long term reliability is still up in the air due to the fact they were released only about 6 months ago, but so far so good! (Knock on wood lol) Definitely recommend!
Lastly, Coolerguys were completely on top of this order. The fan showed up a couple days before it was supposed to and the entire process was easy. 5 stars so far!
reviews.author: Travis

reviews.title: Great forward or reverse fans
reviews.comment: Great fans, quiet.  I needed a combination of forward and reverse fans for my case.  These fans provided both options.  The RGB function and their software work great as well.  Easy to use and easy to configure.  Their controller works good as well, allows you to plug in four groups.  Just plug in the USB cable to the motherboard.  You do not need to sync to the motherboard.
reviews.author: PhotoBuff58

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.comment: Perfect fan cooler and look incredible inside my gabinet
reviews.author: David Escalante

reviews.title: Great looking fan
reviews.comment: Now, you shouldn't buy this fan if you're trying to keep some more cash in your wallet, because for around $30 this isn't the cheapest PC fan out there. But, if you want a gorgeous looking fan inside your PC to level up its' aesthetics (and don't really care about its' price tag) this is a great fan for you! This is an 120 mm fan that is my rear fan in my PC. The RGB and the infinity mirror looks so good! It fit great in my PC and it took me no time to install this. It functions just as how good it looks!
reviews.author: quythu nguyen

reviews.title: I love these fans
reviews.comment: I bought 10 SL-Infinity fans for my new build because I absolutely loved the RGB and the infinity mirror aesthetics. These are REALLY nice fans, maybe a few bucks more than standard fans, but not the most expensive you can get and worth every penny. The RGB is so smooth, the ways in which you can customize it are endless, and the L-Connect software is super easy to use. In my picture, I have the fan RGB off and the ring RGB set to rainbow. Highly recommend!
reviews.author: Jennifer V.

reviews.title: Quiet ARGB and PWM fans. Great quality.
reviews.comment: To begin with, these are the same fans that come with the Thermalright Peerless Assassin 120 SE. I was so happy with my purchase of their CPU cooler, I turned to Thermalright to replace the case fans in my Rosewill S500. Installation is very easy. Each fan comes with power and ARGB splitters, so I was able to daisy chain all 6 fans together (bought two 3 packs) without any issues. Also daisy chained the ARGB plug from the PA 120 SE and everything is synced up without issue. I have found absolutely no reason to purchase a fan hub at this time as the built in splitters did the job. I'm using an ROG B550-F GAMING motherboard, so was stuck with a single ARGB header but this was not an issue. Hooked my fans to one of the system fan headers and adjusted my curves using Fan Control found on GitHub and played around with the RPMs. In terms of air flow, these guys DEFINITELY move air. With these fans at full blast along with the PA120SE, I got my 3700x with PBO enabled (+200 offset) running as low as 27°C at idle. With the original Rosewill case fans, the absolute lowest I saw was 31°C. A similar 5°C was seen when running at full load using a 3DMark CPU profile test. Again, this was at full blast. With fan curves adjusted to lower power and speed, the system is near silent. The water pump in my aquarium is louder than my system running under normal loads. Despite the silence, I still have lower temps than when I had the stock case fans. Before purchase, I tried to find as much information I could on these fans and at best I could find a few reviewers comparing them to the Noctua NF-F12. While I have never used Noctuas and cannot speak from experience, I can only reiterate my system is nearly dead silent. Something to keep in mind is the sound will become noticable above 50% speed. If you need to run your fans at 100% for some reason, however, then you don't have to worry about any whining or related sounds. Your PC will sound like it just has a bunch of air running through it, unlike when a GPU (in my case an EVGA 2080 Super BLACK) ramps up and sounds like a fighter jet taking off. At this time, my fans hover between 8% and 30% speed and I can't hear them unless I really, really try. While watching videos or gaming? You'll only realize they're on due to the RGB lighting, and this is coming from a guy with his case 2 feet from his head. I haven't noticed any resonance issues at this time. Even sliding power from 0-100%, I can't say I've noticed any, so I'm very happy with that. So, they are quiet and absolutely circulate air in your system. The bonus here is the fact these are also ARGB. At the time of this review, a three pack of these are a third of the price of a three pack of Arctic P12 ARGB fans. You can get 6 of these fans (two 3 packs) for the price of a single Noctua A12. Again, these are the same fans you'd find on Thermalright's Peerless Assassin 120 SE and that's a rather quiet and very effective CPU cooler. For now, these are an incredible value and the budget/value space appears to be where Thermalright is dominating right now. From my research, Thermalright used to be what Noctua is to PC fans today. Don't sleep on these guys. I would not be surprised if more PC enthusiasts use these products when trying to maximize bang for buck performance. If you need new case fans or are looking to fill in any extra 120mm fan spots in your case, grab these. I don't care if I come off like a shill, but I am incredibly happy with my setup now. I'm looking to upgrade my CPU to a 5800x3D, and given the temps I'm seeing on my 3700x, I know I can count on these fans to handle that swap and future builds to come.
reviews.author: Turnabout Phoenix

reviews.title: Thermalright TL-C12C-S X3 120mm ARGB Fans – Excellent Value and Performance
reviews.comment: I needed three additional ARGB fans to match the three that came preinstalled in my GAMEMAX case. My son recommended the Thermalright TL-C12C-S X3 fans, so I decided to give them a try, and I’m glad I did. These fans are quiet, well made, and very reasonably priced. Build quality is solid, with no rattles or vibration, and airflow is more than adequate for a typical gaming or productivity system. A pleasant surprise was how closely they match the appearance of the stock GAMEMAX fans; once installed, you’d be hard-pressed to tell them apart. For anyone looking to add or replace ARGB fans without overspending, these are an excellent choice. They deliver good performance, attractive lighting, and strong value. Highly recommended for budget-conscious builds that still care about aesthetics.
reviews.author: RogueScholar61

reviews.title: Fantastic Fans For The Price Worth The Investment
reviews.comment: I built a computer back in November of 2024. I was able to get all new parts except for case fans. I had to use the old ones from my previous build. That being said, my computer was lightning fast but had an ugly whirring sound that was very obvious and apparent to anyone who entered my office and listened to the fans. Enter these fans. Yesterday I cleaned up my computer and gutted out all 5 of the old fans. I purchased two packs of these 3 quantity ThermalRight rgb fans. WARNING: If you want RGB functionality make sure you have enough RGB headers on your motherboard! I purchased a FAN hub that only gave power to the fans, NOT a fan hub that ALSO has RGB functionality!! If you're looking for your fans to light up make sure to either have an appropriate amount of RGB headers on your MB or buy a fan hub with RGB functionality! As of this review the hub that I purchased only gives power to my fans and one of the fans has its rgb 3 pin connector attached to my motherboard-- it is the only fan with light and color. If I had a fan hub with RGB connection all of my fans would be on right now. So beware; if you have regular fans that don't have rgb just get a regular fan hub because the one I purchased is technically doing it's job. All of my fans are on and began spinning successfully on the first time POST'ing again... They are ULTRA quiet. I don't hear a single thing. Major boost in peace from the older fans I had -- their sound is wedged into my soul forever... Now this computer feels like the new computer that it actually is. Fast, efficient, and deadly quiet. They all run fast up to 1500rpm and my CPU and GPU are idling at least 10 degrees celsius cooler than before with all 6 fans installed. Overall I am very very happy with these fans; just make sure if you get the RGB variant to have enough connectors on your motherboard or to have a fan AND rgb hub. The one fan that does have its light on is incredibly bright and is adjustable with motherboard software; can be made brighter or dimmer to your preference. Once I purchase the fan and RGB hub I will come post a picture to my review of my rig.
reviews.author: Kevin Brea

reviews.title: Great fans for price but colors could be more vibrant
reviews.comment: Pros: These fans work extremely well and are very quiet for the price. I believe they are the most affordable pack of 3 fans on Amazon. The build quality is very nice as well. I like the square build of the fans, as it makes it look clean and sleek opposed to other brands that have some crazy designs. I’m not sure how they will hold up over time, but the Thermaltake brand has been increasing in popularity for its great price to performance, and these fans prove it. The airflow is what you can expect of any pc fan. It pushes air in and out of the pc case, and my GPU and CPU haven’t gotten dangerously hot at all. Cons: I do have three other cooler master fans on the right side as you can see in the video, and there is a color difference, which I understand they are two different brands. I did notice that the thermaltake fans are not as vibrant and can’t turn some specific colors like brown. I have the colors set to brown here, but they look more white than brown. Conclusion: Overall, extremely great fans for the price especially if you’re on a budget, but I do wish the colors were more vibrant. If you have other Thermaltake products like the AIO I have, the fans are the same so the colors will match. I highly recommend this product for the price, but there is room for improvement.
reviews.author: Carlos Paredes III

reviews.title: Excellent Value Fans with Standard Connections
reviews.comment: These Thermalright TL-C12C-S 120mm ARGB fans are fantastic for the price. They look good, the RGB lighting is clean and evenly diffused, and best of all, they use standard 4-pin PWM and ARGB connectors instead of forcing you into a proprietary hub. Noise levels are improved over expectations for budget fans; they stay quiet at low to moderate speeds and don’t develop any annoying tones under load. Build quality also feels above average compared to other fans in this price range. If you’re looking for affordable case fans that don’t compromise on compatibility, noise, or appearance, I’d highly recommend Thermalright. These are an easy win for budget or mid-range builds.
reviews.author: Ben Lords

reviews.title: Good cheap replacement fan
reviews.comment: I picked up the Thermalright TL-M12Q-S X3 120mm fans as an upgrade from my older Corsair fans, and overall I’m pretty happy with them. The build quality feels solid and they look clean once installed. They do run a little noisy, but still noticeably quieter than the Corsair fans I was using before, so for me it’s an improvement. Airflow seems good and they’ve been doing a nice job keeping temps in check. For the price and performance, these are a solid upgrade if you’re coming from older or louder fans. Not completely silent, but they get the job done well.
reviews.author: cheng s.

reviews.title: Excellent, high-performance, durable fans.
reviews.comment: My entire PC is made up with these fans.  I have a contrast theme going where there are black RGB exhaust fans on the top and the side, rear and bottom are the clear/white RGB fans. Let me start by saying, these are HIGH QUALITY.  They are solid, well-built and sturdy.  They are not cheap in the slightest and will give you years of good performance.  The RGB lighting is subtle and superb, not in-your-face bright. The only quirk is that these series (idk if all fans are this way) need a special adapter to make them work.  This is what I mean.  Say you want 1 fan in the rear and 2 fans on the top, you will need TWO adapters.  Since these interconnect.  Now the package comes with 1 adapter and additional adapters are remarkably inexpensive on Amazon, I recommend getting a few in case you want to mod later or whatnot.
reviews.author: Katarax

reviews.title: Great fans for the price
reviews.comment: The fans are amazing!! My pc is a lot more cooler, the RGB lights are amazing, and they are very quiet. I definitely recommend these fans
reviews.author: Chavonne Gourdet

reviews.title: Perfect Lian Li Dupes!
reviews.comment: These lian li dupes are super beautiful, and the daisy chaining they offer is so nice to reduce the amount of cables flying around in the case. Temps look amazing and the fans sound perfect. As long as you use a decent hub, and pray to the gods that it's detected by your software you should be able to set it up quite easily. These things are bright, beautiful and honestly stunning. Definitely a must if you're going for the infinity light setup and the airflow on these definitely hold up.
reviews.author: Brandon Vang

reviews.title: Ducks in a Row, but Great Ducks
reviews.comment: These case fans are basically idiot-proof. Easy to install with basic knowledge of computer case wiring and airflow. Only ding I would give these fans is that all three fans have to orient in the same direction. I have mine on a Montech King 45 midtower with three bottom fans and one rear case fan. I wanted to orient the fan on the left as exhaust, but the installation would not support it. Still very happy with the product- they look great installed with a air cooler.
reviews.author: TreadHead

reviews.title: Holy
reviews.comment: Very pricey fan, but it is inaudible and very good circulating air. They've yet to go at full rpm in my build. There's definitely more accessories with this chromax fan compared to previous chromax fans. This is the quietest you can get while still achieving amazing airflow and cooling. Still a premium product with a premium price and I believe it to be worth every penny, though, so if it's not within you're budget Artic's and Be quiet's are you're next bet.
reviews.author: Santiago

reviews.title: Dropped my CPU temperatures a couple degrees ° C from the G1 fan.
reviews.comment: I used this in place of the G1 140 mm PWM fan that came with my Noctua CPU cooler (NH-C14S), which is how I was able to compare the difference in performance. This is a premium 140 mm fan, but you probably already know that.  There are fans which move more air, but none that offer this performance within such a low noise envelope.  I've also seen reviews of some competing models that they don't sound as pleasant, under high load. The packaging has changed since the G1 fans, but you still get a generous set of accessories.  Note that if you use the Y-cable, it will interfere with RPM monitoring.  I had used it as a short extension cable, but wondered why I didn't see any RPM reading.  Then, I switched to the proper extension cable and RPM monitoring worked properly.
reviews.author: Not My Real Name

reviews.title: Works so well! So quiet.
reviews.comment: The amount of air this moves even at the lower RPMs compared to other 140mm fans is impressive. I wish these were cheaper but they do work well.
reviews.author: John H.

reviews.title: Can't go wrong, Noctua is king
reviews.comment: I love me some Noctua fans! I was excited to grab these G2s and they haven't disappointed. Sound: They're very quiet up to about 50% with three identical 140s in my system and a 120 variant for exhaust and CPU. You begin to hear them above this level, but the sound profile is pleasant, unlike the stock fans that came with my NZXT case. Great case, average fans tho. Performance/Temps: These keep my 5080 and 9800X3D cool and happy. Gaming load temps sit from 56C to mid 60s on average. Looks: Some love the brown and tan, some prefer the black, I like 'em both but went with black for these to match the rest of my system's aesthetic. They look great. Materials: Sturdy as heck. Noctua fans feel next-level compared to your average fan. Thicker, better blades, high-quality frame and materials overall.
reviews.author: Dominic Minischetti III

reviews.title: Good performance while staying silent
reviews.comment: This is the best computer cooling fan I've ever used, but the price is a bit pricey .
reviews.author: Lan Ngoc

reviews.title: Want to have your PC case stand out? This is 1 way to do it
reviews.comment:
Quite possibly the best case fans I have purchased. Very colorful and don’t make a lot of noise, and for only $35, you get the best “Bang for your buck.” RGB, infinite mirror design, daisy chain, plug in, installed. Was debating Lian Li fans over these, but bought these instead and glad that I did.
These fans function very well, compatible with any fan hub that has a 3 pin ARGB header on the hub itself.
Overall a great pick, would definitely buy again
reviews.author: Hunter

reviews.title: Great price, Looks great and quality as expected.
reviews.comment:
Fans look great and comes with both long and short screws for installation, please avoid using the silicon tips as a screw replacement as the fans do not have the notches for the tips to be secured properly. Great looking fans nonetheless despite the price, you can daisy chain the fans as well using both the RGB connectors and the pwm power connectors..
Avoid attaching over 5 fans per RGB header just in case it causes instability in the motherboard.
reviews.author: Adrian Lewis

reviews.title: <insert fan-based pun here>
reviews.comment:
Previously, I had an NF-P14 that was pulling double-duty in the middle of my old NH-D14 heatsink (the other fan that was originally with it currently resides in the case's exhaust slot directly aft of the heatsink). This setup worked fine during winter months, but in recent weeks has resulted in intermittent overheating due to the warmth of the room.
Rather than restore the heatsink's stock configuration, I opted to simply beef up the heatsink's fan and move the NF-P14 to the case front to supply it; I'd been intending to replace the low-end Cooler Master fan I had there anyway. As both high airflow and high static pressure were needed...this fan was a bit of a no-brainer, even if it is pricy.
First off: if you too have an NH-D14, rest assured that this fan will fit. It won't fit as intended (the original mount kit was designed for 120mm-mount fans, the NF-A14 has 140mm mounts), but the heatsink is wide enough to support the fan, and you'll have a bottom overhang for RAM/VRM/etc cooling as with the original NF-P14. Just make sure that there aren't any components extruding from the board that will interfere with the corners. See attached pictures for my super-exotic mounting method.
Secondly: despite Noctua's best efforts, this fan is definitely not quiet at higher speeds. Even throttled at 50%, it's quite noticeable, though it's not unbearable. At 100% (which comes to ~2750rpm on my board...something I find slightly worrying actually), as noted in other reviews, it sounds akin to a small vacuum cleaner. If you plan to run it in a gaming PC, make sure you figure out what speed you need for adequate cooling, and stick to that under load. Look up your CPU to find its maximum safe temperature, and set your fan curve to have it kick up to 100% ~5 degrees before that. The fan has PWM control for a reason...use it! There's no reason to deafen yourself under light or no load.
Noctua's site lists the minimum speed as 800rpm, however, my board's minimum PWM setting is able to run it at ~400rpm. I wasn't able to test at what point it becomes "silent", but it certainly is at the lower end. I'd expect it to be no louder than the NF-P14 up to 1300rpm, and I never had a problem with that fan's noise.
Finally...it's a solid fan. Noctua, in my experience, makes high-quality stuff; this fan is no exception. The price of it made me handle it carefully, but it didn't feel fragile at all. Even the blades, thin as they are, feel solid...I would recommend not putting your fingers anywhere near them while the fan is running.
The box is quite nice, but what you actually get is just barely above OEM-level; the fan and wide-thread screws for plastic fans, nothing more.
I imagine that the common user would be disappointed by lack of low-noise adapter and/or splitter, but consider: the fan is PWM (a control method far superior to resistive/voltage-based control), and is rated for more than half an amp at full load. It seems to be commonly accepted that motherboard headers shouldn't be loaded above 1 amp, which would be easily exceeded by pairing two of these at full speed on a single header. I would guess that the cost of including a splitter in every box is a drop in the bucket for Noctua, but they chose to not include one to protect themselves if users decided to overload motherboard headers and potentially burn them out.
They can't be held responsible if the user finds a splitter elsewhere and decides to risk it, after all.
In summary,
It's an expensive fan, costing as much as an 8gb stick of DDR3. But for the price you get a fan that performs well and quietly for day to day use, and unlike Noctua's consumer-grade offerings, can go full-out balls-to-the-wall if high levels of static pressure and airflow are needed. It can be made to fit an NH-D14 with the mildest of adaptation, and (according to reviews and Noctua specs) will directly fit an NH-D15. The included accessories are...well, non-existent, but with a proper setup you won't need them anyway.

reviews.author: Matt Duncan

reviews.title: Extremely quiet! Just need to configure them properly
reviews.comment:
I love these fans! I was hesitant to order them because of some reviewers saying they're horribly loud and others saying they were quiet. I was willing to take the risk and bet on the fact that those complaining they were too loud just didn't take any time to configure them, and I am so glad I did!
I installed 4 of these 140mm fans and 3 120mm in my new rig and I absolutely love them. I have 2 140's as front intake, a 140 as rear exhaust, a 140 as bottom intake next to PSU, 2 120's on my H100i radiator and a third 120 next to the radiator as exhaust. They all come with rubber brackets and I installed all but the radiator fans with Cosmos rubber rivets. Super easy! They all come with rubber sleeved cables that aren't too short and aren't too long. I did have to run a y-splitter for my two front fans because I ran out of pins on my motherboard, and it was enough of an extension to help them make it across the huge case to get them plugged in. If you have a large case and intend to put these near the front of your chassis, you will most definitely need extensions so plan ahead! I'd rather have to extend one set of fans than have 7 fans with super long cables cluttering things up.
After the quick and easy installation, I powered everything on and I was shocked at how loud it was. It was loud enough that my 10 year old and I had to raise our voices to hear each other clearly when sitting 4-5 feet away. HOWEVER, using ASUS' UEFI on the Maximus VII Hero motherboard, I was able to use the built in Qfan to quiet them down enough to the point that I could tolerate sitting near it while I installed the OS.
Once Windows was installed, I installed AI Suite (included with my motherboard, you may need to locate another fan controller if you don't have an ASUS board) and went into fan setup. It has 4 predefined modes to choose from with further customization possible if desired. Silent mode literally turns off all fans except the CPU fan, which it turns down considerably and the entire rig is dead quiet. Standard mode is a step up but still extremely quiet, even when sitting only 2-3 feet away. When on the other side of the room playing games on the TV, I don't hear it at all. The other two settings include turbo (around 1500 rpm) and full power. When all fans are running at top speed (about 2700-2800 rpm), it is extremely loud. Turbo is tolerable. The sweet spot is around 900rpm, which is enough to keep an EVGA GTX 980 Ti under 60 degrees while gaming and keeps my i7-4790k under 40 degrees, even under load. The result is a very stable, quiet and cool rig. I haven't found anything that can cause this system to break a sweat and I attribute it largely to these fans.
I am so very pleased with these fans, I can't say enough good things about them. They are roughly twice as expensive as other popular fans, but I'd much rather take the cool, quiet performance of Noctua fans than have fancy loud LED fans in my rig. I'll definitely be picking up more Noctua's when I build my husband's rig next month.

Putting the P12 Pro and P14 Pro on my CPU cooler the temps when put under 150w stress test increased from 82C to 86C. According to the box they are supposed to have higher static pressure than the Icegale but apparently not. However, that is still very well within reasonable temps during a stress test and best of all, I would guess about a 50% reduction in noise overall. Cannot recommend these enough
reviews.author: hanna

reviews.title: Huge Improvement. These Fans Dropped My Temps Under Load
reviews.comment:
Huge Improvement — These Fans Dropped My Temps Under Load
I picked up the 5-pack of ARCTIC P14 Max fans to finally overhaul the airflow in my PC, and I’m genuinely impressed with how much of a difference they made. I’m running them through an open-source program called Fan Control, which lets me fine-tune each fan curve, and the P14 Max fans respond really smoothly to RPM changes. No weird ramping, no buzzing; just clean, controlled airflow.
The cooling improvement was immediate. Prior to installing these, my CPU and GPU would flirt with the mid-80s to mid-90s Celsius during heavy gaming or rendering sessions. I work with a lot of different intensive software, from video rendering/editting to 3d modeling and rendering, and of course, dare I say.. Cyberpunk 2077. After swapping my old standard case fans with the P14 Max fans, my temps stay under 75C max under full load. For me, that’s a huge win.
Noise-wise, they’re surprisingly quiet for the amount of air they push. At lower speeds, they’re practically silent. At higher speeds, you definitely hear air movement, but it’s more of a clean whoosh rather than an annoying hum or rattle. Very tolerable, especially considering the cooling performance. I will say though if you use headphone's or have an AC, etc. You will not be affected.
Installation was straightforward, and the daisy-chain cables are a nice touch — makes cable management a little less chaotic in a crowded case. Build quality also feels solid, not flimsy like some budget fans.
Overall, this 5-pack was absolutely worth it. If you fine tune your fan curves with something like Fan Control and want a ton of cooling power without turning your PC into a wind tunnel, these fans are fantastic. My system runs cooler, quieter, and doesn't turn my PC into a space heater. Highly recommend.
reviews.author: Dr I

reviews.title: Not directly comparable against the Noctua NF-A14, but there's no doubt this is a good fan
reviews.comment:
Been using Noctua NF-A14s on my 280mm AIO for my R7 7800X3D in a SSUPD Meshroom S (I know a 280mm is overkill for this processor, I originally had a 7900X in there), and recently decided to switch up to these fans since I've had good experiences with Arctic products and I know the P12 Max is an excellent fan.
Out of the box the first thing to note at 27mm, it is the same thickness as the normal P14, but this is a slightly thicker fan compared to other 140mm fans out there that are usually 25mm thick. This made it slightly cramped w/ my case since I use a fan grille, but there was still enough space. Unlike the normal P14 which only maxes out at 1700rpm (which made them quiet even at 100% rpm, great for radiators, but less flexible if you wanted to run a fan very fast and very loud), the P14 Max has a max RPM of 2800rpm (my Gigabyte B650i reported a max of of ~2700rpm), significantly higher, which also meant I had to detune my fan curves since the Noctua NF-A14 only has a 1500rpm max. At similar RPMs and noise levels though I did end up with about the same temps on my 7800X3D (CPU draws ~89W in Cinebench R23, pump always at 100%, CPU temps ~77.5C).
The fan feels very well-built, and the only "complaint" I have is unlike the P14 PWM, there's no fan header daisy chaining option available. Thankfully the fan cable is of a decent length and is pretty easy to hide. Rubber padding along the 4 corners for anti-vibration isn't necessary but a great nice-to-have.
The price varies a bit, but at the time of this review (and the time I ordered these fans) they're $13 each. Sure for a similar amount of money you can get a 3-pack of Thermalright TL-C12C-S 120mm ARGB fans, but this is a great price for a performance 140mm fan. It performs well, can push out a lot of air through a radiator from the sheer RPMs if noise isn't a concern,. If you don't need RGB, this is an excellent no-nonsense fan. However, these fans absolutely need proper PWM control, you need to have a way to control fan speeds because otherwise, 2800rpms max means this fan can get very loud. Once tuned though, these fans are great. I will note however the P14 PWM PST is still a good option if the price is right (currently Arctic's fan pricing is all over the place), since if you don't need the ability to go fast on the fan RPM or if you're a bit more noise sensitive and you know you have enough cooling headroom to warrant using a slower fan, the P14 is still more than enough for AIOs/radiators and has fan header daisy-chaining.

After looking around for a bit, this particular fan caught my eye because it has a 4 pin PWM connector on it with plenty of cable length and the RPM for the fan speed was perfect for what i needed (2100RPM).  I'm glad i still had my other mounting brackets from my original heatsink box which lay flat against this fan so the install for the brackets onto the fan was pretty easy. I have no complaints about this fan.  This fan is made using a rifle bearing sleeve so you get the best of both worlds.  I'm very glad i chose this fan over others and i hope i get many years of use out of it.

My CPU temperatures are a little lower on average (about 2 to 3 degrees centigrade) when playing Cyberpunk 2077 or working in really demanding office files. The fans typically run between 55% and 75% during my office tasks, and they ramp up to 100% generally when gaming. Even then, the sound is a pretty soft hum. It's noticeable if I lower the volume on everything, but when playing at a normal volume or with my headphones on I never notice the sound. The sound is certainly less noticeable than my GPU fans, which are quite loud above 70%. I can't comment on their lifespan yet. The first couple weeks of using these fans has been great, so if they continue this way I will be quite happy.

reviews.comment: Purchased the three pack of fans.  Package included: - 12 mounting screws, enough for all 3 fans - 2 extension cords to allow you to connect fans to the mother board. - 3 fans, each having a male/female connection cords to allow you to daisy chain the fans.  The length of cable to the female connection is very short, and will likely not connect to the motherboard on its own without an extension cord, but has enough room to daisy chain to another fan.  So with only being given 2 extension cords, at least 2 of the fans will need to be daisy chained together without buying additional cables. Installation was easy, dimensions were as advertised. Airflow is very good.  In my set-up the fans defaulted to maximum speed and I had to tinker in my BIOS to lower the fan speed.  At maximum speed, there was a noticeably loud humming noise that couldn't be corrected.  At lower fan speeds, the humming noise stopped and fan noise was quiet.

reviews.title: One of the very best airflow fans on the market
reviews.comment:
I was looking to get the best low-noise but high performance fan for the single output of my case to balance with the 4 low-noise fans I had running for air intake. Originally I had Fractal Design Dynamic GP14 fan that came with the case but I swapped that to be an additional input when I upgraded to a higher powered Corsair ML140 Pro. With the Corsair fan performance was decent but I found it seemed to get a bit noisy at moderate speeds.
Realistically, my cooling setup was always more than adequate, I didn't have any temperature issues whatsoever, but I am a bit of a nerd for good air cooling and just like upgrading something once in a while and it seemed like there was room for improvement here.
I had the corsair for several years but I would occasionally do research on fans or watch the latest reviews and comparisons of fans on youtube. Eventually the time felt right that I felt like spending the money and that there were some good options to upgrade to. This fan has been a definite improvement capable of moving more air at lower sound levels. I also like that it has the headroom to push to even higher speeds than I need with my current setup just in case I ever feel like it or was trying to max my performance having fun overclocking and benchmarking.
I didn't bother to do any recorded tests of my temps but my subjective experience has been that I am very happy with the performance as I created a fan curve for it that gives me what I want airflow wise and my computer remains quieter than it did before. I also stepped away from having my computer with so many LED lights so the transition to a fan without lights worked for me. A few months ago I made significant upgrades to my processor and my video card and this still handles everything I can throw at it with ease and quietness.  I have been super happy with the performance of this fan and will definitely have them in mind next time I am building a system.

reviews.title: Best 140mm silent fans on the market
reviews.comment:
I’ve tried a lot of high-end fans from Noctua, Phanteks, Lian Li, Arctic, etc, and I was really surprised with how good the SWP 4’s are. In some ways IMO they are one of the best 140mm fans on the market, if not thee best. Let me explain why. In terms of brands the two best fans I’ve ever used are the Noctua NF-A12 G2’S and the Phanteks T30. Like the SWP 4’s they both strike the perfect balance between high airflow and silent operation. HOWEVER, the reason why I ended up going with the SWP 4’s is because (1) the Noctua G2’s only come in their distinctive yet fugly brown color, and (2) Phanteks still hasn’t released a 140mm version of the T30. So essentially, if you need black 140mm fans that are both high performing and silent, the SWP 4’s are currently the best option on the market today. They’re also a very attractive fan with high quality cabling so if you’re into aesthetic building like I am they look great on a radiator.
In terms of how quiet they are, I have them in my SFF PC which sits directly on my work desk and while idle my PC is completely silent. But even at higher RPM my PC sounds similar to an air purifier - no vibrations, motor sounds, droning, etc, just a pleasant and subtle rush of air akin to white noise. Overall I definitely recommend these fans especially if you need 140mm.

For right now, the fans motors are quiet but I don't know how long there gonna be like that.
For me, I only use these fans as case fans. There not great radiator/heatsink fans due to the lack of pressure. You probably could get away using these fans on a 360mm aio (Even better if its a push/pull since these fans are so cheap). If you play your CFM cards right, these fans will cool your PC well.
If I really had to nit pick on problems, is that some of my fans rings have some plastic bits left in from the factory. Its a case of "Once you see it, you'll always see it." Considering the price, its a small issue. Another issue I have is the lack of a 0% PWM option. Ring fans have the benefit of not looking funny when the fan stops moving unlike normal full-blade RGB fans, and I think Thermalright should've offered that. If I really had to nit pick even harder, they don't offer an AMP rating for the RGB section.
Why 5 stars considering what I experienced? The ring fan market is small and there isn't much options. 3 good rings fans for a very good price in a small market, what a treat. The price outweighs the bad but a long margin.

The packaging was neat and secure, and each fan felt solid and well-made. The matte finish and minimal branding gave them a clean, professional look that blends in nicely with any setup. Mounting them was simple, and the included screws worked without any fuss. No weird vibrations, no misaligned holes, just an easy install all around.
What really stood out to me was the airflow-to-noise ratio. These fans are impressively quiet, even when running at full speed. I’ve used more expensive fans in the past that made more noise while pushing less air. These keep my CPU and GPU temps stable, especially during longer gaming sessions and heavier workloads like video editing. The airflow feels strong without being turbulent, and there's no annoying humming or whirring.
Pros
Excellent airflow with whisper-quiet operation
Sturdy, well-built construction with clean aesthetics
Great value for a 5-pack
Easy to install with no alignment issues
Ideal for both intake and exhaust configurations

Dropped my temps quite a bit, from 40 degrees on light load to dropping it to 30 to 35 degrees, gaming wise sits nicely around 49 to 55 degrees in temps. My main gripe is that one fan LEDs does flickers and it hasn't been a full day since I installed them. At first it was only during the blue transition when running it on cycle mode after I put my computer to sleep. Then it started to flicker on red. So I checked the connection, still flickers, then decided to daisy chain the rgb plug that single fan to another fan and the flicker hasn't happened (hopefully this solved it). I know my PSU isn't the issue since it's 850W and my fan hub is new and the other fans from Thermalright aren't flickering either. Absolutely functions perfect in my case and settings. Keys to quiet: Bigger fans offer more flow at lower RPM = lower noise.  More fans = more flow allowing lower RPM of all fans. reviews.title: Killer performance for the price.
reviews.comment: I forgot to take photos *before* installing them but the fans are mounted to the top of my P400 case. I decided to get 2 140mm fans to replace the two 120s I had previously because I recently (about 5 weeks ago) I landed with an ASUS Dual OC 3060 Ti, replacing my much smaller in size MSI Gaming X 1660 Ti. With the new card, temps were hovering anywhere between 70°C to 78°C on some games and varying ambient temps. The below list are max temps reached during these games with my previous top 120mm fans and my current 3060 Ti: 71°C Rainbow Six Siege 78°C Apex Legends 74°C DiRT Rally 2.0 75°C Monster Hunter World 76°C Shadow of the Tomb Raider All games were tested for 45 minutes, max possible settings for each game on a 1080p 144hz monitor; Ray Tracing enabled for Shadow of Tomb Raider, Ultra setting. As mentioned previously, I have a Phanteks P400 case with a front-mounted NZXT X52 cooling a Ryzen 5 3600 paired with a 3060 Ti from Asus, the DUAL OC model and the two 120mm fans mounted at the top. These are my temperatures now with two Arctic P14 top-mounted fans: 62°C Rainbow Six Siege 64°C Apex Legends 66°C DiRT Rally 2.0 68°C Monster Hunter World 67°C Shadow of the Tomb Raider By no means were my previous temperatures bad as my GPU still performed below it's 83°C limit but there's real performance to be gained by dropping temps as much as I did; 14°C less on Apex Legends with the Arctic P14 fans, simply incredible and I can't explain how. I am no expert when it comes to airflow but I figured that now having a larger GPU in size, my old 120mm top-mounted fans were not exhausting enough hot air and a lot of it was recirculating within the case, driving my temperatures up. I'm running these new P14 fans at their max rated RPM of 1700 and the sound is personally not bothersome enough for me to slow them down. I hope my use case gives others an idea of what kind of gains you can get temperature wise and ultimately better performance by keeping your components cooler. In my case, this upgraded targeted specifically my GPU and it worked just as I expected. I will recommend these fans to anyone and everyone looking for super quiet, high performance fans at an incredible cost when compared to the competition. I will lastly like to thank Hot Deals 4 Less for the incredibly fast shipping from the US to Costa Rica, the fans arrived in excellent conditions. I will be happy to be a regular customer for them moving forward.

reviews.title: Effective Cooling at a Bargain
reviews.comment: These fans are a German design and feature a very smooth bearing that Arctic developed. I have noticed that when I power the system off these fans coast down over a much longer period than other non-Arctic fans in the case (the AIO cooler I used is a different brand). That is an indication that the Arctic fans (this model, at least) should have a pretty decent MTBF. They move a lot of air, I pretty much don’t hear them, and I doubt I’ll ever need to replace them before the system itself becomes obsolete. These fans plugged directly into the motherboard fan headers and effortlessly interfaced with the motherboard fan control (I used an ASUS motherboard, but I expect the fan headers follow an industry standard - so Gigabyte, MSI, ASRock… brand shouldn’t matter for this feature). These are non-RGB, so one need not be concerned with RGB control. Personally, I was concerned that too much RGB would make my system more clown car than functional. So interface was plug and play - I literally did not need to do anything else. BIOS adjustments will work through the motherboard so customization of the fan control is straight forward. These should just go along with any configuration a user sets up. Simply leaving the BIOS at factory settings is also an option - the point being; install to the frame, plug into the board, and no other action is required on the fan itself. Installation was pretty easy as well. These use an ABS plastic frame in their design - its durable, yet has some surface pliability. The installation is simply to use the provided screws which will cut their own threads into the plastic. So, while installation is simple, one needs to take care not to over-torque - these are not steel. One downside of this is that a certain amount of care and dexterity is required to maintain a straight line while initiating the threads or the screw can end up a little crooked. Not a big deal, but just worth noting. In theory one may be concerned that over time the screws would work loose from vibration and the ABS would no longer be able to accept sufficient torque. But these fans are so well balanced that their operation is glass-smooth. So I doubt vibration will be a factor. Should I discover this to change however, I’ll revisit this post. For now, these fans have everything where it counts; simplicity, effectiveness, silence and presumed service longevity. I’m pretty happy with them. And all at a bargain price, too.

With a PWM range of 200-1700 RPM, they adapt efficiently to system demands while remaining whisper-quiet, even under load. The PWM Sharing Technology (PST) is a game-changer—it allows multiple fans to be controlled via a single signal, reducing cable clutter and ensuring consistent cooling performance. The build quality is fantastic, with sturdy materials that feel durable and long-lasting. Installation was a breeze, and the fans run incredibly silent, even at higher RPMs. The pressure-optimized blade design enhances static pressure, making them an ideal choice for restrictive airflow setups like radiators or mesh-front cases. If you're looking for high-quality, efficient, and quiet cooling solutions, this 5-pack is an absolute steal. Highly recommended for gamers, PC builders, and enthusiasts who want the best balance of performance and noise reduction!

reviews.title: Great fan, but a headache to get working.
reviews.comment: First, I’ll start with how awesome the RGB on these things are. It’s a very bright, very smooth looking LED ring, with 4 LEDs in the center as well (16 total). I have not noticed any noise, even using two as exhaust and they keep it cool at a steady 1200 RPM. I dinged this on installation due to the hoops (and $) you have to go through to set up the RGB. The fan will plug into any sysfan on the motherboard. However, unless you have a jcorsair header, you apparently can’t run these on a regular RGB header. Especially not if you wish to use iCUE. I already had a Lightning Node Pro, but it turns out the fan is a 4 pin RGB whereas the Node only sockets 3 pins. So I then ordered the Commander Pro thinking it would work, but apparently the fan slots are for RPM control, not RGB. So I cancelled it. Turns out only the fan hub will receive the RGB cables. They sell this on Corsair’s site for $10, but I did not want to wait. At the time of writing this, it has already been a week since I ordered. So what do I do? Buy the $130 pack of three fans, a fan hub and a Node. I had only intended to get one, but you need BOTH the hub and the Node to use the RGB... Absolutely ridiculous and expensive. I hate that I endorsed that but these fans do look good at least...
reviews.author: Cameron

reviews.title: amazing, quiet,great airflow,must have for any higher mid range build.
reviews.comment: i love these fans, the noise level compared to my old stock rosewill prism rgb fans i had when recording sound clips for my custom keyboards is mind boggling, actually being able to take software control of speed, and color of these fans really makes things a ton easier on me, and the rgb effects themselves are incredible, the fans are super brighter, i didnt wanna spend 100+ for fans for my entire nzxt h70i case, but after finally doing it i see why theyre so much money. worth every dime, the only downfall with these is they dont have rgb rings on both sides like the QL versions have, which i wasnt aware of, so that was pretty disappointing to me when i found out, and i also dont love how many wires and diffrent things fans like this take to function,  you need the fan header control hub, AND THE RGB LIGHTING NODE its insane, the cheap rosewill fans i had had a plug that was an all in on, power, and rgb all into one plug into the fan hub and you could control the rgb effects and colors from a restart button on the case if you have one, or via software control if you had the proper header which until my recent mobo upgrade i did not have. but i feel if a cheaper brand like that can stream line the rgb and power into a single plug, their should be no excuse for a brand such as corsair to get away with having so many cables for such a basic function of a fans because when you have a whole bunch of them, it REALLY starts to add up fast and without proper cable management your case will be flooded and cluttered with cables.
reviews.author: Jess

reviews.title: Really nice fans
reviews.comment: As long as you’re ok with using Corsair everything, and using icue, you will love these fans. I don’t love icue, but it is ok and works. The build quality and bright LEDs are great, and if you use a Commander Pro and lighting hub you will have no issues with connection. It’s also cool that you can download more icue profiles if you, like me, hate icue and can’t figure out how to do all the customization yourself. So that’s a plus. Icue does not play well with GPU rgb though, so you’re bound to need at least 2 applications to control all your lighting. I’m forced to have 3 since I also use Razer keyboard/mouse. The rgb situation really is ridiculous, companies need to have a single standard and go with that, because I think part of my issue is all these different rgb control applications running can cause issues when gaming or running other jobs. But that has nothing to do with these fans, just a rant about rgb. The fans are great, just a bit too expensive, but you do get what you pay for with fans anyway. Buy them!

reviews.title: Corsair LL Series LL120 RGB 120mm Dual Light Loop RGB LED PWM Fan Single Pack
reviews.comment: +1 - Item arrived on time, and not damaged +1 - Item is as described +2 - Super quiet fans, and RGB LEDs look great -1 - No instructions from Corsair for control the LEDs Thoughts: These install like a standard fan. Depending on how you're connecting them is how you'll control them. If you are connecting them straight to a board, make sure your MoBo software supports controlling RGBs. Otherwise, you'll need the Lightning Node Pro - which I was getting anyway since I was controlling multiple fans. My complaint is with Corsair providing instructions. They simply just tell you to go to Corsair software downloads to download the latest software. From there you get the option of downloading a couple different pieces of software. What they don't tell you is that iCUE is the latest rendition of their software, and what you should use. The other option is LINK - which of course is what I went with first. LINK ended up messing up the RGB on my Corsair RAM, but it controlled the fans just fine. After contacting support, is how I found out that iCUE is the software to use. Once i installed that, RAM was good to go and controlling the RGBs on my Radiator, RAM, and Fans was a breeze. So just use iCUE and you'll be good to go.
reviews.author: randy21m

reviews.title: Excellent fans, and even better if you catch them on sale
reviews.comment:
I bought two, which replaced the two stock fans that were included with my case and were set up as exhaust fans. I previously purchased a 3 pack which includes an RGB hub elsewhere, and it was better to buy them separately (on sale, $12.99 each at time of purchase), so I went for that.
Functionally and structurally, they're identical to the stock fans included in my 5000D Airflow, the only difference pretty much being the RGB lighting. Software is not the best but it's manageable and easy to use, and the fans just work and look great; can't say many more positive things than that.
One potentially negative thing about these fans is that the screw holes don't have threads from the factory. It's probably a common thing among PC fans, but I feel it's still worth noting. If you are going to use the screws to install them, I strongly recommend screwing and threading OUTSIDE your PC case BEFORE installing them. Believe me that things will be significantly better and easier if done this way. Don't make the same mistake that I made the first time.
Very solid RGB fans, especially if you can grab them on sale. They've been going for a week now with zero issues. Will try to update if anything comes up.

reviews.title: Good Value for a High Quality Fan
reviews.comment: This fan works flawlessly. I've used it for quite a bit now, and I can tell you this fan is worth it for the price. The fans are pretty quiet despite having all the same fans (except for the top ones in the photo). I honestly was expecting another air conditioner sound level when I'm gaming. But I've tested and maxed out the fan speed, and the noise was really impressive, definitely better than those cheap Lenovo Legion fans I used to have. My old fans don't compare to these Corsair fans. Depending on the chassis you're using, I would also like to point out that these fans are bright . . . with 4 of the same fans installed in my chassis, I don't even need an RGB strip to see my components inside the case. Also very fast shipping too, my new motherboard didn't even come in yet. Just make sure that you have a Corsair fan controller. Other than that, I have no complaints, and I am happy with my purchase.

reviews.title: Good fan, but using it with my Corsair Capellix H115i causes some weird quirks.
reviews.comment:
I'll start off with if you have a Corsair Commander 6 port fan hub (mine came with my aio), it's super easy to install and the RGB does what it's supposed to do!
The downside is I hate how the fan controller this plugs into uses a USB 2.0 header on the Mobo instead of the CPU fan header. You wouldn't think it, but it annoys me how the fans ramp up briefly to near max rpm for a couple moments then they slow down again. Some people that have been doing system builds awhile know what I'm talking about and are used to it (I'm not). So the fan works great, but this feedback is still relevant considering most will pair these fans with a fan hub and this is what you're treated to. Corsair tech support said it's expected behavior because of the boot order on motherboards which makes sense.
Just an gripe from an annoyed customer but the performance is spot on. Oh and the screws with one of the fans got stripped as I was mounting them. My fault probably.

reviews.comment:
I bought this fan to integrate as an exhaust fan for the Corsair case I used in my build.  The case came with 3 iCUE fans and a 6 port iCUE hub so I  decided to spend extra to get an iCUE fan.
It installed with no issue...coming with the necessary screws to easily connect onto the rear exhaust port of the case.  The PWM cable connected easily to the MB as did the RGB cable to the iCUE hub. The iCUE software detected it right away and it integrated with the other 3 fans for the lightshow immediately.
It is very quiet and moves a decent amount of air.
I'm happy with the fan BUT, unless you specifically need an iCUE fan, you can probably find an equivalent fan for less money.

reviews.title: Very nice fans for the price!
reviews.comment: These fans are surprisingly nice! Their 15mm thickness means they fit well in smaller cases, they were perfect for my Cooler Master Qube 540 build. They're very quiet, nearly silent at low speeds and still quiet at full speed. No humming, ringing, whining, etc. The airflow is pretty good for their small size, and they keep my PC nice and cool. They also don't draw much current, which means you can safely connect multiple fans to a single fan header using a splitter cable.
reviews.author: AJP22

reviews.title: Goes toe to toe with the pricier options at this slim size
reviews.comment: From a sheer performance perspective, and I'm talking pushing the most air through your case or into a heatsink, and doing so quietly, these fans are tough to beat. Considering they're only 15mm thick, I put them into my own best-of-class category. But while they do work great, they are on the flimsy side. I'll give you an example. After looking up the stats and reading some reviews, I decided to replace a competitor fan (name begins with 'Noc') with the P12 Slim in a sub-5 liter mini-itx case. I found the P12 to have slightly better performance by 2-3 degrees C in my case overall, with the noise the same as the Noc, at less than half the price. Only, when I first closed the case, the P12 wobbled at slow speeds, making an obvious noise along with it at startup and shutdown. This lasted for about 3 startups/shutdowns and just went away. I checked cables and all were clear, so it had to be coming from the fan. Considering its the same size as the other fan, which had no weird noise issues, I just felt the word flimsy came to mind. Maybe it twisted slightly to fit or something? I couldn't tell by looking. I'm not going to take a star off for this, but just be aware. I would have returned it if things didn't settle down. But it did, and it's been great, and mostly quiet, as the primary cooling fan for a Ryzen 9 7945HS. I'm not undervolting, and yet my temps are stable and well under 80C in normal use with temporary spikes up to 88C max. For the performance and value for the money, this is one of the best fans on the market at the 15mm height size.
reviews.author: well-read and still learning

reviews.title: Dropped my GPU temperatures by at least 10 degrees C
reviews.comment: I installed these two slim fans in the GPU bay of my Fractal Design Node 202 mini-ITX case to help cool an RTX 4070.  They immediately dropped GPU temperatures by at least 10 degrees C under load, while also reducing overall noise because the noisy GPU fans no longer need to spin up as high. The cable length is generous and works well for the Node 202, and since these fans can be daisy chained, I didn't need any additional adapters to plug the fans into a single fan header on my motherboard. I went with these Arctic fans over Noctua, because they're nearly half the price and still very quiet.  Overall, I'm very happy with them.

reviews.title: Be Quiet out performs my expectations once again.
reviews.comment:
Be Quiet! Light Wings 120mm PWM: Silent Symphony with a Touch of RGB Flair
Overall Rating: 4.5 out of 5 stars
For: Silent PC enthusiasts, RGB lovers seeking low noise, case fan and radiator upgrade seekers
Against: Limited ARGB control options, higher price than some non-RGB alternatives
Performance: 5 out of 5 stars
Be Quiet! lives up to its name with the Light Wings 120mm PWM. It delivers exceptional cooling performance while remaining whisper-quiet. Even at its maximum 1700 RPM, the noise level stays incredibly low, making it a dream for silent PC builds. The airflow optimization ensures efficient heat dissipation, making it suitable for both air coolers and radiators.
Features: 4 out of 5 stars
The Light Wings 120mm boasts a robust build quality with a sleek black design. The included PWM control allows for flexible fan speed adjustments based on your needs. The highlight, of course, is the vibrant ARGB lighting that adds a touch of personal flair to your PC. However, unlike other RGB fans, the control options are limited to the included hub, lacking software control or integration with major motherboard ecosystems.
Value: 4 out of 5 stars
While the Light Wings 120mm falls on the pricier side compared to some non-RGB fans, its exceptional quietness and build quality justify the premium. If you value silence and want a touch of RGB without sacrificing performance, it's a worthwhile investment.
Things to Consider:
Limited ARGB Control: No software control or motherboard integration for the lights, relying solely on the included hub.
Higher Price: More expensive than some non-RGB alternatives with similar performance.
Black Design: Might not be ideal for builds with different color schemes.
Final Verdict:
The Be Quiet! Light Wings 120mm PWM is a remarkable achievement in balancing powerful cooling with near-silent operation. Its sleek design, vibrant ARGB lighting, and robust build quality make it a top choice for silent PC enthusiasts and RGB lovers alike. While the limited ARGB control and higher price tag are minor drawbacks, its overall performance and quality shine through. If you prioritize silence and want a touch of RGB magic in your PC, the Light Wings 120mm PWM is a worthy addition to your symphony of silence.

reviews.comment: With a fervent heart filled with zeal for technological prowess, I embarked on a quest to seek out the finest fans that the market had to offer. Lo and behold, my pilgrimage came to a triumphant culmination upon my encounter with the Arctic F12 fans, a testament to ingenuity and craftsmanship. Permit me to regale you with a tale of my profound experience, wherein I shall extol their virtues in great detail. First and foremost, let us discuss the undeniable allure of their affordable price. A boon to those with discerning budgets, this fiscally prudent choice in no way sacrifices quality or performance. Nay, it boasts an exceptional value that casts an enchanting spell upon all who seek premium cooling solutions without breaking the coffers. The narrative of installation unfolds as a tale of ease, evoking nothing short of admiration for the designers' astute considerations. I, a mere mortal with limited technical prowess, found myself pleasantly surprised by the simplicity with which these fans were affixed to my system. A seamless process that, much to my delight, required naught but the most basic of tools and skills. Oh, how the fates smile upon those who bask in the breeze of the Arctic F12. Yet, as with all great journeys, there lie trials and tribulations in wait. For those, like myself, whose motherboard lacks sufficient fan connectors, a word of caution: an essential component thou must secure, lest thou find thyself bereft of the full blessings of these wondrous fans. A case fan splitter or a case fan hub shall serve as the key that unlocks the potential of the Arctic F12's cooling prowess, rendering any previous impediments as mere trifles in the grand tapestry of your computing experience. In the realm of acoustic harmony, these fans prove to be virtuosos, emitting nary a cacophonous note to mar the serenity of your abode. In my hours of meticulous scrutiny, I discovered no discordant whispers of excessive noise, but rather, a harmonious symphony of silent efficiency. Engulfed in this tranquil reverie, I basked in the reassurance that my computational haven was undisturbed by the clatter that oft plagues lesser fans. Venturing forth into the realm of airflow, I found myself enchanted by the Arctic F12's prowess. Mighty currents of cooling air surged forth from their supple blades, encapsulating my beloved components with tender care. The perils of inadequate airflow, a bane that can undo the noblest of systems, found no foothold in the face of these formidable fans. For assuredly, they have been crafted with an unwavering dedication to unyielding performance. Lastly, my fellow admirers of simplicity, rejoice, for in the Arctic F12, you shall find the epitome of elegance. Embracing an understated aesthetic, these fans stand as paragons of sophistication, free from the distracting allure of gaudy lights and ostentatious embellishments. Their simple black attire befits any system, harmonizing with a myriad of configurations, thereby bestowing upon thee a timeless allure that is both chic and unpretentious. Thus, dear readers, in the Arctic F12, I discovered a revelation—a treasure trove of cooling mastery that surpasses all expectations. Herein lies a sage counsel to heed: let not thy gaze wander further, for no greater marvel shall be found. Embrace the Arctic F12 and witness the metamorphosis of thy computing experience into a symphony of efficiency and tranquility.

reviews.title: Pretty quiet and amazingly inexpensive!  I purchased 2 five packs and am going to buy more.
reviews.comment: I’m very happy with this purchase!  Based upon some Amazon reviews I was a little concerned when ordering but I need not have been.  The fans arrived in fine shape, they’re well built and work!  At 12 VDC they made a tiny bit of noise so I run them at 9 VDC… at that voltage the fans are for all intent and purposes silent and they still move a lot of air!  Five of these fans just sip electricity when driven at 9 volts… just around 6 watts, 144 watts per day. Obviously I’m not using the fans for their intended purpose inside a computer case or electronic equipment.  These little box fans allow a very simple approach to keep rooms that are distant from our fireplace heated.  For my project I built some wood frames, routed a channel into the frame, wired them, set some hooks in the top of the doorway and DC power from a cheap transformer, hung them up, plugged ‘em in and there you have it. As said in the old HBO series Game of Thrones… WINTER IS COMING!
