reviews.title: Quiet but not "silent"
reviews.comment: Great quality fan, but it should be noted that this isn't a "silent" fan at its default RPM.  I would characterize the noise level as low, but still audible from 6 feet away at the default 1350RPM.  This is a 3-pin fan without PWM, so without a 3-pin fan controller, it will run at a fixed 1350RPM which will be quiet but not silent.  If you have a compatible fan controller and drop the RPM to ~1000RPM or lower, it would be considered silent.

reviews.title: Easily One of the Best!
reviews.comment: I'm like most people who at first didn't think or know that fans were very important. Up to a certain point, I usually had computers that had maybe 1 fan in them. I'm not a gamer, but I work from home on 4 screens and I also trade equities. When I first went on a journey of finding a half decent gaming computer for all the tasks I needed to do, that's when I realized fans were quite important. Once I came to this realization, like many people, I started with Noctua, which as we all know, is one of the best. While I'm still a fan of Noctua due to how compact and amazing the U12a is for CPU cooling(also love their NT-H2 thermal paste), I'm not quite there with their case fans. For me the top case fans are Scythe Kaze Flex and Arctic P series. Kaze Flex just slightly edging out Arctic in a number of case fan shoot outs, however, Arctic has a few things going for them: 1) They come in white 2) They are amazingly quiet without sacrificing cooling 3) They are daisy chainable, so you can attach multiple together and use 1 header on your motherboard 4) They are amazingly inexpensive for the performance you get and almost never arrive in unusable condition. With all that said, even your $30 fans have trouble competing. They don't have rubber corners, but I have yet to install any (P12's or P14's) that have any kind of vibration noise. I had Noctua, Scythe, Phantex, etc...all the 'best' staples, and I'm honestly happiest with the 5 P14's I have in my beQuiet! 500dx case. My 5900x is overclocked to 4.4ghz at 1.25v being cooled by a Noctua NH-U12a. I have my rear exhaust P14 set to 'Performance' mode in the bios, so it's mostly staying at about 60% unless the cpu hits 50 degrees, then it starts to ramp up, hitting 100% at 80 degrees. My motherboard is an AsRock x570 Taichi Razer Edition(I know, not cheap), which has good VRM's. My 2 top and 2 front P14's I have set in 'Normal' mode in the bios, which has them sitting at 50%, so around 6v most of the time. The machine is effectively silent. Whatever sound it generates is usually moreso from the graphics card or cpu cooler ramping up. Even with the overclock, I'm idling under 40 degrees most of the time and at night when the sun goes down and the ac kicks in, I see 36/37 degrees. All in all, I think I'm an Arctic P series fanboy now.

reviews.title: Quiet but does have resonance
reviews.comment: After doing a lot of research on fans, this is one of the ones I wanted to try. It's definitely quiet for most of its RPM range, and has a good sound. However, it does have resonance, and this intrigued me. I ran it through it's entire RPM range manually using a Noctua NA-FC1 PWM fan controller, which is more precise than varying voltage, and allows the entire range to be utilized. Then I plugged that setup into a precise bench power supply set to 12 volts (which is easier than connecting it to a running PC that makes noise itself). After trying the RPM range a bit, and slowly ramping up and down multiple times, I counted 5 passes through resonance. Without resonance, it has a good low noise level, however when passing through or staying at a resonance RPM, it makes a significantly annoying whining sound. If you've ever heard a large industrial motor start up and pass through resonance frequencies, it sounds like that, except annoying in this situation, whereas industrial motors sound really cool. After thinking about it a bit, I am not sure if the resonance comes from the fan's motor, the frame, or perhaps interactions between the blade design and the frame, etc. If they can solve the resonance issue these would be excellent fans. In fact, the resonance issue is the only common complaint about these fans, they satisfy other requirements excellently, according to fan reviewers. If you're interested in the resonance issue, research around the web as there's significant discussion about it.

reviews.title: Killer performance for the price.
reviews.comment: I forgot to take photos *before* installing them but the fans are mounted to the top of my P400 case. I decided to get 2 140mm fans to replace the two 120s I had previously because I recently (about 5 weeks ago) I landed with an ASUS Dual OC 3060 Ti, replacing my much smaller in size MSI Gaming X 1660 Ti. With the new card, temps were hovering anywhere between 70°C to 78°C on some games and varying ambient temps. The below list are max temps reached during these games with my previous top 120mm fans and my current 3060 Ti: 71°C Rainbow Six Siege 78°C Apex Legends 74°C DiRT Rally 2.0 75°C Monster Hunter World 76°C Shadow of the Tomb Raider All games were tested for 45 minutes, max possible settings for each game on a 1080p 144hz monitor; Ray Tracing enabled for Shadow of Tomb Raider, Ultra setting. As mentioned previously, I have a Phanteks P400 case with a front-mounted NZXT X52 cooling a Ryzen 5 3600 paired with a 3060 Ti from Asus, the DUAL OC model and the two 120mm fans mounted at the top. These are my temperatures now with two Arctic P14 top-mounted fans: 62°C Rainbow Six Siege 64°C Apex Legends 66°C DiRT Rally 2.0 68°C Monster Hunter World 67°C Shadow of the Tomb Raider By no means were my previous temperatures bad as my GPU still performed below it's 83°C limit but there's real performance to be gained by dropping temps as much as I did; 14°C less on Apex Legends with the Arctic P14 fans, simply incredible and I can't explain how. I am no expert when it comes to airflow but I figured that now having a larger GPU in size, my old 120mm top-mounted fans were not exhausting enough hot air and a lot of it was recirculating within the case, driving my temperatures up. I'm running these new P14 fans at their max rated RPM of 1700 and the sound is personally not bothersome enough for me to slow them down. I hope my use case gives others an idea of what kind of gains you can get temperature wise and ultimately better performance by keeping your components cooler. In my case, this upgraded targeted specifically my GPU and it worked just as I expected. I will recommend these fans to anyone and everyone looking for super quiet, high performance fans at an incredible cost when compared to the competition. I will lastly like to thank Hot Deals 4 Less for the incredibly fast shipping from the US to Costa Rica, the fans arrived in excellent conditions. I will be happy to be a regular customer for them moving forward.

reviews.title: Noctua Quality, Better Appearance and Excellent Price
reviews.comment: For the last 15 years of building PCs, case fans were more or less an afterthought for me. I either used what the case came with, or if necessary, added some cheapo fans I had lying around. Throughout the years I've become much pickier about how my system sounds both at idle and under load. This is where these fans come in. I'm currently doing a major upgrade on my current rig which started with the purchase of a Lian Li Lancool II mesh. To go along with it I purchased a couple of Noctua 140mm fans for the front intake and moved the 3 stock fans to the rear of the case. When I first fired the system up I was a bit disappointed. While the case itself is great, I noticed a bit of a clicking or grinding noise, even at idle. After making sure nothing was making contact with any of the fan blades, I started unplugging fans one by one. Surprise surprise, all the noise vanished after disconnecting all the stock Lian Li fans and leaving the Noctuas connected. Within a couple days I had some more Noctua fans and chucked the Lian Li fans in the spare parts bin. Again, these fans may not make a huge temperature difference vs other fans, but they maintain excellent thermal performance while being virtually silent at idle and very pleasant-sounding even at their max of 1200RPM. Bear in mind there is a point of diminishing returns with fans. If you don't care about a bit of extra noise, 2 or 3 of the higher RPM versions of this fan will be more than enough to cool most systems comfortably while being unobtrusive to most people, especially headphone users. I'm a little strange, so in total I have about 8 Noctua fans including the NH-D15S stock fan, all running at very conservative speeds to keep the noise down and it's mind blowing how quickly air moves through this system relative to how quiet it is. Make no mistake, most of Noctuas products are aimed at enthusiasts and priced accordingly. These fans are different. They're cheaper than a lot of fans from reputable competitors like Scythe, Corsair and Arctic, while being much nicer looking than the OG Noctua brown fans and often way quieter at all RPMs. In spite of being cheaper and not having Noctua's latest and greatest engineering inside, these redux fans are lightyears ahead of most case fans out there. If you hate the way your case fans sound and don't care about RGB bling factor, these are an excellent option. Chances are, these fans will probably outlast the system they're cooling.

reviews.title: Buy them if you don't want RGB.
reviews.comment: The Noctua NF-P14s redux-1200 PWM is a high-quality computer case fan designed to provide efficient cooling while maintaining low noise levels. In this unbiased review, we'll evaluate its various aspects to give you a comprehensive overview. **Performance (4.5/5):** The NF-P14s redux-1200 PWM excels in terms of cooling performance. With a maximum speed of 1200 RPM, it can move a decent amount of air to help keep your system cool. The fan is well-balanced, delivering adequate airflow without generating excessive noise. It's an excellent choice for maintaining optimal temperatures without creating a disruptive acoustic environment. **Noise Levels (4.5/5):** Noctua is well-known for its focus on noise reduction, and this fan is no exception. The NF-P14s redux-1200 PWM operates quietly, thanks to its advanced design and PWM control. At lower speeds, it's virtually silent, making it an ideal choice for those who value a quiet computing environment. **Build Quality (4.5/5):** Noctua is renowned for its premium build quality, and this fan is no exception. It features high-quality materials and precise engineering, ensuring durability and reliability. The fan's construction is robust, and it comes with anti-vibration pads to reduce noise and maintain stability. **Installation (4/5):** Installing the NF-P14s redux-1200 PWM is relatively straightforward. It comes with standard mounting options and clear instructions. However, some users might find the installation process a bit fiddly, especially when dealing with tight spaces or smaller cases. **Value (4/5):** While Noctua fans are not the most budget-friendly options on the market, they offer excellent value in terms of performance, noise reduction, and build quality. If you're willing to invest a bit more for a reliable, long-lasting fan that won't disrupt your peace and quiet, this fan is a solid choice. **Aesthetics (3.5/5):** Noctua's fans are known for their functional rather than flashy design. While their brown and beige color scheme may not be to everyone's taste, it's a design choice that emphasizes Noctua's identity. Some users may prefer a more neutral or customizable appearance. **Conclusion:** The Noctua NF-P14s redux-1200 PWM is a highly efficient and quiet case fan with a focus on performance and noise reduction. It excels at maintaining optimal temperatures while operating almost silently, which is a considerable advantage for those who value a peaceful computing experience. The fan's build quality and durability are exceptional, though the design may not appeal to users looking for a more aesthetically versatile option. Overall, if you prioritize cooling efficiency and low noise in your system, this Noctua fan is a worthwhile investment.
reviews.author: ILoveWritingReviews

reviews.title: Quiet, good airflow, better value than non-redux
reviews.comment: Would buy again. Like: The grey color blends in with most build better than the tan/brown of the non-redux line or even the black of the chromax line. The RPM range (in PWM mode) is far superior to the non-redux/chromax 140mm fans (see comment below). The price brings them into the range of mid-tier non-ARGB offerings from other manufacturers. Dislike: They don't come with anti-vibration dampers, but you can (and I did) buy them separately. These are in a home office build that I also do light gaming on. I'm running an Intel i5-11400, mATX ASUS TUF Gaming mobo, a Sabrent 1 TB PCIe 4.0 X4 M.2 drive, and an EVGA RTX 2060 KO GPU in a Fractal Design Meshify 2 Mini case. With the additional (and unnecessary) filters removed, these fans are nearly silent. I'm using FanControl with a linear curve and the pair of front 140mm Noctua redux fans are normally running around 500 RPM. Below whisper quiet. I recently build another PC in a Meshify 2 Compact (ATX-compatible) case with an i7-13700K, RTX 4080, MSI Z790 mobo, 5 M.2 drives, and with the black chromax 140mm fans. They had a terrible drone at lower RPMs - something that was apparently a known issue. Fan Control doesn't want to spin them below 800 RPM as well. I should have gone with these redux fans from the beginning and saved a ton of money and hassle. Overall, will buy again and highly recommend for non-ARGB builds.

reviews.title: Superb quality and performance. You get what you pay for.
reviews.comment: Pros: - Quality Construction - Extremely quiet - Moves a lot of air - PWM Cons: - Price - Comes with cheap silver screws. Would've preferred rubber screws, but whatever. I'll be honest, I wouldn't have bought this fan if it weren't for me needing a fan that did not exceed 25mm in depth. I usually go for the Arctic F14, which is a great fan below $10, but they're 27mm deep and because of that, they won't fit in the front of my case. I have a Fractal Design Define R4 case which has a screw-less mounting solution for the front intake fans. They're held in by tiny clips and a fan that is too thick won't snap into place. I had Fractal fans in there before hand but they became noisy so the only other company I really thought to go to was Noctua. This is my first Noctua product and I'm very impressed with the quality of this product. It seems extremely well made and it performs wonderfully. I wouldn't have bought it simply because of the price if an Arctic fan could've fit but it is what it is.Popped this bad boy in, set up the fan curve in the BIOS and away I went. PC is scary quiet now. Damn near silent at idle. Everyone raves about Noctua and now I've experienced why. I will update in the future in terms of reliability, my Fractal fans seemed to last about 12-18 months before becoming a vibrating nightmare.
reviews.author: Tyler D.

reviews.title: Its a Noctua fan at a cheaper price, and arguably better colors.
reviews.comment: Its a Noctua fan! - That alone usually says everything. The 1500rpm ones seem to be more popular, I'm not entirely sure why, but I got the 1200rpm because I wanted silence. I'm never going to run these things at their max speed. I dunno how people say at full speed these things are 'silent' - Maybe the fan it's self is, but the air turbulence it makes isn't. That isn't the fans fault, thats just physics. I have 3 of them hooked up to a PWM hub, and at ~50% speed they are really silent. Most people when they walked into my computer room couldn't tell the PC was on at first. They are still great at 750rpm, but I am happy I bought these 1200 ones so I could get that much lower. If your chasing that 'Silent' just a fair warning: Much like how the retina of your eye adjusts in darkness to give you better 'night vision'. A similar thing happens with your ears, So yeah in the dead of night you will probably start hearing the airflow, but I find the noise it makes a lot nicer then other fans. Also you'll probably start hearing other components in your PC that your fan noise used to cover up like your PSU's fan, or your HDD. - It will be a battle you cannot win. All that said, I can't recommend these enough! They move plenty of air even at slow speeds, and are quiet. I think the only thing bad I can say about them is that their cables are shorter then my old fans by a good a few inches. This might be problematic in some cases, but in my Define R4, with a PWM hub attached near the 5.25" bay, all the cables of the 2 front and 1 rear fans reached just fine. EDIT:  I would also like to confirm something that isn't really listed anywhere. The starting voltage for this fan is just under 5V in case you need to use voltage speed control for some reason.
reviews.author: Scruffy

reviews.title: The best fans I have ever seen
reviews.comment: These are amazing. Even at top speed, they are very low noise, they install as fast as you are with a screwdriver (faster if you use the noise dampening connectors), they are super high quality, and the gasket works perfectly. My cpu is a liquid cooled and I have 2 of these in a push-pull configuration on the radiator and now the cpu temperature maxes out with a max load and max overclocking ten degrees C lower and the temperature overall is lower and drops much faster than with the previous fans that were actually pretty good. Airflow through the radiator is amazing. These fans and the 4 pin pwm version of the same physical configuration are the best I have ever seen in decades of working with computers when it comes to radiators and air cooling heatsinks. I have already ordered more for use in other systems and to blow air out of the tower itself (my system doesn't have a powered intake for some reason, but I would use these for that too, if I could). I actually like the colors and look of these, I know that the general opinion is that they look ugly, but they look pretty good to me in my system. There are tons of ways to attach them both physically and electrically. So you can connect them directly to the motherboard or pci card via 3 pin connector or directly to the power supply. So you can actually use as many as you want, creating new intakes and outputs in the case and/or for duct channels as the power supply connection can be chained with as many fans as you can power. They do cost more than usual, but they are absolutely worth it. They will last forever. I have had very good fans in the past and they have never had the six year warranty that these have. They also do not have the travel between the rotor and the stator base that other fans have, which is a good indicator of the longevity of almost any device. And the cable attachments to lower the top speed of these fans are nice to have, but these fans are so quiet that I can have them permanently running at top speed without any problems. I have both light and sound sensitivities and these fans aren't a problem for that at all. I also have chronic migraines and I can leave my computer running during them because they are so quiet. I really can't say enough about how much I love these things
reviews.author: Dave

reviews.title: A masterpiece, I rarely am impressed to this extent
reviews.comment:
premium build quality, premium packaging, sound? I added this one as a rear fan and it's like I've added nothing whatsoever in terms of noise, had a pretty easy time setting this thing up, a bit tough with the included rubber mounts but it's so worth it
And for the big part, as a single rear fan on my TD500 white mesh case this had like 4-5 C° decrease in temps when multitasking & while playing games (full load) to both the cpu and gpu which is pretty drastic for a one fan
The only cons I'd consider which are pretty minor and subjective are the color options, (tho it went well with my white case) , and the pricing - which is to be expected at this build quality and performance
reviews.author: Man

reviews.title: Quiet and huge improvement
reviews.comment:
I don’t have a gaming pc but a little desktop, and it only has 1 fan. It kept getting incredibly hot with the original fan. I installed this one and it’s been a world of difference. Not only much quieter but also a lot cooler! Never hitting above 60 C
Awesome product! I love it!!
reviews.author: Amazoncustomer

reviews.title: Quiet and effective fan for water cooled CPUs
reviews.comment: I read about these fans and thought that I would plunk down the cash to try one. Well, color me surprised and satisfied! I had purchased an Arctic Cooling Liquid Freezer 120 for my new Ryzen 2 2600X. The stock fans were mostly quiet except at full speed (1500 RPM) you could hear them. This Noctua fan is as quiet at 2000 RPM as the Arctic Cooling fans at 1500 RPM! I put this Noctua fan on the radiator to push and left the stock Arctic on the other side to pull and my CPU temps dropped 3 degrees Celsius by just changing the fan out! This is a very well designed fan with lots of accessories included in the box. I was always hesitant to buy Noctua fans due to the higher costs, but this fan is worth it in my opinion.
reviews.author: N Wieling

reviews.title: they are the best 120mm fans money can buy
reviews.comment:
Yes, these fans are expensive.  However, they are the best 120mm fans money can buy.  They are quieter at 1500 RPM than most 120mm fans are at 1000.  They have excellent static pressure performance, so they work exceptionally well on water cooling radiators.
If money isn't an issue, and you just want the best of everything, I recommend these fans.  If value-for-money is a concern, though, I'd recommend looking at fans closer to $10 or $15.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Best standard form-factor 140mm I've used.
reviews.comment: I bought this because I needed a 140mm fan with a standard, square frame to fit my case's odd front-intake mounting system. It seems that the few 140mm fans that don't suck are of the 120mm mounting hole variety, which are handy for heatsink placement but wind up being a hassle as case fans. Noctua's previous 140mm fan was, in my opinion, one of their less impressive products. The A14 finally gives Noctua a 140mm fan worth their name. Its bearing runs silky smooth, and the fan is near-inaudible beyond 12 inches, running at 800 rpm while moving more than sufficient air for a properly laid out case. An intake fan doesn't need to blow leaves off your components; it just needs to provide current that reaches far enough to lower the case's ambient air temp in the right places. Noc has moved beyond mere acoustics to engineer some fans that produce refined, focused current. The result is a fan that doesn't seem like it's pushing a ton of air, but manages to be effective in getting it where it needs to be. I noticed temp drops compared to my previous fan (a fairly high quality one at that) that was running 100rpm faster. The silicon dampeners are a nice touch, though really the fan is balanced and smooth running enough that they probably aren't even necessary. It comes with a voltage limiter, but the thing is so quiet at its 800rpm full speed that I can't imagine ever using it. That attached wiring is rather short, but an extension is included. That's actually nice, since for placements where you don't need much length it prevents having a bunch of slack. Now Noctua just needs to offer some different colors. I'm not hung-up on their current color like some people are, but some coloring that isn't so conflicting with just about every case interior would be nice.
reviews.author: S. Scruff

reviews.title: Quiet operation.  Great quality.
reviews.comment: The fan is extremely quiet and has enough air flow for my needs.  If the color of the fan matches your setup, it is a great choice.
reviews.author: Kathy Forsythe

reviews.title: Worth the Wait
reviews.comment: Yes it came three days late, who cares. I rarely write reviews but this one time I will. I am using this as an - external - fan I placed on top of my fanless Mini ATX PC to cool the surface a bit. (to usb port) Meaning, the fan actually sits on top of the machine and the machine is about 2 feet away from my keyboard. Reason I invested in a fanless PC is that I am particularly sensitive to mechanical noise. Can't hear this fan. I tried. I just cannot hear this thing. Not an excessive amount of air flow but silent. Not whisper quiet, silent. It does cool the internals of my machine a bit more, I placed the fan one inch above the vent, super nice build, and silent. Why did I not do that earlier ?
reviews.author: Client d'Amazon

reviews.title: Noctua Premium Fan for a truly silent system. Great fan.
reviews.comment: This review is short. I ordered this to keep my cable box (HD-DVR) from misbehaving. I noticed it runs hot and I grabbed a cpu fan on a wimp and gave it a try by placing it on top of the unit. It cooled the box nicely but the noise was ridiculous. But the box started to work well without needing to reset often. So I looked and looked for a silent fan. Although bigger than I thought I needed, I went with this unit. It comes in a beautiful package with lots of extras. I ended it connecting it with the additional wire reducer for a total silent operation. You can't hear it at all when the equipment is completely off. I have a nice Home Theater system and no fans run when everything is off. The Noctua is the only one 24/7. And you can't hear it at all. And that was what I wanted. Funky color which is visible slightly over the box but overall great product. Highly recommended.
reviews.author: Sapukai

reviews.title: Works well; fussy to mount
reviews.comment: Fussy to mount - I could never get their special "noise-dampening" silicone screws to work, but if you use regular screws, it goes in fine, though the ones provided are *barely* just long enough if you screw it in tightly. The fan seems to work well. My computer stays nice and cool.
reviews.author: GiveUpYourPtolemy

reviews.title: It sounded like a vacuum cleaner
reviews.comment:
I bought an Antec rack-mount computer case about 8 or 9 years ago. I needed this type of case configuration for my recording studio. I use computers for recording work. Most everything around me is rack-mounted so it made sense to rack-mount the PC too. Ambient/mechanical noise is a no-no in this field. If I can hear it, so can a microphone (especially a large diaphragm condenser mic). All these years I never bothered to hook up the front panel fan. I sort of instinctively knew it was going to generate noise so I relied on internal cooling (large CPU fan, power supply fan, fanless video card, etc). Never had an issue. But from one rebuild to another, the internal cooling seemed to get less and less. The new PS I bought has a fan but the fan doesn't turn on at all unless the internal temp exceeds a threshold. I felt the current rebuild needed some additional cooling so I decided to hook up that unused front panel fan. It sounded like a vacuum cleaner. I could hear it in the other room. I can only assume that case fan manufacturers many years ago gave no thought whatsoever to ambient noise. Maybe they figured this case/PC was going to end up in an isolated IT room somewhere. There was no way. I had to replace it.
I looked around, did a little research. Some of the better PC builders (in this field) were using Noctua fans so I just followed their lead. This fan mounted right into the available front panel fan slot. That part was a simple install. The package came with four smallish screws and four rubber vibration insulator stand-offs. You choose one or the other mounting solution. I just went with the metal screws. I didn't think vibration was going to be an issue.
Originally, I wasn't sure what to do with the low-noise adapters. There are two different types included with the fan: LNA and ULNA. They're just shorty extension cables with a resistor soldered in-line. The LNA version supposedly reduces RPM to 1100 and noise to 16.9 dB. I decided to try the LNA version first. For some reason the fan didn't work. I removed the LNA adapter and just went "straight-in" connected to an available fan connector on my MSI motherboard. The fan started working immediately so there must be some issue with these adapters and certain motherboards. In BIOS, I can adjust the fan speed easily so I played around with the different settings. The fan was quiet at all settings but more quiet as I reduced the RPM setting. I chose a middle setting.
Re: noise. The fan makes noise but compared to what I had before, it's night and day improvement. I can hear the fan if I get close enough to the case, but I don't think the noise level is going to pose a problem as far as recording is concerned. I would never record anything that close to the computer case anyway.
I can feel cool air blowing through some small ventilation holes in the rear of the case so I can tell this thing is moving plenty of air.
I'm not an expert on case fans. I couldn't tell you the advantages or disadvantages of one brand to another. But this particular brand/model seems very high quality. It moves air (which is the whole point) and it's quiet. It's not as quiet as no fan, but it's quiet enough and should be absolutely fine for general purpose (non-audio) needs. These days, it seems like the CPU and other internal components are more heat tolerant than before. But audio users often have DSP sound cards and other heat generating devices that mount inside the case so those need to be dealt with. I'm very pleased with this purchase and Amazon got it to me in a couple of days. They absolutely rock when it comes to shipping!
reviews.author: Larry Kriz

reviews.title: Best fans on the market
reviews.comment: This fan has been running like a workhorse for almost 8 years of constant use, and multiple rig changes. I retired it only because I got a completely new rig. These fans don't look the best, and they are pricier, but the sheer quality on display cannot be beaten by any other fan on the market. It's quiet, even through hours of heavy use. Use Noctua fans, your work or battle station will thank you for it.
reviews.author: Gear Masaki

reviews.title: My Vote for Best Radiator Fans - No Question
reviews.comment:
This is my 5th Noctua purchase in total and my second build to utilize their fans exclusively. When it comes to quality and performance delivery, I'm not sure you can do better than one of these brown beauties.
I thought it was prudent to write a new review since this is the first one I've purchased from Amazon. I new right away this would be different; the fan doesn't have the plastic covers on the corners like my previous NF fans installed on my Corsair H60 in my multimedia PC. It doesn't come with the low-noise adapter or the PWM splitter cable in the PWM version packaging, but that was expected. I purchased the 3-pin version to replace the stock radiator fan on my EVGA 980 TI Hybrid graphics card. To put it bluntly, this fan made a HUGE difference in audible sound and keeps the cooler at lower temperatures. WIN/WIN
Since you can't see the fan due to the radiator setup, the color is a non-issue. For applications where colors will be present and you're going for a "themed' look, you can plasti-dip the outside of the fan any color to match. I wouldn't recommend painting or dipping the blades due to balance issues that could occur due to uneven painting. That being said, the color doesn't bother me so much anymore, but I did decide to use the light grey "redux" version of this fan in 140mm for my Kraken X61 AIO cooler and the performance is the same.
In conclusion, if you have the need for a static pressure fan without PWM connection, this is a solid choice. If you are looking to replace the stock fan on your AIO cooler for a graphics card, I can't imagine anything that'd outperform this other than some $50+ special German design. Noctua is well-worth the cost and will last for years and years.
reviews.author: DM1986

reviews.title: Not bad
reviews.comment:
I like these fans. I bought 4 of them for my case. I like the feel of them. I don't love the color as most people don't either but it isn't very visible when it's inside the case. The rubber mounts are nice although I don't see any instruction how to properly install them any where. There is a small diagram that doesn't help much. Installing these rubber mounts is pretty difficult because there will always be 1 or 2 holes that is impossible to reach because it's too close to components in a case.
I have an NZXT case with a fan controller. These fans are pretty quiet and are more quiet if they run on slower speeds. Out of the 4 fans that I bought, I have a problem with one or two of them not spinning on the lowest fan controller speed when I turn on the computer. The fan works once I increase the speed to a higher setting and then reduce it back to lowest setting. I find this a little strange. This is a small hassle because if I forget to turn the speed up at first, one or two fans won't be doing their jobs and not cool the system.
Here is my problem with these fans. I really didn't see much of a temperature drop with these from the original NZXT fans that come with the system. The NZXT fans are about $7 and cool the system to a similar temperature. These Noctua fans might cool it to 1 or 2 degrees Celsius lower. I don't know if it is really worth buying fans that are more than double the price to get a similar temperature.
They are more expensive but are some of the quietest ones I've used.
reviews.author: Axel

reviews.title: Great Slim fan
reviews.comment: I Used this on my Lian Li 185M case as a front intake fits in front of the panel and cooled an M-ATX 7600k perfectly. with out it the case was warm to the touch. Now it serves as an auxiliary fan for the CPU cooler in a different case. Fan moves good amount of air and quite and the fans can be daisy chained. Good purchase
reviews.author: Kelly

reviews.title: Slim spin
reviews.comment: They are slim and work. I added some fans on top of my push/pull rad config as these are not super strong, but I’m fully satisfied with these. I wasn’t super nice to them and they didn’t break like others have reported.
reviews.author: Corey Langseth

reviews.title: Excellent
reviews.comment: I'm not sure anyone else makes a slim 140mm fan, but these are great. I have 5 or 6 of the full size ones in my server and they've been perfect and quiet for the last year, so when I saw the brand again, I figured they'd be good, and they are. Super quiet and move a lot of air, quality hefty feel to them. I used these specifically for my Fractal Ridge PC case to fit a thicker GPU and not have things rubbing together. My build being a small form factor, it's also great that they have a daisy chain plug, so I only needed one fan header. My only nitpick about these fans is that if you are mounting the front of the blade side of the fan against a case, at low speeds the blade wobbles slightly and will rub the case. Higher speed it doesn't do this. I bought a pack of cheap rubber washers to put between the fan and case to move it a few millimeters away from the case mounting points and it resolved the issue.
reviews.author: Nick Henderson

reviews.title: Works fine but cheap quality
reviews.comment: I usually only use Noctua, Phantek, or BeQuiet fans but for my most recent SFF build I needed slim 140mm fans and none of the aforementioned brands make one. Only other 140 slim fan out there is from Silverstone but I've had good experiences with arctic in the past so I went with that. Here are my thoughts: Overall if you absolutely need slim fans then these do work fine and they are fairly silent, however they are very cheap in quality IMO. Unlike Noctua and Silverstone slim fans which have thicker housing and rubber gaskets, these Arctic slims are just a thin plastic frame around the blades. They also have a bit of blade lift so when my fans turned on the blades started hitting the case even though I checked the clearance during install. I ended up having to 3D print fan spacers to prevent the blades from hitting. Outside of that the fans are pretty silent. Overall if you want the best of the best thats out there I would probably check out the Silverstones first or hope that Noctua gets their head out of their behinds and makes a slim 140mm. Otherwise these are fine in the interim.
reviews.author: Mad Mensch

reviews.title: Exactly what I needed
reviews.comment: I use the Arctic Freezer 280 in a nzxt h7, and it didn't fit up top due to the motherboard heatsink and colum in the case. Using these, it fits perfectly with some room to spare, and performance wasn't really all that affected with my oc'd 13700k. Temps maybe changed 1-2c, maybe? But nothing to worry about. They're also very quiet, even running at max speed. Fwiw, I also received the fan blades that are connected at the ends, they feel pretty durable and I haven't experienced any of the issues mentioned in other reviews. I'll update if I do, but in the meantime, I would recommend them if you need to fit a radiator in a tight area.
reviews.author: J&V

reviews.title: Awesome, Great quality budget fans.
reviews.comment: Built a cheap gaming pc and decided to go with this fan/controller set as the price was great and it looks great in the build, but I’m honestly surprised with them, they are quiet and move air thru the case really well, I also paired it with their air cooler and it has been super stable with great thermals. Lots of RGB settings to choose from as well
reviews.author: Jamison

reviews.title: Best at this price range!
reviews.comment: I really can't believe this Fan set's price, it's simply fantastic! Really good airflow, incredibly quiet, more RGB, single or combined color and brightness options than you could ever possibly want, good cable length on the fans, a fan hub to connect all the fans to with a SATA power connnector and a remote control for your lighting preference! You really can't ask for more at this price, and yes, I'm aware that the fan hub does not connect to the RGB header of your motherboard so that you can control the lights via software directly from your PC, but then again, I refer you once more to the price. Want that feature? Go up 2 or 3 levels higher in price and you'll be set, but at this price range? Best in class, bar none. Five Stars! :-)
reviews.author: Alejandro Javier P

reviews.title: DOPE
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/D13AGHx8NoL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/514QC+HUVWL._SY256.jpg These fans are seriously impressive—I’m not easily wowed, but these delivered. Installation was incredibly simple with no extra wiring, and they powered directly through the hard drive without any hassle.
The airflow, noise level, and lighting are all excellent. They offer great performance and look fantastic, especially for the price. I originally bought them for my son’s build, but I’ll definitely be purchasing more for future builds.
My only concern is the remote—if it gets lost, you won’t be able to control the fan speed. The RGB app works well for changing colors, but it doesn’t replace the remote for speed adjustments.
reviews.author: Amanda O’Neill

reviews.title: So much more than I expected!
reviews.comment: It is so rare to receive something that you've ordered, and it turns out to be so much more than you expected or paid for.  This was definitely the case when unpacking this order that was very nicely boxed and the 5 fans were very sturdy and well made.  I was also pleasantly surprised that it came with a very nice 10 port hub and multiple function remote even though there was no mention of either in the description when I purchased it.  Installed all 5 fans in no time and at first thought that the fan speeds were nowhere near what was in the description until I realized that you could increase/decrease the fan speeds with the remote control that was included.  Definitely recommed.
reviews.author: Rodney Rea

reviews.title: Cheap. Gets the job done.
reviews.comment:
Decided to replace the stock fans on one of my pcs. Normally, I go noctua and control each fan through the MB headers with Fan Control. But this pc isn't that important and was missing some rgb bling. I knocked down a star because the fans use some kind of old serial cable with like 6 pins, these are never going to connect to your motherboard needless to say. You HAVE to use the included fan hub, the fan hub has a RGB connector so it can connect to and receive RGB signal from the MB but that hasn't worked at all. [knocked half a star for that] and lastly, you will not be able to control the fan speed and set fan curves or any of that stuff which is quite important in my opinion [knocked a half star for that ]
The hub is pretty ugly and clunky, but can accommodate a large amount of fans , up to 10 i think. Wish it was simpler, maybe just the board and that way i could hide it in the rear panel. Hub connects directly to the PSU via SATA power.
As far as sound. its great! Chuggs along pretty silently and you can manually adjust the fan speed [ as a whole ] with the remote. The ring led is nice at a distance or while in rainbow mode, static colors show where the LED is just cause the diffusor material isnt the greatest. Overall you cant go wrong with this. This wouldve been amazing for my first build years ago . There are better fan and hub sets out there, but none that give you as much bang for your buck as these.
reviews.author: Carlos Ortiz

reviews.title: Pricey but worth it.
reviews.comment:
I bought this for an NZXT Source 210 case. I am using it in one of the top fan mounts. I primarily bought this fan because the advanced bearing allows mounting in any orientation with no problems. I was also interested in quiet operation and longevity. You can buy quiet fans with fluid bearings for cheaper or about the same price but honestly, superior cooling with good engineering and reliability is worth the price to me. I keep my computers until they wear out (generally) so expensive fans are not a waste of money for me.
I love the cabling options. I have come to not be so fond of PWM fans and other methods of controlling fan speed. PWM doesn't always work right and it can be hard to get exactly the speed you want. With this Noctua, the low noise adapter was perfect. I cannot hear this fan over the other five fans in my case and it has brought every temperature reading I have down a few degrees.
Anyway, I connected this to a molex from my PSU with the low noise adapter. It's a good thing it came with this adapter because I don't have an open fan port on my motherboard anyway. I would have had to buy a splitter anyway.
In conclusion, as is it's reputation as a Noctua product, everything about this fan says quality. It feels like it's built to last. It's surprisingly heavy for a fan. The sleeving on the cables is high quality. I know I do not have to worry about this thing failing anytime soon.
reviews.author: Brian

reviews.title: Good fan, but still hums louder than I'd hoped.
reviews.comment:
Many good things can be said about this fan.  Since you can read those elsewhere, I will focus on my specific scenario.
I bought this fan to replace a Cougar CF-V14HB 140 mm fan.  That fan was purchased to replace the stock intake fan in my Lian Li case.  The stock fan was an LED fan, so I never even considered using it.
Anyway, everything I say here should be regarded with the caveat that the Cougar had less than 100 hours of use on it, and the Noctua is pretty much fresh out of the box.  It's possible that the Cougar might have quieted down after a longer break-in period, since most of its noise seemed to be coming from the motor or bearing.
I did a side-by-side comparison, and it was difficult for me to say which fan was louder (from distances between 0.1 to 0.5 meters).  I will say that the Cougar seemed to have more motor or bearing noise, whereas the Noctua seemed to be emitting more noise from its fan blades.  Also, the Cougar seemed slightly out-of-balance, when you hold it in your hand (with the power on).  Both fans were run at full 12V (i.e. without any attenuator) and have similar airflow specs.
While the amount of (upstream) noise was similar, I feel the character of the noise from the Noctua fan is more pleasant.  It's a soft, whooshy hum, whereas the Cougar seemed to have a bit more whine and buzz to it.  That sounds a bit harsh on the Cougar, which really isn't bad (especially when I got it at roughly half the price).  But it was noticeable enough that I decided to take a chance and see if the Noctua fan was better.  In hindsight, I'm not sorry I tried, but I don't think the improvement was worth the full price of the Noctua fan.  But if I were starting over from square one, I'd buy the Noctua without a second thought.
Finally, I just want to say that this fan is a little louder than I'd hoped.  Since I don't know if my expectations were reasonable, I'm not going to deduct a star.  Just be warned that this fan is definitely not silent, at full speed.  And I bought it to run at full speed, since I also upgraded the exhaust fan and want to maintain the ratio to preserve a positive pressure configuration.
reviews.author: Not My Real Name

reviews.title: Recently converted to the faithful
reviews.comment:
Yes, these fans are fugly, my advice is to get over it and look at the performance.  Noctua is a high performing fan and its whisper quiet, my rig's temps dropped by a full 11C after switching to 3 top mounted Noctua 120mm and a bottom 140mm compared to my previous fans' performance (and which were obnoxiously loud).  If I crank the rpms higher I can get another 1-3C temp drop and they're still significantly quieter than my previous "performance" fans.  Initially noise reduction is why I gave the Noctua a closer look, but after reading several critical reviews of their performance I decided to make the spend and see if it was worth it.  Placement of fan and deciding on how you want to set your air pressure/flow is of course a important part of it all, but I was quite literally surprised at how well these performed while being so very quiet in the process.
The fan came with silicon mounting pins which I decided not to use as I am more comfortable with simple machine screws, but the built in corner mounts do a great job of absorbing vibration all by themselves. reviews.title: Best fans on the market.
reviews.comment:
Have had these for nearly 1 1/2 years at the time of this review.  While high priced, you get what you paid for, functionally at least.  I have 4 of these fans in a large liquid cooled rig blowing over a 560mm radiator hooked up to a high end fan controller through a 4-pin specific fan hub.  At least with the right monitoring and control hardware along with a distributed heat dissipation setup, these fans can cover the range of silent operation to very good performance, better than anything else I have tried and I have tried a lot of different fans over time.  My preferred method of more precise control is to monitor coolant temp and adjust fan speed accordingly as CPU temp for example can jump around wildly without any real bearing on coolant temp, especially with such a large radiator holding down coolant temps pretty much no matter what and there are other components in the loop anyway.
Some key points to this fan are:
1. One of the best speed / static pressure to noise ratios of any fan on the market today.
2. Motor itself is dead quiet.  Only hear whooshing fan noise when revved up high.  Most any other PWM fans in this category on the market has an annoying motor whine, but this one uses a quite sine wave speed controller (converting the incoming PWM signal to a variable sine wave) and smooth 6 pole motor.
3. Out of several fans purchased, all still have perfect bearings, even after 1 1/2 years.  All competing fans I have tried in any volume have had at least one bad, noisy bearing in the batch, at least by this point.  Especially when doing arrays of fans on radiators, this has frustrated me as it is a bit of a PITA zeroing in on that bad fan, but with these no such thing has ever happened.
4. Fan can handle water and dust very well from what I hear.  I use HEPA filters to reduce dust in my operating environment and my liquid cooling setup has been leak free, so have not put these points to the real test yet.
5. Wide speed range.  I have run the gamut from 250 RPM, which is half of the rated minimum speed to 2,000 RPM and these fans have operated flawlessly throughout this range.
For optimal operation I have come up with the following (for my liquid cooled setup):
1. For a high powered system, distribute heat load across multiple fans so all can spin relatively slowly and quietly.
2. The fans are optimized for certain operational parameters around it.  Don't place directly up against restrictive intake grates.  Recess intake of fan away from restrictive grates if possible.  For radiators, only use fans on one side, do not do a push / pull combo.  All of these things seem to disrupt careful airflow modeling around the fan blades and cause turbulence, which leads to significant extra noise as the fans are revved up.  I at first tried push/pull with these fans, but found I get better cooling performance per unit of noise with the fans on just one side as I can rev up the fans a lot higher before I hear them now and even in the higher than I need range it is still a lot quieter.
3. For fan speed in a quiet room I would not try to go above 1,100 RPM on these fans as you start hearing them after this (unless your hearing is better than mine).  These fans are good enough to move quite a bit of air at this point so say two of these on a 280mm radiator for your 140W TDP CPU will probably do you well for example.  Even at 1,500 RPM on these fans is fairly OK sound level wise.  If say on a hot day you have a noisy window or wall mounted A/C, it may make sense to crank these up to much noisier ~1,800 RPM while under heavy load as they will probably still be quieter than a noisy A/C at this point and you may need this extra cooling capability anyway when it is particularly hot in the room.  (2,000 RPM will probably be heard over most window / wall mounted A/C units.)  With how I have things dialed in with the fan controller, if I ever hear the fans, it is either a fresh reboot or something is going wrong causing the temperature sensors to read abnormally high and thus the fan controller to compensate with higher than expected fan speeds before temps getting high enough to trigger an alarm and ultimately an automated emergency shutdown of the system.  Anyways at the full 2,000 RPM there is a strong wind coming off of these fans even through fan grates and a thick radiator (at least for me) which provides a sense of extreme overkill.
Maybe one thing to consider are the 1,500 RPM version of these fans as if you are using a crappy BIOS based fan controller that does not give you enough control of the speed range, you may find that going over 1,500 RPM is too annoying.  However with a quality fan controller, I don't see why it would matter beyond you will probably find yourself not actually using that extra capability or maybe the lower top speed fan comes with prettier vibration dampers around the mounting holes than the brown only option with these.

reviews.title: Love it
reviews.comment:
This fan comes in a box. In the box is the fan and four screws. That is it and it is all I needed.
The fan is a plain black fan which I like, but on the corners they put removable Noctua brown colored rubber vibration dampers. This little touch still lets people know this is a Noctua fan but you can easily remove them for an all black fan if you so choose.
I put this fan in the back of my Coolermaster HAF X and connected it to the fan 3 header on my Gigabyte G.1 Sniper 3 motherboard. I have the fan speed in the bios set to normal.
When the system is idle on the desktop and I stick my ear right up to it I can hear a tiny buzz sound, but only when my ear is right up to it. My PC sits on my desk and I don't hear it when sitting next to it.
When the system warms up and the fan speeds up I can then hear it move air but it is not annoying. When it speeds up it doesn't have any tick or weird annoying sounds.
Not all fans that other people seem to like sound good to me. For example, I tried some Cooler Master JetFlo 120 fans in a case because they were getting really good reviews. They looked like nice fans and seemed to be built well. It turned out that they sounded really annoying to me. They bothered me so much that I removed them and put other Noctua fans in the system. This fan has a minimal and unobtrusive sound to it like most other Noctua fans from my experience.
Typically if you want the good stuff you will need to pay for it. This fan costs a little more than your average fan but I think that it is worth it. It moves a good bit of air, it is generally quiet in my system, and when I do hear sound it doesn't make any stupid noises that would drive me nuts.
It has quality written all over it, an awesome warranty, and the company stands behind their products from what I have read. I wouldn't know though; none of my other 8 Noctua fans installed in my other PCs have ever given me a problem.
Overall a great fan that I wouldn't hesitate to recommend.

reviews.title: Its a tornado!
reviews.comment:
No user will or should use these at 100% RPM. It is unavoidably loud at that level, but given its full 2000RPM, it is expected. Perfect spot for me is up to 65% RPM, which up until that point every sound is cancelled due to my headset.
That being said, I have 3 of these installed as intake fans on my P600S case, and my current gig with Arctic Liquid Freezer II 280MM is keeping my I-7-7000 OC'd at 4.8ghz at idle 30 degrees Celsius while up to 65 degrees during CPU heavy games (Squad etc.). Currently my fan speed is set at 50% intake/exhaust at all points up until 70 degrees Celsius within the bios and have not crossed that threshold as of yet. My GPU stays cool at heavy loads barely crossing 80 degrees Celsius threshold as well. Albeit summer should put these numbers to test.
Overall, this is a product of fine engineering. Alternatives are available for sure, but given the warranty and the consistent RPM values, these fans are some of the best that is out there. If you are serious about keeping your system within ambient temperatures at any given season of the year, Noctua's are as reliable and trustworthy as it gets.
Oh Also, NO RGB, so... yeah!!!

Anything more expensive than this and it would be a waste of money in my opinion.  It is meant for four-pin connectors (PWM) on more modern motherboards, meaning it can be made to spin extremely slowly when appropriate - much slower than the older 3-pin standard (DC or TX3). reviews.title: High quality but still a little loud. Still I recommend them.
reviews.comment:
First off I bought a pair of these fans for two different projects. The first is for my Asus RT-AC5300 router which alone doesn't overheat, but in effort to make the router last a long as possible this fan does an awesome job dropping the CPU temp by 20-25F to right around 108F for the CPU. Second fan I used for my laptop which I have sitting under it to blow cool air through the intake duct.. The goal here again is to keep the PC as cool as possible as well preventing the builtin laptop from kick on (one less thing to replace down the road). For both of these project I used a NOYITO 5V USB speed controller (https://amzn.to/2KkZudL) so I could control the fan speed. What is interesting about this speed controller is that is offer more power to the fan on full speed then if I had the fan connected directly into the same usb port. You would think they will be the same.
As for cons, while the fans are on full speed they are loud. You can still have a normal conversation with them at 100% the sound carries from several rooms away. At 25% they are near silent, but I run them around 40-50% with is just enough to hear them but not annoying. Second the color is odd and I'm not a fan of them....I'm sure that is to make them unique.
In summary quality fans and I would recommend them.

reviews.comment:
Using 5 of them in a case with a Core i7 4770 and R9 380. Running off of molex (double-stacked), and the system stays impressively cool in a Zalman T7 case. Under full load in Aida64 (GPU+CPU combined) with a cheap $20 stack cooler, the CPU maxed out at 67 degrees and the GPU maxed at 73 degrees even with power limit set to +20% and a substantial overclock.
The fans definitely have some noise, and they aren't built to be silent. I have four Noctua SP-120's on a 240mm radiator in my primary gaming rig. But fans are fans, they move air, and they work "fan"-tastic.
If you need cheap fans, buy these, period. It's better value than spending $20/fan and you can squeeze a bit more out of your budget.

reviews.title: Excellent Fan!
reviews.comment: I used two of these 140mm industrial fans for perhaps a somewhat uncommon purpose.  I am using these fans as gable vent fans in my plastic 11'x11' storage shed.  My Lifetime shed has a vent built into each gable end.  I have a 50W solar roof panel connected to a charge controller and a 12v deep cycle battery, and this battery powers my two fans set in series, through a digital 12v thermostat.  I mounted the fans inside the shed directly in front of each gable vent opening, arranging them such that one fan (on the north shaded side of the shed) draws slightly cooler outside air into the shed, and the fan at the other end of the shed (on the hotter, sunnier south side) expels hot air inside the shed outward.  This push-pull arrangement seems to maximize air movement and cooling effect inside the shed.  These fans are super efficient, only drawing about 1/3 amp each.  They are very high RPM, efficient little air-movers, and they are surprisingly pretty quiet considering how fast they spin and move air.  I wasn't concerned about noise in my shed, but nevertheless, I was pleased with the relative low noise they produce.  With the weather-sealed bearing arrangement on these fans, I will have no concern about any dust or moisture effect in my outdoor setting.  My single 12v battery being charged by my one 50W solar panel is able to stay fully charged even when these fans run as much as 16-18 hours per day in the heat of the summer.  I love these fans!  They are super fast, super efficient, relatively quiet air-movers.

reviews.title: Whisper-Quiet, Powerful, and Built Like a Tank
reviews.comment: I picked up a couple of these MACH140 140mm fans to upgrade my PC’s cooling setup, and I’m seriously impressed with their performance. Performance & Airflow: These fans move a lot of air. The PWM control range (500–2200 RPM) is perfect — they’re silent when idling and ramp up smoothly under load. My CPU and GPU temps dropped by about 5–7°C after swapping out my old fans. Noise Level: Even at higher RPMs, they stay surprisingly quiet. The FOC motor design really minimizes vibration and hum I barely notice they’re running most of the time. Build Quality: The materials feel premium and durable. The LCP blades are sturdy and perfectly balanced, and the overall construction feels like something you’d find on a much more expensive fan. Ease of Installation: Standard 4-pin PWM connectors make setup simple. The cable length is generous, and I had no issues fitting them into my case (HAVN BF 360 Flow). Overall, these are top-tier fans for anyone who cares about both cooling performance and silence. Excellent airflow, premium quality, and smooth operation totally worth the price. I’ll definitely be buying more for my next build.

reviews.title: Amongst the best in class, with a caveat from a noise sensitive customer
reviews.comment: Fans are GREAT for enthusiasts who care about maxing out thermal performance with top ranked specs. Do your research on these fans, you'll find alot of the hardware testers like these. Fan noise is great, and as long as you know how to manage fan curves you should be good. For my Ryzen 9900x + 360mm aio, I don't need to run them above 1300 RPM. As far as temperatures go, my temps dropped around 2 degrees compared to average static pressure fans. BUT, and this may be a nitpick coming from someone who is very sensitive to noise - I also mainly build "silent" PCs - there is a slight coil whine at lower RPMS - mainly 650 RPM and below. It's not audible through a glass panel, but those with mesh panels might hear it from a few feet away. Otherwise, these are the BEST black/gray fans you can get for around 70 bucks. Figure out if you have clearance for 30 mil thick fans. Figure out if you can deal with that coil whine or not, or spend about 30$-40$ extra for Phanteks T30 or Noctua G2.

reviews.title: Silent, efficient, and plain sexy
reviews.comment:
I never thought I’d have much to say about a computer case fan, but the Noctua fan completely changed my perspective. The build quality is incredible—everything from the sturdy plastic to the thoughtful design exudes top-notch craftsmanship. The fan geometry is ultra-quiet and ultra-efficient, even at high speeds, delivering performance far beyond expectations.
The inclusion of rubber gaskets and the innovative rubber nodules for tool-free installation make mounting the fan an absolute breeze. Noctua clearly understands its customers’ needs, even providing adapters for older systems, ensuring compatibility and extending the fan's utility.
And then there’s the simplicity of the colors. The plain tans and earth tones don’t scream for attention—they’re understated and confident, almost as if the fan is saying, "I don’t need to look pretty. I know who I am, and I am a badass fan."
Even the packaging stands out—it’s immaculate and clearly designed with care, making the entire experience feel premium from start to finish. I can confidently say this fan sets a new standard for quality, efficiency, and quiet operation. I don’t see myself purchasing any other brand of computer fan in the future.

reviews.title: 120mm Mounting Pattern on ‘r’ designated variation
reviews.comment:
I’ve been waiting on the release of the 140mm x25 fan, this version features a 120mm mounting pattern, these variations are designated with an ‘r’, and have a round frame style, and are purpose designed as 140mm fans with 120mm screw placement. The traditional square frame version (non-r), which will have a 140mm mounting pattern, has not been released at the time of this review. Scheduled for September 2024.
That said, I really wanted to mount these fans on a 280mm radiator. Fortunately, Noctua makes a mounting adapter that, with a little modification (a rough trim with aviation snips), can be cut down to the corner pieces, providing the perfect fit for 140mm mounting points. I’m sure a neater job could have been accomplished with a rotary tool, or even 3D Printing. But for ~$13 adapters, they were cheap enough to just modify.
I’ve attached a photo showing the NF-A14x25r on a 280mm radiator, alongside another photo with the 120mm Square brethren, the NF-A12x25 for comparison Side-by-side. And the final put together radiator with semi-DIY adapters.

reviews.title: Solid 140mm ARGB fans
reviews.comment: I bought a 3-pack because these 140mm fans are the exact same model used on the large Liquid Freezer III 420mm radiator. Now the top and bottom fans in my case match. PROs: They're daisy-chainable so you don't need a ton of fan and A-RGB headers on your motherboard. The colors are pretty good and they're very quiet at low to mid RPMs. Also I think Arctic might be the only brand offering a 6-year warranty on all their products (most other brands only cover 2-3 years) so I expect them to last. CONs: The connections for chaining them are closer to the far end of the cables, which could make chaining them a little challenging in some situations. If you arrange these adjacently then it would make more sense to connect right by the fan body itself. Some others (e.g. Lian Li)  even snap together directly but these don't. Also they don't make a reverse version, so I had to install these upside down. They don't look as good as they could because now the supports are visible, as well as the 12 LEDs that run along the back inner circumference of each fan. There are no LEDs elsewhere like fancier fans, so it's just the translucent blades that illuminate. Note: Don't over-tighten the screws, or the blades might scrape on the mounting bracket or case housing. That's true for any large fans though if you warp the frame slightly.

reviews.title: Showy fan for an air-cooled system
reviews.comment: I installed these into my ever-changing review system to see how they fit, sounded, looked, and of course cooled. As these were my first time using "chained" fans, I was interested in seeing if that made any difference.  My normal motherboard has enough fan headers for individual control, but in this configuration they would be wired in series, controlled together. My final verdict, at least with these fans, is that it made little difference to cooling or noise - It did make cable running nicer and neater however.  So it seems like I would give this a thumbs-up.  If you do zoned cooling however, you wouldn't want this kind of configuration. The fans look nice enough, but I'm not really an RGB kind of system builder, so I'll leave the subjective look to others for review.  On the semi-objective side, I would call these "showy" - bright and hard to ignore.  If you like that, then they might be good for you. As air-movers, they seemed average - at low speed generating some air movement, and higher speeds of course moving more air, and of course generating more noise.  I wouldn't call the noise levels high at any speed, and there wasn't any objectionable spike at any frequency, just some white-noise of the air and the fans.  You will notice however when they ramp it up. CFM is fine for an air-cooled system of reasonable volume case but not really enough to use these with a radiator - you want more than 4mm H2O on the static pressure to push air through a radiator.  If you're an extreme OC kind of builder, these probably aren't your first choice fans anyway.  For the average mid-tier DIY build for air-cooling, these fans give some flash and aren't budget breaking.

While QD OLED is embarrassing in comparison. The screen is actually cleanable!!!!!! QD OLEDs screens are just awful with cleaning. Glossy coats on monitors are just terrible. Following the manufacturers guidelines in cleaning won't prevent scratches. But here, with LG, yea you won't even see a scratch!!! Matte finish... where do I start. First you can't even see the matte finish, it's not the same matte finish you see on other gaming monitors. It's borderline glossy, but much better than glossy. It won't take away from the game, it doesn't make the image look fuzzy what so ever. And again note here that I have BOTH panels!! This one embarrasses QD OLED and it was cheaper?!!! Brightness, and color. This monitor will show realistic colors and the true blacks will blow you away in contrast. On QD OLED, colors are far to vivid making it look over saturated even with calibration!!! WOLED, never had this issue and has the correct and accurate colors even out of the box which is insane! The brightness is good here, it's Oled so your not going to get insane 2000 nits but your definitely getting an upgrade from QD OLED, VA, IPS, or TN. All in all amazing monitor, don't listen to Reddit, get one your self and see! A great idea is to go to Best Buy and see them side by side and you'll realize how much better WOLED is. 5 amazing stars wish I could give it more.

reviews.title: Great for Stationary and Travel Use
reviews.comment:
I recently replaced my old MacBook Pro with a new Mac Mini M4 Pro as my main workstation.  I already had an external UHD monitor connected to that laptop, so I needed a small monitor to replace the 16" one that was built in to that laptop.  Not only is this monitor perfect for my use, but the touchscreen capability is a bonus!  The glass panel and thin bezels look great and the monitor is the perfect size to replace the screen I had before.  I wasn't expecting the touchscreen function to work with my Mac but it does.  If this were the only monitor connected to my Mac, it would work completely as expected for single-taps, but when the Mac has multiple monitors and is set to "extend" across monitors, the touchscreen function works as expected but only when the cursor is already on this 16" monitor.  I can accept that because everything else is great - especially for the price.  This monitor is also great for use as a temporary or mobile monitor for my iPhone and iPad.  The touchscreen functions don't work with them, but this is still a great 16" screen for my phone and tablet.  Another surprise is that the monitor's built-in menu system works with the touchscreen function so you don't have to mess around with funky button combinations to adjust its brightness or volume settings.
This screen also has built-in speakers that aren't too bad, and works with HDR on my Mac mini and looks great when used in combination with my other external UHD monitor.
The multi-position kickstand supports the screen well even when poking at it with your fingers, and stores discretely when not needed.  One of the few small suggested improvements would be to add rubber "feet" closer to the middle edge of the screen to support using the monitor on narrower surfaces like small tray tables on a plane or train, etc...
This screen also comes with a neoprene sleeve for travel and storage.  While it works as intended, I would have liked a folio-style case that remains attached to the screen a little better.  Not a deal-breaker as I don't plan on traveling much with this screen and when I do, the included sleeve will provide good protection.  It's just not as convenient as an attached folio-style would have been.
BTW, a ton of cables were included for nearly all connection scenarios.  A USB power adapter was also supplied if needed to power the screen separately.
Overall, a great screen and a great value!

reviews.comment: PhD student here so spend A LOT of time needing multiple screens for research and the ability to see with clarity and ease. I also need a screen that is easy to fit in my book bag for easy transport. I've been incredibly happy with the CAPERAVE touchscreen monitor on all counts. My eyes are tired from the reading so I like the resolution as well as the ability to dim and brighten with ease. Additionally, I have a Microsoft Surface Pro, Mac laptop , and HP laptop to use depending on if I'm working from home or the office. reviews.title: Genuinely useful second screen if your setup supports it
reviews.comment:
I bought this portable touchscreen monitor a while back and I’m still using it regularly, which says a lot because most tech “helpers” end up in a drawer. For my everyday laptop setup it’s been a solid upgrade. The 15.6 inch size is the sweet spot where it actually feels like a real second screen, but it’s still easy to toss in a bag. The picture is crisp for 1080p, viewing angles are good, and the touchscreen is more than a gimmick. It’s great for quick taps, scrolling, and basic controls when you’re working with multiple windows.
The biggest thing I’d tell anyone is to use the cables that come in the box. That sounds obvious, but it matters here. I tried using a couple of my own USB C cables and an older HDMI cable and that’s when I saw little issues like the screen not waking properly or the connection acting finicky. Switching back to the included wires fixed it immediately and it’s been reliable since.
What really makes this worth it for me is that if you set it up correctly, you usually don’t need an extra power source. In the right setup it can run off your main device power, so you’re not dragging around another brick or hunting for an outlet. That keeps everything clean and portable, especially when you're on the go. When it’s working that way, it feels like the monitor is just an extension of your laptop instead of another device you have to babysit.
I wouldn’t say it’s a perfect fit for every situation, because it depends on what you’re plugging it into and what your ports support, but for the way I use it it’s been genuinely useful and absolutely worth the money. If you want a portable second screen that you’ll actually keep using, this one does the job.

reviews.title: Good gaming monitor with some downsides but at an excellent price.
reviews.comment:
Purchased on: April 19, 2021 and reviewed as of January 17, 2023.
I tend to look at Asus more favorably because of my good experience with the brand so I ended up buying this monitor after reading Rtings' review on this model. (if you are interested in a very technical and more in depth review, I would suggest to look them up)
The quality it offers for the price is great. I didn't have any issues with dead pixels, packaging was great and it arrived in good condition, the color profile looks great and very accurate (although I don't have the measuring tools to make this claim from a creative standpoint). The VESA mounting screw holes are well positioned in a way that you should be able to use any VESA plate. (this is important to consider as other models, like my other monitor, which has a square hole for the entire plate and it is a little to small to fit most VESA mounts despite having accurate screw holes)
For general media consumption and gaming, this is an incredible monitor. In general, I would say I could never go back to using a standard widescreen for a PC. Ultrawide is a massive upgrade with the extra screen size. The resolution this monitor offers is great too as the text looks clean and it isn't as resource taxing as a 4K monitor would be. I would say this monitor is a great entry point for anyone considering an ultrawide screen. Black uniformity looks good in my opinion despite the lack of any dimming zones.
Another great feature that it has is the 4 USB hub right underneath (USB 3.2 type A). Although I wouldn't use it for a keyboard and mouse if you are a serious gamer, it is very useful for other things such as charging your devices, plugging in an RGB strip so you can use it as a backlight, external storage or any other accessories or USB drives. (In addition to those, it has 2 Display ports, 2 HDMI 2.0 ports and a 3.5 headphone jack)
On the other hand, there are a few things to keep in mind. You will not be able to use 10bit colors with the 165hz this monitor supports at the same time. If you go for 165hz, you will be limited to 8bit colors. However, if you are okay with 144hz, you can enable the full 10bit colors range.
Another thing often criticized about this monitor is the slight smearing sometimes appearing in dark scenes where you might see the trails of a red/greenish pixels turning as a brighter object moves. This can be somewhat mitigated with overdrive settings. Unfortunately, this is more of a VA panel common issue than anything else and your best option if you really can't stand it is to go for an IPS or OLED panel at much higher cost.
Overall, I would say this is a good quality product and I would highly recommend it. I can't speak much about the stand as I use a monitor arm and, I would suggest everyone to use one as well due to the flexibility and movement it offers on top of making your setup much cleaner.

reviews.comment: At ~$350 this is a great price for such a quality monitor. It's high framerate at 165hz, HDR content looks vibrant, and g-sync/freesync makes for a butter smooth image during gaming. I struggle to think of any negatives about this monitor, aside from maybe the shock of unboxing and realizing just how wide the stand is. Make sure you have the desk space!
reviews.author: Mit

reviews.title: Great widescreen VA panel
reviews.comment:
Coming from a 24" 60hz IPS display, this is a huge step up.  The unit I received has very even lighting and no dead pixels.
I had heard complaints about purple/green ghosting on this panel when the overdrive setting is turned up, but I can't detect any ghosting regardless of what settings I use of what game I load up.  I did have some flickering with freesync turned on, so I turned it off, but I was using old display drivers.  I've since updated the drivers and turned it back on, and haven't seen any flickering since then (we'll see).  Please note that the freesync issues reportedly seem to be more of an issue for those with NVIDIA graphics cards (I am using an AMD product).
Aside from minor freesync issues, any negatives I can attribute to this display have mostly to do with the slightly different character of the image and colors as the result of the VA panel when compared to IPS.  Personally, I use this screen in a dark-ish room, and am more sensitive to glare than most people, so the excessive brightness and backlight bleed from IPS panels bothers me a whole lot more than any of the quirks of VA panels (which again, are minimal here).  This is ultimately a matter of taste regarding differences in display technology.
I also hated the physical styling of all of the "gaming screens" that look like they were designed by kids.  The styling on this monitor is VERY toned down, and you wouldn't know it was marketed as a gaming display by looking at it.  This was important to me.
I was cross shopping this with the Gigabyte W34WQC (curved VA version), and the LG 34WP65C, both of which are cheaper, but reviews seem to indicate that these panels have more QC and image quality issues than this Asus.
Once IPS local dimming and/or OLED become more ubiquitous, I may upgrade.  However, that's highly dependent on price, and I don't feel like the immature implementations of these technologies are currently worth the price premium (~2x the cost).  There's nothing wrong with old tech as long as the implementation is good quality, as is the case with this display.
This is a good quality VA widescreen display at a great price, if that's what you're after then this should be an easy decision.  I am rating this 4/5 only because of the speakers, and freesync issues.

reviews.title: A Massive Productivity Upgrade for Any Laptop Setup
reviews.comment: I honestly cannot recommend the Lenovo L15 Portable Monitor enough. This thing completely changed the way I work and travel.
