It genuinely feels like having a second workstation that can go anywhere with you. The display quality is surprisingly sharp and clean for a portable monitor. Colors look great, text is crisp, and the brightness is honestly better than I expected. Even in brighter rooms or during daytime use, the screen remains very clear and comfortable to look at. I also appreciate how easy it is on the eyes during long work sessions. Whether I’m studying, multitasking, monitoring applications, or watching videos, the screen always feels smooth and high quality. One of the biggest advantages is how much productivity this adds. Having a second screen dramatically improves workflow efficiency and organization. Instead of constantly alt-tabbing between windows, I can keep documents, research tabs, monitoring software, emails, spreadsheets, or videos open separately. Once you get used to dual-screen productivity, it’s honestly hard to go back to a single monitor setup. Setup is also incredibly simple. The USB-C connectivity makes it basically plug-and-play with modern laptops, and the cable management stays very clean and minimal. No complicated setup process, no extra clutter — just connect it and instantly expand your workspace. I also really love the built-in stand design. It feels surprisingly sturdy and stable for how thin the monitor is. A lot of portable monitors can feel flimsy or shaky, but this one actually feels solid and well-engineered when sitting on a desk or table. The viewing angles and adjustability are excellent too, making it easy to position exactly how you want it whether you’re at home, in a hotel, office, coffee shop, or traveling. Another thing I appreciate is the professional aesthetic. It has that clean Lenovo design language that matches modern laptops perfectly and gives off a very organized, efficient “mobile workstation” vibe. It genuinely feels like a serious productivity tool instead of just a cheap accessory. For long work sessions, this monitor is a game changer. It helps reduce mental clutter, improves focus, and makes multitasking feel significantly smoother and more natural. Whether you work in IT, business, school, finance, engineering, content creation, or simply want a more efficient setup, this monitor delivers extremely well. Overall, the Lenovo L15 Portable Monitor feels premium, reliable, bright, stable, and incredibly practical. reviews.title: Great build quality!
reviews.comment:
This dual 18"m 2K (2.5K) monitor is superb.  I initially paired it with an older Surface Pro 6 and was not able to get it into Extend mode like a wanted.  This was due to limitations of the Surface Dock video controller.  I ultimately paired it with a Surface Pro 10 and it works perfectly in all display modes.  I am also using a single Anker 130W Charger to power the Monitor and Surface.  The display draws 21W at 100Hz, full 2560x1600 resolution, and 100% brightness.  I have not been able to power the monitor through a single USB-C cable from the surface so separate USB-C is needed for display power (not unexpected).  I am also able to power the monitor and laptop using a Baseus 100W, 20AHr Power Bank which shows is using 34W which suggest that the video USB is providing about 14W of power.  On this Power Bank it reports that it will las about 2 hours.  The monitor refresh rate does not have a big impact on power draw, but the brightness has an almost proportional impact on power.
The kickstand is very versatile, and the monitor is very secure in any configuration.  Even standing stacked vertically they are stable.  The folding hinge is smooth but firm, there is little change of it slipping; perhaps after a few years they may start loosening but that remains to be seen.
The screens are large, bright, and crisp.  While 4K might be better for photo/video editing, these are perfect for normal business use and CAD work as I intend to use them.  I bought a separate single 4K monitor for photo work.  Out of the box the color/contrast closely match my Surface (at default settings); I did bump the monitor brightness up from the default 80% to 100% for a perfect match.
I found a 17.3" Monitor Sleeve from CaseDeer that fits like a bespoke case.  The monitor in the sleeve and my Surface drops perfectly into the laptop compartment of my TUMI fold-top backpack.
reviews.author: JJacobs

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.comment:
I bought a competing industrial/portable dual display from another OEM last month, it was okay - but plagued with sleep mode issues, not supporting MST USB C on my intel chipset - and was only 1080p
This 4K innoview has impressed me within 10 minutes
1. Immediately enabled both independent displays with a single USB cable (and of course separate USB power) to my Intel 275HX integrated graphics, streaming 2x 4k signals over one USB C so seamless means the hardware and firmware guys got this right
2. Screens are sharp with good color settings out of box
3. Built-in menu is solid, gamer crosshairs are cute addition - but this is not a gaming monitor
4. These are solid IPS displays, brightness is great even in a well lit room (power meter on my USB power bank says 60W power draw)
5. sleep mode and waking works great and OST has a black background for its power notification (competitor had a 10 second full screen blue background sleep mode status, which was jarring)
I will update this review when I test more of the features, HDR did not impress me immediately - will likely need to try the other HDR modes, not worried as SDR is brilliant here - and HDR is really for OLEDs or other technologies with better backlight control
Only negative: Included display cables are short, luckily I have my own - but at this price point, 5-6ft should he standard
I also have an innoview 2k 180hz 24in which shares a lot of DNA with this, also very good
Someday I hope to learn the origin and story about where these displays come from and how brands package them differently, they are very cool - and Innoview has impressed with their implementations
Unrelated feedback: Innoview website needs an update, I know these models change quickly - would be cool to see upcoming model previews, and see more detailed specs
reviews.author: JJB

reviews.title: Fantastic dual monitor for portable and travel productivity
reviews.comment:
As someone who works behind a laptop the majority of the day, multiple monitors are a must to staying productive at home or away from home. I have been looking for a solution that would maximize viewable space/resolution in as compact as a package as possible.
As a result, I decided to pick up the InnoView 15.6" Portable 4K Dual Monitor for a number of reasons
- viewable space (dual 15.6 monitors), resolution (4k)
- size/weight (folded, it is comparable to my Macbook Air 15 in in footprint and weight ~3.5 lbs)
- build quality (the monitor is feels very solid and well-made)
- connectivity (HDMI, usb-c, DP2.0)
The monitor came with various cables for connectivity and power (included a power brick). It felt solid all around from the hinges, to the adjustable stand, and to the cable connections. The monitor feels very solid in hand and has good weight. Once the monitor is set-up, it holds form and angles very well. The monitor is best used in landscape mode, although it can be used in portrait if needed. In portrait mode, you won't have as many viewing options. Also, you'll have to consider the connectivity ports and cables connected.
I am using with my Macbook M4 air, which will natively support multiple external monitors. I believe an M1 or M2 would need an external dock/adapter to support multiple external monitors, so  you would need one with an older Mac to use this monitor in a muti-external monitor set-up.
For my set-up, the M4 works very well. Connectivity is straight forward, and I used a usb-c and HDMI (usb-c-HDMI cable) to the InnoView. Luckily, with the Macbook, you will still be able to power via Magasafe connector. The monitor connected perfectly, and I was able to utilize 4k 60hz refresh rates for both monitors. Picture was clear, accurate, and vibrant. From a productivity standpoint, you can use this in multi-monitor or single monitor mode. Single monitor mode allows you to create one single large monitor.
You can power this from the provided power supply, an OEM, or if needed a power bank that can output 30W+. The powerbank option is great for working in an airport lounge or coffee shop. The only challenge with my setup has been a clean cable setup, as you are connecting two video sources and a power supply to the monitor and laptop.
I've been able to use this with my work and home macbooks without issues as well as phones (android, ios).I do hope to try testing with a windows machine.
Overall, great productivity device, well-made, and versatile. The only downside was cable management (which isn't  really the monitor's fault).

reviews.title: UPerfect Monitor is the Perfect monitor for U and Me!
reviews.comment: I tested several products before trying out this UPERFECT 4K Portable Monitor.  I even ended up returning 3 of them because they weren't satisfactory (other monitors).  For me, quality is the most important for me.  I'm the type of person that enjoys good sound and good visuals.  As you can see in my setup, I have a gaming PC attached to a wide screen monitor, a 4k OLED monitor, and the 17.3" UPERFECT monitor at the base of the two other monitors.  I wanted something matte, something with Apple-like retina display, something bright and something large enough.  The screen size was perfect.  It was easy to set up and connected without any issues.  I did have one super minor issue with the power plug; it was making a slight humming noise but works perfectly fine.  Still, I'm a bit of a perfectionist.  I emailed the customer support that was listed on their card/website and they got right back to me and offered to ship me a new power plug.  Again, the monitor works perfectly!  I was so happy with the product, that I ordered a different UPERFECT 17.5" monitor for my office.  This company's products are great as well as their customer service.  I'll look here first to buy monitors before other brands!
reviews.author: J. Lee

reviews.title: Great portable monitor, top notch customer service
reviews.comment: This is a fantastic 1080p monitor that gives you options to power it using a single USB-C cable connected to your laptop to deliver power and data or use an additional USB-C cable through an outlet to solely deliver power.  If you opt for the former, the monitor will be dimmer since the single USB-C cable is providing power and data, so your best experience is definitely going to be when you have the second USB-C cable to deliver power. The monitor itself is lightweight so it's quite easy to carry it around (recommend you use a case) and even fit in a backpack along with your laptop to take it with you on the go.  The stand is built-in, so it gives you a quick and easy way to stand the monitor up for it to be used.  With all this, the build quality on this is very good. For the monitor performance, the color and brightness representation is great for a portable monitor and text was mostly easy to read, with the exceptions of some Webex meetings that involved very tiny text which is just the nature of a 1080p monitor for which their 4k monitors would address. There is a myriad of settings you can play around with whether that's contrast, brightness, enabling other modes to get the monitor to display to your preference. Also, I want to call out the quick responsive customer service.  I did have an intermittent issue that caused the screen to go black and flicker, so I reached out to them via email.  They responded within a few hours, and I was able to work with them on some basic troubleshooting.  After the basic troubleshooting didn't work out, they made it right very quickly by just offering to send me replacement and avoid all the remaining hoops of troubleshooting.  I got the replacement in just a couple of days, and it's been working great for me since. The product is great and the customer service is top notch, and I would have no hesitation buying from this brand again as they stand behind their products.
reviews.author: Christopher H.

reviews.title: UPERFECT Almost Perfect, However a Good Portable Monitor.
reviews.comment: I like this monitor for having a normal HDMI and not just a HDMI mini, it's slim and very portable! Thing is it doesn't have a case, I didn't know I could get a free case until the company messaged me about how I like my product, they pointed me in the direction to get a free case by emailing the customer support email on the back of the instructions of the product and gave me a PDF version in the message for my convenience which was nice, after emailing the support email, I got a response quickly about how to get my free case, which is to provide an address, and in addition to the free case as a separate offer in the same email, to be in their VIP club to try out other products. I declined the second offer as I have too much stuff already that I don't want to add to the pile, and expressed that I am only interested in the free case. There was no response after that until about two days and I was told that they had a weekend that they came back from. It was a little misleading as the page the email was listed on said it was 24hrs, (picture in this review), immediately they said they sent the free case that will come within two days and apologized for not responding sooner because of their weekend, so that was nice. I gave this product 4 stars because of the little bit of a hassle to get the free case, if you're going to have a free case, just include it in the product box! The other monitor I had and returned from a different company had a free case included and I liked that, I returned the other monitor because it only had HDMI mini and it advertised that it had HDMI not specifying mini only! The monitor from UPERFECT, when I first turned it on had a brighter spot on it near the top right, but quickly paned out as I played my game. (It was probably cases by the monitor before shipping being stored in a position not natural for the screen to handle before turning it on). The sound is fair, it does have a headphone jack, I just let the sound come from the monitor's speakers when playing my game. Over all I feel it's a good purchase and great for a gaming personal space!
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Great monitor, great size
reviews.comment: This is a great monitor, nice way to compliment my work environment and my wife's work environment, working hybrid this is great I can take the monitor to work where I don't have an office, just a desk and I can set this up as a secondary monitor at the office, and then when I get home, if I don't want to lug the monitor from the basement to the main floor, I can easily set this up. Depending on the laptop it can be powered by a single USB-C cable, but most of the time, this will need an external power. With the 2 included USB-C cables, I was able to easily power the monitor with my laptop, and if you don't have USB-C ports, you can use the included power adapter, which you would need anyway if you are using the mini HDMI to HDMI. I like the kickstand so much better than the smart screen covers that flip over backwards, most of the time those slip and the monitor falls. I do wish this had a standard HDMI port with the size of the monitor so you didn't have to carry a special cable with you. This has a great picture and it is a great travel addition.
reviews.author: Computer Doc

reviews.title: Confirmed! It's the NEW 280Hz REVISION
reviews.comment: This is a total Win-Win! I was a bit skeptical because the Amazon description still mentions 240Hz, but I can confirm that I received the New Revision (V2) which hits a native 280Hz. If you are looking for the updated AG276QZD2, this is the one that fixes the minor issues from the previous batches. ​Key highlights from my experience: ​Stunning Image Quality: As a UX/UI designer, the QHD resolution combined with the QD-OLED panel offers a depth of blacks and color accuracy that is second to none. The resolution and clarity are simply beautiful. ​No "Washed Out" HDR: This new revision comes with the updated firmware, and the HDR performance is spot on—no more dull or greyish tones where there should be pure black. ​Extreme Speed: Connected to my laptop with an RTX 5070 Ti, the 280Hz fluidity is out of this world. ​Shipping to Colombia: It arrived in Bogotá earlier than expected and in perfect condition. ​If your box arrives marked with the 280Hz logo, you’ve won the panel lottery. It is a professional-grade work tool and an absolute beast for gaming. Highly recommended!
reviews.author: Felipe Londoño

reviews.title: Great monitor
reviews.comment: Honestly was very hesitant dropping 500 clams on a monitor but I was tired of my 1080p ips panel. Aoc puts the calibration report in the box so you know what your monitors color accuracy and everything is. The stand is solid but doesn't give crazy positioning options. The panel has great brightness and good io, also the RGB on the back is subtle and a nice touch without being distracting and has a nice diffusion layer. The 1440p resolution is great at this size coupled with it being an oled panel the contrast is just fantastic. You do need to go into a couple of games that you play and tweak the settings for the best visuals. I've heard but not tested the HDR of the monitor is supposedly lacking as I said I just leave HDR off and tweak my panels settings to preference with the games I play and then go into YouTube videos and give final adjustments to give myself the best average. It has nice quality of life settings to keep the oled burn in at a minimum and overall I am very happy with this monitor. I can't take advantage of the full refresh rate at higher settings on some games (specifically ue5). But it's a great buy especially if you wanna squeeze all the performance out of your gpu before you commit to upgrading it. To get the full refresh rate.
reviews.author: Bryce

reviews.title: Good gaming monitor
reviews.comment: Very good for the price for gaming, and pretty much ONLY gaming. Playing Street Fighter 6 or an FPS of some kind, it's a godsend. Bright, fast, smooth, nice blacks and nice colors (AFTER messing with the settings -- by default for me at least everything was pretty washed out). Fast and smooth being the reasons you're going to buy this. For everything else... it's not great. Color settings take some dialing in, the OLED need to run the refresh routine every couple hours is annoying, and text fringing is vaguely noticeable. I ONLY turn it on for gaming or situations where I really need a second monitor for something. Otherwise I keep it off.
reviews.author: Austin Yun

reviews.title: Perfect Monitor
reviews.comment: Underrated solid monitor. If you’re looking to upgrade to an oled or 1440p I would buy this one. Great price for a 1440p 240hz oled. Amazing contrast, no fuzzy text unlike Woled. Nice set of settings. Comes with hdmi and display port cables, great  fully adjustable stand etc. don’t waste your money on the same features for other brand names. And 4 year warranty if you’re worried. I bought it one sale for $400 which is honestly completely worth it for this monitor. I use it for pc and ps5, it’s the perfect monitor for ps5 does 1440p 120hz hdr gaming and 4k 60hz also hdr when on YouTube, Netflix etc. it switches between 4k and 1440p automatically so just leave it at 4k. No vrr but I don’t have any issues and no flicker so far. It also has speakers but they’re bare minimum if you don’t mind bad quality and just plain sound it’s a bonus. You get used to the sound so I’d say it’s a plus overall for budget gamers. For most people this would be the perfect monitor.
reviews.author: Jake Solorzano

reviews.title: THIS MONITOR IS STUNNING
reviews.comment: I was hesitant about OLED with some users reporting eye strain. But the colors and HDR on this monitor make games like Doom Eternal full on eye candy. This monitor feels great for Valorant and Delta Force. Curious to see how the warrant program stacks up however. I would definitely buy this monitor again. The glossy finish looks premium OSD is simple and quick to learn Brightness peaks around 240nits but thats all I need. HDR is stunning Im sure its better with mini led monitors due to higher peak brightness, but I'm more than satisfied with this monitor. The stand is great it doesn't take up too much desk space can comfortable game with 19"x15" mousepad. This monitor is also priced perfectly for its worth around the $600usd mark. Sure there are 360hz qd oled panels out there, but you cant make use of it unless you have a beefy pc. My build has a 5900x and 3080 ti and i can run 240 hz most games. Great value monitor. This monitor made me a firm believer in OLED. This monitor is factory color calibrated also.\ Edit: Download AOC G menu and make it easier on yourself to adjust brightness and color settings to your liking.
reviews.author: Jose Ed Gonzalez

reviews.title: Gawfolk GF320M 32 Inch 4K UHD Curved 1500R Computer Monitor, Ultra-Clear (3840×2160p), USD 189.99
reviews.comment:
Gawfolk GF320M 32 Inch 4K UHD Curved 1500R Computer Monitor, Ultra-Clear (3840×2160p), USD 189.99:
This is the best screen I’ve ever used for office work. Perfect resolution. Huge real state. It shows photos taken with high-end mobile phones with crystal-crisp details, when reviewing vacations pictures it feels like being there again. Curve is noticeable.
When used at 4K (3840×2160p) and 100% Windows display scale the ribbon’s icons and menu fonts in Word and Excel appear quite small… just as I love them! Naturally, you can zoom at your taste the size of documents and webpages, or change the display resolution, or change the display scale.
I cannot speak about its performance on games, not interested in them.
reviews.author: LW

reviews.title: Pretty good budget productivity monitor
reviews.comment:
I bought this to be my central monitor for my home office setup. I do coding and automation workflow development and need a lot of pixels and my 50-year-old eyes need those pixels to be not super dense so I can actually read what's on the screen. 32" 4k for me is the sweet spot. I also find that at this size curvature becomes important so you don't have to turn your head as much to see what's at the edges. Unfortunately 32" 4k *curved* monitors tend to be mostly aimed at the gaming market, with high refresh rates, RGB lighting, and other doodads that add no value for a productivity setup but add a lot of cost. I finally found this one and despite being a no-name brand I took the plunge and have been pleased so far.
The picture is good and the color matches my other monitors well without any tweaking, though your mileage may vary.
The curvature is just right. Subtle but definitely helpful, and it helps prevent screen glare.
The stand the the monitor comes with seems a bit... not flimsy exactly but not well-constructed either. Also it does not afford any adjustability whatsoever. Furthermore it leaves the screen fairly low to the desk and tilted slightly forward, which really is not ideal for ergonomics unless you use it leaning back in a reclined chair, which for me at least isn't how I work.
But I was planning to mount the monitor on an arm to keep my desktop uncluttered, so the stand was not a concern for me. However, what I discovered is the VESA mounting holes are too shallow for the screws I had on hand (including the screws that came with the monitor for mounting the stand). I was able to shim them with washers but I feel this could have been handled better with design.
reviews.author: Jay C Boal

reviews.title: Flickering overheating mess
reviews.comment: Received it with a flickering middle part of the screen, damaged and it grows extremely hot to the touch during use. The color accuracy was fine around the broken part.
reviews.author: M

reviews.title: Perfect for Gaming and Graphic Design!
reviews.comment:
I’ve never owned a 4K display before.  I was in the middle of moving, and found this one for a steal.  I was hesitant at first, but I made the purchase.
This display is perfection!  I’ve got my PS5 and my MacBook hooked up to that screen in 4K.
Don’t freak out if the box you get looks beat up.  My monitor was securely packaged with lots of foam from the seller.  But then it was shoved in a bigger, empty box.  That box got shredded in transport, and I was immediately worried that there would be damage to my display.
My worries were unfounded.  That screen is BEAUTIFUL!!!  And, it arrived in perfect condition.  No dead pixels.  That thing was wrapped tightly.  Even though it was tossed inside an additional box, and jostled around for no reason, the seller’s packaging was exemplary.
The 34”, 4K display is perfect for gaming.  Marathon looks amazing!  I also downloaded Starfield just to see how it looked.
This display exceeded my expectations by miles from the minute go!
I cannot recommend this product enough!!!
reviews.author: Joel

reviews.title: A great monitor.  Perfect if using the stand.  A little less if you want to mount them.
reviews.comment: These (I got 2) were a great find.  Priced accordingly, nice curvature.  I like that it has 2 HDMI and 2 DP ports for input.  I wish the cable provided was HDMI and not DP, but something's better than nothing.  The stand is metal and stiff and unyielding.  The refresh rate is good enough for working (I haven't tested movies on it yet). The screen is nice and bright too.  My only gripe is the VESA holes.  They're VERY shallow.  I had to cut rubber tubes to makeshift the padding to get a good grip. Not heavy.  The packaging was also nicely done, with the Styrofoam contouring to the curve of the screen.  I'm going to keep the boxes for transport in the future.
reviews.author: Antonio R.

reviews.title: Is This 200Hz Monitor Worth It? My Honest Review 👀
reviews.comment: This 24-inch 200Hz gaming monitor is actually really good. The picture quality is clear and smooth, especially for gaming—the high refresh rate makes everything feel fast and responsive. The monitor itself looks nice and does what it’s supposed to do performance-wise. The only downside is it doesn’t have built-in speakers, so you’ll need headphones or external speakers. Other than that, it’s a solid monitor and I’d definitely recommend it 👍🏽
reviews.author: Adrianna

reviews.title: Mon
reviews.comment: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Great monitor for the price! The picture quality is crisp, and the refresh rate makes everything super smooth—perfect for gaming or everyday use. Setup was quick and easy too!
reviews.author: Page Turners Anonymous

reviews.title: Good for what it is!
reviews.comment: Very good monitor! Fast FPS and decent size screen! It came quickly thanks to Amazon and saved me from having to spend hundreds of dollars on a new monitor! Runs well with my PC and the FPS hasn't dwindled after dual monitors! Great buy!
reviews.author: Kieran

reviews.title: Love it!
reviews.comment: I don’t usually write reviews but I am extremely happy with this monitor. It works great and is very smooth compared to my old monitor. Easy to decorate (like I did in the photo) and stand holds up pretty well. It’s amazing for the price and made my setup look so much better. It’s not too bright and not too dark it’s perfect. 5 stars for me.
reviews.author: TwinBookMom

reviews.title: Not 4k nor hdr
reviews.comment: Good graphics great on most things good refresh rate size is like perfect, the power is cool the value for money is there I just wished it was 4k and hdr
reviews.author: Nathan

reviews.title: Worth every penny.
reviews.comment: After months of using it, I’m very happy with this curved monitor so far. The screen size and subtle curve make a noticeable difference, especially for multitasking, watching videos, and general computer work. The curve feels natural and helps keep everything in view without needing to constantly move my head. The design is clean and modern with slim bezels, and it looks great on my desk. Setup was quick and easy right out of the box. The display quality is solid—colors look good, text is clear, and brightness is more than enough for daily use. It performs well for office work, browsing, and streaming, and even casual gaming feels more immersive compared to a flat screen. Build quality is decent for the price. While it’s not a high-end premium monitor, it feels sturdy and well-made. Overall, this is an excellent value if you’re looking for an affordable curved monitor that delivers good performance and comfort.
reviews.author: Emily Jin

reviews.title: Very good monitor for low price
reviews.comment: The monitor was fairly easy to set up; it comes with the screws (4 mini screws to attach the base handle to the monitor and 1 medium screw to attach the legs to the base handle of monitor). Overall, you should have 2 mini screws and 1 medium screw left over. The picture quality is very good for the price and it runs my online game very well (no lagging) but I do prefer to play on my other monitor but simply modifying the graphic settings can make it better. Cons: the on/off button is on the back of the monitor and looks like a joy stick so ensure to read the directions to know how to toggle the settings, etc. Also, although it is a 24-inch monitor and curved, it does not adjust like my other monitors so it sits very low compared to the other ones. If your space permits it, you may need a monitor rise so it isn't so low to your other monitor if you are using two monitors. Pros: Good quality for the price. It comes with an HDMI cord so as long as your computer can take HDMI, you don't need to buy one. It is fairly easy to set up (should take no longer than 15 - 20 minutes from opening to turning it on.
reviews.author: Sherri Fauci

reviews.title: AMAZING Gaming Monitor!!
reviews.comment: I bought this monitor for my son and he absolutely loves it! It's got phenomenal clarity, the color is amazing, the curvature is amazing, it works really well, it's high quality and it was very easy to install. We love it! The size is perfect and it's extremely sturdy. The mountability was great & easy to do, manage and maneuver. It's very sturdy and secure. We love it!
reviews.author: Heidi M.

reviews.title: Great product
reviews.comment: I bought this monitor, and it exceeded my expectations. The quality is very good for the price. I liked it because it delivers exactly what it promises. I’ve been using it for several days, and so far, everything has gone wonderfully—without any issues. Plus, it arrived quickly and was well-packaged.
reviews.author: Yunier Madrigal

reviews.title: Excellent replacement for my old Dell monitor
reviews.comment: This 24” 1800R curved monitor has absolutely no business being this good at this price. The 180Hz refresh rate and 1ms response time are legitimately smooth—none of the ghosting, smearing, or “maybe my eyes are tired” excuses you get with cheap panels. Flip on FreeSync and it’s just clean, fluid motion. Fast games feel great, and the curve actually adds to the experience instead of being a gimmick. Colors? Surprisingly solid. Viewing angles? No drama. The build feels sturdier than it has any right to be. They even toss in an HDMI cable, which is more generosity than most “premium” brands manage. VESA mount support is there if you want to stick it on an arm and pretend you’re running a command center. (I am.) I’ve been using it daily for over a week, and honestly—it’s one of the best budget gaming monitors I’ve picked up. If your wallet is not cooperating but you still want a real high-refresh curved display, this is the one.
reviews.author: Jennifer Guerrero

reviews.title: Very nice monitor
reviews.comment: This is my 2nd Z-Edge monitor. My first one went out after 5 years, and it was awesome until the very end. Tried to buy an LG monitor, but the colors looked muddy and inaccurate. This one seems to be spot on, just like my old one. And it was less expensive than the LG! I'm not a gamer, so I can't really attest to refresh rate, but it does very well in Photoshop. Nice curve and no glare, and a very good size too. I'm a fan.
reviews.author: TXBookLover

reviews.title: It's great just got a little unlucky is all but it happens.
reviews.comment:
Well I like it very much, so nice, big screen, can keep up with anything I have put on it. There is only one problem, there is one dead pixel about the center more to the right bottom corner and I just got it, it happens but I have only heard good things though about their customer service so not, not worried at all lol. Screen still worked though turned right on with my custom pc and all of the features were there and worked. I did everything I know how to troubleshoot the dead pixel but no luck it's a Sunday so not worried. still great product great for 1080p gaming nice price great performance from what I have seen and if you want to know about on board speakers it's a monitor not a TV so not loud at all or even close to being good but this is a great MONITOR that has sound. Would definitely recommend this it is very nice lol didn't even see or read about the rgb before it got here haha went off the black and white for this one and yes it's good...one dead pixel though.
To add to my previous up above, they replaced my defective product and sent me a new one. It is still working just fine, great product, great customer service. It has been a while since I bought this so I can better update with more time and good to go. Thank you for sending the new one way back and game on.
reviews.author: Ryan

reviews.title: Excellent monitor
reviews.comment: I was super skeptical about purchasing this even through online, but I have to admit I am not disappointed! The screen is beautiful, only down fall id say is the mount.  The mount appears to be super cheap and could use an update.  Aside from that, is as pictured and advertised!
reviews.author: Taylor

reviews.title: Great Monitor, great support, minor issue.
reviews.comment:
This monitor is a nice monitor. However, the first one I recieved had a dead pixel at eye level. I contacted their support and they were top notch and replaced the monitor. Unfortunately that monitor also had a dead pixel that was now in the lower right corner. I tried several applications to revive the dead pixels on both monitors to no avail.
I did not contact their support the second time as the dead pixel was not in a primary field of view and didn't obscure my vision or "catch my eye" if you will. It was in area that wasn't blinding.
The picture on the monitor is great. The colors are vibrant and it's a good monitor for the price. Refresh rates and frame rates are quick and seamless.
It would be nice to be able to control the back led lights. Of course being honest, I didnt check into it that hard. It's not that bright and with my desk LED lights I forget it even has an led on the back.
Assembly was quick and simple.
Again, their customer service was on point, and I am certain they would of replaced this monitor too, but it wasn't a major issue for me, so I didn't bother with it.
Overall a great product, my only suggestion to them is have quality control check the monitors more thoroughly before shipping them out. I will buy my second monitor from them.
reviews.author: Jeff K.

reviews.title: seems legit
reviews.comment: unless the picture quality suddenly drops off for a reason or another, thumbs up! i felt this was too good of a deal in my current situation to pass up; not to mention i was pondering upgrading to 1440p and this price point was virtually unmatched. This monitor even has speakers! most value gaming monitors dont. another positive, slight rgb which isnt that big of a deal for me personally, but still a nice finishing touch!
reviews.author: Spoonbard

reviews.title: It’s worth the quality and 4K capability
reviews.comment: Excellent picture quality with sharp 4K resolution and vibrant, accurate colors. The build quality feels solid, and the stand is stable and well-designed. It offers great value for the money, especially for a 32-inch display. Setup is quick and straightforward, and overall performance is smooth and reliable.
reviews.author: Edward Richey

reviews.title: 10/10 Would Recommend!! Love this monitor!
reviews.comment: Great price and great monitor! I would def buy again. I paid about the same for a Samsung monitor pictured to the left, and I like this one much better. Easy to turn on and off, screen color and resolution are awesome. In love how large it is as well!!
reviews.author: Mahina Moon

reviews.title: Outstanding buy
reviews.comment:
Not for intense gaming or pro design work, but with 60 Hz refresh rate, for office and streaming it's perfect. Color is good (fairly close to pantone reference sheet surprisingly) and menu is easy with lots of settings. Just as good as the best inexpensive monitor. Bezel is ultra thin, 1/8th inch or less. For what it is, you can't beat it.
I'd recommend it too anyone.
reviews.author: South Texan

reviews.title: Good monitof
reviews.comment: The price is right, great little monitor for the money clarity is good and speed for gaming
reviews.author: john warner.

reviews.title: Gawfolk 24 inch gaming monitor 200hrt
reviews.comment: Surprisingly really good,  it's not a 4k OLED or anything but it's decently clear, size is nice. 200hrt is really nice to play around with, the only issue Is the stand could be a bit more sturdy. But the set-up is easy, light weight and not bad when you have your window open and don't have a horrible glare or anything. Would rate 9 if I could.
reviews.author: August

reviews.title: Lightweight, Simple, and Travel-Friendly Monitor
reviews.comment:
Absolutely Love This Monitor – Perfect for Work and Travel!
I can’t say enough good things about this monitor! It’s unbelievably lightweight and setting it up is a breeze—just one USB-C to C cable for both power and display. No extra cords, no hassle. The connection is instant, and the picture quality is crisp and vibrant. It’s not full HD, but honestly, it looks way better than any traditional monitor I’ve used.
The travel case included is a lifesaver. I take this monitor everywhere—coffee shops, offsite locations, even on trips—and the case keeps it safe and easy to carry. Plus, you get three cables (two USB-C to USB-C and one HDMI), so you’re covered for any setup.
The price? Totally reasonable for the quality and convenience you get. And the customer service was outstanding—quick, helpful, and friendly. This monitor has made my workflow so much smoother, and I can’t imagine going back. If you’re on the fence, don’t hesitate—grab this monitor. You’ll love it!
reviews.author: An N.

reviews.title: Excellent screen at a great price
reviews.comment: This is for the 2560x1600 Upperizon 16in monitor - it's fantastic!  Excellent image quality.  Gets very bright if you want it to.  You can choose the color space between P3, sRGB, Adobe RGB, and Native.  Native looks closest to my laptop screen and also close to P3.  Having an onscreen menu to choose color space and other settings is a huge bonus in a portable screen.  The resolution is excellent allowing large documents to be offloaded from my primary laptop screen.  My laptop is 1800 vertical, and this screen is 1600, which works well.  I didn't want a 16:9 HD display (only 1080 vertical), and this extra screen resolution is much more useful.  Very happy with this screen: it provides excellent imaging, portability and configurability in a lightweight and inexpensive package.
reviews.author: MG1

reviews.title: A great monitor for my purposes
reviews.comment: I bought this monitor to use with my Mac Mini on my roll top desk. Because of limits imposed by the desk, this was the largest monitor I could buy, so many conventional monitors would not fit. For me, it doesn’t matter. The monitor looks great, both in terms of sitting on my desk, and in terms of the video quality. It came with all the cables I would have needed, but in my case this was a very simple plug and play. It also came with a very nice, padded carrying case. I won’t be using it, but for someone who wants to take advantage of this monitor’s portability, it is a very nice touch. I have no way of knowing how long it is going to last in daily use, but so far I am very pleased. About the only downside is that the built in speakers are not very good. The sound quality is tinny and the volume is weak. My Mac Mini’s internal speakers are better, but I intend to add some external speakers to get even better volume. But the monitor’s speakers are a very minor issue. Overall, this is a good buy, IMHO.
reviews.author: Wayne P.

reviews.title: Larger screen - Huge Improvements!
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/E1ucAGNx-0L.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/71NoODw7wXL._SY256.jpg I purchased the Upperizon Portable Monitor 10-inch monitor three years ago.  It was a breeze to setup for use as a third monitor for as my dedicated Chat screen.  Even back then- their customer service is PHENOMENAL The one complaint I had was the stand mechanism.  When approached to consider upgrading to the 18.5 inch, I declined because I had the smaller screen situated to prevent the monitor from slipping due to the flimsy stand. I was happy with it.
I contacted them last week about another 'issue' with the 10-inch that turned out to be my error.  I was asked to try the upgraded 18.5 inch.  They assured me improvements were made.  I agreed and ordered it yesterday.
I am SUPER happy I did.  The setup was a breeze - unplugged the old monitor. Plugged in the new one. Seamless. It booted up and automatically integrated with my setup.  The best part is the new stand.  It's perfect!  It's metal, firm and adjustable.  They actually listened to my complaint!
The monitor arrived well packaged, it has a nice carrying case with a pocket. For those of you looking for a sleek, lightweight, flexible travel monitor, this is the one for you.  For those of you still on the 10.5-inch monitor, it's time to upgrade.  You won't be disappointed.

reviews.author: p0

reviews.title: Inexpensive and impressive option for a "pop-up" office
reviews.comment: About a year ago, a customer support rep from a company I work with was raving about the "portable monitors" her team had acquired. I remember being intrigued by the concept but I'd yet to encounter an application for such a thing -- both my home and on-site offices were already equipped with full-sized, dual screens. However, since then, my wife and I acquired a travel trailer, out of which I plan to work remotely on occasion. I started thinking about using the trailer's onboard HD TV as a second monitor but it's really too far away from my workspace to serve as a 2nd monitor. I then thought of hauling and extra, full-sized monitor along but the work to set it up, tear it down and find storage space seemed to outweigh the benefit. Then I remembered that conversation last year about portable monitors .... The ZenScreen seemed to garner good reviews, and I've been happy with other Asus products I've purchased in the past. Mine arrived yesterday and I gotta' say that I'm rightly impressed. I'm not sure why you'd want to consider the larger models as those seem to fly in the face of portability. But the 16" model (15.6" viewable) is lightweight and small enough to coexist with a laptop in most computer bags. Setup is fast and easy – a quick-connect kickstand allows you to place the display right next to your laptop at the perfect angle. Power and video are simultaneously delivered via a single USB C connection. And brightness, contrast and image quality really exceeded my expectations. My local Target store has a similar Asus 16" ZenScreen for twice the price. The performance specs seem identical to this one. The only difference seems to be that it has an integrated folding stand verses the screw-on "kickstand." While the integrated stand seemed a bit more convenient, it didn't look as sturdy (especially when propping up the display in portrait mode) and I couldn't justify twice the price. Obviously, I have not yet had enough time to speak to the long-term reliability of this product. I'll be sure to edit this review in the future if I encounter any issues. However, this Asus backs the ZenScreen with a 3-year warranty and, as I said, the company has a good reputation for quality. So far, I enthusiastically recommend the ZenDesk portable display for those who travel with a laptop and have the need for dual displays.
reviews.author: Topcat

reviews.title: Portable Productivity Powerhouse for Remote Work
reviews.comment: As someone who travels frequently for work and values a dual monitor setup, this ASUS ZenScreen has become an indispensable tool. The ability to have a second screen anywhere transforms laptop productivity from cramped and limiting to spacious and efficient. The 16-inch size is the perfect balance between portability and usability. Large enough to actually work on comfortably, small enough to slip into a laptop bag without adding significant bulk or weight. The slim profile and light weight make it genuinely portable, not just technically movable like some "portable" monitors. The IPS display quality is excellent. Colors are accurate and vibrant, viewing angles are wide, and the Full HD resolution provides crisp text and clear images. This is not a compromise display you tolerate for portability. This is a legitimate quality monitor that happens to be portable. Reading documents, editing spreadsheets, and viewing presentations all look great. The USB-C connectivity is brilliantly simple. One cable provides both power and video signal. Plug it into your laptop and it just works. No separate power adapter to carry, no multiple cables to manage. The simplicity cannot be overstated. For travel, reducing cable clutter is a massive benefit. The dual USB-C ports provide flexibility. You can use either port for connectivity, and the extra port can charge your phone or connect other devices. The inclusion of Mini-HDMI means you can also use this with devices that do not support USB-C video output. Versatility matters for real-world use. Setup is literally plug and play. No drivers to install, no configuration needed. Connect the cable and the monitor works immediately. Windows recognizes it instantly and you can start using the extended display right away. The simplicity makes it accessible even for less technical users. The auto-rotate feature and portrait mode work well. For reading documents or coding, portrait orientation is fantastic. The monitor detects orientation and adjusts automatically. Small touches like this show thoughtful design. Eye care features including flicker-free technology and blue light filter make extended use more comfortable. When you are working on the road all day, reducing eye strain matters. These features actually make a difference during long work sessions. Build quality feels premium. The materials are solid, the stand works smoothly, and everything feels well-engineered. This is not a flimsy gadget. It is a serious productivity tool built to withstand regular travel and daily use. For remote workers, digital nomads, consultants, or anyone who works from different locations regularly, this monitor is transformative. Turn any coffee shop, hotel room, or client site into a productive dual-monitor workstation. The productivity gains easily justify the investment. Highly recommend for mobile professionals.

reviews.title: Great Display and Portability, but Feels a Bit Fragile

However, the build feels a bit delicate, so you need to handle it carefully. Overall, a useful portable monitor with a slightly fragile feel.

reviews.title: Oddly Practical Must Have for the Mobile Professional
reviews.comment: Happened to be in Taipei during the Computex Electronics show and saw this new ZenScreen on the show floor at the ASUS booth. Was so immediately blown away by the road warrior practicality of it that I ordered one from Amazon right then on the show floor. Then later when I got back to the hotel room I ordered another one (why stop at two? My MacBook Pro has 4 USB C ports!). Have had the ZenScreens for a couple days now and I love them. Can't wait to hit the road again so I can put them to work in hotel rooms, coffee shops, etc.  The work flow I've developed works best on a 3 monitor setup, which I have in my home office, but I always lose that when I travel and am confined to laptop. So being able to take my workflow with me now and have all my dashboards setup on additional displays the way I need to is a godsend. Overall, I find this one of the most oddly practical and magical "accessories" to come out for a long time. Blows my mind that the ZenScreen gets both power and video from the same cable. That you don't have to find additional power outlets to plug it in makes it so much more practical.  Also find it amazing that a phone can power the display (plugged it into a Galaxy S8 and the screen powered on and got video - doesn't work with all phones though).  Also love that it just gets detected as a display, so you can set it up how you want to - landscape or portrait. The screens are big and I think deceptively lightweight for just how big they are. I like that you can avoid lugging around the covers/stands if you want to save some weight and just rely on a pen (included!) to prop up the displays.  Since getting them I've already had half a dozen friends and work colleagues pick one up.

I do believe it is an ips panel just a crappy one as it doesn't have black smearing issues like VA. Overall, not too bad for $140 ultrawide if buying it for secondary monitor like I am. reviews.title: Absolutely incredible.
reviews.comment:
Just not really any other way to put it. From the overall design of the monitor itself, to the picture quality, to the built in safety features to prevent any damage to the panel, this display is just killer.
[Some gripes I have]
Firstly the packaging it came in, though good, needs serious improvement. Primarily the wrapping it comes in leaves bubble wrap stains on the display which looks abysmal and though some reports claim they were never able to get these markings off their panels, mine came off with just a bit of screen cleaner and a good wipe.
I also dislike that there's no ability to personally upgrade the firmware. This results in having to buy an entirely new panel if a better firmware becomes available and that's a bit asinine with how expensive this display is.
The blacks aren't super good if you're in a bright room due to problems with ambient lighting, which could take away from the enjoyment you get from the display, so it's, in my opinion anyways, most enjoyable in a darker room which is primarily where Im using it.
No HDMI 2.1 which is extremely disappointing as this hurts the ability to use this monitor in its full capacity on a gaming console. That doesn't affect me however because I have an LG 55 inch oled for just such the occasion and primarily pc game. Fortunately for me.
The ultra wide aspect of this display has been.. an adjustment period as well. Although overall the quality of this is, as aforementioned, incredible, it's worth pointing out that it takes a lot of adjusting if you're coming from your typical 16:9 displays and you'll see this primarily in things like watching YouTube videos, movies, and in some video games. You especially notice the difference in one of my worst examples, the game Hell Let Loose. I absolutely cannot play it in 21:9 whatsoever. Just cannot. It's so stretched out and hideous looking that it almost made me nauseous. And that sucks primarily because that's one of my favorite games, and 16:9 leaves black bars on the sides of the game which isn't a huge deal but I digress. So expect not all your games to look ideal to you when getting this and potentially having to compromise.
[Praise and tips]
Frankly I just don't have anything short of absolute praise for this display. I've found the best experience to be sitting back a few feet from my desk with a controller, or my wireless mouse and keyboard upon my lap-table. I personally use HDR 400 true black over the HDR 1000 option because it truly, in my opinion of course, looks insanely better, darker, significant and more atmospheric this was especially true in the modern warfare 2 campaign.
Overall I'm greatly enjoying this display, I hope it lasts me a very long time as I baby it about as much as someone could possibly recommend babying an OLED. I personally use brave browser with the darkreader extension, use windows dark theme, a Screensaver after 2 minutes of not being at my desk, I hide my Taskbar, and I make sure that in any games there's no static red anywhere. I absolutely love that after four hours of use on this panel, when shut off it'll do an automatic pixel refresh. Now that doesn't mean this panel is susceptible to any burn-in whatsoever, it is an oled panel after all..but with a lot of TLC and awareness of what you have on your display, the likeliness of it burning in is about as likely as a meteor striking your house and even if SOMEHOW you do everything I recommend and it still burns in, well Dell has your back with a three year warranty. Just make sure you register it on their website when you get the display. However, and I cannot stress this enough whatsoever, this display, much like any oled display, is probably not the ideal choice if you're somebody who works from home and sits infront of their computer for an asinine amount of time. This is pretty much ideal for gamers who game for long periods of time where stuff is happening on the screen constantly.
Again though, Im loving this display, it has been nothing short of a game changer for me and leaves me excited for the future of oled monitors. I'm in no rush to upgrade my pc to a 4090 an 13900k to game in 4k 120fps, and as an owner of both a 4k oled and now this, there really isn't that HARDCORE of a noticeable difference imo and this is perfect for my current pc specs. Couldn't be happier, couldn't rate this higher, trust me you're going to want this badboy when it comes back and isn't being scalped for 1600.
reviews.author: Kurtis M

reviews.title: Incredible picture and smoothness!  Not without minor annoyances...
reviews.comment:
Upgraded from a 5 year old Acer 34 inch, and holy cow I didn't realize what I was missing.  The colors, brightness, and smoothness of this monitor are absolutely phenomenal.  I do a lot of sim racing and FPS games where a high refresh rate and good response speeds are important.  This monitor absolutely delivers on those fronts.  I also use my display practically all day every day for work, and this monitor is fantastic to work on.  You may want to turn the brightness down a bit to avoid eye strain, but I've had no issues in several weeks of use.
I was a little worried about the glossy panel, but so far glare and reflections haven't been a problem at all.  The cable management in the back of the monitor is quite nice in my opinion, and I love having a few extra USB ports to work with.  I'm also fond of the configurable lighting.  Mine has a wall right behind it, so gives a little bit of ambience when it's dark.
I have only two minor complaints, and these have been mentioned in other reviews:
- Fan noise
It's minor.  Most of the time if you're doing anything on the machine - especially gaming - you're not going to hear it.  It is there, but it's very faint.  Sometimes mine does this annoying thing where one of the fans spins up and down, up and down for a few minutes.  That makes it was more noticeable, but over time I've gotten used to it.  It's a minor downside for all the positives that this display brings.
- OLED Panel Refresh warning
A message pops up every 4 hours of use and asks you to do a pixel refresh now or allow it to do so when the monitor goes on standby.  For the price of this thing, most people are probably going to want to follow this routine to ensure the panel lasts as long as possible.  I'm a little afraid to just turn it off for fear I won't take care of the panel properly.  However, this notification can be *very* annoying if it pops up in the middle of a critical point in your game!  This is easily the most annoying thing about the monitor, but as with the fan noise - over time I've gotten used to it, and I'm not worried about it being manageable over time.  If you turn this off, the panel will still do the pixel refresh automatically when the monitor sleeps every 4 hours of use.
Overall an amazing display.  Mine arrived quickly and without a single dead pixel.  My jaw literally dropped when it fired it up the first time, and it dropped again during my first gaming session.  If you can deal with some of the downsides of an OLED display, this monitor is very much worth a look.  I love mine!
reviews.author: Kevin

reviews.title: Great value and surprisingly great quality
reviews.comment: After a month of use I am ready to give it a simple review. As a lifelong gamer with eyes sensitive to ghosting  I'm usually a harsh critic when it comes to most screens. So when I say that this discount off-brand monitor blew my mind please know that this isn't an exaggeration. Yes I may have gotten lucky, but regardless the model sent to me is surpassing every expectation. PROS: Speed - The screen seems most comfortable at either 120hz or 200hz. It felt a little off at 165 but that may be my own eyes. Setting overdrive to Off or Normal seems to give the best results along with the high refresh. Color - HDR is pretty damn good on this thing. Not as good as some expensive oleds would be but still surprisingly good. Otherwise set the screen to Movie for the brightest and most vivid SDR colors. Cons: MPRT felt weird to me. Reverse ghosting weird. So just leave that off. Wasn't too big a fan of the VRR but it definitely works fine. Just kinda mutes the colors a notch and feels like strobbing but that is probably just my eyes. My friends and wife have all said it looks great with VRR to them. I just keep it set to 200hz Conclusion: For the money you cant beat this screen. Ive been using it with games both on my PC and also streaming with GeForce Now (which seems to lock to 120hz on it) and it works great either way.

reviews.title: It has quite high brightness, very good for gaming.
reviews.comment:
I bought this ultrawide monitor to enhance my workspace, and it honestly exceeded my expectations. The screen is enormous, and the curve truly makes a difference, as it feels much more immersive compared to a regular monitor.
I use it to work with multiple windows open simultaneously, and it's incredibly convenient not having to constantly switch between applications. I also tried it for watching videos, and the experience is quite immersive. The image quality is good, the colors are vibrant, and the size greatly enhances productivity.
The design is also a strong point; it looks modern and clean on the desk. Overall, I consider it a very good option if you're looking for more screen space and a more professional experience. I highly recommend it.
reviews.author: Alexander

reviews.title: Sleek design
reviews.comment: Nice monitors for the money. I used these monitors to replace some old high end lcd monitors for multiple dvr camera systems. The camera preview images are much softer and detailed now. These monitors are 1/3 the weight of my lcd monitors and made setup much easier. Image adjustment is easy with the back mounted controls and they keep  their adjustments when power is removed, not just turned off. Sleek looking minimal frame design allows top, bottom, or side stacking to form an tight fitting array. The cables all exit the bottom and can be seen but this is not an issue for what I'm using them for.

reviews.title: Best budget 4K monitor with good features!
reviews.comment:
I wanted an additional monitor for my work setup and debated for a bit before narrowing down on this model. I wasn’t looking for anything really expensive nor dirt cheap with nil features. This one fit the budget and features I needed perfectly.
I recvd it today and got to set it up immediately. It was a very simple to put it together and connected to my Mac via the included DP cable. Yes, I have a docking station with DP port.
The quality is great, very thin bezel and color/brightness are awesome. The screen size was one of the main factors of choosing this one and it didn’t disappoint me at all in reality.
Durability is not something I am worried about as I’m not expecting to abuse it beyond its capabilities. Functionality wise, it’s exactly serving my purpose and I’m very satisfied with my purchase overall. Just waiting for monitor mount to arrive to make it even more versatile.
Overall best budget 4K monitor out there in this screen size and best suited for work setup in my humble opinion.

reviews.title: Good value for the money
reviews.comment: Pros: Does what a 1080p screen should.  No issues getting it to run at the advertised refresh rates, two HDMI and two DP inputs.  Seems like decent color quality.  No dead pixels, and I love the thin bezel.  No extra frills, decent specs. Cons: Pictures on Amazon for it are slightly out of date since it doesn't show the correct inputs on the revision I received.  Power supply is a barrel connector with a wall adapter at the end, and the total length is ~1 meter.  Personally I am neither a fan of the wall adapter nor the short lenght, I prefer a standard cable with the necessary transformer either in the screen housing (if possible) or a box inline with the cable (ex. standard laptop power adapter) so it can more easily fit with power strips/surge protector. A 2m total length would give more reasonable flexibility. Also, the labeling on the inputs (and specs) advertise DisplayPort 1.4, but they include a DisplayPort 1.2 cable.  It works for what I need it for, but why the disparity?  No HDMI cable included, but those are quite readily available...but it can be annoying when one is not in the box.
reviews.author: Jonathan Hensley

reviews.title: OLED early adopter pain points. Still worth it.
reviews.comment: I've been tracking OLED for about 20 years now. I'm THRILLED that this display is available on the mainstream market for a reasonable price. It's worthy of the steep entry fee, but it still comes with some pain points for us OLED early adopters. Namely the annoying prompts to perform some form of Screen Care to prevent burn in that happen even if you just sat down after the display was in sleep mode for 12+ hours. I wholly expected a firmware update to remedy this, but apparently isn't in the cards. PROS It's OLED baby. Perfect blacks, vibrant colors. No better image quality than this. High refresh rate and low latency! Been using it for a year, rarely performing screen care when prompted, and no burn in. CONS Annoying 'Screen Care' prompts Does need some tuning out of the box for the best experience Can actually be too bright even at lowest brightness setting. Power LED is very bright... had to cover mine completely. Power brick... would prefer it was integrated into the display, or the display MUCH thinner overall.

reviews.author: Israel Hernandez

reviews.title: Great cheap office productivity 4k monitor with extra pixels (x2560 v. x2160)
reviews.comment: Bought two of them. They arrived last night. Spent far too much time testing them. Summary: great cheap office productivity 4k monitor with extra width. Huge pro: the resolution. Those extra pixels (x2560 v. x2160) are incredible for usability, either in portrait mode or landscape. Even at 200% scaling (to avoid blurry text caused by the rendering that Windows 10/11 has at anything other than 100%/200%/300% because DPI scaling in Windows 10/11 is atrocious. So in landscape mode, I can see two pages, even at 200%. The portrait mode allows me to have very usable, larger text, fitting a page & the header of the next page. Very clear text. Ahhhh..... Huge Pro: has DC dimming, not PWM. That's critical for my eye strain. I cannot use PWM because my eyes tire quickly. I don't have a physical device, but the app that I use says that the flickering is very low (below 5%). I don't notice anything, in any event. Pro: supports FreeSync, which means G-Sync worked for me on my ancient 1060 card. YMMV, I guess. Pro: slightly above average contrast ratio (for an IPS) of 1,200 to 1. Pro: supports DCR. Probably not a higher end implementation, of course. Pro: has a blue light mode. I don't use that, because I prefer using software for that. Con: the stand is perfunctory. I put it on a $30 stand that I previously bought for another monitor. The 75x75 VESA mounting holes are at the bottom of the panel, which means it works well for landscape but do not work for portrait without significant effort (the monitor in portrait mode is also on a custom stand and to offset the sag caused by the mounting hole placement, I have a small shipping box propped under the sagging side, with more cardboard as spacers to level the monitor. Update: I fixed the sagging by buying two VESA adapters (https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0741CFJVW), which allows the monitor to be very close to the center of the monitor stand. Con: although the display is IPS, the panel's viewing angle is not that great. Even looking at it straight on, the right side of the landscape and the right side of the portrait mode monitor are washed out. Think of this as poor man's BenQ RD280U. I don't know if it's the same panel, btw, just the same resolution, contrast ratio, and both have a matte finish. This has 120% sRGB; the BenQ has 100% sRGB. Perhaps this is a prior iteration of the panel used in the BenQ (the BOE MV282CVB-N11). Perhaps it is uses the BOE MV282CVB-N10. I don't know, though as software does not show the panel manufacturer (other than the Gawfolk model, GF005. Small Con: HDMI does not run at 60 hz. But the two DP ports are 1.4 and can easily handle 60 hz. I'm now very tempted to buy another set for my office at work.
reviews.author: Jonathan in Arizona

reviews.title: For the money, I don't know how I could be any happier.
reviews.comment: 28 Inch 3840x2560p display. I replaced a 32" 4k monitor with this. It doesn't sound like the extra vertical resolution is all that much, but it's VERY noticeable in real life. I feel like I can get so much more "stuff" on screen at once, or I can view long chunks of text without scrolling. Plus, the slightly smaller screen fits my desk better, and means I can see everything at a glance instead of feeling like I have to "look around" to see the whole screen. It really seems like this must be using the exact same panel as the "BenQ RD280U 28.2” 4K 3840x2560 3:2 Programming Monitor" that sells for $600! I have no dead or stuck pixels, the backlighting is reasonably bright, and text looks great on either light or dark backgrounds. Really, this monitor gives you such a great display for such a small amount of money I feel like I stole it! Of course the rest of the package is the cheapest possible plastic and pot metal. Nothing about it feels premium, and apparently there is a speaker, but I don't know why they bothered as it's completely useless. Just like with the 3:2 BENQ monitor, you have to use DisplayPort (not HDMI) to get 60hz at full resolution, but it has two, separate DisplayPort connections (along with 2 more HDMI ports), so I had no problem hooking it up. It works fine with an M1 Pro Mac, a Dell laptop using a Dell dock, and a desktop PC, all using DisplayPort. For this price, the only complaint I have is that my desk isn't big enough for me to buy another one! I'd been complaining that there aren't enough 3:2 monitor options. I guess you really don't need a lot of options when you can get one this good for this cheap!

The added vertical resolution was super useful while coding and editing photos. My only real gripe with it was that the inputs were really close to the bottom of the monitor. There wasn’t a good way to keep the cables from being visible without ordering some 90 degree connectors. I ultimately returned mine because I need a monitor of similar resolution that’s just bigger. I need all the resolution because I need a lot of info available at one time. When scaling was set to 100% on this monitor, the text was too small for me to read it while scripting. That’s not a fault of the monitor. It was great otherwise.
reviews.author: Alex Midgett

reviews.title: Really useful
reviews.comment:
Great Monitor, Even Better Customer Service
The package arrived quickly and was very well-packed. Inside, everything was snugly wrapped in soft foam. I found the 15.6" monitor itself with a protective film that had a quick-start guide printed on it—a clever touch. You get everything you need: two USB-C cables, a USB-A cable, an HDMI cable, a power adapter, and a user manual.
Setting it up was a breeze. It works perfectly with both my Lenovo T15 and my desktop PC. The only minor hiccup was with the desktop; to get both the display and touch functions working, I had to use the HDMI cable and the USB-A cable. It would have been even more convenient if a single USB-A could handle it all, but hey, no big deal!
I also tried it with my wife's MacBook Pro, and just as the seller clearly states on the product page, macOS has very limited support for touchscreen functions. It basically works like a single-click mouse—no multi-touch gestures or anything advanced. In comparison, Windows feels like it's running at full power, with complete touch support that really unleashes the screen's potential. It makes me wish Apple would release a patch to loosen these restrictions—maybe someday!
Another thing worth mentioning is how slim and lightweight this monitor is—it feels like carrying just half of a laptop screen. I’ve been using it not only for work but also for casual gaming: whenever I want to relax, I simply connect it to my Switch and jump into a game right away. While the Switch's screen is quite small and 720p only, this monitor provides a perfect portable big-screen alternative. The whole setup is so hassle-free that it’s become my go-to solution for quick entertainment.
Their customer service was second to none. I was consistently impressed by how quickly they responded to my queries, making me feel appreciated as a customer. My satisfaction stems from much more than just the product itself. A standout moment was when they proactively reached out to ensure my experience with the display was living up to expectations. It was a thoroughly positive experience from start to finish.
Hope this helps!
reviews.author: Angelia

reviews.title: Great portable monitor — super clear and easy to use!
reviews.comment:
A Perfect Portable Extension for Laptop – Touchscreen Works Flawlessly!
I bought this portable monitor primarily to use as a secondary screen for my laptop, especially when working with data reports and spreadsheets. It saves me from constantly switching windows on my main display and has seriously improved my workflow.
Right out of the box, I was impressed by how slim and lightweight it is. The thin bezels give it a modern look, and the metal stand is both sturdy and space-efficient. The matte screen is another big plus—it doesn’t pick up glare like glossy glass displays, which makes long work sessions much easier on the eyes.
The touchscreen is highly responsive and works seamlessly with Windows. A simple finger swipe lets me scroll, zoom, or flip through pages effortlessly. One thing to note: the touch function required a quick initial setup to be recognized by my system. Fortunately, the seller provides clear instructions, including a video tutorial and a printed guide, which made the process smooth. I also occasionally use this 15.6” screen as a display for my iPhone 16 and ipad. While touch doesn’t work with those devices, it still serves as a handy large screen for viewing content.
While the default brightness is a bit dim , turning it up to 100% makes a big difference, and it's perfectly adequate for daily use as a portable monitor. There are built-in speakers, which are okay given how thin the monitor is—they do the job, though I did notice that sound gets louder and clearer when the monitor is plugged into power. That said, I still prefer using my laptop’s audio for better quality.
Connectivity is well thought-out: it comes with two Type-C ports and a mini HDMI port. The package includes all necessary cables—USB-C, USB-A, and HDMI—so it works right away with pretty much any device. A power adapter is also included. For basic use, a single USB-C cable can power the screen, but as I mentioned earlier, connecting it to the power adapter does improve both brightness and audio performance.
All in all, this monitor offers great value for the price. It does what it promises, and does it well. No regrets.

reviews.title: Very nice little monitor, some potential flaws
reviews.comment:
I took a gamble and purchased this based on only Vine reviews.  Just received it and wanted to update with my first impression.
I wanted a monitor so that I could quickly interact with my desktop without switching from my laptop (I have a KVM setup, but sometimes watch videos on my desktop while using the laptop).  Unfortunately, I wasn't able to test out this exact setup as the DP to HDMI-mini cable I purchased won't fit.  I put some blame on the cable for being a bit too thick at the shielding, but also on the monitor.  The port area is recessed, and even the cable that they provide with the package sits tightly flush with the body of the monitor.  Also, you have to remove the cables to close the stand.  Between the very tight fit, and the need for frequent insert/remove cycles if you're actually using it as a portable monitor, I worry that the ports will be a point of failure.
That being said, I did test it by using the provided HDMI cable. The picture is very nice, the touch works well, and usb-a to usb-c cord from my desktop is enough to supply the data and power.  Very happy with it so far, will update once I try it out alongside my KVM setup.

reviews.title: An Epic Ode to Gaming Glory
reviews.comment:
Behold the monitor—no mere machine,
But a portal forged in obsidian sheen.
Its resolution, 1440p divine,
Where clarity and carnage intertwine.
Helldivers descend in pixel-born flame,
Each frame a vow, each death a name.
The screen does not blink, does not forgive—
It renders the cost of the will to live.
IPS-born, with colors true,
It paints each dive in spectral hue.
FreeSync binds the chaos tight,
No tear shall mar the sacred fight.
Response time? A blink, a breath—
1ms defying death.
This is no screen. It is decree—
A lens through which the brave break free.

reviews.title: Excellent monitor , but no instructions & no explanations of settings.
reviews.comment:
This is a beautiful monitor. However it needs instructions & explanations for some of the settings. Like the brightness settings which is normal or highlights seem to work opposit of what i was expecting. Normal seems to be the HDR1000 setting found on other QD OLED monitors whereas as highlights seems to be the True Black HDR 400 setting. I would have expected it to be the other way around.
Getting the best picture out of this monitor is a challenge as a result. However, the result is definately worth it.
In terms of brightness with best settings, it is competitive with other latest generation of monitors that are rated for True Black 500 in many scenes except for full white screens & even there it is not too far off thier mark.
When using Windows HDR Calibration Tool with the normal setting I set the peak brightness to 1000. Other have mentioned setting it to 500, but that would have resulted in blown out highlights with loss of color & detail. The 500 setting might work for the highlight HDR setting but I did not try it as I preferred the normal setting.
I used the normal HDR setting as that gave the brightest highlights even though the highlights setting gave the brightest overall scene. Even though the highlights setting was overall brighter the highlights just didn't pop the way they should have & normal setting was bright enough for most situations.
Sometimes the views can look a little hazy but I don't think the screen coating is affecting that. Some people have said these have the worst matter coating of all monitors. I totally disagree. I have seen other matt coatings that are far worse and this one's reflection handling is really quite good. There is very little pinkish coloring in a bright room that I have seen. It looks like more of a grayish background in a bright room. There is a slight pinkishness from the anti reflective coating but that is definately the coating and not the interaction with bright light on the quantum dot layer in this case.
I believe the slight sense of hazyness I mentioned before could just be a result of greater resolution  allowing a smoother appearance when not dealing with high detail which this monitor handles superbly. It does have substantially more resolution than the other 27" OLED monitors I have.
The monitor is light weight, but doesn't seem flimsy. The stand seems quite sturdy and the base is sufficiently heavy to be stable.
It gets only 4 stars due to missing instructions. Otherwise it is a 5 star unit.

reviews.title: Great
reviews.comment: Awesome for the price point. I did put prints on the qwerty zone, the number line, and the arrow keys (you only need one central print on the three point keys, exception is the space bar, use three there). This is replacing my old beat up K57 that I got for $20 at Target on clearance probably 5 years ago. I tried a K55, very unhappy with that for multiple reasons. IMO, the mechanical keys are... Gimmicky. Yeah, I'm sure a lot of haters are lining up... But I have had an enormous amount of experience with over two dozen keyboards, at least ¾ of which were various mechanical type keying. These work great, but they are loud, hence the need for o rings. All things considered, I have never had a problem or complaint about old school keying. Some membrane types aren't great, but a lot are just fine. I mainly got this to keep my 50 or so advanced RGB configs for various software and games running. Can't do that with the k55, it must be an RGB pro type like the k57 or k70. At the end of the day, this is a great keyboard if you either tolerate the noise or dampen it with o rings. Looks great, feels great, since I have literally almost 100% Corsair components on my series 2 build, ICue is basically home for me, so the customization is immaculate as far as being seamless and easy. I believe this is THE best customization platform as far as dynamic lighting for the average enthusiast user, and this is coming from a hardware engineer who fiddles with EVERYTHING. 9/10, minus one for noise
