reviews.title: Tactical, well back lit, and a formidable keyboard input device for your System!
reviews.comment: My go to for computer keyboard. Tactile feeling of mechanical "Cherry" switches, full keyboard layout; function, ten key, cursor movement, page control movement, even media/volume control features, and back lit keyboard lighting. Built robust, weighted nicely, a little pricey, but it does last, and a formidable keyboard. Nice "gap" of the keys above the base to allow blowing out cleaning. Even if you're as cautious as I am in trying to keep debris from finding its way under the keys, sooner or later, it happens, and that space is nice for those mistakes. If you want a "quiet" keyboard, this isn't for you, look to "Cherry Brown", or "membrane" keyboards. But, if you like the tactical, and clickety-click feel, these "Cherry Red" switches give you just the right feedback. Not able to use the included driver software due to my choice in Operating Systems, the lighting programmability isn't an option, but even Linux and the "default" program of the keyboard software allows you to have a nice "wipe" pattern at least. Even though I can't do anything about the default back lighting, it does provide a great key lighting for those dim to dark room lit environments, all the keys are well back lit to be seen. Durable & designed for punishment, this is my choice for coding, and a little game playing. I'm not much of a gamer, but I do depend on my keyboard for reliable coding/typing. I've tried many types, and kinds of keyboards over the years, and I feel that ever since I found this brand, it will always be "my choice" for an input device, if I have the choice.

reviews.title: Unreal feel and performance — my new go-to gaming keyboard
reviews.comment: I recently upgraded to this keyboard and I honestly don’t see how anyone could give it anything less than 5 stars. My previous keyboard was a fully mechanical unit with Cherry MX Brown switches, so I had a good benchmark—and this one absolutely stands out. The keystrokes are super fast and precise—if you’ve ever watched keyboard ASMR videos and thought “I want that,” this is it. Gaming performance is fantastic. Every input feels responsive, smooth, and satisfying. Uses USB-C  for modern, reliable connection. One of the killer features is the adjustable actuation pressure: I can dial in exactly how far I need to press a key  (0.1mm to 4.0 mm) range, and that significantly reduces accidental key-presses. The lighting quality is excellent. The customizable RGB effects are rich and make it easy to match the keyboard to any build or desk setup. The form factor and build feel premium: the tenkeyless layout keeps things compact (my desktop is less cluttered) and the materials feel incredibly solid. I’m completely sold on this keyboard! It is the perfect fir for those who heavily type for long hours or a gamer looking to maximize their setup. Overall rating: ★★★★★ (5/5) In my experience, this keyboard delivers an exceptional blend of feel, responsiveness, customization, and build quality. If you’ve been looking for a keyboard that not only works great but feels great to use every day—this is one of the best I’ve tried.

reviews.title: Great keyboard
reviews.comment:
The G PRO TKL is a solid competitive gaming keyboard with excellent build quality. The compact tenkeyless design saves desk space and is genuinely portable for tournaments or travel. The detachable cable is a smart feature - no more damaged fixed cables, and you can easily swap in a custom one.
The switches (GX Blue in my case) feel consistent and responsive with good tactile feedback. No key wobble or stabilizer rattle issues that you sometimes find in gaming keyboards. The RGB lighting is bright and even across all keys, with good customization options through the G HUB software.
Some practical notes: The plain black design keeps it professional-looking despite the RGB. The keycaps are decent quality but not exceptional - they'll show shine over time like most ABS caps. The removable cable connection is secure - no disconnects during intense gaming sessions.
Minor gripes: The USB connection could be recessed a bit more to better protect the port, and the included cable is somewhat stiff. The media controls being function-layer only takes some getting used to if you're coming from a full-size board. The wrist rest is sold separately, which feels a bit stingy at this price point. Software is feature-rich but can be finicky with updates sometimes.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​
reviews.author: CJ

reviews.title: A good mechanical keyboard for those who want their experience to be "one and done"
reviews.comment:
I have owned several mechanical keyboards over the past 3 years. Ranging from cheap crap like Red Dragon, to consumer stuff like Corsair and Razer, as well as some of the higher end custom boards like the TOFU60 and some KBDfans stuff.
For the money, I think you can do SO much better. While I appreciate the RGB quality and the sheer amount of endless RGB customization the GHUB software allows you, that is about the only thing I can rate highly.
Construction is not totally terrible for a board built primarily out of plastic. But it is very hollow sounding and does not have much substance to it when typing. Has a nice weight to it and the adjustable angle stands are nice and have been useful. Stabilizers are average, but definitely nothing special. Why are they STILL using MICRO USB? It literally would cost them less than $0.30 to use USB-C instead. I dont get it. Keycaps dont seem to be double shot PBT, but theyre decent quality nonetheless. Nice RGB shine through. Switches are proprietary Logitech Blue clicky switches. They are pretty meh. If you like the sound of a loud dry keypress with significant amount of travel and play, then youll like it. Otherwise, if youve used boards that have a more consistent and overall smooth feeling keypress, this will not be a treat to use.
I think this keyboard is half decent for most folks who want something they can buy once and not have to think about again after that. But if you have very high standards, have used modded or custom or just better quality keyboards prior, this one will very likely not be a great experience.
Personally, I went out on a limb because I finished building my latest PC much quicker than I anticipated and have since sold the TOFU60 I had and my backup board which was a Corsair. So I bought this on a whim wanting to give a GPRO product a try. However after a month of use, I am going to revert to building a good starter 60% or maybe TKL mechanical keyboard since that can be done for under 150 and overall can feel 10 times better than this GPRO. :l
TLDR
6/10. Would recommend to people wanting something that they dont have to worry about ever again after purchasing. Anyone else, I would suggest taking a pass and getting an entry level custom starter board that has intent to be modded down the road.
reviews.author: AcidStrawbz_

reviews.title: Great Keyboard
reviews.comment:
Hey folks! Just gotta drop some love for the Logitech G PRO Mechanical Gaming Keyboard. Let me tell ya, this bad boy is a game-changer.
First off, the build quality? Top-notch! Feels like it could survive a nuclear apocalypse and still be clickin' away like a champ. Plus, them mechanical switches? Pure magic under your fingertips. Typin' on this thing feels smoother than butter on a hot skillet.
Now, let's talk about them RGB lights. Man, oh man, they're like a party on your desk! Customize 'em however you want, match 'em with your mood, your game, heck, even your socks if you fancy! And the software? Easy peasy lemon squeezy. No PhD in computer science required to figure it out.
Oh, and did I mention the compact design? Perfect for us desk space strugglers. Fits like a glove, leaving plenty of room for all your other gaming gear.
Sure, it ain't the cheapest keyboard out there, but hey, you get what you pay for, am I right? And with the G PRO, what you're gettin' is pure gaming bliss.
So, if you're in the market for a new keyboard that's gonna take your gaming experience to the next level, look no further, my friend. The Logitech G PRO Mechanical Gaming Keyboard has got your back. Trust me, you won't regret it!
reviews.author: Argyle Gargoyle

reviews.title: Great keyboard
reviews.comment: I bought this as a gift but I used it for some writing and gaming. The keys are satisfyingly clicky and responsive. The key placement like arrows, print screen/delete etc. and the game mode button are perfect in my opinion. Lighting looks great and the software is much nicer to use than Razer's.
reviews.author: 龜毛

reviews.title: The special characters aren't lit & my lighting preference wont stick. Otherwise pretty good!
reviews.comment: I'm a lousy keyboardist , have been for 60 yrs so the fact that secondary characters aren't lit is a big problem for me.The G Logo is way too bright sio I covered it with tape, and I would love audio controls. esp. a wheel type. Otherwise I like the feel of the keyboard, not too loud & I learned to live without the 10 key pad in exchange for the extra space more easily than I thought. I'm not into fancy keyboard software or gaming so I prefer lighting options that stick where set without having to load software. This keyboard reverts to rolling colors all to often as a default so I really don't like that; I don't need the distraction! One bright note is that I dumped a decent amount of water on it and it survived, a big plus. Plus no lights have dimmed of failed in the several months of use.  Overall, a solid board if these little lighting issues were fixed!
reviews.author: Sandra Warmbreath

reviews.title: False Advertising - Don't Bother
reviews.comment: Didn't ship with firmware. No per-key RGB settings or zoning, and a handful of other features are missing. Don't bother with this company, they aren't what they used to be.
reviews.author: Dave

reviews.title: Excellent monitor, return of first defective one was a breeze.
reviews.comment:
The first monitor that I received displayed tearing, flickering, and artifacts at 144hz refresh, using an RTX5080 Nvidia graphics card when playing Il2-Sturmovik at highest graphic settings. I thought I would give Crua another chance and requested a replacement. Amazon sent me a new monitor immediately which arrived 2 days later. I simply swapped out the screen and returned the defective monitor in the box the replacement was sent in. It was painless.
I have had the new monitor for a couple of weeks and it has been flawless. Great color, sharp image, no dead pixels, stable at 160hz refresh. I cant vouch for its longevity yet, but I will give an update after 6 months or so.
Otherwise, this is the best monitor for the money that I have found in its class, and has made an impressive improvement to my setup.
reviews.author: Vieux

reviews.title: Surprising quality, great for work
reviews.comment: I know this is advertised as a gaming monitor, but I decided to get a large, wide monitor for long work hours to replace my two 27 inch monitors. It has just enough width that you can easily split the screen and work side-by-side. It is genuinely helped my neck pain since my posture is staying straight. There is no lag in the monitor and it has a pretty good design. Nice and thin, sleek. The amount on the back of it was a little strange, but I figured it out. The only thing I don’t like about this monitor is you cannot adjust the height up and down and it does not tilt but for the price I can live with that. It does give you the option to mount on a wall, which is nice. This might be a me problem, but it didn’t want to register with my thunderbolt docking station. I ended up needing to plug it directly into the laptop, which is an ideal. Haven’t figured out if that’s the monitor operation or if I need to connect it in a different way. Overall, this is a great value for the money.
reviews.author: Kim

reviews.title: Good and meh
reviews.comment:
It’s a budget monitor that functions as intended. It’s a great secondary monitor that offers good picture and color quality as well as good refresh rates and response times for the price range.
The good:
The color is consistent with my more expensive monitor. The refresh rate is good for the price. The borders are small and great for using with other monitors. The settings are easy to change and navigate.
The bad:
The stand sucks. It mounts to the monitor in a not great way that allows it to fall out easily. It only rotates in one direction, and at least for me it will not connect to the stand fully when rotated, so it’s kind of just hanging there. More ports would be nice, but hey, it’s a budget monitor.
reviews.author: Aidan C.

reviews.title: Very poor delivery and unboxing experience
reviews.comment:
2/12/26 Shipping was beyond poor. Amazon packaged this in a oversized box with no padding. Monitor box inside was damaged, but product seems ok. I was initially going to return and left a scathing feedback review for amazon delivery being beyond poor, when I requested a call there service kept hanging up on me. Shame on you Amazon, unfortunately I am removing one star for that. Now onto the real review...
Monitor is sharp with no dead pixels, however the protective film is weird. So weird I thought I had received a used product, when I went to peel the film the sticker ripped and I had to carefully inspect to discover there was actually film and not someone pulling one over on amazon on a return. One star removed for that horrible film experience, it was very jarring. There is no height adjustment only tilt, which is fine nothing unexpected there. Stand is actually quality and is a Metal Injection Molding (MIM) material which is impressive for the price, not weighted plastic like some of the higher end brands. I like that there is no horrible blue light signaling the monitor is on, but that can be a turn off for some as the black levels of monitor can confuse someone into thinking it is not working. However if you are a photographer or a gamer this is a huge plus. Kudus to CRUA for doing that.
I will update review upon testing to see if product needs less stars or if amazon wants to chime in on their part in this experience to add stars back. CRUA get on amazon so you can be a solid 4 stars! At this point I would recommend, but beware the film.
reviews.author: Mystic

reviews.title: I works fine so far as work display, not the cheapest but metal stand legs and overall good quality
reviews.comment: Except the tiny stereo speakers that are a joke , just marketing since they are utterly useless as volume is so low. The 3 or 4 inputs available is great addition. The panel input buttons on the side works ergonomically when changing inputs and brightness (you will be changing brightness a lot during the day, trust me. It is not very bright but with 100%brightness is barely usable in low light indoor, at night it needs to go down to 25 ~20% instead. The images, (text) is crisp since 4K+ and extra lines gives more screen space for working , not the ideal format to watch movies as you know.Any case, I like it and recommend it. Color gamut and HDR 10 is just marketing but for text display and working space , works fine
reviews.author: Matt

reviews.title: The Deathadder v3 Pro is PHENOMENAL
reviews.comment:
Just to start right off the bat. I have large hands and this mouse is for large hands. Large hands meaning big width and long fingers. For example the Logitech g pro wireless I consider 'small' for myself. Take that into account.
Razer is on absolute fire recently with their gaming mice department. I do not know if they got some type of freedom from their old product manager or got their own factory - who knows. All we know is they have been taking feedback and releasing exactly what the community is asking for and the products are FIRE.
The Razer Deathadder v3 pro talks for itself, the biggest change for those who actually used the Deathadder is the mouse has reduced the flares on the left/right, and moved the hump more center instead of back. It is still ergonomic for sure but feels more similar to ambidextrous now. The best part is you can FULLY extend your ring finger comfortably across the right-side of the mouse. Your pinky has room as well and does not need to touch the mouse pad.
The thumb buttons have been raised so your thumb has full extension access as well with zero contact to the thumb buttons. PERFECT. The mouse has great contact with the underside of your knuckle and some small contact with the palm.
Besides the shape which is generally the most important part in deciding to buy a mouse the rest of the mouse is what I would call 'flawless'
Sensor - Perfect tracking, zero sensor malfunction, zero jitter, zero +/- acceleration. (Side note, I have not tested 4000hz mode and while I am sure it is great I will be using it in 1000hz mode for longer battery life. I am older now and do not compete like I used to, 1000hz works perfectly fine for me).
Coating (White version) - Absolutely wonderful, easy to grip, feels great in hand
Main clicks - Perfect, split trigger design, amazing actuation force feeling. No complaints
Side Buttons - Perfect, love the size and placement as well
Scroll Wheel - It works, doesn't feel great, doesn't feel bad, feels good. I use it for jump in-game zero issues
Weight - Seriously. It's a large ergo mouse in the 63-64g range.. It's LIGHT
Battery life - Haven't tested it yet but I am sure it's fine, running it in 1000hz mode.
USB-C Connectivity - Great. Modern standards. Love it
Cable - They provided a lightweight usb-c cable for the receiver which is also used to charge the mouse, if you did have to run it in wired it is actually a great cable as well.
Mouse Feet - Perfect glide zero issues on my end
Overall for a large hand gaming who was seeking a wireless option. The Razer Deathadder v3 pro is the best thing I have ever graced my hands on. Tested it for several hours and after a quick muscle memory adjustment I was not only aiming fantastically (which I can do on several mice) but I was also comfortable. Comfort being the most important factor for me.
The large size and lightweight also makes micro-tracking/adjustments even easier to do. I was using the G703 prior and it was do-able but fatigue hit sooner and it felt like a lot of effort sometimes to track something that was spinning around you (this is less an issue in tactical games like Counter-strike and Valorant, and more for fast paced games with a lot of tracking think Quake Live and Overwatch).
The entire team that developed this product. I really wish I was in your industry - I would be absolutely proud to have released such a top-tier gaming product. The market of large hand competitive gamers were requesting this and it has been delivered. Beat both Logitech and Zowie to market which is incredible. Give yourself a pat on the back. I bought two of these one for daily and one for backup. Razer be proud, I truly feel like this is a, 'For Gamers, By Gamers' product.
Amazing, 10/10 product for me. Love it. If you're a daily G703 user like I was, your upgrade is here. Zero-regret purchase.
reviews.author: NT

reviews.title: Phenominal... Instantly helping with Carpal tunnel and my K/D
reviews.comment:
5 Day Update: I have played HARD with this mouse, Worked all day on this mouse, and my pain is FADING! I'm talking, I was literally going to consider surgery in 2 months, to now just needing to stretch my hand and take a break every now and then. This mouse costs basically save me from paying medical bills. I'm just baffled how a small and simple design can go from agony, tingling, burning in my hands to just playing carefree. Still more time to tell, but at this point after 5 straight days? I would have taken a 2 week break. Insanely awesome job by Razer. You have saved my favorite hobby!
They somehow made a mice that is ergo and pro. First time I've played for hours pain free, while also playing better than ever.
Any gamers experiencing wrist/hand pain, or want to prevent it, this mouse is it.
Original Review:
I've been on a wild chase for years trying to balance pain with gaming. I wear braces at night, standing desk, ergo chair, countless mice.. nothing worked. I work on a computer by day, and then do heavy competitive gaming on a low sensitivity... my Carpal tunnel, my thumb have just been screaming, and I've had to take days or weeks off, only to play for a few days and be right back where I started.
I've been using the Razer Viper UItimate for 2 years now.. it's been an amazing mice but is absolutely horrible or your hands, or in my case, larger hands. Constantly squeezing the mouse causes so much strain over time. With the DA V3, the hump in the palm and the slight tilt makes an insane difference. It feels like my hands is just taking a huge sigh of relief when I place it on top of it. My thumb and ring/pinky used to having to death choke most mice, now just has to be presently holding the mouse
I have NEVER had an 8 hour session on a game like Overwatch and had my hands/wrist feel GOOD the next day, until now. It does make you a bit more of a palm/relaxed claw grip, but coming from pure claw grip and pain, I just don't care. After tweaking dpi and sensitivity, my K/D in game has gone up 30-50%. I can just track enemies now, flicking I'm getting used to, as the micro mobility of switching claw to palm is taking practice. I easily got 39/6 K/D in Competitive last night.
Overall:
-Insanely light, feels like you are holding just a shell of a mouse.
-Buttons are instant/clicky, best I've ever felt.
-Zero latency issues, even moved fro 800 to 1600 dpi and halved my in-game sens to get the most out of the sensor.
- IT WILL SAVE YOUR HANDS! I'm actually thinking of giving this mouse a go and seeing if I actually need Carpal Tunnel Surgery. I'll take spending 150 bucks over American Healthcare any day.
-Grip tape, cable, dongle, all premium
Just an awesome mouse. I was so sad that clunky giant ergo mice like my Logitech vertical mouse was all I'd get.. but Razer actually somehow did it.
If you are looking for a ergo mouse that is gaming friendly, this is it. Don't spend the hundreds of dollars and hours I did, this is the one. Measure your hands, and if you are medium-large, get this now.
reviews.author: Scott

reviews.title: Keychron Q6 Max Review – My Endgame Keyboard
reviews.comment:
The Keychron Q6 Max is, without a doubt, my endgame keyboard. Coming from a $30 “mechanical” gaming keyboard, the difference is night and day—this is what a real mechanical keyboard should feel like.
The full aluminum chassis gives it a premium, rock-solid feel, and the gasket-mounted design makes typing incredibly satisfying with just the right amount of flex. The hot-swappable switches add a layer of customization, but even stock, they feel smooth and responsive.
I use it wired-only, so I can’t speak to the Bluetooth or 2.4GHz wireless, but it’s great knowing the options are there if I ever need them. The wired experience has been flawless—zero lag, ultra-responsive keystrokes, and a typing feel that makes every keystroke satisfying.
Compared to my old keyboard, this is a massive upgrade. No more hollow keystrokes or mushy feel or squeaky keys—just pure mechanical bliss. If you want a high-quality, customizable, and premium keyboard, the Q6 Max is absolutely worth it.
Final Verdict: 10/10 – This is the one.
reviews.author: WyldHalfling

reviews.title: Q6 max keyboard review
reviews.comment: Very crisp feel and sound, definitely easy to setup and use. I feel like it’s super sturdy and will last me a while. Comes with key cap removal tools and easy to switch out the switches. The LED isn’t super bright but it’s good enough for me. It’s definitely worth the cost as the macros are easy to setup and it feels like it’s built to last
reviews.author: Matthew F

reviews.title: Great quality for the prices good for gaming
reviews.comment: The red switches are smooth and quieter than the other options which is a blessing if you do alot of gaming me personally I prefer not to here alot of clicking while I'm gaming the keychron mapping and back lighting software works good no issues and easy interface
reviews.author: Jarrett

reviews.title: Nice
reviews.comment: Really happy with it. It’s a solid, heavy mechanical keyboard and the red switches feel and sound great. I like a full keyboard and the stock keycaps, but it is really easy to pop them off with the provided tool if you want to switch them out and customize from there. Out of the box it had the Mac layout installed, but again it was easy to switch to the Windows keys provided too. It’s been great and easy to use. I can’t comment on Keychron’s software, I haven’t had any reason to download it since my computer recognized the keyboard as is. I turned the backlight off using the key commands and haven’t needed to change any settings otherwise. It’s been responsive and I haven’t lost connection once so far. It’s has great battery life too compared to other wireless keyboards I’ve had. I usually only need to charge it once a month, and even less frequently when I’m not on the computer as much. Seems like it will hold up, so it’s been a good upgrade for me.
reviews.author: L

reviews.title: Like the Keyboard, Not the Experience
reviews.comment:
I originally ordered this keyboard (Q6 Max) on November 30, 2025, and it arrived on December 8 properly shrink-wrapped. During setup, I discovered that the Wi-Fi dongle was not working. Bluetooth and wired connections functioned fine.
I also learned that programming the keyboard using Keychron Launcher requires a wired connection, apparently you can't use the dongle on this model. I wanted to assign two of the four keys above the number pad for use with Adobe Lightroom and Photoshop, but they would not stay learned into the keyboard once the keyboard was unplugged. Every time I programmed the keys (for whatever application) and disconnected the cable, the programmed functions or shortcuts stopped working. I also attempted a factory reset, which did not resolve the issue.
For the issues I was experiencing, I contacted Amazon. The representative suggested that the dongle may have become unpaired, though they didn’t have a clear explanation or solution for the programming issue. Since I had purchased the keyboard during a Black Friday sale and it was no longer discounted by the time it arrived, Amazon offered to send a replacement and have me return the original unit. Aside from the dongle and programming issues, the original keyboard itself worked perfectly in terms of typing, overall feel, and they keys themselves did not have any issues.
The replacement shipped on December 15 and arrived on December 20. Unfortunately, when I opened it, it was clearly used and in very poor condition. The box was covered in stickers, there was no shrink wrap, the keyboard bag had already been opened, and there was even hair stuck to the adhesive on the bag. I took photos immediately and contacted Amazon again.
While the customer service representative was polite, they implied the issue was with the manufacturer/seller (Keychron), even though these keyboards are shipped and sold by Amazon. Because I had already received one “bad” replacement, Amazon said they could not send another and advised me to return it. If I wanted another keyboard, I would have to place a completely new order with a later delivery date.
I really like this keyboard overall. It has a great sound and a nice pop without being overly loud or disruptive. I also appreciate the 20+ lighting pattern options, though I do wish the lighting went through the tops of the keycaps like it does on my K2.
The major downside is my overall experience. For the price point, it has been extremely frustrating just trying to receive a fully functional, brand-new product. My older K2 keyboard worked perfectly fine and was less expensive but was not as customizable - this product should be customizable when it works, but I wanted to upgrade to a full-size keyboard.
At this point, I’m not sure I will reorder the Q6 Max due to the hassle involved. I’ve also seen other posts mentioning this same keyboard arriving with rocky or uneven-feeling keys or other problems. The first unit I received didn’t have that issue at all, which makes it even more disappointing that the problem with it was the non-working dongle and programming.
reviews.author: Renee

reviews.title: Replacing a Gen 1 - just as good as the OG
reviews.comment: I had a Gen 1 before this and it was my favorite mouse. I had to replace it because after years, the finish is starting to peel off under where my thumb rests and it became a sensory nightmare. I am extremely happy to find that this Gen 2 not only has a new finish, but also comes with a braided cord. For the price, this mouse is great quality. It's lightweight and just the perfect fit for my hand (size Large gloves). Functionality seems good, works just like my Gen 1 did. Only other change I've noticed so far is a brighter, more expansive underside RGB light.
reviews.author: Jamie

reviews.title: Durable and good quality. Connects like a dream
reviews.comment: Works well and haven’t had problems for the few months I’ve had it and I’m not very careful with it lol. Feels well and the quality is obviously good from my last statement.
reviews.author: Joel

reviews.title: Perfect gaming mouse for a great price
reviews.comment: My mouse wheel broke on my last steel series and I bought this to replace it. I absolutely love it and the mouse sensitivity that it has the presets for is perfect for me and my gaming.  And the size fits my hand perfectly as well.
reviews.author: KellyW

reviews.title: Unexpected Upgrade
reviews.comment: Needing a new mouse to replace my scuzzed up, bafflingly-pock-marked-rubber surface Corsair that was near-impossible to clean, and had the scroll wheel start to malfunction withing months, budget only allowed for a “cheapo” one I plan to use as a backup, thus, we get to this review. Yay: + Immediately more-favourable packaging experience. I had to break the Corsair out, while this came out without any issues at all. + Very light, which may be a con to some, but I found the other one's moment of inertia to be way too high. + Smooth plastic on all surfaces but the scroll wheel, meaning it can be wiped off, and cleaned to begin with. + Much better in-hand feel to me than the previous, this being an immediate “Oo!” + On that topic, the light immediately dazzled, with me not knowing just how dim my Corsair was. + Additionally, most of the lighting on this is actually visible, being under-lit, and thus having the one feature I liked of the Razer mouse I had. + Software, on that topic, was immediately more functional, and less convoluted than Razer Synapse, or Corsair Icue. + No “Sniper” button whose border was positioned right on my thumb pad. + Clicking with anything, causes a little wave to descend down the lights, this being the first peripheral I've ever owned to have such a feature. + Only $35 Manufacturer-Suggested Retail Price. + It feels much better to click, to me. + The sensor seems to really track 1:1, which, while this means it emphasised the shortcomings of the Corsair mat I have, the cursor outright stopping in 2 zones, I have faith this annoyance will turn into an advantage with a non-coated desk mat. Meh: ~ Had a bit of an issue getting accustomed to my mouse mat at first. ~ Does not include top lighting. ~ I suspect things will get into the body from around the scroll wheel. ~ Textured Rubber wheel. ~ No side-scrolling capacity. ~ No “infinite” scrolling, either. ~ Seems – in spite of the fact the setting for lines per tick is “3” still – to scroll less of the page than my Corsair. Nay: - Nothing, amazingly. Verdict: While I expected this to be better in some fashions, it – at least to me – being better in most of them was a deep surprise, and I look forward to seeing if the keyboard of theirs I'm getting will have the same “wow” factor as this. Highly-recommended.
reviews.author: Teominious

reviews.title: If you loved the 310, you probably won't like this. GG software invades your privacy now.
reviews.comment: Not a mouse for large hands, despite its visual appearance. It's very light weight, which isn't always a good thing. I'd prefer something a little heavier. Besides the small size, the paracord isn't a rubber cable wrapped in paracord, the wires are inside of the paracord, which is a mod some people started doing years ago. It's fine I guess. The "GG" software can apparently be turned off after you are satisfied with your profile which is saved to the mouse; it doesn't need to run all the time. However, the "GG" software itself has become a monstrosity of privacy invasive functionality. This is the primary reason for my 1 star rating. The old SteelSeries Engine isn't compatible with this mouse as it was released later. By default, screen and game capture, game auto-detection (scanning your computer for installed software), microphone recording, etc is all turned on by default. It also encourages you to create an online GG account, (which you can skip at the time of this review). Auto Run when Windows boots up is also turned on. I'd recommend you use a Virtual Machine with USB pass-through (Windows Sandbox can't do it) to install the software and configure the mouse. Either that or disconnect from the internet before installing it. This is just unacceptable and disgusting behavior by an increasing number of companies all looking to cash in on YOUR DATA. Children use these products. Reason I purchased this to begin with: I've owned the original Rival, Rival 300, and Rival 310, which has just now begun to fail on me. The mouse wheel skips and the middle mouse button double-clicks. I've tried most of the solutions and am quite familiar with how to repair mice and how the components work. Honestly I'm tired of taking mice apart to deal with the same issues that have plagued every plastic mouse since laser mice were invented. New Omron switches, feet, etc can quickly add up in cost due to markup prices unless you want to buy bulk switches. This replacement is a major disappointment. SteelSeries no longer produces the 310 so that wasn't an option. If you like this mouse, I recommend purchasing a dozen of them, because functionally perfect models of product tend to go away after a couple of years of production. They are at least still making the Apex line of keyboards. I packed this mouse up to keep it as an emergency spare, but I can't use something this small.
reviews.author: Anonymous User

reviews.title: This keyboard is Razor sharp.
reviews.comment: First off, this Razor Huntsman V3 Pro is a great keyboard, period! In 2015 I purchased a Logitech G910 Orion Spark. After a little over a year (as the warranty had expired), I had the left CTRL key cap break. I contacted Logitech, and to my surprise, they sent a complete key cap set for the keyboard. I was sold on Logitech after that. Time moved forward, and eventually, the keyboard started missing key strokes, where double and triple strokes on a letter became a sign that replacement was in order. Along with the Logitech keyboard, I purchased a Logitech mouse G502, which served well for over 10 years. The presets on the mouse started to bounce off my DPI settings, so I started researching keyboards and mice. I ordered a Logitech mouse G502 Hero since it received consistently good reviews. Unfortunately, the mouse wheel had a heavy spot, which would allow web pages to scroll without any input, so it was returned. I also purchased a Corsair K70 keyboard since the reviews were good. I liked the Cherry MX switches, yet the key caps do not cover the bottom of the switches. From the top looking down (which most pictures show) the RGB lighting looks good; however, from the front, it looks like little colored teeth shining from the bottom of the key caps, it just looks cheap.  The slope of the key caps from front to back was not constant. The wrist pad I read about was soft to the touch; somehow, Corsair found a way to make small triangles out of plastic feel soft and yet be as hard as a rock. So, I sent it back as well. Remember Razor? This is a review about Razor. This keyboard, Razor Huntsman V3 Pro, is great to type with and to game with as well. With the Synapse 4 program suite, it not only gives this keyboard life it also connects my new Razor Balilisk V3 35K mouse and Razor Hypersense headphones without a hitch. I've been a PC gamer since the 80's with my first PC, a 386 with 1 meg of sipp ram, 40 MB hard drive, and a 256K monitor. To date, this mouse and keyboard combo is the best I have purchased. I remember throwing quarters at Brick Breaker and Asteroids on a black and white screen. At 67, I game daily, you're never too old to game, and I'm always out of gum. :-)
reviews.author: Shindoru

reviews.title: Accidentally Funded an Esports Career
reviews.comment: I thought I was buying a keyboard. What I actually purchased was a glowing, clicky portal to another dimension where my son communicates exclusively in callouts like “HE’S ONE HP!” and “CLIP THAT!” First of all, this thing is TINY. It’s 60%, which apparently means 100% serious. No number pad. No wasted space. Just pure, compact, competitive energy. It’s so small it looks like it skips leg day — but don’t let that fool you. This keyboard means business. The keys? Lightning fast. I don’t know what “analog optical switches” are, but my son explained it to me with the intensity of a TED Talk. Something about actuation points and competitive advantage. All I know is he now blames losses on “ping” instead of his keyboard, so I guess it works. The RGB lighting is aggressive. This keyboard doesn’t glow — it announces itself. At night his room looks like a small but highly profitable nightclub. I’m half expecting a cover charge. Build quality? Solid. It sounds like tiny, confident raindrops when he types. Or like a very determined squirrel sending emails. Has it improved his gameplay? According to him, absolutely. According to his report card, we’re still evaluating performance metrics. Would I buy it again? Yes. Because if we’re going to hear rapid-fire clicking for hours, it might as well be on a keyboard that could qualify for the Olympics. Five stars. Zero stars for my electricity bill.
reviews.author: Joey Smith

reviews.title: Top-tier performance for competitive play
reviews.comment: I decided to pick this board up because I mainly play shooters and I was getting tired of my full-sized setup taking up so much mouse pad real estate. I wanted something that would give me more room to move without sacrificing the arrow keys, so this TKL layout seemed like the right middle ground. The switches are honestly the standout feature here. The analog optical triggers feel incredibly snappy, which is exactly what you need for competitive gaming. You can really feel the difference with the rapid trigger feature; it makes strafing and movement feel much more precise compared to a standard mechanical switch. The build itself is excellent, too. The doubleshot PBT keycaps have a nice texture that doesn't get slippery, and having the dedicated media dial and buttons right there is a convenient touch I use more than I expected. It is a very compact unit, which fits perfectly on my desk and clears up a ton of space. It feels premium and heavy enough to stay put during intense matches. If you are looking for a serious piece of gear to tighten up your movement in games, this is a fantastic option.
reviews.author: Troy

reviews.title: Great Gamer Keyboard!!
reviews.comment: My boyfriend loves his 60% keyboard! He’s a gamer so this keyboard gets used every single day. Gamer people know they need desk space to be able to move their mouse around freely without hitting the keyboard. This keyboard is a perfect size for gamers or even regular use if your limited desk space. It’s easy to use, set up and you can change the click sounds on the settings! The lights aren’t too bright either which I thought would be of concern but it isn’t a problem. You can also change the lights with several modes. It’s lightweight but durable! I also bought him the 60% arm rest from Razer. Great gift for a gamer of daily computer user.
reviews.author: Levanna Lopez

reviews.title: Great Keyboard untill an issue came up
reviews.comment: It's a great keyboard and I like the Huntsman line. This is my first Analog keyboard however (it's honestly a hybrid keyboard, more info later in my review). Tried SnapTap feature once and stopped using it due to how it's messing me up in terms of fine grain movements. It's a me user error than the keyboard itself. Typing on it feels the same as any other keyboard, although I feel like it is a slught improvement to the previous one I bought (Huntsman V2 TKL). Same sound for mechanical keys. Nothing's different imo. This is where the problem with any Razer products. You really need Razer Synapses to do any changes you want with the keyboard. It isn't really easy to use to get to where you want with this keyboard. Sadly, I'm still using the default profile and haven't looked back at it. Too sensitive and i have issues . SnapTap again is a user issue for me. Keyboard has great functionalities but it's more of a niche case for me. It will be different for everyone else. The cool thing about with this keyboard that it is analog which can be turned into like a controller. When it mentions Analog, this keyboard is a hybrid keyboard. Typing and controller. A lot of games will recognize tbe keyboard as typing by default and analog if you set your profile to that. Ohhh boy, one game does NOT recognize the keyboard as a keyboard. That is Skyrim. Skyrim treats this keyboard as a physical controller and will overtake ANY AND ALL peripherals! From what I read from previous experience, this issue has not been fixed on Razer side. It does not feel great that you have to physically disable the "Xbox Controller for Windows" device and reboot. Or simply use another keyboard just to play Skyrim. I'm not sure about other games that have the same issue, but very noticable on that one particular game. Is it worth buying this keyboard? I guess if you are a Razer fan and like the feature it offers. Huntsman line is really good and I will always like the value of it. But do check if the features are worth it for your case before buying it. I only knocked a star off because of how this keyboard can sometimes be treated as controller in some areas when typing is currently set and how Razer didn't really fix the issue (they never bothered to look at it) since V2 from researching about it.
reviews.author: Shiny

reviews.title: Epomaker TH99 PRO Review: Versatile, Rock Solid, THOCK!
reviews.comment: The TH99 PRO from Epomaker is a keyboard with a lot to offer for the price you pay, including unique features and solid fundamental components. I recommend it most strongly to productivity users, however, gamers and keyboard enthusiasts alike will still find that the TH99 PRO to be a compelling option. With a coupon, the TH99 PRO is available for $76.50 before tax at the time of writing this review. Opening the box, the TH99 PRO comes with a combination keycap and switch puller, a USB-C cable, spare switches, and some literature. The manual included is a “quick start guide,” however, a full manual in multiple languages is available online. This is also where the software for the keyboard is available to access and download. I highly recommend anyone picking up this keyboard to visit Epomaker’s website to access all of the materials available. For keycaps, what you see already on the board is what you get. If you bought the black and grey colorway like I did, there are no black keycaps to replace the alternately colored arrow keys, enter keys, and escape key. I like the way these keycaps look, but if you don’t, keep that in mind before ordering. The doubleshot PBT keycaps feature walls 1/16” (~1.6mm) thick and bottom out with a satisfying, bassy thock. This is especially true for the stabilized keys, such as space and backspace. Speaking of stabilizers, the included plate-mounted stabilizers are fantastic. Anyone who has had to disassemble their keyboard to clip and lubricate their stabilizers can breathe a sigh of relief with the TH99 PRO, as the stabs are already lubricated and feature no rattling or clicking. The spacebar feels and sounds consistent, no matter where your thumb lands to strike the key. None of the stabs feel sluggish due to over-lubrication. In terms of switches, I went with Creamy Jades, and I’m very satisfied with their performance. These prelubed switches are smooth, responsive, and consistent. I found the 45gf trigger force to be a sweet spot in terms of smoothness and sensitivity. Especially lightweight linear switches can be too sensitive and trigger when you’re resting your fingertips on the keycaps, but the Creamy Jades do not suffer from this issue. And at the end of the day, if you find switches you like better or want to try something entirely different, the hotswap PCB is compatible with both 3 and 5 pin switches. The overall construction of the keyboard is rock solid. There are no rattling or loose parts. When typing, there is no hollowness or reverb from empty space inside the case. This is because there’s no empty space between any of the components whatsoever. The TH99 PRO features a multilayered sound dampening system, including poron foam, switch/socket pads, and a gasket mount. The software for the TH99 PRO opens in your web browser, so you don’t need to install an .exe file to make and save changes to the keyboard. Make sure your browser can access HID devices on your machine. Not only can you reassign individual keys, but you can also change the function layer. If you want to change the FN key combo to switch between Bluetooth devices, for example, you can do so. Macro creation is available here as well. You can also customize the GIF that plays on the keyboard’s screen with the software. I recommend GIFs with perfect loops and large objects. I used a program in safe mode to confirm that the TH99 PRO really does poll at 1000hz in USB and 2.4GHz mode. See screenshot in my attached pictures. In summary, the TH99 PRO is a versatile keyboard that gives users of all kinds a superior typing experience out of the box, and includes features that allow for further customization and personalization in the future. For the price, it’s a compelling offering by Epomaker.
reviews.author: C.

reviews.title: Perfect keyboard
reviews.comment: Absolutely love this keyboard. I wasn't sure I'd like the blue keys because I've never been a fan of blue, but I love purple. I wanted this because I've heard good things about the brand Epomaker so I gave it a shot. The blue is actually beautiful. I got a purple mouse, wrist rest, & mouse pad & it made the purple keys pop more. The keys feel nice under your fingers when typing & omg the sound.. it's creamy but a little clacky at the same time. It is loud so keep that in mind. But I prefer loud keyboards, the sound is soothing to me like ASMR lol. The software it comes with is easy to use, I just plugged my keyboard in & went to the website it gives you a qr code for & connected. So many different options & colors for the lights. The lights stand out beautifully, even in bright fluorescent office lights..you just can't see them good in my picture. Right now I have mine on the flower petal mode with rainbow colors. You can even upload gifs to put on the little screen it has on the top left, or you can have it just display the time & battery life. I have a gif of a cat typing lol. Comes with everything you need. USB cord, Bluetooth connection, extra switches, & the key/switch remover so you can swap them out for more customization. Overall this is the best keyboard I've ever had. Quality is great so I think it'll last a long time. In comparison to other brands & considering all of the features, it's a really good deal for the money. Highly recommend!
reviews.author: Megan Bowden

reviews.title: Excellent 96% Keyboard Quiet, Smart, and Amazing Battery!
reviews.comment: I recently purchased the EPOMAKER TH99 PRO and I am very satisfied. The 96% layout is perfect because it saves desk space while still having the numpad, which is a huge plus for me. The RGB lighting looks great on my desk. One smart feature I really like is the power management: if the keyboard isn't connected via dongle or Bluetooth, the RGB lights stay on for just a few seconds and then turn off automatically. This is a very smart way to prevent the battery from draining for no reason. The Sea Salt Silent switches sound great and are very comfortable to use. They aren't annoying or distracting at all, which is exactly what I like. The 10,000mAh battery is very powerful and lasts much longer than any other wireless keyboard I have used. The screen and knob are easy to use and customize with the driver. Also, the 2.4GHz connection is stable with no lag. Thanks to Amazon, we have easy access to technology and can order exactly what we want. A big thanks to the Amazon team for combining trust and quality! Your success is well-deserved. They have earned our trust with high-quality service over the years. I highly recommend this to everyone.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Honestly obsessed with this keyboard
reviews.comment: I’ve been using the EPOMAKER TH99 PRO for a while now, and I’m genuinely impressed. The typing experience feels amazing, super smooth, soft, and satisfyingly “thocky” without being loud or harsh. It’s comfortable enough for long work sessions and still great for gaming. The screen and knob are surprisingly useful. I love being able to quickly check battery, time, and adjust volume without leaving what I’m doing. Battery life is also excellent, I rarely think about charging it, even with RGB on. The 96% layout is the perfect balance between compact and functional. You still get a numpad, but it doesn’t feel bulky on the desk. The PBT keycaps feel premium and don’t get that greasy shine over time. Overall, it feels premium and fun to use. Zero regrets buying this, easily one of my favorite desk upgrades.
reviews.author: YK

reviews.title: Creamy jade is top stuff.
reviews.comment: Creamy jade switches are amazing. An awesome typing experience with perfectly tuned sound and feel. The injection molding quality on the PBT caps is spot on, very high quality and precise. Case is ABS plastic with no visible screws. Plate is HDPE on top of a 7 layer damping material sandwich that works perfectly. Clearly a lot of thought has gone in to this! Lighting is also highly configurable with the online utility. Separate zones can be changed for the board, and back light strip. It's extremely easy to upload .gif images with no software download necessary. Wireless works flawlessly too with incredible battery life. In general these boards are such an incredible value compared to established PC gaming brands it's wild. If you're looking for an efficient full size board, you cannot go wrong with this. Seriously, the online configuration tool works instantly and is incredibly easy to use. Genuinely great.
reviews.author: Parker

reviews.title: Review of the Razer Basilisk V3 Pro 35K Wireless Gaming Mouse
reviews.comment: I recently purchased the Razer Basilisk V3 Pro 35K Wireless Gaming Mouse from Amazon, and I couldn’t be happier with my choice. This mouse has exceeded my expectations in terms of quality, performance, and ergonomics. Exceptional Quality The build quality of the Basilisk V3 Pro is outstanding. It feels solid and well-constructed, which is essential for a gaming mouse that’s meant to endure hours of use. The materials used are top-notch, providing a premium feel that enhances the overall experience. Ergonomics One of the standout features of this mouse is its ergonomic design. It fits perfectly in my hand, making long gaming sessions comfortable. The shape and grip are well thought out, allowing for precise movements without causing fatigue. Performance I’ve been using this mouse for some time now, and I’ve encountered no issues with response time. The tracking is incredibly accurate, which is crucial for competitive gaming. I’ve noticed a significant improvement in my gameplay, thanks to the reliable performance of this mouse. Battery Life The battery life is impressive as well. Depending on my usage, it lasts up to two days or even three, which is fantastic for a wireless device. I appreciate not having to constantly recharge it, allowing me to focus on my gaming sessions. Features and Software The Basilisk V3 Pro comes packed with features that enhance its functionality. I downloaded the Razer software, which was straightforward and user-friendly. Customizing settings and adjusting performance options is a breeze, allowing me to tailor the mouse to my preferences. Final Thoughts Overall, the Razer Basilisk V3 Pro 35K Wireless Gaming Mouse is a quality investment for any gamer. With its excellent ergonomics, reliable performance, and impressive battery life, it has become an indispensable part of my gaming setup. I highly recommend this mouse to anyone looking for a high-performance gaming accessory!
reviews.author: Jason Youngblood

reviews.title: Great product
reviews.comment: Definitely recommend this mouse it has supper fast response time and no input delay despite the wireless connection. Supper smooth click feed back. Tactile wheel and it has a convenient button to make the scroll wheel not clicky and just a free spin. And if I don't want to use it wirelessly the mouse can be used wired.  And I always leave the mouse on and after a few minutes the mouse will go to sleep and not use power almost like a standby phase definitely worth the price
reviews.author: carlos

reviews.title: One of the best gaming mice I've ever used
reviews.comment: I had a really old Logitech mouse and was overdue for an upgrade. I game a lot and have bigger hands, so I spent some time researching, trying to find something that wouldn't result in cramps or awkward grips. I know the fit comes down to grip style, but I never gave it much thought before this purchase. I noticed that my hand very naturally met the form of the mouse, and it stays comfortable to use throughout the day. I will work for a full 8 hours and then spend a few hours in the evening gaming, and it just feels great. I use it with the wireless charging hub, and I have no issues with latency or lag. The charge will last for multiple days if I forget to set it on the charging dock overnight. The mouse feels sturdy and firm with a good weight to it. Never too heavy or cumbersome. The wheel scroll is clean and it has just the right amount of extra buttons for productivity and gaming macros. 100% reccomend.
reviews.author: Christian J. Estrada

reviews.title: Nice mouse for most users.
reviews.comment: Finding a mouse that will work well without loading down the computer with excess software can be a challenge. I replaced my logi gaming mouse with this one so I could offload the logi software. I does mouse things well. I can use this mouse for extended periods in comfort. I don't play competitive PVP games and have noticed no lag or response times issues in any of the games I do play. I can't say much about using it wireless for competitive shooters. PROS: ergonomic enough, good response time with no noticeable lag in wireless mode CONS: battery life is acceptable, not great. I do recommend this mouse. Good value and I would buy it again.
reviews.author: Topwatch

reviews.title: Get it if its what you're looking for.
reviews.comment: I love it. I don't prefer very light mice, i find the weight to be perfect for me. I have the non 35k version too and its held up, and the batteries do last pretty long on the basilisks mice. Clicks are good. Scroll wheel is somewhat gimmicky and usless, but the tilt wheel comes in handy for gaming. Skates are ok, not the best for the price, but its not an issue. The phantom white looks nice. I seen other users have issues with the rubber grips over time getting smashed in, but my non k model has held up good I dont squeeze them to d**th though. Haven't had the phantom white long enough to see.  Wireless works flawless so far, i don't expect problems with any basilisks mice.
reviews.author: A

reviews.title: New main. Excellent mouse with a ridiculous battery life
reviews.comment:
The box didn't have much protection, but it arrived in great condition. As for the mouse itself, it is amazing.
I won't talk much about shape because that's highly subjective (I'll just say it fits my hand size and grip style), but everything else is excellent: coating is smooth and grippy, very nice to the touch; main clicks are light and tactile, tho they could have a little less post travel; side buttons are well tensioned and positioned; the wheel might be the weakest aspect, because the scrolling feels a bit off, but it's totally functional; M3 click is very tactile; skates are smooth and fast; build quality is perfect, solid as a rock; performance is top tier, no complaints; and finally, the battery is absolutely insane. I have been using the mouse for 12 days at 1000hz (sometimes 8000, but only for a couple of Apex matches) and it has only gone down to 60%.
On top of all of that, Razer has finally made a web software. That means 2 things: 1) you don't have to deal with the bloatware that is Synapse (except for firmware updates); and 2) you can change your settings on Linux, which has been a game changer for me (I dual boot Windows 11 and Bazzite).
I think it is worth the price, but only if you don't have a Viper V3 Pro (or even a Viper V3 Pro SE). On paper, the V4 Pro has many improvements, but the only real upgrade that a player will notice is the battery life and the web software. I recommend it to people who have never owned a Viper V3 and want the latest technology and power efficiency. I can recommend it to those who just want to try the shape, but they might also want to take a look at the V3 Pro, since it is cheaper right now.
reviews.author: Marco

reviews.title: Worthy of the praise
reviews.comment:
I have been using it a full week now, and I think it's worth all the praise. It's a safe shape that will work for everyone except if your hands are on the smaller side. Switches, side buttons, scroll wheel, and sensor all feel perfect. My honest favorite thing about this mouse is the battery life is otherworldly good compared to anything I have used. I likely won't have to charge it until about 5-6 weeks of moderate to heavy use at 1000Hz, which is huge when I need to charge my other mice practically after a weekend.
The first negative is the price is steep, especially when you could get the V3 Pro Se for like have the price. Two, the M1/M2 switches are on the loud side, but you won't notice them with headphones. You will annoy anyone around you though if they have to listen to you click. Three, the black version is a bit of an oil magnet, but the coating at least feels good. Might be worth using either Razer's provided grips or another brands for long-term use.
Overall, it's a very good mouse if it's within your price range, and your hands are moderately large in size. Maybe it's placebo, but I also dropped my first nuke in Call of Duty on keyboard and mouse using it. That might be influencing might personal opinion of it, but I promise it's a great mouse.
reviews.author: Nick

reviews.title: it’s the best mouse i’ve used
reviews.comment: i’ve used a few different mice for gaming but honestly this one has the edge. it’s light and smooth and feels super comfortable. insane battery life too. the build feels firm and is honestly at a reasonable price for how good it is.
reviews.author: Mikey Ellsworth

reviews.title: Love this mouse!
reviews.comment: The mouse is fantastic. It feels good in the hand, extremely light, buttons are very snappy, movement is extremely responsive, software is good. I honestly had a really good mouse already, but it was a little older and about 100 grams. With this mouse being half the weight I thought I’d treat myself and I’m glad I did. This thing is just great, 180 hr battery at 1000 Hz, but I really like the dynamic sensitivity. My previous mouse didn’t have that and I didn’t know what I was missing. Overall I was skeptical because of the price but I’m glad I bit the bullet and bought it.
reviews.author: Matthew

reviews.title: Excellent gaming mouse
reviews.comment:
This is an excellent mouse and the clicks are very satisfying but some may think it’s too loud but for me it is isn’t.
The software is now web based so no more intrusive synapse soft ware and that’s what really sold it for me and on top of that it’s a really fast mouse and the battery level is just amazing.
I highly recommend this mouse!!
reviews.author: Justin B.

reviews.title: The perfect peripheral
reviews.comment:
I have long fingers but a narrow hand, so the skinny shape and low profile allows me to fingertip grip pretty well while still offering enough key anchor points to feel secure. Weight is great, just light enough to still feel substantial, and the distribution is perfect for my preference. I'm incredibly impressed by how sturdy it feels despite the weight, no creaking no matter how hard you squeeze the sides and the buttons have no real wobble. 8k might be a gimmick but whatever, no battery to burn through so you can just leave it on. With a mouse bungee you hardly even notice the cable.
More than anything though, just from the software alone I'd give this 10 stars if I could. One app with two pages of settings, no account sign up bs, no dynamic profile macro garbage, you just pick your settings and save it to the hardware. In and out in 2 minutes. With all the bloated garbage that big peripheral companies subject you to just to configure your mouse, this is a breath of fresh air that I can't praise enough. And all this for less than the big brands charge? It's a no brainer. As long as you're not obsessed with rgb, endgame makes THE mice to buy.
reviews.author: Reya

reviews.title: OP1 8Kv2 goat mouse
reviews.comment:
After trying out a lot of different mice over the years, I can confidently say that this mouse is one of the best made that I have ever tried.
The build quality on the mouse is phenomenal, with no creaking or any points where the mouse feels cheaply made. There are a lot of thoughtful touches on this mouse that not many others do, with the stock skates allowing for easy access to the screws that allow the mouse to be opened up. The mouse clicks are hot-swappable as well so if anything ever breaks, it is really cheap to repair anything that can go wrong.
This mouse also is the best mouse in terms of performance. The mouse has the lowest or one of the lowest click latencies out there with each click registering in microseconds, which is basically instant. This feature is called gx speed mode. There are also a lot of features that comes with the firmware/software to help maximize the performance of the clicks and sensor.
The weight is also not too bad with it coming in at around ~49.5g which is definitely considered lightweight.
In conclusion, I feel like this mouse is a perfect fit for those who really want a mouse that comes in at a very respectable price with performance that shoots well above its price point.
reviews.author: Dylan Pangilinan

reviews.title: Op18kv2 Gaming Mouse.
reviews.comment:
Shipped Fast. Came in sooner then Amazons delivery date. Awesome mouse! Thanks!
Op18kv2 Gaming Mouse:
Size: Medium - (still fit my Large hand pretty good)
Weight: Very light feels almost weightless
Speed: top tier responsiveness while gaming
Quality: For a gaming mouse it’s probably perfect
Clicking: All bottoms are satisfying with clicking
Software: The least likable thing. VERY BASIC.
I’d say my Razor Basilisk v3 Gen3 is definitely more comfortable, but the Op18kv2 performs better while gaming. Also Razor’s Software for customizing your mouse and gameplay is LEAGUES above Endgames. But it’s not for all gamers because the software will run your pc a little heavier if you have a weak or outdated build. Endgames is very basic and more universal for everyone to use with almost no CPU usage at all.
reviews.author: D & J

reviews.title: OP1 Review by a real gamer
reviews.comment:
I've mained this mouse for about 3 weeks now.
It's a very good mouse, I've used plenty such as GPX2 , Viper V3 Pro, Pulsar X2 CL. It's value for quality and performance is unrivaled. I have medium sized hands, it fits better with the GPX / V3 Pro, but I still found the shape to be atleast top 3 i've used, I have palm contact and I can use relaxed claw / fingertip hybrid while not sacrificing stability.
However, it still is a wired mouse. If you're wanting to purchase this based off aim training people like Viscose, please keep this in mind. The wire is not heavy, it's quite flexible and paired with a bungee you do forget about it after a while, but switching back to a wireless mouse, it's very obvious. The 'freedom' you feel on wireless can never be replicated on a wired mouse, even if you strip off the cable jacket.
The performance is amazing, and the shape is good, but it's definitely NOT for everyone with medium+ sized hands, it will 100% take some time getting used to. My suggestion is you either hardcore main this mouse or you'll switch back to wireless within a couple weeks.
reviews.author: Jack

reviews.title: New main mouse.
reviews.comment:
Bought cause I always wanted an op1. Lucked out waiting and skipped the virus scandal that happened with their software. Non- invasive setup software where you can get really deep with the settings. Very responsive, small and Very light (Attack shark R6 v2 feels almost the same . R6 is lighter ) . Build
Quality is amazing .skates are pretty meh though. Get some hyperstars.
reviews.author: Telvin tucker

reviews.title: Amazing!
reviews.comment: I got this for my son about 2 years ago and it still works perfectly! It is so comfortable and soft. The sound quality is amazing! My son says he almost never has to charge it due to the long battery life. It was well worth it.
reviews.author: WineLady

reviews.title: Must buy better then more expensive headphones
reviews.comment: Had some connection issues, use the phone app instead to update and later deleted it from my phone which fixed the problem. Sound is amazing and so is the battery life. For this price point I was not expecting it to be a top competitor since it is cheaper then most so a lot of value for money. Very light weight, comfortable, and functions at peak. Would recommend.
reviews.author: Sarkawt  Hamad

reviews.title: Awful connectivity
reviews.comment:
These headphones are a great price. The sound quality (when they work) is really good for the price. They are very lightweight and not uncomfortable.
Now for the bad; They don't work, or rather they stop working and need to be rebooted/connected or require a computer restart daily. I wear a headset a LOT, 3+ hours per day at a minimum. I have had these for 3-4 days and am returning them. I primarily used these headphones with my desktop PC using the 2.4 ghz wireless connection.
Just before writing this review I sat down and put these on my head and for the third day in a row they just don't work. I have to open volume mixer and make sure they are still connected, then turn the headphones off and unplug the dongle. Today I did all of that stuff and they still don't work. The volume knob is adjusted to max volume and the PC sound works fine out of the speakers if I swap to them. They are in wireless mode and the dongle shows a "green" connected light. On paper everything is working, but no sound. I worked for a decade in PC shops building custom PC's, helpdesk, virus removals, upgrades, etc. if you have to be more knowledgeable than me to get these things to work the problem isn't the consumer.
reviews.author: cody basham

reviews.title: Excelente vendedor
reviews.comment: Los mejores para jugar los recomiendo mucho
reviews.author: Michael

reviews.title: SO COMFY!
reviews.comment: Best headphones I’ve ever used. So comfy too
reviews.author: Alex

reviews.title: WOW- these are amazing- HUGE upgrade over the v2
reviews.comment: TLDR: These are the best deal in gaming headsets right now just make sure to download the THX spatial software to really get the most out of them. It makes a HUGE difference! Trust me, it's worth registering to get the activation code. I had the blackshark v2 for a couple of years and loved them. They were just solid wireless gaming headset. They sounded good enough, the mic was good enough to use at work too, and the battery life lasted all day easily. Sadly, my puppy decided to make them a chew toy so they are in headset heaven now. R.I.P.  I liked them so much I was honestly considered just ordering another pair lol When I searched for them I saw there was a new version! This got me to research what's new in the gaming headset world. Review after review, article after article, spoke VERY highly of these. My research led me to deciding between these, the v3 pro's , and the Audeze maxwell (I am a sucker for Magnar Planar headphones).  All the reviews I read stated the only real difference between these and the Pro's is the ANC (noise cancelation) and that they sound virtually identical otherwise. So that left me with these or the Audeze and for HALF the cost of the Maxwell's I figured I'd order these to try em out and if they weren't good enough I'd just get the Maxwell's (I KNOW those sound amazing they're just heavy lol). Now that I've done some testing let me tell you these are INCREDIBLE. I am SHOCKED at what a massive upgrade they are from the Blackshark V2's. I was pretty happy with those and these are drastically better. The ear cups are much more comfortable, the sound stage is insanely good for closed back cans, bluetooth WITH simultanious sound capability (you can connect to bluetooth AND 2.4ghz wireless at the same time. So you could listen to tunes from your phone while gaming on ur pc/ps5/switch/xbox. AT THE SAME TIME.),  the addition of THX spatial surround sound is a GAME CHANGER , and they still do all the things the V2 did great as well like all day comfort, light weight, great comfy design, the fantastic "knob" , and all day+ battery life. I do mean ALL DAY plus too. I work from home using them a solid 9 hours every day then immediately fire up my gaming pc lol so the avg day is 10 hours at least and I've never once even gotten a low battery warning let alone having them die. Now, I need to mention you absolutely MUST download the THX spatial sound app if you have windows 11. I know it's annoying but it is a massive improvement. It is not some meaningless gimmick that software takes this headset from "yeah that's alright" to "WOW. That is INCREDIBLE". The quick profiles are VERY noticeable. The bass boost actually does something meaningful to the sub bass (not just cause muddled nonsense lol) . Turning on THX Spacial and watching a movie with these really feels like being at the theatre. The sound stage is wild for a closed back gaming headset. If you are into nice headphones you know how much better the sound stage is on open back headphones and while yes, this isn't quite that, it is one of the best I've ever experienced from a "gaming headset" let alone one that is only $150. AND IT'S WIRELESS!? Games are just as amazing. The details , sound stage, and again surround sound is fantastic. I know EXACTLY where those footsteps and gun fire are coming from. Explosions are FULL and ear shaking. The volume on these is also very good. Normally I am a "crank it" listener but with these at 70% i'm tapping out lol Music sounds full and detailed on this headset. I typically use speakers or my nicer plug in amp/cans for music but these are actually good enough I don't IMMEDIATELY reach for them like I have for the past few years lol The bass on these is pretty solid and it does an impressive job at allowing the each sound/instrument have it's own "lane" in the sound stage. There is very very minimal "muddying" when you have the music EQ dialed in. Overall, if you're looking for a new headset OR having an aging wireless headset from the previous generation (v2, arctis 7, Hyper cloud alpha, A50, etc)  I HIGHLY recommend you at least give these a try because you will not find anything remotely close at this price. To find a higher quality set you're going to spend at least twice as much and they tend to be quite a bit heavier which is a bit rough for long sessions. If you need noise cancelation or the upgraded mic then spend the extra $100 on the Pro's but if you don't NEED those 2 features save the $ and buy these. I really can't see how anyone could be disappointed with these if they are using the THX app and dialing in the EQ these bad boys absolutely SHINE. Just order them already and thank me later.
reviews.author: Tred009

reviews.title: Impressive sound and mic quality, connectivity and battery life
reviews.comment: I spent WAY too much time researching headsets and finally settled on this one. I have enough high end headphones to have been pretty impressed with the sound quality but I’m MOST impressed with the connectivity options. reviews.author: Andoresu

reviews.title: Finally a New Generation of Good Headphones
reviews.comment: Bought this on a a few weeks after I returned a Logitech Pro X (terrible sound quality and surround sound) and the refund finally came in. I had no idea a new generation of Razer headsets were coming out, and only came across it because I had to wait for the refund. That being said, this was my first time buying a wireless headset (usually only do wired), and I could only find one review on Google for it and it's high range version that said it was good, so I decided to take a chance. Let me tell you, I AM BLOWN AWAY. The sound quality on this beats the G Pros that I returned prior, especially with THX Spatial Audio on, and as my ears have acclimated to them, I can honestly say the sound quality is better than my HyperX Cloud Alpha S that I had before that (and I LOVED that headset). Battery life is also really good, I have yet to have it die on me while in use, and will last even 100+ hours if you turn off the ultra-low latency 10ms setting (they claim 70-80 hours with it on)., and if you don't play competitive games, you might as well turn it off since it's still very low latency regardless. I was a little worried about comfort at first because I have a big head, and while I will say it's not quite as comfortable as my HyperX Cloud Alphas, that's a high bar anyways since that headset sets the golden standard for comfort with gaming headsets. I've worn it for 3-4+ hour straight and I can safely say that I notice no discomfort even after long sessions. I even find myself walking around doing housework with them because it's that comfortable. Going back to the THX Spatial Audio, it does require you to use Razer's software, Synapse, which I know has a checkered past, and a reputation for bloatware (I used a Razer mouse prior, and I would always turn it off), but I was pleasantly surprised to see that Razer seems to have updated the software so it's far more use friendly, and MUCH less intensive to run in the background that it used to be. In addition, for the headphones themselves, the EQ adjuster within Synapse is actually pretty good, and does a good job of helping you clearly understand when your changing the highs, lows, mid-range, etc., and they have some pretty good presets too. They even have specific custom THX presets for supported games too like Baldur's Gate 3, Elden Ring, and a lot more that actually make the game sound pretty incredible, and I would 100% recommend using that feature if you get these headphones. All in all, I've been very pleasantly surprised with these headphones, it's really nice to see a new headphone generation finally release, and not just the same rehashed models that came out 6 years ago. And for coming in the mid-range slot of this generation, I would say it's the best you can get at this price point without spending another $100-$150 for the high-range version, or other similarly priced headphones, but while also still getting some of the premium features that you wouldn't get with the budget Hyperspeed version.

reviews.title: Battery, sound and comfort all in one right here!
reviews.comment: The HyperX Cloud III S Wireless is an astonishing product. I have the OG Cloud III Wireless and they're amazing themselves. Very immersive for all 3. Makes gaming more interactive and helpful hearing stuff in a 360 degree radius. Helpful for competitive FPS multi-player. Seriously, don't consider anything else. These are worth it. Just get them and be Seriously imoressed!! A MUST BUY!!
