reviews.title: Great case!
reviews.comment: Have been turned off by all the plastic on Fractal’s other cases, but this one is nearly all metal and I love the integrated look of the fans.  Beautiful case with plenty of room for whatever you want to throw in it!  Appreciate the metal upper mesh panel—was a nice surprise.  Would have preferred 4-pin fans, but the 3-pin fans it came with are working well and nice and quiet.  Would also love to see integrated vertical mount capability in a case like this, so adding a big bulky bolt on wouldn’t be necessary to show off your video card.  Overall good build quality and I would recommend if you like the fishbowl style of this case!
reviews.author: Lucas Fisher

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.comment: Love it. Super easy to build. Love the pre installed fans.
reviews.author: June Mathews

reviews.title: Beautiful Case With a Classic Wood Design and Great Functionality
reviews.comment:
I used this case for my custom PC build and I absolutely love it. What originally drew me to it was the design. The wood front immediately reminded me of my dad’s old stereo cabinet, and that warm brown wood detail gives the case a very clean and classic look that stands out from typical gaming cases.
Beyond the looks, the build experience was excellent. I was able to fit an AIO cooler and a full sized graphics card with no issues at all. There was plenty of room to work in, and everything felt well thought out during installation.
The case also has a lot of great features that make building and maintaining a system easier. Airflow is solid, cable management is straightforward, and the overall construction feels sturdy and high quality. It manages to look stylish without sacrificing performance or practicality.
If you want a case that combines modern PC functionality with a timeless design, this one is an excellent choice. It looks great in a room and performs just as well as it looks.
reviews.author: Jakari Jones

reviews.title: ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ This Case Made My First PC Build Feel Like a Premium Showcase
reviews.comment:
I honestly couldn’t have picked a better case for my first PC build.
The Fractal North is technically a mid-tower, but once you start building in it, it feels incredibly spacious. There’s plenty of room for a full-size GPU, large air cooler, and clean airflow paths without ever feeling cramped or awkward. Everything fits exactly how you want it to.
The design is what initially sold me—and it looks even better in person. The modern, minimalist aesthetic paired with the real wood slat front panel is stunning. It’s understated, mature, and premium without screaming “gaming PC.” This is a case you’re proud to display, not hide under a desk.
Cable management is excellent. The layout, tie-down points, and space behind the motherboard tray make it easy to get a clean, professional look—even for a first-time builder. You can see from my build how well everything routes and disappears. On top of that, it’s incredibly easy to maintain: dust filters are accessible, panels come off smoothly, and cleaning doesn’t feel like a chore.
Airflow has been fantastic. I’m running a full-size GPU and a large dual-fan air cooler, and temps stay consistently solid. I liked the case so much that I even designed and 3D-printed a custom bottom piece to improve GPU airflow while hiding cables—and the case handled that customization beautifully. It invites creativity.
I’ve owned this case since August 2025, and it’s been rock solid long-term. No rattles, no flex, no regrets. This was my first PC build, but it absolutely won’t be my last—and I can confidently say it won’t be the last time I choose Fractal for a case.
If you care about design, airflow, build quality, and actually enjoying the build process, this case is an easy recommendation.
Fractal nailed it. 🔥
reviews.author: Luke McKinnon

reviews.title: A premium quality case with great features and lots of room.
reviews.comment: I needed a good size case with lots of room for a work machine running a I-9 Core 285k with a Nvidia 5070ti. This case is very roomy and is very easy to use without cutting your hands up. The airflow is excellent with my temps well within expected ranges. It isn't cheap but you get what you pay for. Everything feels solidly built and very premium. While it wasn't a big consideration for me, if you like a mid century modern design, this case has a beautiful look that appears like a piece of fine furniture.
reviews.author: sonik

reviews.title: Beauty meets brains, with just enough brawn
reviews.comment:
I have built in many cases and the North still feels special. The genuine walnut slats on the front, the dark tinted tempered glass, and the brushed accents give it a furniture grade vibe that actually looks at home in a living room or studio. Airflow is strong for a design first chassis, cable management is painless, and the build quality is exactly what you expect from Fractal. It is solid, thoughtful, and quiet.
I did squeeze an ASUS ROG Astral RTX 5090 in here. It fits but it is right at the envelope. If you are running a 360 mm front radiator or an especially long or thick 5090, expect careful measuring and some compromises. The fact that it can be done in a compact mid tower with real wood aesthetics is impressive.
What I loved
- Stunning design that does not scream gamer. Real walnut front, dark tinted glass, clean lines
- Excellent airflow for the size. Open front plus fine mesh, two 140 mm Aspect PWM fans included
- Easy build experience. Removable panels, smart cable routing, captive screws where it matters
- Modern I O. Front USB C Gen 2x2 alongside dual USB A and audio
- Versatile cooling. Up to 360 mm front radiator, 240 mm top with RAM clearance to check, 120 mm rear
- Respectable GPU support for a mid tower. Up to 355 mm with front fans with careful planning for big 4000 and 5000 series cards
- Quiet out of the box. Sensible fan tuning and airflow path keep noise restrained
What could be better
- Tight for ultra flagship GPUs. 5090 class cards fit but it is a squeeze. Front AIOs reduce clearance further
- Limited PSU and HDD space combo. Long PSUs with dual HDD trays can get cramped
- Top radiator RAM clearance. Tall RAM and thick top radiators can clash. Measure before you commit
- No fan hub in the TG version. The Mesh variant typically fares better here. Plan motherboard headers accordingly
- Glass version has fewer total fan mounts than the Mesh. If maximum airflow is your priority then consider the Mesh side panel
Build notes and tips if you are pushing big GPUs
- Measure twice and mount once. The case supports GPUs up to around 355 mm with front fans installed. If you add a 360 mm front radiator the effective GPU length drops noticeably. Look up your specific GPU length and cooler thickness before buying
- Consider air cooling or a top mounted 240 mm AIO if you are using a very long GPU. This preserves front clearance
- Keep PSU length modest if you need both HDD trays installed. Shorter PSUs make cabling and airflow easier
- Use low profile or standard height RAM if you plan a top radiator to avoid clearance headaches
Verdict
The North Charcoal Black TG Dark blends premium and timeless design with competent thermals and a smooth build experience. If you want a PC that looks as good as it runs and you are willing to plan your component sizes it is fantastic. For maximal airflow or the absolute largest GPUs without compromises the Mesh version or the larger North XL are worth a look. As a tasteful and compact mid tower that can still handle a powerful build the North is a winner.

reviews.title: So much better than a stock AMD cooler!
reviews.comment: Ok, let's be honest...this is an absolute insane deal for a CPU cooler. Does it perform as good as something that costs 3-4 times as much? I built a PC for my nephew using an AMD Ryzen 5 3600 CPU and I was forced to use the stock AMD wraith stealth cooler that came with it. Then I came across this cooler a few months ago and I was astonished at how cheap it was. I wanted to give it some time and wait for some reviews to be submitted before I ultimately decided to purchase it. After seeing some YouTubers review it, I decided to save up some money (all $17) and just buy it. Here's my thoughts so far: - Aluminum heatsink fins do seem a bit flimsy and you have to be very careful when installing to not accidentally bend one of them. - I like how it included an extra set of clips in case you wanted to get a second fan to stick on the other side of the heatsink. Making this cooler a dual fan solution might be a good experiment in the future. - The temps did change considerably after installation. Not only did the CPU temps decrease by 10-12 degrees at load but the ambient temps in the case changed as well since this cooler helps push air out of the case. - It's honestly not that loud under load. I may even under-volt the CPU a bit to make it even quieter! - I am noticing more and more cheap alternatives to this product but I went with this one because I really liked the all black design.

If you want to install it the other way for some reason, I foresee RAM clearance being an issue. Installation was my only pain point, the instructions seemed clear at first, but getting into it, it was harder to install than expected. Bags were mislabeled for what socket they were supposed to be for. Parts didn't fit snuggly enough which made it a bit harder to install. But once everything was in place, it works well. It's not unexpected, but I'm still happy that it included extra fan clips. I had another fan from a previous cooler that I was able to attach and improve performance. reviews.title: Low Profile Power - Cool and Quiet
reviews.comment:
The AXP90 is an amazing low profile CPU cooler and for the price it is completely unbeatable. Wherever you simply cannot use a tower cooler (because of height restrictions) or don't want to invest in an AIO, this cooler will suit your needs well.
The Good:
Cooling - For coolers with appropriate wattage, about 90W or below, the AXP90 will keep them cool, with the idle temps of lower draw chips, such as the Ryzen 5600G, being only slightly above ambient. Even running a full core workload at 100% the chip will be nowhere near thermal throttling.
Noise - The fan used here, despite its size, is nearly silent. Even when almost completely open in the side of a Deskmini X300 I cannot hear it at all past a couple feet away from it; the fridge in the kitchen makes more ambient noise despite being half a house away.
Price - I don't think you can get better for $23. Out the door for $25 with tax, having a low profile cooler be effective and quiet for less than half the cost of a competing Noctua option is enormous; I'd never pay twice the amount for something that can't do much better.
The Bad:
Mounting - The mounting, while being part of the nature of low profile options, is definitely tedious and you need to be prepared to replace the backplate to make this work. Unlike a lot of AM4 coolers which use the backplate already, this cannot. So be mindful of the order of assembly or you'll be forced to mount the cooler in-case behind a mess of wires (be real, you didn't cable manage)!
Overall, I am very satisfied and would definitely recommend the AXP90 to anyone needing a low profile CPU cooler, limited budget or otherwise.

I haven't measured the temps that this gives me yet since I don't have my case or gpu yet, but it seems to keep things cool. It will fit in my case, and it isnt too loud. Very happy with it so far. reviews.title: Good low-profile cooler for <65W TDP CPUs
reviews.comment:
If you are building in a case with sub-40mm clearance for a CPU heatsink and fan, there are not too many options out there, let alone for reasonable prices. I used this in a U-NAS 4-Bay enclosure and it fits fine with enough clearance that the fan is able to draw air in to flow through the heat sink.
The installation is not as straightforward as some other manufacturers as you have use hex nuts to secure the heatsink on the motherboard from the back. There aren't springs or similar tension adjustment mechanism found on other coolers so you just have to gradually tighten the screws and watch out you aren't over tightening things. This is typical with other Thermalright coolers so if you've installed one of their other units, this should be similar for you.
Performance wise, this cooler is able to cool a stock 5600G under typical workloads without issue. The fan is fine, but definitely louder than other brands. Upgrading to a 15mm Noctua, Scythe, or Arctic could get you a better noise profile and maybe improve thermals slightly.
But the main attraction is the price. It's basically half the price of the Noctua L9 and you prob get 90% of the performance in extreme cases. In every day use, i don't think there's much difference between the two performance wise (beyond the fan quality). This unit is definitely a solid option for more budget builds, media pc/NAS builds, etc. A lot will depend on the case you have and how much case airflow you have to allow the CPU fan to get clean air. IF it doesn't have to work too hard, you'll be fine.

reviews.title: Reliable Thermal Control For Modern CPU Builds
reviews.comment:
The PCCOOLER RZ620 MX is a well‑engineered dual‑tower air cooler that delivers strong thermal performance while maintaining low noise levels, making it a solid choice for modern Intel and AMD systems. The six direct‑contact copper heat pipes provide efficient heat transfer from the CPU into the dual‑fin stacks, and the included PWM fans push a high volume of air through the towers without creating the harsh tonal noise common in budget coolers. Even under sustained workloads, the fans maintain a stable acoustic profile that stays comfortably below typical gaming‑rig noise levels.
Installation is straightforward thanks to the simplified mounting system, and the cooler provides clear access to the screws once the center fan is removed. The hardware fits securely on both Intel LGA1700/1200/115X and AMD AM5/AM4 sockets, and the mounting pressure feels even across the CPU surface. The included thermal paste performs reliably, and the overall installation process is beginner‑friendly while still feeling robust enough for experienced builders.
Thermal performance is where this cooler stands out. The dual‑tower design offers a large surface area, and the airflow path is optimized so the fans can maintain consistent cooling even during heavy gaming, rendering, or stress‑testing scenarios. Idle temperatures remain low, and load temperatures stay well within safe operating ranges for high‑performance CPUs. The cooler’s weight and dense fin structure give it a premium feel, and the build quality is noticeably higher than many similarly priced alternatives.
Clearance is generally good, with the design shaped to avoid interference with most RAM modules and motherboard components. However, because this is a full dual‑tower cooler, users with very tall RAM heat spreaders or compact cases should double‑check their available space. In a standard mid‑tower or larger case, fitment should not be an issue.
Overall, the RZ620 MX offers excellent value for its performance class. It provides strong cooling capacity, quiet operation, and a secure, easy installation process. For builders looking for a dependable air cooler that can handle demanding CPUs without resorting to liquid cooling, this model is a highly capable option.

reviews.title: Compact cooler, easy install, looks nice
reviews.comment:
This heatsync is nice in a number of ways. I was excited to get it because it's smaller than the one I have but also has the LED lighting to match the rest of my system. It includes brackets to install for both Intel and AMD CPUs. My system uses an AMD Ryzen CPU with an AM5 socket so I only needed the smaller pair of brackets and the screws.
This was quick and easy to install (way easier than my old one). During the install you remove the fan from the middle of the towers which provides clear access to the screws and makes the job easy. The fan clearly indicates which way the air moves and because it's connected to the top plate combined with the LED placement on the tower, there is only one correct way to orient it, so just pay attention to avoid having to redo it. The instructions only use pictures - no words. The double ended riser screws need to be oriented correctly with the side labeled "D" facing upward. The pictures don't make this clear so again, pay attention.
This came with their own brand of PCCOOLER EX90 thermal paste. I was going to use my Thermal Grizzly stuff but decided to give this a try first. To test this I did some CPU stress testing both before and after install. I found that my overall system idle temps average 2-3C lower than before and during the stress test it was about 2C cooler. Several factors could affect that so I don't know if this cooler itself or the thermal paste is necessarily more capable than my old setup but at least it's not worse and it opens up a lot of space. Visually it's also a nice change from my previous silver cooler to a black one that matches everything else.
Right now I don't have anything negative to say about this cooler. If you like the size and look, then I definitely would recommend it.

I don't understand why there's bad reviews. Looks like there were a few people that received used/returned items. That aside, this cooler is fantastic. GamersNexus has this rated pretty high and it Looks great and keeps my 7800x3D cold. The fans do ramp up a little prematurely in my opinion, but never to a major level if the cooler and thermal paste are properly installed. It's a thick boy at 38mm for just the radiator, so make sure it's going to fit, but if you do your due diligence for planning your PC build, you should be fine. I suspeect this would fit most modern cases with front radiator support. Top is preferable in my opinion for exhausting hot air, but may be a little less compatible unless the radiator is offset plenty from the motherboard VRM heatsinks. Install wasn't hard if you follow the instructions. The only gotchas for me was that the brackets are left and right AND I accidentally installed them upside down the first time, so I didn't think that was intuitive, at least for me.  Also the pump block isn't centered on the die, so it goes right to the edge of the CPU heatspread on the top and that preplexed me greatly, but it's by design. I think they designed it so the waterblock fan blows on that edge I guess. It's cold so it works. Only other thing that was weird with mine was the waterblock fan was ticking for the first hour or so. Not sure what that was about, tried adjusting things, eventually it went away. Not sure if there was a flap of tape or something?
FYI, a 280mm is only about 10% less surface area than a 360 AIO, yet 36% more cooling than a 240, not to mention the thickness and waterblock design.  So a pretty good alternative when you can't fit a 360mm.

reviews.title: Performance-Per-Dollar
reviews.comment:
Positives: My 14900k dropped an average of 3-5 degrees C from my Noctua NH-d15 and it’s half the price.
Negatives: Based on reviews on major hardware sites I expected cooler temperatures overall. My processor is referenced in many reviews as being tamed by this cooler, but during rendering in After Effects and Premier Pro Temperatures were spiking over 100C and throttling occurred often enough to completely stall the render. The 14900k runs notoriously hot, but having to underclock the CPU to maintain stability is disappointing. Average temperatures during idling are around 40C which is still too hot.
Its  loud. Not the worst thing for most people, but when recording audio this has to be mitigated through other means. I never heard a peep from the NH-D15.
Overall: I can deal with the sound, and it’s way better performance per dollar than the Noctua. If the dBs aren’t an issue go for it. It can hang with the big dogs, but don’t expect miracles if you’re running a bleeding edge CPU. You want the biggest radiator your case can handle, but make sure to measure before you order. Installation was no more difficult than other comparable coolers at least on the ASUS ProArt z700 Creator mobo.

reviews.title: Very Good Cooler
reviews.comment:
As of July 2025 this is undoubtedly the best budget air cooler for AM5 series CPU’s.  The size (compared to a field of what are largely monstrously sized coolers) is pleasantly unobtrusive.  The cooling is likewise impressive.  A few warnings:  At the motherboard the standard ‘base’ gets replaced by what are essentially two ‘bridges’.  A two screw ‘bar’, at the base of the cooler, screws into the peak of those two bridges.  The effect is that the two base/bar screws and the heat-sink base itself form a three-way force connection to the board & cpu.  It’s not as stable as a 4 way connection.  If you bump it (even a little) it may twist a little on the cpu.  The heat sink has very innovative insets that let you ‘plug-in’ fans using standard fan screws.  This means you can work setting-up the other connections/memory etc. without most the cooler (fans) being in the way.  HOWEVER, be very careful applying force when pressing those fans into the heat sink … the base can twist around at the CPU connection point fairly easily.  The design is good, the price is right, but you need to be gentle & thoughtful putting it together.  Which I suppose is true of the other ‘monsters’ out there as well.
For what it’s worth the Black Freezer 36 is replacing an older Arctic Freezer Xtreme (On my 10 year old FX 8350) … which since it fits AM4’s … should also work with an AM5 ?  The older cooler is ~10.5 years old, so I’m guessing half way to it’s 100,000 MTF hours ?  I also used that cooler model on an early Ryzen system I built for my son.  Great performance from both.  I’m very happy with ‘Arctic’ products in general (Price, performance & innovative design).

I personally decided to mount mine on the top of the case and it was a pretty good fit as it allows the fans to be exhaust, pushing hot air out of the radiator and out of the chassis. The pre-applied thermal paste on the copper plate was definitely a great touch as it would allow for beginners to minimize mistakes with applying that. The Cooling on this AIO is definitely very efficient, generally keeping temps under 60-70°C under load for my R7 9800x3d which is described to run hotter, the Kraken Elite handles it extremely well. The pump & fans seem to be very quiet and doesnt cause any noise issues even at higher speeds, it handles it very well and even better with the Zero RPM Mode. Now when it comes to aesthetics, this thing definitely shines with its premium LCD Screen at 2.7inch IPS at 640x640 allowing for endless ideas of image/gif customization and the ability to show real-time system stats on top of that. Of course being done with the NZXT Cam software which has given me little to no issues at all! The NZXT Cam software is very straightforward and easy to customize your rig, especially if you are pairing other NZXT fans with the AIO, it allows for different RGB modes and separate profiles and tweaking of fan performance and so much more! reviews.title: More Than Just an LCD: A Masterclass in Aesthetic Thermal Management
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/C1I4L78E6FL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/61hRWrqrgVL._SY256.jpg As a builder who has run the gamut from air towers to custom loops, the Thermaltake TH360 V2 Ultra is the most balanced AIO I’ve integrated into a build. It successfully bridges the gap between "enthusiast performance" and "showpiece aesthetics."
Thermal Performance & Acoustic Profile: Testing this on a Ryzen 7 9800X3D , the 360mm radiator surface area is more than sufficient. Under a sustained 30-minute Cinebench loop, my temps stabilized at 35°C which is an impressive level of performance; the PWM fans remain remarkably quiet at the 1200rpm mark. The 500-1500rpm range is perfectly tuned, inaudible at idle, but powerful when the TDP spikes.
The 2.1” LCD Display (The X-Factor): The resolution on the 2.1" screen is surprisingly sharp. Using the TT RGB Plus 2.0 software, the customization is intuitive. I transitioned from monitoring real-time GPU/CPU temps to uploading custom weather-informed GIFs. It’s bright, the viewing angles are wide, and it doesn't suffer from the "washed out" look of cheaper LCD blocks.
Installation & Cable Management: Thermaltake clearly listened to feedback on the V2. The fan interlocking/cabling is streamlined, which made the "cable-tuck" phase of my build 20 minutes faster than usual. The mounting bracket for AMD was sturdy and provided even pressure across the IHS.
Pros:
Visual ROI: The LCD transforms the look of the entire interior.
Daisy-Chain Efficiency: Significant reduction in cable clutter.
Versatility: High thermal ceiling for overclocking, but quiet enough for a studio environment.
Cons:
Software Dependency: To get the most out of the LCD, you must be comfortable with the TT software suite (ensure you have an internal USB 2.0 header available and 5V rail header).
Footprint: It’s a beefy 360mm radiator; verify your case clearance for mounting.
Final Verdict: If you are building a "zero-compromise" rig where you want to see your data and your style simultaneously, this is the unit. It justifies the "Ultra" moniker through build quality and ease of use. 5/5 Stars.

The only way this would fit on the memory side is with memory without a heat sink. Wraith stealth was running 50W at 65C where I had 65C thermal limiting the performance. It was hitting cinebench scores of 7800.
The configuration I have with this case sg13bq, is intake 120mm, I am using p12 slim from arctic reversed and exhausting air into the psu. my psu is facing downward towards the cooler.
If you want to use another slim 15mm fan like noctua or arctic, you need to get another screw set. I am using "Hillman 3-mm 0.5 x 20-mm Phillips-Drive Machine Screws" Item #755504 Model #127111 and I am using "Hillman 3-mm x 0.5 Zinc-plated Steel Hex Nut " Item #755591 Model #127081 as a spacer or Danco 10-Pack 1/2 Rubber Washer Model #88569 would do. I purchased from Lowes. Any taller than 20mm, and it will not fit in the sg13. The original screw set for 15mm fan is too short by 2mm. Its because the fan they provide has screw holes that are shorter than the standard 15mm fan.
The good thing though, is the 25mm fan mounting set is compatible with 25mm fans. It was able to mount my actic P12 120mm and my arctic F12 120mm no problem. If it doesnt work for you, then just get a taller screw set. They are standard 3mm diameter x .5 thread pitch screws. I would assume 3mx.5x28mm or 3mx.5x30mm should work and use nuts as spacers if needed.
The fan they provided is sufficent in performance, but louder than any other slim fan I have used. Quieter than the wraith stealth though. Wraith stealth had an annoying ticking sound. Also, the fan they provide has a bit of turbulance, even with the rubber insulation.
Mounting system was similar to noctua. If you know how to mount noctua, it will be the same experience. I am iffy on the mounting quality compared to noctua. Noctua is top notch in quality. I didn't feel too refined to me. I feel like it was just off the line and stuck in the box. But only time will tell how well it stands up.

reviews.title: High-performance cooling with innovative triple-stack design
reviews.comment:
What a great deal! I got this cooler for my 12-core 24-thread Ryzen 9 7900, an AM5 system that has a 65W TDP but runs at 90W, and it worked perfectly to cool it, even under demanding long-term workloads. As you can see in my pictures, it easily maintained a nice and steady 70°C temperature during a full stress test, with the heatsink reaching a steady state at that temperature and staying there as the CPU pulled a demanding 90W. I have been a PC enthusiast for 25 years and have built more PCs than I can count, and I can say that this heatsink gets the job done.
The cooler itself has a three-tier fin stack that is very innovative, with the large fin stack up top being fed by four of the heatpipes, while a smaller secondary fin stack underneath is fed by two more heatpipes. Perhaps most innovative of all, the cooler has yet another fin stack implemented directly into the coldplate at the bottom itself, ensuring that the part that mates directly with the processor gets even more auxiliary cooling. This seems to be overkill, but it works perfectly in practice!
The package has everything you need, including all of the fasteners and thermal paste. It also has a nice instruction booklet that is very clear and outlines a simple installation process. The cooler installed very easily. I simply placed the brackets and fasteners correctly, and then tightened the two main screws, which you accomplish through two access holes that are on the top of the heatsink. It really was simple!
The 120mm PWM heatsink fan is not loud at all for this class of heatsink (26.5 dBA), and the PWM nature of the 1550 RPM fan means you can modulate the speed with granularity to keep noise even more in check. Do note that this only comes with one 120mm fan and all of the illustrations show that, but it oddly says it is a dual 120mm fan in the title.
The height of the tallest fin stack, which is the only one that will overhang the RAM or rear VRM heatsinks, is tall enough that it can clear either obstruction easily. I installed mine with the top part overlapping the rear heatsinks, which then means I can change the RAM later without removing the heatsink. However, it would work in either orientation, and it looks wonderful, too, matching the dark theme of my ASRock Taichi AM5 motherboard perfectly, as you can see in the pictures.
The fan blows downward, which provides some auxiliary cooling for your VRMs, VRM heatsink, and RAM. You really can't beat this cooler at this price. For some unknown reason, performant low-profile coolers always seem to carry the most ridiculous price tags, but that obviously isn't the case with this model. Yes, it is a low-profile cooler, so it might have more of a problem with super high-heat processors that suck down 250W or more, but those types of systems would need a larger cooler anyway. For the target market and processors with reasonable power draw, this cooler is a huge win.

reviews.title: Budget-friendly cooler that delivers solid performance for mid-range builds
reviews.comment:
If you are not familiar with Amazon Vine, it is basically Amazon trading free* products for honest reviews. You see a lot of Vine reviews that are cookie cutter and based on templates. I aim to make my reviews honest and non-cookie cutter (other than this intro and disclaimer).
* These items are not actually free as Vine members pay income tax on the items they receive. Therefore, I will never order something from Vine unless I actually intend to use it. I think this is important for readers to understand because it means I will never order an item just to provide a fake five star review to a company. If I review something as good, it means I actually enjoyed using it or it fills its intended purpose correctly. Items that don't meet my expectations will be reviewed accordingly.
Why I ordered this item: I needed a solid CPU cooler for an AM5 build and wanted something that wouldn't break the bank. The specs looked good and the price was right compared to the big names.
Likes:
* The cooling performance is legitimately impressive for what you pay. I'm running a mid-range CPU and the temps are sitting right where I want them, even under load. Not fancy, but it works.
* The fan is quiet at idle and only ramps up when it needs to. The PWM control responds to what's happening instead of running at full blast all the time.
* Build quality feels solid. The aluminum fins are well-made and the copper base is smooth without any obvious defects. The heat pipes look properly finished.
* Thermal paste is included and it's decent stuff. I tested a transfer on my first mount and it made a noticeable difference in temps compared to some cheaper pastes I've used.
* Installation was straightforward once I figured out the mounting system. The AM5 bracket works fine with my motherboard's existing backplate, which saved me some hassle.
No likes:
* Only comes with one fan despite what the product description says about "dual fans." That's a bit misleading. I get that you can add another, but the listing should be clearer.
* If you've got a power-hungry CPU, this cooler is going to tap out. It's designed for mid-range processors, not the absolute top-end stuff.
* Once the fan gets going under heavy load, it's noticeably louder than some premium coolers. Still not bad, but you'll hear it.
Would I pay full price for this product: Yes
Final thoughts: This is a no-nonsense cooler that does its job without the premium price tag. If you've got the case space and a CPU that doesn't run at max power draw, it's a solid choice. Just verify compatibility before you order.

1 Inspect the 4 Philips screws inside the LCD housing.

reviews.title: Thermalright AXP90
reviews.comment:
This Low Profile CPU cooler is good for keeping relatively low wattage CPUs cool. I have it installed on P8H77-i ASUS motherboard with an Intel Xeon e3-1230v2 CPU (69W TDP according to Intel). I think the max temp that I saw was 74°C while gaming. It's not too loud either.
The installation is not for a first time builder. Now, installing this cooler is an experience. I believe it is referred to as a reverse install. The standoffs are to be installed to the heatsink which *should* extend through the metal backplate. You then hand tighten the fasteners. Make sure you check the edge of the motherboard for flexing. If your motherboard is flexing, the fasteners are too tight. Overall, it's a good low profile 90mm CPU cooler for a  low power, small form factor (SFF) build. Follow the installation instructions and be mindful of how tight you tighten the fasteners, it'll be satisfying to know you didn't bork your motherboard when it boots and isn't overheating.

This is a nice cooler...it is in a inwin b1 on a 5700G built around the ASRock b450 itx fatality...my main complaint with noctua similar but more popular offering is the direction it vents, it pushes air out left and right vs up and down so basically airflow is cut off by the memory and IO area ..this one from thermalright is exactly opposite it vents out the top and bottom(with convection mostly top) so this little problem as basically gone, the mounting mechanism defenetly isn't noctuas famously easy to use one but it's effective and considering I'm not going to be taking the cooler off twice a week it's fine and iv defently seen worse on soposedly high end cooling solutions so I have no complaints...if I were to pick a single thing to hone in on with this brand it's the smorgusborg for varients they offer, 36mm copper(black or gray) 43mm aluminum copper or black copper, 53mm in all versions mentioned above, all difrent weights...ya it's a bit much for your average consumer...but that being sead I was able to find 2 that I liked that would not only maximize the height in my specific case wile leaving enough of a gap to pull in air but I also had a choice of color so there is that...but I think to drive my point home here I ended up buying 2 one all black that is soposed to be coated copper and one that is just all copper becase aperently even tho they are the same under the coating they are showing in the description as difrent weight and wattage so we will see about that once I receive the secound all shiny copper heavy one lol...overall I like them they are not over engenered just to make a basic mistake like push the air in a direction that on every itx motherboard made in the last 10years has many large tall things called ram modules RIGHT there basically eliminating any benefits of your product being heavy dense and well built lol...good job thermalright you didn't forget the basics
-----------
Update I just received the full copper revision of this model and yes it is infact noticeably heavier...I will defently be swapping out the all black one for this one and pairing it with the noctua slim 92mm fan from a nh-l9a and probebly artic MX 4 compound and doing some before and after testings on all the difreces...I'm not realy shur why this model is heavier than the black one as the black one is soposed to be full copper aswell just painted with a thermaly conductive paint and also nickel plated but we are going to find out what the results are of the difrences after testing...I want to be clear I like the all black model and the fans on these are ok, I will not be returning whichever one I don't use for this build long term I just want to make shur I am pairing the best possible solution with this 5700G to get the best possible cooling performance so I don't have to worry about my CPU temps in this airflow anemic case that is the inwin b1...lol
I will likely just copy and paist this review for the copper one so there is a bit more feedback for both models becase as of right now there is very little user feedback on these and that a shame as they both have the same benefits over the noctua LP coolers that being they blow air up and are not blocked off by the memory or IO area(cooler or integrated sheald) but all the info in this review is still relevant for the copper one especial this part lol

At about 6 ft the combined noise added to ambient (55db) was only about 1db as measured by an instrument (not a phone) and most was from the PS fan. A motherboard power cable seemed to need to go on top or close to one side of the heatsink and just had room for the wires. I didn't try orientation or even looking at the heatsink geometry to see if orientation matters. The two fan headers just had enough room to plug in a case fan and CPU fan. Other motherboards will have a different arrangement, of course.
Used an i9-13900 65W CPU. Being for audio the CPU load is minimal. Wanted to see if more cores improve sound quality over an 8 core 16 thread PC with the same Win11 Pro OS - still evaluating. Sounds great regardless. Turned Turbo Boost off which took the edge off making it sound more relaxed (base speed 2GHz). Even with Turbo Boost enabled and as an audio player no real heat is produced so this unit keeps up fine. So, for more severe applications this review won't help with regard to CPU temperature but the heatsink has to be less than 54mm and this is around 32 to fit in a DeskMeet B660.  Good low-profile heatsink.

reviews.title: Perfect low-profile cooler for Mini-ITX TrueNAS build - quiet and efficient
reviews.comment:
This little CPU cooler was perfect for my Mini-ITX TrueNAS home server build. I needed a small, low-profile cooler to fit in a tight case, and this was exactly what I needed. It's rated for 150W TDP and handles my 65 watt TDP 8600K processor with no problem. Even under load, my CPU temps are perfectly acceptable.
Installation:
Easy to install with clear instructions and all the necessary hardware included for both Intel and AMD platforms. The mounting system uses nuts on the backplate, so make sure they're tightened evenly to avoid any issues. Installation took just a few minutes following the included guide or the manufacturer's installation video.
Performance:
This 53mm height cooler combines a 92mm PWM fan with 4 pure copper heat pipes and a pure copper base. The AGHP 3.0 technology handles both horizontal and vertical mounting orientations well. CPU temps stay in check even during sustained loads, and the cooler runs quietly. The fan noise level is just 22.4dB at max, which is whisper quiet for a home server running 24/7.
Build quality:
Well constructed with aluminum fins, copper heat pipes, and a sturdy mounting bracket. The white color looks clean and professional. The included thermal paste works fine, though you can always use your own if you prefer. The TL-9015W slim PWM fan is reliable and adjustable via fan curve settings.
Who it's for:
Ideal if you're building a Mini-ITX system, NAS, HTPC, or any small form factor build where clearance is limited and you need a low-profile cooler that can handle up to 150W TDP. Great for home servers, media PCs, or compact gaming builds with mid-range CPUs.
Verdict:
Extremely reasonable price for a quality low-profile cooler. It looks good, runs quiet, and keeps temps in check. If you need a low-profile cooler for a small build, this works perfectly. Would definitely buy again.

reviews.title: Low Profile Power - Cool and Quiet
reviews.comment: The AXP90 is an amazing low profile CPU cooler and for the price it is completely unbeatable. Wherever you simply cannot use a tower cooler (because of height restrictions) or don't want to invest in an AIO, this cooler will suit your needs well. The Good: Cooling - For coolers with appropriate wattage, about 90W or below, the AXP90 will keep them cool, with the idle temps of lower draw chips, such as the Ryzen 5600G, being only slightly above ambient. Even running a full core workload at 100% the chip will be nowhere near thermal throttling. Noise - The fan used here, despite its size, is nearly silent. Even when almost completely open in the side of a Deskmini X300 I cannot hear it at all past a couple feet away from it; the fridge in the kitchen makes more ambient noise despite being half a house away. Price - I don't think you can get better for $23. Out the door for $25 with tax, having a low profile cooler be effective and quiet for less than half the cost of a competing Noctua option is enormous; I'd never pay twice the amount for something that can't do much better. The Bad: Mounting - The mounting, while being part of the nature of low profile options, is definitely tedious and you need to be prepared to replace the backplate to make this work. Unlike a lot of AM4 coolers which use the backplate already, this cannot. So be mindful of the order of assembly or you'll be forced to mount the cooler in-case behind a mess of wires (be real, you didn't cable manage)! Overall, I am very satisfied and would definitely recommend the AXP90 to anyone needing a low profile CPU cooler, limited budget or otherwise.

reviews.title: Great product at a reasonable price, as usual.
reviews.comment: Overall, seems great so far. I use Thermalright and Arctic whenever I need something involving fans. If one of them doesn't have what I’m looking for, the other almost certainly does (in this build, as an example, Thermalright had a CPU cooler that fit, and arctic has 40mm fans that’ll fit). Everything I have gotten from thermalright, which at this point includes an aio, a cpu cooler, and two kinds of fans of different thicknesses and sizes, has been great,  and this one seems no exception. I haven't measured the temps that this gives me yet since I don't have my case or gpu yet, but it seems to keep things cool. It will fit in my case, and it isnt too loud. Very happy with it so far. I also seen people with my same case use this cooler with higher powered cpus than my 9600x, so I figure this should last me a long while. This is also my second time using the included thermal paste. The applicator could be better, but the paste is good, and they include enough. If it means I don't have to buy my own paste quite as often, then I am happy. For $20 vs noctuas $60 price tag for the same thing, this is by far the better use of money.

reviews.title: Good low-profile cooler for <65W TDP CPUs
reviews.comment: If you are building in a case with sub-40mm clearance for a CPU heatsink and fan, there are not too many options out there, let alone for reasonable prices. I used this in a U-NAS 4-Bay enclosure and it fits fine with enough clearance that the fan is able to draw air in to flow through the heat sink. The installation is not as straightforward as some other manufacturers as you have use hex nuts to secure the heatsink on the motherboard from the back. There aren't springs or similar tension adjustment mechanism found on other coolers so you just have to gradually tighten the screws and watch out you aren't over tightening things. This is typical with other Thermalright coolers so if you've installed one of their other units, this should be similar for you. Performance wise, this cooler is able to cool a stock 5600G under typical workloads without issue. The fan is fine, but definitely louder than other brands. Upgrading to a 15mm Noctua, Scythe, or Arctic could get you a better noise profile and maybe improve thermals slightly. But the main attraction is the price. It's basically half the price of the Noctua L9 and you prob get 90% of the performance in extreme cases. In every day use, i don't think there's much difference between the two performance wise (beyond the fan quality). This unit is definitely a solid option for more budget builds, media pc/NAS builds, etc. A lot will depend on the case you have and how much case airflow you have to allow the CPU fan to get clean air. IF it doesn't have to work too hard, you'll be fine.

reviews.title: Supports 9800x3d CPU easily.
reviews.comment:
This is THE low-profile cooler.
9800x3d (Kryonaut paste) in a Fractal Ridge case and RTX 5080 OC GPU. Fractal Ridge was in vertical orientation and ambient temperature was 76. Tests were with no restraints (no Eco mode) from the CPU side. Horizontal position was not possible with Fractal Case due to heat build up and recirculating of hot air. This is a side effect of the case design and not the cooler.
CPU Package Temps reported by HWMonitor:
Idle: 34C
Cinebench Multi-Core: 76C
Heaven Benchmark: 64C
PUBG: 68C
The CCD hit a maximum of 85.4C under extended, mixed usage of Benchmarking (running different benchmarks at the same time) while the package never went higher than 76C. CCD can run hotter than overall package. Total win for a 67mm low-profile cooler without compromising CPU speed or thermal headroom/throttling.
I had used a Noctua NH-L12S and it was abysmal. It didn't fit the Gigabyte X870i Pro Ice ITX board nor the case, forcing it to be in an orientation with offset. Idle was 57C and just downloading with steam, it was hitting 95C. Several re-pastes and orientations didn't resolve the issue. And it always mounted without covering the entire CPU (regardless of offset holes they offered). To be clear, I'm sure it's a good low-profile cooler, but it just cannot handle the 9800x3d. The 4 heat pipes of the Noctua vs the 6 heat pipes of the Thermalright is night and day better.
Bonus: This cooler is 1/3 the price of the Noctua and easier to mount (though the mounting system is nearly identical, the process was simply easier) with better cooling.
If you have a height restriction of 70mm or less, this is a fantastic cooler that will meet your needs.

reviews.title: Slick Design, Ram Clearance, and Good Cooling
reviews.comment:
I waited on getting an air cooler for a long time due to a few things: Ram clearance, height clearance, aesthetics, and price. My PC is custom-built by another company, with the parts handpicked by me. While I picked my parts based on friends' recommendations and a general gist of what I personally needed, after three years, I went into looking for an air cooler for easier maintenance and long-term reliability. I have a mid-case tower, and my RAM sticks are way too high for the big chonky air coolers on the market, and I wasn't going to spend more money just to get better clearance of 32 GB of RAM. That would be a total waste, and after some research, I stumbled upon this brand.
I was replacing a 120mm AIO (which I know is essentially pointless unless you lack space or airflow), so finding this air cooler that not only is perfect for my RAM clearance, but also meets my height clearance too. I'm thankful this air cooler doesn't have those annoying nubs at the top, because I don't think I would've met my height clearance otherwise. The design is super slick too, which makes my PC build look real nice, so that's a bonus. I'm using this to cool an AMD Ryzen™ 7 5700G, which is a low TDP CPU of 65W, so the cooler will do its job well.
The cooler and fans are well made, and installation was a breeze. The fans runs my PC cool with little to low noise if you adjust the fan curve. It depends on the time of year and where you live, but since I live in a cooler area, my idle temperature sits nicely at 30C and during some gaming sessions with Chrome and Discord in the background, between 47-55C. However, I do have other fans installed for more optimized airflow, so other people’s results will vary. The price is just right, and certainly beats similar air coolers that go over $100 for the same performance. I highly recommend this air cooler if you're looking for RAM clearance, decent CPU cooling, height clearance for mid-sized towers, and a slick design to boot.

Clearance was reasonable in a standard ATX case, though as with any larger air cooler, it’s important to check RAM height and case compatibility before installing.

reviews.title: Solved a difficult ITX-mini desktop heat problem.
reviews.comment:
I have an ITX-Mini industrial type all-in one ultra-slim open air mesh frame chassis & motherboard with an i7-4790S cpu, that has been a beast to tame workload heat, in this smallest of form-factor chassis, in an open to the elements temperature environment, and much to much dismay, and satisfaction, the Be Quite! Pure Rock LP finally solved my CPU heat throttling problems.
The original OEM installed CPU cooler was essentially the basic original Intel aluminum lug & fin, topped with a fan, reference CPU cooler, but cut down to very low 37+mm profile to fit in an ultra-slim desktop chassis.
Searching for better replacements I found the Noctua NH-L9i cooler was a few mm's tool tall to fit in the chassis, and that it had height tolerances problems in the CPU clearance zone underneath the CPU cooler.
An ARCTIC Alpine 12 LP did fit the clearance issues, and had lower noise, and power use; however still being based on an aluminum lug & fin design, (no heat pipes), still was not able to keep up with sustained temperatures, under even moderate loads.
When Be Quite announced their new LP cooler and that it was a copper heat pipe design, fit into the most minimal/maximal dimensions limits allowed for CPU cooler tolerance zones, and could tame even newer generation CPU's, I was skeptical.  But as a still last ditch resort to keep a workhorse computer thermally tamed, I decided to purchase one, give a try, with the clearance issues, see if I could even get it installed, and if it could improve on the Alpine LP.
Mission successful !!!
The install was razor shave close cut; not even micro-micrometers to spare in clearance tolerance all the way around, after mounting; from the top of the fan just barely touching the chassis cover, and with the CPU cold plate fit and around & underneath the cooler; including the cooler and mounting bracket just barely fit over a row of power capacitors sitting just below the bracket.  The mounting certainly is "flexible" but this turned out to be a benefit, after getting the mounting brackets and screws tightened into place.
The bracket installation wrench provided & needed to tighten the CPU mounting bolts, (not the mounting screws), had some difficulty getting around tight part clearances, that were right up and into the CPU cooler clearance zone, but I was able to work the wrench enough to secure the mounting bolts to the brackets; then tighten the mounting screws.
After turning the system back on, immediately I noticed a 10-20 deg F. reduction, as compared to typical temps with the Alpine LP.  And even with now spring summer temperatures coming on, and the ability to cool the cpu is being impacted by increase in ambient air temps, the Be Quit! LP has continued to maintain the heat dissipation, through all load testing; most notably that CPU is staying below throttle temperatures where; the OEM installed could never do, and Alpine LP could barely keep up with!
Additionally noticed is that the noise level was way down, even at full RPM the Be Quit! Any fan noise had a slight low hum winy noise, but only noticeable at maximum RPM.
Overall, this CPU cooler solved a long and ongoing cooling problem in a very minimalist chassis install, and it does it with no no high speed fans, or related added noise.

reviews.comment: A fantastic small form factor cooler if you are space restricted. I'm using mine in the Fractal Terra and I've been loving it. reviews.title: Low Profile Beast
reviews.comment: This little cooler had proven QUITE effective in my use with a 7800X3D and 9800X3D. Both are on Xproto open-air frames, but the cooler easily handles both chips, keeping gaming temps 70C or below, and is nearly silent under any gaming load. The low-profile blends nicely into the Xproto design. The cooler comes with a multiple-direction mount for AMD so you can turn your cooling in the orientation to best suit your needs. Mounting it as I did the downdraft gives my VRMs a direct airflow and the orientation of the fins means the NVME drive gets solid air movement as well. If your board has too large of an I/O area cooler the various orientation options mean you can find an orientation that works for you with ANY motherboard.
reviews.author: E. Crisler

reviews.title: Great cooling, fan can be loud under high load
reviews.comment: First, the size. This cooler is very compact and fit snugly in my ITX motherboard (ASRock B550M-ITX/ac). You are given the option to orient the portion that has a bulk of the heat pipes in one of two configurations, and I was able to install it with no conflict to either my RAM or VRM heatsink.  Installing the cooler was not difficult, the tools they provide are enough and the instructions are straightforward but kinda IKEA-ish so if you are having difficulty installing it you can find a youtube video that walks you through it (I did). I'm planning a small form factor build and momentarily installed this cooler in my micro-ATX case (Cooler master 300L) where I currently I have a Ryzen 7 5800x. This CPUs tend to run hot as it is, and I can definitely hear the fan kick in under full load, yet this cooler keeps it at a toasty 70C allowing me to maintain high clocks. I will say that high air turbulence negatively affects cooling in many cases. I saw this in my case (pun intended) which contributed to the higher fan noise, but changing the placement of my intake and outflow fans helped with both the cooling and the fan noise. Always make sure to not significantly disturb the flow of air exiting the cooler so that it can cool the heatsink with cooler air rather than recycled warmer air. The fact that the fan pulls air from the heatsink rather than blowing it down helps keep motherboard components cooler. If you are thinking of installing this cooler on an AMD system you should be adjusting your PBO settings in order to optimize your cooling as it is. This is a great buy for anyone making a compact system, just plan ahead and consider your airflow. I look forward to putting this to use in my Cooler Master NR2000 case.

This water cooling setup has exceeded all my expectations. It works flawlessly—keeps my CPU running at the perfect temperature even under heavy load, and it’s whisper quiet while doing it. Installation was straightforward, and the build quality feels solid and reliable.

No complaints at all so far. If you’re looking for a high-quality water cooling solution with awesome lighting and zero hassle, this one’s a great choice.  Great value for the money.

reviews.title: Excellent Cooling Performance with Stunning ARGB Effects
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/D1ACEVbAspL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/71xy0ZHbO-L._SY256.jpg I recently installed the ID-COOLING FX360 INF 360mm AIO liquid cooler in my new build, and it’s been a fantastic upgrade. First off, the cooling performance is top-notch — it keeps my Ryzen/Intel CPU running cool even under heavy load, with temperatures staying impressively low. The included 3x120mm fans are quiet, even at high speeds, with a max noise level of just 27.2dB(A), which is great for a near-silent setup.
What really sets this cooler apart is the ARGB infinity mirror on the pump — it looks absolutely stunning in a tempered glass case. The lighting is vibrant, smooth, and syncs easily with my motherboard’s ARGB header. The daisy-chained fans also simplify cable management, making the installation much cleaner and easier.
Mounting was straightforward, with clear instructions and wide compatibility across both Intel (LGA1851/1700/1200/115X) and AMD (AM5/AM4) sockets. The build quality feels solid throughout.

reviews.author: Le1

reviews.title: ID-Cooling FX360 INF - Great Price & Performance!
reviews.comment:
I built a computer for an arcade I was building and didn’t know what I needed to run the emulators. So I used an i9 14900k with an Asus ROG Strix 4090 OC because no one would tell me what would work. So, I used the motto go big or go home. Needless to say it was overkill and then I find out that the i9 runs hot and my DeepCool AK620 worked for the emulator games, but not for AAA Steam games. My CPU kept thermal throttling.
I purchased an Artic Liquid Freezer III 420, but was unable to get it to fit into my Lian Li Lancool III case. So I purchased this ID-Cooling FX360 INF since it got great reviews from those who do PC content.
I’ve had this now for about 2 months and I’ve never had an issue with thermal throttling since. The highest temps I’ve seen is 70C-75C and that was during a CPU-Z stress test. Idling I’m around 30C-32C and playing 2 AAA games (Indian Jones & Hogwarts), at 4k, the highest I’ve seen is around 60C.
This AIO has worked flawlessly and like a lot of people have said, it was really easy to install.
Because it’s inside my arcade pedestal (and fears of my CPU over heating) mines set to run at 100% all the time and the fan noise isn’t bad at all. Those that complain the fans are loud or the pump is loud, I wish they were around in the 80’s and 90’s when fans were extremely loud!! They’d think twice about calling these loud. Only time will tell as to how well it holds up.
reviews.author: T.J.

reviews.title: Surprisingly good cooling performance for its cheap price, if you can tolerate cheap build quality.
reviews.comment:
This is a very performant AIO for its price. Even included with a sizable (I made two applications) thermal paste that also has good reviews.
However, the included fans wobble and create vibration noise when ramping up. They would physically shake your whole case. A full replacement with better fans is recommended.
The pump produces a high-frequency resonance whine after 64% and slowly creeps louder and louder to 100%. I have to cap my pump to 63% in software. The pump whine isn't too loud compared to the fan, but the high frequency makes it unbearable to me.
Also, be aware that the pump is connected with a 3-pin DC header, not the advertised 4-pin PWM. Make sure your motherboard can do and is configured to voltage control on pump headers; otherwise, your pump will be stuck with 100% RPM.
Aside from build quality, the raw cooling performance of this AIO is very good. It's the best you can get in this price range.

reviews.author: Matteo D'Angelo

reviews.title: Biggest waste of money in my current build
reviews.comment: I generally don't write reviews, but this thing has been such a thorn in my side. First of all, when you first turn your computer on you'll notice that the pump is extremely loud at default settings. Like hearing it down the hallway loud. I waited a week to see if the bubbles would settle and make it quiet like people say it is, tilted my PC to work them out, and no change. So I figured maybe I had a dud and returned it to swap them out. Same story. I asked their support about it, gave videos, showed the audio spectrum near the PC at different pump speeds, and was told this is normal. I had to lower the pump speed from the what is already mid-range 2300rpm default to specifically 1690rpm as both 1700rpm and 1680rpm have higher noise. Then there's the software. It's terrible. For months it didn't even work properly and you had to regularly reinstall it to reset and have it working again for another couple of weeks until it tried to do an update and crashed itself. And the service running in the background is constantly polling the hardware for information like power usage, temperatures, etc. Which makes sense for something like this, but it was causing issues for me in SteamVR and some games with stuttering until I killed the process. And it's a dice roll every time there's an update whether it will start using up 10% of your CPU constantly; increasing the temperatures and eating up resources. This is on a 14900k, mind you. But the LCD has its own issues: the one of the big things that made me want to pay $275 for this on launch. It works great for about 6 months, but then you'll notice once in a while the image flickers. Then it happens more and more frequently. You try to change images or background colors to see if it fixes it and notice the previous images are "sticking" like there is screen burn in or something, but it very slowly resolves itself over time if you're lucky. Then it really looks like there is screen burn in when you have nothing but a white background on that LCD and the whole thing looks like someone held a candle to it. This has happened to me with the original LCD that came with it AND the replacement they sent me 8 months ago. Which, by the way, they won't just replace the cooler. They'll send you a new LCD and have you rip apart your cooler to put the LCD on. So, if you're not prepared to do that, be ready to ask someone for help. Pros: - Cools a 14900k decently well considering how much heat that puts out. - Infinity fans look nice and are pretty quiet when not cranked up really high. - LCD looks nice when it works and there is a simple editor to put videos and gifs in it. Cons: - LCD has a life span of 6-8 months and has needed replacement twice. - Loud unless you lower the pump speed a lot and find the magic number to make it silent. - Troublesome RMA process that some people won't be comfortable with. - The supporting software is terrible and either causes issues or eats up too much system resources for what it does. Not worth it. I gave it 1 star since it did a decent job of cooling, especially for running at only 1690rpm and being attached to a 14900k. Maybe just get the non-LCD version if noise doesn't bother you and use third party software or motherboard controls, because I'm not sure they have a QA process or proper testing procedures.
reviews.author: Zoey

reviews.title: Blending Elite Cooling with Dynamic Visuals
reviews.comment: Cooling Performance Beyond the dazzling display, the core function of an AIO is cooling, and Lian Li's 360mm LCD coolers consistently deliver top-tier performance. Powerful Pump: These AIOs typically feature an Asetek 8th generation pump, known for its high efficiency and quiet operation. With pump speeds reaching up to 3600 RPM (or even 3200-4200 RPM depending on the model), it ensures robust coolant flow for effective heat transfer from the CPU. Effective Radiator Design: The 360mm aluminum radiator, with its optimized fin design, provides a large surface area for heat dissipation. When paired with the included high static pressure fans, it efficiently expels heat from even the most demanding CPUs. Thermal Performance: In real-world scenarios and benchmarks, these coolers consistently keep high-TDP processors (like Intel i9s and AMD Ryzen 9s, including X3D variants) well within safe operating temperatures, even under sustained heavy loads like gaming or video rendering. Users often report CPU temperatures well below critical thresholds, even in demanding applications like Cinebench. Low Noise Profile: Despite their cooling prowess, the combination of efficient FDB fans and a well-designed pump means these AIOs can maintain a surprisingly low noise profile, especially at idle or moderate loads. The fans offer a wide RPM range, allowing for tuning between silence and maximum performance via software. LCD Screen & Customization This is the feature that truly sets the Lian Li LCD AIO apart. The integrated IPS LCD screen is not a gimmick; it's a powerful customization tool: Vibrant Display: The 2.88-inch screen is bright (up to 500 nits) and offers sharp resolution, making displayed content clearly visible. Real-time Monitoring: Through Lian Li's L-Connect 3 software, users can display a wealth of real-time system information, including CPU/GPU temperatures, load, frequencies, fan speeds, and more. The layouts are customizable, allowing users to prioritize the data most important to them. Personalization: Beyond system stats, the screen supports custom images, GIFs, and even short videos. This allows for unparalleled personalization, transforming the CPU block into a dynamic visual centerpiece that can match your build's theme or express your personality. Software Integration (L-Connect 3): The L-Connect 3 software is the command center for the cooler, offering intuitive control over pump speed, fan curves, and extensive customization options for the LCD screen and ARGB lighting. While software can sometimes be a point of contention for PC components, L-Connect 3 generally provides a comprehensive and user-friendly experience, though occasional software glitches have been reported (and often addressed by updates). Installation & Compatibility Installation is generally straightforward for a 360mm AIO. Lian Li includes mounting hardware for all modern CPU sockets (Intel LGA 1700/1851, AMD AM4/AM5), ensuring wide compatibility. The pre-installed fans (on some models) and thoughtful cable management options (including daisy-chainable ARGB fans for less cable clutter) further simplify the process. The flexible tubing and rotatable pump block make it adaptable to various case layouts. Areas for Improvement Price Point: As a premium product with an integrated LCD screen and top-tier cooling performance, the Lian Li LCD 360mm AIO comes with a higher price tag compared to non-LCD or less feature-rich AIOs. It's an investment in both performance and aesthetics. Software Dependency: While L-Connect 3 is powerful, reliance on software for full customization means some users might encounter occasional software-related quirks or a learning curve. Pump Noise (Specific Batches): While generally quiet, some early batches of certain models experienced pump rattling or whining at specific RPM ranges. Lian Li has actively addressed these issues with revised designs and firmware updates, but it's worth checking user reviews for the specific model and batch if concern arises. Tube Orientation (Hydroshift): For the Hydroshift series, optimal performance is achieved when the tubes on the pump are oriented upwards, which might dictate placement in some builds. Conclusion The Lian Li LCD 360mm AIO cooler is an exceptional cooling solution that masterfully blends high-performance thermal management with stunning visual customization. It delivers powerful and efficient cooling for even the hottest CPUs, while its vibrant, customizable LCD screen transforms the humble CPU block into a dynamic display of system data or personal flair. While it represents a premium investment and requires software management, for enthusiasts building a high-end system where both top-tier performance and eye-catching aesthetics are paramount, the Lian Li LCD 360mm AIO is a highly recommended and truly insightful choice.

reviews.title: Beautiful AIO, Bad Temperatures, Pump Noise
reviews.comment: An AIO with a beautiful LCD screen and smart tubing design, but inconsistent cooling, pump noise, and LCD connectivity issues on a Ryzen 7 9800X3D. Pros: - LCD screen is absolutely beautiful, and it abstracts so much of the clutter on a typical motherboard. - The tubing hidden behind the radiator is a genuinely clever design. I’m surprised more companies haven’t attempted something like this before. Visually, it looks excellent—and after using this AIO, traditional exposed tubing in a PC starts to look awkward by comparison. Cons: - CPU temperatures ran hot with inconsistent cooling behavior. - The pump made noticeable noises on startup and would occasionally do so at random afterward (see attached video). - The LCD screen would intermittently lose connection with L-Connect. Resolving this required a full PC reboot. When this happened, the screen would revert to the default out-of-box display, which still looked fine—but the main appeal of the LCD is being able to reliably run a custom display. - The mounting mechanism felt a bit awkward. Sliding the unit in from right to left while working around the standoffs made installation slightly annoying. This isn’t a dealbreaker by itself, but it’s worth noting. My Experience: I initially replaced my Cooler Master AIO (which was using Lian Li P28 fans) with this fanless HS2 pump and installed the same P28 fans onto the radiator. Right away, CPU temperatures were extremely spiky. I would see jumps from ~45 °C to ~62 °C just from opening a browser tab. Running Cinebench pushed temperatures straight to 95 °C. While troubleshooting, I checked the thermal paste application and noticed it appeared slightly uneven (see attached photo). After reapplying the paste, the temperature spikes became noticeably calmer. I also adjusted the fan step-up and step-down timers in the BIOS to reduce constant fan ramping caused by erratic CPU temperature behavior. These changes helped stabilize temperatures, though they still ran somewhat high. Cinebench would now peak around 91–92 °C. At that point, I considered the results acceptable and continued using the system. For a couple of days, everything seemed fine. However, on the third day, while playing Marvel Rivals, CPU temperatures suddenly jumped from the usual ~60 °C range straight to 95 °C. At the same time, my frame rate dropped from ~240 FPS down to 20–25 FPS. Even after closing the game, CPU temperatures remained elevated and did not recover as expected. After all that, decided to put back my Cooler Master AIO back on, and live without the pretty LCD screen (unfortunate). I do miss it, but I can play my games  with the peace of mind that my temperatures are in normal operating ranges, no massive spikes, no throttling. See video of noise, picture of the initial "bad" paste application, and the picture of it on my PC. UPDATE: Lian Li did reach out to me to apologize for my experience and offered either a replacement or a refund. I appreciate the attentiveness from them and will definitely try a different product in the future.

reviews.title: Excellent Monitor for Home Office!
reviews.comment: Best monitor choice for my needs.  I do primarily a lot of Excel files (with Visual Basic), PDFs, email, family photo and video editing.  I’m retired so not into gaming though I own several gaming consoles.  I build a new PC every 4-5 years and I wanted to step up from my 28” 1080p monitor without using dual monitors as I used dozens throughout my work career.  My primary goal was being able to open at least 2 full width documents without having to scale them down (normally 80%).  I usually have an Edge window open as well streaming news.  With this monitor I have the display scaled to 125% in Windows (my eyes not what they used to be) and I can keep documents scaled at 100%!  Glad I went the ultra-wide 1440p route and though the screen is much wider it actually cleared up a lot of desk space with its stand design.  I tried 2 different 32” 4K IPS monitors but both made me sick if I used them too long.  One was a LG and its stand and function were subpar compared to this one.  Dell has another almost identical ultra-wide not geared toward gaming (S3425DW 120Hz) with USB-C (Displayport 1.4 compatible) but no dedicated Displayports.  I decided to go with the Alienware as my primary computer is a desktop though I also use a laptop for travelling.  If your primary PC is a laptop you may want the Dell which was $50 more when I bought this.  Since there is no built-in speakers I bought an inexpensive small sound bar at the same time. The monitor stand on this is one of the best and easiest I have used (height and forward/back tilt) though no side to side tilt but not needed for my use.  Just make sure to never grab /carry from the sides as it may damage the screen.  The base is minimal and frees up a lot of desk space.  The speaker I bought fits well sitting on the stand base. The curvature may take a while to get used to but almost required for this wide of a monitor if using at normal desk distances. The On/Off button IS the LED light on the bottom far right.  The OSD toggle is directly in the center bottom and the easiest menu I have used to date. It took me some time to set it up to my liking and so far this works best for me: Monitor: Preset – MOBA/RTS Smart HDR – Off Dark Stabilizer – 2 Brightness – 60 (though occasionally change based on lighting conditions as near a window) Contrast – 75 Windows 11 Pro: Scaling 125% (though occasional take to 150%) Frequency: 120 Hz (tried all up to the max 180) Included in the box:  Both Displayport 1.4 and HDMI 2.1 cables, USB Type A to B upstream cable, power cord and very basic instructions (I had to download the manual to find the Power Button)! There are 2 downstream USB ports left bottom.  One says charging but both appear to charge my cell.  The Dell version has a push down exposing the 2 USB ports facing forward (I believe 1 Type A and 1 Type C).  I was able to plug my USB speaker into the LEFT port and it works great.  Only gripe is both USB ports are Type A.

reviews.title: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (…but also 😬) Alienware 34” Curved Gaming Monitor – AW3425DWM Review

The colors are solid, the brightness is clean, and the curve makes you feel just a little more important than you actually are. Now here’s where I messed up. I made the fatal, unforgivable, absolutely rookie mistake of putting this beautiful, innocent, perfectly fine monitor directly next to an OLED. Listen… If you’ve never compared a normal panel to OLED side-by-side, DO NOT START NOW. Save yourself. Save your expectations. Save your wallet. Because the moment I powered up my OLED and saw those deep blacks, explosive colors, and “I can see into another dimension” contrast, the AW3425DWM never stood a chance. It was like parking a Honda next to a Ferrari — the Honda is great, reliable, budget-friendly… but guess what I’m driving home in? Gameplay on the AW3425DWM was genuinely enjoyable. But once the OLED lit up next to it, my eyes said: “Nope. Not doing this. Return it.” And that’s exactly what I did. So here’s my official verdict: 👍 If you’re NOT comparing it to an OLED: This monitor is fantastic for the price. Great curved experience, solid colors, fast response, everything you’d want in a mid-tier setup. 👎 If you ARE comparing it to an OLED: You’re going to cry, pack it up, and send it back like I did. Alienware makes awesome stuff — but OLED is a different universe. Once you cross over, there’s no coming back.
