reviews.title: Great upgrade from FHD monitor - except text, menus, windows now TINY
reviews.comment: The main drawback I'm experiencing, and imagine most customers would also, isn't a fault of this product which would be better on other 27" 4K monitors, but nonetheless if you're considering buying it you should know this. I got this to upgrade from using a M4 Mac Mini with 3x 1920x1280 monitors; before that I had a 27" 5K Retina iMac which had a beautiful, highly-rated screen similar to what's still in their $1599 Studio Display Monitor and the transition back to FHD was too frustrating in terms of screen real estate, how much I could fit onto the monitor. I don't know if the increased PPI of the display to show more detail in playback of video was an important benefit for me of having the 5K iMac, and admittedly the 5K iMac did take some getting used to because everything was smaller than on the FHD monitors (as to be expected) - but it had incredible flexibility of resizing elements. I always had wondered why Apple went to 5K for just a 27" monitor, when there's barely any content available streaming at 4K, as far as I'm aware there isn't content available in 5K and ofc 5K is a far cry from 8K. NOW I'm pretty sure I understand why they did the 5K retina in 5K - it speaks to the drawback I'm experiencing in 4K at 27" , its because if you want to scale the resolution to make windows not appear tiny and harder to read on these high-resolution monitors compared to the FHD 1080p monitors. I can't speak to the experience with Windows, but the principle should hold, so the bottom line here is that upgrading from a 1920x1280 (or 1920x1080) monitor WILL ABSOLUTELY result in the title bars, menu bars, all icons etc being SMALLER, much smaller. On MacOS you can set the resolution to be scaled to 1080p - but then not only are you reverting to the pixel density from which you just upgraded, to me at 2x scaling everything looked too big which compromised my goal of being able to fit more on the screen. Some Reddit posts suggested that selecting the 1080p (scaled) resolution in MacOS would still allow 4K video to be displayed at the high PPI so if that's true it would be a good solution for customers who only wanted the 4K for the increased detail in video playback. I have decently-young eyes and am sitting just a few inches from the screen, so while annoying I'm going to accept the stuff being smaller because of the terrific newfound ability to fit twice as much on my 27" screen compared to the 24" screen it replaces. But if I had the money, I'd instead get the 32" size - not because 27" isn't big enough, it is, and frankly a 32" monitor would feel overwhelmingly large on my desk, but that size would allow me to use this 4K resolution without the title bar of every window being tiny. Now I will discuss elements of this monitor in the context of comparisons to other 27" 4K monitors. It is INCREDIBLY thin, and lightweight, that's a huge plus. I paid a small premium compared to the other 27" 4K monitors because at $199 to get a Samsung brand monitor seemed smart, in case there is trouble requiring warranty support. The bezel is so thin that - I kid you not - this 27" monitor's total size makes it sit side-by-side next to a NEC 24" and a HP 24" and they've all got approximately the same exterior dimensions! It's like when I upgraded iPhones recently to one with a slightly (but signifigantly) bigger screen - sitting next to the old iPhone, their exterior dimensions are very similar. I am very bothered about one thing - what's the deal with the USB-A port? It's marked as being "Superspeed" (USB3), yet its not mentioned ANYWHERE in the manual! On a Thunderbolt or USB-C monitor (or if it had a USB-B uplink port, like older monitors with built-in hubs) it would make sense to me what it does and how it works, but I'm pretty sure USB data can't be transfered over any HDMI or DP connection which leads me to assume, given its placement adjacent to the 1/8" analog headphone output, that its for USB audio. The monitor is so barebones-featurewise that all functionality is controlled by just a single button (stick) on the backside of the monitor (you must reach under, and around, which is OK except that you may not know its there) and yet they opted to have audio outputs. Perhaps this is for devices that don't have 1/8" analog audio output, or USB-A supporting audio, if you connect say a new iPad or iPhone to it and want your audio to come out of headphones/speakers, I suppose that would be very appreciated. The image is really nice. I read countless reviews complaining that each time the monitor turns on, or wakes from sleep, that it would show some stupid OSD or other unwanted functionality, but I have yet to see any behavior that bothers me. The OSD message goes away pretty quickly from a cold start. There was a complaint by someone who intended to use the monitor with two devices (such as a computer AND a video game console) always plugged in, expecting to be able to easily switch between inputs using the monitor's controls as is very easy to do on many monitors, and I agree this isn't the best model for that. It seemed inconsequential that the monitor comes with a HDMI cable included, but this is actually an important aspect because I realized quickly that all the HDMI cables I already had couldn't supply it with 4K video (FHD max). It's annoying that HDMI cables aren't labeled for which version they are, but suitably the included cable is HDMI 2.0 at least.

reviews.title: A Good Home Monitor with Some Trade Offs
reviews.comment:
Overall this is a good monitor for home use.
There are better ones out there, but the price point makes this one worth considering.  I bought it because I wanted to display text files in larger sizes -- so far, it's doing an excellent job.  Text is crisp, and the larger size allows me to both read more easily and multitask.  Arguably a similar arrangement could be done through two smaller monitors, as is the case in my business office, but I don't like the screen being divided.
My old monitor was 27 inches.  It, too, worked well for many years, but as my eyes have changed, I was feeling more strain to read text.  Because I write and edit a lot, among other things, I often have more than one full-sized page open at a time.  The problem was larger monitors without higher resolution were not necessarily an improvement.  Yes, they enlarged the images, but then the text wasn't as readable.  This higher resolution, 4K monitor bridges that gap.
The good:
1) Crisp images and text -- I can run a 4K movie in a window and still have plenty of real estate for other applications.
2) A decent refresh rate -- videogamers no doubt will have quibbles, but for ordinary business use and all but the most sophisticated graphics, it's fine.
3) No dead pixels or screen bleed -- I've been using the monitor a while now, but, of course, these flaws often don't show up right away.
The bad:
1) Color reproduction seems a bit off compared to my old, non-Samsung monitor.  The colors lean toward the blue portion of the spectrum.  I may play around with the settings more to see if I can warm things up.
2) The display stand is not adjustable and does not swivel.  This is a bigger issue than it sounds because it's actually in an computer cabinet with fixed shelving.  Yes, I can raise the office chair, but this is the first monitor I've ever owned that can't simply be raised or lowered at the stand.
3) Physical buttons are awkward.  There's a circular control in the back that's tough to reach (especially since the monitor also does not swivel).  The HDMI and power plugs are on the opposite side . . . which is awkward since the feed for cables in my display cabinet as well as the wall socket are opposite of that.  Because the power cable is short, I actually have to use an extension cord to plug it in.
So, if you can live with these limitations -- some of which are specific to my furniture and den set up -- this is a good value for the price.
Time will tell how long it lasts.  For the past 10 years or so, I've sworn by Samsung televisions, but a more recent one developed significant display problems because of a long, purple "cloud" across the top of the screen.  I'm guessing because the television is so razor thin, the screen buckled from it's own weight, warping that portion.
It's too early to tell if this monitor, which is similar in proportion, will do the same.  In more recent years, Samsung seems to be using cheaper parts and components, so I may need to update this review in a few months.

I bought this monitor based on Samsung's brand believing I was buying a quality monitor. Unfortunately, a couple weeks after setting it up, the HDMI2 port started to fail and the connection from my laptop would cut on and off randomly. This started once in a while and proceeded to quickly get worse to the point that I could no longer use the port. I called Samsung and they refused to exchange it and said I'd need to send it to a repair center. The repair center was on the other side of the US in New Jersey (I'm west coast) and took forever just to arrive. They then kept it there for 3 weeks while sending automated text and email messages stating all sorts of weird things like there was physical damage to the sides (there was not) and all sorts of other random things. I called and spoke to several representatives over this 3-week period that I did not have a monitor to do my job and every representative said different things including to not pay attention to the text and email messages because they were wrong and I should trust them and not their system. Really shoddy process.
Anyway, I finally got a message that they had replaced a part in the monitor and were sending it back. Lo and behold, after a couple of weeks the HDMI2 port is doing the same thing. Switched to the HDMI1 port because I can't deal with not having a monitor for another 3 weeks to do my job. Well, the HDMI1 doesn't flicker, but it does display tiny little red pixels randomly on dark colors, and also shows horizontal lines at random times.
Called customer service to request a replacement and have been given the runaround now by 5 representatives, told that a manager would call me back (they never did), told that the monitor doesn't qualify for a replacement because it needs to be sent for repairs twice before they will replace it. Absolutely horrible experience.
Samsung is not the company it used to be. Do yourself a favor and look elsewhere. There are plenty of other choices for this price.

reviews.title: Nice, feature rich, value-oriented monitor that punches above it's weight class
reviews.comment:
An Impressive Value-oriented monitor
Tested with both my (multiple) Macs
I am pleasantly surprised by this monitor.  It offers a strong feature set at it's price point, particularly for those who balance productivity with some gaming.
The "Retina" Comparison (Clarity & Text)
As a Mac user, my benchmark is usually a Retina display. Here is how this monitor stacks up:
* This device vs. M1 Max / M3 Air Retina: It isn't nearly as crisp as a native Retina display (the M1 Max is the clearest).
* This device vs. LG Ultrawide (my daily driver when I need the screen real-estate): This is the best comparison. It "feels" very similar to my LG Ultrawide in terms of clarity and color.
Eye Strain: I work all day on monitors, and some lower-end panels cause immediate squinting. This one does not. Text clarity is adequate for full-day productivity work without fatigue. It isn't "super clear" like the M1 Max (my benchmark), but it is definitely adequate, and is superior to other monitors I have tried. I can say this: I work all day with the LG Ultrawide and this monitor "feels" like that monitor in clarity. I haven't had a chance to hammer on this for days like the LG, but from what I can see, this is adequate clarity for productivity work and should not create eye-strain. I have OTHER monitors that have me squinting and rubbing my eyes quickly. I do not think that will be a problem with this device.
Gaming & Performance:
Refresh Rate: I drove the monitor at 144 Hz via my Mac, and it performed smoothly.
Note: I didn't push to the full 180 Hz due to cable/hardware limitations, but 144 Hz was stable and recognized immediately by macOS.
Ghosting: I noticed some minor ghosting with fast-moving objects, but it handled 90% of what I threw at it very well.
Display Quality & HDR
Blooming: While it can’t compete with OLED or the Mac M1's Mini-LED display, the blacks are surprisingly deep with minimal, non-distracting blooming.
Color: It sits right alongside my LG Ultrawide. It's not as vibrant as a Mac display, but it’s very respectable for this tier.
HDR: I was less impressed here. HDR content seemed a bit "washed out" compared to the default SDR mode. I ended up sticking with the defaults and just bumping the brightness slightly for a better overall picture.
Build & Ergonimics
The Stand: This is a highlight. It’s sturdy and provides height and tilt adjustments.
Portrait Mode: It supports a full 90-degree rotation. This is a "nice to have" feature that many competitors lack, making it great for long documents or coding.
Ports: 2x HDMI and 1x DisplayPort.
Final Thoughts
When looking at my attached photos, please note that any "wavy" patterns (Moire) are a camera artifact—the screen is much cleaner to the naked eye.
Pros: Great value, sturdy stand with portrait mode, easy on the eyes for work.
Cons: HDR is a bit weak, minor ghosting in high-speed gaming.
Overall: If you need a reliable secondary monitor or a budget-friendly primary for a mix of work and play, this is a solid choice. Recommended.

It is pure marketing since I can get all these via applications menu.  Attached is a picture of the Remote. I'd rather have regular Samsung remote buttons with the functions I need like: "Sleep", "Exit"... "
2. The "Sleep" function is not available at all, though the menu options pretend it is there. Their solution for "Sleep" is actually "Power on/off". It means that I cannot put it in "Standby" and resume exactly at the place I left.  It always returns to "Samsung TV Plus" and I cannot even change the startup default app/screen, though again the menu pretends to allow it.
3. There is no "Pairing" monitor with Remote, so when I use the Remote, my other Samsung devices react. I have several of them: I used to be a Samsung fan until now.
4. The monitor reacts to remote with significant delay in many menus (not all of them though). I just see a black screen for a couple of seconds. It is confusing and creates additional difficulties, because these menus are the only way to achieve some functions since there are no "usual" buttons.
Hopefully someone from Samsung will contact me with explanations. If not, I will return this M50F monitor to Amazon.
As for the value for money, it would be better to buy regular (not smart) Samsung Monitor and plug $30 Smart TV device in.  Sound is OK, Color is OK, Picture is OK. Setup is not easy because of the Remote.
Summary: this is a new product, maybe all it requires is a software update, but Samsung support could not help me to achieve the above functions

reviews.title: Highly Recommend It!
reviews.comment: This is my very first monitor and it’s surprisingly good. I make music, commentaries and i game a lot, so I was in need of a monitor. It takes up a lot of space on my desk, my desk is about 5ft to 6 ft wide. I did a lot of research before I bought it (4 months before I bought it). I was very hesitant because of the price and not a lot videos on YouTube gone in depth about the monitor other than showing gameplay. I wasn’t expecting it to be so big let alone run this well either. Finding a gaming monitor at the moment is hard just because finding a well made monitor that plays and runs most games is somewhat rare. It took no more then 12 hours for it to come in after i purchased it (I have Amazon prime) and the box itself was actually pretty big. Setting everything up was easy and simple. Using it for gaming: There’s a bit of settings and you can play it at native 4k 60hz on the Xbox one x and there’s a major difference with some games like Cod MW (2019) Halo MCC & Halo 5, and any game that plays at 60fps. It may not be a noticeable difference with games that are locked to 30fps, but there is a major difference when playing games at 60. Some games looked better but ran somewhat worse compared to 1080p or 1440p. With the One X you can play some games in HDR and there’s a major difference with HDR and some games looked better with HDR. I’ve seen HDR on 4k tv’s and looked amazing, but being able to use it on a monitor like this was also really surprising. Again not all games on the One X have HDR, but the games that do have HDR ran somewhat better but frames did drop considerably when things picked up in combat. Cyberpunk 2077 while looked better on the One X, ran a lot worse at native 4k and with HDR on. Some parts of cyberpunk were steady and nice, as soon as combat picked up, the games frames would drop. So again it just depends on your settings and what games you play the monitor on. Using it for my Music & commentaries: For the last few weeks I’ve been making music & commentaries on this monitor and my workload had jumped up considerably. I can finally see everything and mix the way I need too. It’s a lot easier for me to see my mixes, I had to get a new keyboard, mouse, and desk mat just for this monitor. My work flow has improved and the monitor goes well with the lights around my studio. I’m getting a gaming computer soon to see how it truly runs, I have laptop at the moment so it runs well but I’m in need of upgrade for a new computer. Final Thoughts: Buy at your own cost. The settings are customizable and it looks good on my Xbox one X, I plan on getting a gaming computer to see how it truly runs. It’s worth the price and ships really fast (if you have Amazon prime). Picture quality is amazing, the brightness is adjustable and it’s really good for gaming. Worth the price! If you have the money, get it, if you game a lot, get it, if you’re in need of good monitor, get it. You can’t go wrong with it. Even after a month, I haven’t had any problems with it. I’ve been using it everyday since I’ve bought it.

reviews.title: Best Monitor I've Bought
reviews.comment: The ASUS TUF Gaming VG32VQ1B is a monitor that I’ve been using for quite some time and it has definitely enhanced my setup. It has a 32 inch carbon curved screen with a 1440p resolution. In my eyes, that combination of size and resolution is the best. Clarity of the text is impeccable, sharpness of graphics is very pleasing and there is a lot of screen space without it being overwhelming. It has a maximum refresh rate of 165Hz and combined with a 1ms response time, everything from fast paced games to smoother experiences feels incredible. I primarily play racing and shooter games and the difference in performance when compared to a 60Hz monitor is very noticeable. That smoother performance does wonders with reaction time and overall improves the experience in gaming. The curvature of the monitor is not highly aggressive, it is in fact very subtle but extremely useful for immersion, especially for when you sit right in front of it. It encapsulates your viewpoint to just the right extent to feel more connected and engaged with the on screen actions. Also, there’s the Free-Sync Premium tag, which is carried quite nicely since there’s no tearing or stuttering even when frame rates slightly dip, and there’s the ELMB feature that stands as ELMB is strong, preventing things from becoming blurry during fast movements in scenes with high action. It has speakers built in. Not great, but really not bad at all, especially if you’re not plugging anything else in. That being said, I use a headset most of the time so I don’t really have a use for them. It’s also VESA mountable so that’s cool if you’d like to clear up your desk with an arm mount or just get it off the stand. Well, brightness and color are more than fine for me. It gets plenty bright, and colors look pretty natural to my eye. HDR is supported. It’s not the most amazing HDR I’ve ever seen, but it does improve the look in some games and videos. Don’t expect OLED-level blacks or anything, though. Overall, this thing has been totally worth it. It has everything I look for good image quality, smooth performance, and that little bit of immersion from the curve. If I had to do it all over again, I’d still buy it. No regrets.
reviews.author: Michael

reviews.title: Great performance and screen - meh HDR
reviews.comment: I have tried and compared several 32" VA and IPS 1440p 144Hz+ monitors and out of all of them, the ASUS TUF 32" 1440p 165Hz (VG32VQ1B) has the best balance of cost, performance, and quality. The Pros: Deep blacks, good contrast (superior contrast to an IPS panel), great color for a VA panel, excellent refresh rate (165), quality materials, lots of fine tuning options, gentle curve for immersion. Cons: like most all other VA panels, this one is not immune to ghosting (google if you do not know what that is), black screen uniformity is Meh (more on that below), colors are a little subdued but better after calibration, orange stand by light is pretty bright. The panel that came the closest to this one, for me, was the Samsung G5 32" but the G5 is dimmer than this one. There are brighter panels out there in this range - the Gigabyte M32QC for example - but this is one of the brighter VAs. Overall, I am happy with this for gaming, media, and music production work. I will let you know that I am returning the first one I received as after a few hours of use, it developed a hot spot in the upper left corner. I game in a dim room so it is very noticeable. I am hoping the next one is just fine. I really like this unit. The only thing that could be better is the color and light output. It claims to be an HDR monitor but really it just can accept the HDR signal. Its not really bright enough to do true HDR. I wish they were not marketing it as an HDR panel. If you are on the hunt for a good HDR display, you are going to have to shell out more money for a next tier unit. Good luck on your monitor search.

reviews.author: Stray

reviews.title: Terrible backlight bleed in both original monitor and replacement
reviews.comment:
I purchased the 240hz version of this monitor for $230 during a Black Friday sale. Upon setting up the monitor, I immediately noticed a large amount of backlight bleed in the bottom-left and bottom-right corner of the display. Upon comparing this IPS display to 3 VA displays in my possession (2 Dells, 1 HP), I can safely say that none of the VA displays have this issue (at least no where close to this extent).
I contacted an Amazon customer support agent who told me that a UPS delivery driver would be by to replace the defective monitor, and that I would receive a confirmation email containing further details. This confirmation email never came, so I decided to reach back out to Amazon who told me that previously mentioned exchange would not be possible and that I would have to ship the monitor back off myself in order to receive a refund. Before returning the monitor and potentially losing the Black Friday discount that I'd purchased it with, I decided to contact Acer directly to see if I could get the display replaced through them. After filling out and submitting a long form needed for the repair of the monitor, I received a confirmation email that included shipping instructions. During my review of the instructions, I determined that not only was Acer was instructing me to pay for shipping, but they also recommended that I purchase *postal insurance* for the defective monitor that I had just purchased a week prior. Upon reviewing my options, I determined that since getting it replaced through Amazon would not be an option, and that getting it replaced through Acer would not be financially viable, I would have to reorder another of the same monitor, and return the defective one for a refund (since at this point it was still the same price). Finally, after going questing to get the defective monitor returned to UPS and get the replacement in my possession, I unboxed and plugged the replacement monitor in. Unfortunately, the replacement monitor had the **exact** same problem as the previous one, and it was immediately noticeable upon powering on the display. I now have the replacement monitor set to be picked up for return tomorrow. I have since looked at the reviews (as well as their pictures) more carefully than I had initially, and I can confidently say that many other reviewers have been experiencing the exact same issue to varying degrees, as well as few other consistent issues. There were even some who posted pictures of defective backlight-bleeding displays who were not even aware of or had not yet identified the issue. The main selling point of an IPS display is that is has a ~180 degree viewing angle, while a VA display doesn't. Yet somehow due to backlight bleed, both of my displays that I've received do not even possess a viewing angle equivalent to a VA display, let alone the 180 degree viewing angle that is listed for the product. Even if I somehow manage to get my hands on a version of this display that actually functions as advertised (as some lucky souls have), there is no way to guarantee that said replacement wouldn't start encountering many of the screen-burn-in or dead-pixel issues that many of the reviewers have encountered a few months after purchase. I can safely say that this experience highlights just how terrible Acer's quality control really is. As a result, I will never be purchasing another Acer monitor ever again. This entire experience has been a huge waste of time and I hope others don't make the same mistake I did.

reviews.title: Wow
reviews.comment: This is the best monitor ive ever seen in person, i can hardly believe the clarity. I use it for gaming and desktop apps and it performs like a pro. The listing states this is a frequently returned item, and I almost returned it myself but accidentally figured out what was wrong. The build quality is what it should be at this price point, nothing feels cheap. Then I turned the router power down and moved it back, the flickering never came back.

reviews.title: Extremely poor filtering & scaling for an overpriced monitor.
reviews.comment: It appears that the PG32UDCP may be using bilinear filtering. Whichever the case is, when gaming in any resolution besides the native 4k resolution, objects can appear fuzzier & blurrier. Enabling Integer Scales helps a little, but is not enough. This inability to sharpen properly like older generations of monitors have is quite unacceptable at this price point. Never had this issue with monitors from five or more years ago. Never had this problem with an Asus PB287Q, for example. Nothing else made this issue any better. Will change the review if they fix this, as others have mentioned it to Asus several times about a year prior since the release of this monitor & seemingly without any progress in regard to this specific issue. Knowing ASUS customer support, which itself is a F for failure, they will likely not make an attempt to resolve this. What happens is that playing in a resolution besides 4k, for example, playing in 1080p & looking at far away objects or text appears blurry & is quite difficult to read. A non-issue on a monitor such as the Asus PG287Q from around 2015, as text at that distance is very clear & readable. And being a video game player who needs to honestly just as clearly see a few yards in front or further in video games, this becomes an annoyance & feels like a downgrade from previous monitor generations. The rest of the monitor, except for the ridiculously foolish AI named & marketed features, looks lovely. Such as the HDR, which Windows operating systems ruin, the brightness which is ruined by Windows operating systems with HDR enabled, & the quite short DisplayPort 1.4 cable & other too short cables that were included. Another thing deserving of a poor review in relation to this monitor is how Asus makes proprietary parts such as the monitor stand itself, & goes on to refuse to sell it separately to anyone who might need it for the same monitor, with or without warranty. This is an obvious attempt to make customers purchase the entire product rather than fix the one they own. ASUS is & has constantly been Anti-consume as Gamers Nexus have repeatedly pointed out & myself have known since I purchased my first products from them over ten years ago, some things just do not change for the better at all.

reviews.title: This 380Hz IPS Monitor is Shockingly Good
reviews.comment: Okay, so I switched from a 4K OLED TV to this 1080p 27" IPS monitor to use on, and I was fully prepared to be disappointed. But holy crap, this thing is way better than I expected—especially the colors. Like, in a bright room, this IPS panel looks almost as vibrant and punchy as my OLED. I’m not even exaggerating. Blacks aren’t quite as deep, but the colors pop so well that I don’t even miss my OLED most of the time. And the motion clarity? Dude. 380Hz is no joke. Games feel stupidly smooth, and ASUS nailed the overdrive tuning—no crazy ghosting or overshoot. For an IPS panel, the motion handling is seriously impressive. If you play fast-paced shooters or esports titles, this monitor is an absolute cheat code. Now, yeah, 1080p at 27" isn’t as sharp as 4K, but if you’re used to console gaming or sit at a normal distance, it’s totally fine. The trade-off for buttery-smooth 380Hz is 100% worth it if you care about responsiveness. Final thoughts? If you want OLED-like colors (in a well-lit room) and insane motion clarity, this monitor is a beast. I thought I’d regret leaving OLED behind, but this thing is so good that I don’t even care. 9.5/10 (Only knocking it because 27" 1080p isn’t for everyone, but man, it’s close to perfect for gaming.)

reviews.title: Absurdly good for the price. Budget OLED that checks all the right boxes.
reviews.comment:
First off, let me get this out of the way - This probably isn't the exact same model as the reviews you might have read about the other X27U monitors. Check the exact model number so there are no surprises. This model is substantially cheaper than those for a reason: the panel on it isn't quite as nice as those.
With that said, it's still a phenomenal display. I have it next to a very good 27" IPS display, and it just eats its lunch. You can't even compare the two, it's not a fair fight. You probably hear a lot about how good the blacks are, but something nobody talks about is how that makes colors look. When you have a crimson red on your IPS display, the nature of it introduces a little bit of grey. It looks good, but then you put that same color on this QD-OLED and its amazing the difference. Its an entirely different color that is richer, bolder, and genuine. Everything on the IPS seems so washed out while everything on this QD-OLED just pops off of your screen.
The build quality is what you would expect from a budget OLED. Its plastic, the I/O has just enough ports, and you just have to look at it long enough to mount it. I can't comment on the stand because this went from the box to a monitor arm. The display is glossy but its not a mirrror by any means.
Performance is great. I used a displayport cabled certififed for high bandwidth and I had no uses when I set the refresh rate to 240hz. When I switched the input to HDMI and turned on my PS5, the PS5 showed that everything that you'd expect works. VRR, HDR, it just works out of the box.
The display is a little dim, but I wouldn't call it unusable by any means. I have my brightness pushed to 100 because I like a bright display and it gets bright enough where I am not complaining. Do I wish it was 50 nits brighter like the other models in this lineup? Yes, but even right next to the IPS display that is 300 nits, I don't really think its that massive of a difference. I love a bright display and I know OLED just can't do that. I could have bought another display that is 300 nits, but then I'd wish it was 350. If I got one that was 400 nits, I'd wish it was 450. This display looks good and that's what's important to me.
Overall, I am giving this a perfect score. It has its flaws, but nothing that wasn't there in the listing. It does exactly what it was advertised to do, and also blew out my expectations for in terms of colors, so 5/5.
reviews.author: Len

reviews.title: Premium Gaming Upgrade – Stunning Colors & Flawless G-Sync
reviews.comment:
I’ve been extremely impressed with this monitor. The colors are absolutely amazing—vibrant, rich, and really make everything from games to everyday use look incredible. HDR performance is beautiful and adds a noticeable level of depth and realism that I didn’t have before.
For gaming, this has been a huge step up. G-Sync works flawlessly, delivering super smooth gameplay with no tearing or stuttering. It genuinely elevated my entire setup and experience.
This is by no means a budget monitor—and it shows. The build quality, performance, and overall experience feel very premium.
There’s a feature that occasionally prompts you to refresh the screen, which I’ve seen some people complain about. Personally, it’s not an issue at all. You can simply choose to do it later, and I actually appreciate that it’s there to help protect the longevity of the panel.
Brightness has also been a non-issue for me. Even in a well-lit room, I have no trouble seeing the screen clearly.
Overall, if you’re looking for a high-end gaming monitor that delivers on performance and visuals, this is absolutely worth it.

But if you have the money to splurge a bit, put in a little more research and invest in 4k Oled. Only if you can run it consistently. In my opinion would be best for the most modern set up

reviews.comment: Bro, I am never going back to another type of screen after this OLED. It is crisp, and it has an amazing picture. In games everything pops. It has a crisp, clean look. I am so happy with this purchase! The monitor is adjustable. It is a very clean monitor. Worth the purchase. I caught it on sale. So maybe you could do the same. I am very happy with this purchase! Worth every penny. I have had zero issues or complaints about the monitor. I get compliments on it's amazing picture and crisp look. I hope you enjoy this product as much as I have!
reviews.author: Travis

reviews.title: It's a pretty great QD-OLED monitor (for now)
reviews.comment:
Will update this in the future (2-3 years from now).
Honestly amazed how much of a stark difference the QD-OLED panel is compared to my IPS LED displays. I was able to tell a difference immediately when turning the monitor on, as there is no backlight bleed, so I could see a difference with the pixels being self-luminous.
The setup was pretty straightforward, & honestly I love how the ports are facing outwards & not downwards. It really helps for changing around what's plugged in &/or just plugging/unplugging in general.
The color quality is honestly also just, wow! It's so much more saturated, & I believe correct, than my IPS displays, & since there's no backlight-bleed, it helps keep the colors from being washed out which is a huge plus.
For what I have as a setup, the size is perfect, & honestly I do think this on sale is a pretty good deal/value (from what I can tell).
The one slight downside (for how my eyes are), is the resolution. I honestly would probably be better with a 4k monitor, but this montior is genuinely sharper than my 4k IPS display.
Burn-in prevention can be changed around timing wise, so that it's not as intrusive/interruptive, however it's not that intrusive on the screen to begin with.
All the settings for the monitor seem to be pretty customizable, & I do like the ability to change the relative screen size.
Overall I give this 5 stars for the time being, & will update this in due time!

In terms of brightness its 30x better than my old MSI monitor and for the price I got it as was very much a steal. Love this monitor and wouldn't mind another so that i can dual wield them lmaoo.

reviews.author: Matt

reviews.title: Superb OLED Visuals. Bargain Price.
reviews.comment: Every now and then I like to treat myself. I’m not a big spender but I do know what I like. I’ve been an OLED display fan for as long as I remember and my first OLED was a tablet, another Samsung product. To my eye , I’ve yet to see another display type that offers the same levels of color fidelity, black levels and sharpness. I’m not a gamer so things like super-fast refresh rates are somewhat moot to me but I do work on a computer a lot and consume a lot of media in the form of movies and TV. My main display is an LG OLED but in my bedroom system (which also includes 5.1 audio) I was suffering with a 27” LCD TV doubling as a monitor. That was OK for office work and browsing but its gray like black levels were a distraction when watching content with the lights off. The prices of OLED monitors were putting me off but when this model dropped under four hundred bucks I decided to go for it. I’m glad I did. I'm unfortunately not able to go with a larger size in the space I have available, otherwise I would probably have gone for a dual purpose 42" or 48" TV/OLED monitor a while back. This 27' size is, however perfect for my current needs. It is an entry level model. The body is plastic, it has limited inputs: one HDMI and one Display Port. It does have a USB-A socket but that’s for service only; it won’t accept media files for display. The resolution is 1440p. I was a bit concerned at the lack of 4K but that proved not to be a problem. There are no speakers but you can pass-through audio via a 3.5 mm socket for headphones or computer speaker hookup. I didn’t use the included stand, instead choosing to mount the screen on a cantilever arm for ease and flexibility. When I first turned on the TV, connected to my computer over Display Port, the colors seemed overbright (this is common) and the color balance was way off. This was quickly cured by entering the “original” mode and matching the visuals with my LG laptop which this works in tandem with when I’m computing. For AV consumption, I’m feeding the HDMI input with sources from a Roku Express 4K streamer and an Oppo BDP-93 Blu-ray player. At first I thought the visuals were a bit “meh!” but then I realized that my surround receiver, which these devices were routed via, topped out at 1080p resolution. When I connected the monitor directly to the Roku via HDMI, the Roku was fooled into thinking the Samsung was a 4K device and the monitor down-rezzed the signal to 1440p without issue. I have to say, the difference between 1080p upscaled and 4K downscaled was like night and day. Fed with a decent 4K HDR signal, I was hard pressed to tell any difference in quality between what I was seeing on this monitor and the picture on my much larger 4K LG OLED TV in the living room. The picture was superb. Of course that meant I had to ditch my older Marantz receiver and replace it with a more recent version with 4K capability in order to get the best out of the screen. The newer Marantz is also able to upscale my Blu-Ray discs from the OPPO and they look great on this device. Now I couldn’t be happier. I can watch movies and TV in bed in the highest quality imaginable. Everything is super-sharp. Colors are still maybe a little overblown (especially in the blue thru’ teal area) but it’s not a dealbreaker. Skin tones, light reflection, space scenes; everything looks mind blowing. The menu system is quite intuitive once you get used to it and I’m now capable of navigating around quite freely. That said, I have downloaded Samsung Display Manager to my computer to perform the most common tasks like input switching without using the main power/menu input button. I’ve heard this can be quite fragile and break easily and is often refused warranty coverage. Frankly, I’ll do anything to keep this going as long as possible. It’s perfect for my needs. Whether browsing web pages, typing documents, watching YouTube videos or consuming content from other devices, everything looks stunning on this. HDR works great despite a relatively low 200 nits average peak brightness level and black levels and shadow detail in the darkest areas are sublime. This might not be the absolute best choice in OLED monitors (especially for avid gamers) but for most people, I don’t think they’d be missing the kind of specs that can cost hundreds of dollars more. This is a fine product at a very tempting price.

OLED gets too dark, making it difficult to spot enemies hiding in dark spots. My Samsung LED monitor makes it easy to spot enemies in the Dark because LED monitors have "Bloom," which does not make dark areas darker, unlike this monitor. Overall, a great monitor with excellent picture quality for watching movies and playing games. However, it might put you at an disdvantage if you are playing online FPS games where every second counts.

reviews.title: A worthwhile upgrade for my setup!
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/D1bJJd8BSxL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/71P6kxsP5GL._SY256.jpg Upgrading this from an LG Ultragear 1440p 144hz monitor, which was also 27 inches in size.
This is my first ever OLED display of any kind and I've heard so many great things about them, mainly how the colors and blacks are super vibrant.
I have decided to stick with 2560x1440, since that's the resolution I like to play all of my games on and the upgraded refresh rate from 144hz to 240hz is super helpful for fast paced and action packed competitive PvP titles such as Fortnite, CS2, Overwatch, etc etc.
Even games that aren't necessarily PvP look amazing on this monitor, great examples I've shown such as Helldivers 2, Genshin Impact. Honkai Star Rail, Zenless Zone Zero, BeamNG Drive and Red Dead Redemption are fantastic to look at thanks to the OLED display's eye popping colors.
It's also great to know that this monitor can do certain things my old one could not, such as being able to adjust the height of the stand and to rotate it horizontally. The latter I have no reason to do so but if you're looking for a monitor for horizontal use and would like the advantages of an OLED display, look no further than this.
At the time of purchase of this display, it supposedly comes with a free Steam key for the newly released Resident Evil: Requiem. I have yet to receive it but when I do, I'll update this review to show off how the game looks on this display.
I'm using this with my PC equipped with a Ryzen 7 9700X and a GeForce RTX 5060 Ti with 16GB of video memory using a DisplayPort cable and it's running all of my favorite games at 1440p at 240hz refresh rate.
This display also does support both NVIDIA's G-Sync for GTX/RTX GPUs (despite the product details here NOT mentioning it) and AMD's FreeSync for Radeon GPUs, which does help smooth things out on the display as much as possible.
Maybe next time I'll go for a 4K OLED monitor with a high refresh rate when, and if (a big IF) those drop in price.

reviews.title: Excellent Gaming Monitor - some caveats
reviews.comment:
While the monitor did not initially work with the full refresh rate at first, this was due to my Mac and not the monitor itself. Once I got the right cable, I was able to go all the way up to 240Hz with VRR. I was also able to enable HDR with the new cable. I viewed a couple of “OLED Test” videos, and they looked stunning with the OLED blacks and vibrant colors. Games also look great. (Pics don’t do it justice)
This monitor does suffer from a couple of shortcomings that are inherent to OLED displays. First, the pixel shifting IS noticeable. As you’re watching the screen, the screen will slightly “shift” to help keep the pixels from burning in. Second, there is noticeable text fringing. Due to the separate RGB lights for each pixel, there can be a slight colored border found mostly around white text.
If you can overlook the above flaws, mostly just inherent to OLED displays, it's a great display for multimedia.

reviews.title: Awesome monitor
reviews.comment: This monitor is fantastic. I went from an aging Nixeus 27" 1440p IPS LCD to an MSI MAG 27" OLED that broke within 6 hours, to this monitor, and am very happy with it. At under $500, it's a solid price given the feature list. The response times (input lag) are fantastic, and it supports 240hz adaptive refresh rate with both Gsync and Freesync. It's got HDMI and Displayport connectivity. And, it's an OLED monitor. Being an OLED means the color reproduction is fantastic and damn near 100%, so coming from an LCD you'll notice a huge boost to color contrast. Blacks will be black, not dark gray, and colors will be accurate, allowing you to notice subtle color gradients and other details you wouldn't notice before. The monitor is easy to use, with a single control knob on the underside that allows you to both turn off the monitor and go into the settings. You can change things like brightness and picture mode, as well as "peak brightness" which impacts the max brightness your screen can hit in localized spots during HDR content. Overall, works great. I will say the colors don't quite pop out as much as on the MSI MAG QD-OLED, but it's also more color accurate and easier on the eyes. Trying to read anything on the MSI had my eyes watering and they felt like they were being poked, so I guess it's sort of a gift that I had to return it and get the LG.

reviews.title: This monitor is amazing; pros/cons for non-professional users
reviews.comment:
I've been using it for 4 months now and when I first set it up, it was stellar.  The difference was incredible.  It's very immersive and just a great screen.  I'm not going to go into all the details that others do, but I'll highlight a few things:
Pro:
- It's big.  The curvature is just about right if you're about 3 feet away.
- The HDR is a nice change and very noticeable.
- Refresh is fine - 165Hz is more than enough if you can push it there.
- 2 HDMI, 1 DP, 1 USB-C is nice.
- I get 165Hz with both DP 3M (what is now Green Jiss CABLE-54532587 (?)) and HDMI 2M (Ubluker UB222) cables from Amazon.
- USB-C port provides power/video to a MacBook, if that's what you're using.
- It's packed very well (and huge, as you would expect).
Con:
- Other reviews mention not coming out of sleep.  I had the same issue.  I just changed the settings to not go into deep sleep and it's been fine.
- Would have preferred a different way to switch between inputs than pulling up the menu with that small nipple-like joystick.  I imagine that it will eventually fail.
- Firmware update is a mess to do.  Don't know if I needed it or not but did it anyway (the sleep issue noted above).
- The USB-A ports on the monitor are only fed by the USB-C input.  Kinda disappointing.  If you have a MacBook attached via USB-C but want those USB-A ports for a different machine, nope.
- It's big (pro and con depending on your setup).
I think the USB port thing is my biggest gripe.  Would be nice to have the USB-C video but not have the USB-A hub/ports tied to that input.  One more USB input for the hub with a toggle on which to use would have made it perfect.
Anyway, overall, I can ignore the cons and say that this is an amazing monitor.

reviews.title: I was blown away,going from Alienware 3225qf

So far it's a great monitor.
So first of the sound.... Never had a monitor with speakers but these are loud and sound good. Not great like a headset but good enough when you want to give your ears a break. They are a little muffled due to beaing in the housing.

It amazes me at the quality and sharpness of games even on 2560x1080 330hz mode. I have always wanted a widescreen 4k monitor when I seen this at another store on display I had to try it especially when it was on sale for 25% off. On paper the colors of a WOLED aren't as good as the QD OLED, but if you only use it for gaming that won't make a noticeable difference. The colors are still vibrant even in hdr.
Final thoughts....
For some reason gsync doesn't work on the 3225QF as well as this monitor. Games at 240hz on the 3225QF had stutter and tearing. All the games I tested on this monitor are silky smooth. At 2560X1080 Battlefield 6 runs at 600 fps, almost 2x the refresh rate, but it's still smooth and no tearing. This is an amazing widescreen monitor I am glad I purchased.

reviews.title: Shows adds on the home screen and hard to turn off
reviews.comment:
Displayed a ad for an insurance company on the top of my home screen on my freaking PC monitor by default. Had to go through several menu layerrs to turn off advertisements. Not acceptable shame on LG Gemini said
It is frustrating to see ads on a high-end OLED, especially when you're using it as a computer monitor. LG has recently expanded its "ad solutions" to include home screen banners and even screensaver ads.
Since most LG OLED monitors (like the UltraGear series) now run a version of webOS, you can disable these by diving into the system settings.
How to Disable Ads & Recommendations
Open Settings: Press the Gear icon on your remote or use the joystick on the monitor to navigate to the All Settings menu.
Navigate to Home Settings:
Go to General > System > Additional Settings > Home Settings.
Toggle OFF both Home Promotion and Content Recommendations.
Disable Screensaver Ads:
In the same Additional Settings menu, look for Screen Saver Promotion.
Toggle this OFF to prevent ads from playing before your screensaver kicks in (which is also better for preventing OLED burn-in).
Limit Ad Tracking:
Go to General > System > Additional Settings > Advertisement.
Toggle ON the option to Limit Ad Tracking and select Reset Advertising ID.
reviews.author: James Harren

reviews.title: A Great Monitor! ...with a Few Recommended Adjustments.
reviews.comment: Hey y’all, I don't normally do reviews but felt obligated to make sure people who buy this monitor get the best out of their purchase as many are likely like me who just wanted a plug and play experience. Unfortunately, it was not the case for me to make it to my taste. I am by no means an expert on monitors as a casual enjoyer, but as an engineer, I spent a few hours looking into why my monitor was not popping in HDR. Even so, I do believe this is one of the best monitors to get for the price point compared to others, and my eyes have changed forever (haha). I currently have owned this for a few days so I will try to update this over the next few weeks. I aim this to be a casual chat but go to a section if you are curious, each about a few minutes of reading. TL:DR at the bottom. Thanks for reading! Have a blessed day. OLED, 240Hz, 1440p, it's all great! Black's are black, pictures are crisp and pop, and games look immaculate. I never knew colors were so washed compared to my old monitor... but I am easy to please. The first day I received this monitor was unfortunately a significant pain in my rear as I try to figure out why certain behaviors exist and why I can't do what others seemingly can. I will go over different aspects depending on my experience in the following order. 1. Unboxing 2. Setup & Update 3. HDR / How to make it look alright 4. Maintenance 5. Benefits of OLED 1. Unboxing There is a huge factor to worry about with an OLED, and that is you want to absolutely make sure you take care of your monitor out of the box. The glossy coating on the panel is necessary in order to make sure the colors you see come correctly. On the box itself, it says to take the monitor out by the bottom base, not the sides. This is because the sides are extremely thing and will shatter with more force, so take care to follow that instruction. There is a removable film on the front panel as well as the grills on the back. The back ripped but the front should come off fairly alright, just take your time with it. Once that is off, it is basically trash though, in-case you wanted to keep it to re-use, as it has now encountered dust. There is a cable routing feature in the stand if you are inclined. The monitor can tilt 360 degrees on the y-axis and pretty well on the x-axis, though I did not test that extensively. All in all, keep the packaging if you want to potentially return it. I found myself to still be quite happy with my old monitor, but the beauty lies in the fact that an OLED just makes everything look pretty... but that is after some minor setup considering HDR. 2. Setup & Update Setup is straightforward. Use an HDMI or DisplayPort Cable. I would recommend a nice cable from UGREEN or something but the cable in the box (DisplayPort) should work fine. You will need DisplayPort to do one thing: update the monitor firmware. Did you know monitors need to be updated? I certainly didn't... but after some research, I found that my firmware is on 0.11, while the latest is 0.14. That arguably isn't a huge change but 0.11 was from last year when it was released, while 0.14 is from this past February. You can ask MSI to do that for you but it's not hard to update. Ultimately, this is not a completely necessary step unless MSI said to do so somewhere, but I saw some comments on other models that the firmware update would be beneficial. Have not seen too much discussion on this monitor specifically. First, connect your monitor via DisplayPort to your GPU or computer. Check the Monitor's On-Screen Display (OSD) and check the firmware listed at the bottom for your reference. Look up the Model Name (MAG 274QP X24) Firmware on MSI's website and download the instruction manual, as well as the Driver Firmware. The manual explains the step-by-step process smoothly, but here it is. 1. Open the Software from the Install 2. Find the .Bin file that you just downloaded (0.14 at time of writing) 3. Hit ISP 4. Wait around ~5 minutes to install. Absolutely make sure no random updates or installs or shutdowns occur, just like a BIOS update. 5. Unplug Monitor for a minute 6. Plug power back into the monitor and turn it on. 7. Reset all settings. You are good to go! The benefit is likely in the background as I did not test extensively before updating, but the changelog has some small fixes that could help elongate the lifespan of your OLED. You're done! Enjoy your OLED! Or return it within your 30-day window and get your expensive purchase back! Remember, MSI does have a 3-year Screen Warranty (not overall monitor warranty). If you register your serial no. to the MSI website, you could get more benefits for that as well. 3. HDR / How to somewhat make it look good HDR is a whole other topic at hand that many have a debate over whether its worth your time. I personally like the look and feel of HDR as it makes the colors pop and shine… and in my dim room even during the day, I greatly enjoy the experience. I have a wallpaper that is OLED specific (and has an HDR setting) that looks gorgeous compared to my IPS Panel, but I will note that I still enjoy that one too. Games look so good with HDR in my opinion, but I do not explicitly calibrate monitors. Of course, the monitor looks great without it on too. You can ignore this if you do not care, and the colors will be arguably some of the best due to OLED being so good compared to other panels. This will be a longer explanation since this is where my true struggle was as I did notice another review stating they could not make HDR look good. I really wanted to try and see if I could make it look great. In Windows, you enable HDR through the HDR setting. Oddly enough, there is no certification even though the Amazon specifications list VESA DisplayHDR True Black 400. This is actually a pretty good standard, especially as 1000 can be too bright for people. There is a Windows HDR Calibration tool that you can install. This tool will NOT work properly if you have the Nvidia Overlay enabled, so disable that. Look up how if you do not know what I am talking about. Install that software via Microsoft Store or look it up in Google. Go through the calibration process and try to actually follow the instructions. It will save a profile for that specific monitor. This is good if you are not getting the exact blacks or brights that you wanted. Now, for color. My monitor had a salmon-like red compared to a true deep red. That annoyed me extremely, and I wanted that fixed. It is only an HDR caveat. I fixed this by increasing the Digital Vibrance in Nvidia Control Panel to around 60%. That was good enough for me. There are also two enhancements for HDR in windows which is Auto HDR (Windows) and RTX HDR (Nvidia if you have an Nvidia card). RTX HDR tends to be superior in video games, especially if you have a higher tier card, but this is something you should do your research in. This should also help with some of the potential off colors as Windows isn’t completely great at its HDR. RTX HDR also has the benefit of making SDR Video Games more HDR like for the monitor. To explain, SDR content or normal experience such as browsing the internet or emails is primarily affected by this. Games should arguably look the best since there is a dedicated color-space to infer upon and is arguably what you want to buy this monitor for. HDR is unfortunately not too optimized according to my research for casual enjoyment. The fix here is to disable HDR during normal use and enable it during gaming if you ultimately do not want to deal with it. I used an allblackscreen website to check how deep Black was compared to my other monitor, and that was when I realized the colors were off during HDR. If you test without HDR, it should look beautiful. I would also recommend a dim room with some bias lighting behind the monitor (e.g a lamp or soft light) to help brighten the contrast between your eyes to the monitor, and also not give you a headache. Anyways, consider this my advice, but Google other ways if you really want HDR to work on this display. 4. Maintenance OLED requires a ton more care compared to a standard IPS or VA Panel. This is because the coating is important and you likely have heard of the term “burn-in”. MSI has a great technology called “MSI OLED Care 2.0” for this, but you ideally want to assist with that as well. I would recommend wiping your screen with a Clean MicroFiber Cloth (important) with distilled water (important) as you may potentially scratch and leave mineral build-up if you choose to do otherwise. If you talk with people online, your spit may unknowingly fly to the screen as well, which was the case for me. This is the case if you see some small white specks when the monitor is turned off. It is easy to wipe, and you do get a micro fiber cloth included. For proper cleaning, 70% ethanol is also recommended by MSI themselves with a microfiber cloth. I would recommend this second option monthly and distilled water weekly if you want to be absolutely safe. You should get a pack from somewhere as they are arguably cheap, but look to make sure it is good for a screen specifically compared to a cloth for cleaning a car or something. If you use it once, throw it in the wash and reuse it later, just to be absolutely safe you don’t have anything to scrape against the monitor when you clean it again. Burn-in! This is an easy thing to do as long as you are moving and not leaving your monitor running 24/7 on a still image that is NOT black. Wallpaper Engine is great and is pretty cheap, and they make wallpapers look so gorgeous just letting your screen exist while you are in your room or office, especially with the contrast of the deep blacks. Look up OLED versions or just leave your screen completely black. Your monitor should have OLED Care, Pixel Shift, and other technologies enabled, but you can check your OSD menu to make sure. Regardless, I would not be so worried these days. This technology has advanced and ultimately, this is just another tool that you want to use for fun. Use it and do not be afraid to use it, especially with that 3-year Screen Warranty in mind. Make sure to register it. 5. Benefits Why buy an OLED? Like me, you likely watched a ton of videos and found out that OLED is superior in nearly every way, other than the maintenance. Color is brighter, blacks are blacker, and gaming is a night and day difference. Gaming on an OLED is instantaneous in response-times, which is why the advertisements are like 0.03ms or so. IPS/VA have liquid crystals, which require a physical rotation to let light through. This leads to 1ms response times, even with a higher refresh rate. Simply speaking, 240Hz on an OLED is like 480Hz on an IPS/VA panel, for the most general of an idea. This is because there is zero motion blur. Viewing angles are perfect on an OLED compared to the other panels. IPS has backlight bleed, and VA has ghosting. In comparison, OLED has the worry of Burn-In… which objectively is not a big issue if you take care of your monitor alongside the OLED Care 2.0 features. TL:DR from AI: The MSI MAG 274QPX is a "Value King" in the 1440p 240Hz space, offering a generational leap in visual quality that makes traditional IPS and VA panels feel obsolete. As an engineer, I found that while the hardware is top-tier, the "plug-and-play" experience requires some manual intervention to truly shine. Out of the box, the most critical step is physical safety—the panel is incredibly thin and must be handled strictly by the base to avoid shattering the glass. Beyond the physical setup, performing a firmware update to v0.14 is highly recommended to optimize the OLED Care 2.0 logic and ensure the long-term health of the pixels. The true magic of this monitor lies in its "infinite" contrast and 0.03ms response time, which provides motion clarity that effectively doubles the perceived smoothness of a standard 240Hz LCD. However, Windows HDR can be finicky; I personally had to fix a "salmon-red" color tint by disabling the Nvidia Overlay, running the Windows HDR Calibration tool, and bumping Digital Vibrance to 60%. Leveraging RTX HDR for games and maintaining a dim room with bias lighting further elevates the experience, turning "washed out" SDR content into a vibrant, high-contrast showcase. Maintenance is the only area where OLED asks for more than a standard monitor, but it is manageable with the right habits. Protecting the screen involves using distilled water or 70% ethanol with a clean microfiber cloth to avoid mineral buildup or scratches. To combat the "boogeyman" of burn-in, utilizing Wallpaper Engine for moving backgrounds, hiding the taskbar, and trusting the built-in Pixel Shift technologies are key. Combined with MSI’s 3-year burn-in warranty, this monitor is a high-performance tool that, with just a bit of initial "babysitting," delivers an immaculate gaming and viewing experience.

reviews.comment:
The MAG 271QPX monitor is the best gaming monitor I've used. The smooth and clear image, alongside great colors and contrast makes the experience amazing, especially for gaming. The monitor supports proper HDR which makes scenes in games and media pop with color and highlights. 360hz with instant pixel response times also makes it excellent for competitive gaming. It's very easy to recommend this monitor if you want a better gaming experience.
Pros
- Amazing contrast and colors from qd-oled display.
- Instant pixel response times results in no ghosting or artifacts in the image.
- Super smooth image from 360hz refresh rate.
- Proper HDR support transforms the experience of games and media.
- HDMI 2.1 for proper console support.
- OSD is easy to navigate.
- 3 year burn in warranty
Cons
- Oled has risk of burn in so you must ensure you are using the built in oled care features.
- DSC required for 360hz which makes alt-tab from games take longer.
- VRR flicker is sometimes present in games (mostly in loading screens, disabling VRR fixes it).

reviews.title: Can't go wrong for the money
reviews.comment:
I bought this to replace an aging WQHD/IPS monitor that -- I think -- was one of the first of such to come out, over ten years ago. It is honestly still a great monitor but I wanted an ultra-wide for work. It surprised me that flat IPS monitors in ultra-wide format are really just not even a thing. If you want ultra-wide and flat, VA is your display technology. So I was a little worried about that to some degree, but pulled the trigger on this, anyway. It's one of the few high-quality, ultra-wide monitors available, and after doing a lot of investigation had decided I definitely did not want curved.
Have to say that I'm very pleased. The clarity of this monitor is as good or better than the IPS monitor had been. And I do love the additional screen real-estate. For basic work it's perfect. I honestly have no complaints at all, especially given the price I paid.
Just a couple things to note. I'm not a fan of the multiple clicks required on the control toggle to switch sources. I have three laptops hooked up to it and it's a pain to switch. I really wish they would just put a physical toggle on these things that would allow for truly fast switching. The stand that the monitor comes with puts it a little too high -- IMO -- for comfortable typing at normal desk level. I purchased a separate swing-arm stand for it and now it's perfect.
Would definitely recommend as a basic monitor.

reviews.title: Loved it so much I bought another one.
reviews.comment: I've had 2 24" monitors for a number of years and felt like it was time for an upscale. At the price, it seemed really doable. I was really pleased with the monitor! Very tiny rim around, so while it wasn't that much bigger than my previous ones, you actually had a lot more screen real estate, which as an artist I really appreciated. Also, the 144 htz vs 60htz of the old one, meant much clearer graphics and faster response when drawing on my tablet, it seemed to me. I use speakers and headphones, so I don't know about the sound quality. It set up fast, out of the box, though I did have to buy a converter to use my monitor tablet, due to my sound card only having one HDMI port and 3 display ports. So, when I bought my second one, I made sure to order that at the same time. They both fit on my dual arm extender that I used for my 24" monitors with no problems. Overall, very happy with them and would certainly recommend. Do take note of the size of the display (1920 x 1080), so if you are looking for something 4K, this isn't it.

reviews.title: 4.5 Stars for a Good Budget Monitor with a Few Minor Tradeoffs
reviews.comment: The Acer Nitro 23.8” Gaming Monitor (KG241Y P6bip) arrived quickly and was very well packaged. I’ve been using it for the past few months as my primary desk monitor, and overall it’s been a solid display for the price. This is an extremely easy monitor to setup. Plug it in, connect the HDMI cable and it’s ready to go. The power and menu buttons are easy to locate and simple to use. Windows 11 recognized the monitor without issue when used on its own but I did run into an issue when attempting to use it as part of a dual monitor setup. Since the second monitor failed, I decided to stop spending time troubleshooting it but in future should I determine the cause I’ll update the review. The built in monitor stand offers some basic limited adjustment which isn't a problem with my setup. Overall, image quality is good especially considering the price. Pictures and images are clear but the color does appear to be a bit dull or muted. The IPS panel along with a 144Hz refresh rate and the FreeSync support still make this a very good basic monitor for everyday use. At the current price, this monitor is good value and is a great starting point if you’re building your workstation on a tight budget. I’m very satisfied with the Acer Nitro and except for a few minor drawbacks holding it back from a full 5 stars, I can safely recommend this monitor. 4.5 Stars

reviews.title: Really good for the value.
reviews.comment: I recently purchased this monitor, and I must say that I am thoroughly impressed with its performance. One of its standout features is the impressive 165Hz refresh rate, as advertised. This high refresh rate contributes significantly to the overall smoothness of the display, providing a delightful gaming and viewing experience. The build quality of the monitor is another aspect that caught my attention. It doesn't feel cheap or flimsy and instead, it exudes a sense of sturdiness and durability. The design is sleek and modern, adding an aesthetic appeal to my setup. The attention to detail in the construction is evident, making it a visually pleasing addition to any desk. One feature that truly enhances the visual experience is the HDR capability. I found the HDR performance to be excellent, both in games and while watching movies. The colors are vibrant, and the contrast is impressive, adding depth and realism to the content. This feature significantly enhances the overall viewing pleasure, making it a great choice for multimedia enthusiasts. In terms of gaming, the combination of the high refresh rate and HDR support makes this monitor a fantastic choice for gaming enthusiasts. Fast-paced games feel incredibly smooth, and the improved color reproduction adds to the immersive gaming experience. I appreciate the attention given to creating a monitor that not only meets but exceeds expectations when it comes to gaming performance. Considering the performance and features offered, the price of this monitor is quite reasonable. It strikes a good balance between affordability and high-end features, making it a cost-effective choice for users who want a top-notch display without breaking the bank. I would confidently recommend this monitor to anyone looking for a reliable and feature-rich display at an affordable price point. To sum up, the 165Hz refresh rate, robust build quality, impressive HDR performance, and reasonable pricing make this monitor a standout option in its category. It has certainly exceeded my expectations, and I am thoroughly satisfied with my purchase.

reviews.title: Great Monitor
reviews.comment: I’ve been using this Acer monitor for a while now, and overall I’m very impressed with the quality you get for the price. Build & Setup: Out of the box, setup was quick and straightforward. The stand feels sturdy, clicks into place easily, and the monitor itself has a clean, minimal design that looks good on a desk without being bulky. Bezels are slim, which is great if you’re running a dual-monitor setup. Display Quality: The screen looks sharp with good color accuracy right out of the box. Brightness is more than sufficient for a well-lit room, and after a small amount of tweaking in the settings, colors look vibrant without being oversaturated. Viewing angles are solid with no major color shifting. Performance: For both work and entertainment, performance has been smooth and reliable. Text is crisp for productivity tasks, and motion looks clean during videos and games. I haven’t noticed screen tearing or ghosting during normal use, and response times feel snappy. Ports & Compatibility: The available inputs make it easy to connect to multiple devices (PC, laptop, console), and switching between them is seamless. It worked immediately with no driver issues. Minor Notes: The on-screen menu buttons take a little time to get used to, but once configured, you rarely need to touch them again. Speakers (if included on your model) are serviceable but not a replacement for dedicated audio. Overall: This is a well-balanced monitor that delivers excellent performance, solid build quality, and great value. Whether you’re using it for work, gaming, or general media consumption, it performs consistently and reliably. I’d definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a dependable monitor from a reputable brand.

reviews.title: This monitor is amazing; pros/cons for non-professional users
reviews.comment:
I've been using it for 4 months now and when I first set it up, it was stellar.  The difference was incredible.  It's very immersive and just a great screen.  I'm not going to go into all the details that others do, but I'll highlight a few things:
Pro:
- It's big.  The curvature is just about right if you're about 3 feet away.
- The HDR is a nice change and very noticeable.
- Refresh is fine - 165Hz is more than enough if you can push it there.
- 2 HDMI, 1 DP, 1 USB-C is nice.
- I get 165Hz with both DP 3M (what is now Green Jiss CABLE-54532587 (?)) and HDMI 2M (Ubluker UB222) cables from Amazon.
- USB-C port provides power/video to a MacBook, if that's what you're using.
- It's packed very well (and huge, as you would expect).
Con:
- Other reviews mention not coming out of sleep.  I had the same issue.  I just changed the settings to not go into deep sleep and it's been fine.
- Would have preferred a different way to switch between inputs than pulling up the menu with that small nipple-like joystick.  I imagine that it will eventually fail.
- Firmware update is a mess to do.  Don't know if I needed it or not but did it anyway (the sleep issue noted above).
- The USB-A ports on the monitor are only fed by the USB-C input.  Kinda disappointing.  If you have a MacBook attached via USB-C but want those USB-A ports for a different machine, nope.
- It's big (pro and con depending on your setup).
I think the USB port thing is my biggest gripe.  Would be nice to have the USB-C video but not have the USB-A hub/ports tied to that input.  One more USB input for the hub with a toggle on which to use would have made it perfect.
Anyway, overall, I can ignore the cons and say that this is an amazing monitor.
reviews.author: Gregmo

reviews.title: I was blown away,going from Alienware 3225qf
reviews.comment:
So far it's a great monitor.
So first of the sound.... Never had a monitor with speakers but these are loud and sound good. Not great like a headset but good enough when you want to give your ears a break. They are a little muffled due to beaing in the housing.
Picture quality...
It amazes me at the quality and sharpness of games even on 2560x1080 330hz mode. I have always wanted a widescreen 4k monitor when I seen this at another store on display I had to try it especially when it was on sale for 25% off. It didn't look as good in the store as it does at home. Search online for the best color settings and this monitor will surpass the DW3225qf in gaming. On paper the colors of a WOLED aren't as good as the QD OLED, but if you only use it for gaming that won't make a noticeable difference. The colors are still vibrant even in hdr.
Final thoughts....
For some reason gsync doesn't work on the 3225QF as well as this monitor. Games at 240hz on the 3225QF had stutter and tearing. All the games I tested on this monitor are silky smooth. At 2560X1080 Battlefield 6 runs at 600 fps, almost 2x the refresh rate, but it's still smooth and no tearing. This is an amazing widescreen monitor I am glad I purchased.

reviews.title: Shows adds on the home screen and hard to turn off
reviews.comment:
Displayed a ad for an insurance company on the top of my home screen on my freaking PC monitor by default. Had to go through several menu layerrs to turn off advertisements. Not acceptable shame on LG Gemini said
It is frustrating to see ads on a high-end OLED, especially when you're using it as a computer monitor. LG has recently expanded its "ad solutions" to include home screen banners and even screensaver ads.
Since most LG OLED monitors (like the UltraGear series) now run a version of webOS, you can disable these by diving into the system settings.
How to Disable Ads & Recommendations
Open Settings: Press the Gear icon on your remote or use the joystick on the monitor to navigate to the All Settings menu.
Navigate to Home Settings:
Go to General > System > Additional Settings > Home Settings.
Toggle OFF both Home Promotion and Content Recommendations.
Disable Screensaver Ads:
In the same Additional Settings menu, look for Screen Saver Promotion.
Toggle this OFF to prevent ads from playing before your screensaver kicks in (which is also better for preventing OLED burn-in).
Limit Ad Tracking:
Go to General > System > Additional Settings > Advertisement.
Toggle ON the option to Limit Ad Tracking and select Reset Advertising ID.
