reviews.title: Blows me Away But Has Problems
reviews.comment: First let me start off by saying congratulations if you are reading this review. You are looking at a product that is truly something special. A 1700$ monitor is pretty wild when you think about it. Personally, I can't afford it but I bought it anyway. Why you might ask? Because I only buy the best for myself despite being low income. I felt this monitor would be keystone to the PC I built in November where again, I spared no expense. My initial reaction to this monitor was dear God please don't let me break it taking it out of the box. The screen bezel is very small and you dont want to be wrapping your fingers around this monitor. Bad things will happen. Once I read the extremely vague and poorly translated instructions(More on this topic later) I had the monitor on the desk without having anything bad happen. I felt lucky this was the case. The way this thing was packaged felt like an accident waiting to happen. But I digress. On to the good stuff. The monitor is absolutely stunning and beautiful and almost every imaginable way. Visually it has me looking up from my pillow at night thinking "Damn Daniel." Once properly set up I soon realized I was dealing with a huge leap forward in picture quality and color representation from my nearly 13 year old 1080p BEN Q monitor. I mean...Que Owen Wilson Voice here..."WOW" Its gorgeous. Gaming has been super fun on this bad boy (Or girl) not sure what the monitor identifies as. Personally I believe the finest things in life are female. Like a ferarri. Ya that's right. This thing is a Ferrari of monitors compared to the Lexus I had been using for so long. But I feel there's some things I'm a little worried about. Here are some of my negative things to say and this is why it's not a perfect 5 stars. The documentation with the monitor seems very lacking. I didn't find a real owners manual explaining things in great detail. I even looked online and that also wasn't anything impressive or super helpful. I'm trying to better understand what it means to own an OLED. A type of screen known for it's issues with Burn in. That's right. The documentation is vague and unhelpful when it comes to burn in. They have no problem saying they won't cover burn in with their warranty but it's ok for the consumer to drop nearly 2 grand on something with a user manual translated by God only knows. LG your "Long periods of time" advice for preventing burn in is very vague in my opinion. You should also offer burn in protection. Im not talking about the obvious situations. I dont expect to have a monitor replaced if I freeze frame on Pedro Pascals face for 12 hours and it destroys the screen. But this is a gaming monitor. I dont play a single game that does not have static HUD elements present. These are objects which do not move or go away during play. How long until one of these in game elements damages my gaming monitor? I only have a vague answer for that. Big Problem. Additionally is seems like cleaning this thing is going to be interesting. The monitor has technologies for keeping it healthy, but again; The information on them and how often they should be run is pretty vague in my opinion. In closing, this is a fantastic product that I have my fingers crossed that it works out to my expectations. So far is has only impressed and changed my opinion completely on curved displays and 1440p resolution gaming. I hope if you order one it comes in good condition. My box was a little banged up and that had me worried but alas all is well so far. For windows or Netflix, I bump it up to 4K 120hz. It looks stunning. Historically, I have been all Sony (pre-2000), followed by all Samsung(pre-2020). reviews.title: LG UltraGear 32GS75Q-B: A Highly Capable Gaming Monitor
reviews.comment: After using the LG UltraGear 32GS75Q-B (31.5" QHD IPS gaming monitor) for about a month, I am thoroughly impressed with its performance. I upgraded from a previous LG VA panel that exhibited noticeable ghosting and trailing behind fast-moving objects, such as the mouse cursor. This issue stemmed from the slower gray-to-gray (GtG) response times typical of VA panels compared to IPS. With this UltraGear model, featuring a 1ms GtG response time, those artifacts are completely eliminated, delivering crisp and fluid motion.While the static contrast ratio is 1200:1 (lower than the 3000:1 on many VA panels), the IPS technology provides superior overall image quality, with excellent viewing angles and color accuracy (sRGB 99% typical). The VESA DisplayHDR 400 certification ensures solid HDR performance, producing vibrant highlights and satisfactory dynamic range for gaming and media consumption—far better than I expected for an entry-level HDR implementation.A standout feature is its compatibility with both AMD FreeSync and NVIDIA G-SYNC Compatible technologies, making it future-proof for my planned upgrade to an NVIDIA GPU while delivering tear-free gameplay on my current setup.The primary minor drawback is the pixel density of approximately 93 PPI at 2560x1440 resolution on a 31.5-inch panel. At very close viewing distances, individual pixels become faintly visible, which could bother users sensitive to such details. However, at typical desktop distances (around 2–3 feet), this is imperceptible, and it poses no issue during gaming or video playback.Other aspects are excellent: the On-Screen Display (OSD) menu is intuitive and responsive, and the stand assembles quickly while offering height, tilt, and pivot adjustments for ergonomic comfort. Connectivity includes two HDMI 2.1 ports and one DisplayPort 1.4, providing ample bandwidth for the QHD 180Hz specification (though the higher versions are not fully utilized at this resolution).P.S.: For Linux users interested in HDR, note that robust support is currently limited to recent versions of KDE Plasma (Wayland session) and GNOME (starting with version 48 or via experimental flags in earlier releases). Additional libraries or extensions may be required for full functionality, and some setup tweaks could be needed. In contrast, Windows 11 enables HDR seamlessly out of the box via the display settings.Overall, the LG 32GS75Q-B offers outstanding value for QHD gaming, with responsive performance, reliable adaptive sync, and impressive visuals that make it an easy recommendation.

reviews.title: Great performance: 160Hz works perfectly with the right cable
reviews.comment: I’ve been using this monitor for a few days now (received in January 2026), and so far my experience has been excellent. My graphics card is an ASUS TUF Gaming NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4080 Super OC Edition, and at first, I had some doubts about reaching the full 160Hz at 4K in Windows. I followed many comments and reviews online and tried different cables. I even bought a certified HDMI 2.1 (48Gbps) cable, thinking that would solve the issue. While that cable works perfectly, with HDMI I could only reach 4K @ 120Hz uncompressed, which seems to be a limitation of how this monitor and NVIDIA GPUs handle HDMI. However, the DisplayPort cable included in the box works perfectly. Using DisplayPort, I can get 4K @ 160Hz in Windows without any issues on my RTX 4080 Super. On macOS, I was also able to reach 160Hz using HDMI, which worked smoothly. The dual mode is another big advantage: I tested 1080p at 320Hz, and it works very well for competitive gaming. Motion is extremely smooth and responsive. Regarding performance, DisplayPort uses Display Stream Compression (DSC) to achieve 160Hz at 4K. This adds only about 0.1–0.3 ms of latency, which is completely negligible in real gaming. In practice, the higher refresh rate reduces overall input lag compared to 120Hz, so gaming actually feels more responsive. Image quality is excellent, colors look vibrant, and build quality feels solid. I haven’t noticed any input lag issues, stuttering, or visual artifacts. I’ve only had the monitor for a short time, so I may update this review in the future if anything changes. For now, based on my experience, I’m very satisfied and giving it 5 stars. I will also upload a video as evidence showing the refresh rates working correctly. Highly recommended if you’re looking for a versatile and high-performance 4K gaming monitor.

reviews.author: Erwin

reviews.title: Give it some time before returning
reviews.comment:
EDIT: I've discovered that the horizontal lines come back after the standby pixel cleaning runs. It seems like a firmware update is needed to fix this. Updating from MCM102 to MCM104 did not resolve the issue. It is easily fixed by running a manual pixel cleaning, but I shouldn't have to do this every time I wake the monitor up. Im hoping ASUS addresses this issue.
If you're worried about the grey banding after unboxing, don't be until your return window is actually about to close. After I unboxed mine, I immediately ran a few pixel cleaning cycles and it definitely helped, but it was still pretty bad out of the box. The banding was noticeable enough to be annoying during daily use (productivity and gaming), but I could tell it was slowly getting better the more I used it and the more refreshes I did.
About 3 weeks in, I was honestly about to box it up and send it back. The graininess on the greys really bothered me. It was like this thin horizontal and vertical banding that created a grid pattern across the whole screen for grey backgrounds. But I ran one last refresh and now it’s very minimal, to the point I almost don’t even notice it anymore. Plus, seeing how it got better over time from normal use, I'm expecting it to get even better as I put more hours on it and do more cleaning cycles.
For reference, I’m at 108 hours on this screen with 35 pixel cleans. I don’t love that you have to "work" for a good looking display, but once the banding is gone, I think the screen is incredible. Colors are great, brightness and HDR look really good, and the sub-pixel layout makes text look way clearer than my QD-OLED monitor. For the price, it’s a great value.
If you don't have a huge reason to upgrade right now and don't want to wait 100+ hours for a screen to look right, maybe wait for the next gen of tandem oled to see if the manufacturing gets better. But if you are thinking about buying it, I dont think there's any harm in buying it and trying it out since Amazon returns are easy anyway.
Note: Im not including pictures of the screen because the pictures just dont capture the banding issue properly and I dont want to mislead anyone. My monitor looked similar to a lot of pictures you will find online, and now it looks very similar to the greys on my QD-OLED.
reviews.author: Johnathon

reviews.title: Significant Upgrade from MSI G27C2
reviews.comment:
My previous monitor was the MSI G27C2 which is a 1080p 144Hz VA panel from around 2018. This ASUS OLED monitor is a massive step-up in all respects. There is not much to put other than that, it's simply a great monitor. Additionally, I have almost no fear of burn-in thanks to the Tandem tech and the many built-in OLED-Care features. I did have to run a pixel refresh cycle because I was seeing grey banding but that cycle fixed the problem completely. From what I gather, this is normal for many OLED panels and might not have anything to do with your quality of unit, unless the grey banding is persistent after several cycles.
The only downside I ran into was the extremely quick pixel response time. It's 1 millisecond or less, so each frame doesn't blur (great to have at high framerates). This makes framerates below 144 Hz look slightly choppy because there's no blur to hide the framerate gaps, this effect gets worse the lower in framerate you get. For the first time ever, I started enabling motion blur in my games. Not a big deal, just know that you'll want to be at high framerates (ideally 280Hz) to not have the choppiness. To be extra clear, this is not a real problem with the monitor, it's just the nature of extremely quick pixel response times.
Overall, this is a great monitor. I absolutely recommend it if you're scared of OLED burn-in but want the benefits of OLED.

reviews.title: Great Monitor for 1440 Gaming
reviews.comment: Although they can be a bit pricy for my liking, ASUS products don't miss in my experience. Neither does this one. For 100$ off the original price, this monitor was a steal. It's OSD features multiple visual settings that can give your screen deep blacks like a VA while still providing the colorful visuals of an IPS. Brightness is great as well, even at 50% it's still more than adequate to see everything on screen. Its height and tilt adjust makes it great for desks with elevated monitor stands and people using chairs lacking adjustment capabilities. The buttons and tiny joystick behind it on the right side make the OSD easy to control and access. As far as gaming goes, it's great, however there is one hiccup I had. Turning on VRR made this monitor spewing bricks, the refresh rate kept changing so frequently that the monitor's upper half would flicker until I clicked a window that would make it stop, only for it to continue once more. Not sure if this is a monitor side issue or if I did something wrong on my end, but after endless troubleshooting I leaned towards the former and ultimately decided to turn it off. It's no big deal for me personally, I can still get 240FPS on the games I play that allow it. All things considered, I scored big time with this monitor, and if you choose it, so will you.
reviews.author: E.C

reviews.title: A Console Gamer’s Dream!
reviews.comment: ASUS ROG Strix XG27ACS Review: A Console Gamer’s Dream The ASUS ROG Strix XG27ACS is a standout choice for console gamers who want to maximize the capabilities of modern systems like the Xbox Series X and PS5. Offering a perfect mix of 1440p resolution and support for 120 fps, this monitor hits the sweet spot between stunning visuals and fluid gameplay. Key Features Tailored for Console Gamers: - 1440p Resolution with 120Hz Refresh Rate: The highest resolution available on most consoles while maintaining 120Hz performance, delivering crisp visuals without sacrificing smoothness. - 4.5ms Average Response Time: Though not the absolute fastest, this response time ensures smooth transitions with minimal ghosting, perfect for nearly any gaming scenario. - Low Input Lag: With near-imperceptible input lag, every button press translates into instant on-screen action, a must for competitive and fast-paced games. Why It’s the Best Bang for Your Buck: The XG27ACS combines premium specs with an affordable price, making it an incredible value for gamers looking to upgrade their experience. Its balance of performance, visual quality, and affordability, make it a top-tier option without venturing into overly expensive territory. When to Consider Upgrading: There are only two scenarios where upgrading might make sense: 1. Esports-Level PC Gaming: If you're diving into competitive PC gaming, you might need a monitor with a 240Hz or higher refresh rate. At that point, it’s likely time to invest in a high-end gaming PC as well. 2. Cinematic 4K Experiences: For players who prioritize stunning visuals in single-player games, a 4K monitor running at 60 fps may be worth considering. Final Thoughts The ASUS ROG Strix XG27ACS is arguably the best monitor for console gaming at 1440p and 120 fps, offering incredible performance and visuals without breaking the bank. Unless your gaming needs shift dramatically, this monitor is the perfect long-term choice for console gamers looking to get the most out of their hardware.

reviews.title: XG27ACS - Impressions after opening and setup.
reviews.comment: Day 1 Impression: On-Sale $234 shipped. 27qhd highHZ, can't complain. nice packaging and accessories. Love the stand - matches my RogStrix G513QY laptop nicely, very sturdy. Purchased to mount on a mobile desk with the 15inch laptop screen removed. The screen itself is rather light, easy vesa mounting if needed. usb-c to usb-c display is a bonus. The Display is... "As expected" for the price and NAME BRAND. except.... The anti-glare "FOG" almost looks like backlight bleeding at angles, definitely a tradeoff for no major glare in well-lit areas. My Display showed Zero dead pixels, 1 small spot (1inch) of backlight bleed on the bottom horizontal run, but I can live with it... for the price. Menu/Picture settings are easy to navigate, and the QHD is beautiful, even with standard hdmi 60hz. Very Happy purchase for a budget laptop extension/extra display. If it works like this for 3-5+ years no troubles, I'll say it's a good purchase. Time will tell. ***In the picture shown, the blue areas are the Anti-Glare FOG, noticeable in dark scenes when in a dark room or when viewing at angles. It is not truly noticeable during day/lights-on. The Green area is the small Backlight Bleed (Not noticeable during day or other than black screen) Second photo is during the day on black screen test, slight "Angle-AntiGlare Fog" nothing harsh. For the SALE price, I would repeat the purchase, no real complaints, hope it holds up.
reviews.author: Chris

reviews.title: Samsung 49" Odyssey OLED – Reliable After-Sales Support Makes All the Difference
reviews.comment:
I purchased the Samsung 49" Odyssey OLED monitor a few months ago and was thoroughly impressed with its stunning picture quality, deep blacks, vibrant colors, and ultra-wide immersive experience right from the start. It quickly became my favorite display for both work and gaming.
Unfortunately, just within the first 90 days, the monitor suddenly stopped working. I was disappointed, especially given the premium price point.
What pleasantly surprised me was Samsung’s warranty service. They arranged for a technician to come directly to my house for the repair — a huge plus for such a large and heavy monitor. No need to pack it up, ship it, or risk damage during transport. The technician handled everything professionally, and the monitor is now fully back up and running.
I’m once again enjoying the incredible OLED visuals that made me buy it in the first place. While the early failure was frustrating, Samsung’s responsive and convenient customer support has restored my confidence in the product.
If you’re considering this monitor, be aware that early issues can happen, but Samsung’s on-site warranty service is a strong safety net that’s worth factoring in.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Pretty much perfect right out of the box!
reviews.comment: I was one of the lucky ones and got a perfect monitor right out of the box. Set up was a breeze. I only had to buy one new cable for it. I have this thing connected to two machines, a PC and a Mac Studio. I had to buy a new DP to Thunderbolt cable for it to work at 144Hz since my Mac Studio is old. But it was a small price to pay to not have two giant monitors on my desk anymore. It feels so liberating and looks so much cleaner! I opted for this model because I wanted to stay clear of all the bloatware. I had originally planned to get the 57" model, but that curve was way too out of control for my taste. Not to mention the blacks on this monitor are spectacular! People that complain about color accuracy need to suck it up and get a monitor calibrater. With a few minutes of tweaking this thing is perfectly fine for all the photo editing and graphics work that I do for a living. The only thing I find weird about this monitor is the pixel shifting it does I'm assuming its an OLED burn in thing? I sit in front of this thing about 12 hours a day and I notice it doing it a few times a day. Another things that I feel compelled to complain about (since this is a product review) is the power cable is a bit short. The brick hangs about 4 inches shy of the floor. An extra 6 inches would have helped!
reviews.author: enero30

reviews.title: Don't pay more than $800 for this - LG 45GX950A-B blows it out of the water at full price
reviews.comment:
Very nice display, has some issues. Main thing is the fact that it's actually two 27" panels fused side-by-side, not one big panel.
That's all well and good, but if, like in the one I received, the two panels have very slightly mismatched brightness calibration, you'll get a nice little gradient right down the middle. Only really visible on dim grays, but very annoying once you notice it.
Aside from that, there's some odd VRR-related behavior, random white flashes particularly when using Firefox. Not an issue I've noticed in games, and it's occasional enough that I don't really care that much, at least not yet.
One last downside is that it only has one displayport input, and I haven't been able to get it to work at full res over HDMI, meaning I needed to pick up a 2>1 displayport switch in order to be able to switch between my desktop and work laptop without fiddling with cables twice a day. Not the worst thing in the world, just be aware of it before buying, and make sure you use DP 1.4+ cables that are 3 feet long or shorter - otherwise you're likely to get all sorts of lovely artifacting. Also, if you ever have to move, this thing is a PAIN to lug with you, but you probably knew that already.
That aside, colors are beautiful, it's phenomenal in HDR, gets plenty bright, it's not nearly as heavy as you might expect, the three year burn-in warranty is good for peace of mind, and the field of view it gives you over a 16:9 is really nice in games or wide-shot movies. Don't be fooled by Amazon's perpetual "sale" price, though - the actual MSRP as listed on Samsung's website is $900 at time of writing, and even that is a bit much considering the other options on the market right now.

reviews.comment: Huge monitor and looks great. Only downside is there aren’t built in speakers. Set up is a breeze. Definitely easier with two people but the connections are very easy. Just heavy and awkward. Quality is great. Waited for Black Friday sale so the value was there for me.
reviews.author: Shaun

reviews.title: Happy! Every day office use with 1 monitor.
reviews.comment:
I purchased the SAMSUNG 49-inch Odyssey G9 (G91F) DQHD, 144Hz Curved Gaming Monitor for everyday office use to replace three separate monitors across my desk. Until I switched to the Odyssey, I truly didn’t realize what I was missing.
The curve is perfect and greatly improves my viewing angle. I have ongoing neck and shoulder issues, and this monitor provides a much more natural and comfortable viewing experience compared to using three individual screens. I’m especially happy to no longer deal with monitor bezels breaking up my workspace. I can resize applications freely and still read everything clearly within each window.
I often work with three different applications visible at the same time while developing and troubleshooting in an EMR system, and this monitor handles that workflow beautifully. Everything feels more streamlined and efficient.
Packaging was impressive and well thought out, and assembly was very easy. Overall, this monitor has significantly improved both my comfort and productivity, and I would highly recommend it for anyone looking to replace multiple monitors with a single, seamless display—especially for office or professional use.
reviews.author: non

reviews.title: 49 inches of beautiful, curved slab of unbroken visual real estate
reviews.comment:
This monitor is 4 feet wide, providing the horizontal resolution of almost three regular monitors side by side, but with no bezel gaps. The 1m radius means that every spot on the screen is nearly the same distance to your eyes.
While this is excellent for gaming, giving a field of view you've never had before, it's pretty great for regular working as well. You can put a window anywhere you want without the span gap of separate monitors.
The only minor nit I have is it's not technically IPS. But it's still quite bright and doesn't suffer the color inaccuracies and inversions typical of other non-IPS (and non-OLED) monitors.
Performance wise, I am chuffed!
reviews.author: rkr

reviews.title: Best Monitor EVER
reviews.comment: If you are looking for a monitor for productivity/working and gaming, this is unequivocally without hyperbole the best monitor that you can buy, and for a great price. I purchased it recently and have nothing about amazing things to say. The size of this thing is so perfect that once you start using it you'll never want to go back to any other sized monitor. And the resolution and pixel density is absolutely stunning, this thing looks better and more dense than most 27 or 32 inch monitors which is a feat with how big it is. I use mac and although you can only get max 120 HZ, you still can get full native resolution 7680 x 2160 as long as you use DP2.1, which is more than enough for just working which I presume is what most mac users will be doing. The brightness, colors, contrast and HDR on this thing is also amazing everything looks so vibrant and this monitor has an extremely high max brightness. And for work it is SO convenient having literally two 32 inch screens side by side and having this much screen space, you can have so many applications open at once. As long as you have the money to afford this monitor, the desk space to have the monitor on your desk (which is important because the stand takes up a lot of space and this monitor is very heavy so I wouldn't trust it with an arm), and a rig that can run this at full resolution with good FPS/refresh rate, it is an absolute no brainer in my opinion and is one of my favorite purchases that I've ever made. The build quality does feel a bit flimsy I will admit, but honestly it doesn't matter when the monitor works and performs as well as it does. Just make sure out the box that you calibrate the picture settings, enable HDR, set your Display port/HDMI input to 2.1 (by default it is on 1.4), and tweak the settings to your liking. For me I am using original picture mode, 50 brightness, 50 contrast, 10 sharpness, 22 color, local dimming on HIGH (very important setting), contrast enhancer off, active HDR tone mapping, natural color tone, and native color space settings with the rest of settings on default. Make sure to DISABLE any eye care settings for best quality.
reviews.author: Oliver Khan

reviews.title: Beautiful Monitor, Firmware has Room for Improvement
reviews.comment: I can't help but love this monitor. There are few flaws but nothing that detracts from the experience when using this beast for work or play. My work laptop is using integrated intel graphics, and has no problem running the full resolution albeit at a refresh rate of 60Hz. My gaming PC, equipped with a Nvidia 4080 runs full resolution at 120Hz. A few examples of gaming performance on the 4080 running max resolution: Forza Horizon 5 locked at 60 fps no problem. Final Fantasy XIV variable from 60 to 85 fps. Typically around 80Hz. Games that support the ultrawide display are gorgeous. Having so much displayed in your field of view really helps with emersion in the game. The quality of the screen really shines. Deep blacks, with little halo effect. Color reproduction is really good. Brightness can be blinding, I typically have brightness set to about 15 out of 50. Text is sharp. For work, having this much real estate to play with is great. I went from running 3 27" monitors to this single setup. No breaks for bezels, and being able to throw windows around anywhere is a game changer. When working with large datasets, or those horrible spreadsheets that are 50 columns wide, max the window and see everything at once. I see the other reviews where people are experiencing flickering, strange gray lines, or bad pixels, but luckily I have had none of those issues. For the bad: The 3' Display Port cable that comes in the box. This is unacceptable as half that length is just getting it from the input on the monitor through the cable management, so you only have maybe 18" to play with getting it to your device. At this price point, Samsung could do better. Only 1 display port on the monitor. HDMI works fine, but I would have liked at least 2 display ports. Not a deal breaker, but a "would have been nice" item. Firmware really needs some work. When waking the computer from sleep mode, the monitor does not come off standby mode automatically unless you have Auto Source Switch+ turned on. But if the work laptop wakes while I am in the middle of a game, I really don't want the monitor to switch automatically to the new input, so I like to keep that off.
reviews.author: Kevin W.

reviews.title: Amazing. I use it for Day Trading. Might get another one to hover above this one. SPACIOUS!
reviews.comment: Love it. Was unsure about moving from two, side-by-side ASUS monitors, pivoted in towards the center, to this monitor, but now I wonder why I didn't make the move sooner, and don't think (at least for Day Trading), that I can ever go back to my previous setup of side-by-side monitors. Was also a little apprehensive about a curved monitor and it maybe being "too close," but loving it. Form Factor Lines are clean, back cable insertion bay (and cover) are tidy, response time is great, resolution is crisp. Running this off a 2025 Mac Studio M3 Ultra. Had a few little wonky times setting it up (more Mac related, I think). Because I wanted to utilize as much real estate as the monitor would allow, I set the resolution to 5120 x 1440. When I'd restart the computer, my Mac Studio would sometimes reset the resolution to something else (ie: lower res / bigger windows / less able to fit on the screen). I found an App called "Better Display" / "Better Display Pro", and that has been a Godsend. If it's monitor related, this App will let you configure it in a zillion ways. The App has more resolution options than I've ever seen (I'm used to seeing like 4-8 options....this App was offering up to like 30(?)+ resolution options. Have actually thought about replacing the multiple ASUS 27" Pro Art monitors I have above THIS Samsung unit, with ANOTHER one of these Odyssey Neo G9's...but, need to make a little more money to be able to justify that (haha)...but, seriously considering it. If you need an arm for this monitor, so that it levitates off your desktop, I highly recommend: ULTRARM Heavy Duty Monitor Arm for Ultrawide Monitors up to 57" and 44 lbs, Single Desk Stand, Pneumatic Height Adjustable, Modular Extension Arms - Max VESA 100x100, White, MODEL: MA20PW-S
reviews.author: jman995x

reviews.title: Stunning Display but Make Sure Your Desk Can Handle It
reviews.comment: The Samsung Odyssey NEO G9 is an absolute powerhouse when it comes to immersive gaming and productivity. The 49-inch curved display with Quantum Mini LED technology delivers incredible picture quality, with deep blacks, vibrant colors, and exceptional contrast. Whether you're gaming or working, the 5120x1440 resolution provides crystal-clear visuals, and the 240Hz refresh rate ensures smooth, responsive gameplay. One of the standout features is the HDR2000, which makes everything look incredibly lifelike. The G-Sync and FreeSync Premium Pro support eliminate screen tearing, making it perfect for high-intensity gaming sessions. The ultra-wide screen is like having two monitors in one, which is great for multitasking without the need for multiple displays. However, there’s one big drawback: its size. The monitor is so large that it overwhelms my 23-inch deep desk, making it difficult to position comfortably. If you don’t have enough desk space, you might find it challenging to fit this beast into your setup. Despite this, if you have the room and budget, the Odyssey NEO G9 is a top-tier monitor that delivers an unrivaled experience in both gaming and productivity. Just be sure to measure your desk before making the investment!
reviews.author: EatSleepAmzn

reviews.title: Told myself I'd never buy another Samsung product again...
reviews.comment: I've been running with mostly Samsung products for literally the past 10 years, from their smartphones, to earbuds, to even an 8K TV. They are always at the forefront of cutting-edge technology, and for that part, they are hard to beat in that regard. Where they fail is their manufacturing & craftsmanship. After 3.5 years, my expensive world's first 8K TV died and was irreparable from my own efforts. And then my only 2-year-old Galaxy S23 Ultra started acting wonky following one of Samsung's software updates, not unsuspiciously. I told myself I was done with Samsung --- never again... When it came time for me to downscale & downsize from three 4K 32" OLED monitors, it was necessary for me to still maintain the vertical height of a 32" monitor. And, unfortunately or fortunately, that's where this monitor (the Samsung Odyssey G9 57"), and only this monitor, came into play. At the time I was looking (6 months ago), this was the only 57" super ultrawide screen monitor in existence -- the 57" is the equivalent to two 32" monitors, which is the perfect compromise for me. As much as I scoured the web for 57" current & future alternatives from OTHER manufacturers including LG & ASUS, this Samsung was the only thing on the horizon. (Looks like Acer made a 57" -- that one is only 120Hz though, and I don't know much about their reliability, either.) Luckily, this has been an amazing monitor -- SO FAR, of course. Coming from OLED's, this Samsung is as good as it's going to get for an LED VA panel -- the closest thing you are going to get to OLED picture quality, without actually being an OLED. Very good blacks, very good contrast, great features/options: 7860x2160 resolution, 240Hz, DP2.1, local dimming options. Is the shadow detail in games as good as OLED? Of course not...but it's still pretty damn good. Are dark scenes/images a bit milky and washed out? A little. But again, I would still categorize the image as "great", even if not the best possible. The huge positive of this monitor not being an OLED is there is zero threat of burn-in. (As a person who has actually experienced burn-in on early OLED's.) I can accidentally leave this monitor on for hours with a still image & not worry about the screensaver not turning on for some reason; I can keep my Windows taskbar on 100% of the time; I don't need to worry about moving windows around periodically so the pixels are not sitting in the same position for too long; I don't need to worry about game HUD's being on the screen too long. That, along with the great picture, just might be enough for me to be okay with not having an OLED... I've seen some reviewers complain about this monitor having a matte screen instead of glossy -- well, there's positives and negatives to that. Is the image 100% as sharp/clear on a matte screen? No -- but you probably would not even notice the difference. But then again, with a matte screen you won't need to worry about the image clarity degrading due to the direct reflections of a glossy screen, either... That said, I will always have my doubts about this Samsung's reliability. I have already experienced a handful of times when I woke up the monitor, but the screen remained black. (I could actually faintly see my desktop on the screen, as if the monitor was at 1% brightness.) Luckily, unplugging the monitor power plug, waiting, and plugging back in got it working properly. (That, of force shutting down my PC.) I've seen reports of this monitor no longer powering on & dying for good, for some users... Well, and that is why I chose to purchase the extended warranty, because I *do* really like this monitor, and I plan to have it for a very long time. If it dies within the next 4 years, I can get it repaired or replaced. And if it's after 4 years, I might be ready to upgrade by then, anyway. It's a Samsung, so buy with caution -- or with an extended warranty -- but it is indeed a very good monitor.
reviews.author: illeagle45

reviews.title: From business to gaming, these are the monitors you need
reviews.comment: Amazing monitor for the price that looks amazing on my desk. Did need to change my docking station to hand two of these, but works great.  Use these for work and gaming with no complaints. Easy on eyes for spreadsheets and great graphics for the games.
reviews.author: Audra Karwoski

reviews.title: Worth it!
reviews.comment: I’ve had this monitor for a few months now it has helped with speed and eye strain, the quality is pretty good and if you have a PS5 most games at 120 FPS are capped lower than 4K. it doesn’t take much room at room and it’s very adjustable and can move in whichever way you want it to move. the brightness can be adjusted and so much more but keep in mind that if you turn the eye saver mode you can’t adjust the brightness, Very easy to set up and will definitely purchase another one for my set up soon!

reviews.title: Absolutely, beautiful picture and great for the price
reviews.comment: Absolutely love this Odyssey. Great monitor great quality of picture how they recommend. I currently use it on my DJ set up picture and brightness are beautiful replacing almost a 20 year-old Samsung that still works way about half of what that one does some install if you’re using an arm is way easier highly recommend this product

reviews.title: Love Samsung products, they never disappoint.
reviews.comment:
Plug and play, changed the refresh rate, getting 270 fps. Easy to put together and light, I am disabled and was able to attach the stand. Daughter put on desk and zoom zoom zoom I can see again! Resolution is crisp, Very happy with my purchase. Would buy again.
Love the flat screen not curved and the size is more than enough for my old eyes. Looks great, no flickering, little bright but adjusted to my eyes via panel.
Samsung has always provided top notch quality, never disappointed with a Samsung.
reviews.author: Mahlady

reviews.title: A Remarkable Upgrade for Everyday Use and Visual Comfort
reviews.comment:
I purchased this Samsung monitor for my mother, who had been using the same 15-year-old display for years and was experiencing some eye strain. While her old monitor still functioned, she saw no reason to replace it. After some convincing, we set this one up, and now she wouldn't dream of going back. The difference in quality was immediately apparent.
Although this is marketed as a gaming monitor, its technical specifications are precisely what make it so exceptional for general use. The high refresh rate and crisp HD resolution deliver a remarkably clear, smooth, and vibrant picture that has made a world of difference for her. While we are still hoping it helps alleviate her eye issues over time, she genuinely appreciates the enhanced clarity—a benefit she didn't even know she was missing.
From a practical standpoint, the monitor is superbly designed. The stand is fully adjustable for height, swivel, and tilt, which allowed us to find the perfect ergonomic position for her. The single joystick control for the power and menu, located conveniently under the center of the screen, is intuitive and far easier to use than traditional button layouts.
Having owned Samsung TVs and monitors before, I trust their brand for its experience and reliable technology. This purchase has only reinforced that confidence. My mom may not be playing games, but she is thrilled with the crispness and quality of her new display. This monitor is an excellent value and a fantastic choice for anyone looking to improve their daily computing experience.
reviews.author: Matt D

reviews.title: Calidad de construcción
reviews.comment: Diez puntos. Los colores no están a la altura de un OLED pero bastante bien
reviews.author: Christian

reviews.title: Poor Quality Control
reviews.comment: Quality control on this monitor is terrible. I ordered five of them and 4 out of 5 had a dead pixel or stuck pixel that could not be fixed. Two of them had multiple dead or stuck pixels in the middle of the screen making them totally unusable. Would not recommend this monitor until the quality control improves.
reviews.author: David

reviews.title: El mejor ips en este rango... si estas dispuesto a moverle la configuración un poco
reviews.comment: Conseguí este monitor a menos de 199 usd, y por ese precio y hasta al rededor de 230 usd no hay competencia en calidad de los colores y contraste, todo ve se impresionante en el y no detecto suttering con la frecuencia variable, pero el calibrado por defecto esta un poco sobresaturado y el brillo máximo tampoco es sobresaliente, así que si no estas dispuesto a calibrarlo un poco o el brillo es un problema para ti, buscaría otras opciones
reviews.author: Alejandro Montoya

reviews.title: Defective panel with dead pixel. Multiple monitor problem.
reviews.comment: Brand new M27Q2 QD, did have damage to the box but that didn't matter. Panel had a dead pixel right out of the box, having owned the monitor for less than 24 hours. Gigabyte manufacture and QC problem. Had a different model and it also had the same issue. Avoid these monitors. Even with the game bundle of RE9 you are still getting a defective panel.

reviews.title: Overclock to 260hz. 400 nits brightness
reviews.comment:
Very nice. Windows says it's about 400 nits peak brightness even though it says 300 nits on the product page and it certainly looks bright enough.
You can also overclock it to 260hz.
Downside is it only comes with hdmi so you might need a separate displayport.
reviews.author: Kindle Customer

reviews.title: Worth the price on sale.
reviews.comment:
I am very happy with the purchase and it's worth the money when it's well under a thousand. I wanted something bigger and higher res for playing games on plus general internet and streaming. This does that great. The color isn't as accurate as on my previous LG IPS monitor, but sitting side by side I can get it fairly close. Plenty good for gaming and movies. I use the included display port cable and have not seen any flickering on an AMD gpu and Linux. You will need a beefy video card to push this many pixels in games.
Picture is not great out of the box. I use Custom: Brightness 40, Contrast 32, Sharpness 15, Color 30, Tint R2, Local Dim high, Contrast Enhance off, Color Tone warm 1, White Balance (-1 r, -2 b), Gamma 2, Shadow Detail 0, Color Space native for Picture looks great. FreeSync on, Black Equalizer 0 on the Game tab. I could maybe get it slightly closer by further tweaking the white balance, but it is close enough to the accurate 34UC88 beside it for me to not bother. I'm happy with it.
The cons: I do think the 1000r curvature radius is too steep. I would much rather see it with the 1900r radius of the LG beside it, but that's not how they made it. The viewing angle could also be better, but I think that is partly a result of the curve as well. There is some noticeable backlight bleed on a completely black screen when you look for it, but I can't say I even notice it in a dark game like BG3.
Considering it can usually be found under 1000, I think it's worth it. The further under the better. For over it, I think I would try to find something with oled or a flatter curve.
reviews.author: D Westover

reviews.title: Great 5k2k monitor
reviews.comment: I had been looking for a new monitor for awhile and had been researching for a new one.  I decided I wanted a high quality display, but burn in was a fear I was having for alot of the new OLED monitors since I do a good amount of office work/internet browsing in addition to some gaming.  Thats why when I saw this monitor go on sale I jumped onboard.  I have been nothing but happy with this purchase as I get the wide screen experience, but still get the height I need for my office work.  Much cheaper than the LG and Dell options, yes I know it is a VA panel, but as the monitor sits directly in front of me at my desk I have NO issues with viewing angles or anything like that.  A great monitor overall and if you can get it on sale it is a NO BRAINER to purchase.  Picture quality is great, screen is bright enough for my office and everything is functioning as I would expect.  My 4080 video card truely allows this monitor to shine.  Highly recommend for those of you who dont want to risk the burn in of OLED or avoid the high prices of the OLED screens.  Obviously those other monitors may have better blacks and brightness, but for the price you won't be disappointed.  I will admit, that like most Samsung monitors/TVs, you do need to do some adjustments to get a more accurate color, but that little bit of work is well worth it.
reviews.author: Anthony J. Rios

reviews.title: Best Monitor!
reviews.comment:
I would love to spend the time to write all the reasons I love this monitor as well as give the best details on it.
Quality: Super solid. The only thing with quality I would improve is the base. It’s just ugly and awkward. Samsung, I know you can do better.
Value: On sale, awesome. MSRP is high.
Brightness is perfect for what I need.
It performs super well for the 4 computers I have hooked up to it.
HDR is a bit weird and I will need to look into that more but I don’t need it for my day-to-day.
reviews.author: Jeremy C. Ziegler

reviews.title: High quality monitor
reviews.comment: These are initial impressions after a few hours of use:  picture and build quality are great.  Bright and colorful.  Text and images are crystal clear.  Backlighting appears pretty even.  Size is perfect for me coming from a 32" 4K monitor.  Smaller widescreen monitors felt like they had been squashed vertically but this feels like I gained real estate.  Hooked up with DisplayPort; no problems.  Menus are easy to navigate and logical.  Box was a bit awkward to handle but the monitor is pretty light - I could easily assemble and move it without help.  Powertoys recommended to control the placement of windows.  Gaming with an rtx 4090 and no problems driving this resolution.
reviews.author: Timothy Lesnick

reviews.title: Absolutely Gorgeous
reviews.comment: This monitor is amazing. Should have bought this thing a long time ago. I’m a 53 year old gamer on a PS5 so seeing everything on a smaller screen can be somewhat challenging, especially many of these subtitles and their smaller sizes. This thing is massive, almost as if you’re sitting in a cinema.Every game on this monitor looks amazing, true 4k @ 120 hz…huge difference over my old G5 flat monitor. The curve is perfect. If you’re on the fence, pull the trigger, you won’t be disappointed!
reviews.author: Stephanie

reviews.title: I should have brought this long time ago
reviews.comment: This is the best monitor I own by far. I owned many third-party monitors never had a high end brand . I should have got this monitor a long time ago, this change my whole gaming experience, the resolution, speed, color and HDR you will not be disappointed. The brightness is smarter is perfect the sound quality is as well. Adjustment capability is as good.
reviews.author: John M Torres

reviews.title: Quality Monitor with Unique Screen Size
reviews.comment: The Samsung Odyssey g7 37" is a real quality machine. When I first saw the 37" size I was curious and with there being so little reviews so I took the leap and bought it. I upgraded from a Samsung Odyssey g5 to this one and the upgrade was drastic; the picture quality is top tier, the color accuracy is shockingly good, and the contrast is very good for a non OLED display. The refresh rate is good for me mostly because I game with a console. I do miss the UltraWide 21:9 sometimes but being able to watch most videos without black bars is always a plus and it's a huge monitor so it is not lacking in screen real estate. Overall, It's a very good monitor but the price is definitely what sets it back, I bought mine used- like new- so I saved some money but do not buy it for full price as there are much better OLED alternatives for the around the same price new.
reviews.author: Leon

reviews.title: A software engineer's dream monitor
reviews.comment:
As a software engineer I love having a single large display. It has to have very high resolution, brightness, and ideally a decent refresh rate. I prefer a single display over two monitors because I don't like moving my neck so much throughout the day. For the same reason I'm not a fan of ultra-wides.
Until now I've been using the Gigabyte M32UC - an absolutely fantastic 32" monitor that checks all the boxes above. The only thing I wanted beyond what the Gigabyte offers is a bit more surface area.
Over the past few years I've tried a few other options, but none of them did it all: some were too dark, some had bad refresh rate, some were too wide.
When I saw that Samsung had recently released this one I bought it immediately.
It checks all boxes. The curve is more aggressive than my Gigabyte and I love it. Brightness and refresh rate are great and the resolution is top notch. This is the best monitor I've ever owned and I suspect it will be a long time until one is good enough to replace it.  I wouldn't hesitate for a minute to recommend it.

Still haven't gotten a code for it and when you bring it up to them it's they don't have a clue about it.  Terrible customer service.

reviews.title: Excellent product that gets the job done!
reviews.comment: I love these.  They're silent, sturdy and with solid air flow!  Their no frills flat black is just what I wanted...no RGB nonsense using energy, adding complexity and cost.  They're 4pin PWM case fans, so they are compatible with speed sensors and software and hardware controls.  They are immediately recognized by utility apps like "Fan Control".  Connectivity is, of course, simple and standard, but each fan also comes with a daisy chain attachment. These are the ones to get if you're just looking for reliable, silent, effective fan cooling!  I bought 9 and the all work great!

reviews.title: Quiet, Reliable, and Affordable
reviews.comment: These fans are awesome, and the price makes them even better. They’re super quiet, even under load, and push plenty of air to keep my system cool. Build quality feels solid, and installation was easy. For the cost, you’re getting performance that rivals more expensive fans. You really can’t go wrong with Thermalright. Definitely recommend if you want reliable, quiet cooling without breaking the bank.
reviews.author: Brandon

reviews.title: Great Value, But Can Introduce Noise...
reviews.comment: Needed to replace my original Lian Li OEM fans, as they started dying after 15 years in a high-dust environment. Pros: - 4-Pin connectors, allowing for custom fan profiles. - Passthrough cables, so that fans can be daisy chained. - Built in rubber pads to dampen vibration noise. - Seems to move more air than the original OEM fans. Cons: - While they are quiet, they do emit a low hum that's definitely audible. Final thoughts: other reviews mentioned missing screws, but I can confirm that matching black screws were included within my package. At full RPM, these things are definitely audible, but not loud. While I'll miss the whisper quiet performance of my Lian Li fans, it's hard to beat the value you get for a 3-pack with a few extra features, and if they last half as long as my old fans, it'll be worthwhile. UPDATE: I had to remove as star, as fans are now running at ~50% RPM after setting up a PWM profile and I'm sorry to say that two of the fans exhibit coil whine. While it's not loud, in a quiet environment, it's definitely noticeable. So if you already have quite a bit of ambient noise or don't care about an potential increase in noise, then it's hard to beat this value. Otherwise, if you need whisper quiet fans, I'd recommend looking elsewhere. UPDATE 01/08/2025: upgraded the motherboard (MSI B450 to ASUS B650) and the coil whine is gone, so culprit may have been the previous motherboard's implementation related to the fan curve, so I'll give back another star. While they may not be the quietest fans in my system, they are able to move air and are still running fine.
reviews.author: B. Goodman

reviews.title: Cools well, and PWM helps it stay quiet
reviews.comment: Bought these to replace noisy/dying fans on my Corsair 7000D case. The airflow is much better than the stock fans, and the fans are much quieter. I appreciated that I could also get just plain black color fans with no RGB lights, as my case and build is just about RGB free. The 4PWM cables was also the other selling point, that way I can setup my fans to be running dead silent and then ramp up as needed.  Because they have such good cooling, I never even notice the fans over the general noise of my computer.

reviews.title: One of the BEST!
reviews.comment:
GIGABYTE - AORUS FO27Q3-27" QD OLED Gaming Monitor  Review: One of the BEST
**Introduction:**
I keep the review simple and in laments terms. I try not to get too technical, although I can! My goal is to translate my reviews so anyone looking for a TV or display will know if this is for them or not.
**Design:**
Describe the monitor's physical appearance. Mention the build quality, bezels, stand, and any unique design features.
**Display Quality:**
This is a very sleek, QD third generation OLED monitor. If you're looking for vibrancy, brightness, details. Look no further! This monitor will provide you with everything you've come to expect from OLED monitors and then some. I'm a big fan of the thin display design with the components being set to 'boxed' area on the back. I prefer this to a full enclosed body shape so if this is a design you like, it's got it! Check the pictures to see how incredibly thin this monitor is.
My only gripe is the bezels are still a little big around the edges. not distracting, doesn't feel cheap but still bigger than I'd like.
**Performance:**
If you're getting this as a primary gaming monitor. You've landed on it. Price to performance it's incredible. I'd say this is definitely a top tier monitor. It's going to be really hard to find a monitor that looks better than this one. Third gen QD OLED, 'nough said to be honest.
**Features:**
• Glossy anti-reflective coating --- This is not pure Matte as it says in the Amazon description!!!
• QHD 2k
• Picture in Picture, Picture By Picture
• VESA Certified - HDR 400
• VESA Certified - ClearMR 13000
• 360Hz
• 0.03 ms response time (and yes it's actually extremely responsive, not just advertised as such)
• KVM. One for All
• OLED Care
• 3 year warranty
**User Experience:**
I absolutely love my LG 39GS95QE because it has awesome brightness and awesome colors. This monitor came out this year just a few months ago.
The Aorus monitor has even better colors that pop and seems like even better contrast. It's just a beautiful display that is pure eye candy. The monitor does have a slightly warmer calibration out of the box but it's not noticeable unless you have a pure white background.
Inky blacks, amazing contrast ratio, spectacular performance with almost zero latency. I've been saying it but this is pretty much a 27 inch monitor dream. If you've been waiting for the best 1440p monitor to replace your old IPS or LED - you can stop searching.
**Value for Money:**
Evaluate whether the monitor is worth its price. Consider its performance, features, and how it compares to similar models in its price range.
**Pros:**
* Inky blacks
• Colors pop. Movie watching, gaming is top tier!
• Ability to downscale image to 24.5 inches for competitive gaming
• high PPI makes things look very crisp
• better color accuracy than WOLED
• Glossy finish (my personal preference. If you like Matte, sorry not sorry lol)
This will probably remain an undisputed champion in the market of 1440p monitors for some time.
**Cons:**
• If you're looking for 4k, consider 4k options - they will still have better PPI
• Color fringing still visible in text. See photos for an example. It's very minor but some may notice.
• No options for cool temperature adjustment. If you like a cool color temp instead of warm you won't be able to adjust this.
**Conclusion:**
The price is fair. The colors and inky blacks will have you feeling like you're in your own personal home theater setup. It's bright and crisp. I had to look for negative things to say about this monitor!
**Rating:**
5 out 5 stars - without a doubt! The negatives are far outweighed by the positives. I can safely say you won't regret this purchase.

reviews.title: Best value 4K monitor on the market and it's not even close
reviews.comment:
tl;dr At ~$300 it's an immediate buy.
The value for money of this monitor is truly insane - the number of ports, high quality screen with accurate colors, metal stand, high refresh rate, 1080p 320hz mode, and KVM functionality is not something you ever see at this price. The clarity of the screen is great, I'd put it on par with my Macbook Pro display which I thought couldn't be beat.
I also like how they designed the stand *properly*, it's a single piece of metal vs. a bunch of legs so you get much more space on your desk as a result. My old monitor used 3 legs and it basically took up all of the vertical space on the desk which forced me to sit very close to the monitor.
The only negatives I can think of and I'm mostly nitpicking here as the price justifies these concerns:
1. The stand doesn't have a hole for cable management + there is a very slight bit of wobble (it's not too noticeable and corrects itself fast)
2. Viewing angles are good and perfectly workable, but not perfect.
3. Brightness is again good enough but not perfect - I sit in front of a window in direct sunlight and could probably use another 50-100 nits of brightness, but I never feel like I'm having a hard time seeing what's on the screen, only that my old monitor with mini LEDs was a bit brighter by maybe 10%.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Excellent value for the money!
reviews.comment:
$310 with coupon goes a lot farther than it did just 2.5 years ago. Back then I got a 4k 60 panel that was color accurate, but didn't even have auto input switching and had a terrible control interface. This 4k 160 / 1080p 320 hz panel is excellent. The vignette effect others have complained about is real, but unless you are sitting extremely close to your display, you won't notice it in day to day use. I have a TN panel that I use as a side panel, and it has such a small view angle range. The M27UP is hardly noticable in comparison. The KVM is also very helpful between my work laptop and my gaming desktop. It will auto switch the inputs if one is off. Had to manually move a bunch of cables around previously, now I never do.
Response time in Smart OD mode is good. I tend to play older games, so modding Batman Arkham Asylum to be 300+ fps was cool. I can easily read text while panning.
If this was to be used in a vertical orientation, keep in mind this monitor has a chin that would make the Crimson Chin blush. The control nub is quite sensitive, takes a bit to get used to.
Wide connectivity support, very bright, obviously do not use this for HDR though. My workstation/gaming setup is now complete!

reviews.comment: used these for H6 flow case, work great, look great. Max fan speed was about 1800RPM on full power on the 140mm. Since it is forcing me to review both the 140mm 2 pack, the 120mm 3 pack, and a single 120mm fan all in one because they are different variants, i will mention them as well. the 120mm fans are great, a little loud when at 100% but the RPM max is 2100-2180, so yea its not going to be quiet lol, they are PWM 4 pin, also have daisy chain option built in, one of the products i forget which maybe the 3 pack came with 2 ARGB and 2 PWM extensions which can be useful, i had to set up the fans "sideways" not that you can tell, because the wire placement was in the way for the wire channel when upright position. What i did so the fans were not on top of another's wires was took the wires out the little holder and that gave just enough slack to not have the wires under the fan and the wires were no where near the fan blades after. I went from nzxt to these, nzxt had a lower rpm rate on both 140 and 120s, therefor was more quiet, but i am fine with the noise, i have a headset on 90% of the time im using the PC lol. So crank away. 5 star on all products, would recommend, good quality, high RPMs, ARGB!, style is great, would 100% recommend the 120mm fans to put on a radiator as they have a high rpm and push pretty good, the 120 fans on my cooler master max rpm is like 1800 so i almost want to swap them for the extra pressure.
reviews.author: Nate

reviews.title: Very Nice Fans
reviews.comment: These are really nice fans. Airflow and rotation directions are clearly marked. They work well with motherboard ARGB control or with a discrete ARGB string controller. The PWM and ARGB connections can be daisy chained to control 2 or 3 fans from a single PWM and ARGB header. The colors look great and definitely get bright enough. They move plenty of air when they need to, and are whisper quiet when operating at low and even moderate speed. I've used them in two different cases recently with no problems, they fit well where a 120mm x 25mm fan is expected to go. The three fans come with standard black mounting screws and with two additional ARGB extension cables and two additional PWM extension cables.

reviews.comment:
absolutely love these Corsair RGB fans. The ability to daisy chain the connections makes cable management so much easier and keeps my build looking clean and organized. Installation was straightforward, and everything synced up perfectly.
They look incredible in my white case—the lighting is vibrant, evenly diffused, and really elevates the overall aesthetic of my PC. Performance has been great as well, with solid airflow and quiet operation.
Highly recommend these fans if you want great performance, easy setup, and top-tier RGB visuals.

reviews.title: Short power and RGB leads—beware!
reviews.comment: Replaced a couple fractal aspect 120s with these 140s and my CPU temp at full load dropped by 5+ degrees, from mid 80s to high 70s (5800x3d with a Thermaltake Fs 140).  They’re just about dead silent at idle and audible but tolerable at higher RPMs, no annoying whine or whistle with these just a rush of air.  Wanted RGB for the kids and the colors and diffusion look fine to my eye.  These are pricey however they don’t have rubber pads at the mount holes and they have comically short power and RGB cables which caused an additional purchase of 4 pin extension cables.  A nice long RGB cable on my 120mm thermalright cpu fan had a daisy chain part to it and is the only reason I could finish the build without RGB extension cables.  So these aren’t perfect but they’re fair quality with decent overall performance.  Hope they last!

reviews.comment: (These are the top and bottom fans pictured as well as on the cpu cooler, not the ones at the front or back of the case) wowza, these are an incredible value! As compared to fans triple the price for a single fan, they provide comparable performance and almost as good aesthetics. The white color is pretty good for my liking, not too blue or yellow. Other colors look great as well. Lighting is simple and good enough, some may not find them bright enough, but THEY’RE CHEAP, so who cares? The airflow is great. I also love the daisy chaining ability. Sure, it could be better, like the fancy, expensive snap together fans, but this design works fine, and being able to daisy chain both the fan speed and rgb was a welcome surprise. reviews.title: Great fans.
reviews.comment: I purchased these fans based on the positive reviews and price/value. I was disappointed to find out I could not connect them to my MOBO, as it does not have a 3-pin 5V ARGB header. It only has a 12V 4-pin RGB header. The fans themselves work fine and are very quiet, but they would have been only white without any color effect. To some extent, I blame myself for not carefully reading the full description, and I was planning to return them for a refund. Luckily, I purchased an adapter/controller, powered by SATA and it allows daisy chaining the 3-pin ARGB connectors. I tested them and all is good, with wonderful ARGB effect and ultra quiet spinning. I cancelled the return. I am very pleased with these budget ARGB fans. Highly recommend. Thank you.

reviews.comment: These CORSAIR iCUE Link LX140 RGB fans are a great upgrade for my PC build. reviews.title: Performance and quality of life fixes done great by Corsair
reviews.comment: Sooooo let’s just start off by saying that these fans are clear night and day difference both visually and performance wise. I’ve always used Corsair fans since I started building computers back in 2010.  When I first started fans had 1 molex or 1 3-4 pin pwm cable. Now they have 2 cables 1 pwm and 1 argb.  With modern day cases  having upwards of 10 to 13 fans that’s 20+ cables you’d have to cable manage along with cables from fan controllers controllers and rgb hubs.  My last pc build I had 10 fans an  the cables were piling up in the back of the case making it. Hard to manage as well as hard to close the case panel.  Que in these amazing. Icue link fans and omg it’s amazing.  I went from 26 cables from fans and controllers Al the way Down to  2-4 cables. 2 from the fans and two from the controller.  The Daisy chain feature is Great and quick to assemble 2 connector pieces per fan for 240mm set up or 4 pieces for a 360mm fan assembly and they lock the fans together. Great way to Have modular assembly approaches.  You have two ports on each side of the hub, each port is cable of  running 12 fans At once using 1 cable. Granted if you have 10 fans like I do. I have to use one small cable from one 360 array to the next 360 array then to the hub  and connected To the port  the other four fan. One from the rear case fan to the  360 on the AIO water cooler then to the controller hub.  Now people complain about the Icue software which I don’t understand why. I’ve never had an issue With the software. It is pretty straightforward forward And User friendly. The software picked up and recognized all 10 fans. And was able to set each fan curve individually or in groups of 3  Depend on location of said fans.  The Rgb on the fans are fully addressable and are brighter the most other say they are are fully addressable brightness. These people are comparing them to the QX120 fans. Which have 8 more rgb bulbs than the LX120s. Down side is the performance on the QX line is terrible And the airflow and static pressure is not optimized like the LX line.  I’m an avid huge gamer. and I play. Most games Full blast on the settings. I have my fans on the AIO set to a static 50%  at all time  and I idle at 35-40c on my AMD 9800X3D and. I never exceed 50–60c when playing games like cyberpunk, battlefield 6, or arc raiders.  Even my RTX 5070 runs considerable cooler. After these fans were installed I went from 60-65c  when gaming down to 50-60c.  That’s just shows you the sheer quality and performance Of the fans. Now the cons. Two cable lengths provided Some people have complained about. Lengths being too short. For their builds build honestly if you know how to route your cables properly. And place the hub in a central location in your build you won’t have to go to corsairs website to buy additional longer cables. Only con I have is like everyone says is the price per fan is crazy expensive 45$ for one (no hub no cable) or 120-140$ for a set of 3 (comes with  hub and two cable lengths). When you have 10 fans like I do that’s over 400$s just for fans In your case.  But I believe if you’re building a Gaming PC from scratch you’d have the money to invest in it. 400$ is a small price we pay to have. Better air flow  And  FAR LESS cable management. The pictures I’ll post here will show you just how much better it’s made the pc look both visually and cable wise.  So if your mind is up in the air don’t hesitate  on these fans they are amazing in my honest opinion.

reviews.title: Quiet, Cool, and Built to Last
reviews.comment: I picked up the CORSAIR iCUE Link LX120 RGB fan for my setup and it’s honestly been great. Right out of the box, it feels like a high-quality fan. The build is solid, not flimsy or cheap feeling at all. It’s got that durable, long-lasting kind of vibe, like it's made to handle some serious run time. The RGB is super clean and smooth. It lights up bright, but not too flashy, and with the iCUE software, it’s easy to control the colors and sync it with the rest of your setup. Whether you want a single color or full-on rainbow effects, it all looks great and runs without any hiccups. Performance-wise, it does the job well. It keeps my system cool and stays quiet, even when I’m gaming or running heavier tasks. I’ve noticed a slight drop in temps since installing it, which is always a plus. It moves a good amount of air for a 120mm fan, and I never have to worry about noise—it’s just smooth and consistent. The iCUE Link system is also a big win. Connecting multiple fans with one cable keeps the inside of the case super clean. Less cable mess means better airflow and a way more organized build. Plus, setup is quick and simple. Overall, the LX120 is a solid pick if you want something that performs great, looks awesome, and feels like it’ll last for a long time.

reviews.title: A Smooth Setup and Great Performance
reviews.comment:
I recently upgraded my PC with the CORSAIR iCUE Link LX120-R RGB 120mm 3-Fan Pack, and I’m genuinely impressed. The fans are sleek and stylish, with a reverse rotor design that keeps the RGB lighting visible even when mounted as intake fans . The dual light loops create smooth, synchronized lighting effects that really enhance the look of my build.
Installation was a breeze. The iCUE Link system uses a single cable to connect all components, reducing cable clutter and simplifying the setup process. The included iCUE Link System Hub allows for easy management of up to seven devices per port, and the reversible cables make connecting components straightforward .
Performance-wise, the fans are quiet and efficient. They operate at a noise level ranging from 10 to 38 dBA and can reach speeds up to 2400 RPM, providing a good balance between airflow and noise . The magnetic dome bearing ensures low friction and contributes to the fans' quiet operation.
One thing to note is that the iCUE Link system is not backward compatible with older Corsair controllers, so you’ll need to use the included hub and cables .
The CORSAIR iCUE Link LX120-R RGB 120mm 3-Fan Pack is a solid choice for anyone looking to enhance their PC's aesthetics and cooling performance. The easy installation, clean design, and reliable performance make it a worthwhile investment.

reviews.title: Perfect for MMO and MOBA Gamers!
reviews.comment:
I've been using the Corsair Scimitar RGB Elite for a few weeks now, and it has completely transformed my gaming experience. Here’s a breakdown of my thoughts:
Design and Build Quality:
The build quality of the Corsair Scimitar RGB Elite is excellent. The mouse feels sturdy and well-made. The black matte finish is sleek and gives it a premium look. The backlit RGB LED adds a nice touch, allowing for a customizable and vibrant aesthetic. The mouse fits comfortably in my hand, making long gaming sessions much more enjoyable.
Performance:
With an 18000 DPI optical sensor, the precision and responsiveness of this mouse are top-notch. Whether I'm playing fast-paced MOBA games or complex MMOs, the mouse tracks flawlessly. The customizable DPI settings are a great feature, allowing for on-the-fly adjustments to match the needs of different games and playstyles.
Button Layout and Customization:
One of the standout features of this mouse is the 12 programmable side buttons. The Key Slider control system is ingenious, allowing you to adjust the position of the side buttons for maximum comfort and efficiency. Programming these buttons using Corsair's iCUE software is straightforward, giving you endless possibilities for custom macros and key bindings.
Comfort:
Ergonomically, the Scimitar RGB Elite is fantastic. It’s comfortable for extended use, which is crucial for long gaming sessions. The textured side grips provide a secure and comfortable hold, reducing strain and fatigue.
Software:
Corsair’s iCUE software is intuitive and powerful. It allows for easy customization of the RGB lighting, DPI settings, and button assignments. The ability to save profiles directly to the mouse is a nice touch, especially for those who switch between different gaming setups.
Renewed Product Experience:
I was initially hesitant about purchasing a renewed product, but my experience has been excellent. The mouse arrived in like-new condition, with no visible wear or performance issues. It’s a great way to get a high-quality gaming mouse at a more affordable price.
Final Thoughts:
The Corsair Scimitar RGB Elite is an outstanding gaming mouse for MMO and MOBA players. Its combination of precision, customization, and comfort make it a top choice for serious gamers. The renewed version offers the same great performance at a reduced cost, making it a fantastic value. Highly recommended!
