reviews.title: My data on my terms.
reviews.comment: This review is for the Western Digital 20TB WD Red Pro NAS Internal Hard Drive HDD - 7200 RPM, SATA 6 Gb/s, CMR, 512 MB Cache, 3.5" - WD202KFGX. The products arrived on time and in great condition. I bought these to install them into a UGREEN interface. I wanted to use them as RAID drives. The UGREEN device supplied mounting hardware for these drives and everything lined up correctly. I installed the drives and formatted them using the UGREEN interface. Please realize that when you format two 20 TB drives as RAID drives, formatting can take up over a day to complete. So, don't be in a hurry and don't think there is something wrong when it just doesn't happen in a flash. Both drives worked perfectly and I am very pleased with how the UGREEN interface uses them. The reason that I got the interface was because I had recently lost a USB hard drive that was connected to my computer. Not sure what made the drive go bad, but all attempts to recover the data from the drive were futile. I could send the drive off to some places that recover data, but that can cost into the thousands. I was looking for a replacement hard drive like the one I had and then I read a review from someone who lost the information off of his hard drive and he made a great point. The manufacture of the hard drive will stand by their warranty, but you must send your old drive back to them before they will send the new one out. He was not comfortable with letting a hard drive company have his old disk with all of its data. The company could easily fix what was wrong with the drive and possibly collect all of the data that is on it. That might seem paranoid, but I have had too many hackers take over some of my accounts online and I don't want anyone having access to my data. So, instead of just buying a new hard drive that could one day fail again and lose all the data, he suggested buying this UGREEN interface with two to several hard drives set up in a RAID configuration. In this configuration, if only one hard drive fails, you still have all of you data on the other hard drive. This way, if you need to send the hard drive back to take advantage of the warrantee, you might be able to just reformat the old drive if it works at all and then send it back for the replacement. However, if the drive is too far gone to reformat it, you just forget about the warrantee and order a new hard drive. Since you data is safe on the other drive, you don't have to worry about losing it. You get the new drive and put it into the interface and the interface automatically syncs the new drive to all the data. You at least have a chance this way to take advantage of the warrantee and you maintain your data in a safe place. If you can't take advantage of the warrantee on the hard drive, then you can take a sledge hammer to the drive to destroy its ability to impart the data to anyone. This just made more sense to me. And the added benefit of this UGREEN interface is that you don't need to connect it to a computer through the USB. You connect it to your home network using an ethernet cable. Then with the UGREEN app, you can store and retrieve your data from any of your devices on your network. This is like having your own cloud storage, but it is in you house instead of being out there in the ether. And you can reach the drive remotely when you are away from home as long as you have internet access. I have a DROPBOX account, but I am thinking of backing up my DROPBOX data onto this drive. Then, if I am home and there is no internet, but my home network is still working, I can get to all the information that has been stored on DROPBOX because it is also on my home network drive. I have been using the UGREEN interface for several weeks and it and the two hard drives have been functioning great. So, this is something to consider.

reviews.title: It’s a Hard Drive. It’s Big. That’s Pretty Much It.
reviews.comment: So, here it is: the Western Digital 18TB WD Red Pro NAS Internal Hard Drive — aka the “Big Boy” of data storage. What can I say? It’s a hard drive. It’s quite big. Like, “I could bench press this if I really wanted to” big. But please don’t — it’s expensive. 18 terabytes of space means I could theoretically store every embarrassing photo, weird Spotify playlist, and downloaded PDF I’ve ever made. The digital equivalent of a hoarder’s dream garage. Installation was straightforward: slot it in, screw it down, pray to the tech gods it spins up on the first try. Spoiler alert: it did. No strange noises, no smoke, just pure, reliable mechanical magic. Pros: So much space, I could hoard cat videos for decades. Designed for NAS, which means it’s the responsible adult of hard drives — steady, dependable, and ready to work overtime. Quiet enough that I almost forget it’s humming away, plotting how to store my entire digital life. Cons: It’s heavy. Not “drop on your foot” heavy, but “maybe I should use two hands” heavy. No flashy lights or cool holograms, just good old-fashioned spinning platters. Does not come with a personal assistant to organize your files or delete your bad decisions. Final Verdict: ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ – 5 stars. It stores data. It’s big. It doesn’t complain. Honestly, what more do you want from a hard drive?

reviews.title: DOA - makes weird noise and doesn't spin up! BEWARE
reviews.comment: I bought two of WD Red PRO 18TB in October when they were on sale to replace the current disks in my Home Backup NAS. I bought 2 because I need two identical drives for the NAS. Disk 1 arrived a few days later and disk 2 arrived  a few days later. And now the problems begun: Disk 2 which was sent to me wasn't an 18TB drive, it was only 6TB! A harmless mistake? Fraud? Who knows... Very annoying anyways... Now I tried to get disk 2 exchanged, but Amazon could only offer a refund, because the drives were out of stock with unknown restock date. Too bad because I didn't want a refund, since I got the drives for a good price and now they were more than 25% more expensive... So I had to wait about 3 weeks for the disk to be back in stock and be able to have it exchanged instead of  just getting a refund. Today the exchanged drive finally arrived. This time it was as ordered 18TB. I installed both drives in my NAS. One drive was GOOD the other was recognized as BAD during the drive self test. The temperature reading was off and caused a S.M.A.R.T error. In fact there was no temperature reading at all for 1 drive. So I let the drive warm up for a few hours and tried it again. Same thing. SMART could no be read and there was no temperature shown for 1 of the 2 drives. I took both drives out of the NAS and tried to see what's going on by installing them in a Windows PC. One drive is fine. SMART is OK. No errors. The other drives just makes a weird repetitive noise and doesn't spin up. It's not recognized by windows. It's DOA (Dead On Arrival)! I checked which drive it was and it was the 2nd drive. The one I received as replacement today! So after the long wait and the whole odyssey of exchanging the drive the drive arrived DOA. Was it bad luck? Maybe. Do I trust these drives? No, not anymore. Never had a drive DOA. This was by far my worst experience buying Western Digital drives on Amazon! And I have quite a lot of them (in total probably about 16 different WD Elements and MyBooks). Since these 2 drives were supposed to be used in a NAS which should hold the backups of my personal and work PCs I thought I'd buy the more expensive "real" WD Red Pro drives, which are designed for 24/7 operation, but what did I get? Just a way too long frustrating experience overall. Maybe I was just unlucky in this case, but I never had a problem with a shucked drive. So back to shucking external drives... I CANNOT recommend the WD Red Pro 18TB drives at this point. PS: the HDD came in the original Western Digital box which then was packed in one of the thin Amazon air bubble envelopes. Maybe it's an issue that the drives aren't shipped better protected? Not sure. The delivery driver dropped it off quite carefully, though. No idea what happened to the drive in between...

reviews.title: Reliable Storage for Network Attached Systems
reviews.comment: When you're building or upgrading a NAS system, drive reliability is paramount. The Seagate IronWolf Pro is designed specifically for enterprise NAS environments, and it delivers the performance and durability you need for always-on storage. This is a serious drive for serious storage needs. The 8TB capacity provides substantial storage space for a single drive. Whether you're storing large media files, running virtual machines, or handling heavy data workloads, having 8TB per drive means you can build high-capacity arrays without needing excessive drive bays. The capacity-to-cost ratio is excellent for this performance tier. CMR (Conventional Magnetic Recording) technology is a key advantage. Unlike SMR drives that can have performance issues with certain workloads, CMR provides consistent performance for NAS applications. Write operations don't bog down, and the drive handles simultaneous read-write operations smoothly. That consistent performance is crucial for multi-user environments. The 7200 RPM spindle speed delivers solid performance. Data access is quick, transfer rates are strong, and the drive handles demanding workloads without bottlenecking. Whether you're streaming multiple 4K video files or running database operations, the performance keeps up with what you're asking it to do. The 256MB cache is generous and helps with performance optimization. Frequently accessed data stays in cache for faster retrieval, and the drive can manage multiple operations more efficiently. That large cache contributes to the smooth, responsive performance you experience during actual use. SATA 6Gb/s interface provides the bandwidth needed for high-performance NAS applications. The drive can saturate the interface when needed, delivering the throughput that modern NAS workloads demand. Transfer speeds are consistently strong across different file types and access patterns. Build quality and reliability engineering are where the IronWolf Pro designation matters. These drives are rated for higher workload limits than consumer drives, with specifications that support 24/7 operation. The mean time between failures is rated at 1.2 million hours, indicating enterprise-grade reliability expectations. Vibration tolerance is engineered for multi-drive environments. NAS enclosures typically house multiple drives running simultaneously, which creates vibration. The IronWolf Pro is designed to maintain performance and reliability even with the vibration levels present in populated NAS chassis. That tolerance prevents performance degradation and premature failure. Noise and heat levels are reasonable for a 7200 RPM enterprise drive. It's not silent – there's the characteristic spinning platter sound – but it's not excessively loud either. Heat output is manageable with proper NAS ventilation. These drives operate within acceptable temperature ranges in well-ventilated enclosures. The rotational vibration sensors actively monitor and correct for vibration in real-time. This technology helps maintain performance and positioning accuracy even when multiple drives are working simultaneously in the same enclosure. It's one of the features that distinguishes NAS-specific drives from desktop models. Data recovery services are included for three years, which provides additional peace of mind. If a drive does fail and you need professional data recovery, having that service available can be invaluable. While you should always have backups, having recovery service as a safety net is reassuring. Power consumption is optimized for NAS environments. The drive balances performance with power efficiency, which matters when you're running multiple drives 24/7. Lower power consumption means lower operating costs and less heat generation in your NAS enclosure. Compatibility with major NAS platforms is excellent. Whether you're running Synology, QNAP, or another NAS operating system, these drives are recognized and work without issues. Seagate provides compatibility lists and optimization guides for popular NAS brands. Performance consistency over time remains strong. These drives don't show significant performance degradation as they age. The combination of quality components and robust firmware keeps them running reliably throughout their service life. Warranty coverage at five years demonstrates Seagate's confidence in these drives. That long warranty period provides protection for a substantial portion of the drive's expected lifespan. Having that coverage matters when you're investing in enterprise-grade storage. For anyone building or upgrading a NAS system and needing reliable, high-performance drives, the IronWolf Pro is an excellent choice. It's engineered specifically for NAS workloads, delivers consistent performance, and provides the reliability needed for always-on storage systems. Whether you're setting up a home media server or deploying small business storage, these drives give you enterprise-level reliability at a reasonable price point.

reviews.title: Dumpster fire trash, nonexistent support
reviews.comment: Don't buy.  That's the tl;dr.  Unless you hate your data and enjoy not getting warranty service. Bought four of these.  Two were DOA.  Two out of four brand new drives simply don't spin up.  That's ridiculous on its own.  The seller refused to replace them, despite having more in stock, and would only issue a refund and sell me two more for a 50% higher price.  That's pretty ridiculous, too.  So I went to seagate "support".  Their warranty site was down, try back later.  Well I did.  It stayed down.  It's still down weeks later.  I finally called support.  Waited on hold for 30 minutes.  Finally got someone who directed me to a different page by giving me a direct URL.  Said to click on a button that wasn't there.  Then told me that unless I accepted all cookies, I wouldn't be shown the button.  Pretty sure that violates various laws around the world.  Finally got to the RMA page, went through all the hoops, and they would only send me REFURB drives to replace brand new drives that were DOA.  No.  Absolutely not.  So I ended up returning them to the seller who refused to replace them for a refund.  He'll be getting an appropriate review, too. In short, quality control is clearly non-existent if my small sample of 4 drives with a 50% DOA rate is any indication.  I certainly wouldn't expect them to last in a NAS.  And when a drive failed, I certainly wouldn't expect to get a replacement in time to rebuild my raid before another failed.  These are trash.  Better to go with a Western Digital, which is what I did.  Capacity is slightly smaller, 26tb instead of 28, but I know they'll work and I know if I have problems I'll get actual support. I've worked in datacenters that go though large volumes of drives.  All manufacturers have failures, and they go through ups and downs over the years, but seagate was always pretty bad, and they just keep getting worse with time.  Never buying seagate again unless we need a new puck for datacenter hockey.

reviews.title: WD Red Pro NAS drives are solid drives
reviews.comment: Using 2, 4TB drives in a home RAID array for photos, videos, etc. Main drive is an SSD but decided to go with these for bulk storage as they are a bit cheaper (guessing my last time buying HDD's and next time will just use SSD's because they are just so much faster). Drives seems to perform nicely and other than a little HDD noise here and there don't find them bothersome at all. Previously had 2, 2TB of these red drives in a RAID array (had it running for about 8 years) and never had any issues. In our office we have Gold versions of these running on a backup server for about 6 years with no issues. All in all, very reliable. Speed is fine, but obviously not going to compare to SSD. One thing about size of the drives which I see some comments on... The size of the 4TB drive is going to be approximately 4 trillion bytes (mine is 4,000,765,177,856 bytes), however your system will likely report that as 3.64 TB or 3.726 GB. The reason for this is that Windows computes 1GB as equal to 1,073,741,824 bytes and 1TB as equal to 1,099,511,627,776 bytes. These numbers are achieved by raising 2 to an increasingly greater power till you get your first number in the billions and then trillions. There is some technical reason why this is done, but ultimately it is just confusing as it creates 2 different ways of computing size. One, counting the actual number of bytes and the other, dividing your bytes by one of those numbers to get the amount of GB's or TB's. For MB the number Windows uses is 1,048,576 bytes (for example a 20,000,0000 byte file will be reported as 20,000,000 / 1,048,576 = 19.07MB). In any case, here is a summary of the approx drives sizes and around what Windows will report the size as (assuming the drives sizes represent actual bytes exactly, so 4TB for this calculation will be 4,000,000,000 bytes and not the number my computer showed above... so expect the actual numbers to be slightly higher than these): 2TB Drive = 1.82TB or 1,862.65GB 4TB Drive = 3.64TB or 3,725.29GB 6TB Drive = 5.46TB or 5,587.94GB 8TB Drive = 7.28TB or 7,450.58GB 10TB Drive = 9.09TB or 9,313.23GB 20TB Drive = 18.19TB or 18,626.45GB Hope this clears up some confusion here.

reviews.title: Well-performing drive and not too noisy, but make sure to avoid OEM/grey-market units
reviews.comment: I bought two units of the 20TB version of this WD Red Pro drive for my new storage system. I particularly went with the 20TB version, because - according to the datasheet on Western Digital's website - it is less noisy than some of the lower capacity models. I tested one of the units, not in my storage system, but in my open bench USB 3.0 to SATA Adapter (with a max transfer rate of over 500MBps). It performed well, the sequential read and write speeds as high as ca. 270 MBps and ca. 130 MBps on the low-side. This is typical of all HDDs: on the outside of the drive they can pack more data on one track than on the inside, so on each rotation they can write and read more data on the outside area of each disk platter. The write and read tests were also successful, no bad blocks were reported. For some performance figures, please see the attached screenshots (which have the serial number removed/redacted). Please note that the CrystalDiskMark results are performed on an empty HDD, so they seem to be executed in the "fast" section of the drive. The other graphs were taken from HDSentinel, relevant there are the bottom graphs, which show transfer rates across the surface of the drive. The sound of my test unit was also pleasant enough, the clicking wasn't too bothersome. But since I will move this drive into the case of my storage system very soon, the clicking will be a lot less noticeable than it is already. One action I always perform, BEFORE opening the product box of an HDD or SDD is to check the serial number on the box against the manufacturer's warranty website to ensure that the item is covered by the manufacturer's warranty. I do this both when amazon is the seller and when a 3rd party is the seller and amazon is just the fulfillment party. (I do not buy HDDs from a 3rd party seller that does not have fulfillment with amazon.) This is to avoid OEM/gray-market units that aren't covered by the manufacturer's warranty. A store warranty by a 3rd party seller is of no use to me, since these sellers come and go and I also don't want the hassle of dealing with them. Since the Red Pro series offers a manufacturer's warranty of 5 years, and HDDs fail frequently enough to make such a warranty very valuable, I always insist getting the manufacturer's warranty and even will query 3rd party sellers, if their stock with amazon is covered by such a warranty. As it turned out, the serial number of second 20TB HDD that I ordered (from a 3rd party seller, since amazon themselves were out of stock) did not show up in the manufacturer's database for U.S. warranty, so I can only assume that it is a gray-market unit and I immediately returned it. (I can only hope that the 3rd party seller will have to bear the full cost of this return, since I emailed them and asked about the manufacturer's warranty, before the item ever shipped, but they didn't answer my question.) One more tip: There has been some research that failure rates of HDDs from the same batch are somewhat correlated, so I always try to space out my purchases (either in time or by using different vendors) to increase the chance that I will be getting units from different batches. That's why I bought from two different 3rd party sellers on amazon (one of which apparently sold a grey-market unit), without disclosing that fact ahead of time.

reviews.title: GPT protective partition in Windows
reviews.comment: I purchased the 4T version for home PC with a windows operating system. I need this particular HDD because it is listed 7200RPM. I didn't meet any challenge when I installed other WD hard drives. It involved only a few clicks when I switched from WD 1T to 2T months ago, for example. I simply inserted the new disk into a USB case and cloned the entire disk in Minitool participation and got the job done. I was not lucky with this disk. It gave me so much trouble and wasted my two days to figure this out. First, sector size was different from my old 2t WD Blue drive thus I couldn't clone it directly. Because the target drive was not the main OS drive so I decided to simply copy all the folders into the new HDD and switch the two. Then I used Minitool to format it. It refused the command, software reported error. I then tried all other software including the one recommended on WD website (Acronis True Image for Western Digital). I finally got it done by using EaseUS. I formatted it and copied all folders from the old disk and switched it with the old internal disk. When I opened windows, none of the partitions created in EaseUS showed up. HDD showed up in BIOS menu so I knew it was there. I googled answer to this problem, read all articles to educate myself. Checked "Manage disk" in OS and realized one of the partitions was listed as GPT protective partition. I then followed the article published on Seagate website (ironic) and cleaned the entire disk using diskpat command. All data were removed. I returned to day 1. If your partition software doesn't work in Windows, check whether this disk is GPT protective in disk management. Don't repeat my mistake. I am glad I didn't do anything harmful to the old drive thus I spent the second day repeating what I did before, copy and paste. Now the new drive works and it works faster than old WD blue 2T. It is quite noisy but not scary. I am satisfied with the product so far but I hope WD can improve the product to meet various needs from customers. I am not a tech guy but switching HDD shouldn't be so difficult and time-consuming, thus I removed one star (should have been two stars when I felt frustrated yesterday).

First: the build quality. It feels exceptionally sturdy for its size. It doesn’t have that “cheap metal” type of feel a lot of other matx cases have. It feels very well built. The features on this case are extraordinary as well. The magnetic front mesh panel is a godsend. Cleaning out the fans will be a breeze for whoever gets this. Second: building in the case. It was EXTREMELY easy to build in this. I’ve built in plenty of matx cases and this one by far was the easiest I’ve built in. The cable management was practically done for me before even beginning the build. I altered some things around but otherwise I left the cables where they were. reviews.title: Superb design and quality
reviews.comment: This is a beautiful case in all white.  The is more than enough room for just about anything you want to put in there.  Even with a vertically mounted 5070 ti, there is a lot of extra space left over, giving the final result a nice open feel.  That said, it's a large case - make sure you have room for it at close to 13" deep.  There a several things that made this the easiest build I have done.  Aside from the interior size, the dual chambered design makes cabling easy and keeps the front side clean-looking.  Additionally, every bracket, screw hole and snap connection matched up perfectly with overall fit and finish being near-perfect.  I have six intake fans and four exhaust fans, including the AIO cooler for plenty of airflow, though on the down side, the slatted exterior covers probably restrict the airflow to some extent.  One other concern is that it will be a tight fit to get even one low-profile pci card in along with the gpu and pci riser.  Not an issue right now, but possibly in the future.  The case does not come with any fans, though given the range of fan choices and options, included fans probably be not what the user wants anyway.  The case is not inexpensive, but I think worth the cost.  It is heavy also, but built very sturdily.

reviews.title: Love this case!
reviews.comment:
I adore this case! Yes, it's definitely a luxury case as it's pricier than others, but this version does have the 2k screen included. The glass is tempered and I didn't have any issues with it cracking or scratching during the pc build. The bottom compartment does fit three fans, just know you need to fit one inside the case before attaching it to the bracket to make them all fit.
As far as the screen goes, it's a beautiful screen, do note, you need to connect it directly to the motherboard for the picture to work and download the software so you can set your picture/widgets. The cables to hook it up are already ran to the back of the case when it arrives, so you'll just need to hook them up to your motherboard and power supply.
The top of the case does have a compartment that lowers if you want to mount fans or your AIO closer to your motherboard.
Do note, this case includes a PCIe riser 4.0 to connect your GPU to your MOB so the GPU sits upright in the case. IF you need a 5.0 connection like I did, you'll need to purchase the 5.0 riser off Hyte's website, at the time I purchased, they were $99 and you can choose which color you'd like.
The case has plenty of places to route your cables for easy cable management as well as preinstalled Velcro in the bottom to hold some of the cables.
The only downside I saw was needing to buy an updated PCIe riser, I wish they would have had that as an upgrade option at purchase, as well as there being two open spots on the back of the side where you mount the GPU etc. I'm assuming its for easier access, but I do worry about the amount of dust etc that allows into the pc, though I'm sure it's great for airflow.

reviews.title: Thinnest gauges steel I've ever seen
reviews.comment: This is the best looking case for ITX with two fans bottom and top!  All the big name brands try to check too many boxes on paper such as 120/140mm fan support, radiator/fan mounting brackets, and they just end up looking a mess.  This case: 1. Doesn't have a huge gap to the right of an ITX motherboard 2. Only has mounting holes for 120mm fans resulting in a clean look 3. Has room for a 240mm radiator on the side, with push and pull fans! 4. No support in the corner blocking your view 5. Tempered glass is nicely tinted for black version 6. Fits full size ATX power supply 7. Doesn't waste space trying to fit a 360mm radiator This is kinda cheap though, so there are some downsides: 1. You can bend this steel with your hands 2. The ventilation has way too much material-to-hole ratio, blocking airflow.  This goes for both the steel and magnetic screen/filter. 3. The height should have been raised 30mm above the motherboard to allow a radiator to be mounted on the top.  There is only room for fans, and adding a 30mm radiator would cause a collision with your RAM and CPU cooler. 4. The black strips on the glass edge should be as thin as possible to allow you to see the sides of your fans.  Unless you have ugly fans? I ended up cutting out the steel where fans are placed, and 3D printing fan filters with a 0.2mm nozzle instead.  Much better airflow.

reviews.title: A Game Changer in Portable Storage
reviews.comment: In the realm of portable storage solutions, the SanDisk 1TB Portable SSD emerges as a formidable contender, offering a blend of speed, durability, and compactness that caters to the needs of professionals and everyday users alike. Design and Portability: The SanDisk 1TB Portable SSD impresses with its sleek and compact design. Encased in a durable yet lightweight aluminum shell, it exudes a premium feel while ensuring protection against accidental drops and shocks. Its diminutive size makes it effortlessly portable, fitting snugly into pockets or laptop bags without adding unnecessary bulk. Performance: Where the SanDisk 1TB Portable SSD truly shines is in its performance. Equipped with high-speed NVMe technology and USB 3.2 Gen 2 interface, it delivers blazing-fast data transfer speeds, significantly reducing file transfer times. Whether you're transferring large multimedia files, backing up extensive photo libraries, or running demanding applications directly from the drive, the SanDisk SSD handles tasks with remarkable efficiency. Reliability and Durability: Reliability is paramount when it comes to storage devices, and the SanDisk SSD doesn't disappoint. Built to withstand the rigors of daily use, it boasts impressive durability features, including shock resistance of up to 1500G and vibration resistance, ensuring data integrity even in challenging environments. Moreover, its solid-state design means there are no moving parts susceptible to wear and tear, enhancing its longevity. Value for Money: While the SanDisk 1TB Portable SSD may come at a slightly higher price point compared to traditional HDDs or lower-capacity flash drives, its exceptional performance, reliability, and portability justify the investment. The peace of mind knowing that your data is secure and easily accessible on the go makes it a worthwhile purchase for professionals and enthusiasts alike. Conclusion: In summary, the SanDisk 1TB Portable SSD sets a new standard for portable storage solutions, combining top-tier performance, rugged durability, and compact design in a single package. Whether you're a photographer needing to back up large RAW files on location, a videographer editing high-resolution footage, or a student transporting essential documents between classes, this SSD delivers the speed, reliability, and convenience required to meet your storage needs. If you're in the market for a portable storage solution that doesn't compromise on performance or durability, the SanDisk 1TB Portable SSD undoubtedly deserves your consideration.

The only thing I wish it had was more fan mounting options in the bottom bay. At most, you can have 2 exhaust fans in the lower bay, depending on the PSU size and placement. Meanwhile, there are front, side and rear mounting positions for the upper bay. I’d really like to have intake fans blowing air across the drives in the bottom.
Hopefully someone makes a 3d printable mod to add front intake fans like with the N4.
Regardless, this is a solid case, highly recommend it.
[Edit - April 21, 2026] There is a 3d printable mod for this case to add 2x120mm fans for intake on the front. It adds a bump to the front of the case, but also dropped my drive temps by ~8-10C, so a good trade in my opinion.

reviews.title: Solid Build with one major flaw: Needs an SFX-to-ATX bracket
reviews.comment:
Great NAS case with solid build quality and ventilation. However, there is a design oversight when using a 240mm AIO. The radiator takes up the space intended for the PSU, forcing you to mount the power supply elsewhere.
Since I have an SFX PSU, I had to mount it at the bottom next to the drive cage. The cables down there are extremely tight and push against the HDD backplane, which isn't ideal. It would be a huge improvement if Jonsbo included an 'SFX-to-ATX' bracket to mount the small PSU in the top rear slot (where the ATX PSU usually goes). This would completely clear up the bottom chamber, leaving plenty of room for the drive cables and better airflow for the disks.
Great NAS case, but watch out for AIO/PSU clearance
reviews.author: luis velilla walker

reviews.title: Best NAS case!
reviews.comment: This is the best NAS case I've seen and used in the past 20 years. If you have a M-ATX or ITX motherboard. This is the best NAS case!
reviews.author: Jeffrey W. George

reviews.title: Research before purchase!
reviews.comment: I love the way how this case looks and the amount of drives this thing can take. The included fans is nice but they are a tiny bit noticeable on noise depending on what setting you have it on, if connected to the fan speed switch on the case. I'll probably switch those out for something quieter. As for having options for installing a power supply/SFX, its still limiting on where you can put them due to how your setup is and how long the cables are on the power supply. If you plan on using a regular sized power supply you'll only have one spot to put it and it also covers a good chunk of the motherboard so you'll have to get a low profile cooler or water cool if it fits. So please do your research and look at how you would set it up BEFORE you think about buying this case.
reviews.author: Humberto Castellanos

reviews.title: Superb design and quality
reviews.comment: This is a beautiful case in all white.  The is more than enough room for just about anything you want to put in there.  Even with a vertically mounted 5070 ti, there is a lot of extra space left over, giving the final result a nice open feel.  That said, it's a large case - make sure you have room for it at close to 13" deep.  There a several things that made this the easiest build I have done.  Aside from the interior size, the dual chambered design makes cabling easy and keeps the front side clean-looking.  Additionally, every bracket, screw hole and snap connection matched up perfectly with overall fit and finish being near-perfect.  I have six intake fans and four exhaust fans, including the AIO cooler for plenty of airflow, though on the down side, the slatted exterior covers probably restrict the airflow to some extent.  One other concern is that it will be a tight fit to get even one low-profile pci card in along with the gpu and pci riser.  Not an issue right now, but possibly in the future.  The case does not come with any fans, though given the range of fan choices and options, included fans probably be not what the user wants anyway.  The case is not inexpensive, but I think worth the cost.  It is heavy also, but built very sturdily.
reviews.author: EricAZ

reviews.title: Love this case!
reviews.comment:
I adore this case! Yes, it's definitely a luxury case as it's pricier than others, but this version does have the 2k screen included. The glass is tempered and I didn't have any issues with it cracking or scratching during the pc build. The bottom compartment does fit three fans, just know you need to fit one inside the case before attaching it to the bracket to make them all fit.
As far as the screen goes, it's a beautiful screen, do note, you need to connect it directly to the motherboard for the picture to work and download the software so you can set your picture/widgets. The cables to hook it up are already ran to the back of the case when it arrives, so you'll just need to hook them up to your motherboard and power supply.
The top of the case does have a compartment that lowers if you want to mount fans or your AIO closer to your motherboard.
Do note, this case includes a PCIe riser 4.0 to connect your GPU to your MOB so the GPU sits upright in the case. IF you need a 5.0 connection like I did, you'll need to purchase the 5.0 riser off Hyte's website, at the time I purchased, they were $99 and you can choose which color you'd like.
The case has plenty of places to route your cables for easy cable management as well as preinstalled Velcro in the bottom to hold some of the cables.
The only downside I saw was needing to buy an updated PCIe riser, I wish they would have had that as an upgrade option at purchase, as well as there being two open spots on the back of the side where you mount the GPU etc. I'm assuming its for easier access, but I do worry about the amount of dust etc that allows into the pc, though I'm sure it's great for airflow.
reviews.author: Amazon_Customer

reviews.title: Premium Case with a Built-In Touchscreen – Still One of the Best After 2 Years
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/E15OAZcxEjL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/61kkYUGl7UL._SY256.jpg ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ – One of the Best Cases I’ve Ever Built In
I’ve had the HYTE Y70 Touch Infinite Dual Chamber ATX Case for about two years now, and honestly, it’s one of the best PC cases I’ve ever built in.
First off, the build experience is incredibly smooth. The dual-chamber design gives you tons of room to work with, making cable management clean and stress-free. Everything feels thoughtfully laid out, so even more complex builds come together easily without feeling cramped.
Compatibility and size are a huge plus. This case easily supports larger GPUs, multiple radiators, and high-end components without any issues. Whether you’re running a high-performance gaming setup or a workstation build, there’s more than enough space to work with.
One of the standout features is the built-in touchscreen, which is honestly amazing. It adds a completely different level of customization and functionality—you can display system stats, animations, or anything you want. It’s not just a gimmick, it actually enhances the overall experience and makes the build feel premium.
Installation overall is very straightforward. Panels come off easily, parts line up well, and the modular design helps speed things up. It’s clear this case was designed with builders in mind.
Price-wise, it’s definitely on the higher end, but after using it for two years, I can say it’s absolutely worth it. The quality, features, and overall experience justify the investment.
Pros:
• Extremely easy and enjoyable to build in
• Spacious with excellent compatibility for high-end parts
• Dual-chamber design keeps everything clean and organized
• Built-in touchscreen is a standout feature and works great
• Premium look and feel
Cons:
• Higher price point, but you get what you pay for
Overall, if you’re looking for a high-end case that combines performance, aesthetics, and innovation, this is a top-tier choice.
reviews.author: Aaron medina

reviews.title: Best case I've built in.
reviews.comment: Fantastic case, I enjoyed building in it. Looks good and can fit all my components with room for more if I decide to add to my pc. Cable management is simple and you can really spend some time with it and make it nice. Room for fans keeps this case pretty cool, really helped my build that easily overheats normally, and has good dust filters and everything to keep it nice inside. Not a lot of thought went into the look of my build but it still looks quite nice in this case. Worth it for the price for sure.
reviews.author: Andie

reviews.title: Easy to build in, great case for beginner builders and experienced builders alike.
reviews.comment: No dust filter on top, dust filter in front and bottom. The infinirail is neat, and does save time and effort. Just not a lot. Hands down, this is the easiest case I have ever built in. Both of my sons have a PC using this case, and I would strongly recommend it as a top tier budget case. This case has what is, in my opinion, the greatest functionality improvement in years. The consolidated front panel connector. The mesh filter in front is easy to remove and clean, allowing for plenty of airflow. The case itself is sturdy.
reviews.author: Brandon Wirtz

reviews.title: Exceptional Case — Airflow, Style, and Ease of Build All in One
reviews.comment:
✅ Review: 5 out of 5 stars
The CORSAIR 4000D RS ARGB Frame is one of the best cases I’ve ever built in. It perfectly balances a clean, minimal aesthetic with thoughtful functionality, making it ideal for both first-time builders and experienced enthusiasts.
🧩 Modular & Spacious
The modular design is a huge plus—panels, PSU shroud, and drive trays are all easy to remove and reposition. It fits full ATX motherboards, supports reverse-connector boards (like ASUS BTF), and has plenty of clearance for modern GPUs and cooling setups. Installation was smooth with excellent cable management features like Velcro straps, channels, and a clean PSU shroud.
🌬️ Airflow and Cooling
Out of the box, it comes with three RS120 ARGB fans that are quiet and look great. The front mesh panel allows for incredible airflow, and you can install up to ten 120 mm fans or a 360 mm radiator without issues. Temps in my build dropped noticeably compared to my older case.
✨ Design & Aesthetics
It has a sleek look that doesn’t scream “gamer,” but still feels modern and premium. The pre-installed ARGB fans add just the right amount of lighting without being overbearing—and no separate RGB controller is needed. The tempered glass side panel showcases your build beautifully.
🛠️ Practical Touches
USB-C on the front I/O is a welcome addition, and the GPU support arm is a great touch to avoid sag. I also appreciated the tool-free panel design—it makes upgrades and maintenance fast and painless.
⚠️ Minor Downsides
The side panel feels a bit thin and needs to be handled gently, especially when removing it. Also, if you plan to mount a 360 mm AIO on the top, be aware that RAM or VRM clearance might be tight depending on your motherboard.
🔍 Final Thoughts
This case is a top-tier pick for airflow-focused builders who want clean aesthetics, solid thermal performance, and ease of use. Whether you’re doing a standard ATX build or going for something more high-end with reverse cable routing, the 4000D RS ARGB handles it all gracefully. Highly recommend!
reviews.author: Austin P.

reviews.title: Best Case Scenario
reviews.comment: Awesome case. I was told the front looks like a cheese grater, but other than that it is very spacious and easy to build in. The modernized features make accessing all components easy. Wish it came with a dust cover for the top like a couple of the other cases I've used. It seems very open and susceptible to dust, but time will tell if that becomes an issue.
reviews.author: mikaela

reviews.title: Great mid-sized case.
reviews.comment:
Nice, cozy look, as you can see in the photo (build isn't done yet so not pictured is the power supply shroud that can mount two more fans pointed at the graphics card.) Excellent fan placements, although I think they could have at least included the rear exhaust fan. Still gets a little cramped for your hands while working on it as any.mod-sized case does. Being mid-sized means the fan mounts on the power supply shroud will be fairly close to the graphics card and should cool it down by a good couple degrees, though.
The built-in structural support for the graphics card is a nice touch, but the panel it's attached to is too wide for some videocards; I had to remove it to fit my RX9070 into the case and use a more typical brace to prevent sagging. With the side panel off you can clearly see the empty space where it went. Fortunately, all the different parts are easy to remove or replace.
The one actual thing that makes this four stars instead of five, however, is that the bottom side panel and the top panel do not have dust filters pre-installed. Technically you don't need either, but if you're going to use the power supply shroud fan mounts, you're going to need to put a filter in the bottom side panel because that's where those fans are going to get their intake from. Baffling that there isn't a dust filter already there.

reviews.author: Aaron medina

reviews.title: Great case
reviews.comment: Show-stopping touchscreen display adds flair and functionality most cases don’t offer. Massive internal space & cooling support, great for custom water-cooling builds. the app was slow, memory-hungry, and occasionally forgetful, making the touchscreen experience less smooth than anticipated. If you want something that stands out visually and adds a new layer of interactivity to your setup, it’s one of the few cases that delivers on that promise. The hardware design and cooling support are excellent for high-end builds. However, if you prefer a straightforward, no-nonsense build or care more about pure performance than showmanship, you might find the touchscreen feature a bit gimmicky, especially given the bumpy software experience. This isn’t just a gimmick — it can display real system information and interact with apps — but the software side still needs polishing and can be heavy on RAM or laggy with more complex widgets. The HYTE Y70 Touch is a premium ATX mid-tower PC case that stands out primarily for its large integrated touchscreen, along with a spacious dual-chamber interior and strong cooling potential. It’s designed for high-end systems where aesthetics, display integration, and build showcase are as important as performance.
reviews.author: Savana

reviews.title: The perfect pc case!
reviews.comment: This has been my dream case for the longest time now! I finally did a big pc upgrade and I was super excited to make a hyte build. I thought the glass panels and regular panels would be hard to remove from the case but it's super easy to pop off ( and I have long nails ). The case is a lot bigger than what I thought it would be but I love how spacious it is, it makes it super easy to build your pc in. I was also surprised to see it had a section at the bottom of the case for fans so I might add some down there later on. The case filters out dust well and makes it super easy to clean when dust builds up in the filters. Like I said before it's so easy to remove the case panels cleaning your pc is not a chore, you can easily pop out the panels making removability easy. I definitely think it's worth the money, I'm so in love with the touch panel I use it mainly for discord and Spotify and I just love how the case looks! And because it's so big air flow is great and the pc itself is very quiet.
reviews.author: Victoria Jones

reviews.title: Quality case, competitive price, but buy a modular or semi modular PSU for your build.
reviews.comment: well built case - full size atx board fit comfortably. Not to plentiful for hard drives, but space for one in a bracket for a 3.5 and two 2.5, though I had to tweak for a third. PSU fit fine, screws are well fitting and well made. Documentation is rather sparce, but this was my first build, really kind of forgiving. Follow the directions of the motherboard. Fans work fine and cooling is no issue for me, rather really overkill for my needs. Nice glass side panel to see your setup working away, good for RGB lighting if you have any, but this case was without the RGB lighting. I don't care to have my room light up like a disco. ANyway that's me. For the quality I thought it was really a good deal. competitive price. Cable management wasn't too bad, but in the end I wish I would have bought a modular or a semi modular PSU instead of the basic one I bought, have some extra cables that are just taking up space, had to wrap some with quick ties. Thanks.
reviews.author: Justin Huber

reviews.title: Gran look
reviews.comment: Luce muy atractiva, deja que los componentes internos se ventilen bien.
reviews.author: Mauricio A. Quiroga R.

reviews.title: Easy to use
reviews.comment: Easy installation. Works perfect.
reviews.author: Anand Bollineni

reviews.title: Ocypus Gamma A40 BK cooler
reviews.comment: The Ocypus Gamma A40 BK is a decent cooler with good results and capability for a Ryzen 3700X (65w) and it looks good, even if the top cap is plastic. I must have gotten a little new product discount before the price increased to the current cost. It's size is perfect for the smaller towers and fits well. The 100 mm CPU fan is a good compromise between sizes of those 120 or 92 mm fans. When I sliced a flexible dragon using Cura the unit was capable of keeping the CPU below 77°C. It's working fine but you can probably do better with a bigger cooler and you're planning on using a CPU in the 125w+ range and having it pegged at a hundred percent. It's definitely better than the last tower cooler I used on a AMD FX6300 which was a Thermal take if I recall correctly. When the fan needs replacement I'll see what the company has available for it, and I'll design and 3D print something if I need to, but for the money it's definitely a very good and solid product to choose! I'd recommend it highly. No LEDs is a definite BONUS too. 😁
reviews.author: SprayMax Headroom

reviews.title: Great Budget CPU Cooler w/ Great Looks
reviews.comment: Why did you pick this product vs others?: Product looks quite nice and RGB is very well diffused. Looks pretty clean. Despite the small size, 100mm fan vs 120mm on a more normal tower it was great for the ryzen 5 3600 I used it for. Value for money: got it on sale and it was a great value for the price. Instructions were written and installing was quite easy Cooling: The included thermal paste was disappointing and I would recommend maybe getting aftermarket paste. Otherwise cooling was great on a mid range or budget cpu
reviews.author: Gabriel

reviews.title: Soild cooler for the price.
reviews.comment: Nothing short of the perfect upgrade over the stock AM4 cooler for only $20. Was incredibly straight foward to install and it has decreased my idle temp from 33 degrees all the way down to 23 degrees, with full load temp being at 45 degrees. Quality is alright and the fan isn't too loud.
reviews.author: XxNyaaaxX

reviews.title: Not bad
reviews.comment: Cheap, but surprisingly effective. However there are better options for only a few dollars more.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Clean & Cool
reviews.comment: Super clean & runs cool, it is a smaller than average looking cooler but it’s still super nice!
reviews.author: Noelia Pena

reviews.title: Perfect cpu temps at unbeatable price
reviews.comment: For the price the cooler is a fantastic value and it works great. I have mine configured with both fans and during stress testing the cpu never went over 76c. Idle temps sit between 33-45. Mounting wasn't too difficult, but you do need access to both sides of your motherboard. I didn't need to remove my mobo, I just needed to open the other side of the case. The airflow on the fans are adequate. My hardware monitoring puts the max speed of the fans around 2k rpm. Personally, I will replace the fans just because I like faster fans but the ones that came with it seem good enough.
reviews.author: Dan

reviews.title: It cools very well, and it is quiet.
reviews.comment: This dual-tower CPU cooler completely exceeded my expectations. The build quality is excellent, with its six copper heat pipes that truly help dissipate heat quickly and efficiently. Since installing it, my processor stays much cooler even under heavy load , which makes a noticeable difference in performance.
reviews.author: Blanca Gutierrez

reviews.title: Big beefy boi of a cooler with amazing cooling ability and remaining quiet when under load
reviews.comment: Amazing cooler for the price. It keeps the cpu on my lga1150 intel i74770k cooler than the stock fan and is super quiet while also being RGB if I want to use that. Installation is super simple and it comes with thermal paste that works well out of the box. Would definitely suggest for a budget cooler if it fits your socket type. Just one word of caution is that this cooler is beefy and might not fit in some tower cases, so make sure you check max clearance between the cpu/processor and side of case.
reviews.author: Cody

reviews.title: Good budget option
reviews.comment:
Good budget option, keeps my R5 3600 around 60 deg while gaming.
Its a bit on the noisy side, rpms are 2000 +/- 10%
Argb controller is not included, either your mobo has the argb header or you have an external argb contoller.
Would buy again.
reviews.author: Vladimir dominguez

reviews.title: Good, nice, and cheap
reviews.comment: It works well, and it's affordable and looks nice. I haven't seen the temperatures go above 60 while gaming. I recommend it, the RGB works with a Corsair Commander Duo.
reviews.author: Jose Angel Gutierrez

reviews.title: Worked so well I didn't need it anymore :)
reviews.comment: I had an old i5-2500K that I just couldn't bring myself to get rid of, and decided that it was either time to let it go or get it to run at a useful speed.  I was running overclocked at 4.4Ghz on the stock Intel cooler and getting temps of around 81c under full load, so to go further I needed better cooling., This looked like a great budget option. The result was a 30c drop in core temps while running a stress test!  Averages dropped to 51c and max observed temp was only 54C!  Awesome! With that kind of cooling performance I was ready to let the horses run on that old processor, and run it did!  Right up until the 12-year-old Gigabyte z68 motherboard decided that 4.9GHz and 1.385v was just too much for its old components and beta UEFI.  It died a good death right there on the dining room table... a bittersweet end to a legendary combo. But that no fault of the cooler.  Performance was beyond expectations.  It was well-packaged, easy to install, well-made, had everything I needed including thermal paste (saved me a trip to the basement), and man was it QUIET.  Excellent cooler on-par with another brand I just installed that cost twice as much. I'm not sure whether I am going to hang onto it or not since I just ordered a replacement CPU that comes with a stock cooler (budget build - stock is good enough), but for under twenty bucks I wouldn't mind keeping this in the parts bin in case one of my machines needs a replacement.
reviews.author: Dan V.

reviews.title: Good Budget CPU Cooler
reviews.comment: This Thermalright Assassin X120 Refined SE CPU cooler is a solid option for the price. It feels well-made, the 120mm PWM fan runs smoothly, and the 4 heat pipes help provide good cooling for everyday PC use. It’s a nice upgrade over a basic stock cooler and works with a wide range of AMD and Intel sockets.
reviews.author: FK

reviews.title: Chill Force One
reviews.comment: Mister Twiggly is an ardent gamer, and his home-built gaming rig, while ancient, is capable. However, the stock cooler was getting a little noisy at times, so it was time for a replacement. Enter the Thermalright Assassin X120 Refined SE. Installation was fairly straightforward, though he had to pull out the motherboard to attach the backplate. From then on it was plain sailing. Testing showed that the CPU temperature is 10-15°C cooler at rest and 20-25°C cooler under load than the stock cooler, which he is holding in his right paw. Moreover, fan noise is barely noticeable - hardly surprising, since the fan is huge and runs far more slowly than its predecessor to cool that monster heatsink. This is music to Mister Twiggly's fluffy but sensitive ears. A very good solution at a modest price. Mister Twiggly says "Hurrah for Thermalright!", and gives this product his highest recommendation.
reviews.author: Mister Twiggly

reviews.title: No frills, excellent quality cooling. Don't forget air flow and thermal paste.
reviews.comment: heavy and well built. don't even try to put this on with the motherboard on it's end, lay the sucker down. it is quite heavy. Like I said well built, more than enough for my needs. Good for most CPUs, maybe not for the big suckers and more modern CPUs.  I have an older setup so this works perfectly, almost overkill really. No frills, just excellent cooling. Don't forget the pea sized amount of thermal paste, very critical. the cooler is made with main stacks of copper with aluminum (?) grills. Fan is quiet and runs just fine, before installing ensure you have the fan pointing towards the exit air flow, because if you're pointing it towards an incoming fan you'll lose out on alot of the efficiency and could create hot pockets perhaps. So THINK before you install. these fans go only one way.  NO RGB lighting on this, if you just need cooling and don't need a disco lighting setup. LOL.
reviews.author: Justin Huber

reviews.title: Thermaltake my money
reviews.comment: Another awesome unit from thermaltake for cheap. Keeps my r5-3600 super cool under heavy gaming. Easy to install and very secure. Just make sure you follow the included instructions to make sure it seats properly. Also fairly quiet
reviews.author: Bert

reviews.title: Great cooler!
reviews.comment: Very quiet and efficient. Large fan and powerful cooler! Keeps the CPU very cool while busy. Excellent value!
reviews.author: Chris Brickner

reviews.title: Amazing Budget Cooler; 100% suitable for an APU system ✅
reviews.comment: for just 17 bucks for a ThermalRight cooler, its an amazing deal; you get very good cooling for an excellent value, especially for APU systems. I only have 1 intake on my PC and this thing stays around 72C max when doing OCCT which is awesome. despite it going 2k rpm in intense workloads, it stays quiet. Quality seemed fine to me for 17 bucks, what more could you ask for? It can go up to 2.2k RPM and even then, its still pretty quiet and does a good job cooling my 5600G down. Now of course, if you have a very hungry CPU like 120W+, I would get a better cooler but for APU builds like mine, its an amazing deal.
reviews.author: JLW

reviews.title: Great value.
reviews.comment: I grabbed this because it was highly rated for the price.  I'm using it with a 9600x processor, so didn't need a more powerful cooling system as that CPU does not run that hot.  This has worked great so far.
reviews.author: Richard M. Lippincott

reviews.title: Makes a HUGE Difference in Temps--Quality Build and Operation
reviews.comment: Bottomline up front: This little CPU air tower cooler makes a huge difference and fits great in smaller PC cases Bought this to cool my Dell Inspiron 3670 MT i5-8400 PC that I was turning into a casual gaming machine as well.  Stock CPU cooler was just not cutting it--CPU was heating up to over 85 Celsius and shutting off.  A better thermal solution was needed, I didn't want to drop a bunch of $$ to fix it, and it had to be something smaller than the standard size air towers using a 120mm cooling fan.  Enter the Thermalright Assassin X90 SE V2, which uses a smaller 90mm fan unit and appropriately sized fin/block tower. This smaller size cooler is AMAZING!  Just opening the box (unboxing video uploaded) I could tell the build quality was already there.  For something small, it had some decent weight.  Everything was packaged well, and the cooler itself looks and feels well built.  From the heat pipes to the fins to the metal top cap (not plastic...ahem, ID Cooling)...this thing looked legit.  Came with instructions, thermal paste, brackets, screws and standoffs, I installed it on my CPU and fired it up. Immediately I noticed CPU temps were 10-15 degrees Celsius lower at idle.  With the stock cooler, idle CPU temps were hovering around 45-50 Celsius.  With the Assassin, idle temps were only 35-40 C. But the real magic happened under load.  Using OCCT to stress test my CPU, with the stock cooler temps hit 85 C before the PC shut down to save itself, and this is only after 3 minutes of testing.  With the Assassin X90, temps never got above 70 C, and this was done over 3 separate 10 minute continuous tests, where the CPU was at max utilization for 10 minutes straight each time. Bottomline: if you need a low cost, smaller sized thermal solution for your CPU, this is definitely one to consider!!

reviews.title: Cooling things down with this cpu cooler.

Installation isn't too bad for someone with PC knowledge. It is rather big, so be cautious of spacing, but it should cool well with the added thermal paste. This cooling system is installed in a HP Victus 15L desktop with the Ryzen 7 processor.

reviews.title: Great Cooler-Replace Thermal Paste
reviews.comment:
These AMD CPU Coolers work great except the thermal paste almost glues to the CPU.  I recently tried to upgrade my AMD Ryzen 5 to 7.  Ran computer for over 30 minutes and the CPU came off with the fan heat sink.  I had to heat it up with a hair dryer to finally get the CPU to move.
Did some checking and this is supposedly a well known problem.  Recommendation is to remove the pre applied thermal paste on the AMD Wrath cooler.  Then apply a good quality thermal paste on CPU.  If you ever have to upgrade or change cooler you will have issues.  If already used the cooler with pre applied paste several people said to run stress test software on CPU to get real warm.  Issue with coming off with fan is bending or Miss alignment of pins.
reviews.author: OregonBob

reviews.title: Great fan for $8
reviews.comment:
The main selling point is the price, and the value proposition for $8 is insane. It comes with the fan, heatsink, and thermal paste. Basically just screw it on and plug it in. Great and easy setup and it fits in a low profile case just fine. My only complaint is that the fan can be a touch loud, but it's still quieter than my GPU and again, $8.
No actually, my main complaint is that there is so little metal on the heatsink that it cannot absorb any small, quick frequency boosts. This means that the fan will often go from fast to slow to fast to slow over just a handful of seconds, which can be annoying. Still, this behavior is relatively infrequent (mostly just at system startup), and again, $8. I can live with that for $8.
This was used on a Ryzen 5700x, and it worked good enough.
reviews.author: Nathan P.

reviews.title: Very impressive Cooler
reviews.comment: I recently bought the Geometric Future Model 5 PC case, and wanted to have a unified fan system, so I bought this CPU Cooler to go with it. Love the look of the Cooling block and the fans have a really nice RGB ring around them, although the fans do get a little loud at times.  Also the fans come daisy chained together so it very easy to install into your PC case. Been monitoring the temperature of my CPU (a Ryzen 9 7900x) while doing various task and so far this cooler has done a great job at keeping everything nice and cool. So overall very good value for the money. Also, when i first got the CPU Cooler, i was given the incorrect amount of bracket screws for my motherboard. You are suppose to get 4 Intel screws and 4 AMD screws, but i was given 5 Intel and only 3 AMD. I managed to make it work using the screws of one of my previous CPU coolers but I emailed them on a whim seeing if there was anyway I could get the missing screw and I was impressed by how fast they responded back. Within almost 24 hours, they responded and notified me that they shipped out a replacement set of screws (I can't even get companies like ASUS to respond to  my emails). So overall very impressed by this company and their Customer Service.
reviews.author: Nick O.

reviews.title: Excellent service and product
reviews.comment: The pump is making a terrible noise. Water cooling 420 mm. As if an old compressor refrigerator is working. Moreover, the pump does not start making noise right away, but on the second or third day. I don’t know what this is connected with. I wrote to the official website of Geometric Future, but they never answered me. I had to return the first copy to Amazon because I thought it was a factory defect. I received a new set exactly the same from Amazon. And three days later it also started making noise. It’s terrible. I tried to solve the problem and turned the case to release bubbles and tried to adjust the speed. I noticed that the pump does not whistle at low speeds. At medium speeds from time to time. At full 100% speed, all the time. I will return it and buy something else. It’s a pity, because it fits so perfectly into the case from this brand Mesh 5 P. S. After reporting an issue with the AIO in my Geometric Future case, their support team immediately reached out and provided me with a new 420mm cooling system. I replaced the radiator for the third time, and now the system runs quietly and flawlessly. I am truly impressed by Geometric Future’s customer support — the company shows real care and dedication to both their products and their customers. As a gesture of appreciation for the effort I put into replacing the radiators, they even sent me a nice bonus gift. I couldn’t be happier that, while building my first PC, I chose Geometric Future components. Excellent service, excellent product. Keep up the great work!

reviews.author: W. Piorun

reviews.title: Staggering Performance
reviews.comment: I run an i7-4790k, which is notorious for running hot. To test it, I ran a benchmark before and after installing the Thermalright cooler. Before installation, the temps were around 98°c, but after the temps never broke 65°c. I was slightly skeptical when ordering due to the low price and unfamiliar brand, but the performance is truly incredible, and I cannot recommend it enough. It came with fitting brackets for a number of different sockets, including my LGA 1150, and even had TF7 thermal paste, which was a more than welcome surprise. Installation was genuinely easier than the OEM Intel heat sink, though you will need access to the back of your motherboard, so if you don't have an detachable back panel, be prepared to pull out the whole board. It fit perfectly in my case which I assume is around average size, leaving about 2cm or so clearance from the side panel once put back on. If you have a thinner form factor case, I'd check to make sure it'll fit, but it should fit the vast majority of full size cases. I paired it with a three pack of Thermalright case fans, and they've definitely made a lifelong customer out of me. Installation was a breeze, airflow is streamlined and great, each fan had connectors for daisey chaining if you're low on motherboard connection ports, and it runs like a charm. TLDR: Well worth the money. Dropped over 30°c off of my full throttle CPU performance temps, and is a fraction of the price of comparable competition
reviews.author: Joseph

reviews.title: Absolutely perfect PC upgrade
reviews.comment: The Thermalright Peerless Assassin 120 SE ARGB is easily one of the best CPU coolers I’ve ever used — and that’s saying a lot after years of building and upgrading PCs. It’s rare to find something that combines top-tier cooling performance, silent operation, and clean aesthetics all in one package, but this cooler nails it perfectly. Right out of the box, you can tell it’s built with quality in mind. The dual-tower heatsink design is solid, the fins are dense and well-machined, and the included fans feel premium. Everything about it screams durability — no cheap plastics or wobbly mounts here. It’s a heavy-duty, well-engineered piece of hardware that gives off that “premium” feel from the moment you hold it. Installation was surprisingly simple for a dual-tower cooler. The mounting system is straightforward, the instructions are clear, and the included hardware feels secure. It fit perfectly on my motherboard without blocking any RAM slots, which is a big plus for a cooler this size. Performance-wise, it’s phenomenal. I paired it with a Ryzen 9 5900X, and it keeps temperatures impressively low even under heavy gaming and streaming loads. The fans are whisper-quiet — even when they ramp up — and the ARGB lighting looks incredible once powered on. The lighting isn’t overly flashy; it’s clean, soft, and gives off that professional glow that makes your setup look like a studio rig. If you want to see this exact cooler in action during live streams, check out SassieJoXO on TikTok and Twitch — her system runs this same cooler paired with a Ryzen 9 5900X, and the stability and cooling performance speak for themselves. The CPU stays cool, the stream runs flawlessly, and the ARGB lighting adds a subtle but beautiful touch to the background. Thermalright really outdid themselves with this one. It easily rivals much more expensive coolers on the market in both cooling efficiency and noise levels. For anyone running a powerful processor and wanting a balance between top performance, silent cooling, and clean aesthetics, this is the one to get. An absolute 10/10 product — heavy-duty, silent, and stunning in every way. Highly recommend.
reviews.author: Cale Calfy

reviews.title: Great cooler, but prepare yourself for the installation.
reviews.comment: Let's start with the positive. This cooler is awesome. It keeps temperatures way down and is quiet in the process.  You can purchase it with confidence, though I would advise getting a separate tube of thermal paste, as the tube that came with this cooler was empty and dried out. Installation is an ordeal all its own.  It's a beast size wise.  In addition to making sure it will fit in your case, you need to also be aware that once it's installed, it's going to be a pain in the neck to access just about anything else on your motherboard.  So, if you are upgrading several items on your PC, save this for the very last thing you do.  If you're building new from the ground up, get this installed and connected before you put the motherboard in the case. Another note:  if you're upgrading from another cooler and doing so in the case, first of all, lots of luck. You're going to need it along with a bucketful of patience and probably a third hand, preferably with very skinny fingers.  Be sure to connect the Y-adapter that connects your motherboard to the two fans before you install the cooler itself. Getting to the plug after the fact, particularly if you're working with an mATX motherboard, is going to be frustratingly difficult. But, once you've got it in, it will definitely be worth the time invested in the installation. It really is an amazing product, and I'm very impressed with it.
reviews.author: Brian C. Farmer

reviews.title: Works great with 9800X3D
reviews.comment: Whether you go air or liquid cooling really depends on the power draw of your CPU, as well as the type of case you have. That said, for the 9800X3D in particular, this cooler does very well, so long as your case airflow is also good. This is a great option for full-tower builds in pure function sense, or if you like the peace-of-mind that air coolers provide in that they do not have any real risk of failure. If you have a 9800X3D, get this instead of the more expensive AIO coolers. It'll last longer, isn't particularly loud, and is much more affordable. Cooling performance under load for me, with an antec flux pro case, is about 65-70C tops, which is well under the maximum safe temps for a 9800X3D. Being an air cooler, it will require a more spacious case, and installation might be somewhat tricky, but it does the job with no frills, no unnecessary bells and whistles, and no ridiculously inflated price tag. If you're like me and prefer function over form in all ways, this cooler will serve you well should your CPU pair well with it. For more power-hungry CPU's, an AIO might be a better option, but this and the 9800X3D are like a horse and carriage.
reviews.author: Geoffery C Carter

reviews.title: Aligning the screws for mounting is annoying. Similar to 360mm but worse temp spikes.
reviews.comment: This is an impressive air cooler and it performs similarly to my EK 360mm aio but the temperature spikes are higher. The reason I switched is because I was intrigued by the longevity of air cooling where water cooling has some risks and I saw that this air cooler performed similarly in online reviews. My cpu is a 13900K with hyperthreading turned off and undervolted with 0.36 ac_ll and 0.98 dc_ll on a Z690-E. I am using PTM7950 for thermal interface material and using Noctua industrial 120mm 3000rpm fans instead of the ones included. Idle runs from ~33-55c and gaming at ~100-150w is ~55-77c. Full load for prime95 small fft is thermal throttling at 253w which is disappointing. My 360mm idled at ~29-52c and gamed at ~59-69c and full load of prime95 small fft would run from ~80-85c at 253w. The 253w performance is disappointing since I saw online that the Thermalright PS120SE would not thermal throttle at 253w. I am also disappointed by the temperature spikes being way higher. The installation was simple on paper which was to attach the plastic backplate which thankfully had glue pads and then put plastic spacers and finally the lga 1700 brackets with the pointed ends inwards and then the screws. Then came the heatsink which needed to be aligned with the screws and it was impossible to tell if it was perfectly aligned since vision is obstructed and there is NO haptic feedback to determine if the screw is over the threads meaning you need to lift up and move around the heatsink until it seems like it might be aligned smearing thermal paste everywhere. Then tighten the heatsink screws down and attach the fans with the metal clips. Overall the temps seem similar to a 360mm in idle and gaming but for 253w workloads I was misinformed by online reviews and am left disappointed since I hoped it would be about ~85c and not thermal throttling. I also expected better in other workloads because online reviews say 60c for 150w but I am seeing 77c spikes at 145w. The installation also needs to be improved since guessing if the screws are aligned is messy and risky. I also have to give Thermalright praise for allowing this to work with the Z690-E which has a notorious vrm heatsink design flaw and makes it incompatible with a lot of air coolers but Thermalright was able to make this compatible with my motherboard which is impressive.

reviews.author: Nicole Velez

reviews.title: Amazing product
reviews.comment:
I wish I could rate this cooler higher than 5 stars.
I upgraded from the (still excellent) Arctic Freezer 4U air cooler because my use case changed to  require a liquid cooled solution. After searching through frankly overpriced options ($600+), I found this model. Even at full retail, this product is an absolute steal.
I am using the AIO with an AMD EPYC 7F52 (240W TDP), utilizing the seamless fit of the Threadripper (sTRX4) bracket on the SP3 socket.
The performance is phenomenal: At idle, the temperature sits between 16C – 19 C (though, room  ambient was around that, so you can expect near ambient room temperatures on the cpu under normal usage ).
Curious, I ran Prime95 to pull the full 240W.
The CPU would not exceed 48C.
To call this product overkill is an understatement. It cools so effectively that the air pushed out by the fans is cold enough to turn your fingers stiff, thankfully computers are far  more cold tolerant than my hand.
On top of the raw performance, the build quality is like a tank, and the installation took barely 10 minutes thanks to the clear instructions.
I highly recommend this product to anyone. Whether you're cooling an ordinary gaming CPU or a high-wattage server/workstation chip, this cooler can handle it, with included mounting brackets for both use cases.
Buy this, put it on your CPU, and it will likely never feel what anything higher than 50C feels like again.

reviews.title: Excellent Cooling Performance with Very Low Noise
reviews.comment:
I installed the be quiet! Pure Rock Pro 3 LX on a mid-range Intel build and was immediately impressed by the overall build quality. The heatsink feels solid, the mounting hardware is well organized, and installation was straightforward following the included instructions.
Cooling performance has been very consistent. Under gaming and stress testing, temperatures remained stable without sudden spikes. The dual-fan setup moves air efficiently while keeping noise levels extremely low — even under load, the system stays noticeably quieter compared to stock coolers.
Clearance was reasonable in a standard ATX case, though as with any larger air cooler, it’s important to check RAM height and case compatibility before installing.
For anyone looking for strong air cooling performance without moving to liquid cooling, this is a dependable option that balances thermals, noise, and build quality very well.

reviews.title: It's my go-to CPU cooler!
reviews.comment: Any time I do a build, I always include the be quiet! Pure Rock Slim 2. It's silent, cools very well no matter what CPU I have, and it's simple to install. It comes with all the mounting hardware I need, and the thermal paste is pre-applied, so I don't have to worry if I applied too much or too little. Also, the price is very reasonable.

reviews.title: Overkill but worth it!  Much quieter than stock.
reviews.comment:
Used on an AM4 3800X.
Stress test CPU for an hour. Before and after change.
84 degrees before. 72 degrees after.
This did have pre-installed thermal paste. But the plastic protecting it was broken into pieces all over paste.
The installed paste is conductive and supposed to do superior job at cooling compared to MX-7 paste.
I'm not upset about paste.  The MX-7 does a great job.
