reviews.author: Jerry

reviews.title: Solved a difficult ITX-mini desktop heat problem.
reviews.comment:
I have an ITX-Mini industrial type all-in one ultra-slim open air mesh frame chassis & motherboard with an i7-4790S cpu, that has been a beast to tame workload heat, in this smallest of form-factor chassis, in an open to the elements temperature environment, and much to much dismay, and satisfaction, the Be Quite! Pure Rock LP finally solved my CPU heat throttling problems.
The original OEM installed CPU cooler was essentially the basic original Intel aluminum lug & fin, topped with a fan, reference CPU cooler, but cut down to very low 37+mm profile to fit in an ultra-slim desktop chassis.
Searching for better replacements I found the Noctua NH-L9i cooler was a few mm's tool tall to fit in the chassis, and that it had height tolerances problems in the CPU clearance zone underneath the CPU cooler.
An ARCTIC Alpine 12 LP did fit the clearance issues, and had lower noise, and power use; however still being based on an aluminum lug & fin design, (no heat pipes), still was not able to keep up with sustained temperatures, under even moderate loads.
When Be Quite announced their new LP cooler and that it was a copper heat pipe design, fit into the most minimal/maximal dimensions limits allowed for CPU cooler tolerance zones, and could tame even newer generation CPU's, I was skeptical.  But as a still last ditch resort to keep a workhorse computer thermally tamed, I decided to purchase one, give a try, with the clearance issues, see if I could even get it installed, and if it could improve on the Alpine LP.
Mission successful !!!
The install was razor shave close cut; not even micro-micrometers to spare in clearance tolerance all the way around, after mounting; from the top of the fan just barely touching the chassis cover, and with the CPU cold plate fit and around & underneath the cooler; including the cooler and mounting bracket just barely fit over a row of power capacitors sitting just below the bracket.  The mounting certainly is "flexible" but this turned out to be a benefit, after getting the mounting brackets and screws tightened into place.
The bracket installation wrench provided & needed to tighten the CPU mounting bolts, (not the mounting screws), had some difficulty getting around tight part clearances, that were right up and into the CPU cooler clearance zone, but I was able to work the wrench enough to secure the mounting bolts to the brackets; then tighten the mounting screws.
After turning the system back on, immediately I noticed a 10-20 deg F. reduction, as compared to typical temps with the Alpine LP.  And even with now spring summer temperatures coming on, and the ability to cool the cpu is being impacted by increase in ambient air temps, the Be Quit! LP has continued to maintain the heat dissipation, through all load testing; most notably that CPU is staying below throttle temperatures where; the OEM installed could never do, and Alpine LP could barely keep up with!
Additionally noticed is that the noise level was way down, even at full RPM the Be Quit! Any fan noise had a slight low hum winy noise, but only noticeable at maximum RPM.
Overall, this CPU cooler solved a long and ongoing cooling problem in a very minimalist chassis install, and it does it with no no high speed fans, or related added noise.

reviews.title: One and done
reviews.comment:
One issue after another. I wanted the cooler to work since it had the stealth pump tubes.
The first issue was getting the fans and pump to work with my MSI motherboard. Due to the power draw and fan RGB, the motherboard may not provide enough power to run the system properly. A SATA daisy-chain plug was included in the box, but that did not allow me to control the pump or fans. I had to purchase the USB controller separately for that.
Second, the L-Connect software is far behind the curve. Between the downloading, firmware updates, and multiple media downloads required, the AIO is nowhere close to plug-and-play. I had to use multiple websites and do research just to get the system running.
Third, after everything, I finally got the system running and started testing. I noticed temperatures fluctuating severely. I re-pasted the system twice and eventually realized the CPU mounting bracket was not sitting flush. After doing some research, I found that Lian Li may have sent out AMD thumb screws with improper tolerances.
This was my first Lian Li product, and it will most likely be my last.
reviews.author: Mcginnis

reviews.title: Good, But Could Have Been Great
reviews.comment:
My Old AIO was loosing performance as it was aging and the water was evaporated enough where you can hear it sloshing around very freely within the radiator so it was time to get a new one.  I like the idea of the Hydroshift with it's minimalistic design with no tubes draping across the inside of the case so I decided to give it a try.
Pros:
* Tubes/Wiring - The best thing  about the Hydroshift series is that the tubes are mostly hidden behind the radiator, so a minimum is visible going from the block/pump to where it "appears" to disappear towards the top of the case.  What's even better is that the wiring is also ran along the tubes so there are no visible wires going from the block which make a very clean look.  Also you can adjust the tubes in the back of the radiator so that they go straight up from your CPU instead of in an angle for an even cleaner look.  Another plus is that there are only 3 cables going out from the radiator, 2 PWM cables and a single cable going out to the USB header, no controller box is a plus in my book.
* Fans - For an extra $20 for the CL version compared to the fan-less this is a no brainer in my opinion.  You're basically getting 3 fans that normally cost about $20+ for 1, so you're getting 2 for free when you get the bundle.  If you don't use them you can sell them and get extra money back so that's a win in my book.  The other nice thing about going with one of the fanned versions is that all the cables for the fans are completely hidden inside of a compartment at the end of the radiator.
* Screen - This is also a good implementation as the screen as it is only connected via some pogo pins on the block, no wires at all.  My Asus one had 2 wires coming out from the screen so while you could take off the screen easily there were wires going to the USB header and the controller box so it would just half to hang if I had to do any maintenance.  This fixed the greatest gripe about the screen in comparison to my old one.  This is also an IPS display so the viewing angles are much better.
Cons:
* Radiator - I don't know the reason but the radiator seems to be a downgrade from the previous generation, I'm guessing it might have to do with the improved pump.  The previous generation was 27mm thick while this one is only 24mm, would be nice if it was the same or upgraded to 30mm for improved performance.
* Cables - While it is nice that it only has 3 cables, there is one downside to it being that if it doesn't get a certain amount of power then the Lian Li L-Connect software won't see the AIO.  The solution they give you is a PWM splitter hooked up to a SATA port (which I needed to use for my setup).  For this it can be a bit confusing as the instructions don't make it clear as to which of the PWM cables will do the job, basically you will need to hook up the connector with 4 wires to the CPU header on your motherboard and the one with 2 cables to they adapter.  I think a better solution would just to have a dedicated SATA power cable coming out as well with the other cables.
* Lighting - While the lighting works good, unfortunately at the time of this review there isn't a way to have the AIO sync with your motherboards lighting, you have to use Lian Li's software.  While there is a  MB Lighting Sync switch in the Quick/Sync Lighting tab it has no effect on the AIO nor the fans.
* No Fill Port - Would have been a nice addition so extend the life of the AIO for when the water evaporates.
* No VRM Cooling Fan - Your VRMs can get hot so when you have an air cooler it is designed to blow air down onto the VRMs but for AIO there is nothing there to give them that extra air.  While not necessary for the overall functionality it a good feature to add a down firing fan on the pump to help the VRMs a bit.
While not perfect this overall is a very good AIO.  Hopefully they will make improvements on the next iteration of the AIO and to the software adding sync support, but overall I'm happy with my purchase and would recommend.
reviews.author: Brian

reviews.title: Bang for your buck
reviews.comment: Nice air cooler! Easy to install and mount on your motherboard. Good price to value ratio. I am satisfied with the size and quality of the cooler. The design is nice and simple. I like the ascent design. I have two of these in separate PC towers and they have kept my rigs cool.
reviews.author: RJ

reviews.title: Amazing Temps
reviews.comment: A really good cooler that cools my LGA 1700 13700k phenomenally despite it being an air tower. Works great and installation is really straight forward, nothing out of the ordinary here. Outperformed my previous thermal right peerless assassin by about 4 degrees Celsius, but this one looks much better in the case. Fits in my dan a3 case by Lian li even with moving the front fan up a bit for RAM clearance. Would highly recommend this case. Great value for money and gives thermal right a run for its money.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: its the one thing keeping my computer from going nuclear
reviews.comment: bought this for my computer, it wasn't terribly overheating but i needed an upgrade from the stealth cooler i bought when i first built the computer so i bought this thing, money well spent it turns out. it's got a bit of noise but my case fans drown out what little noise this gives off boy at full blast it's got a bit of a deep hum to it, which is pretty good sounds. the installation was easy, it's not toddler level intuitive, you might have to read the manual but if you know what you are doing, it's a pretty easy install, even with tall ram, just move one of the fans around. you'll find a good fit if you have tall ram if you experiment a little. after installing, my cpu was... well it would still burn me but in cpu world, it's a lil chilly. my cpu overheated a lot less now, it overheated so little i was able to sneak in a little overclocking on the side and squeeze more performance out. overall a great upgrade for a computer starting out with a stealth cooler if you want a performance boost on the side too. if not, it might keep your cpu cool enough to extend it's life a good amount.
reviews.author: M1SSINGNOwO

reviews.title: Aesthetically Pleasing with Great Performance
reviews.comment: As soon as I seen the looks of this cooler, I knew it was the one I have been looking for. Upon opening the box, however, I was immediately worried about the quality. The fins feel really fragile, and the black coating can easily be scratched if you are not careful, which could instantly ruin some of the looks you are paying the extra $10 for (It is $30 for the original one and $40 for this one). The fin covers where it has the design and 'FROZN' logo is also extremely cheap feeling as it is thin plastic. The cooler was pretty easy to install. Despite the feelings of cheap materials, this cooler is extremely slick to look at. If you want a 'Blacked Out' build, I recommend this cooler. I am thinking about dropping it into a white case just to make my hardware "pop" even more. The performance is also actually really great too. I'm only using this on a 5600x, but it dropped my gaming temps from around 84c down to 62c. I was only using a Wraith Prism before I bought this cooler, and I am overall satisfied. The fans that came with this cooler feel solid overall and stay relatively quiet until higher temps, but I can't hear it over my headset while gaming. No reverb or bad bearings as of yet. $40 feels a little much for how cheap some of it feels, but it only feels cheap and doesn't look cheap. I suppose since the performance is great it is worth that price as it is a competitive price with similarly designed dual tower coolers. (In case it could be important and if anyone is wondering, I am using a 5600x paired with a RX 6700 XT at 1440p. Around 100 frames in demanding games. My PC case doesn't have the best airflow either so performance might vary for you if you bought this cooler. I would recommend it.)
reviews.author: Jeff

reviews.title: Excellent Air Cooler for sub-$40 (120mm x 27mm Fans)
reviews.comment: Very nice air cooler for the money, has 27mm Fans for more efficient air flow.
reviews.author: MICHAEL STARUSZKIEWICZ

reviews.title: Great value for money, but get some extra thermal paste beforehand
reviews.comment: Hands down one of the best affordable low-profile coolers out there. Quiet and effective, does a great job with my i5-12600K. Installation steps are pretty trivial, and I didn't have any RAM clearance issues on MSI PRO-B760M-P-DDR4 motherboard. I will complain about the thermal compound though. Maybe I got an "old stock" item or something, but the thermal paste I got was much closer to a "play-doh" than a "paste". It would form blobs/balls and wouldn't spread out on the CPU. Thankfully I had some leftover MX-4 from *six years ago* that still wasn't dried out, so I used that instead. I could deduct one star for that, but honestly it's a minor one-time inconvenience for something that's going to stay in service for many years.
reviews.author: Szymon

reviews.title: Amazed by how well this works
reviews.comment: I’m running this on a AMD Ryzen 7 7700X. I’ve had no issues with temperatures. I have been able to keep my fans quiet which is a huge plus. The mounting process was painless.
reviews.author: Bryant

reviews.title: Great, low profile cooler
reviews.comment: Reliability keeps my 9600x under 70° under load. Hovers around 50° in while gaming and even less in everyday tasks. Great for such a small cooler.
reviews.author: Sam Hughes

reviews.title: good for the price
reviews.comment: Even though this is the top-performing low profile cooler in its size class, I would strongly recommend undervolting your CPU if you're on AMD. Regardless, you should cap the fan to a max of ~1500RPM. Once all is said and done, this is a pretty good cooler. It cooled my 7700X in a Fractal Terra with no problems. Note for builders in cases with adjustable spines: make sure there's an air gap between the fan and your side panel to reduce turbulence.
reviews.author: Alden

reviews.title: Works well for AM4 Ryzen 5 CPUs
reviews.comment: Bought this to cool a Ryzen 5600 in an ITX case that doesn't have a lot of room for a cooler. It doesn't have a lot of airflow either, but that hasn't hindered its ability to cool the CPU.  Granted, Ryzen 5's aren't known for being overheating monsters, but mine usually stays in the 70's unless under very heavy load, when it can creep into the low 80's briefly. I have never seen it throttle. The fan is pretty quiet as well.  Installation is about as easy as any cooler (except for maybe the stock AMD cooler) can be.  Just like with 90% of heatsinks and fans, you have to remove the brackets that come on your motherboard and replace them with the ones that come with this. After that, it's just two screws and clip on the fan and you're set.  Thermalright has a reputation for excellent price to performance, and this is no exception. I have since bought another Thermalright air cooler for a micro ATX build and that one is also performing better than expectations.
reviews.author: Tmach

reviews.title: Nice budget cooler! Make sure to calibrate fans.
reviews.comment:
Was a little confused after installing it, as I seemed to be getting the same temps on my i7-4790 as I did with my stock Intel Delta cooler. But, I soon realized it was using the same fan curve my motherboard had dialed in for it. After going into ASUS AI 3 software and running the automated fan tuning, then adjusting my fan curve to 10% at 35°C, 50% at 48°C, and 100% at 68°C my temps are several degrees lower across the board and much more stable. Mind you, I have a very old custom Apevia X-Sniper G case which only allows for 3 120mm case fans. One bottom front intake, one side intake affixed to the acrylic side panel, and one rear exhaust. With only 2 of those useable with the cooler installed due to it's height. Which I think adds to the quality of this cooler.
I had to remove my side intake fan due to the cooler's size interfering with it, and tape off the inlet holes to ensure proper airflow and avoid negative pressure. I chose this cooler because it is just a bit shorter than the SE-224-XT, which has very good reviews, to ensure it would fit my case. So it's a great option for those with a minimum clearance of 255mm. Oh! Another important aspect is that I bought an additional matching ID-COOLING AF-125-K fan to utilize a push-pull config on this cooler also. The fan included doesn't have a PWM daisy chain connector, but the AF-125-K does so you can hook them together and they become controllable as a pair via 4-pin motherboard fan connector. Though, according to testing with other coolers, push-pull vs pull config only affects temps by 1-3°C in most cases. I also have 5.25" and 3.5" drive bays fixed to my case which sit flush and directly above my front 120mm intake fan. So my case is a bit crowded and has much less capability for airflow than modern cases.
Packaging is very nice inside and out. Manual contents are decent. I easily figured out how to assemble and install it. Though there was an LGA 115X descriptor missing on the first page, it is mentioned elsewhere in the guide. Fan is superb quality, but missing a daisy chain connector. Includes 4 fan mounting brackets to utilize a push-pull config with an additional fan later, and should be compatible with any 120mm fan of typical thickness. My mounting brackets had some paint chipped off of them leaving a rough surface, but not worried about that.
The 4 copper heatpipes are sandwiched between what I assume is brushed aluminum. A flat surface and mirror finish. One thing that did catch my eye is that there are a few very small gaps on the edges between the copper and aluminum on the bottom, which tends to catch q-tip fuzz while going to clean it, or could trap residual thermal paste after applying it. But, as far as I know and can tell this doesn't affect the temperature threshold. Though it is a bit concerning that old paste could get dried up and trapped in there.
All in all, for the overall quality, aesthetic appeal of the design, ease of installation, and thermal results, I am very happy with this purchase. Where I was close to overheating or receiving temps around 75°C while gaming with a stock Intel Delta cooler, now my temps stay mostly under 70°C even while playing GTAV or RDR2. GTAV saw the largest thermal drop - where it was reaching 80°C it now stays under 65°C even while zooming around in a vehicle.
I would highly recommend this cooler for quite possibly the cheapest way to get temps under control via air cooling. Not to mention how versatile it is between multiple generations of AMD and Intel sockets. And with it being just a bit shorter than most standing air coolers, it's sure to fit in almost any ATX/mATX case - even if you're like me and still rocking a case from the mid-2000s.
reviews.author: Terrapin

reviews.title: Great value, looks clean, and noticeably cooler running 5600x, happy customer!
reviews.comment:
Perfect for my needs! It changed my cpu temperature under load noticeably. Not sure why I've used my stock cooler for so long.
Background: I have a 5600x with the stock stealth cooler (non-rgb version). I tested it with the side panel off. It could be the fact that I need to replace the thermal paste after a few years of use, but after looking at my temps - it has been reaching the high 80's and even saw it reach a max of 90c while gaming, running discord, and playing music. The fans were all running at 100% speed and cpu was not overclocked. My idle at the lowest was about 41-42c. I didn't want to deal with throttling. This was not ideal and needed to upgrade.
Being a lower TDP (65watt) 6-core processor, it does not require the "best" cooler. I wanted something that would make a noticeable impact on temperature, has copper for conductivity, not break the bank, and look okay enough to look nice with my all black build.
With the same settings, 23-25c ambient temperature, I had a huge improvement with this single fan Frozn 410 cooler. I maxed out to 62-65c while gaming and running the same applications in the background. My idle dropped to about 34c at its lowest.
I tried placing a second fan in a push pull config since I had one laying around just for kicks. It only dropped 2-3c for those that were considering the dual fan set up. I thought about getting the dual fan setup, but glad I didn't as it doesn't make much of a difference for my cpu. This test also justifies why I didn’t go for an all-in-one liquid cooler. The price comparison isn’t worth the small decrease in temps for this cpu.
The installation process was smooth as well. I didn't have parts that were bent, screws that didn't turn properly, or were too short. I plugged it in and now I have peace of mind that my computer won't shut off while taking losses in my games. The fan runs quiet and will obviously be a little bit louder, but not obnoxiously loud. I'm sure there are slightly cheaper options that will have similar results, but for what I needed, this was a win.
reviews.author: Doctorworks

reviews.title: Affordable, sleek, and dead silent
reviews.comment:
I took a chance on a brand I've never heard of, and holy smokes: they don't disappoint.
Randomly passed by this model on youtube 30 minutes after the video was posted, and decided to buy it for my new build.
The fan is amazing, can move some serious air with Noctua-level silence.
The heatsink's build quality and mounting hardware (and instructions) are some of the best I've ever had.
Playing games like Cyberpunk 2077 and Armored Core VI on max, and the temps don't go over ~45C.
For as little as this costs, I'm blown away by the quality. I'm buying the three pack of the fans they have, too.
reviews.author: Actual Reviewer

reviews.title: Great CPU Cooler
reviews.comment: I installed this cooler to replace the stock Intel cooler when I upgraded my CPU.  So far it's keeping up with an Intel core i9 9900 just fine! The install was easy since I already had the motherboard removed. The cooler comes with basic instructions and a set of brackets that are compatible with a variety of CPU sockets. The kit also included some thermal paste.
reviews.author: John Tanner

reviews.title: A mighty cooler.
reviews.comment:
Incase anyone is wondering, this cooler will cool and keep a 10600k at around 33-35 at idle, and the highest I've seen it reach in cinebench is 77 to 80.
SUPER QUITE OPERATION.
I do not overclock but my i5 was running with turbo.
Some say it won't work but it 100% will. Cools better then the be-quite rock 3  tower cooler I had installed before. The 4 points of contact for the mounting surface is a plus as well. Looks great with blackout builds. Does sits pretty close if not flush against your ram if your running 4 sticks.
reviews.author: William

reviews.title: AMAZING over stock cooler but instalation is not easy
reviews.comment:
I bought the black low profile. This cooler is heaps better than the stock AMD stealth cooler. Smaller all around works way better. Installing it is not easy tho. If your motherboard is already mounted and your system is put together get ready to take everything apart it is not just drop in and screw down. If your building a new pc Installing this isn't that bad tbh but its def not the easiest. Also directions are trash.
My cpu is an amd ryzen 5 5500 running a home server. I had the stock cooler installed with idle temps sitting at around 43 to 45 and running cinebench my cpu would thermal throttle.
With this coller I dropped my idle temp to 34 to 36 and running cinebench never got over 73 c. So a massive massive improvement over stock.
Honestly if your building out a new pc or home lab with an older cpu this cooler (i got the black one) Honestly is worth it for the 20$. That and Honestly its no louder than the stock amd cooler and runs at a higher rpm under load. My hd cooler fan is louder than this thing running at full speed and that's a  21$ noctua fan.
reviews.author: greg petroski

reviews.title: The copper design really catches the eye—10/10.
reviews.comment: It's heavy for its size. I struggled to assemble it, but that was my own fault for being stubborn and not checking the instructions. It's a good cooler and maintains better temperatures than my stock heatsink.
reviews.author: Beto

reviews.title: Cpu cooler
reviews.comment: It works fine if you let the fan at full speed. Then it keeps the cpu nice and cool. I just wished the price was 20 like the others. These do have a weird bracket setup as the 1700 brackets that came installed didn't actually fit my 1700 cpu. I had to use the second largest and that worked perfectly.
reviews.author: Admin

reviews.title: Amazing ITX or Budget Cooler
reviews.comment:
I have used a bunch of Coolers from different size AIO's to many different air Cooler brands and this is honestly one of the best I've come across. I had an ID-Cooling IS-33 before this and was great cooling wise it was so loud I added a noctua fan to reduce noise. After doing so I still wasn't completely satisfied with it so I went with this since it has a bigger fan stack and has clearance for large motherboard IO and it gets the job DONE. I have a 7700x PBO Tuned in this open air build that never goes over 75C and it is really quiet under load opposed to other coolers I've had in the past. Easy to mount, looks fantastic and its audible but not annoying ( Imean it is an open air case after all). Ultimately I recommend this product whole heartedly and I think it is being slept on as it only had a few reviews when I decided to give it a shot.
Since my initial review I swapped out my 7700x for a 9800x3d and this thing still rocks! I have ut overclocked 150mhz to about 5.5ghz and have lower the voltage curve by -15 and this thing keeps it under 70c while playing games like Monster Hunter Wilds at 3440×1440 maxed out or around 80c in THE FINALS. This cooler is definitely for more efficient chips and if you go AM5 always PBO tune the chip but it is seriously an impressive cooler on an open air setup. For a case configuration I could see it adding 5-10c more but still more than cool enough for most modern ryzen chips that are rated to go 95c max.
reviews.author: Zero Cool 170

reviews.title: Small and great cooler
reviews.comment: Keeps my CPU cool enough to function, while being small enough to fit in my small case
reviews.author: Deakin

reviews.title: Keeping my ryzen 7 7700x much cooler than my previous noctua did!
reviews.comment:
I just installed this about 25 minutes ago. It replaced a noctua low-height fan that was failing intermittently after 3 years.
The immediate difference was so drastic compared to the noctua that I thought my sensors were messed up.  Previously the only time I ever saw my 7700X hit temperatures below 40 were when it first started up on a cold morning after being off all night.
Right now it's currently running at 37 degrees while I'm writing this review.
A stress test brought it up to the 95 degree mark and I could barely hear the fan at full speed.
I read lots of reviews about how well it performs which is what made me take the chance on it and I'm not disappointed.  I would like to stress what others have said regarding the instructions for installing it.  They are awful.  You're probably just going to have to figure it out on your own because they're the worst instructions I think I've ever seen for a fan installation.
Also I had to take the fan off and rotate it because it would only clear my motherboard's panel one way.  It only BARELY clears my ram and I was afraid it might have caused issues with my RAM when I was installing it because the heatsink kept bumping into two of the sticks, but everything seems to be working fine.
I'd recommend NOT installing it with the fan already on because it was pretty hard to align the little spring loaded screws with the brackets with the fan covering everything so you can't see.  I'd recommend taking the fan off and installing the heatsink itself, then clip the fan back on afterward.
Other than the horrid instructions everything seems to be better than I expected for such a cheap price.  I'm impressed.  I just hope it lasts longer than the 3 years my noctua lasted.
reviews.author: Brad

reviews.title: Not At All As Advertised
reviews.comment:
First, it won't work with an AM3 CPU.  It only ships with one set of mounting brackets, and they're for AM4/AM5.  I needed this for an FX-8350, and it just doesn't fit.
Second, it's poor quality.  There's zero percent chance this would effectively cool a 150W TDP CPU without tons of airflow.  I have a $10 cooler that has more mass and cools more effectively than this ever would.  And the fan couldn't be any cheaper.
I'm only giving it one star because I can't give it zero stars.  Even with my expectations set low for something off-brand, it failed to even come close.  I couldn't recommend it less.
reviews.author: L. Heidelberger

reviews.title: Good value and fucntions well, installation a slight bit tricky.
reviews.comment: Good value for the price and good fit. It required a bit of moving the cross-braces around so the mounting bolts lined up, but once installed, it sits solid and is not very loud. Keeps a Xeon processor in a generally well-ventilated chassis 30c-40c, well in the lower range of temperature tolerance.
reviews.author: Elteto

reviews.title: A great inexpensive upgrade versus a stock cooler
reviews.comment: I recently purchased an Intel 13400 processor for a new system build. This is a 65W processor so it shouldn't produce a ton a heat, and I'd read that the cooler Intel includes in the box was adequate to the job. Which it was, in the sense that it kept the CPU under thermal limits under heavy loads. But it was still running hotter than I would like, in the 70s (C), and worse, the stock fan was running at 3,200+ RPM to maintain that temperature and it sounded like a leaf blower. This Thermalright Assassin King was about the cheapest upgrade I could find, but it has done wonders versus the stock cooler. Under load I am running 20 deg C cooler, at least, and the fan never gets beyond 1,200 RPM and is barely audible even under stress tests. So, I am very pleased with the results. Besides the fact that I had to disassemble the just-assembled system to install the backplate for this new cooler, which is no one's fault but mine, the installation went smoothly. This cooler is designed for multiple socket configurations so there's a lot of different parts and so on, but everything was clearly labeled and explained. Double-stick tape on the backplate eliminates the problem of trying to hold the backplate while screwing on the standoffs on the other side. One note: the mounting brackets have two sets of holes for attaching to the backplate, but the holes overlap and it's really one slot, and it's easy for the screws to slide to the other end of the slot, so just double check that they are in the right spots for your CPU socket before tightening the screws. I don't know if this design would work as well for much hotter CPUs, overclocking, etc., but if you are in a situation like mine, I can definitely recommend.
reviews.author: V. Anton Spraul

reviews.title: Good cooling for my AMD Ryzen 5 7600X  (updated 10-12-2024)
reviews.comment: It was easy to install , lower cost than most high performance coolers.  I live in a high elevation area, 7,150 Ft (thin air is poor for heat conduction and very low humidity also single digit in winter).  My typical temps are under110 F (43 C).  while surfing of doing office work and while gaming never over 150 F.  I have never even thought of going the water cooling route yet, water and electronics are a very bad mix.  I have read numerous disaster reviews about leaks in the computer cases, it's not worth the risk to me,  Liquids always find a way out - given enough time.  Take your car for example or water faucets air-conditioning, plumbing, etc..  Also over time the water in the AIO cooling system needs to be replaced about every 5 yrs, that sounds like fun.  Update: unit is still running well,  added 2 photos - showing temp and processes using "Ryzen Master - CPU app".  One while surfing the other when producing a 2k .mp4 video (heavy CPU load).  I would still recommend this item, over a year later
reviews.author: SH

reviews.title: Good cooling, budget priced and easy to install
reviews.comment: This is a solid air cooler that's become my go to for budget build.  Good cooling, budget priced and easy to install.
reviews.author: George N. Condoyannis

reviews.title: Great for bench testing systems!
reviews.comment: Needed this to bench test my cpu after bending pins. I have water cooking loops so I can’t fill up and drain as it’s time consuming. This is cheap and makes a perfect bench cooler for testing.
reviews.author: M

reviews.title: Quiet, and cools well.
reviews.comment: It's a big boy for sure.  But it does the job, looks nice, and is decently quiet.  I supervised while my kid (18) installed this on his 5800X.  What an amazing value, can't do better for $20. The thermal paste is really thick compared to other pastes we've used (Arctic, Noctua, Vetroo) a lot of reviews on the paste complain that it is hard to spread, it's Thermalright TF4 if you are wondering.  We just used the "X" method no need to spread it around, it'll get spread plenty when you tighten the heatsink. My only complaint is: installing the AM4 bracket is very fiddly it definitely took 3 hands in the case to get it mounted.  You might have some difficulty if you have a smaller case or are doing this yourself.
reviews.author: Aeta Capella

reviews.title: Have a spare
reviews.comment: It works great for a long time, at least it did in my two Rig's, I have no complaints about this product, it just gave up the ship!
reviews.author: Robert Fennern

reviews.title: Easy setup
reviews.comment: had to change my computer cooling system and had to upgrade to the new Icue link and easy setup
reviews.author: JonT

reviews.title: Excelente producto
reviews.comment: Sin problemas , Excelente producto
reviews.author: Felipe Lira

reviews.title: No regrets!
reviews.comment: At first I had issues with my icue hub, but after reaching out to support I found out that my hub was an older model. Instead of having a usb-c port, it had a micro usb port. I was sent a new model and used the new cable from usb 2.0 mother board header to usb-c on hub and everything works. Sometimes icue is slow to pull up system info on dashboard but otherwise works flawlessly. Currently powering 8 RX120 max fans and 4 rx140 max fans. Also using the corsair icue 4 way signal splitter. Dashboard recognizes and shows info for corsair ram, corsair nvme ssd, all fans, hub itself, and then system info. Icue also automatically detected gigabyte sdk and after accepting it started controlling the rgb on my gigabyte gaming 5080 OC gpu. All in all very impressed with the hub and associated software once it's all set up and working properly. Only complaint is Icue software UI isn't optimized for high dpi screens. I'm on a 65 inch LG C2 running 300% scale.
reviews.author: Griffin Barnett

reviews.title: Overly priced and potential fire hazard
reviews.comment: This is the worst Corsair product I have ever purchased. Overly priced and almost destroyed my newly built system. I purchased the iCue link 140 RGB fan (single) and did not read that it required the system hub to go with the fan. The system hub is REQUIRED. That was not a problem and I purchased the system hub for an additional fifty dollars. Received the system hub and read the online manual which is not provided in the box you have to look this up yourself. The instructions were simple. When I turned on the system the iCue fan didn't power on. Figured time to go into inspection mode, disconnected the power and opened the case. Checked the cables to ensure they were not loose. No power to the fan again. Swapped out the 3 different proprietary link cables that Corsair provided with the fan and system hub. On the fifth boot the system hub had a audible pop and the connector port started smoking. I immediately powered down the system checked the extent of the damage. Luckily only the hub had its port burnt.

reviews.title: Easy AM5 installation and total RAM clearance; top tier air cooler
reviews.comment:
This is a hefty, high-quality cooler, which you can sense right when you take it out of the box. The cooler has six heat pipes and a massive fin stack that is very effective at dissipating heat. There are two fans, one in the front and one embedded in the middle of the fin stack, where it remains hidden.
The cooler easily handled my Ryzen 9 9900X without any issues, keeping temperatures well under the thermal throttle point at full load. In fact, it held the 9900X, which has a 162W maximum power draw (PPT), to under 80C during extended tests with the AIDA AVX stress workloads.
As you can see in my pictures, the cooler comes with everything you need to install it, with the brackets, thermal paste, a screwdriver, and a handy plastic nut driver. There are also well-written instructions. Installation was simple on AM5; you just install the standoffs in the backplate (using the handy included nut driver), install the brackets on top, apply the thermal paste to the chip, and then place the cooler on top. There is a magnetic top plate that you simply pop off, and underneath you'll find two holes for the screwdriver. You extend the screwdriver through the top, tighten down the two fasteners into the brackets, and after snapping the top back on and plugging in the fans, you are done. The fans are connected to a Y-splitter, so you only need one fan header on your motherboard to power both fans.
The cooler looks great once installed, and it performs very well, too. As mentioned, it holds temperatures down to 75C during heavy use. The fans are quiet under low and medium loads; you'll only notice them if you're listening for them. However, it does get a bit louder at full speed, but it shouldn't be distracting inside most PC cases.
The cooler is rather large; it has essentially two cooling towers that are merged into one, but with a fan in the middle. However, it fits perfectly over the socket, leaving room for the GPU and the heat shield on the motherboard. Best of all, this cooler doesn't hang over the RAM slots, so RAM clearance won't be a worry at all.
Overall, this is a great cooler for the price point; you'll be hard-pressed to find a better CPU cooler at this price point.
reviews.author: Jim Tango

reviews.title: Another wonderful cooler from ID Cooling!
reviews.comment:
ID Cooling has been around a while, mostly in China... but, they are well known there.  They have finally made it to the States and I love it!
They are offering some great products at very affordable prices.
This A620 is looks great and does an amazing job of cooling.  My CPU pours out 230w of power on a full Cinebench load, which is not realistic in most cases.  It unfortunately could not hold the CPU back for too long, but it did do quite a good job before getting extremely loud.
I really like how the install works for this, its a very clean looking cooler and would blend in well with a non-RGB stealth build.
The top cover is magnetic and will grant you access to the second fan as well as nicely label holes for the mount.  Also, I appreciate that little "GPU" sign and an arrow, telling you where the GPU should be once installed correctly. Once you are done, you just pop the magnetic cover back on and everything looks super clean!
Installation is very easy and its classic ID Cooling, they use a simplified mounting system for both AMD and Intel and its very easy to get installed and up and running.
One very nice touch was the little plastic nut driver?  It is this small 3-4" plastic tube that can help you screw in and tighten the main bolts on the brackets.  I love this because with many motherboards today they have large VRM heatsinks and sometimes getting your fingers in there is tough.  This made installation so much faster and pain free.
Overall I think ID Cooling has a winner on their hands.  This may not have handled 10min with 230w going, but it will easily cool your CPU for everyday tasks and gaming especially.
reviews.author: PCTA

reviews.title: Beautiful addition to ID's lineup.  Works well.  Almost perfect.
reviews.comment:
This cooler does a lot of things right. Aesthetically, it is very pleasing, especially in a system with black components where RGB isn't the focus.
I love the magnetic outer panel.  Just pull that straight off to access the holes to screw down the cooler.  Unfortunately this panel is prone to finger prints, so wear gloves during assembly.  Otherwise, the overall build quality is very good.
ID-Cooling's design with this model makes installation noticeably easier.  The fans and wiring are already connected and ready to go on this model.  You dont need to clip any of those items into place, so you can save some time and this will absolutely help new builders.
In fact, the only installation steps are installing the stand offs and brackets, adding thermal paste, and then dropping on the pre-assembled CPU Cooler carefully to align the top and bottom mounting screws to the brackets.
I really like this cooler.  It works well, keeps temps down, and runs quiet.
That said, it has some flaws...  The current price point at $50 brings some heavy competition.  I would love to see this closer to the $40 price point.
The top and bottom mounting screws took a little finesse to get them started.  This model might benefit from some attention in that area for the design and/or manufacturing process.
Finally, ID-Cooling continually misses the mark with their thermal paste.  I personally like to see thermal paste with a slightly lower viscosity.  As a builder, I like to stick to paste from Noctua and Cooler Master.

reviews.title: Works so well, I had to slow the fans down.
reviews.comment:
I just upgraded from a 120 mm water cooler to this 240 mm model. For reference, my processor is rated at 125 W. I purposely picked the same brand cooler with the hopes that the mounting would be identical. For my socket, this unit requires the factory mounting bracket that many other coolers, including my original cooler, do not use. It is a simple process to install, if the bracket is already on the motherboard. Otherwise, you have to find one. Luckily, they are under $10 to replace, if missing.
Performance wise, I had my old cooler from the factory constantly running at 100% fan speeds to maintain decent temps. This new cooler is so efficient that I had to reduce the fan speeds to keep the temps above ambient levels. (Can’t drop below ambient in Florida unless I want a wet processor.) At constant 100% fans, this new cooler dropped my temps to below 20° C. With the motherboard now in control and adjusting the fan speed, I am about 30° C at idle and peak in the 40’s with moderate activity. This is about a 10° C drop from my old cooler for idle temps. I am not a gamer so I rarely push the processor too hard. Video production is the main thing stressing the system and that only happens in bursts.
Based on some other reviews, I used a name brand thermal paste instead of what came with the cooler. I don’t know how much that changes things. The setup works great so I like it. Also, important to note that the factory paste originally installed was still extremely wet so it had not dried out. For whatever reason, the old setup was just not keeping up with the heat being generated.
If I am hearing the pieces correctly, the fans are extremely quiet and I hear a little bit of pump noise. Since I am always wearing headphones, I don’t hear anything with them on.
The RGB system works, but seems to have extremely limited options. I wanted a decent, budget cooler, more than lights, so I am happy with the product.

reviews.title: The Cooler is a Significant Improvement over the OEM CPU fan and easy to install
reviews.comment:
Personal Experience:
After my wife made a comment on how loud the OEM CPU fan was for my desktop I decided it was time to get a liquid cooled replacement.  I wanted something that would not only be quieter but keep my CPU cooler.  Read some reviews and I was between the 120mm and 240mm radiator, I settled on the 240mm radiator because my case had the space and for the price it was a good deal.  Install of the cooler is relatively easy if you have experience building computers or swapping out components and your case has room to accommodate the radiator and cooling tubes.  My setup uses an AMD chipset but the cooler accommodates both AMD and Intel chipsets; the directions are easy to follow on how to install for either style.  Make sure you clear cables out of your way with Zip ties and ensure that everything fits before you bolt/strap it down.  If you are upgrading your existing CPU Fan/Cooler I would suggest purchasing good thermal paste remover so you can start with a clean surface.  Overall it took me about 45 minutes to remove the old fan, clean off the thermal paste, layout the new Cooler setup then bolt everything down/apply new thermal paste.  The lights on the cooler are a nice touch.  All in all I was pleased with CPU cooler upgrade from install to performance.
Recommend:
Yes
Pros:
Far quieter than the OEM fan that came with the CPU
Easy to install in a large case
Came with all the mounting equipment you would need
Lights are a nice touch to customize your setup
Works with both AMD and Intel chip sets (AMD on my setup)
Cons:
Will not fit in a smaller case (did not affect me but be aware)
Installation Suggestions:
If you are upgrading get thermal paste remover and be generous when cleaning the CPU
Layout everything before you tighten everything down; I had to move the radiator slightly to get everything to fit nicely
Read the directions on which way to install the fans the first time (I have installed fans backwards before and it sucks)

reviews.title: A very pleasant surprise!
reviews.comment:
So my use case for this is in a mATX home server with an 8th gen i7-8700k, 32GB of RAM, NVIDIA Quadro P1000 GPU and approx 100TB of storage. The case is a Fractal Meshify 2 Nano. I have 3x 3.5" drives internally, as well as 2x 2TB M.2 SSDs (Windows 11 Pro on one, and mirror backup of the OS on the other). This server is primarily used for data backups, Plex Media Server and also does a lot of the grunt work for encoding blu-rays to MKV files via Handbrake. The CPU barely ever needs to work hard, and my existing cooler was a well trusted and heavily used 10 year old Coolermaster Hyper 212 cooler. It's an exceptional air cooler. However, as you can see in the original installation the flaw in the plan. It blows warm CPU heat onto one of the 24TB Seagate Drives. I actually had to RMA the previous drive in that location, likely due to heat. Despite the cool temps inside the case, the blowing of warm air directly onto it probably did it no favours.
Enter, a replacement AIO! There is no longer warm air onto the drive at all. I have the radiator front mounted, and venting out of the front panel. This is opposite to how most of my builds are since I typically pull air in from the front and out via the rear. Well, this different layout makes sense in this configuration. I will be adding a 120mm intake fan in what little free space is above the CPU.
Installation was stupidly easy. I just picked the Intel parts, (Yes, it doesn't say on the listing but it WILL fit a LGA 1151) and then mounted the back plate. I then had to shuffle the top mounted HDD back an inch or two, and finagle the front radiator into place without the fans (micro ATX case, so tight space). Once I had it set just right, I pre-wired the fans and  routed their cables and then secured them to the radiator. I reattached the vent panel on the bottom of this particular case for maximum airflow efficiency. Once I connected the 4 pin fan header and 4 pin water pump header, I installed the pump/block itself. I was pleasantly surprised to find that the fan headers are actually still accessible after mounting the pump. These were completely blocked off by the old air cooler.
I fired it up, ran some bench testing to verify it was working - as well as see what noise level was like. It's actually pleasantly quiet! Some pumps have a whine, but this one does not. I have used a Corsair Capellix H150i in my gaming build for several years so this is my only AIO to compare with - I have so far been impressed. Just 15c after a reboot from doing stress tests, temps barely kicked up to 19-21c during testing. This is a big improvement over the air cooler. At this price point, you cannot go wrong. Great price, great fit, great compatability. I am happy.

reviews.title: Works with my Mac Studio
reviews.comment: I wanted a dual display setup for my Mac Studio. I was able to get two beautiful 4k displays for less than I could get 1 of some other brands. Some people feel that if you are going to pay so much for a computer you need to go ahead and also pay top dollar for monitors. I don't disagree with that mindset, but I also think it's important to stay within your budget, lol. These screens checked all the boxes for me. They connect directly from the Mac using thunderbolt to display port cables. The screens look great. The colors a nice and vibrant and the image is sharp. I have edited photos and video with them and paired with the Mac Studio they are a major upgrade from my old set up. I went back and watched some videos I edited some time ago and I feel like I was seeing my videos for the first time. The only compromise has been that I can't control the screen brightness from the computer or keyboard. This brings up the one negative I have had from the monitors is that the menu system is not the best. IF you don't care about having an OLED display but want a great 4k monitor, I definitely recommend these.
reviews.author: Faith

reviews.title: I highly recommend upgrading to 4k
reviews.comment: I thought I was buying a 4k monitor to help me with my video editing... previously I was editing 4k videos on a non-4k monitor.  I have to say, the difference in video upgrading to this monitor was pretty underwhelming.  BUT, I was never expecting text and regular tasks on the PC to look so crisp.  It was like going from 20/40 vision to 20/15. This listing is for several products, the one I'm reviewing is PRO MP273U. When I first unboxed this monitor and started using it, it immediately blasted me with eye pain and strain. I had to go into the settings on the monitor using the 5 buttons on the bottom (which is NOT an intuitive process) and turn the brightness WAY down.  Rest assured, unless you're trying to use this monitor outside on the beach in direct sunlight, it can be plenty bright in any environment.  I read that insufficient brightness was a problem in other budget 4k monitors, that is definitely not the case with this model. In Windows 11, if HDR is activated with this monitor, it cranks the brightness way up and there is no way to turn that down.  This is fine if watching HDR videos, but afterwards I need to go back into Windows settings and turn the HDR off.  So there are extra steps required if one wants to watch videos in HDR and then later check email or whatever without getting blasted with too much brightness. I don't have any regrets.  I would have preferred a larger monitor, or one with 120 Hz, or easier HDR management, but I didn't buy those things.  I bought what I could afford. I almost forgot to include, this monitor has speakers.  The sound quality is horrible, so should only be considered as an emergency backup option.  I didn't factor this into my rating.  I just provide this as information. I bought this on a Black Friday "deal" that looked dramatic and as I write this review two months later.... it's being sold for the exact same price! reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: This monitor didn’t just change my setup I now see in 4K, and possibly in the fourth dimension
reviews.comment: Let me preface this by saying I’ve never written a review longer than a haiku, but the ASUS 27” 4K Eye Care Monitor (VY27UQ) deserves a literal standing ovation—and since I sit for 14 hours a day, that’s saying something. I bought this because my previous monitor was about as vibrant as a DMV waiting room. When I upgraded to this majestic beast of pixels, it was like removing a film from my eyeballs that had been there since 2002. I loaded up a 4K wallpaper of a mountain range and I’m pretty sure a hawk flew out of the screen and nested on my ceiling. That’s how real it looks. Let’s break this beauty down: UHD 3840 x 2160: This isn’t just Ultra High Definition. This is Ultra Holy-Cow-I-Can-Count-The-Pores-On-This-YouTuber’s-Nose Definition. IPS Panel: The colors are so consistent from every angle that I now invite guests over just to sit beside me and whisper, “Look at the reds, Brad. Just LOOK at them.” HDR10: I watched a documentary about mushrooms and the spores basically levitated out of the screen. It’s like being part of a planetarium exhibit that cost $249 and came with free shipping. Adaptive Sync: My games no longer tear like emotionally unstable relationships. I play, it adapts. I cry a little. Not out of lag, but out of joy. Eye Care Plus / Blue Light Filter / Flicker Free: My eyes used to dry out faster than hotel shampoo. Now? They’re practically spa-treated. I stare at this monitor for hours and my retinas send me thank-you notes. Built-in speakers: Are they audiophile grade? No. But will they save your butt during a Zoom call when your headphones are tangled in a knot made by a spiteful ghost? Absolutely. DisplayWidget: I didn’t even know I needed this until I started using it. Now I adjust brightness and color like I’m piloting the bridge of the Starship Enterprise. 3-Year Warranty: I’ve had shorter romantic relationships than this warranty. ASUS believes in this monitor more than I believe in finishing my laundry. Let’s be real: For $249, this is probably the best thing I’ve ever bought that didn’t require monthly payments, a therapist’s approval, or a permission slip from my significant other. I now gaze lovingly at this screen even when it's off. My productivity is up, my gaming has improved, and I’m pretty sure I look slightly cooler just sitting next to it. My cat has started sleeping in front of it like it’s a tiny sun. Final thoughts: If you need a monitor, this is it. If you don’t need a monitor, you’re wrong. Buy it. Mount it. Bask in it. And when someone comes over and says, “Wow, that’s a nice monitor,” you can lean back, nod slowly, and whisper: “It’s more than a monitor. It’s a lifestyle.”

If you’re doing design work (or just want your emails to look majestic), it holds up. • Adaptive Sync keeps everything smooth. No screen tearing, no weird stutters—just clean visuals, whether it’s meetings, edits, or YouTube “research.” Bonus: The stand doesn’t wobble like a cheap lawn chair, and it doesn’t look like it was designed by a discount gaming brand trying too hard. Bottom line: If you want a monitor that works like it’s supposed to, looks how it’s supposed to, and won’t make your eyes beg for mercy after a 10-hour day—this is the one.

reviews.title: Yes
reviews.comment:
As another reviewer noted, the cardboard used in the box has a terrible smell. They should obviously address that. The monitor itself I also agree with reviews regarding color shift. To me it's not terribly significant side to side, however you can see the screen get noticeably washed out when moving up/away from the screen. Viewing angles aren't the best but honestly this is a common occurrence. I don't know about the quality of this particular VA monitor, just that IPS monitors in general tend to and SHOULD have better viewing angles. I'm pleased with it overall but it's still something to consider. I think it gets bright enough, I was more concerned before I changed the color settings because next to an IPS monitor the white was more yellow. They're different panels though and the IPS monitor is smaller and lower resolution. I think the colors look good - great and the monitor itself gets bright enough unless you have a very bright environment where I could see 'potential' for issues. What really surprised me was the bump in clarity. I understand some monitors are sharper but having nothing similar to compare it to, I'm satisfied with the resolution and it absolutely blows away a 1080 monitor. The speakers are excellent. They're not a replacement for dedicated speakers but they can certainly be used as such. It's not necessarily the quality but the loudness. They get LOUD. The quality is also very good. They're approaching the sound quality of a good, large TV. The interface is operated via button on the back and slightly annoying but easy to use and functional. A prompt came up on the screen to download additional software to customize the display. I honestly didn't know a monitor does this, I'm assuming through Windows update. I haven't done that yet and I'm satisfied with the quality enough that I might not get around to it. Setup was easy enough although I found it odd that there was no instruction manual whatsoever in the box. Not mine at least. Light bleed around the edges is practically non existent (on this panel) and the colors and resolution are good. I haven't noticed any flickering or dead pixels. BTW the monitor is flipped in the manufacturer box and Amazon placed it front of the box side up, which is logical and they probably don't know it's upside down in the box, but so that means it constantly got dropped directly on the screen whenever it was set down. They also shipped it inside another box for whatever reason so the package was massive. I'll update this review if anything odd starts happening but as of now I'm satisfied with it and would recommend it.
Pros:
Resolution
Speakers
Display colors
Design
Size
Cons/not the best:
Huge Amazon box 🤔
Brightness
Color shift
Noxious packaging
No instructions
Price

reviews.title: Good quality WQHD resolution monitor for gaming or general PC use
reviews.comment:
I bought this monitor to replace one that got damaged by accident. This monitor has everything I was looking for, and I was surprised with the easy height and tilt adjust (vertically and sideways). There is a bit of assembly required, but it it rather quick and easy - there are three main assemblies - the weighty base, the vertical adjustable stem and the monitor itself. The vertical stem easily screws into the heavy metal base (the screw even has a thumb grip), then that assembly easily mounts to the back of the monitor with a simple but sturdy spring loaded latch. Then connect the monitor to your PC - I highly recommend to use the display port (DP) connection if your graphics card supports it (most have more than one). There is only one DP connection on the monitor, but two HDMI - I wish it was the other way around since I have two PCs I wanted to connect to this monitor. They do supply an HDMI and DP cable - nice touch.
There is a set of switches on the lower rear right side - you can feel your way around without having to look there as the joystick knob is distinctly shaped. You can use the joystick to change all of the settings except power. In use, you don't have to touch the power button as the monitor turns off/on automatically when a signal is detected on the video ports.
The height is easily adjustable with a light push up or down. Horizontally the monitor can swivel a bit too with a vertical tilt adjustment as well. I really liked the ease with which this monitor is adjustable. The base has a fair amount of weight to it so it won't easily tilt and fall off the table as my previous monitor did - that's a big plus for me.
The display is bright, crisp, flicker free and very clear with resolution of WQHD 2560x1440 - which is just right - 4K would be too much but this is perfect being right between FHD and 4K. My operating systems - both Windows and Linux Mint were able to automatically detect and set the WQHD resolution, but do check the refresh rate - it will default to 60 Hz - this monitor is capable of 180 Hz on DP, but "only" 144 Hz on HDMI which is one reason I recommended using the DP connection. You can set/check the refresh rates and resolution from the "display settings" of Windows or Linux.
The only disappointment is the built in speaker audio quality which sounds muffled and tinny - definitely use external speakers or headphones either connected to the PC or to the audio out jack on the bottom of the monitor. This was a minor criteria for me since I use headphones anyway.
reviews.author: CG

reviews.title: Outstanding Value at $199
reviews.comment:
I've noticed a distinct lack of good technical reviews for this specific model, so I'm gonna go into a bit of detail here. If you want the tl;dr: If you see it on sale, buy with confidence.
Color Reproduction/Panel Quality:
Color volume is outstanding - not just for the sale price, but in general. Color accuracy is very good to my naked eye after setting picture mode to normal from the default of warm, requiring no calibration whatsoever. Contrast performance seems good for an IPS panel. There is some backlight bleed in the lower left corner, but it's invisible against any color other than deep black.
Freesync functions well with zero flicker but clamps the overdrive setting at Normal, so most users aren't going to be seeing the advertised response time. Still, input lag is imperceptible and I have thus far been unable to detect any ghosting or overshoot.
The advertised brightness of 250 nits appears to be correct. I'm in a moderately lit room and find any setting over 84 a bit uncomfortable with this panel, but I could see it failing to measure up in a room with lots of natural light.
Ergonomics:
The stand is of decent quality and wobble is kept to a minimum, though you probably will notice some if your typing surface isn't perfectly stable. All movement options are accounted for, though it needs to be said that the panel can't be lifted very high. Very tall users may wish to invest in a fashionable box to set this thing on.
HDR Performance:
Very good for this price point with surprisingly high color volume and decent handling of contrast for an IPS panel, but SDR color volume is so good that the HDR mode ends up looking inferior by comparison. As ever, outstanding HDR is the only HDR worth using and you won't find that here.
Overall:
If this monitor holds up over the years I'll most likely be buying Acer again when it comes time to upgrade. This panel feels incredibly premium for the price I paid ($199) and you can tell that great care was taken to provide a clean, color accurate image straight out of the box - most users will be happy to simply enable freesync and set color temp to normal.

reviews.title: Love it with an asterisk
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/D17DgrtFcML.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/61D6NDGiOtL._SY256.jpg This is a review after 3 months of usage, spoiler alert, I’m pretty happy with it.*
I bought this 27inch 1440p 180Hz (KG271U N3bmiipx) monitor for around 170 usd with offer and taxes.
Pros:
1. 2K, very fast 180hz refresh rate, with built in speakers for 170 USD.
2. Pretty high color range (DCI-P3 95%), not verified, but to naked eye, love the vivid colour accurate display, this was important to me.
3. IPS screen, meaning good viewing angles, also important for good viewing experience.
4. Decent HDR for an IPS LCD budget monitor.
5. Didn't notice any flickering.
Reasons for asterisk:
1. In standard or other modes, even when set to 100, brightness feels low in well lit environments. Turning HDR mode on solves this issue, probably because of increased peak brightness, but this makes it too bright in dark environments, you won't be able to adjust screen brightness in HDR mode. Switching between standard and HDR mode felt a little tedious.
2. Overshooting is noticeable to naked eye if overdrive setting is set as extreme. Recommend setting it to minimum, or off, then it’s not at all noticeable.
3. Speakers are like what you’d expect in your typical gaming monitors. Pretty mediocre, will get the job done. They lack any base or instrument clarity or separation. In movies or songs, vocals are pretty crisp, but the background music sounds pretty low. Could be solved with headphones or speakers.
4. HDMI connections only supports upto 144hz.
5. Lack of height adjustment for stand.
6. Felt like a thick monitor, build quality is decent, all plastic, does not give you premium feels, but good for it's price.
At this point you might be thinking, why did this guy give 5 stars when the cons list is bigger than pros. It's because I compared this with similarly priced Sansui ESA-G27F6Q and Arzopa M1RC side by side, and overall Acer seemed like the best pick in this price range.

reviews.title: Amazing Monitor! The Stand? Not So Much.
reviews.comment: This monitor works great and getting it on sale made it even better. 1440p is all you will ever need especially for console gaming. It runs up to 180hz on display port but hdmi it can reach 120hz easily allowing you to maximize your response time for your console and give yourself more time to react. You can quickly switch between different modes for different games and even create user specific modes that you can adjust to your hearts desire. All of the display settings are easily adjustable through the analog button on the rear of the monitor. Also the monitor has settings that can actively adjust your picture for different situations in games (I currently cannot recall the term for it). You can adjust the brightness, saturation, and more. One of my favorite features is the different display presets such as low blue light that can help when working late on the monitor. reviews.author: Joe Christman

reviews.title: Works beautifully with the Mac Mini M4
reviews.comment: I just upgraded to a Macintosh Mini M4 (I have posted a separate review of that) and needed a monitor to go with it. I did a lot of research, and while the perfect match would be a Macintosh Retina monitor, those are pricey. Amazon had quite a price reduction on this (I paid $199), and I compared (online) it to other 4K monitors and it seemed like a great deal—plus, I’ve had various Samsung products over the years (tablets, phones, TVs) and have been very satisfied with them. I am not mechanically inclined, and the stand assembly instructions are only pictorial, so I did have a bit of a problem figuring that out. Once I did, I realized how easy it is. I think I was just afraid of scratching the screen or breaking something. The monitor, mounted on the stand, can be rotated to be portrait or landscape, and it can be raised and lowered. The angle can be adjusted, but as far as I can tell, it can’t be 90%—it’s always on a slight angle. The monitor itself is very lightweight. The screen has a matte finish, which I like, though it can be reflective if you have bright light (such as through a window) behind you. Screen brightness out of the box is very good—good contrast, bright whites, dark blacks—and the picture is very clear and sharp. In tandem with my Mac, five different resolutions are available through System Preferences: 1152 x 648; 1504 x 846; 1920 x 1080 (set as the default by the Mac); 2560 x 1440; and 3840 x 2160. My preference is 2560 x 1440, and for my eyes, that works best with the M4. 3840 x 2160 is amazingly sharp, but I find the text too small to read at that resolution. But you can certainly get a lot on this 27” screen with that latter setting. The type is very sharp—photos and graphics maybe not as sharp as an Apple monitor, but nevertheless, excellent quality, in my opinion. This offers a few different ways to hook up to a computer—from my M4, HDMI was the easiest and that does give very high res and no delays. This came with three different high-quality cables, including HDMI. I thought this had speakers but apparently not. It does, however, have a headphone jack, and I have that hooked to an external amp, and the sound is excellent. Note that the jack is analog 1/8”. Apparently no one uses optical out anymore, and I don’t know why not. What I do find difficult are the controls. It has a lot of fine-tuning options, generally as many as you’d find on an HDTV. But all those intricate adjustments cannot be made through the Mac. There is one button on the back of the monitor, which turns it off and on, and the button sort of has edges to get to the menus and scroll through them, but I found that very frustrating. And also, backwards—I’d have to scroll up to go down; left to go right. You may not need to make adjustments though, as the factory settings looked good to me. All in all so far (I’ve only had this setup for about a week), I am very pleased with this monitor and find it to be a very good match with the Mac mini M4.
reviews.author: SiskiyouScoj

reviews.title: My "Go To Monitor" Perfect Size
reviews.comment: I’ve been using the Samsung 27 inch ViewFinity S8 monitor for a few weeks now and the first thing I noticed is how big and clear the screen looks. The 4K UHD resolution makes everything super sharp, whether I’m watching videos, playing games, or working on school projects. Small details are easy to see and text looks very crisp without looking blurry. The color quality is another strong point. With HDR10 support, the contrast between dark and bright areas looks more real, and the colors appear bright without looking fake. Movies and games look especially good on this screen. The stand is also very useful because it lets me adjust the height, tilt the screen, and rotate it vertically, which helps a lot with long webpages and homework. Connectivity is really convienent. There are multiple ports so I can plug in my laptop and other accessories without constantly unplugging things. This helps keep my desk more organized. I also like the Eye Saver Mode because it makes long sessions easier on my eyes, especially at night. It is not perfect. The menu buttons can be a little confusing at first and take some getting used to. Still, the picture quality and features make up for it. Overall, the Samsung ViewFinity S8 is a great monitor with excelent image quality and flexibility. I would recommend it to anyone looking for a large and sharp screen for work or entertainment.

reviews.title: More than enough for gaming
reviews.comment: ’ve been using the Samsung Odyssey G4 25″ gaming monitor for a few weeks now, and overall it’s been a very impressive display, especially for fast-paced gaming. Performance: This monitor is very smooth. The 240 Hz refresh rate combined with a 1 ms response time makes motion feel fluid and crisp — perfect for competitive shooters, racing games, or any title where input speed and clarity during rapid movement matter. There’s very little motion blur, even when things get hectic on screen. Visuals: The FHD (1080p) resolution on a 25″ screen looks clear and sharp for most use cases. The IPS panel means colors are vibrant and viewing angles are wide — side-by-side games and videos look consistently good even if you’re not sitting perfectly center. It’s not a 4K panel, but for gaming this size/resolution hits a great balance of performance and graphical clarity. Adaptive Sync & Compatibility: I tested it with both G-Sync Compatible on my NVIDIA GPU and Adaptive Sync on AMD, and the experience was smooth — fewer tears or stutters compared to V-Sync-only setups. If you’re into esports titles or any competitive gaming, this is where the panel really shines. Build & Features: The design is fairly minimal but gaming-friendly — slim bezels and a clean stand that doesn’t take up too much desk space. The OSD menu is intuitive, and setting up presets for different game genres is quick. A couple of things to note: The resolution is 1080p, which is great for high frame-rate gaming, but if you prefer really detailed visuals for single-player games or creative work, a higher-res panel (1440p+) might feel sharper. It doesn’t have integrated speakers, so you’ll need separate audio if you want sound from your setup. Overall: This Samsung Odyssey G4 monitor delivers excellent performance for gamers, particularly if you care about refresh rate and responsiveness. The IPS panel keeps colors nice, and the adaptive sync support makes gameplay feel smooth. If your priority is competitive gaming and fast visuals without sacrificing quality, this monitor is a strong choice at its price point.
