reviews.title: Cools a Ryzen 9 5900x
reviews.comment: Been a few months of using it with my Ryzen 9 5900x and it does a pretty darn cool job. I dont think I get above 75 celsius very often and thats always when I am pushing the system pretty hard. It idles around 50c and esports titles usually run around 65c. Its very bright and RGB is not really my thing but I dont see it in my case so it doesnt bother me. It fits like it should.
reviews.author: Pixel dork

reviews.title: Cools very well
reviews.comment: It really keeps my CPU cool. It was very easy to install in my box. I have a 11900K processor and I do a lot of gaming. So heat can be a real problem and it can destroy your processor, But this cooler seems to be up to the job and i will recommend it.
reviews.author: Ginabean

reviews.title: Some parts missing
reviews.comment: I did not receive thermal paste or the 3-to-1 fan cable splitter with mine — they were easy and cheap enough to replace, but that’s still a disappointment. The plastic cover for the underside of the heat sink was also taken off already when I opened the box, so I’m wondering if I received a repurposed return that they didn’t quite check over enough. But, if you have all the correct parts, this system runs great! Keeps my Intel 12th gen i9 CPU cool, runs super quiet for the most part, and the RGB lights are beautiful.
reviews.author: James

reviews.title: Hyper T2 Specs and Review -- great value for the price!
reviews.comment: I just got this and installed it today, but I wanted to write this review to answer all of the questions I had in mind before I purchased a fan, just in case there are other people wondering the same things but struggling to get a good answer.  I'll update this review if, after some time and use, I feel it deserves less stars. First, I will list the specifications of the Hyper T2 fan that came on the box. Fits the following CPU sockets: -Intel Socket LGA 1156/1155/1150/775 -AMD Socket FM2+/FM2/FM1/AM3+/AM3/AM2+/AM2 Dimensions: 93 x 80 x 140mm (3.7 x 3.1 x 5.5 inch) Heat Sink Dimensions 90 x 51 x 140mm (3.5 x 2.0 x 5.5 inch) -- From the bottom flat pipes that adhere to to the CPU to the top 2 pipes of the fan, this is 140mm tall. (Something I wish I had known beforehand. Luckily this fit in my case just fine, but it's likely that some of the 4 pipe fans would not have). Heat Sink Material: 2 Direct Contact Heatpipes/ Aluminum Fins Heat Sink Weight: 248g/ 0.55lb Heat Pipe Dimensions: Ø6mm Fan Dimensions: 92 x 92 x 25mm (3.6 x 3.6 x 1 inch) Fan Speed: 800 - 2800 RPM (PWM) Fan Air Flow 15.7 - 54.8 CFM Fan Air Pressure: 0.35 - 4.27 mm H2O Fan Life Expectancy: 40,000 hours Noise level: 17-35 dBA  (I find it to be silent when I'm not gaming, but still pretty quiet when I am) Bearing Type: Long Life Sleeve Connector: 4 Pin Rated Voltage: 12 VDC Safety Current: 0.6 A Rated Current: 0.26 A Power Consumption: 3.12 W Max. Fan Weight: 91 g / 0.20 lbs Weight: 340 g / 0.75 lb So far the only con to this fan is that installation was a bit tricky. It has 4 push pins just like the stock coolers you will get from Intel (thought it also comes with some sort of clip for AMD mobos... wouldn't know about that since I'm using Intel products), so it seems like things should be relatively simple. They are, but only after you figure out which way to rotate all the pins before pushing them into the holes. The directions are just pictures with no explanation, which is why I struggled at first. I did eventually figure things out, but it would be nice if they updated the directions to have some written instruction. As for the the fan, it's perceptibly better than a stock cooler. When doing very simple things (like writing this review) you shouldn't be experiencing high temperatures anyway, but the cooler has dropped things a few degrees C. However, there seems to be a relatively decent difference while playing games. The highest I've noticed the stock cooler at was 55 C, which is kind of pushing it since apparently you don't want to get any hotter than 60. Doing a quick test run of a solo dungeon in the game, Tera, at max graphics, most of my cores are staying near 40-43 C. Again, I'll come back and update this review once I've used the fan for longer or tried it with different games. I bought this fan for essentially $5.50. The list price was 9.99 (10.50 with tax) and there was a 5$ mail in rebate. I highly doubt I could find a better fan for 5$. Stock coolers on Amazon are listed for around 8. For the price, this is a pretty damn good value.
reviews.author: Jenni K.

reviews.title: Works as should, no problems and a perfect replacement for my setup.
reviews.comment: Just to start off, I have a ASRock H97M PRO4 Micro ATX LGA1150 Motherboard. The previous fan, a Cooler Master Hyper TX3 54.8 CFM Sleeve Bearing CPU Cooler, started dying on year 4. I needed a replacement therefore I checked my options on PCPartPicker and found this fan here on Amazon. I bought it, unboxed it once delivered and took my old fan out to replace it with this. First of all, I hate replacing fans. It's always annoying and bad luck for me. I used the setup for my last fan because it was easier that way; Basically took off the part holding the old fan and put in on the new one, disregarding whatever the new fan came with. Would have worked fine but I would've had to move some wires and I just wanted to get this over with. The prongs never seem to sit in right and then you worry about the thermal paste not getting smeared and blah blah. After some colorful language and locking the fan in place, I fired up my computer to hear a silent fan and watched my temps on Coretemp to make sure it was working well and nothing was overheating and everything seemed fine! Safe to say it's all still working groovy after several weeks of constant use. <3.... also, sorry for the crap photo.
reviews.author: Maddeh

reviews.title: Replace the fan and it's great (but *BEWARE* of the fan!)
reviews.comment: I set out to make a "nearly" silent PC, in that I didn't want to go fanless, but I wanted it to have the fans running so slowly (or off) during normal operation that  it was silent, and it was only during intensive activities that the fans would ramp up.  I bought this Hypter T2 CPU cooler as it is the biggest Cooler Master that fits in a standard case and then replaced the fan with a Noctua NF-A9, and am very happy with the resulting solution. I give it 4 stars instead of 5 because I needed to swap out the fan, but I'd still recommend doing that instead of buying a much more expensive Noctua CPU cooler.  It saves about $30 even when taking into account the extra fan purchase. Why did I have to replace the fan?  Because the Cooler Master fan sucks and doesn't allow you to reduce the fan speed below ~32%.  I was very frustrated as I didn't know why it wouldn't go that low.  Was it the fan controller on the motherboard?  Or the fan software (either BIOS or at the OS)? But after doing a lot of debugging I finally determined that it was the Cooler Master fan's internal controller that was at fault.  It would stay at about 850 RPM for any PWM setting below 32%, including zero, but once it got over that, it would ramp up to the correct speed all the way up to a max of 2500 RPM. I do have one slight workaround to provide you with a little more control if you want to stick with the stock fan: Switch to DC fan mode on your fan controller.  With DC mode I could get the fan down to about 500 RPM at 32% (3.84V) and I could also get it to shut off entirely when desired, something in PWM mode the fan won't allow *EVER*.  It's really frustrating that the stock fan won't allow that control and I wonder how many people have blamed their fan controller not realizing it's the stupid fan's fault. So, what I'd suggest is buy the Hyper T2 and then swap out the fan for a Noctua NF-B9 (yes, the B9 instead of the A9 I am using, as it is cheaper and works just as well). The good news is that with this CPU cooler and the right fans both on this CPU cooler and the rest of the system, as well as an EVGA gold power supply in "eco mode" I have a truly silent PC, where a pretty sensitive dB meter can not detect it being on.  I have to do the test in the middle of the night, because even cars going by outside are detectable.  But at 3 AM, it reads 21.1 dB with the PC off and 21.1 dB with it on.  My stomach gurgles and the stupid thing goes up to 24 dB or I click the mouse and it goes up to over 30 dB so trust me when I say the dB meter is sensitive enough to detect pretty small readings. To be fair and give a caveat, to keep it silent, the fans are running at 13% on the rear of the case, 10% on the CPU and 5% on the GPU and the front of case fan is off.  But that's just enough air flow with the good heatsinks that in normal operation the system temp stays around 40 and both the CPU temp and GPU temps stay in the mid 50's. Build details: -Intel Core i3-8100 CPU -MSI Z370M Mortar motherboard -Gigabyte GTX 1050 Ti "Windforce OC" GPU (Note: Gigabyte is the only vendor with a good fan controller on their 1050 GPU.  The other companies have junk 2-pin fans.  Also note I replaced the fans it comes with, with Noctua NF-B9's as their fans were noisy on ramp up.) -2 of 4 GB DDR4 2400 Kingston Fury DIMMs -Samsung 960 EVO M.2 SSD -EVGA 650 GQ PSU in eco mode
reviews.author: K. Crawford

reviews.title: Hyper T2.  Very Impressive Performance.
reviews.comment: I'm not a Gamer, but I do take and edit lots of photographs.  Who would have thought that when I ran a function to reduce shake on a photograph that my CPU temp would shoot from 120f (48c) to 171f (77.2c)? I sure as hell didn't. I installed this unit today and then ran the same editing function on the same photograph.  The CPU temp never rose above 89f (31.6c) - which is pretty close to my previous temps at idle.  My new idle temps are down by 30 degrees fahrenheit. My previous cooler was the one boxed by AMD along with my CPU (AMD Phenom II X4 840). It requires a lot of space - it was intimidating just seeing it in the box - but it the installation was no more difficult than that of a standard CPU fan.  I purchased this on Amazon over Black Friday for less than $10.00.  Sweet. Cooler Master Hyper T2 - Compact CPU Cooler with Dual Looped Direct Contact Heatpipes, INTEL/AMD with AM4 Support
reviews.author: trdavidson

reviews.title: Cools Great. Simple. Compact. Quiet. A+
reviews.comment: This T2 is one of the newest versions from Cooler Master.  Everyone raves about the Hyper 212 EVO but seeing that this was a compact size cooler I decided to give the T2 a go.  Bottom Line: It works very well.  Definitely better than the stock intel CPU cooler and I could fit it facing up toward the top fan of my case (Above my graphics card on a ASUS 87-Plus motherboard)  or I could fit it as it is now with the CPU fan blowing out toward the rear case fan (And this includes having 2 sticks of high profile RAM in the first two RAM slots; If you have 4 sticks of high profile RAM it's not going to fit but it might be possible with low profile RAM I have no way of testing it out).  Anyway, my CPU runs about 3 degrees Celsius cooler in idle and doesn't make the loud fan noise on initial startup of my computer as my stock fan did.  Airflow is a definite improvement since I now have air flowing from front to back continuously. I have not run stress tests on my CPU such as Prime95 but don't think it's necessary given that I only occasionally game on my computer for short periods of time.  I'm sure it will hold up just fine in stress tests; I mean really all you need to make sure of with any type of CPU cooler is that you apply just the right amount of thermal paste and have a good connection between the copper and CPU so heat can conduct.  I just didn't like my stock intel because it was louder and the airflow was less than optimal.  This is a great fan. Simple. But it works. The pins that insert into the motherboard are also very durable.  I accidentally bent a few of the white plastic pins on the CPU clip when trying to insert them into the motherboard. You would definitely think they would break how much I pressure I put on the thing not realizing it wasn't going in, but they didn't break! It was just severely bent but I could bend them back to shape to insert into the board for a secure fit! Just be aware of this when inserting this push-in and click type CPU attachment and make sure the holes line up! I was impressed with how durable the clip was and the way it attaches to the board is a big selling point for a lot of aftermarket CPU buyers.  Worked fine for me just be patient when installing!
reviews.author: Sebastian

reviews.title: Great monitor, great deal
reviews.comment: Great value for a great monitor. Picture is terrific 4K, w good color and contrast. The BEST? Nope. But at this price, this pretty great screen becomes a bargain. Plus I can use my VESA arm. Also, I got mine “like new” and got a nice discount on what appeared to be a brand new monitor. No one ever bought a computer monitor for the speakers, but these are essentially nonexistent, so much so I had to turn the volume up all the way and then put my ear right up to the screen to even find them (on the bottom edge btw, presumably intended to bounce sound off the desk). My iPhone speakers sound better. Again, not a big deal since no monitor speakers are good, but some can at least add some fill to your setup. Not these.
reviews.author: BMC

reviews.title: Big Bang for Your Buck
reviews.comment: I bought this to replace an earlier, non-HDR version that I dropped. I'd just upgraded my video card anyway. I can't emphasize enough the quality of this monitor at the price point. It may not have the ultra-crisp look of monitors costing two or three times this (or more) but it certainly does the job(s) I want from it at this price point. Gaming: Elder Scrolls Online doesn't necessarily challenge the combination of RX760XT and this monitor, but the game looks great with the auto-HDR function. Photo Editing, the more important aspect for me, has taken on a new "flavor". Between upgrading from a RTX3060 to RX7600 XT and this monirot, images in Lightroom have a depth on this monitor that makes me want to try out some "crazy" editing functions that didn't look very satisfying on my old monitor.
reviews.author: Charles H. Black

reviews.title: Very good for the money
reviews.comment: Pleased with the quality of this monitor for the price.  I didn't notice that the stand is not height adjustable when ordering.  The bottom edge of the monitor is 4" above the surface of the desk.  Some may want to take note of that. The default color settings are complete garbage (everything is overblown, especially green) but are easily adjustable  to provide a good image.  Off axis viewing is pretty terrible with uneven brightness in the edges at merely 10 degrees off center.  Won't be a problem for me since I'm looking at them straight on.  The bezel looks razor thin out of the box but there is an unlit area (about 1/4") inside of the bezel that makes it appear a bit thicker when powered on.  Still a thinner overall bezel than my 12 year old Asus HD monitors.  If you are new to adjusting monitors, here are my adjusted settings (brightness 100, contrast 100, gamma 24, red 61, green 60, blue 85).  If off axis viewing wasn't so bad, I'd give it 5 stars.
reviews.author: Todd W. Carnes

reviews.title: Worth the price.
reviews.comment: Great monitor. Works great and captures colors well
reviews.author: Jason

reviews.title: Great value for money.
reviews.comment: Great screen for the price - excellent value. Easy to set up. Color calibrated relatively easily (unlike other screens at the same price point). Good picture quality. Unobtrusive bezel. Clear and intuitive (single) menu button. Love the Vesa mount compatibility. I don't use the speakers so no comment on the audio. If you're looking for an inexpensive 4K screen.. this is a great contender.
reviews.author: NotInUse

reviews.title: Great display, but the OSD settings are changed by using the on/off button as a joystick
reviews.comment: This is a nice monitor at a great price.  The ability to change settings via the on screen menu is NOT intuitive.  The manual illustrates using directional arrows, like those on a keyboard.  The only button on back is the on/off button. A brief call with their excellent customer service informed me that the on/off button functions like a joystick.  That means after entering the OSD menu you need to make/change setting by pushing the button up/down or right/left.
reviews.author: Walk The Talk

reviews.title: Met expectations - good value
reviews.comment: I had this monitor in my Amazon wish list last year. When it was discounted on a Prime Day, I bought it. I'm pleased with this monitor, especially at the price point. I haven't had any problems with its function. Its resolution is better than the older monitors it replaced. I had been using a setup of two older 25" monitors. Now I use this this 31.5" monitor sitting next to my Macbook Pro's screen, and that's fine for my needs. I don't play sound through the monitor speakers, so I don't know how good they are as monitor speakers go. I use a Bose bluetooth speaker for better sound quality than I would expect from the speakers in a monitor or a laptop. My only negative comment about this monitor: its power cord is stupid short. It wouldn't reach from the monitor - sitting on the desktop of course -  to the power strip on the floor below. I've never had a computer peripheral with such a short power cord. I bought a heavy duty extension cord to safely connect the monitor to the power strip.
reviews.author: Free Range Clickin'

reviews.title: Dead pixel line accross the screen out of nowhere
reviews.comment: I had this for 15 days, and everything was going ok, I know is the award winning monitor, great resolution, OK monitor, OK colors, but good price and value. Well, today I just turned on my computer... dead pixel vertical line in almost the middle of the screen, nothing touched the monitor, nothing hit the monitor, just happened. Is unacceptable, I'm returning it.
reviews.author: Jorge Aguilar

reviews.title: WARRING NOT BACKWARD COMPATIBLE
reviews.comment: DP works great, but HDMI has a pink color on HDMI one and two, change the cable and it is still the same, put the DVD player on a 32-inch 1080p Viewsonic monitor, and it works fine. Using the same cable and player, hook it back up again to the ASUS, and still, Pink Video, but then again, the DP is fine. I checked all the YouTube videos on how to fix this error, but no luck. Bought on Jan 25, 2025. I have bought many ASUS items over the years and if you name it, I have bought it from ASUS, but the build quality is going downhill. I'm just a few days past the return date. reviews.title: Very Nice UHD Monitor
reviews.comment: Tha Asus 32" UHD Monitor works great with our Apple computers. The picture is great and they are easy on the eyes. The screen size and picture quality is top notch.  We have 2 and will be buying a third monitor!
reviews.author: Baja Alan

reviews.title: Fantastic monitor
reviews.comment: I am very happy with this monitor, the image is clean, sharp and well lit, I like to play in the fps/rts mode, but have to switch to race mode when video editing and color grading in order to get correct colors. The speakers are ok (better than none) but as with most monitors they leave a lot to be desired. I purchased a pc sound bar and it actually fits right under the screen as if the two were made for one another. The stand is adjustable with just the right amount of tension. Plenty of inputs and a powered usb-a output and an audio out port that allows the soundbar to function connected directly to the monitor. If someone were to ask me to recommend a gaming monitor, I would point them towards this product model without hesitation.
reviews.author: Terry L.

reviews.title: Great monitors but this was ridiculous.
reviews.comment:
The monitors themselves are very, very nice for the price and I’m glad we got them and would definitely recommend. Setup takes less than a minute once plugged in (setting refresh rate mostly) very excited to continue using them in the future.
That being said, this was the most frustrating purchase I’ve ever made from Amazon. I ordered 2 of these monitors in March and the first monitor I received was disgusting, it was obviously opened previously, with the box cobbled back together with scotch tape, protective packaging was missing, it was missing the instruction booklet, had greasy fingerprint smears all over the screen and did not work, back light would come on but would not respond to any video input, why this returned item was sent out in that condition in the first place is beyond me. We received the second monitor the next day and it worked with no issues. We had to contact customer service and setup a return for the first one we received because they wouldn’t just replace it, it took about a week to get to their return facility and about 2 weeks for them to issue a refund which was very frustrating and finally in the middle of April we received a replacement monitor after reordering the item again.
As far as the monitors go, they function beautifully but Amazon really dropped the ball on this one.
reviews.author: Brenden

reviews.title: Great monitor
reviews.comment: Happy with this purchase, looks great, colors and brightness is awesome for the price, 100% recommended
reviews.author: 100% recommended, very useful.

reviews.title: Awesome PC Display!
reviews.comment:
Beautiful display!!!
So many built-in function options in the GamePlus menu such as FPS Counter, Crosshair, and even a Display Alignment setting to adjust corner to corner offset in case it seems off a bit but upon playing around with it it is already set nicely by default.
The 1440p resolution is so crisp, also has very vibrant colors, and the true blacks in-game is really good! The default brightness was a bit high but I changed that withing the Windows 11 display settings. Very impressive performance coming from the 180Hz refresh rate blew me away! The 27" screen was perfect for my small corner desk setup.
Set up was a breeze with the DP cable that was included in the box and simple to attach the stand. I really like the futuristic and rugged look of the line of TUF Gaming products and matches well with the other PC parts I combined such as the Motherboard, GPU, Mouse, Keyboard, Mouse pad, and cooling fans on my system.
I highly recommend this item if you are looking for a smaller size but powerful and price worthy display. Thank you, ASUS!!!
reviews.author: ShooterB80

reviews.title: Best PS5 monitor on a budget
reviews.comment:
Just updated from a 1080p 60hz tv to play Crimson Desert on my PS5
Looks amazing, crisp graphics, no tearing or blur, almost zero latency, menus easy to navigate, great price (I'm a late-adopting penny pincher).
Simple: if you're on a budget, JUST BUY THIS
reviews.author: Old_Shoe

reviews.title: Wow. What a value.
reviews.comment: Day one review. Subject to revision. This monitor rips. It looks crisp. The 4k pops in HDR and the refresh is handling everything ive thrown at it with my PS5 Pro. Time will tell if this monitor holds up but i am pleasantly pleased with the build quality. The UI and the easy to use settings. Did i mention that this monitor rips?? Rips meaning shes fast. So far ive run Cyberpunk 2077 (4k at 120hz-wowsa) Ive run Forza 5. ZERO LATENCY. I play with a wheel and the throttle pedal is instant. This was the main reason i purchased a gaming montior. My 4k 60hz could not keep up with these titles and i wanted the FPS. Day one and it's 5 stars top to bottom for me. I will 100% come back and revise this review if anything happens to change my opinion. I also connected a sound bar to this. Through the aux out. Sound syncing is spot on. I dont know if i could have found a better monitor with these specs at this price. If youre in the market for a budget curved 4k 165hz monitor,  this is it.
reviews.author: Robert Dennis

reviews.title: Top Brand Performance at a budget price
reviews.comment: I was in the market for a 32 inch 4K monitor with a bright sharp display. I tried a VA panel and found the text slightly blurry and colors washed out. I am running Win10 and Linux Mint and both are beautiful. Not sure if it is the IPS technology in this model, but this is a much better monitor. It has all the needed inputs like HDMI, DP, and even has a speaker. One thing to be aware of, the stand is very wide, so you need a big desk or shelf. The OSD menu is fairly easy to understand. I was hesitant to buy from an unknown brand like ZZA. But they seem to build great products. Very happy with my purchase. Amazon delivered it in one day. Thanks Amazon.
reviews.author: music_collector

reviews.title: OK, but know the limitations-no remote, sound, not very high or tall monitor.
reviews.comment: No remote; have to get up and use funky controls on back of monitor to switch devices should I want to connect anything else up - not convenient, so nothing connected except my PC. Colors seem fine overall but swirly lights on back of monitor sometimes work sometimes not; strange noises come from  this monitor like trapped critters inside. Overall this curved 49+ inch monitor is like two and a half 27" monitors put together; I wish the monitor was higher, width is nice but the monitor just seems to narrow from top to bottom to be truly 5 star worthy. Disappointing for a $500 monitor - my flat 55" 4K TCL television that I also have connected to my PC is much more enjoyable to watch and easier to read from a distance. The ZZA is just OK for true wide screen movies to watch in the background while I work mostly on my 55" flat screen. And no, this monitor has no built in sound which I knew going in, I use my PreSonus monitors as normal so it didn't concern me.
reviews.author: Jason Bourne

reviews.title: Good for the price.
reviews.comment: It's really impressive for the price (140 USD when I night it, 165 is a little steep in my opinion). As others have mentioned it does indeed only go up to 144,Hz in 2560x1440 resolution, but that's not really a huge deal considering the value. The picture is decent, much better than I was expecting at the price point, but doesn't compete with high end competitors (wasn't expecting it to). Interestingly, despite the refresh rate only being 144Hz compared to the advertised 165Hz, resolution can seemingly go up to 4k, which was surprising, that's why I gave it the 5 star to make up for the Hz mislead.
reviews.author: The Thinking Pig

reviews.title: False Advertising??
reviews.comment: I bought this monitor because there was essentially no bezel on 3 sides. I was excited when the monitor arrived. When I hooked it up however, I found that there was a 1/4" black border on the 3 sides that were supposed to be essentially bezel-less. I tried new cables, I tried scaling and different resolutions with my Mac, I tried searching the menu on the monitor its self to see if there was a setting but there wasn't. I tried to look up the ZZA website for a firmware update but apparently it doesn't exist. I can't contact their customer support because it apparently doesn't exist either. Other than that issue, the picture that I do have is good. the colors are good and the lines and text are crisp. But because the picture doesn't go edge to edge like advertised, I have to give it a 1 star. I really wish these companies cared more about their customers.

The color is accurate, it is feature rich, and easy to use out of the box.

reviews.author: Juan

reviews.title: Good Monitor for Gaming
reviews.comment: I bought this monitor awhile back and has served me well so far. I bought this monitor since I play competitive games such as Fortnite and MW3. Before this monitor I had a 1440p 165hz panel. I then bought a higher-end pc, requiring me to buy this to push more frames. With that being said, this thing loves pulling watts right out of my wall. Even with the wattage draw, the physical monitor itself doesn't seem to get very warm. The picture is good for what it is. The color range is alright. But again, the main draw to this monitor is the refresh rate. I found a lazy pixel about a month and a half into owning it, but I only see it when I'm trying to look for it. All in all, this monitor is a good choice for anyone looking into competitive gaming, especially when it goes on sale.

reviews.title: My fears were overblown...
reviews.comment:
Update: It's been about two months since I started using this, zero issues, still working like a champ, will try to update periodically.
I was initially very hesitant on buying this, my prior monitor was a Sceptre 32" curved gaming monitor (C326B-185RD), the Sceptre is a VA panel monitor, 1920x1080 with no HDR support.
I was hesitant about buying this one because it has an IPS panel, if you Google it you'll find lots of people saying IPS panels have two problems compared to VA panels:
1. "IPS glow"
2. Blacks would appear gray.
These issues caused some hesitation, I considered going with VA again but ended up going with this instead since I've never tried IPS for a gaming monitor. It turned out those fears were overblown, there is a TINY amount of IPS glow but it's at the four corners and it appears to be a viewing angle artifact, because I can make the glow move by moving my head around. It's definitely not a physical defect like "light bleeding" where the backlight is separating from the panel or something, it's only noticeable on a completely black screen (such as a loading screen) and even then it's barely noticeable, it looks like a very slight hue on the very tips of the four corners. The vast majority of the time you won't be in a situation to even be able to notice it, even the darkest areas in actual gameplay such as caves, or dark settings in movies, it's completely unnoticeable, and the blacks do appear as deep blacks, not grays.
I attached pictures I took of the Sceptre and Samsung side-by-side with the same images shown on each monitor: a black screen and SMPTE color bars, you be the judge. Note that I turned exposure down when taking these pictures, since these were taken in a room with all lights off, I took them in a room with all lights off to demonstrate how dark the blacks are and to highlight any glow. You can clearly see that the Sceptre's black screen looks almost light gray with a tremendous amount of glow around the edges, the colors on the Sceptre wash out as a result, the Sceptre is a VA panel that's supposed to be better at blacks than IPS panels are, yet it's far worse, the Samsung wins in both colors, blacks, and lesser glow.
My Samsung arrived with no defects and no dead pixels. I test that by using an all white screen and an all black screen for dead and live pixels respectively, the monitor has a self-diagnosis feature in the menu that shows you something similar to SMPTE color bars as well.
Compared to the Sceptre:
✅ This has the same screen size as the Sceptre but a much higher resolution so the pixel density is much higher, making things look less grainy than the Sceptre, very crisp.
✅ The IPS panel doesn't have noticeable ghosting or black smearing compared to the Sceptre's VA panel.
✅ The colors on the IPS panel are extremely vivid compared to Sceptre's VA panel. The color difference is startling, it breathes new life into even old games that appear washed out or dull in comparison.
✅ It has HDR10 support, the Sceptre is SDR only. HDR makes a huge difference, the layman's explanation for HDR is that things which are supposed to be bright (like sunlight or sunlit areas in games) become physically brighter by increasing the brightness/nits for the actual pixels themselves, which makes the game world pop. On monitors without HDR (SDR), all of the pixels are uniformly lit to the same brightness. I never thought I would need it but now I can't do without it.
✅ I use both Windows 11 and MacOS, the Sceptre had weird issues with MacOS on Apple Silicon, especially in clamshell mode where it would not wake MacOS from sleep or be recognized, this has none of those issues, works perfectly with MacOS on Apple Silicon via HDMI connected to a Belkin Thunderbolt 3 dock.
✅ Has much more configurability and robust settings than the Sceptre has.
What don't I like about it?
❌ Only having two inputs: it should have one DisplayPort and two HDMI at a minimum, instead it only has one of each which is a bit paltry and stingy.
❌ Putting the menu joystick on the back of the monitor, you have to fumble blindly for it.
❌ There's a feature to draw a fixed crosshair at the center of the screen, kind of "cheating" for gaming. While nice this feature was not implemented well, in that once you activate it it's on all the time, even when you're not playing a game, you're browsing the web with a crosshair at the center. If you want this eye sore out of the way you have to go back to the menu, navigate through two or so levels to turn it off and repeat when you want to turn it on. The menu joystick shows the same source menu if you toggle it left or right, instead of making both left and right do the same thing they couldn't reserve one of those for a quick on/off for the crosshair? I know you can probably toggle the virtual crosshair with Samsung's software but I don't really want to install that and have it running just for that.
If you do get it and you have Windows 11, after you have your new monitor in place and configured properly (the color "mode"), make sure you go to the HDR settings and click the link for the calibration tool to download it through Microsoft Store and use that to make an accurate color profile.
Overall very satisfied I chose this monitor and went through with it, a solid 9/10.

reviews.title: Amazing Monitor for 1440p gaming
reviews.comment:
Value for money – This monitor offers a tremendous amount of value for the cost. Typically, you would have to pay a lot of money for a 27-inch 1440p monitor with such a high refresh rate (as high as 300Hz), however this monitor provides similar performance at a fraction of the cost.
Build Quality – I find this monitor to be very solid overall. The stand is heavy-duty and the monitor itself does not feel cheaply made; it is a typical ASUS TUF design that is simple yet still focused on gaming. Additionally, the matte finish on the anti-glare screen greatly assists in keeping your eyes comfortable in brightly lit rooms.
Screen Quality – Absolutely wonderful. The Fast IPS panel allows for very vivid and true-to-life colors and the 1440p resolution on a 27-inch screen provides a very crisp image. The monitor covers approximately 95% of the DCI-P3 color space, so colors pop in games and everyday use. In addition, viewing angles are very wide and allow you to easily see what is happening on the screen regardless of how far away you are.
Performance – This is where the monitor really shines. The monitor is capable of running up to 300Hz with a response time of as low as 0.3ms, providing an incredibly fluid experience while playing fast paced games. It also supports Adaptive-Sync, FreeSync Premium, and G-SYNC compatible modes to provide a tear-free gaming experience even when frame rates vary.
Gaming Features – ASUS has included many useful tools for gaming on this monitor. These include ELMB Sync, Shadow Boost, GameVisual presets, Dynamic Crosshair, and ASUS DisplayWidget software which allows you to modify monitor settings directly from Windows rather than using the monitor’s on-screen buttons.
HDR and Brightness – It was nice to see HDR10 supported on this monitor. Although it is not the same level of HDR found on OLED monitors, it still adds a bit of extra brightness and depth to certain games.
Speakers – I found these built in monitor speakers to be quite surprising. While they will not replace real speakers or headphones, they are convenient if you need quick audio without connecting external devices.
Not Crazy About – While the monitor does have a good level of brightness, it is not extremely bright. Like most IPS panels, the contrast ratio is not as deep as VA or OLED monitors. I also found the on-screen menu to take a little time to get used to.
Overall – I truly believe this monitor is a beast for gaming. The combination of a 1440p resolution, an extremely high refresh rate, and a fast IPS response time makes everything look smooth and sharp, especially in fast paced competitive games.
Overall Rating: 9.5/10

reviews.title: THIS IS AN ABSOLUTE STEAL!
reviews.comment:
This thing is such a steal at $98. Although it is now $104 as of the making of this review. But still, for that price this monitor is a steal.
First, the size is 27 inches. An IPS panel this size at this price is great.
Second, the picture quality is great. Of course it's no OLED or QLED but for an IPS panel, this thing rocks. The color accuracy is on par with most IPS panel at higher price out of the box. But you can easily tweak these settings to get the best color accuracy out of this monitor. But then again, you can just turn on HDR and Auto HDR on Windows 11 to get the best possible color profile for this monitor, being it is HDR capable.
Third, it has adaptive sync with 144hz refresh rate and 1ms MPRT. So if you like gaming like I do, this monitor will definitely do the job. It actually punches above it's weight. I have the response time to normal setting in this monitor and I experience no noticeable lag when playing online FPS games even with MPRT is off. There's no noticeable ghosting either. Just absolute smooth gameplay. I also use this for video editing and music production and it has been great on both as well.
But one of the biggest reason why I purchased this monitor was the features it has for eye care. I needed a monitor that will help my eyes be less strained on pro long use of the PC. This monitor has Anti Flicker and is TuvRheinland Certified, which many monitors at this price point does not have.
Overall, the functionality and performance of this monitor definitely makes this monitor a steal at this price. Seems durable enough, not that you're going to punch this after rage quitting an online match but it definitely doesn't feel cheap and on par with most gaming monitors at around and above this price point. You can also VESA mount it if you don't like the plastic, but durable, stand.
For reference, I use this as an external monitor on my 2022 Razer Blade 15. I don't know why I waited this long to buy an external monitor for gaming, video editing and music production. But I'm glad I found this gem. Grab one before the manufacturer realize that this monitor should be more expensive and raise the price.

reviews.title: A Total Knockout — This Monitor Rewired My Entire Gaming Experience
reviews.comment:
Let me tell you — this SAMSUNG Odyssey G50D absolutely blew my mind. I’ve used a lot of monitors over the years, from budget displays to “premium” competitors, but the moment I powered this one on, it felt like stepping into an entirely new world. The mix of clarity, speed, and pure smoothness is unreal.
QHD + Fast IPS = Visual Heaven
The jump from Full HD to QHD isn’t subtle — it’s dramatic.
1.7x the pixel density may sound like a spec sheet number, but in real life?
It’s razor-sharp, pin-clean detail everywhere.
Textures in games look richer, UI elements look crisp, and the IPS panel gives gorgeous color from every angle. I can move around the room and the picture still holds its integrity.
180Hz + 1ms Response = Instant Reaction Power
This is the part that changed everything for me.
The 180Hz refresh rate is smooth beyond belief.
Fast movement feels natural, not smeared.
A genuine 1ms response time means enemies appear, and I literally react the second I see them. No blur. No ghosting. No lag. This thing is built for competitive play.
HDR400 That Actually Makes a Difference
The deeper blacks and brighter highlights are real — not “marketing HDR.”
I’m spotting enemies hiding in shadows that used to look like muddy darkness on my old display. The contrast jump is huge. Dark scenes look cinematic, not crushed.
FreeSync + G-Sync Compatible = Zero Disruptions
This monitor keeps sync locked perfectly. No tearing, no stutters, no screen hiccups. Whether I’m watching movies or running intense games, the motion stays buttery smooth.
Comfort Features That Really Do Matter
The adjustable stand is fantastic — tilt, swivel, height, whatever I need.
Eye Saver Mode genuinely helps during long sessions.
And the flicker reduction makes extended gameplay feel easier on my eyes.
Bottom Line:
This monitor hits everything I care about — sharpness, speed, color, contrast, comfort, and flawless motion. It outperforms displays that cost a lot more, and it brings a level of refinement I didn’t expect at this price.
If you want your games to feel faster, cleaner, smoother, and more immersive, this is the one. I’m totally thrilled with it.

Pros:

-Deep Blacks (See it, and you never want to go back to LCD or IPS monitor ever again, YOU'VE BEEN WARNED).

-3 Year Warranty ***Unclear for BURN-IN Related defects***

-$1000, if you got the money to purchase it, or you are an avid gamer and want the best visuals, if not better than a traditional GPU upgrade would provide, go for it. Otherwise, go for the 1440p OLED equivalents.

-Max Brightness: Full Window at ~250 nits, enough for low light or dark rooms, peaks ~1000 nits @2% window with the right settings.
-Text Fringing: not a huge deal given the size and resolution, but still worth mentioning, especially for productivity work.
Overall, if you are a hardcore gamer that wants the best visuals, gaming experience, as well as the best monitor you can buy for the money, I highly recommend it! WOLED technology has gotten a lot better in recent years, and it's great to see massive improvement when it comes to burn-in defects. However, it's still a potential problem and this monitor like most is still susceptible to it. It's also a $1000, definitely be aware and don't be abusive with it. With that said though, if you put yourself in the right mindset like using screen saver and using neo proxy the monitor comes with, keep all oled preventative features turned on, slowly work on habit building like when to use HDR for console gaming and desktop use, and treating the monitor well through thoughtful treatment and respect, you will not have to worry about burn-in anytime soon.
***UPDATE*** (12/21/25)
Make sure to update your monitor's firmware from MCM101 to MCM103. I used the USB-C to laptop method. Fixes the visual static noise issues on my monitor when HDR is enabled, now works flawlessly.
reviews.author: Daniel Simecek

reviews.title: Beautiful monitor!
reviews.comment: If you buy this around the lowest price of $799 it’s a steal! Connected it to my new M5 MacBook via OWC Thunderbolt 4 cable and it’s running at constant 165hz with no issues on MacOS Tahoe! The screen is absolutely beautiful! Way better than my old Samsung M80C monitor! Very bright and vivid once you dial in the right settings! Build quality is great and the controls are very easy to navigate! It’s nice and versatile that I can also connect my PS5 Pro to it as well and switch between those two devices seamlessly!
reviews.author: mike canvas

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.comment: Expensive, high end, and utterly stunning monitor.  Speed, color, detail, if this monitor does not please, there is no hope for you!
reviews.author: Bluemanticore

reviews.title: Trueblack WOLED
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/C1oTJVQ1LCL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/71NKt2xgY9L._SY256.jpg Edit: one week of ownership after purchasing from Amazon Used official and I have the worst screen retention I have ever seen on a display. reviews.author: Nathaniel

reviews.title: My first OLED
reviews.comment: This is a lovely viewing OLED for those who want crisp true black image and clarity for a smaller form factor. It's bright, crisp fast and looks marvelous for my games. But what i bought it for was movies on my computer, and there is no more bloom, no fades and rough outlines of my older IPS and VA panel monitors. It's a decent size screen for desks with good power, and crisp clear visuals, and a nice light weight. Good options for HDMI, Displayport, headphones or speakers, and a few USB connections.
reviews.author: Alex

reviews.title: Elite Display for Gaming and Creation – Absolutely Worth It!
reviews.comment:
The ASUS ROG Swift PG27UCDM is nothing short of breathtaking. The 27” 4K QD-OLED panel delivers stunning visual clarity, true blacks, and incredibly vibrant colors. Whether I’m gaming, editing photos, or watching HDR content, the color accuracy is top-tier and the contrast makes every scene feel immersive. Out of the box, the calibration is excellent, with no need for tweaks. The 240 Hz refresh rate paired with the ultra-fast response time makes fast-paced gameplay unbelievably smooth—no ghosting or tearing at all. This monitor truly feels like the perfect fusion of performance and beauty.
Functionality is just as impressive. It supports DisplayPort 2.1 and HDMI 2.1, making it future-proof for next-gen GPUs and consoles. The USB-C port with 90W power delivery is super convenient for laptop users like me. The stand is fully adjustable and feels solid, while the screen’s anti-glare coating does a great job even in bright rooms. Even the RGB lighting is tastefully done. Yes, it’s a premium price, but for what you get—240Hz at 4K, flawless OLED visuals, and unmatched versatility—it’s absolutely worth every penny.
reviews.author: Thong Nguyen

reviews.title: Great, but not perfect.
reviews.comment:
No flickering.  240hz, displayport 2.1 (uncompressed), Dolby Vision, KVM switch, and 1/4" tripod/screw for camera mounting makes this monitor a beast.  You can hook a Xbox and Two PCs and switch between them with one mouse and keyboard flawlessly (and switch between speakers automatically too, if you use the monitor's 3.5mm jack).
The only downside of this monitor is that it uses a Triangular QD-OLED subpixel layout since it's newer technology (versus traditional RGB stripe like some cheaper 4K monitors and IPS monitors), so fonts in Windows don't appear as clear in as they would on other 4K monitors (like the Strix XG27UCS).  However, this is only for windows fonts and not game fonts, so text in games will still be crisp.  It's a very small downside (and one you may not even notice if I didn't say this) but some people care about this.
The other downside is that it doesn't have built-in speakers, which actually matters a lot to me.  For $5 they could've added a single mono speaker and they would've been enough for me (I like having it as a backup or in cases where i don't want to lug speakers around, or in case I ever want to mount it in a wall -- who wants to attach separate speakers for a wall-mounted display?? Nobody, and all cheaper models of Asus monitors even have speakers).
If you want the best monitor for the money, though, go with with bad boy.  The extra money is well spent. I had the Strix XG27UCS before this, so I already had 4K, but this is a huge upgrade other than the font thing.
I wish they also made the ports on the side instead of pointing down, but you can fix this problem with some shirt extension cables I guess, maybe (idk if they make DSP80 extensions that don't hinder anything, but I'll look).
I'm also having a problem with windows not being able to turn HDR on (even in games), but I'm 99% sure it's some software error I'm having, since it was working before and only stopped working after windows detected this monitor as two monitors, but I wanted to note this anyway.
It's a great monitor though.  Only thing I don't care for is the light on the bottom (would've rather had speakers than that light).  The lights on the back are pretty neat, but again, I'd rather have speakers or smoother fonts.
Biggest thing by far is the built in KVM switch.  I've used KVM switches before but I never had one built into the monitor like this -- wicked cool and useful.
The menu isn't very intuitive, but you'll figure it out. Most menus are worse. Just don't get annoyed and break the button or something, before you learn it.
reviews.author: Amazon Guy

reviews.title: Premium OLED Gaming Monitor With Excellent Motion Clarity
reviews.comment: The ASUS ROG Swift PG27UCDM delivers exactly what you would expect from a flagship gaming monitor: extremely sharp 4K image quality, outstanding motion clarity at 240Hz, and near-instant response time that makes fast games feel exceptionally smooth. The QD-OLED panel gives deep blacks, vivid color, and strong HDR performance, while text clarity is noticeably improved compared to earlier OLED generations. Build quality feels premium, and the included connectivity options make it flexible for both PC and console use. It is expensive, but for anyone wanting top-tier gaming and image quality in a 27-inch size, it offers excellent overall value.
reviews.author: Arthur

reviews.title: Great
reviews.comment:
My alienware 4k monitor (AW2725Q) died after little over a year. Decided to get this as replacement.
I set to hdr 400 true black and games look amazing.  Strange that gaming hdr setting has less punch in games, but 400 true black pops. Gaming hdr is brighter than 400 so I like this setting when watching YouTube.
Great monitor.
reviews.author: Rob

reviews.title: Great display upgrade for multiple uses
reviews.comment: Coming from an old 27" UHD, this is next level in terms of image quality, clarity, etc. Checks all the boxes in a display you could wish for. I was originally thinking the 32" would be better but after reading around the 27" seems to be an ideal size. I appreciate the anti-burn-in features as I also use this as my main display for work and general use beyond gaming. It also serves as a TV when I'm just chilling in the office. Does everything well in any scenario. Integrated speakers would have been nice but I added a set of Creative Pebbles using some reward $ and everything works well together. The desk projection of the logo is cool but it would be nice to be able to customize colors, etc., unless I missed something. All around great display.
reviews.author: Doug

reviews.title: Best gaming monitor I’ve ever owned!
reviews.comment:
The Samsung 27” Odyssey OLED G6 (G60SD) is an outstanding gaming monitor. The screen quality is absolutely amazing. The QD-OLED panel delivers vibrant, accurate colors with deep blacks and incredible contrast. Everything looks sharp and smooth in QHD, and the 360Hz refresh rate with the 0.03ms response time makes gameplay feel incredibly fluid and responsive.
One of the biggest surprises for me is how comfortable it is for long gaming sessions. I can play for hours and my eyes don’t feel strained or fatigued. The anti-glare coating really helps, and the overall brightness and color balance are easy on the eyes while still looking vivid and immersive.
The color scheme and overall design are sleek and modern. It looks great on the desk and feels premium. The built-in cooling system is a nice bonus for long-term performance, and the 3 year warranty adds peace of mind.
For everything this monitor offers OLED quality, 360Hz performance, FreeSync Premium Pro support, and solid build quality, this is a great price. If you’re serious about gaming and want top-tier visuals and performance, this monitor is perfect!
reviews.author: Jennifer Reed

reviews.title: 360HZ OLED BEAST!
reviews.comment: I waited over a year to write this review and honestly it's going to be a short one because this monitor has been flawless! I mostly play competitive FPS games, COD, counter strike, Apex, etc. Let me say this monitor improved my gameplay more than upgrading my whole computer to the current generation of top tier gaming hardware. I also own a similar LG monitor and LG 65" OLED TV but this stays as my main display. Build quality is excellent, colors, clarity are insane. Every game I played looked incredible and the movements felt so much better!
reviews.author: Chris H.

reviews.title: BEST GAMING MONITOR EVER!
reviews.comment: Very easy to put together right out the box and easy to set up! The games I play on my pc play at a much higher frame rate than they did before this monitor (and this is on max settings). Highly recommend! 5/5 stars.
reviews.author: Patrick

reviews.title: Overall 10/10
reviews.comment: Amazing picture quality , Inky blacks and amazing response times. Only con i’ve found so far is the occasional oled care feature that basically turns the screen off and back on. I haven’t learned how to de activate or put so that it can only be manually activated. One thing to have in mind is that the stand that it comes with is screwless so if you have a monitor arm and no extra M4 screws to attach the plate i didn’t see any in my box , maybe it’s a QC issue and i didn’t get mine but im not able to say. HDR experience is really good only quirk i found is that my speakers that are connected to the monitor don’t work while HDR is on. I use it with decent natural lighting shining on it and I haven’t had any issues with reflections or the magenta tint many people talk about in reviews. Still 10/10 if you want the best of the best OLED and high refresh rate , this has the same panel as the Alienware AW2725DF and the MSI QRX27Q1PXQD but is a little cheaper couldn’t recommend more 👍 (Also lighting looks really good bouncing off any white wall)
reviews.author: Hugo A.

reviews.title: Power button broke and doesn't work.
reviews.comment:
Not worth the $700+ I paid. The power button on the back of the monitor broke from minimal use. Very disappointed in this purchase and Samsung. I really liked the monitor and thought it was a great upgrade but if the power button is at risk of breaking so easily it's not worth it. I wouldn't recommend any of these Samsung monitors that have this defective flimsy/cheaply made joystick power button. The only time I would recommend it is if you have the remote controller to bypass using the flimsy/cheaply made joystick power button. My monitor did not come with a remote controller. To make matters worse if you search this issue online you'll see it's a common issue and the saddest part is people online clearly state that Samsung will refuse to fix it and claim that their warranty doesn't cover it. What a joke. And even if they fix it it's still going to be replaced with another flimsy/cheaply made joy stick power button that is only bound to break again in the future. I don't like getting burned. This will be the last Samsung monitor I ever buy in my lifetime from them nor will I never recommend it to anyone I know. It's a crappy feeling when I've been a loyal customer for most of my life and spent thousands of dollars on their products (tvs, Galaxy buds, ssds, nvme ssds, etc) but this isn't a product worth purchasing. Stay far away from these monitors that have this cheaply made joystick power button or be prepared to be let down when it breaks.
As for the monitor itself it is beautiful and oled is a great experience. The refresh rate is superb as well as the image quality. But if it can't even last several months without the power button breaking then what's the point of even owning it?
reviews.author: Kevin

reviews.title: A premium and quality monitor that’s in it’s own class!
reviews.comment: This monitor is awesome! The size and curve create an immersive experience like nothing else. Setup was easy and I’m extremely happy that I didn’t need any tools or Allen wrenches. The image quality is amazing in games and the over performance of the screen exceeded my expectations. It’s a lot to look at and can strain your eyes at first, but after adjusting to it I can’t imagine using anything else. Definitely worth the price if you have the hardware to run it at it’s full potential.
reviews.author: Randall Ouellette Jr.

reviews.title: Love this monitor!
reviews.comment: Wow!  I should have gotten one of these long ago!  Works beautifully and it takes the place of 3 big screens.  And easy on my eyes!
reviews.author: Kindle Customer

reviews.title: Great monitor. The rest, Amazon should be ashamed!
reviews.comment: When these went on sale it was like someone was listening. I had been using a 4K TV for the last year as an "Experiment" for my monitor. The problem with TVs are the font, it was very hard for me to see it. I ordered two since like 2 monitors for productivity. I received them yesterday and set one up. Great monitor. The resolution (font), quality and screen size are great. I woke up early to get the other one up and running and off to my office I went. Here is the reason for the one star. The second box was beat up, holes and LOTS of tape. I opened it and couldn't believe my eyes. The contents, stand etc. was on top of the monitor screen. Packing material was missing, booklets etc. It was obvious to me that this was a return, basically everything had been thrown into the box and taped up. Finally got through to someone at Amazon Support, Sorry to digress, but it sure seems that Amazon is trying as hard as possible to hide the ability to get support from a real person. Anyway I finally got a hold of someone, they issued a refund and sent a letter to the company that supplies the hardware. My question; you can obviously see the distressed box and with holes and things rattling inside. Nothing should be rattling in a monitor box. This SHOULD NEVER HAVE BEEN SHIPPED TO ME full stop! Very disappointed with Amazon!
reviews.author: GrumpyandDopey

reviews.title: Absolute stunner of a monitor
reviews.comment: This behemoth is an absolute beauty. It looks stunning, is perfectly sized, and mounted easily and securely to the heavy duty monitor arm I purchased alongside it. The 1000R curve is perfection. I tried one with an 1800R and did not like the angle at all. I couldn’t find a comfortable distance to view the screen from. This feels perfect from any distance. I wired it up to both HDMI and DP on my one PC to simulate a dual monitor setup. Coming from a dual monitor setup, it just feels better than using the whole screen during my work day. But then I can turn off PBP for gaming and turn off one of the display panels in Windows. And Windows is smart enough to remember my monitor config when I swap between the two. As for gaming, it’s incredible to see one running across this whole thing. Some games aren’t exactly widescreen compatible, but most I’ve tried at least have a 32:9 resolution available. And I can certainly see the difference of the 240hz. Everything is so smooth, even just scrolling a webpage. Games do take a little more power than before, but I’m on a 3080 and it’s handled everything I’ve thrown at it like a champ. I am very happy with this purchase especially since I caught it at $799.
reviews.author: Deadman875

reviews.title: Good monitor
reviews.comment: It works good. At first I thought the screen was messed up. I calibrated it and it fixed the issue its been fine since.
reviews.author: LaRowick Harrrison

reviews.title: Amazing monitor, would buy again.
reviews.comment: Incredible picture quality and latency, I was worried that the 165Hz wouldn’t be enough but it’s amazing for 4k gaming. Coming from a 1080P 144Hz IPS monitor, this monitor makes every game look like the game trailer. Incredibly smooth picture in every game I’ve played including Red Dead 2, GTA V, Arma 3, Kingdom Come Deliverance 2, forza Horizon 5. I’m glad I didn’t spend the extra money for the MSI 31UPX, I only game with the monitor and don’t need a built in KVM switch since I don’t run dual monitors. Also I get more than enough bandwidth out of the DP1.4 for 4k gaming over 165 FPS. I’m running a 9800X3D and RX7900XTX and I couldn’t be happier with this monitor. OLED Pros: - Amazing picture quality, color, and latency - Great price for a major upgrade (sub $800) - 3 year factory burn warranty - You can decide when to do the OLED care to avoid burn in, only takes a few minutes and you can skip it if you’re in the middle of important tasks or games. OLED Cons: - I have to turn up the brightness in some games, the true black on this monitor is TRULY BLACK, if you’re in a dark game you may have to turn up your gamma or your brightness, I think the newer generation OLEDs are slightly brighter but it isn’t bad and actually adds to the intensity of certain games like KCD2 when you’re sneaking around at night. - Controls on the back underside of monitor, I wish they would add a cheap remote so I don’t have to reach underneath to skip the OLED care. I gamed all day on this thing and the OLED care came up twice, it’s very easy to skip or you can just take bathroom/food breaks and let it do its thing when you want. People made the OLED care out to be some kind of major issue and it’s not. (Maybe for MLG guys it might be an issue but if you like semi competitive gaming or story driven games it’s not an issue) - Very short power cable (2.5 Feet long)
reviews.author: Floody Fontana

reviews.title: Msi mag 321up QD OLED 4K review
reviews.comment: This a great monitor it’s a night and day difference between other panels, the colors pop much more vivid than my current 4k mini led monitors. The deep colors make gaming so much more immersive. For me it was between this and the rog 4k oled but that one was much more expensive plus I’ve always liked Msi monitors my first ever gaming monitor was from them they offer some amazing products. This monitor does everything you’ll need although I did wish that it came with built in speakers that would be my only gripe. Easy to assemble very sturdy has a height and tilt adjustable stand that comes in handy. I would be interested in comparing that flat panel to the curved panel as well to compare viewing angles as I feel the flat panels are less flexible. All in all great monitor for a great price would definitely recommend.
reviews.author: Darryl Harris

reviews.title: Stunning visuals and smooth performance for gaming and work
reviews.comment: I’ve been using the MSI MAG 321UP QD-OLED monitor for a few weeks now, and it’s been an absolute joy for both gaming and daily use. The 32-inch 4K display is gorgeous—colors are incredibly vibrant thanks to the QD-OLED technology, with deep blacks and excellent contrast that really make games and movies pop. The sharpness at UHD resolution is perfect for multitasking and creative work too. What really stands out is the 165Hz refresh rate combined with Adaptive Sync. Gameplay is super smooth and responsive, with no noticeable screen tearing or stuttering. Whether I’m playing fast-paced shooters or immersive RPGs, the experience feels fluid and immersive. Setup was straightforward, and the monitor’s design is sleek and modern. It has plenty of connectivity options which make hooking up multiple devices a breeze. If you’re looking for a high-end monitor that delivers stunning picture quality and buttery smooth performance, this MSI QD-OLED is definitely worth considering. It’s a noticeable upgrade from traditional LCDs and really enhances the gaming and viewing experience.
reviews.author: Kyle

reviews.title: "Panel Protect" maintenance feature *always* interrupts my work day.
reviews.comment: This monitor has a "panel protect" feature that makes the monitor unusuable for several minutes for some kind of maintenance task.  I used to use this as a gaming monitor and now I use it at work.  I thought it would run its "panel protect" maintenance at night, but the damn thing keeps interrupting my work with this automatic task that makes it unusable until it's done. I'm writing this now after I literally came back to work from a bathroom break to find that my monitor is unusable. Don't buy this.  I have a second 4K OLED monitor from a different brand that has no such problem. Yes, the display quality is good, but there are much better products available. Not recommended for gaming, office work, or any other purpose.
reviews.author: Vivian River Langdon

reviews.title: Excellent Monitor
reviews.comment: This is an excellent O-LED monitor. Color & pixels are great, and the Refresh Rate is more than enough. When running 4k on games the monitor provides stunning colors and runs smoothly with no screen tearing or artifacts. It works smoothly and is very easy to set up or customize how ever you like. Also the stand it comes with provides plenty of room to move around as needed. The Panel Protect feature does not impede normal use, and if needed can be set to 16 hour intervals instead of 4 hours or done manually. Also came with an 8k DP and 8k HDMI cable which is useful as I have multiple devices to take advantage of the different inputs. This is a great entry level monitor for 4k O-LED with a reasonable refresh rate for games.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Durable, Spacious, and Perfect for Gaming or Work
reviews.comment: I’ve been using the Corsair MM350 PRO mouse pad for a few weeks, and it has completely upgraded my desk setup. The extended design gives plenty of room for both my keyboard and mouse, allowing smooth and uninterrupted movement during gaming or work. The surface is premium and spill-proof, so I don’t have to worry about accidental drinks, and the textured fabric provides excellent control for precise mouse movements. The edges are stitched and very durable, preventing fraying even with heavy use. It stays firmly in place without slipping, making it reliable for intense sessions. Overall, this is a high-quality, spacious mouse pad that combines durability, comfort, and functionality.
reviews.author: Kyle

reviews.title: Massive, high-quality, and truly spill-proof!
reviews.comment: I am extremely impressed with the Corsair MM350 PRO. The size is perfect—it easily fits my keyboard and mouse with plenty of room to spare for low-DPI gaming. The "spill-proof" claim is no joke; liquid beads right up on the surface and wipes away without leaving a stain. It feels premium, the edges are stitched so there's no fraying, and the glide is incredibly smooth. Definitely a top-tier pad for any setup!
reviews.author: Bartek

reviews.title: Just how big is it? (See picture)
reviews.comment: This mousepad is incredible and I have to thank my fiancé for it. She put the idea in my head and I'm glad she did because before she brought it up, it was never even a thought in my mind. When she bought it for me, she asked if I thought the MM350 Pro Extended XL would be too big at a whopping 36.6" x 15.75" but it turned out to be perfect. I have a hybrid gaming machine / workstation setup for which I have a lot of tools and toys. So when you see those dimensions you may think to yourself, "Ok, that's a hair over 3 feet in length but just how big is it?" If you check the image attached, you'll see the Corsair MM350 Pro spread across a 47" wide desk. On top of it, I've placed the following items: - Logitech G602 (Mouse) - Logitech G512 Carbon (Keyboard) - Logitech F310 (Gamepad/Controller - Razer Tartarus Pro (Keypad) - Wacom Intuos Pro Medium (Graphic Tablet) - Wacom Pro Pen & Case (Tablet Stylus - Main) - Wacom Grip Pen & Stand (Tablet Stylus - Backup) - Focusrite Scarlet 2i2 (Audio Recording Interface) As a quick recap, that's a mouse, full keyboard, keypad, gamepad, audio interface, 15" graphic tablet and two separate pens pretty comfortably. Granted the tablet is only there when it's not in use, everything else can set comfortably without interfering with anything else. The thickness is pretty beefy at 4mm but personally I think it's perfect. Less might feel cheap but more might be less comfortable but these are suppositions. I love the construction of the mousepad as it feels well made, durable, soft, smooth and comfortable. My mouse GLIDES over the surface unlike anything I've ever experienced. The rubberized bottom is nice for keeping the mat in place no matter what I'm doing. Despite the mouse's ability to move effortlessly around the surface, the rest of my peripherals stay firmly in place which is especially great when using the Razer Tartarus Pro & Wacom Intuos Pro M for my work in Illustrator & Photoshop as I am able to use both within full range of motion without either peripheral moving on the surface of the mousepad (especially important for linework and complex path/shape building!). I haven't had a chance to test my forthcoming Razer Basilisk Ultimate vs 20k DPI sensor on this surface yet but it feels great and effortless whether I'm clicking on shapes or heads. It also ties the workspace together nicely and makes it looks neat and sharp. My only complaint about this mousepad is on this front and I didn't see a single person mention it: if you do not keep an exceptionally tidy workspace, do not get the black finish. My home office is currently shared as a thoroughfare between myself, two other humans, two dogs and three cats. Despite having a dedicated can of compressed air at the ready and a vacuum designed to stand up to the specific hassle that is constant animal hair shedding, the black is so striking that even a single dog hair or dust molecule contrasts so heavily that the smart money says your could see it from space. This is not the mousepad's fault obviously, just wanted to give other pet owners a buyer beware.
reviews.author: KC

reviews.title: Genuinely great mousepad
reviews.comment: Softest and smoothest mouse pad i’ve ever had; and i’ve gone through about 10. It’s so large and covers everything, absolutely great glide, the edges are smooth and don’t hurt your wrist / forearms. If you like having a clean setup, ample room, and a mouse that glides like butter; this is for you. I’d recommend getting it on sale though… lol
reviews.author: Widum Boise

reviews.title: Perfect mouse pad
reviews.comment: Easily one of my favorite mouse pads. Have had and used mine for over a year with daily gaming, and no issues. Good quality, it lays flat and cleans off easily. Mouse tracks perfectly on it. The size is great and covers a large portion of my desk, I especially like how wide the mat is. The thickness is nice and gives soft and durable feel. Corsair is always a good option.
reviews.author: Ashley M.

reviews.title: Pretty.
reviews.comment: These fans are my go to when I’m looking for pretty and functionality. They are bright and colorful! And the airflow is great.
reviews.author: Christina Griffith

reviews.title: Looks greats
reviews.comment: Looks great and seems to work well like most all corsair products
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Awesome!
reviews.comment: Love these fans!
reviews.author: abraham jimenez

reviews.title: Excelente producto
reviews.comment: Excelente producto sin embargo buscaría una alternativa en la siguiente bilis por algo más moderno
reviews.author: Tian Echeverry

reviews.title: Great fans in the ecosystem
reviews.comment: As long as you are in the corsair ecosystem they work fantastically. Just use a commander pro(the hub that comes with their higher end AIO's)
reviews.author: Justin H.

reviews.title: Watermelon head approved
reviews.comment:
This is literally the only headset in my life I've ever worn that actually fits my massive head. (For context I am 6'4, 295lbs). I am in shock. That said I have a massive head so
I've tried virtuoso XT, nova pro wireless, g50x, audeze maxwell, rog delta II, all had to be returned due to being too tight at the top of my head (I am extremely sensitive to clamp force).  There are no "big head" reviewers that really have a big head like mine. Each time I try a headset based on a review saying "SO COZY SO COMFY!!" Is a person with a tiny head and they never fit or work for me. Every single person I watched that review the Kithara made fun of the extra tall frame, saying they look like alien antennas and goofy. Nope, THIS is what makes the Kithara actually usable for me. It looks like a normal headset on my head and my ears actually fit into the cups comfortably. I've been testing these out the last few nights since receiving them and been blown away by the sound quality (my first pair of hifiman headphones) and the COMFORT. These are so light on the head, I gamed for 4 hours straight the other night and didn't even notice the headphones. That's unheated of for me where every other gaming headphone I've used I've simply tolerated in short bursts due to ear pain or head pain after 30min to an hour.
These have actually enabled me to game at night again because I don't have to use my speakers only anymore! And it comes with a mic for party chat! (Does sound a little nasally but decent clarity still)
Definitely pair this with a solid amp/dac (I'm driving them with the Fosi K7 and switch between Ps5/PC, trust me absolutely worth it) as the included adapter can't quite drive the volume high enough on its own imo.
If you have an unconventially large melon for a head like me, look no further. It's a pricy investment between this and an amp, worth it to finally own a pair of headphones I actually WANT to use and CAN use for an extended period.

reviews.title: Great first entry level midfi/ audiophile headphones/ headset
reviews.comment:
This will be a great upgrade for customers accustomed to "gamer brand headset" caliber sound. The Kithara, particularly with a DAC/ amp, is entry level audiophile sound that frankly blows the Maxwell 2 away in audio quality with relative ease as well as being less expensive and considerably lighter and more comfortable. I think the Kithara is probably based on HiFiMan's Ananda line and has similar tuning to some of their best high end audiophile headphones like the Arya Stealth and HE1000se that are well known to be S-tier for gaming. The Kithara obviously not at the technical level of those more expensive models, but a less detailed and spacious version of that available at only $299 with some nice accessories is still an exceptional deal. I've tested the Kithara with a couple of DAC/ amps, the Schiit Gunnr and EF600 using a PC, PS5 Pro, and Switch 2, and all sounded great. It should be noted Xbox only gets 3.5mm jack compatibility through the controller, so Xbox owners may be better off with the Maxwell 2, which also has Atmos support.
You may need to get some extension cables for a console depending on how far away you sit from your display for the headphone and mic cables, which can be found cheap here on Amazon. The mic is a bit sensitive, but you can address that by turning it away from your mouth and also keeping it at a decent distance away from your mouth, which improves the sound significantly.
I'm curious to see the reception for this product because people from the audiophile camp are going to tend to be surprised it's only $299 whereas the Astro and Turtle Beach customers who would probably benefit most from upgrading to the Kithara might think it's too expensive and aren't sure if open back, wired headphones are a good idea for gaming (they definitely are). Although I recommend a DAC/ amp given the nature of planar drivers just need more power to move than dynamic drivers and tend to sound fantastic with extra juice, you could probably get away with a relatively cheap/ small one. I use a Schiit Gunnr with my consoles, but I think a ~$100 DAC/ amp like the Topping DX1 would probably do the job fine given these are more sensitive and thus easier to drive than most planars. It's on the polar opposite end of the spectrum compared to low sensitivity ravenous power vampires like the HE6se or Susvara.
I'll note I got a very early batch unit with the loose headband issue seen in early units sent to reviewers that was supposed to have been fixed before final release to the public but apparently wasn't in mine, but this was quickly addressed with a replacement. I'm not going to take a star or two off for that because it doesn't represent the design most people have and what I now have. That shouldn't affect anyone after that first batch shipped that I initially received. If you do have that problem, it's a defect that wasn't supposed to be in the final version. Just get it replaced for a unit without that defect.

reviews.title: good general purpose PSU, but im wary of its lack of an efficiency rating
reviews.comment: i have a few cheaper PSUs that i use for miscellaneous PC projects, but recently i've needed one that was at least 850W. most importantly for me, i wanted one that's modular, since unfortunately cheap PSUs tend to be hardwired since they're usually included for OEM builds that don't need to be configured. this looks to be a good fit for what i'm doing, and checks all of those boxes. i haven't had any issues using it over the past few hours in a basic low-end build with some high-wattage IO, and it feels very good quality given the price and the fact that i've never used parts from this company (although i have used their cases recently, and they are surprisingly great quality) however, i'm a little wary of using it with any high-end or very demanding parts, particularly high-wattage or expensive GPUs. on the surface, it *looks* perfectly suitable for that use case -- the modular cables feel like they are made well, and overall the build quality is pretty good. but notice how the listing and the packaging has no mention of an efficiency rating (80 PLUS bronze, silver, gold, etc)! it's a voluntary standard, so maybe this was just a cost-cutting measure to help it reach this price point. but without even the most basic consumer standard rating for PSUs, it makes me a little nervous to power an expensive GPU or something like that with this unit. that's my main reason for giving this 4 stars, i just don't feel comfortable using it for anything high-end like i might want to with a more well-known name brand PSU. maybe another reviewer will do some more extensive power analysis to see how it handles current spikes, and that could sway me a bit more -- but until then, i don't want to risk plugging this into a $1000 GPU and possibly frying it upon hitting max load overall, i think this is a promising PSU! but i would just be very wary of using it with expensive components for now, at least until the quality of its power draw characteristics are measured and validated by someone with the equipment (and disposable high-end components) to do so. otherwise, for more basic builds or general purpose usage, i think it's pretty good!
