reviews.title: Excellent Budget AIO With Great Cooling, Quiet Fans, and a Surprisingly Premium Screen
reviews.comment:
The Jungle Leopard PF 360 CPU Water AIO turned out to be a much better cooler than I expected for the price. The build quality out of the box feels solid, and installation on my Intel i7‑14700K was straightforward. The kit includes brackets for Intel 115X, 1200, and 1700 sockets, along with AMD mounting hardware. Setting the bracket size for LGA 1700 was simple, and attaching the backplate through the motherboard was just as easy. The pump head bracket twists and locks into place cleanly, and choosing the correct LGA 1700 spacers made securing the pump to the CPU quick and hassle‑free.
The included 360mm fans were a pleasant surprise. They’re very quiet, even under load, and the RGB implementation looks fantastic. The 360 fans has four infinity‑mirror accents on the front plus full-length infinity mirrors along both sides, giving the radiator a premium look. I usually replace stock AIO fans, but in this case I don’t feel the need to—the performance and aesthetics are already excellent.
Cooling performance is strong as well. At idle, my 14700K sits between 36–46°C across the cores. Under a full 100% burn‑in load, temperatures rise to 60–70°C, and none of the cores hit thermal throttling. For a CPU known to run hot, that’s impressive for an AIO in this price range.
The pump‑head screen is another highlight. It’s removable and can be mounted in three different orientations. I chose the vertical position with the tubes entering from the bottom, which limits the screen’s rotation options, but it still ended up exactly how I wanted it. If you want the screen oriented vertically downward, you’ll need the tubes coming in from the side due to the pin alignment—but the flexibility is still better than many AIOs.
The software worked with some issues on my system. The interface isn’t immediately intuitive, so I watched a couple of YouTube videos to get familiar with it. Once I understood the layout, I was able to upload video clips or screen captures, add system stats like CPU temperature, and customize the screen with various widgets. It supports multiple image and video formats, and so far it hasn’t conflicted with any of my other RGB software.  One item I noticed if I used some animated videos, the screen saver would not execute for windows.  Since I am concerned about screen burn in, I wanted the screen saver to work so I had to go with still images which did not affect the windows screen saver.  Hopefully this will be addressed in future software updates.  Another option I hope they will add to future software updates is some sort of picture and video shuffle so the screen could change over time.
Overall, this AIO delivers excellent cooling, quiet fans, great RGB, and a customizable display—all at a very competitive price. It exceeded my expectations in almost every category.

reviews.title: Very good performance at a reasonable price, you may need to upgrade the firmware
reviews.comment: This is a M.2 SSD with very good performance at a reasonable price. I am using quite a few of these on Raspberry Pi 5 boards (using the official Pi M.2 NVMe HAT+). Despite the Pi only having a single PCIe lane, I'm seeing over 850MByte/sec on sustained sequential writes - a huge upgrade from the 30Mbyte/sec I was getting from a SDXC card in the Pi 5's SD slot. Using the benchmark from the Pibenchmarks site, it reports a performance score of 56968 which would seem to put it in the top 20 of all of their storage benchmarks. Note that this is a cache-less card (no DRAM onboard) so it relies on a small SLC buffer as a front-end to its main TLC storage. It normally requests a HMB (host memory buffer) from the operating system. Raspberry Pi OS does not provide this, so the speeds reported above are the raw speeds writing to the card. Using this card in a system that supports HMB and with more than the one PCIe lane the Raspberry Pi 5 provides should improve performance beyond my test results. The card ships with an older version of firmware (I received one with version 12000103 and three with version 12000102). I don't know what was fixed or changed between the those and the latest 12000104 firmware, so I decided to update them all to 12000104. One potential issue is that these are Dell OEM drives, so there's no updates or support from Kioxia. However, Dell does have the latest firmware available on their web site. I believe the review rules prevent a direct link, but if you search Dell's support page for "XYVG7" you'll find the firmware revision 12000104 update. It is Windows-only and you need some way of attaching this card to your computer to do the update. I used a StarTech adapter I previously purchased from Amazon. It does not support the 2230 form factor of this card, so I used tape to hold the card in place on the board while doing the firmware update. If your system already has an M.2 slot, this will be a lot easier. I don't know if the update utility will run on a non-Dell system - I used an Optiplex 9020.

reviews.title: One Mouse to Bind Them, in the Long Hours of the Desk
reviews.comment: It was the winter of the endless scroll, when the days in River Grove stretched thin and pale as old parchment and the light from the monitor became the only sun we knew, that my old mouse—poor, faithful thing—began its slow betrayal. Clicks faltered like the last breath of a dying Rohirrim steed; the wheel spun loose and reckless, sending spreadsheets cascading into chaos as though the very order of Middle-earth had unraveled; the cursor wandered with the aimless grief of a man who has lost his king. I sat there in the dim room above the garage, wrist aching like the shoulder that once bore the weight of Andúril, staring at the screen while deadlines crept closer, silent and inexorable as the shadow over Mordor. Then the Logitech MX Master 4 arrived, graphite-dark as the armor of Isildur’s line, shaped not for haste but for endurance, its curves rising like the hills of the Shire remade for the hand of a weary scribe. I took it up and felt the weight settle—not heavy, but certain, as though the mouse itself understood the gravity of long labor. The MagSpeed wheel turned under my thumb with the smooth inevitability of the Anduin in flood, ultra-fast when the document must race to its end, precise when a single pixel demanded mercy. The haptic feedback thrummed beneath my fingers like the deep pulse of the earth when the Ents march—subtle, insistent, alive. Every scroll, every gesture carried the quiet authority of a thing forged to outlast lesser tools. It paired without ceremony—Bluetooth to the laptop, Logi Bolt to the desktop—crossing between machines as swiftly as the Eagles bore Gandalf from the tower, no fumbling, no oaths sworn in frustration. The side buttons waited like loyal vassals: one to summon the hidden application switcher, another to gesture across screens as though drawing maps of realms unseen. The gesture button itself became my quiet command—thumb pressed, fingers sweeping, and windows arranged themselves in obedient array, the way the hosts of the West might have arrayed themselves upon the Pelennor Fields. And when the battery whispered low, the USB-C cord drank from the wall like a pilgrim at the fountains of Imladris, three hours of life from a single minute’s charge. I have worked with it now through the gray mornings when the snow muffled every sound outside, through the late nights when the house slept and only the cursor moved, through the sudden urgent revisions that once would have left me cursing the heavens. It does not slip. It does not tire. It endures, as the light of Eärendil endures above the storm, a small fierce companion against the gathering hours. If your days are measured in documents and deadlines, in the slow turning of wheels both literal and metaphorical, take this MX Master 4. It is not mere plastic and circuit; it is covenant between hand and machine, a shield against the tedium of the long watch, the fellowship your desk has hungered for in its quiet exile. Ten stars out of five, though the heavens ration light to fewer. I would carry it into the Cracks of Doom itself and fear no misclick. 🖱️🧙‍♂️📜🌑
reviews.author: Donald.50

reviews.title: A Worthy Upgrade to an Already Legendary Mouse
reviews.comment: I’ve been a fan of Logitech’s MX Master line for years — my old MX Master 2S chugged along for almost six years of daily use before finally showing signs of wear. When I saw the newest version with “Ultra‑Fast Scrolling” and haptic feedback, I decided to treat myself. It was absolutely worth it. The ergonomic shape is familiar and comfortable; it still fits my hand like a glove. The new MagSpeed scroll wheel is pure magic: it can click through spreadsheets one line at a time or spin freely to zip through long documents, and you can feel a gentle vibration thanks to the customizable haptics. I didn’t think I’d care about haptic feedback in a mouse, but it makes the scroll and gesture controls feel precise and satisfying. Connectivity has improved, too. It pairs via Bluetooth or the included receiver and can switch between three devices. The 8k DPI sensor tracks on glass and just about any surface, which means I’ve stopped lugging around a mouse pad when I travel. Logitech’s Options+ software lets me assign shortcuts and macros to the side buttons, and the new Actions Ring shortcuts promise to save time by putting common tools under my thumb. Have I mentioned the battery life yet? I don't think I've had to charge this once since I got it over a month and a half ago. According to Windows BT settings, it's still at 40%+. Impressive! It also charges via USB-C so no need for an unnecessary micro-USB cable on my desk. If I had to nitpick, the price is on the high side — but considering how long my last MX Master lasted, I see it as an investment. Overall, this is the best productivity mouse I’ve ever used, and it’s a joy to see the MX series continue to get better.

reviews.comment: Very good computer mouse. Originally I had a basic logitech bluetooth mouse, but this one is legit. My workflow improved and is much more efficient and smooth. I can easily navigate around any screen I'm on and since actions like the infinity scroll and side scroller literally make actions I want to do faster, I find that I'm getting more done in a shorter amount of time. My forearm and hand were a little sore on the first day but that quickly went away the next day and I never noticed it again. The battery inside this computer mouse holds a charge forever too. Love this thing.
reviews.author: James

reviews.title: A Premium Mouse That Mostly Lives Up to Its Price
reviews.comment: I’ve used plenty of mice over the years, and this one immediately stands out for its build quality. It feels solid and substantial in the hand, with buttons that are quiet and smooth in a way that gives it a very refined feel. The haptic feedback turned out to be far more intuitive and useful than I expected, and the action rings were a surprise feature I didn’t know I’d appreciate until I tried them. That said, the price is definitely on the high side, and it stings a bit considering the lack of onboard memory for storing settings. The limited number of predefined application profiles also makes the setup feel a little more manual than it should be for a premium device. What I Liked •  Excellent build quality; feels premium and solid •  Quiet, smooth buttons •  Haptic feedback is surprisingly useful •  Action rings add a unique and enjoyable control option •  Overall experience feels well thought out What I Didn’t Like •  The price is higher than I’d prefer •  No onboard memory for settings •  Very few predefined application profiles •  Setup requires more tweaking than expected •  Not the best value for casual users Category Ratings Value for Money: 5/10 Quality: 8/10 Matched Description: 9/10 Final Thoughts This mouse delivers a premium experience and introduces features that genuinely enhance daily use. While the price and lack of onboard memory hold it back from perfection, it’s still a strong choice for anyone who appreciates high‑quality peripherals and doesn’t mind paying for them.
reviews.author: D. Adamec

You can get the software and customize functionality I didn’t but it’s great so far, absolutely no complaints! Also very easy to clean. Excellent value for money. Highly recommend.

reviews.author: SRTmouse

reviews.title: Other Brands Charge Way More for Similar Specs
reviews.comment: My daily driver is the Logitech MX Master 4, it's excellent for productivity, however it's not that good for gaming. So, I picked up the Redragon M925 PRO, which is fantastic for gaming. I also have a Redragon M811, which offers a ton of side buttons, but depending on the game you're playing, I found that having too many inputs could actually get in the way during gameplay. The M925 strikes a much better balance—it gives you enough programmable buttons to be useful without overwhelming you, and the added thumb trigger is a really nice touch for quick actions. Performance-wise, this mouse delivers exactly what you’d expect from a modern gaming mouse. The adjustable DPI (up to 26,000) and polling rate options make it easy to fine-tune responsiveness depending on the game you’re playing. It feels smooth and precise, whether you’re making quick flicks or more controlled movements. The wireless connectivity options (Bluetooth and 2.4GHz) work well and keep your setup clean, while the battery life has been solid thanks to the efficient sensor and power-saving features. The ergonomics and customization are also strong points. The mouse is lightweight and fits comfortably in the hand, making it great for longer gaming sessions. Redragon’s software also allows you to remap buttons, create macros, and save different profiles for different games, which is a huge plus if you like tailoring your setup. The RGB lighting looks great if you’re into that, but it’s easy to turn off if you prefer a more minimal look. *It might be important to note that after downloading their software, Windows does caution you on the installation. Overall, the M925 PRO is an excellent gaming mouse that hits a sweet spot between functionality and simplicity. It avoids the clutter of too many buttons while still offering meaningful customization and strong performance. If you’re looking for a capable wireless gaming mouse that won’t break the bank, this is definitely a solid option.
reviews.author: SoapBoxintheSky

reviews.title: Feature rich. Lightweight.
reviews.comment: I had a mouse that was disintegrating, so I thought this one might be worth a go as the price is very reasonable. I'm past the point of caring about the fancy, pulsating lights, but if that's your thing then this one is pretty good looking. It has three modes of operation: BT; 2.4k wireless (if not used the dongle resides in a little slot on the bottom of the mouse); and wired. As I have enough wireless and BT gizmos already bombarding me, I will be using this one wire. That said, all the connections worked fine and without any issue. I would note that when d/l the software (which is not too bad...macros, keymapping, etc), be careful to install the 'wireless' version, even if you are using the cable. The wired version never connected to the mouse and I eventually uninstalled and found the correct version. There are multiple buttons for macro/gaming/etc. I'm sure they would handle most scenarios once everything is mapped as you want. Personally, I really prefer a heavy mouse. I'm not sure why they are so hard to find. This one is so light that even with the dpi turned down one can get unnecessary motion. As we get older the fine movements often start with a bit of jolt and I have found that using a mouse that's heavy can mitigate those problems. But there's no way to add weight to this one, so lightweight it is. *NOTE*  My reviews do not and will not contain any AI generated content.
reviews.author: grinder

reviews.title: A light, responsive mouse, smooth and fast enough
reviews.comment: My gaming needs are simple: I like strategy, historical, and occasionally role-playing games, all of whose motor requirements are on the low side and that almost never require twitch and click responsiveness. When I'm gaming, I almost always move in slow motion, and sometimes during some games I rarely move at all. That remarkable lack of motion is naturally reflected in my mouse requirements. I use a modified claw grip that usually responds best to larger, heavier mice. I used my Logitech g700 gaming mouse for 12 years and found it perfect for my needs. It finally wore out and so I began a search for a new favorite, especially when I (finally) discovered the responsiveness of smaller, lighter mice. This Redragon M925 PRO Wireless Gaming Mouse is my latest attempt at marrying my current tactile habits with an appropriately responsive mouse. I don't require complex responsiveness fine-tuning. This gaming mouse features more than enough programmable buttons for any rational user, but my simple needs were quickly satisfied with a fast set-up. I found the included software to be more than sufficient for most gamers: especially in creating profiles, button mapping, and something I never use because I nearly always mess it up, creating macros. If your requirements lay in that direction, this software should meet most or all of your needs. This mouse is light, responds quickly, glides easily with minimal applied energy, matches my grip, is attractive without being obnoxious, and feels durable enough to last if treated well. If you're a more restrained gamer, not currently engaged in serious action-oriented games, you could do a lot worse than this mouse. It's reasonably priced, making it a good value, and weeks of solid use indicate that battery life is good.

reviews.title: Pretty good mouse for being a G-502/Basilisk clone

While this will not replace my G-502X Lightspeed or Razer Basilisk V3 Pro on my main computers, it will be a good mouse to keep with my laptop when I need to use it.

reviews.author: J. Sami

reviews.title: Finally, a Good Gaming Mouse for Everyday People and Isn’t Just Weight Obsessed – Logitech G309
reviews.comment:
I’ve never really understood why some gamers are so fixated on weight. Does a few grams really change performance that much? If you’re not playing in tournaments for prize money, I don't think it really makes a huge difference. For most of us though, a good gaming mouse should just be comfortable, reliable, and fits our normal everyday lifestyle, which is exactly what the Logitech G309 delivers for me.
That said, this mouse probably isn't entirely designed for ultra-competitive players who obsess over little details such a weight or the fact it uses a single AA battery. I feel it was made more for people like me. Someone who is more of a casual gamer who balances gaming with work, hobbies, and other devices. And for that purpose, it’s perfect to me.
One of the standout features is its Bluetooth capability, which I’ve been hunting for in a gaming mouse. A mouse that connects to multiple devices and runs on AA batteries is incredibly rare. I’ve checked out Razer’s options, but the connectivity issues made them a hard pass. I did switch my G305 to a Pebble though because multi-device support was more important to me than pure gaming performance. The G309, though, hits both needs—solid gaming performance and seamless switching between devices.
The use of AA batteries is another win for me. I love the convenience of popping in a new battery (rechargeable or disposable) on the go, and in my experience, the battery life on AA-powered mice tends to outlast internal rechargeable ones. Brands often skip AA batteries to save on weight, but despite not doing so the G309 still feels super lightweight, and it even has an option to go lighter with a powerplay mousepad if I ever wanted that extra versatility.
The comfort level also deserves huge praise. Coming from the G305, I always found the shape a bit awkward, but I went with it for the battery life and price. It’s funny that some people now look back fondly on the G305’s shape, but for me, the G309 is a very clear improvement. The shape is more comfortable, and with my medium-sized hands and a claw grip, this is probably the most comfortable mouse I’ve ever used (not even exaggerating). The clicks feel solid, also with just the right amount of pressure to prevent accidental clicks, and the glides are smooth.
In conclusion, I’m definitely surprised that there are gamers who find the G309 heavy and hate on this mouse just because it isn't a direct copy of the G305 with refreshed internals. To me, it actually still feels lightweight and even comes in 13 grams lighter than my old G305. Overall, I’m thrilled with the G309. It’s practical, versatile, comfortable, and I'd personally say it's without a doubt the perfect choice for a more casual gamer like me, as well as a clear improvement from the G305 which I've used for several years. Kudos to Logitech for such a great mouse. Love it.

reviews.author: Jack H.

reviews.title: Such an INCREDIBLE mouse!
reviews.comment:
The Logitech G309 LIGHTSPEED Wireless Gaming Mouse is a game-changer in every sense. Its ultra-lightweight design at 86g makes it incredibly easy to maneuver, while the LIGHTFORCE Hybrid Switches deliver unparalleled click performance with an almost tactile feel. The HERO 25K Sensor ensures pinpoint accuracy and smooth tracking, perfect for both high-stakes gaming and detailed professional work.
One of the standout features is the extraordinary 300+ hour battery life with just a single AA battery. This means I can rely on it for weeks of intensive use without worrying about recharging. The six programmable buttons provide a high degree of customization, which significantly enhances productivity by allowing me to tailor the mouse functions to my exact needs.
The G Hub app takes the customization to the next level. It offers an intuitive interface where I can assign different commands, create macros, and adjust DPI settings effortlessly. The ability to save multiple profiles in the app is incredibly useful, as I can switch between gaming and work setups with ease. This mouse has seamlessly integrated into my daily routine and fits perfectly in my work purse, making it an indispensable tool for both professional and personal use. Overall, the Logitech G309 is the perfect blend of performance, customization, and convenience.
reviews.author: CNellyTX

reviews.title: This is a good mouse, almost a great mouse
reviews.comment:
I've purchased 3 so far, only because once you've used it, you can't go back to anything else.  The pointer precision with this mouse is spot on.  The "feel" is even better when you have a high refresh rate capable display.  "Smooth as Butter" they used to say.  The oldest one I've had is so far 1 year and no signs of problems yet.  I use the mouse more than 12 hours a day every day.  The battery has only been replaced once.  No issues with clicking or the scroll wheel.
Everything about this mouse is fine tuned.  The default settings out of the box are good, the scroll wheel requires just the perfect amount of force to move, and the DPI/sensitivity is set to a good rate.  I do not feel fatigue in my hand while using it and it's easy to disable to DPI shift button with the software.  There are a lot of positives with this $90 mouse that outperform the more expensive and "premium" models.  #1 best part of this is the replaceable battery.  Why anyone would make a mouse without a replaceable battery (let alone buy one) is beyond comprehension.
Logitech's software is still the weakest component in all their products.  Most software these days is terrible due to poor developer skills.  It's a dying art for sure.  Recent versions of G HUB are better, but it's till very clunky and resource heavy.  Logitech please all we need is just the most basic UI to manage our settings.  A simple Win32 App with no fancy stuff will do.
Time will tell if the optical switch solves one of the biggest issues with Logitech mice.  I have several other models that are useless because the switches malfunction.
With just one minor change this could be a perfect mouse.  It only needs hyperscroll.

reviews.author: Shmeezer

reviews.title: Perfect for Wide Hands Silent Grid Real Palm Grip and Surprisingly Good for Heavy Weight
reviews.comment: I am coming from a SteelSeries Aerox 9 and a Razer Naga V2 HyperSpeed. Both of those mice forced me into a fingertip grip because they were too narrow for my 12 cm wide hands. The Redragon M913 MAX is the first MMO mouse that actually lets me use a full palm grip. This makes a huge difference during long World of Warcraft sessions because my hand can finally relax instead of hovering behind the mouse. The thumb grid is completely silent. My wife sits at the desk right next to mine and the Naga grid was loud enough to bother her. The Aerox 9 was quieter but required a lot of force to press. The M913 MAX fixes both problems. The grid makes no sound at all and the buttons are light enough that I can use them for hours without thumb fatigue. The mouse is very heavy at around 170 grams. For most games that would be a downside, but World of Warcraft does not require large or fast mouse movements. The extra weight actually helps reduce unintentional movement when I am spamming abilities to clip global cooldowns. It feels planted and stable instead of sluggish. Tracking has been solid. The sensor is older and did not work well on my SP004 glass pad at first. Setting the lift off distance to 2 millimeters solved the issue. My only complaints are with the software. The RGB controls are hidden under a colored bar inside the DPI menu which is confusing. I locked the mouse to a single DPI setting at 1600 and ignored the rest. You cannot reassign the DPI switch buttons which is unusual for an MMO mouse. The default profile maps the grid to the number pad on a full keyboard. I had to remap everything to the number row from 1 to the equal sign so it would match my other mice. None of these issues are deal breakers but they are worth knowing. If you have large hands want a real palm grip and need a silent grid for a shared workspace this mouse gets the important things right. The hardware is excellent and the software only needs refinement.

reviews.title: Great Value
reviews.comment: This Redragon M913 MAX is a great value for the price. It worked well right out of the box, feels great in my hand, and the button layout is very useful for gaming, especially if you like having extra side buttons for keybinds or macros. The mouse feels comfortable, responsive, and overall performs really well. For an MMO-style wireless gaming mouse with this many features, I think it offers a lot for the money. The only drawback I noticed is that the RGB lighting changes do not seem to work while the mouse is plugged in. The RGB customization appears to only apply when using 2.4GHz wireless or Bluetooth mode. That is not a dealbreaker for me, but it is worth mentioning. It works wired, 2.4GHz, or Bluetooth. The software is decent but could be more polished. Overall, I’m happy with it and would recommend it to anyone looking for a solid, comfortable MMO mouse at a good price.

If I had to mention one complaint, it would be the limited color options, but that feels like a minor issue. I am planning to standardize this mouse for the IT department.
reviews.author: The Jose V

reviews.title: A Great Upgrade - Pretty solid
reviews.comment:
If you are looking for a solid gaming wireless mouse this is your best option.
I've had the previous model O wireless and after 2 years it never failed me, but i had to buy another mouse because it didnt fit so well in my hand. Then i got the Deathadder V3 and it was like grabbing a cloud, pretty comfortable, Great sensor, no issues at all, i gotta say i got bid hands. But i wanted a wireless gaming mouse to watch YT from my bed across the room like i used to with the model o wireless, so i found this mouse at 30$, Used, in amazon resale, and it was a complete bargain fr!
So, aside the lore i just explained, it has the best of both worlds: wireless, comfy, solid, reliable, its an experience for me. But still has some weak points, which im gonna explain:
PROS
- Great sensor, never failed
- Fast wireless connection, no lag or delays
- REALLY Comfortable for big hands.
- Precise click, always aims where i want it to.
- Great side buttons position, no wrist harm while using it
- Pretty light, it feels like having nothing on your hand
- Has usb C, something you can say is obvious but Logitech didnt add it to G Pro X Superlight
- The gliding is soft, never has stuck in my mousepad
- Maybe have some more features i don't mind rn
CONS
- wth did they did to the software?!?! It used to be more intuitive and easier to understand, atleast had a better aesthetic look, but now is just like Redragon software, it has been hard switching from Razer Synapse to this new version of Glorious core, it doesnt even show my actual battery %
- The scroll is a bit hard for my taste, and clicking the scrollwheel button is a pain, i like em softer.
- The materials are not much better than the rubby plastic of the Deathadder V3, that one was easily to scratch. But this one feels a bit cheap, and yes, the scrollwheel feels kinda cheap, but i guess is to make it lightweight.
- The clicks are loud, i like them, but for some people may be anoying, it would be a problem if you share your room while gaming, and idk if its my unit, but the lateral back click is almost LOUDER than the normal Left click
- The wheel rubber can get dirty easily and is hard to clean
Overall is a good gaming mouse, and for 30$ sure is a deal you should get, but for the original price of 100$ i would recommend the Deathadder V3 Hyperspeed for a bit more, but if you cant afford it this still a comfy, solid, durable and reliable gaming wireless mouse, and yeah, go ahead, get this one, i swear it will be a pretty nice experience
reviews.author: Roy

reviews.title: Cheap feeling. Not worth the money at all
reviews.comment:
I've used an original Model D Wireless for many years and "upgraded" to this D 2 Pro when the battery on mine started to die. I really did love the original.
This mouse just feels cheap. Everything about it feels like a cheapo off-brand $20 mouse. The sensor is great and the latency is great, but how they packaged that all up together is just bad.
The switches are the loudest I have every heard on a mouse and they are optical which makes replacing them with something quieter a little more complicated. Not to mention that they made the mouse basically impossible to open up without breaking.
The plastic housing is just smooth, no texture for grip or anything special about it. The led indicator for which DPI mode you're in is on the bottom which is just a terrible design.
If this mouse was $20 it would be a five star from me. But even at the discount that I got it at, its a waste of money.
I won't be buying Glorious products again after this.
reviews.author: Daniel Minter

reviews.title: Solid mouse, 2 years later no issues
reviews.comment:
Bought this mouse 1-9-2024 and it's still working fine. I know people rag on Glorious mice but I've tried 3 others over these last 2 years and I'm back to the model D2 pro. Pulsar xlite v3 the hump in the front is high and caused wrist pain during long sessions, razer deathadder v3 pro (bad scroll wheel) and logitech g703 that double clicked the M1 button within 3 months.
After dealing with those 3 I busted out ole faithful and realized I should've just stuck with this one. I just bought the 4k/8k version since it's on sale for only $45 and ordered a new pair of g floats that I'll throw on it when it gets here. I'll dedicate this one as a back up in case I have any issues with the new one.
Pros- The sensor is solid, never had a spin out issue or felt like it was off
Wireless connection has been great, battery life has also been solid, I can go days between charging it easily
Clicks all feel good and I've had no mechanical issues with it.
Cons- Of course there has to be cons, nothing is perfect and this mouse is no exception.
The glorious software is terrible, luckily you don't have to mess with it really. Set your dpi how you like and call it a day
The back click button is loud, it's louder than all the other buttons but causes no issue
At the end of the day for $35 it's the best wireless ergo mouse you can get but splurge and spend the extra $10 to get the 4k/8k model as it's the best bang for buck ergo mouse with that high of a polling rate
