reviews.title: I think it's best to pass on these
reviews.comment:
First off, the mouse to me feels like an extension of my hand it fits perfectly for what I like and has solid clicks and wheel. If these were it I'd give it a 5.
But the software is flaky and I bought one for each computer I have, and one lasted only a few days before it just flat out failed (the mouse). So it's really a mixed bag. Glorious has had QA issues for years and this has not improved with time. It seems like they just use the cheapest sweatshop they can find to make this stuff, and the lack of reliability shows.
Like I said I love how it fits my hand and works, when it works, but sadly one of them NEVER worked from the get go and another lasted a few days. That's NOT a good track record so I would buy something else if I had it to do over despite how much I like these when they work. Throwing 80 dollars into the garbage is never a good feeling. Value for the money, I feel shafted. Build quality - meh. Functionality 10 out of 10 when it actually works but frankly that just isn't enough.
reviews.author: Ed Erdman

reviews.title: Great entry mechanical keyboard with solid feel and comfort
reviews.comment: I bought this for my 14-year-old, and it’s been a great keyboard for both gaming and schoolwork. The hybrid switches feel clicky and responsive without being overly loud, and the RGB is bright and customizable enough for their setup. The included wrist rest adds real comfort and doesn’t slide around. No issues with software or macros so far. It’s a well-rounded keyboard that feels more premium than its price suggests.
reviews.author: Ibrahim Amir

reviews.title: Outstanding, with a possible caveat
reviews.comment:
Five months into owning this keyboard and it's easily my favorite keyboard I've ever had. Reasonably heavy so it easily stays in place even banging out page after page of typing documents, but doesn't feel like a slab of lead. The entire assembly is well put together; the keyboard has a nice, satin texture across the body and the keys, which feels great under the fingers, though it does show some oils more easily so I recommend regular cleaning/wipedowns.
This keyboard uses an odd hybrid system between mechanical/membrane, some proprietary/trade secret Steelseries BS, though honestly, if this wasn't pointed out to me after the fact I probably wouldn't have caught on. This uses cherry stems and switches, and the keys are naturally a cherry profile, so finding aftermarket replacements/decorative keycaps is easy as well. The keys feel responsive and clicky, delightfully so, when gaming or typing for general purpose. But there's a catch; it's a hybrid, so not truly mechanical. It does feel very good, but I have concerns that the membrane will wear down in time as opposed to a true blue mechanical keyboard, which will stay responsive and snappy for a lesser eternity where membranes begin to show wear after a year of heavy use. Time will tell.
The lighting is phenomenal - the LEDs are bright, responsive, and have great color depth and range compared to a lot of RGB hardware out there. You can use Steelseries' own software to customize and program this keyboard outside of the 5 existing presets saved onto the board's memory, but you can also use other third-party RGB control software like SignalRGB.
All in, it's a quality keyboard for a great price; one wire connects everything, you have a stop/start button, a wheel for volume, and a built in profile-swap button, which is entirely unnecessary but quite nice.
reviews.author: Ken

reviews.title: Great Keyboard and Great Features!
reviews.comment: This keyboard is probably the best one I've ever had. It is built so well. It is made mostly of some sort of aluminum. It does not bend at all and it just feels very nice. I have had a keyboard that was so cheap that it bent even when I was typing normally (I don't type very hard), so this was a nice change. The metal volume dial is very high quality, and yet again, just feels well-built. There is also a little button that controls 4 things. It will pause and play your music, skip to the next song, go to the previous song, and open up menus in the OLED display. The OLED screen is very nice. It could be a little brighter, and the larger pixels make it harder to display certain things. But, what makes up for that is that with the program you can install, you can download apps that will change what the screen says. My 2 favorites are Discord and System Monitor. They RGB lighting is really nice. Each light can be its own color and with the program, you can make your own lighting configurations. The keys sound very nice. They are clicky, but too clicky. They are also easy to press, but not so easy that I could see myself accidentally pressing one. It also comes with a wrist rest. It magnetically attaches and feels very smooth and high quality. Overall this keyboard just feels very premium and super high quality. I would recommend it to someone who wants a good keyboard with some very nice features from a good brand and does not mind spending the premium cost.
reviews.author: Barbara Smoyer

reviews.title: Good quality, tactile and finger friendly
reviews.comment:
Genuinely pleased with both the keyboard and mouse - makes my Corsair keyboard and RGB mouse garbage in comparison. I write a lot and this keyboard just feels far better than my Corsair RGB keyboard ever did. (I liked those too, but this series is leaps ahead.)
After running with the Corsair mouse with weights, I was worried that this lightweight mouse would throw me off, but to my surprise, it's exactly the opposite.  Even with matching DPI, this Steelseries Aerox 5 mouse blows the old one away - performant, responsive and the buttons are very thoughtfully positioned (no more accidental DPI / profile switches like I had constantly with the Corsair.)
Software wise, the layouts and options are great. I will note that there's a momentary 'blink-out' from time to time where the keyboard blacks out then returns after a 1/2 second. I really like the ability to set a custom profile for each game / app.
Cons:
Menu for setting individual key colors is less than intuitive and online documentation is behind.
Scrolling volume wheel feels a bit sketchy - works, but isn't smooth feeling and is akin to feeling like its rubbing against the housing or something.
Overall: 4.999 stars out of 5.
reviews.author: Fortress Tech LLC

reviews.title: Great keyboard
reviews.comment: Love this keyboard, great feel, and solid
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Premium feel & Perfect satisfying click
reviews.comment: Heavier than I thought it would be and it feels premium for the low price tag. There are tons of color options for the RBG and you can even write your own to fully customize. The perfect satisfying click sound - like an old 90’s IBM computer. It came with a charging cord and keycap remover tool. Very worth the price!!! I personally didn’t like the keys but always planned to swap them out. They were easy to remove so 5++++ stars for sure
reviews.author: Andie

reviews.title: Beautiful Keyboard!
reviews.comment: This keyboard is so nice! It has a fantastic weight to it, it's not heavy per se but it feels expensive. This might sound stupid, but I bought this specifically for Fortnite Festival. My other keyboards have keys that get stuck easy and I have a difficult time cleaning underneath the keys. This keyboard fixed all of those issues. There are no sidewalls for dust and hair to get stuck in, which can be a pro and a con. You can easily see the switches, but I think that's a pro because I can easily lube the switches if I want to in the future. The sound is super clacky, so beware of that, but you can always watch youtube videos on how to lube your own keys and get cheap key lube from microcenter or best buy! I think this keyboard is worth it!! Especially with the wireless option!
reviews.author: Rebecca

reviews.title: For those who want the typewriter qualities and modern day exepince this is the keyboard to buy!
reviews.comment: This keyboard is wonderful; the colors, functionality, and aesthetics are beautiful. The keyboard sounds are 100% amazing. The animation in the color changes is phenomenal. Please do buy this item. The only reason I returned it was because I mistook it for one that had Bluetooth when it didn't. The weight and the stand are durable and lightweight. Easily moved, and the cords came and worked. The packaging was absolutely wonderful. Overall, the experience was luxurious. I am actually using this keyboard to write my review before I return it. Please do try this product!
reviews.author: Aurelila Rabitito

reviews.title: Awesome sound!
reviews.comment: I love this keyboard. One of my computers serves two rooms, with monitors on both sides of a wall. This keyboard works perfectly in both rooms. So the wireless connection is strong. The sound when typing is very satisfying, and the lighting is nice. I have used Redragon mechanical keyboards on all my computers for years and they are very quality keyboards, this is my first time using the wireless ones, I have one black and one white, and both seem to be the quality I have come to expect. And the price point is good.
reviews.author: Deanna Powers

reviews.title: Awesome Keyboard!!!
reviews.comment: I love this keyboard!!!! I use it for work and gratefully the sounds of the keys aren’t annoying my coworkers. I’ve got coworkers who actually want to order one for themselves!!! It’s functional, stable keyboard, durable, compatible with my PC and no issues. It’s a heavy solid keyboard. I love the lights on it too. This keyboard looks great and the size isn’t too big or too small. It’s perfect for what I need it for!!
reviews.author: Darlene Cocivera

reviews.title: Fair Pricing / Comfortable for Typing / Good weight distribution / Flashy LEDs
reviews.comment: I was very surprised at the quality and options that this keyboard has for the price point.  For a mechanical keyboard it feels good and looks amazing as well.  It was also nice that they come with a whole other set of keys and led lights just in case you need to replace them for breaking or want to do a different color.  The weight of the keyboard feels good and keeps it in place on your desktop when typing.  I've only been using this for 2 weeks but I have seen no issues at all and I am on it over 8 hours day.  Will update feedback if there are any issues, but this seems like a very solid purchase.
reviews.author: Aaron

reviews.title: For someone looking for a nice budget keyboard look no further.
reviews.comment: This is a nice budget keyboard especially someone who is used to buying Corsair metal keyboards. I was looking for a nice replacement keyboard for when my Corsair K60 was double or triple pressing certain keys so I was looking for a good alternative. The RGB lighting looks amazing, the key action is nice and smooth and the detachable USB cable is really nice. I would recommend this keyboard for anyone who wants a nice keyboard without spending a lot of money on a expensive keyboard, the build quality feels good and the keyboard does feel durable. The extra set of keycaps so you can customize the keyboard as well as the keycap/switch puller is a nice plus. After some research i was a little hesitant to try a new brand (Redragon), but i was pleasantly surprised. 5/5 stars for sure!
reviews.author: Lorbic

reviews.title: Awesome value works great with Linux!
reviews.comment: This is my first day with this keyboard, i am very impressed for the price. I heard the Amazon driver DROP my package outside my door, very annoyed, no damage that i could tell yet however. I was a little annoyed also that there was no extra package, only the manufacturer's default box. On to the things i love - the keyboard has a little weight to it, which is nice , does not feel cheap. Better than that, every key has backlighting, i saw other reviews that stated some keys were not backlit. Even better - I use linux exclusively, and was super pleased that the extra function keys worked perfectly, i was sure i would have to hack them. Sound mute, screen lock, calc, all work fine. I am not actually a gamer, i just wanted this keyboard because of so many great reviews, and its PRETTY! this replaces my beloved Logitech G413, and I am using the default pattern ( a multi color breathing pattern) as i won't use the gamer profile patterns. For 40$ i am super pleased !!! I will edit or post a new review after a month's time.
reviews.author: Kindle Customer

reviews.title: Not bad, but it has room for improvement.
reviews.comment: for the price this isn't a bad board, but its not great. It has RGB, check, but, you can't access all modes from the FN+ combos you have to install Redragon's software. The brightness of the LED's is sub-par. Lets be honest here I have several boards with RGB that cost less than half what this board costs that have brighter LED's. This board has some custom linear switch that isn't terrible but I'd prefer a bit stronger spring. The key presses are nice and smooth so its got that going for it, the board is definitely hot swappable as I pulled a switch out with one of the keycaps lol. Setup is not particularly straight forward unless you want to just use the board as it comes. For me, if a board just works out of the box and I don't have to install some proprietary software that's a win. You can only setup certain features using Redragon's software. The keycaps are another story, I really didn't like them, like not at all. I liked the color profile I thought they were quite nice looking but my goodness these things are tall, like an extra 1/4" taller than a standard OEM or Cherry MX profile. Plus, a lot of the keys were "short shot" which means that a full shot of plastic didn't get into the second shot of plastic which is what makes them "double shot" basically double shot caps are an over-molded keycap. Also, I'm not a massive fan of the font used on the keys, and now I'm getting into nit-picky territory so I will just say, I didn't like them. I had a nice set of shine through caps that I swapped them out with and now I'm quite pleased with the board overall. I might even keep it lol. I have like a dozen keyboards and I swap them out and what not as I like. I have a number of systems and several workstations so I have many keyboards depending on space and needs. Overall this is not a bad board, but this segment of the market, at this price point, I think the board needs to do a little better. For the money, it's a keyboard, the switches all work, it feels pretty nice and now that I've got some nice keycaps on it, it sounds halfway decent. I have several TKL boards that sound way better than this one but its growing on me now. The board is also pretty light, which is reflected in its all plastic construction. I have a couple other custom boards that are probably 2-3x as heavy and feel much more solid than this one. I'm not complaining, just observing. I think if I was to add some insulation to this it would improve the sound so I may crack it open and see what can be done to deeping the tone a bit. Overall decent board. It does keyboard things. RGB is sup-par, switches are nice enough but not spectacular or anything. I added a couple pictures of the board with my shine through keycaps. If only the backlight had a bit more oomph.
reviews.author: P. Wells

reviews.title: Excellent mechanical keyboard for under $100
reviews.comment: I've used an assortment of mechanical keyboards of the years from brown to red to blue switches. Excellent keyboard for under $100. This keyboard can be paired via Bluetooth, wireless dongle, or wired via USB-A to USB-C cable. The keys are very soft and nice to type on. Quiet compared to my red switches. I personally love that EVERY key on this keyboard can be re-mapped to whatever you'd like. Macros, mouse clicks, media controls. I also enjoy the customizable RGB. The LED lighting illuminates through the key caps. It isn't super bright, but at night, it's nice and not overwhelmingly bright.
reviews.author: John Amazon

reviews.title: An excellent fullsize made to last
reviews.comment: Within Keychrons huge lineup of keyboards, the Q serieswoukd be their flagship. When you pick one of these up you will immediately understand why. With a solid aluminum back and front panel, it's dense and has some serious weight to it relative to most other consumer boards. The packaging is great. Printed manuals/guides, extra windows keycaps, extra switches, tools for maintenance, and a USB cable. The USB cable is pretty cool in that it matches the color scheme of the board itself with something like an iridescent effect. It's a cool cable with a nice length, however I will say it is very stiff. I have to call out the great color. The aluminum anodization is pretty good with a deep, rich purple color. Everything here is aluminum. The knob, the entire case, even the toggle switches. It's a very high quality feel and presentation. I also like that the screws are easily accessible on the back of the board. These screws are appropriately hex heads to ensure you can't strip them out. Keycaps are also nice quality with double shot construction. This means the legends are not printed or etched - they are a separate layer of plastic embedded under the keycap. This ensures the legends are perfectly crisp and will never rub off over time. The KSA profile of the keys might take some getting used to. They are much higher profile than your standard cherry keycaps, or even OSA as found other Keychron boards. This is a hotswap board, too. So, you have a ton of options for customizing the sound and feel of this board. The Brown switches are pretty good and if you have prior experience with MX Browns you'll probably like these as well. I will say that these are tactile but, as someone used to heavier tactile bumps, these feel almost like linears because the bump is so mild. The keyboard sounds good though and the Browns definitely sound more mellowed out than something like the Bananas would. Functionally, it's basically plug and play. Sadly this board does not have 2.4 ghz wireless, although it does have Bluetooth and wired USB. If you need 2.4 ghz, you want to look at the Q6 Max which is the same board just with that feature added in. Other than that, you can flip between Mac/PC mode with a toggle switch. It has full per key RGB, which you can customize in the Launcher web software. This software is a major selling point for these boards because of how non-invasive and intuitive it is to use. There is no download necessary, it's entirely web based. Within this software you can customize just about everything, including macro creation. It's really useful. Quick summary - Pros: - Excellent build quality with good materials - Heavy - Lots of useful features - Sounds great with well lubed stabilizers - Hotswap PCB - Easy to customize every aspect of it Cons: - Expensive for a board with no 2.4 ghz - USB cable is quite stiff Overall this is a great board. It's expensive and it may be worth the extra $20 for 2.4 ghz, but it gets all the fundamentals right and looks good doing it. Easily a recommended board if you want to experience some of the best Keychron has on offer.
reviews.author: Blakk

reviews.title: Beautiful and as-described with minimal need for improvement
reviews.comment: I may have made the mistake of getting the keyboard with nasty brown switches, but that is on me and I always planned to change them anyways. Brown switches, including Keychron's, are just nasty feeling and sounding. They aren't quiet even though they are supposed to be, the have a scratchy feel when pressing, and they are unsatisfying to use. To get past that, they keyboard itself is quite pretty. Seems well-built, keys are nice (though hard to adjust to), and the software/lighting is reliable as usual. The reason it loses a star isn't because of the brown switches, that's on me as the buyer to know what I bought. The reason is actually the mode toggle on the back. I am paying a premium for this keyboard and, when I went to switch modes, the toggle feels like it was hastily fit into the keyboard with spare parts. It wobbled in all directions and the click of mode change felt just nasty. Keychron needs to make sure their products feel premium and they've done a good job on the frame over the years, but that switch has no excuse to be so bad. It's small, but noticeable if you have a habit of turning off devices when not using them. And good on them for including a thematic keyboard.
reviews.author: Doc Kidd

reviews.title: Great sturdy keyboard!
reviews.comment: I’m a big fan of this keyboard so far. The color is gorgeous and I like that it can be formatted for multiple OSes. I prefer thockier switches so I’m going to swap those out soon, but that’s just a matter of preference and not a slight on the quality of the keyboard. The wireless function works great, though there’s an included matching cable to use wired if you want. There are a lot of backlight options which I really like. My only caution is that this is a big heavy keyboard. I’m fine with that, but if you want something lighter this probably isn’t for you. Overall this feels like a really quality keyboard. $219.99 is a fair price for this level of keyboard and I’d definitely recommend it.
reviews.author: QueenMab

reviews.title: High-Quality Build, very heavy
reviews.comment: This is a great mechanical keyboard. The full aluminum construction makes it feel extremely sturdy and premium; it’s definitely a solid, heavy piece of equipment that won't slide around on your desk. The typing experience is fantastic—the keys are quiet with great travel, and the overall type feel is very satisfying. Everything about it feels well-made and durable, definitely not cheap. The battery life has been reliable for wireless use, and the RGB lighting is a very nice touch, offering a vibrant look that really stands out. If you're looking for a high-end, full-size keyboard that delivers on both performance and build quality, this is a perfect choice!
reviews.author: Kirby

reviews.title: Awesome first time mechanical keyboard!
reviews.comment: So first off, a few disclaimers. One, I am no mechanical keyboard expert so take everything I say as experience, not expertise. Two, this is my very first mechanical keyboard purchase so I have no other mechanical keyboards I can compare this to. Three, if you know nothing about mechanical keyboards - go and read at least a couple articles about what the different aspects to them are. Especially the different types of switches. Depending on what type of sound and feel you want, knowing the switches will potentially make the difference between a happy purchase and an unhappy one. I’m glad I did the research because I ended up very happy with both the sound and the feel. Ok, all that said… on to the review. After using my last keyboard for about three years, I decided it was time to replace it. I had been hearing a lot about mechanical keyboards for a while and had been talking to others about their experience. I decided it was time to take the plunge. The challenge here is that there are A LOT of options out there. Here’s how I chose. I’m a big fan of the folks at the Wirecutter (don’t love that they sold out to NYT, but whatevs). So I read their research and testing on best options. Their pick felt way over my head, both in terms of acquisition (had to go some mechanical keyboard online shop), costs, options, and wait time. Their budget pick, the Keychron C1 caught my eye. But this was a wired KB and I wanted wireless. I also noticed that their upgrade pick was also a Keychron - so when I found this one, I thought it couldn’t be too bad. Plus it had the two main features I wanted (bluetooth and backlight). Plus it looked pretty awesome. The overall package - I have to admit for a brand I had never heard of before, the whole package - keyboard and all - was made with a considerable amount of quality. The construction feels solid and sturdy. The instructions were understandable and clear. It included extra keycaps if you wanted to use this keyboard with a windows machine. You could even change the keys in the corner to gray or orange. Your choice. But the most important question - how does it feel to type? Mind you I’m not wildly picky nor a typing snob - but I thought it was great. I love the feel of it and it has just the right amount of feedback and sound. I got the brown switches for just this reason. Again, I will stress the importance of knowing what kind of switches you want. What I like - Typing feels awesome.  It looks amazing on my desk and blends well with my Mac and all my accessories. Holds a charge for a long time. Lots of fun backlight options. Easy to configure. Can use as wired or wireless. Everything is high quality. What I don’t like - It goes to sleep a little too frequently for my taste. Mind you, this is configurable and you can change the amount of idle time before sleep or turn off auto sleep altogether.I tried this, but I think I got something wrong and now it seems to go to sleep even faster. But this is truly a PEBKAC and not a problem with the keyboard itself. Who would I recommend this for - I would definitely recommend this keyboard for anyone looking for their first foray into the mechanical world. Nothing to overthink here. Just pick the type of switches you want (thank goodness there are only three available as opposed to the dozen or so that are out there) and order and you’re on your way to clickety-clackety nirvana.
reviews.author: Marshall Mobley

reviews.title: A great keyboard if it fits your needs
reviews.comment: I bought this for a home office that occupies a niche off the family living space and therefore should be as neat and minimal as possible. I especially want to avoid a tangle of cables. For years I used a Unicomp Model M at work, which I loved, but it was way too loud for home. I wondered how I would do with the Gateron blue switches, but in practice I like them just fine. The touch is lighter than the buckling springs of the Unicomp, but I have adjusted quickly and may soon prefer them. Anyway, after years of being forced much of the time to use laptop keyboards or the mushy junk at various offices this is quite satisfactory. I was also worried about using a Bluetooth connection, since other people have sometimes reported trouble, but it has worked like a charm. The connection was easy to establish and easy to restore after using the keyboard with other devices. I see no lag, no dropped characters, and no repeated characters. I don't game, so there may be a degree of responsiveness others need that I don't, but as far as I'm concerned each stroke has an instant result. It probably helps that I'm using this with a new NUC that has up-to-date Bluetooth 4.0. The keyboard goes to sleep after ten minutes and requires a keystroke to wake up. I realize that some sleep algorithm is necessary for battery life, but I wish that it were adjustable -- I would trade more frequent charging for longer wakefulness. However, I have quickly developed the habit of hitting the shift key after returning to typing. I was already acclimated to that from using laptops on dark airplanes to restore back-lighting. Speaking of which, I have found the back-lighting to be more useful than I thought I would. I got the model with the plain white LEDs and only the use the most boring, straightforward setting. I makes it easier to work in the dark, which I often do, and it serves as a reminder that the keyboard is asleep. The biggest bonus for me has been how well the keyboard works with other devices, like my iPhone and a smart Samsung television, filling a need I didn't know I had. I dislike typing long emails and texts with my thumbs. If the keyboard is in reach function-1, -2, or -3 quickly lets me switch with no problems. It has also spared me the tedium on text entry using the television remote when I am trying to search for a movie on Netflix or enter a password. My only objection to the keyboard is that, in practice, I don't love the form factor. That is not a design criticism. I thought I would, but now I think I would prefer a more expansive tenkeyless design, with the conventional layout for arrow keys and a little gap between the numbers and the function keys. This is perfectly designed for someone who wants to able to toss this in a backpack and use it in many places, but for pure keyboarding in one place, it is more compressed than I need. It also stands slightly higher than I would prefer, but that is really just a matter of the right wrist rest. The build quality is excellent, the keyboard feels solid and inflexible, and the weight (though far less than the good old Unicomp) is enough to keep it firmly in one place. I will definitely keep this keyboard, even if I end up buying a larger one for daily use. I know now how well Bluetooth and blue keys work for me. I recommend this to others for quality, but always subject to subjective preference and the job at hand.
reviews.author: Paul Turner

reviews.title: Great budget board, with some issues
reviews.comment: Great keyboard with a few issues. Switches work fine. Plastic case has a not too cheap feel, with a great color scheme. Biggest issue is the cable connection not working like half of the time, I was going to use it in Bluetooth mode 99% of the time so not a big deal. Software is a mess though, it will not register my keyboard despite it  being actively connected. But having a Keychron on sale for about 60 dollars can’t be beat.
reviews.author: Jorge Duarte

reviews.title: Has weird quirks, but one of the best keyboard designs
reviews.comment: I got the K2 because most mechanical keyboards are designed with the "gamer aesthetic", and I needed multi-device support, similar to what Logitech has on their keyboards. Unfortunately compared to the K1, the base K2 does not have an aluminum backplate, which makes you question why you're paying so much for a keyboard. However, the plastic is pretty well constructed, and the features really makes this keyboard shine. First, multi-device support over cable and bluetooth. I use multiple devices between Windows and macOS, so having OS-specific modes was a really nice experience. The cable is type C, which is a really nice touch. Typing is what you would expect. I have the brown switches (wanted to get the red but the brown was on sale), so both typing and gaming are pretty good experiences. The backlight is great, but when I bought the non-RGB version of the K2, I wasn't expecting it to contain the same flash patterns as the RGB version, which is annoying for me since I was expecting the backlight to be only a off-on affair. It's not as big of an issue compared to the K1 though, since it's not as low profile and it's harder to bump into the backlight key. I think there's a firmware upgrade that gives you a feature to lock light patterns, so that probably solves this problem. I have found some weird things going on with this keyboard though. It doesn't play nicely on bluetooth with some macOS devices, and it seems to "keep" my 2008 Macbook pro constantly awake, which really annoying. A firmware update might fix this in the future. With power savings on the backlight, I got more than 2 days on battery with the backlight on when active. I normally keep it plugged in because I need the cable connection, but I wouldn't say battery life is too bad, given the backlight. Overall, there's not that many keyboards that is both mechanical and looks professional, let alone have both and multi-device support. I do feel the K2 is a bit overpriced, but if you can get a good deal on it, it's a very good keyboard. Just be sure you do want to invest in using mechanical keys, they might not be the best typing experience for some people.
reviews.author: Ovaltine Jenkins

reviews.title: Great keyboard! It's a keeper.
reviews.comment: I really love this keyboard. The white backlight is enough for me, I don't need all the RGB color flashing everywhere. I got the model with the Brown Switches which provide perfect tactile feedback that feels amazing, it keeps wanting me to want to type and type more. I've been having a hard time finding a perfect keyboard that I want to keep, and I gotta say this one is a keeper. It comes with keycaps for an Apple computer, but they also include all the keycaps for Windows. Since I'm a Windows user, they were very easy to remove with the included key removal tool and pop on. Some other things that are great: It's light, it has keyboard title legs which I always need. (I actually purchased a keyboard a couple of months ago that didn't have these legs which left me puzzled.) The only alternative keycap colors are orange. There are two of these. One is for the ESC key and the other is for the far right of the keyboard where there is a button for toggling the lighting effect the keyboard backlight displays. The absolute only con is I wish they included colored keys for W, A, S, and D. Unfortunately they didn't. This is something I wish they did. I might email them and ask if there is any way I can get orange keycaps for those keys. Or there might be alternative keys you can buy that will fit on the keyboard perfectly. This is for a new computer I just built and it pairs perfectly with it. On my other system, I have cherry red switches, and they're just a little too clicky and loud. The brown switches make the sound just a little more muted and softer. The only other thing I'd have to say is I think the price point should be more around 80 dollars for this keyboard, so you're paying a premium price for this, however, there are much more expensive keyboards so it's hard to complain. If you're looking for an amazing keyboard I highly recommend this. I also want to mention it does come with a cable in case you don't want to go Bluetooth. That's what I'm doing at the moment, but I might try the BT later. Good luck!
reviews.author: The Emu Pirate

reviews.title: Cadillac of keyboards
reviews.comment: Beautiful looking, sounds nice, feels smooth. It's very large and heavy, but that's what I was looking for. I love the wood accents on the side. Really improves the whole computer experience to have a nice keyboard to work with. The web app used to set it up is easy and has more features and options than I'd never need, but that keyboard gamers will probably love (I'm a gamepad guy).
reviews.author: eric

reviews.title: Pleasantly surprised, high quality product
reviews.comment: I hadn't heard of this company before, and previously I have been a Corsair loyalist, but I found this keyboard's design to be very attractive so I figured I would give it a shot—worst case scenario I don't like it and I send it back. But I certainly won't be doing that, this keyboard is excellent. The K70 it replaced had been with me for about 10 years before it finally gave out, and this one is a major improvement on that keyboard in multiple areas: - The switches feel solid and definite while still being quiet (the old keyboard was MX brown, nice feel but very loud). - The cable management is much nicer, there's only one cord and it's detachable with a wireless option. - The layout is programmable but doesn't require me to install any driver software. My biggest concerns when I purchased it were the quality of the materials, including the authenticity of the wood accents. I am pleased to report the construction appears very solid with a metal frame, and the wood is real with a nice finish. I should note that my use case for this keyboard is an office setting requiring a mix of code and scientific applications, and in terms of its features this is certainly overkill (though I am very happy I was able to set a macro to type µ so I don't have to use an alt code). But I do appreciate the analog input capability, and if I were using this for gaming it would be excellent. I actually regret that I didn't know about this brand when I built my home PC, I would be excited to have this feature set for fun stuff! Highly recommended, if you're on the fence about a less well-established brand like I was you will not be disappointed.
reviews.author: Kirk Butler

reviews.title: Amazing Keyboard
reviews.comment: I couldn’t have picked a better keyboard in terms of feel, looks and responsiveness. The keys are buttery smooth and the sound is super satisfying. I love the wood accents, they’re subtle and that’s completely the look I was going for. The keychron launcher software is also very user friendly and the RGB light settings have incredibly variety. I’m extremely happy with this purchase so far.
reviews.author: Serg

reviews.title: It feels so good it makes you want to type!
reviews.comment: This is the most comfortable and slick feeling keyboard I've had in decades of pc'ing. I mean, it has to "sharp/softness" to it that can't be compared to mechanical keys. This is though my first magnetic so maybe that's why I'm all giddy over it. Regardless, I've had some top tier keyboards. I wanted this one because first, looks. I mean, that's real wood on the side. And the keyboard body is itself - HIGH QUALITY. It's a little weighting but I don't care about that because I'm not walking around with my keyboard. It stays placed and won't budge. Connection is pretty simple. It can be wired or wireless. I have had it wired but will be doing wireless soon. I've to do some re-arranging and definitely look forward to getting rid of the cable. Pros: Typing that's feels so good you'd not want to stop typing. The magnetism creating the springing touch is excellent. And I like the fact it can be adjusted. The keyboard is of high quality material. You won't feel ripped off at all if you get this keyboard. And the sound is excellent. Not banging or hard noise clicks. The keyboard layout is standard. Though I'm a gamer and editor I'm from the old school. And I still prefer a keypad. The F keys are also standard with functions tied in to them be default. This keyboard is a looker. And it feels so good to type on. It almost enhances one's WPM. Cons: I'm maybe spoiled from previous keyboards I've owned. But, I do not like that there is no volume knob. Instead, one has to hold down the "fn" (function) key and then whatever function you want to control (i.e. volume). I mean, a knob is quick and easy. Also, this keyboard has RGB. But, the light is very dull. Even when it's maxed out. I'm not expecting the bat signal, but, compared to other keyboards, this max seems like the minimum on other keyboards. I wish it could be more powerful. Overall: I'm VERY happy with this keyboard. There were a few sacrifices feature wise, but absolutely no regrets. I highly recommend it.
reviews.author: James M.

reviews.title: Best keyboard I've owned
reviews.comment: Excellent keyboard! The Keychron K10 HE feels incredibly smooth and responsive, a noticeable upgrade super precise and satisfying to type on. Keyboard is solid and premium, wood inlays are classy.  The LED's are a nice touch.  So many color options.  I use it for work.  I spend 8-10hr/day on computer.  It's very comfortable.  Worth the money.
reviews.author: Panayiote73

reviews.title: A great and quiet keyboard
reviews.comment:
So I bought this for my wife as she’s been wanting a new keyboard but is EXTREMLY picky about what she wants. We narrowed it down to 1.) it MUST be as quiet as possible. 2.)  keys needed to work with her nails. (She’s always having them done) 3.) must be backlit with see through keys.
This keyboard is very quiet; quieter than my mechanical, clikety-clakety, keyboard. The sound these keys make is very “thocky” - subtle but enjoyable. They have this “creamy” feel to them as you press down each key. You don’t have to push down hard at all. She is able to type using longer nails. The key caps have a small, concave shape to them that helps with her fingers not slipping off due to the length of the nails.
It’s rechargeable and it lasts for about 40 hrs or so before needing a charge with backlight off. Cut it in half with the backlight on.
Full keyboard- yes; 10 key is on it.
The keys aren’t see through but the backlit board is great regardless. You can adjust the brightness. Change the lighting options and the cycling speed. Great price for a “budget” keyboard.
reviews.author: Jose Aguilar

reviews.title: First impression: Good keyboard for typing, gaming, and small hands.
reviews.comment: I only just received this item today, so I cannot yet speak to its longevity, but I am very happy with it so far. My previous keyboard was a permanently borrowed Corsair Strafe RGB Mechanical Gaming Keyboard. It worked well enough, but one of the arrow keys had stopped working, and one of the letter keys was hit or miss if it worked. On top of that, it was very heavy (I game/type with the keyboard in my lap) and the cord loved getting in the way. This keyboard, on the other hand, is much lighter. It has a heft to it that seems to be just about right. It doesn't dig into my legs, but it's not so light that it feels cheap. Typing is fast and easy (I can type over 100 wpm with few errors on a regular day, but I am backspacing much less with this keyboard, and I seem to be able to go a bit faster) The sound is not too loud, nor too quiet, and is quite satisfying. I have small hands (small isotoners are a bit too long for my fingers) and it doesn't feel uncomfortable to reach all the standard keys. And even though it makes it longer than would be fully comfortable for long gaming sessions, the number keypad was a must-have for me as an old-school typist and data entry person. I do wish the keys had a bit of light coming through for when it's dark, but it's not essential for me since I've been touch typing since high school in the late 80s/early 90s. So far there has been no lag using it wirelessly with the 2.4hz option. I appreciate that the lighting goes away after 3 minutes of no typing and I look forward to seeing how long the battery lasts since I spend long periods of time either just using the mouse to navigate around streaming services and often have the computer asleep on days when I take care of the grandkid. Overall I'm happy to have found this purple keyboard, and am pleased with the quality for $60.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Great option!
reviews.comment: THE BEST keyboard I have ever owned. The sound is everything I was expecting and more, super creamy! The color goes great with my desk theme. The rainbow backlit is chef’s kiss & you can’t beat the price.
reviews.author: Dulce

reviews.title: Best sounding keyboard!
reviews.comment: I’ve gone through a lot of different mechanical keyboards over the years, and the Redragon K745 PRO Wireless Mechanical Keyboard is easily one of my favorites so far. I originally bought the purple version, but ended up switching to the blue one, which I like much better. The sound is what really stands out. This keyboard sounds super creamy, which is exactly what I was looking for. I personally prefer creamy keyboards over the really loud clicky ones, and this one has a smooth, satisfying sound that’s hard to find. The board uses linear switches with multiple layers of sound dampening, which helps create that softer typing sound. Another great feature is the multiple ways to connect. You can use it wired with USB-C, Bluetooth, or the 2.4GHz wireless dongle, so it’s really easy to switch between devices depending on what you’re using. It also comes with extra keycaps and a keycap remover, which makes customizing or cleaning the keyboard really simple. The key puller works well and makes swapping keys quick and easy. Overall, after trying a lot of mechanical keyboards, this is the first one that really had the exact sound and feel I was looking for. If you like smoother, creamy-sounding keyboards instead of loud clicky ones, this is definitely worth checking out.
reviews.author: Hannah

reviews.title: I bought this for gaming and ended up typing more
reviews.comment:
Just got the Redragon K745 Pro yesterday and after a few hours of gaming I’m honestly impressed. The sound is incredible — it’s one of those keyboards where the typing noise is genuinely satisfying and almost “brain calming.” I actually found myself typing more instead of using voice/chat because the sound is that good.  An unexpected benefit of this is that I'm looking for more excuses to type more often and procrastinating my writing less.
The stock switches are linear, and while I’m not totally in love with the feel (I prefer a little more tactile feedback), the acoustics are amazing. Compared to my old Corsair K70 with Speed Silver switches, this keyboard also feels like it has noticeably less travel, which I ended up liking.
My only real complaint is the included PBT keycaps aren’t shine-through, but that’s not a deal breaker. I already ordered a cheap shine-through PBT set and I’m looking forward to swapping them on.
Overall, for the price, this is a great keyboard if you care about sound, RGB, and want a hot-swappable board you can upgrade later.  If you aren't a competitive gamer something like this is more than enough, and you can find even cheaper deals on the smaller keyboards (TKL, 75%, 65% etc.)
I also spent too much time obsessively comparing and researching keyboards.  I know more about keyboards now then I ever thought I would want to.  If words like 'creamy' and 'thocky' make no sense now, you aren't the only one.  Once you hear and feel the difference you understand immediately.
reviews.author: 65galax1e

reviews.title: A Small Factor with Lighting and Switchable Keys Offers a Lot
reviews.comment:
This space saving design is kind of interest. I typically use keyboard that large because I want that numpad, which the G512 X98 has, but it removed some of the more specialized keys like Home and End, PG Up and PG down. This gives it a smaller footprint without removing the glorious numpad. I am still learning whether I find this good enough to replace the larger keyboard or if I am going to miss those buttons too often. Still on the subject of hardware, I love the the key removers and switch removes function as the keyboard feet. Too often we get these little parts that need to remain available but without any place to put them except some drawn or baggie with the hopes that when we need them we  one, remember where they are and two, remember what they are. This solves that problem complete. They're the feet of the keyboard and they are labeled.
The included USB A / USB C cord is long but not braided. I like the feel of braided cords better and they don't kink, but if length is what you are looking for, it's there.  The keys are solid feeling and are actually quieter than my cherry mx keyboard. This would please anyone around me.  The volume and lighting knob is easy, love the feel of them and pushing them mutes it.  As for lighting, I am still convinced somewhere out there is some sort of programming boot camp that everyone gets together to figure out how to make the light schemes a lot more difficult than they should be. The software is just not enjoyable to use. I spent an hourish just messing around with it and getting my purples and blues and just generally getting a theme I prefer. I hate that the keyboard fades and then the lightning turns off within minutes of no use. I've searched online looking for solutions, but it doesn't work.  This is a software issue of some kind, and I am sure a solution is out there somewhere. Now the hot swappable keys for analog and mechanical is what makes this keyboard more adjustable than most. You can change the coloring. You can change the keys themselves and get the sensitivity you want. It says it is hot swappable but the software recommends you disconnect the keyboard to make the change which is... not hot-swappable. Recommendations is not a n explicit no though. So hot-swappable does work even if the software suggests you need to do otherwise.
If a small form factor is what you are looking for, with a num pad, and not losing the handy features of lighting and volume control, this could very well be what you are looking for. The key presses are familiar, the ability to change the lighting and the keys themselves quickly are all pluses.
reviews.author: Tanya McHenry

reviews.title: Compact analog keyboard with strong features
reviews.comment:
This Logitech G512 X 98 keyboard feels well built and has a clean white design that looks sharp on a desk. The hot swappable TMR analog and mechanical switch setup is the main strength, giving it more adjustment than a basic gaming keyboard. Custom actuation from 0.1 to 4.0 mm, rapid trigger, an 8K polling rate, and LIGHTSYNC RGB all make it feel responsive and flexible during initial use. The linear switches feel smooth, and the compact 98 layout keeps most keys without taking up too much space. The main drawback is that the feature set comes with a higher cost.
Pros
~ Smooth linear switch feel
~ Hot swappable switch design
~ Fast 8K polling rate
~ Clean compact 98 layout
Cons
~ Higher cost
~ Wired only setup
reviews.author: KG

reviews.title: Above expectations.
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/D1Me8S+qI1L.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/61VKrGINn0L._SY256.jpg I’ve used almost every mechanical keyboard imaginable, believe me it gets old and you will miss the simple quiet membrane keyboard.
I started with “Razer” and moved up to “Das keyboard” and many other more affordable options later on. The clicky keys got old and some brands started releasing linear keys that are quiet to press. These sounded good but lacked the resistive feedback in some cases. I recently got an MSI keyboard that was almost perfect. This Logitech keyboard is perfect in almost every way, the feedback of the keys, the customization, analog switches…I never cared for backlighting except for the enhanced ability to see the keys but this keyboard has some amazing options and customizable lighting zones you can set up based on the game you want to play.
Pros:
- awesome minimalist design that doesn’t eliminate all necessary keys
-endless customization
-perfect key lighting options
-linear switches that are nice and quiet. Fun to press.
-lighting turns off after a while of no activity
-great weight stays in place
-room saving on desk even with the 98%
-adjustable switch distance (using Logitech G hub software)
-
Cons:

-If you remove the sticker on the back to access the analog switches the “SAPP” rings will freely fall out so be aware of this.
reviews.author: Jess & Randy.

reviews.title: Smooth keys, very high quality
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/C1la4Qev8xL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/61DPV9IerKL._SY256.jpg I’ve been really impressed with this keyboard so far. Right out of the box, it looks super clean and modern, especially with the white and teal color combination. The RGB lighting is bright without being overwhelming, and the underglow around the base gives it a really premium gaming/setup aesthetic.
The keys feel smooth and responsive while typing, and the switches have a satisfying feel without being excessively loud. I also really like the included volume/control knobs at the top corner — they make it feel much more high-end and are actually very convenient to use.
reviews.author: Luis

reviews.title: This keyboard is Razor sharp.
reviews.comment:
First off, this Razor Huntsman V3 Pro is a great keyboard, period!
In 2015 I purchased a Logitech G910 Orion Spark. After a little over a year (as the warranty had expired), I had the left CTRL key cap break. I contacted Logitech, and to my surprise, they sent a complete key cap set for the keyboard. I was sold on Logitech after that. Time moved forward, and eventually, the keyboard started missing key strokes, where double and triple strokes on a letter became a sign that replacement was in order. Along with the Logitech keyboard, I purchased a Logitech mouse G502, which served well for over 10 years. The presets on the mouse started to bounce off my DPI settings, so I started researching keyboards and mice. I ordered a Logitech mouse G502 Hero since it received consistently good reviews. Unfortunately, the mouse wheel had a heavy spot, which would allow web pages to scroll without any input, so it was returned. I also purchased a Corsair K70 keyboard since the reviews were good. I liked the Cherry MX switches, yet the key caps do not cover the bottom of the switches. From the top looking down (which most pictures show) the RGB lighting looks good; however, from the front, it looks like little colored teeth shining from the bottom of the key caps, it just looks cheap.  The slope of the key caps from front to back was not constant. The wrist pad I read about was soft to the touch; somehow, Corsair found a way to make small triangles out of plastic feel soft and yet be as hard as a rock. So, I sent it back as well. Remember Razor? This is a review about Razor. This keyboard, Razor Huntsman V3 Pro, is great to type with and to game with as well. With the Synapse 4 program suite, it not only gives this keyboard life it also connects my new Razor Balilisk V3 35K mouse and Razor Hypersense headphones without a hitch. I've been a PC gamer since the 80's with my first PC, a 386 with 1 meg of sipp ram, 40 MB hard drive, and a 256K monitor. To date, this mouse and keyboard combo is the best I have purchased. I remember throwing quarters at Brick Breaker and Asteroids on a black and white screen. At 67, I game daily, you're never too old to game, and I'm always out of gum. :-)
reviews.author: Shindoru

reviews.title: Accidentally Funded an Esports Career
reviews.comment:
I thought I was buying a keyboard.
What I actually purchased was a glowing, clicky portal to another dimension where my son communicates exclusively in callouts like “HE’S ONE HP!” and “CLIP THAT!”
First of all, this thing is TINY. It’s 60%, which apparently means 100% serious. No number pad. No wasted space. Just pure, compact, competitive energy. It’s so small it looks like it skips leg day — but don’t let that fool you. This keyboard means business.
The keys? Lightning fast. I don’t know what “analog optical switches” are, but my son explained it to me with the intensity of a TED Talk. Something about actuation points and competitive advantage. All I know is he now blames losses on “ping” instead of his keyboard, so I guess it works.
The RGB lighting is aggressive. This keyboard doesn’t glow — it announces itself. At night his room looks like a small but highly profitable nightclub. I’m half expecting a cover charge.
Build quality? Solid. It sounds like tiny, confident raindrops when he types. Or like a very determined squirrel sending emails.
Has it improved his gameplay? According to him, absolutely. According to his report card, we’re still evaluating performance metrics.
Would I buy it again?
Yes. Because if we’re going to hear rapid-fire clicking for hours, it might as well be on a keyboard that could qualify for the Olympics.
Five stars.
Zero stars for my electricity bill.
reviews.author: Joey Smith

reviews.title: Top-tier performance for competitive play
reviews.comment:
I decided to pick this board up because I mainly play shooters and I was getting tired of my full-sized setup taking up so much mouse pad real estate. I wanted something that would give me more room to move without sacrificing the arrow keys, so this TKL layout seemed like the right middle ground.
The switches are honestly the standout feature here. The analog optical triggers feel incredibly snappy, which is exactly what you need for competitive gaming. You can really feel the difference with the rapid trigger feature; it makes strafing and movement feel much more precise compared to a standard mechanical switch. The build itself is excellent, too. The doubleshot PBT keycaps have a nice texture that doesn't get slippery, and having the dedicated media dial and buttons right there is a convenient touch I use more than I expected.
It is a very compact unit, which fits perfectly on my desk and clears up a ton of space. It feels premium and heavy enough to stay put during intense matches. If you are looking for a serious piece of gear to tighten up your movement in games, this is a fantastic option.
reviews.author: Troy

reviews.title: Great Gamer Keyboard!!
reviews.comment: My boyfriend loves his 60% keyboard! He’s a gamer so this keyboard gets used every single day. Gamer people know they need desk space to be able to move their mouse around freely without hitting the keyboard. This keyboard is a perfect size for gamers or even regular use if your limited desk space. It’s easy to use, set up and you can change the click sounds on the settings! The lights aren’t too bright either which I thought would be of concern but it isn’t a problem. You can also change the lights with several modes. It’s lightweight but durable! I also bought him the 60% arm rest from Razer. Great gift for a gamer of daily computer user.
reviews.author: Levanna Lopez

reviews.title: Great product
reviews.comment: Work great and feels sturdy!
reviews.author: The sharesquare,inc

reviews.title: Amazing product
reviews.comment: Great product, Logitech never disappoints. Super comfortable, very durable. Took some getting used to not having a number pad though 😅
reviews.author: Pawel Z.

reviews.title: Great keyboard for rapid trigger, more budget friendly vs the wooting 80he
reviews.comment:
Coming from a wooting 80he, this is good. I had to return my wooting because the rapid trigger would make buttons stopped working, I even had another one sent to me and still same issues, could be my hardware I have no idea, so looking for a replacement I’ve choose this one over the razer which is a big competitor and mostly choose Logitech to stay in the ecosystem because I have a super light 2 mouse.
This review will be compared to the wooting 80 he which is the best keyboard in the market.
The wooting keys feel way better and the sound clicks are much better too. Coming to Logitech is a huge difference I wish the sound of clicks were more dreamy like wooting also wish the buttons are softer
Software to me is all the same on both of them. Wooting probably has a slight edge but not by much. Wooting has more rgb lights and it sticks out more if you care for that.
Rapid trigger works excellent and it feels like I’m moving faster on games on cs2/valorant the respond time Is amazing the upgrade to a rapid trigger keyboard is worth it for that alone.
This keyboard has a volume knob which is big to me and wooting doesn’t.
Overall if the wooting was able to work on my computer I’ve give it a 5/5 and this Logitech keyboard 4.5/5 for the price
I got this brand new on sale $150 which imo should be the retail price, I wouldn’t pay $190 might as well spend more on a wooting.
My honest non sponsored review.
reviews.author: Yah

reviews.title: Great keyboard except for one major issue
reviews.comment: Great keyboard, very smooth and solid feel to the actual typing. Really feels built to last, and the texture is pleasant to the touch. It's not slick like uncoated keyboard keys. One thing that's annoying, though, is this keyboard has a tendency to disconnect, and unplugging it and replugging it in doesn't seem to help matters. The only thing that fixes this is a full PC reboot, which is time consuming and annoying. I hope they fix this. It'd be one thing if it were a bluetooth issue but this is a *wired* keyboard, so it makes even less sense.
reviews.author: Tech Sherpa

reviews.title: Innovative Hall-Effect Analog/Linear Mechanical Switch Keyboard
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/F1CCS4XuQyL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/81IFba4Pj2L._SY256.jpg Typing experience was amazing. The key press feels noticeably smoother and faster than Cherry MX Brown Switch as well as Cherry MX Blue and Cherry MX Red Switches. You can customize rapid trigger, key actuation point, as well as Lightsync RGB lighting, Button mapping, etc. via Logitech G Hub software.
Only side is that it does not come with numpads since this is TKL (Ten Keyless) version which was why it was specifically designed for competitive eSport players to compete other players during tournament. But since I'm not pro tournament gamer, I just want to use this keyboard for typing, gaming, and professional productivity work such as animation and sketches. In addition, it doesn't come with Lightspeed Wireless technology which is a bummer. Not only that, but it also doesn't come with carry pouch to transport for vacation on flight.
Yes, it comes with USB C to USB A Cable to connect from your keyboard to your computer.
Other than that, the Hall-Effect mechanical switches were very impressive and innovative to address actuation key presses, and also ideal to improve gameplay responsiveness and especially input lag, regardless game engine title.
P.S. if you need numpads, you can purchase numpads from 3rd party vendors which they sell wide variety of key numpads on the market which may cost roughly between $15-$25 before sales tax.
reviews.author: Danny Lim

reviews.title: R65 vs. R87 Pro - You should get this keyboard ASAP!
reviews.comment:
Let's cut to the basics, lighting, sound, and feel.
Today I will be comparing the Royal Kludge R65 keyboard and this one.
R65 + R87 Pro = Both have amazing build quality, no input lag, I love the overall layout and everything on both of these keyboards and can really see this being a open door to anyone wanting to come into the world of keyboard enthusiasts, and the best part both keyboards come with a tool that you can use to pull out mechanical switches and keycaps.
Lighting:
Both have amazing lighting, but its worth noting the R87 Pro (this keyboard) has the RGB lights on the bottom of the switch so lighting could be a little off to be honest. But overall, lighting is there and the keyboard looks amazing due to the side profile also having RGB lighting.
Sound: This is where it gets good.
R65 - If you love creamy switches and a nice smaller design to it, I would suggest getting the R65
R87 Pro - If you love creamy switches but also love the thocky sound I would recommend the R87 Pro!
Feel:
Both keyboards feel amazing due to their pre lubed switches and I honestly feel like they are very similar in feel. Both feel absolutely priceless and literally the best typing experience I've ever had.
Typing:
I love linear switches on my keyboards now than ever, I used to want to feel the tactile feel and all that but overall typing on both keyboards (R65 and R87) are fantastic and I would go as far to say they both are better than some of the razer keyboards I've used myself.
Notable mention: Royal Kludge, you gained another loyal customer today, and not only that, the fact that you did something no one ever does with their products which is make it to where you don't need to download anything for lighting affects to work flawlessly is the cherry on top of this amazing product.
Both their R65 and R87 Pro come with no input lag at all. I've ever had any sort of issue with typing, gaming, producing, or coding with either of these keyboards.
What's the main difference between the 2?
R65 is going to be the top choice for someone who wants a nice 65% keyboard that sounds as good as it looks and is as good as the price is.
The R87 is what I would recommend to those that also do coding, gaming, producing, and more. This keyboard has everything you will ever need whenever it comes down to basic productivity and gaming. I was absolutely sold whenever they released this keyboard.
Overall score for Royal Kludge for the R87 Pro is 5/5 stars in my book. If you are looking for a good keyboard that won't let you down and is backed by an amazing company with promising quality and all, I would easily recommend this to you, and to all of my friends.
Good job Royal Kludge!
reviews.author: Josh

reviews.title: Great keyboard
reviews.comment: I can't believe I snagged this for under $60. Board feels solid, the typing sounds and feels nice. This keyboard is also pretty quiet which I'd a plus because I don't wear headphones. I was going to replace the keys but once I typed on these MDA keys I instantly became a fan. Love the volume knob as well. My only gripe is the rgb color is slightly off and it's hard to get the software to work on Linux. This keyboard feels more premium than my previous $100+ dad and in paradise boards.
reviews.author: Mike

reviews.title: Updated Review: After Speaking with Amazon Retailer
reviews.comment:
This board is absolutely amazing when it comes to the stock switches and it has bright south facing lighting. I’m not super knowledgeable when it comes to custom boards, as I’m still learning, but I’d say this would have to rank up there among budget boards, for sure.
Unfortunately, my RGB’s became defective after ~3-4 months and going through Royal Kludge official, I did not have a good experience. However, the certified reseller which I bought my board from here on Amazon is was absolutely fantastic. They offered a full replacement at no cost to me and without having to return my old board. And it’s been over 6 months, so I’m not sure exactly how long their warranty is, but it anything happens during your warranty they will make it right, even if it’s an issue that doesn’t affect functionality like the RGB’s failing.
Furthermore, the seller informed me that you’re generally supposed to contact the actual seller of your board to get the most effective service. It’s very possible that my bad experience with RK’s customer service was simply due to the inefficiency of me contacting an entirely different entity than the company that sold my board. And even though I didn’t have a great experience with RK, they tried to help anyways despite me contacting the wrong place for service. It’s very likely they were avoiding RMA simply because I didn’t buy the board from them and all they could really do was answer my questions and try to help fix the problem in other ways. Still, I wish RK was more transparent with the firmware files for qmk flashing as the only way to obtain it is to contact RK. There’s no link or anything in the manual which would be nice if it was readily available to the end user.
In any case, overall it’s an amazing board and if you contact your actual seller the service should be exceptional. I cannot speak for any seller, but the seller I’m reviewing here and the one for this keyboard here on Amazon is fantastic. They contacted me quickly and said they wanted to make things right with my keyboard as well as my experience with RK. So as I stated earlier, they did a full replacement and all they asked was I provide some pictures so they could send the information to their R&D team to ensure they can prevent it from happening in the future. Which I think is really cool and shows they’re committed not only to fixing immediate issues, but long term issues with their products as well.
After being contacted by the seller and speaking with them I would absolutely recommend this keyboard as well as the customer service of this retailer. It’s a great board, great warranty, and great service. And of course, the keyboard itself is awesome. I literally had no complaints and other than getting unlucky with the RGB’s dying in my old one and the firmware not being easily accessible, it’s a great little budget board that types like a dream. I feel like the “cream switches” that come with the board are a perfect description for what the typing experience is like.

reviews.title: Great keyboard... but the low-profile version should be called the Node96
reviews.comment: I was extremely excited about this launch. I love 100% low-profile keyboards, especially with deep thocky sounds and premium feels. I've been desperate for something comparable to the K5 Max (my daily driver) or G915 X, but with a sound and feel profile similar to nuphy's keyboards. I was extremely disappointed when I saw that the low-profile version of this keyboard is actually their 75% layout with a numpad stitched on. This is a 96% keyboard, not 100%. Still, it's the closest this side of the market has come to 100%, so I wanted to give it a shot. Truly, it does feel and sound great. Typical nuphy quality. I have no complaints about the keyboard, and typing on this was a blast. The web app at nuphy.io was also simple to use and the keyboard was highly configurable; compared to the competition, the web app hits every mark except it lacks the ability to configure a numlock indicator (via RGB backlighting or otherwise). If you like 96% keyboards, or if you like 75% keyboards but want a numpad, and you prefer the thocky sound profiles of nuphy or lofree, then this could be among the best keyboards on the market for you right now. But as expected, I myself cannot use this as a daily driver. I've learned to take advantage of nearly every single key on a 100% keyboard. The shorter right shift key can be learned, as can the new locations of the various console keys (ins/home/pgup/pgdn/etc), but the missing right alt/opt key proved to be a deal-breaker in real usage. I hope nuphy releases something comparable to this keyboard in a true 100% layout in the future.

reviews.title: Best low-profile, nearly 100%, keyboard I've ever used.
reviews.comment: Great keyboard!  It's nearly the 100% full layout and significantly narrower than a usual 100% keyboard.  The nuphy io website worked flawlessly for rebinding a few keys.  Works perfect on my linux machine as well.  The default show desktop key (designed for windows) is actually just a Super + D keybind, which I have bound as my launcher in linux!  I got mine with the brown switches which are very satisfying. My only very minor gripe would be I wish the extra keycaps included a colored key with ESC written on it and a colored Enter key.

reviews.comment: Second Nuphy keyboard I’ve purchased / the 100% layout works much better for me as opposed to my small halo. Switches do make a difference, found I like the brown switch (over the blush). Compatibility into my Mac set-up was seamless and looks great aesthetically as well.
reviews.author: Kevin

reviews.title: Best High-End looking base
reviews.comment:
If you're on the hunt for an affordable yet well-built RGB keyboard base, this keyboard has got you coverd. Priced competitively, it manages to deliver a sturdy construction without compromising on quality. It’s durable enough for daily use, and the finish is sleek and minimalist, offering a modern look that fits well with any desk setup.
One of the most impressive features of this keyboard base is its RGB lighting. The lighting is vibrant and customizable, offering a range of effects that can be easily adjusted through software or keyboard shortcuts. You can choose from a variety of pre-set profiles or create your own, with the ability to tweak brightness and speed. The RGB illumination provides a captivating glow that enhances your gaming or typing experience, making it a visual treat without breaking the bank.
In terms of performance, the keyboard base is surprisingly good for its price. The layout and key switch compatibility ensure smooth typing and gaming. While the base itself doesn’t come with switches or keycaps, it’s highly compatible with most standard key switches, making it an excellent base for custom builds. The mounting options for stabilizers are stable, and the base doesn’t flex much, even under heavy use, which is a nice bonus at this price point.
What truly sets this keyboard base apart is its affordability. While many RGB keyboard bases on the market can be quite expensive, this one offers a budget-friendly alternative without sacrificing the quality you’d expect from a premium product. It’s a great option for anyone looking to build their own keyboard but doesn’t want to spend a fortune on the base alone. Whether you're new to custom keyboards or an experienced enthusiast, this RGB base offers a perfect balance of performance, aesthetics, and value.

reviews.title: Great Barebones board
reviews.comment: I order the first one which 2 keys did not work, i believe this was due to water damage because it was heavily raining the day it was delivered. I returned it and got another one back and it works perfectly fine. The software is pretty good and all the led features work and it also works with signal rgb which is a huge advantage, but you do have to disable the glorius software first. I got gatreon brown linear switches and it is very quite, and has a very nice feel to it. The noise level is perfect for my needs and is not picked up by any mics. I did buy the Barebones, which was a pretty good price. the keycaps I got with it are https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0D541DJWW/?coliid=I20UVEF1S9QNY6&colid=8IWVDSFIR9KI&ref_=list_c_wl_lv_ov_lig_dp_it&th=1 note this is not an affiliates link. They are fully compatible with this keyboard.

reviews.title: Seriously good, but one flaw.
reviews.comment: I was planning to wait on writing a review to see how this thing is in a few weeks, but I was so impressed that I felt inclined to write one now. I ordered the prebuilt one as I was planning on just getting the barebones, keycaps and switches, but this one was on sale for cheaper than the barebones, so I got it. I also ordered Kahil jades and different keycaps. I'm not a fan of linear switches, but out of the box, I was seriously considering keeping the ones it came with as they are so incredibly smooth, sound amazing, and have a good actuation force (I was in Best Buy earlier this week looking at keyboards, and the closest one to this that I tested was a $250 Logitech board, this one is seriously good feeling). Anyways, I decided to stick to the original plan and throw my new switches on there, and I am still very impressed. Good sound, stabilizers do not rattle, and the keys don't move around. Build quality is very good, nice and heavy. Looks great on my desk. One complaint is the lighting. The software is a bit tricky to use and the lights just aren't that bright, and the color is off. -1 star for that. Everything else exceeded my expectations.

Mine had yellow switches and they felt very good. I recommend this keyboard if you run MS Windows or are a gamer. Read about the features and software requirements to see if they meet your own needs. The keyboard worked out of the box, but the synapse configuration software is for MS Windows, so I could not change the backlighting from the factory setting. You can change the brightness, but you cannot change the colors or lighting pattern, which is constantly changing rainbow of colors. Feels great but no tactile feedback. Gaming is better but typing you have to get used to. Still highly recommend and great Razer quality! Don't forget to get a deathadder mouse, best mouse IMHO!

reviews.author: KH

reviews.title: Amazing keyboard with light silent switches
reviews.comment: This keyboard is definitely worth the price. The keys are extremely sensitive and barely any touch will trigger a keypress. If that's a problem for you, this keyboard might not be the one, I, however personally love it. The keys are extremely quiet. There are many setting that are useful in the software. Snap tap is extremely easy to both set up and use. And there are many options for the lighting, if that's a thing you're into. reviews.author: Judah Eberly

reviews.title: Excellent keyboard
reviews.comment: I've used a lot of keyboards going all the way back to the original IBM PC. Most modern keyboards feel mushy to me. This feels great. I bought both the brown and the blue switch variations. The blue had a great feel, but its relatively high-pitched click was annoying. The brown is closer to a Goldilocks switch, quiet and with good tactility, although just a tiny bit mushy. I chose the K3 for its low-profile design, as I had read that the standard Keychron keyboards are very thick and need wrist rests. The K3 at only 7/8" thick feels fine without one. Key travel is also quite good. Fresh out of the box, I don't seem to have lost any typing speed compared with the MacBook Pro keyboard which I've been using for the last few years. I haven't had any problems with the Bluetooth connection. I have it paired with three devices – an iMac, a MacBook Pro and an iPad Pro. Just a few seconds each to pair initially, then no trouble with any of them. Switching between devices takes just a couple of keystrokes. As a Mac user, I really like that the media function keys work out of the box and are labeled properly. Likewise the command and option keys. I have no real need for the backlighting and certainly not for all the fancy, flashy chasing light modes. It's a keyboard, not a theater marquee. But I do find it handy to have on at minimum brightness when I have to work in a darkened room. If there's one thing I wish Keychron offered, it's a low-profile numeric keypad to go with this. I didn't want a full-size keyboard like the K5 which would force me to reach pretty far for my trackpad. But a numeric keypad comes in handy when I have to type in more than few digits, and it would be nice to have one to put to the right of the trackpad.
reviews.author: Spirit of 76

reviews.title: Excellent reasonably priced slim mechanical TKL keyboard!
reviews.comment: I've been looking for a slim TKL mechanical keyboard for a long time. I've read about the Keychron products, but hesitated to pull the trigger because other brands had more reviews with similar ratings. I shouldn't have and hope my review will help others who are relying on the number of reviews to make an informed decision. This little beauty is the best slim TKL mechanical keyboard I've tried by a long shot! The form factor is perfect, quality is great (especially given the very reasonable price) and it feels and works great! I might end up buying one or two more, one for the office and the other just so I have a replacement for when this one wears out. I have not tried using it in wireless mode or using it with a Mac. The default key configuration is for Mac, but there are spare key caps to replace Mac specific keys with Win (which I promptly did :) ). It is small enough to leave plenty of space on your desk, yet heavy enough to not move about when you type. The keyboard comes with brown mechanical switches, which are smooth and quiet enough to not annoy people sitting around you. All keys are mapped correctly to their designated functions. I'm actually using it with a Chrome book, was super impressed that all the keys do what they said they would, even the screenshot button. All in all, I've very happy with my purchase - great product Keychron!
