reviews.title: Fantastic keyboard with one minor complaint
reviews.comment: I think it is a great keyboard - I enjoy everything about the switches, keycaps, lighting, features, software and it's appearance. It has a very great typing feel and has performed perfectly with gaming and work. My only complaint is that I feel the magnetic cover could have slightly stronger magnets. Other than that, I love this keyboard and look forward to using it for many years to come!
reviews.author: Stephen N.

reviews.title: Defective Product, Worse Service
reviews.comment: Multiple burnt out LED lights up on arrival. HyperX and Amazon refused to replace or acknowledge the issue, both placing blame on the other party.
reviews.author: Kyle

reviews.title: PERFECT FOR GAMERS
reviews.comment: I am honestly very impressed with the quality of this keyboard. The keys feel smooth when typing optimizing overall performance and the RGB backlighting looks sick! I really like the dedicated media controls and how easy it is to set up this keyboard. It comes with a usb C power cable which in my opinion could be a bit longer. It also comes with a tool to help remove the keys. This keyboard has a lot of customization options and for the price I think it’s a great deal!
reviews.author: Joshua Lively

reviews.title: Great keyboard!
reviews.comment: The HyperX Alloy 75 keyboard can be incredibly useful in a studio setup for musicians. Its compact design saves valuable desk space. The responsive switches ensure accurate input, making it great for composing music or controlling software instruments. Additionally, the customizable RGB lighting can create a visually inspiring atmosphere in the studio, enhancing creativity. With programmable macros, musicians can streamline their workflow by assigning common tasks to specific keys, saving time and increasing efficiency. Overall, the HyperX Alloy 75 keyboard is a versatile tool that can greatly benefit musicians.
reviews.author: Kenzie Coyne

reviews.title: Best value for the cost!
reviews.comment: I have only had the keyboard for a couple days- so I will come back and update if anything changes. But this seems like the best deal available right now. Even being refurbished the keyboard appears to be in excellent shape. For anyone looking to get into a gaming keyboard I would highly recommend this deal. Great value for the insanely low cost. RGB is bright and the keys are super sensitive.
reviews.author: Bridger & Taylor

reviews.title: Fine keyboard but had to replace the first. Second with same problem.
reviews.comment:
The first one I ordered had a gunked up/glitchy volume knob that would change around the pc’s levels randomly. Either you can lube that yourself but risk making it unreturnable or just get it replaced.
Update: Good value but it happened again so maybe it's the inherent product that's vulnerable to volume knob inconsistencies. Some people fix it by putting some tissue in it but we shouldn't have to.
reviews.author: Corey OD

reviews.title: Great board for the price
reviews.comment: Great quality board. I love the rotary knob and the backlight. I do wish you could turn it off completely, so far I've only figured out how to switch between key backlight + side lights, just backlight, and just side lights. I got this refurbished and it included everything in the box and didn't seem like it had been used at all. Everything was clean, no scratches, no missing documentation or accessories. One thing I have noticed is the right function key doesn't seem to register on my mac even though it does work for accessing keyboard settings, so I expect there's a setting or configuration I need to change for this and not an issue with the board itself. I love the silver aluminum color. It's not white, it's definitely a light metallic silver. I have this paired with some Durock Ice King switches and some cheap Amazon keycaps, and it's a great typing experience.
reviews.author: Zach

reviews.title: The first one looked used
reviews.comment: Order this frame for my son. Opened it and everything seemed fine. Installed switches and he hooked it up to his computer and found out some of the keys were working. So we swapped out the switches, still not working. Requested a replacement and got it the next day (quick and easy). When opening the package of the replacement, compared to the other this one didn’t look like it had been opened before, frame in a plastic bag. I think someone bought and returned the first one we got. Maybe a little better QC team to ensure this doesn’t happen with that same one we returned.
reviews.author: Jeremy Ruffe

reviews.title: Needs some tweaks but it's perfect
reviews.comment: Buy the glorious V2 or better stabilizers. Be sure to lube up your new stabilizers. The pre installed ones are bad. Be sure to update firmware with glorious core and then you can flash qmk to be compatible with signalrgb. This board is excellent value. With the updates and new stabilizers it sounds very good. I have silent switches and it feels and sounds perfect.
reviews.author: Jonathan.B

reviews.title: Did not come working
reviews.comment: Did not come working, unfortunately. the weight is perfect, and I like the sound of the lynx switched I got, but it needs to be able to work for it to matter.
reviews.author: Pearl

reviews.title: Heavy and solid keyboard
reviews.comment: The build quality is ridiculously good, it’s like a keyboard inside a block of marble. That being said, it is super heavy - which is also a good thing.
reviews.author: Ed

reviews.title: Very solid choice for a first mechanical build.
reviews.comment: First off, it's a floating key design. This means there is no bezel around the switches. That look was popular with gaming keyboards a few years ago. Custom keyboard enthusiasts generally frown upon it now. That out of the way, at 55 dollars this board is a good buy. It feels solid. The weight is from 3 cheap metal blocks stuck in the case, not from thick, high-density structural materials like some high-end boards But the weights don't move around, and are only visible with the case open. My board is modified. I replaced the included foam with thicker neoprene foam. I left the stabilizers stock, as they seemed to be adequately lubed. If you're doing your first build, they might not bother you. They're better than those on cheap, standard/gaming keyboards. But if you're looking for good sound, you might want to consider modifying or replacing the stabilizers. With Kailh Pro Purple switches, the look, sound, and feel of this board is something I'm proud of. I've gotten compliments on it several times. I you're looking to build your first budget mechanical keyboard and don't want to go with a more enthusiast entry level board, I say go for it. This is a great platform to start with. If I couldn't build another board and had to use this one indefinitely, I think I'd be quite happy with it. But building custom keyboards is addictive. I've already ordered some higher-end entry-level boards to explore the hobby further. I'm going for more thock next time.
reviews.author: Guardfather

reviews.title: Fantastic entry level board for mech enthusiasts or p much anyone
reviews.comment: This is my first jump into custom mech keyboards and all my criticisms are nit picky garbage that doesn’t at all change the fact that I highly recommend this board. First note: the included keycap pry tool is a bit finicky to get out of the chassis and the experience of trying to pry it out makes me nervous I might scratch or damage the case. Second note: documentation doesn’t say anything about the win lock key’s existence and there aren’t labels for the two LED’s that sit above the arrow keys (caps lock and win lock respectively). Only other criticism: I sometimes wish the feet on the bottom of the board propped it up a bit higher. Now for the good stuff: the case feels well built, sounds nice, the stabs are a huge upgrade over the stock crap I was using before, the RGB looks great and is very flexible, the software is highly customizable and has great macro support, absolutely zero noticeable input delay or rollover issues, and even the included cable is pretty sweet. Honestly really enjoy using this board, I don’t see myself upgrading past it any time soon. Again, all my criticisms are basically non-issues in day to day use, and this is overall a 5 star product. These minor criticisms are really more there for the manufacturers’ benefit than users because all of these issues are pretty easy fixes if they were to make another edition of the board and this is just my two cents. To someone looking at getting into custom mech keyboards, this is one of the best options out there and I stress again that after messing with this board for a while I absolutely do not see myself needing to upgrade any time soon.
reviews.author: Sam

reviews.title: Very nice, prelubed stabs, put one popped easily
reviews.comment: To say this is the best barebones keyboard for the price out there would be an understatement. Arrived with two keycaps, switch puller and keycap removal puller. Along with a 4-6 feet cable, not sure exactly. The cable is braided very nice, long, and durable. Now let’s talk about the actual keyboard itself. It has a awesome durable frame, good elevation clips to put it on a angle, and it’s super beautiful. No big logos anywhere, and has a silver outlining. The stabilizers are awesome, insane. They all come Pre-Lubed which is outstanding for this price, and they are nice stabilizers in general. Although the left shift stabilizer popped, which basically it’s like the sound of it stock. It doesn’t effect it working wise. It will though change the sound of it so it sounds like a regular old stabilizer. That’s OK, as long as you have a good switch to pair it with. I used Gateron Yellows lubed, and they sound just immaculate. They were super easy to pop in, but one of them if you misplace the switch, the one or two pins bend which isn’t good. You can try bending them back, but it could be hard depending on how bent it got. I do think the RGB could use a tiny, tiny bit of help. Don’t get me wrong, the software is awesome. But not that. When you turn it on with no switches, it’s super bright, not with switches. I used Gateron Yellows lubed and Gateron switches have the standard opening for the RGB, but it still doesn’t shine through with colored HK gaming Gateron Lubed Yellows. I highly recommend getting the GMMK switch test pack along with this, so you can hear them in the board itself and choosing which one you like, you can’t find Gateron yellows in the Test Pack, but you can find switches like, Kailh Coppers, Kailh Box Brown, Kailh White Box, Kailh Red box, Gateron Blue, Gateron Green, and a few more. The pack also comes with O-rings as well. I honestly believe the Drop Barebones Keyboards are good, but not for the hefty price, (Around 170-200$) so I really think, this is a great option for people that wanna build but don’t wanna solder and program. Thank you for your time.
reviews.author: James W. Althoff

reviews.title: This is a great board for a first build!
reviews.comment: First, let me start off with the fact that I got this on the Black Friday deal for $19.99. So that in itself is just a great deal for a DIY keyboard. I was very surprised that this kit actually came with a thin (and I mean thin) layer of foam in the bottom of the board. It also had another thicker type insert that I personally have never experienced in a kit. It is a heavier/rubbery type of padding with all of the holes for the mounting stems cut out. There are 2 metal plates added for weight that can be removed at your discretion. This board is quite customizable for what it is. It's a very slim body in a floating keycap style. I will say that putting in the switches on this board was the most difficult that I have ever come across so far. It did come with a nice, braided cable that is USB C also. All in all, I would highly recommend this board kit to anyone who is looking to get into building their first keyboard, even at the current price.
reviews.author: Slussman

reviews.title: Excellent Board for First Time Builders
reviews.comment: I bought this product with the goal in mind to build my first keyboard, I already had my switches (Kailh Box Jade) and keycaps (HyperX Pudding), and I just now needed something to build on. I chose this as it comes from a company from whom I have heard before and have seen many positive reviews, and now I see why. While not super heavy on its own, the case and the plate are very rigid and sturdy and show quality construction, and once the switches and caps are on, it feels very solid. All the stabilizers on the board had no rattle at all, which was something that I have never had on a keyboard before, but feels amazing to type on. All in all this product was definitely worth the money, if I had one negative thing to say about it, it is not even hardware related. My only problem is that the software that controls the RGB and macros is not very in-depth and can be described as very rudimentary with not a whole lot of customizability. Aside from that though, this board has earned all the highest marks that I could give.
reviews.author: Andy

reviews.title: Excellent keyboard for the price with great volume wheel
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/B1MRVvTcokL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/61AYiA8BGEL._SY256.jpg For context, when I got this keyboard, I already had a Lofree flow (10/10 switches, 6/10 Bluetooth connection management) and a budget keyboard with blue switches. I use the flow for my main PC and the budget one at work, and I wanted another keyboard for everything else, including travel. I love brown switches and low profile caps. I've been using my RK for a few months at the time of writing this review.
I have to say, I'm blown away by the quality of this keyboard, given its price ($70 at time of purchase).
**Battery**: I absolutely love the massive battery. I was a little thrown off by the hefty weight of the keyboard (not necessary a drawback for me, just unusual), but when I realized I could use it for days and not worry about plugging it in at all, it occurred to me how nice that was. No more battery budgeting!
**Connections**: The small monitor on the volume wheel and the solid variety of ways to connect to devices make it a breeze to set up and switch between devices. I hardly have to think about it at all, and in a different league compared to other keyboards where you can only swap Bluetooth connections with the finicky fn+<number> method that is common for other keyboards.
**Switches**: Quite good for the price. They get the job done well and are fairly sturdy.
**Key caps**: I wasn't a huge fan of the material at first, and I do think the key press sounds would be nicer with something a bit more dense. That said, I like the somewhat retro appearance and the feel of the caps on my fingers.
**Baseboard**: The baseboard is plastic, but feels pretty darn solid. The arrow keys and Del/PgUp/PhDn are separated from the main section of keys and the F keys are also separated and split into thirds, all of which I find to be much more comfortable and convenient than the lack of gaps.
**Volume wheel**: This is the thing I love the most about this keyboard. Having a mini UI here makes it so easy to use the keyboard by switching connections, light effects, color, etc. The wheel is surprisingly sturdy and never in the way. It's even easy to fix the date and time.
**RGB LEDs**: There are some pretty neat patterns. I don't really care about that kind of thing, but it's not hard to have a little fun with the light effects or turn them off if you'd like. I thought I'd be a tiny bit bothered by not having shine-through key caps, but it hasn't bothered me.
reviews.author: Marco Giancarli

reviews.title: It's trendy to buy prebuilts these days
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/E1UnOqiZEQL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/61oi5Fz1RCL._SY256.jpg It's pretty incredible how good these pre-builts are getting. There's a lot of very impressive and affordable keyboards out there on Amazon. That being said - if you are interested in a keyboard with a more "niche" specification, like this one, it get's a little more difficult to find one.
This is one of the only keebs I could find that has low profile keycaps, tactile switches that aren't too loud, and a TKL. Ultimately, a great spec for working in the office. It's light and easily portable with how slim it is. It's not thoccy - but it's not trying to be that. All keys sound tight, except for the spacebar which sounds a little too hollow. The knob with display is fantastic for this price point - I mainly use it to keep track of battery.
The software is decent too. Has RGB too but I personally prefer to keep it off. The low profile keycaps make this look very sleek, although it does make accidental key presses more likely. For this reason, I would recommend considering the tactile switches over the linears.
It's a great keyboard for the price. Obviously, it doesn't provide the same experience as more premium boards do, but it's not trying to compete in that space. Sacrifices are made smartly (e.g. cheap cable). It's a pleasant keyboard to look at and all the touchpoints are quality.
reviews.author: Laurence

reviews.title: Quality semi-custom mechanical - but no shine thru!
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/C1coFqT+DfL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/41J-W4wuc7L._SY256.jpg This keyboard is a perfect entry point into a semi custom, or mechanical keyboard. I was hovering over purchasing a Nuphy for a few weeks - and just couldn't bring myself to spend $140 on a keyboard. I knew there had to be a cheaper alternative that was just as good.
Pros:
Price - the quality for this price point seems REALLY good actually. This thing is sturdy
Profile - I enjoy the keyboard layout, with the exploded arrow keys. The half height or low profile keys are really well done.
RGB - The RGB lighting is actually REALLY good. I was expecting to see a lot more hot spotting for the price, but its really nice.
Software - Yeah - the software is really good too. It gives you all the options you could want, and even to design your own RGB effects.
The knob - yeah - that was probably my favorite thing. You can upload your own custom 20 frame GIF to it, and it will play on repeat.
Sound - It's no nuphy thock, but this thing has a really satisfting milky, creamy, thick sound to it. The padding and insulation in the keyboard really shines through here.
Cons:
Keycap color - This is a big meh for me. It's pretty boring and mute. There IS color to the keys and they are very consistent in the color, but the choice of color is just not for me. It's just too earthy for me.
Keycaps - There is keycap wiggle on every switch. Usually with higher end mechanical switches there is zero wiggle, the key should just travel up and down, but there is smoosh to every key on the board. Big negative for me.
Polling rate - the polling rate for the keyboard isn't published, and when I went to test it I wasn't happy with it's latency. The avg latency for BT was around 100ms, the avg latency with 2.4ghz was 80ms, and the avg latency with USBc was 11ms. The polling rate for BT was 60hz, and for 2.4ghz it was 111. I was expecting this to be similar to the nuphy with 1k hz polling for the 2.4ghz. So for this I cannot recommend this keyboard as a gaming keyboard, there is just too much latency.
Keycaps - Allwhile they are printed very well, and have a very nice feel to them. They are not shine-thru!!!! This is the worst attribute about this keyboard. If you are going to use this keyboard in low light - you better have your keyboard skills up - because you will not be able to see the printing on the keys. I might argue the RGB backlighting makes it even worse. This is a terrible design and I don't see anyone being a fan of non-shine thru keycaps.
Overall:
If you can get this for $60, this is going to be an upgrade from anything that is OEM. But it is that - it's a $60 keyboard. There are just too many bad negatives that could have been addressed to really bring big value to this product. If you are going to game wirelessly on this though, I cannot recommend this for $5 even. The latency is just terribly bad.
reviews.author: Todd Martin

reviews.title: Its Glorious!
reviews.comment: Excellent keyboard, might be the best so far. However, if you download the software for this legacy keyboard, it wont work for custom lighting. The keys are pointing to the wrong ones. I did a search on the issue, apparently when they updated the software for some reason, they messed it up. The old version software for compact works fine. Google search for  "GMMK-COMPACT-USA software" was what I found to be working for me. Love this keyboard, except the switches. Brown isn't my favorite for feel  and sound.
reviews.author: Rick Friar

reviews.title: Top tier value for the money and very hard to beat
reviews.comment:
I've owned the keyboard for about 7 months with my previous keyboard being the Razer black widow TE, overall super happy with the upgrade especially since my biggest complaint of my last keyboard being how loud the switches were and it's just nice to not have to be concerned if its audible to other people now.
Besides that, everything I enjoyed about it from day 1 still holds true, build quality feels phenomenal especially for the price and since a keycap puller is provided it's very nice especially since the switches are what I would describe as great beginner switches and it being hot swappable having the option to upgrade the switches later on makes it such an amazing starting point to get into keyboard customization with.
reviews.author: Joel W.

reviews.title: "Renewed"
reviews.comment: Keyboard arrived brand new, not even a speck of dust inside the box.  Easily worth the gamble to save $25, this thing is totally pristine.  Amazing keyboard and I'm extra happy to have saved $25 on it.  All accessories were included(also brand new) and all work as expected.  Paired with the 1 year warranty I am extremely happy with this purchase. To keep this review brief I just wanted to cover the "Renewed" aspect, for reviews of the keyboard itself just check the non-renewed listing, but I would say it earns 5 stars for both product rating and the quality of the "renewed" product.  It is literally a brand new keyboard.
reviews.author: Brad

reviews.title: Somewhat reccommend depending on if you mod or not
reviews.comment: I do not recommend this keyboard if you plan to mod it. This thing was the biggest pain in the butt to mod. Every single switch was a pain to remove and the stabilizers in this keyboard are not good. They make the keys feel mushy almost like you’re using a membrane keyboard. I would recommend it if you plan to use it as is but only if it’s on sale as it was when I bought it. The keyboard is built good and it’s heavy and also taller than most that I’ve used which is not something I’m complaining about, it still feels good to use. But the key caps are also low ish quality and definitely not something you want to play full price for. So far I’ve had to change the key caps, the switches, and the stabilizers to get my desired custom sound and feel. Recommend buying at sale price if you are not gonna change anything. Do not recommend if you plan to mod it.
reviews.author: Joe Dominguez

reviews.title: Switches are good. Keycaps are bad
reviews.comment: The switches are fantastic. The keycaps not so much. Only had this keyboard for a week and the aswd keys are already losing the texture and are mostly smoothed out from moderate gaming.  Ordered a pack of HyperX keycaps. Those should hold up wayyyyyy longer.
reviews.author: iequalsnoob

reviews.title: Silent switches, rebuildable, solid
reviews.comment: I like it. I like the full keyboard. And getting into a rebuildable platform at this price is great. The keys are silent which isn't what I wanted but I like it. Maybe new switches in a few months.
reviews.author: Claude G.

reviews.title: Great quality and customizability
reviews.comment: I love this thing. If there is something you don't like about it you can customize it to insane levels. I use this daily for work and traded in some panda switches for the fox ones it comes with to get a tactile feel.
reviews.author: Cory Russell

reviews.title: Same as new
reviews.comment: Fast delivery. Working great :)
reviews.author: Eitan

reviews.title: Working keys.
reviews.comment: Great keyboard. A bit on the higher priced side, but for the customizability I'd say its worth it.
reviews.author: Kindle Customer

reviews.title: GMMK3 overpriced go buy GMMK2 if interested in these keyboards
reviews.comment:
Over $100 for a keyboard that feels like $30 out of the box. What hit me as I unboxed the keyboard was that Glorious’ design intent was for you to drop $100 on this thing, and then spend $200-$400 more to “build” it into something you really wanted. Sorry, just no. I want something I like out of the box and then be able to swap components. Not make a diamond from trash.
If you are eying these glorious keyboards I’d recommend the GMMK2 model. Solid out of the box, aluminum frame top, switch presses feel awesome with no frame sag on press, and only $80 (right now). GMMK2 also has a quality weight aspect to it. Not sure if it helps but I like its sturdiness. GMMK3 is just not even in the same league as last gen models.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Passmore

reviews.title: Giant paper weight
reviews.comment: can't do zero stars.  AVOID this.  will never bluetooth connect with windows.  search Google.  Been an issue for years and they never fixed it
reviews.author: James Boone Powell

reviews.title: A Very Nice Keyboard, Better Than Anticipated From Redragon
reviews.comment:
I have sensitive hands after my car wreck back in 1996 and must have a bvoard that is easy to use and soft tot he touch. I prefer chocolate or chicklet keys, but they are hard to maintain. Thsi board took some geting used to and I had to put the rubber dampers under the keycaps, but it is really not all that bad. The keys are soft and smooth and I can type for a good while without pain. I learned very quickly that Redragon has some hidden features in their higher end boards that they don't include in the manual ((I don't care to have to find out stuff like that with no included instructions *Batteries not included) kind of thing)).. like holding Fn+W causes the WASD to change over to the arrow keys or back.. kind of did that by accident. It is really nice to have an on KB function key for the calculator again, I've missed that. I have had a few other Redragon products over the years and have been far less satisfied than I am with this board. FYI folks... Be sure the product says that it uses the "Pro Software" as their regular soft is annoying and lacks essential features, including firmware updates. The pro soft is no bother at all and is not even necessary to run after you program this board. Bluetooth connects just fine, but I have not tested the Wi-fi dongle. Some folks have questioned the metal top... It's a bit thinner than some, but is still sturdy and I have no complaints. I have tested the key puller and used the cap puller to put on the keyboard dampers. The actual key puller is a bit tricky and I am considering buying a better one for future use, but it works... just take care to not scratch the surface fo the board and be patient.. The key wiiiiiil come out.. it's just in there rather tightly. It is an A+++++ mention that they send tbothy pullers and 5.. count it FIVE replacement keys with this model.. I didn't like the cheap cord they sent with it.. REALLY cheap and short, so I got a nice one, at least it was a right angle cord at the KB side. The box presentation is very nice and smooth and sleek in design... I really appreciated the aesthetics, and the inner packing was quality.. The price point is also, most excellent.. You just can't beat $41.99 for a keyboard this decent with genuine Cherry MX keys and all the accessories.. You can easily find additional replacement keys online from aliexpress, just look fro REDRAGON SMD RGB MX Low Profile 5.5 switch. One last thing.. When you go to the website to DL the soft be sure to get the "Cherry MX" model of the soft or it won't see the Keyboard..
In conclusion.. This is a good keyboard and I can logically satisfactorily recommend it. Take care fo ti and it will last you a long time.
Namaste.
reviews.author: Aurihazuma

reviews.title: Amazing Quality and Features and an Amazing Price!
reviews.comment:
Best Overall Amazon Experience Product and Value!
-Amazing Keyboard!
-Value!!
-High End Feel, Features, and More!
-Great typing experience!
-2.4Ghz USB Wireless Adapter Included
-Hotswapable Switches Adds More Value/Customization!
-Amazon Warehouse Purchase(additional added) Great Value!
This Redragon K618 PRO Red Switch Keyboard is the first time I've bought an Redragon product. This also the first time buying an Amazon Warehouse item. I cant say it enough how happy I am with the quality of this keyboard! Especially happy compared to the higher end more expensive keyboards Ive owned in the past. I've gamed for years, and use a PC daily. I've owned Corsair, Logitech, HyperX, and Razer keyboards, and i'd rate this Redragon K618
PRO at least as good, or even better than some of those high end brands that can cost 3x 4x more than the cost of this keyboard.  This keyboard has hot-swappable switches !! Being able to change 1 or ALL switches is a great option to have! Typing and Gaming with the Red Switch version feels good. The longer i've used the keyboard the better it feels overall. The keys sound and feel good. I mostly use the wired, and 2.4Ghz wireless modes and have had no issue with either of the modes. I like that the backlighting turns off after a short time when the keyboard in not in use while on battery power.  This helps save battery, which i appreciate.  The backlighting stays on all the time when keyboard is in wired mode. Amazon Warehouse item experience deal only added to the value of this purchase! 5 star for Redragon Keyboard and 5 Star for Amazon Warehouse.
Redragon K618 PRO Red Switch Keyboard is phenomonal quality and feature set for the price! The build quality feels good, and typing feels great!!
reviews.author: AmazingCustomer

reviews.title: Very good Keyboard and great tech support
reviews.comment: Purchased the Red Dragon K618 Keyboard for couch-gaming on my large HDTV that was in a different room from my PC. Ran a short USB extension cable to within 8 feet of the intended Keyboard location.  Keyboard light are excellent and vivid, with good uniformity and brightness. Key feel is also very good, with a light pressure actuation and are fairly quiet. Battery life is also very good. Approximately a year after purchase, the 2.4Ghz wireless began to experience connectivity issues.  I contacted Red Dragon through the website and was very pleased when they replied to my tech support request within a few hours. A few back and forth emails resulted in Red Dragon shipping me a new Keyboard under warranty. I'm very satisfied with both the product and the support.
reviews.author: John S. Lum

reviews.title: Great keyboard and features for the money
reviews.comment:
It's a great keyboard, lighting is perfect, I like the fact you're not required to install software just to change the RGB lighting colors and brightness.  I primarily bought this keyboard to have a better work/gaming keyboard than my current SteelSeries Apex 3.  I needed a keyboard I could wirelessly correct to 2 other PCs and a tablet.
Unfortunately, I'm in the process of returning it.  My error rate has gone up by 50% due to the low profile keys, I slightly drag my fingers across the keys when typing which happens to to be just enough pressure to activate the keys.  The problem with just using longer stroke key switches is that they tend to be too noisy for my liking.
reviews.author: Tenaciouss

reviews.title: Better than any LP Keychron currently out
reviews.comment: Honestly one of the best low profile keyboard Keychron has put out. I wish they had better switches but there are plenty of options out there.
reviews.author: Carlos

reviews.title: Really a great low-profile with a silent typing experience
reviews.comment: Keychron does a good job with packaging and I'll start there. It's boxed nicely with a bunch of handy extras, along with printed guides and manuals. Out of the box it comes equipped with Mac keys but keycaps for Windows keys are included, as are a colored Enter key to match the orange Esc. Also included is a keycap puller, a screwdriver, and a decent 90° USB cable since the USB port is positioned on the side. Software is standard fare for Keychron, and that is a good thing. Launcher is web based so no download is required and it's super intuitive, anyone can use it to tweak their board to their liking. It's always a huge selling point for me with Keychron boards. Being low profile, this board is light. Moreso than I expected, having seen that this was aluminum and wood. Actually though, the bottom case, which makes up most of the assembly is completely plastic. The only aluminum on the board is the front and back edge of the top case, then of course the actual wood sides. This was a bit disappointing to me but then again I'm not too surprised based on the price. Even so, the aluminum feels good and this cuts down on the weight, which is probably a net positive on a low profile setup. The wood looks great as well with the deep color and nice finish. Overall it's a quality aesthetic, minimal and elegant. Connectivity is as good as all the other Keychron boards out there. You have the standard wired mode, then Bluetooth or wireless as options. Another feature this has is per key RGB which you can configure in the easy to use web software. These are north facing LEDs and if there was one weak point to this board, it would be that these are not very prominent even when turned to the max brightness. This is probably more to do with the profile of the keys. Not something that matters to me as I prefer to not use RGB, but worth considering. Also, this is a hotswap board. This means you could purchase whatever low profile switches you want out there to tweak your sound and feel. What really matters though is how a keyboard sounds and feels. I'm happy to say that this sounds and feels fantastic for a $100 low profile, actual mechanical board. With banana switches, it reminds me a lot of what I'd imagine a mechanical mac keyboard to be. You get that tactile bump with very little travel. It's a pleasant typing experience. It also sounds surprisingly good with my only issue being the right shift key. It's a bit rattled but I think this could be fixed with the stabilizer. But I'm picky, and I look for these things. It's quite silent too. Not completely silent, but I would say this is very suitable for an office environment, and easy to travel with to boot. Refer to my video for a typing demo and just realized that I'm micing this up with noise reduction so it'll probably sound louder than in a live environment with ambient noise. Okay, so a summary of my thoughts here - Pros: - A light and agile board - wonderful sound and feel - aluminum top case with actual wood sides - completely hotswapable - looks great - good connectivity options Cons: - underwhelming RGB - still mostly plastic with the bottom case - slight rattle on a single modifier key Overall a great board. It's probably the nicest sounding and feeling low profile I've used and given that it's hotswap, you could potentially go completely silent if you wanted with the right switches. Easily a recommendation if you are looking to test out a low profile or a quieter mechanical board.
reviews.author: Blakk

reviews.title: Extremely capable low-profile mechanical keyboard
reviews.comment: I already own three Keychron keyboards, all of which are either Cherry or OSA profile and use full sized switches. Keychron is more expensive than the competition, but in my evaluation of over a dozen different keyboards, the premium is well worth it for the materials, build quality, and unique layouts. The K3 Max SE is no exception. What makes the K3 Max SE stand out is the low profile switches and keys. I had the chance to use a NuPhy Air75 V3 with brown switches, which is a highly rated low profile keyboard retailing around the $30 more than the K3 Max SE. I disliked the mushiness of the Air75’s brown switches and overall cheap feel of the plastic body. The Keychron on the other hand stands out with an impressive Banana switch that has a very prominent bump and is what a tactile switch should feel like. Additionally, the real wood and aluminum body of the K3 Max SE feels much more premium than the NuPhy. At 1.25lbs, this keyboard is light, much lighter than the Air75 (at 1.6lbs). There are a few things that surprised me that I would have preferred to be different: 1. Although the sides are wood and aluminum, the back tray is plastic. It would have been better if this was also aluminum. This was likely to accommodate the three different angle adjustments available, which is nice. 2. The switches and USB port are located on the left side of the keyboard, and aren’t particularly noteworthy in build - they are simple, black plastic toggles on a black body with black text. It would have been preferred to have the usb port on the top of the keyboard, and for the toggles to be better quality; right now because everything is black, it is a bit difficult to see. This is my biggest disappointment on the keyboard, and the reason I can’t give it a full 5 stars. 3. The north facing RGB lights and the opaque switch housing leave a lot to be desired for lighting. The backlight appears to be about half the brightness of a normal profile keyboard, such as the K2 HE All-Wood Edition that I also use. 4. At 120 hours of runtime, that is far lower than the Air75 V3’s 1200 hours. The typing experience of the K3 Max SE is exceptional. It is ergonomic, and has plenty of travel that makes it feel like a no-compromise device. I’ve tried Gateron BBKs, Jupiter Bananas, which are sometimes referred to as the best tactile switches you can get, but my main keyboard I use has Keychron Super Bananas on it for a reason. The low profile switches on the K3 Max SE feel great, just a step below the snappiness of the fullsize Super Bananas. It sounds good, but you aren’t going to get “thock” or even “clack” from this profile of keyboard. Keychron’s online launcher to customize keys is top tier and very easy to use. My personal preference is to use cherry profile keys and fullsize switches for my main desktop, and these low profile ones away from my desk with my iPad Pro. For those looking for a premium tactile experience, even at the desk, I would highly recommend considering this keyboard, as it is a pleasure to type on.
reviews.author: JMC

reviews.title: A Remarkably Superior Low Profile Custom Mechanical Keyboard for Professional Efficiency
reviews.comment: This ultra-slim hardware was selected to optimize a sophisticated home office desk arrangement. The initial unboxing reveals a professional-grade build quality that aligns perfectly with a modern, minimalist aesthetic. The low-profile design serves as an ideal entry point for those seeking a streamlined typing experience without sacrificing tactile feedback. The connectivity options deliver seamless integration across multiple devices, facilitating a smooth transition between professional tasks and personal projects. My partner, currently finalizing her cancer research doctorate, found the design so compelling that she immediately integrated it into her own daily workflow. The build quality remains robust, providing a stable platform for high-volume data entry and communication. The Keychron Banana switches offer a unique tactile sensation characterized by significantly lower resistance than traditional mechanical alternatives. While some enthusiasts might prefer a firmer response, the lighter touch supports extended typing sessions with minimal fatigue. Maintenance remains straightforward due to the hot-swappable nature of the custom board. This is a top-tier product that delivers an elite level of hardware utility. The investment represents a savvy move for anyone prioritizing desk ergonomics and build integrity. This keyboard provides a distinctly superior experience compared to standard office peripherals.
reviews.author: Billu Master

reviews.title: Slim, Premium, and Incredibly Customizable — A Perfect Daily Keyboard
reviews.comment: The Keychron K3 Max SE has been an outstanding upgrade for both work and everyday typing. The ultra‑slim 75% layout is perfect for saving desk space while still keeping all the keys I need, and the aluminum top frame gives it a solid, premium feel instead of the hollow sound many low‑profile keyboards have. The low‑profile PBT keycaps feel great under the fingers and resist shine nicely. Connectivity is one of its biggest strengths. Tri‑mode support (2.4GHz wireless, Bluetooth, and wired USB‑C) makes it easy to switch between my laptop and desktop, and the 2.4GHz mode feels fast and responsive with no noticeable lag. The ability to connect multiple Bluetooth devices is especially convenient for multitasking. What really sets this keyboard apart is QMK support. Full key remapping, macros, and customization through the Keychron Launcher make it incredibly flexible for productivity or light gaming. Add in solid battery life, smooth low‑profile switches, and excellent build quality, and this becomes an easy recommendation. If you want a sleek, modern mechanical keyboard that works equally well for Mac and Windows, the K3 Max SE is a fantastic choice.
reviews.author: JP

reviews.title: Great keyboard... but the low-profile version should be called the Node96
reviews.comment: I was extremely excited about this launch. I love 100% low-profile keyboards, especially with deep thocky sounds and premium feels. I've been desperate for something comparable to the K5 Max (my daily driver) or G915 X, but with a sound and feel profile similar to nuphy's keyboards. I was extremely disappointed when I saw that the low-profile version of this keyboard is actually their 75% layout with a numpad stitched on. This is a 96% keyboard, not 100%. Still, it's the closest this side of the market has come to 100%, so I wanted to give it a shot. Truly, it does feel and sound great. Typical nuphy quality. I have no complaints about the keyboard, and typing on this was a blast. The web app at nuphy.io was also simple to use and the keyboard was highly configurable; compared to the competition, the web app hits every mark except it lacks the ability to configure a numlock indicator (via RGB backlighting or otherwise). If you like 96% keyboards, or if you like 75% keyboards but want a numpad, and you prefer the thocky sound profiles of nuphy or lofree, then this could be among the best keyboards on the market for you right now. But as expected, I myself cannot use this as a daily driver. I've learned to take advantage of nearly every single key on a 100% keyboard. The shorter right shift key can be learned, as can the new locations of the various console keys (ins/home/pgup/pgdn/etc), but the missing right alt/opt key proved to be a deal-breaker in real usage. I hope nuphy releases something comparable to this keyboard in a true 100% layout in the future.

reviews.title: Best mechnical keyboard for open office concepts! Quiet, but feels substantial.
reviews.comment:
I bought this keyboard because I wanted a mechanical keyboard that would still work well in an open office, and it’s been a great fit. It has the tactile feel I wanted, plus that satisfying little clunk and thunk when I type, but without being obnoxiously loud to everyone around me. I type pretty heavily, so I wanted something that could handle that gracefully, and this keyboard feels solid and steady instead of flimsy or harsh.
It also strikes a really nice balance on size. My desk is small, but I still wanted all the keys, and this layout works really well for that. The low profile is another huge plus for me. Low profile keyboards help me type a little less heavily, which also keeps the noise down, so it ends up being perfect for office use.
One thing I didn’t know going in was what Banana switches would feel like. I usually avoid red switches, and brown switches have been a nice alternative for me, so that was my main point of comparison. Banana switches feel more tactile than brown, but without adding much sound. They just feel really nice to type on.
This replaced my Apple Magic Keyboard, and honestly, it’s a huge improvement. It feels better, sounds better, and I can type faster on it. The backlighting is nice, and I like the colors a lot too.
My only hesitation is the rubberized, slightly grippy coating. I actually love how it feels right now, but I do wonder how well that finish will hold up over time. Still, so far I’m really happy with it.

reviews.title: Non-standard font and reversed regular/shift layout on keycaps
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/J15nyyR3qML.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/61joQtHT9uL._SY256.jpg This is a solidly built keyboard with individually controlled RGB LEDs under each mechanical key.  The key action and feel is great, although if you are not a fan of mechanical keyboards you will find them too clicky and loud.
The LED's can be quite bright (or can be turned down). To get full use out of the programmable lights (and keymaps) you will need to use the Cherry XTFY software on windows to customize the layout/colors/patterns, but even without use of the software the keyboard is fully usable and ships from the factory with many fully usable default lighting patterns.
Some of them are as subtle as a simple backlight, while others flash and roll back and forth, either continuously, or in response to keyboard presses. Just using the function keys you can turn the lights on/off, pick different modes, adjust the speed or brightness.  You can also pick how the keyboard connects to (multiple) devices.  It can pair with up to 3 devices via Bluetooth, another device via the included USB-A 2.4ghz wireless adapter, and another device via the USB cable.  So you can conceptually have up to 5 devices connected at once, and switch between them using keyboard commands.
I tested the USB cable, USB-A wireless adapter, and Bluetooth with my Linux laptop (Ubuntu 24.04) and they all worked perfectly without needing any extra software or drivers (although I could not modify the default lighting patterns or keyboard layout).
My only real complaint about this product is that it uses an "edgy" " gaming" font to label the keycaps, which trades style for legibility. This won't matter much to you if you are touch typist, and the keyboard has the standard QWERTY laytout, but it annoyed me.  Perhaps more importantly, the "default" action of the key is labeled on the top, while the shifted action of each key is labeled on the bottom. [Bass Ackwards compared to every other set of keycaps I've ever seen]  So for example, on the + = key, the equal sign is on the top, and the plus sign is on the bottom. The key still functions as you would expect, but years of using every other keyboard in the world makes me want to press the shift key to get the top icon.
But since they are Cherry key-switches, if you don't like it, you can always buy a set of keycaps you like more. [If you got some translucent or transparent ones, the RGB LED's would be even more visible.]
And of course, there is the price, which is a premium price for a premium keyboard.  It doesn't strike me as outrageous for a full mechanical keyboard + RGB Gaming lights, but it is certainly more expensive than any "generic" keyboard on the market, so you have to really want the feel of mechanical key-switches and the RGB lights to justify it.

reviews.title: Attractive, lightweight, quality, recommended at the price
reviews.comment: Having used the Keychron K3 for the past four months in a professional office environment, I've come to appreciate this compact, portable mechanical keyboard for its functionality, aesthetics, and the comfortable typing experience it provides. Firstly, the optical brown switch configuration lends a significantly quiet yet tactile typing experience, ideal for shared workspaces where noise can be a concern. The auditory feedback is negligible, but the feel under your fingertips will assure you of each keystroke. The battery life on the Keychron K3 is another big win. With regular usage, I found that a single charge could easily sustain me through a full five-day workweek, eliminating the need for constant charging or battery swaps. It's a reliable companion for a busy work schedule. In terms of aesthetics, the Keychron K3 is impressive. Its look is understated and professional without screaming 'gaming keyboard.' In fact, I've received numerous compliments on its look during my usage at work. The  The compact design also adds to its portability, making it easy to transport between locations, a must-have feature for anyone on the move. Multi-device Bluetooth connectivity is a standout feature. The keyboard was able to seamlessly connect and switch between different devices. This functionality proved invaluable, allowing me to quickly move between different work laptops without having to set up the Bluetooth connection each time. However, no product is without its flaws, and the Keychron K3 is no exception. Initially, the Bluetooth connection would drop after just a few minutes of inactivity. I resolved this issue by disabling sleep mode, using the keyboard shortcut provided on the manufacturer's website. Additionally, I noticed a slight wiggle with the keys. This didn’t affect typing performance, although it could be a point of concern for those who prefer a solid, immovable keycap feel. To conclude, despite its minor issues, the Keychron K3 has proven to be an excellent addition to my workspace. For a price tag of $69.00, it provides a high-quality, quiet, and tactile typing experience that I highly recommend, especially for those seeking to improve their productivity in an office setting. It's lightweight, portable, and exudes a professional appeal, all the while delivering on performance and battery life. However, potential buyers should be aware of its initial Bluetooth connectivity issues and slight keycap instability.
reviews.author: John P.

reviews.title: THIS KEYBOARD IS AMAZING!
reviews.comment: This Keychron K3 V2 is HANDS DOWN, the best keyboard I've EVER used, let alone owned. Switched to this Keychron K3 With Brown Switches, from a RK61 Mechanical Keyboard with red switches and couldn't go back if I wanted to. I would easily recommend this, and if this isn't your cup of tea, go check out a Numphy Air 75 for $130 USD. Will update if ANYTHING changes or wears out, but as of today I can HIGHLY recommend this keyboard over almost every other 75% keyboard. Also the Brown Switches have more of a tactile bump and a like 25% stiffer spring, and the reds have a little more of a click, but Press very easy from what I hear. If you're looking for your first, 10th, or 500th Mechanical Keyboard, Then this Low Profile, Hot swap able, 75% TKL Keyboard I can 110% recommend The ONLY downside IMO, Is that it doesn't have extra Key Caps sets, the keys you get are the only ones you'll find, and they aren't PBT so they could shine after awhile. Definitely not a deal breaker, but just keep that in mind. Will update if mine start to shine, or anything goes wrong!
reviews.author: Jacob Shields

reviews.title: Good keyboard with some caveats
reviews.comment: I bought this keyboard on Prime day, at ~$70 is hard to beat given there is no competitors at this price (Nuphy Air 75 cost ~$130 and Logi MX Mech Mini cost $150+) Thanks to Amazon's generous return policy I was able to test other switches as well, below are pros/cons: Pros: 1. Good price. At $70, as a low profile hot swappable Mech keyboard, it has no competitors. 2. Decent layout. It is much smaller than a regular keyboard or a TKL keyboard, the right shift key is a bit small but I got used to it quickly 3. Good ergo. Thanks to its low profile nature, it is much lower than the regular keyboard which your wrist can rest on the desk naturally. The key distance is much shorter which is good for people typed a lot 4. Good switch: It seems the Brown switch issue was fixed, as I don't have typos when rest my fingers on the keyboard. The mint switches are even better. Cons: 1. No White color (it's only available on keychron.com, which you need to pay $20 shipping and they have poor customer service) 2. Non-standard keycaps. The long keycaps (Enter / Backspace / Right Shift / Space key) has non-standard layout so you can not use your own keycaps. 3. Backlight button on top-right, and you can't customize it. It would be much better use combo key to enable backlight, almost all other brands are doing that. 4. Poor customer support: Don't get me wrong, Amazon has great customer service and the return policy is great, however customer support from keychron.com is another story, it's email only and it took 4~5 days for them to respond 5. No good clicky/linear switches: Due to its low-profile nature, linear switches lead to tons of typos (even for Black switches), and click switches (K3 only support hotswappable optical) sound weird, I tried both blue and orange and they all have the strange mush sound when typing. The gateron low profile blue ones sound much better but they are not supported. Overall, if you are looking for a good low profile hotswappable Mech Keyboard, and you like tactile switches, K3 is a good choice. If you like clicky switches, go with Gateron low profile blue. If you like linear switches, go with regular profile keyboard, low profile + linear switches is a weird combo and it's a typo hell.
reviews.author: Luc

reviews.title: Great keyboard, but not for beginners
reviews.comment: TL;DR: I REALLY like this keyboard, especially once you add different switches and keycaps, but it didn't work out because my accuracy sucks. Definitely not for beginners. Long review: I got the optical reds with this keyboard and it's definitely not for me since I'm a heavy typist. It's just too sensitive so I got the orange and bananas (yellow) optical switches to try them out. I do like the oranges but the ping on some of the switches is too dang loud and annoying so I settled with the bananas (yellow). Once I got them to my liking, it's time to test drive the keyboard. I'm not a typist per day but I can type. Not 100% accurate though, and that's where my problems arose. When I do make a mistake, I will almost 50% of the time would hit the "page up" instead of the backspace.. I do use "del" a lot as well and would hit the light switch instead.. If you're competent and have 99% accuracy when you type, it may work for you. Otherwise, get the K1 DE (what I did instead).
reviews.author: Reginald

reviews.title: Smooth and has improved my typing
reviews.comment: Context: I heavily use this for office work and am a heavy typer - use it for notes, document writing and also taking notes during interviews I am writing this review after using this for 2 months so that I know that this is the right product and that it really helps me in my work. And I can definitely say it does. This is my first mechanical keyboard and I purchased one after a year of deliberation. I always used to type on my laptop keyboard even while using a separate monitor just so that I could become faster in my typing. I use a Mac and right off the bat this comes with a Mac oriented layout. The keys click but but as much to make the experience too loud. When I talk to people and type they are not disturbed when on video calls. I used it in a office setting the noise was not too loud at all for people around me to be bothered by it. The keyboard is smooth and it took me a week to get used to the actuation force but once done my sped definitely improved. The base is aluminum and it gives off a really premium feel and helps with the stability of the product. There are 2 levels of lift in the keyboard, which is a huge plus  for me - if I stand and work there is a different inclination versus  when I sit and type and this keyboard helps in both. The lights on this one are white and I am quite ok with that. One thing to note - the intensity or backlights is less when on bluetooth mode versus directly being connected (I have attached 2 photos for reference). I prefer smaller keyboards as travel times to keys are less and the fact that I have been typing on laptop keyboards for a long time. The keyboard is sleek and great in transporting and carrying around.

reviews.comment: Looks, feels, and sounds beautiful. Solid build, easy volume wheels, the semitone works well for room awareness. The dual simultaneous dongle + Bluetooth is a game changer, can take calls while playing, or hear music and audiobooks, etc. The light mute indicator on the microphone is great.  My only problem is that the mute button has a loud sharp beep every time it’s pushed in or out, I dunno if it can be adjusted. The earpads are comfortable and breathe well to stay cool and it doesn’t have that faux leather coating that eventually peels off and looks ugly. I feel like I got a good deal vs my previous headset (Sony Pulse Elite), it has mostly the same features but the build quality is much better with the Nova as my Elite broke on the headband in less than a month, even with careful handling.

reviews.title: Extremely comfortable and flexible Definitely worth the price!
reviews.comment: Very comfortable and extremely light. They fit perfectly over my afro and I had even forgotten that they were resting on my head at some point. The band is very flexible and seems to be durable, but only time will tell, but in my first couple weeks it’s survived a couple drops and a lot of stretching to fit over my hair. The microphone is clear enough for gaming and my friends haven’t complained which I see as a win. Very good product especially for the price and would buy again even if my current pair broke.

reviews.comment: Great quality and super lightweight I was surprised how light it was and it's great that I can switch between Bluetooth and the USB dongle with a press of a button and is also has good battery life and last quite long without a charge
reviews.author: Matthew Nissen

reviews.title: Stay away from wireless logitech headphones!!
reviews.comment: Terrible headset. Do NOT buy wireless logitech headphones! I've had the absolute worst experiences with them. This one specifically has the issue where there is a constant delay when the mic is on. Everytime I would play a game and had my mic on, there would be a 1 second delay from the game visuals and my audio. In fast paced competetive games 1 second is absolutely unacceptable and makes it unplayable. The only way to fix this issue is to either, have the mic on before you turn the headset on, which didn't even work every single time, or to simply not use the microphone and have it set to off. Even if you do turn the mic on before turning the headset on, what if you need to mute the mic and then turn it back on? Well, guess what, that would reintroduce the horrible delay. I don't want to deal with this BS in the middle of a competetive game. Unplugging wireless logitech headphone dongles from pc ports midgame also results in a total system crash, forcing you to restart your pc. Happened on two fully functional pcs with two different wireless logitech headphones. Just don't buy wireless logitech headphones, please. You'll save yourself a headache and money. As for everything else, this headset doesn't really have much going for it. The audio quality is decent at best, it has a pretty bad battery life, less than 24 hours. The only positive thing about it is the comfort, it's light on the head and doesn't make you want to take it off after several hours. Besides that, bad headset.

reviews.comment: The Logitech G321 Lightspeed headset has been awesome so far. It’s super comfortable for long gaming sessions and fits well without feeling too tight. The sound quality is clear, and the 16 kHz boom mic picks up my voice nicely. I also love the long battery life — easily lasts over 20 hours. Works perfectly with my PC and consoles, and Bluetooth makes it easy to switch to my phone. Overall, a solid wireless headset for the price!

reviews.author: Eric

reviews.title: Amazing headset. Best color imo. Works on PS5 and PC too!
reviews.comment: Amazing headset. Ill say, after watching countless review and comparison videos to find exactly what I needed, I'm glad I finally went with this. I needed something I could connect to my PS5 and on my laptop for work at the same time. I wanted a very quick swap between the 2. This beast filled all my requirements. Great sound. Super long battery life. Great build and feels hefty and durable enough for long use. The pads are also perfect for glasses wearers too. I will say I prefer the Cobalt color over the PS version white one. I knew the USB transmitter would work on the PS but was a little worried the XBOX transmitter wouldnt work if connected to the PC because of how xbox likes to add their own proprietary method. Decided to buy it anyway since the XBOX method would only require an additional connection req and shouldn't affect normal 2.4 connection so I was still confident it would work. So for anyone else in the same boat, yes this version will work on PC and PS5 simultaneous connection. Connect the USB transmitter to your PS and the XBOX one to your PC.
reviews.author: MY

reviews.title: a must for 2 simultaneous audio sources
reviews.comment: Stop thinking and buy this.  I have a number other headsets, some for work, and some for gaming - including Logitech Lightspeed G733, Bose Quiet Comforts,  a nice Razer, a bunch of cheap ones, and more.  But if you are trying to use multiple sources SIMULTANEOUSLY, then this is the one for you.  It's the right balance between comfortable, quality audio, easy to use, and affordable.  It's got simple yet powerful controls, it can connect via 2 included 2.4ghz dongles, plus Bluetooth, and the mic mute function is spectacular (just flip it up).  I fell in love with this within 15 minutes and I've never looked back.  I wish I had found it sooner, but I thought of other brands as being higher quality.  I was wrong. I use this with a bluetooth connection to my Yealink office phone and with a 2.4 connection to my PC - plus the other USB dongle can move from gaming system (or other  computer) as needed.  I can talk to someone on the phone while listening to a video on my PC (sometimes needed for work).  I can independently adjust the volumes. That being said "super human hearing mode" is only useful for games as far as I can tell.  Also, you can't control the priority of the microphone.  If you are using it with the 2.4ghz dongle, say for a Teams meeting, and then you get a bluetooth call.  The blueooth call connects to the mic and the meeting loses it.  You still hear audio from both though.  And as soon as you disconnect from the the call, the 2.4 dongle gets the mic again.  Perhaps giving you that control would make the headset far more complicated, but it was the only part that took me a couple minutes to figure out.
reviews.author: Techguy

reviews.title: Mad Catz quality meets medieval torture device
reviews.comment: Don’t waste your time / money. Worthless product. Will not stay connected using 2.4 or BT methods. Sound quality is mid and not worth the asking price. At first was disconnecting consistently every couple mins and sound quality was tinny and distorted. There is a ‘feature’ that allows you to switch between normal/ok sound and bad quality sound (why would you make this a feature of your headphones???) but this was different, wayyy more distorted and everything sounded far away. So, I updated the firmware and software for the headset and the 2.4 transmitter. After that completed it became stable, sound quality improved (although I stand by my earlier statement that they are still not asking prices level of quality). However, not too long after thinking it’s fixed and all good, it then got worse. Now it disconnects whenever it feels like it :D This could be 5mins into using them or 36 and a half mins, or 2hours 6mins and 23secs. Who knows?! Also, post update it now hands sound back to external source when it randomly decides to disconnect. So playing games or watching a movie at night (whole reason I bought these is so I can keep gaming and not disturb anyone) and if I forget to turn my mixer down… it just blasts out of my speaker system and defeats the entire purpose of the headphones. I could go on about how they aren’t very comfortable, how poorly laid out the button and volume adjusters are, etc etc etc. but none of that matters if the one major feature, being a wireless headphone, fails to function in a consistent manner. Learn from my mistake. Save yourself from the inevitable pain and suffering that awaits you if you decide to purchase these woefully engineered cans…what an infuriating and torturous experience.
reviews.author: Brady

reviews.title: Best headset I’ve ever had
reviews.comment: Year later and it’s still just like new. Best head set I’ve owned. I love it. It really does have great audio, I can hear all the steps and their directions. It’s even great for just listening to music. It’s also just so so comfortable. If this ever breaks I’ll be getting another one.
reviews.author: Manda

reviews.title: High quality headset. App name is SWARM II use it.
reviews.comment: This will be long winded sorry. Here are the feature I have found so far as well as some pointers for anyone who doesn't want to read the whole thing. What you get: (1) 2 dongles one for Xbox one for PC and Playstation. (2) the headset made of pretty high-quality stuff in my opinion (3) a charging cable type C What app to use: SWARM II it has a purple icon with the turtle beach logo. You can update directly from the app it will tell you how. I do not know why it's not advertised. Has most of the options from the last app plus you can make your own equalizer presets. What you can do: Page One General Audio Setting/ custom equalizer: (1) turn off and on the Superhuman Hearing setting and choose from 3 separate settings (Non-Adjustable) Legacy, footsteps, and gunshots. (2) Choose from 4 Non-Adjustable audio presets or make up to 5 of your own. Page Two Mic settings: Not much to say here, you can change the sensitivity and make your own presets. Page Three Not much here either, map the mode button with two options and adjust the LED brightness on the dongles. Yes you can do this. Page Four Hyperlinks to help center, social media and tells you if your headset needs an update. Jesus... still long winded. THE ACTUAL REVIEW The difference between the stealth 700 gen 2 max and these is kind of insane. My biggest problems with the last generation was that it was made of primarily plastic and were super quiet, whereas these are made of pretty high quality materials (the actual hinges are made of metal, a big plus) and they are loud when you want them to be. At the moment my only complaint is the comfort has gone down just a bit. The earmuffs are harder than gen 2 but the trade off in actual quality is more than worth it. The amount of customization you get with these in the app is also a big improvement over the last gen. If you are looking to get some nice headphones these are for you.

reviews.author: Aryn Yeoman

reviews.title: Premium headphones, affordable price
reviews.comment:
As a homeschool mom of 5, I’m always paying attention to how our kids use tech for learning, gaming, and downtime, and when it comes to audio gear like this RK Royal Kludge wireless gaming headset, I usually look at it through the lens of comfort, versatility, and how well it holds up in a busy household. This type of headset is typically designed as an over-ear gaming headset with memory foam ear cushions for comfort during longer use sessions. It usually includes a detachable or retractable microphone for voice chat or online gaming, along with features like Bluetooth 5.3, wireless 2.4GHz connectivity, and sometimes a wired option for flexibility across different devices.
Many versions also include virtual 7.1 surround sound for a more immersive audio experience, especially in gaming or media use, plus RGB lighting for a more “gamer-style” aesthetic. The multi-platform compatibility (like PC, PS4, PS5, and Nintendo Switch) makes it a flexible option for families with different devices. The adjustable headband and cushioned ear pads are meant to improve comfort for extended wear, which is helpful for kids or teens during long sessions.
In everyday use at home, it works well for gaming, online learning, video calls, or entertainment. My kids tend to use headsets like this for focus during educational games or to reduce background noise in a busy home environment. The wireless option is especially convenient for movement, while wired mode ensures it can still be used if the battery runs low. For the price, it feels like a versatile all-in-one gaming headset that balances comfort, features, and multi-device use for both fun and practical everyday tech needs in a family setting. Excellent value
reviews.author: Cargilper

reviews.title: A headset that actually makes games sound better! FOR REAL! Surround also works great!  :D
reviews.comment:
This headset approaches audio like it expects to be used regularly, which I do indeed use it everyday, and delivers accordingly. The RK ROYAL KLUDGE HG101 features 7.1 surround sound, multiple connection options, and a retractable microphone for flexibility. The memory foam ear pads add comfort, while the overall build feels durable enough for daily use. The RGB lighting provides a subtle visual accent but not really needed. This is about sound, not visuals. It is designed for both performance and style.
Setup involves choosing between Bluetooth, wireless, or wired connections, depending on the device. The process is simple and does not take much time. The controls are intuitive, allowing quick adjustments during use. The retractable mic integrates smoothly into the design. It feels practical.
The headset provides clear and balanced audio, with good bass for those BassHeads out there, with surround sound enhancing immersion in games and media. The mic delivers consistent voice clarity, making communication easy. The comfort level supports longer sessions without noticeable strain. It performs well across different scenarios. It feels reliable.
There are a few small limitations to consider. The surround sound effect may vary depending on the content. The RGB lighting may not suit all preferences. Even so, it delivers a strong overall experience. Great value for the bucks! :D

reviews.comment: Nice sound. They do not connect to PS5.
reviews.author: Imani

reviews.title: Battery Indicator?? Died too fast to depend on for work :(
reviews.comment:
I wore these for work the first day and loved them, but didn't charge overnight intentionally to see how they'd last. There's no indicator anywhere that I've seen for battery remaining. ! How is this possible? I even checked the settings on the computer it paired with for a percent battery remaining...
I did turn them completely off later to sleep. They died during the first hour of workday 2.
I jumbled cords and devices all morning to get back connected to my corded set to function at work.
Pretty disappointed as I loved them, but to rely on these for work, they can't be unreliable or die mid work call.
They also died VERY quickly after the first "battery low" announcement. I got it repeated once in one phone call and on the third time it died. I got lucky I finished the call quickly.
I didn't turn the accent lights off that I remember as it was first use, which may help battery, but that much? Someone stated the option to plug in a direct line when battery dies. I may have to return, as the whole point of a wireless set was not to plug in. I had a tethered set already.
I hope to update this, but after searching weeks for the right set, just already a little let down on the battery 🪫 features.
reviews.author: V Smith

reviews.title: Comfortable to wear
reviews.comment: These wireless gaming headphones from RK fit well.  They have enough weight to feel like you are wearing something, but not enough to pinch my ears while I wear them.  The disappointing thing about them is that they don't hold charge very long.  So if you're in a long gaming session, or needing to use your headphones for watching YouTube or anything else, they won't last.
reviews.author: Fortysomethingsci

reviews.title: Amazing Sound & Mic Quality
reviews.comment: I'm a former audio engineer, so I prefer great sound, and this headset brings it all. I love the Blue Microphone software it comes with, but that only works, while plugged into a PC, via the USB port, and not the 3.5mm jack The Blue Microphone software allows you to better fine tune your audio, and how you sound on the mic, so I come across more clear. I have a naturally loud voice, so being able to equalize things, so it doesn't sound like I'm yelling all the time is nice Another awesome feature, is the software had a lot of games with prebuilt audio profiles, so many game will sound better automatically, and it updates frequently. I got this same headset for my sons, and because they are not former audio engineers, it helps them game more, with amazing sound quality The price seems high, but with everything you get, it's an amazing value. Plus, it's really comfy. It comes with pleather or fabric ear guards, so you can choose what you like. My kids prefer the pleather, but I prefer the fabric because it breaths better. However, switching them out, is the biggest drag of all, so get comfortable with one, and just stick to it...trust me Long review, but one last cool feature. When plugged in via USB, you can save audio profiles, to the USB dongle, so when going to another computer, it saves your audio settings. This is better for my kids because they game on 2 computers The value, quality, and comfort is why I can't recommend this headset enough. It was a great buy. Plus, I got a refurbished one, and it worked perfectly I also have health issues, and have brought this to the hospital with me. It doesn't store easy, but it plays streaming services really good, so spending days in the hospital isn't so bad, and that's why I prefer to bring it, over other headphones
reviews.author: James Roach

reviews.title: In New Condition
reviews.comment: I received the refurbished G Pro X headset in the original box with the headset and all the accessories in perfect condition. They are as-new, without any wear or marks at all.  The set came with the Blue Voice microphone usb DAC that works perfectly. They even included the additional velour ear cups as they would when purchaed new.  This is my second set of the G Pro X headset and this one is exactly like my first set.  The Blue Voice microphone gives a great sound with the DAC paired with the G Hub software.  I use this headset exclusively on Zoom calls and I get lots of compliments on the sound of my voice.  I am a teacher of adults online and my classes last 4 hours but my ears are never sore due to the comfort of the ear cups.  Thanks to the excellent sidetone, (that allows me to hear my voice when I'm talking), I no longer blowout my voice as with cheaper headsets. I am very happy with this purchase due to the perfect condition of this refurbished headset.
reviews.author: James W

reviews.title: They're a great set of headphones
reviews.comment: To be clear, I purchased a pair that didn't work out and had to send it back. Due to the fact that I needed a working headset I purchased the wireless version the same day I returned these. They sound great and for short sessions feel great. They block out noise really well. The microphone is solid, but could be better*, at least the controls allow for greater customization of your voice. *Logitech let's you purchase a blue microphone that you can plug into the headset for better microphone quality. I haven't purchased it yet, but it looks great.
reviews.author: Jan Anthony

reviews.title: More than I expected!
reviews.comment: I bought this renewed. I expected a generic brown box with some but not all of the original accessories. Turns out that my item was complete in the original retail packaging with all of the original manuals and accessories included and none of it had been used yet. You could tell the box was opened previously. But, everything still had stickers, plastic bags, and twist ties on them as if they were brand new. Way more than I expected to receive! I was skeptical of this headset. A lot of reviews state it has great sound quality but a poor microphone. I wanted it for gaming. And I play a lot of online games and wanted a quality mic without buying a condenser mic. I read all of the reviews and looked at all of the settings in the Logitech software and made some adjustments and it sounds exactly like I wanted it to sound. Thoroughly impressed with Amazon on this purchase and extremely happy with the quality of the product as well! I can’t say anyone else would receive theirs renewed in the same quality and condition. But, I just got lucky I guess!
reviews.author: Brian

reviews.title: Works great. Sounds good enough. Very comfortable.
reviews.comment: Sound quality is nothing special but it sounds as good as you can ask for the price point and the benefit of never having to recharge your headphones. The headset is comfortable, i really have no complaints or praises here. Seems very durable, I play VR in the same space I use them and have thrown them off my desk twice now on accident with no problems. So these should stand up to most normal use. Overall this headset is one that I would absolutely recommend and while it's not perfect it is a quality, low cost, and something I use daily headset.
