reviews.title: Great keyboard!
reviews.comment: I love this keyboard. It's my first mechanical, and they keys are a lot more sensitive than my other keyboard, so it's taken some time to get used to it. Lighting is nice. It's noisier than my other keyboard, but I know that's a normal thing for mechanicals, though I can't compare it to other mechanicals, of course. It's easy to set up, and I haven't had any issues with the software. I was able to program the keys easily, and I appreciate the "game mode" key so if I accidentally hit my Windows key, it doesn't interrupt my game.
reviews.author: N. Ruggles

reviews.title: Good keyboard
reviews.comment: Good keyboard. But a little too expensive.
reviews.author: Jose

reviews.title: Logitech G915 Lightspeed Keyboard – Great for Gaming and Work, Slim, Tactile and Responsive
reviews.comment: I’ve been using the Logitech G915 keyboard for several weeks, and it’s outstanding for both work and gaming. The low-profile mechanical keys are tactile and responsive, making typing and gaming feel effortless. The RGB lighting is bright and customizable, and I love being able to adjust profiles for different setups. The wireless connection is rock-solid with almost no lag, and the battery life is excellent, even with the lighting on. The keyboard feels premium with a solid build, and the low-profile design saves desk space while still feeling comfortable for long typing sessions. I also got it on sale, which makes it an amazing value considering the quality. Overall, it’s a versatile keyboard that blends style, functionality, and comfort perfectly, and I highly recommend it for anyone looking for a high-end wireless mechanical keyboard.
reviews.author: Michelle Kim

reviews.title: EXTREMELY please with this keyboard
reviews.comment: I first saw and used they clicky version of this keyboard at Best Buy a few months back and immediately knew I'd eventually buy one.  I'd been using the Razer Anansi for years, but I went through two of them rather quickly and they really wore out quickly, collected dirt and gunk easily, and eventually became unusable. I decided to pick this up as I had received a few promotional bonuses as Amazon gift cards. This thing is just incredible.  It feels great, the keys respond exactly as I expected, but it's also not even remotely as loud as I thought it would be-basically the volume of a mouse click. The quality of the parts seems very good.  I was a little skeptical about the macro/device/brightness/media keys, but they feel very good as well and are very responsive.  Additionally, it seems as though it will be quite easy to keep clean. My only, very marginal beef, is that for the money spent, a good palm/wrist rest really should be included. The "lightspeed" connection really is as fast as advertised.  There is no noticeable input delay-if anything, I feel like this thing MIGHT even be faster wireless (with dongle) than connected with the charging cable. Battery life is very good.  This has been my every day keyboard for about a month now.  I've only even charged it maybe 3 times, and that was overkill. A lot of reviewers comment on the G HUB software.  I'm really blown away by how much this keyboard can be customized, but I don't have any big plans to do so.  I haven't had any major problems with the software-it does what it's supposed to for me so far. Overall, I can't recommend this keyboard highly enough.  $200+ is most certainly way up there for a keyboard, but I'm optimistic that I will end up being a good value long-term.  As long as it holds up, I don't have any problem stating that it's completely worth the money. Update 12/24: I've had this keyboard for 5 years and it works as well as the day I bought it.  Of course the tops of the A and S keys are pretty worn, and one of the rubber grip strips on the bottom came off, but other than that, this keyboard may as well still be brand new.  I use this as both my everyday keyboard and my gaming keyboard, so it's been heavily used for 5 years now.  I still rarely have to charge it.  It's currently sitting at 60%, and the last time I charged it was more than a month ago. My only complaint is that Logitech doesn't offer the ability to purchase a replacement receiver/dongle directly.  When I accidentally broke the old one, I had to buy a 3rd party replacement, however it connected very easily and quickly through G Hub and has worked flawlessly ever since. For the price these regularly go for now (generally around $150) I can't recommend this keyboard highly enough.
reviews.author: MB

reviews.title: Overpriced, but not obscenely so considering the quality of the board
reviews.comment: Obviously, it's pretty expensive.  $250 is a lot to ask for any keyboard.  That being said, while I feel like it's slightly overpriced I definitely don't feel like it's a complete ripoff considering what you're getting.  I've had it for a week and I'm completely satisfied with it so far.  The build quality feels very solid, it looks super sharp on my desk, and the low-profile switches (I got the clicky blues since I use it for both gaming and productivity) are among my favorite of any mechanical keyboard I've ever used.  It's loaded with features, the RGB looks vibrant and evenly-lit, and I really appreciate being able to quickly swap between the wireless dongle and standard bluetooth when I want to switch to my work laptop. Shockingly, the Logitech G-Hub software is actually pretty decent, which is not a thing I'm used to for gaming peripheral drivers, even from Logitech.  It's not flawless, but it looks nice, it's reasonably fast and responsive, and it generally does what it needs to do without any fuss, which is really all you need out of software like this. If you don't care for the wireless, the G815 is the exact same keyboard but without wireless for $50 less, which is pretty reasonable. UPDATE: It's one and a half years and one WFH pandemic later, I still really, really like this keyboard.  I've used the hell out of it and aside from some small nicks on the squared off bottom edge of the aluminum case where I  bumped it against random mugs/keys/whatever on my desk, it still looks and works great.  All of the lights illuminate as brightly as they did when I first got it and the keycaps have held up well over the last 18 months. For the past month I've been seeing rare double or missed inputs on a few keys (spacebar, P, R usually), but a few days ago I took all of the keycaps off and thoroughly cleaned the entire unit and underneath all of the caps and the issue no longer occurs, so I suspect the issue was a small amount of debris interfering with the rebound on the low profile switches. Post-Covid, I'll probably bring my old keyboard to the office and buy the newer TKL version of this board for home use.
reviews.author: Victor

reviews.title: Great Hardware- Garbage Software
reviews.comment: I want to like this keyboard so much.  The hardware is great- I can switch seamlessly between the USB on my main PC and bluetooth to my work PC.  The keys are laid out great and the clicky keys I prefer  feel prefect.  The wireless latency is literally negligible and battery life is amazing. BUT! The GHub software is absolute canine crap.  When installed, it automatically sets up profiles for any games or apps you have on your machine that it supports whether you want them or not- and you can't delete them. The lighting will randomly turn off and no amount of setting combinations prevent this.  You can't save most key assignments to onboard memory. I cannot for the life of me figure out how to save a lighting configuration to onboard memory so when I switch to bluetooth the color patterns switches to it's default, and really ridiculous wavy rainbow pattern.  And, the keyboard will randomly switch profiles. The culprit in all of this is the GHub software, and the interweb is literally full of complaints about this software going back at least a half a decade, if not more. Logitech's "give a s@#'" factor over this is laughable- they really don't seem to give a rats rectum.  I didn't know this before I bought. If you want a great keyboard and really enjoy stabbing your eyes out in frustration- this is the one for you.  If you prefer your eyes intact- look elsewhere.  For the money spent, I'm really disappointed in Logitech.  Spend your hard earned cash on another company.
reviews.author: Charles Boothe

reviews.title: Great keyboard
reviews.comment: This keyboard was a great purchase, although it's kind of expensive, I loved the aesthetics of while also having the macro keys. It arrived quickly, and was ready to use right out of the box, besides needing to connect it to charge the battery, and needing Logitechs software to change the lighting effects. Other then that, I have very little complaints. Overall, the battery can last about a week without needing to charge (I use it everyday for 6 or more hours and I keep it at about 50% brightness), and the lighting on the keyboard looks very clean and is easy to customize. I've seen a lot of people complain about the macro profiles, and the media buttons being made of membrane (squishy button), however, it has not been a problem for me. The buttons are very sensitive so you won't really have to push them, and as someone who uses them a lot, I think they're perfectly fine as they are. The only complaints I do have is that when my keyboard received a software update a few weeks ago (first one I've ever had since purchasing a few months ago) it disabled my macro keys until I updated the software. After the update, everything was working as normal. My last complaint is that after you shut down your computer, your keyboard will of course shut down with it. However, if you accidentally press a button on the keyboard after you shut down the computer, your keyboard will turn back on, and in my case, it would not turn back off. So I have to manually turn off the keyboard. Other then that, this was a great purchase and I hope it lasts a long time, especially with the cost of the keyboard.
reviews.author: AmazonCustomer99138

reviews.title: Great keyboard with a great typing experience.
reviews.comment: I bought this keyboard at the recommendation of a friend that has the ten key version.  I prefer the TKL layout to save space on my desk.  I really like the formfactor of this keyboard.  The low profile of the housing and the keyswitches is very sleek and looks great.  The switches themselves are great to type on and the shorter throw is easy to adapt to from Cherry MX.  The Wireless receiver took no setup to work and plugging in to charge the battery was a sinch.  I also love the volume roller on this keyboard.  It has enough friction to not freewheel but you know how much you're turning it up or down.  I haven't synced this keyboard up via Bluetooth to anything yet.  I imagine the bluetooth experience is also solid.  The battery seems to last a reasonable amount of time.  I prefer to leave the keyboard plugged in to keep the backlight active as I often game in the dark.  Logitech's game mode is also a great way to suppress certain keys that you won't use while in a game (Looking at you Windows key!)  I also tend to turn off Capslock in game mode as well. The RGB effects are not too bright but provide a splash of color to a gaming setup.  There's four brightness levels accessible with a nice dedicated button.  If you prefer, the keyboard can be set to single color, though I'm a sucker for RGB effects.  I put this keyboard up there with my other custom mechanical keyboards at a similar pricepoint in terms of quality.  Logitech didn't disappoint.
reviews.author: Jared J.

reviews.title: Great gaming keyboard with weak shift key
reviews.comment: Keyboard Super Review (gaming and basic computing perspective) Logitech G915 TKL: The keys on this board are lightweight, which is a selling point. I have large man hands scuffed up from working outdoors with the lifelong dexterity of a computer gamer -- yet the lighter keys can be easier to counter strafe in FPS games. The layout of the board feels natural and I do not misfire keys. I immediately played very well with this keyboard. Compared to the Corsair K65 with its instant activation, I game much better on this keyboard. My criticism is the Shift key, a common button for games, is a wide key but supported like it is a single wide key, unlike the rest of these keyboards which reinforce the shift key. This can be frustrating when toggling sprint in a game like Tarkov. Corsair K65  65%: (OPX Switches, PBT Double-Shot Keycaps) The switches are very easy to activate, there is no wiggle room, as with other switches/keyboards, they will activate and reset with little distance before the switch can be triggered again. This can take some getting used to for twitch competitive gaming. My main criticism is the size. I ordered the 75% for the Function Keys although it has different switches. If you dont use those readily then the small size of this is a boon. The small size takes a bit getting used to, for better and worse, as its very nice to have page up/down so close to the arrow keys, etc. Also, this keyboard is FUN to use, I want to press the keys; despite buying several keyboards to test, I am not a keyboard/switch fetishist either. The size is great if you dont need function keys. Corsair K65  75%: (PBT Dye-Sub Keycaps, Pre-Lubricated MLX Red Linear Switches) The prelubed switches are amazing; I don't know why more keyboards come this way (it is a lot of work to lube them yourself). If you are partial to buttery sounding/feeling switches then this is a good contender. The switch activation point is ideal for my crack FPS playstyle. The bluetooth and wireless dongle are useful for playing on the TV. The sound knob is not easy to turn and is even more difficult to grab with the Home key right next to it. This is my overall favorite keyboard and what I use for computing and gaming. Sadly, it is my least favorite keyboard aestetically, from keycaps to backlight effects. Ducky One 3 TKL: (Double Shot PBT, Cherry MX Red) This might be my favorite keyboard. The switches have a bit of give before activation which is a concern for my precise FPS gaming playstyle--I am not as confident when a key will trigger compared to some other boards. This is understandable, the Ducky is not marketed as a gaming keyboard; which might also be why it is my favorite to use for typing/word processing. The Corsair, for comparison, has no give and trigger with the slightest force. Maybe its my past habit of using keyboards but I like to put a little weight down on the keys, especially when strafing in games or waiting to press a key. Somewhat unrelated, this keyboard was missing a few keycaps but Ducky mailed me the missing caps ASAP. tldr: Not the best keyboard for freak FPS gaming, short of that it is tied with Corsair K65, with difference being when you like the key to trigger (a little give with Ducky or instantly with K65). Might also be worth noting I am typing a lot of reviews with this keyboard. Logitech G413 TKL: Amazon cancelled my order of this, probably because they doubled the price after I purchased it. Unfortunate because one of my past favorite gaming keyboards was a similar Logitech, which I gifted to my sister. Das Keyboard 6 Professional: (Tactile Cherry MX Brown Switches) This was my old keyboard. It is very disappointing. It is incredibly overpriced. The caps are not PBT (newer, nicer key cap plastic tech). I lubed the switches myself and it is slightly better. I have posted a very long review on its page. Das 4 keyboard was one of the best of its time (cat urinated on mine). I hope the future iterations will be better for Das' sake...since the rest of these boards are almost half the price and better per most metrics.
reviews.author: mcgees

reviews.title: Better than the reviews lead me to believe
reviews.comment: I was skeptical about buying this keyboard based on the reviews I saw. I took a chance and am happy that I did. I wanted a TKL, wireless, USB/Bluetooth keyboard that is good for typing/work and gaming, has the Home/End/Pg Up/Pg Down keys in the traditional locations and also has the F keys offset (not directly above the number keys). $200 is a lot for a keyboard, but I trust Logitech and wanted to give this a try. It exceeded my expectations. I need the keyboard to be able to switch back and forth between a PC (Gaming) and a Mac (Work). On PC, I plugged in the lightspeed wireless dongle and I was done. On Mac, I paired the keyboard with bluetooth, it asked me press certain keys on the keyboard and I was done. When connected to the Mac via bluetooth, the Windows key changes to the Apple/Command key and the Alt key changes to the Option key automatically. It was seamless. I did not have to download any software or set any preferences to make this happen. I wanted to point that out because I couldn't find any other reviews that touched on that subject and this was important to know for my needs. They Keychron I was using did not have a wireless USB option, so I had to toggle back and forth between Wired USB and Bluetooth. To do so, you have to flip a switch on the side of the keyboard, then you have to flip a second switch based on if you want the keys to be Mac or PC. With the G915, all of this is gone. Its all wireless, and when you press the USB button its automatically set to PC keys...when you press the bluetooth button its automatically set to Mac keys (because I paired it with a Mac). Huge QoL improvement for me. Gaming wise...my first night I played with it, I won 6 straight in overwatch and got promoted to platinum so....take that as you will. In all seriousness though, there is no delay, no ghosting issues, no missed key presses or anything like that. It works perfectly. Typing wise, I prefer the tactile keys. The actuation point isn't super deep (like it is with Keychron) and the keys feel crisp and make a slightly audible click. I am fast and accurate. Very happy with this. The profile is suuuuper thin. So thin in fact that I don't need my wrist rest anymore. The Keychron I had was incredibly thick and without a wrist guard, it felt like my wrists were constantly angled up. Not the case with this keyboard. I don't care about lights but.....it has them, and there are several options available in the G-Hub software. On the negatives, the keys aren't as tight as I am used to. They wiggle around kind of like a loose tooth might. It's not a huge deal, but its something I noticed that I thought was weird. The price is going to be the biggest negative for me. Paying $200 for a keyboard is unattractive, but since it covered all of my (weird) bases, I paid it. Wish it was close to $150. Overall, it fit my needs, performs better than expected and it cleaned up my setup quite a bit. Happy with the purchase, even if it was pricey.
reviews.author: SoBeDragon

reviews.title: Excellent Low Profile Wireless Keyboard
reviews.comment: In short, this keyboard feels extremely satisfying to type on, and for someone coming from a laptop keyboard I highly recommend it.  For those coming from mechanical keyboards, you really need to feel this to know if you like it or not, but I really like the feel of the tactile switches. Pros: - Tactile switches feel excellent for both typing and gaming (although pure gamers might prefer reds) - Wireless (basically zero latency; no cables;  just fantastic) - RGB is extremely bright (turns off quick, but you can adjust the sleep times and colors in GHub) - Great battery life (I have to charge maybe once every two weeks, although that is usage dependent) - Volume wheel is fantastic Cons: - Expensive (Do not pay $230, that is absurd.  For the $170 I got it for, it is an expensive but great keyboard) - Micro usb to charge (In 2022, placing Micro usb instead of usb c for $230 is absurd, but again, find a sale) - GHub is required to adjust sleep states and RGB (I don't mind much, but some do, so it's worth mentioning) I am a longtime laptop user, and only in the past year or so did I begin using external keyboards.  First, I used apple's magic keyboard, and while this keyboard enabled me to type accurately (I'm a longtime mac user), it does not feel great due to the incredibly short keys and lack of tactility.  Then, I used a ducky one two mini given to me by a friend with Cherry silent red switches, and this keyboard was just much too sensitive.  The actuation force required by the keys was ridiculously low, which is fantastic for gaming, but for anything else it creates typos unless you can adjust.  Thus I went looking for low profile mechanical keyboards.  This was the only low-latency wireless one I could find.  It is premium, feels great, and I really do not have any major complaints so far.  No, the switches aren't replaceable.  But that's also not really their target demographic.  If you want the best in low profile mechanical keyboards for work and gaming, this is it.
reviews.author: Clint D

reviews.title: A Solid Performer with Some Room for Improvement
reviews.comment: The Logitech G915 TKL wireless keyboard deserves a 4 out of 5-star rating for several compelling reasons, including its remarkable build quality, dazzling lighting effects, superb wireless connectivity, and outstanding battery life. However, there are a couple of areas where it could see some enhancements. Pros: 1. Exceptional Build Quality: The Logitech G915 TKL exudes quality from every angle. It's solid, well-constructed, and has a premium feel that's immediately apparent. The brushed aluminum top plate not only looks sleek but also adds durability to the keyboard. 2. Stunning Lighting: Logitech has always been a pioneer in RGB lighting, and the G915 TKL is no exception. The customizable lighting effects are nothing short of fantastic. Whether you want a subtle ambiance or a mesmerizing light show, this keyboard has you covered. 3. Superb Wireless Performance: The wireless performance of this keyboard is outstanding, providing a responsive and lag-free experience. It's perfect for gaming or simply enjoying the freedom of a clutter-free desk. However, keep in mind that it may suffer at extended ranges, so stay within a reasonable distance for the best results. 4. Unrivaled Battery Life: One of the standout features of the Logitech G915 TKL is its exceptional battery life. It sets a new standard for wireless keyboards, lasting for an impressively long time on a single charge. You can enjoy extended gaming sessions or work without the constant worry of recharging. Cons: 1. Prone to Grease: One downside I've noticed is that the keycaps tend to get greasy easily, which can be a bit of a nuisance. Regular cleaning is required to keep it looking pristine. 2. Typing Experience: While I opted for the tactile keys, I found the typing experience to be somewhat disappointing. The keys feel a tad mushy, and the tactile feedback is not as pronounced as I'd like. It's a matter of personal preference, but it didn't quite match my expectations for a premium keyboard. In summary, the Logitech G915 TKL is a commendable wireless gaming keyboard with a lot going for it. Its build quality, lighting effects, wireless performance, and exceptional battery life are all top-notch. However, it could benefit from some improvements in terms of keycap resistance to grease and the typing experience. If Logitech can refine these aspects in future iterations, it could easily become the perfect gaming keyboard. For now, it's an excellent choice for gamers who prioritize aesthetics, wireless freedom, and extended battery life.

reviews.title: Sounds great, looks great, and overall very nice
reviews.comment: Keyboard was super easy to set up! Keys also sound amazing and I love the unique font and graphics that are on the keys. Being able to have a keyboard that looks custom for such a good price is awesome for someone like me who is new to PC gaming but loves aesthetics. The smaller screen is also super nice with showing the time and making it easy to adjust the RGB of the keyboard itself. I will note that I can't figure out how to change the date on the keyboard screen and it's set to one day ahead of the current date, but that's not a major issue and probably something I am just not figuring out yet. The volume control knob also works great and is a nice added convenience. Very happy with my purchase and will recommend this keyboard to others!
reviews.author: DeL B

reviews.title: Well worth it!!
reviews.comment: Absolutely loving this keyboard by Redragon!! When I was looking to upgrade my keyboard this was one of the options I was considering and I’m so happy I went with it. I love the feel of this board when typing, depending on how hard you push and how fast do you type the sound is great not too overwhelming and the feel it gives is very soft and smooth. It’s super easy to customize, the software was fairly easy to find on their website and uploading gifs and changing the rgb is very easy to figure out. Compared to the other keyboards, I was looking at this one isn’t expensive at all and is still a great quality keyboard. If your thinking about getting it you won’t regret it!!
reviews.author: Lauren & Richard

reviews.title: Way better than I expected, great entrance to mechanical keyboards.
reviews.comment:
I wanted to build my own keyboard, but wanted a small form with a number pad. the cheapest barebones kit that met that criteria was over $80, so I figured I'd give this a shot. I have never had/used a mechanical keyboard and didn't want to put a ton of money into it right away. I also didn't want a super loud click, I think those ones sound really annoying. I was very pleasantly surprised by the feel, quality, weight, and sound of this. I actually am able  to type faster on this than my old membrane keyboard. The RGB is way better than I was expecting, it's bright, has tons of modes, and the battery is surprisingly long with it on.
Connectivity hasn't been an issue either, I have the usb dongle in my computer, and the bluetooth linked to my phone so I can quickly switch between them if I have a long text to send.
My brother is a mechanical keyboard snob, and he was very surprised by how quality this felt and typed. The switches are smooth and quiet enough that I don't feel a need to change them, but I like that I have that option for so little cost.
I think my only criticism is that I wish the keyboard was a little wider so that the 0 key in the numpad could be a full size. I still hit the right arrow button a lot when I'm using the numpad quickly. Overall it's not too big of a deal though.
reviews.author: Kevin M.

reviews.title: Love this keyboard and the company!
reviews.comment: I have had this keyboard for a couple of months now and I gotta say that it is so gorgeous! I get compliments on it all the time at work and I love bragging about it! The keyboard is made well, it is able to handle my incessant pounding and the sound is light enough to not bother my coworkers. The keys have a milky quality to them, so if you like a noisy keyboard this isn’t for you, but the layout and the larger than average lettering has made my typing speed so much better. I don’t often use it off the usb wire, but what I have seen indicates that it has a good amount of battery life. One of the keys came damaged and while the company was not able to get me a replacement, they did give me some credit back on the keyboard. Considering similar keyboards are in the $100+ range, this one is a good option for those wanting to either dip their toes into mechanical keyboards or budget-conscious folks.
reviews.author: Krys

reviews.title: I love this keyboard
reviews.comment:
I have owned several red dragon mechanical keyboards over the years, I love them for their high quality and low price, but this is by FAR my favorite keyboard so far. The keys are mint switches which I've never tried but I'll never not use again, they feel and sound absolutely amazing. When you're typing away you don't get that loud, audio spiking click like a red or blue switch, you get a solid low thud. It sounds like raindrops hitting a wood roof, you could easily sleep through it. The tactile sensation doesn't even suffer like having a membrane keyboard, it provides a nice balanced resistance force that thuds right when it bottoms out, something that's hard to describe the feel of. I cannot stand a numpad-less keyboard so the inclusion of this full sized numpad while keeping the overall size relatively small is phenomenal. The volume knob has a nice tactile feel as well. The little LCD screen is awesome, and surprisingly crisp at a low resolution thanks to its small size. A lot of keyboards have had monochrome screens in them but this one is full color and you can upload your own gifs to the app, which you'll need to download in order to customize the keys, RGB, and screen. I wish it had SignalRGB or openRGB support but unfortunately it does not. The frame is plastic, usually red dragon makes nice cheap metal frame keyboards, but it doesn't flex when you're typing on it so it's a pass for me. It can flex a little bit you need to be deliberately trying. This also makes it a little on the lighter side so it's easier to accidentally move.
Note:
-You might need to download the red dragon k719 software and update the firmware with it in order for the windows key (and some others) to work
reviews.author: Alex F.

reviews.title: Bigger quantity
reviews.comment: I would give 5 stars but I’m giving it 4 only because there’s not a bigger quantity option. If I wanted to replace my whole keyboard it would coast me a new keyboard
reviews.author: Matt

reviews.title: Yabba dabba poooooo!
reviews.comment: Looks great. Working good so far.
reviews.author: Eire1961

reviews.title: HIGHLY recommend
reviews.comment: Product: Air75 V3 with Blush Switches in ANSI layout. Received this today, and I have to say, this is by far one of the best tech purchases I’ve made so far this year. Quite frankly, in a while. The keyboard came 50% charged and made connecting to multiple devices via bluetooth, the 2.4ghz dongle, and even wired, seamless, easy, and intuitive. I haven’t used it long enough to determine what connectivity will look like after some usage, but I can confidently say that I’m looking forward to using the keyboard everyday to test this. The Air75 v3 looks slim, but practical, simple, but elegant. It’s the perfect blend of function, purpose, and focus. For just around $150, I can say that there is no buyers remorse around so far. The keys feel weighty enough to confidently hit each keystroke with a gentle thock. The version I ordered came with the blush switches (use mainly in office) so I prioritized noise over thockiness, however, it still thocks quite well. I’d argue that it’s probably just as quiet or if not quiter than some scissors switches from enterprise cookie cutter keyboards. The package came with additional keycaps to switch from MacOS to Windows, knob accessories, and a cable for wired connections. This made the set up to to switch layouts very easy. Only complaints (minimal so I’m not even going to dock a star): the blossom keys are VERY quiet. If I weren’t planning to have this be my daily in office use, I’d go with the brown or cherry switches. The blossom switches are a bit too dampened, so the feedback (keys resetting position or return height) can sometimes feel not as responsive. This is something to get used to, however it doesn’t really affect the typing experience overall. The other complaints would be with the instructions on how to navigate the keyboard settings, remembering which button combination does what… gave me old game shark cheat code memories… regardless, this is expected with simple keyboards, once set, it should “just work”. Which it has proven to, so far! Overall, I would HIGHLY recommend this to anyone who wants an upgrade in their office set up, want a more minimalist approach, and need focus/declutter.
reviews.author: Xiong Yang

reviews.title: Very portable, and very cool.
reviews.comment: This cute little keyboard is getting a ton of attention on my work desk.  I appreciate the aesthetic of it, but I really love the easy of typing on it. It’s very satisfying with the brown switches and not so loud that my colleagues are bothered.  I have asked a few times and they would not hesitate to tell me if it was too loud. Set up was easy, but note that the initial set up is much easier if you are using the wired connection. I had to find an adapter as the provided cable is USB A to USB C, and my MacBook can’t accommodate USB A. Switching from a top right corner key to a knob was very easy and they provide everything you need.  I  thought the knob might be a little gimmicky, but I find myself using it frequently. The RGB function is something that I will use only occasionally, but it does work well and has tons of customization.
reviews.author: Kerrie_T

reviews.title: Amazing 75% keyboard
reviews.comment: Genuinely amazing typing experience. The switches could have a bit more of a tactile feel but nothing wrong per se. The keyboard feels well made, not like it's going to fall apart at any time. The typing sound itself, that chonky sound" is incredibly satisfying. I didn't buy it for gaming, but in day to day activity I don't notice any meaningful delay in typing, regardless of connection mode. Solid investment
reviews.author: Alex

reviews.title: Great improvement. King of the low profile keyboards all around
reviews.comment: If you have been a fan of Nuphy keyboards, you'll feel right at home. This is a noticeable improvement over the V2 (which I loved) but was torn between the LoFree because it offered a much better typing feel. This improvement fixes all of that. The gasket mount makes a huge difference compared to the V2 and the connectivity issues I used to have with the V2 are absent. Typing feel is incredible for a low profile keyboard and have no complaints. Ultimately went with the Brown switches, but the red ones were great if you enjoy a linear experience. Battery life is excellent even with the backlights on. Also appreciate the new keycap color scheme. Still feels unique, but predominantly simple. Included keycaps allow you to make the board entirely neutral colored if you don't appreciate the pop of color. Overall, no complaints and couldn't recommend this keyboard enough. One thing to note is that if you are coming from a V2, the lowest typing angle is a bit higher on this one. You get used to it, but I really became accustomed to the lower one.
reviews.author: Tech Guru

reviews.title: Great keyboard bad quality control.
reviews.comment: First off, let me say I love this keyboard. I opted for the blush nano switches which feel amazing. I didn't want a loud clicky switch and this provides a good THOCK but yet remains quiet in my office setting. However, the USB port has malfunctioned and it can no longer recognize the device via USB within a week of ownership (which doesn't bode well). Luckily, I can still use the keyboard in wireless mode until the replacement arrives. I would normally just cut my losses, but I am attempting to get a replacement unit as like I stated previously I really do like this keyboard. Update- Amazon's replacement was incorrect (it was a used unit and someone swapped it out for a totally different keyboard). Bad quality control on Amazon's behalf. Lowering to one star. Do better
reviews.author: Kyle Swerlein

reviews.title: Best 60% i’ve used out of 6+
reviews.comment: I fell down the custom keyboard rabbit hole back during lockdown and tried a lot of custom boards. Even though I dropped out and sold most of my customs I can still appreciate a quality keyboard, and this is legit one of them. 2.4ghz wireless is something i missed and having it here is so nice. It’s nice to type on, sounds amazing for a stock board, and the stabilizers are actually perfect. Easy custom bindings with VIA is great to see on ‘accessible’ boards and honestly it’s laid out pretty great stock. My only complaint would be the keycap colorway but that’s my last lingering bit of snobbery from the dark ages. Legitimately a solid buy, even if it is pricier than the competition.
reviews.author: LJ

reviews.title: Excellent Upgrade – Fast, Sleek, and Worth It
reviews.comment: This is a fantastic keyboard. I upgraded from a Keychron and haven’t looked back. The NuPhy Air60 V2 connects almost instantly—no lag or hassle switching between devices—and the battery life has been phenomenal. I only charge it occasionally, even with heavy daily use. It’s definitely on the pricier side, but you get what you pay for: solid build quality, low-profile comfort, and buttery-smooth switches (I went with Gateron Moss). It’s also lightweight and compact, perfect for desk setups or travel. If you’re on the fence because of the price, I’d still say go for it—especially if you're replacing something like a Keychron. This feels like a true step up.
reviews.author: Caden Cannon

reviews.title: Its my daily driver for work.
reviews.comment: I have a collection of custom machanical keyboards but this one is just perfect for work. Nice liner switches that are silky smooth and quiet compared to me other machinical keyboards. All the special function keys are easy to use and I have it paired to all kinds of devices with no issues. From PC to Mac, IPad OS to Android it all works. One slight issue come when you want to look for keycaps ( I wasn’t a fan of the white keys ), and again not a issue with the keyboard itself.  Just remember that you will need to find “low profile” replacement keycaps. You can buy them from over vendors online or from Nuphy themselves but it will take a while for them to ship to the US and its a little more expensive due to shipping. Over all love the keyboard.
reviews.author: Bandersnatch

reviews.title: Great product with a few quirks
reviews.comment: This is a solid product with a few quirks to be aware of. Ultimately I am returning it because Nuphy just announced the Air75 V3 and that's more what I wanted (the extra row). Pros: - Fantastic typing experience; great feel, great sound (I got the Cowberry Switch version) - High-quality materials and construction; this thing is gorgeous and feels high quality - Decent (though not amazing) battery life - Rock-solid Bluetooth connectivity (zero drop outs since I've been using it, unlike LoFree which is a disaster in comparison) - Near-immediate wake-up and connection to Bluetooth, nearly as good as the Apple Magic Keyboard experience Cons: - They should really include white keys in the box to replace the "fun" coloured keys; making a customer spend $20 for a white set of keys + $10 in shipping just to get a white keyboard really sucks. -  Compared to every other device I have, the power switch is the opposite direction to turn on, which is strange. - There are some weird battery quirks with Bluetooth; the keyboard was at 7% power, I plugged it in for 10 minutes and it was reporting 100% battery (which seemed impossible), so I unplugged it and it showed 72%, then rapidly dropped to 67%...very strange. - For the LIFE of me, I couldn't figure out how to get the ~ character out of this keyboard. I tried FN, CMD, etc. and I could only ever get the ` character. That's irksome as I use that character fairly often. - There's no "LED lights off mode"; I wasted way too much time going through all the modes until I asked an AI how to turn off the damn lights. The solution is turning the brightness down to zero, which isn't all that intuitive. I'd have appreciated a "no LED mode" as part of the modes that the customer flips through.
reviews.author: Jason Dunn

reviews.title: solid keyboard with nice keys
reviews.comment: Nice keyboard, good keys and easy to use with all options it has available, built nice and good structure
reviews.author: Justin Weber

reviews.title: Love this headset!
reviews.comment:
I love this headset.  A few highlights:
* Comfort:  The band on the top is really comfortable.  I have a larger head and sometimes I feel the squeeze on my ears.  Not with this headset.  It feels very light and I have gamed for a 10 hour session with no issues.
* Lights:  So I really like how the lights face forward.  A lot of others go to the side, but for who to see them?  If I turn my camera on, then I get to see the lights (I have a light/aqua blue theme going that looks great on the white headset)
* Sound:  The sound is great!  The materials talk about angled drivers and that may be the reason, I don't know; but the sound is great.  Kudos on the immersion!
* Mic:  Very clear, others had no issues hearing me
Overall I really like this headset and it is a great value compared to others which are priced higher (using $10-30 higher).  I get that RGB may or may not be someone's thing, but he headband and the USB-C connection justify the upgrade from the non-RGB version (IMO).  Highly recommend.
reviews.author: Ben

reviews.title: A great headset!
reviews.comment:
For me personally the GLORIOUS GHS Eternal RGB fit nicely into my life. They come with USB-C to USB-C cable, USB-C to 3.5 mm headphone jack, and USB-C to USB-A adapter. The headset is well made with good flex and cushioning. They are also quite comfortable on my head and ears. I chose to connect using the USB-C to USB-C cable and adapter to my PC. I downloaded the Glorious Core application which allows for adjusting the RGB, equalizer, updating firmware, etc.
Sound quality is on par with my Logitech headset I typically wear. I am not an audiophile, so I can't necessarily speak to the sound profile, but they sound good while watching videos, playing music, and all work calls. I tested the mic by recording myself speaking through zoom and sound recorder and playing it back. On the "mid" mic setting, I sound good to me, and coworkers seem to hear me just fine during calls. I really only play single player games, so I was not able to test the mic and chat/audio balancing features of this headset.
A few notable things I like. I really like that when I click the mic off button, that a red light appears on the tip of the mic. So if I accidentally press, it is pretty obvious. I love that I can push the knob on the right side to pause/play whatever I am watching. I like that the ear cushion is easy to remove, for cleaning, maybe replacement down the line.
A few things that don't work today, but I hope is resolved. I wish these worked with SignalRGB. I did request the addition. They support Glorious keyboards, so it may happen, but something people should be aware of. I also do not care for the volume handling. Turing the volume up and down on the headset should also do this in Windows. I do not like managing the volume on two devices. This is how every other headset I have ever owned has worked.
reviews.author: Snorlaxin

reviews.title: Pleasantly surprised with this headset
reviews.comment:
As someone who owns the Audeze Maxwell and ROG Kithara, I was not expecting much from this headset.
What I found is that this was actually easy to setup.  The nice light and clean design is actually a welcome touch to all the new headsets with rollers and buttons all over the place.
As for sound, its good.  Its using the usual dynamic drivers you find in many other headsets.  The tuning feels bass heavy, but not as much as I usually expect "gamer" headsets to be, and I also appreciate that they kept the "gamery" look down.  On my model this has RGB, but its not over the top and can be turned off if you want.  The two knobs on the back of the ear cups allows you to adjust volume and one will allow you to adjust voice/game mix.
This headset obviously doesn't hold a candle to high end headsets from Audeze or HiFiMan, but I do appreciate that they did not go crazy on the bass tuning, I actually felt there was a great presence with the tuning and does help keep footsteps and other fine sounds from being muddied out from too much bass.  The drivers are supposedly angled for better placement to your ears... I can only say they sound good, but I cant say that the angle was much more than just a marketing buzzword list.  The positional audio did well in FPS, being closed back does limit the sound stage, but I could easily make out footsteps and subtle noises thanks to the tuning.
The mic actually sounds good, at least compared to the Logitech G735, which is what my wife uses.  I found it to be nice crisp and clear.  Not a ton of bass and not too boxy or nasal sounding.  Overall impressed!  This is where many gamer headsets fall short.
Now, this is a wired headset, which is going to be a turn off for many people.  Many people are want to go wireless and while I do think this should have been included, I think the exclusion might work in its favor.  Most mics lose clarity over 2.4Ghz on a good connection and so does sound in general.  I think this might be why I think this headset sounds as good as it does.  I think its easy to mess up wireless sound, so it was probably a good call here.
Glorious Core is not the greatest software, but it does get the job done.  Technically you don't need it as you can use it as a analog connection or USB.  However if you want to adjust the RGB and other minor features, you will want to use Glorious Core Software.
Overall, I do recommend this headset if you don't need wireless.  The cables are of decent length, and the USB one looks like a typical USB-C to USB-C cable, so you could get a longer one if you needed to.  We tried with one of our 10 foot cables and it seems to be working just fine.  The USB-C to 3.5 Headphone cable might be harder to find, but you could probably find a decent USB-C to C extension cable.  The included cables are both very compliant and easy to work with.
I think this sounds good, its not great like some of the hifi headphones that I currently own and use, however I don't think they would hold me back from enjoying music and gaming.
reviews.author: PCTA

reviews.title: Absolutely perfect. Worth every penny.
reviews.comment:
The Logitech G PRO X Wireless is hands down the best headset I’ve ever owned. The sound quality is incredible; crisp highs, deep bass, and amazing clarity whether I’m gaming, listening to music, or chatting with friends. The comfort level is top-tier; I can wear it for hours with no pressure or discomfort.
The wireless connection is flawless with zero lag, and the battery life easily lasts through long sessions. The microphone is crystal clear, and the overall build quality feels premium and sturdy.
I have zero complaints, this headset delivers everything I hoped for and more. If you’re on the fence, just buy it. You won’t regret it!
reviews.author: Jessica Pendley

reviews.title: Great headset
reviews.comment: Bought this to replace my astro a50s that had mic issues and am honestly impressed with this headset. The sound quality is great its fits comfortably and the mic is of good quality. I bought it renewed and it looks brand new zero flaws. Would highly recommend.
reviews.author: Roland Taylor Daniel

reviews.title: Wireless Mic has an internal issue and REFERBISHED?? NOT!
reviews.comment:
I knew better than to purchase RENEWED items having worked in the tech field previously but I needed a headset that could both be wireless and wired and this headset was it, however, I could NOT afford NEW. So I thought I would give it a try.
I get it and unbox it  download the drives and the Logitech G App I test it out wireless, but no one can hear me, but I can hear them. I work through everything I can find in troubleshooting the issue since it did not come with directions on what to download, and how to use this headset.  After 24 hours of trying to get the wireless mic to work, I have determined it is an internal issue. I HAVE GONE THROUGH EVERY POSSIBLE STEP TO MAKE THE MIC WORK WIRELESSLY, but it is fruitless.
It works great wired, but that is not the reason I spent so much money on a headset. If I wanted a wired headset I could spend $50 and get a great Razor product.
I know that REFERBISHED is really a word for returned and re-sold, but I was desperate enough I ignored all the reasons for NOT buying refurbished.  The price is not even close to low enough to be worth purchasing a refurbished product. If it was only $50 I would say, well, at least it wasn't nearly $200!  Shame on me... I'm going to return this and get my money back. I will never again be desperate enough to buy "REFERBISHED" Electronic items.  Don't you be fooled... I was a tech person for years, I knew better and I let me desire to have one get the better of me. DON'T do it!
reviews.author: Linde Fam

reviews.title: Love it
reviews.comment: I really enjoy the Logitech G325 LIGHTSPEED headset. It’s lightweight and extremely comfortable, even during long gaming sessions. The Lightspeed wireless connection is fast and stable, with almost no lag, making gameplay smooth and immersive. The battery life is excellent, lasting through multiple sessions without needing a recharge. Sound quality is clear and accurate for games and videos, though the bass could be slightly deeper. The built-in microphone works fine for chat, but isn’t as strong as a dedicated boom mic. Overall, this headset offers excellent performance and comfort at a budget-friendly price, and I highly recommend it for gamers who want quality without spending a fortune.
reviews.author: Nino Nadiradze

reviews.title: Over delivered!
reviews.comment: I’ve gone through my fair share of gaming headsets over the years, and the Logitech G325 LIGHTSPEED Wireless Gaming Headset genuinely stands out as one of the best values I’ve used. First off, the comfort is exceptional. It’s incredibly lightweight—almost to the point where you forget you’re wearing it—and the dual-layer foam ear cushions make long gaming sessions effortless. Whether I’m gaming for hours or just using it casually, there’s zero fatigue.  ￼ The sound quality punches well above its price range. The 24-bit audio delivers crisp highs, solid mids, and surprisingly immersive depth for a headset in this range. Everything from footsteps in competitive games to music and videos sounds clean and detailed.  ￼ One of my favorite features is the built-in beamforming microphone. Not having a bulky boom arm gives it a sleek, modern look, and the voice clarity is excellent—especially with the added AI noise reduction. It’s perfect for gaming, Discord, or even work calls.  ￼ Pair that with 20+ hours of battery life, and you’ve got a headset that easily keeps up with your day.  ￼ What really impressed me most is how much Logitech packed into this headset at around the $80 price point. It feels like a premium product without the premium cost—great design, reliable performance, and excellent all-around usability. Bottom line: If you want a wireless headset that nails comfort, sound, and versatility without breaking the bank, the G325 is an easy recommendation. It’s one of those rare products that actually overdelivers.
reviews.author: Jared Greenleaf

reviews.title: Clear sound
reviews.comment: Great headset for the price. Very comfortable — I can wear it all day without any discomfort. The sound is clear and immersive, perfect for both gaming and music. The microphone picks up my voice well with minimal background noise. Battery life is solid and lasts a long time. Easy to connect to different devices. Very happy with this purchase 👍
reviews.author: Anastasiia

reviews.title: It’s about perfect
reviews.comment: I don’t know much else to say besides I love this headset.  I have had so many and this one is tops for me. - Comfortable enough for hours of listening - Connects to everything Bluetooth (except PS5, boo Sony) - The lightspeed connector for PC/PS5 is great, plug and play - Mute button for the mic is convenient - I have yet to charge it and had it for 5 days, used a couple hours each day, and it was 50% when I got it - USB C charging - Great audio - Quailty padding on the ears and headband - Super light! Only con is not having a case, but at this price, I didn’t expect it.  It doesn’t drop signal, audio quality is nice.  I just love it.
reviews.author: Cody A.

reviews.title: A really comfortable and affordable gaming headset
reviews.comment: What I like the most is how light and comfortable they are. They connect super fast too. I literally opened the box, connected the dongle to my PC, turned them on, and it just connected instantly. The only flaws is that the mic isn’t the best but it’s perfectly usable. The sound quality is your pretty average bassy gamey sound profile so if you dig that kind of sound from other gaming headsets you’ll probably like this one too.
reviews.author: Maud etc

reviews.title: Quality headset with incredible customer service!
reviews.comment: I strongly recommend this headset! I wanted to have a headset that I could wear for 8-12 hours a day for classes, meetings, and just listening to music while I work. This headset is very comfortable as far as headsets go and does fairly well with noise cancellation! I would say comfort and quality are the main strengths of the headset over noise cancellation (but for the price and size, this is still better than I would expect!) After long, continuous use (> 5 hours), my ears would be a little sore, but not bad at all! The sound quality is great, the flip bar for speaking/muting was extremely helpful, and the headset was easily portable. A little less than a year in, one of the speakers stopped working; however, within 24 hours of contacting customer service, they were setting up a replacement to be sent. The customer service experience was seamless and easy! For reference, please be sure to keep the serial number sticker on your headset in case it happens to have a faulty speaker or part!
reviews.author: Jeccine

reviews.title: Great headsets!
reviews.comment: I bought these for my husband since he works from home and is constantly have to take calls. These replaced his last set which broke and we wanted a better quality headset. These are incredibly comfortable and he said he can hear callers clearly now and that they do not hear any background noise. We are very happy with the purchase and product.
reviews.author: lauren myers

reviews.title: Good headset that broke after only 5 months
reviews.comment: It's a solid headset. Fairly comfortable (although the clamping is a bit much, and I have a small head), great sound quality, and useful controls. The mic is okay and blocks out sound as advertised. However, one ear on the headset went out after about 4 months, and the other ear went out a month later. It seems to be a problem with the cord, but since the cord isn't detachable, I can't fix it or replace it easily. I've used a few headsets now (I'm a teacher online). Maybe you'll have better luck with this one than I did, but overall I'm quite disappointed. I spent a hefty amount of money on this only for it to start breaking down after 4 months. For reference, my favorite headset that I've tried is the Nulaxy computer headset. I've had three of them, and they lasted about 4-6 months each on average. However, they only cost $20-25, so it's no problem. Also, my students say that I sound better and clearer with the Nulaxy headset than with this one! I'm honestly not sure why these cost $100 more. Totally not worth it for me. I wanted to get a headset that would last a long time because I felt bad about throwing a pair out every few months. Well, so much for that.
reviews.author: Tristan

reviews.title: Great headset
reviews.comment: This is a wonderful headset. It's very comfortable and can be worn for long periods of time. The noise cancellation mic is excellent. Almost no background noise gets through, even very close noise. The sound quality is outstanding. My only problem with this one is that the cords twists easily and quickly becomes a mass of tangles that end up fraying and making the headset not work. I also don't feel it's worth any price over $40. This is a very expensive headset when there are others just like it for a third of the price.
reviews.author: WKPaulino

reviews.title: a gaming headset is not a work-productivity headset. and for this product, that's a good thing.
reviews.comment: this headset checks all the boxes for a meeting-focused headset. in short: if you're on a lot of virtual meetings in an open (or otherwise noisy) workspace, get this. the positives: light, but seemingly robust construction. good comfort level for my 7-3/8" hat-size, for whatever that's worth. sidetone sidetone sidetone. this is such a critical feature for feeling "tuned in" to your speaking presence. settings (like EQ and sidetone) are stored on the headset itself. so if you're in an environment like mine that doesn't let you install vendor apps all willy-nilly, you can download the app on a personal machine to change your settings, and they'll remain in place if using the headset on another machine. note: the logi tune android (and possibly iphone) app is completely useless for setup and options. it asks you to pair your (what it assumes is a wireless) headset, and doesn't give you an option to bypass this step. get the desktop version instead. very good mic attenuation from background noise/voices. this is a big point that many headset users in corporate environments have not appreciated. huge drivers, over-the-ear cushions, and even active noise cancellation... these make little difference if the microphone design doesn't attenuate background noise in these new "collaborative workspaces" we're in. even if a headset sounds isolated to you, this may mean nothing to your colleagues if all the noise around you is being transmitted to them. on a related note, the on-ear construction of this headset does a better job of passive noise cancellation than many over-ear headsets i've owned. so don't be dissuaded into thinking that on-ear construction will provide worse isolation than bigger, bulkier over-ear designs. cons/neutrals: the cable, while very nicely fabric-coated, is incredibly noisy. it's almost like there's an amplifier where the cable attaches to the headset. thankfully, the provided "lapel clip" prevents a lot of cable movement, at least if you're relatively stationary at your workstation. definitely utilize it. the inline controller is well-built, responsive, and generally a nice touch. but since i am not a "stand and pace" kind of worker, and this is a wired headset, it's not really a burden to adjust controls on my machine instead of using the controller.
reviews.author: e pilar

reviews.title: Perfect - and cool to the touch
reviews.comment: I did a taste test challenge. I put on the original leather, the original cloth, and these new ones. I used them in combination with one another to see how soft they were, how long I could wear them, and how hot I got with each set. These are by FAR cooler than the leather. And for me personally, not only is the sound much better and isolated than the other two, they literally feel cold. They're very soft, feel like much better quality, and I am done searching.  Someone said that the cups themselves were smaller than the factory, which is completely false. They are identical in size and shape. I have fairly large ears and they cover them completely. So in my opinion, they have the best noise isolation, are as soft or more soft than the original leather, and I found them to be cooler than the other two. Someone could perhaps say that cloth is just as cool, and that would be more on the breathable side, which I would say is a matter of preference. However, if you're looking for the best sound, I can wear these just as long if not longer than the cloth, it's a good decision. Side note: When I say quality, I don't just mean the cooling gel and the silk, the outside plastic/rubber ring is MUCH better than the factory pads.  It's super sturdy and I had almost no issues getting them on.  You have to tug them quite a bit because they're not broken in, but I can tell these will last. I can tell that if people are extra cautious it could be frustrating, but the quality is there, put a little effort into it and it's no problem. I did not use any tools, I got them done in seconds with my fingers only. Highly recommend these to anyone like me.  I'm on the computer every day for work: video conferences, music, sports, all of it. Having the upgraded pads makes a huge difference. I'll keep my cloth ones as backups, but I'll never go back to any pleather.  I also did something similar with my airpods and went with the foam tips.  I think when it comes to headphones, I'll always be upgrading as soon as I buy. To me it's a no brainer.  I only leave reviews when someone completely knocks it out of the park or completely drops the ball LOL. These are in the former category. I did not receive these as a promotion, and despite this ridiculous review, I don't work for them either. They're just deserving of a good and thorough review. At the time of purchase they were like 21 dollars with tax. worth it.

As a audiophile I wasn’t sure what to expect especially after doing research and reading so many varied reviews so here my honest opinion from various use (mostly music and for work/phone calls all day).
Arrived fully charged and was super easy to setup.
Just know they are “only” wireless and no backup 3.5mm or USB audio connection (can only charge and no audio connection which is a flaw in my opinion).
They are very nice quality and pretty much resemble airline/cockpit cans/headsets, lol.
They don’t save your height/adjustments but are on smooth arms along each side and very easy to adjust.
I wouldn’t say they are light nor heavy either so a very good balance. Maybe a bit tight grip over the ears but not enough to be a bother. So you are able to wear them all day for work, like I do, and are very comfortable.
The mic is one of the best there is (it’s between these and the Beyerdynamic MMX300), and just great quality.
As for audio quality they are good but not great (the Beyerdynamic ones are way better but missing crucial feature like the app/eq control).
They have good top end and highs but seriously lacking in the lows (as expected with Bluetooth/wireless only connections) so just know that going into it.
And one of their best features is the app/software and being able to fine tune both the listening eq as well as the mic eq, adjust the volume of hearing yourself in the mix, and see status/battery levels…All of which are missing from others that might have better audio quality but missing all of those extra features (looking at you Beyerdynamic, lol).
So if you don’t need high resolution/high fidelity then these are just about the best there is right now.

reviews.title: A (Really) Great Entry Level Wired Headset
reviews.comment: For what it costs, I had relatively low expectations of this headset.  I came from a Corsair Virtuoso SE wireless headset that had a great mic and very good sound, but the connection with my PS4 was never very solid and I would notice relatively frequent dropouts in audio.  Friends with PS4s swore by using the 3.5mm jack on the controller and I decided to use this to test. Build Quality When you pick up the headset the first thing you notice is just how light it is.  It feels somewhat solid, but also it's clear that this is not a headset that prioritized premium materials.  It's also extremely comfortable because of how light it is.  Although I've never had issues with heavier headsets and neck pain, if that is a consideration the light materials should be great for long term sessions. The pads are faux leather on the interior ring and exterior ring.  The part that rests against your head feels like something a little more breathable.  I don't think I will have any issues wearing these for long sessions.  The clamping force is a good moderate level where they won't fall off accidentally, but I don't feel like I am in a death grip. Mic Quality I made some calls using the mic and, I believe this to be a great compliment to the quality of the mic, no one thought I was on a headset.  "It's like you were actually talking through your phone."  Although they have a gamer vibe, I could definitely see using these on conference calls (as long as the video was off.)  Basically, the mic is great. Audio Quality Here's where I was expecting things to fall apart, but they really didn't.  I decided to make a completely unfair comparison between these and my pair of Sennheiser HD600s run off of an AudioQuest DragonFly Black DAC/AMP.  There was clearly no contest between the two headphones in terms of vocals or detail retrieval, but the Razer wasn't a bad headphone by any means.  It had a clear and present bass, without being muddy.  I do feel like the Corsair Virtuoso had a more full sound, but the spotty connection ruined it. Gaming tends to be, I think, more forgiving than listening to music ... so I ran through a couple of games as a test.  I tried a game that I feel focuses on background music (Unravel), which sounded great.  I also tried something with more exploding (Borderlands 3) and the headset felt equally competent. Flaws (But Not Deal Breakers) The volume knob goes the opposite of the way my mind treats every other volume knob in my life.  Clockwise turns the sound down?!  WHY?! I would have loved an LED to remind me that I'm muted.  My first attempted call failed because the mute was engaged. Conclusion The Razer Blackshark V2 X might have a terrible name, but it's an amazing product at the price point.  I don't play as many games online as I used to and I listen to a lot more music.  For me, it makes sense to have a great pair of headphones for music and solo play as well as a cheap headset for online play with friends and conference calls.  This works for me.

I prefer how these have a little knob for the volume control; it's much easier to find than a tiny swivel. One bad thing, when I listened to a recording, it would sometimes get picked up by the mic as if I was speaking, but I wasn't. The other one did it as well... MIC QUALITY: The mics are very similar with marginal differences. This one has a little muffler thing to help with gummy noises when you talk. I like the other mic a little bit better, but the difference is very minute. These pick up a bit more background humming if you have a fan or AC on. But again, it's a very slim difference. UPDATE May 2024:  I've had this pair since Feb 2021 and use them almost daily for hours at a time.  Last night, they decided to retire and stopped working.  This is no fault to the headphones, as I have logged over 3 years of use on a ps5 for both gaming and media.  So I have just placed an order for a new set.  I have had zero issues over the last 3 years, (they even recovered from the Destructo attack of my son almost 2 years), and could recommend them more. I am also increasing my rating to 5 stars because of how well they have treated me.  I am pleased to see they are still available and haven't been discontinued.  This is a no doubt must buy over any other model or brand. -- (Below is original review) I bought these in Feb 2021 initially as a headset mainly for steam but also to backup my PS4/5 Sony Golds (they aren't Pulse 3D), but I quickly moved to only using these for PS5. APPEARANCE: the camo is very slick and I cabinet them when I'm not playing so no clash with the PS5 blanco FIT:  I've got kind of a big head I guess, wear hats 7 1/4 and usually have glasses on when playing and the fit is pretty good.  They fit snug with good compression over you ears that cancels noise a bit better than the PS4/5 gold.  The cord plugs into the controller of course so I wouldn't want it any longer for sure. SOUND: you won't think you have Cowin or Beats on because the range doesn't compare but you won't notice.  I play almost daily and I am not disappointed whatsoever.  I also use them to watch movies/shows including Narcos, Loki, Mandolorian, Marvel, etc and the quality is not lost. VOICE SOUND: I've asked and have been told I sound clear and chat comes in clear. CONTROLS:  what's nice about this over the PS Gold is that the mic arm folds back flush with the head phones which mutes the mic.  In some games, the PS5 controller mute button will mute all audio instead of just the mic.  There's only one volume control, so no independent chat control.  Also, unlike the PS Gold headset, when this headset is plugged in, it doesn't auto-mute your sound system, so you'll have to manually turn it down to stop concurrent audio. DURABILITY:  the photo attached was taken June 2022, 16 months after purchase with semi-daily use.  I play and/or watch 5-7 nights a week for 2-4 hours a night, give or take and that's how they held up.  My prior PS4 Gold headset before my current one looked like chop suey in the same amount of time. PRICE:  a steal, plain and simple.  Look at the above to confirm.  I wouldn't buy any other headset if you're not going all out for a $100+ set. OVERALL:  I'm writing this review as I am perusing Amazon for a new headset to replace these due to the issue above, even though my PS Gold are in "perfect" working order, which says a lot. This is a game-changing investment that delivers professional results!

reviews.title: I love this Microphone! Love Shure
reviews.comment:
Review of the Shure MV7 Microphone
Introduction
Hey there! Today, we’re going to talk about a super cool microphone called the Shure MV7. Imagine having a magic wand that makes your voice sound amazing when you sing, talk, or record videos. The Shure MV7 is just like that! It helps you sound super clear and professional, just like your favorite singers and YouTubers.
What is the Shure MV7?
The Shure MV7 is a microphone that you can use to record your voice for singing, talking, or making videos. It’s really special because it can connect to both your computer and your phone. This means you can use it to make awesome recordings no matter what device you have!
Why is it Special?
1. Crystal Clear Sound: The MV7 makes your voice sound super clear and professional. It’s like having a recording studio right at home.
2. Easy to Use: Even though it’s very powerful, it’s really easy to use. You just plug it in, and you’re ready to start recording.
3. Adjustable Settings: The microphone has cool features that let you change how your voice sounds. You can make it sound deeper, brighter, or just the way you like it.
4. Built-in Headphone Jack: It has a place to plug in your headphones, so you can hear exactly how you sound while you’re recording. This helps you make sure your recordings are perfect.
5. Strong and Durable: The MV7 is built really well, so it can handle lots of use without breaking. It’s made to last!
How Does it Work?
Imagine you want to record a song or tell a story. You take the Shure MV7 and connect it to your computer or phone. Then, you start your recording app and begin speaking or singing. The microphone captures your voice and makes it sound super clear. You can even use the ShurePlus MOTIV app to change the settings and make your voice sound exactly how you want it.
What Do People Like About It?
People love the Shure MV7 because it makes their voices sound amazing and it’s really easy to use. Kids and adults both enjoy using it for singing, podcasting, and making videos. They also appreciate the adjustable settings that let them customize their sound.
Anything Not So Great?
The Shure MV7 is a little bigger and heavier than some other microphones, so you’ll need a stand or a place to put it while you use it. Also, it’s a bit more expensive, but it’s totally worth it because of how awesome it makes your recordings sound.
Conclusion
The Shure MV7 microphone is like a magic tool that makes your voice sound fantastic. It’s perfect for kids who love singing, storytelling, or making videos. It’s easy to use, super durable, and makes everything you record sound professional. If you want your voice to shine like a star, the Shure MV7 is the perfect microphone for you. So grab your computer or phone, plug in the MV7, and start creating your amazing recordings!

reviews.title: Excellent for Voice Recognition
reviews.comment:
Tried a number of different brands.
I use voice recognition with a system that calls out fields so you can keep your eyes on the main screen not the text screen.
Problem with a handheld microphone, speaker combo is either
1.  System reads the field, then TRANSCRIBES its own read
Or
2.  You program a delay so it doesn’t “listen” to itself.  This works but is unnatural and awkward to use.
I also need to be able to hear the people around me.
This gives me the best of all worlds.
It only covers one ear, so I can hear the voice cues but the microphone DOESN’T pick them up.
I can hear the people around me and talk to them easily as only one ear is covered.
The voice recognition pick up is as good as I’ve found anywhere.
It also links to my computer AND my phone.  The only problem (and maybe there is a fix) is it doesn’t pass through the messaging text cues, so I miss phone texts if I don’t keep an eye on the phone.
Battery life has been great, I work up to 11 hours and have not had any problems.
The single ear cover is very comfortable.  I may add some padding on the opposite head clip, but that should be easy.

reviews.title: Very good sound; not dependent on software; easy manual controls
reviews.comment:
This is probably the best USB microphone available. It sounds smooth and natural, and it does not require any software to be installed on the computer or iPad. You just plug it in to any computer or tablet or smart phone, and it is recognized as a microphone.
You simply adjust the dials on the microphone to get the right settings, and your headphones connect directly to the microphone so there is no delay in hearing yourself as you speak.
This is significantly better than many USB microphones that rely on software being installed in order to work correctly. Software is always buggy and unreliable. If you update the operating system on the computer or phone, you often lose functionality in this kind of third part audio software. Over time, if the manufacturer stops maintaining the software as happens frequently, your microphone becomes a paperweight.
The Sennheiser Profile microphone simply uses the universal USB audio standard built in to every computer, tablet, and smart phone. The microphone will work for decades into the future.
The sound is smooth and clear and professional. Other USB mics sound thin and tinny. This one does not suffer from that problem.
You can definitely get an even more refined sound from an XLR microphone and stand-alone microphone amplifier (if you know what you're doing), but this mic will sound better than 90% of the cheap USB mics that people are using all over social media.

Performance & Sound Quality Right out of the box, the NT1 delivers studio-grade clarity with an incredibly low noise floor. The warm, rich tone captures vocals beautifully, making it perfect for recording music, podcasts, and voiceovers. My son immediately noticed how crisp and detailed his voice sounded—no harshness, no distortion, just pure, natural audio. reviews.comment: Many people say that the shure sm7b would outrank any mic. Why not a Scarlett? Hmm. What a tough decision. The solution is here, folks! It’s a usb mic with AWESOME sound quality. If you are just on discord all day talking, a yeti mic will only do you good if you have enough ram (in certain context) for all you people out there that do not know what ram is. If you are just starting out in the music industry or you do gaming on a mid end pc, this is the way to go. Have tons of friends that use it that say all good things about it. reviews.comment: Pros: + Equally good sound to Blue Yeti for half the size + Volume knob and lighting looks cool and works well + Don't miss the extra sound settings as only ever used cardioid or full surround Cons: - Need the Blue Sherpa software to control the gain, but... - Installed the software (Windows 10, 64 bit) and it recognized the mic the first time and the controls worked, but after a re-boot, it would no longer recognize the mic ("Uh-oh!  It appears you don't have any devices connected...").  But the mic is still working, light is lit, but I can't control the gain without going several clicks deep into Windows setting.  Blue tech support was not helpful.  Followed all their instructions including uninstall/reinstall, installing Logitech's hub software also, and has never worked since.  Mic is still excellent sounding, but lack of control is a hassle.  I found several posts of others having this issue and no resolution.  YMMV. - REALLY MISS THE HARDWARE CONTROL GAIN KNOB ON THE BLUE YETI Overall I highly recommend, as it is at it's core an excellent quality microphone and delivers professional sounding recordings and webinar broadcasts.  Just know you may need to really play deep in Windows settings to tune it to your specs.
reviews.author: JLarkin555

reviews.title: Customize Your Sound
reviews.comment: A great mic for any purpose but I got Yeti Nano to improve my voice quality on conference calls (e.g. zoom, google meet, MS teams, webex, etc.) I have a windows desktop computer and added a video camera but was unhappy with first several headphone/mic combinations I tried.  Finally, the Yeti is a great mic option and I have stopped searching.  It has a headphone jack so you can eliminate any chance of feedback from unmatched devices. I'm using KZ ZS10 Pro earbuds plugged into the Yeti headphone jack. Back to the mic--definitely make sure you download the Blue Sherpa app search for it online. The app allows you to control the mic sound, such as gain, cardioid or omni pickup, headphone playback volume, but the coolest feature gives you complete control over sound filters and equalization. I was able to completely eliminate that sound many mics produce which I call "you sound like you are talking from the bottom of a can." (Solution set bass at -2dB, and set a high pass filter at 130 Hz.) Another problem solved with Yeti--conference call attendees would say my voice would breakup. This is just a hunch, but the app has a dedicated analog to digital (ADC) function and I think this means the computer doesn't use an unknown app with a low process priority that causes problems on conf calls, anyway my problem went away. One problem I had was a yellow blinking light on the Yeti; if this occurs you need to make a setting change on the computer.  Go to control panel; select "hardware and sound", click sound, a Yeti device will appear under both playback and recording lists. You need to make sure the sample rate setting under advanced properties, is the same for both playback and recording.  Change both sample rate settings to 48kHz or 44.1kHz and use the one that keeps the green LED light lit on Yeti.  One last note, on conference calls I have been able to use my desktop speakers (instead of headphones) with the Yeti mic and it doesn't seem to cause problems, but watch out for reverb problems.
