reviews.title: Nice and not too heavy
reviews.comment: Great microphone for podcast, very effective and easy to use. Noise canceling and get for the price.
reviews.author: Dee

reviews.title: Hardly any Background
reviews.comment: Loving it! First off I love the signature look and style that they use across their products. It's just frikking nice to look at! Setting it up was easy. Ready to go straight out of the box. I was concerned for a moment when I saw the USB-C to USB-C cord that it comes with. Luckily though I discovered that I do have such a port on my laptop. But hey that was a close one. This review could have gone differently. Also I have a Rode USB mic from a few years ago which I was able to remove the stand from and hook it onto my new PodMic. So that was really cool since the PodMic doesn't come with any kind of stand. Tested it out on my DAW of choice and it sounded really crisp yet warm. Immediately had that nice podcast feel. I played with it while creating a new default preset chain for it which was also telling about the sensitivity. Yeah being close up on it is beneficial but I didn't feel that it was as serious as some people make it seem in the reviews. Maybe it depends on what you're trying to use it for. As of right now I'm not intending to use it for a podcast. I'm making recordings with it. It really doesn't pick up a lot of background noise and even when I normalized the recording there was hardly any background, which is even more awesome for when I go to isolate it and remove it there will be less to detract from the original quality of the recording! Yes!!! Yeah so I'm really happy with it and though I don't remember exactly how my first USB mic performed a few years ago, I think this PODMIC does better even though it may be intended for something different than Rode's first USB mic.
reviews.author: Shaun McLaren

reviews.title: Terrible Mic and Company
reviews.comment: I did a bit of research and found good reviews for this mic. People said it was high quality and it looked like it was. I ordered the mic, mic stand and pop filter all through amazon together for just about $320. I was using a blue yeti before for years but finally needed to get a new mic. The mic came and I set it up on the stand no problem although the usb-c wire they sent didn't work at all. So I ended up having to purchase my own usb-c wire. I got ones that were usb-c to usb-c and usb-c to just normal usb. They all worked but another issues persisted. I had a bit of trouble trying to get it to function using the software and everything but eventually made it work. The sound quality was much better than my previous mic and everything seemed awesome for a few days. The issue I began to have was the mic would just stop working while I was gaming. The only way to fix this was to unplug the mic and plug it back in which is very inconvenient especially when it could happen every 2-5 minutes or just once an hour with no warning. I contacted RODE support about the issue and thus begun the month process of being gaslit by them claiming it was my problem. I needed to send photos and videos of the mic working and not working and trying it out on different devices and using different cables. In the end nothing worked and I ended up finally getting them to allow me to send it back to them but not for a refund because they refused to refund me anything as it's not bought directly from them. I had to spend another $20 to ship it back to them and then just wait. Eventually I heard back and they didn't tell me anything about the mic or any issues but rather said they will try to send me a replacement but they didn't have any in stock. So I would have to wait even longer. Pretty quickly they got one in stock luckily and then I was sent the replacement mic in the mail. I set it up last night and gave it a try. Just like before the wire doesn't work but mine do. The program even though I had it set up before gave me problems. And the big kicker is that it is having the same exact issue as before where the mic just stops working and I have to unplug and replug it for it to work again. I did some research and found others have had many issues with this specific mic and with RODE's AWFUL customer support system. I HIGHLY recommend avoiding this mic and any RODE products for that matter. I am about $340 in the hole for this purchase and they refuse to refund me a dime.
reviews.author: Jacob Chetwynd

reviews.title: Great Mic with Minor Cosmetic Issue
reviews.comment: I picked up this Rhode mic for my webinar meetings and overall I'm really happy with it. The sound quality is exactly what I was looking for and it's been working great for my needs. One thing I noticed when I first got it was that there were some white marks on the surface. I was a bit concerned at first thinking they might be scratches or permanent damage, but turns out they just wiped right off with a cloth. Not sure if it was from packaging or handling during shipping, but it wasn't a big deal since they came off easily. The mic itself performs really well and feels solid. Setup was straightforward and I haven't had any technical issues with it. The build quality seems good and it's been reliable so far. Would definitely recommend this mic - just don't worry if you see some white marks when you first unbox it. They're probably just surface residue that cleans off no problem.
reviews.author: Kate

reviews.title: Compact, Heavy-Duty Mic That Feels Pro Right Out of the Box
reviews.comment: Right out of the box, this mic feels solid and well-built. It’s surprisingly heavy for its size, which honestly makes it feel premium and durable — definitely not cheap plastic. The compact design is perfect for smaller setups or desks, and the magnetic base keeps it stable while recording. From what I’ve seen and read, the sound quality is clear and crisp thanks to the studio-grade condenser capsule. It’s made to pick up natural-sounding vocals with very low background noise, which makes it great for podcasting, streaming, or recording music. The USB-C cable it comes with is a decent length — long enough to reach from a desk setup to your computer without stretching or needing an extension. It also connects instantly with no extra software needed, which is super convenient. I haven’t recorded with it yet, but just based on the build quality and RØDE’s reputation, this feels like a professional-level mic made to last.
reviews.author: Marco espinoza

reviews.title: A tiny tank built for performance and quality
reviews.comment: The first thing that comes to mind when handling this microphone is its weight. This little guy is deceptively heavy. That's due to its all metal framework. I'll never try it, but it really does feel like that if I tossed the mic across the room it wouldn't receive even a tiny scratch. Really impressive build quality for the price. For just $100 I wasn't expecting very much in the way of sound quality but I can say that it makes my friends, all of which own Blue products and other overpriced microphones, quite jealous. The way this mic handles plosives is great. A built in pop filter adds some serious value to an already excellently valued product. The sound is also crystal clear. What you hear through audio monitoring is also what the mic output sounds like. No dips or hiccups when it comes to output. The one complaint I do have about the overall package is its desk stand. While the desk stand is somehow ALSO tanky as hell, along with bearing a magnetic mount, It's always better to invest in a microphone arm. There are plenty of cheap ones on amazon, but given the fact that this microphone is EXTREMELY sensitive, I recommend buying a quality microphone arm with some sort of shock mount or pad to dampen vibration as the desk moves. Also buyer beware: This microphone has only one polar pattern and lacks the multiple polar patterns that more expensive microphones have. That being said, this microphone was designed specifically for casual use, but delivers the cardioid polar pattern just as good as competing brands. If this is a deal breaker for you, I apologize. Otherwise, the RODE NT USB MINI is a fantastic low cost, highest quality option for people in the market for such a thing. Whether it be for studio recording, streaming, or just sweaty gaming. This little monster does it all better than the rest.
reviews.author: Matthew

reviews.title: One of the best small USB Mics you can buy
reviews.comment: Overall this a great little mic if you need some small for voice. Pros: Small size High quality nylon and aluminum construction Simple magnetic base Strong headphone amplifier built in, able to drive many headphones, including those with higher impedance like the MDR V6 at 53ohms Compact and portable Solid USB C connection with a quality, adequate length included cable Cons: Limited to 96khz.  People debate this, but 192khz does often sound a bit better to me, though it's not necessary. Somewhat high noise floor - the mic can sound a bit sizzly Included stand is very low, and easily picks up background noise.  Depending on your use case you'll almost definitely need to pick up a separate stand that brings the mic within 6 inches of your mouth to take advantage of the proximity effect.  You can get an aftermarket stand for not too much money, but frankly I'm not sure why they included such a short stand. Depending on your voice timbre, it can sound somewhat flat and 'robotlike'.  This is more a personal problem for since I have a very monotone voice. Different mics can make it sound better. Overall, for the money you really can't go wrong.  It's far better than any included headset mic, the headphone amp is very good, and it also sounds pretty decent for acoustic guitar.
reviews.author: Alex Corll

reviews.title: Very good quality (manufacturing wise)!!
reviews.comment: I use this microphone with my android phone for recording and streaming/performance acoustic instruments (piano, cello, violin). Though I use it everyday, I am a casual user. Cons: - The app/program to update the firmware. On my phone, it just kept turning the microphone on and off and eventually just stayed off. Same thing happened when connected to my laptop. Kept turning the device on and off but it eventually updated. Not quite sure what was happening. I used the included USB cable. Updating the firmware fixed some obvious bugs (e.g. light turning on inappropriatly). - The stock volume is very low. Using the app/program helped with this issue by allowing you to adjust the gain. - There's very few options for a case. -Since I use with my phone, I'd like a good phone and microphone mount but the microphone is so heafty...(which is a good thing). reviews.title: Good microphone and the best AI chatbot support I've encountered
reviews.comment: I don't normally give 5 star reviews but this goes beyond the product. RODE earned that 5th star. The microphone is certainly more sensitive than the MOVO VXR10 and the SmallRig Forevala S20, two very popular camera microphones on Amazon. The VideoMicro 2 performs much better than those 2 in quiet environments. Is it worth double the price? That's your decision to make but I am content with the $80 I spent for the VideoMicro 2. SmallRig's gimmick of including a lav mic and a way to connect it is nice. But a good lav mic can be had later on with a cheap Y adapter. The VideoMicro 2's deadcat and foam windsocks are quite a bit larger than the competition. But is almost necessary. I do not recommend running the microphone without these installed as the popping sounds from speech are very noticeable. The microphone mount is your standard cold shoe. If you own a camera such as the Sony ZV-E10 Mk1 or Mk2 you will need an adapter that slides into your smaller proprietary hotshoe. Another note about the mount. You will need a 3/8in to 1/4 in grub screw adapter. The mount uses the larger 3/8in screw and is not compatible with most consumer tripods and mounting equipment. What earned my 5th star despite some of these minor compromises is the website support. I had a simple question as to why there is a metal contact on top of the microphone. I've seen it on several of RODE's microphones. Now I don't support AI chat bots to fully replace humans but RODE's implementation of it was perfect. I had a question about the metal contact and the chat bot answered it. It's an alignment tool to ensure the microphone is oriented correctly in the mount. The inquiry was over in 2 minutes. THIS is how AI support should be done. Answer the simple questions and move to a human for anything more complicated.
reviews.author: Paul R.

reviews.title: Not bad...
reviews.comment: As a pro shooter I was looking for something smaller and more inline with professional shotgun microphones which basically just plug into your camera without all the software and infrequencer gimmickry. In general I usually use the Tascam DR-40X handheld recorder as my audio solution for my DSLR cameras. Even though it's mics are excellent and allows me to use my professional phantom power shotgun mics, it requires to be powered up and put in standby mode every time I start recording and needs to be reconfigured every time I want to use my phantom powered shotgun mics. The Rode Video Micro II shotgun mic eliminates these extra steps while also being lighter and much more compact, while still offering high quality acceptable audio. I am impressed with it's audio quality and when used with my Olympus OM1 its output level is ideal. It is very clean with a flat response curve without the booming bass I usually find with other mics in this price range. Another excellent feature is that it also includes a foam and dead cat wind screen. The dead cat is a must have for shooting outdoors. This micro condenser shotgun mic should be in every pro shooters kit. Plus it easy to use for family videos and casual shooting. This mic is now a fixture on all my DSLR cameras. Highly recommend.
reviews.author: Pro Video and Audio

reviews.title: Great mic but shock mount causes audible turbulence
reviews.comment: I use this mic on my Sony ZV-E10 every day. I also have the Rode NT-1 studio condenser mic, but my students say the VideoMicro II is clearer and so it's easier for them to hear my voice. I suspect this is due to it having strong response in the mids (where the voice resides) and less in the higher and lower ranges. (It's probably also better when played back on the students' laptop speakers or cheap earphones, which probably also lack highs and lows.) So, for this purpose, it works perfectly. However, it's not so good outdoors. Sometimes I record students outdoors for promotional videos. The included wind protection options are great, but after some testing I discovered that there is excessive wind noise when the wind comes from the side or back. This is due to the flat, ribbon-like shape of the shock mount. If you cover this area on the rear of the mic (and it would probably help to cover the cable too), you can blast it with powerful wind and it stays silent (as confirmed by my tests in a controlled environment). Recommended for indoor use only, or outdoors if you don't mind rigging up an extra cover for the shock mount to supplement the benefits of the fluffy wind shield. It's also highly directional, which is good if you want to somewhat isolate one speaker in a noisy location. I often mount it on a pole with a long cable and use it like a field reporter. Works perfectly and sounds great when you get closer to the interviewee (and without having to stick the camera right in their face).

reviews.title: Clean, Low‑Noise Performance for Any Recording Setup
reviews.comment: The RØDE NT1 Signature Series is an excellent studio mic for anyone who wants clean, detailed vocals without spending a fortune. It has that classic NT1 sound—smooth, neutral, and extremely low‑noise—making it great for voiceovers, streaming, singing, and instrument recording. The self‑noise is so low that recordings come out crisp and professional even in less‑than‑perfect rooms. Build quality is solid, and the included shock mount and pop filter feel like real upgrades rather than throw‑ins. The mic has a sturdy, premium feel, and setup is straightforward. It handles sibilance well and captures a natural tone that’s easy to mix. If you want a reliable large‑diaphragm condenser that delivers studio‑grade clarity and pairs well with almost any interface, the NT1 Signature Series is a fantastic choice.

Paired with a Scarlett Solo 3rd gen USB audio interface connected to my Mac laptop, using Garage Band to record vocal tracks. I recently upgraded to the Sennheiser Professional Profile USB Microphone Streaming Set with Boom Arm, and it has exceeded all my expectations. reviews.title: Awesone mic ser you may not need to upgrade
reviews.comment:
This microphone works great and the boom arm is a must have for many application. The boom arm is made extremely well and far surpasses any of the cheap secondary arms out there for the price difference between this package and the one without it.
If you want good quality, ease of use (plug it in and start using it, no software necessary). I had to use a USB-C to USB-A converter but that did not affect its functionality at all. Having all the necessary controls on the mic without having to go into any mic settings on the pc is also extremely friendly to use with no real sound transfer when using them. The mute button doesnt cause any noticeable clicks thru the mic either.
I ise this for several purposes but mostly for voice chat while gaming and proper positioning doesnt pick up keyboard clicks with a quieter mechanical keyboard.
On a side note it also pairs nicely with other specialized microphone software for much more control of its sound quality or style if you need that, such ss the SteelseriesGG. Doesnt quite have the sound quality of a Shure but the price difference for me doesnt justify paying so much more for the Shure. A true audiophile may think differently but for a good quality, feature rich mic with a boom arm that is easily worth $100 in itself, this is a great microphone set.
It can easily do everything you need for quality gaming and even podcasting for those starting out and not wanting to break the bank on a high end Shure. I’d look into a Shure later if your podcasting starts to make you money to justify it but until that point you may just live this Sennheiser for a long time, and it will certainly last you for as long as you want it to.

reviews.title: I've been using Sennheiser mics professionally for years, this one does NOT disapoint!
reviews.comment: As an audio engineer for 20+ years in the heyday of rock (80s-90s) I used Sennheiser in both the studio and live.  They have a reputation as being 'delicate', but I found with reasonable care, they did well for years on the road.  This mic was purchased for our podcast work and for the dozens of Zoom meetings I have each month.  It set up fast, worked immediately, and has continued to function flawlessly now for months.  It's a bit sensitive to 'body noise' so an isolation mount is really required (get on the stick here Sennheiser, I had to adapt an aftermarket mount.  You should have one available!!) and I used the AT2020 mount from Youshares, which works well.  Careful the mount you choose does not obstruct the knobs on the front of the mic, but otherwise any mount that accepts a 1.5" mic will work.  Great mic for voice, and the arm is pretty nifty too!

reviews.title: Exactly What I Needed for Precision Gaming
reviews.comment: I’ve been using the Logitech G440 for a few weeks now, and I have to say—it’s made a noticeable difference in my gaming setup. As someone who plays a lot of competitive shooters like Valorant and Apex, I needed something that offered low-friction movement without sacrificing control. This mouse pad nails it. Right out of the box, the hard surface feels durable and premium. It’s not your typical soft fabric pad; instead, it has a smooth polymer surface that lets my Logitech G Pro X Superlight glide effortlessly. Tracking is accurate, and I haven't noticed any stuttering or cursor jump, which is essential when aiming quickly or making micro-adjustments in-game. The rubber base keeps it firmly in place even during longer sessions or high-intensity moments, and it doesn’t curl at the edges like some of the cheaper pads I’ve used in the past. I was also pleasantly surprised by how easy it is to clean—just a quick wipe and it's good as new. One thing to keep in mind: if you're used to cloth pads, there is a learning curve with the speed and glide. But once you adjust, it’s hard to go back. Whether you’re gaming competitively or just want more precision in your daily mouse use, this is a solid, well-made pad that delivers on what it promises. Highly recommend for anyone looking to upgrade from a standard mouse pad.

reviews.title: Perfect for Local LLMs - 5060 Ti vs 3060 for AI Work
reviews.comment:
Got this PNY RTX 5060 Ti specifically to run local LLMs on my ThinkStation P520, and it's been exactly what I needed. At $491 for the renewed unit, it's a steal compared to overpriced RTX 3060s.
My Setup:
- Lenovo P520 with 64GB RAM
- Dual GPU: Existing GTX 1660 (6GB) + new RTX 5060 Ti (16GB)
- OLLAMA running in WSL2 on Windows 11
- Total VRAM: 22GB across both cards
Real-World Experience:
Since I already had the 1660 installed, driver setup was already done - literally plug-and-play. The only hiccup was the power connector location: it's at the far end of the card, opposite from the PSU, so I had to buy an 8-pin extension cable. Minor inconvenience, worth mentioning.
Performance for AI:
- 16GB GDDR7 is a massive upgrade over the 3060's 12GB of slower memory
- Local LLMs load and run smoothly
- Heavy-duty build quality, runs efficiently under sustained AI workloads
- Dual-fan cooling keeps temps in check during long training sessions
Why 5060 Ti over 3060?
I looked at RTX 3060s but they're overpriced for 12GB of slower VRAM. Also tried an AMD RX 9060 with 16GB - OLLAMA wouldn't even use it because Linux driver support is lacking. If you're comparing 3060 vs 5060 for LLMs, the 5060 is the clear winner: faster memory, more capacity, better long-term value.
Bottom Line:
Verified purchase, expert/professional user running daily AI workloads. Packaging was good, card arrived in excellent condition. For local LLM work, this is the sweet spot. Skip the 3060, grab this 5060 Ti.

reviews.title: They will ALL die. (Edit, faulty Asus board).
reviews.comment:
Edit: It is my Asus board. I was getting latency spikes and freezes when acceleration needed to happen in windows. I was also getting severe latency when more than 3 USB devices were plugged into the board.
I changed from my Asus z790 D4 Strix to my old trusty z690I Aorus Ultra Plus ddr4 and ALL the issues (other than degradation that already took place) are solved. This is not my first asus board that kills components with terrible vrm regulation. This will be my last Asus board.
Shoutout to Intel support. They are amazing to deal with. Literally one phone call, & 20mins later my rma was approved and a crosship approval also issued. Amazing. Seriously.
It doesn't make sense that both CPUs (new 13700k and 14900k) would die in literally like 2-3 months and have the same symothoms. It is not just ring that collapsed on the two new 13700k and 14900k. Its the memory controller from my observed behavior.  The first 13700k was oxidized which is why the entire chip died. I'll need to get my hands on a ddr5 board to test my theory. I'll make another edit when I do.
Original Review: All of them will eventually die, Ring collapse is something ive seen on three 13th-14th chips. First a 13700k, then another, and now a 14900k.
The first 13700k ran auto voltages and was delidded. It Ring collapsed due to voltage spikes on the old microcodes (I presume). My second 13700k (also delidded) collapsed for seemingly zero reason. It was ran at below 1.35v on adaptive voltages at all times on a static clock speed. My 14900k (which i left 100% stock with paste on my aio) collapsed on 1.25v set static (vid and vrm), with a voltage protection cap of 1320 in the uefi. 1.25v is core voltage.
1.35vddqtx
1.25v-1.35V (MAX) Vccsa
^ These voltages were ran on all of them. They all died.
No matter what you do, they will die. There is something SERIOUSLY wrong with this architecture. My 12900KS had ZERO issues with ring clock stability. I will likely ask for a refund and buy it once more. Ironic how things worked out.
Edit: When these CPUs work and are in a board that works properly. It is by FAR, the best experience I've ever had on a desktop. Monolithic architecture is something that you cannot beat. The instant feeling of everything you do. It just works, and it works amazingly. Thats why ive had 3 of them and keep gong back. Nothing else comes close. Specially when you go to windows 10 LTSC Iot with e cores off. Its a different world. Trust me.

reviews.title: Intel support is top tier awful
reviews.comment:
My Intel CPU failed in under a year. I never overclocked it. The system was running perfectly one day and completely dead the next.
I tried to troubleshoot myself for 5-6 hours, checking connections, removing and testing components, flashing BIOS, everything. No luck.
On day 3 I took it to Geek Squad at Best Buy. Cost: $100. The PC was there for 2 days. They called and confirmed the CPU was dead after testing with a known working CPU. At least now I knew the issue.
Day 5 - Best Buy Geek Squad calls and confirms the CPU was dead after testing the system with a known working CPU. At least now I knew the issue.
I called Intel Support. The number is a +44 UK line even though I live in the U.S. The call quality was awful, and the rep struggled to understand English. She seemed kind, oddly she ends up being the better part of this nightmare experience, but it took over 20 minutes just to get my name, email, and phone number entered correctly. Please, AI wizards, start replacing call centers with something functional. Begin with Intel’s.
While on the phone with support, I emailed the Intel support agent i was speaking with photos of the CPU, confirmed serial numbers, proof of purchase, and the full Geek Squad report from Best Buy verifying the CPU was defective and undamaged. You’d think that would be enough for a quick replacement, right? Nope.
Here’s how Intel handles support:
First, I was told they would send me a special return box that I’m required to pay $25 for, non-refundable, I think she said there was an option to upgrade to a faster delivery service that I could pay more for. just so I can ship their faulty CPU back to them. This has to be done before they even start sending out a replacement. I’m well within the 1-year warranty period, and it’s not exactly a secret that 14th-gen i9 chips have issues.
Second, before Intel ships me the new CPU, I have to pay the full price of a replacement CPU upfront “for Intel’s safety (support agent's actual words).” They said it would be refunded sometime after they verify things on their end. Apparently, a Geek Squad diagnosis, serial numbers, and proof of purchase aren’t enough verification for Intel.
So realistically, it’s going to take 2–3 days to get the return box, another 1–3 weeks (if I’m lucky) before getting a working CPU back, and a few hundred dollars out of pocket during the process. My money and time, customers money and time for Intel's product failure.
Wrapping it up
Intel CPU fails within warranty → customer spends hours troubleshooting → pays for a repair shop to confirm defect → pays Intel $25 (or more for faster time frame) to ship the bad unit back → pays again upfront for Intel’s “safety” → waits weeks for a replacement and refund.
Is there support from Intel hidden somewhere in this process I can't see? I'm actually involuntarily supporting Intel essentially.
So when your latest-gen Intel CPU dies, expect it to cost you around $800 total and a couple weeks of downtime. If I were a company with a high failure rate on a product and wanted to avoid replacing tons of them.. I wonder if i'd try making the process a nightmare and way more costly to the consumer to discourage that to save myself money.

reviews.title: Fantastic for gaming and productivity, but missing USB-C rechargeability
reviews.comment: I recently purchased the Razer Orochi V2, and overall, it is an amazing mouse. The build quality is absolutely fantastic, and it feels premium. It fits perfectly in my palm, and the materials and clicks have a very pleasant tactile feel. I use it daily for both gaming and work, and it performs flawlessly in both scenarios. Compared to my Razer Pro Click, the Orochi V2 actually fits my hand much better. In fact, I now only use the Pro Click as a backup for when the Orochi's battery suddenly dies! There is really only one downside for me: it runs on disposable batteries rather than having a built-in rechargeable one. On the plus side, it only needs a single battery to operate, and I love the clever design that allows you to use either a standard AA or a smaller AAA battery depending on your weight preference. However, I would really love to see a future version of this exact mouse with a built-in battery and a standard USB Type-C charging port. reviews.title: Amazing mouse even for big hands.
reviews.comment: So I have big hands and what any big hand gamer understands is that you either have to get a big ol heavy G502 size mouse or use a certain grip to hold all these mice for smaller handed people. I previously owned a Model O, G pro, and Model O wireless. Having big hands my biggest peeve with all the other mice is that they’re ambidextrous mice so they are even harder to hold with fingertip/claw grips because the smooth, near flat, symmetrical sides. I only really make contact with the sides by pinching my fingers with them. I never make contact with the butt or base of the mouse with my grip. There’s where the Orochi changes things The Orochi somehow is a smaller mouse than all of the above but fills out my hand and grip SO much better. The sides actually have slight grooves so I don’t slip off the sides of my mouse and the shorter but bigger hump in the middle makes me for once actually feel the mouse in my palm if I want. Overall the feel is amazing. Battery life varies of course but I can barely tell there’s a battery in the thing even when flicking and the weight and balance of it feel so good. Mobile gaming is the main reason I got this mouse. I like that the dongle stores inside the mouse, uses batteries so I don’t have to worry about keeping it charged or bringing around extra cables to charge it, and the Bluetooth is good for casual gaming but doesn’t do great with big flicks so the 2.4ghz connection is required for esports games. Overall a great mouse and really awesome to game with and a little plus to it is that the shell comes off the back so satisfying, it’s hard to not fidget with it by taking it on and off haha. Well worth the money and I’d expect they’ll make a rechargeable one with all the success this mouse has accrued so far so if the swappable batteries don’t tickle your pickle, I’d just buy a sub $20 rechargeable battery station or just wait for a new rechargeable Orochi to come out.

reviews.author: Thomas

reviews.title: Lightweight Fingertip Grip, But Double Click Issues
reviews.comment: First some context for how I use this mouse. I do about an hour of aim training every day, and then anywhere from 0-8 hours of FPS gaming per day. Average of probably 2 hours of gaming per day. I have a relaxed fingertip grip, my fingertips usually rest about 1/3 of the way down from the tip of the mouse. This means I usually end up clicking near the back part of the mouse buttons. I also have pretty small hands for my height. The first thing I noticed about this mouse is how dang light it is. It comes with a 15gram AA battery to use with it. There is also a slot for a AAA battery if you want, however that slot is farther back and makes the mouse feel less centered. You can buy adaptors (usually about 3 grams) to fit a AAA lithium battery (usually about 7 grams)  into the AA slot if you want, and this would shave about 5 grams off of the weight while still keeping it feeling balanced. I hadn't bought a new mouse for about 5 years, so my old G403 felt like a sack of potatoes compared to using this thing. The mouse skates are also great, nice and wide and completely pure white teflon. The second thing I noticed was the shape. It's obviously a small mouse, and I'm fine with that, but I found that I really disliked the taper on the back of the mouse. Since I have a gripstyle that sits pretty far back on the mouse, I really noticed the lack of control that my pinky now had - I had to curl my pinky in a bit. On my G403, there is a small hump back there that really helped my pinky contribute to my aim. Similarly, it felt like my thumb was contributing slightly less to my aim, although not quite to the same effect as my pinky. Everything mechanically felt great, clicks feel good and the thumb buttons feel good as well. I like the size of the thumb buttons, I wish more people made them "thin" like they are on the Orochi. I barely use the scroll wheel due to the nature of the games I play, so I can't speak to that part of the mouse. In my aim training, I noticed some immediate differences. Tracking was SOOOO much easier. My tracking scores in Kovaak's literally immediately jumped up. This isn't too surprising considering that the Orochi is about 50 grams lighter than my previous mouse was (G403). However, I also had an immediate dip in my static scores. There simply is no stopping power in this mouse, and I had grown used to my G403 having a bit of friction due to weight. This is something that I adapted to over time, and I eventually ended up beating my static high scores with the Orochi after a few weeks. The coating is not great. Or really just the lack of a coating. It's like a textured ABS plastic or something, it's certainly not the most slippery thing in the world, but I would often have to re-adjust my grip after about 15 seconds of very fast tracking that covers large swaths of area. There are grip pads you can use to help with this, but personally I'd rather deal with a mild amount of slipperiness than to put a stick-on grip pad onto my mouse. I found that my grip actually ended up changing mildly because of this, my ring finger ended up resting on the right "edge" of the mouse between the top and the side. This allowed it to have a "hard" edge to grab onto. The DPI button is nicely recessed, so I never had any issues with accidentally clicking it like I've had on other mice. It's still usable if you wanted to do a DPI shift mid game for certain games where that can be advantageous. Never had a single issue with connectivity, but I also keep my mouse dongle in a spot where it should have a great connection to the mouse. The battery life is kind of insane, after 3 months of almost constant use, it still has a nearly full battery. I never really used the mouse in Bluetooth mode, so I can't speak to how that functions. Now with all of the bases covered, time for the biggest issue I had with this mouse: double clicking. My index finger rests to the far right of the left click, almost touching the scroll wheel. After about 3 months of use, I noticed that while holding down left click during tracking scenarios, I would occasionally miss a "beat" of the left click being held down. I thought it was user error, but it kept happening once in a blue moon. The click would be held down, and there would be no mechanical feedback of the click being let go or "reclicked", but it would still blip out for a bit. Then, after a little bit of this, I started to have a much larger issue - I was getting the occasional double click. Again, I thought this might be user error, but there were a couple of situations that made it extremely obvious to me. One such scenario was in Overwatch, where I shot someone as Cassidy and then instantly started channeling my ultimate, but the ultimate instantly got "used" despite me not clicking again. I also noticed it while playing Bloons TD6, where I accidentally bought two upgrades instead of a single one for one of my towers. I started looking into it and used a "double click test" that I found online that shows the latency between clicks, and I found that I could somewhat consistently (about once every 10 tries) replicate the double click situation. You can see this in the picture that I have attached, where I am clicking about every 0.8 seconds, but once there is a second click at about .28 seconds. It seems to be something with the release of the click, like if I click but *EXTREMELY SLIGHTLY* ease the pressure mid-click, the click is still being held down mechanically, but the mouse almost seems to interpret that the click was quickly let go and then re-clicked. I haven't had any issues with the right click. I also didn't have the double-click issue for several months, or if I did it was rare enough that I never noticed it. TLDR: The mouse is extremely light, feels good, slightly awkward shape, is a little slippery, insane battery life, and works well, except mine had a double click issue. If yours doesn't have the same issue, then I would recommend it for fingertip or claw grip.

reviews.author: Ryan Boulds

reviews.title: Best all around gaming keyboard for the price with no weaknesses
reviews.comment:
This keyboard has everything you want for gaming. Only 0.7ms input lag on rtings which is really good. The new optical switches are really consistent and I love how I can switch the actuation point depending on if I'm gaming or typing. The choice between 3 levels of elevation is also nice.
For gaming, this is one of the best keyboards you can possibly get.  I'm a high-mmr CSGO player and I can tell you this delivers. Your counter-strafing and ability to stop on a dime is amazing. This keyboard can take as many inputs at once as you can press and doesn't have cord splitting or other artifacts. It's true 1000hz polling too.
You also have a good USB-C cord that's braided and detachable. You can also keep the tool under the keyboard if you travel to LANs or in general. It's perfect. You also have onboard memory and it's very easy to use the SteelSeries software to configure. It's easy to update firmware as well.
The build quality is very good too. They used aluminum in the body and the higher quality PBT keycaps. Also, if anything breaks, you can easily replace the keycaps OR the switches themselves and SteelSeries actively sells replacement parts unlike Logitech for example who only sells switches and not keycaps.
There's really nothing I can complain about. The only thing maybe is that some keyboards like the wooting have release triggered as soon as your key starts going back up. However the wooting has slightly more input lag on direct press and CSGO, Valorant, and most games honestly favor new inputs over releasing inputs anyway. Also some keyboards like the Corsair K65 have 8000hz polling rate which is insane.
However with that being said, the 8000hz polling and early release triggering from those competitors really aren't a big deal and have their own downsides - especially the 8000hz polling because it can actually take up some more cpu usage so I don't think it's necessarily efficient at the sub 1ms level.
Overall, I looked at all of the popular keyboards for gaming in this price range and this one was the best for the price for my setup. I didn't talk much about typing btw but I am a megaracer on typeracer.com and it feels very good to type on in the 1.5mm mode + 7deg incline. If you're looking for a gaming keyboard, look no further, this has literally everything with no downsides.

reviews.title: Perfect keyboard with some slight modifications
reviews.comment:
This is your end stage keyboard. Every review says it is heavy but to put it in perspective, this keyboard without switches and caps weighs exactly 4lbs. My personal build included Gazzew and Boba U4T Thocky tactile switches (v2 black at 68g) and MOA style keycaps.
The good: They keyboard is solid and heavy. It has the full spectrum of connection options and the battery seems to last as long as my other Keychron keyboard. Make sure when buying caps, you buy a set that supports 110 keys. While I don't use them, the RGB function and customization seems incredible. The online app for configuring works well without needing a thick client to install. The sound combined with my switches is exactly what I was looking for. A USB-C cable is also included and the connection is at the top of the unit unlike other Keychron boards where it is on the side. For my other board, it was really hard to find a usb-c coil cable with a right angle on just the one side.
Opportunities: I only have 2 areas I would like to see improved (hence the 4 stars). First, others have mentioned it, but either the switch plate or the supports for the plate are not up to the standards as the rest of the keyboard. I noticed this mostly around the top left near QWERT. It flexes too much when inserting the switches. However, I don't notice this when typing and gaming (WASD is fine). The second is the complete lack of feet and ability to raise the board. It is too flat by default. I resolved this by finding a model on printables and then remixing it to the exact height that I prefer. I then had to mount these to the keyboard by removing the existing m3 screws and replacing them with longer ones. This is the biggest hangup for me. For a keyboard that costs more than $200, adding feet to the bottom shouldn't require custom cad work and a 3dprinter. Don't let these opportunies dissuade you from getting the keyboard, they are merely recommendations for the next version of it.
reviews.author: Chris Martin

reviews.title: Expensive and heavy. but worth it
reviews.comment: This is my fourth Keychron keyboard, having previously purchased and used a K5 Pro, a Q6 Pro and a V6 Max. I installed Gazzew Boba U4 silent tactile switches and Keychron OSA keycaps, which added another $120 to the total cost, but I have been extremely happy with the overall feel after having used it daily for the past several weeks. It is a very heavy keyboard, weighing in at close to 5 pounds, but the weight provides a solid feel and sound when typing. The VIA website (caniusevia.com) does require a Chromium-based Windows browser (e.g., Chrome or Edge) to remap the keys, but it is straightforward enough to do once you download the keymap JSON file from the Q6 Max product page on the Keychron website.
reviews.author: ChrisW

reviews.title: Sleek, Responsive, and Wireless - A Gamers' Dream Keyboard
reviews.comment: When I had the opportunity to use the Logitech G915 TKL, I was eager to see how it held up as a wireless mechanical gaming keyboard. Its tenkeyless design and advanced features promised a premium experience, and it didn’t disappoint. Pros: ✅ Low Profile Switches: The linear switches provide a smooth, quiet typing experience with fast actuation, perfect for gaming and productivity. ✅ Wireless Performance: The Lightspeed wireless technology ensures ultra-fast and stable connections, rivaling wired setups. ✅ Dual Connectivity: Seamlessly switch between Lightspeed wireless and Bluetooth, making it versatile for gaming and multi-device use. ✅ Battery Life: Exceptional battery life of up to 40 hours on a single charge with RGB lighting enabled. ✅ LIGHTSYNC RGB: Fully customizable RGB lighting that syncs with your games and other Logitech devices for immersive effects. ✅ Build Quality: The brushed aluminum frame feels solid and durable, with a sleek and modern design. ✅ Compact Design: The tenkeyless layout saves space on the desk, allowing for better mouse movement during gaming. Cons: ❌ Price (Renewed): Even as a renewed product, it remains a premium-priced option, but its quality and features justify the cost. ❌ No Wrist Rest: A wrist rest would have been a welcome addition for extended gaming or typing sessions. Performance and Usability: The G915 TKL impressed me with its seamless performance. Whether gaming or typing, the low-profile linear switches delivered a responsive and comfortable experience. Switching between wireless and Bluetooth modes was intuitive, and the battery life exceeded my expectations, lasting over a week of moderate use. During a gaming session, the compact design proved advantageous, offering more desk space for mouse movements. The customizable LIGHTSYNC RGB lighting added a touch of personalization, syncing perfectly with the game environment for an immersive experience. Comparison: Compared to other mechanical keyboards in its class, the Logitech G915 TKL stands out for its advanced wireless technology and sleek, low-profile design. While it lacks some features like a wrist rest, its performance and aesthetic make it a top choice for gamers and professionals alike. Who Is This For? This keyboard is ideal for gamers who value responsiveness, portability, and wireless functionality. It’s also great for professionals looking for a high-quality mechanical keyboard that blends performance with style. Conclusion: Overall, the Logitech G915 TKL Tenkeyless Gaming Keyboard is a fantastic investment for those seeking a premium wireless mechanical keyboard. Its performance, design, and customization options make it an excellent choice for gaming and productivity. Highly recommended for those who want the best of both worlds—compactness and functionality.
reviews.author: Ghost2401

reviews.title: As a renewed product, there is no sign at all of being used. Great keyboard also.
reviews.comment: The box it came in was just a little scuffed on the outside. I do not care at all about that. The keyboard itself has literally no sign of wear on it at all, and if functions perfectly. This was a great way to save ~$60. The keyboard's linear keys have just a little bit of a squishy feel (I got the linear version). Not quite on par with other linear mechanical keyboards I've used, but it could possible be because of the short travel distance. The latency is perfect... very very low. The keyboard is slim, and very sturdy. There's no flex. The RGB stuff was easy to turn off, which is what I do any time I get an RGB item. So I can't really review all the colors and stuff- but I'm happy that it was easy to turn off! The volume scroller works great, very sturdy and smooth. Overall, it takes up little space on my desk, with no wire, and basically no latency. Really improves the aesthetic, and maintains a great typing experience. I recommend this keyboard, new or renewed... the renewed version works great.

reviews.title: This is a fine, solid keyboard for a former typist/word processor operator, back in the 1980s.
reviews.comment: I offer my keyboarding experience as a reference point, and not at all as a criticism.  I learned typewriting in high school, which would have been about 1975, just when electric typewriters began to outnumber mechanical typewriters in business and, increasingly, home office settings.  I learned to type on a mechanical machine, then graduated to an electric portable, which served me through college.  Also a pianist, I had very good finger agility and was able to impress all sorts of people with my typing speed.  Fast forward, if you will, to the 21st century, where key location, keystroke tactility, and ergonomics seem to have been mostly tossed out the window in favor of cheap, short-lived, low-quality goods, especially in the field of electronics.  After many keyboard experiences, all of which have sought the perfect balance between the certainty of the mechanical experience and the sensitivity of the high-end keyboards, I cannot say that I've found the perfect mate to my fingertips.  I can say that this keyboard has, over a course of two years, proven to be solid.  I type a great deal, as an amateur writer and poor correspondent, and this keyboard has not flagged or quavered.  I enjoy the backlighting for typing at night while my lover sleeps, and the backlighting effects are fun.  It is quiet enough, confirming enough at the bottom of the keystroke, and quick enough (at least for my fingers, now aging and stiff at 64 yoa, lol).  So I am no longer the fastest typist I know:  this keyboard helps me feel plenty competitive.  I recommend.

Being able to customize the lighting effects to match my mood or game aesthetic is just fantastic. The build quality is top-notch, and the TKL design saves valuable desk space without sacrificing functionality. Overall, I couldn't be happier with this purchase. If you're in the market for a high-performance wireless gaming keyboard, look no further than the Logitech G915 TKL!

The LIGHTSYNC RGB lighting gives it a nice premium look without being too flashy, and the 48 kHz boom mic picks up my voice clearly with zero background noise complaints from friends.

The Logitech G Astro A20 X Lightspeed Wireless Gaming Headset blew me away from the moment I unboxed it. The sound quality is crisp, balanced, and super immersive — I can hear every little detail whether I’m gaming, watching movies, or listening to music. What really sets this headset apart is the 2-System PLAYSYNC Audio feature. I love being able to seamlessly switch between my PS5, Xbox, and PC without constantly unplugging or repairing. It’s a total game changer for anyone who uses multiple consoles.
The Bluetooth connection is smooth and convenient, and the LIGHTSYNC RGB lighting gives it that sleek, modern gaming look. The headset itself is lightweight and super comfortable — perfect for long gaming sessions without any ear fatigue.
Battery life is impressive too. I can go hours and hours before needing a recharge. Overall, Logitech really nailed it with this one — premium sound, comfort, and connectivity all in one. Highly recommend to any gamer who wants performance and style in one headset!

The headphones are good. They fit well on the head and are not heavy. The ear cushions are fabric and very soft. Switching between PC (2.4GHz) and phone (Bluetooth) happens instantly with the press of a single button. The sound and recording quality are very good for a wireless headset. The battery holds a charge for a very long time. The application has many settings for the microphone and equalizer.
But there are also downsides: a button on the case for pausing playback is sorely lacking. If you're listening to or watching something away from the computer, you have to run to it to pause it.
Also, the volume balance rocker for games/calls is very annoying: it's easy to accidentally press it.
In short, the headphones are excellent, but not at full price. It's better to wait for a sale or buy them used.

I have not used them for entertainment, so I can't offer an opinion in that respect. For daily use at work, however, they are without compare
reviews.author: Average Consumer insight

reviews.title: The perfect web conference headset!
reviews.comment:
I have just finished testing my new Sennheiser SC 60s, the sixth headset I have purchased in two years, and (at least on day one) they are far and away the best I've ever purchased for under $40. Specifically:
* In music playback, they have a subjectively full-frequency response (caveat, this was not evaluated with equipment and, like everyone over 25 I do not have full-frequency hearing).
* Sound isolation is moderate, as expected from on-ear rather than over-ear headphones. I wouldn't use these for high-fidelity music reproduction.
* Voice recording quality, when mic boom is positioned just outside outer corner of the mouth, was excellent both for recording and over a JoinMe web conference.
* Microphone noise cancellation is outstanding. During playback of a voice recording made three feet away from a fan, voice was clear, but close listening was necessary to hear the sound of the fan. Recording while one foot from the fan, with wind noise plainly audible during the recording, was reduced at playback to just a mild and undistracting sound audible behind the clear voice.
* Microphone directionality permitted loud typing away on a noisy keyboard to be only barely audible behind a clear voice during playback.
* Comfort is good. These headphones sit gently on the ear, but I would not want to wear them all day.
* Compatibility: Headset was instantly recognized by Windows 10 computer; no other platform tested.
Caveat: While these are the best headphones I have ever used for web conferencing, I don't know how long these qualities will hold up over time. I plan to update this evaluation in a year.
Hello all, this is me 5 years later (apologies if you've been waiting the previous 4 years for my follow-up ;). The reviewed Sennheisers lasted 4 years before almost daily use caused the wire casing to fray just below the ear cups. They still worked perfectly, but I replaced them since a reliable headset is vital in my work. This set is just as good as the last, and I have recommended them to many clients in online teaching. To be honest—but please don't share this with Sennheiser—they'd probably be the best you could buy at US$80. The fact that they are only $40 is quite remarkable.

reviews.title: This is the perfect conference call headset-and I've tried a lot of them
reviews.comment:
I bought my first pair of Sennheisers about 5 years ago. The quality is so good I also record a podcast on it. I am on Zoom as the CEO of a services company some 6-8 hours a day-both before and during the pandemic.
I have since issued these headphones to anyone in my company who needs a pair.  They're phenomenal. And it's not just "good for the price" -- recently the foam earpads got just so worn out I set out to see if I could "upgrade."
I tried every one of Wirecutter's picks and none of them had the mic quality this one does for the price.  It absolutely kills background noise (all but the worst of it). Think gas powered lawn mowers, dryers, etc.  the boom is adjustable too. I wear glasses and the headset doesn't hurt my ears after being worn for hours.  I've also really abused these things, thrown them in backpacks for travel without a case, and they just keep going.  if Sennheiser wold just sell me some foam ear pads I'd probably just replace those.  This thing is THAT good.
I tried headsets that cost 10x what this costs--and the mic quality was nowhere as good.  Those other headsets also don't let you wear the mic on the left side if you wish, nor do they have a cord that's as long as this one, with an inline control.  I like being able to mute with a button on the line vs fiddling with my headset on a video call. It's distracting to people.
On top of it, I don't look like an air traffic controller because the ear pieces are not large. Even music from my laptop sounds just fine.
I really did try to replace these with something "better"- but in the end, I couldn't do it. I tried to spend a lot more money but nothing was as good as these.
It almost never happens anymore that you get a great product at such a great price.  Thanks, Sennheiser!
I don't know how they can do this for the price, but I'm glad they can.

reviews.title: IMO better than Corsair RGB XT
reviews.comment: I used a Corsair RGB wireless XT gaming headset with the "broadcaster quality mic" for more than a year. I finally pitched them due to the problems I had with the quality of the sound, and even replaced the mic due to the mute button (on the mic piece) wearing out after a number of uses. It was just a high maintenance device with very short range issues as well as the iCUE app constantly crashing and losing my settings. The Corsair also had music listening issues where a deep drum or bass note would cause the master volume to compensate and was quite unnatural. I assume the volume would pulsate due to some kind of overload protection algorithm that I was unable to simply disable. It was quite annoying. Knew about the JBL reputation with stereo systems, and high quality HiFi systems in the passed, and decided to give them a try. They were also cheaper than the Corsair XT I had. Installed the driver program, turned on the "DTS" mode with the JBL Quantum surround mode and the sound BLEW ME AWAY! I NEVER had this kind of sound quality with the Corsair when listening to music. The bass is plentiful, and the equalizer works great all around. That's a positive. A negative I have is related to things like the "surround sound" mode. I don't get a true sound that makes me think there are things behind me, or directional like you get in a movie theater. Could be I really don't have a proper source to prove it out, but the windows positioning test isn't surrounding me like expected. When I'm gaming, I sometimes have a wide variety of sound sources that I mix into my headset. I have three separate PC's that sound outputs/inputs are "daisy chained" to allow me to monitor all the pc's outputs within my single headset. It allows me to do things like watch TV, game, monitor chat apps, listen to the radio, and a few other esoteric functions related to other hobbies all at the same time. So, I'm generally dealing with up to 5 separate PC monitors, and all the audio feeds from what ever I may have going on. The JBL seems to deal with them just fine without losing music quality, the gaming output, and others, simultaneously. Definitely a positive. I use the 2GHz dongle on a USB port, and even though we have a house full of wifi and wireless devices, the range is CONSIDERABLY farther than the corsair RGB XT. The corsair also would "cut out" when someone would use the microwave in the kitchen (which is attached to the room I'm in). Interestingly, the JBL headset does NOT cut out with microwave use, which again, is another positive here. I've seen folks complain that they don't get enough volume out of this headset, but that is not my experience. I'm retired with "older ears", and the volume is more than I would ever safely use. So, definitely a positive. The "noise canceling" is pretty good. Its not "get on an airplane and not hear white noise" good, but for gaming and listening to music, its quite good. The headset does claim to have ANC (Active Noise Canceling). Anyway, for the price, its better, IMO, than the high end corsair headset, yet less expensive. In my opinion JBL has a very high quality product that is very forgiving of an RF crowded environment, and a longer battery life. Just turn off the pretty flashy RGB lighting on the headset, and you'll get a ton of battery time. Specs claim you get 43 hours of battery time between charges. That's considerably better than the high end corsair.
reviews.author: Mark Wardell

reviews.title: Great headset option
reviews.comment: Overall, I'm very happy with this purchase. JBL is a brand that I generally trust when it comes to audio. The noise canceling function is okay. It isn't the best that I've used, nor is it the worst. Gave that aspect 3 stars because it is middle-of-the-road. The sound quality is good and the ear pieces are comfortable, though they don't breathe very well. I primarily use these for meetings on Microsoft Teams. I find myself moving them off one ear if I'm 3 hours into back-to-back meetings. I believe the auto-shutoff is around 4 hours, as I've had them turn off mid-meeting before. I really like the dual mute option. There is a button, or you can flip up the microphone. The microphone could use a little more resistance in movement. I sneezed once and the mic fell back down to the "on" position. No one heard the sneeze, so not a big deal. I was just surprised that it didn't stay up. All-in-all, the mic stays where you put it (unless you have a violent sneeze). My biggest complaint might be more with Teams than the headset, but I'm not sure. The headset has to be powered on BEFORE I join a meeting. If they aren't on and connected prior to joining, no one can hear me. I have to switch to the computer mic and then back to the headset. A minor inconvenience. My last headset could be switched on while connecting to the meeting and it worked every time. The noise canceling mic works amazingly. By comparison, my last headset seemed to pic up ambient noise and amplify it. They were great if the room was quiet, but anyone else talking sounded like they were in the conversation. These do what they say! Ambient noise does not seem to be picked up. I've had kids playing and or talking loudly in the same room and people on calls do not hear them. To reiterate, that's kind of amazing! Battery life is adequate. I get about 2 days use on a charge. That's pretty good considering. On that note, I read that the cheaper JBL headset could not be used while charging. That's just dumb. These advertised that you can charge and use at the same time. A surprise feature that I LOVE is the dual audio source. I connected them to my phone via Bluetooth to test them out before connecting to my work computer via the wireless USB dongle. While on a meeting (and still connected to my phone) I heard my text notification from my phone while still on the call at work! You can even listen to music while people are going on about boring work stuff and never miss a beat (get it?)! I have not installed the software that is loaded on the USB dongle, so I don't know what customizations can be made. Another thing that I'm still figuring out is the various audio level adjusters. I believe one is for mic and the other for incoming audio. Sometimes someone on a call will sound faint and I just roll one or the other until I get them to the proper volume. It's a nice feature, but I haven't fully figured out which adjuster controls which audio level. It's really good if you have someone who talks too loud... you can turn them down on the fly. In summary, they are great headsets! There are a few quirks, but those are easy to work around. The pros far outweigh any cons.

reviews.title: Great Sound with Minor Inconveniences
reviews.comment: I've liked this headset a lot since I've owned them - I would even say I loved it at first. However, after extended use I've noticed some of its flaws. Starting with the pros, this headset is so comfortable. I always prefer over-ear headphones or headsets for comfort and these just melt away when you put them on to where you may even forget you're wearing them. They're lightweight for a headset of their size and can be adjusted in size, too. The sound quality is fantastic. I love my JBL Charge 3 for its strong low pass and this headset is no different. Any input of media sounds quality through these: Games, YouTube, Netflix, etc. The USB wireless connector is a blessing for keeping a stable connection but you can use them for wireless Bluetooth as well. Now for the cons. The microphone stopped working within a few months. I understand that it isn't the priority on a headset like this but after what I would consider light-moderate usage it failed on me. First it just produced a loud static whenever I would try to talk into it before just stopping outright. This isn't a big deal for me since I mainly use my primary microphone, but it would've been nice to keep chatting with my friends when I get up to make dinner, for example. A much bigger issue for me personally is the auto turn off function. I'm not sure why, but after what I would say was 6 months of owning these, they just started turning off randomly. After some research, I found out this is to save battery in case you leave the headset running on accident, which is a great feature! However, as I said about 6 months into owning these it started doing this in the middle of me using them. Whether it be playing a game or talking in a call, they would just turn off in the middle of audio input. I'm no tech wiz, so I couldn't fully diagnose the issue, but my guess is that some kind of audio sensor broke in my headset. Research online was of no help so as of today it's still an issue. Overall, the headset is still quality and works for what it does, but with my issues I've had with it overtime I can't recommend it with 5 stars. It's worth noting I purchased this when it was 50% off ($100). I don't know if I would recommend it very highly at full price but if you get the same discount I had it's a pretty great deal.
reviews.author: Alexander

reviews.title: Well worth the price
reviews.comment: I have had this headset for 2 years now and have no issues with them. When I first got them, there were intermittent connection issues with the dongle, then JBL released firmware updates and ever since then, I had no issues. The audio is nice and clear, the same when I use the 3.5mm jack with a good headphone amp. I can walk 1/2 my house without issue. Bluetooth has been rock solid. I love that I can play and talk at the same time, something I can't do my other over priced headsets. The noise cancelling is good for what it is, it keeps me focused and immersed in the game without loss of audio quality. Spatial cues are accurate and clear. The LED's are neat, but I mostly leave them off, you can't see them when wearing the headset anyways. Battery life is awesome. I can game for 8hrs and have more than 60% battery remaining, even after 2yrs. of use. Durability has not been a problem as I take really good care of all my headsets, but the quality is there. I also have a hard case that I store them in when not in use or travelling. The microphone is clear and natural enough for me,  and has worked without issues. The only thing I would say that could be improved on is the volume. Even at max, I find myself doubting that I have everything setup properly. Overall, I say that with this headset, it is money well spent. I tried to replicate many of the issues that many others have stated: using them on other computers, such as friends and family's, in there homes just to ensure the dynamics, and they continue to work flawless. So much so that my peeps eventually purchased the headset. I also purchased the 910x model with the same satisfaction. Keep in mind, there is no perfect headset, just find what works for you, and this headset works really well for me.

reviews.title: Excellent mic for the price with impressive range
reviews.comment: I picked up the HyperX SoloCast 2 mainly because of the price, and honestly, it ended up exceeding my expectations. It’s noticeably cheaper on Amazon than at most other retailers, which already made it feel like a good deal before even plugging it in. Sound quality is where this mic really shines. You can be surprisingly far away from it and still be heard clearly. I tested this from across the room, easily 25 to 30 feet away, and my voice still came through without cutting out or sounding distant. That alone makes it great for casual gaming, voice chats, or even quick recordings without needing to sit directly in front of it the entire time. That said, the sensitivity is both a pro and a con. While it picks up your voice extremely well, it also picks up everything else. Even with noise suppression enabled in something like a Discord voice channel, background sounds are still noticeable. If you’re in a shared space or have a lot of ambient noise, that’s something to be aware of. It’s not a deal breaker for me, but it’s worth mentioning. Build wise, it feels solid and well thought out. The cord is very long, around 3 feet to the computer, which gives you plenty of flexibility for desk setup. It also comes ready to be mounted to a boom arm if you want to go that route, which is a nice option at this price point. I also like that you can angle the mic instead of it being locked in one straight position. One of my favorite features is the tap to mute function. Tapping the top of the mic to mute is super convenient and works exactly as expected, which is great during gaming or calls when you need to quickly mute yourself. Shipping was fast too. It arrived within about 2 days of ordering, which was a nice bonus. Overall, this is an excellent USB mic for the price. It sounds great, has useful features, and feels well built. As long as you’re aware that it’s very sensitive to background noise, it’s an easy 5 star recommendation, especially for gaming or everyday voice use.

reviews.title: Clean Sound on a Budget – Just Add a Boom Arm
reviews.comment: I bought the HyperX SoloCast 2 because my headset mic was making me sound like I was in a tunnel during work calls and game chat. I travel a lot for business and sometimes record quick voiceovers in hotel rooms, so I wanted a compact USB mic that’s plug-and-play, doesn’t need an audio interface, and has a mute button I can hit fast. I used to live in Florida, now I’m in Delaware, and between Zoom meetings and Discord with friends, I needed something that makes my voice clear without a lot of setup. My expectation: decent 24-bit/96kHz audio, simple controls, and it shouldn’t pick up my whole house. What you get & first impressions It’s a small black cylinder with a built-in stand that tilts, USB-C port, and a tap-to-mute button on top with a red LED. Comes with a USB-C to USB-A cable. It’s light, around 365g, and the base feels stable enough for a desk. The mic has an internal pop filter and shock mount, plus a threaded bottom if you want to put it on a boom arm later. Pros – what works for me Voice quality is good for the price: My voice comes through full and rounded, not thin like most headset mics. It records at 24-bit / 96kHz and sounds “clear and present”. Teammates noticed the upgrade right away in Discord. For casual streaming, calls, and quick voiceovers, it’s more than enough. Plug and play, no hassle: Windows picked it up immediately. No drivers, no mandatory software. The mute button is responsive and the red light makes it obvious when you’re live. That’s handy mid-call. Compact and portable: It’s smaller than a soda can and USB powered, so it fits in my backpack when I travel. The built-in stand tilts, which helps aim it without a separate mount. You can also unscrew it and put it on a boom arm. Internal pop filter helps: Plosives are reduced compared to a naked mic, though not eliminated. You can get close for a “radio” sound without every P popping. Value for money: At around $59.99 MSRP, it’s priced like a budget mic but sounds closer to mid-range options. Reviewers call it “relatively cheap, well-made” and “strong value for beginners”. Cons – where it falls short Picks up background noise: This is a sensitive condenser. It hears my keyboard, PC fans, and even the fridge in the other room if I don’t control the space. One user said “it picks up everything, and I mean everything”. The internal shock mount and pop filter are “on the weaker side”, so desk taps and plosives still get through. Stand is low and basic: The tilt helps, but it’s still too low for ideal mic placement. You’ll be looking down to talk into it. For best sound, you want it on a boom arm 6-8 inches from your mouth. Most reviewers say “we definitely recommend mounting this mic on a boom arm”. No onboard gain knob: You have to adjust gain in Windows or Ngenuity Beta software. The software gives EQ and noise reduction, but it’s still in beta and caps output at 48kHz if you use effects. Red light means on, not muted: Counterintuitive for some – red LED = live, not muted. I got used to it, but it confused me at first. Practical uses I use it for Teams/Zoom calls, Discord, light YouTube voiceover, and recording notes. It’s much better than a laptop or headset mic. For travel, it’s easy – one cable, small footprint. It won’t replace an XLR setup for pro music or podcasting, but for gaming, streaming, and office work it’s solid. If you have a mechanical keyboard, either use software noise reduction or get the mic off the desk. Did it meet expectations? Yes, with one condition. I expected clear, simple USB audio for calls and gaming, and it delivers that. I didn’t expect studio-level isolation. The background noise pickup was expected for a condenser, so I planned to use a boom arm and Nvidia Broadcast. Once I did that, voice-to-noise ratio was fine. If you think the built-in stand and pop filter will solve everything, you’ll be disappointed. Value for money For around $60, you get clean 24-bit audio, USB-C, mute button, and a usable stand. That’s fair. You’ll likely spend another $15-$30 on a boom arm to get the best out of it, so factor that in. Compared to headset mics it’s a big step up. Compared to a $150 XLR setup, it’s not, but it doesn’t pretend to be.

reviews.title: Not the best looking, but very sturdy and easy-to-use
reviews.comment:
This is a review for Shure by Gator Deluxe Articulating Desktop Podcasting Mic Boom Arm with Cable Management Channel; (SH-BROADCAST1).
The boom arm is very sturdy and relatively smooth. It does make a tiny bit of noise when spinning. It’s metal construction and feels premium. The tension rods, which control how easy it is to adjust, are easy to both loosen and tighten. There is a tension mount that is large enough to fit most desks and is relatively easy to tighten.
I am not a fan of the fact that there’s an extra piece to fit the SM7B microphone. This arm is built for Shure - it should fit their microphones. The reason for the extra piece is so that your XLR cable can be plugged in. Otherwise, it hits one of the adjustable caps. The extra piece looks long and silly in my opinion. The Shure lettering also is a bit tacky for such a premium mount. The XLR cable channel is nice but a bit of a pain to manage. I had to squeeze the cable fasteners tight enough to pull them out, then use two fingers to open the fastener to get my cable through it. It was ultimately a 5+ minute job. That’s too long for a 4ft cable run, but at least it works.
Overall, I’m happy with the sturdiness of the product and ease of adjustability. Setting it up was easy besides routing the cable, which you shouldn’t have to do often. My main concern is appearance. The bold Shure logo and long piece to fit the SM7B doesn’t look very good in my opinion.

reviews.title: Excellent Mic Arm: Built to Last, Holds Heavy Mics Like a Champ
reviews.comment:
I've been using the InnoGear Mic Boom Arm for over a year now with a Shure SM7B mounted on it, and it's proven to be rock solid. This arm delivers exactly what you need from a professional mic stand.
The build quality is exceptional. The joints are tight, the spring tension is consistent, and there's zero wobbling even with the weight of the SM7B hanging off it. The SM7B is no lightweight, but this arm handles it effortlessly without drooping or drifting. That's the kind of stability you need for recording and streaming.
After a year of daily use, everything still feels as solid as day one. No springs weakening, no joints loosening, no creep over time. The cable management clips work as intended, keeping my XLR cable organized and out of the way. The mounting clamp is rock solid and doesn't slip on my desk.
Installation was straightforward, and compatibility with the Shure SM7B was perfect. The adjustability is smooth—you can position the mic exactly where you need it without fighting the arm. Once positioned, it stays put. No readjustment needed mid-session.
For anyone running a streaming setup, podcast, or recording studio with a quality microphone like the SM7B, this is a no-brainer purchase. It's affordable, built tough, and will last you years. Highly recommended.

The white finish is cheap. It's clear that this is some white powder-coating paint overtop the original, black product. The material is not smooth, instead noticeably bumpy to the sight and touch. Material-wise, this mic-arm is at-best described as "okay"... At least, nothing is flimsy.
The mic-arm is able to hold up my Rode PodMic with no issues. I say this because, the Rode PodMic is ~937 grams (2 lbs.) in weight. Most mics- especially your average USB Condensor mic- are much lighter. As well, the arms have smooth and functional swivel. The only issues are the cable clips... they tend to pop off easily, especially if you try to get tight and tidy cable-management with an XLR cable through its cable sleeve. You need to position the clips in a place that leaves a little cable slack, for movement. Performance-wise, this mic-arm is decent.
Side-Note: I hate when companies design minimalist aesthetic hardware just to slap a bold, black-letter logo somewhere in the middle. Aokeo brands one side of the mic-arm with such, to which I spray-painted a matching matte-white overtop.

reviews.title: Completely adequate, but not extraordinary
reviews.comment:
I bought this PSU in a bundle deal, paired with the ASRock RX 9060xt Steel Legend GPU. The PSU took ages to ship, and arrived almost an entire week after the GPU. However, that’s not really relevant to the review. It’s obviously a non-modular PSU, and at this power level naturally only has a 6+2 PCI cable. However, the biggest thing to note is the backwards thinking with the accessory power. A single SATA power cable (triple chain) and while they COULD have had another, they instead opted for a 1 SATA + 2 molex cable instead. This confounds me, because….seriously? Molex? I haven’t even seen a molex-powered fan in the last 5 years, aside from a few Temu-level e-waste fans.
The reason I’m giving it 4 stars instead of 5, is that in my mind, 5 stars is reserved for something social. Something extraordinary. And this PSU is not. While it most certainly is 100% sufficient for the computer I’m building (just something basic to run a golf simulator) it definitely lacks firepower for higher/end systems, or PCs with additional storage devices and equipment. So while it’s perfectly adequate, it’s nothing special. That being said, I’m very happy with my purchase, is it was essentially free when bundled with the GPU. Would I buy this standalone? That’s hard to say. Depends on the price. My current go-to for “budget oriented” PSUs are the Thermaltake Smart series, but only time will tell if this unit holds up as well
