reviews.title: Fell short in so many ways, and then didn't fit on my mother boards. Not recommended!
reviews.comment: The instructions are terrible. They don't give you all the parts you need. If you install it, you can't  change CPUs or thermal paste without access to the back of the motherboard. And it looks like it would hit the filter capacitors on my MB. I would NOT recommend this product line. I tried installing it on an ASUS MB with an AM4 socket. I'm mechanically inclined so I ignored the reviews about difficulty of installation. Boy was I wrong! The directions were incomprehensible. (Get a native speaker to fix the English at least.) Most coolers mount to brackets on top the MB which are permanently to a backplate. This one doesn't. It is bolted from the cooler straight through the MB to the backing plate with nuts on the back and nearly inaccessible "thumbscrew" locations between the MB and heatsink. (Which are partly under the heatsink!)  This means you cannot put the cooler on without access to the backside of the motherboard to tighten the nuts underneath. A service nightmare. They also do tell you to use an insulating plate under their backing plate, but did not include one. You are supposed to peel the old one off your OEM backing plate? But the killer was that edge of the heatsink came down on top of the finter capacitors on the motherboard. This happened on two different model ASUS boards. (To be fair, I did this test fit without a CPU in place so there may have actually been some tiny vertical clearance, but it looked too close to call.) So the question about whether it really fit and the service nightmare it would leave me in a tight build caused me to send it back. I'd have taken off two stars for the horrible instructions and the poor design, but the fit questions and the missing insulator plate cost another one.

reviews.title: Full RGB backlit, mech TKL metal base keyboard for <$70? Hell, yeah!
reviews.comment: UPD: The listing has changed since I made the purchase. My review is for the RGB version of this keyboard, item currently sold under this listing seems to be a plain red backlight version. I still enjoy my keyboard and it works perfectly. /UPD I love, no, LOVE this keyboard. * Small (TKL is the way to go, how often do you use the numbers block, really?) * Solid build quality. Metal base adds perfect look and ensures your keyboard won't slide by adding some weight as well. * Rubber pads on all 4 corners. AND on the extended legs. * Perfect click sound and feel. I'm not too picky on this regard but the cherry mx keyboards I've tried before are of a comparable feel and quality, even though this keyboard sports some "custom switches", in my case looks like outemu blues but I'm not 100% sure. * Fully customizeable and actually nice looking RGB backlight. It has built in memory for your programmed configuration and some cute looking presets that I think I actually will use without fear of having a christmas tree in front of me. Most built-in presets that have some sort of movement have configurable speed so that you can slow it down to a comfortable level. I enjoy setting it to full rotation through the colors and slowest speed so that the change is imperceptible if you look at the keyboard but if you glance at it every once in a while it will be different color each time :) * Standard changeable keycaps. Don't like black caps or the font on the supplied ones? Buy any other caps you like. * Did I mention the satisfying click? * For under $70 this is likely the best mechanical keyboard with so many features. There are even cheaper chinese knock-offs but none come close in terms of feature set and many reviews are mentioning quality issues (as expected). The only con I had is that it didn't work on Windows 10 out of the box, which I'm guessing is on windows, not on redragon. They don't even advertise win 10 support, however it works perfectly on 10 if you do the following: (I found this solution by googling for it in about 10 seconds, this was in amazon review of a similar redragon keyboard, authored by  Engr. Jay Mendoza) WINDOWS 10 SOLUTION ▶ If you are using Windows 10, it may require a bit more work. This is what you have to do: 1. Open Device Manager. (Press Windows Key, type "Device Manager", press Enter) 2. Look for to "Universal Serial Bus controllers", and expand it (click the '>' button). 3. Look for "ND-tech USB adapter" created by the keyboard. (If there are more than one, reinsert they keyboard to see which one.) 4. Right-click on that and choose "Update Driver software" 5. Choose and click "Browse my computer for driver software." 6. Choose and click "Let me pick from a list of device drivers on my computer." 7. Choose "USB composite device" and click Next and proceed from there. 8. You should see two entries under Keyboards called "HID Keyboard Device". 9. Congratulations. Enjoy your new keyboard. Thanks to "Skyhawk0123" for pointing this solution (which was from "Sebastian J." on Amazon UK).

reviews.title: Quality, low-profile, and compact keyboard great for typing with stand up desk
reviews.comment: I made the switch from the awesome Logitech K800 specifically because I switched to using a stand-up desk adapter, which reduced my typic area. I also use two monitors so I wanted to be more centered when I typed and didn't use the number keypad as often. I was really annoyed because I had to shift to the left to type AND keep my mouse on the same space, so I scoured the web to find something that was tactile, had good feedback, and overall nice quality. The goal was to find a compact keyboard that was centered and gave me space for my mouse because if I centered the K800 then I had no space for my mouse, which I wanted to keep on the same level. I went down the rabbithole of mechanical keyboards after finding out that they don't really make membrane keyboards like the K800 in compact form. I tried out some of the small keyboards but they are basically attachments for tablets and not something that feels good for typing and reducing typing errors. So looking into mechanical keyboards I ended up trying a bunch like the Logitech G915 TKL, Redragon K539 Anubis, and finally this one. I honestly found the G915 too stiff and expensive, then while the redragon anubis was decent, I still tried this one and really loved how it felt. It's great for reducing typing error that you get for non-mechanical keyboards, it's not stiff and fairly responsive. PLUS it's a low-profile keyboard. One thing that you will see is that most mechanical keyboards tend to have full sized keys and this is one of the few that are tactile, compact, and low profile. I cannot recommend this more, as this is now my go to keyboard and use it daily. Pros: - low-profile - tactile mechanical keyboard - less noisy compared to most mechanical keyboars - compact and can center with smaller typing spaces - lights up and is colorful - wireless works with usb - quality build - charges with type-c - decent battery life Cons: - not too many lighting options - does not tell you how much battery life is left Overall highly recommend you try this especially if you're looking into TKL mechanical keyboards. Get this one and avoid the expensive Logitech G915. Also make sure to get you a low profile wrist rest like the one I have from redragon.

reviews.title: Second time's the charm
reviews.comment: I'm updating this review, the original is below. I'm really surprised that anyone on Windows 10 gives this a 5-star review. The 553-RGB does not "support" Windows 10 as claimed in the product description. You need to manually change the driver to get the keyboard to work. And, as I discovered this morning, there are large Windows Updates that will also reset the driver, which means you'll have to manually change the driver again. Also, if you make the mistake of plugging the device into a USB hub, you'll have to manually change the driver again. Although manually changing the driver only take about 20 seconds, it's really surprising that the keyboard isn't compatible or that the manufacturer doesn't just create a downloadable driver that fixes the problem permanently. But, once you get past that, this is a great keyboard for the money. I'm on my second unit, as my first one was defective (see review, below). The new one is rock solid and level. The keys feel and sound great. And since they're standard Cherry-sized keycaps, I've swapped the caps out with some from another key set for even more customization. I also bought a pack of red O-rings. These really help the 553 feel like a premium keyboard. They cut down on the bottom-out noise quite a bit and give a little bounce at the end of the key travel. I'd highly recommend them. If Redragon could fix the annoying driver issue, I'd give this a 5-star rating. Or, if they even provided warning on the product description I would at least them credit for it. But, buyer-beware, if you're using Windows 10 you should look up the driver fix before you get this plugged in. ***Original Two Star review*** I'm fairly certain I got a defective unit. Still, I'm writing this review now because some of the issues I experienced have happened to other people, so I want to give fair warning. First of all, my unit was *not* plug & play. I plugged the 553 into every USB port on my PC, and it didn't work at all. After searching around on the internet, I found out that you have to manually update the ND-tech USB Adapter driver in your Device Manager on Windows 10. I found multiple websites that explained how to fix this, so this device is clearly not compatible with all builds of Windows 10 (at least, not in the sense that it "plug & play"). To be fair, it's a really simple fix if you google "Redragon 553 not typing," but this keyboard should have a disclaimer that it is not plug & play on Windows 10. Second, when my PC comes out of sleep, the keyboard doesn't illuminate. I can manually illuminated it by pressing FN+[appropriate key]. Or, if I unplug the USB cable and plug it back in, it will illuminate. I think this is a defect because I haven't seen anyone else who has this problem. Will update when my replacement gets here. Third, my unit is not level. The packaging was undamaged, but the unit must have a very slight bend because when I put it on the same surface that I've put two other keyboards, it's tends to wobble. This wasn't a terrible wobble (I fixed it with a thin piece of cardboard), but it was noticeable until "fixed." Fourth, the space bar seems to sit just a little lower than normal. I tried typing for a few minutes and quickly got used to the location, but it did throw me off for a minute. These three things: The hassle of having to manually update some random driver, the failure of the keyboard to illuminate, and the fact that it has a slight bend in it, are enough for me to dock it down to two stars. I'm also returning it as defective, and hopefully the next unit is better. That being said, there's a lot to like about this keyboard. It's light and compact. The switches feel crisp. This is advertised as having Cherry Green clones, but they feel exactly like my Cherry Blue keyboard. They have the same level of loudness and tactile bump, and it feels like a very similar actuation force. The lights are great. In the custom mode, you can assign one of seven colors to each individual key. So, I assigned the very bright green to WASD and the arrow keys. I assigned the more subtle blue to the FN and Volume Control keys (I use volume control a lot). Everything else, I left the rather nice red. It makes glancing at your keyboard really intuitive. The only thing that would be better is if you could save multiple custom profiles. I'm really hopeful that the replacement I ordered will fix these the failure to illuminate and the level issue. If so, I'm looking forward to updating my review.

reviews.comment: I'm not a gamer, just bought this reasonably priced keyboard for the backlight.  Doesn't feel cheap, has a reasonable amount of weight to it.  Key labeling fonts are large and work well with 3  light level rainbow backlight.  Dedicated key for turning backlight on/off.  There is a bit of mechanical feel to the keys but obviously at this price is not a true mechanical keyboard (if that is important to you).

reviews.title: Would be great if it held a charge
reviews.comment:
I've only had it for a couple of days but so far I'm liking this keyboard.  The only issue that I'm currently having is that it won't hold a charge.  I left it plugged in overnight and when I disconnected the power cord, nothing worked.  I can only use it when it's plugged into a power source which technically takes away from it truly being "wireless".  I've contacted the company for assistance so my rating may change depending on the results.  My only other complaint is that the keys aren't as bright as I might like but I love all the color varieties.
The typing aspect of this keyboard is amazing! The keys are super smooth and quiet! Overall, I really like it so hopefully they can help me figure out why it won't charge so I can keep it.
UPDATE: I received an email back from the company telling me that I needed to contact Amazon's Customer Service department to either return or replace the product! No troubleshooting questions, just "call Amazon".  I did call Amazon and they, however, were very helpful!  I received a replacement faster than when I ordered the original!  The company contacted me again (after I gave 3 stars), telling me that they would like to address any issues or concerns and to reply back so they can work to resolve my issues.  After replying that Amazon has already resolved my issues, they apologized for the inconvenience and that I should contact them if I have any issues with the new keyboard. To be honest, I'm thankful that there have been no issues so far because I'm not confident that they wouldn't just send me back to Amazon again. So far, this keyboard is working the way it should and I really like it! I'm going to change my rating from 3 stars to 4. Now that I have a properly working product, I really like it but I'm only giving it 4 stars because the Company's "Customer Service" is lacking in the "service" department.

reviews.comment: Lights up great with the preset patterns! All keys are very receptive and can match typing speed really well. In terms of satisfying sounds from keys being clicked, I'd give it a 6 out of 10, they're not the loudest clicks but you can definitely hear them and be satisfied. It had a great weight to it, well balanced, even with having the volume knob on the top right corner. And the little pegs it has at the top rear of the keyboard allows for good comfort when using it.
reviews.author: Kindle Customer

reviews.title: Works flawlessly
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/D1Rj65spxsL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/61yKpXslFuL._SY256.jpg I ordered this thing renewed. Totally worth it. Saved about $80usd.  Everything works no problem. The keyboard itself is a little pricy but it is packed with tons of features.
The software, Razr synapse, seems to be far better developed than most other software.  There is a small learning curve. I was able to get everything set up fairly easily. Macros, lighting, etc.  I paired the Black Widow v4 pro with a basilisk v3 pro and man they are stunning. I found that synapse can even control the argb on my motherboard and works way better than the native motherboard software does. So, win win for me.
The response on this keyboard is insane and can be set to poll at 2000. I got the green switches. I love the clicky og feel of them. They are loud. I also have a black widow mini with the yellow switches. If you don’t want all the noise, get the yellow switches. They are much quieter.
The pro version does have two wires. One for the keyboard itself and one for powering the rgb. There is also a usb pass through giving you a great place to plug in your mouse dongle to take advantage of light speed tech. Allot of people complain about the two wires, but I’ve noticed most high end wired keyboards with usb pass through and rgb seem to all have them. So, I fully anticipated this and accept it.
So far, while this is not a high end keyboard snob keyboard, it is high end and awesome.

Firstly, this was, and still is not titled as refurbished. That in it's self bothered me, but not enough to prompt a return. When I set up the keyboard I found out that the "D" key was unresponsive about 80% of the time. I took the key caps off, blasted it with air, drivers, the works, nothing. Now I'm furious. I'm pretty sure the keyboard wasn't "refurbished" and was simply re-sold. This defect would have been instantly noticed if it was actually tested. update: I kinda hit it a few times and now it seems to work fine. Still kinda mad though. Sorry for yelling. I will return with another update in the future.

reviews.title: a very fancy keyboard
reviews.comment:
The shipping was a little weird...  No outer box or anything - just stuck in a big padded envelope.  So it arrived a little squished, but intact.
The packaging for the keyboard seemed off, too.  I'm more-used to glossy boxes with pretty pictures and lots of foam or cardboard filler to protect the device.  This was just a plain brown box with the Razer logo on it.
But, weirdness with packaging and shipping aside, the keyboard is pretty nice.  I got the tactile switches, rather than the linear, so they're nice and clicky.  The RGB lighting is fun. reviews.title: Excellent Keyboard - But Plan on a few upgrades
reviews.comment:
The Keychron K10 Max is very close to being a perfect full-size mechanical keyboard, but it took a couple small upgrades to get it exactly where I wanted it.
Out of the box, the build quality is excellent. The keyboard feels solid, the wireless connectivity (both 2.4 GHz and Bluetooth) has been reliable, and the ability to use QMK/VIA for configuration is a huge advantage if you want a keyboard that works across multiple machines without installing software. For anyone who moves between Windows and Mac systems (like I do), that flexibility alone makes this keyboard stand out.
That said, the stock typing experience was just a little harsher and louder than I prefer. I ended up installing thin switch O-ring dampeners (G40-THIN) which softened the bottom-out of the keystroke and noticeably reduced the noise. After that change, the typing feel improved significantly.
The other thing I’d strongly recommend is the separate wrist rest. With a full-height mechanical keyboard like this, a wrist rest really helps with long work days. It works great once you add it — but it honestly feels like something that should have been offered as a bundle option rather than a separate purchase.
I also wanted the enter and delete keys to feel differently, so I swapped the Red Switches of both with switches that I purchased in a sample set.  I like that tactile difference, it makes a difference.
With those minor tweaks in place, the keyboard became exactly what I was looking for:
a full-size, programmable, wireless mechanical keyboard that works seamlessly across multiple systems and feels great to type on.
So why not a full five stars? Simply because I think the out-of-box experience could be better. Including the wrist rest option and slightly softer stock acoustics would make this keyboard exceptional right away.
Still, with a couple small adjustments, it’s a fantastic keyboard and one I expect to keep using for a long time.
reviews.author: AnotherAmazonJunkie

reviews.title: A keyboard for TYPING! Yes!
reviews.comment:
After decades of typing, I became an inadvertent keyboard expert.
The best keyboards used to be those from IBM. Great shape, just the right pressure, perfect tactile feedback. They had low error rate and were tough.
Over time I found myself “settling” for mediocre or even bad keyboards. Chiclet type keyboards just don’t work for me. I have a Mac with standard desktop keyboard - the upgrade to the Keychron is wonderful! After years of accepting mediocre keyboards this has taken me back to the old IBM keyboards. Only better.
reviews.author: Dalekchap

reviews.title: Amazing sound and comfort for long gaming sessions
reviews.comment: I’m really impressed with these headphones. The sound quality is clear, immersive, and perfect for gaming, especially when it comes to hearing footsteps and small details. The wireless connection is stable and easy to set up on different devices. They are also very comfortable, even after hours of use, thanks to the soft ear cushions and adjustable fit. The battery life is excellent and lasts a long time without needing to recharge. Overall, a great investment if you’re looking for high-quality wireless gaming headphones. Highly recommended!
reviews.author: Heysow Vega

reviews.title: Astro A50 Gen 5. Not A50 X
reviews.comment: My husband has been using these and absolutely loves them. The sound quality is really good, and they’re an upgrade from his old Astro A50. They’re comfortable enough to wear for hours without bothering his head. The wireless connection is solid overall, though he did mention his old headset had a better range — he could walk to the fridge without disconnecting. The mic quality is clear and his friends can hear him well. Setup was easy, and switching between his Xbox and PC is convenient. He has the PLAYSYNC Audio version (not the PLAYSYNC Video & Audio), and it still works great for his setup. Overall, they’re a great headset and definitely worth it if you game a lot and use two or more systems.
reviews.author: Unknown23

reviews.title: Comfortable, versatile, and great wireless performance
reviews.comment: I absolutely love the Logitech A50 Astros. The headset is very comfortable, even during long gaming sessions, and the adjustable fit ensures it works well for different head sizes. The wireless capability is a game-changer, transitioning between PC and other gaming consoles is seamless, and I never experience lag or dropouts. Plus I can easily grab a cup of water in between sessions or while the lobby is loading without fear of ripping cords out of my setup. The ability to be wireless and still have the quality audio cannot be overstated. The included charging stand is incredibly convenient, keeping the headset ready to go at all times and reducing clutter on my desk. Sound quality is excellent, with clear highs and satisfying bass, making both games and chat crystal clear. Getting this on Prime Day added even more value, but I’d happily pay full price for the combination of comfort, versatility, and wireless convenience. 💡 Tip: Keep the headset on the charging stand when not in use to ensure it’s always ready and avoid unexpected battery drain. (It doesn't overcharge and charging will shut off automatically when the headset is charged) Verdict: Comfortable, reliable, and versatile!! This is an excellent headset for serious gaming across multiple platforms.
reviews.author: Michelle Kim

reviews.title: Beautiful headset that brings me right back to the good old days.
reviews.comment: I played for the last 8 hours today on this headset and I am blown away. This is the BEST headset I have ever used. I used the old A40’s for over 10 years. They were a beast of a headset and put me ahead of the competition for years. The only problem was that it was wired. The cord would frey over time and eventually screwed up the mixamp after too many rage induced drops. I decided to get the audio sync only as I have little to no desire to pull up the video at the same time as the audio every time. I tend to play the devices one at a time with no need to switch my HDMI along with it. If needed I can switch it by hand. The headset charged very quickly and was easy to understand out of the box. Watching a YouTube video on the set up might help if you have any questions. The a50s are extremely comfortable and somehow light while retaining their solid feel. The mic quality is unbelievable, you could stream with how good it is. Seriously!  Even though they don’t have noise canceling, I cannot head an outside sound while they are on my head. Bluetooth is great and the controls on the side of the headset are a little strange but it only took me a few hours to get used to them. (Such as to mute the microphone you just push it up). The sound quality is amazing for both music and games especially, you can hear footsteps from so far away. I love the Bluetooth feature as well, it’s just such a great headset. If you have the money I’d pull the trigger. If you really need to switch your monitor at the touch of a button get the PLAYSYNC + Audio version. But for me the audio version is perfect. The only problem I have is the Astro command center app for PC but that’s a different matter entirely.
reviews.author: James Mohtares

reviews.title: Deserves 0 stars IMO
reviews.comment: This is my first set of “high end” gaming headsets, and it’s been nothing but a nightmare. The only things “high end” about it are the price tag, and my blood pressure. In fairness, when it works, the sound quality is impeccable. However, “when it works” is a huge caveat in this design. In my experience, the A50 has both technical issues with connection as well as physical issues with charging. The connection has a mind of its own sometimes, usually on start up. Once it connects, mine does not lose signa during a gaming session. But sometimes just getting it to register on startup is a whole song and dance that involves powering down the Xbox, unplugging the base and toggling through the connection modes, etc., sometimes having to go through this multiple times before it works. The app has also been problematic for me, largely because the buttons that control the sound balance are easy to bump when picking up/putting down the headset. There’s no way to see what you are adjusting outside of the app—which is fantastic when the app doesn’t recognize the headset maybe 50% of the time, leaving you stuck with whatever sound settings it decides it wants. The only way to fix it is to unplug the base, delete the app, forget the device from your phone, and start the whole install all over again. Perhaps the most infuriating part (oh yes, it gets worse!) is the charging bases, which is extremely finicky. If you don’t set the headset into the base at *just the right angle,* it won’t charge—but it will click into place, making you think it’s charging. This issue is compounded by the unclear nature of the charging lights—apparently the headset will connect to the base just enough to register two lights blinking, but not enough to start charging. Every time I put mine down, I have to sit there and wait for it to decide whether or not it’s going to charge. And once you’ve got it seating correctly, don’t worry—it will come out of place with the slightest bump of your desk or table. I seriously regret this purchase. When this headset dies (likely due to me flinging it into the wall one day), I’m going back to wired Astros—or another brand altogether.
reviews.author: James

reviews.title: Exceptional mic and good audio quality.
reviews.comment: Due to Covid-19, I am now working from home on most days. We are doing a lot of video conferencing as result. The feedback I received from a colleague was that the earpiece I was using was really bad and he recommended getting this headset instead. I ordered this but was a little apprehensive at first as my wife did some research and found that the price I paid for was much higher than what Amazon used to sell it for. In addition, this model is a couple of years old. However, whatever reservation I had vanished when the headset arrived. First of all, the mic quality is exceptional. During video conferencing, it sounds way above the rest who were using other mics. If you are looking for a headset with a fantastic mic, get this one. This is its best attribute. The headset uses a USB connection rather than a 3.5mm jack. So it is limited to laptops and devices that has a USB port. Audio quality was also excellent. While obviously not as good as a $300 headset I owned in the past, the audio quality is still very good. I really enjoyed listening to music using this headset. Volume is also good. Overall, this is a very good headset and very good value for what you are paying. As mentioned earlier, I paid more for this headset than what it used to sell on Amazon but I still think that it is worth every cent and a steal for the quality and what I am getting. The selling point for this headset is the mic quality, so if you do a lot of video conferencing or dialog, this will come in handy. Love this product.
reviews.author: JT

reviews.title: Great sound quality
reviews.comment: They are lightweight and convenient to carry. On the other hand, they do not feel like they fit well in the ear because of their lightness when placed on the head. Also, the parts will break easily if not handled with care. The sound quality seems to be good, as all people rave about the sound coming from this headset. Perhaps it is not only the voice transmission, but also the excellent noise cancellation function. I have been using them for seminars for more than three years now, and they are still working fine as long as I take care of them.
reviews.author: WRX

reviews.title: Very good sound, a bit uncomfortable, but great value for the price.
reviews.comment: I teach online and bought this headset in order to create tutorials and make comments on student assignments. I have a recording studio and some high quality mics, but needed a simple USB mic for my purposes.  The headset is truly plug and play--no drivers or other obstacles to deal with.  The headset is recognized by Adobe Flash (very important for teaching online), and every recording program I have, including Adobe Audition, Adobe Captivate, and Studio One.  It works within Canvas and Turnitin, for those who work in those teaching environments and want to create audio comments. The audio quality is very good--once you get the mic positioned optimally and make a few adjustments to your sound card settings (I'm still using XP on my work computer).  This is designed as a close mic, so the sound quality drops quite a bit as you get a half-inch or so away from optimal distance.  But I'm pleased overall with the way my voice sounds in voice-over types of projects-- clear, distinct, just a tad sibilant when the audio gets compressed in some applications. The headband is cheap plastic, and uncomfortable, but with some stretching and positioning slightly in front of my ears, rather than directly on them, I soon forget I'm wearing a headset once I get started on a project. I don't use the headphones at all--they didn't sound very good to me, and I really didn't work with them much--I prefer to listen back to what I've recorded through my studio speakers.  But I bought this for the mic quality and convenience of having a headset as opposed to a boom mic, which I was using previously. I'll probably switch back and forth between using this and the Blue Yeti USB mic when it arrives.  (Review soon.) I can't comment on longevity, as I've only had this a few days, but I've already logged quite a few hours.  Overall, the sound quality is pretty much what I expected after reading reviews.
reviews.author: soundman

reviews.title: economic choice and exceeds my expectations - 3+ years strong
reviews.comment: i did a lot of research prior to purchasing this headset for work, and it paid off. excellent quality microphone, lightweight, and have lasted me at least 3 years of daily use for work. i get compliments on the microphone quality in teams meetings, and even with dogs barking or people acting up around me, the sound cancellation must be incredible to only capture my voice. pretty comfortable, i just need to change out the ear pads and they're probably good for another 3 years. cord length is fine, doesn't need to be super long, and the mute/volume toggle in-line in the cord is great. for the price, you can't beat that quality.
reviews.author: lukas

reviews.title: USB-A Connection Creates a Static Sound.
reviews.comment: The earphone worked well for day one, but it started to have static noise (vibrates with the sound) on day 2. I have tried to plug in 3 different USB-A ports ang got the same result. I have to use an adapter so I could plug in to USB - C, and the static sound went away.
reviews.author: QHF

reviews.title: Great mic at a great price!
reviews.comment: My microphone on my headset had finally broken after a few years and I was in need of a replacement. My friend recommended one of the generations of the Razer Seiren microphone and it was an easy-buy! And I still feel that way after a few weeks of owning it! It was super simple to set up (one cable) the sound quality is a sincere improvement from my headset mic (all my friends said so after hearing me) and it’s quite sensitive to outside noise and blocks it really well. It has a simple mounting process (you screw it into the base and set it in your desk) and I have zero issues with durability. Finally, the simple touch mute on the surface is perfectly consistent and at that price it was almost an insta-buy! Great value on a great product!
reviews.author: Easton

reviews.title: Amazing and cute
reviews.comment: It's lightweight and small enough to fit on my small desk. It was easy to set up and has amazing sound quality. You can't control things like sensitivity or volume, but there is a function to mute the mic. The mute button is sensitive sometimes, but at other times, you have to tap it a few times to get it to actually work. It worked with both my Chromebook and desktop. The color is really pretty and matches well with my setup.
reviews.author: Kylie

reviews.title: good, clear sound quality for a cute mini desktop mic
reviews.comment:
a great quality, cute, small desktop microphone. I primarily use it on discord calls and for work zoom calls, and I’ve been told that the voice quality it provides is clear & crisp.
I like the small size so it doesn’t take up much space on my desk, plus the pink color matches nicely with my set up!
The top has a touch-to-mute feature which is convenient, and it’s not too sensitive to the touch so you won’t accidentally mute/unmute.
I bought this on a black friday sale deal for $35 or so. It’s marked as $59.99 originally and I’d say that price is more expensive than I’d be willing to pay, so I’m glad I was able to get this item on sale!

reviews.title: Cool
reviews.comment: Very good microphone with great quality for the price. The mute button on top is really convenient, and  because of that it’s hard to put the fluffy covers without covering the mute button It’s lightweight, comfortable, and very easy to set up.
reviews.author: Alayla

reviews.title: Good sound quality but get a USB-C extender, the cord it comes with is way too short
reviews.comment:
I have had this Razer Seiren V3 mini for a couple months now. It works great and is crystal clear. However, I recommend getting some sort of mic stand/swivel to put this on. This mic has to be pretty close to your mouth for your voice to be received well. I use this mic for gaming and do not do any streaming or anything. It is perfect if you want to have separate headphones & mic setup. It is INCREDIBLY small which is its greatest feature.
The USB-C cord that this comes with is far too short for anything in my opinion. Look at replacing the USB-C cord with a longer one OR getting a USB extender (I recommend 10'). I went the extender route and it works great. If you want to put this right on your desk, you might be OK. However if you are going to put this on a swivel or stand you will absolutely need to pick up a longer cord or extender!
On the note of swivels/stands - one minor annoyance is that for some reason, it has a hard time screwing into swivel/stands. The thread design that Razer uses might be proprietary or something. My mic does screw in, but it isn't secure and it will fall off if I mess around with the mic too much. I used the proper adapters, it seems to be something with Razer threads.
All in all, If you want to use this for streaming - I would say upgrade to something more streamer friendly. This won't cut it for you. However, if you just want a desk mic to chat with buddies while gaming or to use during work, this is perfect for you. But make sure to get a USB extender! You will thank me later!

reviews.author: Dennis Acosta Rodriguez

reviews.title: The Best Software and High Quality Hardware
reviews.comment: Ordered this to start making Youtube videos and stream on Twitch occasionally.  When I got the microphone I downloaded the Wave Link application on my computer and that's what separates this mic from the other USB mics on the market.  I did a lot of research before ordering this mic and Razer makes the only other mic with a program similar to wave link, but it was known for being more buggy. What is wave link?  Well, it's a free Elgato application you can download from their website where you can link all of your applications and games on your pc. You can add different filters where you can customize the sounds as well as edit the volume of each individual application.  For example while streaming I can control how loud each application (spotify, video game and my voice) is in relation to each other.  Not only for the people watching the stream but also I can separately adjust the sound I am hearing in my headphones.  An example where this would come up is if I want to hear only my game but the stream chat would like to hear Spotify I can turn the Spotify off in my headphones while leaving it on for the viewers. Now for the microphone itself, it feels high quality for sure.  The tap to mute works flawlessly and is amazing to have if you plan on streaming or even just using it to chat.  When the mic is muted it illuminates a red circle around the adjustable knob on the front.  All in all between the features on the mic and the wave link you will be able to make this mic sound really good with a lot of perks other mics do not come with. My downsides for the mic are things I have for many other mics as well.  The original stand is too close to the table and doesn't have a shock mount so you have to be careful not to tap the table too hard or type too hard as you will hear the vibrations. I also would like some kind of pop filter either the foam cover or screen that goes in front of the mic.  Elgato also sells a shock mount for this mic.  I have ordered the pop filter screen and a boom arm in hopes to fix these few issues. All in all if you're looking for a USB mic I would say  this is the one to get for sure!  The Wave Link alone would be good reason but the microphone itself is also very high quality to the touch and sounds amazing!

reviews.author: Tyler delice

reviews.title: Great lavalier mic for a fair price
reviews.comment: I got this lavalier mic after my prior one started getting pops and crackles.  Had this since late 2019 and it has far outlasted my prior brand.  I have been using this with my old smart phone to capture audio for my YouTube videos.  Does a great job for a budget mic.  So if you can't bite the bullet and buy the more expensive audio options that run $100+, this is a great alternative to improve sound quality over built in mic setups on most camera's.  Keep in mind this will not be super high quality, but the wind socks this comes with do a much better job than I would have expected out of a $30 setup.  After several events and many trips packing and unpacking the sound quality still hasn't broken down or degraded.  I have definitely been impressed by the quality of sound you get for a ~$30 product.  The cord length is good, it comes with an extension cord, adapters and it also comes with 2 styles of windsock(the usual foamy style and a 'deadcat' style sock).  The wind socks do a pretty good job of getting rid of wind noise and other small background noises, but it's not perfect.  I use a standard plug on my phone, so haven't needed the adapters.  I would expect the adapters work, but I'll let someone who has used them comment on that part.  I can definitely say this was well worth the price and if I'm not ready to upgrade to a zoom setup by the time this dies, I would buy another.
reviews.author: woody

reviews.title: Worth buying
reviews.comment:
I used it in two ways: a. Directly connected to my DLSR camera. b. Connected to a portable recorder. For both I have more or less the same comments.
In general I am very satisfied by the result such a mic can give compared to its affordable price. Very good job!
I noticed that the final volume is a bit too loud if the mic is adjusted quite close to the chin. It must have a sufficient distance from the mouth to function better. Otherwise, either volume has to be adjusted later with software or you end up with an undesired result.
Some consonants sound well, the "S" for example, one of the most difficult, sounds very well but others like "P" and "B" are quite harsh and one has to try to make some adjustments -if possible- before starting recording.
Another plus point is that you don't get any "noise" from sounds around the source of sound. It can peak very easily only the sound of the person speaking and not other sounds around and it doesn't have any buzzle or noise created from the mic itself.
I also noticed that the low frequencies are a bit higher. Sometimes this is positive, it gives a nice deep color in the voice. But it's not as actual and as accurate as it should be to call it a convincing microphone.
As a conclusion I think there is space for improvement but if you compare the price with the quality of the product, then the result is superb. I recommend it unreservedly.

reviews.title: Excellent camera, but the lighting is a bit harsh
reviews.comment:
The camera quality is fantastic. I tend to use other "warmer" lights or bounce them off the walls so it doesn't look like I'm being questioned by the cops nor look pale as a ghost ... I'm pale enough as it is. The microphone is also pretty darn good, though I also use an external microphone but could use this one and would be fine with it.
The software of this Razor LOVES to autofocus, especially if there is anything with writing on it in the background. It's weird because it's a webcam; it's not like I'm going to be 1 foot away and then like 30 feet away. You can set the focal range, but it will reset to "autofocus on all the things" depending on the application you use. For zoom, as that's often what I use it for, it always defaults to autofocus. It usually remembers to be in NOT autofocus mode for other programs, but I'm constantly turning autofocus off or can't trust that it IS off. The focal range is a little sensative and I had to write the setting for the focal range. It's got all these options for focus and lighting and sound but the autofocus is what makes it annoying.
If you're only going to use this for one program, like twitch (probably why lots of steamers use it) or you like autofocus for some reason, or your work space has you running into the background a lot, the autofocus is fine. I'm fine with having my zooms be a little shifty if my other recordings are crisp, but if you can't be bothered to change it every time, this is the one feature I'd want them to fix.
THIS SEEMS LIKE A SOFTWARE PROBLEM so can that just be patched?

reviews.author: Rudy Stankowitz

reviews.title: Only downside is a wired-in USB cable
reviews.comment: If you need a high-quality webcam--and who doesn't these days?--that's also good for streaming (streaming resolution for webcams is about half what the recording or photo resolution is, and not many cameras stream 1080p at 60fps), this is a great choice. I have mine mounted on an arm above my computer using the included universal tripod mount, but you can also attach it to the top of your monitor with the universal monitor mount. Image quality and detail is good enough to be a bit frightening. (Every freckle and wrinkle shows up, even in low light.) I haven't tested the microphone quality because I already use a studio mic in my office. The USB-C cable is great because that means that I could connect it to my smartphone or my traveling laptop if I wanted to, and those only have USB-C ports. And the USB-C cable is annoying because it's wired in, which means that you can't use a longer or shorter cable. Unlike a more typical webcam, you can't easily attach a privacy cover to it. But since it's an external camera, all you have to do is disconnect it. It does have a pretty obvious light on it that shows you when the camera is activated. I haven't quite wrapped my head around the Logitech Capture virtual camera software, specifically how to get it to work with my green screen. But if I use the camera directly with Zoom, the virtual green screen still works perfectly. (And Zoom still touches up my appearance so I don't see every freckle and wrinkle.) Windows did not actually recognize this as a camera until I'd installed the software, which was kind of annoying, but since then it's worked perfectly. Eventually I may manage to exploit some of the more sophisticated features, but even if I never use them, I'll still consider this camera well worth the money.
reviews.author: Sallie Goetsch (rhymes with sketch)

reviews.title: Good camera, but settings need to stay locked in, and multi cameras don't work in G HUB
reviews.comment: The first camera I bought is blurry on one side but I'm dealing with support about that. When I bought a second one, I realized the G HUB software, which lists all of my other peripherals including several LITRA GLOW lights, will only ever list one camera... so there's no easy way to set up software like OBS with multiple cameras for storing settings. Whether I'm rebooting or restarting OBS and its virtual camera, I often have to go in and tweak several settings on the cameras to make sure they look okay. And if I start Zoom or Google Meet, and it accidentally picks a Logitech camera instead of my OBS virtual camera, I have to go figure out how to reset the settings every time. This is a major hassle and wish Logitech had a better way to "lock" the settings so every software package can't tweak the settings... Overall, it's a good camera and I'm happy with the quality. The auto-focus is a bit too aggressive some times, like turning my head to look at something and turning back to face the camera will trigger the auto-focus sometimes. My main complaint is with the G HUB software to change the settings on the camera, and the fact that we can't set multiple cameras within G HUB.
reviews.author: Ian Douglas

reviews.title: Clarifying Product Information
reviews.comment: I never write reviews, but wanted to clarify some misconceptions and help other folks. There are some negative reviews about this camera, so I wanted to set the record straight. I only use this camera for work meetings (Zoom, Microsoft Teams etc) and so was content to plug it in and let it run. The quality of the image was terrible. People even told me the coloring was overly white and it looked like a cheap camera. I was debating whether to go back to my laptop camera. However, I took the advice of other comments on the logitech website, and downloaded the free software - on my personal laptop and work laptop. The software controls the image quality. I saw an IMMEDIATE difference in the image quality. I no longer looked washed out, but the quality improved dramatically. You can also control if the camera follows your face etc. There is also a free streaming. program for this camera, to further control the image quality. The Apps to download for FREE from logitech are: Logitech Capture Logitech Camera Settings Logitech Camera Settings is for any logitech camera, and you can control every details - lighting, brightening, camera width etc. Logitech Capture is for for this camera - and its a streaming app. With the app downloads, it is 100% beyond worth the value of the money. I have Microsoft Surface computers, so this could be part of the reason why I needed the apps - maybe other types of computers do not.
