Buy with caution; if you're typing out manuscripts, be prepared to correct the extra letters.  Buy with caution. Good for gaming, I've had no problem there.
reviews.author: Richard Lopez

reviews.title: Great Keyboard
reviews.comment:
I got this keyboard to replace my old membrane one, and so far this one is amazing. The keys are easy to remove and replace, the backlight works and offers a multitude of colors and effects, and the software provided allows for easily created custom macros. The clicking sound is not too loud and the little resistance on the keys is quite nice.
The size is relatively average, and the shape of the keys have a slight tilt towards the bottom of the keyboard. I find that I tend to accidentally hold down keys while gaming because of the shape of the keys. This is no fault to Redragon, however.
I will add that they were quick to rectify a manufacture error and replace the first keyboard that arrived—the backlight on some keys weren’t working. Fortunately, the replacement has been perfect.
reviews.author: Phoebe

reviews.title: Redragon is the Perfect Balance of Affordability, Functionality, and Fun!
reviews.comment:
This is overall an excellent keyboard choice. Redragon has consistently proved itself a real comptetitor in the keyboards and peripherals markets -- Their products hold up well to comptetitors such as "Hyper-X" and "Logitech". What I've found is that Redragon consistently offers a delicate balance of affordable value, functionality, and absolute fun. They have an incredible array of products to meet everyone's needs and expectations, whether it be avid gamers and PC professionals alike.
As a loyal Redragon consumer, I have rarely had issues with their product line, however, in this instance there was some damage to the exterior packaging, but it seems directly attributed to poor-handling as sometimes happens -- This is one of many Amazon products participating in the sustainable program, so it does not arrive in extra-padded packaging. This is not the fault of Redragon and therefore doesn't effect my star-rating.
As a mention, I would also like to see the RGB backlighting perhaps improved on this model as well -- While it is fully customizable as it relates to lighting and patterns (with or without Redragon Software), the brightness threshold is lower than most of us enthiusasts would like -- Especially those who find themselves gaming or working in less
than optimal lighting conditions.
Additionally, given that this keyboard has hot-swappable keycaps and switches, perhaps Redragon will include the all-in-one dual-sided pulling tool in the future, rather than a separate keycap puller and U-shaped tool which is included with this model. The all-in-one puller tool is much more functional and effective in my experience. In fact, Redragon does include this tool with many of their keyboards.
I brought these minor concerns to the attention of Redragon, to which they were very receptive and understanding. They backed up their quality product with a replacement. That too is something that really stands out with Redragon, they take customer satisfaction seriously. Thanks for reading and allowing me to share my thoughts and experiences with the K671 keyboard.
reviews.author: Bryan H

reviews.title: Redragon Mechanical Gaming Keyboard—Reliable Build but Noticeable Noise
reviews.comment:
The Redragon mechanical keyboard is a well-built and sturdy piece of hardware. The 11 programmable backlit modes offer great customization for those who enjoy a personalized desk aesthetic, and the hot-swappable feature is a significant plus, allowing for easy maintenance or future switch upgrades. It feels durable and provides the tactile feedback many users look for in a mechanical setup.
However, it is important to note that this keyboard is definitely not silent. Mechanical switches are known for their distinct sound, and this model is no exception—it produces a clear, audible "clack" with every keystroke. For someone specifically seeking a quiet or discreet typing experience to avoid disturbing others or for use in a focused environment, the noise level here may be a drawback.
Bottom Line: A high-quality, customizable keyboard that performs well for gaming and heavy typing. It’s a solid choice if you enjoy the classic mechanical feel, but if a silent workspace is your priority, you will find this model much louder than expected.
reviews.author: Alex KNY

reviews.title: A very good mechanical keyboard without breaking the bank...
reviews.comment: I have 2 Redragon Mechanical Gaming Keyboards and both are wired, but different models. This one I purchased recently for my gaming desktop and it is a very good keyboard. Based on the other model of keyboard of the same brand, this should be the same: durable, responsive, backlit, and some key are modular and can be changed for a fair value price. In short, if you want a mechanical keyboard that is decent enough for gaming without breaking the bank, this is your keyboard.
reviews.author: Joel T.

reviews.title: It comes in a HARD ZIPPERED CASE!
reviews.comment: It comes in a HARD ZIPPERED CASE! When you open the box you're just kind of like "does it NEED to be this fancy?" It's actually an amazing experience for a keyboard. Really makes it feel deluxe. The keys are just effortless to press. It's really unlike anything I've ever experienced. Volume roller is smooth (I prefer a clicky volume wheel) but it still feels really good. It's heavy!  Pulling the box out of the amazon box, it feels like a whole graphics card. Build quality is amazing. I got this on sale which is an incredible value and would absolutely recommend it. I will not be able to judge battery life as I will leave it plugged in. I thought it would take AAs or something but it's a rechargeable battery inside.
reviews.author: Jordan

reviews.title: Best Keyboard I bought!
reviews.comment: This keyboard is amazing! The only problem I have with it is resting my fingers on it can activate a key on accident because of how sensitive it is, but you start to get used to it and I barely have any accidental key presses on it. It's decently heavy; this keyboard won't be sliding anywhere. The battery life can last me almost a week, and it appears to have an auto-sleep feature. It's very high quality, and you can hear it in the clicks and taps on the keyboard. I love that it's portable with a 2.4g dongle or Bluetooth, so it's not restricted to just living on my desk; it even comes in a case to carry the keyboard.
reviews.author: Furiousbanner

reviews.title: Linear Red Switches - phenomenal!
reviews.comment: Two days in, essentially, and I am loving the feel / performance of the keyboard right out of the box. The lightspeed connectivity, from my subjective experience, feels like there is no delay in my inputs, so there’s that! It’s my first time using a wireless keyboard and I’m impressed to say the least; battery life with the static light setting is 50+ hours which is fine by me. What I’m enjoying most is just the feel of the linear red switches Logitech uses on this board; highly recommend these over using clicks or tactile; not sure what the actuation pressure is but it’s not so light that it feels too quick and there is a nice little, even tiny, bit of force needed to press down on the switch. My only major drawback so far is that it’s not a hot swappable board; this makes me nervous for a couple reasons: one, the cost of the keeb being what it is means if a switch goes bad you’re kind of up a creek. I’m playing the dice, so to speak, with this keyboard and hope it continues to perform well while I wait on the Wooting 80HE to arrive this summer. I’m a recent convert to being a fan of the 75 to 85% size of keyboards and don’t see myself going back to 65 or lower; having the dedicated media keys, F-Row, and the other extraneous keys above your dedicated arrows just feels nice “in case” you ever need them for something. All in all, Logitech has a new fan with me and as long as they can iterate upon this Pro X TKL board with features that folks are yesrning for / expecting such as: hot swappable keys, sound dampening tape jobs, Hall effect switches (not required but as an option would be nice), etc, then I can see this line of their keyboards continuing to soar. I’ll revisit this review down the line.
reviews.author: The Lovely Lyss

reviews.title: Best Logitech Keyboard Ever
reviews.comment: Bought the Gen 2 and love it. As a person who makes custom keyboards this is the closest you will get to a custom one from Logitech and it's actually very solid. Overall great product and I would buy again.
reviews.author: RyseUp

reviews.title: Don't recommend the keyboard or the company
reviews.comment: Mid keyboard, terrible software, some truly awful design choices. No way to see if caps lock is on or not unless you lean all the way over your keyboard to type, as the caps lock button is completely hidden from view during normal use. RGB lighting and configurable software fully exist and are pushed on the user, so you'd hope we could configure the caps button to change color based on state - one of the few imaginable uses for all this rgb and configuration software effort.  Unfortunately it doesn't seem like this setting exists, and getting support from Logitech is an ABSOLUTE nightmare.  AI chatbot hell, and when you finally reach someone they barely respond and know nothing about the product, and won't transfer you to someone better. Honestly really disappointing, logitech kills it in important aspects, but completely drop the ball with basic, fundamental requirements.
reviews.author: Erik Roosendahl

reviews.title: Good Entry Level Headphone
reviews.comment: A solid entry-level wireless headphone that punches above its price point. The sound is clean and balanced — true to Audio-Technica’s studio-monitor heritage — making them great for both casual listening and critical audio. Bluetooth connectivity is reliable, and the 60-hour battery life is genuinely impressive. The all-black design is understated and professional-looking. They’re not the most feature-rich option at this price, lacking active noise cancellation, but for pure sound quality and endurance, the ATH-M20xBT is hard to argue with.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​
reviews.author: Susan

reviews.title: Wonderful Product
reviews.comment: This is a wonderful product for those looking not having to choose between wireless and wired. Although lower in price than other models the audio quality is upstanding and noise cancellation works incredibly well. The cord is long enough; it could be replaced by other longer in case of need. These headphones are not as portable as it might seems, the do not sit that comfy on the neck so most likely will have to be transported on a handbag or backpack always fearing to breaking them as they might me more fragile than other models. The mic is strangely placed but it works for calls on a not so noisy space.
reviews.author: Mariano

reviews.title: Still going fairly strong after 3 years
reviews.comment: Very good quality for the price overall, I’ve had these for almost three years and I still use them almost daily. Battery lasts a very very long time on a full charge, especially when you first get it. Sound is a little better when using the cord. Very comfortable and lightweight. I’ve had to replace the soft covers for the headphones because they started to flake and smell from sweat, but this was a relatively inexpensive replacement. The only flaw I’m now facing is there is a very noticeable delay in the audio when using Bluetooth, so if you’re watching a video the audio will be slightly delayed and not match the video. This obviously is not much of a problem if you’re just using these to listen to music or just use the cord to watch videos. Overall, very affordable and high quality option that I have recommended to many people.
reviews.author: Samantha

reviews.title: Long battery life, great design, very snug fit, punchy bass
reviews.comment:
I do music production and also general listening.  After using this BT headset I have to say I am very impressed by the battery life as it can hold an entire session of production (few hours, 6 or more and for numerous days) without getting a low battery notification - After couple weeks I got my first low battery so you probably dont need to have this parked on the usb charger for many times in a month.  That is the mark of a true BT studio headphone for me and reason why I'd recommend it for just that purpose.
The bass quality is actually very noticeable but not overbearing where mid and highs would be flattened out.  However it is very punchy bass without "breaking in" out of the box.  Any low-lows will be noticeable if you need to work on a bassline sequence in Ableton or an alternate program.
The charging time itself from low to full, is at least a couple of hours which is acceptable.  Quality build is very high.  Fit-wise it is very snug to the ears and buttons are on the left side, which some people may find to have a learning curve (not a high one).  Easy to press rectangle style buttons.  I haven't used it to gym or cardio with but they aren't heavy enough to where they would fall, I think the JBL TUNE 500s are made for that, because they are feather weight "light" and do a great job cancelling treadmill noise.  Im sure these would do the job fine at the gym, they aren't bulky.
They do come with a cord in case you want to use without the internal battery, so that's a neat feature.  Overall latest BT specs and long battery Im sure these would do the job for a long time, they are my go to, audio feels twice that for the price so it almost feels like a bargain but they probably sound like $150 phones. Ive had the Monster Inspirations which have a similar price tag but they are 4x as heavy and audio signature is similar but wireless and way more utility.  I highly recommend them.
reviews.author: JDA

reviews.title: Great value headphones
reviews.comment:
For the cost, you'd be hard pressed to find better sounding headphones. These are close to being studio monitors, with the convenience of wireless features.
These headphones do a good job of separating instruments in tracks and provide a better soundstage than I expected for this price. They are a touch, and I mean barely, warm. Meaning, they are mostly neutral as you would expect from a studio headphone, with the slightest bump in the lower end. Sub bass isn't really present, but I appreciate the modest punch in the low end.
Keep in mind, these are not noise cancelling headphones. I find the ear pads fit my average sized head, and smaller ears really well. The seal they create helps block out some ambient sounds on their own. When I'm doing chores around the house and pumping some tunes, I really don't hear anything but the music. I even took these out in public once to get my tires changed. I could not hear the sounds of the storefront or the shop, even as I sat writing at the bar by the shop window. I was able to lose myself in the music and my writing without any problems. I don't find there is much sound leakage as these are closed back, but I also don't listen to my music at excessive levels (~75% at most).
The one problem I have with them so far is the fact that the earcups do not swivel much, and thus cannot fold completely flat for travel. I would have also liked to see a cheap case or bag come with this product to help in transporting them. I have purchased the WS990 BT in the past which came with a leather bag that I still use when traveling. I will likely continue to use that pair for work travel, rather than the M20X.
One concern I have for the long run is their build quality. They are mostly plastic with an aluminum band for extending the earcups. Being constructed as such, they are very lightweight. On one hand, this adds to the comfort of the headphones as I forget I'm wearing them sometimes due to their featherweight and light clamping force. However, I worry that these could be broken if I decide to toss them into a backpack and take them out more often. With the light clamping force I find that I can shake them loose if I shake my head side to side rapidly. While I don't do that often, I think that anyone looking for a headphone to wear while exercising should look elsewhere, or consider finding a different ear pad that provides more grip than the provided pleather set.
For me, these will likely be relegated to around the house wear, when I don't want to be strapped to my computer desk by my R70Xs. I'm perfectly okay with that as I do really enjoy the sound these produce for the money and the comfort they provide. I think they punch above their price in the audio department and are an excellent option for someone looking for a good, reliable headphone for casual wear.
reviews.author: Matt Oliver

reviews.title: Solid Workhorse Headset - Does the Basics Really Well
reviews.comment: Honestly, I wasn’t expecting much when I grabbed the EPOS H3 for my gaming setup down here in Florida. I’d seen it around, knew it was from the old Sennheiser gaming line, but figured it was just another mid-range option. After a couple months of using it daily – for everything from late-night Valorant sessions to Zoom calls while waiting out thunderstorms, and even dragging it on a few trips to visit family in Orlando – I’ve got a pretty clear picture of where it shines and where it falls short. It’s not flashy, but it gets the job done without fuss. What stands out most is how comfortable it is for long stretches. Seriously, I’ve worn this thing for 6+ hour gaming marathons during hurricane season power-outages (yeah, we get creative down here) and my ears don’t feel sore, nor does the top of my head ache. The lightweight build and soft ear pads make a difference; I’ve definitely had headsets that started feeling like a vice grip after an hour, but the H3 just sort of disappears. The adjustability is straightforward too – slid it onto my brother’s bigger head when he borrowed it, and it locked in place easily. Sound-wise, it’s competent. The bass has a nice punch that makes explosions in games like Call of Duty feel impactful without being muddy, and the midrange emphasis really helps pick out footsteps or reload sounds in competitive matches – super useful when you’re trying to clutch a round. For music, it’s okay; vocals can sometimes get a bit buried behind the bass if you’re listening to something dense, but for podcasts or casual listening while working, it’s perfectly fine. Nothing audiophile-grade, but honestly, for gaming and chat, it’s more than sufficient. The microphone is where this headset actually surprises me. My teammates consistently comment on how clear my voice comes through – no muffled sounds or excessive background noise picking up my ceiling fan or the AC unit (which runs constantly here). It’s plug-and-play simple; I didn’t need to fiddle with settings on my PC or PS5. Just plugged it in via the splitter cable, and it worked. The lift-to-mute feature on the boom is handy too – flick it up when I need to yell at the cat knocking over my coffee cup. Now, for the drawbacks. The volume dial is honestly annoying. It’s this flat disc on the right ear cup that’s stiff to turn with one finger – I often end up using my thumb and forefinger, which breaks my concentration mid-game. Worse, the braided cables, while nice and tangle-free *in theory*, somehow manage to create this faint rubbing noise against the left ear cup when I move my head slightly. It’s not loud, but noticeable in quiet moments, like during a cutscene or when waiting for a match to start. And yeah, no software or EQ customization exists – what you hear is what you get. If you like to tweak your audio profiles, this isn’t the headset for you. On the value front, I paid around $80-$90 for it (seen it on sale sometimes), and for that price, it feels fair. You’re not paying for RGB lights or fancy wireless tech, but you are getting reliable comfort, a genuinely good mic, and solid wired audio that works everywhere – PC, my Switch in docked mode, even my phone when I’m using it to chat while walking the dog around my neighborhood. It’s the kind of headset you buy when you want something dependable that won’t need constant charging or troubleshooting, especially useful when you’re traveling and don’t want to deal with pairing issues in airport lounges or hotel rooms. Would I buy it again? Probably, if I needed a straightforward wired replacement tomorrow. It’s not perfect, but it does the core things well – comfort for long wear, clear communication, and decent game audio – without asking much in return. It’s the reliable sedan of gaming headsets: not exciting, but you know it’ll start every morning. After using it regularly for a few months, especially mixing in those Florida trips where I needed something hassle-free, I’d say it earns a solid 4 out of 5 stars. It loses points for those nagging little annoyances (the volume wheel, cable noise) but gains back a lot for being genuinely comfortable and having a mic that doesn’t make people ask if you’re on a speakerphone. If you prioritize comfort and mic quality over bells and whistles, and don’t mind being tethered by a cable, it’s a sensible pick. Just don’t expect it to blow your mind – expect it to work, day in and day out.
reviews.author: Amazon_Customer

reviews.title: Very good sound and extremely comfortable
reviews.comment: They worked out great.  Very good sound and extremely comfortable.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Sounds great. Fits a little tight.
reviews.comment: Tight fit for those with widder heads. Can start to hurt after a while. Sound is great and mic is good for the price point.
reviews.author: MatthewD

reviews.title: Most Reliable Headset
reviews.comment: Because of an incident that happened with one of our dogs, the top port on my computer got ruined as well as my old pair of GSP 300's, which I had been using for the past 4 years. I'm particular about not changing things unless I absolutely have to, so when I tell you I fell in love with these H3's I mean it. It's hard, if not impossible to beat the price and quality of this product, especially when compared to other gaming headsets. The microphone quality is clear, no background noise. The headphones really do noise cancel to an extent, more than I was expecting. Because of the durability of my last Sennheiser's, I can only assume these will last as long if not longer. Highly recommend picking these up if you like wired headsets.
reviews.author: Michael L.

reviews.title: Decent budget option
reviews.comment: Good build quality and packaging. This headset will not wow you, it just does everything OK. Bass is ok, highs are ok, microphone is ok, nothing to really boast about but it feels appropriate at a $50 price point. The analog noise cancellation is excellent which helps you really hear the output of the small drivers. This noise cancellation is credited to thick ear pads and a tight clamping style fit on your head. Not a good headset for large heads. The actual cup of the earphones are precisely ear shaped so that you can really only put the headset on one way, large ears will not fit inside the cups and may get pressed. The microphone has a loud hissing background noise when connected to 3.5 audio port of PC, you will need to constantly adjust levels and settings to get the mic correct.
reviews.author: Jacob

reviews.title: Perfect for Zoom and desk videos!
reviews.comment: I do a lot of Zoom meetings for work and plan on doing podcast style Zoom meetings with clients so this is the best setup. It’s very sturdy and holds my Shure MV7+ well and it’s compatible with other Shure mics as well. It’s very well designed and can move around pretty well. It comes with an adapter so most mics should be able to fit. The price point was amazing as well since other similar quality arms would cost a lot more. This is very high quality.
reviews.author: Weekend Shopper

reviews.title: The most important tool on my desk!!
reviews.comment: This Low Profile Boom Arm is exactly what I needed for my setup! It’s built solidly and feels extremely sturdy, easily handling my heavy Shure SM7B without any sagging. The gear lock structure really makes a difference—once you set it in place, it stays locked and stable, even after hours of use. The low-profile design is perfect for keeping my desk area clean and uncluttered while giving me full range of motion to position the mic exactly where I want it. Installation was simple, and the desk mount is strong and secure without wobbling. It works beautifully not just with the SM7B, but also with my Yeti and Rode PodMic, so it’s versatile too. Overall, this is a professional-quality boom arm that looks sleek, feels premium, and performs flawlessly. Highly recommend for streamers, podcasters, or anyone using a heavier microphone!
reviews.author: MB

reviews.title: Affordable Mic Arm Stand
reviews.comment: The Quality is quite impressive, definitely would say great for the price. Cable management system is simple to use and setup, would definitely say the durability of the nobs it being plastic would have ben great to be metallic, for the size/fit of the location it will definitely would have be within your preference and set up. But really great fit. The appearance is minimalistic and very sleek. Finally the overall durability of the item is well made and has a great feel and extremely easy installation. The Mic im currently using is the Shure MV7+
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Clean look, Easy to Put Together, Reliable Build. 4.5/5
reviews.comment: I love it. It easy to use once you mess with it for about 5 minutes, it works very well in my studio by looking nice as well as noting being in the way. The Joints feel tough due to its twist lock feature (Its good that it stays where you put it, but i have a minor nitpick about it having specific heights that it locks in at, but that's just the trade off for the quality i feel). I do wish that the clamp was larger in surface area to prevent slight bounciness of the boom arm (Genuinely isn't a big deal, just finding something to nitpick at this point.). They also have several thread adapters inside the box so it is VERY versatile. Clean Look, Easy to use/Put Together, Reliable build. Almost a 5 star, but doesn't feel like it should be 5 stars, id say more 4.5 tbh. I'd highly recommend this boom arm.
reviews.author: Austin

reviews.title: This is a great mic stand.
reviews.comment: This is a very well made product.  Good materials, and an excellent fit and finish, and was very simple to assemble.  The clamp is solid, and the stand is extremely stable.  The integrated cable channel keeps the cable out of sight.  The "sound quality" will depend entirely on the quality of your mic, shock mount, filters, etc. - but the mic stand itself certainly isn't going to get in your way.  It's rock solid. If this product is indicative, I wouldn't hesitate to give the brand's other products a chance if they adressed my needs.
reviews.author: Alan Robertson

reviews.title: No Need to Hold Back
reviews.comment: The Elgato Wave Desk Stand is a sleek and sturdy adjustable stand made for microphones like Elgato, HyperX, RØDE, Fifine, and more. What I love is the adjustable height; you can raise or lower it to get your mic right where you need it, whether you’re podcasting, streaming, or recording. The weighted base keeps it stable on your desk, and it doesn’t take up much space, which is perfect if you’re working in a tight setup. It’s simple, functional, and built with that Elgato quality. If you need a reliable desk stand that works with the most popular microphones, this one is definitely worth it.
reviews.author: Crystal R Durham

reviews.title: Sturdy, well designed, great compact desktop mic stand
reviews.comment: A very nice compact desk stand. The base is quite heavy at 4 pounds, meaning no tip-overs. It also has a solid rubber bottom which means no-skid. The boom is solid metal and feels sturdy. The knobs to adjust the boom arms have an extended lever that makes them easy to use. Four silicone ties are included along with two threaded adapters for mounting your microphone. Overall, a really nice mic stand!
reviews.author: Bob W

reviews.title: Solid Microphone stand
reviews.comment: This is my daily driver mic stand for all of my livestreams and recorded videos I do for my YouTube channel and for tutorials I do for college classes I teach. It is rock solid and I love the tightening bolts that allow me to hold heavier microphones like I tend to use.
reviews.author: Tech Troublemaker Picks

reviews.title: Joint clamps are a problem but could be good for certain people.
reviews.comment: This stand might have a nice, heavy base, but the mechanism to keep the mic where it needs to be is cheap. If you turn it too hard, then it gets stuck and is painful to get open. The handles for tightening or loosening the grips at the joints are still so small that you can't get enough leverage to loosen them. If you have a heavy microphone, go with something else. It does NOT hold up my Rode condenser microphone very well at all. If you need to adjust your mic frequently, this is NOT for you. If you have a light mic and want to set it up in one position and never move it. This is great. I think the clamps have to be tightened too much to stay, and when they are easier to move, they're not stable. The joint clamps keep this from being one of the best desktop mic stands out there.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Holds mic in place
reviews.comment: Works great. I like the rotating joint on the end. It works great and is substanial enough to hold a heavy microphone in place.
reviews.author: David D

reviews.title: Top-graded dynamic XLR mic!
reviews.comment: -Quality and construction built feels high quality -comes with swappable mic cover, whether it's black or red -noise level was excellent -no audio distortion -cardioid mode works perfectly fine -However, you may need an audio interface to connect with 48V Phantom power in order to drive this microphone properly but also convert from digital to analog signal for your computer -In addition, you will need to purchase an Elgato Wave Mic Arm Mk.2 in order to mount your XLR microphone -Yes, you will need to purchase XLR balanced cable in order to connect your XLR microphone -Expensive but you pay for high quality graded XLR which is known as balanced mic -built-in shock mount is already included -3.8" adapter is included to mount your XLR mic
reviews.author: Danny Lim

reviews.title: AWESOME!!!!
reviews.comment: LOVE this mic!  I got it on sale on amazon for just 225.00 US  and it has been GREAT!!  Sounds awesome on elgato streamdeck+ XLR dock AND the BEACN Studio!!
reviews.author: Barneyjack

reviews.title: 175 dollars?
reviews.comment: THIS IS A STEAL!! The Yeti Studio is an "SM7b" esque microphone with its look and with how it's been EQ'd out of the box.  This microphone is definitely deeper or "muddier" tone than the SM7b but that can work on some voices but better yet since this is about 90% of the way of a SM7b, it can definitely be EQ'd well. It's built well and is quite heavy giving it a "quality" feeling. Not only that, because of the preamp in this microphone, you can use this with a cheap audio interface (Using it on a Behringer UMC22 and you can get very little preamp noise from your interface due to the preamp in the mic). If you can find it at around 200 dollars or less, it's a steal. 250 dollars, depends on what you're looking for in a microphone. 350 dollars? I recommend not getting it, at that price point you can find better microphones or you're most likely going to get an SM7b.
reviews.author: Samuel W

reviews.title: Professional quality microphone
reviews.comment: By far the best microphone I've used. I primarily use it for gaming and it has not disappointed me. While on the more expensive side, especially when you include the XLR cable and audio mixer, It is a very good-sounding microphone that doesn't take much at all to set up apart from hooking it up.
reviews.author: Jacob

reviews.title: A modern Shure SM7B
reviews.comment: This microphone has been nothing short of fantastic. The sound quality is amazing and it's a decent step up from the microphone I used to have, the Wave 3. I use the Wave XLR as my interface and it sounds great. This microphone is very flexible in terms of tuneability and you can sound like anything you want. You can have a very neutral sound, or you can sound like a professional podcaster. The choice is yours. This microphone has some good weight to it. It really feels like you're using a quality product. You will need to provide your own XLR cable. I use the Elgato XLR cable and it works fine. I highly recommend this microphone if you're looking at a high quality device. The ONLY gripe I have is I wish it had better plosive protection, but just move the mic slightly off to the side and that resolves the issue without sacrificing quality.
reviews.author: Wesley

reviews.title: God of all gods
reviews.comment: This is -the- end game mouse pad. I literally bought it as a joke with full intentions on returning it. No way I'd ever spend $100 on a mouse pad, that's ridiculous. It feels like I'm dancing with people when playing FPS. I saw how big it was and was taken back. Okay, maybe that's why it's so expensive. Once I started using it, I realized why it was that much. I also have a glass textured "mouse pad" that is quite big, but not as big, that was $45. Look up "Vance Industries Frosted Grand Elite Mousepad review" on Overclock.net that I bought in 2014. My point is I've been a mouse pad nerd for over a decade lol. I also have a Razer Destructor 2 ($60), Manticor ($60), as well as dozens of cloth pads and various plastic pads, including CS Hyde. Also have a few aluminum pads. Never got into any Artisan cloth pads, but I think I know my stuff. Alright. So this thing is massive--which I like. It's also very soft with a fine texture. It's obviously going to wear away at your mouse feet. What's weird is, as the feet break in, they get smoother. It's like a new set of brake pads mating to rotors. I mean, we're talking about subjective feeling too. What I might like, you may not. It has very good static friction where is doesn't feel like your mouse is sticking, but it also has decent dynamic friction where you don't feel like you're playing on an air hockey table. It's beautiful, has a nice anti-slide backing, and doesn't feel cold like some aluminum pads can. All I have to say is that as long as you don't break this thing, it's going to last the rest of your life and then some.
reviews.author: Scharfschutzen

reviews.title: Amazing Mousepad. Highly recommend.
reviews.comment: Amazing mousepad in both user experience and performance. It is a little large(love that). At first it will feel a little off if you came from a cloth mousepad previously but after a few hours youll feel how much more precisely you can use the mouse and the feel to it becomes luxurious. It will shave away some of the mouse feet at first but then the mouse and pad get acquainted and it becomes a perfect amount of resistance soon after and the feet stop getting worn away. Once you get used to this mousepad and then switch back to a cloth mousepad for work or at a friends house youll feel like the cloth mousepad is terrible. Also this thing is magic in regards to staying clean; almost no matter what you do to it. A quick wipe without cleaner and its good to go and ive had mine for about 2 years. The razer viper or deathadder with the 8khz polling and a fast refresh rate monitor help to take advantage of  the extra precision you gain out of this mousepad. It might seem expensive but it is definitely worth it. It doesnt show any signs of wear after 2 years despite heavy use.
reviews.author: Kirk G.

reviews.title: Game-Changer Once You Get Used to It
reviews.comment: Absolutely love, love, love this thing. It felt weird at first coming from a regular mouse pad, but once you adjust, it’s hard to imagine going back. The glide is insanely smooth and consistent—no friction, no slow spots, just clean movement every time. It makes tracking feel more precise, especially in fast-paced games. The surface also stays the same no matter the temperature or humidity, which is a huge upgrade over cloth pads. Another big plus is how easy it is to clean. Dust, sweat, and grime don’t soak in—you just wipe it down and it’s back to brand new. The build quality is top-tier too, feels premium and solid without flexing or wearing out. If you’re serious about your setup or just want something that feels different (in a good way), this is 100% worth trying. Once you get used to it, you won’t want to go back.
reviews.author: Hamza Ramić

reviews.title: Amazing Mouse Pad!!
reviews.comment: I've been using gigantus and strider xxl mousepads cloth, they are both amazing. Since new hardpads been released lately and razer made Atlas. I insta ordered it. Why? Tempered glass Smooth, Friction almost non existent controlling is amazing! You feel like your hand is gliding and it goes Wruuum without any obstecals. But theres always bats :( You gotta be careful with it very careful. Also the glass is cold and when u sweat it leaves prints of skin and u gotta fiber cloth it time to time. I am using simple fiber cloth as sleeve and its very fine cheap one. Good cleaner is fiber cloth in ur home kitchen. Overall the product is an  Theater Experience its WORTH A BUY!! The mouse u see its Deathadder v3 Pro. Epic Combo :D very Happy with this purchase thanks razer and amazon!!
reviews.author: Ted

reviews.title: My new favorite mousepad!
reviews.comment: This is an amazing mousepad, I just love how smooth and sturdy it feels compared to a more traditional cloth pad. It is slightly thicker than your average mousepad, but it makes up for that in the quality of the material. Tempered glass will never scratch or chip as long as you’re not placing metal or other glass items on it. It comes in black and white, I got mine white to match my desk. It will make your mouse feel like an air hockey puck, perfect for low DPI gaming! I combo this with my DeathAdder V3 and I’ve never had a better setup.
reviews.author: Enubix

reviews.title: Great item for the price!
reviews.comment:
I'm really enjoying this mouse pad so far from Razer. No unnecessary frills and it gets the job done.
I like the little Razer logo on the corner, subtle and sleek. I was a little disappointed when I saw the size of it once I pulled it out of the box, but that's my bad for not reading the dimensions closely.
I adjusted to the smaller size right away during my gaming session. It's a regular mouse pad size, which isn't bad for me, I was just used to having a bigger mouse pad previously and it threw me off for only a short moment.
Honestly, it's nice having more space on my desk compared to when I had the bigger mouse pad!
The tracking on this mouse pad is excellent, it's working beautifully with my mouse. I also like that this mat is nice and thin, not too thick like some pads, so it doesn't stick too high up off of my desk, which is a plus for me.
Overall, I highly recommend this product. Just be aware that it's your basic mouse pad size, if that concerns you when it comes to gaming.
It's working great for me, no complaints at all. Would buy again!
reviews.author: Kane A. Smith

reviews.title: Cheap Price, Quality Product
reviews.comment: It’s a mystery to me why poorly made mousepads with bulky, uneven stitches on the side sell when such a quality mousepad exists for the same price. The mousepad is thin, very comfortable to use and lay your hand on, and has very good anti-slip material on the bottom. The subtle black etched logo makes for a very clean and professional aesthetic. This mousepad is a great choice for both gaming and work.
reviews.author: Irena

reviews.title: Very nice but a little large
reviews.comment: I had the 2013 version of this mousepad that started to fall apart. The green rubber back started to get sticky and it got stuck on things. Since it was such a good pad I decided to get this as a replacement. The new one is just as good as I remember.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: SteelSeries QcK vs Razer Goliathus Mobile vs iXCC Smooth Silk Stitched vs Glorious Stitched
reviews.comment:
This is a comparison review between the SteelSeries QcK, Razer Goliathus Mobile, iXCC Smooth Silk Stitched, and Glorious Stitched mousepads.
Surface uniformity: the SteelSeries, Razer, and iXCC are perfectly uniform as far as I can tell. The Glorious has some nicks as you drag a mouse across it, and resistance varies slightly by angle.
Surface resistance: surprisingly to me, there’s a big difference. The SteelSeries and Razer are relatively high, the Glorious in the middle, and the iXCC the lowest. The difference is enough that hitting a stationary mouse with a constant amount of force moves it about twice as far on the iXCC as the SteelSeries or Razer.
Using mouseaccuracy.com, I found that I perform best with the higher resistance of the SteelSeries or Razer. With a low-resistance pad you’ll spend more time going from “cursor is moving fast near the target” to “cursor is in the target”; with a high-resistance pad you need more force to move the same distance. I found that I’m better able to compensate for the latter than the former, so, my mousing performance improves with a higher-resistance pad.
Durability: I bought the SteelSeries in 2013 and the other three a few days ago. The SteelSeries degrades severely within a few years: moderate warping, cloth peeling off, crumbling rubber backing, dirt that can’t be scrubbed out. The Razer appears to have the same construction. The Glorious has stitched edges, but they’re somewhat rough and thick, forming a rim around the pad. The iXCC’s stitching is the same height as the rest of the pad, softer, and more uniform.
Thickness: Razer 2/32 in, Glorious center 3/32 in, Glorious rim 4/32 in, iXCC 7/32 in. Measured with a tape measure, so assume some imprecision. I don’t find that thickness makes a difference to me, but I do rub against the Glorious’ rim.
Conclusion: out of my three new pads, I’m choosing the Razer for its surface, but I expect it to degrade quickly. The iXCC has great build quality, but I can’t perform as well on its surface.

reviews.title: The NAS Purchase You Shouldn't Be Debating Any Longer
reviews.comment: I will start by saying I have been in enterprise IT and software all my life, so my needs requirements and standards may vary from the average home user.  That being said, I believe in bang for the buck, and the DXP8800 delivers above and beyond its competition for the price point (as long as you equip it accordingly). I have finished the burn in and testing period with this NAS and I am extremely satisfied.  I purchased this to move off of my aging 6x6TB WD I7 32gb NAS cube.  The UGOS Pro operating system has come a long way and as of this review it is mature and handles everything you will likely be throwing at it except for the most advanced enterprise use cases where this device as a whole wouldn't be considered. My DXP8800 setup is as follows beyond factory delivery:  96gb Crucial Ram, 6x16TB WD Red Pro Spinning Disk, 1x WD 850 2tb nvme, 1x WD 850 1TB nvme, 2x Noctua NF-12 fans.  While I considered moving to TrueNAS, I have found the UGOS pro native operating system to be more than sufficient for my advanced needs.  Despite what you might find in older research, UGOS pro is natively seeing all my RAM and making use of it in Cache (previously the synopsis was UGOS pro was capping at 64gb, no longer the case) Let's start with the drives:  I went with WD Pro because while I primarily stream media, I stream it in 4k and this is my primary use for this NAS (plex >70% use).  I also use the device for Time Machine backups which was especially easy in UGOS pro OS for setup.  These drives are going to run hotter and noisier than the WD Red plus drives and equivalent because they are basically enterprise drives.  My NAS is in my home networking area, so noise wasn't an issue but to be honest these drives click and grind and while you dont want to have this sitting next to your desk, the reality is a NAS of this size should not be sitting at your desk.  I also appreciate the enterprise reality of things that most consumers don't consider:  the WD pro drives have internal vibration controls which mitigate issues when co-habitating with other devices spinning in the same case at 7200 RPM.  The DXP 8800 with these drives alone can saturate the 10gbe connection, but the additional warranty, addition of the helium barrier etc make it worth it vs the plus drives alone.  It's your data, and if you are running a NAS to begin with you run a lot of it and integrity is important to you.  Dont cheap out. Let's talk NVME:  I run all my docker and VM's on the low speed port of the NVME side of the bus with my 2tb WD 850 nvme.  I chose the versions with heatsinks for both NVME's and they fit fine so it was worth the upgrade.  I also used the big thick pads provided by Ugreen to make contact with the NVME heatsinks and the case to improve cooling performance however marginal.  Important to note that I chose NVME with onboard DRAM so there was less processor interaction with data compute.  For this device, my research concluded that onboard DRAM would play a role and I dont regret the decision despite the extra head and +1=1.5w of additional power. I am running the 1tb NVME as a cache drive in the high speed slot, but so far have seen no utilization of cache (so consider your real needs).  The large 30gb media files I am typically streaming are never going to make it to cache.  I am going to leave it in place for now as I move to more smaller files and leverage the storage more across my home, but as of now I dont regret the cache purchase but am seeing no real world improvement thus far.  If you are using TrueNAS you can force a more specific use of the cache, but then you are maintaining an L2ARC tuning environment that as nerdy as I am, I dont see a real-world home use for.  Let's be realistic, this is a Home/SMB NAS, and a very good one.  But if you are trying to throw this in your business enterprise you should be x10'ing your budget and go with something enterprise. Another thing I have come to see debated is noise levels:  for the purposes of this review I will reiterate that anyone looking at an 8-bay NAS really shouldn't be parking it on their desk.  That being said, lets talk real noise world statistics as noise and heat dissipation are unwisely not discussed simaltanseously :  I already discussed why my drives are noisy and if you drop down to WD Red plus drives at 5400 rpm they will never make noise, that I can attest to even with my old 6TB 5400 plus drives.  So let's talk fan noise:  I have upgraded both fans to the Noctua industrial NF-F12 fans.  With the stock fans, I was seeing ~40C per spinning disk and ~42C per NVMW idle / light load temps in the fan's "default" setting (meaning the system controls based on temperature, vs low or full fan setting). In full-fan mode, the stock fans can drop the same idle/light load temps to ~36C and the NVME's to ~40C.  Not terrible, well within operating specs and I am comfortable the stock fans would carry my current setup under load so for most users esp those not using the big fat pro drives I am using, will be fine.  The stock fans are impressive and not as loud as I expected running in "full" mode. I still chose to upgrade to Noctua, not only because I have been using them in most of my builds for year but also because they are the best at what they do.  After the upgrade, I put the drives under load and yes these fans are very loud at "full" setting (but still below typical IT server levels).  However, at heavy load with these fans cranking my drives never got above 40C and my NVME never above 47C.  At idle with "full" fan setting, these fans keep the drives at 22C !!!  In default mode (ie systems controlled) my spinning disks are sitting at 32C and my NVME at 36C with idle to light loads.  Anyone moving towards loading this chassis beyond 5 disks should perform this very inexpensive and easy upgrade. For those interested in Plex, I have had no problems testing a down-convert (heavy) transcode of 4k to 1080p plus audio and found that pulling from an Apple TV 4K has no performance issue whatsoever.  The new i5 in this machine despite being technically a mobile processor spec, holds its own better than my old system by a large margin. Unless you are transcoding 5+ streams at once (at which point this NAS is not your use case) you will not need an external GPU or anything to carry you forward in the near future.  Plex performance has been monumental on this system in a docker container. As I mentioned earlier, while I am an advanced user I dont see the merit in moving off UGOS pro for SMB or Home use at this point no matter how advanced your needs are.  I wish one of the big tech bloggers would let the world know how far this OS has come in a year vs what the forums represent.  It supports VM's, dockers, all SAN NFS and attachment requirements now for use cases that you shouldn't even have for a device like this, but it does it and does it well.  Drive sleep works great, performance is solid, backups are easy and integration and navigation for people who dont really understand remote storage like they think they do is a god send for the prosumer.  You can accomplish very advanced tasks in UGOS pro without risking breaking something because you dont really know what you are doing. I cannot comment on the smaller enclosures first-hand, but I do know that Ugreen 6 bay and 8 bay are identical in terms of my use case and review.  The smaller docks do make some changes, but I believe most users will see results better to if not equal to what you will get on Synology or Qnapp.  I expect those vendors to pivot hard with new offerings coming in the next year, but I dont see them getting to this price point any time soon if ever. Build quality is extremely important, and Ugreen made this thing more aesthetically pleasing than it needs to be but my thanks anyways.  I found it very easy to work on, well constructed and thoughtful to meet the needs surpassing what someone looking at this NAS should be using it for. Performance has met specs.  There are a lot of people out there talking about network, disk etc but these are highly environmentally variable.  I have not performed any advanced or undercover configs or tuning with my setup on UGOS pro and despite the zero cache utilization I can saturate a 10gbe port which lets face it is amazing at this price point.  Your mileage will 100% vary on your setup, but I spent more on drives than the NAS itself:  I understand my use case.  FYI there is value in having 2x10gbe bandwidth available to your NAS even though your devices individually arent 10gbe, but again it varies on your use case.  My Apple TV will soak a full line 1gbe if I let it streaming the right content, no problem for any network unless other things are also making similar requests. In conclusion, the is s a recommended buy:  you just cant go wrong for the price/performance and whatever it is you think you might be missing you arent.  If you genuinely are, this is not the hardware category you should be shopping. The below is a list of my upgrades and where to find them on amazon: FANS: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B00KFCRATC?ref=ppx_yo2ov_dt_b_fed_asin_title RAM: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0C79K5VGZ?ref=ppx_yo2ov_dt_b_fed_asin_title&th=1 NVME: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0B7CKZGN6?ref=ppx_yo2ov_dt_b_fed_asin_title&th=1 Hard Drives: https://www.amazon.com/Western-Digital-16TB-Internal-Drive/dp/B08K3VVKSW/ref=sr_1_1?crid=31QE24X27ZDJ8&dib=eyJ2IjoiMSJ9.dIpadfnImZ7C_0Kqqte1uAL9l3bBfISZMpN4Lm9RnDEI4XsNq2vZ3AKDZwyLljcoO7BXeIcKmOApaZoVB3YMBA1r3D33x5vcDCFmY3N_3y2kyw27LwYZ_-QeP0S-qgwDiRmYRbVBXSbVRttmEA4UM4wDcHPyh6p-7Icu8nIz0fTMOcKt47RdNHpiKtjXZZvvZ0deFR1dA5Fc6y8eordLZ0u1v9iFEy_6cpXbqFDWJGo.uO4pURF5JM1_nzSspjXBlnFqFI3ud5JH-W258FIWLwo&dib_tag=se&keywords=wd%2Bpro%2B16tb&qid=1753114536&sprefix=wd%2Bpro%2B16tb%2Caps%2C157&sr=8-1&th=1

reviews.title: Nice design, solid hardware, software basic but enough for NAS
reviews.comment: This is very nicely designed and built device. It has a quality feel and has all of the I/O ports that you'd expect - including two 10GBase-T ports that can be lagged together and two thunderbolt ports for external storage. It has slots for two M.2 NVME SSDs, that are used for caching - R/W caching uses the two SSDs in mirroring mode (RAID 1), otherwise it is RAID 0. RAM can upgraded - despite the printed RAM limits, I am using 96GB and it works fine. The setup process is straightforward. The software is clearly a "work in progress", although it has enough for a basic multi-protocol RAID NAS, accessible from Windows, MacOS and Linux./ There are some glaring omissions - such as no ability to send email alerts/alarms to the administrator- you can work around by adding your own email logic to the Linux platform, which is accessible via ssh - But this shouldn't be necessary and will probably be undone by system updates. I am using a fairly simple Python script and gmail. The user "admin" is reserved and not in /etc/passwd, it is unavailable for assignment and I'm slightly concerned that this is the basis of recovery access to the device which I would normally lock down by setting my own passwords. ugreen RAID is built using Linux mirroring/RAID functionality, and the relevent Linux commands are available via ssh. I'm happy with my purchase and would recommend it.

reviews.title: Great NAS for those with a large media collection to put on server
reviews.comment: Great NAS for beginner with plenty of room to grow due to the more capable processor, 2-10Gb Ethernet ports, Thunderbolt 4 and USB 3.2. Only couple of drawbacks is that it only comes with 8GB of RAM.  I upgraded mine to 32GB with a 2-16GB Crucial set.  It will support up to 64GB, but some memory modules have been problematic though no problems with my Crucial DDR4-5600MHz Second drawback is noise but this is an 8-bay NAS and if you have near fully loaded its going to click away especially during large write operations. There's a lot good information available on UGREEN's site and others on how to configure apps, docker containers and virtual machines.  In the end its an extremely useful machine.  Using the bulk of mine (currently with 7-24TB drives) as a media server with over 1500 movies that are mostly comprised of 1080p and 4K-HDR rips (no quality reduction) and lossless audio.  Also have about 30 TV shows on it.  Running Plex Server to supply my household displays but also using a Zidoo Z9X Pro in my home theater.  144TB of storage with the 7-drives in RAID5 (one drive parity).  Started with 6 drives and have since added one more.  I'm pretty much caught up on ripping my collection so I don't anticipate filling the remaining space anytime soon.

reviews.title: Excellent TrueNAS System!
reviews.comment: TL;DR: Excellent 8 bay system for use as a TrueNAS box. Very premium build quality and feel, well packaged with great features. Worth it on sale ($1199.99), but not at MSRP in my opinion. Who this is for: This is a great NAS for someone who doesn’t want to build their own NAS from parts but also doesn’t want to be locked into a pre-built OEM NAS OS. You can install TrueNAS, UnRaid or any other OS you like, it’s not locked down. It’s got a reasonably powerful yet efficient CPU, but its strength in specs is expandable DDR5 RAM, an included 128GB SSD for the OS, 2x M.2 NVMe SSD slots and an open PCIe slot for expansion. The dual 10Gb NIC’s are on board and seem to perform well. I added 96GB RAM to mine, which works great (CT2K48G56C46S5). Added 2x 4TB Klevv NVMe SSD’s for small files/app storage (in ZFS mirror) and added 8x 28TB Seagate Exo’s HDD’s to the bays in a ZFS Z2 pool allowing for 2 drive failure tolerance. I was able to use the PCIe slot to add the card included with a QNAP TL-D400S DAS 4 bay enclosure. This worked with 0 effort under TrueNAS. I put my old 8TB Seagate Iron Wolf NAS drives in a ZFS Z2 pool to use for backups/photos storage. TrueNAS see’s these as separate drives, serials numbers and all…basically works like internally connected drives thanks to using an SFF-8088 cable to connect to the PCIe SATA card. The build quality is far better than the QNAP TS-664 its replacing. Metal exterior, drive sleds while not enterprise sturdy seem well engineered and should stand up to infrequent “homelab” use. Many small engineering, attention to detail touches that feel premium. Like the included fully metal, magnetic dust filter for the back. I have it connected to a 10Gb switch and its handling things very well. What I don’t like about the NAS, and really it’s not a big deal…access to the PCIe slot is an ordeal. You have to take out all the HDD drives, remove the bottom access door to the SSD/RAM, remove the screws/feet, remove like 6 screws on the back and then like 4 more inside. Then you can slide the shell off to get to the PCIe slots. A good 5-10 minute process. I can’t speak to the included OS, didnt try it at all. I did a firmware update, let it reboot and then installed TrueNAS in place of the included OS. The only reason not to buy this if it meets your requirements is the price. At almost $1500 I think the appeal of self building really stands out. You can build a system for roughly that price, exactly as you want it with less compromises using all standard brand new parts. When the price drops $200-300 then it becomes really compelling. I managed to get it for $1199.99 during Prime sale and am happy I did. At that price you get 1 warranty/return policy covering everything. I would highly recommend it

reviews.title: Great Keyboard
reviews.comment:
I got this keyboard to replace my old membrane one, and so far this one is amazing. The keys are easy to remove and replace, the backlight works and offers a multitude of colors and effects, and the software provided allows for easily created custom macros. The clicking sound is not too loud and the little resistance on the keys is quite nice.
The size is relatively average, and the shape of the keys have a slight tilt towards the bottom of the keyboard. I find that I tend to accidentally hold down keys while gaming because of the shape of the keys. This is no fault to Redragon, however.
I will add that they were quick to rectify a manufacture error and replace the first keyboard that arrived—the backlight on some keys weren’t working. Fortunately, the replacement has been perfect.

reviews.title: Redragon is the Perfect Balance of Affordability, Functionality, and Fun!
reviews.comment:
This is overall an excellent keyboard choice. Redragon has consistently proved itself a real comptetitor in the keyboards and peripherals markets -- Their products hold up well to comptetitors such as "Hyper-X" and "Logitech". What I've found is that Redragon consistently offers a delicate balance of affordable value, functionality, and absolute fun. They have an incredible array of products to meet everyone's needs and expectations, whether it be avid gamers and PC professionals alike.
As a loyal Redragon consumer, I have rarely had issues with their product line, however, in this instance there was some damage to the exterior packaging, but it seems directly attributed to poor-handling as sometimes happens -- This is one of many Amazon products participating in the sustainable program, so it does not arrive in extra-padded packaging. This is not the fault of Redragon and therefore doesn't effect my star-rating.
As a mention, I would also like to see the RGB backlighting perhaps improved on this model as well -- While it is fully customizable as it relates to lighting and patterns (with or without Redragon Software), the brightness threshold is lower than most of us enthiusasts would like -- Especially those who find themselves gaming or working in less
than optimal lighting conditions.
Additionally, given that this keyboard has hot-swappable keycaps and switches, perhaps Redragon will include the all-in-one dual-sided pulling tool in the future, rather than a separate keycap puller and U-shaped tool which is included with this model. The all-in-one puller tool is much more functional and effective in my experience. In fact, Redragon does include this tool with many of their keyboards.
I brought these minor concerns to the attention of Redragon, to which they were very receptive and understanding. They backed up their quality product with a replacement. That too is something that really stands out with Redragon, they take customer satisfaction seriously. Thanks for reading and allowing me to share my thoughts and experiences with the K671 keyboard.
reviews.author: Bryan H

reviews.title: Redragon Mechanical Gaming Keyboard—Reliable Build but Noticeable Noise
reviews.comment:
The Redragon mechanical keyboard is a well-built and sturdy piece of hardware. The 11 programmable backlit modes offer great customization for those who enjoy a personalized desk aesthetic, and the hot-swappable feature is a significant plus, allowing for easy maintenance or future switch upgrades. It feels durable and provides the tactile feedback many users look for in a mechanical setup.
However, it is important to note that this keyboard is definitely not silent. Mechanical switches are known for their distinct sound, and this model is no exception—it produces a clear, audible "clack" with every keystroke. For someone specifically seeking a quiet or discreet typing experience to avoid disturbing others or for use in a focused environment, the noise level here may be a drawback.
Bottom Line: A high-quality, customizable keyboard that performs well for gaming and heavy typing. It’s a solid choice if you enjoy the classic mechanical feel, but if a silent workspace is your priority, you will find this model much louder than expected.

reviews.title: Darling of reviewers, with a few small caveats
reviews.comment: There's not much else positive that can be said about this affordable workhorse. I appreciate the classic looks and color scheme, as I specifically purchased this to get away from the psychedelic disco ball seizure inducing effect of the RGBs on my previous mechanical keyboard. It's well built, has reliable actuation and works flawlessly with Bluetooth or wired. I appreciate that the USB-C port is on the left side, the muted thwack sound (but not the mushy rebound) and the battery life is excellent using Bluetooth. I recommend using a 5v wallwart charger initially, otherwise it takes forever to bring it to 100%. Complaints Configured for boutique OS usage out of the box, and you have to swap out keys to use for Windows. Apple is only a tiny segment of the desktop market, and I'm glad it will work on multiple OS', the 75%-90% of users shouldn't have to unbox and then pull keys and flip switches to utilize their keyboard. There is a rubberized coating on the key caps that doesn't seem like it will hold up long term and the keyboard always looks like you've been snacking on corn chips because normal skin oils leave smudges. There is an annoying input lag when the keyboard comes out of sleep. Despite disabling power management in the device manager, the LEDs time out and the first few keystrokes do not register, which makes for an annoying experience when you attempt to login when the machine is locked.
