reviews.title: Absolutely wonderful keyboard
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/F1ep9I8osyL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/61wiyc7AIqL._SY256.jpg I bought this little keyboard as a secondary board to go with my tablet/laptop when I'm writing away from my main computer. I have a Mercury K1 Lite as my main keyboard and I wanted something similarly creamy. It's the fourth mechanical keyboard I have ordered (my partner has a Keychron C2 Pro 8k) and it impressed me for the price point. It was on sale and had a coupon and I am beyond pleased for what I paid for it, but it would be well worth the retail price (but just wait for a sale!). This replaced a Womier Q61 V2 which retails at over $50. That keyboard had a terrible case ping that I couldn't stand, the keys were plasticky and too slick, and the switches were wobbly and just sort of sluggish. It was creamy sounding yet hollow, and it felt bad enough that I returned it to get this one. The case was also a weird plastic foggy kind of color that just reminded me of dried glue.
Out of the box, this keyboard is very impressive. The switches are creamy, clacky, and a bit thocky. Good travel, and the stem wobble is noticeable (to me) but it's not as bad as the switches that came stock with my Mercury. To the average person that doesn't feel like swapping switches out of the box and is fine with a lighter touch, this thing is perfect. What I did though took it to the next level. I swapped in some Akko Green Fogs into the alphas and spacebar so far and it just made the best sounding keyboard I have heard (and I've listened to a lot of keyboard videos lately and spent a lot of time swapping switches on boards). For me, it somehow hits creamy, clacky, and a bit of thocky all at once. Not everyone likes heavier switches, but the review shows what they sound like versus the stocks. I have fibro and EDS and for me a heavier switch with a shorter travel I can float on causes less joint pain than lighter switches or tactiles. I think I accidentally stumbled across my endgame board in my secondary board.
I loved the case. Felt very solid with good, thick plastic. I'm actually not a fan of metal cases so this was a plus for me.
The keycaps are also surprisingly sturdy. They're solid, they stick to the switches well (a little too well) and I was going to replace the keycaps because this isn't my favorite colorway, the pink is a bit coral and the blue is a bit country cottage blue, but without spending as much as or more than the board itself I doubt I would be able to find nicer keycaps. They feel better than Keychron OEM and the Cherry keycaps on my Mercury, and certainly better than the smooth shiny keycaps that came on the Womier.
Regarding RGB - some reviews say the RGB is a little weak and this is why. The switches that come stock do not have very good RGB diffusal. They are opaque plastic, whereas the Akko Green Fogs are transparent housing. So, I get the gripe, and if RGB being a little weaker on the bottom bothers you and you don't want to swap switches that's fair, there are other keyboards out there, but none at this price point for the value imo. But if you're comfortable swapping switches, you can find transparent top housing switches for around $20 to replace the whole board if the RGB is that important. I think for the price point the switches they include make sense - something that works well enough for the user not interested in swapping switches that saves money on the board itself. I didn't have any issues with RGB brightness or being able to read the keys in either bright light or low light with RGB on and off.
All in all, out of the box this is a wonderful keyboard that rivals more expensive keyboards for the sound and the feel. With the addition of the Akko Green Fogs, this keyboard is an absolute dream.
reviews.author: E. S.

reviews.title: Exactly what I wanted
reviews.comment: This was exactly what I was looking for in a wireless keyboard. The brightness is perfect, the keys and the keyboard are the perfect size. The quality of the keyboard in general is wonderful, this might be my new brand of gaming keyboards to buy. I love the way the keyboard looks, I love how simple it is to set up, I aboslutley love the color, it looks so much better in person then it does in the image, and I love how quite the keys are compared to the last keyboard I had. The backlight function is really nice and easy to you. I will more than likely buy from this company again in the future.
reviews.author: Debra Foulk

reviews.title: A really nice value, feature packed, and great feeling, gaming wireless keyboard.
reviews.comment:
I needed a replacement keyboard, to replace an older failing logitech K400r membrane.  Very nice build quality. Bright LED Backlit through the keycaps to see the characters.  Selectable for 2.4Ghz wireless w/provided dongle, or Bluetooth, which means you can use this keyboard on two different systems if you like, just switch to Bluetooth once paired with the other system.  Long battery life, and fast charging with the provided USB-C cable, which also the keyboard can be used in wired mode as well.
The keyboard is very sturdy, and the keys are nice feel with medium to light pressure of the Mint Mombo switches and the sound is very thocky too, not annoying clicky.  You will be highly satisfied once you start to use this great keyboard.
Comes with stickers, key cap and key switch puller, 4 additional Mint Mambo key switches, 2.4 Ghz USB dongle, USB-C to USB-C/USB-A adapter cable.
reviews.author: Finn

reviews.title: Good keyboard at a reasonable price.
reviews.comment: This keyboard has been great to me. I love the design and layout and the click of the keys is very satisfying. Works perfectly as described.
reviews.author: oob

reviews.title: Cutest creamy keyboard ever!
reviews.comment: My favourite keyboard in the world it is very comfortable and very pleasing to use. I love creamy keyboards and this keyboard is perfect. The connectivity is easy. The lighting and backlight are awesome because you can change them. I would totally recommend this for any egirl out there.
reviews.author: Tina M Taylor

reviews.title: Wonderful
reviews.comment: Picked this up for the volume and player controls as well as the macro keys.  The lighting is a bonus, and compliments the Razer mouse i have, functionally as well as visually.  I wouldn't recommend the clicky keys if keyboard is to be used for a lot of typing
reviews.author: Mark

reviews.title: Not a great start.
reviews.comment:
Keyboard came poorly packaged, as others here have mentioned.  8 keys were in the bag w/ the keyboard.  Essentially the bottom left corner keys.  No big deal, reassembled.  But the keyboard lags, skips, and repeats key presses.  Tried w/ and w/o Synapse.  Raised and lowered the response timing.  Nothing fixed.  Requested a swap.  Will update how that one turns out.
I've had my V1 FOREVER and I'm typing this review on it.  I just wanted one on my work pc.
reviews.author: Matt B.

reviews.title: Will need updated.
reviews.comment: Good keyboard. When it first arrived it was double typing letters alot. Almost like it wasn't following the synapse refresh rate. Went to razer and they had a firmware update that solved that issue. Shortly after using it though the D key stopped working everytime. Sent out for a return/replacement.
reviews.author: Melinnie

reviews.title: Clickity Clacky Keyboard
reviews.comment: Durable, clickety clackety keyboard. Good input, stylish.
reviews.author: K

reviews.title: Does not function well
reviews.comment: This keyboard has an issue with adding additional letters when used for typing. For example, when I hit the letter "t", it will come out "tttt" instead of just one "t". I have tried updating my computer as well as changing and playing around with the keyboard settings, and nothing has worked. It seems to only have this issue with the left side of the keyboard.
reviews.author: Cole

reviews.title: Great keyboard
reviews.comment:
I wanted a 100% keyboard and found the GMMK 3.  I liked the white color (not for everyone, but why do all the keyboards need to be black?) and realized there are a lot of customizations I could add (will look into that later - keycaps probably first).  I have now been using for about 24 hours and I am extremely happy with the keyboard.  I really like he click feel (Fox switches are the standard).  It has grown on me (not naturally into the click sound) over the years and these hit the right level for me (I don't understand all the ways that people describe switches, I just know I like these - seem pretty straight forward).  The build quality is solid and the included keycaps are pretty nice (will change them because I want to put more of a unique feel to the board).
Overall I highly recommend.  I went with the 100% as I wanted the numpad, if I didn't I would have gone with the 75%.
Oh, and it looks good on my black large mousepad, though I am considering switching that to a white mousepad (just worried about how often I would need to clean it).
reviews.author: Ben

reviews.title: Very nice keyboard
reviews.comment: Feels great, and I like the modularity
reviews.author: Dylan Roberson

reviews.title: Service
reviews.comment: Awesome book
reviews.author: Jerimiah Zeigler

reviews.title: Love this keyboard!
reviews.comment: I love this keyboard! It makes me happy every time I go to work. Love the colors and customization. I changed the keys and they are quiet but responsive.
reviews.author: Angiemo03

reviews.title: Awesome
reviews.comment: Worth my purchase!
reviews.author: Nathan

reviews.title: Top notch!!!
reviews.comment: For context, I work from home and pivot between a windows and mac. The initial connectivity was incredibly seamless. The feel, the look, the size, the strokes are all phenomenal. I had to do no remapping even when using hot keys for a lot of my day to day stuff on both operating systems, worked with just a flip of a switch. I love the size as its smaller than a full traditional keyboard but has a full size feel. No bezel just makes it look so clean. Additionally, I tried to find other brand keyboards and they were not even remotely as seamless and luxurious as this keyboard. I cannot recommend enough!! I haven't even gotten into their native software for the hardware but I am sure that will impress me even more.
reviews.author: Rue Rue

reviews.title: Very happy.
reviews.comment: Keychron is a credible company. Watch some youtube videos and look at the extensive catalog on their website. Excellent keyboard overall. I am used to laptop keyboards and low profile standalone keyboards, so I didn't want a full-travel mechanical keyboard. This one provides the ideal key travel, allowing for fast typing and Fortnite gaming. Glad I went with the Max rather than Pro given the added sound deadening. The keys aren't particularly noisy--they're the right volume. Got the brown switches, which feel great for both primary activities I use the keyboard for. The volume knob is also very nice, and I've programmed the key just to its left to mute and unmute video calls. The 96% layout is also just right. I don't feel like I'm losing any functionality from a 100% keyboard, but it fits nicer next to my mouse pad and looks more modern.
reviews.author: Nick

reviews.title: Mechanical Keyboard Convert
reviews.comment: I work from my keyboard all day and avid gamer  at night/weekends for decades.  I never really liked older mechanical keyboards.  Long travel, noisy, etc.  I always bought the flagshi model big brand name from the stores and liked that they were customizable via software.  I've since grown to hate the software, lack of repairability, and support.  When my last one finally started losing functionality in some keys I wanted something possibly repairable, more customizable and a solid brand.  Keychron is awesome so far and this opened a whole new world for me especially the level of hardware customization.  I love this size.  It takes a bit of getting used to but allows me all of the keys I use daily in a smaller form factor on my desk. It is not too noisy, has a touch I like, can change or replace switches or caps and has a much more solid build than my old ones while remaining light.  I have only two small complaints.  The initial update for firmware took me a dozen or more attempts trying various ways to get it completed. The requirments and steps could be better.  The second is that you're kind of limited on keycaps options, as the low profile graviton switches and layout are unique.  Keychron has a few sets but not had any of the show through ones I want in stock.  If it is really important to you to have more available options on caps this might not be the keyboard for you.
reviews.author: ScubaScott

reviews.title: The perfect Keyboard with loads of upgrade potential. Here is my custom build!
reviews.comment: So far so good! Here is my K17 Max (RGB) and the two modifications I made to it: 1) replace the Gateron low-profile Tactile brown switches with Gateron low-profile *Silent* Reds linear switches, and 2) Womier low-profile shine-through keycaps. See video for details. Note! The knob cap CAN be easily removed and replaced/customized. It uses a D-shaped stem connector. I was not able to find this information anywhere else on the internet. I look forward to putting a custom knob on this board in the near future.
reviews.author: Jenna

reviews.title: I love this keyboard!
reviews.comment: This is my most favorite keyboard!  I have Apple products… and have stuck with the Apple magic keyboard, which I love.  But I wanted to try mechanical keyboards because I kept hearing about how much people like them… especially those who type a lot (which I do for work, and personal as well).  So I tried the Lofree Flow Lite and Logitech MX mechanical.  I love low profile and that’s what I was looking for.  I like them both, but they were just not what I was looking for (feel wise).  However, now only does the Keychron K17 feel the BEST with typing experience, but I love the layout of the keyboard.  It has a full numeric pad with a normal “0” key, not a shortened key.  Plus it’s a full keyboard but just smaller (thus 96%).  The size is perfect and it’s small enough to still have space for my mouse on the side.  I love it and really enjoy it.  This is now my go to keyboard and I get excited just to even use it.
reviews.author: dlovestravel

reviews.title: great gadget that isn't necessary 😂
reviews.comment: Not an essential purchase, but it's beautiful. Besides having brighter LEDs than the previous version, the mouse glides beautifully. Overpriced? Definitely, but Razer makes a "gaming lifestyle product," so if you have other Razer products, this will be a great match.
reviews.author: Sam JL

reviews.title: Nice, solid pad for the Razer ecosystem!
reviews.comment: Smooth surface, my Razer Basilisk v3 glides over this thing! Pretty RGB effects too. A little pricey, but good value of you can get one on sale. Fits well on any desk. Thin enough not to be intrusive, too.
reviews.author: J. Lowery

reviews.title: Solid function with awesome aesthetics: a high quality product.
reviews.comment:
I gotta say I really do love this thing, but mainly for one big reason: the cable catch. It's simple but is very intuitively placed and quite incredible for a wired mouse. It really improves the feeling of a wired mouse. The surface of the mouse pad is quite nice. It's very smooth and my mouse glides across it. There are also no sharp feeling edges where the surface and LEDs meet, and it is kind on your wrist. Because the back of the mousepad has that rubber grippy material uniformly across it, it sits down perfectly flat on a desk and will not move easily with regular use. If you have sweaty hands you probably will not like the feeling of the mousepad for longer gaming sessions, but it is extremely easy to clean. The RGB on this is definitely the best I've seen on a mousepad. It has the most lighting zones and gets very bright. I run mine at around 50% brightness so it's not distracting when playing in the dark.
Overall the mousepad really just screams quality. The packaging is very nice, the unboxing experience is nice and easy. The braided cable feels extremely nice and fits snugly in USB ports. Even the cable management rubber tie thing feels nice. The mousepad surface feels good and is nice for both regular use and gaming. The LED lighting is, in my opinion, best in class and none of the other big manufacturers really come close. If I had to give it a con, I would say that the software isn't the best and it really is a bit daunting to use at times, but it's not really a big deal if you're using the lighting presets anyways. For $50 it is a pricy mousepad, but it really does feel like you are getting your money's worth out of it.
reviews.author: RedAsh

reviews.title: Best RGB Mouspad I have found on the internet
reviews.comment:
Right off the rip I can say I have scoured the internet and can't find a single mouse pad with RBG lights like these. Every mouse pad I've seen that is RGB simply changes the entire bar of light. This mousepad has multiple nodes of light inside allowing for a beautiful stream of rainbows or whatever color combinations you can imagine. The Razer Synapse program as well as the Chroma Studio are great. Chroma Studio works almost like photoshop allowing for insane levels of customization.
The quality of the mouse pad is great, I like that it's a hard surface personally. One complaint I have is that the pad tends to slide across the desk sometimes when I'm playing games. It needs to be readjusted often so the non-slip backing could have been executed better. It has a nice clip for your mouse wire to rest in allowing you to keep the wiring a bit more managed.
Overall, great mouse pad with probably the best RGB lighting you'll ever find online. IF anyone has found something of equal of better quality I'd love to know about them!
reviews.author: Michael

reviews.title: Great Item.
reviews.comment: Excellent item. Very smooth operation with Razor mouse. Nice colors on it. Worth the extra cash.
reviews.author: Devildog

reviews.title: Please buy worth every penny
reviews.comment: Love this microphone. I was kinda nervous buying a microphone again at this price since the last mic I had got that I thought was expensive was a dud, talking to you Jlab pro talk or whatever it was called, but this mic blew me away with how crystal clear it sound. very sensitive, this thing can hear a mouse fart, but for my studio vocal recording for my novel I cant think of anything I could want more than this. I also use it in USB mode which I have found no down fall to that at all. the durability is definitely something, it feels heavy and premium and sturdy for real. I get giddy everytime I get to use it bc I like to own nice things and this is definitely one of the nicest pro pieces of equipment I own. The setup was easy for my M4 Max mac studio and the functionality of everything was definitely plug and play. please buy this mic you will not regret it.
reviews.author: Kayla

reviews.title: Clean, Detailed Vocals with Studio-Level Clarity
reviews.comment: I’m using the RØDE NT1 5th Gen primarily to record my vocals, and the sound quality is immediately noticeable. The vocals come through very clean and detailed, without sounding harsh or overly processed. It captures natural tone and nuance, which makes it great for both singing and spoken voice. I really like the flexibility of having both XLR and USB outputs. It made setup easy right out of the box, and I can switch between interfaces depending on what I’m working on. The included shock mount and pop filter are solid and do their job well, helping reduce plosives and vibrations during recording. This microphone feels truly professional and well thought out. It’s quiet, reliable, and delivers consistent results, especially for vocal recording. If you’re serious about music production, podcasting, or any kind of vocal work, this is a high-quality mic that lives up to its reputation.
reviews.author: Kitkat's Kitchen

reviews.title: Great Budget Mic
reviews.comment: I got the Rode NT1 5th Generation as a birthday gift for my 19-year-old son, who is a college student and an aspiring artist, and I couldn’t have chosen a better microphone! From the moment he unboxed it, he was thrilled with the sleek silver design and the professional-quality build. Performance & Sound Quality Right out of the box, the NT1 delivers studio-grade clarity with an incredibly low noise floor. The warm, rich tone captures vocals beautifully, making it perfect for recording music, podcasts, and voiceovers. My son immediately noticed how crisp and detailed his voice sounded—no harshness, no distortion, just pure, natural audio. It picks up even the subtlest nuances, which makes it feel like a high-end mic at a mid-range price. Ease of Use & Connectivity One of the biggest highlights of the 5th Gen NT1 is its dual USB and XLR output, which makes it super versatile. As a college student with a limited setup, my son loves that he can plug it directly into his laptop via USB without needing an audio interface. When he’s in the studio, the XLR output lets him connect to professional equipment seamlessly. It’s truly a plug-and-play experience with zero learning curve, which is fantastic for beginners and pros alike. SM6 Shockmount & Pop Filter The included SM6 shockmount and pop filter are a huge plus. The shockmount does a great job of isolating the mic from vibrations, and the pop filter eliminates plosives, making recordings sound even cleaner. It’s a complete professional setup straight out of the box—no need to buy extra accessories. Final Verdict This microphone exceeded expectations and was the perfect gift for an aspiring artist. My son absolutely loves it and has been using it nonstop to record new music. Whether for home recordings, streaming, or professional studio use, the Rode NT1 5th Gen is an absolute winner. If you’re looking for a high-quality, future-proof mic for a budding musician, this is it. Highly recommended!
reviews.author: Bob Loblaw

reviews.title: Great for Podcasting and VO
reviews.comment: I am very happy with this mic. It sounds great and is super durable. I use it for music, podcasting, and voice over work. All in all, it's a great entry level mic for the price.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Excellent product
reviews.comment: Absolutely love this product. It exceeded my expectations in both quality and performance. Super easy to use and works flawlessly. You can tell it’s built to last. I’d definitely recommend this to anyone—great value for the money.
reviews.author: Lester

reviews.title: Perfect for video conference /online meetings
reviews.comment: I've had an "overhead" style mic arm in the past but I haven't used it in a while because it takes up too much space and conflicts with my monitor setup. For my video conferencing / online meetings, I've just been using the built in mic on my web cam, until I heard enough people tell me the audio wasn't that good. I recently saw an online review of this and didn't even realize that this lower style of mic arm existed. I decided to give it a try, and I really think it is perfect. Firstly, or where I clamp it onto my desk, it reaches exactly where I need it to be for perfect mic placement during my meetings. It stays low so I can even keep the mic out of the frame. The adjustability and flexibility are great, and the build quality is excellent. The cable management works well with the hidden wire space on the bottom of the arm. It did take me a bit to figoure out how to remove the magnetic panels - unless you know they are there, they are invisible, and it was tricky to pull them off to run the cable. Once you know how to do it, then it is fine, and you probably won't need to take them off often. The clamp to hold this onto the desk is very good. The inside of the clamp is padded so it won't damage the desk, and it can open very wide to accommodate a thicker desktop. The handle is ratcheted so if you are unable to spin the handle a full 360 degrees (which I could not) then you can still clamp this on. It is an excellent design and holds the arm firmly. The two-piece design of the arm makes it very flexible to place the mic at any angle. You can fold the arm back on itself to save space when you're not using it - this is much better than the "up and over" arms which are always in the way. There is also a small riser piece that you can either place on the clamp, or on the middle section where the two arm pieces meet, or leave it out entirely - this gives you a bit of flexibility as to how the arm pieces will sit. With the various attachment adapters included, you can attach different types of microphones or even other accessories such as lights or small cameras. Although it is a "mic arm", you can really use it to hold anything with a screw connector. The tension is adjustable and although I have not had to adjust mine at all for use with a standard vocal microphone, I have seen others adjust it to hold quite heavy items without sagging. My only niggle is that although this comes with an Allen wrench for adjustment and some mic adapters, there is no place to store them with the stand. I'd love to see a place near the clamp to be able to store the wrench and adapters when not in use. Now I have to find a place to put them and remember where they are. They do come in a small envelope so I suppose that I can simply tape that to the stand near the clamp where they are out of the way. PROS: * Build quality and finish are excellent * Very flexible in terms of positioning options * The low arm style is much better than the "up and over" style for many situations * Desk clamp is padded to prevent damage * Clamp handle is ratcheting to allow for installation under all mounting conditions * Comes with two adapters to adapt the holder for different mic mount sizes * Excellent cable management with undersize magnetic covers that hold tight and are invisible CONS: * No place to store the Allen wrench and mic adapters * Although the arms are height adjustable, you can't change their length. Shorter and/or longer replacement options might be nice as an additional accessory Conclusion: You might be able to find cheaper versions from other companies, but in my mind, it's worth it to pay a bit more to get this very high quality product.
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: Works Great Once You Get Used to It – Smooth, Clean, and Very Adjustable
reviews.comment: I got mine used and it works great. It felt a little weird at first because the low-profile design moves differently than a basic boom arm, but once I got used to it, I really liked it. Reviews and specs consistently praise this arm for its smooth gas-spring movement, quiet adjustments, hidden cable management, and strong all-metal build. It also supports up to 3 kg / 6.6 lbs, so it can handle heavier mics better than a lot of cheaper arms. The main downside is the price, and some people may need a little time to get comfortable with the way a low-profile arm positions compared with more traditional boom arms. Overall, it’s a very solid mic arm if you want a cleaner desk setup and smoother
reviews.author: jose navarrete

reviews.title: Fantastic Mic Arm
reviews.comment: The arm is great and the range of movement is really nice. I like the low profile and the ease of adjustment. It’s solid metal, and looks great, but it’s not too heavy. I would say it was well worth the purchase. You’re getting a quality product with this boom arm.
reviews.author: Brody Prudhomme

reviews.title: Great boom arm at a good price!  Even for pro use.
reviews.comment: Im not big on writing reviews, but my experience warranted sharing.  After trying many mic boom arms for my home office desk setup, I found this one to be by far the best.  I have an older Blue Yeti mic (1.5lbs) and I wanted an arm that can hold it overhead out of camera shot.  I also wanted one I could dynamically reposition without having to untighten and retighten a bunch of joints.  I tried several arms including from companies I would normally expect - from experience - to have great products, and was continually disappointed.  A professional studio would use a high end Yellowtec or OC White boom arm but for 3-5x the price.  What is available for the rest of us who need a good product without having to take out a second mortgage?  This boom arm is exactly what I was looking for.  I can put the mic exactly where I want it for a specific use case and it is very stable.  It makes no noise as you move it around and the spring tension is adjustable to the weight of the mic so it will stay where you put it.  It's a little skinnier than a high end arm but it is very adequate to the weight of something like a typical podcasting or vocal mic.  The skinny size makes it unobtrusive and the springs are internal which I prefer.  The magnetic cable covers are brilliant.  It can be mounted overhead or slide out from under your monitors.  Either way, it makes for a very clean and professional looking setup.  Super pleased!
reviews.author: Brian

reviews.title: A notable improvement over standard, but still room for more
reviews.comment: I own both a Rode PSA-1 and the standard Wave Arm LP. Of the three, this is definitely my favorite, but it does have some faults. First, the good things: -It uses the same desk clamp as everything else they sell, which is a great clamp. -It now includes a riser, which solves a problem I had with the original LP. Without the riser, the lower arm would bonk into my audio interface and get in the way of my keyboard. The riser raises it up enough to clear the interface, just barely clear a regular Stream Deck, and keep it far enough away from my keyboard that I could still type under it if I wanted, all without being so tall that it can't go under my monitor. -The ball joint where the mic attaches seems much stronger, especially with the new handle. While it wasn't a big deal, the original could still be moved even when fully tightened. This one holds very strongly. -Much improved magnets for cable management. These are NOT coming off unless you want them to. -Pneumatic upper arm for easier positioning! No more sagging because you've got an SM7B on there. Just a lot of little quality of life updates to an already great arm. But there are still a few things I would've liked to see: -The ball joint doesn't maintain position when adjusting the arm up or down. On the PSA-1, as you move the arm up or down, the mic stays level (or however you positioned it). That is not the case with this one. On the one hand, it's not that big of a deal as most streamers aren't going to be moving this up and down a lot; on the other hand, if it's not going to be moved a lot, there's no reason to have pneumatics in the first place, so you might as well have the mic stay level for the people that are actually going to want the pneumatics. Again, it's pretty minor, but still a con. -The lower arm does not have a hole on the top for the cable to come out of, which would have enabled even cleaner cable management. -The arms are not any wider than the original, which means you still can't hide a Fethead in the cable channels. I wish they made them just a smidge wider for that reason. -The joint covers are not keyed, which means they rotate freely. That does mean you can position them however you want, but it also means that you can't perfectly match the left and right sides to the same angle. I may be the only person who cares about that, though. All in all, a solid upgrade over the original and if you can afford it (the cost is also a con, really), it's definitely the one to get. But it does feel like they could've done a bit more market research or testing and fixed a few odd omissions.
reviews.author: Nick

reviews.title: The missing piece for my Dota 2 grind—no more desk-sliding mid-teamfight!
reviews.comment:
I’ve been stuck in my Dota 2 rank for a while now, and I finally realized my tiny, old office mousepad was holding me back. I upgraded to this SteelSeries XL "Speed" version specifically to give myself more runway for those quick edge-pans and micro-adjustments during chaotic teamfights. Honestly, it’s made a noticeable difference in how smooth my clicks feel when I'm trying to last-hit or blink-dagger out of trouble.
Usability & The Rank Grind: Since this is the XL size, it covers almost my entire desk area. I no longer have to worry about my mouse falling off the edge of the pad during a frantic retreat. It’s helped my consistency a ton, and I actually feel more "in the zone" now that my mouse has a uniform surface to move on.
Silky Smooth Glide: This is the "Speed" variant, and it definitely lives up to the name. My mouse feels like it’s floating. There’s just enough friction to feel in control, but it’s smooth enough that my wrist doesn't feel fatigued after a 60-minute marathon match.
Grip on the Table: One of my biggest pet peeves is a mousepad that wanders across the desk. This one has a heavy neoprene rubber base that basically "glues" itself to my wooden desk. Even when I’m getting a bit too aggressive with my mouse movements, this thing does not budge a single millimeter.
Quality & Feel: You can tell this isn't a cheap knock-off. The "Extra Density" (it's about 3.5mm thick) gives it a premium, cushioned feel that’s comfortable for my wrist. Plus, the stitching on the edges is super low-profile—it doesn't dig into my forearm like some other pads I've tried.
Pros & Cons
Pros:
Massive Surface: Plenty of room for your keyboard and mouse with space to spare.
Stitched Edges: These usually prevent that annoying "peeling" effect you see on cheaper pads after a few months.
Easy to Clean: I’ve already spilled a bit of water on it, and it wiped off pretty easily without soaking in instantly.
Cons:
The "New" Smell: Like most rubber-based pads, it has a bit of a "fresh tire" smell right out of the box. It faded after about two days, though.
Desk Real Estate: It’s big. Make sure you actually have the 34 inches of desk space before you buy it!
The Verdict
If you’re trying to climb the ranks in a MOBA like Dota or even a fast-paced FPS, this pad is a game-changer. It’s high-quality, stays exactly where you put it, and makes your mouse feel ten times more responsive. Easily 5 stars.
reviews.author: Jeggy

reviews.title: Great mouse pad
reviews.comment: So far this has been I great mouse pad. I use it both for home office work and for gaming. It is a nice dense pad that lays flat and is very smooth. My mouse glides smoothly across it. The thing I like most is the size - I didn’t necessarily need a mouse pad that was extra large but ended up being taken over by my keyboard. This was a great fit for a large mouse pad just for putting my mouse on. I’m able to easily move between 3 monitors and I have enough space to lower my DPI on my mouse and have that extra accuracy without running out of mouse pad space. Overall I am very pleased with the mouse pad.
reviews.author: Eric

reviews.title: Amazing value mouse pad!
reviews.comment: I've used various Razer, Glorious, and other "gamer" brand mouse pads for ~10 years now, and this is by far my favorite. Unless you're an absolute mouse pad snob, I don't see any reason to spend more than this much on any mouse pad. The feel is great, and the "speed" marketing is not just marketing... I legitimately needed to lower my sensitivity in games after switching to this pad. Although the mouse pad comes rolled up for shipping, it rolls out and flattens out pretty quickly; I used the pad right away with no issues and it was pretty flat over night. The thickness is pretty accurate to the provided product specifications, and the stitching is very tight and high quality. As a bonus, it doesn't even smell weird right out of the box!

reviews.title: Find something else. Norton is bloated, inefficient, adware, and nearly impossible to uninstall
reviews.comment: I have been a Norton (Symantec) user for about 10 years. As of 2023, I have had enough. I strongly recommend you find something else now. == ADWARE WITH PROTECTION Norton does protect. However, it has become bloated and inefficient. It insists on doing additional scans only to try and sell you upgrades to fix "problems." I am sure less tech-savvy people fall for the urgent recommendations and the tricky subscription sign-ups for additional products. The incessant pop-ups are almost always unnecessary and often lead to these upsell attempts. == PUTS YOU AT RISK OF COMPLETELY DISABLING YOUR COMPUTER One of the "fixes" it now offers is to update drivers. Unless you are careful, applying their updates could cause huge problems with your computer. You should really only be doing this through your computer manufacturer's update methods (website or software app). == THE OUTRAGEOUS UNINSTALL EXPERIENCE Uninstalling Norton is ridiculous!! Using the normal Windows uninstaller fails to complete so you are directed to download and use the "Norton Removal and Reinstall" tool. Running that, it only has a button for "Remove and Reinstall" but if you click on the "Advanced" button, it displays a grave warning that you shouldn't just uninstall and then, finally, a "Remove Button." (see photo) But wait!! You think it's gone, but it might not be. After rebooting one of my computers, an urgent Norton window popped up telling you to reinstall Norton! I had to run their removal tool two more times to get rid of it, not before searching the web to find lots of people needing more help getting it off their system. UPDATE: After over a week, one of our other computers started popping up a window insisting we reinstall Norton with NO CANCEL BUTTON. You have to end the process (very technical) to get it to go away. UPDATE #2: I was at my father's house for the holidays and he also wanted to move to a different antivirus product. I tried to uninstall Norton, ran into the same problems, and I had to contact Norton support to get it removed!!! They had to connect to his laptop to do it remotely!!! If you ignore what I've said and install it anyway, I hope you like it because you'll never remove it on your own. Choose another option. This uninstall experience cemented my decision to switch to something else. It's basically malware. == MY SWITCH My Netgear router has a network protection service that includes their well-reviewed Bitdefender antivirus software, a Norton competitor. I decided to try it out on one computer. It's so much more peaceful. I does need initial tweaking in terms of what protection I do and don't want which is expected. Of course, it has some premium offerings (e.g., VPN), but it isn't aggressive and tricky like Norton. The software itself is priced competitively. == Regarding VPNs Don't use the Norton VPN or any antivirus software's VPN. You'll get much better performance from a separate VPN service for the same or cheaper. I use Windscribe but there are other good ones out there (NordVPN, SurfShark, ExpressVPN, Private Internet Access), Check reviews.

reviews.title: A perfect closed-back addition to the Sennheiser 6-series headphones!
reviews.comment:
I had high expectations for the HD620S and it exceeded all of them.
I own the HD6XX and they're incredible open back headphones, but I personally need closed back headphones most of the time. The HD620S is the answer!
This headphone has a neural response like all HD6-series headphones, but it has a little more low end and high end because it's a closed back. So more bass, more treble... But it's not bass heavy, and it's not overly bright. It's balanced. It's just right.
Music sounds "the way it should" -- but with more detail than what you would hear in the HD650 or HD6XX. However, it's not the kind of detail some headphones add, where the treble is boosted to an absurd degree. Rather, it's just there. It's present.
The bass is the same. It gives you what you need without overshadowing the low mids.
This 6-series headphone uses a 5-series case, because Sennheiser found that the 5-series casing works better for closed back headphones... But it sounds like a 6-series.
No worries about the case, though -- it's very comfortable. I look like Alfred E. Neumann and yet my ears don't touch the drivers at all!
One thing I noticed about this headphone was the sense of space. Usually closed-back headphones sound "in your head", which is fine... But open back headphones have that 'wide sound stage'. The HD620S is a little closer to open backs in that regard, but without the room noise.
As far as blocking external sound -- the HD620S is about average in that regard, which is fine.
The cord comes out of only the left side (unlike the HD6XX which comes out of both sides.) This is a welcome upgrade. The cord is durable enough, but lightweight so there's no sense of imbalance. It is slightly "microphonic" though, which is the wrong word but it's what headphone people use. I'm talking about physical transfer of noise. If the headphone cable is tapping or moving, and nothing is playing in the headphones -- you can hear it a little.  Moreso than most professional quality/audiophile headphones... But not nearly as bad as the HD280Pro.  It's not a problem at all, but just something to be aware of. I don't notice it at all during regular use, and I move my head a lot.
This isn't a headphone you would want to use outdoors. The drivers have a very thin netting over them, which keeps out large debris but you wouldn't want to use these in a dusty area. Think of these as home & studio headphones.
Speaking of studio -- these are phenomenal for music production. They sound like studio monitors, basically, in the best possible way... Meaning they won't make a poorly mixed song sound good -- but a properly mixed song sounds detailed and amazing... With no noticeable peaks or valleys to make mixing confusing.
I would recommend these headphones for anyone who wants a reasonably affordable high end audio experience, or for audio engineers who need closed back headphones but want open back sound and quality.
In short, between the HD6XX and HD620S -- these are the only headphones I need, and I've purchased (too) many before this. I love these headphones, and the HD620S in particular is my favorite.
reviews.author: Jan Michael

reviews.title: I cant believe how good these are at this price.
reviews.comment:
Simply amazing. I have been a headphone guy for years. I almost always exclusively use open back headphones. I have had some closed back headphones in the past that cost multiple times as much as these do and there has always been a sense of claustrophobia in the music making it unrealistically difficult to get a grasp on the spacial qualities of the songs. Out of the box these changed my perception on closed back headphones and the more I use them the better they get. Also, there's nothing wring with that claustrophobic right-next-to-your-head sound, its what I get and expect from Bluetooth wireless headphones, even the nicer ones. The way those create spacial qualities in music is usually with DSP, digital signal processing. That makes the fun happen for sure but its not realistic. The wireless headphones spend much more time on tech in the digital realm than good old sound quality.
What the Sennheiser HD620s do, to my ears, is a revelation in the closed back headphone market. Are there others that sound better, I'm sure there are, the HIFI world is vast and insane. What these do is give me everything I want in a closed back headphone at a price anyone can either afford or save up to. I mean that across the board, it's everything I want. Clarity is nice, mids are Sennheiser's specialty so they are realistic and nice, bass is there when needed but not too deep. The highs are not to pingy and insane and the bass is not so deep that it distracts from the music.
The Sennheiser HD600, as many people know, is possibly the best all around headphone on the market. This is why they have bene unchanged for decades and continue to sell super well. Again, there are many that are better but at the price point the HD600 does everything so well that it is often one of the price point benchmarks that other headphone manufacturers try to beat. Nothing sounds bad on it. It's my go to swiss army knife ol reliable and it scales incredibly well sounding better and better the more the listener invests in their chain. I reach to it often and I have many headphones that are MUCH more expensive. Tons of people feel the same.
The Sennheiser HD620s does not sound like the HD600 so don't expect that. What the HD620s represents to me is the same idea as the HD600, the headphone that will sound great all the time no matter what it connect it to, just this time as a closed back. It's wonderful. It is easier to drive than the HD600, I would assume you could use it from the iphone dongle or the headphone out on a laptop, I have not tried this, but I would HIGHLY recommend using an external dac, amp, or dac/amp. The HD620s, much like the HD600, scales very well and sound better and better higher quality the chain is.

reviews.title: Great but flawed product that can be amazing with EQ

Cons- stock sound quality is wonky but easily corrected with eq. Look up reviewer based Resolves eq adjustments and use an auto eq app to apply them. Regular price is too high I feel. The top headband should be user replaceable but it looks like it’s just glued on.
Final Thoughts- While this isn’t a perfect headphone. The isolation and almost great sound quality out of the box except for certain songs is great. But my experience with this headphone with eq makes the wonkyness of the sound for certain songs disappear and just sound fantastic for the price. The isolation for this headphone if you can get a good seal is seriously impressive, I used this headphone at an event to monitor the audio and I could make out the audio coming from the headphones perfectly with the PA system at volume levels that were uncomfortable for me.  If you know this is compromised headphone and can either deal with the experience or modify it so it’s perfect for your taste I see this as a good value product if you get it at the right price.

reviews.title: Swinging WAY above its weight class!
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/C1GFGM-bgmL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/61vE3YQp0aL._SY256.jpg Solid AIO. No one had a rework written up on it yet so I figured I would be the first.
What I like about this AIO are its performance paired with good looks. It’s sleek, the display is bright and looks crisp, the connectivity is easy, and its performance isn’t sacrificed to give you this.
I’m still running tests on the CPU for thermal limitations and to figure out how long it takes to hit equilibrium, but so far this thing is holding its own against my older arctic 2.
It’s consistently holding my R7 7800X3D at or about the 35c temperature range and under stress it’s not breaking 65c, allowing my CPU to hit boost clock and hold for longer.
What I’m a little skeptical of is the software that comes with it and the radiator thickness. I’m used to having a thicker radiator with more volume in it so I’m a little worried about thermal saturation under heavy pump speeds. Time will tell on this one. At 100.00 I’m willing to take a chance on it and if it lasts me a year or two, I’ll consider it a win for the little guy.
I have another PC running on a v1 peerless assassins, and the cooler hasn’t missed a beat and almost 3 years now, so I do have high hopes, but the jury remains out and I’ll update if something g changes.
My last complaint isn’t so much a complaint as it is more of an old man’s ramblings. The software is fine and serviceable. It does what it says on the box. But Thermalright could do much better if they spend a couple of grand and hire a technical writer to write a manual for the software.
Explaining how the effects layers work, and how you can upload images and use their own stock templates on it would really I think answer a lot of questions people have and soften the user learning curve.
Overall this is a great AIO so far. Time will tell about things like clogging, wear and evaporation rates, but at the price point I’m willing to take that chance and I’m glad I did.
Edit: updated review to reflect my current opinion of the product. After several thermal tests, including an hour long burn in with Cinebench R23 at 100% cpu load, the package temp never broke 70c, and the core temp never broke 60c.
I’m very impressed with this cooler.

reviews.title: The best CPU cooler under 40mm
reviews.comment: This review doesn't exist in a vacuum, as I tried almost every other cooler at this size constraint, and the others don't perform as well. The total mass of the unit, the AM5-optimized hot-spot dissipation, and the manufacturers obsessive commitment to noise reduction = the best AM5 CPU cooler under 40mm. The competition is both louder and less efficient, as they either haven't optimized for the AM5 hot-spots or don't have enough total mass to soak the heat for air transfer. And just to add more QOL improvements, the Noctua NH-L9a-AM5 has the easiest installation, the best fit and finish, clear and detailed instructions, field-leading thermal paste, and additional hardware for mounting taller fans. As always, they include their "low-noise" adapter cable, in a tidy little package that exude quality.

reviews.title: Great keyboard, software is finicky, after setup it's a dream.
reviews.comment:
I got this cause I needed a wireless, smaller keyboard for my desk. I can't believe I only paid 100 dollars for this.
Features:
-This uses a bluetooth dongle and has the option of connecting via bluetooth. That can be helpful if you're switching between your main computer which is connected via dongle and your laptop (or something) that is connected via bluetooth. The switch is instantaneous as well.
-Has a low profile volume wheel on the edge of the keyboard as well as some low profile skip/pause/mute controls on the upper right
-fully customizable RGB. I keep it to audio responsive solid red w/ cyan cause it looks cool. It has an LED indicator for both the battery and caps lock.
-Comes with that old android style of USB cable (USB Micro). The cable that I got with the purchase was not functional for updating the keyboard, however it did work to charge it. I did have to use an old cable I had lying around to actually get it to update. The issue was when updating, the update button would be greyed out and it took some simple troubleshooting to figure out I just needed to try different USB Micro cables rather than the one supplied. This was the thing that ultimately got the update button to show up.
-VERY good battery life. I just keep a coiled charging cable nearby and charge it whenever it needs it. My only complaint here is I would prefer the modern USB Type C charging cable.
-Keys are low profile and I've grown to prefer this style over the full sized keycaps. I like not having to press the keys so far for the keystroke to register.

reviews.author: luis

reviews.title: Apprehensive about "renewed" products, but great experience so far.
reviews.comment:
I was slightly apprehensive about buying a "renewed" or refurbished product after reading a few of the reviews that mention malfunctioning keys, missing parts, or outright an outright broken product.
It seems my fears were unwarranted (though time will tell regarding longevity). I received the keyboard in adequate time. It was well packaged, and delivered to the specified area. It arrived in its factory box, with all of it requisite components, all still factory wrapped.
The keyboard connected to my PC without event, and after a brief firmware update, all of the functions work as advertised, and all seems well. Its very well made, has a reassuring amount of weight, with little to no flex in the keyboard, or keycap wiggle. LED lighting is nice and bright, with more than enough brightness options should the default brightness prove too intense.
The inbuilt lighting modes are all fascinating, and the per-keycap lighting options are loads of fun to play with. The typing experience is very satisfying, and the low profile of the keyboard itself lends itself to very little wrist discomfort. The included feet on the keyboard should help with any deviation in this.
All-in-all, I am very satisfied with my purchase.

reviews.author: Mariah

reviews.title: Top notch
reviews.comment:
Incredible build quality. The GX switches on the main clicks are crisp. Side clicks feel great and are in the perfect spot. The scroll wheel being so close the front is ideal (It’s one of the most underrated aspects of all the EGG mice).
I have 19x10cm hands and I find this mouse to be very comfortable. There's a couple different ways to grip it, but I tend to use a claw-style grip. The coating on the mouse helps with grip and feels nice. The grip can be enhanced with some small patches of grip tape in the right places.
Even at 1000Hz, the mouse is super responsive. This causes battery life to be so-so, regardless of the polling rate. I think you can feel the difference between 1kHz and 4kHz when using a 360Hz OLED. I couldn’t feel much difference on a 144Hz monitor though.
The software is pretty good. It does exactly what it needs to and nothing more. It doesn’t require an internet connection (besides downloading it) or an account.
It’d be great if they could make this mouse lighter. 58g makes it feel pretty dense compared to newer sub-40g mice, but it’s still pretty light. I would instantly buy a newer version of this mouse if they came out with one under 50g.
Objectively this is one of the best mice on the market. I think it’s subjectively one of the best mice as well.
reviews.author: Matthew Curby

reviews.title: Insane hot swappable switch mouse!
reviews.comment:
I’ve gone through a lot of mice trying to find “the one.” I started with the Superlight v1 and v2 but my hand always felt fatigued. Then I tried the Sora v2 and realized shape really is king- it fit my claw grip perfectly but it was a bit too light and the tech wasn't super up to date. I moved to the Lamzu Atlantis Mini 4K, which I thought would be my long term main, but the back hump felt steeper than I liked and it could be inconsistent.
I got the OP1w v2 and it completely blew all of them out of the water.
It has the same overall feel as the Sora v2 in terms of shape and ergonomics, but with the added control from its slightly heavier weight and better tech. The updated sensor, MCU, higher tracking speed, and the option for hot swappable switches are huge.
Small warning: the “hot swappable” part is worded weird... you need to buy the Universal Switch Pack (available thru EGG) to actually get the swappable PCBs. The stock custom Kailh GX switches feel great though, especially with Speed Mode turned on in the EGG tool. I tried Huano Pink Dots (felt mushy and hurt my accuracy) and Kailh 9.0s (pretty good), but I might end up going back to GX tbh.
For reference, my hand size is 18 x 8 cm with a 7.9 cm middle finger and I use a claw grip. If you don’t claw, this mouse might feel weird since it kind of naturally puts your hand into a claw shape but in a comfortable way if that’s already your style. If you actually want to learn claw grip, this mouse might help too.
Overall, this mouse is wild. Not sure what could top it besides future tech upgrades.

reviews.title: Spent hundreds on different mice and finally found one I like

reviews.author: dissapointed customer

reviews.title: A True Endgame
reviews.comment:
The Endgame OP1 shape is one of the strongest in the market and is now my favorite all time next to the Logitech 703, Logitech Superlight, and Razer's DeathAdder V3 Hyperspeed. I would describe the shape as a thinner middle ground between the Pulsar X2 and X2H. I understand the OP1 has been out for some time now but the hype is still real folks.
With absolutely zero creaking, my OP1w4K has one of the sturdiest build qualities I've felt, alongside my Vaxee Outset AX and aforementioned DeathAdder V3H. Both left and right clicks feel pleasant and snappy, and so do both thumb buttons. The sensor feels very accurate and responsive as well.
Running 2000hz polling rate with MotionSync has been my sweet spot, and I would estimate that there's around 35 hours of battery life with these settings. I want to note that my OP1w4K can't run MotionSync simultaneously with Deep Sleep as it would brick the mouse when waking up from Deep Sleep. Endgame's customer support on Discord advised that this was a known issue and to turn off either setting, which has done the trick. That said, there needs to be a future firmware update to fix this bug.
Also wanted to note my initial order received came in an unsealed product box and the OP1w4K inside was entirely used with its mouse feet/skates replaced with aftermarket dots. Whoever out there doing this to gaming mice on Amazon can go to elo hell.
Thankfully Amazon and/or Pro Gamersware USA quickly replaced my item the very next day. The new order received was sealed and the mouse inside was wrapped in plastic and completely brand new.

reviews.title: An absolutely wonderful gaming mouse!
reviews.comment: The Corsair M75 Wireless RGB Lightweight FPS Gaming Mouse is absolutely perfect and it just works. Not the lightest weight gaming mouse, but I actually find the lightweight ones (<60 grams) are too light. I actually prefer this medium weight one. It is very well built and everything works including the scroll wheel (looking at you Razer Viper V2 Pro). I also enjoy having the RGB lighting as it is a quick way to tell if the mouse is turned on or off. I don't use it for looks really, but instead feedback. Really good shape and is comfortable for my finger grip and medium size hands. I was worried about the swappable magnetic buttons falling off as I typically transport my mouse with my laptop in my backpack, but it is a non-issue as they stay attached very well. I had some prior experience with another Corsair mouse which had a magnetic piece and it never came off, so I took a chance on this one. I am not the biggest fan of iCUE software as it is not very intuitive to use, but it does get the job done. Razer's software is definitely more intuitive, but they cannot get their scroll wheels to work. Corsair has definitely impressed me with their products from keyboards to mice.

reviews.title: great mouse if you use MMB press and hold for 3D and CAD applications.

Hard to find a middle mouse button (MMB) that is sensitive and easy to depress. that's an important feature for me because my software demands thousands of MMB presses and holds every day.
good battery life and comfortable in my hand. I'm a Lefty so this mouse is a gold star find.
will probably buy another just to have as a backup in case they stop making these in the near future.
CONS:
side buttons are a bit clunky to use, switch, customize, and overall press is too 'jiggly'. Not a big deal for me since i only use 2 side buttons for FWD/BACK when surfin'.  Something to consider though.
Big issue I have is no "low battery" indicator. Small icon in system tray but can't really notice it.  would love a "pop up" option in windows or even flashing lights on the mouse, but might not be able to see it.
